They do not know the Book except in wishful thinking
, and wishful thinking is not a type of Surat al-Baqarah 2:78
h
And among them are unlettered people
who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, and they do nothing but assume. the Book, as our Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, said:
h
They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption

and assumption is separate from knowledge. And as He said: And no one has with Him any favor for which he will be rewarded * Except seeking the countenance of his Lord, the Most High (al-Layl 92:19-20), and as the poet said: There is no reproach between me and Qais other than stabbing the kidneys and striking the necks As the genius of Banu Dhubyan said: I took an oath that was not dualistic, and I had no knowledge except good opinion of the owner There are similar examples of what we have mentioned, and the book would be too long to list them all.

The word illa excludes what comes after it from the meaning of what came before it and from its description, even if each of them is not of the form of the other or of its type. Some Arabists call this a disconnected exception, because the speech that comes after illa is disconnected from the meaning of what came before it. This is how it is in every place where it is good to replace illa but lakun, so that the meaning of the second is known to be disconnected from the meaning of the first. Don’t you see that if you say:
h
And among them are unlettered people

who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, then you want to replace illa but delete illa, you will find the speech to be correct in meaning, correct and in it is illa? That is if you say:
h
And among them are unlettered people
who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking. Meaning: But they wish. Likewise His statement:
h
They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption
r
(An-Nisa’: 157)
, but the following of assumption means: But they follow assumption.

And so is all this type of speech as we have described. It has been mentioned that some of the reciters read: except for wishes in a lightened form. Those who lightened it pointed to something like their plural of al-Miftah as Mafatih and al-Qarqour as Qaraqir. And when the plural ya was deleted, the original ya was lightened, I mean from al-Amani, just as they pluralized al-Athfiyah as Athafi in a lightened form, as Zuhair bin Abi Salma said: My hearths are burning in a cauldron of a wedding, and my vision is like the trunk of a basin that has not been broken. As for the one who made Amani heavy, he stressed its yaa, and he directed that to something like their plural of al-miftah is mafatih, and al-qarqur is qarqir, and al-zunbur is zanabir, so the yaa of fa’aalil and its lam came together, and they are both ya an, so one of them was assimilated into the other, so they became one stressed yaa.

As for the reading that I do not permit any other reading for a reader in this regard, it is the emphasis on the Ya of Al-Amani, due to the consensus of the readers that it is the reading that the predecessors used to read, and this is widespread among them, and its authenticity and the anomaly of the reader in making it light are not denied, as the evidence is unanimous in that. And sufficient evidence of the error of the reader of this in making it light is their consensus on his error.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: They only conjecture.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And they only assume
, and they are not, as He, the Most High, said:
Their messengers said to them, ‘We are only human beings like you’

meaning by that: We are only human beings like you. The meaning of his saying: except they think, is that they doubt and do not know its truth and correctness. And the suspicion in this place is doubt. The meaning of the verse: And among them are those who do not write or inscribe, and do not know the Book of God, nor do they know what is in it, except by guessing and falsely attributing falsehood to God, thinking that they are right in their guessing and false attribution. God the Most High described them as being in their conjecture, thinking that they were right, but they were wrong, because they had heard from their leaders and rabbis things that they thought were from the Book of God, but they were not from the Book of God.

So God the Most High described them as abandoning belief in what they were certain was from God, which Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought, and following what they were doubtful about, and in reality they were suspicious of, what their leaders, leaders and rabbis had told them, out of stubbornness towards God and His Messenger, and disobeying the command of God, and being deceived by God’s respite for them.
And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement:
h
And they only conjecture
, the interpreters from the Salaf said about it:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they only conjecture
, that is, they lie.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
They do not know the Book except in wishful thinking
, and they do nothing but conjecture, meaning they do not know and do not understand what is in it, and they deny your prophethood based on conjecture.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They only assume, he said: They assume assumptions that are not true.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said:
m: They assume false assumptions.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly.

evidence.text: It is not to be memorized, it is read like this.
If that meant that they recited it, they would not have been conjecturing, and likewise if it meant that they desired it.
It has been mentioned that some of the reciters read: except for wishes in a lightened form.

As for the reading that I do not permit any other reading for a reader in this regard, it is the emphasis on the Ya of Al-Amani, due to the consensus of the readers that it is the reading that the predecessors used to read, and this is widespread among them, and its authenticity and the anomaly of the reader in making it light are not denied, as the evidence is unanimous in that.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement: So woe.
Some of them said what:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman bin Saʿid told us, on the authority of Bishr bin ʿAmara, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So woe, he says: So the punishment is upon them.

x: Others said: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Fayyad, he said: I heard Abu Ayyad say: Woe is what flows from pus at the bottom of Hell.

c: Bishr bin Abaan Al-Hattāb told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyān, on the authority of Ziyad bin Fayyad, on the authority of Abu Ayyad,
m: regarding his statement: So woe, he said: A cistern at the bottom of Hell, in which their pus flows.

c: Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told us, Zaid bin Abi al-Zarqa told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ziyad bin Fayyad, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, who said:
m: Woe is a valley of pus in Hell.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, on the authority of Shuqaiq, he said:
m: Woe, what pus flows at the bottom of Hell.

x: Others said: Al-Muthanna told us, he said:

c: Ibrahim bin Abdul Salam bin Saleh Al-Tastari told us, he said: Ali bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar, on the authority of Kinanah Al-Adawi, on the authority of Uthman bin Affan, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Woe is a mountain in Hell.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Diraj, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Woe is a valley in Hell, into which the unbeliever falls for forty autumns before he reaches its bottom.

x: The meaning of the verse, according to what was narrated from the one whose interpretation I mentioned, is: Woe. The punishment, which is drinking the pus of the people of Hell at the bottom of Hell, is for the Jews who write falsehood with their hands, then say: This is from God.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: For those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, ‘This is from God,’ in order to exchange it for a small price.

He means by that those who distorted the Book of God from the Jews of the Children of Israel, and wrote a book according to their interpretations, contrary to what God revealed to His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, then sold it to people who had no knowledge of it, nor of what was in the Torah, ignorant of what was in the Books of God in order to seek a lowly worldly gain. So God said to them:
h
So woe to them for what their hands have written
, and woe to them for what they earn, as Moses told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: (
h
So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say

, ‘This is from God,’ in order to exchange it for a small price, he said: There were some Jews who wrote a book from themselves, selling it to the Arabs, and telling them that it was from God, in order to exchange it for a small price.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed told us, he said, Bishr bin Amara told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The illiterate are a people who did not believe in a messenger sent by God, nor in a book revealed by God, so they wrote a book with their own hands, then they said to a group of ignorant, base al-Nas 114:This is from God, to exchange it for a small price. He said: A worldly commodity.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: For those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say, ‘This is from God,’ he said: These are the ones who knew that it was from God, but they distorted it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: Then they distort it.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands
the verse, and they are the Jews.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say

, ‘This is from God,’ he said: There were people from the Children of Israel who wrote a book with their own hands, in order to devour people, and they said, ‘This is from God,’ but it is not from God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say

, ‘This is from God,’ in order to exchange it for a small price. He said: They deliberately took what God revealed in their book of the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and distorted it from its proper places, seeking thereby worldly gain. So he said:
h
So woe to them for what their hands have written
and woe to them for what they earn.

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, Ibrahim bin Abdul Salam told us, Ali bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar, on the authority of Kinanah Al-Adawi, on the authority of Uthman bin Affan,
m: may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
So woe to them for what their hands have written

and woe to them for what they earn. Woe is a mountain in the Fire, and it is what was revealed about the Jews, because they distorted the Torah, and added to it what they liked, and erased from it what they hated, and erased the name of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Torah. For this reason, God became angry with them, so He lifted up part of the Torah and said:
h
So woe to them for what their hands have written
and woe to them for what they earn.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Saeed bin Abi Ayoub told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ajlan, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, he said:
m: Woe, a valley in Hell, if the mountains were to be moved through it, they would melt from the intensity of its heat.

x: If someone were to say to us: What is the meaning of his saying:
h
So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands

? Can writing be done without the hand, such that those addressed by this address needed to tell about these people whose story he narrated that they wrote the Scripture with their own hands? It was said to him: The book is from the sons of Adam, even if it is from them by hand, because the book may be attributed to someone other than its writer and the one who is in charge of drawing its script, so it is said: So-and-so wrote to so-and-so about such-and-such, even if the one who is in charge of writing it by hand is not the one to whom the book is attributed, if the writer wrote it at the command of the one to whom the book is attributed. So our Lord informed His believing servants by His saying:
h
So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands

, that the rabbis of the Jews write lies and slander against God with their own hands, knowingly and deliberately lying about God, then they attribute it to being from God and in the Book of God, lying about God and fabricating against Him.
So He, the Most High, denied by His saying:
h
They write the Scripture with their own hands

, that the one who is in charge of writing that is some of their ignorant ones at the command of their scholars and rabbis. This is similar to the saying of the speaker: So-and-so sold me his eye for such-and-such, so-and-so bought himself for such-and-such. What is meant by including the soul and the eye in that is to remove any confusion from the listener, that the one in charge of selling or buying that is not the one to whom the matter is described, and to make the reality of the action obligatory for the one being told about. So too is his saying:
h
So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
So woe to them for what their hands have written
and woe to them for what they earn.
What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His statement:
h
So woe to them for what their hands have written

, is that the torment in the valley of the pus of the people of Hell at the bottom of Hell is for them, meaning: for those who wrote the book, the matter of which we have described, from the Jews of the Children of Israel, distorted, then they said: This is from God, seeking a worldly gain of which few of them would buy it. And His statement:
h
From what their hands have written
, meaning:
h
from what their hands have written

of that, and woe to them also from what they earn, meaning: from what they do of sins, and what they commit of crimes, and what they earn from what is forbidden, with their book that they write with their hands contrary to what God has revealed, then they eat its price, and they have sold it to those who sold it from them on the grounds that it is from the Book of God, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: And woe to them from what they earn, meaning: from sin.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Bishr bin Amara, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So woe to them, meaning: So the punishment is upon them. He said: He says: Who wrote with their own hands that lie, And woe to them for what they earn, meaning: What they eat from the lowly and others.

x: The root of earning is work. So every worker does Surat al-Baqarah 2:79
h
So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands and then say
, "This is from God," in order to exchange it for a small price.
h
So woe to them for what their hands have written

and woe to them for what they earn. work, by directly doing what he does, and by suffering professionally, so he earns what he does, as Labid bin Rabi’ah said: For Maafar Qahd, he quarreled, his body was covered with waste, and his food was not safe
By His statement,
h
And they said

, he means the Jews. He says: And the Jews said, The Fire will not touch us, meaning: Our bodies will not encounter the Fire and we will not enter it, except for a few days. And it was said numbered, even though their number was not specified in the revelation, because God, the Most High, informed us of that, and they know the number of days that they are allotted for their stay in the Fire. For this reason, He left out mentioning the number of those days, and called them numbered, for what we have described. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the number of days that the Jews had specified, saying what God had informed us about them.

c: Some of them said what Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman ibn Saʿid told us, on the authority of Bishr ibn ʿAmara, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
And they said
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days

.’ That was said by the enemies of God, the Jews. They said, “God will not let us enter the Fire except to fulfill the oath, the days in which we killed the calf: forty days. So when those days have passed, the punishment and the oath will be cut off from us.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days
, they said: A few days because of what we did with the calf.

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And they said
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days

.’ He said: The Jews said: God will cause us to enter the Fire and we will remain in it for forty nights, until the Fire has consumed our sins and cleansed us, then a caller will call out: Bring out every circumcised person from the children of Israel. For that is what we were commanded to be circumcised. They said: Then they will not leave anyone from us in the Fire without bringing him out.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said: The Jews said:
m: Our Lord rebuked us for our affair, so He swore to punish us for forty nights, then bring us out. So God denied them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The Jews said:
m: We will not enter Hell except to fulfill the oath, the number of days in which we worshipped the calf.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days

, the verse. Ibn Abbas said: It was mentioned that the Jews found written in the Torah that the distance between the two ends of Hell is a journey of forty years, until they reach the tree of Zaqqum growing at the bottom of Hell. Ibn Abbas used to say: Hell is Saqar, and in it is the tree of Zaqqum. The enemies of God claimed that when the number of days that they found in their book is over, what they mean by that is the journey that ends at the bottom of Hell. They said: When the number is over, the term will end, so there will be no punishment, and Hell will go away and be destroyed. That is what His statement:
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days

, means the term. Ibn Abbas said: When they stormed through the gate of Hell, they walked in the punishment until they reached the tree of Zaqqum on the last day of the numbered days. The keepers of Saqar said to them: You claimed that the Fire will not touch you except for a few days! The number is empty, and you are in eternity! So he took them ascending in hell, exhausting them.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they said
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days
,’ except for forty nights.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Umar told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: “The Jews argued with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
and they said

: We will not enter the Fire except for forty nights, and another people will succeed us in it, meaning Muhammad and his companions. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said with his hand on their heads: Rather, you will abide therein forever, and no one will succeed you in it.” Then God, may His praise be exalted, revealed: “And they say:
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Al-Hakam ibn Abaan informed me, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: The Jews gathered one day to argue with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said:
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days

, and they named forty days, then people will replace us or join us in it. They pointed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have lied. Rather, you will abide in it forever, we will not join you or replace you in it, God willing, ever.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ali bin Ma’bad told us, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days
, he said: The Jews said: We will not be tormented in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection except for forty days, the amount of time we worshipped the calf.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said, my father told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: "I ask you by God and by the Torah that God sent down to Moses on the day of Mount Sinai, who are the people of Hell whom God sent down in the Torah? They said: Their Lord was angry with them, so we will remain in the Fire for forty nights, then we will come out and you will replace us in it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have lied, by God, we will never replace you in it." So the Qur'an was revealed confirming the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and refuting them: And they say, '
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days
.' Say, 'Have you taken a covenant from God?' until His saying: They will abide therein eternally.

x: Others said about this:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Ibn Ishaq told us,
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd bin Thabit, told me, Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Jews used to say: The duration of this world is only seven thousand years, and God will only punish people on the Day of Resurrection for every thousand years of this world, one day of the days of the Hereafter, and they are seven days. So God revealed about this from their saying: And they say, ‘
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days
’ (al-Baqarah 2:170).

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: or ʿIkrimah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, and the Jews were saying: The duration of this world is only seven thousand years, and people are only tormented in the Fire for every thousand years of this world, one day in the Fire from the days of the Hereafter, so it is only seven days, then the torment will stop.” So God Almighty revealed regarding that from their saying: The Fire will not touch us the verse.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: They said, ‘
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days
,’ he said: She used to say: The world is only seven thousand years, and we are only tormented for one day for every thousand years.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: The Jews used to say: The world is only… and the rest of the hadith is similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said:
h
And they said
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days

of time. And they named the number of seven thousand years, and out of every thousand years a day. The Jews say this. Say: Have you taken a covenant from God - God will never break His covenant - or do you say about God what you do not know?

x: When the Jews said what they said, saying: The Fire shall not touch us except for a few days, as we have explained of the interpretation of that, God said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the company of Jews: Have you taken a covenant from God? Have you taken a covenant from God with what you say, for God does not break His covenant, nor does He change His promise and His contract, or are you saying falsehood about God out of ignorance and boldness toward Him?

c: As Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told us, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, on the authority of ʿIsa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “Say: Have you taken a covenant from God?” That is, a confirmation from God that it is as you say.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Surat al-Baqarah 2:80 And they say,
h
The Fire will not touch us except for a few days

. Say, Have you taken a covenant from God - God will never fail in His covenant - or are you saying about God what you do not know? The Jews said: We will not enter the Fire except for the fulfillment of the oath, the number of days during which we worshipped the calf. So God said: Have you taken a covenant from God about what you are saying? Do you have any proof or evidence for this? God will not break His covenant, so produce your proof and evidence. Or are you saying about God what you do not know? Abu Kuraib narrated that Uthman ibn Saeed narrated on the authority of Bishr ibn Amara on the authority of Abu Rawq on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the Jews said what they said, God, the Most High, said to Muhammad, “Say: ‘Have you taken a covenant from God?’” He said: Have you stored up a covenant with God? He said: Did you say, ‘There is no god but God,’ and did not associate anything with Him or disbelieve in Him? So if you said it, then hope for it, and if you did not say it, then why do you say about God what you do not know? They said: “If you had said, ‘There is no god but God,’ and did not associate anything with Him, and then died on that, then it would have been a treasure with Me for you, and I would not have broken My promise to you: that I will reward you for it.”

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When the Jews said what they said, God Almighty said: Say, ‘Have you taken a covenant from God? But God will never break His covenant.’ And He said in another place: And what they used to invent deceived them in their religion
r
(Al Imran 3:24)
, then He told the report and said: Yes, whoever earns evil.

x: These statements that we have narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and Qatadah are similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement: “Say: Have you taken a covenant from God?” Because among the covenants that God has given His servants is that whoever believes in Him and obeys His command, He will save him from His Fire on the Day of Resurrection. And among the covenants that He has given them is the acknowledgment that there is no god but God. And likewise among the covenants that He has made with them is that whoever comes to God on the Day of Resurrection with an argument will have salvation from the Fire, and He will save him from it. And all of that, even if the wording of those who said it differs, the meanings are in agreement, based on what we have said about it. And God knows best.

His statement, Yes, whoever has earned evil, is a denial from God to those who say among the Jews, The Fire will not touch us except for a few days, and an announcement from Him to them that He will punish whoever associates partners with God and whoever disbelieves in Him and His Messengers, and whose sins surround him, and will abide in Hell forever, for Paradise will only be inhabited by those who believe in Him and His Messengers, and those who obey Him, and those who uphold His limits, as Muhammad ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, or ʿIkrimah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas: Yes, whoever has earned evil and whose sins surround him, meaning: whoever does the same deeds as you do, and disbelieves in the same way that you disbelieve in, until his disbelief surrounds his good deeds, and those are the companions of Hell, they will abide therein forever.

As for bala, it is an acknowledgment in every statement that begins with a denial, just as yes is an acknowledgment in a question that does not contain a denial. Its original form is bal, which is a return from pure denial, as in your saying: Amr did not stand, but Zayd. The letter ya was added to it so that it would be appropriate to pause on it, since bal was not appropriate to pause on, since it was a conjunction and a return from denial. And so that I mean bala would be a return from denial only, and an acknowledgment of the action that comes after the denial. The letter ya in it indicates the meaning of acknowledgment and favor. And the word bal indicates a return from denial.

As for the evil that God mentioned in this place, it is associating partners with God, as Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya ibn Saʿid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, he said, Asim told me, on the authority of Abu Waʿil: Yes, whoever earns a bad deed, he said: associating partners with God.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Yes, whoever earns evil: polytheism.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Yes, whoever earns evil, he said: As for evil, it is polytheism.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Yes, whoever earns evil. As for evil, it is the sins for which Hell is promised.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I said to Ata’: Yes, whoever earns evil, he said: Polytheism. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: Evil, polytheism.

c: I was told by Ammar ibn Al-Hasan,
m: he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, his saying: Yes, whoever earns evil, he means: polytheism.

x: We said that the evil that God, the Most High, mentioned, that whoever commits it and his sin encompasses him, is among the people of Hell who will abide therein eternally in this place, God meant by it some evil deeds and not others, even though its apparent meaning in the recitation is general, because God has decreed that its people will abide eternally in Hell. And abiding eternally in Hell is for the people of disbelief in God, not the people of faith, because the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are clear that the people of faith will not abide therein eternally, and that abiding eternally in Hell is for the people of disbelief in God, not the people of faith. God, the Most High, coupled His statement, Yes, whoever commits evil and his sin encompasses him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally with His statement, And those who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
So it was known from this that those who abide eternally in Hell are the people of evil deeds, not those who abide eternally in Paradise are the people of faith.

If someone thinks that those who have eternal life in Paradise among those who believe are those who did good deeds, not those who did evil deeds, then in God’s statement that He will expiate our sins by avoiding the major sins that we are forbidden to do, and our entrance is the noble entrance, there is what indicates the correctness of what we said in the interpretation of His statement: Yes, whoever earns evil, that this applies to a specific type of evil deeds, not all of them. If someone were to say to us: God Almighty has guaranteed us the expiation of our sins by our avoiding the major sins that we are forbidden from, then what is the evidence that major sins are not included in His Surat Al-Baqarah 2:81 Yes, whoever earns evil and is surrounded by his sin - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. statement: Yes, whoever earns evil?

Since it is authentic that minor sins are not included in it, and that the meaning of the verse is specific and not general, it is proven and authentic that judging and ruling with it is not permissible for anyone against anyone, except for the one whom God has informed him of it based on a definitive report that excuses the one who has received it. It has been proven and authenticated that God, the Most High, meant by that the people of polytheism and disbelief in Him, based on the testimony of the entire Ummah. Therefore, it is necessary to judge that the people of polytheism and disbelief are among those whom God meant by the verse. As for the people of major sins, the definitive reports that excuse the one who has received them have become clear to us that they are not meant by it. So whoever denies that from those who have rejected the argument of the widespread reports and the clear report, then it is necessary for him to abandon the definitive testimony that the people of major sins will remain in Hell forever, based on this verse and similar verses that came with their generality in the threat.

Since the interpretation of the Qur’an is not comprehensible except by the explanation of the one to whom God has made the explanation of the Qur’an, and the verse comes general in its apparent category, and its inner meaning is specific to that category. The defenders of the report that the people of major sins are among the people of exception ask us about the denial of stoning the married adulterer, and the removal of the obligation of prayer from the menstruating woman during her period. The question about them is similar to the question about these people, the same.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And his sin encompassed him
What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
And his sin encompassed him

, is that it gathered upon him and he died in it, before repenting and turning to God from it. The root of the word to surround is to encircle something, like a wall that surrounds a house. Hence the statement of God Almighty: A fire whose walls will encompass them (al-Kahf 18:29). The interpretation of the verse is: Whoever associates partners with God and commits many sins and dies upon them before repenting and turning to Him, then they are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein forever. And similar to what we have said in interpreting that, the interpreters said.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And his sin encompassed him
, he said: He died because of his sin.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Razin, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim:
m: And his sin surrounded him, he said: He died upon it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And his sin encompassed him
, he said: His disbelief encompasses his good deeds.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And his sin encompassed him
, he said: That for which God has made Hell obligatory.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And his sin encompassed him
, he said: As for sin, it is the major sin that requires it.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq Aqal told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And his sin encompassed him
, he said: The major sin.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said,
m: Ishaq Q! told us, Waki’ and Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Salam bin Maskeen, he said: A man asked Al-Hasan about his statement:
h
And his sin encompassed him
, so he said: We do not know what sin is. O my son, recite the Qur’an, for every verse for which God has promised Hell, it is sin.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Yes, whoever earns evil and his sin encompasses him, he said: Every encompassing sin is what God has promised Hell for.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Razin:
m: And his sin surrounded him, he said: He died because of his sin.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, he said, Masoud Abu Razin told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And his sin encompassed him
, he said: He is the one who dies in his sin before he repents.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Waki’ said:
m: I heard Al-A’mash say regarding His statement:
h
And his sin encompassed him
, he died because of his sins.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
h
And his sin encompassed him
, the major sin that requires punishment.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr ibn Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: His sin encompassed him, so he died without repenting.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, al-Husayn told us, he said, Hassan told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I said to Ata’: His sin encompassed him, he said: polytheism. Then he recited: And whoever brings evil - their faces will be thrown into the Fire (al-Naml 27:90).

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
Then those are the companions of the Fire
; they will abide therein eternally.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
Then those are the companions of the Fire

; they will abide therein eternally, is that those who have earned evil deeds and whose sins have surrounded them, are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. What He, the Most High, means by His saying, the companions of the Fire, is the people of the Fire. He made them its companions because they preferred in their worldly life that which would lead them to it and its blazing fire over the deeds that would lead them to Paradise. So He, the Most High, made them its companions because they preferred its causes over the causes of Paradise, like the companion of a man who befriends him, preferring his companionship over the companionship of someone else, so that he may be known by him. They are in it, meaning: they are in the Fire, eternally.
And by his saying: eternally he means residing, as:

c: Muhammad bin Hamid told me, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They will abide therein forever, meaning they will abide therein forever.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Saddī:
m: They will abide therein forever, they will never leave it.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: We said that the evil that God, the Most High, mentioned, that whoever commits it and his sin encompasses him, is among the people of Hell who will abide therein eternally in this place, God meant by it some evil deeds and not others, even though its apparent meaning in the recitation is general, because God has decreed that its people will abide eternally in Hell.

x: What is meant by his statement, and those who believed, is that they believed in what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. What is meant by his statement, and did righteous deeds, is that they obeyed God, established His limits, performed His obligations, and avoided His prohibitions. What is meant by his statement, those, is that those who are like that are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein eternally, meaning: its people who are its people, they will abide therein eternally, residing forever. This verse and the one before it are an announcement from God to His servants about the permanence of Hell and the permanence of its people in it, or the permanence of Paradise and the permanence of its people in it, and the permanence of what He has prepared in each of them for its people, as a denial from God, the Most High, to those of the Jews of the Children of Israel who said: The Fire will not touch them except for a few days, and that after that they will go to Paradise.

c: So He informed them
m: about the eternity of their disbelievers in Hell and the eternity of their believers in Paradise, as Ibn Hamid told me, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally. That is, whoever believes in what you disbelieve in and acts according to the religion you have abandoned, Paradise is for them, abiding therein eternally. He informs them that the reward for good and evil is constant for its people forever, never ending.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said, And those who believe and do righteous deeds, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, Those are the companions of Paradise, they will abide therein eternally.

x: We have already demonstrated in our previous book that the covenant is a verbal noun derived from the word to swear an oath and similar things that confirm a statement. So the meaning of the statement is: And remember also, O company of Children of Israel, when We took your covenant that you shall not worship except God, as Ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel means your covenant that you shall not worship except God.
The readings differ in the reading of His statement:
h
Do not worship
Some of them read it with the ta', and some of them read it with the ya', and the meaning is the same. The reading with the ya' and the ta', and to say
h
Do not worship
and
h
Do not worship

while they are absent, is because taking the covenant means taking an oath. Just as you say: I took your brother to stand up, so you tell him what you know about the absent person because he is absent from you. And you say: I took him to swear that you will stand up, so you tell him what you know about the one being addressed, because you had addressed him with that, so that would be correct and permissible. Likewise, His statement:
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
, [saying], 'You shall not worship except God,' and
h
Do not worship

. Whoever reads that with the ta', then the meaning is addressing, since the address had already been made with that. And whoever reads it with the ya', then it is because they were not addressed with that at the time of the reporting about them.

As for the raising of La 'ibadoun, it is with the ta' in ibadoun, and it is not made nasb by an which could have been used with La 'ibadoun illa God, because if it was suitable to be used with a verb and it was deleted and not used, the correct way of speaking about it would be to raise it, as God, the Most High, said: "Say: 'Is it other than God that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?'" (al-Zumar 39:64). So he raised I'badoun because an did not enter into it with the alif indicating the meaning of the future, and as the poet said. Oh, you who deter, I attend the battle and witness the pleasures. Are you immortal? So he raised the letter ahdara even though it is permissible to include an in it if it is deleted, with the letter alif which comes with the meaning of the future. It was only appropriate to delete that from His statement:
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
, ‘You shall not worship,’ because of the apparent indication of it in the speech, so it was sufficient to indicate what was apparent from it.
Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: The meaning of his statement:
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel

, ‘You shall not worship except God,’ is a narration, as if you said: We made them swear: You shall not worship, meaning we said to them: By God, you shall not worship, and they said: By God, they shall not worship. And the one who said that is close in meaning to the meaning of the statement we made about that. And similar to what we said about his statement:
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
, ‘You shall not worship except God,’ the people of interpretation interpreted it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: He took their covenants that they would be sincere to Him and not worship anyone other than Him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
, ‘You shall not worship except God,’ he said: We took their covenant that they would be sincere to God and not worship anyone other than Him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
, ‘You shall not worship except God,’ he said: The covenant that was taken from them at the table.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And to parents
, do good.
And His statement, may He be glorified:
h
And to parents
, good treatment, is in apposition to the position of the omitted that in worship none but God.

i: So the meaning of the statement is:
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
that they would worship none but God,
h
and to parents
, good treatment, so He raised that they would worship none because that was omitted, then He connected to parents to its position, as the poet said:
x: Muawiyah, we are human beings, so be patient, for we are neither mountains nor iron.

So iron was placed in the accusative case in conjunction with the position of mountains, because if it did not have a prepositional ba’ in it, it would have been in the accusative case. So iron was placed in conjunction with the meaning of mountains, not with its wording. So it is the same with what was described in His statement:
h
And to parents
, good treatment. As for the goodness, it is in the accusative case because of an implied verb whose meaning is conveyed by his statement:
h
and to parents
, since its meaning was understood. The meaning of the statement, if he had made the omitted word clear, would have been:
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
, that you would not worship except God, and that you would do good to parents. So it was sufficient to say:
h
and to parents
, instead of saying: and that you do good to parents, since it was understood that this was its meaning according to what was apparent from the statement.
Some Arabists have claimed that its meaning is: And be kind to your parents, so the ba in parents is a connection between kindness and it is placed before it.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: That you worship none but God, and be good to your parents. So they claimed that the ba’ in parents is a connection to the omitted word, I mean be good, so they made that into two sentences. The sentence is only diverted to what they claimed from that, if there is no way for the sentence to be consistent with one sentence. As for the sentence, there is a way that is understood to be consistent with one sentence, so there is no way to divert it to two sentences. Another is that if the statement in that were as they said, it would have been said: And to the parents, be good, because it is only said: So-and-so was good to his parents, and it is not said: He was good to his parents, except on the basis of a forced statement. But what we have said about it is what we have said, which is:
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
with such and such,
h
and to parents
, good treatment, as we have explained before.
So good treatment then is a source of speech, not of its wording, as we have explained in previous similar examples.
What is that kindness that was taken from them by the covenant of parents?

Similar to what God has imposed on our nation for them, such as doing good to them, speaking kindly, lowering the wing of humility out of mercy for them, showing compassion for them, showing mercy to them, praying for their well-being, and other similar actions that God has urged His servants to do for them.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And the relatives, the orphans, and the needy.

He means by his saying and the relatives, and by the relatives they should maintain ties with his relatives and kin. Qurbah is a verbal noun based on the estimation of the verb, from your saying, So-and-so's womb brought me close to him, meaning kinship, proximity, and proximity. As for orphans, they are the plural of orphan, like prisoner and prisoners. Orphans include both males and females. The meaning of this is:
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
, [saying], ‘You shall not worship except God,’ alone, without any other equals to Him, ‘
h
and to parents

, do good.’ And to relatives: that you maintain kinship ties and recognize their rights, and to orphans: that you show them mercy and compassion, and to the needy: that you give them their rights that God has made obligatory upon you, your wealth. The word muskeen is the one who is humble and submissive due to poverty and need, and it is derived from mouskanah.
Poverty is the humiliation of need and want.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And speak to people in a good manner.
If someone were to say: How was it said:
h
And speak to people in a good way

, so that the speech was a command without a command preceding it, but rather the speech is running from the beginning of the verse in the form of a statement? It was said: Although the speech was in the beginning of the verse as a report, it is appropriate in its place to address, with command and prohibition. If instead of: Worship none but God, it was: Worship none but God in the manner of God’s prohibition of them from worshipping anyone other than Him, it would be good and correct. It was mentioned that this is the case in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b. It was only good and permissible if it was read in this way because taking the covenant is a statement. The meaning of the statement, if it had been read in this way, would have been: And when We said to the Children of Israel:
h
Do not worship
except God, as the Most High said in another place: And when We took your covenant and raised the Mount above you, [saying], ‘Take what We have given you with strength’ (al-Baqarah 2:63).
Since it was good to place the command and prohibition in the place of:
h
Do not worship
except God, He connected it with His saying:
h
And speak to the people in a good way
, to the place of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:83 And remember when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel, "Worship none but Allah,
h
and to parents
do good, and to relatives, orphans, and the needy, and speak to people kindly,
h
and establish prayer
, and give zakah."
h
Then you turned away
, except for a few of you, while you were averse.
h
Do not worship
, even though each one of them differs in meaning from what is in it, because of what we described of the permissibility of placing the address with the command and prohibition in the place of
h
Do not worship
. So it is as if it was said: And when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel:
h
Do not worship
except God,
h
And speak to the people in a good way

i: This is similar to what we have explained previously: that the Arabs sometimes begin the speech in the manner of reporting about the absent in the place of narrating what they have reported, then return to reporting in the manner of addressing, and sometimes begin in the manner of addressing, then return to reporting in the manner of reporting about the absent, because of the two meanings in narration, as the poet said:
x: Treat us well or badly, we are not to be blamed or diminished if you are diminished It means: I followed.

As for Al-Hasan, the readers differed in his reading. The majority of the readers of Kufa, except for Asim, read it: Wa Qoolu al-Nas Hasna with the opening of the Ha and the Seen. The majority of the readers of Medina read it: Hasanan with the Damma of the Ha and the Sukoon of the Seen. It has been narrated from some of the readers that he used to read: Wa Qoolu al-Nas Hasna with the example of Fa’ala. The Arabists differed about the difference between the meaning of his saying: Hasan and Hasanan.

Some of the Basrans said: It is of two meanings: Either what is meant by Hasan is Hasan, and both are linguistically, as is said: Bukhl and Bukhl, or that Hasan is made to mean Hasan in the simile. This is because Hasan is a source and Hasan is a good thing.

i: This would then be like your saying: You are only eating and drinking, and as the poet said:
x: And horses have entered upon her, horses greeting her, and a painful blow has struck them.
So he made the greeting a strike.

Another said: Rather, al-Hasan is the general name that includes all the meanings of al-Hasan. Al-Hasan is some of the meanings of al-Hasan. He said: That is why God, the Most High, said, when He recommended the parents: And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, good treatment (al-‘Ankabut: 8), meaning that He recommended him concerning them all the meanings of al-Hasan, and He commanded all other people to do some of what He commanded him concerning his parents, so He said: And speak to people in a good manner, meaning some of the meanings of al-Hasan.

What this speaker said about the meaning of al-Hasan with a damma on the ha’ and a sukoon on the seen, is not far from being correct, and that it is a name for its type by which it was named. As for al-Hasan, it is an attribute that occurs to what it is described with, and that occurs with a specific thing. If this is the case, then the correct reading of His statement:
h
And speak to people in a good manner is because the people were only commanded in this era in which it was said to them

: And speak to people to use al-Hasan from speech, not the other meanings of al-Hasan that are without speech. That is an attribute of a specific meaning of al-Hasan, which is speech. Therefore, I chose to read it with the opening of the ha’ and the seen, rather than reading it with the damma of the ha’ and the sukoon of the seen. As for the one who read it:
h
And speak to people in a good way
, he contradicted the reading of the people of Islam by reading it in this way.

It is sufficient evidence of the error of reading it in this way, that it is outside the reading of the people of Islam, if there is no other witness to its error, so how is it outside the known speech of the Arabs? This is because the Arabs hardly speak with fa’la and af’al except with the definite article or with an addition. It is not said: ja’anī ahsan, until they say: al-ahsan. Nor is it said: ajmal, until they say: al-ajmal. This is because af’al and fa’l are hardly found as descriptions except for something known and familiar, as you say: nay, your brother is the best, and nay, your sister is the best. It is not permissible to say: a woman is the best, and a man is the best. As for the interpretation of the good speech that God commanded and described their affair from the Children of Israel in this verse, that they should say it to the people, it is what Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Bishr bin Ammarah, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in his saying:
h
And speak to the people in a good way

, He also commanded them after this creation: to say to the people in a good way, to command those who did not say it and were reluctant to say it, There is no god but God, until they say it as they said it, for that is a way of drawing closer to God, the Most High.
He also said: Good is also gentle speech, from the good and beautiful manners and noble character, and it is from what God is pleased with and loves.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: h
And speak to people in a good way
, he said, speak to people in a good way.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And speak to people in a good way
, he said: Truthfully regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Harun,
m: who said: I heard Sufyan al-Thawri say regarding His statement:
h
And speak to people in a good way
, that he said: Command them to do good and forbid them from evil.

c: Harun bin Idris Al-Asamm told me, he said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharbi told us, he said: Abd Al-Malik bin Abi Sulayman told us, he said:
m: I asked Ata bin Abi Rabah about the words of God Almighty: And speak to people in good terms, he said: Whoever you meet from the people, speak to him in good terms. He said: I asked Abu Jaʿfar, and he said the same.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Qasim told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar and Ataʿ bin Abi Rabah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And speak to people in a good way
, he said: to all people.
b.via: Abu Jaʿfar and Ataʿ bin Abi Rabah

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: similarly.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And establish prayer
What he means by his saying:
h
And establish prayer
, is to perform it with the rights that are obligatory upon you in it, as Abu Kurayb told us, he said:

c: Uthman ibn Saʿid told us, on the authority of Bishr ibn ʿAmara, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Masʿud, who said:
m: h
And establish prayer
, this. And establishing prayer is the completion of bowing, prostration, recitation, humility, and devotion to it in it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And give zakat
We have previously explained the meaning of zakat and its origin.
As for the zakat that God had commanded the Children of Israel to pay, whose affair is mentioned in this verse, it is what:

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Uthman ibn Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Bishr ibn Amara, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And give zakat

, he said: Giving zakat is what God had imposed upon them from their wealth in the form of zakat, and it was a tradition for them other than the tradition of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The zakat of their wealth was an offering to which a fire would descend and carry it, so it was accepted. And whoever the fire did not do that to, it was not accepted, and what was offered was from an unlawful gain: from oppression or deception, or taking something other than what God had commanded him to do and made clear to him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And give zakat
, meaning by zakat: obedience to God and sincerity.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty:
h
Then you turned away
, except for a few of you, and you were averse.

This is report from God, may He be glorified, about the Jews of the Children of Israel, that they broke their covenant and violated their pledge, after God had taken their pledge to be faithful to Him, that they would not worship anyone other than Him, and that they would be good to their fathers and mothers, and maintain family ties, and be kind to orphans, and fulfill the rights of the poor towards them, and command the servants of God to do what God has commanded them to do and urge them to obey Him,
h
and establish prayer
with its limits and obligations, and pay the zakat of their wealth.
But they disobeyed His command in all of that, and turned away from Him, except for those whom God protected from among them, so they fulfilled their pledge and covenant to God, as:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Bishr bin Amara, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When God, the Almighty and Majestic, imposed on them - meaning: on those whose matter God described in His Book from the Children of Israel - this which He mentioned that He took a covenant from them with, they turned away from it, finding it burdensome and hating it, and they sought what was easy for them, except for a few of them, and they are the ones whom God excepted, so He said:
h
Then you turned away

, meaning: you turned away from obeying Me, except a few of you, He said: the few whom I chose for My obedience, and My punishment will befall whoever turned away and turned away from it, meaning: they left it out of contempt for it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: or on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
Then you turned away
, except for a few of you, and you were turning away, meaning you abandoned all of that.

x: Some of them said: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And you are turning away
, the Jews who were at the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He meant by the rest of the verse their ancestors. It is as if he went to the meaning of the words:
h
Then you turned away

, except for a few of you: Then your ancestors turned away, except for a few of them, but he made it a speech to the remnants of their offspring as we mentioned previously. Then He said: And you, O group of their remnants, are also turning away from the covenant that was taken from you regarding that, and your abandoning it is as your predecessors abandoned.
Others said: Rather, His statement,
h
Then you turned away

, except for a few of you, and you were turning away, is addressed to those Jews of the Children of Israel who were among the immigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He condemned them for breaking the covenant that was taken from them in the Torah, changing God’s command, and committing His sins.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The readings differ in the reading of His statement: Do not worship.
Some of them read it with the ta', and some of them read it with the ya', and the meaning is the same.
The reading with the ya' and the ta', and to say Do not worship and Do not worship while they are absent, is because taking the covenant means taking an oath.
Whoever reads that with the ta', then the meaning is addressing, since the address had already been made with that.
And whoever reads it with the ya', then it is because they were not addressed with that at the time of the reporting about them.
It was mentioned that this is the case in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b. It was only good and permissible if it was read in this way because taking the covenant is a statement.

The meaning of the statement, if it had been read in this way, would have been: And when We said to the Children of Israel: Do not worship except God, as the Most High said in another place: And when We took your covenant and raised the Mount above you, [saying], ‘Take what We have given you with strength’ (al-Baqarah 2:63).
As for Al-Hasan, the readers differed in his reading.
The majority of the readers of Kufa, except for Asim, read it: Wa Qoolu al-Nas Hasna with the opening of the Ha and the Seen.
The majority of the readers of Medina read it: Hasanan with the Damma of the Ha and the Sukoon of the Seen.
It has been narrated from some of the readers that he used to read: Wa Qoolu al-Nas Hasna with the example of Fa’ala.

If this is the case, then the correct reading of His statement: And speak to people in a good manner is because the people were only commanded in this era in which it was said to them: And speak to people to use al-Hasan from speech, not the other meanings of al-Hasan that are without speech.
Therefore, I chose to read it with the opening of the ha’ and the seen, rather than reading it with the damma of the ha’ and the sukoon of the seen.
As for the one who read it: And speak to people in a good way, he contradicted the reading of the people of Islam by reading it in this way.

It is sufficient evidence of the error of reading it in this way, that it is outside the reading of the people of Islam, if there is no other witness to its error, so how is it outside the known speech of the Arabs?

x: His statement,
h
And when We took a covenant from you
, ‘You shall not shed one another’s blood,’ is similar in meaning and syntax to His statement,
h
And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel
, ‘You shall not worship except God.’ As for bloodshed, it is pouring it out and shedding it.
What is the meaning of his saying:
h
Do not shed your blood or expel yourselves from your homes
? He said: Or were the people killing themselves and expelling them from their homes, so they were denied that?
The matter is not as you thought, but they were forbidden to kill each other. So killing one of them was like killing himself, since their religion was one, so they were like one man.

As the peace be upon him said: “The believers, in their compassion and sympathy for one another, are like one body. If one part of it complains, the rest of the body responds to it with fever and sleeplessness.” It may be possible that the meaning of his saying:
h
Do not shed one another’s blood

is: A man among you should not kill another man among you, and be punished for it in retaliation, and thus be a killer of himself, because he was the one who caused himself to deserve to be killed. So it is attributed to him that the guardian of the murdered man killed him in retaliation through his guardian. Just as it is said of a man who commits an act for which he deserves punishment, and is punished in the same way: You brought this upon yourself. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of that, the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when We took your covenant
, ‘You shall not shed one another’s blood,’ meaning, you shall not kill one another, nor expel one another from your homes, and your soul, O son of Adam, is the people of your religion.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when We took a covenant from you
, ‘You shall not shed one another’s blood,’ meaning, you shall not kill one another, nor expel one another from your homes, meaning, you shall not expel one another from their homes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do not shed one another’s blood
, he said: Do not kill one another unjustly, nor expel one another from your homes, so that you, O son of Adam, shed the blood of the people of your religion and your call.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
Then you acknowledged
What he means by his saying:
h
Then you acknowledged

, is that you acknowledged the covenant that We took from you: You shall not shed one another’s blood nor expel one another from your homes, as Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
h
Then you acknowledged
, he says: You acknowledged this covenant.
And he narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: similarly.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And you bear witness
The people of interpretation differed as to who was addressed by the words:
h
And you bear witness

Some of them said: This is an address from God Almighty to the Jews who were among the Jews when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to him during the days of his migration to him, rebuking them for neglecting the rulings of the Torah in their hands, the rulings of which they acknowledged. So God Almighty said to them:
h
Then you acknowledged
, meaning by that, the acknowledgment of your forefathers and predecessors,
h
and you bear witness

, to their acknowledgment of the covenant taken from them, that they would not shed each other’s blood, nor expel themselves from their homes, and you believed that this was a right from My covenant upon them.
Among those who narrated the meaning of this statement from him is Ibn Abbas:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
h
And when We took your covenant
, ‘You shall not shed one another’s blood, nor expel one another from your homes.’
h
Then you acknowledged
, and you were witnesses, that this is a right from My covenant upon you.

x: Others said: Rather, this is report from God, may He be glorified, about their forefathers, but He, may He be exalted, brought out the report about them in a manner Surat Al-Baqarah 2:84 And remember when We took your covenant, "You shall not shed one another's blood nor expel one another from your homes."
h
Then you acknowledged

it, while you were witnesses. of addressing them, in the manner that we described in all the verses that are similar to it, the interpretation of which we have explained previously. They interpreted his statement:
h
And you bear witness
, to mean: And you are witnesses.
Those who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said:

c: Adam told us, he said: Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you bear witness
, he said: And you are witnesses.

x: The most correct interpretation of this, in my opinion, is that His statement,
h
And you bear witness
, is a report about their ancestors, and includes those addressed among them who lived during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as His statement,
h
And when We took your covenant

, was a report about their ancestors, even though it was addressed to those who lived during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is because God Almighty took a covenant from those who were at the time of the Messenger of God, Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Children of Israel, in accordance with what He has explained to us in His Book, and He made it obligatory for all of their descendants after them to follow the rulings of the Torah, just as He made it obligatory for those who were at the time of Moses among them.
Then He rebuked those He addressed with these verses for their and their ancestors’ breach of that covenant and their denial of the covenants they had promised Him to fulfill, by His statement,
h
Then you acknowledged

and you were witnesses. Since it was addressed to those of them who were at the time of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then it is meant for everyone who was confident in the covenant from them during the time of Moses and after him, and everyone who bore witness to the truth of what was in the Torah. Because God, may He be glorified, did not specify some of them without others in His saying:
h
Then you acknowledged and you bear witness and similar verses

. The verse could possibly mean all of them. So if that is the case, then no one can claim that it meant some of them without others. And the same is the ruling of the verse that comes after it, I mean His saying: Then you are those who kill yourselves the verse.
Because it has been mentioned to us that their first ones used to do what their last ones used to do, those who lived in the time of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
There are two interpretations of his statement:
h
Then you are these
: One of them is that what is meant by it is: Then you, O these, so he left out O because of the indication of the speech on it, as he said, Joseph, turn away from this
r
(Yusuf 12:29)

, and its interpretation is: O Joseph, turn away from this. So the meaning of the speech then is: Then you, O group of Jews of the Children of Israel, after your acknowledgement of the covenant that I took from you: You will not shed your blood, nor expel yourselves from your homes, then you acknowledged after your testimony against yourselves that this is a right I have over you, and it is necessary for you to fulfill it for me, you kill yourselves, and expel a group of you from their homes, cooperating against them, in your expulsion of them, with sin and aggression. Cooperation is a demonstration. Cooperation is called a demonstration because some people strengthen each other’s backs.

It is an interaction from the back, which is some people supporting each other’s backs. The other aspect: that its meaning is: Then you are a people who kill yourselves. So it goes back to the report about you. And the word these stands between them and the report about them, just as the Arabs say: I am this one standing, and I am this one sitting.

i: And when it is said:
x: I am this one sitting, it is also correct and permissible: You are that one standing. Some Basrans have claimed that his saying: these in his saying:
h
Then you are these

, is a warning and emphasis of you. He claimed that even though you is a metaphor for the names of the group of those being addressed, it is permissible to emphasise them with these and those, because it is a metaphor for those being addressed, as Khafaf ibn Nudbah said: I say to him, and the spear frames his back: Be clear, I am that.
He means: I am this, and as God Almighty said:
Until, when you are in the ship and it sails with them
Then the people of interpretation differed about who was meant by this verse, similar to their difference about who was meant by His statement: And you bear witness.
Mention of the difference of opinion among those who differed about that:

c: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah,
