m: or Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Then you are those who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting each other against them in sin and aggression to the polytheists, until you shed their blood with them, and expel them from their homes with them. He said: God admonished them for that, from their actions, and He had forbidden them in the Torah to shed each other’s blood, and He had made it obligatory for them in it to ransom their prisoners, so they were two groups: a group of them from Banu Qaynuqa’, allies of the Khazraj, and Nadir and Qurayza, allies of the Aws. So whenever there was war between the Aws and the Khazraj, Banu Qaynuqa’ would go out with the Khazraj, and Nadir and Qurayza would go out with the Aws, each group supporting its allies against its brothers, until they shed their blood among themselves, and they had the Torah in their hands, knowing from it what was against them and what was for them. The Aws and Khazraj were polytheists who worshipped idols. They knew neither Heaven nor Hell, nor resurrection nor Day of Judgment, nor a Book, nor what was forbidden nor what was permissible. When the war ended, they ransomed their prisoners, confirming what was in the Torah and taking Surat Al-Baqarah 2:85 Then you are the ones who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting one another against them in sin and aggression. And
h
if they come to you as captives

, you ransom them, although their expulsion was forbidden to you. Do you then believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part? Then what is the recompense of those who do that among you except Disgrace in the life of this world,
h
and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned

to the severest punishment. And Allah is not unaware of what you do. it from one another. Banu Qaynuqa ransomed their prisoners from the Aws, and Nadir and Qurayza ransomed those from the Khazraj, and they shed the blood they had taken and the dead from among them, in support of the polytheists against them. God the Most High said, when He rebuked them for that:
h
Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part

? That is, you ransomed him according to the ruling of the Torah, and you killed him, while according to the ruling of the Torah, he was not to be killed, nor to leave his home, nor to support against him anyone who associates partners with God and worships idols instead of Him, seeking worldly gain. This story was revealed about what they did to the Aws and Khazraj, as far as I have been informed.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told me, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And when We took a covenant from you, [saying], ‘You shall not shed one another’s blood, nor shall you expel one another from your homes,’ then you acknowledged it, and you were witnesses. He said: God took a covenant from the Children of Israel in the Torah: that they would not kill one another, and any male or female slave you find from the Children of Israel, buy him or her for the price paid, and set him or her free. So the Qurayzah were allies of the Aws, and the Nadir were allies of the Khazraj, and they fought in the Battle of Samir. So the Banu Qurayzah would fight with their allies, the Nadir and their allies. And the Nadir would fight the Qurayzah and their allies, and they would defeat them, destroy their homes, and expel them from them. So if a man from either party was taken prisoner, they would gather around him or her to ransom him. The Arabs would taunt them for that, and say: How do you fight them and ransom them? They said: We were commanded to ransom them, and it was forbidden for us to fight them. They said: Why do you fight them? They said: We are ashamed that our allies should be humiliated. That is why when God, the Almighty, rebuked them, He said: Then you are those who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting each other against them in sin and aggression.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: Qurayzah and Nadir were two brothers, and they were in this position, and the book was in their hands. And Aws and Khazraj were two brothers, then they separated, and Qurayzah and Nadir separated. So Nadir was with Khazraj, and Qurayzah was with Aws, and they fought. And some of them killed each other, so God, the Most High, said: Then you are those who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes the verse.

x: Others said: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said: It was among the Children of Israel: If they oppressed a people, they would expel them from their homes. And they took a covenant from them that they would not shed their blood, nor would they expel themselves from their homes.

As for aggression, it is the two verbs of transgression. It is said: So-and-so transgressed in such-and-such with aggression and aggression, and he transgressed, transgresses, transgression, and that is if he exceeded his limit unjustly and tyrannically. The reading of Tazaharoon differed.
Some of them read it as Tazaharoon on the model of tafa'aloon, so they deleted the extra ta, which is the last ta.

Others read it as Tazaharoon, so they stressed it, with the interpretation of Nathaharoon, except that they assimilated the second ta into the tha, because their points of articulation are close, so they made them both a stressed tha. These two readings, even though their wording differs, they agree in meaning. It is no matter which one the reader reads, because they are both well-known languages, and two readings that are widespread in the lands of Islam with one meaning, and there is no meaning in either of them that would merit choosing it over the other, unless someone chooses the stressed Tazaharoon, seeking to complete the word.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “And
h
if they come to you as captives
, you ransom them, although their expulsion was forbidden to you.
Then
h
do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part
By His saying, the Most High: And
h
if they come to you as captives

, ransom them, He means the Jews. He rebukes them with that, and makes them aware of the ugly deeds they used to do, so He said to them: Then you, after your acknowledgement of the covenant that He took from you: You shall not shed one another’s blood, nor expel one another from your homes, you kill yourselves, meaning: you kill one another, and while you kill those you kill from among you, if you find a captive among you in the hands of someone other than you from among your enemies, you ransom him, and you expel one another from his homes, and your killing them and your expulsion from their homes is forbidden to you, and leaving them captives in the hands of your enemy is forbidden to you, so how can you permit killing them, and not permit leaving their ransom from their enemy? Or how can you not permit leaving their ransom, and permit killing them?

And both of them are the same in the ruling that is necessary for you regarding them. Because what I have forbidden you to kill and expel from their homes is similar to what I have forbidden you to leave them as captives in the hands of their enemy. Do you believe in part of the Book in which I have imposed My duties upon you and made clear to you My limits, and I have taken upon you to act in accordance with My covenant, so you believe in it and ransom your captives from the hands of your enemy, and you disbelieve in part of it, so you reject it and kill those whom I have forbidden you to kill from among your religion and your people, and you expel them from their homes, even though you know that disbelief in part of it is a breach of My covenant and agreement? As: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid ibn Zurai’ told us, he said, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada: “
h
Then you are these
, you kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting one another against them in sin and aggression.
And
h
if they come to you as captives

, you ransom them, although their expulsion was forbidden to you. Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?” Do you believe in part of the Book and ransom, and disbelieve in part of it, killing and expelling? By God, their ransom is faith, and their expulsion is disbelief. So they would expel them from their homes, and if they saw them as captives in the hands of their enemy, they would ransom them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: or on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “And
h
if they come to you as captives

, you ransom them. You know that this is against you in your religion, “and it is forbidden to you” in your book, “to expel them. So will you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part?” Do you ransom them as believers in that, and expel them as disbelievers in that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And
h
if they come to you as captives
, you ransom them. He said: If you find him in the hand of someone other than you, you ransom him, and would you kill him with your own hand?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar said:
m: Qatada used to say regarding His statement:
h
Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part
? So their expulsion was disbelief, and their ransom was faith.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Adam told us, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding His statement: Then you are the ones who kill yourselves Qur’an 1:17, he said: It was among the Children of Israel: If they oppressed a people, they would expel them from their homes, and they had taken a covenant from them: that they would not shed their blood nor expel themselves from their homes, then they ransomed them, so they believed in some of the Book and disbelieved in some. They believed in the ransom, so they ransomed themselves, and they disbelieved in the expulsion from the homes, so they were expelled.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Adam told us, he said: Abu Jaʿfar told us, he said: Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas told us, he said: Abu Al-ʿAliyah told me:
m: Abdullah bin Salam passed by the head of the exiles in Kufa, and he was ransoming women who had not been raped by the Arabs, and he was not ransoming those who had been raped by the Arabs, so Abdullah bin Salam said to him: It is written in your book: Ransom them all.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part? He said, their disbelief is killing and expulsion, and their belief is ransom. Ibn Jurayj said: He says: If they are with you, you kill them and expel them from their homes, but if they are taken captive, you ransom them? It has reached me that Umar ibn Al-Khattab said in the story of the Children of Israel: The Children of Israel have passed away, and you are the ones meant by this hadith.

x: The reciters differed in the recitation of His statement:
h
If they come to you as captives
, you ransom them.
Some of them read it: Prisoners, you ransom them, and some of them: Prisoners, you ransom them, and some of them: Prisoners, you ransom them, and some of them: Prisoners, you ransom them.
Whoever recites this: And
h
if they come to you as captives

, then he intended the plural of the captive, since it was in the form of faʿil, like the plural of the names of those with disabilities whose singular comes in the form of faʿil, since captivity is similar in meaning in the harm and distress that befalls the captive with some of the meanings of disabilities, and the plural of what is attached to it was attached to the plural of what we described, so it was said: captive and captives, just as it was said: sick and sick, broken and broken, wounded and wounded.

As for those who read it as ʿasara, they took it as a plural of faʿlaan, since the plural of faʿlaan which has faʿla may share the plural of faʿil, as they said sakāra and sakāra, and kasāla and kasalā, so they likened ʿasīr and pluralized it once as ʿasāra and another time asra with that.

Some of them claimed that the meaning of ʿasrā is different from the meaning of ʿasāra, and they claimed that the meaning of ʿasrā is the captivity of the people without their being taken captive by the one who took them captive, and that the meaning of ʿasrā is the meaning of the fate of the captive people in the hands of the captors by taking them captive and taking them by force and force.

This is something that has no basis in the language of any Arab. But it is based on what I have described of the plural of the prisoner once as faʿli, because I have explained the reason, and once as faʿali, because I have mentioned: of their likening its plural to the plural of drunkard and lazy and the like. The correct reading in this regard is the one who reads and
h
if they come to you as captives

, because fa’ali in the plural of fa’il is not widespread in the speech of the Arabs. So since that was not widespread in their speech, and it was widespread and prevalent among them, the plural of the attributes that had the meaning of pain and time, and its singular was estimated as fa’il, was fa’li, like what we described before, and one of those was the captive, it was necessary to include it with its counterparts and forms, and to pluralize it and not others who differed from it.

As for the one who read you ransome them, he meant: you ransome them from their captivity, and those among you who took them captive ransome you with Surat Al-Baqarah 2:85 Then you are the ones who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting one another against them in sin and aggression. And
h
if they come to you as captives

, you ransom them, although their expulsion was forbidden to you. Do you then believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part? Then what is the recompense of those who do that among you except Disgrace in the life of this world,
h
and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned

to the severest punishment. And Allah is not unaware of what you do. them, so your captives ransome you with them. As for the one who reads that, You ransom them, he meant: O group of Jews, if those whom you expelled from among you from their homes come to you as captives, then you ransom them and rescue them.

This reading is more pleasing to me than the first, I mean: prisoners they ransomed, because what the Jews are required to do in their religion is to ransom their prisoners in any case, whether the captors ransomed their prisoners or not. As for his statement: And it is forbidden for you to expel them, there are two interpretations of his statement: And it is, one of them is that it is a metaphor for the expulsion that was mentioned earlier. It is as if he said: And you expel a group of you from their homes, and their expulsion is forbidden for you. Then he repeated the expulsion that comes after And it is forbidden for you, repeating it, because there is a distinction between the expulsion and it, a statement. The second interpretation is that it is a pillar, since the waw with huwa requires a noun to follow it without the verb.

i: So when the verb was presented before the noun that the waw requires to follow it, huwa was given priority, because it is a noun, just as you say: I came to you while your father was standing, meaning: and your father is standing, since the waw requires a noun, so it was sheathed with huwa, since the verb preceded the noun, to make the speech correct, as the poet said:
x: Tell Abu Yahya if you find him on the camels with dry sweat in their armpits.

That Al-Salami, who is in Dhariya, the Emir of Al-Hama, has sold the rights of the Banu Abs. With a garment, a dinar, a sheep, and a dirham. Is it raised by what is here a head? I gave it to him, because he asked for the name of the baptism.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Then what is the reward for those among you who do that except disgrace in the life of this world?
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
What is the penalty for he who does that among you

? is: For he who among you kills a person and disbelieves by killing him, by breaking the covenant of God that He decreed upon him in the Torah, and expels a group of you from their homes, supporting their enemies from among the polytheists against them, unjustly and aggressively, and contrary to what God commanded him to do in His Book that He sent down to Moses, there is no penalty. He means by penalty: reward, which is the compensation for what he did of that and the wage for it, except disgrace in the life of this world. And disgrace means humiliation and degradation. It is said from it: a man was disgraced, he was disgraced with disgrace, in the life of this world, meaning: in the immediate world before the Hereafter. Then they differed about the disgrace with which God disgraced them for their previous disobedience to Him.

Some of them said: That is the ruling of God that He revealed to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: To punish the killer for the one he killed, and to exact retribution in retaliation, and to avenge the wronged from the wrongdoer.
Others said: Rather, it is taking the jizya from them as long as they adhere to their religion, humiliating and degrading them.

Others said: Rather, that is the disgrace that they were punished for in this world: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelling the Nadir from their homes at the beginning of the gathering, and killing the fighters of Qurayza and taking their children captive. That was a disgrace in this world, and they will have a great punishment in the Hereafter.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment
What he means by his saying:
h
And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment

is: And on the Day the Hour comes, whoever among you does that will be returned, after the disgrace that befell him in this world as a punishment for disobeying God, to the most severe punishment that God has prepared for His enemies.

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: On the Day of Resurrection, they will be returned to a punishment more severe than the punishment of this world. There is no meaning to what the speaker says. This is because God, may He be glorified, only informed us that they will be returned to the most severe meanings of torment, and for this reason He included the definite article in it, because He meant by it the entire type of torment, not one type of it.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And God is not unaware of what you do
The reciters differed in the reading of this.

Some of them read it: And God is not unaware of what they do with the letter ya’, as a way of informing about them. It is as if they derived from their reading the meaning: “So what is the reward for those who do that among you except disgrace in the life of this world,
h
and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned
to the severest punishment.
h
And God is not unaware of what you do

,” meaning: about what those whom God has informed about do, they will have no reward for their actions except disgrace in the life of this world, and their return in the Hereafter to the severest punishment.
Others read it:
h
And God is not unaware of what you do
with the letter ta’ in the form of addressing. He said: So it was as if they were… They read:
h
Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part
? And God is not unaware, O Jews, of what you do. The reading that I like the most is the reading of the one who brought the letter ya’ closer, following His statement:
h
So what is the recompense of he who does that among you
? and His statement:
h
And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned
. Because His statement:
h
And God is not unaware of what you do and so on is closer than His statement

: Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part? So following the one that is closer to it is more appropriate than attaching it to the one that is further from it. The other interpretation is not far from being correct. The interpretation of His statement:
h
And God is not unaware of what you do

, is that God is not unaware of their evil deeds, but rather He is recording them and preserving them for them until He punishes them for them in the Hereafter and disgraces them in this world, humiliating and disgracing them.

evidence.text: The reading of Tazaharoon differed.
Some of them read it as Tazaharoon on the model of tafa'aloon, so they deleted the extra ta, which is the last ta.

Others read it as Tazaharoon, so they stressed it, with the interpretation of Nathaharoon, except that they assimilated the second ta into the tha, because their points of articulation are close, so they made them both a stressed tha.
These two readings, even though their wording differs, they agree in meaning.

It is no matter which one the reader reads, because they are both well-known languages, and two readings that are widespread in the lands of Islam with one meaning, and there is no meaning in either of them that would merit choosing it over the other, unless someone chooses the stressed Tazaharoon, seeking to complete the word.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The reciters differed in the recitation of His statement: If they come to you as captives, you ransom them.
Some of them read it: Prisoners, you ransom them, and some of them: Prisoners, you ransom them, and some of them: Prisoners, you ransom them, and some of them: Prisoners, you ransom them.

Abu Jaʿfar said: Whoever recites this: And if they come to you as captives, then he intended the plural of the captive, since it was in the form of faʿil, like the plural of the names of those with disabilities whose singular comes in the form of faʿil, since captivity is similar in meaning in the harm and distress that befalls the captive with some of the meanings of disabilities, and the plural of what is attached to it was attached to the plural of what we described, so it was said: captive and captives, just as it was said: sick and sick, broken and broken, wounded and wounded.

Abu Jaʿfar said: As for those who read it as ʿasara, they took it as a plural of faʿlaan, since the plural of faʿlaan which has faʿla may share the plural of faʿil, as they said sakāra and sakāra, and kasāla and kasalā, so they likened ʿasīr and pluralized it once as ʿasāra and another time asra with that.
The correct reading in this regard is the one who reads and if they come to you as captives, because fa’ali in the plural of fa’il is not widespread in the speech of the Arabs.
As for the one who reads that, You ransom them, he meant: O group of Jews, if those whom you expelled from among you from their homes come to you as captives, then you ransom them and rescue them.

This reading is more pleasing to me than the first, I mean: prisoners they ransomed, because what the Jews are required to do in their religion is to ransom their prisoners in any case, whether the captors ransomed their prisoners or not.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The reciters differed in the reading of this.
Some of them read it: And God is not unaware of what they do with the letter ya’, as a way of informing about them.

It is as if they derived from their reading the meaning: “So what is the reward for those who do that among you except disgrace in the life of this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the severest punishment.
Others read it: And God is not unaware of what you do with the letter ta’ in the form of addressing.

The reading that I like the most is the reading of the one who brought the letter ya’ closer, following His statement: So what is the recompense of he who does that among you? and His statement: And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement, are those about whom He informed us that they believe in some of the Book, so they ransom their Jewish captives, and disbelieve in some of it, so they kill those whom God has forbidden them to kill from among their religion, and they expel from their homes those whom God has forbidden them to expel from their homes, in violation of God's covenant and agreement in the Torah to them. So He, the Most High, informed us that these are the ones who bought the leadership of this worldly life over the weak, ignorant, and stupid people of their religion, and they bought the vile and worthless foods in it with faith, which would have been theirs in the Hereafter, had they brought it instead of disbelief, eternal life in Paradise. God, the Most High, described them as having bought this worldly life with the Hereafter, because they were satisfied with this world with their disbelief in God in it, in exchange for the bliss of the Hereafter which God has prepared for the believers.
He made their share of the bliss of the Hereafter, due to their disbelief in God, a price for what they bought with it from the vile worldly things, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those are the ones who have purchased the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter
, they preferred a little of this world over a lot of the Hereafter.

x: Then God, the Most High, informed us that since they sold their share of the bliss of the Hereafter by abandoning His obedience and preferring disbelief in Him and the lowly things of this world over Him, they have no share in the bliss of the Hereafter, and that what they have in the Hereafter is the torment, and the torment will not be lightened for them in it. Because the one for whom the torment will be lightened in it is the one who has a share in its bliss, and these people have no share, because they bought their worldly life for their Hereafter with what was in this world. As for his saying: nor will they be helped, he informed us about them that no one will help them in the Hereafter, and he will ward off God’s punishment from them through his help, not through his power, nor through his intercession, nor anything else.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying,
h
We gave Moses the Book is that We sent it down to him

. We have already explained that the meaning of giving is bestowal, in what has passed before. The book that Moses, peace be upon him, was given to him is the Torah. As for his saying: And we stood behind him, it means: And we followed one after the other, as a man stands behind another: if he walks in his footsteps from behind him. Its origin is from the nape of the neck, and it is said from it: I stood behind someone’s nape, just as it is said: I followed him: if you were in his back. He means by his saying: after him, after Moses. The word messengers means prophets, and they are the plural of messenger. It is said: He is a messenger and they are messengers, just as it is said: He is patient and they are a patient people, and He is a grateful man and they are a grateful people.
What God, the Most High, means by His statement,
h
And We followed him with messengers

, is that We made some of them follow one another on one path and one law. Because everyone whom God sent as a prophet after Moses, peace be upon him, until the time of Jesus, son of Mary, He sent him with the command of the Children of Israel to establish the Torah, act according to what is in it, and call to what is in it. That is why it was said,
h
And We followed him with messengers
, meaning on his path and law, and acting according to what he used to act upon.
He means by his saying:
h
And We gave Jesus
, son of Mary, clear proofs, that We gave Jesus, son of Mary.

What is meant by the clear proofs that God gave him: the arguments and evidence of his prophethood that he demonstrated at his hands: such as bringing the dead back to life, healing the blind, and other similar signs that demonstrated his status with God and indicated his truthfulness and the validity of his prophethood, such as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And We gave Jesus

, son of Mary, clear proofs: meaning the signs that were placed in his hands: such as bringing the dead back to life, creating him from clay in the form of a bird, then breathing into it and it became a bird by God’s permission, and healing diseases, and information about many of the unseen things that they stored in their homes, and what was returned to them from the Torah, along with the Gospel that God had revealed to him.

x: As for the meaning of his saying:
h
And we supported him
, it is that we strengthened him and helped him, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: And We supported him, he says: We aided him. It is said from this: May God support you, meaning He strengthened you, and he is a man with hands, and with a hand, meaning: with strength. And from this is the saying of Al-Ajjaj: Who changed my hand? Meaning: In my youth, the strength of gray hair, and from it the saying of another: If the arrows are gathered together, the one who breaks them is the one with the fortitude and the strength of his hands. Meaning: by hand: strong. Then there was a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of his statement:
h
With the Holy Spirit

x: Some of them said: The Holy Spirit with which God Almighty informed us that He supported Jesus is Gabriel, peace be upon him.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We supported him with the Holy Spirit
. He said: He is Gabriel.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We supported him with the Holy Spirit
, he said: He is Gabriel, peace be upon him. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:87 And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture and followed up after him with messengers,
h
and We gave Jesus
, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him
h
with the Holy Spirit
. So is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? Then a party you denied and a party you killed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We supported him with the Holy Spirit
, he said: The Holy Spirit is Gabriel.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
h
And We supported him with the Holy Spirit
. He said: Jesus was supported by Gabriel, who is the Holy Spirit. Ibn Hamid said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:

c: Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Hussein Al-Makki told me, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab Al-Ash’ari:
m: “A group of Jews asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Tell us about the spirit. He said: I ask you by God and by His days with the Children of Israel, do you know that he is Gabriel? And he is the one who comes to me? They said: Yes.”

x: Others said: The spirit with which God supported Jesus is the Gospel.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And We supported him with the Holy Spirit

, he said: God supported Jesus with the Gospel as a spirit, just as He made the Qur’an a spirit, both of them are the spirit of God, as God said: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command (al-Shura 42:52).

x: Others said: It is the name by which Jesus revived the dead.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Munjab narrated that Bishr bin Amara narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And We supported him with the Holy Spirit
. He said: It is the name by which Jesus revived the dead.

x: The most correct interpretation of this is the one who said: The spirit in this place is Gabriel. Because God, the Most High, informed that He supported Jesus with it, as He informed in His statement: “When God said, ‘O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother
h
when I supported you with the Holy Spirit

so that you spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel’” (al-Ma’idah 5:110). If the spirit with which God supported him was the Gospel, then His statement:
h
When I supported you with the Holy Spirit

, and when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel, would be a repetition of a meaningless statement. This is because according to the interpretation of the statement of the one who said: The meaning of
h
When I supported you with the Holy Spirit
is: When I supported you with the Gospel and when I taught you the Gospel.

And no one can be supported by it except as his teacher, so that is a repetition of one statement, without adding meaning to one of them over the other. This is a contradiction in speech, and God, the Most High, is too exalted to address His servants with what does not benefit them. Since this is the case, then the corruption of the statement of those who claim that the spirit in this place is the Gospel is clear, even though all of God’s books that He revealed to His messengers are a spirit from Him, because dead hearts are revived by them, turning souls are revived by them, and misguided dreams are guided by them. God Almighty called Gabriel a spirit and added him to the sacred because God created him a spirit from Himself, without the birth of his son’s father. So He called him a spirit and added him to the sacred. The sacred is purity, just as He called Jesus, son of Mary, a spirit of God because He created him a spirit from Himself without the birth of his son’s father.
We have previously explained in this book that the meaning of sanctification is purification, and holiness is purity, from that.
The people of interpretation have differed in its meaning in this place, similar to their difference in the place we mentioned.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Jerusalem is the blessing.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, who said: Jerusalem, which is the Lord, may He be exalted.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And We supported him with the Holy Spirit

, he said: God, the Holy. And He supported Jesus with His Spirit, he said: The attribute of God, the Holy. And he recited the words of God, the Most High: He is God, other than whom there is no god, the King, the Holy (al-Hashr 59:23), he said: The Holy and the Holy are one.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Hilal ibn Usamah, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, he said, Kaab said:
m: God, the Holy One.

x: He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying: So, whenever a messenger comes to you with what your souls do not desire, the Jews from the Children of Israel.

m: Muhammad bin Amr told me that, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.

x: God, the Most High, says to them: O group of Jews, the Children of Israel, We gave Moses the Torah, and We sent messengers to you after him,
h
and We gave Jesus
, son of Mary, clear proofs and arguments, when We sent him to you, and We strengthened him
h
with the Holy Spirit

. But whenever a messenger of Mine came to you with something other than what your souls desired, you acted arrogantly and oppressively towards them, as your leader, Satan, did. So you denied some of them and killed others. This is what you will always do with My messengers. His saying: Whenever, even if it came out as an awkward statement in the speech, it is in the sense of report.
There was a difference in the reading of this.
Some of them read it as:
h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
,’ with a lightened and silent lām. This is the reading of all the countries in all regions.
Some of them read it as:
h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered

,’ with a heavy lam and a damma. As for those who read it with a sukoon on the lam and a light lam, they interpreted it as saying: Our hearts are in coverings, ghitaat, and ghalaf. Ghalaf according to the reading of these people is the plural of aglaf, which is the one who is in a ghalaf and ghatha, just as it is said of a man who is not circumcised, aglaf, and a woman ghalfa. And as it is said of a sword when it is in its sheath: a ghalaf sword and a ghalafaa bow, and their plural is ghalaf. Likewise, the plural of what is from the adjectives whose masculine is af’al and its feminine is fa’laa, is pluralized as fa’l with the first letter damma and the second letter sukoon, like ahmr and humr, asfar and safar, so that is a combination of the feminine and masculine. And it is not permissible to make the ‘ayn of fa’l heavy, except in poetic necessity, as Tarafa ibn al-‘Abd said: Boys in our council stripped her of her roses and blond hair He wants: blonde, but the hair forced him to move the second one, so he moved it.
And from it is the report that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Al-Hakam bin Bashir bin Salman told us, he said, Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah Al-Jamali, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said:
m: The hearts are four, then he mentioned them and said among what he mentioned: And a heart that is covered and bound, and that is the heart of the disbeliever. He who said that means: that it is in covers:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
,’ meaning covered.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told us, on the authority of Abu Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Our hearts are covered
, meaning in a covering.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
,’ meaning the hearts that are sealed.

c: Abbas bin Muhammad told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Katheer told me, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
,’ that is, they have a covering over them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, he said, Abdullah bin Katheer told me, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
,’ they have a covering over them.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Our hearts are covered
, he said: They are covered.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
,’ meaning they do not understand.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
.’ He said: It is like His saying:
h
Our hearts are within coverings
r
(Fussilat 41:5)

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Our hearts are covered
, he said: There is a seal on them. He said: It is like his statement:
h
Our hearts are within coverings

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: h
Our hearts are covered
, meaning they do not understand.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
.’ He said: They say: There is a covering over them, which is the covering.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
Our hearts are covered
, he said, he says: My heart is covered, so nothing of what you say reaches it, and he recited,
h
And they said
h
Our hearts are within coverings
from that to which you invite us’
r
(Fussilat 41:6)

x: As for those who read it as ghalaf with a fatha on the lam and a damma on it, they interpreted it as saying: Our hearts are ghalaf for knowledge, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:88
h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered

." Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little do they believe. meaning that they are vessels. He said: The word ghalaf according to their interpretation is the plural of ghalaf cover, just as the word book is the plural of books, veil is veils, and shihab is shihabs. So the meaning of the speech is according to the interpretation of the reading of those who read ghalaf with the lam moved and with a damma. The Jews said:
h
Our hearts are covered
for knowledge and are vessels for it and for other things.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Ubaid bin Asbat bin Muhammad told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
.’ He said: They are vessels for remembrance.

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said, Fadil told us, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Our hearts are covered
, he said: They are vessels for knowledge.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Fadil told us, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: similarly.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Munjab,
m: who said: Bishr bin Amara narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
And they said
h
Our hearts are covered
.’ He said: They are filled with knowledge, and do not need Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or anyone else. The reading that is not permissible other than his saying:
h
Our hearts are covered

, is the reading of those who read covered with a sukoon on the lam, meaning that it is in membranes and coverings, due to the convergence of the evidence from the reciters and the people of interpretation on its correctness, and the deviation of those who deviated from them with what contradicted it, from reading that with a damma on the lam. We have shown that what the evidence has agreed upon is evidence for whoever receives it. And what the individual has brought, it is not permissible to object to what the group has brought, which establishes the evidence in terms of transmission, word and action, in a place other than this, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Rather, God cursed them for their disbelief.

He, may His praise be glorified, means: Rather, God cursed them. Rather, God distanced them, kept them far away, expelled them, humiliated them, and destroyed them for their disbelief, their denial of God’s signs and proofs, and what He sent His messengers with, and their denial of His prophets. So God, may His praise be glorified, informed us that He distanced them from Him and from His mercy because of what they did of that. The root of the word curse is to expel, banish, and exclude. It is said: May God curse so-and-so, meaning he curses him with a curse, and he is cursed. Then the object is declined, so it is said: He is accursed. From this is the saying of Al-Shamakh bin Dirar: The quail was terrified by him and I banished him from the place of the wolf like a damned man Abu Jaʿfar said: In the statement of God, the Most High, Rather, God has cursed them for their disbelief, is a refutation of those Jews who said,
h
Our hearts are covered

Because His statement, Rather, is evidence of His denial and rejection of what they claimed, since rather does not enter into speech except to contradict what is denied. Since that is the case, it is clear that the meaning of the verse is: And the Jews said:
h
Our hearts are covered

from what you call us to, O Muhammad. So God, the Most High, said: That is not as they claimed, but God excluded the Jews and kept them far from His mercy, and expelled them from it, and humiliated them for their denial of Him and His messengers,
h
so few of them believe
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: But few of them believe.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement:
h
So few of them believe
Some of them said that its meaning is
h
So few of them believe
, meaning that only a few of them believe.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, saying: Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, saying: Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement: Rather, God has cursed them for their disbelief,
h
so few of them believe
, by my life, those who returned from the polytheists were more than those who returned from the People of the Book. Only a small group of the People of the Book believed.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So few of them believe
, he said: Only a few of them believe.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They do not believe except in a little of what is in their hands.
Those who said this were:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: So little do they believe, he said: Only a few of them believe. Muammar said: And someone else said: They do not believe except in a little of what is in their hands.

x: The most correct interpretation of His statement, So few believe, is what we have mastered, God willing. It is that God, the Most High, informed that He cursed those He described in this verse, then He informed about them that they have little faith in what God revealed to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. That is why He put His statement, So few, in the accusative case, because it is an attribute of the infinitive that was not mentioned. Its meaning is: Rather, God cursed them for their disbelief, so they have little faith. Thus, what we have explained has made clear the corruption of the statement that was narrated from Qatadah regarding that. Because the meaning of that, if it were as it was narrated that he meant by it:
h
So few of them believe
, or
h
so few of them believe
, then the few would be in the nominative case, not in the accusative case.

Because if that was its interpretation, then the few would be a subject in the nominative case. So when the few and what is in the meaning of who or who has been lost are in the accusative case, then what remains is not subject to a subject. That is not permissible in the language of any of the Arabs. As for the Arabists, they differed about the meaning of ma in His statement:
h
So few of them believe
Some of them said: It is redundant and has no meaning. Rather, the interpretation of the statement is:
h
So few of them believe
, as the Most High said:
So by mercy from God, you were lenient with them
and what is similar to that. So he claimed that ma in that is redundant, and that the meaning of the statement is: So by mercy from God, you were lenient with them.

i: And he recited in support of his statement the following verse of Muhalhil:
x: If Abbanin came to propose to her, no suitor's nose would be dyed with blood He claimed that it means: the suitor’s nose was stained with blood, and that ma is redundant.
Others denied what the speaker said about what, in the verse and in the verse that he recited,
h
and they said

: This is only from the speaker starting the speech with the report about the generality of all things, since what was a word that gathered all things, then made specific and general what it made general by what it mentioned after it. This statement is more correct in our view, because adding something that does not provide meaning to speech is not permissible to add to God, may He be glorified. Perhaps someone might say: Did those about whom God said that they believe little have little or much faith, so that it would be said about them: They believe little? It was said: The meaning of faith is belief. The Jews, about whom God told this report, believed in the oneness of God, in resurrection, reward and punishment, and disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prophethood.

All of that was an obligation upon them to believe in, because it was in their books, and among what Moses brought them. So they believed in some of it, and that was the little of their faith, and they disbelieved in some of it, and that was the much that God told about them that they disbelieved in it.
Some of them said: They were not believers in anything, but it was said: They believe seldom, and they are disbelievers in all of it, as the Arabs say: I have rarely seen anything like this.

c: It was narrated from her,
m: as she heard it: I passed by a country that rarely grows anything but leeks and onions, meaning: It does not grow anything but leeks and onions, and similar statements that are uttered to describe something as few, and the meaning in it is the negation of all of it.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There was a difference in the reading of this.
Some of them read it as: And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ with a lightened and silent lām.
This is the reading of all the countries in all regions.
Some of them read it as: And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered,’ with a heavy lam and a damma.
As for those who read it with a sukoon on the lam and a light lam, they interpreted it as saying: Our hearts are in coverings, ghitaat, and ghalaf.
Ghalaf according to the reading of these people is the plural of aglaf, which is the one who is in a ghalaf and ghatha, just as it is said of a man who is not circumcised, aglaf, and a woman ghalfa.

Abu Jaafar said: As for those who read it as ghalaf with a fatha on the lam and a damma on it, they interpreted it as saying: Our hearts are ghalaf for knowledge, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:88 And they said, "Our hearts are covered."
So the meaning of the speech is according to the interpretation of the reading of those who read ghalaf with the lam moved and with a damma.

The reading that is not permissible other than his saying: Our hearts are covered, is the reading of those who read covered with a sukoon on the lam, meaning that it is in membranes and coverings, due to the convergence of the evidence from the reciters and the people of interpretation on its correctness, and the deviation of those who deviated from them with what contradicted it, from reading that with a damma on the lam.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying:
h
And when there came to them a Book from God

, confirming what is with them, and when there came to the Jews from the Children of Israel, whom He, the Most High, described as a Book from God, he meant by the Book the Qur’an that God sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, confirming what is with them, meaning confirming what was with them from the books that God sent down before the Qur’an, as:

c: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And when there came to them a Book from God
, confirming what is with them, and it is the Qur’an that was sent down to Muhammad, confirming what was with them from the Torah and the Gospel.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what was with them
, which is the Qur’an that was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, confirming what was with them of the Torah and the Gospel.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “And before that, they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved.
h
But when there came to them that which they recognized
, they disbelieved in it.”
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved

, is: And these Jews, when a book came to them from God confirming what they had, from the books that God revealed before the Criterion, they disbelieved in it, they used to pray for victory through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning of prayer is seeking victory, they used to pray for victory through him against the polytheists of the Arabs before his mission, that is, before he was sent, as Ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of ʿAsim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatadah al-Ansari, on the authority of elders among them who said: By God, this story was revealed about us and them, meaning the Ansar, and about the Jews, who were their neighbors, meaning:
h
And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved

, they said: We had prevailed over them for a long time in the Age of Ignorance, and we were the people of polytheism, and they were the people of the Book, so they used to say: Our Prophet, now that his mission has come, his time has come, he will kill you as ʿAd killed Iram.
When God Almighty sent His Messenger from Quraysh and we followed him, they disbelieved in him. God says:
h
But when there came to them that which they recognized

, they disbelieved in it. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, Ibn Ishaq narrated, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, a client of the family of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, a client of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Jews used to seek victory over the Aws and Khazraj through the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was sent. But when God sent him from among the Arabs, they disbelieved in him and denied what they used to say about him. So Muadh ibn Jabal and Bishr ibn al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur, the brother of Banu Salamah, said to them: O group of Jews, fear Surat Al-Baqarah 2:89 And when there came to them a Book from Allah confirming what was with them -
h
and before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved
h
but when there came to them that which they recognized
, they disbelieved in it.

So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers. God and submit to Islam, for you used to seek victory over us through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while we were polytheists, and you used to tell us that he would be sent and describe him according to his characteristics! Then Salam ibn Mishkam, the brother of Banu al-Nadir, said: He has not brought us anything that we know of, and he is not what we used to tell you! Then God Almighty revealed regarding that from their saying: “
h
And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what was with them
- although before they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved -
h
but when there came to them that which they recognized
, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told us, he said,
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of the family of Zayd bin Thabit, told me, he said, Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved

, meaning: They used to pray for victory through the uprising of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the polytheists of the Arabs, meaning by that the People of the Book. But when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they saw him as someone other than them, they disbelieved in him and envied him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ali al-Azdi,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved
, he said: The Jews used to say: O God, send us this Prophet who will judge between us and the people, they used to pray for victory and seek victory through him against the people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ali al-Azdi,
m: who is al-Barqi, regarding the statement of God, may He be glorified: And before that they used to seek victory, and he mentioned something similar. Bishr bin Muadh narrated: Yazid narrated: Saeed narrated: Qatada said: And before that they used to pray for victory over those who disbelieved, the Jews used to pray for victory through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, over the disbelieving Arabs before, and they said: O God, send this Prophet whom we find in the Torah to torment and kill them! But when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they saw that he was sent from someone other than them, and they disbelieved in him out of envy of the Arabs, even though they knew that he was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they found him written in their Torah.
h
But when there came to them that which they recognized
, they disbelieved in it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said:
m: The Jews used to seek victory through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the polytheists of the Arabs, saying: O God, send this Prophet whose name we find written down with us, so that he may torment and kill the polytheists! But when God sent Muhammad, and they saw that he was not from among them, they disbelieved in him out of envy of the Arabs, even though they knew that he was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God said: “
h
But when there came to them that which they recognized
, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.”

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what was with them
- although before they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved -
h
but when there came to them that which they recognized

, they disbelieved in it.” He said: The Arabs would pass by the Jews and harm them, and they would find Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah, and they would ask God to send him so that they could fight the Arabs with him. But when Muhammad came to them, they disbelieved in him, even though he was not from the Children of Israel.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: I said to Ata’ about his statement:
h
And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved

, he said: They used to pray for victory against the disbelievers of the Arabs through the emergence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they hoped that he would be one of them. But when he emerged and they saw that he was not one of them, they disbelieved, although they knew that he was the truth and that he was the Prophet. He said: “
h
But when there came to them that which they recognized

, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers.” He said: Ibn Jurayj told us, and Mujahid said: They begin with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: He will come out. So when there came to them what they recognized and it was from others, they disbelieved in it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, and Ibn Abbas said: They were seeking victory over the infidel Arabs.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Juhaf, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But when there came to them that which they recognized
, they disbelieved in it, he said: They are the Jews, they recognized Muhammad as a prophet and they disbelieved in him.

c: Al-Munjab narrated that Bishr narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved
, he said: They used to pray for victory, saying: We will help Muhammad against them. But they were not like that, they were lying.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I asked Ibn Zayd about the statement of God, the Almighty: “And before, they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved.
h
But when there came to them that which they recognized

, they disbelieved in it.” He said: The Jews used to pray for victory against the disbelieving Arabs, saying: By God, if the Prophet whom Moses and Jesus had given glad tidings of, Ahmad, had come, we would have victory over you! And they thought that he was from among them, and the Arabs were around them, and they used to pray for victory against them through him, and seek victory through him.
h
But when there came to them that which they recognized

, they disbelieved in him and envied him, and he recited the statement of God, the Almighty: Disbelievers, out of envy from themselves after the truth had become clear to them Al-Baqarah 2:109. He said: It had become clear to them that he was a Messenger, and from there God benefited the Aws and Khazraj with what they had heard from them that a Prophet was coming.

x: If someone were to say to us: What is the answer to his statement:
h
And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what was with them
? It was said: The Arab scholars differed in its answer.

Some of them said: It is one of those whose answer was left out, sufficing with the knowledge of those addressed by it of its meaning, and with what has been mentioned of its likes in the rest of the Qur’an. The Arabs sometimes do that when the speech is long, so they bring things that have answers, then they omit their answers, because their listeners are satisfied with their knowledge of its meaning without mentioning the answers, as God the Most High said:
And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak, but to God belongs the command entirely

so He left out its answer. The meaning is: If there were a Qur’an other than this Qur’an by which mountains could be moved, they would have been moved by this Qur’an, sufficing with the knowledge of the listeners of its meaning. They said: So too is His statement:
h
And when there came to them a Book from God confirming what is with them
Others said: The answer to his statement:
h
And when there came to them a Book from God is in the fa in his statement

: And when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it, and the answer to the two conditions in disbelieved in it, is like your saying: When you stood up, and When you came to us, you did well, meaning: When you came to us, when you stood up, you did well.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
Then the curse of God be upon the disbelievers

We have previously demonstrated the meaning of curse and the meaning of disbelief sufficiently. The meaning of the verse is: God’s disgrace and His distance from those who deny what they have recognized as the truth of God and His prophets, who deny what has been proven to them as true regarding the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: In God Almighty’s telling of the Jews what God told them
m: about them in His saying:
h
But when there came to them that which they recognized

, they disbelieved in it, the clear statement is that they deliberately disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the proof of his prophethood had been established for them, and God had cut off their excuse that he was His Messenger to them.
b.via: In God Almighty’s telling of the Jews what God

x: The meaning of the Most High’s words:
h
How evil is that for which they have sold their souls
is:
h
How evil is that for which they have sold their souls

. The root of ba’isa is ba’isa from ba’us. Its hamza was made quiescent, then its vowel was transferred to the ba’, as was said in dhallalta dhallat, and as was said for the liver, kabd, so the vowel of the ba’ was transferred to the kaf, because the ba’ was made quiescent. It may be possible that it is ba’isa, even though its root is ba’isa, from the language of those who transfer the vowel of the ‘ayn from the verb to the fa’, if the ‘ayn of the verb is one of the six throat letters, as they said man la’ab “al-‘ab” and man sa’ima “is’ima,” and this is what is said to be a widespread language in Tamim. Then it was made an indicator of blame and rebuke, and it was connected to what. The Arabists differed about the meaning of ma with bi’sma.

Some grammarians of Basra said: It alone is a noun, and an yakfiru is an explanation of it, like: Yes, Zayd is a man, and an yanzal God is a substitute for anzal God. Some grammarians of Kufa said: The meaning of that is: Ba’sa is the thing with which they bought themselves that they would disbelieve. As for the noun bi’sa, and an yakfiru is the second noun. He claimed that an yakfiru if you wish, you can put an in the nominative case, and if you wish, in the genitive case. As for the nominative case: Ba’sa is the thing that they do this that they do. As for the genitive case: Ba’sa is the thing with which they bought themselves that they would disbelieve in what God revealed out of envy. He said: His statement
h
Bad is what their souls have put forward for them

, that God is angry with them (al-Ma’idah 5:80) is similar to that. The Arabs make what is alone in this chapter, like a complete noun, like his saying: So what an excellent thing it is (al-Baqarah 2:271), and What an evil thing you are.
And he cited as evidence for his saying that the rajaz of some rajaz poets: Do not rush in your journey, for indeed, it is slow and we do not take care of it.

The Arabs say, How bad is a marriage and no dowry, making what it alone a noun without a connection. The speaker of this article does not allow that what follows ba’isa is a temporary definite noun, and its predicate is a temporary definite noun. He claimed that ba’isa is like ba’isa al-shay’ bih bayhu nasuf the evil thing they bought themselves with. So ma connected to it has become a temporary noun, because ashtarawu is a past tense verb connected to ma, according to the speaker of this article. And if it is connected to a past tense verb, it is a temporary definite noun known, so the interpretation of the statement then becomes: ba’isa bih karhumu their disbelief is ba’isa the evil thing they bought themselves with. And that is not permissible in his opinion. The corruption of this statement has become clear. Another one of them claimed that an is in the accusative case if you wish, and in the nominative case if you wish.

As for the accusative case: you return it to the ha in bih as a repetition of two sentences. It is as if you said: They bought themselves with disbelief. As for the nominative case: it is repeated in the place of ma that follows ba’isa. He said: It is not permissible for it to be in the nominative case as you say: Ba’isa the man Abdullah is.

Some of them said: Bisama is a single thing that raises what comes after it. As it was narrated from the Arabs: Bisama is a marriage and no dowry. So Bisama is raised by Bisama, just as it is said: Bisama Zayd, and Bisama ma Amr, so Bisama is raised, with what came after it from the ha. It is as if you said: Bisama is the thing with which they bought themselves, and an is translated from Bisama. The first of these sayings is the most correct, the saying of those who made bi'sama raised by the reference of the ha' in his saying: they bought with it, just as they raised it with Abdullah when they said: bi'sama Abdullah, and made an yakfaru a translation of bi'sama. The meaning of the statement then is: what a bad thing the Jews sold themselves for, their disbelief in what God revealed out of envy and jealousy that God would send down from His grace. And an in his saying: an yakfaru bi'an God is in the accusative case.
Because he means by it that they disbelieve in what God revealed: in order for God to send down from His grace to whomever He wills of His servants. The position of an is a reward.

Some of the Arab scholars from Kufa claimed that an is in the genitive case with the structure of ba. We chose the accusative case for it because the report before it is complete, and there is no preposition with it to lower it. And the preposition does not lower an implied word. As for his saying:
h
They sold their souls for it

, he means by it: They sold their souls, as Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: How evil is that for which they sold their souls, he says: They sold their souls that they should disbelieve in what God has revealed out of envy.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hasan told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said:
m: How evil is that for which they have sold themselves, the Jews, they sold the truth with falsehood, and concealed what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought by making it clear.

x: The Arabs say: I bought it, meaning I sold it. And they bought, in this case, Come on from I bought. And the speech of the Arabs, as far as we have been informed, is that they say: I bought, meaning I sold, and I bought, meaning I purchased.

i: And it was said:
x: The buyer was called a buyer because he sold himself and his worldly life for his afterlife. And from that is the saying of Yazid bin Mufrij Al-Himyari: I bought a cold, I wish I had been cold before And from it is the saying of Al-Musayyab bin Als: He is given a price for it, but then he refuses it and its owner says: Why don’t you buy it?

He means: I sold a cloak. And perhaps I bought is used to mean: I sold, and I bought to mean: I bought. The widespread discussion about them is what I described. As for the meaning of his saying: out of envy, he means by it: aggression and envy, as Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, out of envy, he said: meaning envy, and they are the Jews.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Ghagya, he said: They were unjust towards Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they envied him, and they said: The messengers were only from the Children of Israel, so what about this one from the Children of Ishmael? So they envied him that God would bestow His grace upon whomever He wills of His servants.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: Out of envy, meaning: out of envy that God would bestow His grace upon whomever He wills of His servants, and they are the Jews. They disbelieved in what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly.

x: The meaning of the verse is: What a bad thing they sold their souls for, disbelief in what God revealed in His Book to Moses of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the command to believe in him and follow him because God revealed from His grace - and His grace is His wisdom, His signs, and His prophethood - to whomever He wills of His servants. He means by it: to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of envy and spite for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he was from the descendants of Ishmael, and was not from the Children of Israel.
How did the Jews sell themselves for disbelief?
How evil is that for which they have sold themselves - that they should disbelieve in what God has revealed. Is anything bought for disbelief?

It was said: The meaning of buying and selling among the Arabs is the transfer of one’s property to another, in exchange for something he takes from it. Then the Arabs use this for everything that is exchanged for something from his work, whether good or bad. So they say: Yes, what someone sold himself for and Bad is what someone sold himself for, meaning: Yes, the gain he earned, and bad is the gain he earned if he made it inherit good or bad through his efforts. Likewise, the meaning of the words of God, the Most High: Bad is that for which they sold their souls, when they ruined themselves by their disbelief in Muhammad, so they destroyed them. God addressed them and the Arabs with what they know in their speech, so He said: Bad is that for which they sold their souls, meaning by that: Bad is that for which they earned themselves through their efforts, and bad is the exchange they took from their disbelief in God in their denial of Muhammad, since they were satisfied in exchange for the reward of God and what He had prepared for them if they had believed in God and what He had sent down to His prophets with the fire and what He had prepared for them through their disbelief in that.

This verse and what God has told in it about the Jews’ envy of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his people from the Arabs, because God made prophethood and wisdom in them and not in the Jews from the Children of Israel, until that led them to disbelieve in him, despite their knowledge of his truthfulness and that he is a prophet sent by God and a messenger sent by Him, is similar to the other verse in Surat An-Nisa’, which is His saying: “Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in jibt and taghut and say of those who disbelieve, ‘These are better guided than those who believe in the way.’ Those are the ones whom God has cursed, and he whom God curses, you will never find Surat al-Baqarah 2:90 Evil is that for which they have exchanged their souls - that they should disbelieve in what Allah has revealed, out of envy that Allah should send down of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants.
h
So they incurred wrath upon wrath
h
and for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment

. for him a helper. Or do they have a portion of the kingdom? Then they would not give the people even a speck on a date stone. Or do they envy the people for what God has given them of His bounty? But We had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom and conferred upon them a great kingdom.”
r
The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
That God sends down from His grace upon whomever He wills of His servants
We have already mentioned the interpretation of that and explained its meaning, but we will mention the narration with the correction of what we said in it:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of ʿAsim ibn ʿUmar ibn Qatada al-Ansari, on the authority of elders among them,
m: his statement:
h
In order that God should send down from His grace upon whomever He wills of His servants
, meaning that God Almighty made it for others than them.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: They are the Jews. When God sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they disbelieved and thought that he was sent from someone other than them. They disbelieved in him out of envy of the Arabs, even though they knew that he was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They found him written in their Torah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: similarly.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: They said: The messengers were only from the Children of Israel, so what about this one from the Children of Ishmael?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ali al-Azdi, he said:
m: It was revealed about the Jews.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
So they incurred wrath upon wrath
What he meant by his saying:
h
And they incurred wrath upon wrath

, is that the Jews of the Children of Israel returned after what they had been upon of seeking victory from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and seeking his help, and after what they had been telling the people before his mission that he was a prophet sent, turning back on their heels when God sent him as a prophet sent.
