So they incurred wrath from God, which they deserved from Him by their disbelief in Muhammad when he was sent, and their denial of his prophethood, and their denial that he was the one whose description they find in their book, out of their stubbornness towards him and their envy of him and the Arabs, for a previous wrath that had been from God upon them before that, preceding His second wrath, for their disbelief that was before Jesus, son of Mary, or for their worship of the calf, or for other sins that they had committed in the past, for which they deserved wrath from God, as Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, as narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
So they incurred wrath upon wrath
, so wrath upon wrath, His wrath upon them for what they had wasted of the Torah while it was with them, and His wrath for their disbelief in this prophet whom God had brought to them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed and Abd al-Rahman told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
So they incurred wrath upon wrath
. He said: Disbelief in Jesus, and disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, Yahya bin Yaman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
So they incurred wrath upon wrath
, he said: Their disbelief in Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: similarly. Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated on the authority of Mughirah on the authority of Al-Sha’bi who said: People will be divided into four categories on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:A man who believed in Jesus and believed in Muhammad, may God bless them both, will have two rewards. A man who disbelieved in Jesus and believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will have one reward. A man who disbelieved in Jesus and disbelieved in Muhammad, so he incurred wrath upon wrath. A man who was a disbeliever in Jesus from the polytheists of the Arabs, but died in his disbelief before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he incurred wrath.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So they incurred wrath upon wrath
, God’s wrath upon them for their disbelief in the Gospel and Jesus, and He was wrath upon them for their disbelief in the Qur’an and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So they incurred the wrath of the Jews, because of their alteration of the Torah before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out, because of the wrath, because of their denial of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their disbelief in what he brought.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: h
So they incurred wrath upon wrath
, meaning: God’s wrath upon them for their disbelief in the Gospel and Jesus, then His wrath upon them for their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in the Qur’an.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
So they incurred wrath upon wrath
. As for the first wrath, it was when God became angry with them regarding the calf. As for the second wrath, it was when they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: Ata’ and Ubayd ibn Umair, regarding his statement:
h
And they incurred wrath upon wrath

, he said: God’s wrath was upon them for what they were in before the Prophet’s departure, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their changing and disbelief, then He became angry with them regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he departed, so they disbelieved in him.

x: We have already explained the meaning of God’s wrath upon those of His creation with whom He became angry and the differences of those who differed regarding His description in what has preceded in this book of ours, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment

, is for all people who deny the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, a punishment from God, either in the Hereafter, or in this world and the Hereafter. Humiliating is that which humiliates its owner, disgraces him, and clothes him with humiliation and disgrace.
What punishment is not humiliating to its sufferer, so that the unbelievers are humiliated by it?

The humiliating is that which we have shown is that which causes its owner to be humiliated and disgraced, in which its owner will remain forever, never moving from his humiliation to honor and dignity. It is that which God has made special for the disbelievers in Him and His Messengers. As for that which is not humiliating to its owner, it is that which was a purification for its owner. This is like the thief from the people of Islam, who steals what is required of him for amputation, so his hand is cut off, and the adulterer from them who commits adultery and the prescribed punishment is carried out on him, and what is similar to that of the torment and punishment which God has made as expiations for the sins with which He punished its people, and like the major sinners from the people of Islam who are tormented in the Hereafter according to the extent of the crimes they committed, so that they may be purified from their sins, then they enter Paradise. For all of that, even if it is a torment, it is not humiliating to the one who is tormented with it.
For God’s torment of him with it was to purify him from his sins, then He brings him to the mine of honor and dignity, and makes him eternal in the bliss of Paradise.
What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
And when it is said to them

, and when it is said to the Jews from the Children of Israel who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Believe, meaning believe, in what God has revealed, meaning in what God revealed of the Qur’an to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said, ‘We believe,’ meaning we believe, “in what has been revealed to us, meaning: in the Torah that God revealed to Moses.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And they disbelieve in what is beyond it
What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
And they disbelieve in what is beyond it
, and they deny, what is beyond it, means: what is beyond the Torah.

The interpretation of behind it in this context is: other than it. Just as it is said to a man who speaks well: There is nothing behind this speech, meaning: the speaker has nothing other than that speech. Likewise the meaning of his statement:
h
And they disbelieve in what is behind it

, meaning in what is other than the Torah, and in what came after it of the books of God that He sent down to His Messengers, as Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
And they disbelieve in what is behind it
, he says: in what comes after it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: And they disbelieve in what comes after it, meaning what comes after it, meaning: what comes after the Torah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: And they disbelieve in what comes after it, he said: in what comes after it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And it is the truth
, confirming what is with them.
What He, the Most High, means by His statement,
h
And it is the truth

, confirming, is: what is beyond the Book that He sent down to them from the Books that God sent down to His true prophets. What He, the Most High, means by that is the Qur’an that He sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Moses told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
And when it is said to them
, ‘Believe in what God has sent down,’ they say, ‘We believe in what was sent down to us,’ and they disbelieve in what came after it, which is the Qur’an. God, the Most High, says,
h
And it is the truth

, confirming what is with them. And He, the Most High, said, confirming what is with them, because the Books of God confirm each other. In the Gospel and the Qur’an, there is a command to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to believe in him and what he brought, just as there is in the Torah of Moses, peace be upon him.

Therefore, He, the Most High, said to the Jews when He informed them of what was beyond their book that He sent down to Moses, peace be upon him, from the books that He sent down to His prophets: It is the truth confirming the book that is with them, meaning: It is in agreement with what the Jews deny. He said: This is report from God that they deny the Torah, just as they deny the Gospel and the Criterion, out of defiance of God, in opposition to His command, and in transgression against His Messengers, may God’s prayers be upon them. Say in the interpretation of his saying: “Say: Why then did you kill the prophets of God before, if you were believers?”

What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: “Say: Why then do you kill the prophets of God?” Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews of the Children of Israel who, when you say to them: Believe in what God has revealed, they say:
h
We believe in what was revealed to us

: Why do you kill, if you, O group of Jews, believe in what God has revealed to you, His prophets, and God has forbidden in the Book that He revealed to you to kill them, rather He has commanded you in it to follow them, obey them, and believe in them?
This is from God, the Most High, as a denial of them in His saying:
h
We believe in what was revealed to us
, and as a reproach to them, as:

c: Moses told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: God, the Most High, said while reproaching them, meaning the Jews: Why then did you kill the prophets of God before, if you were believers?

x: How was it said to them:
h
Why did you not kill God’s prophets before
? and the ink began with the wording of the future, then it was reported that it had passed?
The Arabs differed in their interpretation of that.

i: Some of the Basrans said:
x: The meaning of that is:
h
Why did you kill the prophets of God before

, as the Most High said: And they followed what the devils recited (al-Baqarah 2:102), meaning: what they recited, and as the poet said: The vile man ordered me to insult him, so I left him and said, It does not concern me.
He meant by his saying: And he commanded and I passed by. And he provided evidence that this is the case, by his saying:
h
So I passed by him
, and he did not say:
h
So I passed by him

i: And he claimed that the verb fa’ala and yaf’ulu share one meaning, and he cited as evidence for that the saying of the poet:
x: I come to you to thank you for what has passed, and to fulfill what will be in the future.

i: He means by that: what will happen tomorrow, and in the words of Al-Hutay’ah:
x: Al-Hutay'ah will testify on the day he meets his Lord that Al-Walid is more deserving of an apology.

Meaning: He bears witness, and as the other said: I do not spend the morning or evening without seeing myself among you in a state of disgrace. He said: It is morning, then he said: Nor did I spend the evening. Some Kufi grammarians said: It was said,
h
Why did you kill the prophets of God before

? So he addressed them with the future tense of the verb and its past meaning, just as a man rebukes another man for what he did in the past and says to him: Woe to you, why did you lie? And why did you make yourself hated by people?

i: As the poet said:
x: If we were related, you would not have given birth to me as a mean person and you would not have found it useful to acknowledge it.

The reward is for the future, and the entire birth has already passed. This is because the meaning is known, so it is permissible. He said: And similar to it in speech: If you look at the biography of Omar, you will not find him doing wrong. The meaning is: you will not find him doing wrong. So since there is no doubt that the matter of Omar was past, it did not occur to the mind that it was future. Therefore, it was reconciled with his saying:
h
Why did you kill the prophets of God before

? He said: And those who were addressed with killing are not the killers, rather the prophets killed their ancestors who had passed away, so they took them over to that and were satisfied with it, so the killing was attributed to them.

The correct view in this regard, according to us, is that God addressed those Jews of the Children of Israel who had known the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as He addressed them in Surat al-Baqarah and other surahs, regarding His previous kindness to their ancestors, and regarding their ancestors’ previous ingratitude for His blessings, their commission of sins, and their audacity towards Him and His prophets. He attributed that to those addressed by it, similar to the Arabs saying to one another: We did to you on such and such a day, and you did to us on such and such a day, in a manner that we have explained in more than one place in this book of ours. They mean by that: Our ancestors did that to your ancestors, and our forefathers did that to your forefathers. Likewise in His statement:
h
Why did you kill the prophets of God before

? Since it had come out in the form of a report from those addressed by it, a report from God, the Most High, about the action of their predecessors in the manner that we have explained, it was permissible to say before, since its meaning was: Say: Why did your forefathers kill the prophets of God before?
It was known that his saying:
h
Why did you not kill God’s prophets before
? was better than the actions of their predecessors. The interpretation of his saying before is: before today. As for his saying:
h
If you are believers
, he means:
h
If you are believers

in what God has revealed to you as you claim. Rather, He meant by that the Jews who knew the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and their ancestors, if they and you, as you claim, O Jews, were believers. Rather, God, the Most High, reproached them for killing their forefathers, His prophets, when it was said to them: Believe in what God has revealed. They said:
h
We believe in what was revealed to us
. Because they were the ones who killed the prophets of God, along with their saying:
h
We believe in what was revealed to us

, taking charge and being pleased with their actions. So He said to them: If you are, as you claim, believers in what was revealed to you, then why did you take charge of the killers of the prophets of God?
That is: were you pleased with their actions.
What He, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
And Moses came to you with clear proofs

, is that he came to you with clear proofs indicating his truthfulness and the truth of his prophethood, such as the staff that turned into a clear serpent, and his hand that he brought out white for the onlookers. And the splitting of the sea and turning its land into a dry path for him, and the locusts, the lock, the frogs, and all the other signs that demonstrated his truthfulness and the truth of his prophethood. God called them clear signs to make clear to those who look at them that they are miracles that no human being can produce except by God’s making it possible for him. It is the plural of clear sign, like good and good things.
The meaning of the statement is: O group of Jews of the Children of Israel, Moses came to you with clear signs of his matter, his truthfulness, and the validity of his prophethood. And His statement:
h
Then you took the calf after him

, while you were wrongdoers, God Almighty says to them: Then you took the calf after Moses as a god. The ha in His statement: after him is from the mention of Moses. And He only said: after Moses, because they took the calf after Moses had departed from them, going to his Lord for his appointment, as we have explained previously in this book of ours. It is possible that the letter ha’ in ba’dahu refers to the mention of coming. Then the interpretation of the statement would be:
h
And Moses came to you with clear proofs
, then you took the calf after the clear proofs came, and you were wrongdoers. Just as you say: You came to me and I hated it, meaning: I hated your coming.

As for His statement: And you are wrongdoers, what he means by that is: You did what you did of worshipping the calf, and that is not your right, and you worshipped other than the One whom you should have worshipped. Because worship is not appropriate for anyone other than God. This is a rebuke from God to the Jews, a reproach from Him to them, and an announcement from Him that if they did what they did of taking the calf as a god, and He does not possess the power to harm or benefit them, after they knew that their Lord is the Lord who does wonders and wonderful deeds that He performed through the hands of Moses, peace be upon him, of matters that no one from God’s creation is capable of, and that Pharaoh and his soldiers were not capable of, despite his brutality and the large number of his followers, and the closeness of their time to what they witnessed of the wonders of God’s rule, they are quicker to deny Muhammad, peace be upon him, and to reject what is in their books, in which they claimed to believe, of His description and attributes, despite the distance between them and the time of Moses, and closer to denying what Moses brought them of that.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And when We took your covenant

, and remember when We took your covenants, that you take what We gave you of the Torah which I revealed to you, that you act according to what is in it of My command, and refrain from what I forbade you in it with diligence and energy from you in that, so you were given your covenant to act according to that, when We raised the rope above you.

i: As for His saying: And listen, its meaning is: And listen to what I have commanded you to do and accept it with obedience, like a man saying to a man commanding him to do something: I hear and obey, meaning by that: I heard your saying, and I obeyed your command, as the rajaz poet said:
x: Hearing, obedience and submission are better and more beneficial for Banu Tamim What he means by his saying: Hearing is accepting what is heard and obeying what is commanded.
Likewise, the meaning of his saying:
h
And listen is accepting what you hear and acting upon it
The meaning of the verse:
h
And when We took your covenant

is: Take what We have given you with strength, and act according to what you have heard, and obey God, and We raised the mountain above you for that reason. As for his saying: They said, ‘We have heard,’ the speech came out as a report about someone absent after it had begun with an address. This is as we have described, because when the beginning of a speech is a narration, the Arabs address one another and then return to reporting about someone absent, and inform about someone absent and then address one another, as we have explained before. So it is the same in this verse, because his saying:
h
And when We took your covenant

, means: We said to you, and you answered us. As for his saying: They said, ‘We hear,’ it is report from God about the Jews from whom He took a covenant to act according to what was in the Torah, and to obey God in what they heard from it.
They said when that was said to them: We hear your word, and we disobey your command.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And they made the calf drink into their hearts because of their disbelief.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: And they imbibed the love of the calf into their hearts.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they imbibed the love of the calf into their hearts, he said: They imbibed its love, until it reached their hearts.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: And they drank the calf into their hearts, he said: They drank the love of the calf because of their disbelief.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: And they imbibed the love of the calf into their hearts, he said: They imbibed the love of the calf into their hearts.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that they gave them to drink the water in which the filth of the calf had been scattered.
Those who said this mentioned:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: When Musa returned to his people, he took the calf that he found them devoted to and slaughtered it, then burned it with a file, then scattered it in the sea, so that there was not a sea that flowed that day except that some of it fell into it. Then Musa said to them: Drink from it. So they drank, and whoever loved it came out drinking gold. That is when God the Almighty says: And they had drunk the calf into their hearts because of their disbelief.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: When he was dragged and thrown into the sea, they faced the flow of water and drank until they filled their stomachs, and that caused those among them to become cowardly because of his actions.

x: The first of the two interpretations that I mentioned regarding the statement of God Almighty: And they made the calf drink into their hearts is the interpretation of the one who said: And they made the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:93
h
And when We took your covenant

and raised the mount above you, [saying], "Take what We have given you with strength and listen." They said, "We hear and disobey." And they were made to drink into their hearts the calf because of their disbelief. Say, "Evil is that which your faith enjoins upon you, if you are [true] believers." love of the calf drink into their hearts. Because it is not said of water: So-and-so drank into his heart, but rather that is said of the love of something, so it is said of it: So-and-so’s heart drank the love of such-and-such, meaning: he was given that drink until it overcame him and mixed with his heart, as Zuhair said: I woke up from it after an inner love, and love is a disease that your heart drinks Abu Jaʿfar said: But he left out mentioning love, contenting himself with the listener understanding the meaning of the words.
Since it was known that the calf does not drink the heart, and that which the heart drinks from is its love, as God Almighty said:
And ask them about the city that was by the sea
And ask the city in which we were and the caravan in which we came
r
(Yusuf 12:82)

, and as the poet said: I have been given a pitch black drink, a clear drink, a clear drink He meant by that: black poison, so he was satisfied with mentioning black instead of mentioning poison, so that the listener would understand the meaning of what he meant by his saying: I gave black poison to drink. It is narrated: I have given water to a black man who has been drinking The Arabs may say: If you want to look at generosity, then look at Harim or Hatim. Mentioning the name is sufficient instead of mentioning his action, if he is known for his courage, generosity, or similar qualities.

i: From this is the saying of the poet:
x: They say: Fight, Jameel, in a raid!
And fight against Tayy and its fighting. Say in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘Evil is that which your faith enjoins upon you,
h
if you are believers

By that, God, the Most High, means: Say, O Muhammad, to the Jews of the Children of Israel: What a bad thing your faith commands you to do, if it commands you to kill the prophets and messengers of God, to deny His books, and to reject what came from Him. The meaning of their faith is their belief in what they claimed they believed in from the Book of God, when it was said to them: Believe in what God has revealed, and they said: We believe in what has been revealed to us. And His statement:
h
If you are believers
, means: If you believe, as you claim, in what God has revealed to you. God only called them liars by that because the Torah forbids all of that and commands the opposite.

c: So He informed them that
m: their belief in the Torah, if it commands them to do that, then what a bad thing it commands. Rather, this is a denial from God Almighty that the Torah commands something that God hates in their actions, and that believing in it indicates something of disobeying God’s command, and an announcement from Him, may He be glorified, that what commands them to do this is their desires, and what drives them to it is oppression and aggression.

x: This verse is one of the arguments that God used for His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) against the Jews who were among his immigrants, and He exposed their rabbis and scholars with it. This is because God, the Most High, commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him) to call them to a just cause between him and them, in the dispute that existed between him and them. God also commanded him to call the other group of Christians when they disagreed with him about Jesus (peace be upon him) and argued about him to a decisive contest between him and them. He said to the group of Jews: If you are right,
h
then wish for death

, for that will not harm you, if you are right in what you claim of faith and nearness of status to God. Rather, if you are granted your wish of death when you wish, then you will only be at ease from the fatigue, hardship, and trouble of this world, and you will be victorious in the company of God in His Paradise, if the matter is as you claim: that the Hereafter is exclusively for you and not for us.

If you do not give it to them, people will know that you are the liars and we are the ones who are right in our claim, and our matter and your matter will be revealed to them. The Jews refused to answer the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they knew that if they wished for death, they would perish, their worldly life would be lost, and they would be destined for eternal disgrace in the Hereafter. The group of Christians who argued with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Jesus, when they were called to a Mubahala, also refused to do so. It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the Jews wished for death, they would die and see their seats in Hellfire. If those who challenged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out, they would return without finding family or wealth.

c: Abu Kuraib told us that Zakariya bin Adi told us that Ubaidullah bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Adam told us, he said, Othman bin Ali told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then wish for death
, if you should be truthful, he said: If they wished for death, one of them would choke on his saliva.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then wish for death
, if you should be truthful, Ibn Abbas said: If the Jews wished for death, they would have died.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, Abu Jaʿfar said:
m: In what I narrate: He informed us on the authority of Saʿid, or ʿIkrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If they had wished for it on the day he said that to them, there would not have remained a Jew on the face of the earth who did not die.

x: The lies, slander, and oppression of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were revealed to those who were confused about the matter of the Jews on that day. The argument of the Messenger of God and the argument of his companions against them became clear, and it has not ceased, praise be to God, to be clear against them and against others from among the people of all religions. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was ordered to say to them: Wish for death if you are truthful, because, as we have been told, they said: We are the children of God and His beloved ones (al-Ma’idah 5:18), and they said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian (al-Baqarah 2:111). So God said to His Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Tell them: If you are truthful in what you claim,
h
then wish for death
God exposed their lie by their refusal to wish for that, and He proved the argument of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him).

The people of interpretation differed about the reason why God ordered His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call upon the Jews to wish for death, and in what manner they were ordered to wish for it.
Some of them said: They were ordered to wish for it as a supplication against the lying group of them.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told us, on the authority of Saeed,
m: or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God said to His Prophet, may God Surat Al-Baqarah 2:94 Say, "If the home of the Hereafter with Allah is exclusively for you and not for the people,
h
then wish for death
, if you should be truthful." bless him and grant him peace: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of all other people,
h
then wish for death
, if you should be truthful,” meaning: Call for death against whichever of the two groups is more lying.

x: Others said: Bishr ibn Muadh told me, he said:

c: Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, he said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you and not for the people,” that is because they said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian (al-Baqarah 2:111) and they said: We are the children of God and His beloved (al-Ma’idah 5:18). So it was said to them:
h
Then wish for death
if you are truthful.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said: The Jews said:
m: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian (al-Baqarah 2:111), and they said: We are the children of God and His beloved (Al-Maʿidah: 18). So God said: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the people,
h
then wish for death
, if you should be truthful,” but they did not do so.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you” (al-Baqarah 2:111), that is because they said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian (al-Baqarah 2:111) and they said: We are the children of God and His beloved (al-Maʿidah 5:18). As for the interpretation of his statement: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you,” he is saying: Say, O Muhammad: If the delights and pleasures of the home of the Hereafter are for you, O group of Jews, with God. So he was satisfied with mentioning the home, rather than mentioning its delights, so that those addressed by the verse would know its meaning. We have previously explained the meaning of the Hereafter, so there is no need to repeat it here. As for the interpretation of his saying: pure, he means: clear. Just as it is said: So-and-so was pure for me, meaning he became mine alone and a description for me. It is said from it: this thing was pure for me, so it is purely and sincerely, and pure is a source like wellness. And it is said to a man: this is my purity, meaning: my purity from the exclusion of my companions.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he interpreted his saying: pure as meaning exclusive. This is an interpretation close to the meaning of the interpretation that we mentioned about that.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed told us, he said, Bishr bin Amara told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Say, ‘If the home of the Hereafter is yours,’ he said: Say, O Muhammad, to them, meaning the Jews: If the home of the Hereafter is yours,’ meaning Paradise, with God exclusively, he said: exclusively for you. As for his statement: except for the people, what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation is that they said: The Hereafter is for us exclusively with God, apart from all the people. And it is clear that this was their statement without excluding from it any of the children of Adam, as God informed us about them that they said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian Al-Baqarah 2:111, except that it was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said something other than that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed told us, he said, Bishr bin Ammarah told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: except for the people, he says: apart from Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions whom you mocked, and you claimed that the truth was in your hands, and that the Hereafter was yours, apart from them. As for his saying:
h
And wish for death

, its interpretation is: you desire it and want it. It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said in its interpretation: So ask for death. Wishing is not known to mean asking in the speech of the Arabs. However, I think that Ibn Abbas directed the meaning of wishing, since it was the love and desire of the soul, to the meaning of desire and asking, since the question is the desire of the questioner to God for what he asked of Him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed told us, he said, Bishr bin Amara told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Then wish for death
, so ask for death, if you are truthful.

x: This is report from God, the Most High, about the Jews and their hatred of death, and their refusal to respond to what they were called to by wishing for death, because they knew that if they did that, the threat would descend upon them, and death would befall them, and because they knew that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a messenger from God to them, and they denied him, and that he did not tell them anything except that it was true as he told.
So they were wary of wishing for death, fearing that God's punishment would befall them for the sins their hands had committed, like what:

c: Muhammad ibn Humayd told me, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, according to what Abu Ja'far narrates from Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas:
m: Say, 'If the home of the Hereafter is yours' the verse, meaning: Call for death on which of the two groups is more lying. So they refused that regarding the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth, meaning: because of their knowledge of what they have of knowledge of You, and their disbelief in that.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Uthman bin Saeed narrated to us, he said: Bishr bin Amara narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they will never wish for it, he said: O Muhammad, they will never wish for it, because they know that they are lying. If they were truthful, they would have wished for it and desired to hasten to My honor, so they will never wish for it because of what their hands have put forth.

c: Al-Qasim told me, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: Then wish for death, if you should be truthful. The Jews were most afraid of death, and they would never wish for it. As for his statement: for what their hands have put forth, he means by that: for what their hands have put forth. It is only an example, similar to what the Arabs use in their speech, so they say to a man who is taken to task for a crime he committed or a crime he has committed, and is punished for it: This has befallen you for what your hands have wrought, for what your hands have earned, and for what your hands have put forth. So they attribute that to the hand. Perhaps the crime he committed, for which he deserved punishment, was with the tongue, or the private parts, or any other part of his body other than the hand.

x: This was said by attributing it to the hand, because the majority of people’s crimes are committed by their hands, so the speech was based on attributing the crimes that people commit to their hands, until everything for which a person was punished, which he committed with the rest of his body’s parts, was attributed to it being a punishment for what his hand committed. Therefore, God, the Most High, said to the Arabs: And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth. He meant by this: The Jews will never wish for death because of what they put forth in their lives of disbelief in God, in their disobedience to Him in following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought from God, and they find it written in their Torah, and they know that he is a prophet sent. So God, the Most High, attributed what their hearts concealed, their souls concealed, and their tongues uttered of envy of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and transgression against him, and their denial of him and rejection of his message to their hands, and that it is from what their hands have put forth, because the Arabs knew the meaning of that in their logic and speech.
Since God, the Most High, only revealed the Qur’an in their language and dialect.

c: It was narrated from Ibn Abbas in this regard: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed told us, he said, Bishr bin Amara told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Because of what their hands have put forth, he said: Because of what their hands have put forth.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Because of what their hands have put forth, he said: They knew that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a prophet, but they concealed it. As for his saying: And God is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers, He, may His praise be glorified, means: God is All-Knowing of the wrongdoing of the children of Adam, their Jews, Christians, and all other people of other religions, and what they do. The injustice of the Jews: their disbelief in God in their opposition to His command and obedience to Him in following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after they had sought his help and his mission, and their denial of his prophethood while they knew that he was God’s prophet and messenger to them. We have already demonstrated the meaning of injustice in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And you will find them the most greedy of people for life is the Jews

. He says: O Muhammad, you will find that the people who are most eager for life in this world, and most averse to death, are the Jews. As: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abu Muhammad, as narrated by Abu Jaafar on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And you will find them the most greedy of people for life, meaning the Jews.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, Al-Rabiʿ told us, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: And you will find them the most greedy of people for life, meaning the Jews.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Their hatred of death is due to their knowledge of the shame and long-term humiliation that awaits them in the Hereafter.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And among those who associate others with God
What God, the Most High, meant by His statement,
h
and among those who associate others with God

, is more eager for life than those who associate others with God, just as it is said, He is the bravest of people and from Antarah means: He is braver than people and from Antarah. So too is His statement,
h
and among those who associate others with God

, because the meaning of the statement is: You will find, O Muhammad, the Jews among the Children of Israel, more eager for life than those who associate others with God. So when more eager was added to people, and there is an interpretation of from, it was made clear after the conjunction, in response to the interpretation we mentioned. God, the Most High, described the Jews as the people who are most eager for life, because they know what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter despite their disbelief in what the polytheists do not acknowledge.

They are more averse to death than the polytheists who do not believe in the Resurrection, because they believe in the Resurrection and know what torment they will suffer there. The polytheists do not believe in the Resurrection or the punishment, so the Jews are more eager for life and more averse to death than them. It was said: Those who associate partners with God, the Most High, who said that the Jews are more eager for life than them in this verse, are the Magians who do not believe in resurrection.
It was mentioned that those who said: They are the Magians:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: And among those who associate partners with God,
h
one of them would like to live a thousand years
, meaning the Magians.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
And among those who associate others with God
h
one of them would like to live a thousand years
, he said: The Magians.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And among those who associate others with God
, he said: Jews, more eager for life than these.

x: Mention of those who said: They are those who deny the al-Qiyamah 75:Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abu Muhammad, as narrated by Abu Jaʿfar on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, or ʿIkrimah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas: And you will find them the most greedy of people for life, even more so than those who associate others with God. This is because the polytheist does not hope for resurrection after death, for he loves a long life, and the Jew has known what shame he will have in the afterlife, because of what he has wasted of the knowledge he had.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s Surat al-Baqarah 2:96 And you will surely find them the most greedy of people for life, even more than those who associate others with God.
h
One of them would like
to be granted a life of a thousand years, but that will not remove him from the punishment.
h
And God is Seeing of what they do
. saying: One of them would wish that he could live a thousand years.
This is report from God, the Most High, about those who associate others with God, who informed us that the Jews were more eager for life than them.

God, the Most High, says: One of these polytheists, who are hopeless, with the passing of his world and the end of his life, would wish to have a resurrection or a life or joy or happiness after that, if only he could live a thousand years, until some of them made the greeting of others: ten thousand years, out of their eagerness for life, as:

c: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us,
m: he heard my father Ali, Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
One of them would wish only to live a thousand years

, he said: It is the saying of the Persians: Sal Zah Nowruz is a free festival. And it was narrated on the authority of Naim al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr:
h
One of them would like to live a thousand years
. He said: It is what the polytheists say to one another when they sneeze: Zah Hazar sal.
b.via: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq

c: Ibrahim bin Saeed and Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told us: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
One of them would like to live a thousand years
, he said: Sin was made to be beloved to them for a long life.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ali bin Ma’bad told me, on the authority of Ibn Ulayyah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: regarding his statement:
h
One of them would like
, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And you will find them the most greedy of people for life, until he reached even if he were to live a thousand years, the Jews, were more greedy than these for life, and these would have liked for one of them to live a thousand years. And he narrated on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
One of them would like to live a thousand years
, he said: It is the statement of one of them when he sneezes and sneezes, he says: Ten thousand years.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live long
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live long
, and living long, which is a long life, will not remove him from the punishment of God.

i: His saying he is a pillar, because what the noun is more requested than the verb, as the poet said:
x: Is it raised by what is here the head?
The an in an ya’mur is a nominative, with muzahzaha, and the huwa with ma is a repetition, a pillar of the verb, because the Arabs find the indefinite before the definite.
Some of them said: He with what is a metaphor for mentioning lifespan. It is as if he said:
h
One of them would like to live a thousand years
, but that lifespan will not relieve him of the torment. He made that he may live a translation of He, meaning that lifespan will not relieve him of it.
Some of them said: His saying:
h
And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live long
, is similar to your saying: Zaid will not remove him from the punishment that he should live long.
The closest of these sayings to the truth in our view is what we have said, which is that he is a pillar, similar to your saying Amr is not standing.

Some of the people of interpretation said that the an in His statement: that he lives means: and that he lives. This is a statement that contradicts the meanings of the well-known speech of the Arabs.
Those who said this were:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: And it will not remove him from the punishment that he lives, he said: and that he lives.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: That he lives long, even if he lives long. As for the interpretation of his saying: by moving him, it is by distancing him and turning him away, as Al-Hutay’ah said: They said: Move away, we have no need of you, and none of us can mend it. He means by his saying: he moved away, he distanced himself. It is said: he moved away from you, he moves away, he moved away, and he is far away from you, meaning: he distanced himself. The interpretation of the verse is that a long life will not remove him from the punishment of God, nor will it spare him from it, because life must come to an end and will return to God, as Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, as I narrate on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, or on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live long
, meaning: it will not spare him from the punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told me, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: h
And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live long
, meaning: Even if he lives long, that will not relieve him from the punishment nor save him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
One of them would like to live a thousand years
, but that would not remove him from the punishment. They are the ones who visited Gabriel, peace be upon him.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
One of them would like to live a thousand years

, but that would not save him from the punishment. The Jews are more eager for life than these people. These people would like to live a thousand years, but that would not save him from the punishment. If he lived as long as Iblis lived, that would not benefit him, since he was a disbeliever, and that would not save him from the punishment.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty:
h
And God is Seeing of what they do
What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His statement:
h
And God is Seeing of what they do

, is that God is the One who sees what they do. Nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him. Rather, He encompasses all of them, and He is the Preserver and Rememberer of them, until He makes them taste the punishment for them as recompense for them. The root of Basir is Mubsir from the saying: I saw, so I am Mubasir, but it was changed to Fa’il, just as Musma’ was changed to Sami’, “Adhab Mu’alim” to Aleem, “Mubdi’ Al-Samawat” to Badi’, and so on.

All scholars of interpretation agreed that this verse was revealed in response to the Jews of the Children of Israel, when they claimed that Gabriel was their enemy and that Michael was their friend. Then they differed about the reason for which they said that.

Some of them said: The reason for their saying that was because of a debate that took place between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the matter of his prophethood.

Those who said that were mentioned: Abu Kuraib narrated that Yunus ibn Bakir narrated from Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram from Shahr ibn Hawshab from Ibn Abbas that he said: “A group of Jews attended the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Abu al-Qasim, tell us about some characteristics that we ask you about, which only a prophet knows. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Ask whatever you wish, but give me the covenant of God and what Jacob took from his sons. If I tell you something and you understand it, you will follow me in Islam. They said: That is yours. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Ask me whatever you wish. They said: Tell us about four characteristics that we will ask you about. Tell us, what food did Israel forbid himself before the Torah was revealed? Tell us about the woman’s water and the man’s water?

How is the male and female from it? Tell us about this illiterate prophet in a dream and who is his guardian from the angels? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You have the covenant of God. If I tell you, you will follow me, so give him whatever he wants of a covenant and a pact. He said: I ask you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you know that Israel fell seriously ill and his illness lasted a long time, so he made a vow that if God cured him of his illness he would deprive himself of the food and drink he loved the most, and the food he loved the most was camel meat.

As I relate, and the drink he loved the most was camel milk? They said: By God, yes. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: I call God to witness over you and I ask you by God, there is no god but Him, who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you know that the man’s semen is thick and white, and the woman’s semen is yellow and thin, so whichever of them rises above will have the child and resemblance, by God’s permission? So if the man’s semen rises above the woman’s semen, the child will be a boy, by God’s permission, and if the woman’s semen rises above the man’s semen, the child will be a girl, by God’s permission? They said: By God, yes. He said: By God, I bear witness. He said: I ask you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you know that the eyes of this unlettered prophet sleep but his heart does not? They said: Yes, by God. He said: O God, bear witness.

They said: Now you are speaking to us from your guardian from among the angels. Then we will either follow you or leave you. He said: My guardian is Gabriel, and God never sent a prophet except that he was his guardian. They said: Then we will leave you. If your guardian were other than him from among the angels, we would follow you and believe you. He said: What prevents you from believing him? They said: He is our enemy. Then God the Almighty revealed: “
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel
- indeed, it has brought the Qur’an down to your heart by God’s permission” until His saying:
h
As if they did not know
. Then they incurred wrath upon wrath.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me,
m: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Husayn, meaning al-Makki, narrated to me, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab al-Ash'ari: "A group of Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, tell us about four things that we ask you about, and if you do so, we will follow you and believe you and have faith in you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have the covenant and pledge of God upon you regarding that. If I tell you about that, will you believe me? They said: Yes. He said: Ask whatever you wish. They said: Tell us how the child resembles his mother, and the sperm is from the man? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I ask you by God and by His days among the Children of Israel, do you know that the sperm of the man is white and thick, and the sperm of the woman is yellow and thin, so whichever of them is higher than the other will resemble it? They said: Yes. They said: Then tell us how you sleep? He said: I ask you by God and by His days among the Children of Israel, do you know that the eyes of this unlettered Prophet sleep but he does not sleep. His heart? They said: Yes, by God. He said: O God, bear witness. They said: Tell us what food did Israel forbid himself before the Torah was revealed? He said: Do you know that the food and drink he loved most were camel milk and meat, and that he complained of a complaint and God cured him of it, so he forbade the food and drink he loved most out of gratitude to God, so he forbade himself camel meat and milk? They said: Yes, by God. They said: Tell us about the spirit. He said: I ask you by God and by His days with the Children of Israel, do you know that it is Gabriel, and he is the one who comes to me? They said: Yes, but he is an enemy, and he is an angel who only brings hardship and bloodshed, and were it not for that we would have followed you. God revealed about them: “Say:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel
- for he has brought the Qur’an down to your heart” until His saying:
h
As if they do not know

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza narrated to me:
m: “The Jews asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Who is the companion to whom the revelation comes down? He said: Gabriel. They said: He is our enemy, and he only comes with war, hardship, and fighting.” Then the verse was revealed: Who is an enemy to Gabriel? Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: The Jews said: O Muhammad, Gabriel only comes down with hardship and war. They said: He is our enemy. Then the verse was revealed: Who is an enemy to Gabriel?

x: Others said: Rather, the reason for their saying that was due to a debate that took place between Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and them, regarding the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Rib’i ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: ‘Umar came down to al-Rawha’ and saw men rushing towards stones to pray to them. He said: Who are these? They said: They claim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed here. He disliked that and said: What? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was overtaken by prayer in a valley, so he Surat Al-Baqarah 2:97 Say, "
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel
- it is he who has brought it down upon your heart by permission of Allah, confirming what was before it and as
h
guidance and good tidings for the believers

." prayed, then he departed and left him. Then he began to talk to them, saying: I used to witness the Jews during their school day and I was amazed at the Torah and how it confirmed the Criterion, and at the Criterion and how it confirmed the Torah. While I was with them one day, they said: O Ibn al-Khattab, none of your companions is more beloved to us than you. I said: Why is that? They said: You visit us and come to us. I said: I come to you and I am amazed at the Criterion and how it confirmed the Torah, and at the Torah and how it confirmed the Criterion.’ He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by and they said: O Ibn al-Khattab, that is your companion, so join him. He said: Then I said to them: I ask you by God, there is no god but Him, and by what He has entrusted to you of His right and what He has entrusted to you of His Book, do you know that he is the Messenger of God? He said: They were silent. He said: Their most knowledgeable and prominent person said: He has become too much for you, so answer him. They said: You are our most knowledgeable and our master, so answer him. He said: Since you have asked us about him, we know that he is the Messenger of God. He said: I said: Woe to you, if you perish? They said: We are not perished. He said: I said: How is that, when you know that he is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you do not follow him or believe him? They said: We have an enemy from the angels and peace from the angels, and our enemy from the angels has been paired with him. He said: I said: Who is your enemy? And who is your peace? They said: Our enemy is Gabriel, and we are peaceable with Michael. He said: I said: Why did you make an enemy of Gabriel? And why did you make peace with Michael? They said: Gabriel is the angel of harshness, severity, hardship, severity, torment, and the like, and Michael is the angel of compassion, mercy, alleviation, and the like. I said: What is their status with their Lord? They said: One of them is on His right and the other is on His left. I said: By God, besides Whom there is no god, they and the One between them are enemies to those who are enemies to them, and at peace to those who are at peace with them. It is not appropriate for Gabriel to be at peace with the enemy of Michael, nor for Michael to be at peace with the enemy of Gabriel. I then got up and followed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and I caught up with him as he was leaving a gathering place for the Banu so-and-so. He said to me: O Ibn al-Khattab, shall I not recite to you the verses that have been revealed? So he recited to me: “Say:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel

- for indeed, he has brought it down upon your heart, by God’s permission, confirming what was before it” until he recited the verses. I said: My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God, by the One Who sent you with the truth. I have come wanting to tell you the report, but I hear the Kind, the All-Knowing, has preceded me to you with the report.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said, Umar said:
m: I was a man who used to visit the Jews on the day of their school, then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Rubai. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us that one day Umar bin Al-Khattab went to the Jews, and when they saw him, they welcomed him. Umar said to them: By God, I have not come for your love or desire, but I have come to hear from you. So he asked them and they asked him, and they said: Who is the companion of your companion? He said to them: Gabriel. They said: That is our enemy from the people of heaven, he reveals our secret to Muhammad, and when he comes, he brings war and oppression, but the companion of our companion is Michael, and when he comes, he brings fertility and peace. Umar said to them: Do you recognize Gabriel and do not recognize Muhammad? Then Umar left them and went towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to tell him their story, and he found that this verse had been revealed to him: “Say:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel
- for he has brought the Qur’an down upon your heart by God’s permission.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It reached us that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab turned to the Jews one day, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel

, he said: The Jews said: Gabriel is our enemy, because he descends with hardship, war, and famine, and Michael descends with ease, health, and fertility, so Gabriel is our enemy. So God Almighty said:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Say, ‘
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel

- indeed, he has brought it down to your heart by God’s permission, confirming what was before it.’ He said: Umar bin Al-Khattab had land in the upper part of Medina, and he used to visit it. His passage was on the road to the schools of the Jews, and whenever he entered upon them, he heard them. And one day he entered upon them and they said: O Umar, there is no one among the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, more beloved to us than you. They pass by us and harm us, and you pass by us and do not harm us, and we have hope in you. So Umar said to them: Which oath among you is the greatest? They said: The Most Gracious Who sent down the Torah to Moses at Mount Sinai. So Umar said to them: I ask you by the Most Gracious Who sent down the Torah to Moses at Mount Sinai, do you find Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with you? They remained silent. He said: Speak, what is the matter with you? By God, I did not ask you while I was in doubt about anything in my religion. They looked at each other, and one of them stood up and said: Tell the man, either you tell him or I will tell him. They said: Yes, we find it written with us, but his companion from the angels who brings him the revelation is Gabriel, and Gabriel is our enemy, and he is the owner of every punishment, fighting, or sinking. If his guardian were Michael, then we would have believed in him, for Michael is the owner of every mercy and every rain. So Omar said to them: I ask you by the Most Merciful, who sent down the Torah to Moses on Mount Sinai, where is Gabriel’s place in relation to God? They said: Gabriel is on his right, and Michael is on his left. Omar said: Then I bear witness that the one who is an enemy to the one on his right is an enemy to the one on his left? And the one who is an enemy to the one on his left is an enemy to the one on his right, and whoever is an enemy to both of them is an enemy of God. Then Omar returned to inform the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he found that Gabriel had preceded him with the revelation, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and read it to him. Omar said: By Him who sent you with the truth, I have come to you and I only want to inform you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj Al-Razi told us, he said, Abdul-Rahman bin Mughra Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: Umar went to the Jews and said: I ask you by the One Who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you find Muhammad in your book? They said, Yes. He said: What prevents you from following him? They said, God did not send a messenger except that he had a guardian from the angels, and Gabriel is the one who takes care of Muhammad, and he is our enemy from the angels, and Michael is our peace, so if he was the one who came to him, we would follow him. He said: I ask you by the One Who sent down the Torah to Moses, what is their status with the Lord of the Worlds? They said, Gabriel is on his right, and Michael is on his other side. He said: I bear witness to what they say except by God’s permission, and it is not for Michael to be an enemy of Gabriel’s peace, and it is not for Gabriel to be at peace with the enemy of Michael. While he was with them, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by, and they said: This is your companion, O son of Al-Khattab. So he went to him and came to him and it was revealed to him:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel
- then indeed he has brought it down to your heart by permission of God, until His saying: For indeed, God is an enemy to the disbelievers.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Husayn bin Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layla,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel

, he said: The Jews said to the Muslims: If Michael was the one who descends upon you, we would have followed you, for he descends with mercy and rain, but Gabriel descends with torment and vengeance, and he is an enemy to us. He said: So this verse was revealed:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: something similar to that.

x: As for the interpretation of the verse, I mean His statement: “Say:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel

- for indeed, he has brought it down to your heart by permission of God,” it is that God says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to the Jewish community of the Children of Israel, who claimed that Gabriel is an enemy to them, because he is the bearer of tyranny, torment, and punishments, not the bearer of revelation, revelation, and mercy. So they refused to follow you, denied your prophethood, and rejected what you brought them of My signs and clear proofs of My judgment, because Gabriel is your guardian and the bearer of My revelation to you, and they claimed that he is an enemy to them: Whoever among the people is an enemy to Gabriel, and denies that he is the bearer of God’s revelation to His prophets, and the bearer of His mercy, then I am his guardian and friend, and I acknowledge that he is the bearer of revelation to His prophets and messengers, and that he is the one who brings down God’s revelation to my heart from my Lord, by permission of my Lord for that, and he binds it to my heart, and strengthens my heart, as:

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed narrated to us, he said, Bishr bin Ammarah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement: “Say: Who is an enemy to Gabriel?” He said: That is because the Jews said when they asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, about many things and he informed them as they had them: Except Gabriel. For Gabriel was, according to the Jews, a bearer of torment and force, and they did not have a bearer of revelation, meaning: a revelation from God to His messengers nor a bearer of mercy. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them about what they asked him about: that Gabriel is the bearer of God’s revelation, the bearer of His vengeance, and the bearer of His mercy. They said: He is not a bearer of revelation nor mercy, he is an enemy to us. So God Almighty revealed, to refute them: Say, O Muhammad:
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel

, for he has brought it down upon your heart, meaning that Gabriel brought it down, saying: The Qur’an was brought down by the command of God, strengthening your heart and binding it to your heart, meaning: by Our revelation that Gabriel brought down to you from God. And that is what is done with the messengers. And the prophets before you.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: Say, ‘
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel
- for he has brought it down upon your heart by permission of God.’ He says: He brought down the Book upon your heart by permission of God. And he narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: For He revealed it to your heart, meaning: Gabriel revealed the Book to your heart.

x: Rather, God, the Most High, said: For He has sent it down upon your heart, meaning the heart of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He ordered Muhammad at the beginning of the verse to inform the Jews of that about himself, and He did not say: For He sent it down upon my heart. If it Surat Al-Baqarah 2:97 Say, "
h
Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel
- it is he who has brought it down upon your heart by permission of Allah, confirming what was before it and as
h
guidance and good tidings for the believers

." had been said: On my heart, it would have been correct to say, because it is the custom of the Arabs, when they order a man to narrate what was said to him about himself, to use the verb of the one commanded once as a metaphor for the one reporting about himself, since the one reporting about himself? And once as a metaphor for his name, like a metaphor for the name of the one being addressed, because he is being addressed by it.

So you say in a similar way: Tell the people that good is abundant with me, so the metaphor of the name of the one reporting about himself comes out, because he is being commanded to narrate that about himself. And tell the people that good is abundant with you, so the metaphor of his name comes out like a metaphor for the name of the one being addressed, because even though he was commanded to say that, he is being addressed and commanded to narrate what was said to him. Likewise, do not say to the people that I am standing and do not say to them that you are standing, and the ya of I comes out as the name of the one being commanded to say that, as we have described. This includes the words of God Almighty: Say to those who disbelieve, ‘You will be overcome.’
r
(Al Imran 3:12)

with the letters ya and ta. As for Gabriel, the Arabs have different pronunciations of it. As for the people of Hijaz, they say: Gabriel, and Michael without a hamza, with a kasra on the jim and the ra’ of Gabriel and with a light pronunciation.

And the reading in this way is generally the reading of the people of Medina and Basra. As for Tamim, Qais and some of Najd, they say: Gabriel and Michael, like Gabriel and Michael, with the opening of the jim and the ra, and a hamza, and the addition of a ya after the hamza. The majority of the people of Kufa read this way, as Jarir ibn Atiyya said: They worshipped the cross, lied about Muhammad, about Gabriel, and about Michael. It was mentioned about Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Abdullah bin Katheer that they used to recite: Gabriel with the opening of the jim and leaving out the hamza.
It is an invalid reading, because Fa’il does not exist in the speech of the Arabs.

Some of them chose this and claimed that it is a foreign name, just as it is said: Samwil, and he recited about that: So that if you weighed all of Lakhm, it would not weigh a single feather of Samwila’s. As for Banu Asad, they say: Jibreen with a noon. It has been reported that some Arabs add an alif to Gabriel and say: Jibraeel and Mikaeel.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Yaʿmar
m: that he used to read: Gabriel, with the opening of the jim, the hamza, leaving the elongation, and doubling the lam. As for Jabr and Mick, they are two names, one of which means: slave, and the other means: servants. As for El, he is God Almighty, as Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jaber bin Nuh Al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair said, Ibn Abbas said: Gabriel and Michael, like you say: Abdullah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Gabriel is Abdullah, and Michael is the servant of God. And every name of God is God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ismail bin Raja’, on the authority of Umair,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas: That Israel, Michael, Gabriel, and Israfil are like your saying: Abdullah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, who said:
m: El, God, in Hebrew.

c: Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Dahhak told us, he said, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Gabriel’s name is Abdullah, and Michael’s name is Ubaydullah. El: God.

c: Al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi told me, he said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Ali ibn Husayn, he said:
m: Gabriel’s name is Abdullah, Michael’s name is Ubaydullah, and Israfil’s name is Abd al-Rahman. And every temple of Il is Abdullah.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad al-Madani, Al-Muthanna said:
m: Qubaysah said: I think it was Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr bin Ata’, on the authority of Ali bin Hussein, who said: What do you consider Gabriel to be among your names? He said: Gabriel is Abdullah, and Michael is Ubaydullah. And every name that contains El is a place of worship for God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Ali ibn Husayn, he said:
m: He said to me: Do you know what your name is for Gabriel? I said: No. He said: Abdullah. He said: Do you know what your name is for Michael? I said: No. He said: Ubaydullah. Israel was given a name similar to that, but I forgot it, except that he said to me: You see, every name that goes back to El is a place of worship for him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: Gabriel said: Gabriel is a servant of God, and Mika said: A servant of God.

x: This is the interpretation of those who read Gabriel with the fat-ha, the hamza, and the extension. And it is, God willing, the meaning of those who read it with the kasra and left out the hamza. As for the interpretation of those who read it with a hamza, leaving the elongation, and emphasizing the lam, then he intended by his saying that thus, to add Jabr and Mika to the name of God by which He is called in the Arabic language, not in Syriac and Hebrew. This is because the word il in the Arabic language is God, as He said:
h
They observe not towards a believer any pact or covenant
(al-Tawbah 9:10).

A group of scholars said: The word il is God.
