And from this is the saying of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him to the delegation of Banu Hanifa, when he asked them about what Musaylimah was saying, so they told him and he said to them: Woe to you, where did he take you? By God, this speech did not come from il or barr. He means from il: from God.

c: And Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Sulayman Al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: regarding His saying:
h
They observe not towards a believer any pact or covenant

, he said: The saying of Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil. As if he is saying: When he adds Jabr, Mika, and Isra to El, he says: Abdullah. They do not observe in a believer except, as if he is saying they do not observe God Almighty.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Confirming what was before it.
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
Confirming what came before it
, the Qur’an. He placed confirming in the accusative case because of the separation from the ha’ in His statement:
h
He sent it down upon your heart
. The meaning of the words is: Gabriel revealed the Qur’an to your heart, O Muhammad, confirming what came before the Qur’an. Meaning by this:
h
confirming what came before it

of the books of God, which were revealed to His messengers who came before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And his confirmation of them is the agreement of their meanings with their meanings in the command to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought from God, and they confirm it, as Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed told us, he said, Bishr bin Amara told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
Confirming what came before it

, he says what came before it of the books that God revealed, and the verses, and the messengers whom God sent with the verses, such as Moses, Noah, Hud, Shuaib, Salih, and similar messengers, may God bless them.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Confirming what was before it, of the Torah and the Gospel.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And
h
guidance and good tidings for the believers

By His statement, may He be glorified, and guidance, He means evidence and proof. And God, may He be glorified, called it guidance because the believer is guided by it. And his being guided by it means that he takes it as a guide to follow, and a leader to obey its commands and prohibitions, its lawful and unlawful. And the guide of everything is what goes before it. And from that, the forelocks of horses are called: their guides, which is what goes before them. And likewise the neck is called: the guide, because it goes before the rest of the body. As for the good report, it is the glad tidings. God Almighty informed His believing servants that the Qur’an is good report from Him, because He informed them of what He has prepared for them of honor with Him in His Paradise, and what His reward they will attain in their afterlife. This is the good report that God gave to the believers in His Book.

Because good report of the speech of the Arabs is: informing a man of something he did not know about, which pleases him of the report, before he hears it from someone else, or learns it from someone else.
And it has been narrated in this regard from Qatada, a statement close in meaning to what we have said:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Guidance and good tidings for the believers

, because when a believer hears the Qur’an, he will memorize it and understand it, benefit from it and be reassured by it, and believe in the promise of God that He promised in it, and he will be certain of that.

evidence.text: Then Omar returned to inform the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he found that Gabriel had preceded him with the revelation, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and read it to him.
And the reading in this way is generally the reading of the people of Medina and Basra.
The majority of the people of Kufa read this way, as Jarir ibn Atiyya said: They worshipped the cross, lied about Muhammad, about Gabriel, and about Michael.
And it is, God willing, the meaning of those who read it with the kasra and left out the hamza.

As for the interpretation of those who read it with a hamza, leaving the elongation, and emphasizing the lam, then he intended by his saying that thus, to add Jabr and Mika to the name of God by which He is called in the Arabic language, not in Syriac and Hebrew.

x: This is report from God, the Most High, about who is an enemy of God, who is an enemy of Him and an enemy of all His angels and messengers? And it is an announcement from Him that whoever is an enemy of Gabriel has been an enemy of him and an enemy of Michael, and an enemy of all His angels and messengers. Because those whom God has named in this verse are the friends of God and the people of His obedience, and whoever is an enemy of a friend of God has been an enemy of God and has fought against Him, and whoever is an enemy of God has been an enemy of all the people of His obedience and guardianship. Because the enemy of God is an enemy of His friends, and the enemy of the friends of God is an enemy of Him. So He said to the Jews who said: Gabriel is our enemy from the angels, and Michael is our friend from them: Whoever is an enemy of God and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael - then indeed, God is an enemy to the disbelievers, because the enemy of Gabriel is the enemy of every friend of God.

So He, the Most High, informed them that whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, is an enemy to all of His angels, messengers, and Michael whom He mentioned. Likewise, the enemy of some of God’s messengers is an enemy to God and to every friend of His. And: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yahya bin Wadheeh told us, he said, Ubaidullah, meaning Al-Ataki, told us, on the authority of a man from Quraysh who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked the Jews and said: I ask you by your book that you read, do you find in it that Jesus, son of Mary, gave glad tidings that a messenger named Ahmad would come to you? They said: O God, we found you in our book, but we hated you because you consider money and bloodshed permissible.” So God revealed: Whoever is an enemy to God and His angels 1:17.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Husayn ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who said: A Jew met ʿUmar and said to him: Gabriel, whom your companion mentions, He is our enemy. Omar said to him: Whoever is an enemy of God, His angels, His messengers, Gabriel and Michael, then God is an enemy to the disbelievers. He said: So it was revealed on the tongue of Omar. This report ofdicates that God revealed this verse as a rebuke to the Jews for their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and as an announcement to them that whoever is an enemy of Muhammad, God is his enemy, and that the enemy of Muhammad from among all people is among those who disbelieve in God and deny His signs.

x: Are not Gabriel and Michael among the angels?
Yes.
What is the meaning of repeating their names, when they were mentioned in the verse among the names of the angels?

The meaning of mentioning them by their names is that when the Jews said: Gabriel is our enemy and Michael is our friend, and they claimed that they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because Gabriel was the companion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, God informed them that whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, then God is an enemy to him, and that he is one of the disbelievers.

So He mentioned him by his name and Michael by his name, so that no one among them would say: God only said: Whoever is an enemy to God and His angels and His messengers, and we are not enemies to God and His angels and His messengers. Because angels is a general name that can be specific, and Gabriel and Michael are not included in it. Likewise His statement: and His messengers, so you, O Muhammad, are not included in them. So God Almighty mentioned the names of those whom they claimed were His enemies specifically, to cut off their deception of the weak among them, and to resolve their camouflage of their affairs for the hypocrites. As for the mention of the name of God in His statement: Indeed, God is an enemy to the disbelievers, and its repetition in it, while the beginning of the report began with mentioning Him, saying: Whoever is an enemy to God and His angels, so that it would not be confused if it was mentioned as a metaphor, and it was said: then he is an enemy to the disbelievers, to the listener, who is meant by the ha’ in then is it God, or the messengers of God, may His praise be exalted, or Gabriel, or Michael?
Because if it came as a metaphor for what I described, then the meaning of that would be confused for the one who did not stop at the meaning of that, because the speech could be what I described.

i: Some of the Arabists directed that to something like the saying of the poet:
x: If only the crow would always caw tomorrow, the crow would have severed the jugular veins And that it is the manifestation of the name that was meant by the metaphor.

The matter in that is different from what he said. That is because if the second raven was meant by the metaphor, it would not have been confused for anyone who understands the speech of the Arabs that it is a metaphor for the name of the first raven, since there was nothing before it that the speech could be directed to except the metaphor of the name of the first raven. And before his saying:
h
Then God is an enemy to the disbelievers are names

. If the name of God, may He be exalted, came as a metaphor, it would not have been known who was intended by the metaphor of the name, except by the evidence of a proof. Therefore, their two matters differed.
What God, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
And We have sent down to you verses is that We have sent down to you

, O Muhammad, clear signs indicating your prophethood. And those verses are what the Book of God, which He sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, contained of the hidden knowledge of the Jews and the hidden secrets of their report and the report of their forefathers from the Children of Israel, and the report of what their books contained that no one knew except their rabbis and scholars and what their first and last ones distorted and changed of their rulings that were in the Torah. So God revealed them in His Book that He sent down to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So in that of His command were clear verses for he who is fair to himself and is not led to his destruction by envy and transgression. Since it is in the nature of every person with a sound nature to believe in someone who brings the clear signs that have been described as what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought, without learning it from a human being, nor taking anything of it from a human being.
And similar to what we have said about that, the report was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman bin Saeed told us, he said, Bishr bin Amara told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs. He said: So you recite it to them, and inform them of it morning and evening and in between, and you are illiterate in their view, having not read a book, and you inform them of what is in their hands in its entirety. God says: In that is a lesson and a statement for them, and against them is an argument if they only knew.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us,
m: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, the client of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Ibn Suriya al-Futuni said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, you have not brought us anything that we recognize, and God has not sent down to you a clear sign that we can follow you with. So God Almighty sent down: ‘And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs, and none disbelieve in them except the wicked.’”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, he said,
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, told me, he said, Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Ibn Suriya said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And
h
none disbelieve in it except the wicked
What He, the Most High, means by His statement,
h
None disbelieve in it except the wicked

, is that none rejects it. We have already demonstrated in the past part of this book that the meaning of disbelief is denial, so there is no need to repeat it here. We have also explained the meaning of wickedness, which is to depart from one thing to another. The interpretation of the verse: And We have sent down to you, in what We have revealed to you of the Book, clear signs that make clear to the scholars and rabbis of the Children of Israel who deny your prophethood and reject your message that you are a messenger to them and a prophet sent. And none of them denies those signs, which indicate your truthfulness and prophethood, which I have sent down to you in My Book and denies them, except he among them who has abandoned his religion, who has abandoned My obligations in the Book which he believes in.

As for he among them who adheres to his religion and follows the rulings of His Book, then he believes in what I have sent down to you of My signs. And they are those who believed in God and believed in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the Jews of the Children of Israel.

evidence.text: He said: So you recite it to them, and inform them of it morning and evening and in between, and you are illiterate in their view, having not read a book, and you inform them of what is in their hands in its entirety.

x: The Arab scholars differed regarding the ruling on the waw in his statement:
h
Or whenever they make a covenant

Some of the Basran grammarians said: It is a waw that is used with interrogative letters, and it is like the fa' in his statement: So is it that every time there came to you a messenger with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant? (al-Baqarah 2:87). He said: They are both redundant in this sense, and it is like the fa' in his statement: By God, you will do such and such, and like your saying to a man: Will you not stand up? If you wish, you can make the fa' and the waw here a conjunction. Some Kufi grammarians said: It is a conjunction with a question mark added to it. The correct opinion in this regard, in my opinion, is that it is a conjunction waw, to which the interrogative alif was inserted, as if God Almighty said: “And when We took your covenant and raised the mount above you, [saying], ‘Take what We have given you with strength and listen.’ They said, ‘We hear and disobey.’

And whenever they made a covenant, a party of them threw it away.” Then He inserted the interrogative alif on and every time, and said: They said, ‘We hear and disobey.’ Or, whenever they made a covenant, a party of them threw it away. We have previously explained that it is not permissible for there to be a letter in the Book of God that has no meaning, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat the explanation of the corruption of the statement of the one who claimed that the waw and fa’ in His saying: or whenever and afkalma are redundant and have no meaning. As for the covenant, it is the pledge that the Children of Israel gave to their Lord to act according to what is in the Torah time after time, then some of them broke it time after time. So He, the Most High, rebuked them for what they did in that, and He reproached their children for it, because they followed their path in some of what He, the Most High, had taken from them to believe in from the command of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the covenant and pledge, so they disbelieved and denied what is in the Torah of His description and attributes.

So God, the Most High, said: Did every time the Jews from the Children of Israel made a covenant with their Lord and strengthened it with a covenant, a party of them threw it away, abandoned it and broke it? Like: Abu Kurayb told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Ibn Ishaq told us, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd bin Thabit, told me, Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Malik bin Al-Saif said when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, and he mentioned the covenant that he took from them, and what God enjoined upon them concerning him: By God, He did not enjoin upon us concerning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He did not take a covenant from us for him. So God, may His praise be exalted, revealed: Or is it that every time they make a covenant, a party of them casts it aside? In fact, most of them do not believe.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, he said,
m: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of the family of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, the client of Ibn Abbas, or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same.

x: As for nabdh, its origin in the speech of the Arabs is throwing, and therefore the found thing is called manboth, because it is thrown away and discarded. And from this wine is called nabidh, because it is raisins or dates that are thrown into a container, then treated with water. Its origin is maf’ul, changed to fa’il, I mean that wine is originally manboth, then changed to fa’il, so it was said nabidh, just as it was said: a dyed hand, and a greased beard, meaning: dyed and greased. It is said from this: I rejected it, I rejected it nabadh, just as Abu al-Aswad al-Du’ali said: I looked at his address, then discarded it as you would discard a worn-out sandal from yours.
The meaning of His Most High’s saying: A group of them cast it aside, is that a group of them rejected it, abandoned it, rejected it, and refuted it, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A group of them rejected it meaning: A group of them broke it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: A party of them cast it aside, he said: There was no covenant on earth that they would make a covenant but that they broke it, and they make a covenant today and break it tomorrow. He said: And in Abdullah’s reading: A party of them broke it. The letter ha’ in his saying: nadhahu is from the mention of the covenant. So its meaning is: Every time they made a covenant, a group of them abandoned that covenant. The team: the group, it has no singular form, like the army and the group, which have no singular form. The ha and the mim in his saying: A group of them are from the mention of the Jews from the Children of Israel. As for His saying:
h
But most of them do not believe

, He, the Most High, means: Rather, most of these people, whenever they make a covenant with God and firmly confirm it, a group of them breaks it and do not believe. There are two interpretations for this: One of them is that the statement indicates an increase and multiplication in the number of those who deny and break God’s covenant, over the number of the group. Then the statement would mean: Did every time the Jews from the Children of Israel made a covenant with their Lord, a group of them broke that covenant? Not that a group of them broke that, but the one who broke that and disbelieved in God, most of them, not a few of them. This is one of its interpretations. The other aspect: That its meaning is: Did every time the Jews made a covenant with their Lord, a group of them rejected that covenant? Not that a group of them rejected that covenant and broke it, based on their belief that this is not permissible for them,
h
but most of them do not believe
in God and His messengers, nor in His promise and threat. We have previously demonstrated in this book of ours the meaning of faith, and that it is belief.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying:
h
And when there came to them
, the rabbis and scholars of the Jews from the Children of Israel, a Messenger, meaning by Messenger: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when a messenger came to them

, he said: When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them. As for his saying: Confirming what is with them, he means by it that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, confirms the Torah and the Torah confirms him, in that he is a prophet of God sent to His creation. As for the interpretation of His statement:
h
And when there came to them a Messenger from God

, confirming what was with them, it refers to what was with the Jews, which is the Torah. So God, the Most High, informed us that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to the Jews from God confirming what was in their hands of the Torah, that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a Prophet of God, a group threw themselves aside, meaning by that: they denied and rejected him after they had acknowledged him, out of envy and malice towards him. And His statement: of those who were given the Scripture, is the scholars of the Jews to whom God gave knowledge of the Torah and what was in it. And by His statement: the Book of God, He means the Torah. His saying: behind their backs, means they put it behind their backs. This is a proverb, it is said to every person who rejects something that was on his mind: So-and-so has put this matter behind him, and put it behind his back, meaning by it: he turned away from it, turned away, and departed, like:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And when there came to them a Messenger from God

, confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of God behind their backs. He said: When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them, they opposed him with the Torah and argued with him about it, so the Torah and the Qur’an agreed, so they threw away the Torah and took the Book of Asif and the magic of Harut and Marut. This is what God says: As if they did not know. The meaning of His statement: As if they do not know, is as if these Jewish scholars who rejected the Book of God and broke the covenant of God by not acting upon what they had pledged to God to act upon did not know what was in the Torah of the command to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believe in him. This is from God, may He be glorified, informing us about them that they denied the truth with their knowledge and awareness of it, and that they were stubborn about God’s command and disobeyed it with their knowledge that it was obligatory upon them, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
A party of those who were given the Scripture threw away

, meaning: A party of those who were given the Scripture the Book of God behind their backs, as if they did not know: meaning that the people knew, but they corrupted their knowledge, denied, disbelieved, and concealed it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon

It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and that which was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. But these two angels did not teach anyone until they had said, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’ And they learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they could not harm thereby anyone except by permission of God. And they learned that which harmed them and did not benefit them. And they certainly knew that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter. And evil was that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew.” What is meant by His statement:
h
And they followed what the devils recited is the group of Jewish rabbis and scholars whom God
, the Most High, described as having thrown His Book that He revealed to Moses behind their backs, ignoring it and disbelieving in what they knew, as if they did not know.

c: So He informed us
m: about them that they rejected His Book that they knew was revealed from Him to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they broke His covenant that He took from them to act according to what was in it, and they preferred the magic that the devils recited during the reign of Solomon, son of David, so they followed it, and that is the loss and clear misguidance.

x: The people of interpretation differed about those meant by His statement:
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon

Some of them said: God meant by that the Jews who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they disputed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Torah, and they found that the Torah was in agreement with the Qur’an, commanding them to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to believe in him in the same way that the Qur’an commands, so they disputed on the basis of the books that the people had written down from the priests during the time of Solomon.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa bin Harun told me: Amr told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon

during the time of Solomon. He said: The devils would ascend to the heavens and sit in places to listen, listening to the words of the angels regarding what would happen on earth of death, rain, or any matter. They would go to the priests and inform them, and the priests would tell the people and they would find it as they said. Then, when the priests felt secure from them, they would lie to them and add something else to it, adding seventy words to each word. So the people wrote down that hadith in books, and it spread among the Children of Israel that the jinn know the unseen. So Solomon sent to the people, and he collected those books and put them in a chest, then buried them under his throne, and none of the devils could come near the throne without being burned. He said: I will not hear anyone mention that the devils know the unseen without my beheading him. When Solomon died, and the scholars who knew about Solomon left, and after that there were successors, Satan appeared in the form of a human being, then he came to a group of the Children of Israel, and said: Shall I guide you to a treasure that you will never eat? They said: Yes. He said: Dig under the throne, and he went with them and showed them the place. He stood aside, and they said to him: Come closer. He said: No, but I am here in your hands, and if you do not find it, kill me. So they dug and found those books, and when they took them out, Satan said: Solomon only controlled humans, devils, and birds with this magic. Then he flew away and left. It was spread among the people that Solomon was a magician, and the Children of Israel took those books. When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them, they argued with him about them, and that is when he says: It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic. Narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding His statement:
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon

, they said: The Jews asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a time about matters from the Torah, and they would not ask him about anything except that God would reveal to him what they had asked him about, so he would argue with them. When they saw that, they said: He knows better than we do what has been revealed to us. And they asked him about magic and argued with him about it, so God, the Almighty, revealed:
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic.

And the devils took a book and wrote in it magic and divination and whatever God willed of that, and buried it under the council of Solomon, and Solomon did not know the unseen. So when Solomon departed this world, they extracted that magic and deceived the people with it and said: This is knowledge that Solomon concealed and envied the people for it. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them of this hadith. So they returned from him, saddened and God had refuted their argument.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon

, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them confirming what was with them, a group of those who were given the Scripture rejected the verse. He said: They followed magic, and they are the People of the Scripture. So he recited until he reached: But the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic.

x: Others said: Rather, God meant by that the Jews who were during the time of Solomon.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said:
m: The devils recited magic to the Jews during the reign of Solomon, so the Jews followed it during his reign, meaning they followed magic during the reign of Solomon.

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq told me:
m: When the devils learned of the death of Solomon, son of David, peace be upon him, they wrote down the types of magic: Whoever wants to achieve such and such, let him do such and such. When they had created the types of magic, they put it in a book, then sealed it with a seal engraved with the seal of Solomon, and wrote at its head: This is what Asaf bin Barkhiya the Truthful wrote to King Solomon, son of David, from the treasures of knowledge. Then they buried it under his throne, and the remnants of the Children of Israel extracted it later when they innovated what they innovated. When they found it, they said: Solomon, Surat al-Baqarah 2:102
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon
. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but it was the devils who disbelieved, teaching people magic
h
and what was revealed to the two angels at Babylon

, Harut and Marut. And they did not teach anyone until they had said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." And they learned from them that by which they caused separation between a man and his wife, but they could not harm anyone thereby. No one except by permission of Allah. And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them. And they certainly know that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter. And wretched is that for which they have sold themselves, if they only knew. son of David, was nothing but this. So they spread magic among the people and learned it and taught it, and there was no one more skilled than the Jews. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned Solomon, son of David, among those whom God revealed to him, and promised him among those whom He had counted among the messengers, the Jews of Medina said: “Are you not amazed that Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) claims that Solomon, son of David, was a prophet, when by God he was nothing but a magician?” So God revealed concerning that their statement about Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “
h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon

. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved.” He said: When Solomon’s kingdom was gone, groups of jinn and humans apostatized and followed their desires. When God restored Solomon’s kingdom to him, the people continued on the religion as they were. Solomon took possession of their books and buried them under his throne. Solomon died shortly after that, and the jinn and humans took possession of the books after Solomon’s death and said: This is a book from God that was revealed to Solomon, which he hid from us. So they took it and made it a religion, so God revealed: And when there came to them a Messenger from God confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of God behind their backs as if they did not know and followed what the devils recited - which is musical instruments and games and everything that turns away from the remembrance of God. The correct interpretation of His statement:
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon is that this is a rebuke from God to the Jewish rabbis who met the

Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denied his prophethood even though they knew that he was a Messenger sent by God, and a rebuke from Him to them for refusing to reveal it and abandoning acting upon it while it was in their hands and they knew it and recognized that it was the Book of God, and for following, and following the example of their predecessors and ancestors, what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. We have already explained the reason for the permissibility of attributing the actions of their ancestors to them previously, so there is no need to repeat it here. We have chosen this interpretation because what was followed was what the devils recited during the time of Solomon and after him until God sent His Prophet with the truth, and the matter of magic continued among the Jews. There is no indication in the verse that God Almighty intended by His saying: And they followed some of them without others, since it was permissible and eloquent in the speech of the Arabs to add what we described of the following of the ancestors of those reported about in His saying:
h
And they followed what the devils recited to their successors after them

. And there was no transmitted trace of that specifically from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor any evidence indicating it, so what was required from the statement in that regard was to say: Every follower of what the devils recited during the time of Solomon from the Jews is included in the meaning of the verse, in the manner that we have stated.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: What the devils recite.

The Almighty means by His saying: What the devils recite: what they recite. So the interpretation of the statement is: And they followed what the devils recite. There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of his statement: recite.
Some of them said: What he means by his statement: recite is to speak, narrate, talk about, and inform, like a man reciting the Qur’an, which is his reading.
Those who said this interpretation based their interpretation on the fact that the devils are the ones who taught people magic and narrated it to them.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shabl told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon

, he said: The devils used to listen to the revelation, and whenever they heard a word they would add two hundred like it, so Solomon sent for what they had written of that and he collected it. When Solomon died, the devils found it and taught it to the people, and it was magic.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon of divination and magic
. And it was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that the devils had invented a book in which there was magic and a great matter, then they spread it among the people and taught it to them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ said:
m: His statement: And they followed what the devils recited, he said: We see it as what they narrated.

c: Salim bin Junada Al-Suwai’i told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The devils went out during the days in which Solomon was tested, and they wrote books in which there was magic and blasphemy, then they buried them under Solomon’s throne, then they took them out and read them to the people.

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying: What you recite is what you follow, narrate, and act upon.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Hasan bin Amr Al-Anqazi told us: My father told me, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Tatlawa means: Follow.

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Azdi told me: Yahya bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin,
m: the same.

x: The correct thing to say about this is that God, the Almighty, informed us about those about whom He informed us that they followed what the devils recited during the time of Solomon, by following what the devils recited. And the saying of the speaker: He recites such-and-such in the speech of the Arabs has two meanings: One of them is following, as you say: I recited so-and-so if you walk behind him and follow his traces, as God, the Most High, said: There every soul will be recompensed for what it put forth, meaning by that it follows. And the other is reading and studying, as you say: So-and-so recites the Qur’an, meaning that he reads it and studies it, as Hassan ibn Thabit said: A prophet who sees what people around him do not see, and recites the Book of God in every scene. God Almighty did not tell us what the meaning of the recitation was. The recitation of the devils who recited what they recited of magic during the time of Solomon was a report that cuts off the excuse.

It may be possible that the devils followed that by studying, narrating, and acting, so they followed it by acting, and studying it by narrating, so the Jews followed its method in that and acted upon it and narrated it.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: during the reign of Solomon.

He means by His statement, may His praise be exalted: During the reign of Solomon, during the reign of Solomon. This is because the Arabs put in in the place of on and on in the place of in. From this is the statement of God, may His praise be exalted: And I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. He means by this: on the trunks of palm trees. And as He said: I did such and such during the reign of such and such and during the reign of such and such have the same meaning. And based on what we have said of that, Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Ishaq said in its interpretation.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said:
m: On the kingdom of Solomon, he says: In the kingdom of Solomon.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq said
m: regarding his statement: during the reign of Solomon meaning during the reign of Solomon.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: What is this statement of His saying:
h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon

, and there is no good with us? It was said that someone attributed disbelief to Solomon, but rather he only mentioned following those of the Jews who followed what the devils recited. So what is the point of denying disbelief from Solomon after the report about following those whom the devils followed in practicing magic and narrating it from the Jews?

The point of that is that those to whom God, the Most High, attributed following what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon of magic and disbelief from the Jews, attributed what God, the Most High, attributed to the devils of that to Solomon, son of David, and they claimed that that was from his knowledge and narration, and that he only enslaved those whom he enslaved from mankind, jinn, devils, and all of God’s creation by magic. Thus, they made their practice of what God had forbidden them of magic good in the eyes of those who were ignorant of God’s commands and prohibitions, and in the eyes of those who had no knowledge of what God had revealed in the Torah regarding that, and they disavowed Solomon by attributing that to Solomon, although he was a prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from them a human being, and they denied that he was a messenger of God, and they said: Rather, he was a magician. So God acquitted Solomon, son of David, of magic and disbelief in the eyes of those among them who attributed magic and disbelief to him for reasons they claimed against him, some of which we have mentioned, and we will mention the rest of what we have attended to mention of them. And the most liars were the others who practiced magic, adorning their work to the ignorant people by saying that Solomon used to practice it. So God denied that Solomon, peace be upon him, was a magician or a disbeliever, and informed them that they only followed in their work of magic what the devils recited during the time of Solomon, not what Solomon had commanded them of obeying God and following what He commanded them in His Book that He revealed to Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Mentioning the evidence for the correctness of what we have said from the report and traces: Ibn Hamid narrated: Yaqub al-Qummi narrated on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr who said: Solomon used to track down the magic that was in the hands of the devils, and he would take it and bury it under his throne in his treasury. The devils were unable to reach it, so they approached the humans and said to them: Do you want the knowledge that Solomon used to subjugate the devils, winds, and other things? They said: Yes. They said: It is in his treasury and under his throne. The humans provoked him and extracted it and acted upon it. The people of Hijaz said: Solomon used to do this and this is magic. Then God, the Most High, revealed on the tongue of His Prophet Muhammad, Surat al-Baqarah 2:102
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon
It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but it was the devils who disbelieved, teaching people magic
h
and what was revealed to the two angels at Babylon

, Harut and Marut. And they did not teach anyone until they had said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." And they learned from them that by which they caused separation between a man and his wife, but they could not harm anyone thereby. No one except by permission of Allah. And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them. And they certainly know that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter. And wretched is that for which they have sold themselves, if they only knew. may God bless him and grant him peace, the innocence of Solomon, saying:
h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon
... [The verse], so God revealed the innocence of Solomon on the tongue of His Prophet, may God bless them both.
Abu Al-Sa'ib Al-Suwa'i narrated:

c: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: What happened to Solomon, son of David, was because of some people from the family of a woman called Jaradah, who was one of his most honorable wives. Solomon wanted the people of Jaradah to be right and he would judge in their favor, but he was punished because he did not like them at all. Solomon, son of David, whenever he wanted to go to the toilet or have intercourse with any of his wives, he would give the locust his ring. So when God wanted to test Solomon with what He tested him with, He gave the locust his ring one day. Then Satan came in the form of Solomon and said to it: Give me my ring. So he took it and put it on, and when he put it on, the devils, jinn, and humans obeyed him. Solomon came to it and said: Give me my ring. It said: You lie, you are not Solomon. Solomon realized that it was a test with which he was tested. He said: The devils went out and wrote books in those days that contained magic and blasphemy, then they buried them under the throne of Solomon. Then they took them out and read them to the people and said: Solomon used to overcome the people with these books. He said: So the people disavowed Solomon and disbelieved in him, until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God, may He be glorified and exalted, revealed:
h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon
, meaning what the devils wrote of magic and blasphemy. Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, so God, may He be glorified and exalted, revealed and excused him.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la al-San’ani told me: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us:
m: I heard Imran ibn Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, who said: Solomon took a covenant from every animal, and if a man was afflicted and asked about that covenant, he would be released. Then the people saw the rhyming prose and magic and said: This is what Solomon used to do. Then God, the Most High, said: And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic. Abu Hamid narrated: Jarir narrated on the authority of Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of Imran ibn al-Harith, who said: While we were with Ibn Abbas, a man came to him. Ibn Abbas said to him: Where have you come from? He said: From Iraq. He said: From which country? He said: From Kufa. He said: What is the report? He said: I left them saying that Ali is coming to them. He was startled and said: What are you saying? May your father be cursed. If we knew, we would not have married his women or divided his inheritance. As for me, I will tell you about that, that the devils used to eavesdrop from the sky, and one of them would come with a word of truth that he had heard. When he spoke the truth, he would lie with it seventy lies. He said: The hearts of the people would drink it up. So God informed Solomon of it, so he buried it under his throne. When Solomon, son of David, died, a devil stood on the road and said: Shall I not guide you to his forbidden treasure, the like of which is unparalleled? Under the throne. They took him out and said: This is magic. The nations copied it, and even the remnants of it are what the people of Iraq talk about. Then God revealed Solomon’s excuse: “
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon

. And it was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic.” Bishr bin Muadh narrated: Yazid narrated: Saeed narrated: Qatada said: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that the devils invented a book in which there was magic and a great matter, then they spread it among the people and taught it to them. When Solomon, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of that, he tracked down those books, brought them, and buried them under his throne, not wanting people to learn them. When God took His Prophet Solomon, the devils deliberately extracted them from the place where they were and taught them to the people. They informed them that this was knowledge that Solomon had concealed and kept to himself. So God excused His Prophet Solomon and cleared him of that, saying, It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: The devils wrote books containing magic and polytheism, then they buried those books under the throne of Solomon. When Solomon died, the people extracted those books and said: This is knowledge that Solomon concealed. Then God, the Almighty, the Majestic, said:
h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon
. And it was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, Al-Hussein told us, he said:
m: On the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon

. He said: The devils were listening to the revelation from the heaven, and whenever they heard a word they added something similar to it. And Solomon took what they had written of that and buried it under his throne, and when he died the devils found it and taught it to the people. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated:

c: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said:
m: When Solomon’s kingdom was taken away, the devils were writing down magic during Solomon’s absence. They wrote: Whoever wants to do such and such should face the sun and say such and such, and whoever wants to do such and such should turn his back to the sun and say such and such. So I wrote it down and made its title: This is what Asaf ibn Barkhiya wrote to King Solomon, son of David, from the treasures of knowledge. Then I buried it under his throne. When Solomon died, Satan stood up and gave a sermon and said: O people, Solomon was not a prophet, but a magician. Search for his magic in his belongings and houses. Then he showed them the place where he was buried, and they said: By God, Solomon was a magician. This is his magic. This is what we worshipped, and this is what we were subdued by. The believers said: Rather, he was a believing prophet. When God sent the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, he began to mention the prophets until he mentioned David and Solomon. The Jews said: Look at Muhammad, he mixes truth with falsehood, he mentions Solomon with the prophets, but he was only a magician who rode the wind. So God revealed Solomon’s excuse:
h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq told me:
m: Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic. This is because, as I have heard, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned Solomon, son of David, among the messengers, some of the Jewish rabbis said: Are you not amazed at Muhammad claiming that the son of David was a prophet? By God, he was nothing but a magician. So God revealed regarding that from their saying: Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, meaning by following magic and practicing it
h
and what was revealed to the two angels in Babylon
, Harut and Marut.

x: If the matter in that is as we have described and the interpretation of his saying:
h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon - and Solomon did not disbelieve

, but the devils disbelieved - what we have mentioned, then it becomes clear that there is something omitted in the speech that was omitted, and what was mentioned of it was sufficient, and that the meaning of the speech is: And they followed what the devils recited of magic during the reign of Solomon, so you attribute it to Solomon - and Solomon did not disbelieve, so he practices magic, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic. Qatada interpreted his statement: It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved, as we said.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved. He said: It was not based on his advice, nor was it based on his approval, but rather it was something that the devils did without him. We have previously demonstrated the difference of opinion among those who differ on the meaning of tatalawa, and the explanation of those who pointed to tatalawa meaning talat, since what preceded it was a past-tense report, which is his statement: And they followed, and the explanation of those who directed that to the opposite of that. We have explained in it and its counterpart the correct statement, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. As for the meaning of his statement: What you recite, it means what you recite, which is magic.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon
, meaning magic.

x: Perhaps someone might say: Or was magic only during the days of Solomon? It was said to him: Yes, it was before that, and God has informed us about the magicians of Pharaoh what He has informed us about them, and they were before Solomon, and He informed us about the people of Noah that they said to Noah that he was a magician. He said: So how did He inform us about the Jews that they followed what the devils recited during the time of Solomon? It was said: Because they attributed that to Solomon, as we have already explained, so God, the Most High, wanted to exonerate Solomon from what they attributed to him and what they had found either in his treasuries or under his throne, according to what the traces that we have mentioned have brought about that. So He limited the report to what the Jews followed in what the devils recited during the days of Solomon and not others for that reason, even though the devils had followed magic and disbelief before that.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And what was revealed to the two angels in Babylon
, Harut and Marut.
Scholars differed in the interpretation of what is in His statement: And what was revealed to the two angels.
Some of them said: Its meaning is denial, and it means did not.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And what was revealed to the two angels in Babylon
, Harut and Marut, he says: God did not reveal magic.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told me on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas:
m: And what was revealed to the two angels? He said: God did not reveal magic to them. The interpretation of the verse according to this meaning that we mentioned from Ibn Abbas and Al-Rabi’ from their interpretation of the meaning of his saying: And what was revealed to the two angels to: Surat al-Baqarah 2:102
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon
. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but it was the devils who disbelieved, teaching people magic
h
and what was revealed to the two angels at Babylon

, Harut and Marut. And they did not teach anyone until they had said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." And they learned from them that by which they caused separation between a man and his wife, but they could not harm anyone thereby. No one except by permission of Allah. And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them. And they certainly know that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter. And wretched is that for which they have sold themselves, if they only knew. And it was not revealed to the two angels,
h
and they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon

of magic, and Solomon did not disbelieve nor did God send down magic to the two angels, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic in Babylon, Harut and Marut, so then his saying: in Babylon, Harut and Marut is from the postponement which means the presentation.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How is this presented?
The way to present it is to say:
h
And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon

and what was revealed to the two angels, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic in Babylon, Harut and Marut. So what is meant by the two angels is Gabriel and Michael, because the Jewish magicians, as mentioned, claimed that God revealed magic through Gabriel and Michael to Solomon, son of David. So God denied them with that and informed His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Gabriel and Michael never revealed magic, and He acquitted Solomon of what they attributed to him of magic, so He informed them that magic is the work of the devils, and that they teach people in Babylon, and that those who teach them that are two men, one of whom is named Harut and the other is named Marut, so Harut and Marut, according to this interpretation, are a translation for the people and a refutation of them.
Others said: Rather, the interpretation of what is in His statement: And what was revealed to the two angels.
Those who said that mentioned: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Muammar said: Qatada and al-Zuhri said on the authority of Abdullah:
h
And what was revealed to the two angels in Babylon

, Harut and Marut, they were two angels from the angels, and they were sent down to judge between the people. That is because the angels mocked the judgments of the sons of Adam. He said: A woman brought them to judge, and they were afraid of her, then they went to ascend, but they were prevented from that and were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world. Muammar said: Qatada said: So they taught people magic, and they were made to take a covenant from them that they would not teach anyone until they said: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.

c: Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: As for his saying:
h
And what was revealed to the two angels in Babylon

, Harut and Marut, this is another magic that they also disputed with him about. He says: They disputed with him about what was revealed to the two angels, and the speech of the angels among themselves, if it is taught to mankind and he does and acts upon it, it is magic.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They teach people magic and that which was revealed to the two angels in Babylon
, Harut and Marut. Magic is of two types: magic taught by the devils, and magic taught by Harut and Marut.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And what was revealed to the two angels at Babylon
, Harut and Marut. He said: The separation between a man and his wife.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: But the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and what was revealed to the two angels. So he recited until he reached: So do not disbelieve. He said: The devils and the two angels teach people magic.

x: The meaning of the verse, according to the interpretation of this statement that we mentioned from the one we mentioned from him: The Jews followed what the devils followed in the kingdom of Solomon, which was revealed to the two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut. They are two angels from the angels of God. We will mention what was narrated from the report about them, God willing. They said: If someone were to say to us: Is it permissible for God to send down magic, or is it permissible for His angels to teach it to people? We would say to him: God, the Almighty, has sent down all good and evil. And He made all of that clear to His servants, so He revealed it to His messengers and commanded them to teach His creation and inform them of what is permissible for them and what is forbidden to them, such as adultery, theft, and all the other sins that He made known to them and forbade them from committing them.

c: Magic is one of those sins that He informed them
m: of and forbade them from committing. They said: There is no sin in knowing magic, just as there is no sin in knowing how to make wine, carve idols, tambourines, and playthings. Rather, the sin is in doing it and making it. They said: Likewise, there is no sin in knowing magic, but the sin is in acting upon it and harming someone who it is not permissible to harm. They said: There is no sin in God sending it down to the two angels, nor in the two angels teaching it to the people from among His scholars, if their teaching it to the people from among His scholars was with God’s permission for them to teach it after they inform him that it is a trial and forbid him from magic and practicing it and disbelief. Rather, the sin is upon the one who learns it from them and practices it, since God, the Most High, mentioned, forbade him from learning it and practicing it. They said: If God had permitted the children of Adam to learn that, there would have been no difficulty in learning it, just as they would not have been difficult to learn it, since their knowledge of it was from God’s revelation to them.
b.via: Magic is one of those sins that He

x: Others said: The meaning of what is the meaning of which, and it is in apposition to the first what, except that the first has the meaning of magic and the latter has the meaning of separating a man from his wife. The interpretation of the verse according to this statement is: And they followed the magic that the devils recited during the reign of Solomon, and the separation between a man and his wife that was revealed to the two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And what was revealed to the two angels in Babylon

, Harut and Marut, while they knew by what they separated between a man and his wife, and that is the saying of God, the Most High: And it was not Solomon who disbelieved, but the devils disbelieved. And he used to say: As for magic, only the devils teach it, and as for what the two angels teach, it is separation between a man and his wife, as God, the Most High, said.

x: Others said: It is possible for ma to mean who, and it is possible for ma to mean did not. Mention those who said that.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Al-Layth ibn Sa’d told me, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad,
m: and a man asked him about the statement of God: They teach people magic and that which was revealed to the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. The man said: Are they teaching people what was revealed to them, or are they teaching people what was not revealed to them? Al-Qasim said: I do not care which of the two it is.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Bishr bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of some of his companions,
m: that Al-Qasim bin Muhammad was asked about the statement of God Almighty: And what was revealed to the two angels. He was asked: Was it revealed or not? He said: I do not care which of the two it was, except that I believe in it. The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is the statement of the one who refers to what is in His statement:
h
And what was revealed to the two angels to mean what is less than the meaning of what is in the sense of denial

. I have chosen this because if what is directed to the sense of denial, it negates the two angels from having been revealed to them. The two names that come after them, I mean Harut and Marut, are not without being a substitute for them and a translation of them, or a substitute for the people in His statement: They teach people magic and a translation of them. If they are made a substitute for the two angels and a translation of them, then the meaning of His statement: And they do not teach anyone until they say, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve’ is invalidated. They learn from them that by which they separate a man from his wife, because if they do not know what separates a man from his wife, then what can someone learn from them who separates a man from his wife? And then, what is in His statement: And what was revealed to the two angels, if it is in the meaning of denial in apposition to His statement: And Solomon did not disbelieve, then God, the Most High, denied with His statement: And Solomon did not disbelieve, from Solomon that magic was from his work, or from his knowledge or teaching. If what was denied from the two angels of that is similar to what was denied from Solomon, and Harut and Marut are the two angels, then from whom did he learn what separates a man from his wife? And from whom is the report that he informed about with His statement: And they do not teach anyone until they say, We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve? The error of this statement is clear and obvious. And if His statement
h
Harut and Marut is a translation of from the people who are in His statement

: But the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic, then it is necessary that the devils are the ones who taught Harut and Marut magic, and the magicians only learned magic from Harut and Marut from the devils teaching them. If that is the case, then Harut and Marut will not be without one of two things in the opinion of the one who said this statement: Either they were two angels, and if they were two angels in his view, then he has made it obligatory for them to disbelieve in God and to disobey Him by attributing to them that they learn magic from the devils and teach it to people, and their insistence on that and their persistence in it is greater than what was mentioned about them that they committed the disobedience for which they deserved punishment, and in the report of God the Almighty about them that they do not teach anyone what they learn from them until they say: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve, which makes it unnecessary to elaborate on the error of this statement. Or they were two men from the children of Adam, and if that is the case, then it is necessary that with their destruction magic and knowledge of it and practice have been removed from the children of Adam, because if knowledge of that was taken from them and learned from them, then it is necessary that with their destruction and non-existence there is no way to reach the meaning that could not be reached except through them, and in the existence of magic in every time and place there is the clearest evidence of the corruption of this statement. The one who says this may claim that they are two men from the children of Adam, who have not been absent from the earth since it was created, and will not be absent since magic was found among people. He claims something whose length is not hidden. If these aspects that we have shown to be corrupt are corrupted, then it is clear that the meaning of what in Surat al-Baqarah 2:102
h
And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon
. It was not Solomon who disbelieved, but it was the devils who disbelieved, teaching people magic
h
and what was revealed to the two angels at Babylon

, Harut and Marut. And they did not teach anyone until they had said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." And they learned from them that by which they caused separation between a man and his wife, but they could not harm anyone thereby. No one except by permission of Allah. And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them. And they certainly know that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter. And wretched is that for which they have sold themselves, if they only knew. His statement: and what was revealed to the two angels is in the sense of who, and that Harut and Marut are translated by them from the two angels, and therefore the endings of their names were opened, because they are in the position of a genitive in response to the two angels, but since they were not in the accusative case, the endings of their names were opened. If a fool is confused by what we have said, and says: How is it permissible for the angels of God to teach people how to separate a man from his wife? Or how is it permissible for God, the Blessed and Exalted, to send that down to the angels? It will be said to him: God, the Most High, has informed His servants of all that He has commanded them to do and all that He has forbidden them from doing, then He commanded them and forbade them after they had learned from Him what they are commanded to do and forbidden from doing. If the matter were otherwise, then the command and prohibition would not have had an understood meaning, for magic is something that He has forbidden His servants from the children of Adam from, so it is not strange that the Most High taught it to the two angels whom He named in His revelation and made them a trial for His servants from the children of Adam, as He informed us about them, that they say to whoever learns that from them: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve, in order to test His servants whom He has forbidden from separating a man from his wife and from magic, so the believer is purified by his abandoning learning from them, and the disbeliever is disgraced by learning magic and disbelief from them, and the two angels are obedient to God in their teaching of those who know that, since they were taught by God’s permission to those who know that.

x: A group of God’s saints were worshipped instead of God, but that did not harm them, since it was not because they had commanded them to do so. Rather, some of them worshipped, but the one worshipped forbade them from doing so. Likewise, the two angels were not harmed by the magic of the magician who learned that from them after they forbade him from it and admonished him by saying: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve, since they had carried out what they were commanded to do by saying that.
Likewise: Muhammad bin Bashar told us:

c: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And what was revealed to the two angels in Babylon
, Harut and Marut, to his statement: So do not disbelieve, he took that upon them.

evidence.text: Some of them said: What he means by his statement: recite is to speak, narrate, talk about, and inform, like a man reciting the Qur’an, which is his reading.

Salim bin Junada Al-Suwai’i told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The devils went out during the days in which Solomon was tested, and they wrote books in which there was magic and blasphemy, then they buried them under Solomon’s throne, then they took them out and read them to the people.

And the other is reading and studying, as you say: So-and-so recites the Qur’an, meaning that he reads it and studies it, as Hassan ibn Thabit said: A prophet who sees what people around him do not see, and recites the Book of God in every scene.
God Almighty did not tell us what the meaning of the recitation was.
The recitation of the devils who recited what they recited of magic during the time of Solomon was a report that cuts off the excuse.
Then they took them out and read them to the people and said: Solomon used to overcome the people with these books.

x: He mentioned some of the report that describes the two angels, and whoever said that Harut and Marut are the two angels that God Almighty mentioned in His saying: in Babylon: Muhammad bin Bashar narrated: Muadh bin Hisham narrated:

c: My father narrated to me, on the authority of Qatada,
m: who narrated: Abu Shu’bah Al-Adawi narrated to us during the funeral of Yunus bin Jubayr Abu Ghulab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God opened the heavens for His angels to look at the deeds of the children of Adam. When they saw them committing sins, they said: O Lord, these are the children of Adam whom You created with Your hand, and to whom Your angels prostrated, and whom You taught the names of all things, committing sins. He said: If you were in their place, you would have done the same deeds as they did. They said: Glory be to You, it was not fitting for us. He said: So they were commanded to choose who would descend to the earth. He said: So they chose Aaron and Marut, and they descended to the earth, and everything in it was made lawful for them except that they should not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor drink alcohol, nor kill a soul which God has forbidden, except by right. He said: They did not continue until a woman who had been given half of her beauty appeared to them, and her name was Baidhakht. When they saw her, they wanted to commit adultery with her, but she said: No, unless you associate partners with God, drink wine, kill a soul, and prostrate to this idol. They said: We would never associate anything with God. One of them said to the other: Go back to her. She said: No, unless you drink wine. So they drank until they became drunk, and a beggar entered upon them, and they killed him. When they fell into evil, God opened the heavens for His angels, and they said: Glory be to You, I knew better. He said: Then God revealed to Solomon, son of David, to give them the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world. So they were chained from their heels to their necks with things like the necks of camels, and they were taken to Babylon.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, on the authority of Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas, that they said:
m: When the children of Adam increased in number and disobeyed, the angels, the earth, the heavens, and the mountains prayed against them: Our Lord, would You not destroy them? So God revealed to the angels: If I were to send down lust and Satan from your hearts and you were to descend, you would do so as well. He said: So they told themselves that if they were tested, they would hold fast. So God revealed to them to choose two angels from among the best of you. So they chose Harut and Marut, and they descended to the earth, and Venus was sent down to them in the form of a woman from the people of Persia, and the people of Persia called her Bidakht. He said: So they committed a sin, and the angels used to ask forgiveness for those who believed. Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented. When they committed the sin, they asked forgiveness for those on earth. Behold, God is the Forgiving, the Merciful. So he gave them the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they chose the punishment of this world.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Al-Hajjaj told me: Hammad told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Amr bin Saeed, who said:
m: I heard Ali say: Al-Zahra was a beautiful woman from Persia. She argued before the two angels, Harut and Marut, and they tried to seduce her, but she refused unless they taught her speech that if she spoke it, she would ascend to the heavens. So they taught her, and she spoke, and it ascended to the heavens and was transformed into a planet.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muammil ibn Ismail told us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us
m: all, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Ka’b, who said: The angels mentioned the deeds of the children of Adam and the sins they commit, so they were told: Choose two of you. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya said in his hadith: Choose two angels, so they chose Harut and Marut. So it was said to them: I send messengers to the children of Adam, and there is no messenger between me and you. Come down and do not associate anything with me, do not commit adultery, and do not drink wine. Ka’b said: By God, they did not spend the evening of the day on which they were sent down to earth until they had completed everything they were forbidden from. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya said in his hadith: They did not complete the day on which they were sent down until they did what God had forbidden them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Mu’alla ibn Asad told us: Abdul Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah: Salim told me that
m: he heard Abdullah narrating on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar that he had been told that the angels disapproved of the deeds of the children of Adam and the sins they commit on earth. So God said to them: If you were in their place, you would commit the sins they commit. So choose two angels from among you, and they chose Harut and Marut. So God said to them: I am sending My messengers to the people, and there is no messenger between Me and you. Descend to the earth, and do not associate anything with Me, and do not commit adultery. So Ka’b said: By the One in Whose Hand is Ka’b’s soul, they did not complete the day in which they descended until they committed what God had forbidden them.

c: Musa bin Harun told me: Amr told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: It was from the matter of Harut and Marut that they criticized the people of the earth for their judgments. It was said to them: I have given the son of Adam ten desires, and with them they disobey Me. Harut and Marut said: Our Lord, if You had given us those desires and then descended, we would have ruled with justice. So He said to them: Go down, for I have given you those ten desires, so judge between the people.
