So they descended to Babylon Danbawand, and they judged until evening came, and when morning came, they went down. They remained like that until a woman came to them who was disputing with her husband. They were amazed by her beauty. Her name in Arabic was Al-Zahra, in Nabataean it was Bidakht, and in Persian it was Anahid. One of them said to his companion: I like her. The other said: I wanted to tell you about her, but I felt shy before you. The other said: Would you like me to tell her about herself? He said: Yes, but how can we deal with the punishment of God? The other said: We hope for the mercy of God. So when she came to quarrel with her husband, they mentioned herself to her, and she said: No, not until you both judge in my favor against my husband. So they judged in her favor against her husband. Then she made an appointment with them to go to a ruined place, so they went to it for that purpose. When he wanted to have intercourse with her, she said: I will not do that until you tell me with what words you ascend to the heavens? And with what words you descend from it? So they told her, and she spoke and ascended. But God made her forget what she was descending with, so she remained where she was, and God made her a star, and whenever Abdullah ibn Umar saw her, he cursed her and said: This is the one who tempted Harut and Marut. So when night came, they wanted to ascend, but they could not, so they knew their destruction, so they were given the choice between the punishment of this world and the Hereafter, so they chose the punishment of this world over the punishment of the Hereafter. So they became attached to Bal and began to speak to the people with their speech, which was magic.

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me: Ishaq told us: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, who said:
m: When people after Adam fell into what they fell into of sins and disbelief in God, the angels in heaven said: O Lord of this world, I only created them to worship and obey You, but they committed disbelief, killing unlawfully, consuming unlawful wealth, stealing, committing adultery, and drinking alcohol. So they began to invoke curses upon themselves and did not excuse themselves. So it was said to them: They are in the unseen, but they did not excuse them. So it was said to them: Choose from among you two angels whom I will command with My command and forbid them from disobeying Me. So they chose Harut and Marut, and they were sent down to Earth, and He placed in them the desires of the children of Adam, and they were commanded to worship God and not associate anything with Him, and they were forbidden from killing unlawfully, consuming unlawful wealth, stealing, committing adultery, and drinking alcohol. So they remained on earth for a period of time, judging between people with justice. That was during the time of Idris. At that time there was a woman whose beauty among all people was like the beauty of Venus among all the stars. She came to them and they submitted to her in speech and wanted her for herself. She refused unless they followed her command and religion. They asked her about the religion she was following, so she brought out an idol for them and said: This is more worshipped. They said: We have no need to worship this. So they went and were patient as God willed. Then they came to her and submitted to her in speech and wanted her for herself. She said: No, unless you follow what I follow. They said: We have no need to worship this. When she saw that they refused to worship the idol, she said to them: Choose one of three options: Either you worship the idol, or kill a person, or drink wine. They said: None of these are appropriate, and the least of the three is drinking wine. So he gave them wine to drink, and when the wine had taken hold of them, they fell into it. A man passed by them while they were in that state, and they feared that he would disclose them, so they killed him. When their intoxication had gone away, they realized the sin they had committed and wanted to ascend to the heavens, but they could not. So, they were prevented from doing so, and the veil was removed between them and the people of the heavens. Then the angels looked at the sin they had committed and were amazed to the utmost, and they knew that whoever is in the dark is less stunned. So after that, they began to ask forgiveness for those on the earth. When they had committed the sin they had committed, it was said to them: Choose the punishment of this world or the punishment of the Hereafter. They said: As for the punishment of this world, it will be interrupted, but as for the punishment of the Hereafter, it will never be interrupted. So they chose the punishment of this world, and they were put in Babylon, where they are being punished. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Faraj bin Fadala narrated: Muawiyah bin Salih narrated: Nafi’ said: I traveled with Ibn Umar, and when it was the end of the night, he said: O Nafi’, look, the red star has risen. He said it two or three times. Then I said: It has risen. He said: No welcome and no hello. I said: Glory be to God, a star that is submissive, listening and obedient? He said: I only told you what I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: The Messenger of God, may God Surat Al-Baqarah 2:103 And if only they had believed and feared Allah, a reward from Allah would have been better,
h
if they only knew

. bless him and grant him peace, said to me: The angels said: O Lord, how patient are you with the children of Adam in their sins and wrongdoings? He said: I tested them and spared you. They said: If we were in their place, we would not disobey you. He said: Then choose two angels from among you. He said: They did not fail to choose, so they chose Harut and Marut.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: As for the matter of Harut and Marut, the angels were amazed at the injustice of the children of Adam, even though the messengers, books, and clear proofs had come to them. So their Lord said to them: Choose from among you two angels whom He has sent down to judge on earth between the children of Adam. So they chose Harut and Marut. Then He said to them when He sent them down: You are amazed at the children of Adam and their injustice and disobedience. The messengers and books only come to them from behind, behind, and there is no messenger between me and you. So do such and such. And he called upon such and such, and he commanded them to do something and forbade them. Then they descended upon that, and no one is more obedient to God than them. So they judged and were just. They judged during the day between the children of Adam, and when evening came, they ascended and were with the angels. And they descended in the morning and judged and were just. Until Venus descended upon them in the most beautiful form of a woman arguing, so they passed judgment against her. When she arose, each of them found it in himself, so one of them said to the other: Did you find what I found? He said: Yes. So they sent to her: Come to us and we will cancel it for you. When she returned, they said to her and decided for her: Come to us. So she came to them, and they uncovered their private parts for her. Their desire was in themselves, and they were not like the sons of Adam in their desire for women and their pleasure. When they reached that and found it permissible and were tempted, the flower flew and returned to where it was. When evening came, they ascended and were alone, and no permission was given to them, and their wings did not carry them. So they sought help from a man from the sons of Adam, and they came to him and said: Call upon your Lord for us. He said: How can the people of the earth intercede for the people of the heaven? They said: We heard your Lord mention you with good in the heaven. So He promised them a day and a tomorrow and He will supplicate for them. So he supplicated for them and his request was answered, and he was given the choice between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. Then one of them looked at the other and they said: We know that the types of punishment of God in the Hereafter are such and such in eternity and with the world seven times the same. So he ordered that they be brought down to Babylon, and there their punishment would be. He claimed that they were suspended in iron, folded up and flapping their wings.

x: It was narrated that some of the reciters used to recite: And what was revealed to the two angels, meaning two men from among the children of Adam. We have demonstrated the error of this recitation by way of evidence. As for the transmission, the consensus of the evidence on the error of this recitation by the Companions, the Followers, and the reciters of the regions is that this is sufficient as evidence of its error. As for his saying Babylon, it is the name of a village or a place on earth.
The people of interpretation differed about it.
Some of them said: It is Babylon, Danbawand.

c: Musa told me that.
m: He said: Amr told us. He said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi.

x: Some of them said: Rather, it is Babylon, Iraq.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Al-Zinad, on the authority of Hisham Ibn Urwa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha,
m: in a story she mentioned about a woman who came to Medina, and she mentioned that she had been in Iraq in Babylon, so Harut and Marut came with her and she learned magic from them. There is a difference of opinion about the meaning of magic.

x: Some of them said: It is tricks, deceptions and illusions that the magician does, until the bewitched person imagines that something is different from what it is, like someone who sees a mirage from afar, and imagines that it is water, and sees something from afar and believes it is different from what it really is. And like the passenger of a ship moving quickly, it seems to him that what he sees of trees and mountains is moving with him. They said: So is the bewitched person, that is his description, he thinks after what he has achieved from the magic of the magician that what he sees or does is different from what it really is.
Like the one who: Ahmad bin Al-Walid and Sufyan bin Wakee’ told me:

c: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha:
m: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was bewitched, he would imagine that he was doing something when he was not.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: A Jew from the Jews of Banu Zuraiq, called Labid ibn al-A’sam, bewitched the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, imagined that he was doing something when he was not.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said:
m: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab used to narrate: The Jews of Banu Zuraiq tied a magic knot for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they put it in the well of Hazm until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lost his sight, and God showed him what they had done. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for the well of Hazm where the knot was and pulled it out, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: The Jews of Banu Zuraiq have bewitched me. The author of this article denied that the magician could, by his magic, change something from its true nature, or make something of God’s creation subservient to something similar to what the rest of the children of Adam are able to do, or create any of the bodies other than the deceptions and illusions imagined for the eyes of the observers contrary to their true natures that we have described. They said: If it were within the power of the magicians to create bodies and change the true natures of objects from their true forms, there would be no separation between truth and falsehood, and it would be possible that all the perceptible things were among those that the magicians bewitched and changed their true natures. They said: And in the description of God, the Almighty and Majestic, of the magicians of Pharaoh in His saying: Then their ropes and their staffs appeared to him, because of their magic, to be crawling. And in the report of Aisha from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when he was bewitched, it seemed to him that he was doing something when he was not doing it, the clearest evidence of the length of the claim of the claimants: that the magician creates the true natures of things by his magic, and makes subservient what is impossible for other children of Adam to make subservient, such as the dead, the inanimate, and the animals, and the correctness of what we have said.

x: Others said: The magician may be able, through his magic, to turn a human into a donkey, or to enchant a human and a donkey and create objects and bodies.
They based this on the following:

c: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Ibn Abi Al-Zinad narrated to us: Hisham bin Urwah narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha,
m: the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she said: A woman from the people of Dumat Al-Jandal came to me seeking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after his recent death, asking him about something she had entered into regarding magic but had not practiced it. Aisha said to Urwah: O son of my sister, I saw her crying when she did not find the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to heal her. She was crying until I felt sorry for her, and she said: I fear that I have perished. I had a husband who left me. An old woman came to me and I complained to her about that, and she said: If you do what I command you, I will make him come to you. When night came, she brought me two black dogs, and I rode one of them and she rode the other. It was as if nothing had happened until we stopped in Babylon, and there were two men hanging by their legs. They said: What brought you? I said: Do you learn magic? They said: We are a trial, so do not disbelieve and go back. I refused and said: No. They said: Go to that oven and urinate in it. I went and was frightened but did not do it. I returned to them and they said: Did you do it? I said: Yes. They said: Did you see anything? I said: I did not see anything. They said: You did not do it. Go back to your country and do not disbelieve. I refused. They said: Go to that oven and urinate in it. I went and shuddered and became afraid. Then I returned to them and said: I have done it. They said: What did you see? I said: I did not see anything. They said: You lied, you did not do it. Go back to your country and do not disbelieve, for you are at the pinnacle of your affairs. I refused. They said: Go to that oven and urinate in it. I went to it and urinated in it. I saw a horseman wearing an iron mask who came out of me until he went into the sky and disappeared from me until I could not see him. I came to them and said: I have done it. They said: What did you see? I said: A masked knight came out from me and went into the sky until I could not see him. They said: You have spoken the truth. That is your faith that has come out of you. Go. I said to the woman: By God, I do not know anything, and they did not say anything to me. She said: Yes, you will not want anything but it will come true. Take this wheat and sow it, so I sowed. I said: Look up, so I looked up. I said: Plow it, so I plowed it. Then I said: Rub it, so I rubbed it. Then I said: Dry it, so it dried. Then I said: Grind it, so I ground it. Then I said: Bake it, so I baked. When I saw that I did not want anything but it came true, I was disappointed and regretted it, by God, O Mother of the Believers. By God, I have never done anything and I will never do it. The people of this article said what we have described and relied on what we have mentioned, and they said: If the magician had not been able to do what he claimed he was able to do, he would not have been able to separate a man from his wife. They said: And God Almighty has informed us about them that they learn from the two angels what they can use to separate a man from his wife. And if that were not true and was based on imagination and calculation, it would not be a true separation.

c: And God Almighty has informed us
m: about them that they separate in a true manner. And others said: Rather, magic is taking by the evil eye.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And they do not teach anyone until they say, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’

The interpretation of that is: And the two angels do not teach anyone of the people that it was revealed to them of separation between a man and his wife until they say to him: We are only a trial and a trial for the children of Adam, so do not disbelieve in your Lord.
Like: Musa told me, he said:

c: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: If a man came to them - meaning Harut and Marut - wanting to practice magic, they would admonish him and say to him: Do not disbelieve, we are only a trial. If he refused, they would say to him: Go to these ashes and urinate on them. So when he urinated on them, a light would come out of him that would shine until it entered the sky, and that is faith. And it was said that it was something black like smoke until it entered his ears and everything from it, and for that reason God became angry.

c: So if he informed them
m: of that, they would teach him magic. So that is the saying of God: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:103 And if only they had believed and feared Allah, a reward from Allah would have been better,
h
if they only knew
. And they do not teach anyone until they say, We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve 10:13.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us: Yazid told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada and Al-Hasan:
m: Until they say, We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve. He said: He made a covenant with them that they would not teach anyone until they said, We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us: Qatada said:
m: They were teaching people magic, so he took an oath from them that they would not teach anyone until they said: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said: Other than Qatada said:
m: He took a pledge from them that they would not inform anyone until they went to him and said: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: He took it from them that they should say that.

c: Al-Qasim told us: Al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: They took a covenant from them that they would not teach anyone until they said: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve. No one would dare to practice magic except a disbeliever. As for the trial in this context, its meaning is testing and trial, as the poet said. He tempted people in their religion and left Ibn Affan with a long history of evil. And from it is his saying: He tested the gold in the fire: if he tested it to know its quality from its badness, he tested it with a test and tests. Like: Bishr bin Muadh told us:

c: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: We are only a trial, meaning a calamity.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And they learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife.

His statement, may His praise be exalted: And they learn from them is a predicate of the two angels who learn from what was revealed to them, and it is not an answer to His statement: And they do not teach from anyone. Rather, it is a new predicate, and for this reason it was raised, so it was said: And they learn. The meaning of the statement is: They do not teach anyone until they say: We are only a trial. So they refuse to accept that from them and learn from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. It has been said: His saying: And they learn is report about the Jews, connected to his saying: “But the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and what was revealed to the two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut, and they learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife.” They made that from the deferred, which means bringing forward.

What we have said is more like an interpretation of the verse because attaching that to what follows it from the speech is what has a correct interpretation and is more appropriate than attaching it to what has been prevented from it from an interjection of the speech. The ha, mim, and alif in His statement: from them are from the mention of the two angels. The meaning of that is: So people learn from the two angels by which they separate between a man and his wife. And what is with yafreqoon means who. It was said that the meaning of that is: the magic by which they separate, and it was said: it is a meaning other than magic. We have already mentioned their differences in that before. As for man, it means a man from the names of the sons of Adam, and the female of it is woman, it is singular and dual, and the three of them are not pluralized in its form. It is said from it: this is a righteous man, and these two are righteous men, and it is not said: these are men of truth, but it is said: these are men of truth, and people of truth.

Likewise, woman is singular and dual, but it is not pluralized in its form. It is said: this is a woman and these two are women, and it is not said: these are women, but these are women. As for the husband, the people of Hijaz say to a man’s wife: she is his wife, just like the male husband. This includes the statement of God Almighty: Keep your wife to yourself.

i: Tamim and many of Qais and the people of Najd say: she is his wife, as the poet said:
x: And the one who walks, provoking my wife, Kmash, to the lion of the market, will take her If someone says: How does a magician separate a man from his wife?

It is said: We have previously demonstrated that the meaning of magic is to make something appear to a man to be different from what it is in reality and in its true form, sufficiently for those who are guided to understand it. If that is correct, based on what we have cited as evidence, then his separation between a man and his wife is his making each of them appear, through his magic, to be different from what he is in reality of beauty and handsomeness, until he finds him ugly and turns away and ignores him, until the husband causes separation between his wife. Thus, the magician separates them by causing the cause that caused the separation between them. We have demonstrated in more than one place in this book that the Arabs attribute a thing to its cause in order to cause it, even if he did not directly do what was caused by the cause, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
So too is the magician’s separation between a man and his wife through his magic. A number of the people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said about that.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us: Yazid bin Zari’ told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They learn from them what will separate a man from his wife, and separating them means that each one of them will be taken away from the other, and each one of them will be hated by the other. As for those who refused that the two angels teach people how to separate a man from his wife, they directed the interpretation of His statement: They learn from them to They learn instead of what they taught them what they can use to separate a man from his wife, like the saying of the speaker: If only we had such and such instead of such and such, meaning such and such. As the poet said: I collected the good things, medicine, a box and a purse for the descendants of the oppressed And from all the morals of the noble is gossip And in pursuit of the next door neighbor with the son He means by his saying: I have gathered from the good things, instead of the good things of this world, these bad morals and vile actions. And from it is the saying of another: Your qualities are too hard to soften, and you inherited disobedience from your noble ancestors. It means that you inherited the place of your noble ancestors as disobedience from your parents.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And they do not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God

He means by His Most High’s saying: And they can not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God. And those who learned from the two angels, Harut and Marut, that by which they separate between a man and his wife, can not harm anyone by what they learned from them of the meaning by which they separate between a man and his wife, except for one for whom God has decreed that it will harm him. As for the one from whom God has warded off its harm and protected him from the evil of magic, blowing, and incantations, then it will not harm him nor will it cause him harm. There are several meanings of permission in the speech of the Arabs: one of them is the command without the meaning of obligation, and it is not permissible for it to be from his saying: And they will not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God, because God, the Most High, has forbidden the separation between a man and his wife without magic, so how about it in the form of magic on the tongue of the nation.
Another of them is the release between the one who is given permission and the one who is released between him and him.

i: Another of them is knowledge of something, from it it is said: I have given permission for this matter, if I know about it, I gave permission for it with permission, and from it is the saying of Al-Hutay’ah:
x: Oh Hind, if you renew your connection, then inform me of the end.

Meaning, then inform me. And from this is the saying of the Most High: Then they were warned of a war from God. This is the meaning of the verse, as if the Most High said: And they will not harm anyone with what they learned from the two angels except with the knowledge of God. He means with what God had previously known would harm him.
Like: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me:

c: Suwaid bin Nasr told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they do not harm anyone thereby except by permission of God
, he said: By the decree of God.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And they learn what harms them and does not benefit them.

By this, He, the Most High, means: And they learn, that is, the people who learn from the two angels, what was revealed to them of the meaning by which they separate a man from his wife, they learn from them magic that harms them in their religion and does not benefit them in their afterlife. As for the immediate life in this world, they used to earn a living by it and obtain a livelihood from it.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And they certainly know that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter
Meaning by His Most High’s saying:
h
And they have certainly known that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter

. The group who, when there came to them a Messenger from God, confirming what was with them, threw the Book of God behind their backs as if they did not know, and followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. So He, Most High, said: Those of the Jews of the Children of Israel who threw My Book behind their backs, ignoring it, have abandoned working according to what is in it, from following you, O Muhammad, and following what you have brought, after I sent down to you My Book confirming what was with them, and after you sent to them acknowledging what was with them and what was in their hands, preferring over it following the magic that the devils recited during the time of Solomon, and which was sent down to the two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut.
Whoever buys magic in exchange for My Book that I sent down to My Messenger and prefers it over it, will have no share in the Hereafter.
Like: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said:

c: Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they knew that whoever bought it would have no share in the Hereafter. He said: The People of the Book knew that in God’s covenant with them, that the magician would have no share with God on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And they knew that whoever bought it would have no share in the Hereafter, meaning the Jews. He said: The Jews knew that whoever learned it or chose it would have no share in the Hereafter.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And they have certainly known that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter
for whoever buys that by which a man separates from his wife. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:103 And if only they had believed and feared Allah, a reward from Allah would have been better,
h
if they only knew

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: And they knew that whoever bought it would have no share in the Hereafter. He said: The Jews knew that in the Book of God in the Torah it says that whoever bought magic and abandoned the religion of God would have no share in the Hereafter, so the Fire would be his abode and refuge. As for his saying:
h
For whoever bought it
, then min is in the nominative case, and his saying:
h
And they knew is not an agent in it
, because his saying:
h
They knew means an oath
, so it was in the nominative case, because the speech means: By God, whoever bought magic,
h
he will have no share in the Hereafter
. And because his saying:
h
They knew means an oath
, it was confirmed with the lam of the oath, so it was said:
h
For whoever bought it

, just as it is said: I swear to whoever stood is better than whoever sat, and just as it is said: I knew that Amr is better than your father. As for min, it is a particle of recompense. It was said bought it and not buy it, because the lam of the oath entered into min. And it is the custom of the Arabs, when they introduce the lam of the oath into the particle of recompense, that they do not pronounce the verb with it except with a verb without yaf’ul except rarely, out of dislike that they introduce something new into the recompense and it is in the jussive mood, as God Almighty said: If they are expelled, they will not be expelled with them. And it is permissible to show his verb after it as yaf’ul in the jussive mood, as the poet said: Even if your houses are too narrow for you, my Lord knows that my house is spacious.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his statement:
h
He will have no share in the Hereafter
Some of them said: The share in this place means the portion.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He has no share in the Hereafter, he says: no portion.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He has no share in the Hereafter.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told me, he said: Waki’ told us, Sufyan said:
m: We heard in: And he has no share in the Hereafter that he has no share in the Hereafter.

x: Some of them said: The Creator here is the argument.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And he has no share in the Hereafter. He said: He has no argument in the Hereafter.

x: Others said: The Creator is the religion.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us: Al-Hasan said:
m: He has no share in the afterlife. He said: He has no religion.

x: Others said: The Creator here is the Sustainer.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said:
m: Ibn Abbas said: He has no share in the Hereafter. He said: Sustainability. The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of al-Khalaq in this context is share, because that is its meaning in the speech of the Arabs. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God will support this religion with people who have no share or portion in Islam and religion. From this is the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: They call for woe therein. They have no morals except garments of tar and shackles. He means by this: They have no share or portion except garments and shackles. Likewise, His statement:
h
He will have no share in the Hereafter

means that he will have no share of Paradise in the Hereafter, because he had no faith, religion, or righteous deeds for which he would be rewarded in Paradise, so that he would have a share or portion of Paradise. Rather, the Most High said:
h
He will have no share in the Hereafter

, describing him as having no share in the Hereafter, and He meant by that that he will have no share of recompense, reward, or Paradise, except for his share of the Fire. For His condemnation of their actions, for which He denied that they would have a share in the Hereafter, indicated His intention of good, and that He only meant by that that they would have no share in it of the good, but as for the evils, they would have a share in it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And evil is that for which they sold themselves,
h
if they only knew

b.v: Abu Jaafar, may God have mercy on him, said:
x: We have previously demonstrated that the meaning of they sold is they sold. So the meaning of the statement is: How evil is what he sold himself for by learning magic, if he had known the evil consequences of it.
Like: Musa told me, he said:

c: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And evil is that for which they sold their souls. He said: Evil is that for which they sold their souls.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How could He, the Most High, say:
h
And evil is that for which they have sold themselves
h
if they only knew
, and He said before:
h
And they certainly knew

that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter, so how could they know that whoever learns magic will have no share, while they are ignorant of the evil that they have sold themselves for magic?

The meaning of that is not as you imagined, that they are described as ignorant of what they are described as knowing, but that is from the deferred which means to advance, and the meaning of the speech is: And they do not harm anyone with it except by God’s permission, and they learn what harms them and does not benefit them,
h
and evil is that for which they have sold themselves
h
if they only knew
h
and they certainly knew
that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter. His saying: How evil is that for which they have sold themselves,
h
if they only knew

is a censure from God, the Most High, of the actions of the two angels who taught separation between a man and his wife. It is report from Him, the Most High, about them that how evil is that for which they sold themselves, by accepting magic instead of their religion, by which their souls are saved from destruction, out of their ignorance of the evil consequences of their actions and the loss of their transaction, since that could have been learned from them by someone who does not know God, nor does he know what He has permitted and forbidden, His commands and prohibitions. Then He returns to the group about whom God informed that they threw His Book behind their backs as if they did not know: And they followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon, and what was revealed to the two angels. He informed about them that they knew that whoever bought magic would have no share in the Hereafter, and he described them as committing sins against God knowingly, and disbelieving in God and His messengers, and preferring to follow the devils and act according to what they have created of magic over acting according to His Book, revelation, and sending down, out of their stubbornness and aggression against His messengers, and their transgression of His limits, knowing that whoever does that will have punishment and torment from God.
So that is the interpretation of His statement. Some claimants have said that his statement,
h
And they have certainly known that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter
, refers to the devils, and that his statement,
h
If they only knew
, refers to the people. This is a contradictory statement by all the interpreters, because they agree that his statement,
h
And they have certainly known that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter
, refers to the Jews, not the devils. Moreover, it is contrary to what is indicated by the revelation, because the verses before his statement,
h
And they have certainly known that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter
, and after his statement,
h
If they only knew

, came from God condemning the Jews and rebuking them for their misguidance, and condemning them for throwing the revelation of God and the verses of His Book behind their backs, despite their knowledge of the error of their actions.
So his statement,
h
And they have certainly known that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter
, is one of those reports about them.
Some of them said: Those whom God, the Most High, described with His saying:
h
And evil is that for which they have sold themselves
h
if they only knew
, and He denied them knowledge, are those whom God described with His saying:
h
And they certainly know that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter
. And He, the Most High, denied them knowledge with His saying:
h
If they only knew
, after describing them that they had known with His saying:
h
And they certainly knew

, because they did not act upon what they knew. And only the knowledgeable person is the one who acts upon his knowledge. As for if his action contradicts his knowledge, then he is among the meanings of the ignorant. He said: And it may be said to the doer of an action contrary to what he should have done, even if he is knowledgeable about his action: If I had known, I would have fallen short, as Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr al-Muzani said, describing a wolf and a crow that followed him to get some of his food and provisions: If they were present, I would say, If you knew about this, you would know that I am a widow.
So he informed that he said to them: If you knew it, so he denied them knowledge. Then he asked them and said: Did you not know? They said: So is his saying:
h
And they certainly knew for whoever bought it
, and:
h
If they only knew
. This is an interpretation, even if it has an explanation and a face, because it is contrary to the apparent meaning understood by the speech itself. I mean by his saying:
h
And they certainly knew
, and his saying:
h
If they only knew

. It is only an extraction. And the interpretation of the Qur’an according to the apparent meaning of the speech without the hidden and inner meaning of it, until an indication comes from the face that must be accepted with a meaning contrary to its apparent evidence that is commonly known among the people of the language in whose language the Qur’an was revealed, is more appropriate.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: It was narrated that some of the reciters used to recite: And what was revealed to the two angels, meaning two men from among the children of Adam.
We have demonstrated the error of this recitation by way of evidence.

As for the transmission, the consensus of the evidence on the error of this recitation by the Companions, the Followers, and the reciters of the regions is that this is sufficient as evidence of its error.

x: What God, the Most High, means by His statement,
h
And if they had believed and feared God

, was if those who learn from the two angels what would separate a man from his wife, had believed, so they believed in God and His Messenger and what He brought them from their Lord, and feared their Lord, so they feared Him and feared His punishment, so they obeyed Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience, then God's reward for them and His recompense for their belief and fear of Him would have been better for them than magic and what they acquired through it, if they only knew, that God's reward for that is better for them than magic and what they acquired through it. And He only negated knowledge from them by His statement, if they only knew, that they would be knowledgeable about the extent of God's reward and the extent of His recompense for obeying Him. In Arabic, reward is a noun derived from the saying: I established you with reward, reward, and reward.

The origin of this is from: Thaba ilaika al-shay’ meaning: it came back. Then it is said: I established it to you: meaning, I returned it to you and returned it. So the meaning of: A man’s rewarding a man for a gift or something else is to return it to him in exchange for it, and to return it to him in exchange for it. Then he made every compensation other than his work or gift or a favor that was given to him by him: a reward for him. And from this is the reward of God the Almighty for His servants for their deeds, meaning: He gives them compensation and recompense for it, so that it returns to them in exchange for the work that they did for Him. Some Basran grammarians have claimed that his statement,
h
And if they had believed and feared God
, a reward from God would have been better, is one of the things that suffices to indicate the meaning of the speech without mentioning its answer. And that its meaning is:
h
And if they had believed and feared God
, they would have been rewarded, but he dispensed with indicating the report about the reward in his statement: they would have been rewarded.
Some of the grammarians of Basra denied this, and believed that the answer to his statement,
h
And if only they had believed and feared God

, was for a reward, and that if was only answered with a reward, even though it was reported with the past tense of the verb, because their meanings are similar to the meaning of if only, in that they are two rewards, since they are two answers to faith. So he introduced the answer to each of them to the other, so if only was answered with the answer to if only, and if only with the answer to if only, for that reason, even though their answers differed. So it was the rule and the portion of if only that it was answered with the past tense of the verb, and it was the rule and the portion of if only that it was answered with the future tense of the verb, because of what we have described of their similarity. So he interpreted the meaning of his statement,
h
And if only they had believed and feared God
, as:
h
And if they had believed and feared God
, then a reward from God is better.
And what we said about the interpretation of the reward, the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: For a reward from God, he said: A reward from God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And if they had believed and feared God
, they would have received a reward from God. As for the reward, it is the recompense.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
And if they had believed and feared God
, a reward from God would have been better, meaning: a reward from God.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: O you who believe,
h
do not say
, ‘Ra’ina.’
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his statement:
h
Do not say ‘Ra’ina’
Some of them said: Its interpretation is:
h
Do not say
something contrary to what was said.
He mentioned those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do not say
, ‘Ra’ina,’ he said:
h
Do not say
something contrary.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Do not say ‘ra’ina’
h
do not say
something contrary.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

i: Others said:
x: Its interpretation is:
h
Give us your ear
That is, listen to us and we will listen to you.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. His saying:
h
Give us your ear
, that is,
h
give us your ear

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not say
, ‘Ra’ina,’
h
do not say
, Listen to us and we will hear from you.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: Pamper us, that a man from the polytheists would say: Pamper me with your hearing. Then the people of interpretation differed about the reason why God forbade the believers from saying: Ra’ina.

x: Some of them said: It is a word that the Jews used to say in mockery and insult, so God Almighty forbade the believers from saying that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
He mentioned those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
do not say
, ‘Ra’ina,’ a statement that the Jews used to say in mockery, so God warned the believers not to say as they said.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
Do not say ‘ra’ina’
, he said: Some of the Jews used to say: ‘Ra’ina, listen to us!’ until some of the Muslims said it. So God disliked what the Jews said for them, so He said:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not say ‘ra’ina’
, as the Jews and Christians said.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Do not say ‘Ra’ina’ but say ‘Unzurna’
, he said: They used to say: Ra’ina, listen to you! So the Jews would come and say the same thing mockingly, so God said:
h
Do not say ‘Ra’ina’ but say ‘Unzurna’
. Al-Munjab narrated: Bishr bin Ammarah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
Do not say ‘ra’ina’
, he said: They used to say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘ra’ina, listen to me!’ But ‘ra’ina’ is like saying ‘aatana’.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
do not say

, ‘Ra’ina,’ but say, ‘Unzurna,’ he said: Ra’ina is the statement that the people said, they said: We hear and disobey, and hear but are not heard, and ra’ina is a twisting of their tongues and an attack on the religion
r
(An-Nisa’: 46)
, he said: He said: This is the ra’in and the ra’in means the one who makes a mistake. So he said to the believers:
h
Do not say

‘mistake,’ as the people said, and say, ‘Unzurna,’ and listen. He said: They were looking at the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and speaking to him, and he was listening to them, and they were asking him questions and he was answering them.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a word that the Ansar used to say in the pre-Islamic era, but God forbade them in Islam from saying it to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, Hisham told me, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do not say ‘ra’ina’
, he said: It was a dialect among the Ansar in the pre-Islamic era, so this verse was revealed:
h
Do not say ‘ra’ina’
, but say ‘unzurna’ to the end of the verse.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: h
Do not say ‘ra’ina’
, he said: It was a dialect among the Ansar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do not say
, ‘Raʿina,’ he said: When the polytheists of the Arabs spoke to each other, one of them would say to his companion, Listen to me, and they were forbidden from doing so.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: Ra’ina, is the saying of the mocker. So he forbade them from mocking the saying of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Some of them said: Rather, that was the speech of a specific Jew, called Rifa’ah bin Zaid. He was speaking... The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it as an insult to him, and the Muslims took it from him, so God forbade the believers from saying it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
do not say
, ‘Ra’ina,’ but say, ‘Unzurna,’ There was a Jewish man from a tribe of Jews called Banu Qaynuqa’ whose name was Rifa’ah ibn Zayd ibn As-Sa’ib.

x: This is a mistake. Rather, he is Ibn Al-Tabut, not Ibn As-Sa’ib. He used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and whenever he met him and spoke to him, he would say, Give me your ear, and Listen, but do not be deceived. The Muslims used to think that the prophets used to show off with this, so some of them used to say, Listen, but do not be deceived, like you would say, Listen, but do not be deceived. This is what is in Surat An-Nisa’:

“Among those who are Jews are those who distort words from their [proper] usages and say, ‘We hear and disobey,’ and ‘Listen, but do not be deceived,’ and they twist their tongues and attack the religion.”
He means by his statement that he meant attacking the religion. Then he went to the believers and said,
h
Do not say
, ‘Ra’ina.’

The correct statement about God Almighty’s prohibition of the believers from saying to His Prophet, Ra’ina, is to say that it is a word that God hates for them to say to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to what was reported about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Do not call the grapes the vineyard, but call them the grapevine.
h
Do not say

: My servant, but say: My boy. And what is similar to that, of the two words that are used with one meaning in the speech of the Arabs, so the dislike or prohibition comes by using one of them, and choosing the other over it in conversations.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: We have already learned the meaning of the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, prohibition of grapes from being called vineyards, and of a slave from being called slaves. So what is the meaning of his saying,
h
Pay attention to us
, then, for the sake of which God, may His praise be glorified, prohibited the believers from saying it, until He commanded them to prefer His saying, Observe us?

What is in this is similar to what is in the saying of the speaker: The generosity is for the grapes, and the slave is for the slave. That is because the saying of the speaker: My slave is for all the servants of God, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked that some of the servants of God be attributed with the meaning of servitude to other than God, and he ordered that this be attributed to other than Him, in a meaning other than that attributed to God the Almighty, so it is said: My boy. And likewise the reason for his prohibition of saying in the grapes: generosity, for fear of imagining that it is described as generosity, even if it is quiescent, because the Arabs may quiescent some vowels if they follow one type. So he disliked that grapes be described with this. So likewise God the Almighty forbade the believers from saying: Ra’ina, because the saying of the speaker: Ra’ina could possibly mean protect us and we will protect you, and watch us and we will watch you.
From what the Arabs say to one another: May God protect you, meaning may God preserve and protect you.

i: It is also possible that it means: Give us your attention, from their saying: I gave my attention to my hearing, or I gave him attention to my hearing, meaning: I freed it up to listen to his speech, as Al-A’sha Maymun ibn Qays said:
x: He takes heed of the words of the leaders of men if they show him firmness, or whatever he wishes he innovates.

He means by his saying: He is watching over it, listening to it with his ears, devoting himself to it. God, the Most High, had commanded the believers to revere and magnify His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the point that He, the Most Surat al-Baqarah 2:105 Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists do not like that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. And God chooses for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty. High, forbade them, among other things, from raising their voices above his voice, and from speaking to him loudly as they speak to one another, fearing that their deeds would be in vain. So He warned them against saying to him anything that was rude, and He commanded them to choose the best words and the most delicate meanings to address him. This included their saying, Ra’ana, because it could possibly mean: Ra’ana, we will ra’aka, since the reciprocal verb can only be formed by two people, as one says, ‘Ata’ana, “Hadithana,” and Jalasana, meaning: Do to us, and we will do to you, and the meaning is: Ra’ana, your ear, so that we understand you and you understand us.

God Almighty forbade the companions of Muhammad to say that in this way, and to single out his question by waiting for them and giving them time, so that they would understand from him, with reverence and respect from them, and not to ask him what they asked him of that in a manner of rudeness and sternness from them towards him, nor with rudeness and harshness, imitating the Jews in their address to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying to him: Listen, but do not listen, and take care of us. What we have said about this is proven by his statement, Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists do not like that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. Thus, he indicated that what he rebuked them for was something that pleased the Jews and polytheists. As for the interpretation that was reported from Mujahid regarding his saying: ra’ana that it means: contrary, which is not understood in the speech of the Arabs.

Because ra’ayt in the speech of the Arabs is only in one of two ways: One of them means fa’ilat, from ra’iya which means neck and protection. And the other means emptying the hearing, meaning: I gave him my hearing. As for ra’ayt in the meaning of khalfat, there is no clear meaning for it in the speech of the Arabs. Unless he read that with the tanween, then directed it to the meaning of rashness, ignorance and error, in the manner that Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd led in that, so that even if it was contrary to the reading of the reciters, it would have a clear meaning at that time. As for the other statement that was narrated from Atiyyah and from those who narrated it: that his saying: Ra’ina was a word of the Jews meaning cursing and mocking, and the believers used it, taking it from them, then that is not permissible in the description of the believers: that they take from the speech of the polytheists a word whose meaning they do not know, then use it among themselves and in addressing their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

But it is permissible for that to be from what was narrated from Qatada, that it was a correct word understood from the speech of the Arabs, and it matched a word from the speech of the Jews in a language other than Arabic, which is cursing for the Jews, and it is for the Arabs: Ra’ini your hearing and empty it so that you understand from me. So God, the Most High, knew the meaning of the Jews in what they said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that its meaning from them was different from its meaning in the speech of the Arabs, so God, the Most High, forbade the believers from saying it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lest someone whose meaning in that was different from the meaning of the believers would dare to address the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with it. This is an interpretation that has not been reported to be like that, from the aspect that establishes the proof.

Since this is the case, what is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse is what we have described, since that is the apparent meaning understood by the verse and nothing else. It was narrated that Al-Hasan Al-Basri used to recite it:
h
Do not say
something that alarms us, with the tanween, meaning:
h
Do not say

something that alarms us, from rashness, which is foolishness and ignorance. This is a reading that contradicts the reading of the Muslims. It is not permissible for anyone to read it because it is anomalous and deviates from the reading of the predecessors and the later ones, and it contradicts what the proof of the Muslims has brought. And whoever adds the nun to ra'ana, adds the nun to it by saying:
h
Do not say

, because then it is an agent in it. And whoever does not add the nun to it, then he has left out its nun because it is a reported command. Because the people are as if they are saying to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ra'ana, meaning asking him: Either he listens to them, or he watches over them and monitors them - as I have explained previously.
So it was said to them:
h
Do not say

in your question to him Ra'ana. So the indication of the meaning of the command in ra'ana then is the dropping of the ya' that was in yara'aihi and the indication of it, I mean the dropped ya', is the kasra of the 'ayn in ra'ana. It has been mentioned that Ibn Masoud’s reading:
h
Do not say
h
Pay attention to us

’ means narrating a matter that is appropriate for a group to pay attention to. If this reading is correct, then it is possible that the people were forbidden from using this among themselves when addressing one another, whether they were addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or someone else. We do not know that to be correct from the perspective from which reports are authentic.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And say, ‘Respite us.’

What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying: And say, ‘Look at us,’ is that you, O believers, say to your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Look at us and observe us, so that we may understand and discern what you say to us and teach us, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And say, ‘Look at us,’ we understood, explain to us, O Muhammad.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And say, ‘Look at us,’ we understood, explain to us, O Muhammad.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. It is said that he looked at the man and looked at him, meaning he waited for him and watched him. From this comes the saying of Al-Hutay’ah: I saw you at the dinner of the five, and my possessions were prolonged and I forgot about them. And from this is the saying of God Almighty: On the Day when the hypocrites, men and women, will say to those who believe, ‘Wait for us that we may borrow some of your light’ (al-Hadid 57:13), meaning: Wait for us. It has been read: Anzurna and Anzuruna with the alif cut off in both places. So whoever reads it like that means: Delay us, as God the Most High said: He said, ‘My Lord, then respite me until the Day they are resurrected’
r

, meaning, Delay me. There is no reason to read it like that in this place. Because the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were only commanded to draw near to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), to listen to him, to address him gently, and to lower their wing, not to delay him, nor to ask him to delay them. So, if that is the case in the reading, then the correct reading is the one who connected the alif in his saying: Anzurna and did not cut it off, meaning: we waited. It has been said that the meaning of Anzarna with the alif cut off is: Give us time. It was narrated that some Arabs heard it saying: Give me time to talk to you. The one who heard that from one of them mentioned that he checked its meaning, so he told him that he meant: Give me time. If that is correct from them, then Anzarna and Anzarna with the alif cut off and connected are close in meaning. However, even if that is the case, the reading that I do not approve of other than it is the reading of those who read Wait for us, with the alif connected, meaning: Wait for us, because the evidence unanimously approves of it, and they reject other readings.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty: And listen, and for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying: And listen, is that you listen to what is said to you and recited to you from the Book of your Lord, and understand it and comprehend it, as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And listen, listen to what is said to you. So the meaning of the verse is: O you who believe!
h
Do not say
to your Prophet:
h
Pay attention to us

and listen to us, so that we may understand you and you may understand from us what we say. Rather, say: Wait for us and watch until we understand from you what we have learned and you make it clear to us. And listen to what he says to you, then understand it, memorize it, and understand it. Then He, the Most High, informed them of the painful punishment in the Hereafter for those who denied His signs from them and others, disobeyed His commands and prohibitions, and denied His Messenger, saying: And for those who disbelieve in Me and in My Messenger is a painful punishment. He means by His saying: painful, “painful.” We have already mentioned the evidence for that previously, and the effects thereof.

evidence.text: Unless he read that with the tanween, then directed it to the meaning of rashness, ignorance and error, in the manner that Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd led in that, so that even if it was contrary to the reading of the reciters, it would have a clear meaning at that time.

It was narrated that Al-Hasan Al-Basri used to recite it: Do not say something that alarms us, with the tanween, meaning: Do not say something that alarms us, from rashness, which is foolishness and ignorance.
This is a reading that contradicts the reading of the Muslims.
It is not permissible for anyone to read it because it is anomalous and deviates from the reading of the predecessors and the later ones, and it contradicts what the proof of the Muslims has brought.

If this reading is correct, then it is possible that the people were forbidden from using this among themselves when addressing one another, whether they were addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or someone else.
It has been read: Anzurna and Anzuruna with the alif cut off in both places.
So whoever reads it like that means: Delay us, as God the Most High said: He said, ‘My Lord, then respite me until the Day they are resurrected’ (Sad: 79), meaning, Delay me.
There is no reason to read it like that in this place.
So, if that is the case in the reading, then the correct reading is the one who connected the alif in his saying: Anzurna and did not cut it off, meaning: we waited.

However, even if that is the case, the reading that I do not approve of other than it is the reading of those who read Wait for us, with the alif connected, meaning: Wait for us, because the evidence unanimously approves of it, and they reject other readings.

x: What he means by his saying he does not like is what he likes, meaning: many of the People of the Book do not like. It is said: So-and-so likes so-and-so, he likes him with love, affection, and affection. As for the polytheists, they are in the accusative case in apposition to the People of the Book. The meaning of the words: Those who disbelieve among the People of the Book and the polytheists do not like that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. As for that in his statement: that he descends, it is in the accusative case because of his statement: would like. We have already demonstrated the way in which from enters into his statement: from good and similar statements that begin with denial, in what has passed, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. The interpretation of the statement is: The disbelievers among the People of the Book and the polytheists among the idol worshippers do not like that any of the good that was with God should be sent down to you.

So the polytheists and disbelievers among the People of the Book wish that God would not send down to you the Criterion and what He revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of His wisdom and verses. Rather, the Jews and their followers among the polytheists liked that out of envy and malice towards the believers. This verse clearly indicates that God Almighty forbade the believers from relying on their enemies from the People of the Book and the polytheists, listening to what they say, or accepting anything they bring to them as advice from them, by informing them, may He be glorified, of what the People of the Book and the polytheists harbor towards them of resentment and envy, even if they express with their tongues the opposite of what they harbor.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And God chooses for His mercy whom He wills,
h
and God is the possessor of great bounty
What is meant by His statement, may He be glorified:
h
And God singles out for His mercy whom He wills

is: God singles out whom He wills for His prophethood and message, so He sends him to whomever He wills of His creation, and bestows faith upon whomever He loves and guides him to it. And His singling them out for it is His singling them out for it, without any of His creation. And God made His message to whomever He sent to of His creation, and His guidance of whomever He guided of His servants, a mercy from Him to him, so that He may lead him to His pleasure and love and win him Paradise through it, and deserving His praise through it. And all of that is a mercy from God to him. As for his saying:
h
And God is the possessor of great bounty

, it is report from God, may He be glorified, that every good that His servants attain in their religion and their worldly life is from Him, from His beginning and as a favor from Him to them, without them deserving it of Him.
In His statement:
h
And God singles out for His mercy whom He wills
h
and God is the possessor of great bounty

, God Almighty is referring to the People of the Book: that what He gave to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him of guidance is a favor from Him, and that His blessings cannot be attained by wishful thinking, but rather they are gifts from Him that He singles out for whomever He wills of His creation.

What God, the Most High, means by His statement, Whatever verse We abrogate is what We transfer from the ruling of a verse to another, so we change it and alter it. That is by turning the permissible into the forbidden, and the forbidden into the permissible, and the permissible into the prohibited, and the prohibited into the permissible. This only occurs in commands and prohibitions, prohibitions and generalizations, and prevention and permissibility. As for the report, there is no abrogating or abrogated in it. The origin of abrogation is from the copy of the book, which is its transfer from one copy to another. Likewise, the meaning of abrogating a ruling to another is its transformation and transfer of its expression to another. If that is the meaning of abrogating a verse, then it is the same if its ruling is abrogated and its obligation is changed and replaced, and the obligation of the servants is transferred from the necessary, then it is theirs whether its writing is confirmed and then abandoned, or its trace is erased and then overlooked and forgotten, because in both cases it is abrogated, and the new ruling, which was replaced by the first ruling, and the obligation of the servants was transferred to it, is the abrogator.
It is said of it: God abrogated such-and-such a verse, He abrogates it by abrogation, and abrogation is the name.
And similar to what we said about that, Al-Hasan Al-Basri used to say:

c: Suwar bin Abdullah Al-Anbari told us, he said, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said
m: about His statement:
h
Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it
, he said: Your Prophet recited the Qur’an, then he forgot it and it was nothing, and there is some of the Qur’an that has been abrogated and you are reciting it.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding his statement:
h
What We abrogate
Some of them said: Musa bin Harun told me, he said:

c: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
What We abrogate
of a verse, as for its abrogation, it means its seizure.

x: Others said: Al-Muthanna told me, he said:

c: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We do not abrogate a verse
, meaning: We do not change a verse.

x: Others said: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of the companions of Abdullah bin Masoud, that they said: Whatever verse we abrogate, we confirm its script and change its ruling.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Whatever verse We abrogate, we confirm its script and change its ruling. I narrated it on the authority of the companions of Ibn Masʿud.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Bakr bin Shawdhab told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of the companions of Ibn Masoud:
m: Whatever verse We abrogate We confirm its script and change its ruling.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying: or we forget it.
The readings differed in his saying that. The people of Medina and Kufa read it: or
h
we make it forgotten

. And the reading of those who read that has two aspects of interpretation. One of them is that its interpretation is: What verse do We abrogate, O Muhammad, and change its ruling or cause it to be forgotten. It has been mentioned that it is in the Mushaf of Abdullah: What verse do We forget or abrogate, We bring forth something like it. So that is the interpretation of: forgetfulness. And this is the interpretation that a group of the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten

, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it, he would abrogate one verse with the next, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recite the verse or more than that, then it would be forgotten and removed.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten
, he said: God Almighty would make His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forget whatever He willed, and abrogate whatever He willed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Ubayd ibn Umair used to say: We will make it disappear, we will remove it from you.

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, Khalid bin Al-Harith told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he said:
m: Concerning his statement: or
h
we make it forgotten

, he said: Your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the Qur’an and then forgot it. Saad bin Abi Waqqas also interpreted the verse, except that he would recite it: or you forget it in the sense of addressing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as if he meant: or you forget it, O Muhammad.

x: Mention of the narrations on that:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Yaʿla bin Ataʿ told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Rabiʿah, he said:
m: I heard Saad bin Abi Waqqas say:
h
We do not abrogate a verse

or you forget it, I said to him: But Saʿid bin Al-Musayyab recites it: or you forget it, he said: So Saad said: The Qur’an was not revealed to Al-Musayyab or to the family of Al-Musayyab! God said: We will recite to you, and you will not forget
r
(Al-Aʿla: 6)
And remember your Lord when you forget (al-Kahf 18:24) Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said:

c: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Ya’la bin Ata’ told us, he said: Al-Qasim bin Rabi’ah bin Qanif al-Thaqafi told us, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abi Waqqas mention something similar. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Adam al-Asqalani both narrated on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Ata’, who said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Rabi’ah al-Thaqafi say: I said to Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas: I heard Ibn al-Musayyab reciting:
h
We do not abrogate a verse
or you cause it to be forgotten. Sa’d said: “God did not reveal the Qur’an to al-Musayyab or to his son! It is: “
h
We do not abrogate a verse
or you cause it to be forgotten,” O Muhammad. Then he recited: We will make you recite, and you will not forget and Remember your Lord when you forget.
b.via: Al-Qasim bin Rabi’ah bin Qanif al-Thaqafi

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten

, he said: We cause it to be forgotten we remove it. And God, the Blessed and Exalted, had revealed matters from the Qur’an and then removed them. The other aspect of it is that it means abandonment from the statement of God, the Most High: They forgot God, so He forgot them (al-Tawbah 9:67), meaning: they abandoned God, so He abandoned them. So the interpretation of the verse then according to this interpretation is:
h
We do not abrogate a verse

, changing its ruling or replacing its obligation, We bring one better than the one We abrogated or similar to it. And according to this interpretation, a group of the people of interpretation interpreted it.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: or We cause it to be forgotten, he said: or We abandon it and do not change it.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying: or we forget it, we leave it and do not abrogate it.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten
, he said: the abrogating and the abrogated.

x: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd used to say about that what:

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-Aʿla told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about his statement:
h
We make it forgotten
, we erase it.

x: Others read it as: or we forget it with a fat-ha on the noon and a hamza after the seen, meaning: we delay it, from your saying: I postponed this matter, I postponed it, nasa’ and nisa’an, if you delay it. It is from their saying: I sold it for nisa’, meaning by delaying it.

i: And from that is the saying of Tarafa bin al-Abd:
x: By your life, death does not make a young man forget you, like a long, slack-jawed man who has been bent over by the hand.
