He means by his saying: I will postpone, I will delay. Among those who read this were a group of the Companions and Followers, and a group of Kufi and Basri reciters read it, and a group of interpreters interpreted it in this way.
Those who said this were:

c: Abu Kurayb and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, they said: Hisham told us, he said: Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten
, he said: We delay it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us,
m: I heard Ibn Abi Nujayh say about God’s statement:
h
Or We postpone it
, he said: We postpone it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
or We postpone it
, we postpone it and delay it.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Fadil told us, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
or We postpone it
, he said: We delay it and do not abrogate it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah bin Katheer told me, on the authority of Ubaid Al-Azdi, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair:
m: h
or We postpone it
, means delaying it and postponing it.

c: This is what Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Ubaid Al-Azdi,
m: but it is on the authority of Ali Al-Azdi.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Ali Al-Azdi, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair
m: that he read it: We will delay it.

x: The interpretation of whoever reads it thus is: We do not change a verse that We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, by nullifying its ruling and confirming its line, or delaying it and postponing it Surat Al-Baqarah 2:107 Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have not besides Allah any protector or helper? and confirming it and not changing it or nullifying its ruling, but We bring one better than it or similar to it.
Some of them read it as:
h
We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten

. The interpretation of this reading is similar to the interpretation of the reading of the one who read: or cause it to be forgotten, except that the meaning of or cause it to be forgotten is you, O Muhammad.

Some of them read: What we abrogate of a verse, with a damma on the nun and a kasra on the seen, meaning: We do not abrogate you, O Muhammad, from a verse that I abrogate, so I abrogate you. This is a reading error according to us, because it departs from what the proof has brought from the reading by widespread transmission. Likewise the reading of those who read tansaha or tansaha, because it is an anomaly and departs from the reading that the proof has brought from the readers of the ummah. The first reading of the verse in His statement: or we forget it is correct, from the reading or we forget it meaning: we leave it. Because God, the Most High, informed His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that no matter how much he changed a ruling or altered it, or did not change it or alter it, He will bring him something better than it or similar to it. So what is more appropriate for the verse, since that is its meaning, is that when he presented the report about what he will do if he changed and altered the ruling of a verse, he should follow that with the report about what he will do since he did not change or alter that.

So the report that should come after His statement: Whatever verse We abrogate is His statement: or we leave its abrogation, since that is the well-known and common speech of the people. Although that, if it is read in the same way with the meaning I described, it includes the meaning of forgetting which means leaving, and the meaning of women which means delaying. Since everything that is abandoned is delayed in the state in which it is abandoned.

Some people have rejected the reading of the one who recites: or you forget it, if he means forgetfulness, and they said: It is not permissible that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgot something from the Qur’an that was not abrogated, unless he forgot something from it and then remembered it. They said: And then, if he had forgotten something from it, it would not have been permissible for all of his companions who recited it and memorized it to forget it. They said: In the statement of God, may He be glorified and exalted:
h
And if We willed
, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you
r
(Al-Isra’: 86)
, there is what indicates that God, may He be glorified and exalted, did not cause His Prophet to forget anything of the knowledge that He had given him.

This statement is attested to by the falsity and corruption of the unanimous reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, similar to what we have said:

c: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, he said: Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, he said: Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Anas ibn Malik told us:
m: Those seventy of the Ansar who were killed at Bir Maʿuna, we read to them and among them a letter: Convey from us to our people that we met our Lord and He was pleased with us and pleased us. Then that was lifted. What we mentioned about Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari is that they used to recite: If the son of Adam had two valleys full of wealth, he would desire a third. Nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust. And God accepts the repentance of whoever repents. Then he was raised. And there are similar stories that would take too long to list in a book. It is not impossible in the nature of a person with a sound mind, nor on the basis of a hadith, that God would cause His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to forget some of what He had revealed to him. So since that is not impossible from either of these two aspects, it is not permissible for someone to say: That is not permissible. As for His statement:
h
And if We willed
, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you
r
(Al-Isra’: 86)

, He, the Most High, did not inform us that He would not take away any of it, but rather He informed us that if He willed, He could take away all of it. So He did not take it away, praise be to God, but rather He only took away what they had no need for of it. That is because whatever was abrogated from it, the servants have no need for it. And God, the Most High, said: We will cause you to recite, and you will not forget, except what God wills (al-A’la 87:6-7), so He informed us that He would make His Prophet forget whatever He willed of it. So what was taken away from it is what God excluded. As for us, we chose what we chose from the interpretation to seek the consistency of the speech in a system of meaning, not to deny that God Almighty had caused His Prophet to forget some of what was abrogated from His revelation and sending down to him.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
She brought something better than it or similar to it
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of his statement:
h
She brought something better than it or similar to it
Some of them said what:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muʿawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
She brought something better than it or similar to it
, he said: better for you in terms of benefit, and easier for you.

x: Others said: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to me, he said:

c: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: We have brought one better than it or similar to it, he said: A verse in which there is relief, in which there is mercy, in which there is a command, in which there is a prohibition.

x: Others said: We have brought one better than the one we abrogated, or better than the one we left out and did not abrogate it.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: We have brought one better than it, he said: We have brought one better than the one we abrogated, or similar to it, or similar to the one we left out. The ha’ and the alif in his statement: from it refer to this article on the verse in his statement: whatever verse We abrogate. The ha’ and the alif in his statement: or its like, refer to the ha’ and the alif in his statement: or We cause it to be forgotten.

x: Others said: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Ubayd ibn Umair used to say: We will remove it from you, we will bring something like it or better than it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Or We forget it, we remove it, we bring something better than it or similar to it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Bakr ibn Shawdhab told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of the companions of Ibn Masoud,
m: similarly. The correct statement regarding the meaning of that according to us is: We do not change the ruling of a verse and alter it, or we leave its alteration and leave it as it is, we hope for something better for you than the ruling of the verse whose ruling We abrogated and changed, either in the immediate future, because it is easier for you, because it was imposed as an obligation upon you, so its burden was removed from you, such as what was imposed on the believers regarding the obligation of standing at night, then that was abrogated and removed from them, so that was better for them in the immediate future, because the burden of that and the burden of carrying it was removed from them, or in the afterlife, because of the great reward, because of the difficulty of carrying it and the weight of its burden on the body, such as what was imposed on them of fasting a certain number of days in the year, so it was abrogated and in its place it was imposed on them to fast a full month every year. So the obligation of fasting a full month every year was heavier on the body than fasting a certain number of days. However, even if that is the case, the reward for it is more abundant and the recompense is greater, because of the greater difficulty it brings to those charged with it than fasting a certain number of days. Even though this is more difficult for the body, it is better than the first in the hereafter due to the superiority of its reward and the greatness of its recompense, which is not like that of fasting the specified number of days. This is the meaning of His statement: It has brought something better than it. Because it is either better than it in the hereafter due to its lightness for the one who is obligated to do it, or in the hereafter due to the greatness of its reward and the abundance of its recompense. Or it could be similar in terms of the hardship on the body and the equal reward for it, like God the Most High abrogated the obligation of prayer towards the Holy House, to its obligation towards the Sacred Mosque. So facing towards the Holy House, even if facing towards the mosque is different, the cost of facing towards whichever one faces the same is the same. Because the burden of facing towards the Holy House is the same as the burden of facing towards the Kaaba, the same as the burden of facing towards the Kaaba, the same. So that is the meaning of the example in which God the Most High said: or its like. What He, the Most High, meant by His statement,
h
Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten
is
h
what We abrogate

or cause to be forgotten of the ruling of a verse. However, since the meaning of the verse was understood by those addressed by it, it was sufficient to indicate that the verse refers to its ruling. This is similar to all the other similar examples we have mentioned in the past in this book of ours, such as His statement, And they have made the calf to be drunk into their hearts (al-Baqarah 2:193), meaning the love of the calf, and the like. The interpretation of the verse is: We do not change the ruling of a verse by substituting it, or leave it and do not change it. We bring for you, O believers, a better ruling than it, or one similar to its ruling in lightness and heaviness, reward and recompense.

x: We have already learned that the calf does not enter hearts, and that it is not confusing for anyone who hears His statement: And they made the calf enter their hearts, that it means: And they made the love of the calf enter their hearts. So what is the evidence that His statement:
h
Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten
, We bring forth one better than it is similar to that?
What indicates that this is the case is his statement:
h
He brought something better than it or similar to it

. It is not permissible for one thing in the Qur’an to be better than another, because all of it is the speech of God, and it is not permissible to say about the attributes of God, may He be exalted, that some of them are better than others, and some of them are better than others.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Do you not know that God has power over all things?

The meaning of God, the Most High, by His statement, ‘Do you not know that God has power over all things?’ Did you not know, O Muhammad, that I am able to compensate you for what I have abrogated of My rulings and what I have changed of My obligations that I had imposed upon you, with whatever I will of what is better for you and My believing servants with you, and more beneficial to you and them, either in the immediate world or in the hereafter, or by replacing it for you and them with something like it in benefit to them, in the immediate world and in the hereafter, and similar in lightness for you and them? So know, O Muhammad, that I am capable of that and of all things. The meaning of His statement, Powerful in this context is: Strong. It is said from it: I have power over such and such, if I am strong Surat Al-Baqarah 2:107 Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have not besides Allah any protector or helper? over it.

I am able to do it and I am able to do it with power and qidran and qadaranah, and Banu Murrah from Ghatafan say: I was able to do it with a kasra on the dal. As for the estimation from the saying of the speaker: I estimated the thing, it is said from it that he estimated it, I estimated it, a quantum and a quantum.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in his saying that.
The people of Medina and Kufa read it: or we make it forgotten.
And the reading of those who read that has two aspects of interpretation.

Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth [one] better than it or similar to it, he would abrogate one verse with the next, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recite the verse or more than that, then it would be forgotten and removed.

Saad bin Abi Waqqas also interpreted the verse, except that he would recite it: or you forget it in the sense of addressing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as if he meant: or you forget it, O Muhammad.

Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Yaʿla bin Ataʿ told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Rabiʿah, he said: I heard Saad bin Abi Waqqas say: We do not abrogate a verse or you forget it, I said to him: But Saʿid bin Al-Musayyab recites it: or you forget it, he said: So Saad said: The Qur’an was not revealed to Al-Musayyab or to the family of Al-Musayyab!

Others read it as: or we forget it with a fat-ha on the noon and a hamza after the seen, meaning: we delay it, from your saying: I postponed this matter, I postponed it, nasa’ and nisa’an, if you delay it.
Among those who read this were a group of the Companions and Followers, and a group of Kufi and Basri reciters read it, and a group of interpreters interpreted it in this way.

Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said, Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Ali Al-Azdi, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair that he read it: We will delay it.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The interpretation of whoever reads it thus is: We do not change a verse that We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, by nullifying its ruling and confirming its line, or delaying it and postponing it Surat Al-Baqarah 2:107 Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have not besides Allah any protector or helper? and confirming it and not changing it or nullifying its ruling, but We bring one better than it or similar to it.
Some of them read it as: We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten.

The interpretation of this reading is similar to the interpretation of the reading of the one who read: or cause it to be forgotten, except that the meaning of or cause it to be forgotten is you, O Muhammad.
This is a reading error according to us, because it departs from what the proof has brought from the reading by widespread transmission.
Likewise the reading of those who read tansaha or tansaha, because it is an anomaly and departs from the reading that the proof has brought from the readers of the ummah.
The first reading of the verse in His statement: or we forget it is correct, from the reading or we forget it meaning: we leave it.
Although that, if it is read in the same way with the meaning I described, it includes the meaning of forgetting which means leaving, and the meaning of women which means delaying.

Some people have rejected the reading of the one who recites: or you forget it, if he means forgetfulness, and they said: It is not permissible that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgot something from the Qur’an that was not abrogated, unless he forgot something from it and then remembered it.
They said: And then, if he had forgotten something from it, it would not have been permissible for all of his companions who recited it and memorized it to forget it.

x: If someone were to say to us: Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, not know that God is capable of everything, and that He owns the heavens and the earth, until that was said to him? It was said: Yes!

Some of them used to say: This is from God, the Most High, as report that Muhammad knew that, but he made the speech and made it a statement, as the Arabs do in addressing one another. One of them would say to his companion: Did I not honor you? Did I not do you a favor? Meaning: informing him that he honored him and did him a favor, meaning: Did I not honor you? Did I not do you a favor? Meaning: I knew that.

This has no basis in our view. That is because the words of God, the Most High: Have you not known? only mean: Have you not known? It is a letter of denial with a letter of interrogation added to it, and letters of interrogation are only used in speech either in the sense of affirmation or in the sense of negation. As for the sense of affirmation, that is not known in the speech of the Arabs, especially when they are added to letters of denial. However, in my opinion, even though the address appears to be to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is only meant for his companions to whom God, the Most High, said: Do not say ‘Ra’ina’ but say ‘Unzurna’ and listen. What indicates that this is the case is the words of God, the Most High:
h
And you have not besides God any protector or helper

. Al-Baqarah 2:107, so He returned to address them at the end of the verse, and He began the beginning of it by addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with His words: Did you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth?

Al-Baqarah 2:107. Because what is meant by that are those of his companions whose affair I described. This is a common and eloquent expression among the Arabs: that the speaker utters his speech as an address to some people while intending someone else, and as an address to one person while intending a group other than him, or a group and the addressee is one of them, and as an address to a group, while the intended one is one of them. From this is the statement of God, the Most High: O Prophet, fear God and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Then He said: “And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.” (al-Ahzab 33:1-2) So he returned to addressing the group, and the statement began by addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Similar to this is the statement of Al-Kumait bin Zaid in praising the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: To the shining lamp Ahmed, neither desire nor fear equals me From him to someone else, even if people raised their eyes and watched It was said: You went too far!

Rather, you intended, even if the speakers rebuked me or slandered me. By preferring your tongue, even if you are noisy and stubborn You are the pure, refined, refined one in relation, for the text of your people is relation. So he directed his words to address the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he meant his family, so he used a metaphor for describing and praising them by mentioning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for the Umayyads, as the harsh speakers. Because it is known that no one is described as harshly praising and preferring the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor as making much noise and obstinacy in going on at length about his virtue.

i: As Jamil bin Muammar said:
x: Behold, my neighbors are leaving this evening, called by the motives of passion and desire. He said: Behold, my neighbors are here tonight. So he began the story about a group of his neighbors, then he said: I am going, because his intention in beginning what he began his speech with was to tell about one of them without their group, and as Jamil also said in his other statement: My two friends, in all your lives, have you ever seen a dead person cry for love of his killer before me?

He means his killer, because he is only describing a woman, so he used the man’s name to refer to her, even though he meant her. Likewise, His statement: Do you not know that God has power over all things? Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? Even though the apparent meaning of the statement is to address the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is intended to mean his companions. This is clear from the evidence of His statement:
h
And you have not besides God any protector or helper
. Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before?”

the three verses that follow indicate that this is the case. As for his saying: To Him belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and he did not say: the kingdom of the heavens, then he meant by that the kingdom of the sultan and the kingdom without the king. And when the Arabs wanted to report on the kingdom that is the kingdom of the sultan, they said: God ruled the creation with a kingdom.

And if they wanted to report on the kingdom, they said: So-and-so ruled this thing, so he owns it with a kingdom, a kingdom, and a king. The interpretation of the verse is: Did you not know, O Muhammad, that I have the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and their authority, and no one else does? I rule in them and in what is in them as I will, and I command in them and in what is in them as I will, and I forbid what I will, and I abrogate, change, and alter from My rulings by which I rule over My servants what I will when I will, and I confirm from them what I will? Although this report is from God Almighty, addressing His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the form of report about his greatness, it is from Him. Glory be to Him, He is the One Who refuted the Jews who denied the abrogation of the rulings of the Torah, rejected the prophethood of Jesus, and denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they brought what they brought from God by changing what God changed of the rulings of the Torah.

c: So God informed them that
m: He has the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and their authority, for the creation is the people of His kingdom and obedience to Him, and they must listen to Him and obey His commands and prohibitions, and that He has the right to command them as He wills, and to forbid them from what He wills, and to abrogate what He wills, and to confirm what He wills, and to cause to be forgotten what He wills of His rulings, commands, and prohibitions. Then he said to his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers with him: Obey my command, and come to my obedience in what I abrogate, and in what I leave and do not abrogate, of my rulings, my limits, and my duties, and do not be frightened by the opposition of one who opposes you in my command, my prohibition, my abrogating and abrogated verses, for there is no one who can take charge of your affairs except me, and there is no one who can support you except me, and I am the one who is alone in your guardianship, and defending you, and the one who is alone in supporting you with my glory, authority, and power over whoever opposes you and opposes you, and sets up a war of enmity between him and you, until I raise your argument, and make it against them and for you. The word wali means a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: I took charge of the matter of so-and-so, if I became his guardian, then I am his guardian, he is his guardian and his guardian. And from that it was said: So-and-so is the crown prince of the Muslims, meaning: the one who takes charge of what is entrusted to him of the matter of the Muslims. As for the supporter, it is a verbal noun derived from the word Nasir which means I supported you, I support you. So I am your supporter and your helper. It means the supporter and the strengthener. As for the meaning of his saying: other than God, it means other than God, and after God. From this is the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: O soul, you have no protector but God, and nothing remains in the events of time. He means: You have no one but God, and after God, who can protect you from harm? The meaning of the statement is: O believers, after God, you have no one to take care of your affairs, nor a supporter to support you and strengthen you, or to aid you against your enemies.

x: The people of interpretation differed about the reason for which this verse was revealed.
Some of them said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said:

c: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to me, and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, they said: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said:
m: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the freed slave of Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to me, he said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr or ʿIkrimah narrated to me from Ibn ʿAbbas: Rafiʿ ibn Huraymila and Wahb ibn Zayd said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Bring us a book that you send down to us from the heaven so that we may read it, and cause rivers to gush forth for us, so that we may follow you and believe you! So God revealed regarding that from their statement:
h
Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before
? the verse.

x: Others said: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before
? Moses was asking, and it was said to him: Show us God openly.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before
, to show them God openly. So the Arabs asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to bring them God so that they could see Him openly.

x: Others said: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God:
h
Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before

, that God should show them openly. So the Quraysh asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that God should make Safa into gold for them, he said: Yes! And it is for you like the table of the Children of Israel if you disbelieve! So they refused and went back.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The Quraysh asked Muhammad to turn Safa into gold for them, and he said: Yes! It is for you like the table for the Children of Israel if you disbelieve! But they refused and went back, so God revealed:
h
Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before
? That is, to show them God openly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: Others said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said:

c: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, he said:
m: “A man said: O Messenger of God, if our expiations were the expiations of the Children of Israel! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, we do not seek them! What God has given you is better than what He has given the Children of Israel. When one of the Children of Israel committed a sin, he would find it written on his door and its expiation. If he expiated it, it would be a disgrace for him in this world, and if he did not expiate it, it would be a disgrace for him in the Hereafter. God has given you better than what He gave the Children of Israel. He said: “And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful”
r
(An-Nisa’: 110)

. He said: And he said: The five daily prayers, and from Friday to Friday, are expiations for what is between them.” He said: “Whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, a good deed will be recorded for him. If he does it, ten times as much will be recorded for him. And none is lost to God except one who is lost.” Then God revealed:
h
Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before
? The Arab scholars differed on the meaning of umm in his statement:
h
Or do you want

x: Some of the Basrans said: It means interrogation. The interpretation of the statement is: Do you want to ask your Messenger?

Others of them said: It has the meaning of a future interrogative that is disconnected from the speech, as if you are inclining it to its beginning, like the Arabs saying: Are they camels, O people, or sheep? And such and such happened, or is it my own intuition? He said: His saying:
h
Or do you want

is not based on doubt, but he said it to make their actions ugly. And he cited as evidence for his saying that the following verse by Al-Akhtal: Did your eyes lie to you? Or did you see a shadow through the darkness of the night?
Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: If you wish, you can make his statement:
h
Or do you want

? an interrogative on a statement that preceded it, as God the Most High said: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The revelation of the Book, there is no doubt about it, from the Lord of the worlds. Or do they say, “He has invented it”?” (al-Sajdah 32:1-3). So Am came without an interrogative before it, so that was, in his view, evidence that it is an interrogative beginning on a statement that preceded it. The author of this statement said: Am in meaning is a response to the interrogative in two ways: One of them is to separate the meaning of any, and the other is that it is used to ask questions, so it is in the manner of sequence, and what is intended by it is the beginning, except that it is an beginning connected to a statement. So if you start a statement that has no words before it, then ask questions, there is no need for the letter alif or hal.
He said: If you wish, you can say in his statement:
h
Or do you want
? There is a question before it, so respond to it. It is in his statement: Do you not know that God has power over all things? (al-Baqarah 2:106).

The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, based on what the narrations that we have mentioned from the people of interpretation have brought, is that it is a question of beginning, meaning: Do you want, O people, to ask your Messenger? It is permissible for the people to ask with am, even though one of the conditions of am is that it be a sequence in the question to precede what precedes it from speech, because it is a question of beginning if it is preceded by a previous speech. And it was not heard from the Arabs to ask with it and not preceded by speech. Similar to it is the statement of the Most High: “The revelation of the Book about which there is no doubt is from the Lord of the worlds. Or do they say, ‘He has invented it’?” (al-Sajdah 32:1-3). Umm may mean rather, if it is preceded by a question that does not fit any. So they say: Do you have a right over us, or are you a man known for injustice?

i: The poet said:
x: By God, I don't know! Is it Aslami who has become arrogant, or is it sleep, or is it all my beloved?
Meaning: Rather, all of my beloved ones are mine.
Some of them used to say, denying the statement of those who claimed that the word am in His statement,
h
Or do you want

? is a future interrogative that is disconnected from the speech, and that it inclines them to its beginning: The first is a predicate, and the second is an interrogative, and the interrogative does not occur in the predicate, and the predicate does not occur in the interrogative, but doubt overcame him, according to his claim, after the predicate had passed, so he asked.

If the meaning of am is what we have described, then the interpretation of the statement is: Do you want, O people, to ask your Messenger for things similar to what the people of Moses asked before you, so you become disbelievers if you deny him in your question what it is not permissible in God’s wisdom to give you, or that you perish if it is permissible in His wisdom to give you, so He gave it to you, then you disbelieved after that, just as the nations before you perished who asked their prophets for what they could not ask of them, and when they were given it, they disbelieved, so they were hastened with punishments for their disbelief, after God gave them what they asked for.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And whoever exchanges
disbelief for faith.
God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And whoever exchanges
h
and whoever exchanges

disbelief, and the Sunnah of disbelief is denying God and His signs, with faith, meaning believing in God and His signs and acknowledging Him. It has been said: What is meant by disbelief in this place is hardship, and by faith is ease. I do not know the hardship in the meanings of disbelief, nor ease in the meaning of faith, unless the one who said that meant by his interpretation of disbelief in the meaning of hardship in this place, and by his interpretation of faith in the meaning of ease: what God has prepared for the disbelievers in the Hereafter of hardships, and what God has prepared for the people of faith in it of bliss, so that would be a face, even if it is far from the concept understood by the apparent address.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah:
m: h
And whoever exchanges
disbelief for faith, he says: He exchanges hardship for ease.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hasan told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah,
m: similarly. And in His statement:
h
And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the right path
, there is clear evidence for what we have said: that these verses of His statement:
h
O you who have believed

, do not say, ‘Ra’ina,’ are an address from God, the Most High, to the believers among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a rebuke from Him to them for a matter that had happened in the past, which the Jews were pleased with, and which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked for them, so God disliked it for them, so He rebuked them for that, and informed them that the Jews are people of deceit, envy, and aggression, and that they wish them harm and seek to cause them calamities, and He forbade them from seeking their advice, and He informed them that whoever among them apostatizes from his religion and exchanges his faith for disbelief has strayed from the right path.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
He has strayed from the right path
As for his saying:
h
He has gone astray

, he means by it: he has gone and deviated. The root of straying from something is to depart from it and deviate, then it is used for something that is lost, and something that is not paid attention to, like their saying about a lazy man who has no mention or notableness: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:109 Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves [i.e., after the truth has become clear to them]. So pardon and overlook until Allah delivers His decision. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
h
He has gone astray
, son of lost, and said, son of said.

i: And like the saying of Al-Akhtal, about something that has perished:
x: I was the speck in a murky, foaming wave, the one who brought it threw it as a gift of misguidance.
Meaning: He perished and went away. What God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
He has strayed from the right path
, is that
h
he has gone astray
from the right path and deviated from it. As for the interpretation of his saying:
h
The straight path
, he means by straight the intention and the method. The root of straight is the middle.

c: It was reported on the authority of Isa bin Omar the grammarian that he said:
m: I continued writing until my straight path was cut off, meaning: my middle path. Hassan bin Thabit said: Woe to the supporters of the Prophet and his descendants after sunset in the midst of the atheists It means in the middle. The Arabs say: He is in the middle of the path, meaning at the level of the path. And the level of the ground, according to them, is its level. As for the path, it is the paved road, changed from paved to path. The interpretation of the statement is: Whoever replaces faith in God and His Messenger with disbelief, and turns away from his religion, has deviated from the path and its clear and established middle way. This statement appears to be a report about the removal of the one who exchanges faith for disbelief from the path, and what is meant by it is the report about him that he abandoned the religion of God which He has chosen for His servants, and made it a path for them to shed to His pleasure, and a way to take to His love and to win His gardens. So He, the Most High, made the path which if one takes His path and walks on it, and adheres to its middle and passes through it, he will be saved and achieve his need, and attain what he seeks for His religion to which He called His servants, for example, for them to attain, by adhering to it and following it, their desires in their afterlife, like the one who attains the necessary path of the path, by adhering to it, his desire for salvation from it, and reaching the place he headed to and intended. And He made the example of the one who deviates from his religion, who is unjust in following what He called him to of worship, in his failure to attain what he hoped to attain through his work in the Hereafter and attain through it in his afterlife, and his departure from what he hoped for of the reward of his work, and his distance from it from his Lord, like the example of the one who deviates from the path and the intention of the way, who does not increase in his wrath in the direction he took, except that he increases in distance from the place of his need, and from the place he headed to and wanted further away.

c: This path that God has informed us
m: about, that whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has gone astray, is
h
the straight path
, which He has commanded us to ask for guidance to, saying: Guide us to
h
the straight path
, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favor (al-Fatihah 1:6-7).

evidence.text: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to me, and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, they said: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the freed slave of Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to me, he said: Saʿid ibn Jubayr or ʿIkrimah narrated to me from Ibn ʿAbbas: Rafiʿ ibn Huraymila and Wahb ibn Zayd said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Bring us a book that you send down to us from the heaven so that we may read it, and cause rivers to gush forth for us, so that we may follow you and believe you!

x: This statement is made clear by the words of God, the Most High, that His address in all these verses, from His saying: O you who believe, do not say, ‘Ra’ina’ and even if He diverted the speech in Himself to addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is only an address from Him to the believers among his companions, and a rebuke from Him to them, and a prohibition against seeking the advice of the Jews and their counterparts from the people of polytheism and accepting their opinions in any of the matters of their religion, and evidence that they used, or some of them used, in their address and questioning of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, harshness, and what he was not allowed to use with him, following the example of the Jews in that or some of them. So their Lord said to them, forbidding them from using that: Do not say to your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as the Jews say to him: Ra’ina!

Rather, say: Look at us and listen, for harming the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is disbelief in me and denial of my right that is due to me upon you to honor and respect him. And for those who disbelieve in me is a painful punishment. The Jews and the polytheists do not wish that any good should descend upon you from your Lord, but many of them wish that they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves for you and for your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
after the truth has become clear to them

regarding Muhammad and that he is a Prophet to them and to all of My creation. It has been said that God Almighty meant Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf when He said: Many of the People of the Scripture wish that they would have been saved.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: regarding his statement: And many of the People of the Book wished, he is Kaʿb bin al-Ashraf.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Sufyan Al-Maamari told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri and Qatadah:
m: Many of the People of the Book wished, he said: Ka’b bin Al-Ashraf.

x: Some of them said: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us, and Abu Kurayb told us, Yunus ibn Bakir told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd ibn Thabit told me, Saeed ibn Jubayr told me, or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Huyay ibn Akhtab and Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab were among the Jews who were most envious of the Arabs, since God had singled them out for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. They were striving to turn people away from Islam as much as they could, so God revealed about them: Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back Al-Bukhari and Muslim.

The statement of the one who said, And many of the People of the Scripture wish refers to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, does not have a clear meaning. This is because Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf is one person, and God, the Most High, has informed us that many of them wish that they could turn the believers back to disbelief after their belief. One person is not called many, in the sense of being numerous in number, unless the one who said that meant by the manner of the abundance with which God described the one with whom He described him in this verse, abundance in honor and high status among his people and clan, as it is said: So-and-so is numerous among the people, meaning abundance in status and rank. If he meant that, then he made a mistake, because God, the Most High, has described them with the description of a group, saying, If they could turn you back to disbelief out of envy after you have believed, so that is evidence that he meant abundance in number.

Or he may have thought that it is a statement that is taken as a report about a group, and what is meant by the report about him is one person, similar to what we said earlier in the verse of Jamil, in which case that would also be a mistake. This is because if the speech has that meaning, then there must be an indication in it that indicates that this is its meaning, and there is no indication in his saying: And many of the People of the Book wish that what is meant by it is one person rather than a large group, so it is permissible to divert the interpretation of the verse to that, and to refer its apparent evidence to something other than what is most common in usage.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Out of envy from themselves.

What He, may He be glorified, means by His saying, out of envy from themselves, is that many of the People of the Book wish for the believers what God, may He be glorified, informed us about them wishing for them, of apostasy from their faith to disbelief, out of envy and malice towards them. Envy is not an adjective for the disbelievers, but rather a verbal noun that comes outside the meaning of the speech whose wording differs from the verbal noun, like when someone says to another: I wished for you what I wished of evil out of envy on my part for you. Envy is a verbal noun from the meaning of his saying: I wished for evil. Because in his saying: I wished that for you, there is a meaning: I envied you for that. So, envy is in the verbal noun, because in his saying: Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, there is a meaning: The People of the Scripture envied you for what God gave you of success, and bestowed upon you of guidance for His religion and belief in His Messenger, and He made you special with it by making His Messenger to you a man from among you, kind and merciful to you, and He did not make him one of them so that you would be followers of them.
So his saying: out of envy is a verbal noun from that meaning.
As for his saying: from themselves, he means by that: from their own selves, just as someone says: I have such and such with you, meaning: I have before you, and just as:

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, his saying: from their own selves, he said: from their own selves. God Almighty informed the believers about them that they wished that for the believers, from themselves, informing them that they were not commanded to do that in their book, and that they do what they do of that with knowledge of God’s prohibition of it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
After the truth has become clear to them
What He, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
After the truth has become clear to them

, is after it became clear to these many of the People of the Book who wish to turn you back as disbelievers after your belief in the truth regarding the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought from his Lord, and the religion to which he called, so that it became clear to them that this is the truth about which they have no doubt, as Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
After the truth has become clear to them
, after it became clear to them that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Islam is the religion of God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah:
m: After the truth became clear to them, he says: It became clear to them that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and they find it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly, and he added to it: So they disbelieved in him out of envy and malice, since he was not from them.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: After the truth became clear to them, he said: The truth is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it became clear to them that he is the Messenger.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: After the truth became clear to them, he said: It became clear to them that he was the Messenger of God.

x: His statement indicates that the disbelief of those whose story he related in this verse in God and His Messenger was out of stubbornness, and with their knowledge and awareness that they were lying about God, as Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman bin Saʿid told us, he said, Bishr bin ʿAmara told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
h
After the truth has become clear to them
, God Almighty says:
h
After the truth has become clear to them
, they were not ignorant of anything of it, but envy led them to deny. So God reproached them, blamed them, and rebuked them with the most severe reproach.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command

By His saying, So pardon, He, the Most High, meant that you should overlook their wrongdoing and mistakes in their opinion that they suggested to you regarding your religion, intending to turn you away from it and trying to make you apostatize after your faith, and what they said to your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Hear, but do not listen, and beware of their tongues and their attack on the religion
r
(An-Nisa’: 46)

. And overlook their ignorance in that until God brings His command, and He will bring about for you from His command what He wills regarding you, and He will decide regarding them what He wills. So He, the Most High, judged regarding them and brought His command, and He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers in Him: “Fight those who do not believe in God and in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what God and His Messenger have forbidden and who do not adopt the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture until they pay the jizyah with willing submission” (al-Tawbah 9:29).

So God, the Most High, abrogated the pardon and forgiveness of them by imposing fighting them on the believers, until their word becomes one with the word of the believers, or they pay the jizyah with their own hands, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: “
h
So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command
. Indeed, God is over all things competent,” and this was abrogated by his statement:
h
Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9

c: Bishr ibn Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command

? So God brought about His command and said: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day (al-Tawbah 9:29), until he reached while they are humbled (al-Tawbah 9:29), meaning: humbled and as a punishment for them. So this verse abrogated what came before it: So pardon Surat Al-Baqarah 2:110 And establish prayer and give zakat, and whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do. and overlook until God brings about His command.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His statement: So pardon and overlook until God brings about His decision, he said: Pardon the People of the Book until God brings about a decision. Then God brought about a decision after that, and said: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day until while they are subdued (al-Tawbah 9:29).

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command
, he said: It was abrogated by: Kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5).

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command
. He said: This is abrogated, abrogated by: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day until His saying, while they are subdued (al-Tawbah 9:29).

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is over all things competent.

We have previously demonstrated the meaning of Al-Qadir, which is the Strong. The meaning of the verse here is: God is able to do whatever He wills with regard to those whose situation I have described to you from the People of the Book and others. If He wills, He will take revenge on them for their stubbornness towards their Lord, and if He wills, He will guide them to what God has guided you to of faith. Nothing He wills is difficult for Him, and nothing He wills to carry out is difficult for Him, because He has the creation and the command.

We have previously demonstrated the meaning of establishing prayer, and that it is performing it within its limits and obligations, and the interpretation of prayer and its origin, and the meaning of giving zakat, and that it is giving it willingly as it was imposed and obligatory, and the meaning of zakat and the differences of those who differ about it, and the evidence indicating the correctness of the statement that we have chosen in that, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this situation. As for His statement:
h
And whatever good you send forth for yourselves
h
you will find it

with God, He, the Most High, means by that: Whatever righteous deeds you do during the days of your life, and send them forth before your death as a reserve for yourselves in your afterlife, you will find its reward with your Lord on the Day of Resurrection, and He will reward you for it.
Good is the work that pleases God.
He said,
h
You will find it
, and the meaning is: You will find its reward, as I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: his saying,
h
You will find it
, means: You will find its reward with God.

x: Because the listeners of that do not need any clear evidence of the intended meaning, as Omar bin Luja said: And the city swam, do not blame it for seeing the moon in their market during the day, but rather he meant: And the people of the city swam. Rather, He, the Most High, commanded them in this place with what He commanded them to do, of establishing prayer, paying zakat, and offering good deeds for themselves, so that they would be purified thereby from the mistake they had made in seeking advice from the Jews, and those who had relied on them, and those who had been rude to them, in addressing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying: Pay attention to us, since establishing prayer was an expiation for sins, and paying zakat was a purification of souls and bodies from the filth of sins, and in offering good deeds was attaining the attainment of God’s pleasure.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do.

This is report from God, may He be glorified, to those believers whom He addressed with these verses, that whatever good or evil they do, secretly or openly, He is All-Seeing of it and nothing is hidden from Him, so He will reward them for good with good, and for evil with the same. This statement, even though it was issued in the form of a report, contains a promise, a threat, a command, and a warning. That is because He informed the people that He is All-Seeing of all their deeds, so that they would find in His obedience, since that was stored up for them with Him until He rewarded them for it, as He said:
h
And whatever good you send forth for yourselves
h
you will find it

with God. And so that they would beware of disobeying Him, since He was aware of its rider, after He had sent it to him with the threat against it. And whatever our Lord, may He be glorified, has threatened against is forbidden, and whatever He has promised against is commanded.
As for his saying: All-Seeing, it is that All-Seeing was changed to All-Seeing, just as Creative was changed to Innovative and Painful was changed to Painful.
God Almighty meant by His saying: And they said, and the Jews and Christians said, He will not enter Paradise.

How were the Jews and Christians combined in this report, given the difference in the statements of the two groups? The Jews prevent the Christians from having a share in the reward of God, and the Christians prevent the Jews from the same?
The meaning of that is different from what you have gone to.

Rather, what he meant by it is: And the Jews said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew? And the Christians said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Christian. But the meaning of the statement, since its meaning was understood by those addressed by it, the two groups were combined in the report about them, so it was said: “They said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian” the verse, meaning the Jews said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew, and the Christians said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Christian. As for his saying: Whoever is Hud, there are two opinions about Hud 11:One of them is that it is the plural of Ha’id, as came ‘Awt is the plural of ‘A’it, and ‘A’udhah is the plural of ‘A’idh, and ‘Hawl’ is the plural of Ha’il, so it is a plural for the masculine and feminine with one word. And Ha’id is the repentant one who returns to the truth.

The other: that it be a source for everyone, as it is said a man who fasts, and people who fast, and a man who breaks his fast, and people who break their fast, and women who break their fast. It has been said that his saying,
h
Except for those who are Jews
, is actually his saying,
h
Except for those who are Jews
, but he deleted the extra ya and reverted to the verb from Jewishness. It has also been said that in Abu’s reading it is:
h
Except for those who are Jews
or Christians. We have previously explained the meaning of Christians, and why they were called that and pluralized in that way, so there is no need to repeat it. As for his saying:
h
Those are their wishful thinking

, it is report from God Almighty about the saying of those who said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, that they are wishful thinking from them that they wish from God without right, argument, proof, or certain knowledge of the truth of what they claim, but rather through false supplications and the wishful thinking of false souls, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Those are their wishful thinking
, wishful thinking that they wish from God that is false.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Those are their desires. He said: Desires: they wished from God something that was not right. Say in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘Produce your proof, if you should be truthful.’

x: This is a command from God, the Most High, to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call those who said: None shall enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, to a just command between all sects: Muslims, Jews, and Christians, which is to establish proof for their claim that they claimed: that none shall enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian. God says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, say to those who claim that none shall enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, and none other than them from among the rest of humanity: Bring your proof, for what you claim about that, and we will accept your claim if you are right in your claim that none shall enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian.
And proof is the statement, argument, and evidence, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Bring your proof, bring your evidence.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Bring your proof bring your argument.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “Say: Bring your proof,” he said: Your argument.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Say, ‘Bring forth your proof,’ meaning your argument.

x: Although this statement appears to be the apparent supplication of those who say, None shall enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, to bring proof for their claim, it means that God has denied their claim and what they said, because they were never able to bring proof for their claim. His statement, Yes, whoever submits his face to God while he is a doer of good, makes clear that what we have mentioned of the statement means that God has denied the Jews and Christians in their claim and what God has said about them. As for the interpretation of his saying: Say, ‘Bring your proof,’ it means: bring it and produce it.
What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: Yes, whoever submits, is that it is not as those who claim: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, but rather
h
whoever submits his face to God
and is a doer of good, he is the one who will enter it and enjoy it, as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: He informed them that whoever enters Paradise is the one who submits his face to God, the verse. We have explained the meaning of bala previously. As for his saying:
h
Whoever submits his face to God

, what he means by submitting his face is humility to His obedience and submission to His command. The root of Islam is submission, because it is from I submit to His command, which is obedience to His command. And the Muslim is called a Muslim because of the submission of his limbs to the obedience of his Lord, as Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ: Yes,
h
whoever submits his face to God

, he says: He is sincere to God. As Zaid bin Amr bin Nufail said: I surrender my face to the one to whom the rain clouds surrender, carrying pure sweet water. He means by that: I surrendered to the obedience of the one to whom the clouds surrendered to their obedience and submitted to him. God, the Most High, singled out the one who He spoke about with His saying: Yes, he who submits his face to God, by submitting his face to Him without the rest of his limbs, because the most honorable of the limbs and organs of the son of Adam is his face, and it is the greatest of them in sanctity and right over him. So if he submits to something his face, which is the most honorable part of his body to him, then the rest of his body is more likely to be more submissive to it. Therefore, the Arabs mention in their logic the report about the thing and add it to his face, and by that they mean the thing itself and its identity, like the saying of Al-A’sha: I interpret the judgment according to its face, not my judgment based on unjust whims He means by his saying: on its face, on what it is in terms of its health and correctness, as Dhu al-Rummah said: So I complied with my concern, and the face of Basil was cleared of the matter, leaving no trace of its disappearance. He means: And the puzzle was revealed from the matter, so it became clear, and what is similar to that, since the beauty and ugliness of everything was in its face, and in describing the face of a thing with what it describes, there was clarification of the essence of the thing and its self. So likewise the meaning of His statement, may He be glorified: Yes,
h
whoever submits his face to God

, only means: Yes, whoever submits his body to God, so his body submits to Him in obedience, and he is a good person in his submission to Him with his body, then he has his reward with his Lord. So He was satisfied with mentioning the face instead of mentioning his body, because the speech indicates the meaning intended by mentioning the face. As for his saying: And he is a doer of good, he means by that: in a state of his doing good. The interpretation of the statement is: Yes, whoever sincerely devotes his obedience to God and his worship of Him, doing good in that action.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
Then he will have his reward with his Lord
, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
Then he will have his reward with his Lord
, is that the Muslim who submits to God and does good will have his reward and recompense for his Islam and obedience to his Lord with God in the Hereafter. What he means by his saying:
h
And there is no fear for them is that the Muslims will face God while they are doing good

, sincere in religion to Him in the Hereafter from His punishment and the torment of His Hellfire, and from what they have done of their deeds. What he means by his saying: nor will they grieve, is that they will not grieve over what they left behind in this world, nor will they be prevented from the bliss that God has prepared for the people of His obedience. Rather, He, the Most High, said: And there is no fear for them, nor shall they grieve, and He had said before:
h
Then he will have his reward with his Lord
, because the of in His statement: Yes,
h
whoever submits his face to God

is in one wording and the meaning of all, so the singularity in His statement: Then he will have his reward is for the wording, and the plural in His statement: And there is no fear for them is for the meaning.

It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about a group of people of the two books, who disputed before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of them said to each other.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, and Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us,
m: they both said, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit told me, he said, Saeed bin Jubayr, or Ikrimah, told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When the Christians of Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Jewish rabbis came to them, and they disputed before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Rafi' bin Huraymila said: You are on nothing! And he disbelieved in Jesus, son of Mary, and in the Gospel. A man from the people of Najran, from the Christians, said: You are on nothing! He denied the prophethood of Moses and disbelieved in the Torah, so God Almighty revealed about that from their saying:
h
And the Jews say
, ‘The Christians are not upon anything,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Jews are not upon anything,’ until His saying: in that over which they differ.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his saying:
h
And the Jews say

, ‘The Christians are not upon anything,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Jews are not upon anything,’ he said: These are the People of the Book who were at the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: As for the interpretation of the verse, it is: The Jews said: The Christians are not right in their religion, and the Christians said: The Jews are not right in their religion! God only informed about them by their saying that to the believers, informing them of each group of them neglecting the ruling of the Book, which they clearly acknowledge as correct and that it is from God, and their denial of what God revealed in it of its obligations. Because the Gospel, which the Christians believe in its correctness and truth, confirms what is in the Torah of the prophethood of Moses, peace be upon him, and what God imposed on the Children of Israel in it of obligations, and the Torah, which the Jews believe in its correctness and truth, confirms the prophethood of Jesus, peace be upon him, and what he brought from God of rulings and obligations. Then each group of them said to the other group what God had informed us about them in His statement:
h
And the Jews say
, ‘The Christians are not upon anything,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Jews are not upon anything,’ while each of the two groups recited his book that testified to his lie in what he had said.

So God, the Most High, informed us that each group of them said what it said of that, knowing that they were falsifying what they said? And they did what they did of their disbelief in what they disbelieved in, knowing that they were heretics in it.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: Were the Jews and Christians after God sent His Messenger on something, so that the group that said that to the other group would be invalidating what they said about that?

We have narrated the report that we mentioned from Ibn Abbas before, that the denial of each group of them was only a denial of the prophethood of the prophet who they claim to believe in and what the other group brought, not to prevent the other group from being on something of their religion at the time when God sent our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of their denial of the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. How can the meaning of that be that each group of them denied that the other group was on something after the sending of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when both groups were denying the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the time when God revealed this verse?
But the meaning of that is:
h
And the Jews said
: The Christians have not been on anything of their religion since they adopted their religion! And the Christians said: The Jews have not been on anything since they adopted their religion!
This is the meaning of the report that we narrated from Ibn Abbas earlier, so God denied both groups in what they said, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the Jews said

, ‘The Christians have nothing,’ he said: Yes! The first Christians were on something, but they innovated and split up, and the Christians said, The Jews have nothing,’ but the people innovated and split up.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And the Jews said
, ‘The Christians have nothing,’ and the Christians said, ‘The Jews have nothing,’ he said, Mujahid said: The first Jews and Christians were on something. As for his statement:
h
And they recite the Book

, he means by it the Book of God, the Torah and the Gospel, and they are witnesses to the two groups of Jews and Christians in disbelief, and their opposition to the command of God that He commanded them with in it, as:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah bin Al-Fadl told us,
m: they both said, Ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, he said, Saad bin Jubayr told me, or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “
h
And they recite the Book

. Thus say those who do not know the same as they say,” meaning each one recites in his book the confirmation of what he disbelieved in, meaning the Jews disbelieve in Jesus, and they have the Torah in it, which contains what God took from them of the covenant on the tongue of Moses to believe in Jesus, peace be upon him, and in the Gospel, from what Jesus brought, the confirmation of Moses and what he brought of the Torah from God, and each one disbelieves in what is in the hand of his companion.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
Thus said those who do not know
, the same as their statement.
The people of interpretation differed about those whom God meant by His statement:
h
Thus said those who do not know
Some of them said what:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Those who do not know said the same as they said, he said: And the Christians said the same as the Jews before them.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Those who do not know said the same as they said, he said: The Christians said the same as the Jews before them.

x: Others said: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said: I said to Ata’: Who are these people who do not know? He said: Nations that existed before the Jews and Christians, and before the Torah and the Gospel.
Some of them said: He meant by that the polytheists of the Arabs, because they were not people of the Book, so they were accused of ignorance, and knowledge was denied them because of that.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Thus said those who do not know
the same as they said, meaning the Arabs, they said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is not upon anything.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Blessed and Exalted, informed us about a people whom He described as ignorant, and denied them knowledge of what the Jews and Christians knew. They said in their ignorance, similar to what the Jews and Christians said to each other, which He informed us about what they said in His statement:
h
And the Jews say

, ‘The Christians have nothing,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Jews have nothing.’ It is possible that they were the polytheists among the Arabs, and it is possible that they were a nation that existed before the Jews and Christians. No nation is more deserving of being said to be the one meant by that than another, since there is no indication in the verse of which of which, nor is there any report of that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, whose proof has been established by the transmission of a just person, nor by the widespread transmission.
God Almighty intended by His statement:
h
Thus said those who do not know

, like their statement, to inform the believers that the Jews and Christians have come with false speech, fabricated lies about God, and denied the prophethood of the prophets and messengers, and they are People of the Book who know that they are lying in what they say, and by their denial of what they deny of their religion they are outside and fabricating against God like what was said by the people of ignorance of God, His Books, and His Messengers, to whom God did not send a messenger nor reveal a book. This verse indicates that whoever commits a sin against God knowing that God has forbidden it, his affliction in his religion is greater than the affliction of someone who commits it out of ignorance. This is because God Almighty greatly rebuked the Jews and Christians for what He rebuked them with in what He told them about them in His statement:
h
And the Jews say
, ‘The Christians have nothing,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Jews have nothing,’ because they are People of the Book.
They said what they said knowing that they were lying.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Then God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: So God will judge and separate between these disputants, some of whom will say to others: You Surat Al-Baqarah 2:114 And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of Allah from being mentioned in them and strives toward their destruction? It is not for those to enter them except in fear. For them in this world is disgrace, and in the Hereafter they will have a great punishment. have nothing of your religion on the Day when creation rises before their Lord from their graves. Then the truthful among them will be distinguished from the false, by rewarding the truthful with what He promised the people of His obedience for their righteous deeds, and punishing the false among them with what He threatened the people of disbelief with for their disbelief in Him, in what they differed about in their religions and sects in this world.

As for the resurrection, it is a source of the saying of the speaker: I stood up and stood up, just as it is said: I visited so-and-so and protected this matter.
