What he meant by the Resurrection is the rising of creation from their graves to their Lord. So the meaning of the Day of Resurrection is the day when creation rises from their graves for their gathering.
We have previously demonstrated that the interpretation of injustice is to put something in the wrong place. And the interpretation of His statement:
h
And who is more unjust

, is: Who is more transgressive and bold against God and disobeys His command than a man who prevents God from being worshipped in the mosques of God? Masajid is the plural of Masjid, which is any place where God is worshipped. We have previously explained the meaning of prostration. The meaning of Masjid is the place where one prostrates to God, just as the place where one sits is called a Majlis, and the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:115 And to God belong the East and the West, so wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. Indeed, God is All-Encompassing and Knowing. place where one descends is called a Manzil, then it is pluralized as Manazil and Majlis, similar to Masjid and Masajid. It has been reported by some Arabs that Masajid is the singular of Masajid, but that is like a mistake on the part of the one who said it.
As for his saying: That His name be mentioned therein, there are two interpretations of this. One of them is that its meaning is:
h
And who is more unjust

than he who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned therein? Then that would be in the accusative case, according to the saying of some of the Arab scholars regarding the absence of the preposition and the attachment of the verb to it. The other aspect: that its meaning is:
h
And who is more unjust

than he who prevents the name of God from being mentioned in His mosques? So in that case the an would be in the accusative case, repeating the location of the mosques and responding to it. As for his saying:
h
And he sought to destroy it

, its meaning is: Who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned therein, and he who seeks to destroy the mosques of God? So sought is in apposition to prevented.
Who is meant by his saying:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being remembered in them and strives toward their destruction
?? And which mosques are they?
The people of interpretation differed on this.
Some of them said: Those who prevented the mosques of God from mentioning His name are the Christians, and the mosque is the Holy House.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And who is more unjust
than he who prevents the mosques of God from mentioning His name therein? They are the Christians.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned in them
and strives toward their destruction? The Christians, they used to throw harmful things into the Holy House and prevent people from praying in it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: Others said: It is Bukhtanasr and his army and those Christians who helped them, and the mosque is the mosque of Jerusalem.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned therein
, His name, the verse, those are the enemies of God, the Christians: their hatred of the Jews led them to help the Babylonian Bukhtanasr the Zoroastrian to destroy the Holy House.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being remembered in them and strives toward their destruction
? He said: It is Bukhtanadr and his companions, he destroyed the Holy House, and the Christians helped him in that.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And who is more unjust

than he who prevents the mosques of God from being remembered and strives toward their destruction? He said: The Romans, they had supported Nebuchadnezzar in destroying the Holy House until he destroyed it, and ordered that corpses be thrown into it. The Romans only helped him in its destruction because the Children of Israel had killed John, son of Zechariah.

x: Others said: Rather, God the Almighty meant in this verse the polytheists of Quraysh, as they prevented the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from entering the Sacred Mosque.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned in them

and strives toward their ruin? He said: These are the polytheists, when they prevented the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Hudaybiyyah from entering Mecca, until he slaughtered his sacrificial animal at Dhu Tuwa and made a truce with them, and said to them: No one was to be prevented from entering this House, and a man would meet the killer of his father or brother in it and nothing would stop him! And they said: Let not the one who killed our fathers on the day of Badr enter upon us while there is still one among us! In his saying:
h
And he sought to destroy it
, he said: When they cut off those who would build it with his remembrance, and come to it for Hajj and Umrah.

x: The most correct of the interpretations that I mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse is the statement of those who said: God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned in them

? the Christians. That is because they are the ones who sought to destroy the Holy House, and helped Nebuchadnezzar in that, and prevented the believers of the Children of Israel from praying in it after Nebuchadnezzar left them for his country. The evidence for the correctness of what we have said in this regard is the establishment of the argument that there is no statement regarding the meaning of this verse except one of the three statements that we have mentioned, and that there is no mosque that God the Almighty meant by His saying: and strove toward its destruction except one of the two mosques: either the mosque of Jerusalem or the Sacred Mosque.

Since this is the case, and it is known that the polytheists of Quraysh never strove toward the destruction of the Sacred Mosque, because they had prevented the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and his companions from praying in it at some times, it is correct and proven that those whom God the Almighty described as striving toward the destruction of His mosques are not those whom God described as building them. Since the polytheists of Quraysh built the Sacred Mosque in the pre-Islamic era, and their pride was in building it, even though some of their actions in it were not in a way that God would be pleased with from them. Another is that the verse before His statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned in them

? proceeded with the report about the Jews and Christians and the condemnation of their actions, and the verse after it alerted to the condemnation of the Christians and the report about their fabrication of their Lord, and there was no mention of the Quraysh or the polytheists of the Arabs, nor of the Sacred Mosque before it, so the report is directed by the statement of God Almighty:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned in them
? to them and to the Sacred Mosque.

Since this is the case, then what is more deserving of the verse is that its interpretation should be directed to it, which is what was similar to the story of the verse before it and the verse after it, since its report was similar and similar to their report, unless there is an argument that must be accepted to the contrary, even if their stories agree and are confused. If someone thinks that what we have said about this is not so, since the Muslims were never obligated to pray in the Holy Mosque, and were prevented from praying in it, then they resort to interpreting his statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned therein

? to mean the mosque of Jerusalem, then he is mistaken in what he thinks about that. That is because God, the Most High, only mentioned the injustice of those who prevented those whose obligation was to pray in Jerusalem from the believers of the Children of Israel, and He intended them by the report about them with injustice and striving to destroy the mosque.
And if he indicated by the generality of his statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned therein

? that everyone who prevents someone praying in a mosque of God, whether his prayer in it is obligatory or voluntary, and everyone who strives to destroy it, then he is among the transgressors and oppressors.
The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty:
h
It is not for them to enter it except in fear

This is report from God Almighty about those who prevented the mosques of God from mentioning His name in them, that He has forbidden them to enter the mosques that they sought to destroy, and prevented the believing servants of God from mentioning God Almighty in them, as long as they were at war, except out of fear and dread of punishment for entering them, like the one who:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It was not for them to enter them except in fear, and they are like that today, there is no Christian in Jerusalem except that he was beaten severely, and the punishment was more severe than that.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, God Almighty said:
m: h
It is not for them to enter it except in fear
, and they are the Christians, so they do not enter the mosque except as thieves, and if they are able to do so, they will be punished.

c: Musa told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
It is not for them to enter it except in fear
, so there is no Roman on earth who enters it today except in fear that his neck will be struck, or he has been frightened by paying the jizya, so he pays it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
It is not for them to enter it except in fear

, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out: ‘No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked.’” He said: So the polytheists began to say: O God, we were prevented from descending! Rather, it was said:
h
It is not for them to enter it except in fear

, so it was brought out in the form of a report on all of them, and it is a report on whoever prevents the mosques of God from having His name mentioned therein, because who is in the meaning of all of them, if its wording is the same.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
For them in this world is disgrace
, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
As for the words of God Almighty: For them, it means: those about whom He informed that they prevented the mosques of God from mentioning His name in them. As for His words:
h
For them in this world is disgrace

, it means by disgrace: shame, evil, and humiliation, either killing and captivity, or humiliation and degradation by paying the jizyah, as Al-Hasan told us, he said, ʿAbd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muʿammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
For them in this world is disgrace
, he said: They pay the jizyah willingly while they are humiliated.

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
For them in this world is disgrace

. As for their disgrace in this world, when the Mahdi rises and Constantinople is conquered, he will kill them. That is disgrace. As for the great torment, it is the torment of Hell, which will not be lightened for its people, nor will they be killed therein so that they die. The interpretation of the verse is: For them in this world is humiliation, disgrace, killing, and captivity for preventing the mosques of God from being mentioned in them and striving to destroy them. And for them, for their disobedience and disbelief in their Lord and striving to spread corruption on earth, is the torment of Hell, which is the great torment. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:115 And to God belong the East and the West, so wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. Indeed, God is All-Encompassing and Knowing.

x: By His statement,
h
To God belong the East and the West

, God Almighty means that they belong to God and that He controls them, just as it is said: This house belongs to so-and-so. He means by that: that it belongs to him, as a possession. So His statement,
h
To God belong the East and the West

, means that they belong to Him, as a possession and as a creation. The east is the place where the sun rises, and it is the place where it rises, just as the place where it rises is called matla’, with a kasra on the lam, and as we explained in the meaning of mosques earlier.
Or did God have only one east and one west, so that it was said:
h
To God belong the east and the west

The meaning of that is not what you have gone to. Rather, the meaning of that is: To God belongs the East from which the sun rises every day, and the West in which it sets every day. So its interpretation, since that was its meaning, is: To God belongs what is between the two parts of the East and what is between the two parts of the West, since the sun rises every day from a place in it and does not return to its rising from it until the following year, and likewise its setting every day.
Even if the interpretation of that is what you mentioned, then God owns everything below Him? Creation is His creation!
Yes!
How did he specify the Easts and the Wests with the report that they belong to him in this place, and not to all other things besides them?

The people of interpretation differed about the reason why God singled out the mention of that with what He singled it out with in this place. We will explain who is more deserving of the interpretation of the verse, after mentioning their statements on that.

Some of them said: God, the Most High, singled out that with the report, because the Jews used to direct their faces towards Jerusalem in their prayers, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do that for a period, then they turned towards the Kaaba. The Jews were surprised by that action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
and they said
: What turned them away from the qiblah that they were facing? God, the Most High, said to them: The Easts and the Wests are all Mine. I turn the faces of My servants as I will therein,
h
so wherever you turn
, there is the Face of God.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The first thing that was abrogated from the Qur’an was the qiblah. That is because when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, and most of its people were Jews, God, the Most High, commanded him to face Jerusalem. The Jews were happy. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced it for about a month. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved the direction of the qiblah of Abraham, peace be upon him, so he would supplicate and look at the sky. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven until His saying: So turn your faces toward it (al-Baqarah 2:144). The Jews were suspicious of that and said: What has turned them away from the qiblah which they used to face? (al-Baqarah 2:142). Then God, the Almighty, revealed: “Say:
h
To God belong the east and the west
,” and He said: Wherever you turn, there is the face of God (al-Baqarah 2:142).

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: Rather, God revealed this verse before He imposed on His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and on the believers in him, to face the direction of the Sacred Mosque. Rather, He revealed it to him to teach His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions that they may face their faces in prayer wherever they wish, in the directions of the East and the West, because they do not face in any direction or direction except that He, may His praise be glorified, is in that direction or direction, because He owns the East and the West, and that no place is devoid of Him, as He, may He be glorified and exalted, said: And not nearer than that or more but that He is with them wherever they are (al-Mujadilah 58:7). They said: Then that was abrogated by the obligation that was imposed on them, to face the direction of the Sacred Mosque.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The words of God Almighty: And
h
to God belong the east and the west
h
so wherever you turn
, there is the face of God, then that was abrogated after that, and God said: And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram (al-Baqarah 2:149, 150).

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:116 And they say, "God has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him. regarding his statement:
h
So wherever you turn
, there is the face of God, he said: It is the qibla, then the qibla was replaced by the Sacred Mosque.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Minhal told us, Hammam told us, Yahya told us,
m: I heard Qatada regarding the statement of God:
h
So wherever you turn

, there is the Face of God, he said: They used to pray towards Jerusalem, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca before the migration. After the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated, he prayed towards Jerusalem for sixteen months, then he turned after that towards the Kaaba, the Sacred House. Then God abrogated it in another verse: We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased to And wherever you are, turn your faces towards it Al-Baqarah 2:144. He said: So this verse abrogated what came before it regarding the matter of the qiblah.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I heard him, meaning Zaid, say: The Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “
h
So wherever you turn

, there is the Face of God. Indeed, God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These are Jewish people facing one of the Houses of God. If only we could face it! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced it for sixteen months, and it reached him that the Jews were saying: By God, Muhammad and his companions did not know where their qiblah was until we guided them! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked that, and he raised his face to the sky, and God, may He be exalted, said: We have certainly seen the turning of your face, toward the heaven (al-Baqarah 2:144).

x: Others said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as permission from God Almighty for him to pray voluntary prayers wherever he faces, east or west, while traveling, in combat, in times of intense fear and when fighting in obligatory prayers.

c: And He informed him that
m: wherever he faces, he is there, by His saying:
h
To God belong the east and the west
h
so wherever you turn
, there is the face of God.

x: Those who said that: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Umar: that he used to pray wherever his mount faced him, and he mentioned that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do that, and he interpreted this verse: Wherever you turn, there is the face of God.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said:
m: This verse, Wherever you turn, there is the face of God, was revealed so that you may pray voluntarily wherever your mount takes you during a journey. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Mecca, he would pray voluntarily on his mount, nodding his head toward Medina.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed about a people who were blind to the direction of the Qiblah and did not know which side it was, so they lined up in different directions. Then God the Almighty said to them: Mine are the Easts and the Wests,
h
so wherever you turn
your faces, there is My Face, and it is your Qiblah, teaching them that their prayers are valid.

Those who said this: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Abu al-Rabi’ al-Samman told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Ubaydullah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of his father, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a dark, black night, and we stopped at a place. A man began to take stones and build a place of prayer in which to pray. When morning came, we found that we had prayed facing a direction other than the Qiblah. We said: O Messenger of God, we have prayed this night facing a direction other than the Qiblah! Then God the Almighty revealed: “And
h
to God belong the East and the West
h
so wherever you turn
, there is the Face of God. Indeed, God is All-Encompassing and Knowing.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told me, he said, Hammad told us, he said,
m: I said to Al-Nakha’i: I woke up, or he said: I was awakened, Al-Tabari was not sure, and there were clouds in the sky, so I prayed facing the qiblah. He said: Your prayer is valid. God Almighty says:
h
So wherever you turn
, there is the face of God.

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Ash’ath al-Samman, on the authority of Asim ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a dark night on a journey, and we did not know where the qiblah was, so we lined up, and each one of us lined up on his own side, then we came in the morning and mentioned it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God Almighty revealed:
h
So wherever you turn
, there is the face of God.

i: Others said:
x: Rather, this verse was revealed about the Negus, because the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disputed about his affair, because he died before praying towards the Qiblah, so God the Almighty said: The Easts and the Wests are all Mine, so whoever turns his face towards any of them, intending Me and seeking My obedience thereby, will find Me there.

Meaning by this that even though the Negus did not pray towards the Qiblah, he did turn his face towards some of the directions of the Easts and the Wests, seeking thereby the pleasure of God the Almighty in his prayer.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Hisham bin Muadh told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your brother the Negus has died, so pray over him. They said: Should we pray over a man who is not a Muslim? He said: Then the verse was revealed: ‘And indeed, among the People of the Scripture is he who believes in God and in what was revealed to you and what was revealed to them, humbly submissive to God.’”
r
(Al Imran 3:199)
. Qatada said: They said: He did not pray towards the Qiblah! Then God Almighty revealed: “
h
To God belong the East and the West
h
So wherever you turn
, there is the Face of God.”

x: The correct statement in this regard is that God, the Most High, mentioned specifically the report about the East and the West in this verse, that they are His possession, even though there is nothing that does not belong to Him, as a notification from Him to His believing servants that He owns them and the creation between them, and that all of them, since He owns them, must obey Him in what He commands and forbids them, and in what He imposes upon them of obligations, and to turn in the direction to which they are directed, since it is the rule of slaves to obey their Master. So He excluded the report about the East and the West, and what is meant by it is: the creation between them, in the manner that I have explained, from the sufficiency of the report about the reason for the thing, from mentioning it and the report about it, as it was said: And they made the calf drink into their hearts (al-Baqarah 2:93), and the like.

The meaning of the verse is: To God belongs the kingdom of creation between the East and the West. He makes them worship Him as He wills, and He rules over them as He wills. They must obey Him. So turn your faces, O believers, toward My face, for wherever you turn your faces, there is My face. As for the statement about this verse, is it abrogating or abrogated, or is it neither abrogating nor abrogated? The correct statement is that it came as a general statement, but the intended meaning is specific. This is because His statement,
h
So wherever you turn

, there is the Face of God is possible: wherever you turn while traveling, during your voluntary prayers, and during your combat. Your enemy is in your voluntary and obligatory prayers, for there is the face of God, as Ibn Omar and Al-Nakha’i said, and those who said that from those we mentioned earlier. It is possible:
h
So wherever you turn

on the earth of God, you are there, then there is the Qiblah of God to which you direct your faces, because it is possible for you to turn towards the Kaaba from it, as Abu Kurayb said, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, and An-Nadr ibn Arabi, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
So wherever you turn
, there is the Face of God, he said: The Qiblah of God, so wherever you are, east or west, face it.
Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:

c: Ibrahim informed me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Wherever you are, there is a qiblah to which you face. He said: The Kaaba. It is possible:
h
So wherever you turn

your faces in your supplication, there is My face, I will answer your supplication, as Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: When the verse Call upon Me, I will respond to you
r
(Ghafir 40:65)
was revealed, they said: To where? So the verse
h
So wherever you turn
, there is the Face of God was revealed. Since the Almighty’s saying:
h
So wherever you turn

, there is the face of God, is open to the aspects we mentioned, no one can claim that it is abrogating or abrogated, except with an argument that must be accepted. Because abrogation can only occur with abrogated things, and no proof has been established that must be accepted that his statement:
h
So wherever you turn
, there is the Face of God means:
h
So wherever you turn

your faces in your prayer, there is your Qiblah? Nor that it was revealed after the prayer of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and his companions towards Jerusalem, as a command from God the Almighty to them to face the Kaaba, so it is permissible to say: It is the abrogator of the prayer towards Jerusalem, since there were some scholars from the companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and the imams of the followers who denied that it was revealed in that meaning, and there is no confirmed report from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that it was revealed in that regard, and the difference of opinion about it existed as described. Nor, since it did not abrogate what we described, did its proof stand that it was abrogated, since it was possible for what we described: that it came in a general way, and its meaning is: in one situation rather than another if what was meant by it was the direction in prayer and in every situation, if what was meant by it was supplication and other meanings that we mentioned. We have demonstrated in our book, The Book of Explanation of the Principles of Rulings, that there is no abrogating verse in the Qur’an and the reports of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except that which negates an established ruling and obliges the servants to impose it, and does not have the apparent or hidden meaning of anything other than that. But if it has the meaning of something other than that, such as being in the sense of exception, or specificity and generality, or ambiguous, or explanatory, then the abrogating and abrogated are separate, so there is no need to repeat it in this place, and there is no abrogated except that which is negated, whose ruling and obligation have already been established. Neither of these two meanings is correct for his statement:
h
So wherever you turn

, there is the face of God, with an argument that must be accepted, so it is said about it: it is abrogating or abrogated. As for his saying: Wherever, its meaning is: wherever. As for his saying: Turn away, what is more appropriate for its interpretation is: you turn toward it and towards it, as someone says: I turned my face toward it and I turned it toward it, meaning I faced it and confronted it. We only said that this is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, because of the consensus of the proof that this is its interpretation, and the anomaly of those who interpreted it to mean: you turn away from it and turn your backs on it, so what you are turning toward is the Face of God, meaning the Qiblah Surat Al-Baqarah 2:116 And they say, "God has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him. of God. As for his saying: then, it means: there. There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of his statement:
h
Then there is the Face of God

x: Some of them said: The interpretation of that is: Then there is the Qiblah of God, meaning by that His Face to which He directed them.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Then there is the Face of God
, he said: The Qiblah of God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibrahim told me, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Wherever you are, you have a qiblah that you face.

x: Others said: The meaning of God Almighty’s saying:
h
Then there is the face of God
, is that there is God, Blessed and Exalted be He.
Others said: The meaning of his saying:
h
Then there is the face of God
, is that then you will attain, by turning to Him, the pleasure of God, who has the noble face.
Others said: He meant by the face the one with the face. And those who said this statement said: The face of God is an attribute of Him.
What is this verse compared to the one before it?

It has a continuation. Rather, the meaning of that is: Who is more unjust than the Christians who prevented the servants of God from mentioning His name in His mosques, and sought to destroy them? And
h
to God belong the East and the West
h
so wherever you turn

your faces, remember Him, for His face is there. His bounty, His land, and His country encompass you, and He knows what you do. And let not the destruction of those who destroyed the mosque of Jerusalem, and the prevention of those who prevented the remembrance of God in it, prevent you from remembering God wherever you are in the land of God, seeking thereby His face.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, God is All-Encompassing and All-Knowing.

By His saying, Vast, He means that He is sufficient for all of His creation with sufficiency, favor, generosity, and management. As for his saying: All-Knowing, it means that He is All-Knowing of their actions. Nothing of them is hidden from Him, nor is it hidden from His knowledge. Rather, He is All-Knowing of all of them.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And they say, ‘God has taken a son.’
Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.
What He, the Most High, means by His statement,
h
And they said

, ‘God has taken a son,’ is those who prevented the mosques of God from mentioning His name in them. They said is connected to His statement, And he strove toward its destruction. The interpretation of the verse: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned in them and strives toward their destruction and says, God has taken a son, and they are the Christians who claimed that Jesus was the son of God. So God, the Most High, said, denying what they said of that and negating what they attributed and added to it with their lies and slander: Glory be to Him, meaning by it: sanctification and absolution from having a son, and being exalted and elevated above that. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of the speaker’s saying, Glory be to God, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

Then He, the Most High, informed us that He owns and creates what is in the heavens and the earth. The meaning of that is: How can the Messiah be a son of God, when it is not impossible that he is either in some of these places, either in the heavens or on the earth, and God owns what is in them? And if the Messiah were a son, as you claim, he would not be like the rest of what is in the heavens and the earth of His creation and His servants, in the manifestation of the signs of creation in him.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: The meaning of that is: obedient.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
All are obedient to Him
, obedient.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
All are obedient to Him
, he said: Obedient. He said: The obedience of the disbeliever in the prostration of his shadow.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly except that he added: with the prostration of his shadow while he was unwilling.

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
All are obedient to Him
, meaning:
h
All are obedient to Him
on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told me, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned it, on the authority of Ikrimah:
h
All are obedient to Him
, he said: obedience.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Munjab bin Al-Harith,
m: who said: It was narrated to us by Bishr bin Amara, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Qantun means obedient.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Everyone is obedient to Him.
Those who said this were:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: Everyone is obedient to Him, everyone is obedient to Him.

x: Others said: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
All are obedient to Him

, he said: All are standing for Him on the Day of Resurrection. In Arabic, there are several forms of supplication. One of them is obedience, another is standing, and the third is refraining from speaking or abstaining from it. The first meaning of qunut in His statement:
h
All are obedient to Him

, is obedience and acknowledgment of servitude to God, the Almighty, as witnessed by their bodies, with what is in them of traces of creation and evidence of the Oneness of God, the Almighty, and that God, the Most High, is their Creator and Maker. This is because God, the Most High, has proven those who claim that God has a son to be liars, by His statement: Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, in dominion and creation.

Then He informed about everything in the heavens and the earth that it is acknowledged by its evidence of its Lord and Creator, and that God, the Most High, is its Creator and Maker. Even if some of them deny this, their tongues submit to Him in obedience, by their testimony to Him with the traces of creation in them in this regard, and that the Messiah is one of them. So how can God have a son when this is His description? Some of those whose knowledge is insufficient to direct the speech in its direction have claimed that His statement:
h
All are obedient to Him

, is specific to the people of obedience and is not general. It is not permissible to claim a specificity in a verse that appears to be general, except with an argument that must be accepted, as we have explained in our book, The Book of Explanation of the Principles of Rulings. This is report from God Almighty that the Messiah, whom the Christians claimed was the son of God, is their liar, as are the heavens and the earth and everything in them, either verbally or by implication.

That is because God Almighty informed about all of them, about their obedience to him, and their acknowledgment of their servitude to him, following His statement: And they said, ‘God has taken a son,’ so this indicates the truth of what we said.
God Almighty means by His saying:
h
Originator of the heavens and the earth

, their Creator. Rather, it is a verb inflected to faʿil, just as al-mâlim was inflected to aleem and al-musmâʿ to samiʿ. The meaning of al-mubdiʿ is the one who creates and innovates something that no one has ever created or innovated before him. That is why the innovator in religion is called an innovator, because he innovates something that no one else has ever done before him. Likewise, every innovator who does an action or a statement that no one else has ever done before him, the Arabs call him an innovator. An example of this is the saying of al-Aʿsha, the blind man of Banu Thaʿlabah, in praise of Hawdhah ibn Ali al-Hanafi: He takes heed of the words of the leaders of men if they show him firmness, or whatever he wishes he innovates. That is, He does whatever He wills. This is evident in the saying of Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj: O you who are the most treacherous, the most obedient, the most obedient to God!

It is not right to be creative Meaning: to say something about religion that was not in it. The meaning of the words: Glory be to God! How can He have a son when He is the Owner of what is in the heavens and the earth? All of them bear witness to Him by indicating His Oneness and acknowledge His obedience, while He is their Creator, Maker, and Originator, without any origin or example for them to follow? This is an announcement from God, the Most High, to His servants that among those who testify to this is the Messiah, whom they attribute to God, the Most High, as his son. It is also an announcement from Him to them that the One who created the heavens and the earth without an origin and without an example is the One who created the Messiah without a father by His power.
A group of the people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said about this.
Those who said this mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: The
h
Originator of the heavens and the earth
, meaning: He originated their creation, and no one shared with Him in their creation.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: The
h
Originator of the heavens and the earth
, meaning: He originated them, created them, and nothing was created before them to be imitated.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And when He decrees a matter

, and when He decides a matter and makes it certain. The root of every judgment is: to rule and to finish it. From this, the ruler among the people is called the judge between them, because he separates the judgment between the opponents, and concludes the ruling between them, and finishes it with it. From this, the dead person is called: it has been decided, meaning: he has finished with the world and separated from it. From this, it is said: I am amazed by so-and-so, meaning: it is not cut off. From this, it is said: the day has passed, if it has ended. From this, the saying of God, the Almighty: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him
r
(Al-Isra’: 23)
, meaning: He decided the judgment in it between His servants, by His command to them to do so. Likewise, His saying: And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture
r
(Al-Isra’: 41)
, meaning We informed them of this and told them about it, so We finished it for them.

From this, the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb: And they are narrated on them, David ruled them or the making of the heavy-duty swords followed. It is narrated: They exchanged two narratives. What he means by his saying: He judged them, he ruled them. And from this is the saying of the other in praise of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. I did things and then left with troubles in my sleeves that never came to an end. It is narrated: Buwaij. As for his saying:
h
He only says to it
, ‘Be,’ and it is, he means by that: And if He decrees a matter and makes it certain, He only says to that matter, Be, and that matter is as God commanded it to be and willed it.
If someone were to say to us: What is the meaning of His statement:
h
And when He decrees a matter
h
He only says to it

, ‘Be,’ and it is? In what state does He say to the matter that He decrees, Be? Is it in a state of non-existence, and that is a state in which His command is not permissible, since it is impossible for Him to command except the one commanded, so if the one commanded is not present, the command is impossible? And just as it is impossible for a command to be commanded without a commander, so it is impossible for a commander to command except to the one commanded. Or does He say that to him in a state of his existence? And that is a state in which it is not permissible for Him to command it to occur, because it is a new and existing thing. And it is not said to an existing thing, Be, except without the meaning of commanding it to occur? It was said: The interpreters have disputed the meaning of that.

We will inform you of what they said about it, and the reasons that each group of them relied on for what he said about that: Some of them said: This is report from God, may He be glorified, about His inevitable command in the form of a decree for whomever He decrees a decree upon from among His existing creation, that if He commands him with a command, His decree will be carried out and His command will go through. Similar to His command of the Children of Israel to be despised apes, while they were present at the time when He commanded them to do that, and He made His decree inevitable upon them with what He decreed concerning them. And like the one whom the earth swallowed up with his home, and what is similar to that of His command and decree concerning whoever was present from among His creation, at the time when His inevitable command was upon him.
Those who said this statement directed his statement:
h
And when He decrees a matter
h
He only says to it
, ‘Be,’ and it is, to the specific rather than the general.

Others said: Rather, the verse is general in its appearance, so no one has the right to refer it to an inner meaning without an argument that must be accepted. He said: God knows everything that exists before it exists. Since that is the case, the things that did not exist while they existed, due to His knowledge of them before they existed, are similar to those that exist. So it is permissible for Him to say to them: Be, and to command them to emerge from a state of nonexistence into a state of existence, due to the conception of all of them to Him, and His knowledge of them in a state of nonexistence.

Others said: Rather, the verse, even if its apparent meaning is general, its interpretation is specific. Because the command is not permissible except for one who is commanded, as I described before. They said: Since that is the case, the interpretation of the verse is:
h
And when He decrees a matter
: such as bringing a dead person back to life, or killing a living person, and the like, then He only says to a living person: Be dead, or to a dead person: Be alive, and other similar commands.

Others said: Rather, this is from God Almighty, report about everything that He creates and brings into being, that if He decrees it, creates it, and brings it into being, it will be and exist. There is no statement there, according to those who say this, except the existence of the created and the occurrence of what is decreed. They said: Rather, the statement of God Almighty:
h
And when He decrees a matter
h
He only says to it

, ‘Be,’ and it is, is similar to the statement of The speaker: So-and-so nodded his head, or gestured with his hand, if he moved his head, or gestured with his hand, and did not say anything, and as Abu al-Najm said: And the sides said to the belly, Go ahead, and it overflowed like a furious phoenix. There is no saying there, because he meant that the back has joined the stomach, as Amr bin Hammah Al-Dawsi said: So I became like an eagle whose chicks fly away. When it tries to fly, it is said: Qa’.
There is no saying there, but its meaning is: If he tries to fly, he will fall, and as the other said: The basin was filled and he said: Take it easy, my belly is full.
The most correct of the sayings about His statement:
h
And when He decrees a matter
h
He only says to it

, ‘Be,’ and it is, is to say: It is general in everything that God decrees and creates. Because the apparent meaning of that is apparent generality, and it is not permissible to refer the apparent to the hidden in interpretation without proof, as we have explained in our book, Kitab al-Bayan ‘an Usul al-Ahkam. Since that is the case, then God’s command to something, when He wills to create it into existence by His saying, Be, in the state of His will for it to be created, does not precede the existence of that which He wills to create and create, nor does His command to be and exist, nor does it come after it. So it is not permissible for a thing to be commanded to exist and willed as such, except that it exists, nor for it to exist, except that it is commanded to exist and willed as such.
Similar to His statement:
h
And when He decrees a matter
h
He only says to it

, ‘Be,’ and it is, is His statement: “And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will emerge” (al-Rum 30:25). The emergence of the people from their graves does not precede God’s call Surat Al-Baqarah 2:118 And those who do not know say, "Why does God not speak to us or a sign come to us?" Thus said those before them the like of their statement. Their hearts are alike. We have made clear the signs for a people who are certain. nor does it lag behind it. And he asks who claims that his statement,
h
And when He decrees a matter
h
He only says to it

, ‘Be,’ and it is, is specific to interpretation, based on the argument that commanding a non-existent is not permissible from the call of the people of the graves, before they emerge from their graves, or after that, or is it specific to creation?
He will not say anything about that except that the same will be required in the end.

i: And he asks those who claimed that the meaning of His Most High’s saying:
h
He only says to it
, ‘Be,’ and it is, is similar to the saying of the speaker: So-and-so said with his head or his hand, if he moved it and gestured, and similar to the saying of the poet:
x: She says, if I ward off her wrath: Is this his religion and my religion forever?

And what is similar to that: They did not hit the mark in the language, nor did they follow the Book of God and what the evidence indicated to be correct. So it is said to those who say that: God, the Most High, mentioned Himself, informed us that when He decrees a matter, He says to it: Be. Do you deny that He would say that? If they deny it, they have denied the Qur’an and left the religion.

Rather, we acknowledge it, but we claim that this is similar to the saying of the one who said: The wall said, so it leaned, and there is no saying there, but rather it is a report about the leaning of the wall. They were told: Do you permit someone who reports that the wall is leaning to say: The only thing the wall says when it wants to lean is to say this and it leans? If they allow that, they have departed from the well-known speech of the Arabs, and contradicted their logic and what is known in their language. And if they say: That is not permissible.

God Almighty informed them about Himself that His saying to a thing when He wants it is to say to it: Be, and it is. So He informed His servants of His saying by which the thing is, and He described and confirmed it. And that, according to you, is not permissible in the expression of something that has no speech or explanation, such as the saying of the one who says: The wall said, and it leaned. So how did they not know by that the difference between the meaning of God’s saying:
h
And when He decrees a matter
h
He only says to it

, “Be, and it is,” and the saying of the one who says: The wall said, and it leaned? There is a place other than this to explain the corruption of this statement, in which we will come to the statement sufficiently, God willing.
If the matter in His Most High’s saying:
h
And when He decrees a matter
h
He only says to it

, ‘Be,’ and it is, is what we have described, that the state of His commanding something to exist is the state of the existence of the thing commanded to exist, then He has made clear that what is more deserving of His saying, and it is, is the nominative case in apposition to His saying, He says. Because the state of saying and existence is one. It is similar to the saying of the speaker: So-and-so repented and was guided, and so-and-so was guided and repented, because no one repents except while he is guided, and no one is guided except while he is repentant. Likewise, it is not possible for God to command something to exist except while it exists, and no thing exists except when He commands it to exist. Therefore, whoever permitted the accusative case of faykun from the reading Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, “Be, and it is” (al-Nahl 16:40), in the meaning we described, meaning: that We say, and it is.

As for the one who raised that, he saw that the report was completed when he said: If We wanted it, We would say to it, ‘Be.’ Since it was known that if God decreed His judgment on something, what was decreed would exist. Then He began by saying: And it is, as the Most High said: That We may make clear to you and cause to remain in the wombs what We will (al-Hajj 22:5), and as Ibn Ahmar said: He treats a barren woman who has become exhausted by him, so that he can impregnate her and produce young camels. He wants: So he produces it as a dialogue. So the meaning of the verse is: And they say, God has taken a son. Glory be to Him, that He should have a son. Rather, He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth and everything in them. All of that is an acknowledgement of His servitude by indicating His Oneness. How can He have a son when He is the One who created the heavens and the earth without an origin, just as He created the Messiah without a father by His power and authority, for whom nothing He wills is impossible.
Rather,
h
He only says to it
when He decrees it and wants to create it: Be, and it exists as He wanted and willed. So was the creation and establishment of the Messiah, when He wanted to create him without a father.

evidence.text: Therefore, whoever permitted the accusative case of faykun from the reading Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, “Be, and it is” (al-Nahl 16:40), in the meaning we described, meaning: that We say, and it is.

x: The people of interpretation differed about who God meant by His saying:
h
And those who do not know say
h
Why does God not speak to us
Some of them said: He meant the Christians by that.
He mentioned those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And those who do not know say
h
Why does God not speak to us
or a sign come to us?’ He said: The Christians say it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, and he added to it:
h
And those who do not know said
, meaning the Christians.

x: Others said: Rather, God meant by that the Jews who were in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah bin Al-Fadl told us,
m: they both said, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me, he said, Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Rafi bin Huraymila said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you are a messenger from God as you say, then say to God Almighty, so let Him speak to us so that we may hear His speech! So God Almighty revealed regarding that from His saying:
h
And those who do not know say
h
Why does God not speak to us
or a sign come to us?’ the entire verse.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant the polytheists of the Arabs.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us:
m: He said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us: He said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
And those who do not know say
h
Why does God not speak to us
or a sign come to us?’ They are the infidel Arabs.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
And those who do not know say
h
Why does God not speak to us
?’ He said: They are the infidel Arabs.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And those who do not know say
h
Why does God not speak to us
?’ As for those who do not know, they are the Arabs. The most correct and true of these statements is the statement of the one who said: God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And those who do not know said

the Christians, and not others. Because this is in the context of God’s information about them, and their fabrication of Him, and their claim that He has a son, so He, the Most High, said, informing about them in what He informed about them of their misguidance: that along with their fabrication of lies against God by saying: God has taken a son, they wished falsehoods from God, so they said out of ignorance of God and their status with Him, while they are polytheists with God:
h
Why does God not speak to us

as He speaks to His messengers and prophets, or why does a sign not come to us as it came to them? And it is not appropriate for God to speak except to His friends, and He does not give a miraculous sign in response to the claim of a claimant except to the one who is right in his claim and calls to God and His Oneness. As for the one who is lying in his claim and calls to slander against Him, and claims sons and daughters for Him, then it is not permissible for God, the Most High, to speak to him, or to give him a miraculous sign that would support his lie and slander against Him. As for the one who claims that God meant by His saying,
h
And those who do not know said

, the Arabs, he is saying something for which there is no evidence of its truth, nor is there any proof of its reality in the apparent meaning of the Book. If the statement comes to that, then its error is clearly evident, because he has claimed something for which there is no evidence of its truth. And such a claim would not be difficult for anyone. As for the meaning of his saying:
h
Why does God not speak to us
? it means:
h
Why does God not speak to us

, as Al-Ashab bin Ramila said: You consider the sterility of the camel to be your Surat Al-Baqarah 2:119 Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and you will not be asked about the companions of Hellfire. greatest glory, Bani Dhutri, if it were not for the masked camel. Meaning: Why don't you consider the convincing quantity as:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Why does God not speak to us
? He said:
h
Why does God not speak to us

x: As for the verse, the meaning of the verse has been established previously, that it is a sign.

c: God only informed us about them that they said:
m: Why does not a sign come to us regarding what we want and ask for, as it came to the prophets and messengers? So the Almighty said:
h
Thus said those before them
, similar to their saying.

x: The people of interpretation differed as to who God meant by His saying:
h
Thus said those before them
, like their saying.
Some of them said about that as follows:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Thus said those before them
, like their saying, meaning the Jews.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Those before them said, meaning the Jews.

x: Others said: They are the Jews and Christians, because those who do not know are the Arabs.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zurai’ told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Those before them, meaning the Jews, Christians, and others.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: They said: He means the Arabs, as the Jews and Christians said before them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
Thus said those before them
, like their saying, meaning the Jews and Christians.

x: We have shown that those whom God, the Most High, meant by His statement,
h
And those who do not know say
h
Why does God not speak to us

?’ are the Christians, and those who said the same thing are the Jews: They asked Moses, peace be upon him, to show them their Lord openly, and to let them hear the words of their Lord, as we have explained previously in this book of ours. They asked for signs that they could not ask for, out of their arrogance towards their Lord. Likewise, the Christians wished from their Lord, out of their arrogance towards Him, that He would let them hear His words and show them the signs that they wanted. So God, the Most High, informed us about them that they said something similar to what the Jews said, and they wished from their Lord something similar to their wishes, and that what they said about that is similar to what the Jews said, because their hearts are similar in their misguidance and disbelief in God.

So even though their doctrines differ in their lies about God and their fabrications about Him, their hearts are similar in their disbelief in their Lord and their slander against Him, and their arrogance towards the Prophets of God and His Messengers, peace be upon them.
In a similar vein to what we said about that, Mujahid said:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Their hearts are alike, the hearts of the Christians and the Jews.

x: Another said: The meaning of this is: The hearts of the Arab infidels, Jews, Christians, and others are similar.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Their hearts are alike, meaning the Arabs, Jews, Christians, and others.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Their hearts are alike, meaning the Arabs, Jews, Christians, and others.

x: It is not permissible to use heavy taʿs in his statement, they resembled each other. This is because the taʿ at the beginning is extra and was inserted in his statement, tafaʿala. If it were made heavy, it would become two taʿs. It is not permissible to insert two extra taʿs as a sign for one meaning. This is only permissible in the future tense, because the meaning of their insertion is different, because one of them is used as a sign for the future tense, and the other is one of them in tafaʿala. Then one of them is assimilated into the other and becomes heavy, so it is said, After today, our hearts resembled each other. The meaning of the verse is: The Christians, who were ignorant of God and His greatness, said: Why does not God, our Lord, speak to us as He spoke to His prophets and messengers, or will there not come to us a sign from God by which we may know the truth of what we are upon and what we ask and desire?

God Almighty said: Just as these ignorant Christians said and wished of their Lord, the Jews before them said, so they asked their Lord to show them God Himself openly and to give them a sign, and they referred to Him and His messengers for judgment, and wished for wishes. So the hearts of the Jews and Christians were confused in their rebellion against God, their lack of knowledge of His greatness, and their audacity towards His prophets and messengers, just as the words they said were confused.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
We have made clear the signs for a people who are certain
What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
We have made clear the signs for a people who are certain

, is that We have made clear the signs that… For this reason God became angry with the Jews, and made them into apes and pigs, and prepared for them a humiliating punishment in their place of return, and for this reason God disgraced the Christians in this world, and prepared for them disgrace and painful punishment in the Hereafter? And for this reason He made the inhabitants of Paradise, who submitted their faces to God and were good-doers, in this Surah and others. So know the reasons for which each group of them deserved what God did to them, and God singled out for this the people who are certain, because they are the people of verification in matters, and seek to know the truth of things with certainty and truth. So God, the Most High, informed that He made clear to those who had this characteristic what He made clear of that, so that their doubts would be removed and the truth of the matter would be known, since this was report from God, the Most High, and the report of God is the report that its listener cannot be excused for doubting it.
And other report may bear what it bears of the reasons that occur in it, such as forgetfulness, error, and lying, and that is denied in the report of God, the Most High.

The meaning of His Most High’s saying: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner: Indeed, We have sent you, O Muhammad, with Islam, which I will not accept from any other religion, and it is the truth, bringing good tidings to whoever follows you and obeys you, and accepts from you what you called him to of the truth, of victory in this world, and attainment of reward in the Hereafter, and eternal bliss in it, and warning whoever disobeys you and opposes you, and rejects what you called him to of the truth, of disgrace in this world, humiliation in it, and humiliating punishment in the Hereafter.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire
The majority of reciters read:
h
And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire

, with the damma on the ta’ of tas’al and the raising of the lam from it, as a statement. Meaning: O Muhammad, indeed We have sent you with the truth as a bearer of good tidings and a warner, so you have conveyed what you were sent with, and your duty is only to convey and warn, and you are not responsible for whoever disbelieves in what you have brought him of the truth, and is among the people of Hellfire.
Some of the people of Medina read it as:
h
And do not ask

in the subjunctive mood. It means prohibition, with the taa’ of tasa’al open and the lam in the subjunctive mood. The meaning of this according to their reading is: We have sent you with the truth as a bearer of good tidings and a warner so that you may convey what you were sent with, not to ask about the people of Hellfire, so do not ask about their condition.
Those who read this reading interpreted it as:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaʿb, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I wish I knew what happened to my parents, so this verse was revealed:
h
And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaydah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I wonder what happened to my parents? I wonder what happened to my parents? I wonder what happened to my parents? three times, then this verse was revealed: “Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
h
And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire
,” but he did not mention them until God took him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Dawud bin Abi Asim told me:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day: I wonder where my parents are? Then this verse was revealed: “Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
h
And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire

x: The correct reading in my opinion is that of those who read it with the nominative case, as a report. Because God, the Most High, narrated the stories of some people from among the Jews and Christians, and mentioned their misguidance and disbelief in God and their audacity towards His prophets. Then He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, We have sent you, O Muhammad, with the truth as a bringer of good tidings to those who believed in you and followed you, those whose report I have narrated to you and those whose report I have not narrated to you, and a warner to those who disbelieved in your Lord and opposed you. So convey My message, so you are not responsible for the actions of those who disbelieved in you after you conveyed My message to them, nor are you responsible for what they did after that. And there was no mention of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking his Lord about the companions of Hellfire, so his saying,
h
And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire
has a face that can be directed to it.

Rather, the meaning of the speech is directed to what its apparent meaning indicates, until a clear indication comes that establishes the proof, that what is meant by it is other than what its apparent meaning indicates, in which case it is accepted by the proof established by that. There is no report that can provide evidence that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade asking about the people of Hell in this verse, nor is there any indication that this is the case in the apparent meaning of the revelation. The interpretation of this report must be based on what was mentioned before this verse, and on those mentioned after it from the Jews, Christians, and other unbelievers, without forbidding asking about them. If someone thinks that the report narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b is correct, then the impossibility of the Messenger, peace be upon him, doubting that the polytheists are among the people of Hell, and that his parents were among them, is what negates the truth of what Muhammad ibn Ka'b said, if the report on his authority is correct.
Although the report begins after his saying: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner with the letter waw with his saying:
h
And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire

, and leaving it out connects that to its beginning with the letter fa, and that Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, so do not ask about the companions of Hellfire is the clearest indication that the report with his saying:
h
And do not ask

, is more appropriate than a prohibition, and raising it is more appropriate than certainty. It was mentioned that in Abi’s reading it is: And you do not ask, and in Ibn Masoud’s reading it is: And you will not ask, and both of these readings testify to the nominative and the predicate in it, without the prohibition.
Some of the grammarians of Basra used to direct his statement:
h
And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire

to the present, as if he thought that its meaning was: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, not to be asked about the companions of Hellfire. This is if the ta' is closed, and he reads it in the sense of a report item. He would allow it to be read:
h
And do not ask

with the ta' open and the lam closed as a report item, meaning: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, not to be asked about the companions of Hellfire. We have explained what is correct in our view in this regard. These two statements that I mentioned from Al-Basri regarding that are refuted by what was narrated from Ibn Masoud and Abi regarding the reading, because their inclusion of what they included of that from what and lan indicates the interruption of the speech from its beginning, and the beginning of his saying:
h
And do not ask

And if it was a beginning, it would not be a state. As for the people of Hell, “Hell” is the fire itself when its fuel is ignited. From this is the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt: If Hell is kindled and then turns, turn away from its sparks, Hell.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The majority of reciters read: And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire, with the damma on the ta’ of tas’al and the raising of the lam from it, as a statement.
Some of the people of Medina read it as: And do not ask in the subjunctive mood.

The meaning of this according to their reading is: We have sent you with the truth as a bearer of good tidings and a warner so that you may convey what you were sent with, not to ask about the people of Hellfire, so do not ask about their condition.
Those who read this reading interpreted it as:
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in my opinion is that of those who read it with the nominative case, as a report.
This is if the ta' is closed, and he reads it in the sense of a report item.

He would allow it to be read: And do not ask with the ta' open and the lam closed as a report item, meaning: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, not to be asked about the companions of Hellfire.

These two statements that I mentioned from Al-Basri regarding that are refuted by what was narrated from Ibn Masoud and Abi regarding the reading, because their inclusion of what they included of that from what and lan indicates the interruption of the speech from its beginning, and the beginning of his saying: And do not ask.

x: What is meant by His statement, may His praise be exalted: And never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you until you follow their religion, is that neither the Jews, O Muhammad, nor the Christians will ever be pleased with you, so leave seeking what pleases them and agrees with them, and turn to seeking the pleasure of God by calling them to the truth with which God sent you, for what you are calling them to is the path to their coming together with you in harmony and the upright religion. There is no way for you to please them by following their religion, because Judaism is the opposite of Christianity, and Christianity is the opposite of Judaism, and Christianity and Judaism cannot come together in one person in one situation. The Jews and Christians cannot come together in being pleased with you, unless you are a Jew and a Christian, and that will never happen from you, because you are one person, and two opposing religions will never come together in you in one situation.

And if there is no way for them to come together in you at one time, then there is no way for you to please both groups. If you do not have a way to do that, then adhere to the guidance of God, which is the path to harmony for all creation. As for the religion, it is the religion, and its plural is religions.

i: Then He, the Most High, said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these Christians and Jews who said:
x: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian: Indeed, the guidance of God is the guidance.

Meaning: God’s statement is the convincing statement and the decisive judgment between us. So come to the Book of God and His statement in which He explained to His servants that in which they differed, which is the Torah, which you all acknowledge is from God, in which it becomes clear to you who among us is right and who is wrong, which of us is the people of Paradise and which of us is the people of Hell, which of us is right and which of us is wrong. God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call them to God’s guidance and His explanation, because it contains a denial of what the Jews and Christians said: that no one will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians, and a clarification of the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that the one who denies him is among the people of Hell, not the one who believes in him.

God Almighty means by His statement, And if you were to follow, O Muhammad, the desires of these Jews and Christians in what pleases them about you of Judaism and Christianity, and you turned from that to pleasing them, and in it you agreed with their love after what came to you of knowledge of their misguidance and disbelief in their Lord, and after what I related to you from their report of this Surah, you will have from God no protector, meaning by that: O Muhammad, you will have no protector to look after your affairs, nor a guardian to carry them out, nor a helper, who will support you from God and repel from you what befalls you of His punishment, and prevent you from that, if your Lord decrees that for you. We have already explained the meaning of the protector and the helper previously. It has been said that God Almighty revealed this verse to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the Jews and Christians called him to their religions, and each party of them said: The guidance is what we are upon, not what other religions are upon.
So God admonished him to do that, and taught him the decisive argument between them regarding what each party of them claimed.
The people of interpretation differed regarding those whom God, the Most High, meant when He said:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture
Some of them said: They are the believers in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what he brought, from among his companions.
He mentioned those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zurai’ told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture
, these are the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they believed in the Book of God and confirmed it.

x: Others said: Rather, God meant by that the scholars of the Children of Israel, who believed in God and believed in His messengers, so they acknowledged the ruling of the Torah. So they acted according to what God commanded in it regarding following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believing in him, and confirming what he brought from God.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture

recite it with its true recitation - those believe in it. But whoever disbelieves in it - those are the losers,” he said: Whoever disbelieved in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the Jews, then those are the losers.

x: This statement is more correct than the statement made by Qatada.
