Because the verses before it proceeded with the accounts of the People of the Book, and the substitution of those who substituting the Book of God, and their interpretation of it in a way other than its interpretation, and their false claims against God, and the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were not mentioned in the verse before it, so his statement,
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture

, is directed to the report about them, and there is no mention of them after it in the verse that follows it, so that is directed to it being a report that begins with the stories of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and after the stories of others have ended, and there is no evidence that this is report about them that must be accepted. Since that is the case, then what is more appropriate to the meaning of the verse is that it is directed to the fact that it is report about those whose stories God, the Most High, narrated in the verse before it and the verse after it, and they are the people of the two books, the Torah and the Gospel.

Since that is the case, then the interpretation of the verse is: Those to whom We gave the Book which you have known, O Muhammad, which is the Torah, and they read it and followed what is in it, and they believed in you and had faith in what you brought from Me, those recite it with its true recitation. The definite article was included in al-Kitab because it is a definite noun. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions knew which book he meant.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
They recite it with its true recitation
Some of them said: The meaning of that is: They follow it with its true following.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Abi Uday and Abd al-A’la told me, and Amr ibn Ali told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us
m: all, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
They recite it as it should be recited
, they follow it as it should be followed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: similarly.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Husayn bin Amr Al-Anqazi told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
They recite it with its true recitation
, he said, they make lawful what it makes lawful and forbid what it forbids, and they do not distort it.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said, Abu Malik said:
m: Ibn Abbas said in:
h
They recite it as it should be recited
, and he mentioned something similar except that he said: And they do not distort it from its places.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Al-Mu’ammil told us, Sufyan told us, Yazid told us, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
They recite it as it should be recited
, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah, who said: Abdullah ibn Masʿud said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the right way to recite it is to make lawful what it makes lawful and to make unlawful what it makes unlawful, to recite it as God revealed it, not to distort the words from their places, and not to interpret anything of it other than its interpretation. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:122 O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and Mansur bin al-Mu’tamir, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud,
m: regarding his statement: recite it as it should be recited, that is, he makes lawful what it makes lawful and forbids what it forbids, and does not distort it from its proper places.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of the one
m: who mentioned it, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
They recite it as it should be recited
, they follow it as it should be followed.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They recite it as it should be recited
, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told me, he said, Sufyan told us, and Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Azdi told me, he said, Yahya bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Sufyan,
m: they all said, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
They recite it as it should be recited
, he said: Acting upon it.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad:
m: h
They recite it as it should be recited
, he said: They follow it as it should be followed. Have you not seen His statement:
h
And the moon when it follows it (Ash-Shams
: 2), meaning the sun when the moon follows it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’ and Qais bin Sa’d, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They recite it with its true recitation
, he said: They act upon it with its true action.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They follow him as he should be followed.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
They recite it as it should be recited
, they act upon it as it should be acted upon.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Muammil bin Ismail told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They recite it as it should be recited
, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.

c: Amr told me, he said, Abu Qutaybah told us, he said, Al-Hasan bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Al-Khalil, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
They recite it as it should be recited
, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.

c: Amr told us, Yahya Al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They recite it as it should be recited
, he said: They follow it as it should be followed, they act upon it as it should be acted upon.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
They recite it as it should be recited
. He said: They act according to its clear verses and believe in its ambiguous verses. They refer whatever is unclear to its Knower.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
They recite it as it should be recited

, he said: They make lawful what it should be and forbid what it should be forbidden, and they act in accordance with what is in it. It was mentioned to us that Ibn Mas’ud used to say: The right way to recite it is to make lawful what it should be and forbid what it should be forbidden, and to read it as God the Almighty revealed it, and not to distort it from its proper places.

c: Amr told us, Abu Dawud told us, Al-Hakam bin Atiyah told us,
m: I heard Qatada say:
h
They recite it as it should be recited
, he said: They follow it as it should be followed. He said: Following it: They make lawful what it makes lawful and forbid what it forbids, and they read it as it was revealed.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They recite it with its true recitation
, he said: They follow it with its true following. Have you not heard God Almighty say:
h
And the moon when it follows it (Ash-Shams
: 2), he said: When it follows it.

x: Others said:
h
They recite it as it should be recited
, they read it as it should be read.

The correct interpretation of this is that it means: they follow him as he should be followed, from the saying of the one who says: I have not ceased to follow his trace, if he follows his trace, because the proof from the people of interpretation has agreed that this is its interpretation. And since that is its interpretation, then the meaning of the statement is: Those to whom We gave the Book, O Muhammad, from the people of the Torah who believed in you and in what you brought them of the truth from Me, follow My Book that I revealed to My Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, so they believe in it and acknowledge what is in it of your description and description, and that you are My Messenger, and My obedience is obligatory upon them in believing in you and believing in what I brought them from Me, and they act according to what I have made lawful for them, and they avoid what I have forbidden them in it, and they do not distort it from its places, nor do they change it or alter it as I revealed it to them with an interpretation or otherwise.

As for his saying: The right to recite it, it is an exaggeration of the description of their following the Book and their commitment to working with it, just as it is said: So-and-so is a truly learned scholar, and just as it is said: So-and-so is a virtuous person, every virtuous person. The Arabists differed about adding haqq to a definite noun. Some grammarians of Kufa said that it is not permissible to add it to a definite noun, because it means any, and it has the same meaning as saying: the best man is so-and-so. “Af’al” cannot be added to a definite noun, because it is partial, and a partial noun cannot be definite. So they referred to saying: I passed by the man, the right of the man, and I passed by the man, the grandfather of the man, just as they referred to saying: I passed by the man, meaning the man. They permitted that for the whole man, the particular man, and the man himself.

They said: We only permitted that because these letters were originally for emphasis, but when they became madduh, they left madduh as they originally were for definiteness. They claimed that his saying: recite it as it should be recited is permissible to add it to recitation, and it is added to a definite noun, because the Arabs consider the letter ha when it refers to an indefinite noun with an indefinite noun. So they say: I passed by a man whose mother is unique, and a unique fabric, and the master of his people. They said: So too is his saying: its correct recitation is permissible to add haq to recitation, and it is added to the letter ha because the Arabs consider the letter ha in similar words to be among the indefinite nouns. They said: If that were the correct recitation, then it would have been permissible to say: I passed by the man as he should be. According to this statement, the interpretation of the statement is:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture
recite it with the right recitation.

Some Basra grammarians said: It is permissible to add haqq to indefinite nouns with indefinite nouns, and to definite nouns with definite nouns. This is similar to the saying of the speaker: I passed by the man, the man’s slave, and by a man, the man’s slave. The interpretation of the verse according to these people is: Those to whom We gave the Book recite it as it should be recited. The first statement is more correct in our view, because the meaning of his saying: the right of its recitation is recitation, meaning praising the recitation that you recited and preferring it. And it is not permissible to add it to one definite noun according to all of them. Likewise, it is not permissible to add it to one definite noun. Rather, it is added in the right of its recitation to what has the ha’ in it, for the reason that was described and explained previously.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Those believe in it.

What God Almighty means by His statement, those, are those about whom He has informed us that they recite what He has given them of the Book with its true recitation. As for His statement, they believe in it, He means: they believe in it. The ha in His statement, by it, refers back to the ha in its recitation, and they are both from the mention of the Book about which God said, those to whom We have given the Book.

c: God Almighty informed us that
m: the believer in the Torah is the one who follows what is permissible and forbidden in it, and acts according to what is in it of the obligations of God that He imposed on its people, and that its people who are its people are those who have this description, not those who distort it, change its interpretation, alter its laws, and abandon what God imposed on them in it. The Almighty described the followers of the Torah as He described them, and praised them as He praised them, because following it is following Muhammad, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believing in him, because the Torah commands its people to do that, and informs them about God, may He be exalted, of his prophethood, and the obligation of obeying him upon all of God’s creation from among the children of Adam, and that denying Muhammad is denying it. So the Almighty informed that the followers of the Torah are those who believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are those who act according to what is in it, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: Those are the ones who believe in him, he said: whoever believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Children of Israel and in the Torah, and the one who disbelieves in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the one who disbelieves in it and is the loser, as God Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in him - then it is those who are the losers.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And whoever disbelieves in it
- it is those who are the losers.
What He, the Most High, meant by His statement,
h
And whoever disbelieves in it

, is whoever disbelieves in the Book which He informed that whoever is given it from the believers will recite it as it should be recited. What He, the Most High, meant by His statement, disbelieves, is denying what is in it of the obligations of God and the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his confirmation, and changing it and distorting its interpretation. Those are the ones who have lost their knowledge and their deeds, so they have deprived themselves of their portions of God’s mercy, and have exchanged it for God’s wrath and anger.
Ibn Zayd said about His statement, with what:

c: Yunus told me that he said, Ibn Wahb told us that
m: Ibn Surat Al-Baqarah 2:122 O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds. Zayd said:
h
And whoever disbelieves in it
- then it is those who are the losers. He said: Whoever disbelieves in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the Jews, then it is those who are the losers.

evidence.text: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: “Those to whom We gave the Scripture recite it with its true recitation - those believe in it.

Since that is the case, then the interpretation of the verse is: Those to whom We gave the Book which you have known, O Muhammad, which is the Torah, and they read it and followed what is in it, and they believed in you and had faith in what you brought from Me, those recite it with its true recitation.
Abu Jaafar said: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: They recite it with its true recitation.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Abi Uday and Abd al-A’la told me, and Amr ibn Ali told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us all, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They recite it as it should be recited, they follow it as it should be followed.

Al-Husayn bin Amr Al-Anqazi told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God Almighty: They recite it with its true recitation, he said, they make lawful what it makes lawful and forbid what it forbids, and they do not distort it.

Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said, Abu Malik said: Ibn Abbas said in: They recite it as it should be recited, and he mentioned something similar except that he said: And they do not distort it from its places.

Amr bin Ali told us, Al-Mu’ammil told us, Sufyan told us, Yazid told us, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding the statement of God Almighty: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.

It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah, who said: Abdullah ibn Masʿud said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the right way to recite it is to make lawful what it makes lawful and to make unlawful what it makes unlawful, to recite it as God revealed it, not to distort the words from their places, and not to interpret anything of it other than its interpretation.

Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and Mansur bin al-Mu’tamir, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding his statement: recite it as it should be recited, that is, he makes lawful what it makes lawful and forbids what it forbids, and does not distort it from its proper places.

Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of the one who mentioned it, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They recite it as it should be recited, they follow it as it should be followed.

Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Razin, regarding his statement: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.
Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: Acting upon it.
Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’ and Qais bin Sa’d, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: They recite it with its true recitation, he said: They act upon it with its true action.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: They recite it as it should be recited, they act upon it as it should be acted upon.

Amr bin Ali told us, Muammil bin Ismail told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.

Amr told me, he said, Abu Qutaybah told us, he said, Al-Hasan bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Al-Khalil, on the authority of Mujahid: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.

Amr told us, Yahya Al-Qattan told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed, they act upon it as it should be acted upon.
Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan: They recite it as it should be recited.

Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They make lawful what it should be and forbid what it should be forbidden, and they act in accordance with what is in it.

It was mentioned to us that Ibn Mas’ud used to say: The right way to recite it is to make lawful what it should be and forbid what it should be forbidden, and to read it as God the Almighty revealed it, and not to distort it from its proper places.
Amr told us, Abu Dawud told us, Al-Hakam bin Atiyah told us, I heard Qatada say: They recite it as it should be recited, he said: They follow it as it should be followed.
He said: Following it: They make lawful what it makes lawful and forbid what it forbids, and they read it as it was revealed.

Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: They recite it with its true recitation, he said: They follow it with its true following.
Others said: They recite it as it should be recited, they read it as it should be read.

As for his saying: The right to recite it, it is an exaggeration of the description of their following the Book and their commitment to working with it, just as it is said: So-and-so is a truly learned scholar, and just as it is said: So-and-so is a virtuous person, every virtuous person.

They claimed that his saying: recite it as it should be recited is permissible to add it to recitation, and it is added to a definite noun, because the Arabs consider the letter ha when it refers to an indefinite noun with an indefinite noun.
They said: If that were the correct recitation, then it would have been permissible to say: I passed by the man as he should be.
According to this statement, the interpretation of the statement is: Those to whom We gave the Scripture recite it with the right recitation.
The interpretation of the verse according to these people is: Those to whom We gave the Book recite it as it should be recited.
The first statement is more correct in our view, because the meaning of his saying: the right of its recitation is recitation, meaning praising the recitation that you recited and preferring it.

Abu Jaʿfar said: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement, And whoever disbelieves in it, is whoever disbelieves in the Book which He informed that whoever is given it from the believers will recite it as it should be recited.

x: This verse is a sermon from God Almighty to the Jews who were among the immigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a reminder from Him to them of His previous favors to them in His treatment of their forefathers, seeking His compassion for them in His religion and belief in His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: O Children of Israel, remember My favors to you, and My favors to you, and My rescuing you from the hands of your enemy Pharaoh and his people, and My sending down upon you manna and quails in your wanderings, and My empowering you in the lands after you had been humiliated and My choosing messengers from among you, and My giving you preference over the scholars among whom you were, during the days when you were in My obedience by following My Messenger to you, and believing in him and believing what he brought you from Me, and abandoning persistence in misguidance and error. We have previously mentioned the blessings that God bestowed upon the Children of Israel, and the meanings that He, the Most High, mentioned of His favors to them, and the world over which they were favored in the past with narrations and evidence, so we disliked lengthening the book by repeating it, since the meaning in that place and there was the same.

This verse is a warning from God, the Most High, to those to whom He has previously admonished, as He admonished them in the verse before it. God says to them: And fear, O company of Children of Israel, those who alter My Book and My revelation, who distort its interpretation from its meaning, who deny My Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the punishment of a Day when no soul will pay for another soul in the least, nor will any benefit be given to it, lest you perish in your state of disbelief in Me and your denial of My Messenger, and die in that state. For it is a Day when no ransom will be accepted from a soul for what is required of it, nor will any intercessor intercede for what is due to it of its right, nor will any helper from God aid it when He takes vengeance on it for its disobedience to Him. The explanation of all the meanings of this verse has already been given in its counterpart, so there is no need to repeat it here.

He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying: And when He tested, and when He put to the test. It is said: I tested so-and-so, I tested him with a test. And from this is the saying of God Almighty: And test the orphans
r
(An-Nisa’: 6)

, meaning: test them. God Almighty’s test of Abraham was a test of the duties He imposed on him and the commands He commanded him to do. These are the words He revealed to him and charged him to act upon, as a test and trial from Him. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the words with which God tested Abraham, His Prophet and Friend, may God’s prayers be upon him.
Some of them said: They are the laws of Islam, and they are thirty shares.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands

, he said: Ibn Abbas said: No one was tested with this religion and established it except Abraham. God tested him with certain commands, and he fulfilled them. He said: So God wrote for him the declaration of innocence and said: And Abraham who fulfilled (al-Najm 53:37). He said: Ten of them are in Al-Ahzab, ten of them are in Al-Bara’ah, and ten of them are in Al-Mu’minin. And a questioner asked and said: This Islam is thirty arrows.

c: Ishaq bin Shaheen told us, Khalid Al-Tahan told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: No one was tested with this religion and carried out all of it except Abraham. He was tested with Islam and completed it, so God wrote for him innocence and said: And Abraham who fulfilled (al-Najm 53:37). He mentioned ten in innocence 112, and said: Those who repent, those who worship, those who praise to the end of the verse, and ten in Al-Ahzab 35: Indeed, the Muslim men and women, and ten in Surat Al-Mu’minun 1-9 to His saying:
h
And those who maintain their prayers
, and ten in Sa’il Sa’il 221-34:
h
And those who maintain their prayers

c: Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwaih told us, Ali bin Al-Hassan told us, Kharijah bin Musab told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Islam is thirty arrows, and no one was tested with this religion and established it except Abraham. God said: And Abraham who fulfilled, so God wrote for him a release from the Fire.

x: Others said: They are ten characteristics of the Sunnah of Islam.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands

, he said: God tested him with purification, five for the head and five for the body. For the head: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, inhaling water from the nose, using the siwak, and parting the hair. And for the body: trimming the nails, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, plucking the armpit hair, and washing away traces of feces and urine with water.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Aban, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly, and he did not mention the effect of urine.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Sulayman told us, Abu Hilal told us, Qatada told us
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands

, he said: He tested him with circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, washing the front and back passages, using the siwak, trimming the moustache, clipping the nails, and plucking the armpit hair. Abu Hilal said: And I forgot one characteristic.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Abu al-Jild, who said: Abraham was tested with ten things, which are Sunnah for humans: sniffing water in the nose, trimming the moustache, using the siwak, plucking the armpit hair, cutting the nails, washing the knuckles, circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, and washing the anus and vulva.

x: Some of them said: Rather, the words with which he was afflicted were ten, some of them in purifying the body, and some of them in the rituals of Hajj.
Mention of who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Harb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi'ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Hubayrah, on the authority of Hanash, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with commands

, and he fulfilled them, he said: Six for humans, and four for the sacred places. Those for humans: shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, plucking the armpit hair, clipping the nails, trimming the moustache, and bathing on Friday. And four for the sacred places: Tawaf, running between Safa and Marwa, stoning the Jamarat, and Ifadah.

x: Others said: Rather, it is: I will make you an imam for the people, in the rituals of Hajj.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands
, and he fulfilled them, among them: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people, and the verses of ritual worship.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, the freed slave of Umm Hani’, regarding his statement:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words
, he said: Among them was Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people, and among them were the verses of ritual worship:
h
And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House
(al-Baqarah 2:127-128).

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the words of God:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands
, and he fulfilled them, God said to Abraham: I am testing you with a matter, so what is it? He said: Make me a leader for the people. He said: Yes. He said: And of my descendants. He said:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

. He said: Make the House for the people. He said: Yes. He said: And security. He said: Yes. He said: And make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. He said: Yes. He said: And show us our rites and accept our repentance. He said: Yes. He said: And make this city [one] of security. He said: Yes. He said: And provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes. He said: Yes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: he told him about it on the authority of Ikrimah, so I showed it to Mujahid and he did not reject it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid and Ikrimah agreed on this statement together.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain commands
, and he fulfilled them, he said: He was tested with the verses that came after it: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people. He said: And of my descendants? He said:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his Surat Al-Baqarah 2:125 And remember when We made the House a place of assembly for the people and a place of safety. And take, [O Muhammad], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer.
h
And We charged Abraham and Ishmael
, [saying], "Purify My House for those who go around it, and those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate." father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding His statement:
h
And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain commands
, and he fulfilled them, the words: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people, and His statement:
h
And when We made the House a place of assembly for the people
, and His statement: And take, [O Muhammad], the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer, and His statement:
h
And We enjoined upon Abraham and Ishmael
, and His statement:
h
And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House
, and the verse. He said: All of these are among the words with which Abraham was tested.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain commands
, and he fulfilled them. Among them was: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people. Among them was:
h
And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House

. Among them were the verses concerning the ritual and the station that was made for Abraham, and the provision that was provided to the inhabitants of the House, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their descendants, peace be upon them.

x: Others said: Rather, this is a specific ritual of Hajj.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Salim bin Qutaybah told us, he said, Umar bin Nabhan told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words
, he said: The rituals of Hajj.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Ibn Abbas used to say regarding His statement:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words
, he said: The rituals.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: He tested him with the rituals.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hassan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, who said: It was reported to us on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The words with which Abraham was tested were the rituals.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words
, he said: The rituals of Hajj.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands
, he said: Among them were the rituals of Hajj.

x: Others said: They are matters, among them circumcision.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Salim bin Qutaybah told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words
, he said: Among them was circumcision.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Yunus bin Abi Ishaq told us,
m: I heard Al-Sha’bi say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us,
m: Yunus bin Abi Ishaq said, I heard Al-Sha’bi and Abu Ishaq asked him about the statement of God:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands
, he said: Among them was circumcision, O Abu Ishaq.

x: Others said: Rather, those are the six characteristics: the planet, the moon, the sun, the fire, the migration, and circumcision, with which he was afflicted and he was patient with them.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said:
m: I said to Al-Hasan:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands

, and he fulfilled them. He tested him with a star, and He was pleased with him. He tested him with the moon, and He was pleased with him. He tested him with the sun, and He was pleased with him. He tested him with fire, and He was pleased with him. He tested him with emigration, and He tested him with circumcision.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid bin Zari’ narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: Yes, by God, He tested him with a matter and he was patient with it: He tested him with the planets, the sun and the moon, and he did well in that, and he knew that his Lord is eternal and does not cease, so he turned his face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists. Then He tested him with the migration, so he left his country and his people until he reached the Levant, migrating to God. Then He tested him with the fire before the migration, so he was patient with that, so God tested him with the slaughter of his son and circumcision, so he was patient with that.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of someone
m: who heard Al-Hasan say regarding His statement:
h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words
, he said: God tested him with the slaughter of his son, with fire, with the star, the sun, and the moon.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Salim bin Qutaybah told us, he said, Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain words
, he said: He tested him with the stars, the sun, and the moon, and He found him patient.

x: Others said: Musa bin Harun narrated to us, he said:

c: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: The words with which Abraham was tested by his Lord: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves” (al-Baqarah 2:127-129).

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Almighty, informed His servants that He tested His friend Abraham with words that He revealed to him, and ordered him to act upon them, and he fulfilled them, as God, the Most High, informed us that he did. It is possible that those words are all of what we mentioned in the interpretation of the words, and it is possible that they are some of it. Because Abraham, may God’s prayers be upon him, was tested in what has reached us with all of that, so he acted upon it, and carried out in it the obedience of God and His command that was obligatory upon him in it. Since that is the case, it is not permissible for anyone to say: God meant by the words with which He tested Abraham something specific of that and not something else, nor did He mean all of that, except with an argument that must be accepted: from a report from the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, or a consensus of the argument.

There is no authentic report in any of that from the Messenger through a single narration, nor from a group whose narration must be accepted. However, two reports were narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a similar meaning to that. If they were proven, or one of them, then the interpretation of that would be correct.
One of them is what: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying:

c: Rashdin bin Saad narrated to us, saying: Zaban bin Faid narrated to me, on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Shall I not tell you why God called Abraham, His friend, the one who fulfilled? (al-Najm 53:37) Because he used to say every morning and every evening: So glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning (al-Rum 30:17-18) until he concluded the verse. The other one is: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Al-Hasan bin Atiyah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And Abraham who fulfilled’ (al-Najm 53:37). He said: Do you know what he fulfilled? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: And in the work of his day, four rakʿahs during the day.”

x: If the report of Sahl ibn Muʿadh from his father was authentic in its chain of transmission, it would be clear that the words with which Abraham was tested and he performed them were his saying every morning and evening: “So glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you rise in the morning. To Him is praise in the heavens and the earth and in the evening and when you reach the noon” Ar-Rum 30:17-18, or if the report of Abu Umamah was transmitted by a trustworthy person, it would be known that the words with which Abraham was inspired and he was tested and he performed them were: to pray four rakʿahs every day. However, there is doubt in the chains of transmission of both reports.

c: The correct statement about the meaning of the words that God informed us that
m: He tested Abraham with is what we explained earlier.
b.via: correct statement about the meaning of the words that God

x: If someone were to say about that: What Mujahid, Abu Salih, and Ar-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said is more correct than what others said, that would be a doctrine. Because His statement: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people, and His statement:
h
And We charged Abraham and Ishmael
, saying, ‘Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf,’ and all the other verses that are similar to that, are like an explanation of the words that God mentioned that He tested Abraham with.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Then complete them.
What God Almighty means by His statement, and he completed them, is that Abraham completed the words.

His completion of them means his perfecting them by doing for God what He has obligated him to do in them, which is the fulfillment of which God Almighty said: And Abraham who fulfilled (al-Najm 53:37), meaning he fulfilled what was entrusted to him, with the words, with what He commanded him to do of His obligations and his trials in them, as:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Then complete them, meaning, perform them.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then complete them, meaning he acted upon them and completed them.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: So he completed them, meaning he acted upon them and completed them.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people.’
Surat Al-Baqarah 2:125 And remember when We made the House a place of assembly for the people and a place of safety. And take, [O Muhammad], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer.
h
And We charged Abraham and Ishmael
, [saying], "Purify My House for those who go around it, and those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate."
What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people, is that God said: O Abraham, I will make you an imam for the people, to be followed and emulated, just as:

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: I will make you an imam for the people, so that they may follow him and emulate him. It is said: I led the people in prayer, so I lead them in prayer, if I am their imam. Rather, God Almighty meant by His saying to Abraham: I will make you a leader for the people, that I will make you a leader for those who come after you from among the people of faith in Me and My messengers, you will precede them, they will follow your guidance, and they will follow your example that you act upon, by My command to you and My revelation to you.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “He said: And of my descendants.”

By that, He, the Most High, meant: When God raised his status and honored him, He informed him of what He would do with him, by making him an imam in good deeds for those in his time, and for those who came after him from his descendants and all other people besides them, who would be guided by his guidance and imitate his actions and morals: O Lord, and from my descendants, make imams to be imitated, like the one You made me an imam to be followed and imitated.
A question that Abraham asked his Lord, as:

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, who said: Ibrahim said: And from my descendants, meaning: So make from my descendants someone who will be followed and emulated.

x: Some people have claimed that Abraham’s statement, And of my descendants, was a request from his Lord to his descendants that they adhere to his covenant and religion, as He said, And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols
r
(Ibrahim 14:35)
. So God, the Most High, informed us that among his descendants would be the oppressors who opposed him in his religion, by saying,
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

. The apparent meaning of the revelation indicates something other than what the author of this article said. Because the statement of Abraham, peace be upon him: And from my descendants, follows the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people. It is known that what Abraham asked for his descendants, if it were not what his Lord had informed him that He had given him, would have been clear. But since the issue was one of those mentioned previously, He was satisfied with the mention that had already been mentioned, by repeating it and repeating it, so He said: And from my descendants, meaning: And from my descendants, so make like that with which You made me, of leadership for the people.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

This is report from God, the Most High, that the oppressor will not be an imam whom the people of goodness will follow. It is from God, the Most High, an answer to what is imagined in his question to him: that he will make imams like him from his descendants. So he informed that he will do that, except for those among them who are oppressors, for he will not have the same fate, nor will he make them in the place of his friends with him, by honoring them with the imamate. Because the imamate is only for his friends and the people of his obedience, not his enemies and the disbelievers in him.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the covenant that God Almighty forbade the oppressors from attaining.
Some of them said: That covenant is the prophecy.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He said, ‘
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
,’ meaning: My covenant, my prophethood. The meaning of the one who said this statement in the interpretation of the verse is: the people of injustice and polytheism will not attain prophethood.

x: Others said: The meaning of the covenant is the covenant of the Imamate. The interpretation of the verse is based on their saying: I will not make anyone from your descendants who is an oppressor, an imam for My servants to be followed.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He said, ‘My covenant does not include the oppressors.’ He said: There will not be an oppressive imam.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: God said:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
, he said: There will not be an unjust imam.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: He said, ‘
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
,’ he said: There will not be an unjust imam to be followed.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Mashraf bin Aban Al-Hattāb narrated to us, he said: Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyān, on the authority of Khusayf, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
, he said: I will not make an unjust imam to be followed.

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us, he said, Muslim bin Khalid Al-Zanji told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
, he said: I will not make an unjust imam to be followed.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

: He said: There will not be an unjust leader. Ibn Jurayj said: As for Ata’, he said: “I will make you an imam for the people. He said: And from my descendants,” so he refused to make an unjust leader from his descendants. I said to Ata’: What is his covenant? He said: His command.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that you have no covenant with an oppressor to obey him in his oppression.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
, meaning: There is no covenant for a wrongdoer against you in his wrongdoing, that you obey him in it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Muslim al-Awar, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He said, ‘
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
.’ He said: The wrongdoers do not have a covenant, and if you make a covenant, then break it.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Harun bin Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: There is no covenant for an oppressor.

x: Others said: The meaning of covenant in this context is: safety. The interpretation of the statement is based on the meaning of their saying: God said: My enemies and the unjust will not attain the desires of My servants. That is: I will not make them feel safe from My punishment in the Hereafter.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He said, ‘
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

.’ That is with God on the Day of Resurrection. No wrongdoer will be included in His covenant. As for in this world, they have attained God’s covenant, so they inherited the Muslims by it, fought them, and married them by it. But when the Day of Resurrection came, God limited His covenant and His honor to His friends.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
, he said: The covenant of God in the Hereafter does not include the wrongdoers, but as for this world, the wrongdoer has attained it, eaten by it, and lived.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: He said, ‘
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
.’ He said: The covenant of God in the Hereafter does not include the wrongdoers. As for this world, the wrongdoer has reached it and believed in it, and he ate, saw, and lived.

x: Others said: Rather, the covenant that God mentioned in this place is: God’s religion.
Who said that?
Narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ, who said:
m: God said to Abraham:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

. He said: So the covenant of God that He has made with His servants is His religion. He says: His religion does not include the wrongdoers. Do you not see that He said: And We blessed him and Isaac, and among their descendants are those who do good and those who are clearly wronging themselves. (al-Saffat 37:113), He says: Not all of your descendants, O Abraham, are on the truth.

c: Yahya bin Jaʿfar told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers
, he said: My covenant does not include an enemy of Mine who disobeys Me, and I do not grant it except to a friend of Mine who obeys Me.

x: Although this statement appears to be a report that the covenant of God, which is prophethood and leadership for the people of goodness, meaning following his example in this world, and the covenant by fulfilling which he who fulfills it in this world will be saved in the Hereafter from among them who was unjust, transgressing, and transgressing in his intention to follow the path of truth, it is an announcement from God Almighty to Abraham that among his descendants will be those who associate partners with Him, transgress the path, and wrong themselves and His servants, like the one who:

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told me, he said, ʿAtab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
My covenant does not include the wrongdoers

, he said: There will be wrongdoers among your descendants. As for the accusative case of the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:125 And remember when We made the House a place of assembly for the people and a place of safety. And take, [O Muhammad], from the standing place of Abraham a place of prayer.
h
And We charged Abraham and Ishmael

, [saying], "Purify My House for those who go around it, and those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate." wrongdoers, it is because the covenant is that which does not include the wrongdoers. He mentioned that in Ibn Masoud’s reading: The wrongdoers will not attain My covenant, meaning: the wrongdoers are those who will not attain God’s covenant. The nominative case is permissible for the oppressors and the accusative case, and likewise for the covenant, because whatever a person has attained, that person has attained, as it is said: I have attained the good of so-and-so, and I have attained his good. The action is sometimes directed to the good, and sometimes to itself. We have explained the meaning of oppression previously, so we disliked repeating it.

x: As for his statement:
h
And when We made the House a place of return
, it is connected with when to his statement:
h
And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain words
. And his statement:
h
And when Abraham was tested is connected to his statement
: O Children of Israel, remember My favor, and remember when Abraham was tested by his Lord, “
h
and when We made the House a place of return

.” The house that God made a place of assembly for people is the Sacred House. As for the word mathaba, Arabs differ on its meaning and the reason for which it is feminine. Some Basra grammarians said: The letter ha’ was added to the word ‘mathabah’ because of the many who return to it, just as it is said: ‘sayarah’ for someone who does that a lot, and ‘nasaba’ for someone who does that a lot. Some grammarians of Kufa said: Rather, the reward and the reward have the same meaning, similar to the place and the place of residence.

The place was mentioned in the masculine form because he meant the place where one resides, and the place of residence was made feminine because it meant the spot. These people denied that the reward is like the caravan and the genealogy. They said: The letter ha was inserted in the caravan and the genealogy to liken Lahab to the preacher. The reward is derived from the verb thaaba which means the people returned to the place, meaning they returned to it. So they return to it with reward, reward, and recompense. The meaning of his statement:
h
And when We made the House a place of return
for the al-Nas 114:
h
And when We made the House a place of return for the people

and a place of refuge, they would come to it every year and return to it, and they would never be satisfied with it. And among the places of return is the statement of Waraqa ibn Nawfal in describing the sanctuary: A place where all the tribes' leaders flock to.
Hence, it was said: His mind returned to him, if it returned to him after his estrangement from him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And when We made the House a place of return for the people
, he said: They do not satisfy their desire there.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And when We made the House a place of return for mankind
, he said: They return to it, they do not satisfy their desire there.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And when We made the House a place of return for the people
, he said: As for the place of return, it is that to which they return every year, and a person who comes to it once does not leave it without returning to it.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when We made the House a place of return for mankind
, he said: They do not satisfy their desire therein, they come to it, then return to their families, then return to it.

c: Abdul Karim bin Abi Umair told me, he said, Al-Walid bin Muslim told me, he said, Abu Amr said: Abda bin Abi Lubaba told me
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when We made the House a place of return for the people
, he said: No one turns away from it while he thinks that he has had his fill of it.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when We made the House a place of return for the people
, he said: They return to it from every place, and they never get their fill of it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us,
m: on the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:126 And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in Allah and the Last Day." He said, "And whoever disbelieves - I will let him enjoy himself for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire - and wretched is the destination." authority of Abdul-Malik, on the authority of Ata’, similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me, he said, Sahl bin Aamer told us, he said, Malik bin Mughol told us, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when We made the House a place of return for the people
, he said: They do not satisfy their desire there.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Hudhayl, he said,
m: I heard Saeed bin Jubair say:
h
And when We made the House a place of return for the people
, he said: They perform Hajj and return.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement: A place of return for the people, he said: They perform Hajj and then perform Hajj, and they do not satisfy their desire for it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Bakir told us, he said, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Ghalib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: A place of return for the people, he said: They return to it.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when We made the House a place of return for the people and a place of security
, he said: a gathering place.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: A place of return for the people, he said: They return to it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: A place of return for the people. He said: They return to it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when We made the House a place of return for mankind
, he said: They return to it from all countries and come to it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And we believed.

Security is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: Security is security. God called it security because in the pre-Islamic era it was a refuge for those who sought refuge in it. If a man among them encountered the killer of his father or brother there, he would not insult him or attack him until he left it. It was as God, the Most High, said: Do they not see that We have made a secure sanctuary while people are being snatched away all around them? (al-Ankabut 29:67).

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: And we are safe, he said: Whoever is safe is safe. A man would meet the killer of his father and brother and not attack him.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for security, whoever enters it is safe.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And we have secured, he said: Its prohibition, there is no fear in it of anyone entering it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement: And we were safe, meaning: safe from the enemy, so that weapons could be carried in it. And in the pre-Islamic era, people would be snatched from around them while they were safe and not being taken captive.

c: Al-Munjab narrated that Bishr told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And we have security, he said: Security for the people.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: And we are safe, he said: Its prohibition, there is no fear in it of someone entering it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer
The reading of this differed: Some of them read it:
h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer

, with a kasra on the kha’, as a command to take it as a place of prayer. This is the general reading of the Egyptians of Kufa and Basra, and the general reading of the people of Mecca and some of the people of Medina.
Those who read it like this went to it, from the report that:

c: Abu Kuraib and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said, Umar bin Al-Khattab said:
m: I said: O Messenger of God, why don’t you take the station as a place of prayer? So God revealed:
h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, and Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: Omar bin Al-Khattab said:
m: I said: O Messenger of God, and he mentioned something similar. They said: God Almighty revealed this verse as a command to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to make the Station of Abraham a place of prayer. So it is not permissible to read it as a command in the form of a report. Some Basra grammarians have claimed that his statement,
h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer

, is based on his statement, O Children of Israel, remember My favor and Take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. So the command with this verse, and with taking the place of prayer from the station of Abraham, was according to what this speaker said to the Jews from the Children of Israel who were at the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as he told us on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, as follows:

c: It was narrated to me on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: Among the words with which Abraham was tested were His words:
h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer

. So He commanded them to take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer, so they prayed behind the station. The interpretation of the one who said this statement: And when his Lord tested Abraham with certain commands, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people, and He said: Take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer.

x: The report that we mentioned on the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before, indicates the opposite of what these people said, and that it is a command from God Almighty, mentioned by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him, and all of the accountable creation.

Some of the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read it: And they took with the opening of the kha as a statement. Then there was a difference of opinion about what he connected to it with his saying: And they took, when it was read like this, in the manner of the report.
Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Its interpretation, if read in this way, is:
h
And when We made the House a place of assembly for the people
and a place of safety, and when they took the station of Abraham as a place of prayer.
Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Rather, it is connected to his saying: We made, so the meaning of the speech was based on his saying:
h
And when We made the House a place of assembly for the people
, and they took it as a place of prayer.

The correct statement and reading in this regard, according to us, is: And take with a kasra on the kha’, on the interpretation of the command to take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer, based on the established report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which we mentioned earlier, and that:

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, he said, Jaafar bin Muhammad told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And take, from the station of Abraham, a place of prayer. Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And take from the station of Abraham a place of prayer
, and in the station of Abraham.

x: Some of them said: The station of Abraham is the entire Hajj.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: The Station of Abraham, he said, the entire Hajj is the Station of Abraham.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer
, he said: the entire Hajj.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: The entire Hajj is the Station of Abraham.

x: Others said: The Station of Abraham, Arafat, Muzdalifah and the Jamarat.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah:
m: h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer
, he said: Because I have made him an imam, so his station is: Arafat, Muzdalifah, and the Jamarat.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer
, he said: His station: Jam’a, Arafat, and Mina. I do not know of him except that he mentioned Mecca.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And take the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer
, he said: His standing place, Arafat.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: This day I have perfected for you your religion (al-Ma’idah 5:3), the verse was revealed to him while he was standing at Arafat, the station of Abraham.

c: Amr told us, he said: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi,
m: the same.

x: Others said: The Station of Abraham, the Sacred Surat Al-Baqarah 2:126 And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in Allah and the Last Day." He said, "And whoever disbelieves - I will let him enjoy himself for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire - and wretched is the destination." Sanctuary.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer
, he said: The entire sanctuary is the station of Abraham.

x: Others said: The Station of Abraham is the stone on which Abraham stood when his building was raised and he was too weak to lift the stones.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us, he said, Ubayd God ibn Abd al-Majid al-Hanafi told us, he said, Ibrahim ibn Nafi’ told us, he said,
m: I heard Kathir ibn Kathir narrating, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Ibrahim started building it, and Ismail was handing him the stones, and they were saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing” (al-Baqarah 2:127). Then when the building was raised and the old man was too weak to lift the stones, he stood on a stone, and it became the Station of Ibrahim.

x: Others said: Rather, the station of Abraham is his station which is in the Sacred Mosque.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer

, they were only commanded to pray at it, and they were not commanded to touch it. This nation has taken on the burden of something that the nations before it did not take on. Some of those who saw the mark of his heel and fingers on it mentioned to us, and this nation continued to touch it until it became worn out and disappeared.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer
. So they pray behind the station.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And take, from the station of Abraham, a place of prayer, meaning the prayer at his station during the Hajj. The station is the stone that the wife of Ismail had placed under Abraham’s feet when she washed his head, so Abraham placed his foot on it while he was riding, so she washed one side, then she lifted it up from under it and his foot had sunk into the stone, so she placed it under the other side, so she washed it and his foot had also sunk into it, so God made it one of His symbols and said: And take, from the station of Abraham, a place of prayer.

x: The most correct of these statements, in our view, is what was said by those who say that the Station of Abraham is the station known by this name, which is in the Sacred Mosque, based on what we narrated earlier on the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, and based on what Yusuf ibn Salman told us, saying:

c: Hatim ibn Ismaʿil told us, saying: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, touched the corner, and jogged three times, and walked four times, then he advanced to the Station of Abraham and recited: And take, [O Muhammad], from the Station of Abraham a place of prayer. So he placed the Station between him and the House, and prayed two rakʿahs. These two reports indicate that God, the Most High, meant by the Station of Abraham the place that God commanded us to take as a place of prayer, which is what He described. Even if there were no report from the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) that supported the correct interpretation of what we have chosen, what we have said would have been obligatory. This is because the meaning of speech is to be taken according to its known apparent meaning, not its unknown hidden meaning, until something comes that indicates otherwise, which must be accepted. There is no doubt that what is known among the people as the Station of Abraham is the place of prayer about which God the Most High said: And take, [O Muhammad], the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer.

x: As for the Almighty’s saying: a place of prayer, the people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning.
Some of them said: It is what is claimed.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer
, he said: The place of prayer of Abraham, is claimed.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Take a place of prayer where you can pray.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told me, he said, Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: They were ordered to pray near him.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: It is the prayer in his presence.

x: It is as if those who said: The interpretation of the prayer here is the one who is called, directed the prayer to be a passive participle, from the saying of someone: I prayed in the sense of I called. The people who said this article are the ones who said: The Station of Abraham is the entire Hajj.
