So its meaning in the interpretation of this verse was: And take Arafat, Muzdalifah, Al-Mash’ar, Al-Jamarat, and all the other places of Hajj that Abraham used to perform, as places of call to Me there, and follow Abraham, My friend, peace be upon him, in them, for I have made him an imam for those who come after him from among My friends and those who obey Me, who will follow his example and his traces, so follow his example. As for the interpretation of those who say the other statement, it is: O people, take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer where you pray, as an act of worship from you and as an honor to Abraham.

This statement is more correct, based on what we mentioned of the report on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab and Jabir bin Abdullah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, saying, ‘Purify My House.’

God Almighty means by His statement: And our covenant, and our command, as Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: I said to Ata’: What is His covenant? He said, His command.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told me, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: And We enjoined upon Abraham, he said: We commanded him. The meaning of the verse is: And We commanded Abraham and Ishmael to purify My House for those who go around it. The purification that God commanded them to do in the House is to purify it from idols, the worship of idols in it, and from associating partners with God.

x: What is the meaning of His statement: And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, ‘Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf’? Was there a house in the days of Abraham, before he built the House, that was purified from polytheism and idol worship in the sanctuary, so it is possible that they were commanding it to be purified?
There are two aspects of interpretation for this, and a group of people of interpretation have said each of the two aspects.

One of them: That its meaning is: And We enjoined upon Abraham and Ishmael that they should build My House purified from polytheism and doubt, as God Almighty said: Is he who lays his foundation on piety toward God and His pleasure better or he who lays his foundation on the brink of a crumbling precipice? (al-Tawbah 9:109).
Likewise, His statement:
h
And We enjoined upon Abraham and Ishmael that they should purify My House
, meaning: Build My House purified from polytheism and doubt, as Musa bin Harun told me, he said:

c: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And We enjoined upon Abraham and Ishmael that they should purify My House

, he says: Build My House for those who perform Tawaf. This is one of its two meanings. The other aspect of them: That they were an order to purify the place of the House before its construction, and the House after its construction, from what the polytheists used to place in it during the time of Noah and those before him of idols, so that this would be a tradition for those after them, since God, the Most High, had made Abraham an imam to be followed after him, as Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said in his statement: that they purify, he said: from the idols that they worship, which the polytheists used to venerate.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair:
m: Purify My House for those who circumambulate it, he said: from idols and doubts.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair,
m: the same.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told me, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: From polytheism.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Abu Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Purify My House for those who circumambulate it, he said: from idols.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf, he said: from polytheism and the worship of idols.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly, and he added to it: and false speech.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: For those who circumambulate.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the circumambulators in this place.
Some of them said: They are strangers who come to the Sacred House from abroad.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said, Abu Hasin told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement: For those who go around it, he said: Whoever comes to it from a foreign land.

x: Others said: Rather, the circumambulators are those who circumambulate it, whether they are strangers or from its people.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Ala’ told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Ata’:
m: For those who circumambulate, he said: If he is circumambulating the House, then he is one of those who circumambulate. The first of the two interpretations of the verse is what Ata’ said. Because the one who circumambulates is Surat Al-Baqarah 2:126 And when Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in Allah and the Last Day." He said, "And whoever disbelieves - I will let him enjoy himself for a little; then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire - and wretched is the destination." the one who circumambulates something and not others. And the one who comes from a foreign land does not deserve the name of circumambulating the House, if he does not circumambulate it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: and those who abide therein.

God Almighty means by His statement: and those who are devoted to it, those who reside in it. The one who is devoted to something is the one who resides in it, as Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan said: They were devoted to their homes, and they were praising them. God threw them into those humble hands. The person performing itikaf is called itikaf because of his stay in the place where he has confined himself to God Almighty. Then the people of interpretation differed about who God meant by His saying: and those who are devoted to it.
Some of them said: He meant the one who sits in the Sacred House without performing Tawaf or prayer.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: If he is circumambulating the House, then he is among those who circumambulate, and if he is sitting, then he is among those who are staying there.

x: Some of them said: The Aakifun are the neighbors who are in retreat.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah:
m: Purify My House for those who circumambulate and those who stay there, he said: those who stay nearby.

x: Some of them said: The people of the sacred land are the people of the sacred land.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said, Abu Hasin told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement: and those who stay there, he said: the people of the city.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And those who are devoted, he said: Those who are devoted are his family.

x: Others said: Al-A’akifoon are the praying ones.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stay there
, he said: Those who stay there are those who pray.

x: The most correct of these interpretations is what ʿAtaʿ said, which is that the one who is staying in the House in this place is the one who resides in it, adjoining it without performing Tawaf or praying. Because the description of staying in the House is what we have described: residing in a place. And the one who is staying in a place may be staying in it while sitting, praying, circumambulating, standing, and in other conditions. So since the Almighty mentioned in His statement:
h
Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stay there

and those who bow and prostrate, the praying and those who circumambulate, it is known from this that the condition that God the Almighty meant of the one staying is not the condition of the one who prays and the one who circumambulates, and that what He meant of his conditions is staying in the House, by way of adjoining it, even if he is not praying, bowing, or prostrating in it.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: And bowing is prostration.

God Almighty means by His statement, and bowing, the group of people bowing to Him, each one of whom is bowing. Likewise, prostration is the group of people prostrating to Him, each one of whom is prostrating, just as it is said: a sitting man and sitting men, and a sitting man and sitting men, so likewise a prostrating man and prostrating men. It was said: Rather, he meant by bowing and prostration the worshippers.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Ata’:
m: And bowing is prostration, he said: If he is praying, then it is from bowing is prostration.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And bowing and prostration, the people of prayer. We have previously explained the meaning of bowing and prostration, so there is no need to repeat it here.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed: Some of them read it: And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer, with a kasra on the kha’, as a command to take it as a place of prayer.
This is the general reading of the Egyptians of Kufa and Basra, and the general reading of the people of Mecca and some of the people of Medina.
Those who read it like this went to it, from the report that:
So it is not permissible to read it as a command in the form of a report.
Some of the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read it: And they took with the opening of the kha as a statement.
Then there was a difference of opinion about what he connected to it with his saying: And they took, when it was read like this, in the manner of the report.

x: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And when Abraham said
, ‘My Lord, make this a secure city,’ and remember when Abraham said: My Lord, make this city a secure city.

By his saying, We have faith, he means that we are safe from the tyrants and others, that they would have power over him, and from the punishment of God that he would befall him as he befalls all other countries, from subsidence, collapse, drowning, and other than that from the wrath of God and its examples that befall all other countries besides him, as:

c: Bishr bin Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, from Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that the sanctuary is a sanctuary opposite the throne. And it was mentioned to us that the House descended with Adam when he descended. God said to him: Descend with you to My House, so that it may be circumambulated as My Throne is circumambulated. So Adam and those who came after him of the believers circumambulated around it, until the time of the flood came when God drowned the people of Noah, He raised it and purified it, and the punishment of the people of the earth did not befall it. So Abraham followed a trace of it, so he built it on an ancient foundation that had been before it.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: Was the sanctuary not safe until after Abraham asked his Lord for safety?
There is a difference of opinion about that.
Some of them said: The sanctuary has always been safe from the punishment of God and the punishment of the tyrants of His creation, since the heavens and the earth were created.
They based this on the following:

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, he said: Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Maqburi narrated to me, he said:
m: “I heard Abu Shuraih Al-Khuza’i say: When Mecca was conquered, Khuza’ah killed a man from Hudhayl, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and gave a sermon and said: O people, God made Mecca sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. It is not permissible for a man who believes in God and the Last Day to shed blood there or cut down trees there. Beware, it is not permissible for anyone after me, and it was not permissible for me except at this moment, out of anger at its people. Beware, it has returned to the state it was yesterday. Beware, let the witness inform the absent. Whoever says: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed there! Say: God made it permissible for His Messenger but did not make it permissible for you.”

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Raheem ibn Sulayman narrated to us, and Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us
m: all, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about Mecca when he conquered it: This is a sanctuary, God made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, and created the sun and the moon, and placed these two pieces of wood. It was not permissible for anyone before me, and it will not be permissible for anyone after me. It was made permissible for me for an hour of the day.” They said: So Mecca, since it was created, has been a sanctuary, safe from the punishment of God and the punishment of the tyrants. They said: The authentic narration from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which we mentioned, has informed us of the correctness of what we have said about that. They said: Abraham did not ask his Lord to protect him from His punishment and the punishment of the tyrants, but he asked Him to protect his people from drought and famine, and to provide its inhabitants with fruits, as his Lord informed him that he asked Him in His saying:
h
And when Abraham said

, ‘My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day.’ They said: He only asked his Lord for that because he had settled his offspring in it, and it had neither crops nor milk. So he sought refuge with his Lord from destroying them there with hunger and thirst, so he asked Him to keep them safe from what He had warned them against. They said: How is it possible that Abraham asked his Lord to make the sanctuary sacred and to protect him from His punishment and the punishment of the tyrants of His creation, when he said, when he settled there with his family and children: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House
r
(Ibrahim 14:37)

? They said: If Abraham was the one who made the sanctuary sacred or asked his Lord to make it sacred, he would not have said: Near Your sacred House when he settled there, but he made it sacred before it and made it sacred after it.

x: Others said: The sanctuary was permissible before the call of Abraham, like all other lands. It only became forbidden by Abraham’s forbidding it, just as the city of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was permissible before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade it.
They said: The evidence for what we have said is what Ibn Bashar told us, he said:

c: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said: Sufyan told us,
m: on the authority Surat Al-Baqarah 2:127 And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [saying], “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Abraham made the House of God sacred and made it secure, and I have made Medina sacred, what is between its two lava plains. Its game is not to be hunted, and its trees are not to be cut.”

c: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, and Abu Kurayb informed us, he said: Abd al-Rahim al-Razi told us, they both said:
m: We heard Ash’ath, on the authority of Nafim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Abraham was his servant and his friend, and I am his servant and his messenger. Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I made Medina sacred, what is between its two lava plains, its trees and its game. No weapons may be carried in it for fighting, and no tree may be cut down from it except for camel fodder.’”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Qutaybah bin Saeed told us, he said, Bakr bin Mudar told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Haad, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Muhammad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Othman, on the authority of Rafi bin Khadij, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I make Medina sacred, what is between its two lava plains.’” And similar report that would take too long to cover in a book. They said: God Almighty has informed us in His Book that Abraham said: My Lord, make this a secure city, but He did not inform us that he asked to make it secure from some things but not others. So no one can claim that what he asked for was security from some things but not others, except with an argument that must be accepted. They said: As for the report of Abu Shuraih and Ibn Abbas, they are two reports that cannot be used as evidence, because of the reasons in their chains of transmission that must not be accepted because of them.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Most High, made Mecca a sanctuary when He created and established it, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us that He made it sacred on the day He created the heavens and the earth, without Him forbidding it through the tongue of any of His prophets and messengers, but by preventing those who wanted to harm it, and by repelling from it the plagues and punishments and from its inhabitants what He has made permissible for others besides it and its inhabitants of punishments. This remained the case until God settled Abraham, His friend, in it, and settled his family, Hagar, and his son, Ishmael, in it. Then Abraham asked his Lord to impose the obligation of its prohibition on His servants through his tongue, so that it would be a tradition for those of His creation who would come after him, following his example in it, since God, the Most High, had taken him as a friend, and informed him that He would make him an imam for the people to follow.

So his Lord answered his question, and obligated His servants to impose its prohibition through his tongue. So Mecca became forbidden after God forbade it, without God imposing the obligation of abstaining from it on His servants, and forbidden by God’s repelling of it, without His forbidding it on the tongue of any of His messengers. He imposed its prohibition on His creation on the tongue of His friend Abraham, peace be upon him, and it became obligatory upon His servants to abstain from considering it permissible, and to consider its game and its animals permissible for it by His imposing the obligation of abstaining from that, by Abraham conveying God’s message to him for that to them. Therefore, its prohibition was attributed to Abraham, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, God has made Mecca sacred. Because the imposition of its prohibition that God has obligated His servants to do as a form of worship to Him, not the prohibition that He had always done as an act of worship to protect and preserve it before that, was about Abraham asking his Lord to impose that on his tongue, or is it the one that the servants were obligated to impose and not others.

It has become clear from what we have said that the meaning of the two reports is correct, I mean the report of Abu Shuraih and Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, God made Mecca sacred on the day He created the sun and the moon, and the report of Jabir, Abu Hurairah, Rafi’ ibn Khadij, and others: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘O God, Abraham made Mecca sacred.’” And that neither of them negates the meaning of the other, as some ignorant people have thought. It is not permissible in the report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for some of them to contradict others, if their authenticity is proven. The two report reports that were narrated in this regard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came in a clear and widespread manner that eliminates the excuse of whoever heard it.
As for the saying of Abraham, peace be upon him: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House
r
(Ibrahim 14:37)

, if he said it before God made it obligatory to prohibit it on His tongue to His creation, then he meant by that God’s prohibition of it, which He prohibited by His protection and guardianship of it, without His prohibition of it to His creation as an act of worship to them by that. And if he said that after God prohibited it on His tongue to His creation as an act of worship, then no one has any question against us regarding that.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And provide his family with fruits, whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day.

This was a request from Abraham to his Lord: To provide the believers of Mecca with fruits, but not the unbelievers. He specifically asked the believers to do so, but not the unbelievers, because God informed him when he asked him to make from his descendants leaders to be followed, that among them would be the unbeliever who would not fulfill his covenant, and the oppressor who would not attain his authority. So when he knew that among his descendants would be the oppressor and the unbeliever, he specifically asked his Lord to provide the inhabitants of Mecca with fruits, the believers among them but not the unbelievers. And God said to him: I have answered your prayer, and I will provide with the unbeliever along with the believers of this country, so let him enjoy it for a little while. As for min in His statement: Whoever among them believes in God and the Last Day, it is in the accusative case for translation and clarification of the people, as God Almighty said: They ask you about fighting in the sacred month (al-Baqarah 2:217), meaning: They ask you about fighting in the sacred month, and as God Almighty said:
And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by people who can afford the expenses
meaning: And Hajj to the House is owed to God by whoever can afford the expenses.

Abraham asked his Lord for what he asked for because he had settled in a valley with no crops, no water, and no people. So he asked that He provide his people with fruit and that He make people’s hearts yearn for them. It was mentioned that when Abraham asked his Lord for that, God moved Taif from Palestine.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj Qaq told us, Hisham told us, he said,
m: I read to Muhammad bin Muslim: When Abraham prayed for the sanctuary: And provide its people with fruits, God moved Taif from Palestine.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “He said:
h
And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little
The people of interpretation differed about who said this statement and how to read it.
Some of them said: The one who said this statement is our Lord, may He be exalted. And its interpretation according to their saying is: He said:
h
And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little

with My provision of fruits in this world, until his time comes to him. And the one who said this statement read it as: So I will grant him enjoyment for a little, with a shaddah on the ta’ and a raised ‘ayn.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said, Abu Al-ʿAliyah told me, on the authority of Abi Ibn Kaʿb,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little
h
then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire
, he said, it is the statement of the Lord, may He be exalted.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq said:
m: When Abraham said: My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day, and he turned away from the call to those whom God refused to give authority to, out of devotion to God and love, and separation from those who disobeyed his command, even if they were from his descendants, when he knew that there would be among them a wrongdoer who would not fulfill his covenant, by his report of that when he informed him, God said: And whoever disbelieves, then I provide for the righteous and the wicked, I will grant him enjoyment for a little.

x: Others said: Rather, Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, said that as a request from his Lord to provide the unbeliever with fruits in the Sacred Land, like that which He provides for the believer and to give him enjoyment of that for a little while,
h
Then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire

with a light ta’ and a jazm on the ‘ayn, and a fathah on the ra’ of I will force him, and he separated Then I will force him without cutting off its alif as a request from Abraham to his Lord for them and a request.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said, Abu Al-ʿAliyah said:
m: Ibn Abbas used to say: That is the saying of Abraham, asking his Lord that whoever disbelieves, then let him enjoy himself for a little.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him enjoyment for a little
, meaning: And whoever disbelieves - I will grant him provision also, then I will force him to the torment of the Fire.

x: The correct reading and interpretation of this, according to us, is what Abi bin Kaʿb said and his reading, because the proof is established by the widespread transmission, with knowledge of the correctness of that, and the anomaly of the reading that contradicts it. It is not permissible to object to someone who is permitted to make mistakes and forgetfulness in his transmission, against someone who is not permitted to do so in his transmission. Since that is the case, the interpretation of the verse is: God said: O Abraham, I have answered your prayer, and I have provided the believers of this city with fruits and their disbelievers with provision for them until they reach their appointed times, then their disbelievers were forced after that to the Fire. As for his saying: Then I will grant him a little enjoyment, he means: I will make what I provide him from that during his life a provision that he will enjoy until the time of his death.

We said that this is the case because God Almighty said that to Abraham in response to his question about the provision of fruits for the believers of Mecca. It was known from this that the answer was only in what Abraham asked for and nothing else. Mujahid said what we said about that, and we have mentioned the narration about that from him.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: So he gave Surat Al-Baqarah 2:127 And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [saying], “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” him enjoyment by remaining in this world.

Another said: So I will let him enjoy himself for a little while in his disbelief as long as he stays in Mecca, until I send Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill him if he continues in his disbelief, or to expel him from it. And even though this is an aspect that the speech allows, the apparent evidence of the speech is to the contrary, for what we have described.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
Then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
Then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire

, then I will push him to the punishment of the Fire and drive him to it, as God Almighty said: On the Day they are called to the Fire of Hell, he will be called (al-Tur 52:13). The meaning of compulsion is coercion. It is said: I compelled someone to do this, if I forced him to do it and made him do it. This is the meaning of his saying:
h
Then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire
, I will push him into it and drive him, dragging and pulling him on his face.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And an evil destination.

We have shown that the root of the word ba’isa is ba’isa from ba’usa with the second letter being quiescent, and the second letter being moved to the beginning, just as the word kabd is said for the liver, and the like. The meaning of the words: And the destination is evil, the torment of the Fire, after the worldly pleasures that they enjoyed. As for destiny, it is a verbal noun derived from the saying of the speaker: I have become a good destination, and it is the place to which the disbeliever in God will go from the torment of the Fire.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The people of interpretation differed about who said this statement and how to read it.
And the one who said this statement read it as: So I will grant him enjoyment for a little, with a shaddah on the ta’ and a raised ‘ayn.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading and interpretation of this, according to us, is what Abi bin Kaʿb said and his reading, because the proof is established by the widespread transmission, with knowledge of the correctness of that, and the anomaly of the reading that contradicts it.

x: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House

, and remember when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House. The word bases is the plural of base. One of the bases of a house is called base, and one of the bases of women and their old women is called qaid. The feminine ha is dropped because it is the subject of the saying I sat down from menstruation, and there is no share for the male in it, just as one says a pure and menstruating woman, because there is no share for the male in that. If it meant sitting, which is the opposite of standing, then it would be said base, and it would not be permissible in that case to drop the feminine ha. The bases of the house are its foundation. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the foundations that Abraham and Ishmael raised from the House. Did they innovate that, or were they foundations that existed before them?

Some people said: These are the foundations of a house that Adam, the father of mankind, had built by God’s command to him. Then its place was destroyed and its traces were erased after him, until God gave it to Abraham, peace be upon him, and he built it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said: Adam said:
m: O Lord, I do not hear the voices of the angels! He said: Because of your sin, but descend to the earth, and build me a house, then surround it as you saw the angels surrounding my house in the heaven. People claim that he built it from five mountains: Hira, Turzita, Tursina, Mount Lebanon, and Judi, and its suburb was from Hira. So this was the building of Adam, until Abraham built it later.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House
, he said: The foundations that were the foundations of the House before that.

x: Others said: Rather, they are the foundations of a house that God had sent down for Adam from heaven to earth, to circumambulate around it as he used to circumambulate his throne in heaven. Then he raised it up to heaven during the days of the flood, and Abraham raised the foundations of that house.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told me, he said: Abdul Wahhab told us, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, he said:
m: When God sent Adam down from heaven, he said: I will descend with you or establish with you a house that is circumambulated around as one circumambulates around My throne, and one is purified at it as one is purified at My throne. So when the time of the flood came, it was raised, and the prophets used to make pilgrimage to it, and they did not know its location, until God gave it to Abraham, and informed him of its location, so he built it from five mountains: Hira, Thabir, Lebanon, Mount Tur, and Mount Al-Khamr.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ismail bin Aliyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, he said:
m: When Adam was sent down, then he mentioned something similar. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abdul-Razzaq narrated, Hisham bin Hassan narrated, on the authority of Suwar, the son-in-law of Ata’, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, who said: When God sent Adam down from Paradise, his feet were on the ground and his head was in the sky, hearing the speech of the people of the sky and their supplications, and he felt comfortable with them. The angels feared him, and complained to God about their supplications and prayers, so He lowered him to the ground. When he lost what he used to hear from them, he felt lonely, and complained about that to God about it in his supplications and prayers. So he headed towards Mecca, and the place where his feet were was a village, and his steps were a desert, until he reached Mecca. Then God sent down a ruby from the rubies of Paradise, and it was on the site of the House now. He continued to circle it until God sent the flood, and that ruby was lifted up, until God sent Abraham, who built it. This is what God said: And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House (al-Hajj 22:26).

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said: Umar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: God placed the House with Adam, when God sent Adam down to Earth, and his place of descent was in the land of India. His head was in the sky and his feet were on the ground, so the angels feared him, but it decreased to sixty cubits. Adam was saddened when he lost the voices of the angels and their glorification, so he complained about that to God, the Most High, and God said: O Adam, I have sent down to you a House that you may circumambulate as one circumambulates around My Throne, and you may Surat Al-Baqarah 2:128 Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful. pray at it as one prays at My Throne. So Adam set out for it. He went out, and He stretched out his steps for him, so that between every two steps there was a wilderness. And those wildernesses did not cease after that. Then Adam came to the House and circumambulated it, and so did the prophets after him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abaan:
m: The House was lowered by one ruby or one dazzle, until when God drowned the people of Noah, He raised it up, and its foundation remained, so God gave it to Abraham, and he built it after that.

x: Others said: Rather, the location of the House was a red hill like a dome. This is because when God wanted to create the earth, the water rose to a red or white foam, and that was in the location of the Sacred House. Then He spread out the earth from beneath it, and it remained like that until God settled Abraham in it, so he built it on its foundation. They said: Its foundation rests on four pillars in the seventh earth.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Jarir ibn Hazim said, Hamid ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The location of the House was on the water, before God created the heavens and the earth, like white butter, and the earth was spread out from beneath it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said:
m: Ata and Amr bin Dinar said: God sent winds that struck the water, and it revealed in the place of the House a gullet like a dome, and this House is part of it. That is why it is the mother of villages. Ibn Jurayj said, Ata said: Then He staked it to the mountains so that it would not be overturned by a flood, and the first mountain was Abu Qais.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The House was placed on the pillars of water, on four pillars, two thousand years before the creation of the world, then the earth was rolled out from under the House.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaqoub told us, on the authority of Harun bin Antara, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, he said:
m: They found in Mecca a stone on which was written: I am God, the owner of Mecca. I built it on the day I created the sun and the moon, and I surrounded it with seven pure angels. Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who narrated, Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh narrated, on the authority of Mujahid and other scholars: When God designated the location of the House for Abraham, he went out to it from Syria, and went out with him with Ishmael and his mother Hagar, and Ishmael was a small child who was being breastfed. And they rode on Buraq, as he narrated to me, and Gabriel was with him, guiding him to the location of the House and the landmarks of the sanctuary. So he went out and Gabriel went out with him, and he said: He did not pass by a village without saying: Is this where you were commanded, O Gabriel? Gabriel would say: Go on! Until he brought him to Mecca, which at that time was a land of peace and travel, and in it were people called the Amalekites outside Mecca and its environs, and the House at that time was a red hill covered with mud. So Abraham said to Gabriel: Was I commanded to place them here? He said: Yes. So he took them to the place of the Black Stone and settled them there, and he ordered Hagar, the mother of Ishmael, to build a hut there, and he said: Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House until His saying: Perhaps they will be grateful
r
(Ibrahim 14:37)

. Ibn Humayd said: Salamah said, Ibn Ishaq said: They claim, and God knows best, that an angel came to Hagar, the mother of Ishmael, when Abraham brought them down to Mecca, before Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations of the House. He pointed to the House for her, which was a red, muddy hill, and said to her: This is the first House placed on the earth, and it is the ancient House of God. Know that Abraham and Ishmael are the ones raising it for the people.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Hisham bin Hassan told us, he said, Hamid told me, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: God created the location of this House two thousand years before He created anything on the earth, and its pillars are in the seventh earth.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, he said: Bishr bin Asim told me, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, he said: Ka’b told us:
m: The House was a scum on the water forty years before God created the earth, and from it the earth was spread out. Sa’id said: And he told us on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib: Abraham came from Armenia with the Ark of the Covenant guiding him to settle in the House, just as a spider settles in its home. He said: So it was lifted from stones that thirty men could or could not bear. He said: I said: O Abu Muhammad, God says: And when Abraham raised the foundations of the House, he said: That was after.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Most High, mentioned that he and his son Ishmael raised the foundations of the Sacred House. It is possible that these were the foundations of a house that he had sent down with Adam, so he made it the place of the Sacred House in Mecca. It is possible that these were the dome that Ata’ mentioned, which God created from the foam of water. It is possible that its ruby or pearl was sent down from the sky. It is possible that Adam built it and then it collapsed, until its foundations were raised by Abraham and Ishmael. We do not know which of these was which, because the truth of this cannot be understood except through a report from God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, through widespread transmission. There is no report of this that can be used as evidence, so we must submit to it.

Nor is it, since there is no report of it, according to what we have described, which indicates it through inference and analogies, so it is used as an example, and its knowledge is derived from independent reasoning. So there is no statement in this regard that is more correct than what we have said. And God knows best.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Our Lord, accept from us.
God Almighty meant by that:
h
And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House
, and Ishmael, they said, Our Lord, accept from us. He mentioned that this is also the case in the reading of Ibn Masʿud. This is the opinion of a group of the people of interpretation.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: They were building and they were calling, the words with which Abraham was tested by his Lord, he said: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a nation Muslims [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Kathir told me, he said, Saeed bin Jubair told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, he said: They were raising the foundations of the House and saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing,” he said: And Ishmael was carrying the stones on his neck, and the old man was building. The interpretation of the verse according to this statement: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, saying: Our Lord, accept from us.

x: Others said: Rather, the one who said that was Ishmael. So the interpretation of the verse according to this statement is: And when Abraham raised the foundations of the House, and when he said, Our Lord, accept from us, then Ishmael becomes raised by the sentence that follows it. And he says then, is a predicate for him and not Abraham. Then the people of interpretation differed about who raised the foundations, after their consensus that Abraham was among those who raised them.
Some of them said: Abraham and Ishmael raised it together.

Who said that: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, saying, ‘Purify My House for those who go around it.’ He said: So Abraham set out until he came to Mecca, and he and Ishmael stood up and took pickaxes, not knowing where the House was. Then God sent a wind called the wind of Al-Khajuj, which had two wings and a head in the form of a snake, and it swept away for them what was around the Kaaba from the foundation of the first House, and they followed it with pickaxes, digging until they laid the foundation. That is when He says: And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House (al-Hajj 22:26). So when they had built the foundations and reached the place of the corner, Abraham said to Ishmael: O my son, find me a beautiful stone that I may place here. He said: O my father, I am lazy and tired.

He said: Bring me that. So he set out and looked for a stone, and he brought him a stone but he was not satisfied, so he said: Bring me a stone better than this. So he went to look for a stone for him, and Gabriel brought him the Black Stone from India. It was white, a white force like a cloud. Adam had brought it down from Paradise and it had turned black from the sins of the people. Then Ishmael brought him a stone and found it near the corner. He said: O my father, who brought you this? He said: Who is more energetic than you? So they built it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Umar ibn Abdullah ibn Urwah, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair al-Laythi, he said:
m: It reached me that Abraham and Ishmael were the ones who raised the foundations of the House.

x: Others said: Rather, Abraham raised the foundations of the House, and Ishmael was handing him the stones.

Who said that: Ahmad bin Thabit al-Razi told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub and Kathir bin Kathir bin al-Muttalib bin Abi Wada’ah, one of them adding more than the other, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Ibrahim came, and Ismail was sharpening arrows near Zamzam, and when he saw him, he went to him, and they did as a father does to his son and a son does to his father, then he said: O Ishmael, God has commanded me to do something. He said: Do what your Lord has commanded you. He said: Will you help me? He said: And I will help you. He said: God has commanded me to build a house here! And he pointed to the Kaaba, and the Kaaba was elevated above what was around it. He said: At that time they raised the foundations of the house. He said: So Ishmael began to bring stones, and Abraham was building, until when the building was elevated, he brought this stone and placed it for him, and he stood on it while he was building, and Ishmael was handing him the stones and they were saying: Our Lord, accept from us.

Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing, until they had gone around the House. Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated, Ubaydullah ibn Abdul Majeed Abu Ali al-Hanafi narrated, Ibrahim ibn Nafi’ narrated, I heard Kathir ibn Kathir narrating, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He - meaning Ibrahim - came and found Ismail fixing arrows from behind Zamzam. Ibrahim said: O Ismail, God, your Lord, has commanded me to build Him a House. Ismail said to him: Obey your Lord in what He has commanded you. Ibrahim said to him: He has commanded you to help me with it. He said: Then I will do it. He said: So he stood with him, and Ibrahim began to build it, and Surat Al-Baqarah 2:128 Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.

Ismail handed him the stones, and they were saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” When the building was raised and the old man was too weak to lift the stones, he stood on a stone, and it was the Station of Ibrahim, and he began to hand it to them, and they were saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.”
Others said: Rather, the one who raised the foundations of the House was Abraham alone, and Ishmael was a young child at that time.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, they said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Haritha ibn Mudrib, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: When Abraham was ordered to build the House, Ismail and Hagar went out with him. He said: When he arrived in Mecca, he saw above his head in the place of the House something like a cloud, in it like a head, so he spoke to it and said: O Abraham, build in my shadow or according to my size, do not increase or decrease. So when he built, he went out, and Ismail and Hagar went out, and Hagar said: O Abraham, to whom do you entrust us? He said: To God. She said: Go, for He will not let us down. He said: So Ismail became very thirsty. He said: So Hagar climbed up Safa and looked, but did not see anything. Then she came to Marwa and looked, but did not see anything. Then she returned to Safa and looked, but did not see anything. Until she did that seven times. Then she said: O Ismail, die where I do not see you. She came to him while he was prostrating his foot from thirst. Gabriel called her and said: Who are you? She said: I am Hagar, the mother of Abraham's son. He said: To whom have you been entrusted? She said: We entrust you both to God. He said: And you both are entrusted to Kaf! The boy probed the ground with his finger, and Zamzam gushed forth and began to hold back the water. He said: Leave it, for it is a quencher. Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated, Abu Al-Ahwas narrated, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara: A man stood up to Ali and said: Will you not tell me about the House? Was it the first House established on Earth? He said: No, but it is the first House in which blessing was established, the Station of Abraham, and whoever enters it will be safe. If you wish, I will tell you how it was built. God revealed to Abraham, Build Me a House on Earth. Abraham was fed up with that, so God sent the Sakina, a strong wind with two heads. One of them followed the other until it reached Mecca, and it folded over the site of the House like a veil folds. Abraham was commanded to build where the Sakina would settle. So Abraham built, and one stone remained. The boy went looking for something, but Abraham said: No! Bring me a stone as He commanded you. The boy went looking for a stone, and when he came to it, he found that the Black Stone had been installed in its place. He said: O my father, who brought you this stone? He said: It was brought to me by someone who did not rely on your construction. Gabriel brought it from heaven. So he completed it.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Samak, he said:
m: I heard Khalid ibn Arʿara narrating, on the authority of Ali, something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said,
m: Shu’bah, Hammad bin Salamah, and Abu Al-Ahwas told us, all of them, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, on the authority of Ali, something similar.

x: Whoever says: Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations, or: Abraham raised them and Ishmael was handing him the stones, then the correct interpretation of what he says is that the pronoun in the statement refers to Abraham and Ishmael. The statement then would be: And when Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations of the House, saying, Our Lord, accept from us. It would have been possible, according to this interpretation, for the pronoun in the statement to refer specifically to Ishmael and not to Abraham, and to Abraham specifically and not to Ishmael, were it not for what most of the people of interpretation believe, that the pronoun in the statement refers to Abraham and Ishmael together. As for the interpretation narrated on the authority of Ali: that Abraham was the one who raised the foundations without Ishmael, then it is not permissible for the implied statement at that time to be for anyone other than Ishmael in particular.

The correct statement in our view is that the implied statement refers to Abraham and Ishmael, and that the foundations of the House were raised by Abraham and Ishmael together. That is because if Abraham and Ishmael were the ones who built and raised it, then that is what we said. And if Abraham was the only one who built it, and Ishmael was the one who handed it to him, then they also raised it, because raising it was done by them: one of them built it, and the other carried the stones to it, and helped put the stones in their places. The Arabs do not refrain from attributing the building to the one who caused the building and his help. We said what we said about that because all the people of interpretation agreed that Ishmael was meant by the report that God informed about him and his father, that they were saying it, and that was their saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.”

It is known that Ishmael would not have said that unless he was either a mature man, or a young man who understood the places of harm from benefit, and was bound by the obligations and rulings of God. And if he was in the case of his father building what God had commanded him to build and raising the foundations of the House of God in this way, then it is known that he did not neglect his father’s assistance: either in building, or in transporting the stones. Whichever of these was from him, it entered into the meaning of raising the foundations of the House, and it was proven that the implied statement is report about him and his father Abraham, peace be upon them. The interpretation of the words: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, they said: Our Lord, accept from us our work, our obedience to You, and our worship of You, in our fulfillment of Your command which You commanded us to do, in building Your House which You commanded us to build.

Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing. In the narration of God the Most High that they raised the foundations of the House while saying: Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, there is clear evidence that their building was not a dwelling place in which they would live, nor a house in which they would descend. Rather, it is evidence that they built it and raised its foundations for whoever wanted to worship God, seeking to draw closer to God by doing so. Therefore, they said: Our Lord, accept from us. If they had built it as a dwelling place for themselves, their saying: Accept from us would not have had any clear meaning. Because if that were the case, they would have been asking God to accept from them something that would not bring them closer to Him. And their place is not to ask God to accept something that would not bring them closer to Him.
The statement in the interpretation of his saying: Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

The interpretation of His statement: Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing is that You are the All-Hearing, our supplication and our request to You to accept what we asked You to accept from us, of obeying You in building Your House that You commanded us to build. The All-Knowing is what is in the depths of our souls of submission to You in obedience, and the destination to that in which there is contentment and love for You, and what we show and conceal of our deeds, as Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, Abu Kathir told me, he said, Saʿid ibn Jubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas: Accept from us, indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, he says: Accept from us, indeed You are the Hearer of supplication.

evidence.text: He mentioned that this is also the case in the reading of Ibn Masʿud.

x: This is also report from God Almighty about Abraham and Ishmael: that they were raising the foundations of the House and they were saying: Our Lord, and make us Muslims to You, meaning by that: And make us submissive to Your command, subject to Your obedience, not associating with You anyone in obedience other than You, nor in worship other than You. We have previously demonstrated that the meaning of Islam is submission to God through obedience. As for his saying: And from our descendants a nation devoted to You, they specifically mentioned some of their descendants, because God Almighty had informed Abraham, His friend, peace and blessings be upon him, before this question of his, that some of his descendants would not fulfill His covenant due to their injustice and immorality. So they specifically mentioned some of their descendants with the call. It was said that they meant the Arabs.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told us, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And from our descendants is a nation submissive to You, meaning the Arabs.

x: This is a statement that the apparent meaning of the Book indicates the opposite of. Because its apparent meaning indicates that they called upon God to make from their descendants people of His obedience and guardianship, and those who responded to His command. And among the descendants of Abraham were Arabs and non-Arabs, and those who responded to the command of God and submitted to Him in obedience, from both groups. So there is no basis for the statement of those who said: Abraham meant by his call a group of his descendants specifically and not others, except for the control that no one is incapable of. As for the nation in this context, it means a group of people, from God’s statement:
h
And among the people of Moses was a nation guiding with the truth (al-A’raf 7
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And show us our rites
There is a difference in the reading of this.
Some of them read it:
h
And show us our rites

, meaning seeing them with the eye, i.e. show them to our eyes so that we can see them. This is the reading of most of the people of Hijaz and Kufa. Some of those who interpreted it in this way made the ra of arana silent, but pronounced it with a kasra. The author of this article and the reader of this reading differed in the interpretation of his saying: Our rituals.
Some of them said: They are the rituals and landmarks of Hajj.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And show us our rites

, so God showed them their rites: circumambulating the House, running between Safa and Marwa, leaving Arafat, leaving Jam’a, and stoning the Jamarat, until God completed the religion or: His religion.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And show us our rites
, he said: Show us our rites and our Hajj.

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: When Abraham and Ishmael finished building the House, God commanded him to call out, saying: And proclaim to mankind the Hajj (al-Hajj 22:27). So he called out between the two wooden pillars of Mecca: O people! Indeed, God commands you to perform Hajj to His House. He said: It was ingrained in the heart of every believer, and everyone who heard him, whether mountain, tree, or animal, responded to him: Here I am, here I am. So they responded to him with the Talbiyah: Here I am, O God, here I am, and whoever came to him came to him. Then God commanded him to go out to Arafat, and described it to him, so he went out. When he reached the tree at Al-Aqaba, Satan met him, and threw seven pebbles at him, glorifying God with each pebble. He flew and landed on the second Jamrah as well, but it stopped him, so he threw it and glorified God, and it flew and landed on the third Jamrah, so he threw it and glorified God. When he saw that he could not bear it, and Ibrahim did not know where to go, he set out until he came to Dhul-Majaz. When he looked at it and did not recognize it, he passed on, and for that reason it was called Dhul-Majaz. Then he set out until he reached Arafat, and when he looked at it, he recognized the description. He said: I have recognized it! So it was called Arafat. Ibrahim stood at Arafat until evening came and he approached a group, and it was called Al-Muzdalifah, then he stopped at Jam’ah. Then he Surat Al-Baqarah 2:129 Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. went on until he came to the devil where he had met him the first time, and he threw seven pebbles at him seven times. Then he stayed in Mina until he had finished the Hajj and his command. That is what he said:
h
And show us our rites

x: Others who read this reading said that the rituals are the slaughterhouses. So the interpretation of this verse, according to the one who said that, was: And show us how we can sacrifice our women to You, O our Lord, so that we may slaughter them for You.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’:
m: And show us our rituals, he said: our slaughter.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: Our slaughterhouses.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ata’ said:
m: I heard Ubayd ibn Umair say: And show us our rituals, he said: Show us our altars.

x: Others read:
h
And show us our rites
with a sukoon on the ra and claimed that the meaning of that is: And taught us, and guided us to it, not that its meaning is: Show us it with our eyes.

i: They claimed that this is similar to the saying of Hatayit bin Ya’far, the brother of Al-Aswad bin Ya’far:
x: Show me a horse that died of emaciation, for I see what you see, or an immortal miser.
He meant by his saying: Show me, guide me to it and let me know its location, and he did not mean seeing it with the eye. This is a reading narrated by some of the predecessors.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ata’ said:
m: Show us our rituals, bring them out to us, we will teach them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Ibn al-Musayyab said:
m: Ali bin Abi Talib said: When Abraham finished building the House, he said: I have done it, O Lord, so show us our rituals and make them clear to us, so we will learn them. So God sent Gabriel, and he performed the Hajj with him.

x: The statement is the same. Whoever breaks the raʿ makes the yaʿ in the saying of the speaker drop, and leaves the raʿ broken as it was before the jazm. Whoever sukun the raʿ in aarna thinks that the iʿrab of the letter is in the raʿ, so he sukun it in the jazm, as they did in lam yakun and lam yakun. Whether it is from the vision of the eye or the vision of the heart. There is no meaning to the difference between the vision of the eye in this regard and the vision of the heart. As for the rituals, they are the plural of mansak, which is the place where one performs rituals for God, and draws near to Him through righteous deeds that please Him: either by slaughtering an animal for Him, or by praying, circumambulating, or walking, and other righteous deeds. That is why the places of Hajj are called its rituals, because they are signs and marks that people are accustomed to and frequent.

The origin of the word mansik in Arabic is: the usual place that a man is accustomed to and familiar with. It is said: So-and-so has a mansik, if he has a place that he frequents for good or evil. That is why the rituals are called manasik, because they are customary and people frequent them for Hajj and Umrah, and for deeds that draw closer to God. It has been said that the meaning of asceticism is: worshipping God. And that the ascetic is called an ascetic because of the worship of his Lord.
Those who said this article interpreted His statement:
h
And show us our rites

, as “and teach us Your worship. How should we worship You? Where should we worship You? And what pleases You about us, so that we may do it?” This statement, even if it is a doctrine that the speech allows, the most prevalent meaning of the rituals is what we described before, that they are the rituals of Hajj whose meaning we mentioned. This statement was made by Abraham and Ishmael as a question from them to their Lord for themselves. Rather, it was a question from them to their Lord for themselves and their Muslim descendants. So when they included their Muslim descendants to themselves, they became as if they were informing about themselves with that. And we said that this is so because the supplication from them for the Muslims from their descendants came before in the beginning of the verse, and came after it in the other verse.

As for what is in the beginning of the verse, it is their saying: Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. Then they included themselves and the Muslim nation from their descendants, in their question to their Lord to show them their rites, so they said:
h
And show us our rites

. As for what is in the verse after it: Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves, they made the question specifically for their descendants. It was mentioned that in Ibn Masoud’s reading: And show them their rituals, meaning by that, And show our Muslim descendants their rituals.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And accept our repentance, for You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.

As for repentance, its origin is returning from something disliked to something beloved. The servant’s repentance to his Lord is his return from what God dislikes from him, by regretting it, ceasing it, and resolving not to return to it. The Lord’s repentance to His servant is His return to him by forgiving him for his crime, and pardoning him for the punishment of his sin, as forgiveness for him and a favor from Him to him.
Did they have sins that made them need to ask their Lord for repentance?

There is no one more pious than God’s creation who has not done work between him and his Lord that requires him to repent and turn to Him. It is possible that what they said was specific to the situation they were in, of raising the foundations of the House. Because that was the place where God would most likely answer their supplication, and so that they would make what they did a tradition to be followed after them, and people would take that spot after them as a place of absolution from sins to God. It is possible that they meant by their saying: And have mercy on us, and have mercy on the oppressors among our children and our descendants whose oppression and polytheism You have informed us of, so that they may turn to Your obedience. So the apparent meaning of the speech is that the supplication is for themselves, but what is meant by it is their descendants.

Just as one says: So-and-so honored me in my children and family, and so-and-so was dutiful to me, if his son was dutiful to him. As for his saying: Indeed, You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful, what he means by it is: Indeed, You are the One who returns to Your servants with favor, and is generous to them with pardon and forgiveness, the Most Merciful to them, the One who rescues whomever You will among them with Your mercy from their destruction, the One who saves whomever You want to save among them with Your compassion from Your wrath.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of this.
Some of them read it: And show us our rites, meaning seeing them with the eye, i.e. show them to our eyes so that we can see them.
This is the reading of most of the people of Hijaz and Kufa.
The author of this article and the reader of this reading differed in the interpretation of his saying: Our rituals.
Others who read this reading said that the rituals are the slaughterhouses.
This is a reading narrated by some of the predecessors.

x: This is the supplication of Abraham and Ishmael specifically for our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is the supplication that our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: I am the supplication of my father Abraham, and the good report of Jesus.

c: Ibn Hamid told us that, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Thawr ibn Yazid, on the authority of Khalid ibn Maʿdan al-Kilaʿi:
m: “A group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Messenger of God, tell us about yourself. He said: Yes, I am the supplication of my father Abraham, and the good report of Jesus, may God bless them and grant them peace.”

c: Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me, he said, Abu Al-Yaman told us, he said, Abu Kurayb told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Maryam, on the authority of Saeed bin Suwaid, on the authority of Al-Arbadh bin Sariyah Al-Sulami, he said:
m: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “I am with God in the Mother of the Book, the Seal of the Prophets, while Adam was still kneading in his clay. I will inform you of the interpretation of that: I am the supplication of my father Abraham, the glad tidings of Jesus to his people, and the vision of my mother.”

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Mu’awiyah told me
m: - and Ubayd bin Adam bin Abi Iyas al-Asqalani told me, he said, my father told me, he said, al-Layth bin Sa’d told us, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Salih, they both said, on the authority of Sa’id bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hilal al-Salami, on the authority of Arabadh bin Sariyah al-Salami, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Suwaid, on the authority of Abd al-A’la bin Hilal al-Salami, on the authority of Arabadh bin Sariyah: that he said:
m: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, and he mentioned something similar. And what we said about that was said by a group of people of interpretation.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from among themselves, so God did that, so He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves, whose face and lineage they knew, who would take them out of darkness into the light, and guide them to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy.

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from among themselves, he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from among themselves, who is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So it was said to him: That has been answered, and it is at the end of time.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
He recites to them Your verses
: He recites to them Your Book that You reveal to him.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And He teaches them the Book and wisdom.
What is meant by the book is the Qur’an. I have previously explained why the Qur’an is called a book, and what its interpretation is. This is the opinion of a group of interpreters.
Mention of who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And He teaches them the Book, the Qur’an. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the wisdom that God mentioned in this place.

x: Some of them said: It is the Sunnah.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And wisdom, meaning the Sunnah.

x: Some of them said: Wisdom is knowledge of religion and understanding of it.
Mention of who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: I said to Malik: What is wisdom? He said: Knowledge of religion, understanding of religion, and following it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: And wisdom, he said: Wisdom is the religion that they do not know except through him, may God bless him and grant him peace, he teaches it to them. He said: And why wisdom, the mind in religion? And he recited: And whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good (al-Baqarah 2:269), and He said about Jesus: And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel
r
(Al-Imran: 48)

, he said: And Ibn Zayd recited: And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he slipped out of them (al-A’raf 7:175), he said: He did not benefit from the signs, since there was no wisdom with them. He said: Or wisdom, something that God places in the heart, enlightening it with it.

x: The correct statement in our view about wisdom is that it is the knowledge of the rulings of God, the knowledge of which cannot be attained except through the explanation of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and knowledge of it, and what is indicated by it from its counterparts. In my view, it is taken from the word hukm which means the distinction between right and wrong, like jalsa and sit from qusulu and qudu sitting. It is said from it: So-and-so is wise in his wisdom, meaning that he is clear in his accuracy in his words and actions. If this is the case, then the interpretation of the verse is: Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from among themselves who will recite to them Your verses, and teach them Your Book that You send down to them, and the details of Your judgment and the rulings that You teach him.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And purifies them
We have previously demonstrated that the meaning of purification is cleansing, and that the meaning of zakat is growth and increase.
The meaning of his saying:
h
And purifies them
in this place:
h
And purifies them
from associating partners with God and worshipping idols, and increases them and multiplies them through obedience to God, as:

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He recites to them Your verses
and teaches them the Book, he said: He means by purification, obedience to God and sincerity.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding his statement:
h
And purifies them
, he said: He purifies them from polytheism and delivers them from it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

By that, the Most High means: O Lord, You are the Mighty and the Strong, Whom nothing He wills is impossible, so do with us and our offspring what we have asked and requested of You. And the Wise in Whose management there is no fault or error, so give us what will benefit us and our offspring, and will not diminish You or Your treasures.

God Almighty meant by His saying: And whoever turns away from the religion of Abraham, which of the people would be indifferent to the religion of Abraham and abandon it out of a desire for something else? God meant by this the Jews and Christians, because they chose what they chose of Judaism and Christianity over Islam. Because the religion of Abraham is the true Islam, as God the Almighty said:
Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim
God the Almighty said to them: And who would abandon the true Islam of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself?

c: As Bishr ibn Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And who would abandon the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself? The Jews and Christians abandoned their religion, and adopted Judaism and Christianity as an innovation not from God, and they abandoned the religion of Abraham, meaning Islam - true Islam? Likewise, God sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the religion of Abraham.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement: And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself? He said: The Jews and Christians turned away from the religion of Abraham, and innovated Judaism and Christianity, which are not from God, and they abandoned the religion of Abraham: Islam.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
Except for he who makes a fool of himself
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
Except for he who makes a fool of himself
h
