except for he who makes a fool of himself
. We have previously explained that the meaning of foolishness is ignorance.

The meaning of the statement is: And none turns away from the pure religion of Abraham except a fool who is ignorant of the place of his own good fortune in what benefits him and harms him in his afterlife, as Yunus told me, he said:

c: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except for he who makes a fool of himself

, he said: Except for he who misses his good fortune. The soul is placed in the accusative case in the sense of the interpreter. This is because foolishness originally refers to the soul, but when it was transferred to whoever, the soul was placed in the accusative case in the sense of interpreting. Just as one says: He is the most spacious of you in a house, so the house is included in the statement on the basis that the spaciousness is in it, not in the man. Likewise, the soul was included because foolishness refers to the soul, not to whoever. Therefore, it is not permissible to say: Your brother was foolish. Rather, it is permissible to explain it with the soul, and it is added to a definite noun, because it is in the interpretation of an indefinite noun. Some Basra grammarians said: His saying: He made himself foolish is considered foolish if the verb is intransitive, but he made it transitive to himself and his opinion and similar things that are in meaning like foolishness, if it is not transitive. As for ghabna and khassara they may be transitive to something else, it is said: ghabna khamsin and khassara khamsin.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And We chose him in this world
God Almighty means by His statement,
h
And We chose him in this world
, that We chose Abraham. The ha in His statement,
h
We chose him

, is from the mention of Abraham. Al-Istifāṭā is derived from al-Ṣafwā, and likewise istashfīna iftālāna is derived from it. Its ta’ was made a ta’ because its point of articulation is close to the point of articulation of the sad. What he means by his saying:
h
We chose him

is: We selected him and chose him for ease, and we will make him an imam in this world for those who come after him. This is report from God, the Most High, that whoever opposes Abraham in what He has prescribed for those who come after him, is opposing God, and informing His creation that whoever opposes what Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, brought, is opposing Abraham. This is because God, the Most High, informed that He chose him for his friendship, and made him an imam for the people, and informed that his religion was the pure, Muslim faith.
In this, the clearest statement from God, the Most High, that whoever opposes him is an enemy of God, for opposing the imam whom God appointed for His servants.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous.

God Almighty means by His saying: And indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous, that Abraham will be among the righteous in the Hereafter. The righteous among the sons of Adam is the one who fulfills the rights of God upon him. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:131 When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds."

c: So the Almighty informed us
m: about Abraham, His friend, that he is his confidant in this world, and his friend in the hereafter, and that he will come to the places of his faithful friends.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
When his Lord said to him

, ‘Submit,’ that his Lord said to him: Be sincere in your worship of Me, and submit to Me in obedience. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of Islam in the speech of the Arabs, so there is no need to repeat it. As for the meaning of his saying: He said, ‘I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds,’ he means, may He be exalted, that Abraham said, responding to his Lord: I have submitted in obedience and devoted my worship to the Owner of all creation and its Manager, and no one else.
You know that idh is a time, but what is it used to time? And what is it related to?
It is a connection to his saying:
h
And We had chosen him in this world
. The interpretation of the statement:
h
And We had chosen him in this world
h
when his Lord said to him
: Submit, he said: I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds. The meaning of the statement is:
h
And We had chosen him in this world
when We said to him: Submit, he said: I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.
So the name of God was made apparent in his saying: “
h
When his Lord said to him

: Submit,” as a report about an absent person, and it had been mentioned before as a report about himself, as Khafaf bin Nudbah said: I say to him, the spear framing his back: Think lightly, I am that one. If someone asks us: Did God call Abraham to Islam? He was told: Yes, he invited him to it. If he said: In what condition did he call him to it? It was said that when he said: “O my people, indeed I am innocent of what you associate with God. Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with God.” (al-An’am 6:78-79), that was the time
h
when his Lord said to him
: Submit, after He tested him with the planets, the moon, and the sun.

God Almighty meant by His statement: And He enjoined it, and He enjoined this word. He meant by the word His statement: I have submitted to the Lord of the Worlds, which is the Islam that His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to follow, which is the sincerity of worship and monotheism for God, and the submission of the heart and limbs to Him. His saying:
h
And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons
, means that he entrusted them with it and ordered them to do it.
As for his saying: And Jacob, he means: And Jacob also commanded this to his sons, as:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said: Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, he said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
And Abraham commanded this to his sons
, and Jacob, he says: And Jacob commanded this to his sons after Abraham.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons
, he enjoined them to Islam, and Jacob enjoined the same.

x: Some of them said that his statement,
h
And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons
, is a contradictory predicate. And his statement, and Jacob, is a subject predicate. For he said,
h
And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons
, that they should say: We have submitted to the Lord of the Worlds. Jacob enjoined his sons:
h
O my sons
, indeed
h
God has chosen for you this religion

, so do not die except as Muslims. There is no meaning to what those who said that said. Because what Jacob recommended to his sons is similar to what Abraham recommended to his sons: urging them to obey God, submit to Him, and submit to Him.
If the matter is as you described, that its meaning is: And Abraham commanded his sons and Jacob:
h
O my sons
, then why is that omitted from the speech?

Because the will is a statement, it was taken according to its meaning. That is because if it had come in the form of a statement, the an would not have been appropriate with it. Rather, it would have been said: And Abraham said to his sons and Jacob:
h
O my sons
So since the will was a statement, it was taken according to its meaning without its wording, so the an that would have been appropriate with it was omitted, as God Almighty said:
“God instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females”

and as the poet said: I will show you, in what I show myself, a longing for Najd I miss Sindh So I deleted the an, since expressing the meaning with the tongue was a statement, so I carried it on its meaning without its wording. Some Arabists have said that the an was omitted from his statement,
h
And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons
, and so did Jacob, because the calling was sufficient, meaning the calling was his statement,
h
O my sons

. He claimed that his reason for that was that it is the custom of the Arabs to be satisfied with the tools instead of an, like their saying, I called, did you get up? and I called, where is Zayd? because.
He said: And perhaps they included it with the tools, so they said, I called, did you get up?

A group of readers read: And Abraham recommended it, meaning: a covenant. As for the one who reads wasaa with emphasis, he means by that he entrusted them with a covenant after a covenant, and he entrusted them with one will after another.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
O my sons
, indeed
h
God has chosen for you this religion
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
God has chosen for you this religion
, that
h
God has chosen for you this religion

which He has entrusted to you, and has chosen it for you. The definite article was included in the religion because those of their children and grandchildren who were addressed with this had known it through their will to them and their covenant with them regarding it. Then they said to them after they had known it to them:
h
God has chosen for you this religion
in which He has entrusted you, so fear God lest you die except while you are upon it.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: So do not die except as Muslims.

If someone were to say to us: Is death and life the property of the children of Adam, so that one of them is forbidden to die except in one state rather than another? It was said to him: The meaning of that is not what you thought. Rather, the meaning of: Do not die except as Muslims, is: Do not leave this religion, which is Islam, during your lives. This is because no one knows when his death will come to him, so they said to them: Do not die except as Muslims, because you do not know when your deaths will come to you, whether by night or by day, so do not leave Islam, lest your deaths come to you while you are not following the religion that your Lord has chosen for you, and you die while your Lord is angry with you, and you perish.

evidence.text: A group of readers read: And Abraham recommended it, meaning: a covenant.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
Or were you witnesses

, were you? But He asked with or since it was a question that resumed a statement that preceded it, as it was said: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The revelation of the Book, about which there is no doubt, is from the Lord of the worlds. Or do they say, ‘He invented it’?” (al-Sajdah 32:1-3). And the Arabs do the same in every question that they begin after a statement that preceded it, they ask with or. Martyrs is the plural of martyr, just as partners is the plural of partner, and opponents is the plural of opponent.

The interpretation of the statement is: Were you, O group of Jews and Christians, who disbelieved in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and denied his prophethood, the presence of Jacob and his witnessing when death approached him? That is, you were not present at that, so do not call falsehoods upon My prophets and messengers, and attribute to them Judaism and Christianity, for I sent My two friends Abraham and his sons Isaac and Ishmael and their descendants with the true, Muslim faith, and with that they commanded their children, and with that they enjoined upon their children after them. So if you were present with them and heard from them, you would know that they were not upon the religions and sects that you attributed to them after them. These verses were revealed as a refutation from God Almighty to the Jews and Christians in their claim regarding Abraham and his son Jacob: that they were of their religion.
So He said to them in this verse:
h
Or were you witnesses
when death approached Jacob? So you learned what he said to his son and what his son said to him?

c: Then He informed them
m: of what he said to them and what they said to him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Or were you witnesses
, meaning the People of the Book.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
What will you worship after me
They said: We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac - one God, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.
God Almighty means by His saying: When he said to his sons, when Jacob said to his sons. This idh is repeated as a replacement for the first idh, meaning:
h
Or were you witnesses
of Jacob, when Jacob said to his sons when he was about to die? What he means by his saying:
h
What will you worship after me

? What will you worship, after me? That is, after my death? They said: We will worship your God, meaning that his sons said to him: We will worship your God whom you worship, and the God of your fathers Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, one God, meaning: We will devote our worship to Him, and we will make His Lordship one, so we will not associate anything with Him, and we will not take any lord besides Him. What he means by his saying:
h
And we are Muslims to Him
, is that we are subject to Him in servitude and obedience. His saying:
h
And we are Muslims to Him
may mean a state, as if they said: We worship your God, submitting to Him through our obedience and worship of Him.
It may also be a new statement, in which case it means: We worship your God after you,
h
and we are Muslims to Him

now and in every state. The best of these two interpretations is that it means a state, and that it means: We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, submitting to His worship. It was said: Ishmael was mentioned before Isaac because Ishmael was older than Isaac.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: They said, ‘We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac,’ he said: It is said that he began with Ishmael, because he is older. And some of the earlier scholars read: And the God of your father Abraham, thinking that Ishmael, since he was Jacob’s uncle, was not… It is possible that he was among those who translated from the fathers, and included among them. This is also from his reader, his lack of knowledge of the flow of Arabic speech. The Arabs do not refrain from making paternal uncles mean fathers, and maternal uncles mean mothers. Therefore, Ishmael was included among those who translated from the fathers. And Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, translation from the fathers, are in the position of a genitive, but they made it accusative because they do not have a genitive. The correct reading for us in this regard is: And the God of your fathers, because the readers unanimously agree on the correctness of this, and the deviation of those readers who disagreed with him and read otherwise. The accusative case of his saying: a god is in the state of his saying: your god.

evidence.text: The correct reading for us in this regard is: And the God of your fathers, because the readers unanimously agree on the correctness of this, and the deviation of those readers who disagreed with him and read otherwise.

x: God Almighty means by His saying: That is a nation that has passed on, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and their children. He says to the Jews and Christians: O group of Jews and Christians, leave the mention of Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Muslims from their children without their being worthy of it, and do not attribute to them the disbelief of Judaism and Christianity, by attributing it to them, for they are a nation. And by the nation in this place he means: the group and the generation of people that has passed away: it has gone its way. The one who has died and gone is called departed, because he has left the world and is isolated from the familiarity with his family and companions in his world. Its origin is from their saying: The man was alone, when he was in a place where he had no one to keep him company, and he was isolated from people. So it was used for someone who dies, in that way.

Then the Almighty said to the Jews and Christians: As for those of My prophets and messengers whom you attribute your misguidance and disbelief to, which you are upon, they have earned nothing. The ha and the alif in his saying: for her refer, if you wish, to that, and if you wish, to the nation. What he means by his saying: For her is what she has earned, is whatever good she has done. And for you, O Jews and Christians, is the same for what you have done. And you, who have given them the religions you have given them, will not be held accountable, so that you will be asked about what Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and their children did. They earned good and evil, because every soul has earned what it has earned and will bear what it has earned. So leave their making up and making up their religions, for making up your claims will not benefit you with God. Rather, what will benefit you with Him is what you have done in the past of your good deeds, if you have done them and sent them forward.
God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And they said

, ‘Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided,’ that the Jews said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his believing companions: Be Jews and you will be guided? And the Christians said to them: Be Christians and you will be guided. By her saying: You will be guided, she means: you will find the path of truth, as Abu Kurayb told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, and Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us all, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zayd bin Thabit, told me, who said: Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abdullah bin Suriya al-Awar said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is no guidance except what we are upon! So follow us, O Muhammad, and you will be guided! And the Christians said the same.
So God, the Almighty, revealed about them:
h
And they said
, ‘Be Jews or Christians [so] you will be guided.’ Say, ‘Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth,
h
and he was not of the polytheists

God provided His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the most eloquent, concise, and complete argument, and taught it to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: O Muhammad, say to those who say to you from the Jews and Christians and to your companions: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided: Rather, come, let us follow the religion of Abraham, which we all agree to bear witness to as the religion of God which He chose, selected, and commanded. For his religion was the pure, Muslim faith, and let us abandon all other religions in which we differ, some of us denying them and some of us affirming them. For despite their differences, there is no way for us to unite upon them, just as we have the way to unite upon the religion of Abraham. There are three aspects to the accusative case of his statement: Rather, the religion of Abraham.
The first is that the meaning of his statement:
h
And they said
, ‘Be Jews or Christians,’ is directed to the meaning:
h
And they said

, ‘Follow Judaism and Christianity.’ Because when they said, Be Jews or Christians, they left Judaism and Christianity, then the word religion is connected to that meaning. So the meaning of the statement then is: Say, O Muhammad, we do not follow Judaism and Christianity, nor do we take them as a religion, rather we follow the religion of Abraham, the upright one. Then the second word follow is deleted, and the word religion is connected to the inflection of Judaism and Christianity. The other: that it is made accusative by an implied verb meaning we follow. The third: that what was meant was: Rather, we will be the people of the religion of Abraham, or the people of the religion of Abraham.

i: Then the people and companions were omitted, and the religion was established in their place, since it conveyed the meaning of the speech, as the poet said:
x: I thought my camel's embrace was an embrace! But it is not an embrace, except for you and others.

Meaning: the sound of an embrace, so the word religion is then in the accusative case, in apposition to the Jews and Christians. It may be permissible for it to be in the accusative case as an encouragement to follow the religion of Abraham. Some readers read it with the nominative case. The interpretation of it, according to the reading of those who read it with the nominative case, is: Rather, guidance is the religion of Abraham. Say in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘Rather, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth,
h
and he was not of the polytheists

The religion is the faith. As for the Hanif, he is the upright in everything. It has been said that the man who has one foot in front of the other is called Hanif, in reference to his safety, just as it is said of a perishable country, meaning the attainment of salvation and safety from it, and just as it is said of a healthy person who has been bitten, as an optimism for his safety from destruction, and the like. So the meaning of the statement is: Say, O Muhammad, but we follow the religion of Abraham, straight. Then, the Hanif is a state of Ibrahim. As for the people of interpretation, they differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: The Hanif is the pilgrim. It was said: The religion of Abraham was called the Hanif Islam because he was the first Imam who required the worshippers who were in his time, and those who came after him until the Day of Resurrection to follow him in the rituals of Hajj, and to imitate him in it. They said: So whoever performs Hajj to the House and performs the rituals of Abraham according to his religion, he is a Hanif, a Muslim according to the religion of Abraham.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said, al-Qasim bin al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Katheer Abu Sahl, he said:
m: I asked al-Hasan about the Hanafi school, he said: The pilgrimage to the House.

c: Muhammad bin Ubadah al-Asadi told me, he said, Ubayd God bin Musa told us, he said, Fadil told us, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: regarding his statement: Hanif, he said: Hanif is the pilgrim.

c: Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Fudayl, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The Hanif is the pilgrim.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Katheer bin Ziyad, he said,
m: I asked al-Hasan about the Hanafi school, he said: It is the pilgrimage to this House. Ibn al-Taymi said: Juwaybir told me, on the authority of al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Hanifa, he said: Hajjaj.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Hanif, he said: A pilgrim.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Wakee’, on the authority of Fadil bin Ghazwan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Qasim, who said:
m: The people of Mudhrijun al-Kaaba in the pre-Islamic era were called Hanifa, then God Almighty revealed: Hanifa for God, not associating anything with Him (al-Hajj 22:31).

x: Others said: Al-Hanafi is the follower, as we described before, from the saying of those who said: Its meaning is: righteousness.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Hanifa, he said: followers.

x: Others said: The religion of Abraham was called the Hanafi religion because he was the first imam to institute circumcision for the servants, and those who came after him followed him in it. They said: So whoever is circumcised in the manner of Abraham’s circumcision is on the same Islam as Abraham was, so he is a Hanafi according to the religion of Abraham.

Others said: Rather, it is the religion of Abraham, the upright one. Rather, it is the religion of Abraham, the sincere one. The upright one according to what they say: is the one whose religion is sincere to God alone.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, he said: sincerely.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the Hanafi school of thought, Islam. So whoever follows Abraham in his religion and adheres to it, he is a Hanafi.

Hanafi, in my opinion, is adherence to the religion of Abraham and following his creed. This is because if Hanafiyyah were the pilgrimage to the House, then those who performed Hajj in the pre-Islamic era from among the polytheists would have to have been Hanafi. God denied that this was Hanafi by saying:
But he was a Muslim inclining toward truth,
h
and he was not of the polytheists
The same applies to circumcision. If the Hanafi faith was circumcision, then the Jews would have to be Hanafi. God excluded them from that by saying:
Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was one inclining toward truth, a Muslim

It is therefore true that the Hanafi school is not circumcision alone, nor the Hajj alone, but rather it is what we have described: adherence to the religion of Abraham, following him in it, and imitating him in it.

Were not those who came before Abraham, peace be upon him, from the prophets and their followers, steadfast in what they were commanded to do in obeying God, as steadfast as Abraham and his followers?
Yes.
How can the Hanafi school be attributed to Abraham and his followers in his religion in particular, and not to all the other prophets before him and their followers?

Every prophet before Abraham was a Hanif who followed the obedience of God, but God Almighty did not make any of them an imam for those of His servants who came after him until the Day of Resurrection, as He did with Abraham. He made him an imam in what he taught of the rituals of Hajj and circumcision, and other Islamic laws, as an act of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:136 Say, "We believe in God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and what was given to the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him." worship to be followed forever until the Day of Resurrection. He made what He established of that a distinguishing mark between the believers of His servants and their infidels, and the obedient among them to God and the disobedient. So the Hanif among the people was called Hanif because of his following of his religion and his steadfastness in his guidance and method, and the one who went astray from his religion was called by all the names of religions, so it was said: Jewish, Christian, Zoroastrian, and other types of religions.
As for his saying:
h
And he was not of the polytheists
, he says: He was not of those who worshipped idols and statues, nor was he of the Jews or Christians, but rather he was a monotheist Muslim.

evidence.text: Some readers read it with the nominative case.
The interpretation of it, according to the reading of those who read it with the nominative case, is: Rather, guidance is the religion of Abraham.

x: God Almighty meant by that: Say, O believers, to these Jews and Christians who said to you: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided, “We believe,” that is, we believe in God. We have previously demonstrated that the meaning of faith is belief, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it. And what was revealed to us, also means: We believe in the Book that God revealed to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he added the address of revelation to them, since they were his followers, and were commanded and forbidden by it. So even if it was a revelation to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the sense of revelation to them, because of the meanings that were described for them in it. What he means by his saying: and what was revealed to Abraham, is that we also believe and have faith in what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and they are the prophets from the descendants of Jacob.
And His statement:
h
And what was given to Moses and Jesus

, means: We also believe in the Torah that God gave to Moses, and in the Gospel that God gave to Jesus, and the books that were given to all the prophets, and we acknowledge and believe that all of that is truth and guidance and light from God, and that all of His prophets whom God mentioned were on the truth and guidance, confirming one another, on one path in calling to the Oneness of God and working in obedience to Him, We make no distinction between any of them, meaning: We do not believe in some prophets and disbelieve in others, and we disavow some and support others, just as the Jews disavowed Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, and acknowledged other prophets, and just as the Christians disavowed Muhammad, peace be upon him, and acknowledged other prophets. Rather, we bear witness for all of them that they were messengers of God and His prophets, sent with the truth and guidance.
As for His statement:
h
And we are Muslims to Him

, He, the Most High, means: We are submissive to Him in obedience, acquiescing in servitude to Him. He mentioned that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that to the Jews, so they disbelieved in Jesus and in those who believed in him, as Abu Kurayb told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit told me, Saeed bin Jubair told me, or Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “A group of Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them Abu Yasir bin Akhtab, Rafi’ bin Abi Rafi’, Azar, Khalid, Zaid, Azar bin Abi Azar, and Ash’i’, and they asked him about the messengers who believed in him, so he said: I believe in God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes,
h
and what was given to Moses and Jesus
and what was given to the prophets from their Lord.
We make no distinction between any of them,
h
and we are Muslims to Him

. So when he mentioned Jesus, they denied his prophethood and said: We do not believe in Jesus, and we do not believe in those who believe in him.” Then God revealed about them: Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, do you blame us for anything except that we believe in God and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are wicked?’ (al-Ma’idah 5:59). Ibn Humayd narrated, Salamah narrated, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated, on the authority of Ikrimah, or Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and mentioned something similar, except that he said: Nafiʿ ibn Abi Nafiʿ instead of Rafiʿ ibn Abi Rafiʿ. Qatada said: This verse was revealed as a command from God, the Most High, to the believers to believe in all of His messengers, as Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saʿid narrated, on the authority of Qatada: Say, ‘We believe in God and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham,’ until His saying: And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.

God commanded the believers to believe in and confirm all of His prophets and messengers, and not to differentiate between any of them. As for the tribes that he mentioned, they are twelve men from the descendants of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham.
Each man of them gave birth to a nation of people, so they were called tribes, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: The tribes are Joseph and his brothers, the sons of Jacob. He gave birth to twelve men, so each man of them gave birth to a nation of people, so they were called: tribes.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for the tribes, they are the sons of Jacob: Joseph, Benjamin, Reuben, Judah, Simeon, Levi, Dan, and Kohath.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: The tribes are Surat Al-Baqarah 2:137 So if they believe in the same as you believe, then they are rightly guided. But if they turn away, then they are only in dissension. So Allah will suffice you against them, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing. Joseph and his brothers, the sons of Jacob, twelve men, and each man of them gave birth to a nation of people, so they were called: the tribes.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me:
m: Jacob, son of Isaac, who is Israel, married his maternal uncle’s daughter, Leah, daughter of Layan, son of Tubal, son of Elias, and she bore him Reuben, son of Jacob, who was his eldest son, and Simeon, son of Jacob, and Levi, son of Jacob, and Judah, son of Jacob, and Rialon, son of Jacob, and Ishgar, son of Jacob, and Dinah, daughter of Jacob. Then Leah, daughter of Layan, died. Then Jacob had a son, Rachel, daughter of Lian, son of Tubil, son of Elias, after his sister. She bore him Joseph, son of Jacob, and Benjamin, which is called Asad in Arabic. He had four sons from two of his concubines: one of them was named Zilpah and the other Bilhah: Dan, son of Jacob, Naphtali, son of Jacob, Gad, son of Jacob, and Asherab, son of Jacob. The sons of Jacob were twelve men. God spread out from them twelve tribes, and none can count their number nor know their lineage except God. God Almighty says: And We divided them into twelve tribes, nations (al-A’raf 7:160).

x: What God Almighty meant by His statement: If they believe in the same as you believe in, is that if the Jews and Christians believe in God and what was revealed to you, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what was given to the prophets from their Lord, and they acknowledge that, just as you, O believers, have believed in and acknowledged, then they have been guided and have adhered to the path of truth, and have been guided, and they are then from you and you are from them, by their entering your religion through their acknowledgment of that.
So, the Almighty indicated with this verse that He did not accept any action from anyone except by believing in these meanings that He enumerated before it, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
If they believe in the like of what you believe in

, then they are guided, and something similar to this. He said: God, the Almighty, informed us that faith is the firmest handhold, and that He does not accept any action without it, and Paradise is not forbidden except to those who abandon it. And a reading was narrated from Ibn Abbas in that regard, but the copies of the Qur’an of the Muslims came with a different reading, and the readers of the Qur’an agreed to abandon it. That is what: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, he said, Ibn Abbas said: Do not say,
h
If they believe in the like of what you believe in

, then they are guided, for there is no like unto God. But say, If they believe in that which you believe in, then they are guided, or he said: If they believe in that which you believe in. So it is as if Ibn Abbas in this narration, if it is authentic, is directing the interpretation of the reading of the one who reads:
h
If they believe in the like of what you believe in

, that is, if they believe in the like of God, and in the like of what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael. And that, if it is directed in this way, is undoubtedly polytheism with God Almighty. Because there is no like to God, may He be mentioned, so we believe in Him or disbelieve in Him. But the interpretation of that is not in the meaning to which its interpretation was directed. Rather, its meaning is what we have described, which is: If they believe in the same way as you believe in what you believe in from all that we have enumerated for you of the books of God and His prophets, then they have been guided. So the comparison only occurred between the two beliefs and acknowledgments, which are the faith of these and the faith of those. Like the saying of the speaker: Amr passed by your brother as I passed by him, meaning by that: Amr passed by your brother as I passed by him. And the comparison only entered as a comparison between the two passings, not between Amr and the speaker. Likewise, his saying:
h
If they believe in the like of what you believe in
, the comparison only occurred between the two faiths, not between the believer in it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And if they turn away
, then they are in dissension.
God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And if they turn away

, and if those who said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, Be Jews or Christians, turned away, and did not believe as you do, O believers in God, and in what the prophets brought and the messengers were sent with, and they differentiated between God’s messengers and between God and His messengers, so they believed in some and disbelieved in others, then know, O believers, that they are only in disobedience, separation, and war against God, His Messenger, and you, as Bishr bin Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatadah: Then they are only in dissension, meaning: in separation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: They are only in discord, meaning separation.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: But if they turn away, then they are only in discord, he said: Discord is separation and fighting. If someone discords, then he has fought, and if he fights, then he has discorded, and they are one and the same in the speech of the Arabs. And he recited: And whoever contradicts the Messenger
r
(An-Nisa’: 115)

x: The origin of the word shaqāq in our view, and God knows best, is taken from the saying of a speaker: This matter was difficult for him, meaning that it distressed and hurt him. Then it was said: So-and-so caused distress to so-and-so, meaning that each of them suffered from the other what distressed and hurt him, and his grievance weighed him down. From this is the saying of God Almighty: And if you fear a breach between the two
r
(An-Nisa’: 35)
, meaning: separation between them.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s Surat Al-Baqarah 2:138 The dye of Allah, and who is better than Allah at dyeing?
And we are His worshippers. saying: Then
h
God will suffice you against them
, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
God will suffice you against them

, that God will suffice you, O Muhammad, against those who said to you and your companions: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided, from the Jews and Christians, if they turn away from believing in God as your companions did, and in what was revealed to you, and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and all the other prophets besides them, and they separate between God and His messengers, either by killing with the sword, or by expelling you from your protection, and other punishments. Then God is the Hearer of what they say to you with their tongues and what they reveal to you with their mouths, of ignorance and calling to disbelief and deviant religions, and the Knower of what they conceal for you and your believing companions in themselves of envy and hatred. So God did that to them quickly, and fulfilled His promise.

He was sufficient for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by giving him power over them, until he killed some of them, exiled some of them, and humiliated and disgraced some of them with tribute and humiliation.

evidence.text: And a reading was narrated from Ibn Abbas in that regard, but the copies of the Qur’an of the Muslims came with a different reading, and the readers of the Qur’an agreed to abandon it.

So it is as if Ibn Abbas in this narration, if it is authentic, is directing the interpretation of the reading of the one who reads: If they believe in the like of what you believe in, that is, if they believe in the like of God, and in the like of what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael.

x: God Almighty means by the dye the dye of Islam. This is because when the Christians wanted to convert their children to Christianity, they put them in their water, claiming that this was a sanctification for them, similar to the ritual bath for Muslims, and that it was a dye for them in Christianity. God Almighty said when they said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his believing companions: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided. Say to them, O Muhammad: O Jews and Christians, rather follow the religion of Abraham,
h
the dye of God

which is the best dye, for it is the pure, Muslim faith, and abandon polytheism with God and straying from the path of His guidance. The dye is placed in the accusative case by reading it in the accusative case, in response to the religion. Likewise, the dye is raised by raising the religion, in response to it.
It may be permissible to raise it in a way other than this. That is on the beginning, meaning: it is
h
the dye of God
. It may be permissible to use it in a way other than responding to the religion, but according to his saying: Say, ‘We believe in God’ to his saying and we are Muslims to Him, “
h
the dye of God
,” meaning: we believe in this faith, so faith then is
h
the dye of God
. And a group of interpreters said the same thing as we said about the interpretation of dye.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
The dye of God
, and who is better than God at dyeing? The Jews dye their children as Jews, and the Christians dye their children as Christians, and
h
the dye of God
is Islam. So there is no dye better than Islam, nor purer, and it is the religion of God with which He sent Noah and the prophets after him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ata’ said:
m: h
The dye of God
, the Jews dyed their children, they went against the natural disposition.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying:
h
The dye of God
Some of them said: The religion of God.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
The dye of God
, he said: The religion of God.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The dye of God
, he said: The religion of God, And who is better than God at dyeing, and who is better than God at religion.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Fadil bin Marzouq told us, on the authority of Atiyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The dye of God
, he said: The religion of God.

c: Musa bin Harun told us, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
The dye of God
, and who is better than God at dyeing? He said: The religion of God, and who is better than God at religion.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
The dye of God
, he said: The religion of God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding God’s statement:
h
The dye of God
, he said: The religion of God.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, he said,
m: I asked Ibn Zayd about the statement of God:
h
The dye of God
, and he mentioned something similar.

x: Others said:
h
The dye of God
, the nature of God.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: The dye of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:139 Say: Do you argue with us about Allah while He is our Lord and your Lord? And to us are our deeds, and to you are your deeds, and we are sincere to Him? God, he said: The nature of God upon which He created people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Harb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And who is better than God at dyeing? He said: The dye is the natural disposition.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: h
The dye of God
means Islam, the nature of God upon which He created people. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Kathir said to me:
h
The dye of God

, he said: The religion of God, and who is better than God in religion? He said: It is the nature of God. Whoever said this statement, directed the dye to the nature, so its meaning is: Rather, we follow the nature of God and His religion upon which He created His creation, and that is the upright religion. From the saying of God Almighty: Creator of the heavens and the earth (al-An’am 6:14). Meaning the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

x: The statement in the interpretation of his saying:
h
And we are His worshippers
The words of God, the Most High:
h
And we are His worshippers

, are a command from God, the Most High, to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the Jews and Christians, who said to him and to those of his companions who followed him: Be Jews or Christians. So He said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say: Rather, we follow the religion of Abraham, the upright one,
h
the dye of God
h
and we are His worshippers

. Meaning: the religion of those who submit to God, who are submissive to Him, in following the religion of Abraham, and in our belief in Him in that, not being arrogant in following His command, and acknowledging the message of His Messengers, as the Jews and Christians were arrogant, so they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, out of arrogance, transgression, and envy.

God Almighty means by His saying: “Say: Do you argue with us about God?” Say, O Muhammad, to the community of Jews and Christians, who said to you and your companions: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided. They claimed that their religion is better than your religion, and their book is better than your book, because it was before your book, and they claimed that for that reason they are more deserving of God than you: Do you argue with us about God, while He is our Lord and your Lord? In His hand are good things, and to Him is reward and punishment, and recompense for good and bad deeds, so you claim that you are more deserving of God than we are, because your Prophet was before our Prophet, and your book was before our book, and your Lord and our Lord are one, and that each group of us has what he has done and acquired of good and bad deeds, and he is rewarded for the best of them, so he is rewarded or punished, not for lineage and precedence of religion and book.
What he means by his saying: “Say: Do you argue with us?” Say: Do you quarrel with us and argue with us?

c: As Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “Say: Do you argue with us about God?” Say: Do you quarrel with us?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: Say, ‘Do you argue with us?’ Do you quarrel with us?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Do you argue with us? Do you debate with us? As for his saying: And we are sincere to Him, it means: And we are sincere to God in worship and obedience, we do not associate anything with Him, and we do not worship anyone other than Him, just as the idolaters worshipped idols with Him, and the owners of the calf worshipped the calf with Him. This is from God, the Most High, as a rebuke to the Jews and an argument for the people of faith, in His saying, the Most High, to the believers from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O believers, to the Jews and Christians who said to you: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided: Do you argue with us about God? He means by His saying: about God, about the religion of God that He has commanded us to adhere to, and our Lord and your Lord are one, just and do not wrong, and He only rewards the servants for what they have earned. And you claim that you are closer to God than we are, because your religion, your Book, and your Prophet have been ancient, and we are sincere in worshipping Him, and we have not associated anything with Him, but you have associated others in your worship of Him, so some of you worshipped the calf, and some of you worshipped the Messiah, so how can you be better than us and closer to God than us?

x: There are two interpretations of the reading of this. One of them is: Or do you say with the letter ta'. Whoever reads it like this, its interpretation is: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you from the Jews and Christians: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided:
h
Do you argue with us about God
, or do you say that Abraham? So that is conjoined with his saying:
h
Do you argue with us about God

? The other interpretation is: Or do they say with the letter ya'. Whoever reads it like this interprets his saying: Or do they say that he invented it? 32:3, and as it is said: It is camels or sheep. And he made it a renewed question because of the arrival of a renewed predicate, as it is said: Do you stand or does your brother stand? So his saying: Or does your brother stand becomes a renewed predicate for a sentence that is not from the first, and a starting question. If it was a sequence of the first question, it would have been report about the first, so it would have been said: Are you standing or sitting?

Some Arabists have claimed that if this is read in this way with the letter ya, then if what comes after am is a complete sentence, then it is an appositive to the first question. Because the meaning of the statement is: It was said: Which of these two matters will happen? This or that?

The correct reading in our view is: Or do you say with a ta’ without a ya’, in apposition to His statement: Say, do you argue with us? meaning: Which of these two matters do you do? Do you argue with us about the religion of God, claiming that you are more deserving than us and more guided than us in path, and that our affair and your affair are as we have described, as we have explained previously? Or do you claim that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and those whom God has named, were Jews or Christians following your religion, so that people can be justified in your slander and lies? Because Judaism and Christianity came after those whom God named from among His prophets. It is not permissible to read that with a ya’, because it is an anomaly from the reading of the reciters. This verse is also a protest from God, the Most High, to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against the Jews and Christians, whose stories God mentioned.
God says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these Jews and Christians:
h
Do you argue with us about God

, and claim that your religion is better than our religion, and that you are on guidance and we are on misguidance, with a proof from God, the Most High, so you call us to your religion? Then produce your proof for that so that we may follow you in it. Or do you say: Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes were Jews or Christians following your religion? Then produce proof for what you claim, so that we may believe you, for God has made them leaders to be followed. Then the Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them, O Muhammad, if they claim that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes were Jews or Christians: Are you more knowledgeable about them and what religions they followed, or is God?
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God

It means: If the Jews and Christians, who said to you and your companions, Be Jews or Christians, claim, O Muhammad, that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes were Jews or Christians, then who is more unjust than them? He says: And who is more unjust than them? And they concealed a testimony they had from God that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes were Muslims, so they concealed that and attributed to them Judaism and Christianity.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that:

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, he said, ʿIsa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God

, he said: In the statement of the Jews to Abraham, Ishmael, and those mentioned with them, that they were Jews or Christians. So God says: Do not conceal from Me a testimony if you have it about them. And He knows that they are liars.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God

, in what the Jews said to Abraham and Ishmael and those mentioned with them: that they were Jews or Christians. So God said to them: Do not conceal from Me the testimony concerning them, if you have it concerning them. And God knew that they were liars.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Ishaq told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: that he recited this verse: Or do you say that Abraham and Ishmael until His saying: “Say: Are you more knowing or is God?
h
And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God

?” Al-Hasan said: By God, the people had a testimony from God that His prophets were innocent of Judaism and Christianity, just as the people had a testimony from God that your wealth and blood are forbidden among you, so how did they make them permissible?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God

? The People of the Book concealed Islam, even though they knew that it was the religion of God, and they found it written in their Torah and Gospel: they were neither Jews nor Christians, and Judaism and Christianity came after them by a time. Rather, God Almighty meant by this that if the Jews and Christians claimed that Abraham and those named with him in this verse were Jews or Christians, it would become clear to the polytheists who are their supporters that they were lying and that they were falsely claiming against God’s prophets, because Judaism and Christianity occurred after them. And if they denied that Judaism and Christianity were theirs, it would be said to them: Then come to the religion they were upon, for we and you both acknowledge that they were upon the truth, and we differ in what contradicted the religion they were upon.

x: Others said: Rather, what God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God
, is the Jews in their concealment of the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prophethood, and they know that and find it in their books.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes were Jews or Christians? Those are the People of the Book who concealed Islam while they knew that it was the religion of God, and they adopted Judaism and Christianity, and they concealed Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while they knew that he was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They find him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God
? He said: The testimony, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is written down with them, and it is what they concealed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similar to the hadith of Bishr bin Muʿadh, on the authority of Yazid.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God
, he said: They are Jews, they ask about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about his description in the Book of God that they have, so they conceal the description.

x: We chose the statement we made in interpreting that because the words of God Almighty:
h
And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God
, come after the story of those whom God named from among His prophets, and before His story for them. So it is more appropriate for what is between that to be from their stories rather than others.
What testimony do the Jews and Christians have from God regarding Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes?

The testimony they have from God regarding their matter is what God revealed to them in the Torah and the Gospel, and He commanded them in them to follow their Sunnah and their religion, and that they were monotheists and Muslims. It is the testimony they have from God that they concealed, when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to Islam, and they said to him: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian (al-Baqarah 2:111). ), and they said to him and his companions: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided. So God revealed these verses about them, in their denial, their concealment of the truth, and their false and fabricated slander against God’s prophets.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And God is not unaware of what you do.

God Almighty means by that: And say to these Jews and Christians, who argue with you, O Muhammad: And God is not unaware of what you do, of your concealing the truth in what He obligated you to explain to the people in His Book regarding the matter of Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes in the matter of Islam, and that they were Muslims, and that the Muslim Hanifiyah is the religion of God that all creation must adhere to, excluding Judaism, Christianity, and other religions. And He is not afraid of punishing you for your actions, but He is testing you so that He may reward you with the reward that you are worthy of in this world and the hereafter. So He rewarded them immediately in this world by killing some of them and expelling them from their homeland and home, and He will reward them in the hereafter with a humiliating punishment.

evidence.text: Abu Ja'far said: There are two interpretations of the reading of this.

Whoever reads it like this, its interpretation is: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you from the Jews and Christians: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided: Do you argue with us about God, or do you say that Abraham?
Whoever reads it like this interprets his saying: Or do they say that he invented it?
Some Arabists have claimed that if this is read in this way with the letter ya, then if what comes after am is a complete sentence, then it is an appositive to the first question.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in our view is: Or do you say with a ta’ without a ya’, in apposition to His statement: Say, do you argue with us? meaning: Which of these two matters do you do?
It is not permissible to read that with a ya’, because it is an anomaly from the reading of the reciters.

Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Ishaq told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Ashhab, on the authority of Al-Hasan that he recited this verse: Or do you say that Abraham and Ishmael until His saying: “Say: Are you more knowing or is God?

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
That is a nation
, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, as:

c: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatada, that God Almighty said:
m: h
That is a nation
that has passed on, meaning: Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: similarly.

x: We have previously explained that the nation is the group. The meaning of the verse is: Say, O Muhammad, to those who dispute with you about God from among the Jews and Christians, if they conceal what they have of testimony regarding the matter of Abraham and those We named with him, and that they were Muslims, and they claim that they were Jews or Christians, then they lie: Indeed, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes are a nation that has passed away - that is, they have gone on their way and turned to their Lord, and have passed away with their deeds and hopes, they have with God what they earned of good in the days of their lives, and they are against what they have acquired of evil, nothing will benefit them except their good deeds, and nothing will harm them except their bad deeds. So know this, O Jews and Christians, for if these are the ones in whom you boast, and you claim that through them you hope to be saved from the punishment of your Lord, with your evil deeds and great sins, nothing will benefit them with God except what they have presented of good deeds, and nothing will harm them except what they have presented of bad deeds, then you are more deserving that nothing will benefit you with God except what you have presented of good deeds, and nothing will harm you except what they have presented of bad deeds.

So beware of yourselves, and hasten to leave them with repentance and turning to God for what you are upon of disbelief, misguidance, and slander against God and His prophets and messengers, and abandon relying on the virtues of your fathers and grandfathers, for you will have what you have earned, and you will be liable for what you have acquired, and you will not be asked about the deeds that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes did, because every soul that comes before God on the Day of Resurrection will only be asked about what it has earned and what it has sent forward, not what others sent forward. Part one is done And the second part will follow, God willing. The first: The statement on the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: The foolish among the people will say
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying:
h
The fools among the people will say
Abu Jaʿfar said: What He means by His saying, may His praise be glorified: The fools will say, is that the ignorant among the people will say, and they are the Jews and the hypocrites.

And God, the Almighty, called them fools because they belittled the truth. So the rabbis of the Jews ignored it, and their ignorant and stupid people among them were too arrogant to follow Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, since he was from the Arabs and not from the Children of Israel, and the hypocrites were confused and became dull. And what we said about the fools - that they are the Jews and the hypocrites - the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said: They are the Jews:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty and Majestic: “
h
The fools among the people will say
h
What has turned them away
from their Qiblah?” He said: The Jews will say it, when they meet the Holy House.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: I was told by Ahmad bin Yunus, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’:
m: h
The fools among the people will say
, he said: The Jews.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’:
m: h
The fools among the people will say
, he said: The Jews.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’
m: regarding His statement:
h
The fools among the people will say
, he said: The People of the Book.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The Jews.

x: Others said: The fools are the hypocrites.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The verse
h
The fools among the people will say
was revealed about the hypocrites.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty:
h
What has turned them away
from their Qiblah which they used to face?
He means by His words, may He be glorified:
h
What has turned them away

: what turned them away from their Qiblah? It is from the saying of the one who says: So-and-so turned his back to me if he turned his face away from him and turned his back to him, so likewise His saying:
h
What has turned them away

? what turned their faces? As for His saying: from their Qiblah, the Qiblah of everything is what faces its face. Rather, it is an action of the one who is in a state of humiliation and sitting, from the saying of the one who says: I faced so-and-so, if I became facing him, facing him, so he is my Qiblah and I am his Qiblah, if each one of them faces the face of the other. Abu Ja'far: So the interpretation of the statement - if that is its meaning - is: The foolish people will say to you, O believers in God and His Messenger, - if you turn your faces away from the qiblah of the Jews which was your qiblah before I commanded you to turn your faces away from it towards the Sacred Mosque -: What is it that turned the faces of these people, turning them away from the place they used to face with their faces in their prayers?

So God, the Most High, informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what the Jews and hypocrites would say when his qiblah and the qiblah of his companions were turned away from the Levant to the Sacred Mosque, and He informed him what his response to them should be, so He said to him: If they say that to you, O Muhammad, then say to them: "To God belong the East and the West.
h
He guides whom He wills to a straight path

." The reason for that was that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards Jerusalem for a period of time, the amount of which we will mention later, God willing, then God, the Most High, wanted to turn the qiblah of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, towards the Sacred Mosque.

c: So He informed him
m: of what the Jews would say when he turned his face away and the face of His companions divided it, and what should be his response to them from the answer. Mention the period during which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions prayed towards Jerusalem, and what was the reason for his prayer towards it? And what prompted the Jews and hypocrites to say what they said when God changed the qiblah of the believers from Jerusalem to the Kaaba?

x: The people of knowledge differed regarding the period during which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards Jerusalem after the migration.
Some of them said what:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us
m: - and Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us - they both said, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me, he said, Saeed bin Jubair told me, or Ikrimah - Muhammad was uncertain - from Ibn Abbas, he said: When the qiblah was changed from Ash-Sham to the Kaaba - and it was changed in Rajab, at the beginning of seventeen months from the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Medina - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Rifa’ah bin Qais, Qardam bin Amr, Ka’b bin Al-Ashraf, and Nafi’ bin Abi Nafi’. This is what Ibn Humayd said, and Abu Kurayb said: And Rafiʿ bin Abi Rafiʿ and Al-Hajjaj bin Amr - an ally of Kaʿb bin Al-Ashraf - and Al-Rabiʿ bin Al-Rabiʿ bin Abi Al-Haqiq, and Kinanah bin Abi Al-Haqiq, and they said: O Muhammad, what has turned you away from the Qiblah which you were facing, while you claim that you are on the religion and faith of Abraham? Return to the Qiblah which you were facing, and we will follow you and believe you! They only want to tempt him away from his religion. So God revealed about them: “
h
The foolish among the people will say
h
What has turned them away
from the Qiblah which they used to face?’” until His saying:
h
Except that We may test who follows the Messenger from who turns on his heels

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash narrated to us, Al-Baraʿ said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards the Holy House for seventeen months, and he desired to be turned towards the Kaʿbah. He said: While we were praying one day, someone passed by us and said: Do you not know that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has turned towards the Kaʿbah? He said: We have prayed two Rakaʿahs towards here, and we have prayed two Rakaʿahs towards here.” - Abu Krayb: It was said to him: Is Abu Ishaq in it? He remained silent.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said:
m: “We prayed seventeen months after the arrival of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Medina towards the Holy House.”

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, who said:
m: “I prayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, towards Jerusalem for sixteen months, or seventeen months” - Sufyan was uncertain - then he turned us towards the Ka’bah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me,
m: who said, al-Nufaili told us, who said, Zuhair told us, who said, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-Bara’: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, first came to Medina, he stayed with his grandfathers - or his maternal uncles - from the Ansar, and that he prayed towards Jerusalem for sixteen months, and he liked that his qiblah should be towards the House, and that he prayed the ‘Asr prayer with some people, and a man from among those who prayed with him came out, and passed by the people of the mosque while they were bowing, and said: I bear witness that I prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, towards Mecca. So they turned as they were towards the House. He liked to turn towards the House, and the Jews liked that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards Jerusalem, and so did the People of the Book, but when he turned his face towards the House, they disapproved of that.” He told me. Imran bin Musa said, Abdul Warith told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards Jerusalem after he had arrived in Medina for sixteen months, then he turned towards the Kaaba two months before Badr.”

x: Others said: Amr bin Ali told us, Abu Asim told us, Uthman bin Saad Al-Katib told us, Anas bin Malik told us: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards Jerusalem for nine or ten months.” While he was standing praying the noon prayer in Medina, and he had prayed two rak’ahs towards Jerusalem, he turned his face towards the Kaaba, so the fools said: What turned them away from the qiblah that they were facing?

Others said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Dawud told us, Al-Mas’udi told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Medina and prayed towards Jerusalem for thirteen months.

c: Ahmad bin Al-Muqaddam Al-Ajli told us, Al-Mu’tamar bin Sulayman told us,
m: I heard my father He said, Qatada narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: The Ansar prayed the first Qiblah, three Hajj pilgrimages before the arrival of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the first Qiblah after his arrival in Medina sixteen months, or as he said. And both hadiths are narrated by Qatada on the authority of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:143 And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. And We did not make the Qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it was a great sin except for those whom Allah has guided. And Allah would not let a person perish. Your faith that God is to the people Kind and Merciful. Saeed. He mentioned the reason why the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards Jerusalem, before it was imposed on him to face the Kaaba.

x: The scholars differed on that.
Some of them said: That was by the choice of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Yahya bin Wadheeh Abu Tamila narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein bin Waqid narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah - and on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah - and Al-Hasan Al-Basri
m: said: The first thing that was abrogated from the Qur’an was the Qiblah. That is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was facing the rock of Jerusalem, which was the Qiblah of the Jews. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced it for seventeen months so that they would believe in him and follow him, and he called the illiterate Arabs to that. So God Almighty said: And to God belongs the East. And the Maghreb, so wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. Indeed, God is All-Encompassing and Knowing.”

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding His statement:
h
The foolish among the people will say
h
What has turned them away

from their Qiblah which they used to face?’ They mean Jerusalem. Al-Rabiʿ said, Abu Al-ʿAliyah said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given the choice to turn his face wherever he wished, so he chose Jerusalem in order to unite the People of the Book, so his Qiblah was for sixteen months, and during that time he was turning his face to the sky, then God turned him to the Sacred House.

x: Others said: Rather, the action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions was by God’s command upon them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muʿawiyah bin Salih told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, and the majority of its people were Jews, God commanded him to face Jerusalem. The Jews rejoiced, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced it for a few months, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was He loved the direction of the Qiblah of Abraham, peace be upon him, and he used to supplicate and look at the sky. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven (al-Baqarah 2:144). The Jews doubted that and said:
h
What has turned them away
from the Qiblah which they used to face? So God, the Almighty, revealed: “Say: To God belongs the East and the West.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
