m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the first thing he prayed toward the Kaaba, then he turned toward the Holy House. The Ansar had prayed toward the Holy House before his arrival for three pilgrimages, and he prayed after his arrival for sixteen months, then God, the Almighty, made him turn toward the Kaaba. Mention the reason for which he said:
h
What has turned them away
from the Qiblah which they used to face?

x: The people of interpretation differed about that. Two sayings were narrated from Ibn Abbas about it. One of them is what: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas said: Some Jews said that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said to him: Return to the Qiblah you were facing, so we will follow you and believe you! They wanted to tempt him away from his religion. The other statement is: What I mentioned from the hadith of Ali bin Abi Talha about him that came before.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
The foolish among the people will say
h
What has turned them away

from the Qiblah they were facing?’ He said: The Ansar prayed towards Jerusalem for two years before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed after his arrival in Medina as an emigrant, towards Jerusalem for sixteen months, then God directed him after that towards the Kaaba, the Sacred House.

x: Some people said about that:
h
What has turned them away
from the Qiblah they were facing? The man longed for his birth! So God Almighty said: “Say, ‘To God belongs the East and the West.
h
He guides whom He wills to a straight path
.’” It was said: The one who said this statement was the hypocrites. They only said that to mock Islam.

Who said that: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned towards the Sacred Mosque, the people differed about it and were divided into groups. The hypocrites said: Why were they on the Qiblah for a time, then they abandoned it and turned towards another? So God revealed about al-Munafiqun 63:
h
The foolish among the people will say
the entire verse.
The statement in the interpretation of the words of God the Almighty: “Say: To God belong the East and the West.
h
He guides whom He wills to a straight path

By that, the Almighty means: Say, O Muhammad - to those who said to you and your companions: What turned you away from your Qiblah from Jerusalem, which you were facing, to facing towards the Sacred Mosque? -: To God belongs the Kingdom of the East and the West, meaning by that: The Kingdom of what is between the two poles of the rising sun and the two poles of its setting, and what is between them of the world, He guides whom He wills of His creation, directing him and granting him success to the straight path, which is the straight path - and by that he means: to the Qiblah of Abraham whom He made an Imam for the people - and He disappoints whom He wills of them, leading them astray from the path of truth. And what God the Almighty meant by His words:
h
He guides whom He wills to a straight path
is: Say, O Muhammad: Indeed, God guided us by facing towards the Sacred Mosque as the Qiblah of Abraham, and He led you astray - O Jews.
The hypocrites and the group of polytheists - so let us down from what He guided us to.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And thus We have made you a middle nation
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And thus We have made you a middle nation

, is that just as We have guided you, O believers in Muhammad, peace be upon him, and in what he brought to you from God, so We have singled you out with success for the Qiblah of Abraham and his religion, and We have preferred you with that over those other than you from the people of religions, so We have singled you out and preferred you over others from the people of religions, by making you a middle nation. We have explained that the nation is the generation of people and the class of them and others. As for the middle, in the speech of the Arabs, it is the best. It is said: So-and-so is of average lineage among his people, meaning of average lineage, if they mean by that his lineage is high, and he is average among his people, and middle, just as it is said: a sheep with dry milk and dry milk, and just as God Almighty said:
So strike for them a dry path in the sea
and Zuhair ibn Abi Salma said about the middle: They are the middle ground, and people are satisfied with their judgment if one of the nights descends upon most of them.

I see that the middle in this place is the middle that means: the part that is between the two sides, like the middle of the house, the middle is heavy, and it is not permissible to lighten it in its sin. I see that God Almighty described them as being middle, because of their moderation in religion, so they are not people of extremism in it, the extremism of the Christians who extremism in monasticism, and what they said about Jesus what they said about him - nor are they people of shortcomings in it, the shortcomings of the Jews who changed the book of God, and killed their prophets, and lied about their Lord, and disbelieved in him, but they are people of moderation and balance in it. So God described them with that, because the most beloved of matters to God is the middle. As for the interpretation, it came that the middle is justice. And that is the meaning of the best, because the best of people are their just ones.
Mention of those who said: the middle is justice.

c: Salim bin Junadah and Yaʿqub bin Ibrahim told us, they said, Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Al-Aʿmash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Saʿid, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, in his saying:
h
And thus We have made you a middle nation
, he said: Just.

c: Mujahid bin Musa and Muhammad bin Bashar narrated to us, they said, Ja’far bin Awn narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar narrated to us, he said, Mu’ammil narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri:
m: h
And thus We have made you a just community
, he said: Just.

c: Ali bin Isa narrated to me, he said, Sa’id bin Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Hafs bin Ghiyath, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement:
h
And thus We have made you a just community
, he said: Just.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id:
m: h
And thus We have made you a just community
, he said: Just.

c: Muhammad bin Amr narrated to me, he said, Abu Asim narrated to us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
And thus We have made you a just community
, he said: Just.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: A middle nation, he said: Just.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: A middle nation, he said: Just.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father,
m: on al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement: A middle nation, he said: Just.

c: Muhammad bin Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
And thus We have made you a middle nation
, he said: We made you a just nation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwayd bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Rashdin bin Saʿd, he said, Ibn Anʿam al-Maʿafari told us,
m: On the authority of Habban ibn Abi Jabalah, who traces it back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And thus We have made you a just nation, he said: The middle is justice.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’,
m: Mujahid and Abdullah ibn Kathir: A just nation, they said: Just. Mujahid said: Just.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And thus We have made you a just nation, he said: They are in the middle between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the nations.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God the Almighty: That you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you, Abu Jaʿfar said: The word witnesses is the plural of witness.

So the meaning of that is: And thus We have made you a just nation, so that you may be witnesses for My prophets and messengers over their nations by the declaration that they have conveyed what I was commanded to convey of My messages to their nations, and My Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be a witness over you, by your belief in him and in what he brought to you from Me, as: He told me Abu al-Sa’ib said, Hafs narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Noah, peace be upon him, will be called on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him: ‘Did you convey what you were sent with?’ He will say: ‘Yes.’ His people will be asked: ‘Did you convey it?’ They will say: ‘No warner came to us!’ He will be asked: ‘Who knows that?’ He will say: ‘Muhammad and his nation.’”
This is what He said:
h
And thus We have made you a just community
that you will be witnesses over the people
h
and the Messenger will be a witness over you

c: Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, he said, Ja’far ibn Awn narrated to us, he said, al-A’mash narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner - except that he added to it: They will be called and testify that he has conveyed.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Mu’ammil narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id:
m: h
And thus We have made you a just community
that you will be witnesses over the people - that the Messengers have conveyed -
h
and the Messenger will be a witness over you
, of what you have done, or You did.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ashja’i, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Utaybah bin Al-Nahhas: That one of their scribes narrated to them on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘My nation and I will be on a hill on the Day of Resurrection, overlooking all creation. There is no nation but that he would wish to be from it, O nation, and there is no prophet who was denied by his people but that we will be his witnesses on the Day of Resurrection that he delivered the messages of his Lord and advised them.’ He said: ‘
h
And the Messenger will be a witness over you

c: Issam bin Rawad bin Al-Jarrah Al-Asqalani narrated to me, he said, my father narrated to us, he said, Al-Awza’i narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Al-Fadl, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: I went out with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to a funeral, and when he prayed over the dead, the people said: ‘What a good man!’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is due.’ Then I went out with him to another funeral, and when they prayed over the dead, the people said: ‘What a bad man!’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is due.’ So Abi bin Ka'b said: O Messenger of God, what do you say, It is obligatory? He said: The saying of God, the Almighty:
h
So that you may be witnesses over the people

c: Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told me, he said, al-Walid bin Muslim told us, he said, Abu Amr told me, on the authority of Yahya, he said, Abdullah bin Abi al-Fadl al-Madini told me, he said, Abu Hurairah told me:
m: A funeral procession was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people said: What a good man! Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Issam on the authority of his father.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Zaid bin Habbab told us, he said, Ikrimah bin Ammar Qar told us, Iyas bin Salamah bin al-Akwa' told me on the authority of his father, he said:
m: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a funeral procession passed by him, and he praised it with good praise, so he said: It is obligatory. Another funeral procession passed by him, and he praised it less than that, so he said: It is obligatory! They said: O Messenger of God, what is it obligatory? He said: The angels are God's witnesses in heaven, and you are God's witnesses on earth, so whatever you bear witness to is obligatory. Then he recited: And say, 'Work, and God will see your work.' And His Messenger and the believers” (al-Tawbah 9:105).

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
So that you may be witnesses over the people
, you may be witnesses for Muhammad, peace be upon him, over the nations, the Jews, the Christians, and the Magians.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said:
m: “The Prophet, peace be upon him, will come on the Day of Resurrection to his group, and no one will be with him, so the nation of Muhammad, peace be upon him, will testify for him that he has conveyed the message to them.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of his father,
m: that he heard Ubayd ibn Umair similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said,
m: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:144 We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.

c: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told me, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: The Prophet, peace be upon him, will come on the Day of Resurrection to his group, and no one will be with him, so the nation of Muhammad, peace be upon him, will testify for him that he has conveyed the message to them.” God's Messenger (may peace be upon him) said on the Day of Resurrection, and he mentioned something similar, but Ubayd ibn Umair did not mention something similar.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
So that you may be witnesses over the people
, meaning that their messengers had conveyed the message of their Lord to their people,
h
and the Messenger will be a witness over you
, that he had conveyed the messages of his Lord to his nation.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam:
m: The people of Noah will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Noah did not convey to us! So Noah, peace be upon him, will be called and asked: Did you convey to them? He will say: Yes. It will be said: Who are your witnesses? He will say: Ahmad, peace be upon him, and his nation. So you will be called and asked, and you will say: Yes, he conveyed to them. So the people of Noah, peace be upon him, will say: How can you bear witness against us when you have not yet met us? They will say: The Prophet of God, peace be upon him, came and informed us that he had conveyed to you, and it was revealed to him that he had conveyed to you, so we believed him. He said: So Noah, peace be upon him, will be believed. And they belie them. He said:
h
So that you may be witnesses over the people
and the Messenger may be a witness over you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So that you may be witnesses over the people
, so that this nation may be witnesses over the people that the Messengers have conveyed to them, and the Messenger may be a witness over this nation that he has conveyed what he was sent with.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam:
m: The nations will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:By God, this affliction almost became all of the prophets! When they see what God has given them.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Rashdin bin Saad, he said: Ibn An’am al-Ma’afari told me, on the authority of Hubban bin Abi Jabalah,
m: with a chain of transmission back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When God gathers His servants on the Day of Resurrection, the first to be called will be Israfil, and his Lord will say to him: What did you do during My covenant? Did you convey My covenant? He will say: Yes, my Lord, I have.” Gabriel, peace be upon them, was brought to him. Gabriel is called and it is said to him: Did Israfil convey to you my covenant? He says: Yes, my Lord, he conveyed it to me. Israfil is left alone, and Gabriel is asked: Did you convey my covenant? He says: Yes, I conveyed it to the messengers. The messengers are called and it is said to them: Did Gabriel convey to you my covenant? They say: Yes, our Lord. Gabriel is left alone, and it is said to the messengers: What did you do with my covenant? They say: We conveyed it to our nations. The nations are called and it is said: Did the messengers convey to you my covenant?

x: Some of them are liars and some are believers. The messengers say: We have witnesses against them who testify that we conveyed it along with your testimony. He says: Who will testify for you? They say: The nation of Muhammad. The nation of Muhammad, peace be upon him, is called and he says: Do you bear witness that these messengers of Mine conveyed my covenant to those to whom they were sent? They say: Yes, our Lord, we bear witness that they conveyed it. Those nations say: How can those who did not And the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, will say to them: How do you bear witness against those you have not attained? They will say: Our Lord, You sent to us a Messenger, and sent down to us Your covenant and Your Book, and You told us that they had reached the age of maturity, so we bore witness to what You entrusted to us. The Lord will say: They have spoken the truth. This is what He said:
h
And thus We have made you a just community
- and the middle way is justice - that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you.
Ibn An’am said: It has reached me that on that day the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will bear witness, except for he who has compassion in his heart for his brother.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement: that you may be witnesses over the people, meaning by that: those who were steadfast on guidance, so they are the ones who will be witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection, for their denial of the Messengers of God and their disbelief in the signs of God.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding His statement: that you may be witnesses over the people, He says: “So that you may be witnesses over the nations who passed away before you, regarding what their messengers brought to them, and regarding what they denied them. So they will say on the Day of Resurrection and be amazed: There was a nation that was not in our time, so they believed in what our messengers brought, and we denied what they brought! So they were amazed to the utmost. His statement: “
h
And the Messenger will be a witness over you
,” means: regarding their belief in him, and in what was revealed to him.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
So that you may be witnesses over the people
, meaning: that they bore witness over the generations regarding what God Almighty named for them.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, he said, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: I said to Ata’: What is his statement:
h
So that you may be witnesses over the people

? He said: The nation of Muhammad, they witnessed over those who abandoned the truth when faith and guidance came to them, from those who were before us. Abdullah bin Katheer said it. He said: Ata’ said: Witnesses over those who abandoned the truth from those who abandoned it from all the people, this came to the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their book,
h
And the Messenger will be a witness over you
, that they believed in the truth when it came to them, and they believed in it.

c: Yunus narrated to me, he said, Ibn Wahb informed us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
So that you may be witnesses over the people
h
and the Messenger will be a witness over you

, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘A witness over his nation, and they are witnesses over the nations.’” They are one of the witnesses of whom God Almighty said: And on the Day when the witnesses will stand
r
(Ghafir 40:51)

, the four: the angels who count our deeds, for us and against us, and he recited His statement: And every soul will come with it a driver and a witness. (He said: 21) And he said: This is the Day of Resurrection. He said: And the prophets are witnesses over their nations. He said: And the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are witnesses over nations. He said: And the stages 1 are the bodies and the skins.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty:
h
And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing
except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn on his heels.
God Almighty means by His words:
h
And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing

, and We did not make your turning away from the qiblah which you were facing, O Muhammad, so We turned you away from it, except to make evident who would follow you from who would not follow you from who would turn on his heels.
And the qiblah which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was facing, which God meant by His words:
h
And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing
, is the qiblah which you were facing before He turned you to the Kaʿbah, as:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing

, meaning: the House of Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata’: And what made the qiblah that you used to face? He said: The qiblah is Jerusalem.

x: The reason for not mentioning the turning away from it was to be satisfied with the indication of what has been mentioned of the speech on its meaning, like all the other similar things that we have mentioned before. We only said: That is its meaning, because the trial of God and the companions of His Messenger in the direction of the qiblah was only - according to what the reports have agreed upon - when the change was made from the Holy House to the Kaʿbah, until - according to what has been mentioned - some men who had converted to Islam and followed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became disgusted, and many of the hypocrites - because of that - showed their hypocrisy, and said: What is wrong with Muhammad that he turns us once here and once there! And the Muslims said about those of their Muslim brothers who had passed while they were praying towards the Holy House: Our deeds and their deeds are null and void!
The polytheists said: "Muhammad, peace be upon him, was confused about his religion! So that was a trial for the people and a test for the believers." That is why God, the Most High, said:
h
And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing

except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels, meaning: We did not make your turning away from the qiblah which you were facing and your transfer to another, as God, the Most High, said:
And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people

meaning: We did not make your report about the vision which We showed you. That is because if he had not informed the people of what he had been shown, there would have been no trial for anyone in it. Likewise, the first qiblah which was towards Jerusalem, if he had not been turned away from it towards the Kaaba, there would have been no trial or trial for anyone in it.
Mentioning the narrations that were narrated in that meaning what we said:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatadah, he said:
m: The qiblah was a trial and a test. The Ansar prayed towards Jerusalem for two years before the arrival of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. “After his arrival in Medina as an immigrant, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards Jerusalem for seventeen months. Then God directed him towards the Kaaba, the Sacred House.”

x: Some people said about that: Why did He turn them away from the Qiblah they were facing? The man longed for his birth! God the Almighty said: “Say: To God belongs the East and the West. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.”

Some people said - when the Qiblah was turned towards the Sacred House - What about our deeds that we used to do towards our first Qiblah? So God the Almighty revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste. God may test His servants with whatever He wills of His command, one command after another, to know who will obey Him and who will disobey Him, and all of that is acceptable, since in that there is faith in Him, sincerity to Him, and submission to His judgment.

c: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray towards Jerusalem, but the Kaaba overturned it. When he turned towards the Sacred Mosque, people differed about it and were divided into groups. The hypocrites said: Why were they on the qiblah for a time, then they abandoned it and turned towards another one? The Muslims said: If only we knew about our brothers who died while praying towards Jerusalem! Did God accept it from us and from them, or not? The Jews said: Muhammad longed for the country of his father and his birthplace, and if he had remained on our qiblah, we would have hoped that he would be the companion we are waiting for! The polytheists of Mecca said: Muhammad was confused about his religion, so he turned his qiblah towards you, and he knew that you were better guided than him, and he is about to enter your religion! So God, the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:144 We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do. Most High, revealed about al-Munafiqun 63:‘The foolish among the people will say: What has turned them away from their qiblah which they used to face? ’ until His saying: ‘And it is indeed difficult
h
except for those whom God has guided
. ’ And He revealed about the others the verses: After that, Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata’: “
h
Except that We may know

who follows the Messenger from who turns back on his heels.” Ata’ said: He tests them, to know who submits to His command. Ibn Jurayj said: It has reached me that some people who converted to Islam returned and said: Once here and once there!

x: If someone were to say to us: Did God not know who would follow the Messenger and who would turn on his heels, except after the follower had followed and the one who turned on his heels had turned on his heels, until he said: We did not do what we did of changing the qiblah except to know who would follow the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and who would turn on his heels? It would be said: God, the Most High, is the One who knows all things before they come into being, and His statement: And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing except that We might know who would follow the Messenger from who would turn on his heels, is not a report [from] that He did not know that except after its existence.
What is the meaning of that?

a.l: It would be said to him:
x: As for its meaning with us, it is:
h
And We did not make the qiblah which you were facing

except that We might know who would follow the Messenger and who would turn on his heels. So God, the Most High, said: Except that We might know, and its meaning is to know My Messenger and My friends. Since the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and his followers were from his party, and it was the custom of the Arabs to attribute to the leader what the followers of the leader did, and what was done to them to him, such as their saying: Umar ibn al-Khattab conquered the lands of Iraq and collected its tax, but his companions did that, for a reason that he had in that, and like what was narrated in its equivalent from the Prophet (peace be upon him) that he said: “God, the Most High, says: I fell ill and My servant did not visit Me, and I asked him for a loan and he did not lend Me, and he reviled Me, and it was not appropriate for him to revil Me.”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar, on the authority of al-ʿAlaʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: God said: I asked My servant for a loan and he did not lend Me, and he reviled Me, and it was not appropriate for him to revil Me! He says: Woe to him! And I am time, I am time.”

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of al-ʿAlaʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman,
m: On the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. So the Almighty added borrowing and visiting to Himself, and that was done by someone else, since that was narrated from the Arabs by hearing: I am hungry in something other than my stomach, and naked in something other than my back, meaning: the hunger of his family and children and the nakedness of their backs. So is His saying:
h
Except that We may know
, meaning: My friends and my party may know. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saih told me, on the authority of Ali Abu Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. Ibn Abbas said: To distinguish the people of certainty from the people of polytheism and doubt.

x: Some of them said: That was only said because the Arabs put knowledge in place of seeing, and seeing in place of knowledge, as the Almighty said: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? (al-Fil 105:1), so he claimed the meaning of Have you not seen is, Have you not known? He claimed that the meaning of his saying: Except that we may know, is: Except that we may see who follows the Messenger.

i: He claimed that the words of the speaker: I saw, I knew, and I witnessed are letters that follow one another, so that some of them are placed in place of others, as Jarir ibn Atiyah said:
x: As if you did not witness Al-Qeet, Al-Hajeb, and Amr bin Amr when he called, O Darem!

Meaning: As if you did not know Al-Qayt, because between the death of Al-Qayt and Hajeb and the time of Jarir, there is a period of time that is not hidden. That is because those he mentioned died in the pre-Islamic era, and Jarir was a short time after the advent of Islam.

This is a far-fetched interpretation. Because seeing, even if it is used in place of knowledge, because it is impossible for someone to see something, seeing it does not necessitate that he has seen it, if he is of sound nature. So it is permissible, from the aspect that he established seeing, to add to it his establishment of it as knowledge, and it is correct to indicate by mentioning seeing the meaning of knowledge for that reason. So that is not, even though it is [permissible] in seeing - for what we have described - permissible in knowledge, so mentioning the report about knowledge indicates seeing. Because a person may know many things that he has not seen and does not see, and it is impossible for him to see something except that he knows it, as we have previously explained [about it]. Although it is not found in any of the speech of the Arabs that it is said: I knew such-and-such, meaning I saw it.

Rather, it is permissible to direct the meanings of what is in the Book of God that He revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of speech, to what was Existing like it in the speech of the Arabs, without what was not present in their speech. So what is present in their speech is I saw meaning: I knew, and not present in their speech is I knew meaning: I saw, so it is permissible to direct except to know to the meaning: except to see.

Others said: Except to know was only said because the hypocrites, the Jews, and the disbelievers in God denied that God Almighty knows something before it happens. And they said - when it was said to them: Some of the people of the Qiblah They will turn back on their heels, if the Qiblah of Muhammad (peace be upon him) is changed to the Kaaba: That will not happen! Or they said: That is false! So when God did that, and changed the Qiblah, and those who disbelieved because of that disbelieved, God, the Most High, said: I did not do it except so that we may know what others knew - you polytheists who deny My knowledge of what will happen of things before it comes into being - that I am All-Knowing of what will happen of what has not yet come into being. So it is as if the meaning of those who say this statement in interpreting His statement: Except that we may know is: Except that we may make clear to you that We know who follows the Messenger and who turns back on his heels.

And even if this has a way of being, it is far from the concept. And others said: It was only said: Except that we may know, and He is All-Knowing before it comes into being and in every case, in a way. Being gentle with His servants and attracting them to His obedience, as He, the Most High, said:
“Say: ‘Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?’ Say: ‘God.’ And indeed, either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error.”

and He knew that He was upon right guidance and that they were upon manifest error. However, He was gentle with them in His address, for He did not say: We are upon right guidance and you are upon manifest error. Similarly, His statement: Except that we may know, means to them: Except that you may know, since you were ignorant of it before it came into being. So He attributed knowledge to Himself, as a gentleness in His address to them.

We have already explained the statement that is more deserving of the truth in that regard. As for His statement: Whoever follows the Messenger, it means: the one who follows Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what God commands him to do, so he is directed towards the direction towards which Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is directed. As for his statement: of those who turn back on their heels, it means: of those who turn back from their religion, and become hypocrites, or disbelievers, or oppose Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that, of those who appear to follow him, as Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about his statement: And We did not make the Qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels, he said: of those who, when doubt enters them, turn back from God and turn back as a disbeliever on their heels.

The root of the word apostate on their heels is: the one who turns back on his heels, returning with his back on the path he had taken, turning away from it. So it was said for everyone who turns back from a matter he was doing, whether it was religion or good. And from that is His statement: So they turned back upon their footsteps, retracing (al-Kahf 18:64), meaning: they returned to the path they had taken. The apostate is called an apostate because he has turned back from his religion and the faith he was following. It is also said that he turned back on his heels because he turned back on his heels to the direction he was in at the beginning of his journey before returning from it. This is made an example for every person who abandons a matter and takes up another, if he turns away from what he was doing, to what he was abandoning and takes it. So it is said: So-and-so turned back on his heels, and turned back on his heels.
The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty:
h
And indeed it is a great sin except for those whom God has guided
The people of interpretation differed about what God Almighty described as being a great sin
h
except for those whom God has guided

Some of them said: What He Almighty meant by the great sin was turning away from the Holy House towards the Sacred Mosque and the conversion. And the feminine form of great sin is used to feminize turning away.
Those who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that God said:
h
And indeed it is a great sin except for those whom God has guided
, meaning: changing it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa bin Maimun told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
And indeed it is a great sin except for those whom God has guided
, he said: What they were commanded to do of changing to the Kaaba from the Holy House.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And indeed it is a great sin except for those whom God has guided
, he said: It is a great sin when the Qiblah was changed to the Sacred Mosque, so it was a great sin
h
except for those whom God has guided

x: Others said: Rather, the major one is the exact qiblah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to face from Jerusalem before the conversion.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah: And indeed it is a great sin, meaning the qiblah of Jerusalem,
h
except for those whom God has guided

x: Some of them said: Rather, the major one is the prayer that they used to perform facing the first qiblah.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And if it is indeed difficult
h
except for those whom God has guided
, he said: Your prayer until God guides you to the qiblah.

c: Yunus told me
m: this another time, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
h
And if it is indeed difficult

, he said: Your prayer here - meaning: towards the Holy House in Jerusalem for sixteen months - and your turning Surat Al-Baqarah 2:144 We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do. here. Some grammarians of Basra said: The great sin was made feminine because of the feminization of the qiblah, and God, the Most High, meant it because of His saying,
h
And if it is indeed difficult

. Some grammarians of Kufa said: Rather, the great sin was made feminine because of the feminization of turning away and detouring. So the interpretation of the statement is according to what the speakers of this statement interpreted: And We did not make Our turning you away from the qiblah which you were facing and Our turning you away from it, except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And if Our turning you away from it and Our turning you away is indeed difficult
h
except for those whom God has guided

. This interpretation is the most correct of the interpretations in my opinion. Because the people were only troubled by the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turning his face from the first Qiblah to the other, not the Qiblah itself or the prayer. Because the first Qiblah and the prayer had been and were not troublesome to them. Unless the feminine of the word major is directed to the Qiblah, and he says: Mentioning the Qiblah is sufficient instead of mentioning the turning and the change, because the speech indicates the meaning of that, as we have described to you in its counterparts. So that would be a correct interpretation and an understandable doctrine. The meaning of his statement: major is great, as Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: And indeed it is great
h
except for those whom God has guided

, he said: Great in the hearts of the people, in what Satan introduces to the son of Adam, he said: Why did they pray in this direction for sixteen months and then deviate! So that was great in the hearts of those who do not know or reason and the hypocrites, so they said: What is this religion? As for those who believed, God, the Most High, established that in their hearts. And he recited the statement of God: And indeed it is difficult
h
except for those whom God has guided
, he said: Your prayer until He guides you to the Qiblah.

x: As for His statement:
h
Except for those whom God has guided

, he means by it: And if our turning you away from the Qiblah which you were facing is difficult except for the one whom God, the Most High, has guided, so He has guided him to believe in you and to have faith in that, and to follow you in it, and in what God, the Most High, has revealed to you, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muʿawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: And indeed it is difficult
h
except for those whom God has guided
, he says: Except for the humbly submissive, meaning: those who believe in what God, the Most High, has revealed.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And God would never let your faith go to waste.
It was said that by faith, in this place, he meant prayer.
He mentioned the narrations that were narrated about that, and he mentioned the statement of those who said it:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Wakiʿ and Ubaydullah told us
m: - and Sufyan bin Wakiʿ told us, he said, Ubaydullah bin Musa told us - all of them, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was directed towards the Kaʿbah, they said: What about those of our brothers who died before that, while they were praying towards the Holy House? So God, may His praise be exalted, revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste.

c: Ismaʿil bin Musa told me, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa,
m: regarding the statement of God, may He be exalted: And God would never let your faith go to waste, he said: Your prayers towards the Holy House.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, he said: Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Baraa,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Nufayl al-Harrani narrated to us, he said: Zuhair narrated to us, he said: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of al-Baraa, he said:
m: Before the qiblah was changed to the Kaaba, some men died and were killed, and we did not know what to say about them. Then God, the Most High, revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh al-Aqdi narrated to us, he said: Yazid ibn Zurai’ narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When the qiblah was changed to the Sacred House, some people said: What about the deeds that we used to do in our qiblah? Then God, the Most High, revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, Amr bin Hammad told me, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned toward the Sacred Mosque, the Muslims said: ‘If only we knew about our brothers who died while praying toward the Holy House! Did God accept it from us and from them or not?’ So God, the Most High, revealed about them: ‘And God would never let your faith go to waste.’ He said: Your prayer toward the Holy House. He says: That is obedience and this is obedience.

c: I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on Al-Rabiʿ who said: When the Qiblah was turned toward the Sacred House, some people said: ‘What about the deeds that we used to do toward our first Qiblah?’ So God, the Most High, revealed: ‘And God would never let your faith go to waste.’”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, he said, Ibn Jurayj narrated to me, Dawud ibn Abi Asim narrated to me, he said:
m: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was directed to the Kaaba, the Muslims said: Our companions who used to pray towards Jerusalem have perished, so this verse was revealed: ‘
h
And God would not let your faith go to waste

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to me, he said, my uncle narrated to me, he said, my father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God would not let your faith go to waste
, he said: Your prayers that you prayed before the Qiblah was established. So the believers feared that those of them who prayed would not have their prayers accepted.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la narrated to me, he said, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And God would not let your faith go to waste
, your prayers.

c: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Fazari narrated to us, he said, Al-Mu’ammil narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab,
m: regarding this verse:
h
And God would not let your faith go to waste
, he said. Your prayers towards Jerusalem.

x: We have previously demonstrated that faith is belief. And belief may be by word alone, by action alone, or by both. The meaning of his saying:
h
And God would not let your faith go to waste

- according to what the narration suggests that it is prayer - is: And God would not let your belief in His Messenger, peace be upon him, go to waste, through your prayer that you prayed towards the Holy House on his command, because that was from you belief in My Messenger, following My command, and obedience from you to Me. He said: And his loss of it, may His praise be glorified - if he were to lose it - is to leave his companions and workers alone for it, so it is lost and becomes void, like the case of a man losing his money, and that is his destruction of it in something for which there is no compensation in the immediate or the deferred. So God, the Most High, informed that He would not invalidate the work of a worker who did a work for Him and it was an act of obedience to Him, so He would not make him repeat it, even if that obligation was abrogated after the worker did it according to what He charged him with of his work.

q.l: So if someone were to say:
x: How did God, the Most High, say: And God would never let your faith go to waste, and attribute faith to the living who were addressed, while the people who were addressed were only concerned about their brothers who had died while praying towards the Holy House, and this verse was revealed about that matter of theirs?

Even though the people were concerned about that, they were also concerned about the loss of the reward for their prayers that they had prayed towards the Holy House before the conversion to the Kaaba, and they thought that their work had been invalidated and lost, so God, the Most High, revealed this verse at that time, and directed the address to the living and included the dead among them? Because it is the custom of the Arabs - when the addressee and the absent person come together in the report - to make the addressee prevail and the absent person enter into the address, so they say to a man whom they addressed in the manner of reporting about him and another absent person who is not present: We did to you both and we did to you both, in the manner of addressing them both while they are present, and they do not consider it permissible to say: We did to them both, while they are addressing one of them, so they return the addressee to the count of the absent person 1.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful.

What is meant by His Most High’s statement: Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful is that God is merciful to all of His servants. Mercy is the highest meaning of mercy, and it is general for all of creation in this world, and for some of them in the hereafter. As for the Most Merciful: He is the One with mercy for the believers in this world and the Hereafter, as we have explained previously. What He, the Most High, meant by that is that God, the Almighty, is too merciful to waste their obedience with which they obeyed Him and not reward them for it, and too compassionate to them to hold them accountable for abandoning what He did not impose upon them - that is: Do not grieve over your dead who died while praying towards the Holy House - for I will reward them - for their obedience to Me with the prayers that they performed in this way - because I am too merciful to them to waste for them a deed that they did for Me.

And do not grieve over them, for I will not hold them accountable for abandoning the prayer towards the Kaaba, because I did not impose that upon them, and I am too compassionate to My creation to punish them for abandoning what I did not command them to do. There are different forms of the word Ra’uf. One of them is Ra’uf on the pattern of fa’ala, as Al-Walid bin Uqba said: The worst of the seekers - do not call him - the killer of his uncle, the Compassionate, the Merciful. This is the general reading of the readers of Kufa. The other is Ra'uf, on the pattern of Fa'ul, which is the general reading of the readers of Medina, and Ra'if, which is the language of Ghatafan, on the pattern of Fa'l, like Hadhar. And Ra'fa'ala, on the pattern of Fa'l, with the Jazm of the 'ayn, which is the language of Banu Asad. The reading is according to one of the first two faces.

evidence.text: This is the general reading of the readers of Kufa.
The other is Ra'uf, on the pattern of Fa'ul, which is the general reading of the readers of Medina, and Ra'if, which is the language of Ghatafan, on the pattern of Fa'l, like Hadhar.
The reading is according to one of the first two faces.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “
h
We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven
, so
h
We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased
So
h
turn your face
toward al-Masjid al-Haram.”

By that, God the Almighty means: We have certainly seen, O Muhammad, the turning of your face towards the heaven. By turning, he means the transformation and movement. By his saying: in the heaven, he means towards the heaven and before it. And this was said to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to what we have received, because before changing his qiblah from Jerusalem to the Kaʿbah, he would raise his eyes to the heavens, waiting for God the Almighty to command him to turn towards the Kaʿbah, as Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, ʿAbd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muʿammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the heaven
, he said: “He, may God bless him and grant him peace, would turn his face towards the heaven, loving that God the Almighty would turn him towards the Kaʿbah, until God turned him towards it.”

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven

, “So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray toward the Holy House, longing and desiring the qiblah toward the Sacred House, so God, may His praise be glorified, turned him toward the qiblah that he longed for and desired.”

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told me, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven

, he said: Your gaze toward the heaven. “And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would turn his face in prayer while praying toward Jerusalem, and he used to desire the qiblah of the Sacred House, so God made him turn to the qiblah that he used to desire.”

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi He
m: said: “People used to pray towards Jerusalem, but when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived in Medina eighteen months after his migration, whenever he prayed, he would raise his head to the sky to see what he was commanded to do. He used to pray towards Jerusalem, but the Kaaba abrogated it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to love to pray towards the Kaaba, so God, the Most High, revealed: ‘
h
We have certainly seen the turning of your face towards the heaven
’ verse.” Then there was a difference of opinion as to the reason why the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) preferred the direction of the Kaaba.

x: Some of them said: He disliked the direction of the direction of Jerusalem because the Jews said: He follows our direction of the ... So he would call upon God, the Most High, and ask for the direction of the qiblah, so the verse was revealed: “
h
We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven
, so
h
We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased
. So
h
turn your face

toward al-Masjid al-Haram.” - and the Jews’ saying: He will oppose us and follow our qiblah! - was stopped in the noon prayer, so the men were made to replace the women, and the women were made to replace the men.

c: Yunus told me, saying,
m: “Ibn Wahb told us, saying, I heard him - meaning Ibn Zayd - say: God, the Most High, said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God’ (al-Baqarah 2:115). He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These are Jewish people facing one of the Houses of God - the Holy House - if we were to face it. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced it for sixteen months, and it reached him that the Jews were saying: By God, Muhammad and his companions did not know where their qiblah was until we guided them! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked that, and raised his face to the sky, and God, the Most High, said: ‘
h
We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven
, so
h
We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased
. So
h
turn your face
toward al-Masjid al-Haram’ [al-Masjid al-Haram], the verse.”

x: Others said: He liked that because it was the qiblah of his father, Abraham, peace be upon him.
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, and most of its people were Jews, God Almighty commanded him to face Surat Al-Baqarah 2:145 And if you brought to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah, nor will you be a follower of their qiblah, nor will some of them be a follower of the qiblah of others. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers. Jerusalem. The Jews rejoiced, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced it for sixteen months. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved the direction of Abraham’s qiblah. He used to supplicate and look at the sky, so God Almighty revealed: “
h
We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven
” (al-Masjid an-Nisa’ 3:10). As for His statement:
h
We will surely turn you to a qiblah that will please you
, it means: We will turn you away from Jerusalem to a qiblah that will please you: that you desire and love. As for His statement:
h
Turn your face
, it means:
h
turn your face

and turn it around. And his saying: half of the Sacred Mosque, he means by half, the grammar, the intention and the reception, as Al-Hudhali said: It is difficult for her to see, and her eyes are full of grief. He means by his saying: half of it, something like it, and as Ibn Ahmar said: She runs with us towards the end, and she is knotted, and the knot has become tight from sending her to the ages. And similar to what we have said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah:
m: Half of the Sacred Mosque, meaning: facing it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Half of the Sacred Mosque, similar to it.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque
, similar to it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: Mujahid, similarly. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada:
h
Then turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram
, meaning: towards al-Masjid al-Haram. Al-Husayn bin Yahya narrated, on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
Then turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram
, he said: towards al-Masjid al-Haram. Al-Muthanna narrated, on the authority of Ishaq, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ja’far, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’:
h
Then turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram

, meaning: towards it. Al-Qasim narrated, on the authority of al-Husayn, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: towards it, something like that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa:
m: Then turn your faces towards it, he said: Before it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: Its side, its direction, its side. He said: Its sides are its two sides. Then they differed regarding the place towards which God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn his face in the Sacred Mosque.

x: Some of them said: The qiblah towards which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned, and God meant it in His saying:
h
We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased
, facing the spout of the Kaaba.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told me, he said, Uthman told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ya’la bin Ata’, on the authority of Yahya bin Qumta, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr:
m: h
We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased
, facing the spout of the Kaaba.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Yaʿla bin Ataʿ, on the authority of Yahya bin Qamta, he said:
m: I saw Abdullah bin Amr sitting in the Sacred Mosque facing the gutter, and he recited this verse: Then
h
We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased
. He said: This qiblah, this is the qiblah.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hisham told us
m: - with his chain of transmission on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, something similar - except that he said: He faced the gutter and said: This is the qiblah that God said to His Prophet: Then
h
We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased

x: Others said: Rather, the entire House is a qiblah, and the qiblah of the House is the door.

Those who said that: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The entire House is a qiblah, and this is the qiblah of the House - meaning the one in which the door is.
The correct statement in my opinion is what God, the Most High, said:
h
Then turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram

, so the one who turns his face toward al-Masjid al-Haram is the one who has the correct qiblah. And it is upon the one who directs his intention toward it in his heart that he is facing it, just as it is upon the one who follows an imam, he is only obligated to follow him, even if his body is not in line with his body, and even if he is at the edge of the row and the imam is at another edge, on his right or his left, after being behind him following him, praying toward the direction that the imam is praying toward. And so is the ruling on the qiblah, even if every worshipper and his body is not in line with it, but he is facing it.

If he is to her right or to her left, facing her, then he is facing her, after what is between him and her or close, from her right or to her left, after he is not turning his back to her or deviating from her with his body and face, as:

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Umairah bin Ziyad al-Kindi, on the authority of Ali:
m: h
Then turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque
, he said: Its side, its front.

x: The qiblah of the House is its door, as:

c: Yaʿqub bin Ibrahim and al-Fadl bin al-Sabah told me, they said, Hisham told us, he said, ʿAbd al-Malik told us, on the authority of ʿAta’, he said,
m: “Usama bin Zaid said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he left the House, he turned his face toward the door, and he said: This is the qiblah, this is the qiblah.” Ibn Humayd and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of Abdul Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’, who said:

c: Usamah ibn Zayd narrated to me:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out of the House and prayed two rak’ahs facing the Ka’bah, and said: This is the qiblah, twice.” Abu Kurayb narrated, on the authority of Abdul Rahim ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Saeed ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated, on the authority of my father, who said: Ibn Jurayj narrated, who said: I said to Ata’: I heard Ibn Abbas say: You were only commanded to perform tawaf and were not commanded to enter it. He said: He did not forbid entering it, but I heard him say:

c: Usamah ibn Zayd informed me that
m: when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the House, he supplicated in all its corners, and did not pray until he came out. When he came out, he bowed two rak’ahs facing the qiblah and said: This is the qiblah.

x: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us that the House is the qiblah, and that the qiblah of the House is its door.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it.

By that, God Almighty means: So wherever you are on the earth, O believers, turn your faces in your prayers toward the Sacred Mosque and toward it. The letter ha in both parts refers to the Sacred Mosque. So, God Almighty made it obligatory for the believers, through this verse, to face the Sacred Mosque in their prayers, wherever they are on the land of God Almighty. The letter fa was inserted in his statement: Then turn back as an answer to the condition. This is because his statement: Wherever you are is a condition and its meaning is: wherever you are, turn your faces towards it.
By His statement, may He be glorified, And those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth
h
from their Lord
, He means the Jewish rabbis and Christian scholars. It has been said that He meant the Jews in particular.

Those who said that: Musa ibn Harun told us, ʿAmr ibn Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, And those who were given the Scripture, that was revealed about the Jews. And His statement, That they may know that it is the truth
h
from their Lord

, means these rabbis and scholars from the People of the Book, who know that facing the mosque is the truth that God Almighty imposed on Abraham and his descendants and all the servants after him. And by His statement,
h
From their Lord
, He meant that it is the duty incumbent upon the servants of God Almighty, and it is the truth
h
from their Lord
, which He imposed upon them.

By this, the Blessed and Exalted means: And God is not unaware of what you do, O believers, in following His command, and adhering to His obedience in what He has imposed upon you of His obligations, and your belief in Him in your prayers toward the Holy House, and then your prayers after that toward the Sacred Mosque, nor is He heedless of it, but He, may His praise be glorified, counts it for you and stores it up for you with Him, until He rewards you for it with the best reward, and gives you the best recompense for it.

evidence.text: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Yaʿla bin Ataʿ, on the authority of Yahya bin Qamta, he said: I saw Abdullah bin Amr sitting in the Sacred Mosque facing the gutter, and he recited this verse: Then We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying: And if you brought to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah, nor would you follow their qiblah, nor would some of them follow the qiblah of others.

By that, the Blessed is His name, means: And if you brought, O Muhammad, to the Jews and Christians every proof and argument - which is the verse - that the truth is what you brought them, of imposing the change from the qiblah of the Holy House in prayer to the qiblah of the Sacred Mosque, they would not believe in it, nor would they follow - despite the proof being established against them - your qiblah to which you changed, which is facing the direction of the Sacred Mosque.

And the answer to if was given in the past tense of the verb, and its rule is the answer in the future, likening it to if, so it was answered in the same way that if is answered, due to the similarity of their meanings, and the explanation of what is similar to that has already passed. And the answer to if was given in the answer of oaths. The Arabs do not do this except in the recompense specifically, because the recompense is similar to the oath: each of them is not completed at the beginning except by its end, and is not completed alone, and is not valid except by what is confirmed by it after it. So when he began with the oath and it was introduced into the recompense, the first lam became like an oath, and the second like an answer to it, as it was said: By your life you will stand up, since the lam was repeated in the word by your life, until it became like one of its letters, so it was answered with what oaths are answered with, since the lam replaces oaths in oaths, without the other letters, except for the one that is most deserving of it, the oaths.

So it indicates oaths, and works like answers, and the rest of the answers to oaths do not indicate oaths for us. So the lam in the answer to oaths was likened to oaths, for what we have described, so it was answered with its answers. The meaning of the statement - since the matter was as we have described - was: If you brought to those who were given the Book every sign, they would not follow your qiblah. As for his statement: And you are not a follower of their qiblah, he says: And you have no way, O Muhammad, to follow their qiblah. This is because the Jews face Jerusalem in their prayers, and the Christians face the east, so how can you have a way to follow their qiblah, despite their different faces? He says: So stick to your qiblah that you were ordered to face, and leave what the Jews and Christians say and call you to about their qiblah and facing it. As for his statement:
h
And some of them are not followers of the qiblah of others
, he means by his statement: And the Jews are not followers of the qiblah of the Christians.
Nor are the Christians following the qiblah of the Jews, so they face it, as:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And some of them do not follow the qiblah of others

, meaning: The Jews do not follow the qiblah of the Christians, nor do the Christians follow the qiblah of the Jews. He said: This verse was revealed because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned towards the Kaaba, the Jews said: Muhammad longs for the land of his father and his birth, and if he had remained on our qiblah, we would have hoped that he would be the one we are waiting for! So God, the Almighty, revealed about them: And those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord until His saying:
h
They conceal the truth while they know

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: in His saying:
h
And some of them do not follow the qiblah of others

, something similar. Rather, God, the Most High, meant by that: that the Jews and Christians do not come together on one qiblah, while each one establishes A party of them on their religion. So the Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: O Muhammad, do not let yourself feel that you are pleasing these Jews and Christians, for that is something that cannot be achieved. Because with their different religions, there is no way for you to please every party of them. Because if you follow the qiblah of the Jews, you will anger the Christians, and if you follow the qiblah of the Christians, you will anger the Jews. So leave what cannot be achieved, and call them to what they have a way to, which is to unite on your pure, Muslim religion, and your qiblah is the qiblah of Abraham and the prophets after him.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of the Almighty: And if you were to follow their desires
h
after what has come to you of knowledge
, indeed, you would be among the wrongdoers.

What He means by His words, the Almighty: And if you were to follow their desires, is that if you sought, O Muhammad, the pleasure of these Jews and Christians, who said to you and your companions: Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided, then you followed their qiblah - meaning: you returned to their qiblah. What he means by his saying:
h
After what has come to you of knowledge
h
after what has come to you of knowledge

, by informing you that they are persisting in falsehood, and in their stubbornness towards the truth, and their knowledge that the qiblah towards which I have directed you is the qiblah which was imposed upon your father Abraham, peace be upon him, and all his descendants after him from the messengers - facing towards it, then you will be among the wrongdoers, meaning: If you do that, then you will be among My servants who are wrongdoers themselves, who disobey My command, and abandon My obedience, and one of them, and among them.
Those to whom We gave the Scripture know him as they know their own sons.
What God Almighty means by His statement:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture know it as they know their own sons

He says: These Jewish rabbis and Christian scholars know that the Sacred House is their Qiblah and the Qiblah of Abraham and the Qiblah of the prophets before you, just as they know their own sons, as Bishr bin Muʿadh told us: He said:

c: Yazid bin Zuraiʿ told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture know it as they know their own sons
, he says: They know that the Sacred House is the Qiblah.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture know it as they know their own sons
, meaning: the qiblah.

c: I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture know it as they know their own sons
, they knew that the qiblah of the Sacred House was their qiblah that they were commanded to follow, just as they knew their own sons.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture know it as they know their own sons
, meaning by that: the Kaaba, the Sacred House.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture know it as they know their own sons
, they knew that the Kaaba is the qiblah of the prophets, just as they knew their own sons.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture recognize him as they recognize their own sons
, he said: The Jews recognize that it is the qiblah, Mecca.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Ibn Jurayj said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture recognize him as they recognize their own sons
, he said: The qiblah and the House.

x: The statement on the interpretation of the statement of God Almighty: And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know.
God Almighty says: And indeed, a party of those who were given the Scripture - and they are the Jews and Christians. And Mujahid used to say: They are the People of the Scripture.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr - meaning al-Bahili - told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: that is.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: similarly.
