x: And His statement, that they may conceal the truth, - and that truth is the qiblah - towards which God, the Almighty, directed His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace - means: So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque, towards which the prophets before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to face, but the Jews and Christians concealed it, so some of them turned east, and some towards Jerusalem, and they rejected what God commanded them to do, and they concealed the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though they found it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. God the Almighty informed His Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his nation about their betrayal of God the Blessed and Exalted, and their betrayal of His servants, and their concealment of that, and He informed that they were doing what they were doing knowing that the truth was not Him, and that what was required of them by God the Most High was the opposite of Him, so He said: that they conceal the truth while they know, that they were not allowed to conceal it, so they deliberately disobeyed God the Blessed and Exalted, as:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, he said, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement: And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know, so they concealed Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him).

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: that they conceal the truth while they know, he said: they concealed Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), although they found it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know, meaning the qiblah.

x: The truth is from your Lord,
h
so do not be among the doubters
The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty: The truth is from your Lord,
h
so do not be among the doubters

God Almighty means: Know, O Muhammad, that the truth is what your Lord has taught you and has given you from Him, not what the Jews and Christians say to you. This is report from God Almighty to His Prophet, peace be upon him, that the qiblah towards which he was directed is the true qiblah which Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, and the prophets of God Almighty followed after him. God Almighty says to him: So act according to the truth which has come to you from your Lord, O Muhammad, and do not be among the doubters.
He means by His words:
h
So do not be among the doubters
, that is: Do not be among those who doubt that the qiblah towards which I have directed you is the qiblah of Abraham, my friend, peace be upon him, and the qiblah of the prophets other than him, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told me, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ He
m: said: God Almighty said to His Prophet, peace be upon him: The truth is from your Lord,
h
so do not be among the doubters
, meaning: Do not be in doubt, for it is your Qiblah and the Qiblah of the prophets before you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
So do not be among the doubters
, he said: Among the doubters, he said: Do not doubt that.

x: The doubter is a verbal noun, from the word mariyah, and mariyah means doubt, and from it is the saying of Al-A'sha: It makes the markets of the passers-by run, if the mirage sways Abu Jaʿfar said: If someone were to say to us: Was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, doubting that the truth was from his Lord, or that the qiblah towards which God directed him was the truth from God, the Most High, to the extent that he was forbidden from doubting that, and it was said to him: So do not be among those who doubt? It would be said: This is one of the statements that the Arabs use as a command or a prohibition to the one being addressed, but what is meant by it is someone else, as God, the Most High, said: O Prophet, fear God and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites (al-Ahzab 33:1). He said: “And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted” (al-Ahzab 33:2).

So the statement was used as a command to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a prohibition to him, and what is meant by it are his believing companions. We have already explained something similar to that before, so there is no need to repeat it.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And for each is a direction toward which he turns.

What is meant by the Almighty’s saying: And for each, is for each of the people of a religion, so He omitted, the people of the religion, and was satisfied with the indication of the speech to it, as:

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, he said, ʿIsa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abu Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: And for each is a direction, he said: For each follower of a religion.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And for each is a direction toward which he turns, so the Jew has a direction toward which he turns, and the Christian has a direction toward which he turns, and God Almighty has guided you, O nation, to the qiblah which is the qiblah.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I said to Ata’, regarding his statement:
h
And for each is a direction towards which he turns
, he said: For every people of a religion, the Jews and the Christians, Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: For every follower of a religion.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And for each is a direction towards which he turns
, he said: For the Jews there is a qiblah, and for the Christians there is a qiblah, and for you there is a qiblah, meaning the Muslims.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And for each is a direction towards which he turns

, meaning the people of religions. He says: for each qiblah they are pleased with, and the face of God, the Blessed and Exalted, is where the believers turn. This is because God, the Most High, said: “So wherever you turn, there is the face of God. Indeed, God is All-Encompassing and Knowing.” (al-Baqarah 2:115).

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And for each is a direction towards which he turns

, meaning: for each people a qiblah that they have turned. So the interpretation of the people of this statement in this verse: and for each people of a religion a qiblah that he faces, and turns his face towards it.

x: Others said what: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
And for each is a direction towards which he turns

, he said: It is their prayers towards the Holy House, and their prayers towards the Kaaba. The interpretation of the speaker of this article: And to every direction toward which your Lord turns, O Muhammad, is a direction of prayer, God Almighty is its master for His servants.
As for the direction, it is a source like sitting and walking, from the direction and its interpretation is: directed, he directs his face towards it in his prayer, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Facade means qibla.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And for every direction, he said: A direction.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: His direction, a qiblah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, he said,
m: I said to Mansur: And for every direction he turns, he said: We recite it, and for each We have made a qiblah that pleases them. As for his saying: He turns it, it means he turns his face toward it and faces it, as:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He is her master, he said: He is facing her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. The meaning of turning away here is approaching, as someone says to someone else: He turned to me, meaning: He came to me. The turning away that is used is turning away from something. Then it is said: He turned to something, meaning: He came to it, turning away from me. Likewise, it is said: I turned away from it, if you turned away from it. Then it is said: I turned to it, meaning I approached it, turning away from someone else. The verb—I mean turning away—in His statement: He is her master refers to all of them. And it is that which is with its master, it is the whole, and it was used alone for the wording of the whole. So the meaning of the statement then is: And for every people of a religion there is a direction, and all of them turn their faces towards it. It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas and others that they read it: He is its master, meaning that he is directed towards it. And the whole then would not have a named agent, and if its agent had been named, the statement would have been: And for every person of a religion there is a direction, God is his master towards it, meaning: He directs him towards it. It has been mentioned from some of them that he read it: And for every direction without the tanween and the addition, and that is a mistake, and it is not permissible to read it like that. Because that - if it is read like that - the report is not complete and it is a statement without meaning. And that is not permissible to be from God, may He be glorified. And the correct reading in our view in that is: And for every direction he is its master, meaning: And for every direction and qiblah. That is all, his face is turned towards it. For the consensus of the proof of the reciters on reading it thus, and correcting it, and the deviation of those who disagreed with that to something else, and what came with the transmission abundantly is proof, and what was isolated from those who were allowed to forget and make a mistake, it is not permissible to object to the proof with it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the saying of the Most High:
h
So race in good deeds
Abu Jaʿfar said: The Most High meant by His saying:
h
So race in good deeds
, so they hastened and hastened, from racing, which is Initiative and haste, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So hasten to do good deeds
, meaning:
h
So hasten to do good deeds
. What he means by his statement:
h
So hasten to do good deeds
, is: I have made clear to you, O believers, the truth, and guided you to the Qiblah from which the Jews, Christians, and all the people of other religions have turned away,
h
so hasten to do good deeds

, in gratitude to your Lord, and provision yourself in this world for your Hereafter, for I have made clear to you the ways of salvation, so you have no excuse for being negligent, and protect your Qiblah, and do not lose it as the nations before you lost it, lest you go astray as they went astray, like the one who:

c: Bishr bin Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zariʿ told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So hasten to do good deeds
, meaning: Do not be overcome by your Qiblah.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: So race one another in good deeds, he said: righteous deeds.

x: The statement on the interpretation of the statement of God Almighty: “
h
Wherever you may be
, God will bring you all together.
Indeed, God is over all things competent.”
The meaning of His statement:
h
Wherever you may be
, God will bring you all together, is in any place or spot in which you perish, God will bring you all together on the Day of Resurrection.
Indeed, God is over all things competent, as:

c: I was told by ʿAmmar ibn al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatadah:
h
Wherever you may be
, God will bring you all together, meaning:
h
wherever you may be
, God will bring you all together on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Musa told us, he said, ʿAmr ibn Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
Wherever you may be
, God will bring you all together, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection.

x: God, the Almighty, singled out the believers with this verse for their obedience to Him and provisioning themselves in this world for the Hereafter. He, the Most High, said to them: “So hasten, O believers, to act in obedience to your Lord and adhere to what He has guided you to, such as the Qiblah of Abraham, His friend, and the laws of His religion. Indeed, God, the Most High, will bring you and those who opposed your Qiblah, your religion, and your laws together on the Day of Resurrection, from wherever you are on earth, until He gives the good-doer among you his reward for his goodness, and the evil-doer his punishment for his evil, or He favors and pardons. As for His statement: “Indeed, God is over all things competent,” He, the Most High, means: God, the Most High, is capable of gathering you - after your death - from your graves to Him, from wherever you were and your graves were, and of anything else that He wills.
So hasten to bring your souls forth with righteous deeds before your death, for the Day of Resurrection and Gathering.”

evidence.text: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, he said, I said to Mansur: And for every direction he turns, he said: We recite it, and for each We have made a qiblah that pleases them.
It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas and others that they read it: He is its master, meaning that he is directed towards it.
It has been mentioned from some of them that he read it: And for every direction without the tanween and the addition, and that is a mistake, and it is not permissible to read it like that.
Because that - if it is read like that - the report is not complete and it is a statement without meaning.
And the correct reading in our view in that is: And for every direction he is its master, meaning: And for every direction and qiblah.

For the consensus of the proof of the reciters on reading it thus, and correcting it, and the deviation of those who disagreed with that to something else, and what came with the transmission abundantly is proof, and what was isolated from those who were allowed to forget and make a mistake, it is not permissible to object to the proof with it.

x: h
And from wherever you go out
, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord.
h
And God is not unaware of what you do
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying: "
h
And from wherever you go out
, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram.
And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord.
h
And God is not unaware of what you do
He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying:
h
And from wherever you go out

, and from whatever place you go out to Whatever direction you face, turn your face, O Muhammad - he says: turn your face. We have already shown that turning in this direction towards the Sacred Mosque means: turning the face towards it. We have already explained the meaning of turning in the direction. As for His statement: And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, He, the Most High, means by it: And indeed, turning in its direction is for the truth about which there is no doubt from your Lord, so preserve it and obey God in your turning towards it. As for his statement:
h
And God is not unaware of what you do
, he is saying: Indeed, God, the Most High, is not oblivious to your deeds, nor is He unaware of them, but He is counting them for you, so that He may reward you for them on the Day of Resurrection.
The statement in the interpretation of the statement of God, the Most High, “
h
And from wherever you go out
, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram.
h
And wherever you are
, turn your faces toward it.”
What is meant by the statement of God, the Most High,
h
And from wherever you go out

, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram, is from whatever place or spot you set out from, O Muhammad, so turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram, which is its direction. What is meant by his statement,
h
And wherever you are
, turn your faces, is wherever you are, O believers, on God’s earth, so turn your faces in your prayer toward Him, before Him, and intending Him. “
h
So that mankind will have no argument against you
, except for those who do wrong among them.
h
So do not fear them
, but fear Me.”
A group of interpreters said: God the Almighty meant by people in His statement:
h
So that mankind will have no argument against you
, the People of the Book.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, Yazid ibn Zariʿ told us, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
So that mankind will have no argument against you

, meaning the People of the Book. They said - when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was directed towards the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House - that the man longed for his father’s house and the religion of his people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
So that mankind will have no argument against you

, meaning the People of the Book. They said - when the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was directed towards the Kaʿbah - that the man longed for his father’s house and the religion of his people!

x: What argument did the People of the Book have regarding the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions towards the Holy House, towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions?
We have previously mentioned what was narrated about that.

It was said: They used to say: Muhammad and his companions did not know where their qiblah was until we guided them! And their saying: Muhammad differs from us in our religion and follows our qiblah! This is the argument that they used to argue with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, in a way that they would argue with them and deceive the ignorant and stupid polytheists. We have previously explained that the meaning of the people arguing with him, which God the Most High mentioned in His Book, is only arguments and debates. So God, the Most High, cut off that from their argument and settled it, by changing the qiblah of His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the believers in him from the qiblah of the Jews to the qiblah of His friend Abraham (peace be upon him). This is the meaning of God’s statement, the Most High:
h
So that mankind will have no argument against you
, meaning: the people who used to argue with them with what I have described.
As for His statement:
h
Except those who did wrong among them
, they are the polytheists of the Quraysh, according to what the interpreters have interpreted.
Those who said that were mentioned: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:150
h
And from wherever you go out
, turn your face toward Al-Masjid Al-Haram.
h
And wherever you are
, turn your faces toward it so that people will have no argument against you, except those who commit injustice among them.
h
So do not fear them
, but fear Me, and I will complete My favor upon you, and perhaps you will be guided.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Except those who have wronged among them
, the people of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, Amr ibn Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: They are the polytheists of Mecca.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Except those who have wronged among them
, meaning the polytheists of Quraysh.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, Muʿmar told us, on the authority of Qatada and Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Except those who have wronged among them
, he said: They are the polytheists of the Arabs.

c: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, Yazid ibn Zuraiʿ told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Except those who have wronged among them
, and those who have wronged are the polytheists of Quraysh.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata’ said:
m: They are the polytheists of Quraysh. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Kathir informed me that he heard Mujahid say the same as Ata’.

x: What argument did the polytheists of Quraysh have against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, in their facing the Kaaba in their prayers? Is it permissible for the polytheists to have an argument against the believers - in what God commanded them to do or forbade them from doing?

The meaning of that is contrary to what you imagined and went to. Rather, the argument in this case is the dispute and debate. The meaning of the statement is: So that no one among the people will have an argument against you and a false claim, other than the polytheists of Quraysh, for they have an unjust claim against you and an unjust dispute, by saying to you: Muhammad has returned to our Qiblah, and he will return to our religion. That is from their saying and their false hopes, and it is the argument that Quraysh had against the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions. For that reason, God the Most High excluded those who did wrong from Quraysh from all other people, as He denied that any of them had an argument regarding their Qiblah towards which He directed them.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

Who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
So that mankind will have no argument against you
, except for those who are unjust among them, the people of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Mujahid said: He says: Their argument is their statement: We have returned to our Qiblah!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: We have returned to our Qiblah!

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
So that mankind will have no argument against you

, except for those who are unjust among them, they said: They are the polytheists of the Arabs, they said when the Qiblah was turned towards the Kaaba: We have returned to your Qiblah, and soon we will return to your religion! God, the Most High, said: So fear them not, but fear Me. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
Except those who have wronged among them

, and those who have wronged: the polytheists of Quraysh. He says: They will argue with you about that, so their argument against the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was his turning toward the Sacred House - they said: He will return to our religion as he returned to our Qiblah! So God, the Most High, revealed about all of that. Al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Ishaq narrated, he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, similarly. Musa bin Harun narrated, he said: ʿAmr bin Hammad narrated, he said: Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi, among other things, on the authority of Abu Malik and on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas - and on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masʿud, and on some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: When the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned toward the Kaʿbah, after his prayer toward the Holy House, the polytheists of Mecca said: Muhammad is confused about his religion! So he turned his qiblah towards you, and he knew that you were more guided than him, and that he was about to enter your religion! So God, the Most High, revealed about them: “
h
So that mankind will have no argument against you
, except those who are unjust among them. So fear them not, but fear Me.”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to me, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I said to Ata’: His statement:
h
So that mankind will have no argument against you

, except those who are unjust among them, he said: Quraysh said, when he returned to the Kaaba and ordered it: He could not do without us! He has turned towards our qiblah! So it is their argument, and they are those who are unjust. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Kathir informed me that he heard Mujahid say something similar to what Ata’ said, so Mujahid said: Their argument is their statement: You have returned to our qiblah! The interpretation of the people of interpretation whose interpretation we have mentioned has made clear the correctness of what we have said in its interpretation, and that it is an exception in the sense of the known exception, in which what was negated from what came before it was established in them after the letter of exception. Just as the saying of the one who said: None of the people walked except your brother, is an affirmation of the brother from the walk that is denied of every other person. Likewise, his saying:
h
So that the people will have no argument against you

, except those who are unjust among them, is a denial that anyone would have a dispute or argument before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or a false claim against him and his companions, because of their facing the Kaaba in their prayers, except those who wronged themselves from Quraysh, for they have a dispute and a false claim against them by saying: You only turned toward us and toward our Qiblah because we were more guided than you in the way, and that you were, by facing the Holy House in Jerusalem, in error and falsehood. Since that is the meaning of the verse by consensus of the argument of the people of interpretation, then the saying of the one who claimed that the meaning of his saying:
h
Except those of them who are unjust

is: nor those of them who are unjust, and that except means and. Because if that was its meaning, the first negation of all people - that they would have an argument against the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and his companions in turning their faces towards the Kaaba - would have made clear the intended meaning, and there would have been nothing in mentioning his saying after that: Except those who wronged among them, except for the confusion that is too high to be added to or described with. This is with the meaning of the speech being excluded - if it is directed except to the meaning of the waw, and the meaning of the conjunction - from the speech of the Arabs. That is because except is not found in any of their speech in the meaning of the waw, except with a previous exception that it may have preceded. Like the saying of the speaker: The people marched except for Amr except your brother, meaning: except for Amr and your brother, so except then would be a conveyer of what the waw conveys, because the second except is connected to the first except. It is also combined with illa and waw and it is said: The people walked except for ‘Amr and your brother, so one of them is deleted and the other takes its place, so it is said: The people walked except for ‘Amr and your brother - or Except for ‘Amr except your brother, for what we described before. Since that is the case, it is not permissible for a claimant from among the people to claim that illa in this place means waw which comes with the meaning of conjunction. The corruption of the statement of the one who claims that the meaning of that is: Except for those among them who are unjust, for they have no argument,
h
so do not fear them

. Like the statement of the speaker in speech: All people are grateful to you except the unjust one who transgresses against you, for his aggression and his failure to praise are not to be taken into account, due to the enmity. Likewise, the unjust one has no argument, and he was called unjust, due to the consensus of the people of interpretation on the error of what he claimed of interpretation in that regard. It is sufficient evidence of the error of his statement that they agreed to reject it. It is apparent from the length of the statement of those who claimed that those who did wrong here are people from the Arabs who were Jews and Christians, so they used to argue with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for the rest of the Arabs, they had no argument, and the argument of those who argued was broken. Because you say to those whose argument you want to break: You have an argument against me, but it is broken, and you argue without an argument, and your argument is weak. And the meaning of
h
except those who did wrong among them
was directed to the meaning:
h
except those who did wrong among them

, from the People of the Book, for they have a weak argument against you. This is the statement of those who said: except in this place means be. And the statement of those who claimed that it began with the meaning:
h
except those who did wrong among them
h
so do not fear them

is weak. Because the interpretation of the people of interpretation came in that that it was from God the Almighty, report about those who were unjust among them: that they argue against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions with what we have mentioned, and he did not intend in that to report the description of their argument as weak or strong - even if it was weak because it is invalid - but rather he intended in it to prove for those who were unjust, what was negated from those before the letter of exception from the description.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, he said, Qatada said:
m: A Jew argued with Abu al-ʿAliyah and said: Moses, peace be upon him, used to pray toward the rock of the Holy House. Abu al-ʿAliyah said: He used to pray at the rock toward the Sacred House. He said: He said: So between me and you is the mosque of Salih, for he carved it out of the mountain. Abu al-ʿAliyah said: I prayed in it and turned it toward the Sacred House. Qatada said: Abu Al-Aaliyah told me that he passed by the Mosque of Dhul-Qarnayn, and his Qiblah was towards the Kaaba. As for his saying:
h
So do not fear them

, but fear Me, it means: Do not fear those whose situation I have described to you, the oppressors, in their arguments, their arguments, and their saying what they say: that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, has returned to our Qiblah, and will return to our religion! Or that they may be able to harm you in your religion, or turn you away from the truth to which God Almighty has guided you. Rather, fear Me, so fear My punishment, for disobeying My command if you disobey it. And that is from God Almighty, presented to His believing servants, by urging them to adhere to their Qiblah and pray towards it, and by forbidding them to face anything other than it. God Almighty says: And fear Me, O believers, in abandoning My obedience in what I have commanded you to do, of praying towards the Sacred Mosque. It has been narrated from Al-Suddi regarding that as follows: Abu Jaʿfar said: By His words, may His praise be glorified, And to complete My favor upon you, he means, from wherever you come from the country and the earth, and to whatever spot you head, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque,
h
and wherever you are

, O Muhammad and the believers, turn your faces toward it in your prayers, and take it as your qiblah, so that no one among the people - except the polytheists of Quraysh - will have an argument, and by that - by My guiding you to the qiblah of My friend Abraham, peace be upon him, whom I made an imam for the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:150
h
And from wherever you go out
, turn your face toward Al-Masjid Al-Haram.
h
And wherever you are
, turn your faces toward it so that people will have no argument against you, except those who commit injustice among them.
h
So do not fear them

, but fear Me, and I will complete My favor upon you, and perhaps you will be guided. people - I will complete My favor upon you, and complete through it the laws of your pure, Muslim religion that I commanded Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and all the other prophets besides them. This is His blessing that He, the Most High, informed us that He will complete upon His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and upon the believers among his companions. And His statement, and that you may be guided, means: so that you may be guided to the correct direction of prayer. And perhaps is in apposition to His statement, and that I may complete My favor upon you, and and that I may complete My favor upon you is in apposition to His statement, lest it be.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Just
h
as We have sent among you a Messenger from among you
who recites to you Our verses
h
and purifies you
and teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you that which you did not know.

He means by His saying, may His praise be glorified: Just as We have sent among you a Messenger, and to complete My favor upon you by explaining the laws of your pure religion, and to guide you to the religion of My friend Abraham, peace be upon him, so I will make for you his supplication with which he supplicated to Me and his question which he asked of Me, saying: “Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.” (al-Baqarah 2:128), just as I made for you his supplication with which he supplicated to Me and his question which he asked of Me, saying: “Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from among themselves who will recite to them Your verses and teach them the Book and wisdom and purify them.

Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” (al-Baqarah 2:129), So I sent from among you My Messenger whom Abraham, My friend, and his son Ishmael, asked Me to send from their descendants. So as - since that is the meaning of the speech - is a connection to the statement of God Almighty: And to complete My favor upon you. His statement:
h
as We sent
among you a Messenger from among you is not connected to His statement: Remember Me, I will remember you.
Some people have said that the meaning of that is: Remember Me
h
as We sent

among you a Messenger from among you to remember you. They claimed that this is from the introduction which means delay, so they drowned the removal, and were far from the truth, and interpreted the speech in a meaning other than its known meaning, and altered its understood aspect. That is because the current speech on the tongues of the Arabs, and the understanding in their speech among themselves - if some of them say to others: As I have been good to you, O so-and-so, be good to me - is that they do not stipulate conditions for the other, because the kaf in as is a condition, meaning: Do as I have done. In the coming of the answer to remember me after it, which is his saying:
h
I remind you
, the clearest evidence that his saying:
h
as We sent
is related to the verb that preceded it, and that his saying: Remember me, I will remind you is the predicate of a subject separated from the first, and that it is - from the reason for his saying:
h
as We sent
among you - separate.
Some grammarians have claimed that his saying: So remember me - if he makes his saying:
h
as We sent
among you an answer To him, with his saying:
h
I remind you

- similar to the reward that is answered with two answers, like the saying of the speaker: If so-and-so comes to you, then come to him and satisfy him, so his saying: Come to him and satisfy him becomes two answers to his saying: If he comes to you, and like his saying: If you come to me, I will treat you well and honor you. And this saying, even if it is a doctrine of doctrines, is not the easiest and most eloquent in the speech of the Arabs. And what is more deserving of the Book of God, the Almighty, to be directed to from the languages, is the most eloquent and most well-known of the speech of the Arabs, without the most abhorrent and ignorant of their language. This, with its face being far from the concept in interpretation.
Mention of those who said: His saying:
h
As We sent
, is the answer to his saying:
h
So remember Me

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us,
m: he heard Ibn Abi Nujayh say about the saying of God, the Almighty:
h
As We sent
among you a Messenger from among you, as you did,
h
so remember Me

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. And His statement:
h
As We have sent among you a Messenger from among yourselves

, He means the Arabs by that. He, the Most High, said to them: O Arabs, adhere to My obedience, and face the qiblah toward which I have commanded you to face, so that the Jews’ argument against you will be cut off, so that they will have no argument against you, and so that I may complete My favor upon you, and you will be guided, just as I began with My favor upon you, so I sent among you a Messenger from among you. And that Messenger whom He sent to them from among them: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His statement:
h
As We have sent among you a Messenger from among you
, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for His statement: He recites to you Our verses, it means the verses of the Qur’an, and by His statement:
h
And purifies you

, it purifies you from the filth of sins, and teaches you the Book, which is the Criterion, it means: He teaches them its rulings. And by wisdom, it means the Sunnah and understanding of the religion. We have explained all of that before with its evidence. As for His statement: And teaches you what you did not know, it means: And teaches you from the report of the prophets - and the stories of the past nations, and the report of what is new and will happen from the matters that the Arabs did not know, so they learned them from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So He, may His praise be glorified, informed them that they will only attain all of that through His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of the Almighty:
h
So remember Me
, I will remember you.
By that, the Almighty means:
h
So remember Me
, O believers, by your obedience to Me in what I command you and what I forbid you from, I will remember you with My mercy to you and My forgiveness for you, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Lahiʿah, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ ibn Dinar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr:
m: Remember Me, I will remember you, he said: Remember Me with My obedience, I will remember you with My forgiveness.

x: Some of them interpreted that as being from remembrance with praise and commendation.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His words: “
h
So remember Me
, I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me,” that God remembers those who remember Him, increases those who are grateful to Him, and punishes those who are ungrateful.

c: Musa told me, he said, ʿAmr told me, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: Remember Me, I will remember you, he said: There is no servant who remembers God except that God remembers him. No believer mentions Him without mentioning Him with mercy, and no disbeliever mentions Him without mentioning Him with torment.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying: And be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful.

The Almighty means by that: Be grateful to Me, O believers, for what I have bestowed upon you of Islam and guidance to the religion that I have prescribed for My prophets and chosen ones, and do not be ungrateful, meaning: Do not deny My kindness to you, lest I deprive you of My favor that I have bestowed upon you, but be grateful to Me for it, and I will increase you and complete My favor upon you, and guide you to what I have guided to whomever I am pleased of among My servants, for I have promised My creation that whoever is grateful to Me, I will increase him, and whoever is ungrateful to Me, I will deprive him and take away from him what I have given him.

i: The Arabs say: I advised you, and I thanked you, and they hardly say: I advised you, and they may say: I thanked you and advised you, from that is the saying of the poet:
x: They have combined my misery and blessings with you.

Why don’t you thank the people when you don’t fight? Al-Nabigha said in his advice to you: I advised Banu Awf, but they did not accept my messenger and my methods did not succeed with them. We have shown that the meaning of gratitude is to praise a man for his praiseworthy actions, and that the meaning of ingratitude is to cover something, in the past, so there is no need to repeat it here.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying: "O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer.
Indeed, God is with the patient."

This verse is an exhortation from God, the Most High, to obey Him and to endure its unpleasantness for the body and wealth. He said: O you who believe, seek help through patience and prayer to carry out My obedience, and to perform My obligations in abrogating My rulings, and to turn away from what I abrogate from them to what I create for you from My obligations, and to which I transfer you from My rulings, and to submit to My command in what I command you to do when I impose its ruling on you, and to turn away from it after I have turned you away from it - even if that befalls you with something unpleasant from the words of your enemies from the disbelievers by their false accusation against you, or hardship on your bodies in carrying it out, or a decrease in your wealth - and to strive against your enemies and fight them in My way, with patience from you towards Me in the unpleasantness of that and its difficulty for you, and to endure its suffering.

And its burden, then by frightening you in what befalls you of the horrific matters to pray to Me. For by being patient in the face of hardships you attain My pleasure, and by praying to Me you attain your requests from Me, and you attain your needs from Me, for I am with those who are patient in performing My obligations and abandoning their sins, I support them, I watch over them, and I protect them, until they attain what they sought and hoped for from Me.
And I have explained the meaning of patience and prayer previously, so we disliked repeating it, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And seek help through patience and prayer
, he says: Seek help through patience and prayer in pleasing God, and know that they are from obeying God.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer, know that they are an aid to obeying God. As for his statement: Indeed, God is with the patient, its interpretation is: God is his supporter and helper and is pleased with his actions, like the saying of the speaker: Do so-and-so, and I am with you, meaning: I am your supporter and helper in doing that.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And do not say about those who are killed in the way of God
, ‘They are dead.’
Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not.
The Almighty means: O you who believe, seek help through patience in obeying Me in the struggle against your enemy, abandoning your sins, and performing all of My obligations upon you.
h
And do not say about those who are killed in the way of God

, ‘He is dead.’ For the dead among My creation are those from whom I have taken their life and deprived them of their senses, so they do not enjoy pleasure or attain bliss. For those of you and all of My creation who are killed in My way are alive with Me, in life and bliss, and a pleasant life, and a year’s provision, rejoicing in what I have given them of My bounty, and what I have bestowed upon them of My honor, as Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His saying: Rather, they are alive with their Lord, they are provided with the fruits of Paradise, and they find its fragrance, and they are not… In it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And say not of those who are killed in the way of God

, ‘They are dead.’ Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not, we used to be told that the souls of the martyrs recognize each other in white birds eating from the fruits of Paradise, and that their dwellings are the Lote Tree of the Limit, and that the one who fights in the way of God has three good qualities: whoever is killed in the way of God among them becomes alive and provided for, whoever is victorious, God will give him a great reward, and whoever dies, God will provide him with a good provision. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated, Muammar narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And say not of those who are killed in the way of God
, ‘They are dead.’ Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not, he said: The souls of the martyrs are in the form of white birds.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not say about those who are killed in the way of God
, ‘They are dead.’ Rather, they are alive, in the form of green birds flying in Paradise wherever they wished from it, eating from wherever they wished.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Uthman ibn Ghiyath told us, he said,
m: I heard ʿIkrimah say about His statement,
h
And say not of those who are killed in the way of God
, ‘They are dead.’ Rather, they are alive, but you perceive [it] not, he said: The souls of the martyrs are in green birds in Paradise.

x: If someone were to say to us: What is in His statement,
h
And say not of those who are killed in the way of God

, ‘They are dead.’ Rather, they are alive, of the specificity of the report about the one killed in the way of God, which does not include anyone else? It has been known that the reports from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) are consistent, and that he described the state of the believers and the unbelievers after their death. He informed about the believers that doors to Paradise will be opened for them from their graves, from which they will smell its fragrance, and they will hasten the coming of the Hour, so that they may return to their dwellings there, and they will be reunited with their families and children there. And about the unbelievers, that doors to Hell will be opened for them from their graves, and they will look at it, and they will be afflicted with its stench and its evils, and those who will oppress them will be empowered over them until the coming of the Hour, and they will ask God to delay the coming of the Hour, fearing the fate that God has prepared for them therein, along with similar reports.

If the reports from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) are consistent, then what is the special privilege of the one who is killed in the way of God, which is not shared by all other human beings except him, while all the unbelievers and believers except him are alive in the intermediate realm, while the unbelievers are tormented therein with a difficult life, and as for the believers, they will enjoy the spirit, basil, and the breeze of Paradise? It was said: What God has distinguished the martyrs with in this regard, and what He has informed the believers with from His report about them, the Most High, is His informing them that they will be provided with the foods and drinks of Paradise in their intermediate state before their resurrection, and that they will enjoy what all of humanity will enjoy when they enter it after the resurrection, from the delicious foods that God has not fed anyone but them in their intermediate state before their resurrection.

So that is the virtue with which He has distinguished them and distinguished them from others, and the benefit that He has informed the believers with from the report about them, so the Most High said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead
. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision, rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty”

And the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came in a similar manner to what we said. Abu Kurayb narrated that Abdur-Raheem bin Sulayman and Abdah bin Sulayman narrated from Muhammad bin Ishaq from Al-Harith bin Fadil from Mahmud bin Labid from Ibn Abbas who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The martyrs are on Barq, a river at the gate of Paradise, in a green dome - Abdah said: in a green garden - their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening.’”

Abu Kurayb narrated that Jabir bin Nuh narrated from Al-Ifriqi from Ibn Bashar Al-Sulami - or Abu Bashar, Abu Jaafar was not sure - who said: The souls of the martyrs are in white domes from the domes of Paradise, in each dome are two wives, their provision on every day the sun rises is a bull and a fish. As for the bull, in it is the taste of every fruit in Paradise, and as for the fish, in it is the taste of every drink in Paradise.

If someone were to say: The report of what you mentioned, that God, the Most High, mentioned that He informed the believers with His report about the martyrs from the blessing that He has singled them out with in the intermediate realm, is not found in His statement:
h
And say not of those who are killed in the way of God

, ‘They are dead.’ Rather, they are alive. Rather, it contains the report about their state, are they dead or alive? It was said: What is meant by mentioning the report about their lives is the report that they are exempt from the blessing, but God, the Most High, mentioned that when He had informed His servants about what He had singled out the martyrs with in His statement:
h
And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead
. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.”
and they knew their state from His report of that, then what was meant by God, the Most High, mentioned in His statement:
h
And say not of those who are killed in the way of God
, ‘They are dead.’
Rather, they are alive, is that He forbade His creation from saying about the martyrs that they are dead, leaving out repeating what He had explained to them of their story. As for his statement:
h
But you do not perceive

, he means: But you do not see them and know that they are alive. You only know that by my informing you of them. And his statement: dead is raised by an implied pronoun for the names of those who are killed in the way of God, and the meaning of that is:
h
And do not say about those who are killed in the way of God

that they are dead. And the accusative is not permissible for the dead, because the statement does not apply to them. And likewise his statement: Rather, they are alive, is raised, meaning: they are alive.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying:
h
And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits
, but give good tidings to the patient.

This is a notification from God, the Most High, mentioned by the followers of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He will test them and examine them with hardships of matters, to know who follows the Messenger and who turns back on his heels, just as He tested them and examined them by changing the Qiblah from the Holy House to the Kaʿbah, and just as He tested His chosen ones before them. And He promised them that in another verse, saying to them: "Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [things] have not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? They were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of God? Unquestionably, the help of God is near. (al-Baqarah 2:214) Ibn ʿAbbas and others used to say something similar to what we said about that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger

, and something similar to this, he said: God informed the believers that this world is a place of trial, and that He will test them in it, and He commanded them to be patient, and He gave them good tidings, saying: And give good tidings to the patient, then He informed them that He did this with His prophets and chosen ones, so that their souls would be at ease, so He said: They were touched by poverty and hardship, and they were shaken (al-Baqarah 2:214). The meaning of His statement:
h
And We will surely test you
, is that We will surely test you. We have already explained that the meaning of trial is testing, in what has passed before. And His statement:
h
With something of fear
, meaning fear of the enemy, and with hunger - which is drought - He says: We will surely test you
h
with something of fear

that will befall you from your enemy, and with a year that will befall you in which famine and hardship will befall you, and your demands will be difficult, so your wealth will be diminished? And wars that will take place between you and your enemies from the disbelievers, so your numbers will be diminished? And the death of your children and offspring, and droughts that occur and reduce your fruits. All of that is a test from Me for you, and a trial from Me for you, so that those of you who are truthful in their faith may be distinguished from those of you who are liars in it, and those of you who have insight into their religion may be distinguished from those of you who are hypocrites, doubters, and skeptics. All of that is an address from Him to the followers of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, as:

c: Harun ibn Idris al-Kufi al-Asamm told me, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger
, he said: They are the companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Rather, the Most High said:
h
with something of fear

and did not say: with things, because of the different types of what He informed His servants with which He would test them. So since that was different - and of indicates that each type of it contains something, then the meaning of that is:
h
And We will surely test you
h
with something of fear

, and with something of hunger, and with something of a decrease in wealth - He was satisfied with indicating the mention of the thing at the beginning, from repeating it with each type of it. So the Almighty did all of that to them, and tested them with various kinds of trials, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits

, he said: That has happened, and something worse than that will happen. God said at that time: And give good tidings to the patient, who, when disaster strikes them, say, “Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return. Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided.” Then the Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, give good tidings to those who are patient in the face of My testing them with what I test them with, and who guard themselves from going ahead of what I forbid them from, and who hold themselves to performing what I have charged them with of My obligations, despite My testing them with what I test them with, who say when disaster strikes them, Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return. So God Almighty commanded him to give good report regarding the hardships He was testing them with, to those who were patient, whose characteristics God had described. The origin of the word tabsheer is when a man tells another man report, whether it pleases him or not, that no one else has told him before. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:155
h
And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits
, but give good tidings to the patient.

x: Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, 'Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return.'

God Almighty means: Give good tidings, O Muhammad, to the patient ones who know that all the blessings they have are from Me, so they acknowledge My servitude, and believe in My Oneness as Lord, and believe in the Resurrection and returning to Me, so they submit to My judgment, and hope for My reward, and fear My punishment, and say - when I test them with some of My trials, and afflict them with what I promised them that I would afflict them with of fear, hunger, and loss of wealth, lives, and fruits, and other afflictions with which I test them -: We are the servants of our Lord and our object of worship, and we are His slaves, and to Him we shall return after our death, in submission to My judgment and contentment with My rulings.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying: "Those are they upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy.
And it is those who are the [rightly] guided."

The Almighty means by His saying: Those, these are the patient ones, whom He described and described, upon them, meaning: for them, prayers, meaning: forgiveness. And the prayers of God upon His servants, His forgiveness of His servants, like that which "It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: O God, bless the family of Abi Awfa." Meaning: Forgive them. We have explained the prayer and its origin in other places. And His saying: and mercy, means: and for them with forgiveness, by which He pardoned their sins and covered them, mercy from God and compassion. Then the Almighty informed - along with what He mentioned that He gives them for their patience in His trials, in submission to His judgment, forgiveness and mercy - that they are the ones who are guided, who follow the path of truth, who say what pleases Him, and who do what they deserve from God in abundance of reward.
We have explained the meaning of guidance previously, for it means being guided to what is right.
A group of the people of interpretation said the same meaning as what we said about that.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement: “Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, ‘Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return.’
h
Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy

. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided,” he said: God informed that if the believer submits the matter to God, and returns and seeks refuge in God when afflicted, three qualities of good are written for him: blessings from God, mercy, and fulfilling the path of guidance. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever seeks God’s forgiveness when afflicted, God will compensate for his affliction, make his end good, and grant him a righteous successor with whom He will be pleased.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy
, he said: Blessings and mercy are upon those who were patient and sought God’s forgiveness.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Sufyan al-ʿAsfari, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: No one has been given what this nation has been given: Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, ‘Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return.’
h
Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy
. If it had been given to anyone, it would have been given to Jacob, peace be upon him. Have you not heard his saying, Oh, my grief over Joseph
r
(Yusuf 12:84)

x: The statement on the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God.
As-Safa is the plural of safa, which is a smooth rock, and from it is the saying of Al-Tirmaah: The One with the strength and the length has forbidden my hoof to ever dry up.

i: My qualities They said that Safa is one, and that the dual of Safwan is Safwan, and the plural of Asfaa is Safiyya and Safiyya, and they cited as evidence for that the words of the rajaz poet: As if his back is like the places of birds on a fine rock They said:
x: It is similar to a stick and sticks [and sticks, and sticks], and a mill and a millstone [and a millstone], and millstones. As for the marwah, it is a small pebble, the small of which is marwat, and the large of which is marw, like a date and dates and dates. Al-A’sha Maymun bin Qais said: And you see a light fading on the ground, but when it encounters a wound, it becomes broken.

He means by Marw: small rocks, and from that is the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb al-Hudhali: As if I am a mirror for events, as clear as the East, knocking every day It is said: Al-Mashqar. And God Almighty meant by His saying: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah, in this place the two mountains called by these two names that are in His sanctuary, not the rest of As-Safa and Al-Marwah. Therefore, He included the definite article in them, so that His servants would know that He meant by that the two mountains known by these two names, not the rest of As-Safa and Al-Marw. As for His saying: Of the symbols of God, He means: Of the landmarks of God that He Almighty made for His servants as a landmark and a place of worship where they worship Him, either by supplication, or by remembrance, or by performing the work that He has imposed on them at them. And from this is the saying of Al-Kumait: We kill them generation after generation.
You see them as ritual sacrifices through which people draw near.
Mujahid used to say about the rituals what:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said,
m: Abu Asim told Surat Al-Baqarah 2:158 Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah -
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them
h
And whoever volunteers good - then indeed

, Allah is appreciative and Knowing. us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God, he said: From the report that I told you about.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. So it seems that Mujahid saw that the rituals are the plural of ritual, from God’s notification to His servants of the matter of As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and what is upon them in circumambulating them. So its meaning is: informing them of that. And that is an interpretation from the concept that is far-fetched. Rather, God, the Most High, informed His believing servants by His saying: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God, that walking between them is among the rituals of Hajj that He prescribed for them, and He commanded His friend Abraham, peace be upon him, to do it, when he asked him to show him the rituals of Hajj. And even though its meaning is the meaning of the report, it is intended to be a command. Because God the Almighty commanded His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to follow the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, and said to him: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], ‘Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth’ (al-Nahl 16:123) and made Abraham an imam for those who came after him. So since it is true that circumambulating and walking between Safa and Marwah are among the rites of God and the rituals of Hajj, it is known that Abraham, peace and blessings be upon him, practiced it and established it for those who came after him, and he commanded our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his nation to follow it, so they must act accordingly, as the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, explained.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God the Almighty:
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs ‘Umrah Abu Ja’far said: God the Almighty means by His words:
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
, the one who comes to it returning to it after starting.

i: Likewise, everyone who frequently differs about something is in need of it, and from this is the saying of the poet:
x: I witness many people from Awf who resort to cursing the saffron-colored Al-Zubayr.
He means by his saying:
h
They perform Hajj

, they frequently visit it because of its leadership and leadership. The pilgrim is called a pilgrim because he comes to the House before the declaration, then returns to it for the Tawaf of the Day of Sacrifice after the declaration, then leaves it for Mina, then returns to it for the Tawaf of the chest. So because of his repeated return to it time and time again, he is called a pilgrim. As for the one performing ‘umrah, he is called a Mu’tamir because if he circumambulates it, he leaves it after visiting it. And what the Almighty means by his saying: or perform ‘umrah, is or perform ‘umrah to the House, and by ‘umrah he means visiting. So everyone who intends something is a Mu’tamir for it, and from this is the saying of al-‘Ajjaj: Ibn Ma'marhin called the meaning of I'tmar a distant destination from far away and he endured, meaning by his saying: when he performed the Umrah, when he intended it and his mother.
The statement in the interpretation of the words of God the Almighty:
h
There is no blame upon him for walking between them
Abu Ja'far said: God the Almighty means by his saying:
h
There is no blame upon him for walking between them
, he says:
h
there is no blame upon him
and no sin in walking between them.

What is the point of this statement, and you have told us that his saying: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God, even if its appearance is the appearance of the report, it is in the meaning of the command to walk between them? How can it be a command to walk between them, and then it is said: there is no blame upon the one who performed Hajj or Umrah in walking between them? Rather, the blame is removed from the one who did what is upon him by his coming, which is blame and hardship? And the command to walk between them, and the permission to walk between them, is not permissible to combine them in one situation?

This is contrary to what you have gone to. The meaning of this according to some people is: “When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) performed the ‘Umrah of al-Qadī’, some people who used to circumambulate them in the pre-Islamic era because of two idols they had on them out of their reverence for them feared them.”

They said: How can we circumambulate them, when we know that the reverence of idols and everything that is worshipped other than God is polytheism? So our circumambulation of these two stones is more difficult, because circumambulating them in the pre-Islamic era was only for the two idols they had on them, and God has brought Islam today, and there is no way to revere anything with God in the sense of worshipping Him! So God, the Most High, revealed concerning this matter of theirs: Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God, meaning: circumambulating them, so He left out mentioning circumambulating them, and was satisfied with mentioning them instead of Him. And since it was known to those addressed by it that its meaning is: from the landmarks of God, which He made a sign for His servants to worship Him at them by circumambulating between them, and to remember Him on them and at them with what is worthy of remembrance for Him, So whoever performs Hajj to the House or Umrah should not fear circumambulating them, because of what the people of ignorance used to circumambulate them because of the two idols they had, for the polytheists used to circumambulate them out of disbelief, and you circumambulate them out of faith, and belief in My Messenger, and obedience to My command, so there is no blame upon you for circumambulating them.
And sin is a sin, as: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
There is no blame upon him for circumambulating them
, he said: There is no sin upon him, but he has a reward. And the narration from the predecessors from the Companions and the Followers is similar to what we said in that.
Mention of the narrations that were narrated about that:

c: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said,
m: Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: That there was an idol on Al-Safa in the pre-Islamic era called Isaf, and an idol on Al-Marwah called Na’ilah. When the people of the pre-Islamic era circumambulated the House, they would touch the two idols. When Islam came and the idols were destroyed, the Muslims said: Al-Safa and Al-Marwah were only circumambulated because of the two idols, and circumambulating them is not one of the rituals! He said: Then God revealed: They are among the rituals,
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs ‘Umrah -
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamir, who said:
m: There was an idol on al-Safa called Isaf, and an idol on al-Marwah called Na’ilah. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Shawarib - and added to it, he said: He mentioned al-Safa because of the idol that was on it, and he made al-Marwah feminine because the idol that was on it was feminine 1.

c: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha’bi,
m: and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Abi al-Shawarib, on the authority of Yazid, and added to it - he said: So God made it a voluntary act of goodness.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said: Ibn Abi Za’idah told us, he said: Asim al-Ahwal told me, he said:
m: I said to Anas ibn Malik: Did you dislike circumambulating between al-Safa and al-Marwah until this verse was revealed? He said: Yes, we disliked circumambulating between them because they were among the rituals of the Age of Ignorance, until this verse was revealed: Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of God.

c: Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told me, Muammil bin Ismail told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, who said:
m: I asked Anas about Safa and Marwa, and he said: They were among the rituals of the Jahiliyyah, but when Islam came, they stopped visiting them, so this verse was revealed: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God.

c: Abdul-Warith bin Abdul-Samad bin Abdul-Warith told me, Al-Hussein al-Mu’allim told me, Shaiban Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Jabir al-Ja’fi, on the authority of Amr bin Habshi, who said:
m: I said to Ibn Umar: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God,
h
so whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them

. He said: Go to Ibn Abbas and ask him, for he is the most knowledgeable of those who remain about what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So I went to him and asked him, and he said: They had idols with them, but when they entered ihram, they stopped walking between them, until this verse was revealed: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God,
h
so whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God, that is because some people were reluctant to circumambulate between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, so God informed us that they are among His symbols, and circumambulating between them is more beloved to Him, so the Sunnah was to circumambulate between them.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for circumambulating them

,” he said: Abu Malik claimed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That in the pre-Islamic era there were devils who played music at night between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and there were gods between them. When Islam came and appeared, the Muslims said: O Messenger of God, we do not circumambulate between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, because it is polytheism that we used to do in the pre-Islamic era! So God revealed:
h
There is no blame upon him for circumambulating them

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God, he said: The Ansar said: Running between these two stones is a matter of the Age of Ignorance! So God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
There is no blame upon him if he walks between them

, he said: The people of ignorance had placed an idol on each of them which they venerated, and when the Muslims converted to Islam, they disliked walking between Safa and Marwah because of the two idols, so God the Most High said: “Indeed, Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of God.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs ‘Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them

,” and he recited: And whoever honors the symbols of God - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts (al-Hajj 22:32) and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made it a Sunnah to walk between them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Asim, he said,
m: I said to Anas: Safa and Marwah, Did you hate to walk around them with the idols that you were forbidden to walk around? He said: Yes, until the verse was revealed: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, he said: Asim narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard Anas bin Malik say: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah were among the symbols of Quraysh in the pre-Islamic era, but when Islam came, we abandoned them.

x: Others said: Rather, God revealed this verse, because of a people who in the pre-Islamic era did not walk between them, but when Islam came, they feared walking between them as they feared it in the pre-Islamic era.
Those who said that: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said:

c: Yazid narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:158 Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah -
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them
h
And whoever volunteers good - then indeed
