, Allah is appreciative and Knowing. God the verse, so there was a tribe from Tihamah in the pre-Islamic era who did not walk between them, so God informed them that As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. It was the Sunnah of Abraham and Ishmael to walk around between them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: There were some people from Tihamah who did not circumambulate between Safa and Marwa, so God revealed: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Abdullah bin Salih told us, Al-Layth told me, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Urwah bin Az-Zubayr told me,
m: I asked Aisha and said to her: What do you think of the statement of God: “Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them

”? And I said to Aisha: By God, there is no blame upon anyone for not walking between Safa and Marwa! Aisha said: What a bad thing you have said, O son of my sister! If this verse had been as I interpreted it, it would have been: There is no blame on him if he does not circumambulate them. However, it was revealed about the Ansar: Before they converted to Islam, they used to perform the ritual of Ihram for Manat, the tyrant that they worshipped in Al-Mushallal. Some of its people were reluctant to circumambulate between Safa and Marwa. So when they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that - and they said: O Messenger of God, we were reluctant to circumambulate between Safa and Marwa - God Almighty revealed: “Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for circumambulating them
.” Aisha said: Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) established the practice of circumambulating between them, so no one should neglect circumambulating between them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: There were men from the Ansar who used to perform the ritual prayer for Manat in the pre-Islamic era - and Manat was an idol between Mecca and Medina - they said: O Prophet of God, we did not circumambulate between Safa and Marwah out of reverence for Manat, so is there any blame upon us if we circumambulated between them? Then God the Most High revealed: “Indeed, Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of God.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them
.” Urwah said: I said to Aisha: I do not care if I do not circumambulate between Safa and Marwah! God said:
h
There is no blame upon him

. She said: O son of my sister, do you not see that he says: Indeed, Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of God! Al-Zuhri said: I mentioned that to Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham and he said: This is knowledge! Abu Bakr said: I heard some scholars say: When God revealed the circumambulation of the House but did not reveal the circumambulation between Safa and Marwa, it was said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): We used to circumambulate between Safa and Marwa in the pre-Islamic era, and God mentioned the circumambulation of the House but did not mention the circumambulation between Safa and Marwa, so is there any blame on us if we do not circumambulate them? So God revealed: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God the entire verse. Abu Bakr said: I hear that this verse was revealed regarding both groups, those who circumambulated and those who did not.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abdul Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: There were some people from Tihamah who did not circumambulate between Safa and Marwa, so God revealed: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Most High, has made circumambulating between Safa and Marwah one of the rites of God, just as He has made circumambulating the House one of His rites. As for His statement:
h
There is no blame upon him for circumambulating them

, it is permissible that it was said to both groups, some of whom feared circumambulating them because of the two idols mentioned by Al-Shaʿbi, and some of them because of what they hated about circumambulating them in the pre-Islamic era, according to what was narrated from Aisha. Whichever of the two matters it was, there is no indication in God’s statement:
h
There is no blame upon him for circumambulating them

, the verse, that He meant by it to remove hardship from the one who circumambulated them, most obviously because circumambulating them was not permissible because God had prohibited it, then He made circumambulating them a concession, due to the consensus of all that God, the Most High, did not prohibit it at any time, then He permitted it by His statement:
h
There is no blame upon him for circumambulating them

Rather, There are several differences of opinion among scholars on this matter: Some of them are of the view that the one who abandons the Tawaf between them abandons some of the rituals of his Hajj, and nothing of it is sufficient for him except to make up for it in particular, just as the one who abandons the Tawaf - which is the Tawaf of Ifadah - is not sufficient for him except to make up for it in particular. They said: They are two Tawafs: God has commanded one of them to be around the House, and the other between Safa and Marwa.

Some of them saw that the one who neglects to circumambulate them is compensated for by a ransom, and they saw that the ruling on circumambulating them is the ruling on throwing some of the pebbles, standing at the sacred site, circumambulating the chest, and the like, which the one who neglects them is compensated for by a ransom, and he is not obligated to return to perform it in the same way.
Others saw that circumambulating them is voluntary, and if its owner does it, he is doing good, but if someone neglects it, he is not obligated. By leaving something.
It was mentioned that those who said that walking between Safa and Marwa is obligatory, and that no ransom is sufficient for it, and whoever leaves it must return:

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: By my life, he who does not walk between Safa and Marwa has not performed Hajj, because God said: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God.

c: Yunus narrated to me, he said, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said, Malik bin Anas said:
m: Whoever forgets to walk between Safa and Marwa until he is far from Makkah, let him go back and walk, and if he has had intercourse with women, then he must perform Umrah and offer a sacrifice. Al-Shafi’i used to say: Whoever leaves walking between Safa and Marwa until he returns to his country, must return to Makkah and circumambulate between them, and nothing else is sufficient for him. Qatada narrated this to us on his authority. It was mentioned that those who said: A blood sacrifice is sufficient for it, and he does not have to return to make it up. Al-Thawri said: Ali bin Sahl narrated to me, on the authority of Zaid bin Abi Al-Zarqa, on his authority, and Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad: If the one who left the circumambulation between them returns to make up for it, then that is good, but if he does not return, then he must offer a blood sacrifice. He mentioned those who said: The circumambulation between them is voluntary, and there is nothing on the one who left it, and whoever used to recite:
h
There is no blame upon him

if he does not circumambulate them. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, Abu Asim narrated, Ibn Jurayj narrated, Ata’ said: If a pilgrim performs the Ifadah after throwing the pebbles at the Jamrat al-Aqabah, and circumambulates the House without performing the Sa’i, and has intercourse with her - meaning his wife - then there is nothing wrong with him, neither Hajj nor ‘Umrah, because of the statement of God in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas’ud:
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs ‘Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him

for not walking between them. So I went back to him after that and said: He has abandoned the Sunnah of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Do you not hear him say: So whoever volunteers good, and he refused to impose anything on him? Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim narrated, Hisham narrated, ‘Abd al-Malik informed us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas that he used to recite: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God the verse So
h
there is no blame upon him
for not walking between them.

c: Ali ibn Sahl told me, Muammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, who said:
m: I heard Anas say: Circumambulating between them is voluntary.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, Asim al-Ahwal told us, Anas ibn Malik said:
m: They are voluntary.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, Abu Asim told us, Isa told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them
.” He said: So there is no blame on one who does not walk between them.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Hajjaj told us, Ahmad told us, on the authority of Isa ibn Qays, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr, who said:
m: They are voluntary. Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated that Asim said: I said to Anas ibn Malik: Is walking between Safa and Marwa voluntary? He said: It is voluntary. The correct statement in our view is that circumambulating them is an obligatory duty, and that whoever leaves it out must return to make it up, whether he forgot or did so intentionally. Because nothing else will suffice, as there are many reports from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he performed Hajj with the people, and that one of the rituals of their Hajj that he taught them was circumambulating them. The narration from him about that is:

c: Yusuf ibn Sulayman narrated to me, Hatim ibn Ismail narrated to us, Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Jabir, who said:
m: “When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) approached Safa during his Hajj, he said: ‘Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God.’ Begin with what God began with mentioning. So he began with Safa and ascended it.”

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Mahmoud bin Maimun Abu Al-Hasan narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, on the authority of Ibn Ata’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. So he came to Safa and began with them, and stood on them, then he came to Marwa and stood on them, and performed Tawaf and Sa’i. So since it is correct, by consensus of all of the nation, that circumambulating them is based on the teaching of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to his nation in their rituals, and his actions in his Hajj and Umrah, and his explanation, may God bless him and grant him peace, to his nation was the summary of what God has stated in His Book, and imposed in His revelation, and commanded of what his knowledge could not attain except through his explanation, and his nation must act upon it, as we have explained in our book, The Book of Explanation of the Fundamentals of Rulings, if the nation differed about its obligation, then there was a difference in circumambulating between them: is it obligatory or not obligatory, it is clear that it is obligatory to make it obligatory for whoever has performed Hajj or Umrah, for what we have described. And likewise the obligation of returning to make up for it. Circumambulating between Safa and Marwa - since there was a difference of opinion regarding what is upon the one who left it, with all of them agreeing that it is something that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did and taught his nation in their Hajj and Umrah, as he taught them the rituals of their Hajj - just as he circumambulated the House and taught his nation in their Hajj and Umrah, as he taught them the rituals of their Hajj and Umrah - and all of them agreed that circumambulating the House does not require a ransom or compensation, and the one who left it does not require anything Surat Al-Baqarah 2:158 Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs Umrah -
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them
h
And whoever volunteers good - then indeed

, Allah is appreciative and Knowing. except returning to make it up, then similar to it is circumambulating between Safa and Marwa, and neither ransom nor compensation is acceptable for it, and the one who left it does not require anything except returning to make it up, since they were both two circumambulations: one of the House, and the other of Safa and Marwa. And whoever differentiates between their rulings, the statement is reversed against him, then he is asked for proof of the difference between them. If he is excused by the reading of the one who recites:
h
There is no blame upon him

if he does not circumambulate them both, it is said: This is contrary to what is in the copies of the Qur’an of the Muslims, and it is not permissible for anyone to add to their copies of the Qur’an what is not in them. It is the same whether a reciter recites it like this, or a reciter recites: Then let them complete their untidiness and fulfill their vows and perform Tawaf around the Ancient House (al-Hajj 22:29) There is no blame upon them if they do not circumambulate it. If one of the two additions that are not in the Qur’an is permissible, then the other is its equivalent, otherwise the one who permits one of them - while forbidding the other - is controlling, and no one is incapable of controlling. It has been narrated that Aisha denied this reading and that it was revealed according to it.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Malik ibn Anas told me,
m: “On the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said: I said to Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was young at that time: What do you think of the statement of God Almighty: ‘Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs ‘Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them
,’? We do not see anything wrong with anyone not walking between them! Aisha said: No! If it were as you say, it would be: ‘
h
There is no blame upon him

for not walking between them.’ This verse was revealed about the Ansar. They used to enter ihram for Manat - and Manat was near Qudayd - and they were reluctant to walk between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. When Islam came, they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and God revealed: ‘Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God.
h
So whoever makes Hajj to the House
or performs ‘Umrah,
h
there is no blame upon him for walking between them

x: It may be possible that the reading of the one who reads:
h
There is no blame upon him
if he does not go around them is that the la that is with an is a connection in the speech, since it was preceded by a denial in the speech before it, which is His saying:
h
There is no blame upon him
, so it is similar to the saying of God Almighty: “He said: What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?”

i: r
(Al-Aʿraf: 12)
meaning what prevented you from prostrating, and as the poet said:
x: The Messenger of God would not have been pleased with their actions, nor were the two righteous men, Abu Bakr and Umar.

If the script of the Mushaf had been like this, there would have been no argument for the protester in it, given the possibility of the statement we have described. Since we have shown that this is something that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught his nation in their rituals, as we have mentioned, and because analogy indicates its correctness, how is it that it is contrary to the scripts of the Mushafs of the Muslims, and if a reader were to read it today, he would deserve punishment, for adding to the Book of God, the Almighty, what is not from it?
The statement in the interpretation of the words of God, the Almighty?
h
And whoever volunteers good - then indeed
, God is appreciative and Knowing.

The reciters differed in the recitation of this, so most of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it: And whoever volunteers good in the form of the past tense with the ta’ and the fatha on the ‘ayn. Most of the reciters of Kufa recited it: And whoever volunteers good - the ya’ and the jazm of the ‘ayn and the shaddah on the ta’, meaning: and whoever volunteers. He mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah: And whoever volunteers, so the readers of Kufa read that, as we have described, considering what we mentioned from the reading of Abdullah - except for Asim, as he agreed with the Medinans - so they stressed the taa' in order to assimilate the taa' into the taa'. Both readings are known to be correct, and their meanings are in agreement and not different - because the past tense of the verb with the letters of reward has the meaning of the future. So whichever reading a reader reads that with, he is correct. [And the correct view in this regard is that] the meaning of this is: And whoever volunteers to perform Hajj and Umrah after completing his obligatory Hajj, then God will be grateful to him for his volunteering to Him with what he volunteered to do of that seeking His pleasure, so He will reward him for it, knowing what he intended and wanted with his volunteering with what he volunteered.
And we said that the correct meaning of His statement:
h
So whoever volunteers good is what we have described

, without the statement of those who claimed that it is meant by it: So whoever volunteers to perform Sa’i and Tawaf between Safa and Marwah, because the one who performs Sa’i between them is not volunteering to perform Sa’i between them, except in a voluntary Hajj or a voluntary Umrah, for what we have described before. And since that is the case, it is known that what he meant by volunteering with that is volunteering with what he does in it of Hajj or Umrah. As for those who claimed that circumambulating them is voluntary and not obligatory, the correct interpretation of that is according to their statement: Whoever volunteers to circumambulate them, then God is grateful - because the pilgrim and the performer of Umrah, according to their statement, can circumambulate them if he wishes, and leave the circumambulation.

So the meaning of the statement according to their interpretation is: Whoever volunteers to circumambulate Safa and Marwah, then God is grateful for his volunteering that - He knows what the one who circumambulates them intended and intended as well, as Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And whoever volunteers good, then God is grateful and Knowing. He said: Whoever volunteers good, then it is better for him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, volunteered, so it was from the Sunnah.
Others said: The meaning of that is: Whoever volunteers good and performs Umrah.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And whoever volunteers good - then indeed

, God is appreciative and Knowing, whoever volunteers good and performs Umrah - then indeed, God is appreciative and Knowing. He said: So Hajj is an obligation, and Umrah is voluntary. Umrah is not obligatory upon any of the people.

evidence.text: If he is excused by the reading of the one who recites: There is no blame upon him if he does not circumambulate them both, it is said: This is contrary to what is in the copies of the Qur’an of the Muslims, and it is not permissible for anyone to add to their copies of the Qur’an what is not in them.

It is the same whether a reciter recites it like this, or a reciter recites: Then let them complete their untidiness and fulfill their vows and perform Tawaf around the Ancient House (al-Hajj 22:29) There is no blame upon them if they do not circumambulate it.
It has been narrated that Aisha denied this reading and that it was revealed according to it.

Abu Jaʿfar said: It may be possible that the reading of the one who reads: There is no blame upon him if he does not go around them is that the la that is with an is a connection in the speech, since it was preceded by a denial in the speech before it, which is His saying: There is no blame upon him, so it is similar to the saying of God Almighty: “He said: What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?”

Since we have shown that this is something that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught his nation in their rituals, as we have mentioned, and because analogy indicates its correctness, how is it that it is contrary to the scripts of the Mushafs of the Muslims, and if a reader were to read it today, he would deserve punishment, for adding to the Book of God, the Almighty, what is not from it?

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reciters differed in the recitation of this, so most of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it: And whoever volunteers good in the form of the past tense with the ta’ and the fatha on the ‘ayn.
Most of the reciters of Kufa recited it: And whoever volunteers good - the ya’ and the jazm of the ‘ayn and the shaddah on the ta’, meaning: and whoever volunteers.

He mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah: And whoever volunteers, so the readers of Kufa read that, as we have described, considering what we mentioned from the reading of Abdullah - except for Asim, as he agreed with the Medinans - so they stressed the taa' in order to assimilate the taa' into the taa'.
So whichever reading a reader reads that with, he is correct.

x: What he means by his saying: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs, are the Jewish scholars and rabbis, and the Christian scholars, because they concealed the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the people, and they left his followers, even though they found it written in their Torah and Gospel. And the clear proofs that God sent down: what He explained of the matter of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his mission, and his description, in the two books in which God, the Most High, said that their people would find his description. And the Most High means by guidance what He made clear to them of His command in the books that He sent down to His prophets. So the Most High said: “Those who conceal from the people what We sent down in their books of the clarification of the command of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prophethood, and the correctness and truth of the religion with which I sent him, and do not inform them of it, nor do they announce it after I have made it clear to the people and explained it to them, in the book that I sent down to their prophets, ‘Those are cursed by God
h
and cursed by those who curse
, except for those who repent’” verse.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us
m: - and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us - they both said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the freed slave of Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to me, Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated to me, or ʿIkrimah narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, saying: Muʿadh ibn Jabal, the brother of Banu Salamah, and Saʿd ibn Muʿadh, the brother of Banu ʿAbd al-Ashhal, and Kharijah ibn Zayd, the brother of Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, asked a group of Jewish rabbis - Abu Kurayb said: about what was in the Torah, and Ibn Humayd said: about some of what was in the Torah - and they concealed it from them and refused to tell them about it, so God Almighty revealed about them: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear to the people in the Scripture - those are cursed by God
h
and cursed by those who curse

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance, he said: They are the People of the Book.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God, Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance, he said: They concealed Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though they found it written down with them, so they concealed it out of envy and malice.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear to the people in the Scripture, those are the People of the Scripture. They concealed Islam, which is the religion of God, and they concealed Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, although they found him written with them in the Torah and the Gospel.

c: Musa narrated to me, he said, Amr narrated to us, he said, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear to the people in the Scripture, they claimed that a Jewish man had a friend from the Ansar called Tha’laba bin Ghanima. He said to him: Do you find Muhammad with you? He said: No! He said: Muhammad: Clear proofs.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty: After We made it clear to the people in the Book.
[Abu Jaʿfar said: God Almighty meant by His words:
h
After We made it clear to the people]

, some people, because knowledge of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and his mission was only with the People of the Book and not others, and God Almighty meant them by His words:
h
For the people in the Book

, meaning: the Torah and the Gospel. And although this verse was revealed for a specific group of people, it is intended for everyone who conceals knowledge that God Almighty has commanded to be made clear to the people. This is similar to the report that "It was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever is asked about knowledge that he knows and conceals it, will be bridled on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire."
And Abu Hurairah used to say what:

c: Nasr bin Ali al-Jahdhami told us, he said, Hatim bin Wardan told us, he said, Ayoub al-Sakhtiyani told us, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: If it were not for a verse from the Book of God, I would not have told you! And he recited: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear for the people in the Scripture - those are cursed by God
h
and cursed by those who curse

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me, he said, Abu Zur’ah Wahb God ibn Rashid told us, on the authority of Yunus, he said,
m: Ibn Shihab said, Ibn al-Musayyab said: Abu Hurayrah said: If it were not for two verses that God sent down in His Book, I would not have narrated anything: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs to the end of the verse, and the other verse: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture to make it clear to the people to the end of the verse
r
(Al Imran 3:178)

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Those are the ones cursed by God
h
and cursed by those who curse
What the Almighty means by His saying:
h
Those are the ones cursed by God is those who conceal what God revealed about Muhammad

, may God bless him and grant him peace, his description and the matter of his religion, that it is the truth - after God had made it clear to them in their books - He curses them for concealing it and not explaining it to the people. And the curse is the action, from God cursed him, meaning He banished him, removed him, and crushed him. The root of the curse is expulsion, as Al-Shamakh bin Dirar said, and he mentioned Ma’ and responded to him: The quail was terrified by him and I denied him the status of a wolf like a cursed man Meaning: the position of the chased wolf. The cursed is an adjective for the wolf, but what he meant is: the position of the chased, cursed wolf like a man. So the meaning of the verse is: God distances them from Him and from His mercy, and their Lord asks the cursers to curse them, because the curse of the children of Adam and the rest of God’s creation is that they say: O God, curse him, since the meaning of the curse is what we described of exclusion and banishment.
We said that the curse of the cursers is what we described: their asking their Lord to curse them, and their saying: May God curse him or upon him be the curse of God, because:

c: Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, they said, Ismail bin Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Those are the ones whom God curses and the ones who curse curse them, the animals, he said: When the yearning becomes old, the animals say: This is because of the sinners of the children of Adam, may God curse the sinners of the children of Adam! Then the people of interpretation differed about whom God Almighty meant by the ones who curse.

x: Some of them said: He meant by that the beasts of the earth and its vermin.

Those who said that: Muhammad bin Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The beasts of the earth curse them, and whatever God wills of beetles and scorpions, they say: We withhold rain because of their sins.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Those are the ones whom God curses and those who curse curse them
, he said: The beasts of the earth, scorpions and beetles, they say: We withheld rain because of the sins of the children of Adam.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And those who curse curse them, he said: The vermin and beasts of the earth curse them, they say: We withheld rain because of the sins of the children of Adam.

c: Mushrif bin Abaan al-Hattāb al-Baghdadi told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasīf, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Those are the ones whom God curses and those who curse curse them
, he said: Everything curses them, even beetles and scorpions, they say: We withheld rain because of the sins of the children of Adam.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And the cursers curse them
, he said: The cursers are the animals.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And the cursers curse them
, the animals curse the sinners of the children of Adam when God withheld rain from them because of the sins of the children of Adam, so the animals come out and curse them.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Muslim ibn Khalid told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement, Those are the ones cursed by God and cursed by the cursers, the animals are camels, cows, and sheep, so the sinners of the children of Adam are cursed when the land becomes barren.

x: What is the reason for those who interpreted His statement:
h
And the cursers curse them

, to the point that the cursers are beetles, scorpions, and similar creatures of the earth, and you know that when they pluralize what is of the type of beasts and other than the sons of Adam, they pluralize it without the ya’ and the noon and without the waw and the noon, and they pluralize it with the ta’ and what contradicts what we mentioned, so they say: the cursers and the like?

Even if the matter is like that, then it is the custom of the Arabs when they describe something from the beasts or other than them - whose plural is ruled to be - the ta’ and without the form of the plural of the males of the sons of Adam - with what is from the description of humans, they pluralize it with the plural of their males, as the Most High said: And they said to their skins, ‘Why did you bear witness against us?’
r
(Fussilat 41:21)

, so He brought out their address on the example of the address of the sons of Adam, since it spoke to them and they spoke to it, and as He said: O ants, enter your dwellings (al-Naml 27:18) and as He said:
And the sun and the moon, I saw them prostrating to me
Others said: God the Most High meant by His saying:
h
And cursed by those who curse
, the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:159 Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear to the people in the Scripture - those are cursed by Allah
h
and cursed by those who curse
. angels and the believers.
Those who said that: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said:

c: Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And cursed by those who curse
, he said: He says: The cursers are from the angels of God and the believers.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His saying:
h
And cursed by those who curse
, the angels.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’ bin Ansaq, he said:
m: The cursers, are from the angels of God and the believers.

x: Others said: He means - the cursers, everyone except the children of Adam and the jinn.
Who said that: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
And the cursers curse them

, he said: Al-Bara’ bin Azib said: When the disbeliever is placed in his grave, a beast comes to him as if its eyes were two pots of copper, with an iron pole with it, and it strikes him with a blow that covers his shoulders, and he cries out, and no one hears his voice except that he curses him, and nothing remains except that he hears his voice, except for the two heavy things, the jinn and mankind.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Ishaq told us, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement: Those are the ones whom God curses and the cursers curse, he said: When the disbeliever is placed in his grave, he is struck with a hammer, and he cries out a cry, and everything hears his voice except for the two heavy things, the jinn and mankind, and nothing hears his cry except that he curses him.

x: The most correct of these sayings in our view is the saying of the one who said: The cursers are the angels and the believers. Because God, the Most High, has described the disbelievers as having a curse that comes upon them from God, the angels, and all of mankind. God, the Most High, has said: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - upon them is the curse of God and of the angels and of mankind, all together. Likewise, the curse that God, the Most High, has informed us will befall the other group: those who conceal what God has sent down of clear proofs and guidance after He has made it clear to mankind. It is the curse of God, and the curse of those whose curse He has informed us will befall those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers, and they are the cursers, because both groups are disbelievers. As for the saying of the one who said that the cursers are beetles, scorpions, and similar creeping things and insects on the earth, then it is a saying whose true nature cannot be understood except by a report from God that this is from their actions, upon which proof is established.

There is no report of this from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it is permissible to say that it is so. Since this is so, the correct statement regarding what they said is that the evidence from the apparent meaning of the Book of God is present, contrary to the statement of the people of interpretation, which is what we have described. If it is permissible for the beasts and all of God’s creation to curse those who conceal what God has revealed in His Book about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prophethood, after they have learned about it, and to curse all the oppressors with them, then it is not permissible to conclusively testify that God meant by those who curse the beasts, the vermin, and the creeping things of the earth, except with a conclusive report of an excuse. There is no report of this, and the apparent meaning of the Book of God that we have mentioned indicates the opposite.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “
h
Except for those who repent
, amend, and declare.
Those, I will turn to them in forgiveness, and I am the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.”

The Almighty means by that: that God and the cursers curse those who conceal from people what they know of The matter of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his description and attributes in the Book that God revealed and made clear to the people,
h
except for those who repent

from concealing it from them? And review repentance by believing in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and acknowledging him and his prophethood and believing in what he brought from God, and explaining what God revealed in His books that He sent down to His prophets, of the command to follow him? And improve his condition by drawing closer to God through righteous deeds that please Him? And between the one who knew the revelation of God that He sent down to His prophets and entrusted them with in His books and did not conceal it, and revealed it and did not hide it, those, meaning: those who did what I described from them, are those whom I accept their repentance, so I make them among the people of returning to My obedience and repentance to My pleasure.

Then He, the Most High, said: And I am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful. He says: I am the One who returns the hearts of My servants that have turned away from Me to Me, and I return them after their turning away from My obedience to seeking My love, and I am the Merciful to those who turn to Me after their turning to Me. I cover them with My pardon, and I overlook the greatness of what they committed between Me and them, by virtue of My mercy towards them.
How can someone who repents be repented to? What is the meaning of His statement:
h
Except for those who repent
, amend, and declare [the truth], for those I will turn to? Can someone who repents not be repented to, or someone who is turned to be repentant not be repentant?
This is something that neither of them can be without the other, so it is the same whether it is said: Except for those who have been turned to and repented - or it is said:
h
Except for those who repent

, for I will turn to them. We have already explained the meaning of this statement in what came before, in a similar context in our book, so we disliked repeating it in this place. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement:
h
Except those who repent

, amend and declare, he said: They amended what was between them and God, and declared what came to them from God, and did not conceal it or deny it. Those, I will accept their repentance, and I am the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Except those who repent

, amend and declare, he said: They declared what was in God’s Book for the believers, and what they asked them about regarding the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And all of this is about the Jews.

x: Some of them have claimed that the meaning of His statement: And declare, is: And declare repentance by sincere action. And the evidence of the apparent meaning of the Book and the revelation is to the contrary. Because the people were only rebuked before this verse for concealing what God the Most High had revealed and made clear in His Book, regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his religion. Then God the Most High excepted from them those who would clarify the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his religion, and repent for their denial and concealment, so He excluded them from the number of those whom God and those who curse curse, and the rebuke was not for their failure to clarify their repentance with sincerity of action. And those whom God excepted from those who conceal what God had revealed of clear proofs and guidance after He had made it clear to the people in the Book were Abdullah bin Salam and his family from the People of the Book, who converted to Islam and their Islam was good, and they followed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
The statement on the interpretation of the Almighty's saying: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers -
h
upon them is the curse of God
and of the angels and of mankind, all together.

What God, the Exalted, meant by His saying: Indeed, those who disbelieved is those who denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and belied him - from the Jews, Christians, and all the people of the religions, and the polytheists who worship idols - and died while they were disbelievers, meaning: and they died while they were denying that and belying Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace,
h
upon them is the curse of God
and of the angels, meaning: so those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers,
h
upon them is the curse of God

, meaning: God distanced them and crushed them from His mercy, and of the angels, meaning: and the angels and mankind cursed them, all together. And the curse of the angels and mankind upon them is their saying:
h
upon them is the curse of God
. We have already explained the meaning of the curse in what came before, so there is no need to repeat it.
How can the curse of all people be upon the one who dies as a disbeliever in Muhammad (peace be upon him) from among the various nations, most of whom do not believe in him or acknowledge him?
The meaning of that is contrary to what he has gone to.
The people of interpretation have differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said: God meant by His saying: and all people, the people of faith in Him and His Messenger in particular, without the rest of humanity.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said: Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His saying: and all people, he means – all al-Nas 114:the believers.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatadah:
m: and all people, he means by all al-Nas 114:the believers.

x: Others said: Rather, that will be on the Day of Resurrection, when the disbeliever will be made to stand before the witnesses and all the people will curse him.
Mention of those who said that:

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah: The disbeliever will be brought to a halt on the Day of Resurrection, and God will curse him, then the angels will curse him, then all the people will curse him.

x: Others said: Rather, that is the saying of the one who says, whoever he may be: God curses the oppressor, and that includes every disbeliever, because he is one of the oppressors.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me,
m: who said: Amr bin Hammad told us, who said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi. His saying:
h
Upon them is the curse of God

, the angels, and all of mankind, for two believers and unbelievers do not curse each other, and one of them says: God cursed the oppressor, except that the curse is incumbent upon the unbeliever, because he is an oppressor, so everyone among creation curses him.

x: The most correct of these sayings in our view is the saying of the one who said: God meant by that all people, meaning that He cursed them by their saying: God cursed the oppressor - or the oppressors. For every one of the sons of Adam is not prevented from saying that, whoever he is, and whatever his religion, so every unbeliever is included in His curse, whoever he is. And that is in the meaning of what Abu al-ʿAliyah said. Because God the Most High informed about those who witness them on the Day of Resurrection that they will curse them, saying:

“And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God? Those will be brought before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, ‘These are the ones who lied against their Lord.’ Unquestionably, the curse of God will be upon the wrongdoers.”
As for what Qatada said, that he meant some people, the apparent meaning of the revelation is contrary to it, and there is no proof of its reality from report or consideration.

If it was thought that what was meant by it were the believers, because the disbelievers do not curse themselves or their allies, then God the Most High informed that they will curse them in the Hereafter. It is known that they curse the oppressors, and every disbeliever is included in the oppression, due to his oppression of himself, his denial of the blessing of his Lord, and his disobedience to His command.
The statement on the interpretation of the words of God Almighty: They will abide therein, their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be reprieved.

If someone were to say to us: What is the reason for the accusative of they will abide therein? It would be said: It is accusative as a state of the ha' and mim in upon them. That is because the meaning of His words:
h
Upon them is the curse of God
, those are cursed by God, the angels, and all of mankind, abiding therein. That is why whoever reads it like that reads it:
h
Upon them is the curse of God

, the angels, and all of mankind, as a directive to the meaning that I have described. That is because it was permissible in Arabic, so it is not permissible to read it, because it is contrary to the copies of the Muslims' Qur'an, and what the Muslims came with in terms of reading is widespread among them. It is not permissible to object to an anomalous statement, as its proof has been established by extensive transmission. As for the ha’ and the alif in his statement: in it, they refer to the curse, and what is meant by the statement is: what the disbeliever has come to through the curse from God, His angels, and the people.
And what he has come to through it is the fire of Hell.
And he spoke about the curse, and what is meant by it is what the disbeliever has become, as we have explained from similar examples in what has passed before, as:

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah, abiding therein eternally, he says: abiding in Hell, in the curse. As for his statement: The punishment will not be lightened for them, it is report from God Almighty about the continuity of the punishment forever, without a time limit or lightening, as God Almighty said: “And those who disbelieve will have the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed for them to die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them”
r
(Fatir 35:36)
, and as He said: Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins
r
(An-Nisa’: 56)
. As for his statement: nor will they be reprieved, it means: nor will they be reprieved with an excuse to apologize, as:

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah: nor will they be reprieved, meaning: they will not be reprieved so that they can make an excuse, like His statement: This is a Day on which they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make an excuse (al-Mursalat 77:35-36).

evidence.text: That is why whoever reads it like that reads it: Upon them is the curse of God, the angels, and all of mankind, as a directive to the meaning that I have described.

That is because it was permissible in Arabic, so it is not permissible to read it, because it is contrary to the copies of the Muslims' Qur'an, and what the Muslims came with in terms of reading is widespread among them.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of the Almighty:
h
And your God is one God
h
there is no god but He
, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
We have previously explained the meaning of divinity, and that it is the worship of creation. So the meaning of His words:
h
And your God is one God
h
there is no god but He

, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful: The One who deserves obedience from you, O people, and requires worship from you, is one deity and one Lord, so do not worship other than Him, and do not associate anyone with Him, for the one you associate with Him in your worship of Him is a creation of your God, like you,
h
and your God is one God
, He has no likeness or peer. And there is disagreement regarding the meaning of His Oneness, may He be exalted.

Some of them said: The meaning of the Oneness of God is the meaning of negating similarities and likenesses from Him, as it is said: So-and-so is one of the people - and he is one of his people, meaning by that that he has no likeness among the people, nor does he have a likeness or peer among his people. Likewise, the meaning of the statement God is One is that God has no equal or peer. They claimed that what indicated to them the correctness of their interpretation was that the statement of the speaker One can be understood to mean four things. One of them is that it is one of a kind, like a single human being. The second is that it is not separated, like a part that is not divided. The third is that it means likeness and agreement, like the statement of the speaker: These two things are one, meaning that they are similar, so that they became like one thing due to their similarity in meanings.

The fourth is that it means negating the likeness and similarity from Him. They said: Since the three meanings of the meanings of One are negated from Him, the fourth meaning that we described is correct.

Others said: The meaning of His Oneness, may He be exalted, is the meaning of His being alone from things, and the things being alone from Him. They said: He is only alone because He is not included in anything, nor is anything included in Him. They said: There is no validity in the statement of the speaker: One from all things except that. The proponents of this statement denied the four meanings stated by the others. As for His saying:
h
There is no god but He

, it is report from Him, the Most High, that there is no Lord of the worlds other than Him, and that He does not require the servants to worship anyone other than Him, and that everything other than Him is His creation, and it is obligatory upon all of them to obey Him and submit to His command, and to abandon the worship of anything other than Him of rivals and gods, and to abandon idols and statues. Because all of that is His creation, and upon all of them is the judgment of Him with His Oneness and Divinity, and divinity is not appropriate except for Him, since whatever blessings they have in this world are from Him, unlike what they worship of idols and associate with Him of association?

And whatever blessings they will attain in the Hereafter are from Him, and that what they associate with Him of association does not harm or benefit in the immediate or the deferred, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. This is a warning from God, the Most High, to the polytheists regarding their misguidance, and a call from Him for them to return from their disbelief and turn from their polytheism. Then the Almighty made them aware of His mention in the verse that follows it, the place where the wise among them would prove the truth of what He alerted them to regarding His Oneness and His clear arguments that cut off their excuse. So the Almighty said: O polytheists, if you are ignorant or doubt the truth of what I have informed you of al-Naba 78:that your God is one God, without what you claim as His divinity of rivals and idols, then ponder My arguments and think about them, for among My arguments is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, and the ships that sail in the sea with what benefits people, and what I sent down from the sky of water by which I revived the earth after its death, and what I spread in it of every creature, and the clouds that I have subjected between the sky and the earth.

If what you worship of idols, gods, rivals, and all that you associate with Him, if it all comes together and appears or some of it is isolated without others, is able to create the like of something of My creation that I have named for you, then you have an excuse for your worship of what you worship besides Me. Otherwise, you have no excuse for taking a god other than Me, and there is no god for you and for what you worship other than Me. So let those with understanding ponder the brevity of God’s argument against all the people of disbelief in Him and the atheists in His Oneness, in this verse and the one after it, with the most concise speech, the most eloquent argument, and the most subtle meaning that will lead them to know the excellence of God’s wisdom and His explanation.
The statement on the meaning for which God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, His saying: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth
h
and the alternation of the night and the day
the verse.
The people of interpretation differed on the reason for which God, the Most High, revealed this verse to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Some of them said: He revealed it to him as an argument for him against the polytheists who worshipped idols. That is because when God, the Most High, revealed to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, "And your God is one God. There is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," he recited that to his companions, and the polytheists who worshipped idols heard it. The polytheists said: What is the argument and proof that this is so, while we deny it, and we claim that we have many gods? So God revealed at that time: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, as an argument for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, against those who said what we mentioned about them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: The verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina: And your God is one God; there is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The infidels of Quraysh in Mecca said: How can one God be enough for the people? So God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth
h
and the alternation of the night and the day
, until His saying: are signs for a people who reason. By this you know that He is one God, and that He is the God of all things, and the Creator of all things.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the polytheists asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a sign, so God revealed this verse, teaching them that in the creation of the heavens and the earth and all that was mentioned, they have a clear sign of the Oneness of God, and that He has no partner in His kingdom, for whoever understands and ponders that with correct understanding.

Those who said that: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, he said: When the verse, And your God is one God; there is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful was revealed, the polytheists said: If this is how it is, then let him bring us a sign! So God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth
h
and the alternation of the night and the day

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq ibn Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, he said, Saeed ibn Masruq told me, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, he said:
m: When the verse, And your God is one God; there is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful was revealed, the polytheists said: If this is how it is, then let him bring us a sign! So God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth
h
and the alternation of the night and the day

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, he said, Saʿid bin Masruq told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, he said:
m: When this verse was revealed, the polytheists were amazed and said: You say that your God is one God! Then bring us a sign, if you are of the truthful! So God revealed: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth
h
and the alternation of the night and the day
(al-Baqarah 2:17).

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ bin Abi Rabah
m: that the polytheists said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Show us a sign! So this verse was revealed: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth (al-Baqarah 2:17).

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yaʿqub Al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid, he said,
m: the Quraysh asked the Jews and said: Tell us about the signs that Moses brought to you!

c: So they told them
m: about the staff and his white hand for the onlookers. They asked the Christians about the signs that Jesus had brought them. They told them that he healed the blind and the lepers and brought the dead back to life by God’s permission. Then the Quraysh said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ask God to turn Safa into gold for us, so that we may increase our certainty and gain strength against our enemy. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked his Lord, and He revealed to him: I will give them, so turn Safa into gold for them, but if they lie, I will punish them with a punishment that I have not punished anyone in the worlds with. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave me and my people, so that I may call them day by day. Then God revealed to him: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth - the verse: Indeed in that is a sign for them, if they only want me to make for them Safa gold. So God created the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day, which is greater than that I make for them Safa gold, so that they may increase in certainty.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day - the polytheists said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Change Safa into gold for us, if you are truthful that it is from it! God said: Indeed in these signs are signs for a people who understand. And He said: People before you asked for signs, then they became disbelievers because of them.

x: The correct statement in that is that God, the Most High, reminded His servants - to the evidence of His Oneness and His uniqueness in divinity, without all other things - with this verse. It is possible that it was revealed in what Ata’ said, and it is possible that it was in what Saeed bin Jubair and Abu Ad-Dhaha said, and we do not have any report that the statement of one of the two groups is correct, which would cut off the excuse, so it is permissible for one of the two groups to rule that the statement of one of the two groups is correct over the other. Whichever of the two statements is correct, the meaning of the verse is what I said.

Statement on the interpretation of the words of God the Most High: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth Abu Ja’far said: God the Most High means by His words: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, that is, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and their origination.

The meaning of God’s creation of things is His origination and bringing them into existence after they did not exist. We have previously indicated the meaning for which it was said: the earth, and it was not gathered as the heavens were gathered, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: Do the heavens and the earth have a creation other than themselves, then it is said: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth?
There is a difference of opinion on that.

Some people said: They have a creation other than themselves. They based their argument on this verse and on what is in Surat al-Kahf 18:I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves (al-Kahf 18:1). They said: God did not create anything except that God wanted it. They said: So things were by the will of God, and the will created them.

Others said: The creation of a thing is an attribute of it, not it, nor is it other than it. They said: If it were other than it, it would be necessary for it to be described like it. They said: If it were possible for its creation to be other than it, and for it to be described, it would be necessary for it to have an attribute that is its creation. If that were necessary, there would be no end to that. They said: So it is known from that that it is an attribute of the thing. They said: So the creation of the heavens and the earth is an attribute of them, as we have described. They also based their argument on the Book of God - that the thing has a creation that is not it - in the same way that the first ones based their argument.

Others said: The creation of the heavens and the earth, and the creation of every creature, is that thing itself, not something else. So the meaning of His statement: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth is: Indeed, in the heavens and the earth.
The Almighty means by His saying:
h
And the alternation of the night and the day
, the succession of night and day upon you, O people.

i: The difference in this place is the causative, from each one Surat Al-Baqarah 2:164 Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth
h
and the alternation of the night and the day
h
and the ships that sail through the sea with that which benefits people

and what Allah sends down from the sky of water and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and disperses therein every kind of moving creature and the directing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the heaven and the earth are signs for a people who They understand succeeding the other, as the Almighty said:
x: And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires to be grateful. (al-Furqan 25:62).

Meaning: that each one of them succeeds the other, if the night goes, the day comes after it, and if the day goes, the night comes after it. From that it was said: So-and-so succeeded so-and-so in his family with evil, and from that is the saying of Zuhair: The spring and the Aram walk behind it, and its young ones rise from every perch. As for night, it is the plural of night, similar to date, which is the plural of date. It may also be pluralized as nights, and they add to the plural what was not in the singular. Their addition of the ya in that is similar to their addition of it in four-letter, eight-letter, and disliked letters. As for day, the Arabs hardly use it in the plural, because it is like light. It has been heard in its plural as river.

i: The poet said:
x: If it weren't for Tharidan, we would have perished from hunger.
Tharid at night and Tharid by the river. If it was said in a small group that it is rivers, it would be an analogy.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And the ships that sail through the sea with that which benefits people

The Almighty means: In the ships that sail through the sea. The ship is the ships, its singular and plural are the same word, and it is masculine and feminine, as the Almighty said in His masculine in another verse: And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship.
r

So He mentioned it. And He said in this verse: And the ships that sail through the sea, and it is a ship because when it sails, it is running, so the description is added to it that which is its. As for His saying:
h
With that which benefits people
, its meaning is: It benefits people in the sea.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And what God has sent down from the sky of water
, and revived thereby the earth after its lifelessness.
The Almighty means by His saying:
h
And what God has sent down from the sky of water
, and in what God has sent down From the sky from water, which is the rain that God sends down from the sky. And His saying:
h
And He revived thereby the earth after its death

, and reviving it is its cultivation and the production of its vegetation. The ha in bih refers to the water, and the ha and the alif in His saying: after its death refer to the earth. And the death of the earth is its devastation, and the disappearance of its cultivation, and the cessation of its vegetation, which is sustenance for the servants and provisions for the people.
The statement in the interpretation of the saying of the Most High:
h
And dispersed therein of every kind of creature
, Abu Jaʿfar said: The Most High meant by His saying:
h
And dispersed therein of every kind of creature
, and that among what He dispersed in the earth is a creature.

And the meaning of His saying: And dispersed therein, and the difference in it, from the saying of the one who says: The prince dispersed his troops, meaning: Differences. The ha and the alif in his saying: in it, refer back to the earth. And the beast, the agent, from the saying of the speaker: The beast crawled crawling, so it is a beast. And the beast, is the name for every living thing that is not a bird with wings, for its crawling on the earth.
Statement on the interpretation of the saying of God Almighty:
h
And the changing of the winds
Abu Jaʿfar said: God Almighty means by his saying:
h
And the changing of the winds
, and in his changing of the winds, so he omitted the mention of the agent and added the verb to the object, as you say: I like your honoring your brother, meaning: your honoring your brother.

God’s changing of it, is that He sends it once as a fertile woman, and once He makes it barren, and He sends it as a torment that destroys everything by the command of its Lord, as: Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And the changing of the winds and the clouds controlled

, he said: God, our Lord, is able to do that. If He wills, He makes it a mercy that fertilizes the clouds and spreads it before His mercy, and if He wills, He makes it a torment, a barren wind that does not fertilize. It is only a torment upon the one upon whom it is sent. Some Arabists claimed that the meaning of his statement:
h
And the changing of the winds is that they come sometimes south and north

, coming and going. Then he said: That is their changing. This description with which he described the winds is a description of their changing, not a description of their changing, because their changing is God’s changing of them, and their changing is the difference in their blowing.
It may be possible that the meaning of his statement:
h
And the changing of the winds is God’s changing of the blowing of the wind with its different winds
The statement in the interpretation of the statement of God Almighty: And the clouds controlled between the heaven and the earth are signs for a people who understand.

God Almighty meant by his statement: And the clouds controlled, and in clouds, the plural of cloud. This is indicated by the statement of the Most High: And He creates the heavy clouds (13:12). He made the subject singular and mentioned it, just as they said: This is a date and this is a large collection of dates, this is a palm tree and this is a palm tree. The clouds are called clouds, God willing, because some of them drag and pull others, like the saying of the speaker: So-and-so passed by dragging his tail, meaning: he dragged it. As for the meaning of His statement: for signs, then they are signs and indications that the Creator of that, His hand and its Originator, is one God. for a people who understand, for those who understand the places of the arguments and understand from God His evidence of His Oneness. So, the Most High informed His servants that the evidence and arguments were only established for those with reason and discernment, and not for others among creation, since they are the ones who are specifically given commands and prohibitions, and are charged with obedience and worship, and they are the ones who will be rewarded and punished.
How can He use His statement, Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth
h
and the alternation of the night and the day

1:13, as evidence against the unbelievers regarding the Oneness of God? And you know that some types of unbelievers deny that the heavens and the earth and everything else mentioned in this verse were created?

The denial of those who denied that does not prevent everything that God Almighty mentioned in this verse from being evidence of his Creator and Maker, and that he has a Manager who is not like [anything], and a Maker who has no equal. And even if that is the case, God only argued with that people who acknowledged that God is their Creator, but they associated in His worship the worship of idols and statues. So God Almighty argued with them and said - when they denied His statement: And your God is one God, and claimed that He had partners among the gods - [Indeed, your God is He who created the heavens and caused the sun and the moon to run in them for you with your provisions, constantly continuing in their course. This is the meaning of the alternation of night and day in the sun and moon. This is the meaning of His statement:
h
And the ships that sail through the sea with that which benefits people

And He sent down to you rain from the sky, thereby making your sides fertile after their drought, and making them fertile after their destruction, and refreshing you with it after your despair. This is the meaning of His statement:
h
And what God sends down from the sky of water

, thereby reviving the earth after its lifelessness. And He subjected to you the livestock in which there are foods and meals for you, and among them are camels and mounts, and among them are furniture and clothing. This is the meaning of His statement: And He dispersed therein of every kind of moving creature. And He sent to you the winds to fertilize your trees for your fruits and your food and your provisions, and He made the clouds move for you whose rain is your life and the life of your livestock and your cattle. This is the meaning of His statement:
h
And the directing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth

c: So He informed them that
m: their God is God who bestowed these blessings upon them, and He singled them out for them. Then he said: Is there among your partners someone who does any of that, so that you associate him with Me in your worship, and make him a rival and equal to Me? If there is none among your partners who does any of that, then in the blessings that I have enumerated for you, and the hands that I have singled out for you, there are proofs for you, if you understand, of the positions of truth and falsehood, injustice and fairness. That is because I am unique to you in my benevolence towards you, unlike anyone else, and you make rivals to Me in your worship of Me. This is the meaning of the verse. And those who are mentioned in this verse and who are used as evidence against it, are the people whose description has been described, not the Mu’attilah and the Dahriyah, although in the smallest of what God has enumerated in this verse, of the conclusive arguments, convincing to all of mankind, we have left out explaining it, disliking to prolong the book by mentioning it.

evidence.text: There is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," he recited that to his companions, and the polytheists who worshipped idols heard it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying: "
h
And among mankind are those who take other than God as equals to Him
, they love them as they love God.
But those who believe are stronger in love for God."

The Almighty means by that: That among mankind are those who take other than God as equals to Him. We have previously explained that the equal is justice, with the evidence that indicates that, so we disliked repeating it. And that those who take these equals to God, love their equals as the believers love God.

c: Then He informed them that
m: the believers love God stronger than those who take these equals to their equals.

x: The people of interpretation differed about the equals that the people took, and what they were.
Some of them said: They are their gods that they used to worship instead of God.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Mu'adh told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Qatadah:
m: His saying: "
h
And among mankind are those who take other than God as equals to Him
, they love them as they love God. But those who believe are stronger in love for God," than the disbelievers for His idols.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the words of God Almighty: They love them as they love God, boasting and comparing the truth with rivals, And those who believe are stronger in love for God, than the disbelievers for their idols.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding his words:
h
And of mankind are some who take other than God as equals to Him

, loving them as they love God, he said: They are the gods that are worshipped other than God, he said: They love their idols as they love God, And those who believe are stronger in love for God, meaning: than the disbelievers for their idols.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His words:
h
And of mankind are some who take other than God as equals to Him

, loving them as they love God, he said: These are the polytheists. Their rivals: their gods whom they worshipped along with God, they love them as those who believe love God, and those who believe love God more intensely than they love their gods.

x: Others said: Rather, the rivals in this context are their masters whom they obeyed in disobeying God, the Most High.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And among mankind are those who take for themselves rivals besides God, they love them as they love God, he said: The rivals among men, they obey them as they obey God, if they command them they obey them and disobey God.

x: How was it said: as they love God? Does God love rivals? Did those who took rivals love God, so it is said: They love them as they love God?

The meaning of that is contrary to what you have gone to, and it is rather similar to the saying of the speaker: I sold my slave as you sold your slave, meaning: I sold him as your slave was sold, and as you sold your slave, and I took my right from him as you took your right, meaning you took your right, so the metaphor of the name of the addressee is deleted from the second, and it is sufficient to use his metaphor for the slave and the right as the poet said: You are not a Muslim as long as you are alive, according to Zaid, by surrendering the prince He means by that: as he greets the prince. So the meaning of the statement is: And among the people are those who, O believers, take for themselves rivals besides God, whom they love as they love God.
The readings differed in the reading of that. The majority of the people of Medina and Ash-Sham read it: And if those who did wrong could see
h
when they see the punishment

that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment. With the opening of an and an both of them - meaning: And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who disbelieved and wronged themselves,
h
when they see the punishment

of God and witness it, that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment.
