Then there are two views regarding the accusative of an and an in this reading: One of them is to open it with the omitted part of the statement that is required in it, so the interpretation of the statement then would be: And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who did wrong
h
when they see the punishment
of God, they would acknowledge - and the meaning of see is to see - that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment.

And the answer then - if you open an in this way - is abandoned, and the indication of the statement is sufficient for it, and the meaning is what I described. This is one of the two aspects of opening that, according to the reading of those who read law tarab with the ta’. The other aspect in opening: that its meaning is: And if you could see, O Muhammad, when those who do wrong see the punishment of God, because all power belongs to God, and God is severe in punishment, you would know the extent of God’s punishment. Then the lam is deleted and it is opened with that meaning, because the speech indicates it, and others from the early reciters read that: (And if you could but see those who do wrong
h
when they see the punishment

. Indeed, all power belongs to God, and indeed, God is severe in punishment). Meaning: And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who do wrong when they witness the punishment of God, you would know the state they will end up in.

c: Then the Most High informed us
m: with a new piece of report about His power and authority, after completing the first piece of report, so He said: Indeed, all power belongs to God in this world and the hereafter, without anyone else of rivals and gods, and indeed, God is severe in punishment for whoever associates partners with Him, claims partners with Him, and makes a rival for Him. Another reading of the one who broke the word in in tarā with a tā may be possible. It means: “And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who did wrong
h
when they see the punishment
, they would say: ‘Indeed, all power belongs to God, and indeed, God is severe in punishment.’ Then you delete the statement and suffice with what is said.

x: Others read it as: “And if those who did wrong could see” with a ya “
h
when they see the punishment

that all power belongs to God, and that God is severe in punishment” with a fathah on the alif of an and an, meaning: “And if those who did wrong could see the punishment of God that is prepared for them in Hell, they would know when they see it and witness it that all power belongs to God, and that God is severe in punishment,
h
when they see the punishment

.” So the first n is in the accusative case because it is connected to the answer to the deleted law, and the answer is left out, and the second is conjoined with the first. This is the general reading of the readers of Kufa, Basra and Mecca. Some grammarians of Basra have claimed that the interpretation of the reading of those who read: And if only those who did wrong could see
h
when they see the punishment

that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment with the ya’ in yaara and the opening of the two alifs in an and an: and if they know, because they did not know the extent of the punishment that they would witness.

The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew, so if he said: and if only you see, then he is addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And if he broke the in as a beginning, if he said: and if only he sees, it is permissible, because if only he sees, if only he knows. And if only it is in a meaning that does not require anything with it. You say to a man: By God, if only he knew, and if only you knew.

i: As the poet said:
x: If your medicine is pampering, then it was in the past and the bygone years This has no answer except in the meaning, and the poet said: And be fortunate in what we live, and do not let nonsense lead you into horrors So he concealed: Live.

He said: Some of them read: And if you see, and he opened that to see. But that is not the case, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew, but… He wanted to teach people that, as God the Almighty said: Or do they say, ‘He has invented it’? (al-Sajdah 32:2) to inform people of their ignorance, and as He said:
h
Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth
? (al-Baqarah 2:107).
Some people denied that an was an agent in his statement:
h
And if he could see
. They said: Those who did wrong knew when they saw the punishment that all power belongs to God, so there is no basis for those who interpreted that:
h
And if he could see
that all power belongs to God. They said:
h
And if he could see

that all power belongs to God was an agent in an, which means knowledge, because the first knowledge came before. Some grammarians of Kufa said: Whoever put the power in the accusative case and that God is severe in punishment, from those who read
h
And if he could see
with the letter ya, put it in the accusative case by applying the vision to it, and making the vision fall upon it. As for those who put it in the accusative case from those who read
h
And if he could see
with the letter ta, they put it in the accusative case on the interpretation: because all power belongs to God, and because God is severe in punishment.

He said: And whoever breaks them from those who read with the ta’, then he breaks them with the report. And others of them said: He opened that in the reading of whoever read: And if those who wronged could see with the ya’, by working with ya’ra and the answer to the speech then is left out, just as the answer to: And if a Qur’an by which mountains were moved or the earth was split apart (al-Ra’d 13:31) was left out, because the meaning of Paradise and Hell is repeated and well-known. They said: It is permissible to break the inn, in the reading of those who read with the ya’ and to make the ru’yah on the idh in the meaning, and they allowed the accusative of the inn on the reading of those who read that - the ta’, for the meaning of the intention of another action, and that the interpretation of the statement is: And if only those who did wrong Surat Al-Baqarah 2:165 And among mankind are those who take for themselves other than Allah equals to Him, loving them as they love Allah.
But those who believe are stronger in love for Allah. And if only those who did wrong could see
h
when they see the punishment
that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment. could see
h
when they see the punishment
[they see], that all power belongs to God. They claimed that breaking the inn face, if it is read, and if only you see - the ta’ is for resumption, because his saying:
h
And if only you see has been applied to those who did wrong
The correct reading according to us in that is: And if only those who did wrong could see - with the ta’ from tarā
h
when they see the punishment

that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment meaning: I would have seen that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment. So his saying: I would have seen the second, is deleted and the indication of his saying:
h
And if only those who did wrong could see does not need to mention it

, since it was an answer to if. And the statement, even if it is addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - is intended by it other than him. Because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, undoubtedly knew that all power belongs to God, and that God is severe in punishment. This would be similar to his statement:
h
Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth
? (al-Baqarah 2:107), and we have explained this in its place.

We chose this over the reading of the letter ya because when the people saw the punishment, they would be certain that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment. So there is no reason to say: If they saw that all power belongs to God - then. Because it is only said: If you saw for someone who has not seen, but as for someone who has seen it, there is no point in saying to him: And you saw.
The meaning of his saying:
h
When they see the punishment
, is when they witness the punishment, as I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his saying:
h
And if those who have wronged could see when they see the punishment that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment
, meaning: if they witnessed the punishment. And what the Most High meant by his saying:
h
And if those who have wronged could see

, is: And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who wronged themselves and took for themselves rivals besides Me whom they love as you love Me, when they witness My punishment on the Day of Resurrection which I have prepared for them, you would know that all power is Mine, not the rivals and gods, and that the rivals and gods will not avail them at all there, nor will they ward off from them the punishment that I have inflicted upon them, and you would be certain that I am severe in My punishment for whoever disbelieves in Me and claims with Me a god other than Me.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
When those who were followed disown those who followed and they see the punishment
The Almighty means by His saying:
h
When those who were followed disown those who followed and they see the punishment
, those who were followed disown those who followed them.
Then the people of interpretation differed about those whom God, the Most High, meant by His saying:
h
When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed
, some of them said what:

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid bin Zari’ narrated to us, he said: Sa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His saying:
h
When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed
, and they are the tyrants, leaders, and chiefs in polytheism, from those who followed, and they are the weak followers, and they see the punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja’far narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed
, he said: The leaders will disassociate themselves from the followers on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to me, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said:
m: I said to Ata’:
h
When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed
, he said: Their leaders, chiefs, and masters will disassociate themselves from those who followed them.

x: Others said: It was narrated to me by Musa bin Harun, who said:

c: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us,
m: who said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: When those who were followed disassociated themselves from those who followed. As for those who were followed, they are the devils who disassociated themselves from mankind.

x: The correct statement in my opinion regarding this is that God, the Most High, mentioned that those who are followed in associating partners with God will disassociate themselves from their followers when they witness the punishment of God. He did not specify some of them over others, but rather He included all of them. So included in this is every one who is followed in disbelief in God and misguidance, who will disassociate himself from his followers who used to follow him in misguidance in this world, when they witness the punishment of God in the Hereafter. As for the indication of the verse regarding whom it refers to by His statement:
h
When those who followed disassociate themselves from those they followed
, it only indicates knowledge that the rivals whom they took besides God, as described by the Most High in His statement:
h
And among mankind are those who take rivals besides God
, are those who disassociate themselves from their followers.
Since the verse indicates this, the interpretation that al-Suddi interpreted in His statement:
h
And among mankind are those who take rivals besides God

, is correct, that the rivals in this place are only meant to be the rivals of men who obey them in what they command them to do, and disobey God in their obedience to them, just as the believers obey God and disobey others. The interpretation of the statement of the one who said:
h
When those who followed disassociate themselves from those they followed
, that they are the devils who disassociated themselves from their human allies is corrupted, because this verse is in the context of reporting on those who take rivals.
The statement in the interpretation of the saying of God the Almighty: And their ties of kinship are severed.

By that God the Almighty means: that God is severe in punishment, when those who followed disown themselves, and their ties of kinship are severed. Then the people of interpretation differed in the meaning of ties of kinship.
Some of them said what:

c: Yahya bin Talhah Al-Yarbouʿi narrated to me, he said, Fadil bin Ayyad narrated to us
m: - and Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us - on the authority of Ubaid Al-Maktab, on the authority of Mujahid: And their ties of kinship are severed, he said: the connection that was between them in this world.

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed narrated to us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ubaid Al-Maktab, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And their ties of kinship are severed, he said: their connection in this world.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar narrated to us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, and Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us
m: - both of them said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Ubaid Al-Maktab, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And their ties of kinship were severed, he said: affection.

c: Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told me: Al-Husayn told me: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: There was a connection between them through affection in this world.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa: Qays ibn Sa’d told me, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And their ties of kinship were severed, he said: affection. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari' narrated, Sa'id narrated, on the authority of Qatada: And their ties will be severed means the ties Surat Al-Baqarah 2:166
h
When those who were followed disassociate themselves from those who followed

, and they see the punishment, and all ties between them are severed. of remorse on the Day of Resurrection, and the ties of connection that were between them in this world, through which they would connect and love each other, but which will become enmity between them on the Day of Resurrection. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others, curse each other, and disavow each other. God the Almighty said: Friends, that Day, will be enemies to each other, except for the righteous (al-Zukhruf 43:67). So every friendship will become enmity towards its people except for the friendship of the righteous. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abd al-Razzaq narrated, Muammar narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement:
h
And their ties will be severed means the ties that were between them in this world

. I narrated on the authority of Ammar bin al-Hasan, who narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Ja'far, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada: And their ties will be severed means remorse.

x: Some of them said: Rather, the meaning of ties is the positions that they had among the people of this world.

Who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And their causes were cut off, he said: their homes were cut off.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Saad told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ bin Anas:
m: And their causes were cut off, he said: the homes are the homes.

x: Others said: The causes are the wombs.

Who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said, al-Hasan told us, he said, al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Ibn Jurayj said, and Ibn Abbas said: And their causes were cut off, he said: the wombs.
Others said: The causes are the deeds that they used to do in this world.
Those who said that: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: As for and their causes were cut off, it means actions.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: and their causes were cut off, he said: The causes of their actions. The people of piety were given the causes of their actions as a document, so they take them and are saved, and the others were given the causes of their evil actions, so they were cut off and they went to the Fire.

x: The causes are the thing that is attached to it. He said: The cause is the rope. Causes is the plural of cause, and it is everything that a man uses to reach his request and need. The rope is called a cause, because it is used to cause the need that cannot be reached except by attaching to it. The road is called a cause, because riding it leads to something that cannot be reached except by cutting it. Marriage is a cause, because it is a cause for sanctity. The means is a cause, to reach the need by it, and likewise everything that is used to attain the requests is a cause for attaining it. If that is the case, then the correct interpretation of His statement:
h
And their ties are cut off is to say

: God Almighty informed that those who wronged themselves - from the people of disbelief who died while they were disbelievers - disavow - when they witness the punishment of God - the follower from the follower, and their ties are cut off.
God Almighty informed in His Book that some of them curse each other, and He informed about Satan that he says to his friends:
“I am not your savior, nor are you my savior. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated before”
God Almighty informed that on that day, friends will be enemies to each other, except for the righteous, and that the disbelievers will not support each other on that day, so God Almighty said:
“Stop them, for they will be questioned. What is the matter with you that you do not support one another?”

and that a man among them will not benefit from his relative or a kin, even if his relative is a friend of God, so God Almighty said in that regard: And Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made. And he promised him, but when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disavowed him” (al-Tawbah 9:114) And the Most High informed us that their deeds would become regrets for them.

All of these meanings are causes that lead to demands in this world, so God cut off their benefits in the Hereafter from the disbelievers in Him, because they were contrary to His obedience and satisfaction, so they are cut off from their people. Neither did their intercourse with one another benefit them when they came to their Lord, nor did their worship of their rivals, nor did their obedience to their devils? Nor did their wombs defend them and help them from God’s vengeance against them, nor did their deeds avail them, rather they became regrets for them. So all of the causes of the disbelievers are cut off. There is no more eloquent meaning - in interpreting His statement: And their causes were cut off - than the description of God [that], and that is what we explained of [cutting off], all of their causes and not some of them, according to what we said about that. And whoever claims that what is meant by that is a specific cause, he was asked about the explanation of his claim from an undisputed origin, and he was opposed by the statement of his opponent in it.
He will not say anything about any of these things without being obligated to do the same in the other.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And those who followed said, ‘If only we had another chance, we would disown them as they disowned us.’

What is meant by the Almighty’s saying: And those who followed said, is that the followers of men - whom they had taken as rivals besides God, obeying them in disobeying God, and disobeying their Lord in obeying them, when they see the punishment of God in the Hereafter - said: If only we had another chance. What is meant by the chance is the return to the world, from the saying of the speaker: I have returned to the people a second time, and the chance is a single time, and that is if he attacks them, returning to them after turning away from them, as Al-Akhtal said: They turned to Fazara as if they were a tribe of men, and then they went to a place of refuge. And as: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada: And those who followed said, ‘If only we had another chance, we could disown them as they disowned us,’ meaning: We could return to the world.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
m: And those who followed said, ‘If only we had another chance, we could disown them as they disowned us.’ He said: The followers said: If only we had another chance to the world, we could disown them as they disowned us. And his saying:
h
Then we could disown them is in the accusative case

, because it is a response to the wish with the letter fa. Because the people wished to return to the world to disavow those who obeyed them in disobeying God, just as their leaders who were followed in the world in disbelief in God disavowed them, when they saw the great punishment that befell them from God, and they said: Oh, if only we could return to the world so we could disavow them, and Oh, if only we could return and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers (al-An’am 6:27).

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God the Most High:
h
Thus does God show them their deeds as regrets for them
The meaning of his words:
h
Thus does God show them their deeds

, is that just as he showed them the punishment that he mentioned in his words: and they saw the punishment, which they denied in the world, so he also shows them their evil deeds for which they deserved punishment from God as regrets for them, meaning: remorse. And regrets are the plural of regret. And likewise every noun whose singular is fa’ala with the first letter open The second letter is silent, so if it is pluralized as fa’alaat, such as shahwa and tamara, it is plural shahwat and tamarat, with the second letter of its letters being heavy. But if it is an adjective, then you leave the second letter silent, such as hakama, the plural of which is hakamaat, and ‘abla, the plural of which is ‘ablaat.

i: And sometimes the second letter is silent in nouns, as the poet said:
x: The vicissitudes of time and its states guide us to the right path So the soul rests from its sighs The second is from the sighs, which is a noun.
It was said: Regret is the most severe remorse.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How can they see
h
their deeds as regrets for them

, while the regretful person only regrets abandoning good deeds and missing them? You know that the disbelievers did not have deeds that they would regret abandoning more of, so God shows them a little of them! Rather, all their deeds were sins against God, and there is no regret for them in that, but the regret is in what they did not do of obedience to God?
The people of interpretation differ in interpreting that, so we will mention what they said about that, then we will inform about what is more deserving of its interpretation, God willing.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Thus God shows them their deeds that He imposed upon them in this world, but they wasted them and did not do them, until He made it obligatory for them - what God had prepared for them, if they had done them in their lives, of dwellings and blessings - to change them through their obedience to their Lord. So what they missed of the reward - which God had prepared for them with Him if they had obeyed Him in this world, when they saw it when they entered the Fire or before that - became a sorrow, regret and sorrow for them.
Those who said that: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
Thus does God show them their deeds as regrets for them

, he claimed that Paradise will be raised up for them and they will look at it and at their homes in it, if they had obeyed God, and it will be said to them: Those are your dwellings, if you had obeyed God! Then it will be divided among the believers, and they will inherit them. That is when they will regret.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, he said, Abu Al-Zura’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah - in a story he mentioned - he
m: said: There is no soul but that it Surat Al-Baqarah 2:167 And those who followed said, "If only we could have another turn so we could disown them as they disowned us." Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will not emerge from the Fire. looks at a house in Paradise and a house in Hell, and that is the Day of Regret. He said: The people of Hell will see those in Paradise, and it will be said to them: If only you had worked! So regret will overtake them. He said: The people of Paradise will see the house in Hell, and it will be said: If only God had not bestowed His favor upon you!
b.via: Abdullah - in a story he mentioned - he

x: How can deeds that they did not do be attributed to them according to this interpretation?

Just as a man is shown his work and it is said to him before he does it: This is your work. Meaning: This is what you should do. And just as it is said to a man who is preparing his lunch before he eats it: This is your lunch today. Meaning: This is what you will eat for lunch today. So too is His statement:
h
Thus will God show them their deeds as regrets for them
, meaning: Thus will God show them their deeds that they were obligated to do in this world as regrets for them.
Others said: Thus will God show them their evil deeds as regrets for them. Why did they do them? Why did they not do other deeds that would please God?
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
Thus will God show them their deeds as regrets for them
, so their evil deeds will become regrets for them on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Their deeds as regrets for them

, he said: Are not their evil deeds for which God has caused them to enter the Fire? So He made it a regret for them. He said: And He made the deeds of the people of Paradise for them, and he recited the statement of God: For what you put forth in the past days (al-Haqqah 69:24).

x: The most appropriate of the two interpretations of the verse is the interpretation of the one who said: The meaning of His statement:
h
Thus does God show them their deeds as regrets for them

, is: Thus does God show the disbelievers their evil deeds as regrets for them. Why did they do them? Why did they not do something else? So they regretted what they had neglected of their evil deeds, when they saw their recompense from God and its punishment, because God informed that He shows them their deeds as regret for them. So what is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse is what the apparent meaning indicates, not what the hidden meaning implies, which has no indication that it is what is meant by it. And what Al-Suddi said about that, even if it is a doctrine that the verse implies, it is a far-fetched opinion. And there is no trace - that it is as mentioned - that can be accepted as evidence, and there is no indication in the apparent meaning of the verse that it is what is meant by it.

By that, the Almighty means: And these disbelievers whom you described - even if they regretted after witnessing what they witnessed of God’s punishment, and their regret for their previous evil deeds became intense, and they wished for the world to return to it so that they could repent and disavow their misguiders and masters whom they obeyed in disobeying God in it - will not come out of the fire that God cast them into by their disbelief in Him in the world, nor will their regret in it save them from God’s punishment at that time, but they will remain in it forever. And in this verse is evidence of God’s denial of those who claim that God’s punishment of the people of Hell from among the disbelievers will end, and that it will come to an end, and after that it will pass away. Because God, the Almighty, mentioned about these people whose description He described in this verse, then concluded the report about them by saying that they will not come out of the fire, without making an exception from Him for a time rather than another.
This is endless.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth [that is] lawful and good
h
and do not follow the footsteps of Satan
Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.”

The Almighty means by that: O mankind, eat from the foods that I have made lawful for you through the tongue of My Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. I have made it good for you - from what you forbid yourselves of the bahā’ir, the sawa’ib, the wasa’il, and the like of that which I have not forbidden to you - but not from the foods and edibles that I have forbidden to you and made impure of dead animals, blood, pork, and that which has been sacrificed to someone other than Me. And leave
h
the footsteps of Satan

- who will destroy you, bring you to the depths of ruin, and forbid you from your property - so do not follow them or act upon them. Indeed, he - meaning by his saying: he Satan, and the ha in his saying: he refers to Satan - is to you, O people, a clear enemy, meaning: he has made his enmity clear to you, by his refusal to prostrate to your father, and his deceit of him until he expelled him from Paradise, and made him slip into sin, and he ate from the tree.

The Almighty says: “O people, do not seek his advice, even though he has made his enmity clear to you. Leave what he commands you to do, and adhere to my obedience in what I have commanded you to do and forbidden you from, which I have made lawful for you and forbidden for you, except for what you have forbidden for yourselves, which you have made lawful, in obedience to Satan and following his command.” The meaning of his statement: lawful is absolute 1. It is a source from the saying of the speaker: This thing has become lawful for you, meaning it has become absolutely for you, so it is lawful for you as lawful and permissible. And from the speech of the Arabs: It is permissible for you, meaning: absolute. As for his statement: good, he means by it: pure, not impure or forbidden. As for the steps, it is the plural of step, and the step is the distance between the two feet of the walker.

And the step with the opening of the kha is the single action from the saying of the speaker: I took one step. The step may be a plural of a mistake, and the step may be a plural of steps and a mistake. The meaning of the prohibition of following his steps is the prohibition of his path and his effect in what he called for, which is contrary to the obedience of God Almighty.
The people of interpretation differed in the meaning of the steps.
Some of them said:
h
The steps of Satan
: his work.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
The steps of Satan
, he said: his work.

x: Some of them said:
h
The steps of Satan
, his sins.
Those who said: Muhammad bin Amr told me, Abu Asim told us, Issa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, in his saying:
h
The steps of Satan
, he said: his sin.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: his sins.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, from Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not follow the footsteps of Satan
, he said: His sins.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib narrated to me, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Juwaybir narrated to us, from Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The footsteps of Satan
, he said: The sins of Satan that he commands.

x: Others said:
h
The footsteps of Satan
, is obeying him.
Those who said that: Musa bin Harun narrated to me, he said:

c: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from As-Suddi:
m: h
And do not follow the footsteps of Satan
, he said: Obeying him.

x: Others said:
h
The footsteps of Satan
, are vows to commit sins.
Those who said that: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said:

c: Jarir narrated to us, from Sulayman, from Abu Majlaz,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not follow the footsteps of Satan
, he said: They are vows to commit sins.

x: These statements that we have mentioned from those we have mentioned about the interpretation of his statement:
h
The footsteps of Satan

, are close in meaning to each other. Because each of them said something about that, he indicated the prohibition of following Satan in his traces and actions. However, the true interpretation of the word is what I have explained, that it is - after what is between his feet, then it is used in all of his traces and ways, as I have explained.
The statement in the interpretation of the words of God the Almighty:
h
He only commands you
to do evil and immorality and to say about God that which you do not know.
God the Almighty means by His words:
h
He only commands you

, the devil, to do evil and immorality and to say about God that which you do not know. Evil is sin, like harm, from the saying of the speaker: This matter displeases you, it displeases you badly, which is what displeases the doer. As for immorality, it is a source like prosperity and adversity, and it is everything that is disgraceful to mention and ugly to hear. It was said: The evil that God mentioned is the sins of God. If that is the case, then God called it evil because it displeases its doer with the evil of its consequences for him with God. It was said: Immorality is adultery. If that is the case, then it is only called [thus] because of the ugliness of its hearing and the abhorrentness of what its doer is mentioned with.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He only orders you to do evil and immorality. As for evil, it is disobedience, and as for immorality, it is adultery. As for His statement:
h
And that you say about God what you do not know

, it is what they used to forbid of the bahīr, sā’ib, wasīl, and hawāmī, and they claim that God forbade that. So God, the Exalted, said to them: God has not ordained any bahīr, nor sā’ib, nor wasīl, nor hawām, but those who disbelieve invent lies about God, and most of them do not reason. (al-Ma’idah 5:103) So God, the Exalted, informed them in this verse that their saying: God has forbidden this! From the lies that Satan commands them to tell, and that He has made it permissible for them and made it good, and has not forbidden them to eat it, but they say about God what they do not know the truth of, out of obedience to Satan, and following in his footsteps, and following in the footsteps of their misguided ancestors and ignorant fathers, who were ignorant of God and what He revealed to His Messenger, and were astray from the truth and His path, and extravagant on their part, as God revealed in His Book to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, when He, the Most High, said: And when it is said to them, ‘Follow what God has revealed,’ they say, ‘Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.’

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “And when it is said to them, ‘
h
Follow what God has revealed
,’ they say, ‘Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.’
Even though their fathers did not understand anything and were not guided.”

There are two aspects of interpretation in this verse. One of them: That the ha’ and the mim in His statement: And when it is said to them refer to whom in His statement: And among mankind are those who take others besides God as equals, so the meaning of the statement is: And among mankind are those who take others besides God as equals. And when it is said to them:
h
Follow what God has revealed

, they say: Rather, we follow what we found our fathers doing. The other: That the ha’ and the mim in His statement: And when it is said to them are from the mention of the people who are in His statement: O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth [that is] lawful and good, so that is a shift from addressing to reporting on the absent, as in the statement of God the Most High: Until, when you were in the ships and they sailed with them with a good wind
r
(Yunus 10:22)

What is more correct to me and more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse is that the ha’ and the mim in His statement to them are from the mention of the people, and that is a shift from addressing to reporting on the absent. Because that follows His statement: O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth.

So it is more appropriate for it to be report about them than it is report about those who were informed that among them were those who take rivals to God, with what is between them of verses, and the interruption of their stories with a new story other than it, and that it was revealed about a group of Jews who said that, when they were called to Islam, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: or on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the Jews of the People of the Book to Islam and encouraged them to do so, and warned them of God’s punishment and vengeance, so Rafi’ ibn Kharijah and Malik ibn Awf said to him: Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing, for they were more knowledgeable and better than us, so God revealed about that from their statement: “And when it is said to them, ‘
h
Follow what God has revealed
,’ they say, ‘Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.’ Even if their fathers did not understand anything and were not guided.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, Yunus bin Bakir told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us,
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, told me, Saeed bin Jubair, or Ikrimah, told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly - except that he said: Abu Rafi bin Kharijah and Malik bin Auf said to him. As for the interpretation of his statement:
h
Follow what God has revealed

, it is: Do what God has revealed in His Book to His Messenger, so make lawful what He has made lawful and forbid what He has made unlawful, and make him an imam for you whom you follow, and a leader whose rulings you follow. And his statement:
h
We found our fathers doing it
, means: we found, as the poet said: I found him not repenting or remembering God except a little. Meaning: I found it, and as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They said, ‘Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing,’ meaning: what we found our fathers doing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

x: The meaning of the verse is: And when it is said to these disbelievers: Eat of what God has made lawful for you, and abandon the steps and path of Satan, and act according to what God has revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in His Book, they will be too arrogant to submit to the truth and will say: Rather, we will follow our fathers and follow what we found them doing, of making lawful what they used to make lawful and prohibiting what they used to prohibit. God, the Most High, said: Or if their fathers - meaning: the fathers of these disbelievers who continued in their disbelief in God the Almighty - did not understand anything of God’s religion and His obligations, His commands and prohibitions, so that they would follow the path they took and their actions would be followed - nor were Surat al-Baqarah 2:170 And when it is said to them, “Follow what Allah has revealed,” they say, “Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.”

Even though their fathers did not understand anything, nor were they guided? they guided to the right path, so that others would be guided by them and those who seek the religion and want the truth and what is right would follow them? God, the Most High, says to these disbelievers: How… O people, do you follow what you found your fathers doing in order to abandon what God commands you? Your Lord is with you, and your fathers do not understand anything about God’s command, nor are they right, nor do they realize the right path? The follower only follows the one who has knowledge of the thing used for it in himself. As for the ignorant, no one follows him - in what he is ignorant of - except the one who has no mind or discernment.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying:
h
And the example of those who disbelieve is like the example of one who shouts to that which hears nothing but calls and cries
The people of interpretation differed in the meaning of that.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: The example of the disbeliever - in his lack of understanding of what is recited to him from God in His Book, and his poor acceptance of what is called to of the Oneness of God and admonished with - is like the animal that hears the sound when it is called to, but does not understand what is said to it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of ʿIkrimah,
m: in his saying:
h
And the example of those who disbelieve is like the example of one who shouts to that which hears nothing but calls and cries
, he said: Like a camel or a donkey, you call it and it hears the sound but does not understand what you say.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zari’ told me, he said, Yusuf ibn Khalid al-Samti told us, he said, Nafi’ ibn Malik told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Like one who cries to that which hears not, he said: It is like the example of a sheep and the like.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father,
m: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: And the parable of those who disbelieve is that of one who shouts to that which hears nothing except calls and cries. Like the camel, donkey, or sheep. If you say to some of them: Eat, they do not know what you are saying, but they hear your voice. And likewise the disbeliever. If you command him to do good or forbid him from evil or admonish him, he does not understand what you are saying, but he hears your voice.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: Like the beast, it is called and it hears but does not understand what is said to it. Likewise the disbeliever, he hears the sound but does not understand.

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Like the one who calls out to that which hears not, he said: The disbeliever is like an animal, he hears the sound but does not understand.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Like the one who calls out, an example that God gave for the disbeliever, he hears what is said to him but does not understand, like the animal that hears the bleating but does not understand.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the example of those who disbelieve is like the example of one who calls out to that which hears nothing but calls and cries
, he said: The example of the disbeliever is like the example of a camel or a sheep, he hears the sound but does not understand and does not know what is meant by it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Like one who calls out to that which hears nothing but calls and cries

, he said: It is a simile that God has given for the disbeliever. He says: The example of this disbeliever is like that of this animal that hears a sound but does not know what is being said to it. Likewise, the disbeliever does not benefit from what is being said to him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: He is like the disbeliever, he hears a sound but does not understand what is being said to him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: I asked ʿAta’ and then I said to him: It is said: It does not understand - meaning the animal - except that it hears the call of the caller when he calls out to it, so they are like that, they do not understand even though they hear. So he said: Likewise. He said: And Mujahid said: The one who calls out is the shepherd to that which does not hear of the animals.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Like the one who cries out the shepherd to what does not hear of the animals.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Like the one who cries out to what does not hear except a call and a cry, he does not understand what is said to him, unless he is called and then comes, or he is called and then goes. As for the one who cries out, he is the shepherd of sheep, just as the shepherd cries out to what does not hear what is said to him, unless he is called or summoned. Likewise, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, calls to one who hears nothing but the murmur of speech. God says: Deaf, dumb, blind
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:18)

x: The meaning of those who say this statement - in their interpretation of what they interpreted, according to what I have related from them - is: The example of the admonition of those who disbelieve and their admonisher is like the caw of the caller to his sheep and his bleating to them. So the proverb was attributed to those who disbelieved, and the mention of the sermon and the preacher was left Surat Al-Baqarah 2:171 And the example of those who disbelieve is like that of one who calls to that which hears nothing except calls and cries - deaf, dumb, and blind -
h
so they do not understand

. out, because the speech indicates that. Just as it is said: If you meet someone, then respect him as you respect a sultan, meaning: as you respect a sultan, and as the poet said: You are not a Muslim as long as you are alive, according to Zaid, by surrendering the prince It is meant by it: as one greets the prince.

It may be possible that the meaning - according to this interpretation that these people have interpreted - is: And the example of those who disbelieve in their lack of understanding of God and His Messenger is like the example of the animal that is called by it, who does not understand the commands and prohibitions except by the sound. That is because if it was said to it: Eat, bring water, it would not know what is being said to it except by the sound that it hears from the one who says it. So likewise the disbeliever, his example in his lack of understanding of what he is commanded and forbidden from - due to his poor contemplation of it and his lack of consideration and thought about it - is like this one that is called by it in what he is commanded and forbidden from.

i: So the meaning is for the one that is called by it, and the speech is outside of the one who calls, as the Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan said:
x: I was afraid, so much so that my fear was no greater than that of a sane ibex in the rain.

Meaning: Until the fear of the ibex does not exceed my fear, and as the other said: It was an obligation to say what you say, just as adultery was an obligation to be stoned. Meaning: Just as stoning was the obligation for adultery, so stoning was made the obligation for adultery, because the meaning of the words is clear to the listener, and as the other said: A lamp is a source of pride for the noble, and the eye is adorned with it when it is exposed. Meaning: It is adorned with the eye, so He made it the eye adorned with it. And there are more similar examples of this in the speech of the Arabs than can be counted, from what the Arabs direct from the report of what they are reporting to what accompanies it, for the meaning of that to be clear to its listener, so they say: Show the basin to the she-camel, and the she-camel is only shown to the basin, and similar to that from their speech.

And others said: The meaning of that is: And the example of those who disbelieve in their call to their gods and idols that do not hear or understand, is like the example of one who cries to what does not hear except a call and a cry, and that echo whose voice is heard but the caller does not understand anything from it. So the interpretation of the speech according to the saying of those who say that: And the example of those who disbelieve and their gods - in their call to them while they do not understand or reason - is like the example of the caller to what the caller hears only a call and a cry, meaning: The caller hears nothing from him except his call.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And the example of those who disbelieve is like the example of one who calls to that which hears nothing but calls and cries

, he said: The man who calls in the depths of the mountains and a voice answers him in them that returns to him and is called the echo. So the example of the gods of these people to them is like the example of one who answers him with this voice, it does not benefit him, he hears nothing but calls and cries. He said: The Arabs call that the echo. And the verse may bear another interpretation based on this interpretation. It is that its meaning is: And the example of those who disbelieve in their calling to their gods who do not understand their call, is like the example of one who calls to his sheep from a place where his sheep do not hear his voice, so they do not benefit from his cries at all, except that he is in trouble from his calls and cries. So likewise the disbeliever in his calling to his gods, he is in trouble from his calling to them and calling to them, and nothing benefits him.

x: The most correct interpretation of the verse in my opinion is the first interpretation that Ibn ʿAbbas and those who agreed with him said. It means that the meaning of the verse is: The parable of the preaching of the disbeliever and his preacher is like the parable of the one who calls out to his sheep and his bleating, for he hears his bleating but does not understand his words, as we have explained before. As for the reason for the permissibility of omitting preaching and sufficing with the parable from it, we have explained it in His statement:
h
Their example is like the example of one who kindled a fire (al-Baqarah 2

:17) and in other similar verses, sufficient to repeat it. We have chosen this interpretation because this verse was revealed about the Jews, and God the Most High meant them by it, and the Jews were not people of idols that they worshipped, nor people of statues that they venerated and hoped for benefit from them or to ward off harm from them.

And there is no reason - since that is the case - for the interpretation of those who interpreted it to mean: The example of those who disbelieved in their calling out to the gods and supplicating to them.
What is your evidence that this verse refers to the Jews?

Our evidence for that is the verses that precede and follow it, for they are the ones meant by it. So what is between them is that It is more appropriate and more deserving of being report about them than report about others, until the evidence becomes clear that the report is diverted from them to others. This, with what we mentioned from the report from those we mentioned that it was revealed about them, and the narration that we narrated from Ibn Abbas that the verse before this verse was revealed about them. And with what we said that this verse is meant for the Jews, Ata’ used to say - Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ata’ said to me regarding this verse: They are the Jews about whom God revealed: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price until His saying: How patient they are toward the Fire (al-Baqarah 2:174-175).

i: As for his saying: cries out, it is the sound of sheep, cawing, and cawing, and from it is the saying of Al-Akhtal:
x: So moan with your sheep, Jarir, for your soul has been lost in the wilderness.
Meaning: A voice with it.
The statement in the interpretation of His statement: Deaf, dumb, and blind,
h
so they do not understand

God Almighty means by His statement: Deaf, dumb, and blind, these infidels who are like someone who cries out to something that hears nothing but a call and a cry. Deaf to the truth, so they do not hear. Dumb means: mute to what is said, the truth and correctness, and the acknowledgment of what God has commanded them to acknowledge, and the clarification of what God Almighty has commanded them to clarify of the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they do not speak it or say it, nor clarify it to the people. Blind to guidance and the path of truth, so they do not see it, as Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatadah, His statement: Deaf, dumb, and blind means: deaf to the truth, so they do not hear it, nor benefit from it, nor understand it. Blind to the truth and guidance, so they do not see it.
Dumb to the truth, so they do not speak it.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Deaf, dumb, and blind, meaning: about the truth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha,
m: Ibn Abbas: Deaf, dumb, and blind, meaning: they do not hear the guidance, nor do they see it, nor do they understand it. As for the nominative in his statement, Deaf, dumb, and blind, it came to him before the beginning and the resumption, as indicated by his statement,
h
So they do not understand
, as is said in speech: he is deaf and does not hear, and he is dumb and does not speak.

evidence.text: Some of them said: The meaning of that is: The example of the disbeliever - in his lack of understanding of what is recited to him from God in His Book, and his poor acceptance of what is called to of the Oneness of God and admonished with - is like the animal that hears the sound when it is called to, but does not understand what is said to it.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying:
h
O you who have believed
, eat from the good things which We have provided for you and be grateful to God if it is Him that you worship.
The Almighty means by His saying:
h
O you who have believed
h
O you who have believed
in God and His Messenger and acknowledged servitude to God and submitted to Him in obedience, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding His saying:
h
O you who have believed

, he says: They have believed. Eat from the good things which We have provided for you, meaning: feed from the lawful provision which We have made lawful for you, so it became good for you by My making it lawful for you, from what you used to forbid, and I did not forbid it for you, of foods and drinks. And be grateful to God, he says: and praise God as He is worthy of from you, for the blessings which He has provided you and made good for you. If you worship Him, He says: If you are obedient to His command, listening and obeying, then eat what He has made lawful and permissible for you to eat, and leave the steps of Satan in forbidding it. We have already mentioned some of the foods that they used to forbid in their ignorance, and it is what He urged them to eat and forbade them from believing in its prohibition, since their forbidding it in ignorance was an act of obedience to Satan, and following the disbelievers among them from God from their fathers and ancestors. Then the Almighty explained to them what He forbade them, and explained it in detail for them.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
He has only forbidden you dead animals
, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God.

God Almighty means by that: Do not forbid yourselves what I have not forbidden you, O believers in God and His Messenger, of the bahā’ir and the sawa’ib and the like. Rather, eat that, for I have only forbidden you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Me. The meaning of his saying:
h
He has only forbidden you dead animals
, is that
h
he has only forbidden you dead animals

. And it is only one letter, and that is why dead and blood are in the accusative case, and it is not permissible for dead if you make dead only one letter, except in the accusative case. If dead were two letters, and were separated from in, then dead and what follows it would be in the nominative case. The interpretation of the statement then would be: What God has forbidden you from dead foods, blood, and pork, nothing else. It has been mentioned from some of the reciters that he read it in this way, according to this interpretation.

I do not permit reading it - even though it has an understandable aspect in interpretation and Arabic - because the argument of the reciters has agreed to the contrary. So it is not permissible for anyone to object to what they have transmitted unanimously. If it was read in haram with a damma on the ha from haram, then dead would have two aspects of the nominative case. One of them is that the subject is not named, but rather one letter. The other is that in and ma are in the meaning of two letters, and haram is from the connection of ma, and dead is the predicate of alladhi in the nominative case as the predicate. And I am not, even though there is a reason for that, permitting reading it, for what I mentioned. As for the dead woman, the readings differ in its reading.

i: Some of them read it with a light pronunciation, and its meaning is emphasis, but he lightens it as those who say: He is easy and soft, the easy and soft, lighten it, as the poet said:
x: Not everyone who dies and finds rest is dead, but the dead are the dead of the living.
So he combined the two languages in one verse, with one meaning.

Some of them read it with emphasis, and they carried it to the original, and they said: It is Mayyut Fay'al from death. But when the silent Ya and the moving Waw came together, and the Ya with its silence is forward, the Waw was changed to a Ya and stressed, so they became a stressed Ya, as they did in Sayyid and Jawyd. They said: And whoever lightens it, he only sought lightness. And reading it according to its original, which is its origin, is more appropriate.

The correct thing to say about that in my opinion is that lightening and stressing the Ya of Mayyitah are two languages known in reading and in the speech of the Arabs, so whichever one that reader reads is correct. Because there is no difference in their meanings. As for his saying:
h
And what is dedicated to other than God

, he means by it: And what is slaughtered for gods and idols, is called by a name other than His, or he intended by it other than His idols. It was said: And what they have dedicated to other than God because when they wanted to slaughter what they had offered to their gods, they would mention the name of the gods to whom they had offered it, and they would raise their voices in that, and this was how they proceeded from their affair, until it was said to every slaughterer, whether he mentioned the name or not, whether he mentioned the name out loud or not: Mahal.

Their raising their voices in that is the ihram that God the Most High mentioned when He said: And what they have dedicated to other than God. And from that, the one who recites the talbiyah in Hajj or Umrah is called mahal, because he raises his voice in the talbiyah. And from that is the ihram of the child, if he cries out when he falls from his mother’s womb, the ihram of rain, which is the sound of it falling to the ground, as Amr ibn Qumay’ah said: The injustice of the valleys is like the pouring of the rivers, and the clear semen is far from the quarry.
The people of interpretation differed on this.
Some of them said: What he means by his saying:
h
And what is dedicated to other than God is what is slaughtered for Surat Al-Baqarah 2
:173 He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah.
h
But whoever is forced
[by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit],
h
there is no sin upon him
. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. other than God.
Those who said this were:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And what is dedicated to other than God
is what is slaughtered for other than God.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And what has been dedicated to other than God
, he said: what has been slaughtered for other than God, without mentioning the name of God over it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And what has been dedicated to other than God
, what has been slaughtered for other than God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said regarding his statement:
h
And what has been dedicated to other than God
, he said: what has been dedicated to tyrants.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: h
And what has been dedicated to other than God
, he said: what has been dedicated to tyrants.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And what has been dedicated to other than God
, meaning: what has been dedicated to tyrants at all. Meaning: What is slaughtered for other than God by the disbelievers, other than the Jews and Christians.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And what is dedicated to other than God
, he said: It is what is slaughtered for other than God.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: What is mentioned over it other than the name of God.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father,
m: on Al-Rabi’, regarding his statement:
h
And what is dedicated to other than God
, he said: What is mentioned over it other than the name of God.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said - and I asked him about the statement of God:
h
And what is dedicated to other than God

, he said: What is slaughtered for their gods, the idols that they worship and name them with their names. He said: They say: In the name of so-and-so, just as you say: In the name of God. He said: So that is His statement:
h
And what is dedicated to other than God

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Haywah told us, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Muslim al-Tujibi and Qays ibn Rafi’ al-Ashja’i that they said:
m: What is slaughtered for the festival of the churches is lawful for us, and what is given as bread or meat for them is only the food of the People of the Book. Haywah said, I said: What do you think of the statement of God: And that which is dedicated to other than God? He said: That is only for the Magians, the idolaters, and the polytheists.

x: The statement on the interpretation of the statement of God the Most High:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity
, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it],
h
there is no sin upon him
God the Most High meant by His statement:
h
But whoever is forced
, whoever is forced by necessity due to famine to eat what has been forbidden to you of dead animals, blood, pork,
h
and what has been dedicated to other than God
- and it is in the manner we have described -
h
there is no sin upon him
for eating it if he eats it. His statement:
h
But whoever is forced is derived from necessity

. And without transgressing [it] is in the accusative case as a state of whoever, so it is as if it was said: whoever is forced, neither desiring nor transgressing [it], and eats it. It is permissible for him. It has been said that the meaning of his statement,
h
But if one is forced
, is that if someone is forced to eat it and eats it, then there is no sin on him.
Those who said that are mentioned:

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
But if one is forced by necessity

, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], he said: The man is taken by the enemy and they call him to disobey God. As for his statement, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], then the people of interpretation differ in their interpretation of it.

x: Some of them said: What he means by his saying: not a transgressor, is not one who rebels against the leaders with his sword, rebelling against them without injustice, nor transgressing against them with war and aggression, thus corrupting their path.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said:
m: I heard Layth, from Mujahid:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity
, neither transgressing nor aggressing, he said: not cutting off the path, nor separating from the group, nor going out in disobedience to God, then he has a concession.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Nujayh, from Mujahid:
m: h
But whoever is forced by necessity

, neither transgressing nor aggressing, he said: not cutting off the path, nor separating from the leaders, nor going out in disobedience to God, then he has a concession. And whoever goes out transgressing or aggressing in disobedience to God, then he has no concession even if he is forced to do so.

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated to us, he said, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: Neither a transgressor nor aggressor, he said: He is the one who cuts off the road, so he is not permitted to eat carrion if he is hungry, and to drink wine if he is thirsty.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim - meaning Al-Aftas - on the authority of Saeed
m: regarding his statement:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity
, neither desiring nor transgressing, he said: The ordinary transgressor who cuts off the road, so he has no permission or honor.
b.via: Salim - meaning Al-Aftas - on the authority of Saeed

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Al-Hammani narrated to us, he said, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed
m: regarding his statement:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity

, neither desiring nor transgressing, he said: If he goes out in one of the ways of God and is forced to drink wine, he drinks, and if he is forced to eat carrion, he eats. And if he goes out to cut off the road, he has no permission.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said, Hafs bin Ghiyath narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Neither a transgressor, on the authority of the imams, nor aggressor, he said: The highwayman.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
But whoever is forced by necessity
, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], he said: not a highwayman, nor one who leaves the leaders, nor one who goes out in disobedience to God, then he is permitted.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
But whoever is forced by necessity
, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], he said: not desiring [it] against the leaders, nor transgressing against the wayfarer.

x: Others said in interpreting his statement, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it]: not desiring to eat what is forbidden, nor transgressing what is permitted to him from it. He mentioned who said that: Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity

, neither desiring nor transgressing, he said: Neither desiring nor transgressing, meaning that he does not transgress in his eating, nor transgressing: that he transgresses what is lawful into what is unlawful, and he finds an alternative.
Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said:

c: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity

, neither desiring nor transgressing, he said: Neither desiring nor transgressing in eating it, and he has no need of it. Al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Ishaq narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of someone who heard al-Hasan say that. Al-Qasim narrated, he said: Al-Husayn narrated, he said: Abu Tamila narrated, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid and Ikrimah, regarding his statement:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity
, neither desiring nor transgressing, “Neither desiring,” he seeks it, nor transgressing: transgresses what he can hold back. Narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
But whoever is forced by necessity

, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], meaning: without seeking what is forbidden and transgressing it. Don’t you see that He says: But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors. (al-Mu’minun 23:7- al-Maʿarij: 31).

c: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity

, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it], he said: That he eats that out of desiring [it] and transgressing from what is lawful to what is unlawful, and by abandoning what is lawful while he has it, and transgresses by eating this unlawful. This is transgression. He denies that they are different, and he says: This and that are one!

x: Others said that the interpretation of this is:
h
But whoever is forced by necessity
, neither desiring to eat out of desire nor exceeding what he can do without.
Those who said this were:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But whoever is forced by necessity

, neither desiring to eat out of desire nor exceeding what he can do without. As for desiring, he means desiring to eat out of desire. As for the one who eats normally, he transgresses in his eating, he eats until he is full, but he eats from it as much as he can hold himself back from until he fulfills his need.

x: The most correct of these sayings in the interpretation of the verse is the saying of those who said: “
h
But whoever is forced by necessity

, neither desiring to eat what is forbidden to him, nor exceeding what he can do without, and he has an alternative and sufficiency in refraining from eating it - because there is something else that God has permitted for him - and that is because God, the Most High, did not give anyone permission to kill himself under any circumstances.” And since that is the case, there is no doubt that the one who rebels against the Imam and the highway robber, even if they have done what God has forbidden them to do - this one rebelling against someone he has designated, and this one striving to spread corruption on earth - then it is not permissible for them to do what God has forbidden them to do - what God had forbidden them to do before they did what they did - of killing themselves, [and returning them to what God has forbidden them to do after they have done what they have done, even if what they were permitted to do before that was forbidden to them, and even if we do not see returning them to what God has forbidden them to do as a prohibition, then it is not permissible for them to do what was forbidden to them before that].

If this is the case, then it is obligatory for highwaymen and rebels against just leaders to return to the obedience of God, and to return to what God has obligated them to return to, and to repent from the disobedience of God - not to kill themselves through starvation, so that they will increase their sin with a sin, and oppose the command of God. As for the one who directed the interpretation of this to the fact that he did not transgress in his eating out of lust, so he ate that out of lust, not to repel a necessity from which death is feared - which has entered into what God has forbidden him - then it is in the meaning of what we said in its interpretation, even though there is a difference in its wording. As for the direction of the interpretation of His statement: nor transgress, nor eat from it a full portion, but what he holds back for himself, then that is some of the meanings of transgression in eating it.

And God did not specify a meaning from the meanings of transgression in eating it, so it is said that He meant some of its meanings. So since that is the case, then what is correct in what we said is: that it is transgression in all of its forbidden meanings. As for the interpretation of His statement:
h
There is no sin upon him
, he says: Whoever eats that in the manner that we have described, there is no responsibility upon him for eating that in the same way and there is no blame.

The statement on the interpretation of the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful Abu Jaʿfar said: What is meant by His statement, the Most High: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, is Indeed, God is Forgiving, if you obey Surat Al-Baqarah 2:173 He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah.
h
But whoever is forced
[by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit],
h
there is no sin upon him

. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. God in your Islam, and avoid eating what He has forbidden you, and stop following Satan in what you used to forbid in your ignorance - in obedience to Satan and following in his footsteps - of what I have not forbidden you, because of what you have done in your past, in your disbelief and before your Islam, in that of error, sin, and disobedience, so He pardoned you and left your punishment for it, Merciful to you if you obey Him.

evidence.text: It has been mentioned from some of the reciters that he read it in this way, according to this interpretation.
I do not permit reading it - even though it has an understandable aspect in interpretation and Arabic - because the argument of the reciters has agreed to the contrary.
If it was read in haram with a damma on the ha from haram, then dead would have two aspects of the nominative case.
As for the dead woman, the readings differ in its reading.

Some of them read it with a light pronunciation, and its meaning is emphasis, but he lightens it as those who say: He is easy and soft, the easy and soft, lighten it, as the poet said: Not everyone who dies and finds rest is dead, but the dead are the dead of the living.
Some of them read it with emphasis, and they carried it to the original, and they said: It is Mayyut Fay'al from death.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price.

The Almighty means by His saying: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book, the Jewish rabbis who concealed from the people the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prophethood, although they found it written in their Torah, as bribes that they had given for that, as:
