c: Bishr bin Muʿadh told us, Yazid bin Zariʿ told us, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His saying: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book, the entire verse, are the People of the Book, they concealed what God revealed to them and made clear to them of the truth and guidance, of the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his command.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price, he said: They are the People of the Book, they concealed what God revealed to them of the truth, Islam, and the status of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book, these are the Jews, they concealed the name of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: his statement: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book, and the statement in Al-Imran: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price
r
(Al-Imran: 77)

were both revealed about the Jews. As for the interpretation of his statement: and exchange it for a small price, it means: they buy with it. The ha in with it is from the mention of concealment. So its meaning is: they purchased with their concealment what they concealed from the people about the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the matter of his prophethood for a small price. That is because what they were giving—in spite of their distortion of the Book of God and their interpretation of it in a way other than its intended meaning, and their concealment of the truth in that— A small amount of worldly goods, as:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And they exchange it for a small price, he said: They concealed the name of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and took a small taste for it, so it is a small price. And I have previously explained the nature of their purchase of that, so there is no need to repeat it here.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God the Most High: “Those eat nothing into their bellies except the Fire.
h
And God will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection
, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment.”

God the Most High means by His words: Those, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book concerning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by giving them the basest bribes, so they distort the verses of God and change their meanings. They eat nothing into their bellies - by eating what they ate of the bribes and the reward for that, and what they took as wages for it, but the Fire - meaning: except what will lead them to the Fire and burn them in it, as God the Most High said:
Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze

meaning: They eat nothing into their bellies except what will lead them to the Fire by eating it, so He is independent of that. By mentioning to their listeners the meaning of the speech, about mentioning what brings them in or enters them.
And in a manner similar to what we said about that, a group of the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Those eat nothing in their bellies except the Fire, meaning what they took as a reward for it.

x: So can the eating be in something other than the stomach, so it is said: what they eat in their bellies?
The Arabs would say: I was hungry in a place other than my stomach, and I was full in a place other than my stomach.
It was said: In their stomachs for that reason, just as it is said: So-and-so did this to himself. We have explained that in a place other than this, previously. As for His statement:
h
And God will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection

, He says: He will not speak to them with what they love and desire. As for what displeases them and what they hate, He will speak to them, because God, the Most High, has informed us that He will say to them - if they say, Our Lord, take us out of it, but if we return, then we will be wrongdoers - Be gone into it, disgraced, and do not speak to me (al-Mu’minun 23:107, 108). As for His statement: nor will He purify them, He means: nor will He cleanse them from the filth of their sins and disbelief, and for them is a painful punishment, meaning: painful.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying:
h
Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance
and punishment in exchange for forgiveness.
The Almighty means by His saying:
h
Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance

, those who took error, and abandoned guidance, and took what would necessitate for them the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection, and abandoned what would necessitate for them His forgiveness and pleasure. So He dispensed with mentioning the punishment and forgiveness, instead of mentioning the reason that necessitates them, so that the listeners of that would understand its meaning and what is intended by it. We have explained similar examples of that previously. Likewise, we have explained the reason for they have purchased error in exchange for guidance with the differences of those who differed, and the evidence that bears witness to what we have chosen from the statement, in what has passed before, so we disliked repeating it.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty's saying:
h
How patient they are with the Fire
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said that its meaning is: How daring they are to do the work that brings them closer to the Fire.
Who said that: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
How patient they are with the Fire
, he says: How bold they are to do the work that brings them closer to the Fire.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
How patient they are with the Fire
, he says: How bold they are with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Bishr, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
How patient they are with the Fire
, he said: By God, they have no patience with it, but how bold they are with the Fire.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, he said, Misa’ar told us
m: - and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Bakir told us, he said, Misa’ar told us - on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Mujahid, or Saeed bin Jubayr, or some of his companions,
h
How patient they are with the Fire
, how bold they are. Narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
How patient they are with the Fire
, he said: How bold and patient they are with the Fire.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: How much they do the deeds of the people of the Fire.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me,
m: who said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, who said: ʿIsa narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
How patient they are with the Fire
, he said: How much they do with falsehood.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me,
m: who said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. And they differed in the interpretation of what is in his statement:
h
How patient they are with the Fire

x: Some of them said: It is in the sense of a question, and it is as if he said: What made them patient? What made them patient?
Mention of those who said this:

c: Musa ibn Harun narrated to me,
m: who said: ʿAmr narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi: How much they are patient with the Fire, this is in the form of a question. He said:
h
What made them patient with the Fire

c: Abbas bin Muhammad told me, Hajjaj al-Awar told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, Ata’ told me:
m: h
What made them patient with the Fire
h
What made them patient with the Fire
, when they abandoned the truth and followed falsehood?

c: Abu Kurayb told us,
m: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash was asked:
h
What made them patient with the Fire
? He said: This is a question. If it was from patience, he would have said: What made them patient, in the nominative case. He said: It is said to a man: What made you patient? What did this to you?

c: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
What made them patient with the Fire
? He said: This is a question. He says:
h
What made them patient with the Fire
that it made them bold enough to do this?

i: Others said:
x: It is an expression of amazement.
Meaning: How bold they are with the Fire by doing the deeds of the people of the Fire!
Mention of those who said that: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: My father narrated, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
How patient they are with the Fire

! He said: How much they do the deeds of the people of the Fire! This is the saying of al-Hasan and Qatadah, and we have mentioned it before. So whoever says: It is astonishment - he directed the interpretation of the statement to:
h
Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance
and punishment in exchange for forgiveness. How much more audacious they are - by doing what they did - in what will necessitate the Fire for them! As God the Almighty said:
How ungrateful is man!

expressing astonishment at his disbelief in the One who created him and proportioned his creation. As for those who interpreted it as a question, its meaning is: These are the ones who purchased misguidance with guidance and torment with forgiveness.
h
How patient they are with the Fire
- and no one has patience with the Fire - that they exchanged it for God’s forgiveness and took something else from it?

The most appropriate of these sayings to interpret the verse is the saying of those who said: How bold they are with the Fire, meaning: How bold they are with the torment of the Fire and how they do the deeds of its people. This is because it is heard from the Arabs: How patient so-and-so is with God, meaning: How bold so-and-so is with God! God amazes His creation by revealing the report about the people who conceal what God the Blessed and Exalted has revealed about the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prophethood, and their purchase of a small price from the ill-gotten gains and bribes that they gave by concealing that - expressing astonishment at their precedence in that. Knowing that this would cause them to incur God’s wrath and painful punishment. The meaning of this is: How bold they are to face the torment of the Fire! However, mentioning the Fire was sufficient, instead of mentioning its torment, just as it is said: How similar your generosity is to Hatim’s, meaning: How similar your generosity is to Hatim’s generosity, and how similar your bravery is to Antarah’s.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “
h
That is because God has sent down the Book with the truth
And indeed, those who differ over the Book are in extreme dissension.”
As for his saying:
h
That is because God has sent down the Book with the truth
, then there is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of that.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is their action that they are doing - of their audacity in the punishment of the Fire, in their disobedience to the command of God, and their concealment from the people what God revealed in His Book, and His command to explain to them about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the matter of His religion - because God, the Blessed and Exalted, sent down the Book with the truth, and His sending down the Book with the truth is His report about them in His saying to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Indeed, those who disbelieve - it is all the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe. God has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their vision is a veil, and for them is a great punishment.” (al-Baqarah 2:6-7), so they - despite what God has informed about them that they will not believe - will do nothing but buy misguidance with guidance and punishment with forgiveness.

Others said: The meaning of that is known to them, that God sent down the Book with the truth, because we have informed us in the Book that that is for them, and the Book is the truth. It is as if the people who said this interpretation of the verse, according to them, were: That torment - which God Almighty said, How patient they are with it - is known to be for them. Because God has informed in places in His revelation that the Fire is for the disbelievers, and His revelation is true, so the report about that according to them is implied.

Others said: The meaning of that is that God described the people of the Fire, and said: How patient they are with the Fire, then He said: This torment is because of their disbelief. And this here, according to them, is what can be replaced by that, as if he said: We did that because God revealed the Book with the truth and they disbelieved in it. He said: So that - if that is its meaning - would be accusative, and it would be nominative with the preposition with.

The most correct interpretation of the verse in my opinion is that God Almighty indicated by His saying: that to all that is contained in His saying: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book, to His saying:
h
That is because God has sent down the Book in truth

, from His report about the actions of the Jewish rabbis, and His mention of what God Almighty has prepared for them as punishment for that, so He said: This is what these Jewish rabbis did, by concealing from the people what they concealed of the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his prophethood despite their knowledge of it, seeking from them a lowly worldly display - and by their disobedience to My command and obedience, and that - from My not purifying them and sanctifying them and speaking to them, and My preparing for them the painful punishment - is that I sent down My Book in truth, so they disbelieved in it and differed about it. So in that there are two aspects of parsing: nominative and accusative.

The nominative is with the preposition ba, and the accusative means: I did that because I sent down My Book with the truth, but they disbelieved in it and differed about it. He left out mentioning that they disbelieved in it and differed about it, as a sufficiency of the evidence of what was mentioned of the speech about it. As for his statement: And indeed, those who differ over the Scripture are in extreme dissension, meaning by that the Jews and Christians, they differed over the Book of God, so the Jews disbelieved in what God related in it of the stories of Jesus, son of Mary, and his mother. And the Christians believed in some of that, and disbelieved in some of it, and they all disbelieved in what God revealed in it of the command to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he said to his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, those who differed over what was revealed to you, O Muhammad, are in dispute and departure from the truth, far from guidance and correctness, as God, the Most High, said:
So if they believe in the same as you believe, they have been guided, but if they turn away, then they are only in dissension

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And indeed, those who differ over the Scripture are in extreme dissension, meaning: They are the Jews and Christians. He said: They are in extreme enmity. And I have explained the meaning of dissension previously.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his statement.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Righteousness is not prayer alone, but righteousness is the characteristics that I will explain to you.

c: Muhammad bin Sa'd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west

, meaning: prayer. He says: Righteousness is not that you pray and do not work, so this has been the case since the move from Mecca to Medina, and the obligatory duties were revealed, and the limits were set. So God commanded the obligatory duties and working according to them.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: On the authority of Mujahid:
h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west
, but righteousness is that which is established in the heart of obedience to God.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: This verse was revealed in Madinah:
h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west
, meaning prayer. He said: Righteousness is not that you pray and do nothing else. Ibn Jurayj said: And Mujahid said:
h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west
, meaning prostration, but righteousness is that which is established in the heart of obedience to God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Abu Tamilah told us, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, that he said
m: about it, he said: Righteousness is not that you pray and do nothing else. This was when he moved from Mecca to Medina, so God revealed the obligatory duties and set the boundaries in Medina, and ordered the obligatory duties to be followed.

x: Others said: God meant by this the Jews and Christians. The Jews pray facing west, and the Christians pray facing east, so God revealed this verse about them, informing them that righteousness is not the work they do, but it is what we explained in this verse.

Those who said this: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The Jews used to pray facing west and the Christians used to pray facing east, so this verse was revealed:
h
It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west

, but righteousness is [in] one who believes in God and the Last Day. It was mentioned to us that a man asked the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about righteousness, so God revealed this verse. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the man and recited it to him. Before the obligatory duties, if a man testified that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger and then died upon that, he would be hoped for and desired for good. So God revealed:
h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west
. The Jews turned toward the west, and the Christians toward the east. But righteousness is [in] one who believes in God and the Last Day.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas, he said:
m: The Jews used to pray toward the west, and the Christians toward the east, so this verse was revealed:
h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west

x: The most correct of these two interpretations of the verse is the one that Qatada and Qatada bin Anas said: That by His statement:
h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west

, he meant the Jews and the Christians. Because the verses before it proceeded to rebuke and blame them, and to tell about them and the painful torment that was prepared for them. This is in the context of what preceded it, since the matter was thus, Righteousness is not, O Jews and Christians, that some of you turn your faces toward the east and some toward the west, but righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Book the verse. If a woman were to say, How can it be said, ‘But righteousness is he who believes in God,’ and you know that righteousness is a verb and whoever is a noun, so how can the verb be the human being? It would be said: The meaning of that is not what you imagined, but rather its meaning is: but righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day, so whoever was put in place of the verb, sufficing with its indication and the indication of its connection which is an attribute of it, from the deleted verb, as the Arabs do, so they put the nouns in place of their verbs by which they are famous, so you say: generosity is Hatim, and bravery is Antarah, but indeed generosity is Hatim and bravery is Antarah, and its meaning is generosity is the generosity of Hatim, so you dispense with mentioning Hatim since he was known for generosity from repeating mention of generosity after what you have mentioned, so you place it in place of his generosity, because the speech indicates what you have deleted, dispensing with What you mentioned about what you did not mention.
As it was said, And ask the town in which we were
r
(Yusuf 12:82)

, and the meaning is: the people of the town, and as the poet said, and he is the one with the cooking rag: I thought my camel's embrace was an embrace! What is it? Who else can embrace you? He means: with the sound of a hug, or the sound of a hug, as one says: I thought my crying was your brother, meaning to him: I thought my crying was your brother’s crying. It may be possible that the meaning of the statement is: But the righteous is he who believes in God, so righteousness is a source placed in place of the noun.
God the Almighty means by His statement:
h
And gives wealth
, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and for the freeing of slaves.
He gave his wealth while he loved it, was stingy with it, and was miserly with it, as Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Saʿib told us, they said:

c: Ibn Idris told us,
m: he heard Layth, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Murrah ibn Shurahil al-Bukayli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masʿud:
h
And gives wealth
, in spite of love for it, meaning: he gives it while he is healthy and stingy, hoping to live and fearing poverty.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us
m: - and al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us - they both said, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Zubayd al-Yami, on the authority of Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah:
h
And gives wealth
, in spite of love for it, he said: And you are healthy, hoping to live and fearing poverty.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Zubayd al-Yami, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said
m: regarding this verse: And he gives away wealth, despite his love for it, he said: And you are greedy and stingy, hoping for wealth, and fearing poverty. Ahmad bin Na'mah Al-Masry narrated, Abu Saleh narrated, Al-Layth narrated, Ibrahim bin A'yan narrated, on the authority of Shu'bah bin Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Zubayd Al-Yami, on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamadani, who said: Abdullah bin Mas'ud said regarding the statement of God: And gives his wealth, in spite of love for it, to his relatives, he said: Eager and stingy, hoping for wealth and fearing poverty. Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub bin Ibrahim narrated, they said: Hisham narrated, he said: Ismail bin Salim narrated, on the authority of Al-Sha'bi, I heard him being asked: Does a man have any right on his wealth other than zakat? He said: Yes! And he recited this verse: "And gives his wealth, in spite of love for it, to his relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask [for help], and to free slaves. And he establishes prayer and gives zakat." Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Suwaid bin Amr Al-Kalbi narrated, he said: Hammad bin Salamah narrated, he said: Abu Hamza narrated, he said: I said to Al-Sha'bi: If a man purifies his wealth, does his wealth become good for him? Then he recited this verse:
h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west

to and give away wealth, though you love it to the end of it. Then he said: Fatima bint Qais told me that she said: O Messenger of God, I have seventy mithqals of gold. So he said: Give it to your relatives.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, he said: Abu Hamza told us
m: - as far as I know - on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Fatima bint Qais that she heard him say: There is a right in wealth other than zakat.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:
m: h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west
, but righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets
h
and gives wealth
, in spite of love for Him, to relatives and orphans and the needy
h
and the wayfarer
and those who ask and for the freeing of slaves and establishes prayer and gives zakah And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made it,
h
and those who are patient in poverty and hardship
and during battle - those are the ones who have been true,
h
and those are the righteous

. Abu Hayyan, he said: Muzahim bin Zafar said, I was sitting with Ata’ when a Bedouin came to him and said to him: I have camels, do I have a right over them after the zakat? He said: Yes! He said: What? He said: The loan of the bucket, the stallion’s mount, and milking.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: he mentioned it on the authority of Marra Al-Hamadani in: And he gives away wealth, despite his love for it, he said: Abdullah bin Masoud said: You give it to him while you are healthy and stingy, you prolong hope, and you fear poverty. He also mentioned on the authority of Al-Suddi that this is something obligatory regarding wealth, and it is the right of the owner of the wealth to do it, other than what he owes of zakat.

c: Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Sulayman, who said: Asad told us, Suwaid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Fatima bint Qays, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There is a right in wealth other than zakat, and he recited this verse: There is no righteousness to the end of the verse.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Zubayd al-Yami, on the authority of Murrah ibn Sharahil, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And he gives wealth
, despite his love for it, he said: That a man gives it while he is healthy and stingy with it, hoping to live and fearing poverty.

x: The interpretation of the verse is:
h
And he gives wealth

- although he loves it, is keen to collect it, and is stingy with it - to his relatives, so he maintains ties of kinship with it. I only said that he meant by his statement: relatives, the relatives of the one who gives the money despite his love for it, because of the report narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his command to Fatima bint Qays. And his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was asked: Which charity is best? He said: The effort of the poor for the sake of the greedy relative. As for orphans and the needy, we have explained their meanings previously. As for the wayfarer, he is the one who passes by a man. Then the scholars differed regarding his description.
Some of them said: He is the guest in that regard.
Those who said that mentioned: Bishr ibn Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada:
h
And the wayfarer

he said, he is the guest. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent. He said: And he used to say: The right of hospitality is three nights, and everything he hosts after that is charity.

Some of them said: He is the traveler who passes by you. Those who mentioned that mentioned: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said, my father narrated, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja’far:
h
And the wayfarer
he said: The one who passes by from one land to another.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid and Qatada
m: regarding His statement:
h
And the wayfarer
he said: The one who passes by you is a traveler.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Suwaid ibn Nasr narrated to us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, on the authority of the one
m: who mentioned it, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid and Qatada, similarly. The traveler is called Ibn al-Sabil because he is always on the road - and the road is the path - so he is called Ibn al-Ma'a because he is always on it during his journey, just as a water bird is called Ibn al-Ma'a because he is always on it, and a man who has been through the ages is called Ibn al-Days, Nights, and Times. From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: It was mentioned arbitrarily, and the Pleiades were like a shaved head of water As for his saying: and those who ask, he means by it: those who seek food and demand it, such as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding His statement: and those who ask, he said: the one who asks you. As for His statement: and for the slaves, he means by that: and for the release of slaves from slavery 1, and they are the freed slaves who strive to release their slaves from slavery by fulfilling their contracts upon which they parted from their masters.

x: The statement on the interpretation of the statement of God Almighty: and establish prayer and give zakat and those who fulfill their covenant when they have made a covenant, Abu Jaʿfar said: God Almighty means by His statement: and establish prayer that he continued to work on it within its limits.
And by His statement: and give zakat, he gave it according to what God had imposed on him.
Is there a right in wealth that must be given obligatorily other than zakat?

The people of interpretation differed on this: Some of them said: It contains rights that are obligatory other than zakat, and they based their statement on this verse, and they said: When God the Blessed and Exalted said:
h
And gives wealth

, in spite of love for it, to the near of kin, and those whom God named with them, then He said after that: And establishes prayer and gives zakat, we know that the wealth - which He described the believers with that they give to their near of kin and those whom He named with them - is not the zakat that He mentioned that they give. Because if that were one wealth, there would be no clear meaning to repeating it.

They said: Since it is not permissible for God the Exalted to say something that has no meaning, we know that the ruling on the first wealth is not zakat, and that the zakat that He mentioned after is not it. They said: And after that, the interpretation of the people of interpretation has shown the correctness of what we said about that. - Others said: Rather, the first wealth is zakat, but God described giving to the believers from those who gave it to Him, at the beginning of the verse. So He informed His servants - by His description of what He described of their affair - the places where they must put their zakat, then He guided them by His saying after that: and give zakat, that the wealth that the people gave to Him is the zakat that was imposed on them, since the people of its shares were those whom He informed at the beginning of the verse that the people gave their wealth to.

As for His saying: and those who fulfill their covenant when they made a covenant, then He, the Most High, means: and those who do not break the covenant of God after the covenant, but rather fulfill it and complete it according to what they covenanted with those they made a covenant with Him, as:

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatadah ibn Anas, regarding His saying: and those who fulfill their covenant when they made a covenant, he said: So whoever gives a covenant of God and then breaks it, then God will take revenge on him. Whoever pledges his allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then betrays it, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be his opponent on the Day of Resurrection. I have explained the covenant previously, so that there is no need to repeat it here.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And the patient in
h
poverty and hardship
We have already explained the interpretation of patience previously. The meaning of the statement is: And those who prevent themselves - in
h
poverty and hardship
h
and at the time of battle
- from what God dislikes for them, and who restrain themselves from what He has commanded them to do of obeying Him.
Then the people of interpretation said in the meaning of
h
poverty and hardship
what:

c: Al-Husayn bin ʿAmr bin Muhammad Al-ʿAnqazi told me, he said, my father told me
m: - and Musa told me, he said, ʿAmr bin Hammad told us - they both said, Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamadani, on the authority of Ibn Masʿud that he said: As for poverty, it is poverty, and as for hardship, it is sickness.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us
m: - and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us - they both said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding His statement:
h
And those who are patient in poverty and hardship
, he said: poverty is hunger, and hardship is sickness.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: poverty is need, and hardship is sickness.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: We used to say that poverty is misery and poverty, and hardship is illness. And the Prophet Job, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.
r
(Al-Anbiya’: 83)
Narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And those who are patient in poverty and hardship
, he said: Misery means want and poverty, and hardship is in the soul, from pain or illness that afflicts him in his body.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us,
m: who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Muʿammar informed us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement:
h
Poverty and hardship
, he said: Misery means destitution, and hardship is the time in the body.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me,
m: who said: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, who said: Ubayd narrated to us, on the authority of al-Dahhak, who said:
h
Poverty and hardship
, is illness.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us,
m: who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
h
And those who are patient in poverty and hardship
, he said: Misery means destitution and poverty, and hardship is illness and pain.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Ubayd ibn al-Tufayl told us:
m: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say about this verse:
h
And those who are patient in poverty and hardship
. As for poverty, it is poverty, and hardship is illness.

x: As for the Arab scholars, they differed about that.

Some of them said: al-Basaʿ and al-Dhraʿ is a verbal noun that came in the form faʿalaʿ without afʿal because it is a noun, just as afʿal came in the form faʿalaʿ, such as Ahmad. And they said afʿal in the adjective, but it did not come in the form faʿalaʿ, so they said: You are more afraid of that, and they did not say wajal.
Some of them said: It is a noun for the verb. For al-Basaʿ is misery, and al-Dhraʿ is distress.

i: It is a noun that can be used for a feminine, if you wish, or for a masculine, as Zuhair said:
x: Then she will produce for you unlucky boys, all of them like the red ones of Ad. Then she will suckle and be weaned.
Meaning: So it will produce for you ill-omened boys.

Some of them said: If that were a noun that could be declined into masculine and feminine, it would be permissible to use af’al for the indefinite, but it is a noun that takes the place of a verbal noun. The evidence for that is his statement: If you seek their support, you will find them not far away, without using af’al. He said: It was a noun for a verbal noun, because if it is mentioned, it is known that it is intended for a verbal noun.

Another said: If that were a verbal noun and it was feminine, it would not be masculine, and if it was masculine, it would not be feminine. Because Whoever is named after Af'al is not declined to 'ala, and whoever is named after 'ala is not declined to Af'al, because every noun that remains in its form is not declined to another, but they are two languages. So if it is in the masculine, it is in a more ominous matter, and if it is al-basa' and al-darra', it is: the trait is al-basa' and the trait is al-darra'. And if it is not based on al-darra', al-adhar, nor on al-ash'am, al-shama' because the masculinity was not intended from its femininity, nor the femininity from its masculinity, as Surat Al-Baqarah 2:177
h
Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west
, but righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets
h
and gives wealth
, in spite of love for Him, to relatives and orphans and the needy
h
and the wayfarer
and those who ask and for the freeing of slaves and establishes prayer and gives zakah And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made it,
h
and those who are patient in poverty and hardship
and during battle - those are the ones who have been true,
h
and those are the righteous
. they said a beautiful woman, and they did not say: a beautiful man, and they said: a beardless man, and they did not say: a woman with a cloak.

So if it is said: the trait is al-darra' and the matter is al-ash'am, it indicates the source, and does not need to be a name, even though the source is sufficient. This is a statement that contradicts the interpretation of those scholars whose interpretation we mentioned in the interpretation of al-basa' and al-darra', even though it is correct according to the Arabic school. This is because the people of interpretation interpreted al-basa’ to mean: misery, and al-darra’ to mean: harm to the body. This interpretation of theirs is based on the fact that they directed al-basa’ and al-darra’ to the names of actions, not the attributes and descriptions of the names. So what is more appropriate for al-basa’ and al-darra’ according to the people of interpretation is that al-basa’ and al-darra’ are the names of actions, so al-basa’ is a name for misery, and al-darra’ is a name for harm. As for the patient ones, it is in the accusative case, and it is from the description of man in the manner of praise.

i: Because it is the custom of the Arabs - if the description of one is prolonged - to interrupt with praise and blame in the accusative sometimes, and in the nominative sometimes, as the poet said:
x: To the venerable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded place This is the opinion when things get dark with the same clang and the same bridle So, the word battalion and this opinion are in the accusative case for praise, and the noun before them is in the genitive case because it is an attribute of one, and from this is the saying of the other: I wish that the stars would be humble towards all of them, good and bad.
The rains of the world are in every place, and the lions of the Sharia protect every den.

Some of them claimed that his statement, and those who are patient in poverty, is an accusative in apposition to those who ask, as if the meaning of the statement was: And he gave wealth, in spite of his love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask,
h
and those who are patient in poverty and hardship
. The apparent meaning of the Book of God indicates the error of this statement. That is because
h
and those who are patient in poverty and hardship

are the people of the time in terms of their bodies, and the people of scarcity in terms of money. The description of the people who give money—whoever has that characteristic—has already been mentioned in His statement, and the needy, the traveler, and those who ask. The people of need and poverty are the people of
h
poverty and hardship
, because whoever is not among the people of poverty and has hardship, is not among those who can accept charity.

Rather, it can be accepted if he combines his hardship with hardship, and if he combines it with hardship, he is among the people of poverty who have entered into the group of the needy who were mentioned before His statement, and those who are patient in poverty. If that is the case, then the patient ones in hardship is made accusative by saying and give wealth, out of love for Him, the speech is a repetition without any meaningful benefit. It is as if it was said: and give wealth, out of love for Him, to relatives, orphans, and the needy. And God is too exalted to have that be in addressing His servants. But the meaning of that is: but righteous is he who believes in God and the Last Day, and those who fulfill their covenant when they make it, and those who are patient in hardship and distress. And those who fulfill is in the nominative case, because it is an attribute of whoever, and whoever is in the nominative case, so it is declined according to its declension.
And those who are patient is in the accusative case - even though it is an attribute of it - in the manner of praise that we described before.
God the Most High meant by His saying:
h
and at the time of battle
, and those who are patient at the time of battle, which is the time of intense fighting in war, as:

c: Al-Husayn ibn ʿAmr ibn Muhammad Al-ʿAnqazi told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of ʿAbdullah,
m: regarding God’s statement:
h
and at the time of battle
, he said: at the time of fighting.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And at the time of battle
means fighting.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And at the time of battle
means at the sites of fighting.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And at the time of battle
means fighting.

c: I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
h
And at the time of battle
means when meeting the enemy.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Nuʿaym told us, he said, Ubaydah told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And at the time of battle
means fighting.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Ubayd ibn al-Tufayl Abu Saydan narrated to us,
m: I heard Adh-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say about His statement,
h
And at the time of battle
, he said: Fighting.

x: What the Almighty means by His statement,
h
Those are the ones who have been truthful

, is those who believe in God and the Last Day, and He described them with the description that He described them with in this verse. He says: So whoever does these things, they are the ones who have been truthful to God in their faith, and have fulfilled their words with their actions, not the one who turns his face toward the sunrise and the sunset while disobeying God in His command, and breaking His covenant and pact, and concealing from people what God has commanded him to be explained, and lying about His messengers. As for His statement,
h
And those are the righteous

, it means: And those are the ones who feared God’s punishment, so they avoided disobeying Him, and were wary of His promise, so they did not violate His limits. And they feared Him, so they performed His obligations. And similar to what we said about His statement,
h
Those are the ones who have been truthful
, Qatada ibn Anas used to say.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: Those are the ones who were truthful. He said: They spoke the words of faith, and its reality was action. They were truthful to God. He said: Al-Hasan used to say: These are the words of faith, and its reality is action. If there is no action with the words, then there is nothing.

evidence.text: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the man and recited it to him.
And he recited this verse: "And gives his wealth, in spite of love for it, to his relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask [for help], and to free slaves.
Then he recited this verse: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west to and give away wealth, though you love it to the end of it.

Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Sulayman, who said: Asad told us, Suwaid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Fatima bint Qays, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There is a right in wealth other than zakat, and he recited this verse: There is no righteousness to the end of the verse.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder
, that it is obligatory upon you.
Is it obligatory upon the guardian of the murdered person to retribution for the murder of his guardian?
No, but it is permissible for him to do so, and to pardon, and to take blood money.
How did He say:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you

The meaning of that is contrary to what you have gone to, and rather its meaning is: “O you who have believed, retribution is prescribed for you in cases of murder: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female,” meaning: If a free man kills a free man, then the blood of the murderer is equal to the blood of the murdered person, and retribution is from him and not from others among the people, so do not go beyond killing to others who did not kill, for it is forbidden for you to kill someone other than the murderer for your murdered person. The obligation that God imposed on us in retaliation is what I described of leaving the transgression of retaliation from killing the killer for his victim to someone else, not that retaliation was imposed on us as an obligation like the obligation of prayer and fasting, so that we would not have the right to abandon it. If that were an obligation that we are not permitted to abandon, then His statement,
h
But if he is pardoned by his brother
, there is nothing, would not have had an understood meaning. Because there is no pardon after retaliation, so it is said,
h
But if he is pardoned by his brother
, there is nothing. It has been said that the meaning of retaliation in this verse is to set off the blood money of some of the dead with the blood money of others.

That is because the verse They revealed it about two parties that fought during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of them killed each other. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that reconciliation be made between them by dropping the blood money of the women of one party to the blood money of the women of the other party, and the blood money of their men to the blood money of their men, and the blood money of their slaves to the blood money of their slaves, in retaliation. So that is, to them, the meaning of retaliation in this verse.
God Almighty said: “
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder

: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.” So why do we have the right to take revenge for the free except from the free, and for the female except from the female?

Rather, we have the right to take revenge for the free from the slave, and for the female from the male, based on the statement of God Almighty: And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority
r
(Al-Isra’: 33)
and based on the widespread transmission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The blood of Muslims is equal.
So if that is the case, what is the interpretation of this verse?
The people of interpretation differed on that.

Some of them said: This verse was revealed about a people who, if a man among them killed a slave of another people, would not be satisfied with the blood of their killer because he was a slave, until they killed his master in return. And if a woman from outside them killed a man, they would not be satisfied with the blood of their companion in return for the woman who killed him, until they killed a man from the woman’s relatives and clan. Then God revealed this verse, informing them that what He had ordained for them in terms of retaliation was that they should kill for a man the male killer and not another man, and for a female the female killer and not another man, and for a male slave the male killer and not another free man. So He forbade them from seeking the killer’s help from another man in retaliation.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu al-Walid told us
m: - and al-Muthanna told me, he said, al-Hajjaj told us. They said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, regarding His statement:
h
A free man for a free man
, a slave for a slave,
h
and a female for a female

, he said: It was revealed about two tribes of Arabs who fought in blind combat, and they said: We will kill for our slave so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and for so-and-so, so-and-so, son of so-and-so. So God revealed:
h
A free man for a free man
, a slave for a slave,
h
and a female for a female

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder

: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female,” he said: The people of the Age of Ignorance were unjust and obeyed Satan. So if a tribe had a number of people and were strong, and a slave of another people killed a slave of theirs, they would say: We will not kill anyone but a free man in return! Out of pride, because of their superiority over others in their eyes. And if a woman of theirs was killed, and the woman of another people killed her, they would say: We will not kill anyone but a man in return! So God revealed this verse informing them that a slave is for a slave and a female is for a female, so He forbade them from unjust treatment. Then God the Almighty revealed His remembrance in Surat Al-Ma’idah after that, saying: “And We ordained for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds there is retaliation” (al-Ma’idah 5:45).

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder

, he said: For those before us, there was no blood money, it was only killing, or pardoning his family. So this verse was revealed about a people who were more numerous than others, so if a large number of slaves were killed from a tribe, they would say: We will not kill anyone but a free man in return for it. And if a woman was killed among them, they would say: We will not kill anyone but a man in return for it. So God revealed:
h
A free man for a free man
, a slave for a slave, a female for a female.

c: Muhammad bin Abd Al-A’la told me, he said, Al-Mu’tamir told us, he said,
m: I heard Dawud, on the authority of Amer, regarding this. The verse: “
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder

: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.” He said: This is only in cases of blind fighting, if one of these is a slave and the other is a slave, they are equal. Likewise in cases of two women, and likewise in cases of two free men. This is its meaning, God willing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The statement of God Almighty: The free for the free includes a man for a woman, and a woman for a man. Ata’ said: There is no preference between them.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed about two groups between whom there was fighting during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group of men and women were killed from each group, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that reconciliation be made between them, by making the blood money of the women from each group retaliation for the blood money of the women from the other group, and the blood money of the men for the men, and the blood money of the slaves for the slaves. This is the meaning of his statement:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder
He who said that: Musa bin Harun told us:

c: Amr bin Hammad told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder

: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.” He said: The people of two Arab tribes fought, one of them a Muslim and the other a covenanted one, in some of the matters that occur between the Arabs, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reconciled between them and they had killed the free, the slaves, and the women - on the condition that the free man pay the blood money of the free man, the slave pay the blood money of the slave, and the female pay the blood money of the female, so some of them paid retribution from each other.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Abdullah bin al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said:
m: There was fighting between two tribes of the Ansar, one of them had the upper hand over the other, so it was as if they were seeking the advantage. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to reconcile between them, and this verse was revealed: The free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. So the Prophet (peace Surat Al-Baqarah 2:178 O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution in the case of those murdered - the free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female. But if any remission is made by his brother, there should be a just pursuit and payment to him with good conduct. That is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy.
h
But whoever transgresses after
that will have a severe punishment. Painful and blessings of God be upon him) made the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, who said:
m: I heard al-Sha’bi say about this verse:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder
. He said: It was revealed about a blind fight. Shu’bah said: It was as if it was about a peace treaty. He said: They agreed on this.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, who said:
m: I heard al-Shaʿbi say about this verse: “
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder

: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.” He said: It was revealed regarding the fight against a blind man. He said: It was during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a command from God, the Most High, to set off the blood money of a free man against the blood money of a slave, the blood money of a male against the blood money of a female, in the case of premeditated murder - if retribution is taken for the murdered person from the murderer - and to take back the excess and increase between the blood money of the murdered person and the blood money taken from him.
He who said that: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: “O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution for those killed: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.” He said: He told us on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib that he used to say: Any free man who kills a slave is liable for retaliation. If the masters of the slave wish to kill the free man, they should kill him and retaliate against them for the price of the slave from the blood money of the free man, and they should pay the masters of the free man the rest of his blood money. If a slave kills a free man, he is liable for retaliation. If the guardians of the free man wish, they may kill the slave and exact retribution for the price of the slave, and take the rest of the free man’s blood money. If they wish, they may take the entire blood money and spare the slave. Any free man who kills a woman is liable for retaliation. If the woman’s guardians wish, they may kill him and pay half the blood money to the guardians of the free man. If a woman kills a free man, she is liable for retaliation. If the guardians of the free man wish, they may kill her and take half the blood money. If they wish, they may take the entire blood money and spare her. If they wish, they may pardon her.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan: Ali said
m: about a man who killed his wife, he said: If they wish, they can kill him and pay half the blood money.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: saying: A man is not to be killed for a woman until they are given half the blood money.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said
m: about a man who killed his wife intentionally, so they brought him to Ali, and he said: If you wish, kill him, and return the excess of the man’s blood money to the woman’s.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed in the same situation when it was revealed, and the people did not kill a man for a woman, but they used to kill a man for a man, and a woman for a woman, until God made the ruling of all of them equal by saying: And We ordained for them therein that a life is for a life (al-Ma’idah 5:45), so He made all of them equal to one another in retaliation.
Those who said that: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying:
h
And a female for a female

, that is because they did not kill a man for a woman, but they killed a man for a man and a woman for a woman, so God Almighty revealed: A life for a life (al-Ma’idah 5:45) and made the free men and women equal in retaliation, in deliberate murder, in a life and what is less than a life. And he made the slaves equal in deliberate murder, in a life and what is less than a life, their men and women.

Since there was a difference in the difference that you described, in what this verse was revealed about, then it is obligatory for us to use it, in what it indicates of the ruling, with the decisive report that is an excuse. And the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been transmitted in a general manner: that the life of a free man is retaliation for the life of a free woman. So since that is the case, and the nation differed in reversing the difference between the blood money of the man and the woman - according to what we have explained from the statement of Ali and others - then it was clear that the statement of those who said retaliation in that and reversing the difference between the two blood moneys is corrupt, with the consensus of all the people of Islam: that it is forbidden for a man to destroy a limb of his body in exchange for compensation that he takes for its destruction, so leave all of it, and that it is forbidden for someone else to know that a part of it was destroyed - like what was forbidden from that - in exchange for compensation that he gives for it.
So it is obligatory that the life of a free man be retaliation for the life of a free woman. Since this is the case, it is clear that the statement of God the Almighty:
h
A free man for a free man
, a slave for a slave,
h
and a female for a female

does not mean that a slave is not to be killed for a free man, nor that a female is to be killed for a male, nor a male for a female. Since this is the case, it is clear that the verse is intended to mean one of the other two meanings. Either our statement: that retaliation does not extend beyond the killer and the offender, so the male is to be taken for the female and the free man is taken for the slave. Or the other statement: that the verse was revealed regarding specific people in particular, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was ordered to make the blood money of their dead retaliation, some for others, as al-Suddi and those we mentioned said.

And all have agreed - there is no disagreement among them - that litigation in rights is not obligatory, and they have agreed that God did not issue a ruling in this regard and then abrogated it. Since this is the case, and His statement,
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you

indicates that it is obligatory, it is known that the statement is contrary to what the speaker of this statement said. Because what was obligatory for those with rights to do, they have no choice in it. And everyone agrees that those with rights have the choice in their set-off of their rights from one another. So since the corruption of this view that we mentioned has become clear, then the correct statement in that regard is what we said.
Since you mentioned that the meaning of his statement:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you

means: Retaliation is imposed on you - the meaning of the statement of the speaker: He wrote is not known except for the meaning: He wrote that, so he drew a line and a book, so what is your proof that the meaning of his statement: He wrote is obligatory?

That is found in the speech of the Arabs, and is widespread in their poetry, and from it is the saying of the poet: Killing and fighting are against us, and chaste women should drag their tails. And the saying of the genius of Bani Ja'dah: My cousin, the Book of God has expelled me from you. Did God prevent what they did? This is more in their poetry and speech than can be counted. However, even if it means: an obligation, I think it is taken from the book which is a drawing and writing.

This is because God, the Most High, has written everything that He has imposed on His servants and what they are to do in the Preserved Tablet. God, the Most High, said in the Qur’an: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, in a Preserved Tablet (al-Buruj 85:1-2: 22), and He said: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an, in a Book well-guarded (al-Waqi’ah 56:77-78). It has thus become clear that everything that He has imposed on us is written in the Preserved Tablet. So the meaning of His statement - since that is the case -
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you

is that retribution for the murdered is prescribed for you in the Preserved Tablet, that you do not kill anyone other than the murderer for the murdered person. As for retaliation, it is from the saying of the speaker: I have repaid so-and-so my right before him from his right before me, as retribution and set-off. So killing the killer for the one he killed is retaliation, because it is the object of the action like what was done to the one he killed, even if one of the two actions was aggression and the other was right.

So even though they differ in this respect, they agree that each one did to his companion the same as his companion did to him. And the action of the guardian of the first slain person, if he killed the killer of his guardian, was made retaliation, because it was because of his killing that he deserved to kill the one who killed him, so it is as if the guardian of the slain person is the one who took charge of killing his killer, so he took retaliation from him. As for the slain, it is the plural of slain, just as the slain is the plural of slain, and the wounded is the plural of wounded. The active participle is only pluralized as fa’il if it is an attribute of the described, in the sense of time and harm that prevents its owner from leaving his place and place of death, like the slain in their battles, the slain in their places, the wounded, and the like. So the interpretation of the statement then: Retaliation for the slain is imposed upon you, O believers: that the free man take retaliation for the free man.
And the slave for the slave, and the female for the female.. Then he left out the mention of retaliation, being satisfied with the indication of his saying:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you
, on him.
The commentators differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: Its interpretation is: If someone is left to be killed unjustly, from what is due to him, his brother will have to pay retaliation - which is the thing that God said:
h
But if someone is pardoned by his brother
- then the one who pardons follows the killer with what is due to him before him from the blood money, and the one who is pardoned pays it to him with kindness.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Abu Kurayb and Ahmad ibn Hammad al-Dawlabi told us, they said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
But if someone is pardoned by his brother
, so pardoning means accepting the blood money in the case of premeditated murder, and following with kindness means asking for this with kindness and paying this with kindness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, he said, Amr bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said
m: regarding His statement:
h
But if someone is pardoned by his brother

, then there is a reasonable pursuit and payment to him with goodness, he said: It is the deliberate killing, and his family is satisfied with the blood money, and a reasonable pursuit: the one who demands it is ordered by the one seeking it, and payment to him with goodness from the one sought.

c: Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us, he said, my father told us
m: - and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us - they both said, Ibn Al-Mubarak informed us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Muslim, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The one who accepts the blood money, that is a pardon from him and a reasonable pursuit, and he pays to him what was pardoned by his brother with goodness.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if any one is pardoned by his brother

, then there should be a follow-up within reasonable limits and payment to him with goodness, which is the blood money: that the one who is asked should do a good job of asking, and payment to him with goodness: which is that the one who is asked should do a good job of paying. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:178 O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution in the case of those murdered - the free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female. But if any remission is made by his brother, there should be a just pursuit and payment to him with good conduct. That is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy.
h
But whoever transgresses after
that will have a severe punishment.

c: Painful Muhammad Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
But if any one is pardoned by his brother
, then there should be a follow-up within reasonable limits and payment to him with goodness, and the pardon is the one who pardons the blood money and takes the blood money.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
But if any one is pardoned by his brother

, he said: the blood money. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said, my father narrated, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, And pay it to him with kindness, he said: This seeker must ask with kindness, and this sought must pay it with kindness. Al-Muthanna narrated, he said, Abu Hudhayfah narrated, he said, Shibl narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
But if someone is pardoned by his brother

, then there is a follow-up in kindness, and pardoning is the one who pardons the blood money and takes the blood money. Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna narrated, he said, Abu Al-Walid narrated, he said, Hammad narrated, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement:
h
But if someone is pardoned by his brother

, then there is a follow-up in kindness and a payment to him with kindness, he said: It is deliberate, and his family is satisfied with the blood money. Al-Muthanna narrated, he said, Al-Hajjaj narrated, he said, Hammad narrated, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, similarly. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
But if someone is pardoned by his brother

, then there should be a follow-up in accordance with what is acceptable and payment to him with goodness, meaning someone who killed intentionally and was pardoned, and the blood money was accepted from him. He says: Then a follow-up in accordance with what is acceptable, so he ordered the follow-up to be followed in accordance with what is acceptable, and he ordered the payment to be made with goodness, and the intentional killing should be repaid in retaliation, without blood money, unless they are satisfied with blood money. If they are satisfied with blood money, then a hundred female offspring are required.

x: If they say: We will not be satisfied except with such and such, then that is theirs.
Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said:

c: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Then a follow-up in accordance with what is acceptable and payment to him with goodness, he said: The one who asked for it should be followed in accordance with what is acceptable, and the one who asked should be paid with goodness.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
But if someone is pardoned by his brother

, then there should be a reasonable follow-up and payment to him with kindness, he said: So if someone is killed intentionally and is pardoned, and the blood money is taken from him, he said: then there should be a reasonable follow-up, he ordered the person who takes the blood money to follow up with kindness, and he ordered the one who pays it to pay it with kindness.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I said to Ata’: His statement:
h
But if someone is pardoned by his brother
, then there should be a follow-up within reasonable limits and payment to him with goodness, he said: That is if he takes the blood money, then he is pardoned.

c: Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza informed me, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: If he accepts the blood money, then he has pardoned retaliation, so that is his statement:
h
But if someone is pardoned by his brother

, then there should be a follow-up within reasonable limits and payment to him with goodness, Ibn Jurayj said: Al-A’raj informed me, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar to that, and he added to it: - If he accepts the blood money, then he must follow up within reasonable limits, and the one who was pardoned must pay with goodness.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim narrated to us, he said, Abu Uqayl narrated to us, he said, Al-Hasan said:
m: Taking the blood money is a good pardon.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And pay it to him with kindness, he said: You, the one who is pardoned.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: his statement:
h
But if any one is pardoned by his brother

, then there should be a follow-up in kindness and payment to him with kindness, which is the blood money, that the one who asks for it should do good, and payment to him with kindness: is that the one who is asked should do good.

x: Others said that the meaning of his statement:
h
But if any one is pardoned

, is that he has a surplus, and he has a remainder. They said: The meaning of his statement: Something from his brother is: something from the blood money of his brother, or from the compensation for his wound, so the killer or the injurer should follow up from him what remained of that before him - with kindness, and payment - from the killer or the injurer - to him what remained of that before him with kindness. This is the statement of those who claimed that the verse was revealed - I mean his statement: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is retaliation for those killed - regarding those who fought during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they should reconcile, so that the blood money of some of them would be paid to others, and some of them would be given more than what they had left before the others.

And I think that those who said this statement directed the interpretation of forgiveness - in this place - to: the abundance of the statement of God the Most High: until they pardon (al-A’raf 7:95). So the meaning of the statement according to them is: whoever has more than what he has before his brother the killer.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
So whoever has been pardoned by his brother in any way

, meaning: he has something left of his brother’s blood money or of the compensation for his wound, then let him follow up with kindness, and let the other party pay him in kindness. And what is required in the interpretation of the statement that we narrated from Ali and Al-Hasan - in his statement:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you

is that it means: settling the blood money of a male soul from the blood money of a female soul, and of a slave from a free man, and returning the excess of what is between their blood moneys - is that the meaning of his statement:
h
So whoever has been pardoned by his brother in any way

, is: whoever Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct statement in my opinion is in his statement: But if his brother pardons him something: So if he pardons him - from the obligation, his brother has to pay him retaliation - for something of the obligation, on blood money that he takes from him, so he should follow up with what is acceptable - from the one who pardons the blood, who is satisfied with the blood money from the blood of his guardian - and he should pay to him - from the killer - that with kindness. Because we have explained from the reasons in what came before: that the meaning of the statement of God Almighty:
h
