Retaliation is prescribed for you

, is only retribution from the souls of the killer who kills or wounds or injures intentionally. Likewise, forgiveness is also for that. As for the meaning of his statement: Then follow up with what is acceptable, it means: follow up on what God has made obligatory for him from the right before the killer of his guardian, without adding to it what he is not entitled to - in the teeth of the obligatory duties or other than that - or charging him Unless God has made it obligatory for him, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It has reached us from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever increases or adds a camel - meaning in the camels of blood money and its obligations - then it is from the matter of the Jahiliyyah. As for the other’s kindness in performing, it is performing what he is obligated to perform for the guardian of the slain person, according to what God has made obligatory for him and made obligatory for him, without depriving him of a right he has before him because of that, or requiring him to collect and demand it.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How was it said: Then follow up with kindness and perform it with kindness, and not say then follow up with kindness and perform it with kindness, as He said: So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike the necks
r
(Muhammad 47:4)

If the revelation had come in the accusative case, and it had been: then follow up with kindness and perform it with kindness - it would have been permissible in Arabic and correct, in the form of a command, as it is said: strike, strike, and if you meet someone, then with reverence. And to glorify, but it came in the nominative case, which is more eloquent in the speech of the Arabs than its accusative case. And likewise in everything that was similar to it, which is a general obligation - for the one who has done it, and for the one who has not done it if he did it - not as a recommendation or an exhortation. And its nominative case is in the meaning: So whoever has been pardoned by his brother for something, then the command in it is: following in a good manner and paying him back with kindness, or the judgment and ruling in it is: following in a good manner.

And some of the Arab scholars have said: The nominative case is in the meaning: So whoever has been pardoned by his brother for something, then he must follow in a good manner. And this is a school of thought, and the first that we have said is the face of the speech. And likewise everything that was similar to that in the Qur’an, then its nominative case is in the face that we have said. And that is like His saying: And whoever among you kills him intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock (al-Ma’idah 5:95) and His saying: Then keep him in kindness or release him with kindness (al-Baqarah 2:229). As for His saying: Then striking the necks, then the correct thing in it is the accusative case, and that is the face of the speech? Because it is on The face of the urging of God Almighty to His servants to kill when meeting the enemy, as it is said: If you meet the enemy, then glorify God and praise Him, as an urging to glorify God, not as an obligation and obligation.

God Almighty means by His saying: That, this is what I have ruled and prescribed for you, of permitting you - O nation - to pardon the retaliation of the killer of your slain, in exchange for blood money that you take and you own it, as you own all your wealth that I had withheld from the previous nations before you, as a relief from your Lord, meaning: a relief from Me for you from what I had made heavy for others, by forbidding it to them, and a mercy, from Me to you, as Abu Kurayb and Ahmad ibn Hammad al-Dawlabi told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Retaliation was prescribed for the Children of Israel, but blood money was not prescribed for them, so God said in this verse:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder
h
a free man for a free man
, to His saying, But if any of his brother pardons him, so pardon is to accept. Blood money for premeditated murder, That is a relief from your Lord.
He says: He has relieved you of what was upon those before you: to ask for this with kindness, and to pay this with kindness.

c: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Those before you used to kill the killer for the one killed, and blood money was not accepted from them, so God revealed: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution in cases of murder, the free for the free to the end of the verse, That is a relief from your Lord, he says: He has relieved you, and blood money was not accepted upon those before you, so the one who accepts blood money, that is forgiveness from Him. Al-Muthanna told Surat Al-Baqarah 2:178 O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution in the case of those murdered - the free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female. But if any remission is made by his brother, there should be a just pursuit and payment to him with good conduct. That is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy.
h
But whoever transgresses after

that will have a severe punishment. Painful me, he said, al-Hajjaj ibn al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, he said, Amr ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
That is a relief from your Lord and a mercy
, from what was upon the Children of Israel, meaning: the prohibition of blood money upon them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The Children of Israel had retaliation for murder, and there was no blood money between them for a life or an injury, and that is the saying of God: “And We ordained for them therein: a life for a life, and an eye for an eye” (al-Ma’idah 5:45). And God made it easier for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and accepted from them blood money for a life and for an injury, and that is the saying of God Almighty: That is a relief from your Lord between you.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
That is a relief from your Lord and a mercy

, and it is only a mercy with which God had mercy on this nation, He fed them blood money and made it permissible for them, and it was not permissible for anyone before them. So the people of the Torah were only retaliation or forgiveness, and there was no blood money between them, and the people of the Gospel were only forgiveness, and they were commanded to do so. So God made for this nation retaliation and forgiveness and blood money if they wished, He made it permissible for them, and it was not for any nation before them. I narrated from Ammar bin Al-Hasan, he said, Ibn Abi Ja'far, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, similarly, except that he said: There is nothing between them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder
, he said: For those before us, there was no blood money, it was only killing, or pardoning his family. So this verse was revealed about a people who were more numerous than others.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Amr bin Dinar told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Retaliation was prescribed for the Children of Israel, and it was made lighter for this nation - and Amr bin Dinar recited: That is a lightening from your Lord and a mercy. As for the statement of those who said: Retaliation in this verse means: Retaliation of blood money from one another, according to what al-Suddi said, then its interpretation should be: This is what I did to you, O believers - of retribution of blood money for those killed, some of you for the blood money of others, and leaving the obligation of retribution on the rest of you for the one killed whom he killed and took.

x: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
But whoever transgresses after

that, whoever exceeds what God has made for him after taking the blood money, transgressing and unjustly to what He has not made for him, such as killing the killer of his guardian and shedding his blood, then for his action and transgression to what I have forbidden him, there is a painful punishment. I have explained the meaning of transgression previously in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, he said, ʿIsa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
But whoever transgresses after
that and kills, for him is a painful punishment.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: But whoever transgresses, after taking the blood money, for him is a painful punishment. Bishr ibn Muadh said, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated to us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
But whoever transgresses after

that, for him is a painful punishment, meaning: whoever transgresses after receiving the blood money and kills, for him is a painful punishment. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: I do not pardon a man who killed after receiving the blood money.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said, Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But whoever transgresses after
that, he said: It is killing after receiving the blood money. He said: Whoever kills after receiving the blood money, then he must be killed, and the blood money will not be accepted from him.

c: I was told by Ammar bin al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
But whoever transgresses after
that, for him is a painful punishment, meaning: whoever transgresses after receiving the blood money, then he is a painful punishment.

c: Sufyan bin Waki’ narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to me, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: If a man killed someone in the pre-Islamic era, he would flee to his people. Then his people come and make peace on his behalf with blood money. He said: The fugitive comes out and he feels safe. He said: He is killed and then the blood money is thrown at him, and that is aggression.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said: Abu Aqil told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan regarding this verse: But if a man is pardoned by his brother, he said: The killer is if he is sought and is not able to, and he takes the blood money from his relatives, then he feels safe, so he is taken and killed. Al-Hasan said: He did not eat aggression.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Muslim told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Harun bin Sulayman told us, he said:
m: I said to Ikrimah: Who kills after taking the blood money? He said: Then he is killed! Haven’t you heard God say:
h
But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But whoever transgresses after
that, after he takes the blood money, and kills, will have a painful punishment.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me.
m: He said, my father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
But whoever transgresses after
that, meaning: whoever transgresses after taking the blood money, then for him is a painful punishment.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
But whoever transgresses after

that, then for him is a painful punishment, he said: He took the blood money, then killed after taking the blood money the killer of his victim, then for him is a painful punishment. And they differed regarding the meaning of the painful punishment that God made for whoever transgresses after taking the blood money, the killer of his guardian passed by.

x: Some of them said: That punishment is killing the one who killed him after taking the blood money from him, and his pardon of the retaliation from him for the blood of his guardian.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim al-Dawraqi told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of al-Dahhak
m: regarding his statement:
h
But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment
, he said: He will be killed, and it is the painful punishment, he said: the painful punishment.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Hisham told me, he said, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr
m: that he said that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, al-Qasim told us, he said, Harun bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment
, he said: killing.

x: Some of them said: That punishment is a punishment with which the ruler punishes him according to the extent of his punishment.
Mention of those who said that:

c: al-Qasim bin al-Hasan told me, he said, al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, Ismail bin Umayya told me, on the authority of al-Layth - except
m: that he did not He attributed it to him, and said: Trustworthy -: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made it obligatory by oath or otherwise that a man who forgave blood money and took blood money, then transgressed and killed, not be pardoned. Ibn Jurayj said, and Abdul Aziz bin Omar bin Abdul Aziz informed me, he said: In a book of Omar from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: And the transgression that God mentioned: That a man takes blood money or takes retaliation or the ruler judges between the wounds, then some of them transgress after he has fully taken his right. So whoever does that has transgressed, and the ruling in it is up to the ruler with what he sees as punishment. He said: And if he pardoned him, no one seeking the truth has the right to [pardon], because this is from the matter in which God revealed His saying: But if you disagree about anything, refer it to God and the Messenger
r
(An-Nisa’: 59)

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad narrated to us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Concerning a man who killed and blood money was taken from him, then his guardian killed the killer for it. Al-Hasan said: The blood money that he took is taken from him, and he is not killed for it.

x: And the first of the two interpretations is: By His saying:
h
But whoever transgresses after

that, for him is a painful punishment, the interpretation of the one who said: “So whoever transgresses after taking the blood money and kills the killer of his guardian, for him is a painful punishment in this world, which is killing. Because God Almighty has given every guardian of a murdered person unjustly authority over the killer of his guardian, as He Almighty said:
“And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed limits in taking life”

Since that is the case, and all the people of knowledge are in agreement that whoever kills the killer of his guardian after he has pardoned him and taken from him the blood money for his murdered person, that by killing him he has committed an injustice in killing him - it is clear that the one who killed him unjustly should not be given authority over him in retaliation, pardon, and taking the blood money, whichever he wants.

Since that is the case, it is known that that is his punishment. Because whoever has his punishment carried out on him in this world, that is his punishment for his sin, and it will not be followed in the Hereafter, according to what has been proven in the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for what Ibn Gregory: That the ruling of the one who kills the killer of his guardian after he has pardoned him, and he takes the blood money of the guardian of the murdered person to the Imam and not to the guardians of the murdered person, is a statement contrary to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the Book of God, and upon which the scholars of the nation have agreed. That is because God has given the guardian of every unjustly murdered the authority and not to anyone else, without specifying one murdered person over another. So whether that person was murdered and the guardian of the one who killed him or someone else.

And whoever specifies something from that is asked for proof of it from the origin or the equivalent, and the statement is reversed to him in it, then he will not say a statement in any of that except that he is obligated in the other like it. Then in the consensus of the argument contrary to what he said in that, it is sufficient to cite other evidence for its corruption.
God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And there is life for you in retaliation

, O you who possess understanding, and for you, O you who possess understanding, in what has been imposed upon you and made obligatory for some of you over others, of retaliation for lives, wounds and head wounds, what prevented some of you from killing others, and some of you from stopping others, so you were kept alive by that, so there was life for you in My judgment between you by that.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that.
Some of them said something similar to what we have said about it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, he said, ʿIsa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His saying:
h
And there is life for you in retaliation
, O you who possess understanding, he said: A punishment, the end of it.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And there is life for you in retaliation
, he said: A punishment, it is more like this.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada:
h
And there is life for you in retaliation

, God made this retaliation a life, a punishment, and a lesson for the foolish and ignorant among the people. How many a man has contemplated a disaster, but had it not been for the fear of retaliation, he would have committed it, but God prevented some from others by retaliation? God has never commanded anything except that it is a matter of goodness in this world and the hereafter, and God has never forbidden anything except that it is a matter of corruption in this world and religion, and God knows best what is good for His creation. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, on the authority of Abdul-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement:
h
And there is life for you in retaliation
h
O you of understanding
, he said: God has made life in retaliation, if the wrongdoer and transgressor remembers it, he refrains from killing.

c: I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement:
h
And there is life for you in retaliation

, the verse, he says: God has made this retaliation a life and a lesson for you. How many a man has been struck by a calamity, but the fear of retaliation prevented him from falling into it! Indeed, God has protected some of His servants from others by means of retaliation.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And there is life for you in retaliation
, he said: A punishment that is more severe. Ibn Jurayj said: Life, protection.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And there is life for you in retaliation

, he said: Life, remainder. If this one fears that he will be killed because of me, he should refrain from me, perhaps he is an enemy of mine who wants to kill me, so he remembers that he will be killed in retaliation, and he fears that he will be killed because of me, so he refrains from retaliation that he feared he would be killed, otherwise he would kill this one.

c: I was told by Ya’la ibn Ubayd,
m: he said, Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, about His statement:
h
And there is life for you in retaliation
, he said: Permanence.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: And there is permanence for you in retaliation from the killer, because no one is killed for the one killed except his killer according to the judgment of God. And in the pre-Islamic era, they used to kill for the female, the male, and for the free slave.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, he said, Amr ibn Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And there is life for you in retaliation
, he said: Permanence, no one is killed except the killer for his crime. As for the interpretation of His statement:
h
O you of understanding

, it is: O you of intellects. Al-Albab is the plural of Al-Lub, and Al-Lub is the mind. God Almighty specifically addressed people of reason, because they are the ones who understand God’s commands and prohibitions, and ponder His signs and proofs, unlike others.

x: The interpretation of His statement,
h
Perhaps you will fear God
, is that you will fear retaliation, so you will refrain from killing, as Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement,
h
Perhaps you will fear God
, he said: Perhaps you will fear killing him, so you will be killed because of him.
What is meant by the words of God Almighty:
h
It is prescribed for you
, He has made it obligatory for you, O believers, to make a will, when death approaches any of you,
h
if he leaves wealth

- and wealth means money - for parents and relatives who do not inherit from him, according to what is acceptable: which is what God has permitted and authorized in a will that does not exceed a third, and the testator did not intentionally wrong his heirs, a duty upon the righteous: He means by that: He has made this obligatory upon you and made it an obligatory right upon whoever fears God and obeys Him to act upon it.
Is it obligatory for a man with wealth to make a will for his parents and relatives who do not inherit from him?
Yes.
If he is negligent in that and does not make a will for them, will he be neglecting an obligation that he will be embarrassed by neglecting?
Yes.
What is the evidence for that?
The statement of God the Most High:
h
It is prescribed for you
, when death approaches any of you,
h
if he leaves wealth

, that he make a bequest to parents and relatives, so know that He has prescribed it for us and made it obligatory, just as He said: Fasting is prescribed for you (al-Baqarah 2:183). There is no disagreement among all that the one who abandons fasting while he is able to do so has neglected an obligation imposed on him by God. Likewise, by abandoning a bequest to his parents and relatives, even though he has something to bequeath to them, he has neglected an obligation imposed on him by God the Most High.
You know that a group of scholars said: The bequest to parents and relatives is abrogated by the verse of inheritance?

And a group other than them disagreed with them and said: It is decisive and not abrogated. If there is a dispute among scholars about the abrogation of this, we cannot rule that it is abrogated except with an argument that must be accepted, since it is not impossible for the ruling of this verse and the ruling of the verse of inheritance to be combined in one case with validity, without the ruling of one of them contradicting the ruling of the other - and the abrogating and the abrogated are the two meanings whose rulings cannot be combined with validity in one case, because one of them negates the other. And what we have said about this was said by a group of the earlier and later scholars.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: that he used to say: Whoever He died without making a will to his relatives, so he ended his work with disobedience.

c: Salim bin Junadah told me, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq:
m: that he was present with a man who made a will for things that were not appropriate, so Masruq said to him: God has divided among you and divided well, and whoever prefers his opinion over the opinion of God, He will lead him astray. Make a will for your relatives who will not inherit from you, then leave the money as God divided it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Abu Tamila Yahya bin Wadh told us, he said, Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak He
m: said: It is not permissible to make a will to an heir, and no one may bequeath except to a relative. If he bequeaths to someone other than a relative, has he committed a sin? Unless he is not a relative, then he may bequeath to the poor Muslims.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, he said:
m: I am amazed at Abu Al-Aliyah, a woman from Banu Riyah freed him, and he bequeathed his money to Banu Hashim!

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: He had no [owners], nor any honor.

c: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Ayoub narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: Abdullah ibn Muammar said
m: about the will: Whoever names it, we will make it where he names it. And whoever says: Where God commands, we will make it for his relatives.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani told me, he said, al-Mu'tamir told us, he said, Imran ibn Hudayr told us, he said:
m: I said to Abu Majlaz: Is a will obligatory for every Muslim? He said: On the one who leaves behind wealth.

c: Suwar ibn Abdullah told us, he said, Abd al-Malik ibn al-Sabah told us, he said, Imran ibn Hudayr told us, he said:
m: I said to Lahiq ibn Hamid: Is a will a right for every Muslim? He said: It is a right for the one who leaves behind wealth.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the ruling of this verse.

Some of them said: God did not abrogate any of its rulings, but it is a verse whose apparent meaning is general for every father, mother, and relative, and what is meant by it in the ruling is some of them and not all of them, and that is those who do not inherit from the deceased and not those who inherit. This is the opinion of the one whose opinion I mentioned, and the opinion of another group besides them.
Mention of those who did not mention their statement in that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid:
m: Concerning a man who made a will to someone other than his relatives and he has relatives who are in need, he said: Two-thirds of the third should be returned to them, and one-third of the third to the one to whom he made the will.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muadh told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: Jabir bin Zaid, and Abdul Malik bin Ya’la that they said - Concerning a man who makes a will to someone other than his relatives and he has relatives who do not inherit from him, he said: They used to give two-thirds of the third to the relatives, and one-third of the third to the one to whom he made the will.

c: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hamid told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: that he used to say: If a man makes a will to someone other than his relatives with one-third of it, then they get one-third of the third, and two-thirds of the third goes to his relatives. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, he said: Whoever makes a will for a people and names them, and leaves his relatives in need, it will be taken away from them and returned to his relatives.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a verse that was obligatory and acted upon for a while, then God abrogated it with the verse on inheritance, the will for the parents of the testator and his relatives who inherit from him, and He confirmed the obligation of the will for those among them who do not inherit from him.
Those who said that: Bishr bin Muadh narrated, he said: Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, he said: Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement:
h
It is prescribed for you

, when death approaches any of you, if he leaves goods, that he make a bequest to the parents and the closest relatives, so the will was made for the parents and the closest relatives, then that was abrogated after that, and a fixed share was made for them, so the will became for the relatives who do not inherit, and a known share was made for the parents, and a will for an heir is not permissible.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and near relatives, he said: The parents abrogated it, and the near relatives left those who do not inherit.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and near relatives, he said: It abrogated those who inherit, but it did not abrogate the near relatives who do not inherit.

c: Yahya bin Nasr narrated to us, he said: Yahya bin Hassan narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: The bequest before inheritance was for parents and near relatives, but when inheritance was revealed, the inheritance abrogated those who inherit, and what remained was those who do not inherit. Whoever makes a will to his relatives, his will is not valid.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Makki, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to the parents and the closest relatives, he said: He abrogated the parents and confirmed the closest relatives who are forbidden and do not inherit.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Mubarak ibn Fadala, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding this verse: The bequest is for parents and near relatives, he said: For parents is abrogated, and the bequest is for relatives even if they are rich.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he leaves wealth

, the bequest is for parents and near relatives, so he did not inherit with the parents, even if they were older, except for a bequest if it was for the near relatives. Then God revealed after this: “And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he had a child. But if he had no child and his parents inherit him, then for his mother is a third”
r
(An-Nisa’: 11)
, so God Almighty explained the inheritance of parents, and approved the bequest of the near relatives in a third of the deceased’s wealth.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and near relatives, so he abrogated the bequest to parents and near relatives who do not inherit.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, his statement:
h
It is prescribed for you
, when death approaches any of you,
h
if he leaves wealth

, to make a bequest to parents and near relatives according to what is acceptable, he said: This was before Surat An-Nisa was revealed, but when the verse of inheritance was revealed, the matter of parents was abrogated, so they were included among those who inherit, and the bequest became for those who are in need of a share who do not inherit.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Minhal told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, he said,
m: he told us Ata bin Abi Maymouna said: I asked Muslim bin Yasar and Al-Ala bin Ziyad about the statement of God Almighty:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and relatives. They said: Concerning kinship.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Iyas bin Muawiyah, he said:
m: Concerning Kinship.

x: Others said: Rather, God abrogated all of that and imposed the obligatory duties and inheritance, so no will is obligatory for anyone over anyone, near or far.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and near relatives 3:13, he said: So God abrogated all of that and imposed the obligatory duties.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Surat Al-Baqarah 2:
m: h
It is prescribed for you
, when death approaches any of you,
h
if he leaves wealth

, to make a bequest in favor of parents and relatives according to what is acceptable. This is a duty upon the righteous. Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That he stood up and addressed the people here. He recited to them Surat Al-Baqarah to explain it to them, and he came to this verse:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and near relatives 3:13. He said: This was abrogated.

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and near relatives, the obligatory duties for parents and near relatives abrogated the bequest.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told me, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Jahdam, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Badr, he said,
m: I heard Ibn Umar say about his statement:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and near relatives, he said: The verse of inheritance abrogated it. Ibn Bashar said: Abd al-Rahman said: So I asked Jahdam about it but he did not remember it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yahya ibn Wadh told us, he said, al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, they said:
m: h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and near relatives, and the bequest was like that until the verse of inheritance abrogated it.

c: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam told me, al-Mu'tamir told us,
m: I heard my father say, Qatada claimed, on the authority of Shuraih, regarding this verse:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest is made to parents and near relatives, he said: A man would bequeath all of his wealth, until the verse of inheritance was revealed.

c: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam told us, al-Mu'tamir told us,
m: I heard my father say, Qatada claimed: The verses of inheritance in Surat al-Nisa were abrogated by the verse in Surat al-Baqarah regarding the bequest.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
If he leaves wealth
, the bequest is for the parents and the near relatives, he said: The inheritance was for the child, and the bequest was for the parents and the near relatives, and it has been abrogated.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The inheritance was for the child, and the bequest was for the parents and the near relatives. It was abrogated, abrogated by a verse in Surat al-Nisa 4:God instructs you concerning your children (al-Nisa 4:11).

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of As-Suddi:
m: h
It is prescribed for you
, when death approaches any of you,
h
if he leaves wealth

, that he make a bequest to parents and near relatives. As for parents and near relatives, on the day this verse was revealed, people did not have a known inheritance, rather a man would make a bequest to his parents and his family, and it would be divided among them, until it was abrogated [An-Nisa], so He said: God instructs you concerning your children (al-Nisa 4:11).

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayyub told us, on the authority of Nafi’:
m: Ibn Umar did not make a bequest, and he said: As for my wealth, God knows best what I used to do with it in life, and as for my four-quarters, I do not like my children to share it with anyone.

c: Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Naseer ibn Tha’luq, he said,
m: Urwah - meaning ibn Thabit - said to Rabi’ ibn Khathim: Bequeath your Qur’an to me. He said: So he looked at his father and said: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God (al-Anfal 8:75).

c: Ali ibn Sahl told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: We mentioned to him that Zayd and Talhah were strict in making wills, so he said: They should not have done that. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died without making a will, and Abu Bakr made a will. Whichever of these you do is good.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Talhah and Zayd were mentioned in his presence, so he mentioned something similar. As for the good that if someone leaves something behind, he must make a will for his parents and relatives who do not inherit, it is wealth, as in:

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Saleh, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he leaves behind wealth
, meaning money.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
If he leaves behind wealth
, meaning wealth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
If he leaves behind wealth
, he used to say: Good in the entire Qur’an is wealth, For the love of good is intense (al-Adiyat 100:8) Good is wealth, Indeed, I love the love of good more than the remembrance of my Lord
r
, wealth, Then write a contract with them if you know any good in them (al-Nur 24:33), wealth, and
h
If he leaves behind wealth
is a bequest, meaning money.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
If he leaves behind wealth
is a bequest, meaning: Money.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
If he leaves behind good
, a bequest. As for good, it means money.

c: I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on Al-Rabi’:
h
If he leaves behind good
, he said: If he leaves behind money.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he leaves behind good
, he said: The good is money.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Yahya, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
If he leaves behind good
, a bequest, he said: Money. Do you not see that he says: Shu’aib said to his al-Nas 114:Indeed, I see you in goodness
r
, meaning wealth.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Amr al-Yafi’i told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata ibn Abi Rabah,
m: he recited:
h
It is prescribed for you
, when death approaches any of you,
h
if he leaves wealth
, Ata said: The wealth in what he sees is money. Then they differed about the amount of money that if a man leaves behind him, he is among those who are subject to the ruling of this verse.

x: Some of them said: It is a thousand dirhams.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal told us, he said, Hammam ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding this verse:
h
If he leaves wealth
, a bequest, he said: The wealth is a thousand or more.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, he said, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of Urwah:
m: Ali ibn Abi Talib entered upon his cousin to visit him, and he said: I want to make a will. Ali said: Do not make a will, for you did not leave anything good to make a will. He said: He left between seven hundred and nine hundred.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Uthman bin Al-Hakam Al-Hizami and Ibn Abi Al-Zinad told me, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib:
m: That he entered upon a sick man and mentioned to him the will, so he said: Do not make a will, God only said:
h
If he leaves behind good
, and you did not leave behind good. Ibn Abi Al-Zinad said about him: So leave your wealth to your sons.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur bin Safiyya,
m: On the authority of Abdullah bin Uyaynah - or: Utbah, I am not sure -: A man wanted to make a will, and he had many children, and he left four hundred dinars. Aisha said: I do not see any merit in that.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: A slave of theirs came to me when he was dying, and he had seven hundred dirhams, or six hundred dirhams, so he said: Should I not make a will? He said: No! God said:
h
If he leaves behind wealth
, and you do not have much wealth.

x: Some of them said: It is between five hundred and one thousand dirhams.
Those who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said:

c: Abdul-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abaan bin Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i,
m: regarding His statement:
h
If he leaves behind wealth
, he said: One thousand dirhams to five hundred.

x: Some of them said: A will is obligatory for a little or a lot of wealth.
Who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said: God made the will a right, whether it is little or much.
The most correct of these sayings in interpreting His statement:
h
It is prescribed for you when death approaches any of you
h
if he leaves wealth

, that he makes a bequest, is what Al-Zuhri said. Because good comes to him whether little or much wealth, and God did not set a limit for that, nor did He specify anything from it, so it is permissible to transfer the apparent to the hidden. So whoever is at death’s door and has wealth, whether it is little or much, it is obligatory for him to bequeath from it to those who do not inherit from him from his fathers and mothers and relatives who do not inherit from him, in a reasonable manner, as God, the Most High, said and commanded.

God Almighty means by that: Whoever changes what the testator has bequeathed - of his bequest to his parents or relatives who do not inherit from him - after he has heard the bequest, then the sin of the change is upon the one who changes his bequest.

q.l: If someone were to ask us:
x: And what is the reason for the return of the ha' in His statement:
h
So whoever changes it

It is upon something omitted from the statement that is indicated by the apparent meaning. That is the matter of the deceased, and his bequest to the one to whom he bequeathed, what he bequeathed, to the one to whom he bequeathed. The meaning of the statement is: It is prescribed for you, when death approaches any of you, if he leaves wealth, to make a bequest to parents and relatives according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous. So make bequests to them, and whoever changes what you bequeathed to them after he has heard you bequeathing to them, then the sin of what he did is upon him and not you. We said that the ha’ in His statement:
h
So whoever changes it

refers to something omitted from the statement that is indicated by the apparent meaning, because His statement: It is prescribed for you when death approaches any of you, if he leaves wealth, that he make a bequest is from the statement of God, and that the replacement of what is replaced is only for the testator’s will.
As for God’s command to make a will, neither he nor anyone else is able to give it, so it is possible that the ha’ in His statement:
h
So whoever changes it
refers to the bequest. As for the ha’ in His statement:
h
After he heard it
, it refers to the first ha’ in His statement:
h
So whoever changes it
. As for the ha’ in his statement:
h
Then his sin is only

, it is a possible substitute, as if he said: The sin of what was substituted from that is only upon those who substitute it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then whoever substitutes it after he has heard it, he said: The will.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
But whoever alters it after he has heard it

, then the sin is upon those who alter it, and the reward of the testator falls upon God and he is absolved of his sin. If he had made a will to cause harm, then his will is not permissible, as God said: Not to cause harm
r
(An-Nisa’: 12)
- Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement:
h
But whoever alters it after he has heard it
, he said: Whoever alters the will after he has heard it, then the sin of what he altered is upon him.

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to us, he said: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But whoever alters it after he has heard it
h
then his sin is only
upon those who alter it. So whoever alters the will that he had left behind, and it was in an acceptable manner, then its sin is only upon those who altered it. Indeed, he has wronged.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Hajjaj bin Al-Minhal narrated to us, he said: Hammad narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, that Ata bin Abi Rabah said
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
But whoever alters it after he has heard it
h
then his sin is only
upon those who alter it, he said: It should be as he said.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
But whoever alters it after he has heard it
, he said: Whoever alters a will after he has heard it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Yazid bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding this verse: But whoever changes it after he has heard it,
h
then his sin is only
upon those who changed it, he said: This is about the will, whoever changes it after he has heard it,
h
then his sin is only
upon those who changed it.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ata',
m: Salim bin Abdullah and Sulayman bin Yasar said: The will is carried out for the one to whom it was bequeathed - Ibn Al-Muthanna's hadith ends here, and Ibn Bashar added to his hadith - Qatada said: Abdullah bin Muammar said: I would like it if he bequeathed it to his relatives, but I would not like it to be taken away from the one to whom he bequeathed it. Qatada said: And I would like it for the one to whom he bequeathed it, God the Almighty said:
h
But whoever alters it after he has heard it
, then the sin is only upon those who alter it.

x: By that God the Almighty meant: Indeed, God is Hearing - of your will that I commanded you to bequeath to your fathers and relatives when you bequeath it, are you just in it according to what I have permitted you to do in terms of doing that in a good manner, or are you being unjust and deviating from the truth and acting unjustly? - Knowing of what your hearts conceal of inclination towards the truth, and enmity, or injustice and oppression.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of this verse.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: If someone is present with a sick person who is making a will when he is on the verge of death, and he fears that he may make a mistake in his will and do something that is not his, or that he may deliberately commit injustice in it and order something that he is not entitled to order, then there is no blame on the one who is present with him and hears that from him to reconcile between him and his heirs, by ordering him to be just in his will, and to forbid them from preventing him from what God has permitted and made permissible for him.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, he said, ʿIsa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh,
m: On the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: “
h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator and makes peace between them

, there is no sin upon him,” he said: This is when a man is about to die, so if he commits an act of excess, they order him to be just, and if he falls short, they say: Do such-and-such, give such-and-such to such-and-such.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator

, he said: This is when a man is about to die, so if he is on the verge of injustice, they order him to be just, and if he falls short of what is right, they say: Do such-and-such, give such-and-such to such-and-such.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Whoever fears - from the guardians of a dead person, or the ruler of the Muslims - injustice on the part of a testator. In his will that the deceased left behind, he reconciled between his heirs and the legatees with what he left behind, so he restored the will to justice and truth, so there is no blame or sin.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me,
m: Abu Salih, the scribe of Al-Layth, told us, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
But whoever fears from a testator injustice -
meaning: sin - he says: If the deceased makes a mistake in his will or deviates in it, then there is no blame on the guardians if they restore his mistake to what is correct.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if a testator fears injustice or wrongdoing
, he said: It is the man who makes a will and is unjust in his will, so the guardian returns it to truth and justice.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if a testator fears injustice or wrongdoing
, Qatada used to say: Whoever makes a will, and the guardian of the deceased or one of the leaders of the Muslims returns it to the Book of God and to justice, then that is for him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saad and Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator

, so if someone makes an unjust will, and the executor returns it to the right path after his death, then there is no sin upon him. Abd al-Rahman said in his hadith: “And make peace between them,” meaning: the executor returns it to the right path after his death, then there is no sin upon him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator
, then make peace between them,” he said: bring him back to the right path.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Masruq, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: I asked him about a man who bequeathed more than a third. He said: Return it. Then he recited:
h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator
. Amr bin Ali narrated, Khalid bin Zaid, the author of Al-Lulu, narrated, Abu Jaafar Al-Razi narrated, on the authority of Qatada bin Anas:
h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator
and reconciles between them, there is no sin upon him, meaning: The executor returns him to his right after his death, so there is no sin upon the executor.

x: Some of them said: Rather, the meaning of this is: If someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator in giving some of his heirs at the time of his death without giving others, there is no sin upon the one who reconciles between them, meaning: between the heirs.
Those who said this: Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Hussein narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata’, regarding his statement:
h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator

, he said: A man commits injustice or wrongdoing at his death, so he gives to his heirs some of them without giving others, God says: There is no sin upon the one who reconciles between them. So I said to Ata’: Does he have the right to give to his heirs at the time of his death? It is only a will, and there is no will for an heir? He said: That is in what is divided among them.

Others said: The meaning of that is: If a testator fears injustice or sin in his will to someone who does not inherit from him, in a way that benefits those who inherit from him, and he reconciles between his heirs, then there is no sin upon him.

Those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Tawus told me, on the authority of his father that he used to say: His injustice and sin is for a man to bequeath to his son’s sons so that the money is for their father, and a woman to bequeath to her daughter’s husband so that the money is for her daughter? And the one who has a large inheritor but little money, so he bequeaths a third of his entire money, and the legatee or the prince reconciles between them. I said: During his life or after his death? He said: We did not hear anyone say this except after his death, and he was admonished at that time.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator and makes peace between them
,” he said: It is the man who makes a will for his daughter’s son.

x: Others said: Rather the meaning of this is: If someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator for his fathers and relatives, and makes peace between the fathers and relatives, then there is no sin upon him.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator and makes peace between them

, there is no sin upon him.” As for wrongdoing, he is making a mistake in his will. As for sin, he is deliberately doing injustice in his will. This is greater for his reward than not executing it, but making peace between them according to what he sees as right, decreasing some and increasing others. He said: This verse was revealed regarding the parents and the closest relatives.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “
h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator and makes peace between them

, there is no sin upon him,” he said: Injustice is when he treats some of them unfairly in the will, and sin is when he has sinned with regard to his parents, “and makes peace between them,” the one to whom the will is made is between the parents and the closest relatives - the son and the sons are the closest relatives - so there is no sin upon him.

x: The most correct interpretation of the verse is that whoever fears from the testator a deviation or sin - which is that he will incline towards something other than what is right by mistake on his part, or intentionally commits a sin in his will, by bequeathing to his parents and relatives who do not inherit from him more than what he is permitted to bequeath to them from his money, and other than what God has permitted him to do of what exceeds a third or a full third, and there is little money, and there is a lot of heirs - then there is no harm in whoever is present to reconcile between those to whom the will is being bequeathed, and between the heirs of the deceased, and between the deceased, by ordering the deceased to do what is right and informing him of what God has permitted him to do in his will and what God has permitted him to do in his will regarding his money, and forbidding him to exceed in his will what is right about which God Almighty said in His Book:
h
It is prescribed for you
, O Muhammad, to do what is right. If death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, he should make a bequest to his parents and relatives according to what is acceptable.

This is the reconciliation that God the Most High said: “Then make peace between them, for there is no sin upon him.” Likewise, for someone who has a surplus and abundant wealth and few heirs, and he wants to limit his bequest to his parents and relatives to one-third, he should make peace between himself and his heirs and his parents and relatives to whom he wants to make a bequest, by ordering the sick person to increase his bequest to them, and to make it what God has permitted of one-third. This is also from making peace between them according to what is acceptable. We have chosen this statement because God the Most High said: But if someone fears from a testator injustice or sin, meaning: if someone fears from a testator that he will commit injustice or sin. Fear of injustice and sin from the testator only occurs before the injustice and sin occur. However, after it occurs from him, there is no reason to fear that he will commit injustice or sin.

Rather, this is the case of someone who has committed injustice or sin. If that was the meaning, it would have been said: “Whoever is proven to have committed a wrongdoing or a sin - or is certain or aware of it - and not: whoever fears wrongdoing from him.” If what we have said is unclear to some people, then they say: What is the point of reconciliation in that case, and reconciliation is only between those who differ in something? It is said: “Even if that is one of the meanings of reconciliation, reconciliation is reconciliation between the two parties, in what was feared to happen between them, in a way that ensures that there will be no difference.” Because reconciliation is the action that brings about reconciliation between the two parties, whether that action brings about reconciliation between them - before the difference occurs or after it occurs.
“How is it that it was said: ‘So he made peace between them’, and neither the heirs nor the differing parties, or the feared ones, were mentioned?”

Rather, those whom God, the Most High, commanded to be bequeathed were mentioned, and they are the parents of the testator and his relatives, and those who… They were commanded to make a will in His statement:
h
It is prescribed for you
, when death approaches any of you, if he leaves wealth, to make a bequest to parents and relatives, according to what is acceptable.

Then the Most High said: But whoever fears from the testator - to whom you commanded him to make a will - “injustice or sin, and make peace between them” - and between whom you commanded him to make a will - there is no sin upon him. And making peace between him and them is making peace between them and the heirs of the testator.
His statement:
h
But whoever fears from the testator has Surat Al-Baqarah 2
h
But if someone fears injustice or wrongdoing on the part of a testator

and brings about a settlement between them, there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. been read with a lightened sad and a sukoon on the waw - and with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the sad. Whoever reads that with a lightened sad and a sukoon on the waw, has read it in the language of someone who says: I bequeathed such-and-such to so-and-so. Whoever reads with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the sad, has read it in the language of someone who says: I bequeathed such-and-such to so-and-so. And whoever reads with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the sad, has read it in the language of someone who says: I bequeathed such-and-such to so-and-so. These are two well-known dialects of the Arabs: Wasitaka and Awsitaka.

i: As for injustice, it is injustice and deviation from the truth in the speech of the Arabs, and from it is the saying of the poet:
x: They are our masters, even if they are unfair to us.

We are indeed afraid of meeting them. It is said: A man was unfair to his friend, if he leaned against him and was unjust to him - unfairness. So the meaning of the statement is whoever fears that the testator will be unfair to him in the matter of the will, and deviate from the right path in it, and deviate from the intention or sin by doing that deliberately with knowledge of the error of what he will do from that, so he reconciles between them, then there is no sin upon him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about the meaning of unfairness and sin.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But whoever fears from a testator unfairness
, he means by unfairness: error.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’:
m: h
But whoever fears from a testator unfairness
, he said: Deviation.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: similarly.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Khalid bin Al-Harith and Yazid bin Harun told us, they said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: similarly.

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said:
m: Janf is a mistake, and sin is deliberate.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us,
m: who said: Abu Ahmad Az-Zubayri told us, who said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ata’, similarly.

c: Musa told me,
m: who said: Amr told us, who said: Asbat told us, on the authority of As-Suddi: So whoever fears from a testator injustice or sin. As for janf, it is a mistake in his will, and as for sin, it is deliberate, he intentionally wrongs his will.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if a testator fears injustice or sin
, he said: By mistake or intentionally.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa’d and Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
But if a testator fears injustice or sin
, he said: Injustice is by mistake, and sin is intentional.

c: Amr ibn Ali told us, he said,
m: Khalid ibn Yazid, the companion of Al-Lulu’, he said, Abu Ja’far told us, on the authority of Qatada ibn Anas, similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
But if a testator fears injustice or sin
, he said: Injustice is by mistake, and sin is intentional.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Fadil ibn Marzouq narrated to us, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: But whoever fears from a testator deviation, he said: a mistake, or sin, intentionally.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: But whoever fears from a testator deviation, he said: a deviation.

c: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Deviation is injustice
, and sin is his inclination of one towards another. And all of it comes to one, just as it can be pardoning and forgiving and forgiving and merciful.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: deviation is a mistake, and sin is intentional.

c: I was told by Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: he said: Al-Fadl ibn Khalid narrated to us, he said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: deviation is a mistake, and sin is intentional. As for his saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, it means: God is Forgiving of the testator, regarding what his soul has thought of of injustice and sin, if he has left it to sin and be unjust in his will, and has overlooked for him what his soul has thought of of injustice, since that did not happen and he did not neglect to hold him accountable for it, Merciful in reconciling between the testator and whoever wanted to wrong him for someone else, or sin for him in it.

evidence.text: Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. been read with a lightened sad and a sukoon on the waw - and with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the sad.
Whoever reads that with a lightened sad and a sukoon on the waw, has read it in the language of someone who says: I bequeathed such-and-such to so-and-so.
Whoever reads with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the sad, has read it in the language of someone who says: I bequeathed such-and-such to so-and-so.
And whoever reads with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the sad, has read it in the language of someone who says: I bequeathed such-and-such to so-and-so.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
O you who have believed
h
O you who have believed
in God and His Messenger and have believed in them and acknowledged them. What he means by his saying:
h
Fasting has been prescribed for you is that fasting has been made obligatory for you

. Fasting is a noun, from the saying of the speaker: I kept silent about such and such - meaning: I refrained from it - I fast from it, fasting and fasting. The meaning of fasting is to refrain from what God has commanded us to refrain from. From this it is said: The horse kept silent, if it stopped walking, and from this is the saying of the Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan: Fasting horses, and non-fasting horses under the dust, and others chewing on the bridles And from this is the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast
r
(Maryam 19:26)
meaning: silence from speech. And His saying: as it was decreed upon those before you, meaning that it was imposed upon you like what was imposed upon those after you.
Before you.
Then the people of interpretation differed about those whom God meant by His saying:
h
As it was prescribed for those before you
, and about the meaning in which the likeness occurred between the obligation of our fasting and the fasting of those before us.

Some of them said: Those whom God informed us about the fasting that He imposed upon us, that it is like what was upon them, are the Christians. They said: The likeness for which He likened one to the other, is their agreement in the time and amount that is obligatory for us today as an obligation.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: I was told by Yahya bin Ziyad, from Muhammad bin Abaan Al-Qurashi, from Abu Umayya Al-Tanafisi, from Al-Shaʿbi that he said:
m: If I fasted the entire year, I would break my fast on the day in which there is doubt, so it is said: From Shaʿban, and it is said: From Ramadan. That is because the month of Ramadan was imposed upon the Christians as it was imposed upon us, so they turned it into a season. That is because they sometimes fasted it in the summer, counting thirty days. Then a generation came after them and they took confidence in themselves, so they fasted before the thirty days and after it a day. Then the other continued to follow the Sunnah of the century before him until it became fifty. That is his saying:
h
Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you

x: Others said: Rather, the comparison is only because their fasting was from the last evening prayer to the last evening prayer. That was the obligation of God, the Most High, upon the believers when He first imposed fasting upon them.
Those who said this statement agreed with those who said the first statement: That those whom God, the Most High, meant by His saying:
h
as it was prescribed for those before you
, are the Christians.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed
, decreed upon you is fasting
h
as it was prescribed for those before you

. As for those before us: they are the Christians, Ramadan was prescribed for them, and it was prescribed for them not to eat or drink after sleeping, and not to marry women during the month of Ramadan. So the fasting of Ramadan became difficult for the Christians, and it began to be imposed on them in the winter and summer. When they saw that, they gathered and made a fast in the season between winter and summer, and they said: We will add twenty days to atone for what we have done! So they made their fast fifty. The Muslims continued to do that, as the Christians did, until what happened with Abu Qais bin Sarmah and Umar bin Al-Khattab happened, and God made it permissible for them to eat, drink, and have sexual intercourse until dawn.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you
, he said: Fasting was prescribed for them from dusk to dusk.

x: Others said: Those whom God, the Most High, meant by His saying:
h
As it was prescribed for those before you
, are the People of the Book.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
O you who have believed
, decreed upon you is fasting
h
as it was prescribed for those before you
, the People of the Book.

x: Some of them said: Rather, it was for all people.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you

, he said: The month of Ramadan has been prescribed for people, as it was prescribed for those before them. He said: And God prescribed for people before Ramadan the fasting of three days of every month.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
O you who have believed
, decreed upon you is fasting
h
as it was prescribed for those before you
, Ramadan, God prescribed it for those who came before them.

x: The most correct of these statements is the statement of those who said: The meaning of the verse:
h
O you who have believed
h
fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you

from the People of the Book, for a specified number of days, which is the entire month of Ramadan. Because after Abraham, peace be upon him, he was commanded to follow Abraham, because God Almighty had made him an imam for the people, and God Almighty has informed us that his religion was the pure Islam, so He commanded our Prophet, peace be upon him, with the same as He commanded the prophets before him. As for the likening, it was only in time. That is because those who came before us were only required to fast the month of Ramadan, just as it was imposed on us. As for the interpretation of His statement, that you may become righteous, he means by it: so that you may avoid eating food, drinking alcohol, and having intercourse with women during it.
He says: Fasting and abstaining from what you would break your fast by not abstaining from, have been imposed upon you, so that you may avoid what breaks your fast during the time of your fast.
And a group of the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for His statement, that you may become righteous, he says: so that you may avoid eating, drinking, and women just as they avoided - meaning: like the Christians before you avoided.

x: He means that God Almighty has prescribed for you, O you who believe, fasting for a specified number of days. And the word days is in the accusative case with an implied verb, as if it were said: Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, that you fast for a specified number of days, as one says: I liked the strike, Zayd. And His statement:
h
As it was decreed upon those before you of fasting

, as if it was said: It was decreed upon you that which is like what was decreed upon those before you: that you fast a numbered number of days. Then the people of interpretation differed as to what God, the Exalted, meant by His statement: a numbered number of days.

Some of them said: The numbered number of days are fasting three days of every month. He said: And that was what was decreed upon the people of fasting before the month of Ramadan was decreed upon them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: They were required to fast three days of every month, and He did not name the month a number of days. He said: And this was the fasting of the people before, then God, the Exalted, decreed upon the people the month of Ramadan.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous, and it was three days of every month, then that was abrogated by what was revealed about fasting Ramadan. So this is the first fast, from the darkness.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Abd God bin Utbah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal:
m: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina and fasted the day of Ashura and three days of every month, then God, the Almighty, revealed the obligation of the month of Ramadan, so God revealed: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you, until he reached And upon those who can do it - a ransom - is the feeding of a poor person.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: God Almighty had prescribed for the people, before Ramadan was revealed, fasting three days of every month.
