x: Others said: Rather, the three days that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to fast before Ramadan was made obligatory, were voluntary. Their fasting. God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you
“for a specified number of days,” the days of the month of Ramadan, not the days that were fasted before the obligation of fasting the month of Ramadan became obligatory.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, he said, our companions told us:
m: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them, he ordered them to fast three days of every month as a voluntary fast, not as an obligation. He said: Then the fasting of Ramadan was revealed. Abu Musa said: His statement: ʿAmr ibn Murrah said:

c: Our companions told us,
m: meaning Ibn Abi Laila, as if Ibn Abi Laila was the one who said: Our companions told us.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us,
m: he heard ʿAmr ibn Murrah say, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:184 for a specified number of days. But whoever among you is ill or on a journey, the same number of other days.
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom
- the feeding of a poor person. But whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you, if you only knew. I heard Ibn Abi Laila, and he mentioned something similar.

x: We have already mentioned the statement of those who said: What is meant by His statement,
h
Fasting is prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you

, is the month of Ramadan. And what is more correct in my opinion is the statement of those who said: What God, the Most High, meant by His statement, a specified number of days, is the days of the month of Ramadan. This is because there is no report that can provide evidence that a fast was made obligatory upon the people of Islam other than the fast of the month of Ramadan, and then it was abrogated by the fast of the month of Ramadan. And God, the Most High, has made clear in the context of the verse that the fast that He, the Most High, has made obligatory upon us is the fast of the month of Ramadan and not any other times, by making clear the days that He informed us that He has prescribed fasting upon us by His statement, the month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was revealed.

Whoever claims that a fast was obligatory upon Muslims other than the fast of the month of Ramadan, which they are unanimously agreed upon as obligatory - and then that was abrogated - should be asked for proof of that from a report that would establish an argument, since that would not be known except from a report that would cut off the excuse. Since the matter in that is as we have described for what we have explained, the interpretation of the verse is: “Fasting is prescribed for you, O believers, as it was prescribed for those before you that you may become righteous. For a specified number of days, which is the month of Ramadan.” It is also possible that its meaning is: Fasting is prescribed for you, meaning the month of Ramadan. As for the specified days, they are those whose amounts and hours are counted.

What He, the Most High, means by His statement, But whoever among you is ill, is whoever among you is ill, who is required to fast, or is healthy and not ill and is on a journey, then an equal number of other days, meaning: then he must fast the number of days that he broke his fast during his illness or travel, from other days, meaning: from other days other than the days of his illness or travel. The subject in His statement, then an equal number of other days, is similar to the subject in His statement, then follow up with what is acceptable (al-Baqarah 2:178). This has already been explained there, so there is no need to repeat it. As for his statement:
h
And upon those who are able to do it
, a ransom of feeding a poor person, the reading of all Muslims is:
h
And upon those who are able to do it

, and this is the line of their Qur’ans. This is the reading that no one among the people of Islam is permitted to differ from, as they have all transmitted the correctness of that century after century.
Ibn Abbas used to read it, according to what was narrated from him:
h
And upon those who are able to do it
. Then the readers of that differed about the meaning of
h
And upon those who are able to do it

Some of them said: This was when fasting was first made obligatory, and whoever among the residents was able to fast it if he wished, and if he wished, he could break it and ransom himself, so he fed a poor person for each day he broke his fast, until that was abrogated.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn Utbah narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina and fasted the day of Ashura and three days of every month. Then God, the Almighty, made the month of Ramadan obligatory, so God revealed: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting until it reached And upon those who can do it [with difficulty] is a ransom [of feeding a poor person], so whoever wanted to fast could fast, and whoever wanted to break his fast could feed a poor person. Then God, the Almighty, made fasting obligatory for the healthy resident, and confirmed feeding the elderly who were unable to fast, so God, the Almighty, revealed: “So whoever witnesses the month shall fast it. And whoever is ill or on a journey” until the end of the verse.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, he said, our companions told us that
m: when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them, he ordered them to fast three days of every month voluntarily, not for sickness. He said: Then the fasting of Ramadan was revealed. He said: And they were people who were not accustomed to fasting. He said: And fasting was difficult for them. He said: Whoever did not fast fed a poor person, then this verse was revealed: “
h
And whoever is present among you in the month

shall fast it. And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days.” So the concession was for the sick and the traveler, and we were ordered to fast. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna said: Amr said:

c: Our companions told us,
m: meaning Ibn Abi Laila. It is as if Ibn Abi Laila was the one who said:
Our companions told us.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Dawud told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said:
m: I heard Amr ibn Murrah say: I heard Ibn Abi Laila, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom of feeding a poor person
, he said: Whoever wanted to fast, he fasted, and whoever wanted to break his fast and fed half a sa’ of a poor person, then it was abrogated by: The month of Ramadan up to His statement:
h
And whoever is present among you in the month

, he shall fast it. He told us. Ibn Humayd said, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, in a similar manner - and he added to it, he said: This verse abrogated it, and the first verse became for the old man who is unable to fast, he gives charity to a poor person for every day half a Saa.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Yahya bin Wadh Abu Tamilah narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri,
m: his saying:
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom of feeding a poor person

, so whoever among them wanted to fast, he fasted, and whoever among them wanted to ransom himself by feeding a poor person, he ransomed himself and his fast was complete. Then he said: And whoever is present among you [in the month], let him fast it, then he made an exception from that and said: And whoever is ill or on a journey, then an equal number of other days.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rifai narrated to us, he said, Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said,
m: I asked Al-A’mash about his saying:
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom of feeding a poor person

, so he narrated to us on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, he said: It abrogated: And whoever among you is present in the month, let him fast it. Omar bin Al-Muthanna narrated, Abdul-Wahhab narrated, Abdullah narrated, Nafi’, Ibn Omar said: This verse - meaning:
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom

, feeding a poor person - was abrogated by the one after it: “So whoever is present among you in the month shall fast it. And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number from other days.” Abu Kurayb narrated, Ibn Idris narrated, I heard Al-A’mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, regarding His statement:
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom

, feeding a poor person, he said: It was abrogated by: So whoever is present among you in the month shall fast it. Al-Walid bin Shuja’ Abu Hammam narrated, Ali bin Masahr narrated, from Asim, from Al-Sha’bi, he said: This verse was revealed:
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom

, feeding a poor person. A man would break his fast and give food in charity to a poor person for each day, then this verse was revealed: “So whoever is present among you in the month shall fast it. And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number from other days.” So the concession was only revealed for the sick and the traveler.

c: Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying, Ali ibn Masahir narrated to us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: This verse was revealed for all al-Nas 114:
h
And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom of feeding a poor person

. A man would break his fast and give his food in charity to a poor person, then this verse was revealed: And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. He said: So the concession was only revealed for the sick and the traveler.

c: Hannad narrated to us, saying, Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, who said:
m: I entered upon Ata’ while he was eating in the month of Ramadan, and he said: I am an old man, and fasting has been revealed, so whoever wanted to fast, fasted, and whoever wanted to break his fast, and fed a poor person, until this verse was revealed:
h
And whoever is present among you in the month

, let him fast it, and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. So fasting became obligatory for everyone, except for a sick person or a traveler or an old man like me, who ransoms himself.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said:
m: God said: O you who believe, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you. Ibn Shihab said: God decreed fasting upon us, so whoever wished could ransom himself from among those who were able to fast, whether healthy or sick or traveling, and he was not required to do anything else. Then when God made fasting obligatory for those who witnessed the month, whoever was healthy and able to do so, He waived the ransom from him, and whoever was traveling or sick, then a number of other days. He said: And the ransom that was accepted before that remained for the elderly who were unable to fast, and the one who was afflicted with thirst or an illness that prevented him from fasting.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God made the ransom for the first fast the feeding of a poor person, so whoever wished, whether a traveler or a resident, to feed a poor person and break his fast, that was a concession for him. Then God revealed about the last fast, Then a number of other days, and God did not mention about the last fast the ransom of a poor rabble, so the ransom was abrogated, and about the last fast, God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship, was confirmed, which is breaking the fast while traveling, and He made it a number of other days.

c: Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman bin Wahb told me, he said, my uncle Abdullah bin Wahb told me, he said, Amr bin Al-Harith told me,
m: Bakir bin Abdullah said, on the authority of Yazid, the client of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’, on the authority of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’ that he said, “We were in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, whoever wanted to fast, he fasted, and whoever wanted to break the fast, he ransomed himself by feeding a poor person, until the following was revealed: “
h
So whoever among you witnesses the month
, he shall fast it.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom

, the feeding of a poor person, he said: It was for all people. Then when And whoever among you witnesses the month shall fast it, was revealed, they were commanded to fast and make up for it, so He said: And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days.

c: Hannad told us, he said: Ali ibn Musahhir told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom
, the feeding of a poor person, he said: It was abrogated by the verse that follows it: And that you fast is better for you, if you only knew.

c: Hannad told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah,
m: h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom
, the feeding of a poor person, he said: It was abrogated by the verse that follows it: And whoever among you witnesses the month shall fast it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: Al-Fadl bin Khalid narrated to us, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
Fasting is prescribed for you - the verse - fasting is obligatory from the evening until the same time the next day

. So when a man prays the evening prayer, food and sexual intercourse are forbidden to him until the same time the next day. Then the other fast was revealed by permitting food and sexual intercourse all Surat Al-Baqarah 2:184 for a specified number of days. But whoever among you is ill or on a journey, the same number of other days.
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom

- the feeding of a poor person. But whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you, if you only knew. night long, which is His saying: And eat and drink until the white thread of the night becomes distinct to you from the black thread until His saying: Then complete the fast until the night (al-Baqarah 2:187). He also permitted sexual intercourse, saying: Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives (al-Baqarah 2:187). In the first fast there was a ransom, so whoever, whether a traveler or a resident, wanted to feed a poor person and break his fast, he could do so. God Almighty did not mention the ransom in the second fast, and said: Then an equal number of other days, so this second fast abrogated the ransom.

x: Others said: Rather, His saying:
h
And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person

, was a special ruling for the old man and the old woman who were able to fast. They were permitted to ransom their fast by feeding a poor person and breaking their fast. Then that was abrogated by His saying:
h
So whoever among you witnesses the month
, let him fast it, so they were required to fast like the young man, unless they were unable to. Fasting, so the ruling that was for them before the abrogation is established for them now as it is.

Those who said that: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Azra, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The old man and the old woman who were able to fast, were permitted to break their fast if they wished and to feed a poor person for each day. Then that was abrogated after that: “And whoever sights the month shall fast it. And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days.” And it was established for the old man and the old woman, if they were not able to fast, and for the pregnant and nursing woman if they fear.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And for those who are able to do it, he said: The old man and the old woman. Then he mentioned a hadith similar to Bishr’s, on the authority of Yazid. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, Muadh ibn Hisham narrated, my father narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The old man and the old woman had the permission to break their fast and feed others, based on the statement of God: And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person. He said: So they had the permission, then it was abrogated by this verse: And whoever among you witnesses the month shall fast it, so the permission was abrogated for the old man and the old woman if they were able to fast, and the pregnant and breastfeeding woman remained to break their fast and feed others. Al-Muthanna narrated, Hajjaj ibn al-Munhal narrated, Hammam ibn Yahya narrated, I heard Qatada say about the statement of God:
h
And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom

, the feeding of a poor person, he said: There was permission in it for the old man and the old woman who were able to fast to feed a poor person for each day and break their fast, then that was abrogated by the verse that came after it, so He said: The month of Ramadan until His statement: Then an equal number of other days, so this verse abrogated it.

x: The scholars saw and hoped that the concession would be established for the elderly man and the elderly woman who were unable to fast, to break their fast and feed a poor person for each day, and for the pregnant woman if she feared for what was in her womb, and for the nursing woman if she feared for her child.

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His statement:
h
And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom

, the feeding of a poor person, so the elderly man and the elderly woman were able to fast Ramadan, so God permitted them to break their fast if they wanted to, and they were required to pay the ransom for each day they broke their fast, feeding a poor person. Then God revealed after that: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur’an, until His statement: Then an equal number of other days.

x: Others who read it said:
h
And upon those who are able to do it
, that was not abrogated, nor anything of it, and it is a ruling that has been established since this verse was revealed until the Day of Judgment. They said: The interpretation of that is:
h
And upon those who are able to do it

- in their youth and youth, and in their health and strength - if they become sick and old and are unable to fast due to old age, is the ransom of feeding a poor person, not that the people were given permission to break their fast - while they were able to fast - if they ransomed themselves.
He mentioned who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom of feeding a poor person

. He said: As for those who are able to do it, a man who was able to do it and had fasted before that, then he is afflicted with pain or thirst or a long illness, or a breastfeeding woman who is unable to fast, then those are required to feed a poor person for each day. If he feeds a poor person, it is better for him, and whoever is required to fast and fasts, it is better for him.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abdah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arooba, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Azra, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If a pregnant woman fears for herself, and a breastfeeding woman fears for her child in Ramadan, he said: They break their fast and feed a poor person for each day, and they do not make up their fast.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: that he saw his mother-in-law who was pregnant or breastfeeding, and he said: You are like someone who cannot bear it. You must feed a poor person for each day, and you do not have to make up for it.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abda told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ali bin Thabit, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, like what Ibn Abbas said
m: about the pregnant or breastfeeding woman.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh narrated to us, saying, Yazid narrated to us, saying, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: saying: It was mentioned to us that Ibn Abbas said, to his pregnant or nursing mother: You are like those who cannot do it. You must pay a ransom and you do not have to fast. This is if she fears for herself.

c: Muhammad ibn Saad narrated to me, saying, my father narrated to me, saying, my uncle narrated to me, saying, my father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And for those who can do it, a ransom of feeding a poor person, he is an old man who was able to fast the month of Ramadan when he was young, then he grew old and was unable to fast, so he should give charity to one poor person for each day he broke his fast, when he broke his fast and when he ate suhoor.

c: Hannad narrated to us, saying, Abdah narrated to us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar - except that he did not say: when they break their fast and when they eat suhoor.

c: Hannad narrated to us, saying, Hatim Bani Ismail narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Harmalah, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, that he said
m: about the statement of God, the Most High: The ransom is the feeding of a poor person, he said: It refers to the old man who used to fast but became old and unable to do so, and the pregnant woman who is not required to fast, so each one of them must feed a poor person: a mudd of wheat for each day until Ramadan ends.

x: Others read it as: And for those who can afford it, a ransom is the feeding of a poor person, and they said: It refers to the old man and the old woman who have become too old to fast, so they are required to fast but are not able to do so, so they may break their fast and feed a poor person for each day they broke their fast. They said: The ruling of the verse has been established since it was revealed, it has not been abrogated, and they rejected the statement of those who said that it was abrogated. He who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it: They are entrusted with it.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ali ibn Mashair told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to recite: And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person. He said: So he used to say: It is valid for people today.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to recite it: And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person. He said: So he used to say: It is valid for people today.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to recite it: And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person. He said: So he used to say: It is valid for people today.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, that he said
m: about this verse: And for those who can bear it, - and this is how he used to recite it -: It is not abrogated. The old man was ordered to break his fast and feed a poor person for each day.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: that he recited: And for those who can bear it.

c: Hanad Taqal narrated to us, Wakiʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Imran ibn Hudayr, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, he said:
m: And for those who can bear it fast it, but those who can bear it are unable to do it.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn ʿAbbad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to me, on the authority of Abu ʿAmr,
m: the freed slave of ʿAishah, that ʿAishah used to recite: They can bear it.

c: Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ,
m: that he used to recite it: They can bear it. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid also used to recite it like this.

c: Hamid ibn Masʿadah narrated to us, he said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of ʿIkrimah:
m: And for those who can bear it. Ibn ʿAbbas said: He is the old man.

c: Ismail bin Musa Al-Suddi narrated to us, he said, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And upon those who can afford it he said: they take on the burden of it, they make it their business.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Muslim Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And upon those who can do it, a ransom is the feeding of a poor person, he said: the old man who cannot afford it, so he breaks his fast and feeds a poor person every day.

c: Muhammad bin Amr narrated to me, he said, Abu Asim narrated to us, he said, Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God: And upon those who can afford it, he said: they make it their business, a ransom is the feeding of one poor person. He said: This is an abrogated verse, and no concession is given except for the old man who cannot afford it, or the sick person who knows that he will not recover.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Those who can afford it means they are obliged to do so. The ransom is feeding one poor person. This was not permitted except for the old man who cannot afford to fast, or the sick person who he knows will not recover. This is from Mujahid.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to say: It is not abrogated.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
And upon those who can do it with difficulty

is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person, he said: Whoever is not able to fast except with difficulty, then he may break his fast and feed a poor person every day, and the pregnant woman, the nursing mother, the very old man, and the one who has a permanent illness.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:184 for a specified number of days. But whoever among you is ill or on a journey, the same number of other days.
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom
- the feeding of a poor person. But whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you, if you only knew. God, the Most High:
h
And upon those who can do it with difficulty

is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person, he said: He is the very old man, and the person who used to fast in his youth, but when he grew old he was unable to fast before he died, so he feeds a poor person every day. Hannad said: Ubaidah said: It was said to Mansur: Who feeds every day half a sa’? He said: Yes.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, he said:
m: I asked Mujahid about a woman of mine whose ninth day coincided with the month of Ramadan, and it coincided with intense heat, so he ordered me to break my fast and feed a poor person. He said: Mujahid said: This concession is also for the traveler and the sick, for God says:
h
And upon those who can do it with difficulty
, is a ransom of feeding a poor person.

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The pregnant woman, the nursing woman, and the very old man who is unable to fast, break their fast in Ramadan, and feed a poor person for each day. Then he recited:
h
And upon those who can do it with difficulty
, is a ransom of feeding a poor person.

c: Ali ibn Sa’id al-Kindi narrated to us, he said: Hafs narrated to us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And upon those who can do it with difficulty
, is a ransom of feeding a poor person, he said: The very old man who is unable to fast, breaks his fast by feeding a poor person for each day.

c: Al-Muthanna Qaq narrated to me, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, he said: Hammad narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: h
And upon those who can do it with difficulty
, is a ransom of feeding a poor person, he said: They are those who undertake it but are not able to do it, the old man and the very old woman.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: It is the old man and the old woman.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Ikrimah
m: that he used to recite it:
h
And upon those who are able to do it
, so they broke their fast.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It is confirmed for the elderly, the breastfeeding woman, and the pregnant woman, and upon those who are able to fast.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I said to Ata’: What does his statement:
h
And upon those who are able to do it

mean? He said: We have been informed that if an elderly person is not able to fast, he must ransom himself from each day by giving a poor person. I said: The elderly person who is not able to fast, or the one who is only able to do it with great effort? He said: Rather, the elderly person who is not able to do it with great effort or with anything. As for the one who is able to do it with great effort, then let him fast, and he has no excuse for not doing it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah bin Abi Yazid told me:
m: And upon those who can afford it, the verse, as if he meant the old man. Ibn Jurayj said: And Ibn Tawus told me, on the authority of his father, that he used to say: It was revealed about the old man who is unable to fast Ramadan, so he must redeem himself from each day by feeding a poor person. I said to him: How much is his food? He said: I do not know, except that he said: One day’s food.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Yahya, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: A ransom of feeding a poor person, he said: The old man who is unable to fast, breaks his fast and feeds a poor person every day.

x: The most appropriate of these statements in the interpretation of the verse is the statement of the one who said:
h
And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person

, abrogated by the statement of God Almighty: So whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it. Because the ha’ in his statement: And upon those who are able to fast, is from the mention of fasting and its meaning is:
h
And upon those who are able to fast is a ransom of feeding a poor person

. If this is the case, and all Muslims are unanimously agreed that whoever is able to fast the month of Ramadan from healthy men who are not travelers, it is not permissible for him to break his fast and redeem himself from it by feeding a poor person, it is known that the verse has been abrogated. This is in addition to what supports this statement from the reports that we mentioned earlier from Muadh ibn Jabal, Ibn Umar, and Salamah ibn al-Akwa’: that they were - after the revelation of this verse during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - in the fast of the month of Ramadan, they had the choice between fasting it and dropping the ransom from them, and breaking the fast and redeeming themselves from breaking it by feeding a poor person for each day?
And they used to do that until the verse was revealed:
h
So whoever among you witnesses the month
, let him fast it, so they were obligated to fast it, and the choice and ransom were nullified.

How can you claim a consensus among the people of Islam - that whoever is able to fast and has the condition you described, then it is not permissible for him to do anything but fast - when you know the statement of those who said: If a pregnant woman or a breastfeeding woman fears for her children, they may break their fast, even if they are able to fast with their bodies, with the report that was narrated about that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, “On the authority of Anas, he said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was eating lunch, and he said: Come, I will tell you, God has relieved the traveler, the pregnant woman, and the breastfeeding woman of fasting and half of the prayer”?

We did not claim a consensus regarding the pregnant woman or the breastfeeding woman, but rather we claimed it regarding the men whose condition we described. As for the pregnant and breastfeeding women, we know that they are not meant by His statement:
h
And upon those who are able to do it
, and men are not meant by it, because if they were meant by that without other men, it would have been said:
h
And upon those who are able to do it
, a ransom of feeding a poor person, because that is the speech of the Arabs, when the speech is isolated to report about them without men.
So when it was said:
h
And upon those who are able to do it

, it was known that what was meant by it was men without women, or men and women. So when it was confirmed by the consensus of all - that whoever among the healthy resident men is able to fast the month of Ramadan, then he is not permitted to break the fast and pay ransom, then men were excluded from being meant by the verse, and it was known that women were not meant by it for what we described: that the report about women when the speech is isolated to report about them is:
h
And upon those who are able to do it

, and the revelation is otherwise. As for the report narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, if it is authentic, then its meaning is that fasting has been lifted from the pregnant and breastfeeding woman as long as they are unable to do so, until they are able to do so and then make it up, just as fasting has been lifted from the traveler on his journey until he stays and makes it up - not that they were ordered to pay the ransom and break the fast without making it up being obligatory.

If the Prophet’s statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, God has lifted the fast from the traveler, the breastfeeding woman, and the pregnant woman, was an indication that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, meant that God Almighty lifted it from them by saying:
h
And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom of feeding a poor person

, then it would be obligatory for the traveler if he breaks his fast on his journey to make it up, and he is not obligated to do anything except pay the ransom for breaking it, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, combined his ruling with the ruling of the pregnant and breastfeeding woman. This statement, if anyone says it, is contrary to the apparent meaning of the Book of God, and to what all the people of Islam have agreed upon.

Some of the Arabists from Basra have claimed that the meaning of his statement, And upon those who are able to do so, is and upon those who are able to eat. This is because the interpretation of the scholars is different. As for the reading of those who read it: And upon those who can afford it, then the reading of the copies of the Muslims’ Qur’an is different, and it is not permissible for any of the Muslims to object with their opinion to what the Muslims have transmitted by inheritance from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a transmission that is apparent and decisive for the excuse. Because what the proof of the religion has brought is the truth that there is no doubt that it is from God. And what has been proven and established as proof that it is from God cannot be objected to with opinions, assumptions, and strange sayings. As for the meaning of the ransom, it is: the reward, from your saying: I ransomed this with this, meaning I rewarded him with it, and gave him a substitute for it.

The meaning of the statement: And upon those who are able to fast is the reward of feeding a poor person, for every day that he breaks his fast from the days of his fast that were prescribed for him. As for his saying: The ransom of feeding a poor person, then the readings differ in their reading. Some read by adding the ransom to the food, and lowering the food - and this is the reading of most of the readers of Medina - meaning: And upon those who are able to fast should ransom it with the food of a poor person. When he made the ransom a substitute for the ransom, it was added to the food, as it is said: I owed you a fine of a dirham, meaning: I owed you a fine of a dirham.

Others read it with the tanween of the ransom, and the raising of the food, meaning: clarifying in the food the meaning of the ransom required of the one who broke his obligatory fast, as it is said: I owed you a fine, a dirham, so clarify with the dirham the meaning of the fine, what is it? And what is its limit? This is the reading of the greatest of the readers of Iraq.

The first of the two readings is the correct reading of the one who read the ransom of food by adding the ransom to the food, because the ransom is a noun for the action, and it is not the food with which the fast is ransomed. This is because the ransom is a source of the saying of the speaker: I ransom the fast of this day with the food of a poor person, I ransom him a ransom, as It is said: I sat, and I walked. The ransom is an action, and the food is something else. Since that is the case, it is clear that the most correct of the two readings is adding the ransom to the food, and the error of the one who said: If he left adding the ransom to the food, it is more correct in meaning, because the food in his view is the ransom. So it is said to the one who says that: We know that the ransom requires ransomed, ransomed by, and ransom. If the food is the ransom and the fasting is what is ransomed by, then where is the verb of the ransom which is ransom?
This statement is clearly wrong and not problematic. As for the food, it is added to the poor. And the readers differ in reading that.

Some of them read it with the singular form of the poor, meaning: And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom of the food of one poor person for each day that they break their fast, as Muhammad bin Yazid al-Rafa’i told me, he said, Hussain al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Abu Amr that he read: ransom - nominative case with a tanween - food - nominative case without a tanween - poor, and he said: For each day a poor person. And on that the readers of the people of Iraq were great. And others read it with the plural of the poor, the ransom of the food of the poor, meaning:
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom

of the food of the poor for the month, if they break their fast for the whole month, as Abu Hisham Muhammad bin Yazid al-Rifai told us, on the authority of Yaqub, on the authority of Bashar, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of al-Hasan: The food of the poor, for the whole month.
And the reading that I like the most in that is the reading of the one who read: The food of a poor person on the singular, meaning:
h
And upon those who are able to do it
for every day they break their fast is a Surat Al-Baqarah 2:184 for a specified number of days. But whoever among you is ill or on a journey, the same number of other days.
h
And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom

- the feeding of a poor person. But whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you, if you only knew. ransom of the food of a poor person. Because in clarifying the ruling on the one who breaks his fast for one day, reaching to knowing the ruling on the one who breaks his fast for the whole month - and not in clarifying the ruling on the one who breaks his fast for the whole month, reaching to clarifying the ruling on the one who breaks his fast for one day, or days that are less than the days of the whole month - and that each one translates for the whole, and the whole does not translate for the whole.
Therefore we chose to read that with the singular. And the people of knowledge differed regarding the amount of food that they used to feed in that if they broke their fast.
Some of them said: The obligatory food for the poor person to break their fast for one day was half a sa' of wheat.
Some of them said: The obligatory food for the poor person to break their fast for the day was a mudd of wheat or from their other foods.
Some of them said: That was half a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of dates or raisins.
Some of them said: That is what the person who broke his fast ate on the day he broke his fast.
Some of them said: That was the pre-dawn and evening meals, and it would be the fast of the poor person. We have mentioned some of these opinions previously, so we disliked mentioning them again.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said what:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid and Ata', on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: But whoever volunteers good, and he added the food of another poor person, "it is better for him. And that you fast is better for you."

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement: But whoever volunteers good, he said: whoever feeds a poor person a sa’.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: But whoever volunteers good, it is better for him, he said: feeding poor people for each day, it is better for him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hanzala, on the authority of Tawus:
m: But whoever volunteers good, he said: feeding a poor person.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hanzala, on the authority of Tawus,
m: something similar. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, Abdurrahman narrated, Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Tawus: So whoever volunteers good, he said: Feeding a poor person. Al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Hajjaj narrated, he said: Hammad narrated, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Tawus, similarly. Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Amr ibn Harun narrated, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated, on the authority of Ata’ that he recited: So whoever volunteers good, with a light ta’, he said: Adding more than one poor person. Musa ibn Harun narrated, he said: Amr narrated, he said: Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi: So whoever volunteers good, it is better for him, so if he feeds two poor people, it is better for him. Al-Qasim narrated, he said: Al-Husayn narrated, he said: Hajjaj narrated, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated, Ibn Tawus informed me, on the authority of his father: So whoever volunteers good, it is better for him, he said: Whoever feeds another poor person.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is, whoever volunteers good and fasts the day of ransom.
Those who said this mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: So whoever volunteers good, it is better for him, meaning that whoever fasts with the ransom, it is better for him.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: So whoever volunteers good, and gives the poor more than his food.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: So whoever volunteers good, and adds more food, it is better for him.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Most High, made it general in His statement: So whoever volunteers good, and did not specify some meanings of good over others. For combining fasting with ransom is a voluntary act of good, and adding a poor person to the reward of ransom is a voluntary act of good. It is possible that God, the Most High, meant by His statement: So whoever volunteers good, that is, these meanings that the one who is redeemed from his fasting volunteers, so it is better for him. Because all of that is a voluntary act of good and voluntary acts of virtue.

God, the Most High, meant by His statement: And that you fast, what has been prescribed for you of the month of Ramadan, it is better for you than breaking it and redeeming it, as Musa ibn Harun told me, ʿAmr ibn Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And that you fast is better for you, and whoever undertakes to fast and fasts, it is better for him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: And that you fast is better for you, meaning: fasting is better for you than the ransom.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And that you fast is better for you...1. As for his statement: If you only knew, it means: If you only knew which of the two matters is better for you, O you who believe, of breaking the fast and ransoming, or fasting as God has commanded you.

evidence.text: As for his statement: And upon those who are able to do it, a ransom of feeding a poor person, the reading of all Muslims is: And upon those who are able to do it, and this is the line of their Qur’ans.
This is the reading that no one among the people of Islam is permitted to differ from, as they have all transmitted the correctness of that century after century.
Ibn Abbas used to read it, according to what was narrated from him: And upon those who are able to do it.
Then the readers of that differed about the meaning of And upon those who are able to do it.

Others who read it said: And upon those who are able to do it, that was not abrogated, nor anything of it, and it is a ruling that has been established since this verse was revealed until the Day of Judgment.

Others read it as: And for those who can afford it, a ransom is the feeding of a poor person, and they said: It refers to the old man and the old woman who have become too old to fast, so they are required to fast but are not able to do so, so they may break their fast and feed a poor person for each day they broke their fast.

He who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it: They are entrusted with it.

Hannad told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it: And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person.

Hannad told us, he said, Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it: And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom, the feeding of a poor person.

Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, that he said about this verse: And for those who can bear it, - and this is how he used to recite it -: It is not abrogated.
Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ, that he used to recite it: They can bear it.
Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid also used to recite it like this.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Ikrimah that he used to recite it: And upon those who are able to do it, so they broke their fast.

As for the reading of those who read it: And upon those who can afford it, then the reading of the copies of the Muslims’ Qur’an is different, and it is not permissible for any of the Muslims to object with their opinion to what the Muslims have transmitted by inheritance from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a transmission that is apparent and decisive for the excuse.
As for his saying: The ransom of feeding a poor person, then the readings differ in their reading.

Some read by adding the ransom to the food, and lowering the food - and this is the reading of most of the readers of Medina - meaning: And upon those who are able to fast should ransom it with the food of a poor person.

Others read it with the tanween of the ransom, and the raising of the food, meaning: clarifying in the food the meaning of the ransom required of the one who broke his obligatory fast, as it is said: I owed you a fine, a dirham, so clarify with the dirham the meaning of the fine, what is it?
This is the reading of the greatest of the readers of Iraq.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The first of the two readings is the correct reading of the one who read the ransom of food by adding the ransom to the food, because the ransom is a noun for the action, and it is not the food with which the fast is ransomed.

Since that is the case, it is clear that the most correct of the two readings is adding the ransom to the food, and the error of the one who said: If he left adding the ransom to the food, it is more correct in meaning, because the food in his view is the ransom.
And the readers differ in reading that.

Some of them read it with the singular form of the poor, meaning: And upon those who are able to do so is a ransom of the food of one poor person for each day that they break their fast, as Muhammad bin Yazid al-Rafa’i told me, he said, Hussain al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Abu Amr that he read: ransom - nominative case with a tanween - food - nominative case without a tanween - poor, and he said: For each day a poor person.
And on that the readers of the people of Iraq were great.

And others read it with the plural of the poor, the ransom of the food of the poor, meaning: And upon those who are able to do it is a ransom of the food of the poor for the month, if they break their fast for the whole month, as Abu Hisham Muhammad bin Yazid al-Rifai told us, on the authority of Yaqub, on the authority of Bashar, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of al-Hasan: The food of the poor, for the whole month.

Abu Jaʿfar said: And the reading that I like the most in that is the reading of the one who read: The food of a poor person on the singular, meaning: And upon those who are able to do it for every day they break their fast is a Surat Al-Baqarah 2:184 for a specified number of days.
Therefore we chose to read that with the singular.

x: The word month, as it is said, comes from fame. It is said: So-and-so drew his sword - if He took it out of its sheath and used it to attack anyone he wanted to strike. He brandished it for a month. And so it is with the 9th month of the month, when its crescent moon appears, and we brandish it when we enter the month. As for Ramadan, some of the people who know the Arabic language claimed that it was named thus because of the intense heat that used to occur in it, until the camels would be scorched, as is said for the month in which Dhul-Hijjah is performed, and in which Rabi' al-Awwal and Rabi' al-Akhir are the two months. As for Mujahid, he disliked saying Ramadan, and said: Perhaps it is one of the names of God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Nu'aym told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: that he disliked saying Ramadan, and said: Perhaps it is one of the names of God, but we say as God said: The month of Ramadan. I have previously explained that month is in the nominative case based on His statement: a numbered number of days, which are the month of Ramadan. It is possible that it is in the nominative case meaning: That is the month of Ramadan, and meaning: The month of Ramadan has been prescribed for you.

x: Some of the reciters have read it month of Ramadan in the accusative case, meaning: Fasting has been prescribed for you to fast the month of Ramadan.

Some of them have read it in the accusative case meaning: Fasting the month of Ramadan is better for you, if you only knew. It is also permissible to put it in the accusative case as a command to fast it, as if it were said: The month of Ramadan, so fast it. It is also permissible to put it in the accusative case as a time, as if it were said: Fasting was prescribed for you in the month of Ramadan. As for his statement: in which the Qur’an was sent down, it is mentioned that it was sent down on the Night of Decree from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, on the Night of Decree in the month of Ramadan. Then it was sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as God wanted it to be sent down to him, as Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Hassan ibn Abi Al-Ashras, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Qur’an was sent down all at once from the remembrance on the night of the twenty-fourth of Ramadan, and it was placed in the House of Honour.
Abu Kurayb said: Abu Bakr told us, and Al-Suddi said the same.

c: Isa ibn Uthman told me, he said, Yahya ibn Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Hassan, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: The Qur’an was sent down all at once on the Night of Decree in the month of Ramadan, and it was placed in the lowest heaven. Ahmad ibn Mansur narrated that Abdullah ibn Raja’ narrated that Imran al-Qattan narrated that Qatada narrated that Abu al-Malih narrated that Wathilah narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The scrolls of Abraham were revealed on the first night of the month of Ramadan, the Torah was revealed on the sixth of Ramadan, the Gospel was revealed on the thirteenth of the previous month, and the Qur’an was revealed on the twenty-fourth of Ramadan.” Musa narrated that Amr narrated that Asbat narrated that al-Suddi said:
h
The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was revealed

. As for in which the Qur’an was revealed, Ibn Abbas said: The month of Ramadan, and the blessed night is the Night of Decree, for the Night of Decree is the blessed night, and it is in Ramadan. The Qur’an was revealed all at once from the Scriptures to Bayt al-Ma’mur, which is the location of the stars in the lowest heaven where the Qur’an was revealed. Then it was revealed to Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after that in commands and prohibitions and in wars, messengers after messengers. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated that Abdul-Wahhab narrated that Dawud narrated that Ikrimah narrated that Ibn Abbas narrated that He said: God sent down the Qur’an to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree. When God wanted to reveal something from it, He revealed it. This is what He said: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (al-Qadr 97:1). Surat Al-Baqarah 2:185 The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights the month shall fast it.
h
And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days

. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [He intends] for you to complete the number and to glorify Allah. To that which He has guided you, and perhaps you will be grateful. Ibn Al-Muthanna said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar - and he added to it: So it was twenty years from the beginning and the end of it.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The entire Qur’an was sent down all at once on the Night of Decree in Ramadan, to the lowest heaven. So whenever God wanted to bring about something on earth, He would send it down from there, until He had gathered it.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Husayn told us, on the authority of Hakim ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The Qur’an was sent down on the Night of Decree from the highest heaven to the highest heaven all at once, then it was distributed throughout the years after that. He said: Ibn Abbas recited this verse: So I swear by the positions of the stars (al-Waqi’ah 56:75), he said: It was sent down in parts.

c: Ya’qub told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: It has reached us that the Qur’an was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid ibn Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us,
m: Ibn Jurayj recited it in His saying:
h
The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was revealed

. He said: Ibn Abbas said: The Qur’an was revealed all at once to Gabriel on the Night of Decree, and nothing would be revealed from it except by command. Ibn Jurayj said: Everything that was revealed from the Qur’an that was revealed from the Qur’an that year was revealed on the Night of Decree. So that was revealed from the seventh heaven to Gabriel in the lowest heaven, and Gabriel would not reveal anything of that to Muhammad except what his Lord had commanded him to do. And similar to that is: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (al-Qadr 97:1), and Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night (al-Dukhan 44:3).

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ubaydullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi al-Mujalid, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: a man said to him: Indeed, doubt has entered my heart regarding His statement:
h
The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was revealed

, and His statement: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night (al-Dukhan 44:3), and His statement: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree (al-Qadr 97:1), and God revealed it in Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi’dah, and other times! He said: It was only revealed in Ramadan on the Night of Decree and a blessed night all at once, then He sent down messengers according to the positions of the stars during the months and days. As for His statement: A guidance for mankind, it means guidance for the people to the path of truth and the right way. As for his saying: and clear proofs, he means: and clear proofs of guidance - meaning: of the explanation indicating the limits of God and His obligations and what is permissible and forbidden. And his saying: and the Criterion means: and the separation between truth and falsehood, as:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for and clear proofs of guidance and criterion, they are clear proofs of what is lawful and what is unlawful.

x: The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of witnessing the month.
Some of them said: It is the residence of the resident in his home.

i: They said:
x: So whoever enters the month of Ramadan while he is residing in his home, he must fast the entire month, whether he is absent after that and travels, or he stays and does not leave. Those who said that: Muhammad bin Hamid and Muhammad bin ʿIsa al-Damaghani told us, they said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Yahya, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his statement:
h
So whoever among you witnesses the month
, let him fast it, he said: It is its crescent in the home.
He means: If it appears while he is residing.

c: Yaʿqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas that he said
m: about his statement:
h
So whoever among you witnesses the month

, let him fast it: So if he witnesses it while he is residing, he must fast, whether he resides or travels. And if he witnesses it while he is traveling, then if he wishes he may fast, and if he wishes he may break his fast.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ubaydah -
m: regarding a man who witnesses Ramadan and then travels - he said: If you witness its beginning, then fast its end. Do you not see that He says: And whoever witnesses the month among you, let him fast it?

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham al-Qardoosi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said,
m: I asked Ubaydah: About a man who witnesses Ramadan while he is a resident? He said: Whoever fasts the beginning of the month, let him fast the end of it. Do you not see that He says:
h
And whoever among you witnesses the month
, let him fast it?

c: Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for
h
And whoever among you witnesses the month

, let him fast it, then whoever Ramadan enters upon him while he is residing among his family, let him fast it, and if he leaves during it, let him fast it, for it entered upon him while he is residing among his family.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Hammad told us, he said: Qatada told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah Al-Salmani, on the authority of Ali - according to what Hammad thinks - he
m: said: Whoever witnesses Ramadan while he is residing and has not left, then fasting is obligatory upon him, because God says:
h
And whoever among you witnesses the month
, let him fast it.
b.via: Ali - according to what Hammad thinks - he

c: Hannad ibn Al-Sari told us, he said: Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Muslim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said:
m: I asked Ubaydah Al-Salmani about the statement of God:
h
And whoever among you witnesses the month

, let him fast it, he said: Whoever is residing, let him fast it, and whoever witnesses it and then travels during it, let him fast it. Hannad narrated, he said: Wakiʿ narrated, on the authority of Ibn ʿAwn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of ʿUbaidah, he said: Whoever witnesses the beginning of Ramadan, let him fast the end of it. Hannad narrated, he said: ʿAbdah narrated, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArubah, on the authority of Qatadah, that ʿAli used to say: If Ramadan comes to him while he is a resident and then he travels, then he must fast. Hannad narrated, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahim narrated, on the authority of ʿUbaidah al-Dhabi, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: He used to say: If Ramadan comes to you, do not travel during it. If you fast one or two days during it and then travel, do not break your fast, fast it. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, he said: Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu al-Bukhtari, he said: We were with ʿUbaidah and he recited this verse: And whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it. He said: Whoever fasts part of it in a city, let him fast the rest of it when he leaves. He said: Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: If he wishes, he may fast, and if he wishes, he may break his fast.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us
m: - and Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah - they both said, Ayoub narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Yazid, on the authority of Umm Dhara, she said: I came to Aisha in Ramadan, she said: Where did you come from? I said: From my brother Hunayn. She said: What is the matter with him? She said: I bid him farewell, he wants to leave. She said: Give him my greetings and tell him to stand, if Ramadan caught up with me while I was on the way, I would stand for him.

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said: Ishaq bin Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Aflah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, he said:
m: Ibrahim bin Talhah came to Aisha to greet her, she said: Where do you want to go? He said: I wanted to perform Umrah. She said: So I sat until the month came upon you, then I went out in it! He said: My burden has gone out! She said: Sit, until you break your fast, then go out - meaning the month of Ramadan.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Whoever witnesses the month, let him fast what he witnessed of it.
Those who said this mentioned:

c: Hannad bin al-Sarri narrated to us, he said: Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq:
m: Abu Maysarah went out in Ramadan, until he reached al-Qantara, he called for water and drank.

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, he said:
m: Abu Maysarah went out on a journey in Ramadan, and he passed by the Euphrates while he was fasting, so he took a handful of it and drank it and broke his fast.

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said: Wakiʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marthad:
m: that Abu Maysarah traveled in Ramadan, and he broke his fast at the gate of the bridge - this is what Hannad said, on the authority of Marthad, but it is Abu Marthad.

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmara al-Asadi narrated to me, he said: ʿUbaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Israel informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Marthad:
m: that he went out with Abu Maysarah in Ramadan, and when he reached the bridge, he broke his fast.

c: Hannad and Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Wakiʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Masʿudi, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saʿd, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: I was with Ali in his estate, three days from Medina, and we set out towards Medina in the month of Ramadan, and Ali was riding and I was walking. He said: So he fasted - Hannad said: And I broke my fast - Abu Hisham said: And he ordered me to break my fast.

c: Hannad narrated to us, saying: Abd Al-Rahim narrated to us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Utbah, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Saʿd, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: I was with Ali bin Abi Talib when he came from his land, so he fasted, and he ordered me to break my fast, so he entered Medina at night, and he was riding and I was walking.

c: Hannad narrated to us, saying: Wakiʿ narrated to us
m: - and Ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us - they both said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Isa bin Abi ʿAzzah, on the authority of Al-Shaʿbi: That he traveled in the month of Ramadan and broke his fast at the gate of the bridge.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, saying:
m: Sufyan said to me: I prefer that you complete it. Ibn Al-Muthanna said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, who said: I asked Al-Hakam and Hammad, and I wanted to travel in Ramadan, so they said to me: Go out. Hammad said, Ibrahim said: But when it is the ten days, I prefer that he stay.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Al-Walid told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said:
m: If someone is caught fasting while he is residing in Ramadan and then travels, they said: If he wants, he may break his fast.

x: Others said: Whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it, meaning: whoever witnesses it while sane, an adult, and accountable, let him fast it.

Among those who said this was Abu Hanifa and his companions. They used to say: Whoever enters the month of Ramadan while he is healthy, sane, and an adult, then he must fast it. If he becomes insane after entering it while he is in the condition we have described, then he recovers after it has ended, he must make up for the days of the month during which he was insane, because he was one of those who witnessed it, and he is one of those who has an obligation. They said: And likewise if the month of Ramadan enters upon him while he is insane, except that he is one of those who, if he were of sound mind, would have to fast it, so the month will not end until he becomes healthy and recovers, or he recovers before the end of the month by a day or more, then he must make up for the fast of the entire month, except for the day that he fasted after he recovered, because he is one of those who witnessed the month.

They said: And Surat Al-Baqarah 2:185 The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights the month shall fast it.
h
And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days

. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [He intends] for you to complete the number and to glorify Allah. To that which He has guided you, and perhaps you will be grateful. if the month of Ramadan enters upon him while he is insane, and he does not recover until the entire month has ended, then he recovers, he is not obligated to make up for any of it, because he was not one of those who witnessed it and was accountable for its fast.

This is an interpretation that has no meaning. Because if insanity exempts someone who is obligated to fast because he lost his mind for the entire month, then this should be the case for everyone who lost his mind for the entire month of fasting. Everyone has agreed that whoever lost his mind for the entire month of fasting due to fainting or paralysis, and then regained consciousness after the month had passed, must make up the entire month. No one has disagreed with this and it is permissible to object to it against the Ummah. Since this is a consensus, then it is necessary that everyone who lost his mind for the entire month of fasting should be the case for someone who was unconscious. Since this is the case, it is known that the interpretation of the verse is different from the one interpreted by those who said this statement: that he who witnesses the month or part of it is obligated to fast it.

If this is invalid, then the interpretation of the interpreter who claimed that its meaning is: Whoever witnesses its beginning while residing and present must fast all of it, is invalid and corrupt, because the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are consistent: He left Medina in the year of the conquest in the month of Ramadan after fasting some of it, and he broke his fast and ordered his companions to break their fast.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, traveled in Ramadan from Medina to Mecca, until when he came to Usfan, he stopped there, and called for a vessel and placed it on his hand so that the people could see it. Then he drank it.”

c: Ibn Hamid and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Hannad told us, Ubaydah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly.

c: Hannad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said, Yunus ibn Bakir told us.
m: He said, Ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out on his journey in the year of the conquest, ten days before Ramadan had passed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fasted and the people fasted with him, until he reached Al-Kadeed - between Usfan and Amja - he broke his fast.”

c: Hannad and Abu Kurayb told us, they said, Abdah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out ten - or twentieth - days before Ramadan had passed in the year of the conquest, and he fasted until he reached Al-Kadeed and broke his fast.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Salim bin Nuh told us, he said, Umar bin Amir told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, he said:
m: “We set out with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, eighteen days before Ramadan had passed. Some of us were fasting and some of us were not fasting. The one who broke his fast did not criticize the one who fasted, nor the one who fasted criticized the one who broke his fast.” So since these two are corrupt, these two are corrupt. The two interpretations, based on what we have shown of their corruption - so it is clear that the correct interpretation is the third, which is the statement of the one who said:
h
So whoever among you witnesses the month
, let him fast it, all that he witnessed of it while staying, and whoever was sick or on a journey, then a number from other days.

x: God Almighty means by that: And whoever was sick or on a journey during the month and broke his fast, then he must fast the number of days that he broke his fast, from other days other than the days of the month of Ramadan. Then the people of knowledge differed regarding the illness with which God permitted breaking the fast, and obligated with it a number from other days.
Some of them said: It is the illness with which its owner is unable to stand for his prayer.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muʿadh bin Shuʿbah al-Basri told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim and Ismaʿil bin Muslim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: If the sick person is unable to pray standing, he should break his fast.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah - or Ubaydah - on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding the sick person who is unable to pray standing, he should break his fast. Meaning: in Ramadan.
b.via: Mughirah - or Ubaydah - on the authority of Ibrahim

c: Hannad told us, he said: Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Ismail, he said:
m: I asked Al-Hasan: When should the fasting person break his fast? He said: If fasting makes him unable to perform the obligatory prayers as commanded.

x: Some of them said: It is every illness in which the most common reason for its sufferer being ordered to fast is an increase in his illness that cannot be tolerated. This is the opinion of Muhammad bin Idris Al-Shafi’i, Al-Rabi’ told us about it.
Others said: It is eating, an illness called a disease.
Those who said that: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said:

c: Al-Hasan bin Khalid Al-Rabi’i told us, he said: Tarif bin Shihab Al-Attardi told us:
m: That he entered upon Muhammad bin Sirin in Ramadan while he was eating, and he did not ask him. When he finished, he said: This finger of mine hurts.
