x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that the illness for which God the Most High permitted breaking the fast in the month of Ramadan is that which the fasting person struggled with to an unbearable degree. So whoever is like that, then he may break the fast and make up a number of other days. This is because if that matter reaches that point, if he was not permitted to break the fast, then he has been restrained from hardship and prevented from ease.

c: This is different from what God informed us that
m: He intended for His creation in His saying:
h
God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship
. As for the one who is not struggling with fasting, then it is in the sense of the healthy person who is able to fast, so he must perform its obligation. As for His saying:
h
Then a number of other days
, its meaning is: a numbered number of days other than these days. As for the last, it is another plural like their plural of the greatest for old age and the nearest for nearness.
b.via: This is different from what God

x: Is not the last one of the descriptions of the days?
Yes.
Is not one of the days a day and it is masculine?
Yes.
How can one of the other be another and it is an attribute of the day, and there is no other?

One of the days, even if it is described by one of the other, is another, because days in the plural become feminine, so its attributes and descriptions become like the attributes of the feminine, as it is said: The days passed, plural, and it is not said: All of them, nor: the days of others.

God Almighty said: But whoever among you is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days, and what that means to you is: He must have an equal number of other days, as you have described previously. If that is its interpretation, then what do you say about someone who was ill or on a journey and fasted the month, and he is one of those who is allowed to break the fast? Does that suffice him by fasting a number of other days, or does that not suffice him, and the obligation of fasting a number of other days is fixed upon him in its form, even if he fasted the entire month? Is it permissible for someone who is sick or traveling to fast the month of Ramadan, or is it forbidden for him, and is it not permissible for him to fast, and is it obligatory for him to break the fast during it, until this one is able to stay and that one is cured?
The scholars have differed on all of that, and we will mention their differences on that, and we will inform the first of them with the correct one, God willing.
Some of them said: Breaking the fast during illness is an obligatory decree from God, and it is not a concession.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us
m: - and Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us - all of them, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Breaking the fast while traveling is a duty.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Wahb ibn Jarir told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ya’la, on the authority of Yusuf ibn al-Hakam, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Umar - or he was asked - about fasting while traveling, so he said: Tell me, if you gave charity to a man and he returned it to you, would you not get angry? For it is a charity from God that He gave to you.

c: Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi told us, he said, al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Humayd, he said, Abu Ja’far said:
m: My father did not fast while traveling, and he forbade it.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Yahya ibn Wadh told us, he said, Ubayd told us, on the authority of al-Dahhak:
m: that he disliked fasting while traveling. The people of this opinion said: Whoever fasts while traveling must make it up when he stays.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Nasr bin Ali al-Jahdhami told us, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Rabia bin Kalthoum told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man:
m: That Umar ordered the one who fasted while traveling to repeat it.

c: Muhammad bin al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of a man from Banu Tamim, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Umar ordered a man who fasted while traveling to repeat his fast.

c: Ibn Hamid al-Himsi told me, he said, Ali ibn Ma'bad told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah ibn Amr, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Ata', on the authority of al-Muharrir ibn Abi Hurairah, he said:
m: I was with my father on a journey in Ramadan, and I was fasting and he was breaking his fast. My father said to me: If you stay, you will make up for it.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, he said, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Asim,
m: the freed slave of Quraibah, he said: I heard Urwah ordering a man who had fasted while traveling to make up for it.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul Samad told us, he said, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Asim,
m: the freed slave of Quraibah: A man fasted while traveling, and Urwah ordered him to make up for it.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Subaih told us, he said, Rabia ibn Kulthum told us, on the authority of his father Kulthum:
m: Some people came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and they had fasted Ramadan while traveling, so he said to them: By God, it is as if you were fasting! They said: By God, O Commander of the Faithful, we have fasted! He said: So you were able to do it? They said: Yes. He said: Then make it up, then make it up. The reason for those who said this statement is that God, the Most High, has imposed, by His saying:
h
And whoever among you witnesses the month

, let him fast it, the fasting of the month of Ramadan on whoever witnesses it as a resident and not a traveler, and He has made it obligatory for whoever is sick or traveling to fast a number of days other than the days of the month of Ramadan, by His saying: And whoever is sick or on a journey,
h
then a number of other days

. They said: Just as it is not permissible for a resident to break the fast of the days of the month of Ramadan and fast a number of other days in their place—because what God has imposed upon him by witnessing the month is fasting the month and not other days—likewise it is not permissible for a traveler who does not witness it as a resident to fast it. Because what God has imposed upon him is a number of other days. They also based their argument on the hadith as follows:

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Saeed al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Yaqoub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Usamah ibn Zaid, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman,
m: on the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:185 The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights the month shall fast it.
h
And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days

. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [He intends] for you to complete the number and to glorify Allah. To that which He has guided you, and perhaps you will be grateful. authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, saying: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The one who fasts while traveling is like the one who breaks his fast while at home.’”

c: Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah ibn Saeed narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Ayyad narrated to us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father,
m: saying: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The one who fasts while traveling is like the one who breaks his fast while at home.’”

x: Others said: The permissibility of breaking the fast while traveling is a concession from God, the Most High, which He granted to His servants, and fasting is obligatory, so whoever fasts an obligation is harmful, and whoever breaks his fast, then he breaks his fast by God’s concession. They said: If he fasts while traveling, then he does not have to make it up if he stays.

Those who said that: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, he said, Urwah and Salim told us: They were with Omar bin Abdul Aziz when he was the governor of Medina, and they discussed fasting while traveling. Salim said: His cousin did not fast while traveling. Urwah said: Aisha used to fast. Salim said: I only took it from Ibn Omar. Urwah said: I only took it from Aisha. Until their voices rose. Omar bin Abdul Aziz said: O God, forgive! If it is easy, then fast, and if it is difficult, then break your fast.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, he said, a man told me:
m: Fasting while traveling was mentioned in the presence of Omar bin Abdul Aziz, then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibn Bashar.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq - and Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, Ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah, he said:
m: Umar ibn Al-Khattab went out on one of his journeys during the remaining nights of Ramadan, and he said: The month has begun to shine - Abu Kurayb said in his hadith: or: nine, and Yaqub was not sure - so why don’t we fast! So he fasted and the people fasted with him. Then he came back once, until he was at Ar-Rawha’, the new moon of the month of Ramadan, and he said: God has decreed the journey, why don’t we fast and not spoil our month! So he fasted and the people fasted with him.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Al-Hakam ibn Bashir told us, he said, my father told me
m: - and Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ubaydullah told us, he said, Bashir ibn Salman told us - on the authority of Khaithama, he said: I asked Anas ibn Malik about fasting while traveling, he said: I ordered my slave to fast but he refused. I said: Where is this verse:
h
And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days
? He said: It was revealed while at that time we were travelling hungry and stopping not full, but today we are travelling full and stopping full.

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said: Wakiʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Bashir ibn Salman, on the authority of Khaithamah, on the authority of Anas,
m: similarly.

c: Hannad and Abu al-Saʿib narrated to us, they said: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Anas:
m: that he was asked about fasting while traveling, so he said: Whoever breaks his fast, it is by permission of God, and whoever fasts, fasting is better.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ashʿath ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, on the authority of Muhammad ibn ʿUthman ibn Abi al-ʿAs, he said:
m: Breaking the fast while traveling is a permission, and fasting is better.
b.via: Muhammad ibn ʿUthman ibn Abi al-ʿAs

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: ʿAbd al-Samad narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Fayd narrated to us, he said:
m: ʿAli was our emir in Syria, and he forbade us from fasting while traveling. So I asked Abu Qursafah - a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Banu Laith. Abd al-Samad said: I heard a man from his people say: It is Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ - he said: If I fasted while traveling, I would not make it up.

c: Hannad told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Bastam ibn Muslim, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: If you fast, it is sufficient for you, and if you break your fast, it is a concession.

c: Hannad told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Kahams, he said:
m: I asked Salim ibn Abdullah about fasting while traveling. He said: If you fast, it is sufficient for you, and if you break your fast, it is a concession.

c: Hannad told us, he said: Abd al-Rahim told us, on the authority of Talhah ibn Amr, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: Whoever fasts, his harm is due, and whoever breaks his fast, it is a concession that he takes.

c: Hannad told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: Breaking the fast while traveling is a concession, and fasting is better.

c: Hannad told us, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: It is teaching. And it is not by determination - meaning the saying of God:
h
And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days
, if he wishes he may fast and if he wishes he may not fast.

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said: Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Concerning a man who travels in Ramadan, he said: If he wishes he may fast and if he wishes he may break the fast.

c: Hamid bin Mas'adah narrated to us, he said: Sufyan bin Habib narrated to us, he said: Al-A'wam bin Hawshab narrated to us, he said:
m: I said to Mujahid: Fasting while traveling? He said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to fast and break the fast. He said: I said: Which of them is more beloved to you? He said: It is only a concession, and fasting Ramadan is more beloved to me."

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Sa'id bin Jubayr,
m: Ibrahim and Mujahid, that they said: Fasting while traveling, if he wishes he may fast and if he wishes he may break the fast, and fasting is more beloved to them.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja’far narrated to us, he said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: Mujahid said
m: about fasting while traveling - meaning fasting Ramadan -: By God, there is nothing from them except lawful, fasting and breaking the fast, and God did not intend by breaking the fast except to make things easy for His servants.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja’far narrated to us, he said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Ash’ath Ibn Salim, he said:
m: I accompanied my father, Al-Aswad Ibn Yazid, Amr Ibn Maymun, and Abu Wa’il to Mecca, and they used to fast Ramadan and other times while traveling.

c: Ali Ibn Hasan Al-Azdi narrated to us, he said: Mu’afi Ibn Imran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Sa’id Ibn Jubayr:
m: Breaking the fast while traveling is a concession, and fasting is better.

c: Muhammad Ibn Abdullah Ibn Sa’id Al-Wasiti narrated to me, he said: Ya’qub Al-Zuhri narrated to us, he said: Salih Ibn Muhammad Ibn Salih narrated to us, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I said to Al-Qasim Ibn Muhammad: We travel in the winter during Ramadan, and if I fast during it, it is easier for me than to make it up in the heat! He said: God said:
h
God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship
. Whatever is easier for you, do it.

x: This statement is more correct in our view, because everyone agrees that if a sick person fasts the month of Ramadan - he is one of those who is permitted to break the fast due to his illness - his fasting is sufficient for him, and he does not have to make it up if he recovers from his illness after a number of other days. Thus, it is known that the ruling on the traveler is the same as his ruling on not having to make it up if he fasts during his travel. Because what is prescribed for the traveler as breaking the fast and ordered him to make up a number of other days is like what is prescribed for the sick person and ordered him to make it up. Then, the meaning of the verse is sufficient and does not require the testimony of a witness to the correctness of that from anything else. And that is the saying of God, the Most High:
h
God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship

There is no hardship greater than for someone who fasts during his travel to be required to fast several days from other days, and he has taken the trouble to perform his obligation in the most difficult of two situations until he has completed it and performed it. If a foolish person thinks that what he fasted was not his obligatory obligation, then in the saying of God, the Most High: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting “
h
the month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was revealed

,” there is what indicates that the month that is prescribed for fasting for every believer is the month of Ramadan, whether he is traveling or staying, because God, the Most High, mentioned that to the believers in His saying: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting “the month of Ramadan.” And His saying:
h
And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days
means: And whoever is ill or on a journey and breaks his fast with God’s permission, then he must fast several other days in place of the days that he broke his fast during his travel or illness.

Then in the convergence of the reports from the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, in his saying - when he was asked about fasting in Travel: If you wish, fast, and if you wish, break your fast. This is sufficient evidence for the validity of what we have said about it, based on something else.

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said,
m: Abd al-Raheem, Waki’ and Abdah narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha: Hamza asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about fasting while traveling - and he used to fast continuously - so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you wish, then fast, and if you wish, then break your fast.

c: Abu Kurayb and Ubayd ibn Ismail al-Habbari narrated to us, they said, Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said, Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us, on the authority of his father,
m: that Hamza asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, he said, Abu Zur’ah Wahb God ibn Rashid narrated to us, he said, Haywah ibn Shuraih narrated to us, he said, Abu al-Aswad narrated to us:
m: that he heard Urwah ibn al-Zubayr narrating on the authority of Abu Marawah, on the authority of Hamza al-Aslami, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: O Messenger of God, I fast continuously, so should I fast while traveling? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is only a concession from God to His servants, so whoever does it, it is good and beautiful, and whoever… He left it, so there is no blame on him. Hamza used to fast all the time, fasting while traveling and at home. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr used to fast all the time, fasting while traveling and at home, and even if he was sick he would not break his fast. Abu Marawah used to fast all the time, fasting while traveling and at home.” In this, along with similar reports that would take too long to include in the book, is evidence indicating the correctness of what is. We said: That breaking the fast is a concession, not a firm decision, and the clear statement on the correctness of what we said in the interpretation of his statement:
h
And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days

x: If someone says: The reports of what I said, even if they are consistent, are also consistent with his statement:
h
It is not righteousness to fast while travelling
? It is said: That is if the fasting is in a situation like the one reported from the Messenger of God, that he said in that to the one who said to him.

c: Al-Husayn bin Yazid Al-Sabiʿi narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin ʿAbd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Muhammad bin ʿAmr bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of Jabir:
m: “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man on his journey who had been shaded, and a group of people were around him, so he said: Who is this? They said: He is fasting. He said:
h
It is not righteousness to fast while travelling

x: I fear that this Sheikh made a mistake, and between Ibn Idris and Muhammad bin ʿAbd Al-Rahman, Shuʿbah.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin ʿAbd Al-Rahman bin Saʿd bin Zararah.
m: Al-Ansari, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:185 The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights the month shall fast it.
h
And whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days

. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [He intends] for you to complete the number and to glorify Allah. To that which He has guided you, and perhaps you will be grateful. on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man around whom people had gathered and who had been shaded. They said: ‘This man is fasting!’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘It is not righteousness for you to fast while traveling.’” So whoever fasts to the extent that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, then his fasting is not righteousness. This is because God, the Most High, has forbidden anyone to expose himself to that which will lead to his destruction, although there is a way to his salvation. Righteousness is only sought through the deeds that God has encouraged and urged, not through those deeds that He has forbidden. As for the reports that were narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The one who fasts while traveling is like the one who breaks his fast while at home, it may be possible that it was said to someone who had reached the level of fasting that he was given shade for, if that was said. It is not permissible to attribute that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the reports that came about that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have weak chains of transmission, and it is not permissible to use them as evidence in religion.
b.via: Muhammad bin ʿAbd Al-Rahman bin Saʿd bin Zararah

x: How can he conjoin the sick person, which is a noun, with his saying: or on a journey, and on is an adjective, not a noun?
It is permissible to coordinate on with the sick person, because it is in the meaning of a verb.
And the interpretation of that is: or a traveler, as God Almighty said:
He called us to his side or sitting or standing
so He connected the sitting and the standing to the lam in to his side, because its meaning is the action, as if He said: He called us lying down or sitting or standing.

God Almighty means by that: God wants you, O believers - by giving you permission in the case of your illness and travel to break the fast, and to make up a number of other days from the days that you broke the fast after your stay and after you recover from your illness - to make it easy for you and make it easy for you, because He knows how difficult that is for you in these circumstances, and He does not want hardship for you, meaning: He does not want hardship and difficulty for you, so He orders you to fast the month in these circumstances, while He knows how difficult that is for you and how heavy its burden would be for you if He were to make you fast, as Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muʿawiyah bin Salih told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: God wants you Ease and does not want hardship for you, he said: Ease is breaking the fast while traveling, and hardship is fasting while traveling.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about fasting while traveling, and he said: Ease and hardship. Take the ease of God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: God intends for you ease - he said: it means breaking the fast while traveling, and making a number of other days - and does not intend for you hardship.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship
, so intend for yourselves what God intends for you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Abdul Karim Al-Jazari, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: There is no hardship on the one who fasts or on the one who breaks the fast - meaning while traveling in Ramadan -
h
God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship

c: I was told by Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: he said, Al-Fudayl bin Khalid told us, he said, Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim regarding His statement:
h
God intends for you ease - breaking the fast while traveling
. And He does not intend for you hardship, fasting while traveling.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And that you may complete the number
, the number of days you broke your fast, which obligates you to make up for a number of days after you recover from your illness or stay in your travel, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His saying:
h
And that you may complete the number
, he said: The number of days the sick and the traveler broke their fast.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His saying:
h
And that you may complete the number
, he said: Completing the number is to fast what one broke of Ramadan while traveling or sick until he completes it, and if he completes it, he has completed the number.

x: What is upon him - with this waw in His saying:
h
And that you may complete the number - is it conjoined
The scholars of Arabic differed regarding that.
Some of them said: It is conjoined to what preceded it, as if it was said: And He intends for you to complete the number and to glorify God.

Some said: Kufa grammarians: This lam in his statement and that you may complete is a lam of ki, if it had been thrown in it would have been correct. He said: The Arabs include it in their speech with an implied verb after it, and it is not a condition for the verb that precedes it and it has the waw, don't you see that you say: I came to you so that you may do good to me, and you do not say: I came to you and that you may do good to me, so when you say it you mean: and that you may do good, I came to you. He said: This is found in the Qur'an a lot, including His statement: And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may listen to it
r
(Al-An'am: 113)
, and His statement: And thus did We show Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth that he might be among the certain
r
(Al-An'am: 75)
. If it did not have the waw, it would have been a condition for your statement: We showed him the kingdom of the heavens and the earth that he might be.
So if the waw is in it, then it has an implied verb after it, and to be among the certain means We showed him.
This statement is more correct in Arabic. Because his saying:
h
And that you may complete the waiting period
, there is no lam before it in the sense of the lam in his saying:
h
And that you may complete the waiting period
, so his saying:
h
And that you may complete the waiting period
is connected to it - and the entry of the waw with it indicates that it is a condition for the verb after it, since if the waw had been deleted, it would have been a condition for the verb before it.
He, the Most High, means: And to glorify God by mentioning to Him what He has bestowed upon you, of the guidance that He has let down.

Others from the people of the religions who were prescribed to fast the month of Ramadan as it was prescribed for you, but they went astray from it because God led them astray, and He humbled you with His honor, so He guided you to it, and enabled you to perform what God prescribed for you of fasting, and to thank Him for that by worshipping Him. And the remembrance that God urged them to glorify Him with is the Takbir on the Day of Eid al-Fitr, according to what a group of the people of interpretation interpreted.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Qais,
m: He said: I heard Zaid bin Aslam say: And glorify God for having guided you. He said: When he sees the crescent moon, then glorify God from the time he sees the crescent moon until the imam leaves, on the road and in the mosque, except that when the imam is present, he stops, and does not glorify God except with his glorification.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us,
m: he heard Sufyan say: And glorify God for having guided you. He said: It has reached us that it is the glorification on the day of Eid al-Fitr.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zaid said:
m: Ibn Abbas used to say: It is obligatory upon the Muslims when they see the crescent moon of Shawwal to glorify God until they finish their Eid, because God the Most High says:
h
And that you may complete the number and glorify God for having guided you

. Ibn Zayd said: When they go to the prayer place, they should say Allahu Akbar. When they sit, they should say Allahu Akbar. When the imam comes, they should be silent. When the imam says Allahu Akbar, they should say Allahu Akbar. They should not say Allahu Akbar when the imam comes except after his takbir. When he finishes and the prayer is over, the Eid is over. Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: The congregation, according to us, is to go to the prayer place with Allahu Akbar.

x: By that, God the Almighty meant: And to thank God for what He has bestowed upon you of guidance and success, and for making things easy for you, if He wills. Perhaps in this context it means so that, and that is why He abstained from it with His statement:
h
And that you may complete the number and glorify God for having guided you
, and perhaps you will be grateful.

evidence.text: Some of the reciters have read it month of Ramadan in the accusative case, meaning: Fasting has been prescribed for you to fast the month of Ramadan.
Some of them have read it in the accusative case meaning: Fasting the month of Ramadan is better for you, if you only knew.
He said: Ibn Abbas recited this verse: So I swear by the positions of the stars (al-Waqi’ah 56:75), he said: It was sent down in parts.
Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid ibn Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Ibn Jurayj recited it in His saying: The month of Ramadan in which the Qur’an was revealed.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, he said: Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu al-Bukhtari, he said: We were with ʿUbaidah and he recited this verse: And whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it.

x: God Almighty means by that: And if My servants ask you, O Muhammad, about Me: Where am I? I am near to them, I hear their supplication, and I answer the supplication of the supplicant among them. There is a difference of opinion about what this verse was revealed about.

Some of them said: It was revealed about a questioner who asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, is our Lord near so that we may talk to Him, or is He far so that we may call upon Him? So God revealed: "And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond" (al-Baqarah 2:17).

m: Ibn Hamid narrated to us that Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Abda al-Sijistani, on the authority of al-Salb ibn Hakim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us that Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us that Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said:
m: The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Where is our Lord? Then God Almighty revealed: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me” verse.

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed in response to a question from people who asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: At what time should they call upon God?

Who said that: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said: When the verse, And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you’
r
(Ghafir 40:60)
was revealed, they said: Then the verse, And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near was revealed until His saying, that they may be guided.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding His saying,
h
I answer the call of the caller when he calls upon Me
, they said: If only we knew at what time we would call! Then the verse, And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near was revealed.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to me, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah claimed that it had reached him: When the verse, And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you’
r
(Ghafir 40:60)

was revealed, the people said: If only we knew at what time we would call! Then it was revealed: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.
h
So let them respond to Me
and believe in Me that they may be guided.”

c: Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, he said: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.” He said: There is no believing servant who calls upon God except that He answers him. If what he calls upon is provision for him in this world, God will give it to him, and if he does not have provision in this world, He will store it up for him until the Day of Resurrection, and will ward off harm from him thereby.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Al-Layth ibn Saʿd narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Salih, on the authority of someone who told him:
m: It reached him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He did not give to the one who supplicated and withheld the answer, because God says: Call upon Me, I will respond to you
r
(Ghafir 40:60)

. The meaning of those who interpreted this interpretation: And when My servants ask you concerning Me: At what time do they call upon Me? Indeed, I am near to them in All the time, I answer the call of the caller when he calls upon me.
b.via: on the authority of someone who

x: Others said: Rather, it was revealed in response to the words of a people who said - when God said to them:
Call upon Me, I will respond to you
-: To where do we call Him?
Those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Mujahid said: Call upon Me, I will respond to you
r
(Ghafir 40:60)
. They said: To where? So, it was revealed: "Wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. Indeed, God is All-Encompassing and Knowing" (al-Baqarah 2:115).
Others said: Rather, it was revealed in response to a people who said: How do we call upon Him?

Those who said that: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, he said: It was mentioned to us that when God revealed: Call upon Me, I will respond to you
r
(Ghafir 40:60)
, some men said: How do we call upon Him, O Prophet of God? So God revealed: And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near until His saying: they guide. As for his saying:
h
So let them respond to me
, he means:
h
So let them respond to me
with obedience.

i: It is said:
x: I responded to him, and I responded to him, meaning I answered him, as Ka’b bin Sa’d al-Ghanawi said: Farewell, he called: O He who answers to the dew? But no one answered him at that time.
He meant: He did not answer him. And similar to what we said about that, Mujahid and a group other than him said.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Al-Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: Mujahid said, his statement:
h
So let them respond to me
, he said: So let them obey me. He said: Responding is obedience.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak about his statement:
h
So let them respond to me
, he said: Obeying God. And some of them said: The meaning of
h
So let them respond to me
is: So let them call upon Me.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Mansour bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Raja Al-Khurasani, he said:
m: h
So let them respond to me
, so let them call upon Me. As for his statement:
h
And let them believe in Me
, it means: And let them be truthful. That is:
h
And let them believe in Me
, if they respond to Me with obedience. That I am for them, behind their obedience to Me, in reward for it, and My bestowing of honor upon them for it. As for the one who interpreted His statement,
h
So let them respond to Me
, that it means: So let them call upon Me, he interpreted His statement,
h
And let them believe in Me
h
and let them believe in Me
that I respond to them.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Mansur bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abu Raja Al-Khurasani:
m: h
And let them believe in Me
, he said: That I respond to them. As for His statement,
h
So that they may be guided
, he means:
h
So let them respond to Me
with obedience,
h
and let them believe in Me
, so that they may be truthful in their obedience to Me with the reward from Me for them, and
h
so that they may be guided
by that from their actions and be guided, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Saad told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
So that they may be guided
, he said:
h
So that they may be guided

x: So if someone says to us: What is the meaning of this statement from God, the Most High? You see many people calling upon God, but their supplication is not answered, and He said: I answer the supplication of the supplicant when he calls upon Him. It was said that there are two meanings to this: One of them is that what is meant by the supplication is doing what God has urged and commanded. So the interpretation of the statement is: And when My servants ask you concerning Me, then indeed I am near to whoever obeys Me and does what I have commanded him to do. I will answer him with the reward for his obedience to Me if he obeys Me. So the meaning of the supplication is: the servant asking his Lord for what He promised His friends for their obedience by their work in obeying Him. And the meaning of the answer from God that He has guaranteed for him is fulfilling for him what He promised to those who work for Him by what He has commanded them to do, as was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his saying:
h
Supplication is worship

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Dhirr, on the authority of Yasaa’ Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:
h
Supplication is worship
. Then he recited: “And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] contemptible.”
r
(Ghafir 40:60)

So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informed us that supplication to God is nothing but worshipping Him and asking Him, by working for Him and obeying Him. And in a similar manner to what we have said about that, he mentioned that Al-Hasan used to say:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Mansur bin Harun told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Qatadah bin Anas, on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said
m: about it: Call upon Me; I will respond to you.
r
(Ghafir 40:60)

, he said: Work and be glad, for it is the right of God to respond to those who believe and do righteous deeds and increase them from His bounty. The other interpretation is that its Surat Al-Baqarah 2:186 And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.
h
So let them respond to Me

[by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided. meaning is: I respond to the supplication of the supplicant when he calls upon Me, if You will. So that, even though it is general in its recitation, is specific in its meaning.

x: What God Almighty meant by His saying: It is lawful for you is that it is made permissible for you. And what He meant by His saying:
h
On the night of fasting is on the night of fasting

. As for al-Rafth, it is a euphemism for sexual intercourse in this context. It is said: It is al-Rafth and al-Rafth. It has been narrated that in the reading of Abdullah: It is lawful for you on the night of fasting to have sexual intercourse with your wives. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about the interpretation of al-Rafth.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam al-Masri told me, he said, Ayoub ibn Suwaid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Al-Rafth is sexual intercourse, but God is generous, He uses a euphemism. Ibn Humayd narrated, he said: Jarir narrated, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Bakr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Muhammad ibn Saad narrated, he said: My father narrated, he said: My uncle narrated, he said: My father narrated, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Rafath is sexual intercourse. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Rafath is intercourse with women. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated, he said: Abu Asim narrated, he said: Isa narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God, Lawful to you on the night of the fast is approaching your wives, he said: sexual intercourse. Al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated, he said: Shibl narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Rafath is sexual intercourse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdul Kabir Al-Basri told us, he said, Ad-Dahhak bin Othman told us, he said,
m: I asked Salim bin Abdullah about his statement:
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the intimacy with your wives
, he said: It is sexual intercourse.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the intimacy with your wives

, he said: sexual intercourse. Rafath in other than this place means obscene speech, as Al-Ajjaj said: About language and obscene speech Abu Jaʿfar said: By that, the Most High means: Your women are your clothing and you are their clothing.

x: How can our women be our clothing, and we are their clothing, and clothing is only what is worn?

There are two meanings for this: One of them is that each one of them was made a clothing for the other, because they are stripped when sleeping, and they are gathered in one garment, and the body of each one of them is joined to the other, like what he wears on his body from his clothing, so it was said to each one of them: He is the clothing of the other, as Nabigha of Banu Jaʿdah said: If the bedfellow bends her, she collapses and becomes like a garment on him. It is narrated: She bent down, so he referred to their meeting naked in one bed with the clothing, just as the clothing refers to the human body, as Laila said, describing camels that a people rode: They threw light garments at her, and she did not resemble anyone but the frightened ostrich.

i: Meaning: They threw it themselves and rode it, as Al-Hudhali said:
x: He disavowed the blood and sins of the murdered man, and the blood of the murdered man hung on her garment.
Meaning: with her belt, herself. And that is what Al-Rabi’ used to say.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them

, meaning: They are a blanket for you and you are a blanket for them. The other interpretation is that He made each one of them a clothing for the other, because he is a dwelling place for him, as the Most High said: He has made the night a clothing for you (al-Furqan 25:47), meaning by that a dwelling place in which you live. Likewise, a man’s wife is his dwelling place, so he dwells in her, as the Most High said: And He made from her her husband that he might find rest in her (al-Aʿraf: 189), so each one of them is a clothing for the other, meaning that he finds rest in her. And this is what Mujahid and others used to say about that. And it may be said about what covers something and conceals it from the sight of those who look at it: it is its clothing and its covering, so it is permissible to say:
h
They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them
, meaning: that each one of you is a cover for his companion - in what happens between you of intercourse - from the sight of all the other people. And Mujahid and others used to say about that what:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them
, he said: a reassurance for them.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them
, Qatada said: They are a dwelling place for you, and you are a dwelling place for them.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They are clothing for you, he said: a dwelling place for you, and you are clothing for them, he said: a dwelling place for them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them
, he said: sexual intercourse.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi told me, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them
, he said: They are a rest for you and you are a rest for them.

x: If someone were to say to us: What is this betrayal that the people were betraying themselves with, which God repented of and forgave them? It would be said: Their betrayal of themselves, which God mentioned, was in two things, one of them: intercourse with women, and the other: eating and drinking at a time when that was forbidden to them, as Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, he said, Ibn Abi Laila told us: When a man broke his fast and then slept, he would not have intercourse with her, and when he slept, he would not eat, until ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab came wanting his wife. His wife said: I was asleep! He thought she was sick, so he had intercourse with her. He said: A man from the Ansar came and wanted to eat, and they said: Shall we heat something for you? 1 He said: Then this verse was revealed:
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives
Al-Akhbar 2:100.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, he said:
m: They used to fast three days of every month, and when Ramadan came, they used to fast, and if a man did not eat when he broke his fast until he slept, he would not eat until the same amount of time, and if he slept or his wife slept, he would not have intercourse with her until the same amount of time. Then an old man from the Ansar called Sarmah ibn Malik came and said to his family: Feed me. She said: Until I make you something hot! He said: His sleep overcame him and he slept. Then Umar came and his wife said to him: I was asleep! He did not excuse her, and he thought she was sick, so he had intercourse with her. So this one and that one spent the night tossing and turning, noon and night, and God revealed concerning that:
h
And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn appears to you distinct from the black thread
, and He said: Now then have intercourse with them, and God forgave that, and it became a Sunnah.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, he said:
m: They used to eat and drink and have intercourse with women as long as they did not sleep, and when they slept they left off eating and drinking and having intercourse with women. There was a man from the Ansar called Abu Sarmah who worked on his land. He said: When it was time to break his fast, he slept, and he became fasting and exhausted. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him, he said: Why do I see you exhausted!

c: So he told him
m: what had happened. A man circumcised himself in the matter of women, so God revealed:
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives
, to the end of the verse.

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq,
m: on the authority of Al-Baraa’ - similar to the hadith of Ibn Abi Laila which Amr ibn Murrah narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila - he said: When they fasted and one of them slept, he would not eat anything until the next day. Then a man from the Ansar came who had worked on his land and was exhausted and ate, so his eyes overcame him and he slept, and the next morning he became exhausted, so this verse was revealed:
h
And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn appears to you distinct from the black thread

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Raja Al-Basri told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said:
m: When a man of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was fasting and slept before breaking his fast, he would not eat for the same amount of time. Qais bin Sarmah Al-Ansari was fasting, and he almost went out that day to work in his land. When it was time to break the fast, he came to his wife and said: Do you have any food? She said: No, but I will go and get some for you. Sleep overcame him and he slept. Then his wife came and said: You have fallen asleep! It was not until midday when he fainted. He mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed concerning him:
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives
to from the black thread. They rejoiced greatly over that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Salih told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives

, that is because the Muslims in the month of Ramadan, when they prayed the ‘Isha’ prayer, women and food were forbidden to them until the same time the next day. Then some of the Muslims had food and women in Ramadan after the ‘Isha’ prayer, among them ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab, so they complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: “God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them,” meaning: marry them, and eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn Al-Mubarak informed us, on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, he said:
m: Musa bin Jubayr, the client of Banu Salamah, told me that he heard ‘Abdullah bin Ka’b bin Malik narrating on the authority of his father, he said: When the people fasted in Ramadan and went to sleep in the evening, food, drink, and women were forbidden to him until he broke his fast the next day. One night, Umar ibn al-Khattab returned from the Prophet (peace and Surat al-Baqarah 2:187
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives

. They are your clothing and you are their clothing. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has decreed for you, and eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the nightfall.
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques

. These are the limits set by God, so do not approach them. Thus does God make clear His verses to the people that they may become righteous. blessings of God be upon him) after he had spent the evening with him. He found his wife asleep, so he wanted to sleep with her. She said: I slept! He said: You did not sleep! Then he had intercourse with her. Ka’b ibn Malik did the same thing. Umar ibn al-Khattab went to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the morning and told him. God the Most High revealed: “God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Al-Hajjaj told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Thabit told us:
m: Umar ibn al-Khattab had intercourse with his wife one night in Ramadan, and that was difficult for him, so God revealed:
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, my father told me, my uncle told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement: “
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives

. They are your clothing and you are their clothing.” to and pardoned you. When people first embraced Islam, if one of them fasted, he would fast that day, until evening came, and he would eat some food between it and the night, until he prayed, and food was forbidden to them until the evening of the following night. While Umar ibn al-Khattab was sleeping, his soul tempted him to go to his wife to fulfill some need, so when he washed himself, he began to cry and blame himself with the most severe blame I have ever seen, then he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I apologize to God and to you for this sinful self, for it made it attractive to me and I had intercourse with my wife! Do you find any dispensation for me, O Messenger of God? He said: You were not worthy of that, O Umar! So when he reached his house, he sent for him and informed him of his excuse in a verse from the Quran, and God commanded His Messenger to place it in the middle verse of Surat al-Baqarah, and He said: Lawful to you on the night of fasting is the intimacy with your wives to God knows that you were betraying yourselves, meaning by that: what Umar ibn al-Khattab did, so God purified his forgiveness. He said: Then He turned to you and pardoned you, so now have intercourse with them to from the black thread, so He made it permissible for them to have sexual intercourse, eat, and drink until dawn becomes clear to them.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: It is permissible for you on the night of the fast to have sexual intercourse with your wives. He said: A man from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, would fast during the day, and when evening came he would eat, drink, and have sexual intercourse with his women, and when he went to sleep, all of that was forbidden to him until the same time the next day. And among them were men who would deceive themselves in that, so God pardoned them and made that permissible for them after and before sleep throughout the night.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to fast during Ramadan. When evening came - then he mentioned something like the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr, and added to it: And among them were men who would betray themselves, and Umar ibn al-Khattab was among those who betrayed himself, so God forgave them and made that permissible for them after sleep and before it and throughout the night.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, he said, Ismail ibn Sharus told me, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas? That a man - I have forgotten his name - from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Ansar, came one night while he was fasting, and his wife said to him: Do not sleep until we prepare food for you! So he slept, and she came and said: By God, you slept! He said: No, by God! She said: Yes, by God! He did not eat that night, and he became fasting and fainted, so permission was revealed for him.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: God knows that you were betraying yourselves. And at the beginning of fasting, they were commanded to pray three days of every month, and two rak’ahs in the morning and two rak’ahs in the evening. So God made it permissible for them during their fast - in three days, and in the first of what was made obligatory for them in Ramadan - if they broke their fast. And food, drink, and sexual intercourse with women were permissible for them as long as they did not sleep. And if they slept, that was forbidden to them until the same time the next year. And the betrayal of the people was that they would eat or take from food and drink and sexual intercourse with women after sleeping, and that was the betrayal of the people themselves. Then God made it permissible for them after that to eat, drink, and sexual intercourse with women until dawn.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives
, he said: Before this verse, if one of the people went to sleep at night, it was not permissible for him to eat or drink or to approach his wife until the next night.

x: Some of the Muslims did that, some of them ate or drank after their sleep, and some of them had intercourse with their wives, so God permitted that for them.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: Ramadan was prescribed for the Christians, and it was prescribed for them not to eat or drink after sleeping, and not to marry women during the month of Ramadan. So it was prescribed for the believers as it was prescribed for them. The Muslims continued to do this as the Christians did, until a man from the Ansar called Abu Qais bin Sarmah, who used to work on the walls of Medina for wages, came and brought some dates to his family. He said to his wife: Replace these dates with flour and make it hot, so that I may eat it, for the dates have burned my stomach! So she went and replaced it for him, then she made it and took a long time, so he slept, so I woke him up. He hated to disobey God and His Messenger, and he refused to eat, and he became fasting. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him in the evening and said: What is the matter with you, Abu Qais? Have you become thirsty this evening? 1 So he told him the story. Omar ibn al-Khattab had had intercourse with his slave girl - among some believers who could not control themselves - and when Omar heard Abu Qais's words, he was afraid that something would be revealed about Abu Qais, so he remembered, so he stood up and apologized to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I seek refuge in God, I had intercourse with my slave girl and could not control myself last night! When Omar spoke, those people spoke, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You did not deserve that, O son of al-Khattab! So he abrogated that from them, and said: “It is lawful for you on the night of the fast to approach your wives. They are your clothing and you are their clothing. God knows that you were betraying yourselves” - meaning: you were betraying them - “So He turned to you and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has decreed for you” - meaning: have intercourse with them. And he returned to Abu Qais and said: And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I said to Ata’, It is lawful for you on the night of the fast to approach your wives. He said: They did not touch women in Ramadan? They did not eat or drink after sleeping until the night of the following day. If they touched them before sleeping, they saw no harm in that. Then a man from the Ansar had intercourse with his wife after he had gone to sleep, and he said: I have circumcised myself! Then the Qur’an was revealed, and women, food, and drink were made lawful for them until the white thread of dawn could be distinguished from the black thread. He said: Mujahid said: The companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to fast during Ramadan, and when evening came, they would eat, drink, and have intercourse with their wives. When they went to sleep, all of that was forbidden to them, even the same as the next day. And there were men among them who would deceive themselves in that, so He pardoned them and made it lawful for them after sleeping and before it at night, saying: Lawful for you on the night of the fast is the intimacy with your wives (al-Qasim narrated to me, he said, al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, that He said about this verse: It is lawful for you on the night of the fast to have sexual relations with your wives, like the statement of Mujahid, and he added to it: That Umar ibn al-Khattab said to his wife: Do not sleep until I return from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So she went to sleep before he returned, so he said to her: You are not sleeping! Then he had intercourse with her, until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so this verse was revealed. Ikrimah said: And eat and drink the verse was revealed about Abu Qais ibn Sirmah, from Banu Khazraj, he ate after sleeping.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban,
m: that Sirmah ibn Anas came to his family one night while he was an old man, and he was fasting, and they did not prepare food for him, so he put his head down and fell asleep, and his wife brought him his food and said to him: Eat. He said: I have already slept! She said: You did not sleep! Then he became hungry and exhausted, so God revealed: And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread. As for direct contact in the speech of the Arabs, it is the contact of skin to skin, and the skin of a man is his visible skin. God only used the phrase Now have intercourse with them as a metaphor for sexual intercourse. He says: Now that I have made lawful for you sexual relations with your wives, have intercourse with them during the nights of the month of Ramadan until dawn breaks, which is the distinction between the white thread and the black thread of dawn. And what we have said about sexual intercourse is said by a group of the people of interpretation.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Sufyan told us
m: - and Abdul Hamid ibn Sinan told us, he said: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sufyan - and Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Hakam told me, he said: Ayoub ibn Suwaid told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Sexual intercourse is intercourse, but God is generous, He uses euphemisms.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah ibn Salih told us, Muawiyah ibn Salih told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Now have intercourse with them, marry them.

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Direct contact is marriage.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I said to Ata’, His saying: Now have intercourse with them, he said: sexual intercourse. And everything in the Qur’an that mentions intercourse is sexual intercourse itself. Abdullah bin Katheer said the same as Ata’ said: In food, drink and women.

c: Hamid bin Mas’adah told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Shu’bah told us
m: - and Ibn Surat al-Baqarah 2:187
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives

. They are your clothing and you are their clothing. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has decreed for you, and eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the nightfall.
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques
. These are the limits set by God, so do not approach them. Thus does God make clear His verses to the people that they may become righteous.

c: Bashar told us, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us
m: - on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Direct contact is sexual intercourse, but God calls whomever He wills by whatever He wills.

c: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me,
m: who said: Hisham told us, who said: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly.

c: Musa bin Harun told me,
m: who said: Amr bin Hammad told us, who said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Now have sexual intercourse with them, meaning: have intercourse with them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me,
m: who said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, who said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Direct contact is sexual intercourse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me,
m: who said: Suwaid told us, who said: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata, similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, who said, Abdah bin Abi Lubabah told me,
m: who said: I heard Mujahid say: Direct contact, in the Book of God, means sexual intercourse.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told us, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, Al-Awza’i said: Someone told us
m: who heard Mujahid say: Direct contact, in the Book of God, means sexual intercourse. They differed in the interpretation of His statement: And seek what God has prescribed for you.

x: Some of them said: Children.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abdah bin Abdullah Al-Saffar Al-Basri told me,
m: who said: Ismail bin Ziyad Al-Katib told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid: And seek what God has prescribed for you, he said: Children.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us,
m: who said: Sahl bin Yusuf and Abu Dawud told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: I heard Al-Hakam say: And seek what God has prescribed for you, he said: Children.

c: Ibn Hamid told us,
m: who said: Abu Tamilah told us, who said: Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding His statement: And seek what God has prescribed for you, he said: Children.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, Muammil told us, Abu Mawdud told us, Bahr bin Musa told us:
m: I heard Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan say about this verse: And seek what God has decreed for you, he said: children.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And seek what God has decreed for you, meaning children.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told us, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And seek what God has decreed for you, meaning children.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And seek what God has decreed for you, he said: children. If this woman does not give birth, then this one.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of someone
m: who heard al-Hasan regarding the statement of God, And seek what God has prescribed for you, he said: It means children.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father,
m: on al-Rabiʿ regarding the statement of God, And seek what God has prescribed for you, he said: What has been prescribed for you of children.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the statement of God, And seek what God has prescribed for you, he said: Intercourse.

c: I was told by al-Husayn bin al-Faraj,
m: he said: al-Fadl bin Khalid told us, he said: Ubayd bin Salman told us, he heard al-Dahhak bin Muzahim regarding his statement, And seek what God has prescribed for you, he said: Children.

x: Some of them said that the meaning of this is: the Night of Decree.

Those who said that: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Amr bin Malik, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And seek what God has decreed for you, he said: The Night of Decree. Abu Hisham said: This is how Muadh read it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Al-Hasan bin Abi Ja’far told us, he said, Amr bin Malik told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement: And seek what God has decreed for you, he said: The Night of Decree.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: what God has made lawful for you and permitted for you.

Who said that: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And seek what God has prescribed for you, meaning: what God has made lawful for you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, he said, Qatada said
m: about that: Seek the concession that has been prescribed for you. And some of them read that: And follow what God has prescribed for you.

x: Who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abd al-Razzaq narrated, Ibn Uyaynah narrated, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: How do you read this verse: And seek or follow? He said: Whichever you wish! He said: You should read the first one.

The correct interpretation of this, in my opinion, is to say: God the Most High said: And seek - meaning: seek - what God has decreed for you - meaning: what God the Most High has decreed for you. God the Most High means: seek what I have written for you in the Preserved Tablet that it is permissible so that you may be divorced. And seeking a child, if a man seeks it through intercourse with his wife, is from what God has written for him in the Preserved Tablet. Likewise, if he seeks the Night of Decree, it is from what God has written for him. Likewise, if he seeks what God has made lawful and permissible, it is from what He has written for him in the Preserved Tablet. All the good meanings required may be included in His statement: And seek what God has decreed for you, but the most similar meaning to the apparent meaning of the verse is the statement of those who said: Its meaning is and seek what God has decreed for you of children, because it follows His statement: Now have intercourse with them, meaning have intercourse with them.

So His statement: And seek what God has decreed for you, meaning: and seek what God has decreed in your intercourse with them of children and offspring, is more similar to the verse than other interpretations that are not supported by the apparent meaning of the revelation, nor by any report from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement:
h
Until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn

Some of them said: By His statement: The white thread, He means the light of day, and by His statement: The black thread, He means the blackness of the night. So its interpretation, according to the statement of those who say this statement: And eat at night during the month of your fast, and drink, and have intercourse with your women, seeking what God has decreed for you of children, from the beginning of the night until… That the light of day falls upon you with the rising of dawn from the darkness and blackness of the night.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told me, he said, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, he said, Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding the statement of God the Most High: Until the white thread of dawn appears to you distinct from the black thread, he said: The night from the day.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn appears to you distinct from the black thread
, he said: Until the day appears to you distinct from the night, Then complete the fast until the night.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn appears to you distinct from the black thread

, then complete the fast until the night, they are two clear signs, so do not let the call of a hypocritical or mentally weak muezzin prevent you from your suhoor, for they call to prayer at a long time in the night. And you may see a white spot on the pre-dawn meal called the false dawn, which the Arabs used to call the false dawn. But do not let that prevent you from eating your pre-dawn meal, for dawn cannot be hidden: it is a way across the horizon. And eat and drink until dawn appears to you, and when you see that, then stop eating.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn appears to you distinct from the black thread

, meaning night from day. So he made it permissible for you to have sexual intercourse, eat and drink until the dawn appears to you. Then when the dawn appears, he made it forbidden for them to have sexual intercourse, eat and drink until they completed their fast until the night. So he ordered them to fast during the day until the night, and he ordered them to break their fast at night.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us,
m: and it was said to him: What do you think of the statement of God the Most High: The white thread from the black thread of dawn? He said: - You have a broad back. He said: This is the passing of the night and the coming of the day. It was said to him: Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Adi bin Hatim? He said: Yes, Hisin told us. The reason for those who said this statement and interpreted the verse in this way is:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Mujalid bin Saeed, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, he said:
