m: I said: O Messenger of God, what about the statement of God: And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread? He said: It is the whiteness of the day and the blackness of the night.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Numayr and Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Mujalid ibn Saʿid, on the authority of ʿAmir, on the authority of ʿAdi ibn Hatim, he said:
m: “I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he taught me Islam and described the prayers to me, how to pray each prayer at its time. Then he said: When Ramadan comes, eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread, then complete the fast until nightfall. I did not know what it was, so I twisted two threads of white and black, and I looked at them at dawn, and I saw that they were the same. So I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, I have memorized everything you advised me to do, except ‘the white thread from the black thread’! He said: What prevented you, O Ibn Hatim? And he smiled as if he knew what I had done. I said: I twisted two threads of white and black, and I looked at them at night and I found that they were the same! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed until his molars were seen, then he said: Did I not tell you ‘from “Fajr”? It is the light of day and the darkness of night.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Malik bin Ismail narrated to us, he said, Dawud and Ibn Ulayyah both narrated to us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, he said:
m: “I said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: What is the “white thread from the black thread?” Are they two threads, white and black? He said: You have a broad back, if you see the two threads.” Then he said: No, but it is the blackness of the night and the whiteness of the day.

c: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, he said, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said, Abu Ghassan told us, he said, Abu Hazim told us, on the authority of Sahl ibn Saʿd, he said:
m: This verse was revealed: And eat and drink until the white thread appears to you distinct from the black thread, but of dawn was not revealed. He said: So when men wanted to fast, one of them would tie a black thread and a white thread to his feet, and he Surat al-Baqarah 2:187
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives

. They are your clothing and you are their clothing. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has decreed for you, and eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the nightfall.
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques

. These are the limits set by God, so do not approach them. Thus does God make clear His verses to the people that they may become righteous. would continue eating and drinking until it became distinct to him. Then God revealed after that: of dawn, so they knew that what was meant by that was night and day. Those who interpreted the statement of God, the Most High, until the white thread appears to you distinct from the black thread of dawn, said that it is the whiteness of the day and the blackness of al-Layl 92:the description of that whiteness is that it is widespread and extensive in the sky, its whiteness filling the roads with light. As for the bright light in the sky, that is not what God meant by His statement: the white thread from the black thread.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aʿla al-Sanʿani told us, he said, Mu'tamir bin Sulayman said:
m: I heard Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz: The bright light in the open sky is not the dawn, but that is the false dawn. The dawn is only when the horizon is exposed.

c: Salim bin Junada Al-Suwai’i told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, he said:
m: They did not consider the dawn to be your dawn, they considered it to be the dawn that fills the houses and streets.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Uthman narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim:
m: They only saw the dawn that spreads in the sky.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arfa narrated to us, he said, Ruh bin Ubadah narrated to us, he said, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said, Ata’ informed me that
m: he heard Ibn Abbas say: They are two dawns. As for the one that shines in the sky, it does not make anything permissible or forbidden, but the dawn that is visible on the tops of the mountains is the one that makes drinking forbidden.

c: Al-Hasan bin Al-Zubayrkan Al-Nakha’i narrated to us, he said, Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Tharban, he said,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The dawn is two dawns. The one that is like the tail of a scorpion does not make anything forbidden, and the one that flies across the horizon makes prayer permissible and fasting forbidden.”
b.via: Muhammad bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Tharban

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Waki’ and Ismail bin Subaih and Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Sawadah bin Hanzalah, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are two dawns. “Nor does the call to prayer of Bilal prevent you from eating Suhoor, nor the prolonged dawn, but the dawn that is spreading in the horizon.”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Muawiyah bin Hisham Al-Asadi narrated to us, he said, Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Sawadah, he said:
m: I heard Samurah bin Jundub mentioning on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he heard him saying: Do not be deceived by the call of Bilal, nor this whiteness, until the dawn appears and breaks.

x: Others said: The white thread is the light of the sun. And the black thread is the blackness of the night.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Hannad bin Al-Sari narrated to us, he said, Ubaydah bin Hamid narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, he said:
m: My father traveled with Hudhayfah, he said: So he traveled, until we feared that dawn would surprise us, he said: Is there anyone among you who is eating or drinking? He said: I said to him: So whoever wants to fast, no? He said: Yes!

c: Hanad and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I went out with Hudhayfah to al-Mada'in in Ramadan, and when dawn broke he said: Is there anyone among you eating or drinking? We said: As for a man who wants to fast, no. He said: But I am! He said: Then we walked until we were slowing down the prayer, he said: Is there anyone among you who wants to have suhoor? We said: As for a man who wants to fast, no. He said: But I am. Then we walked until we were slowing down the prayer, he said: Is there anyone among you who wants to have suhoor? We said: As for a man who wants to fast, no. He said: But I am. Then we walked until we were slowing down the prayer, he said: Is there anyone among you who wants to have suhoor? He said: We said: As for a man who wants to fast, no. He said: But I am. Then we walked until we were slowing down the prayer, he said: So he walked down and had suhoor.

c: Harun bin Ishaq Al-Hamadani narrated to us, he said: Musʿab bin Al-Muqaddam narrated to us, he said: Israʿil narrated to us, he said: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Hubayrah, on the authority of Ali:
m: That when he prayed Fajr, he said: This is when the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black thread.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Al-Salt narrated to us, he said: Ishaq bin Hudhayfah Al-ʿAttar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said:
m: I ate Suhoor in the month of Ramadan, then I went out and came to Ibn Masʿud, and he said: Drink. I said: I have already eaten Suhoor! He said: Drink! So we drank, then we went out while the people were praying. Abu Kuraib narrated that Abu Muawiyah narrated from Ash-Shaibani from Jabalah ibn Suhaim from Amir ibn Matar who said: I came to Abdullah ibn Masoud in his house, so he brought out some leftover food from his suhoor meal and we ate with him. Then the prayer was called and we went out and prayed. Khallad ibn Aslam narrated that Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated from Abu Ishaq from Abdullah ibn Muqal from Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhaifa who said: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq and I were on the same roof during Ramadan. One night I came and said: Will you not eat, O successor of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He gestured with his hand: Stop. Then I came to him again and said: Will you not eat, O successor of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He gestured with his hand: Stop. Then I came to him again and said: Will you not eat, O successor of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He looked at the dawn and gestured with his hand: Stop. Then I came to him and said: Will you not eat, O successor of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He said: Bring your lunch! He said: So I brought it to him and he ate, then he prayed two rak'ahs, then he stood up to pray.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Mahdi told us, he said: Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The witr is at night, and the suhoor is during the day. Other than that has been narrated on the authority of Ibrahim.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja'far told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The suhoor is at night, and the witr is at night.

c: Hakam told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ja'far, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The suhoor and the witr are between the tathweeb and the iqamah.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja'far told us, he said: Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Shabib Ibn Gharqadah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Hubban, he said:
m: We ate suhoor with Ali, then we went out and the prayer had been called, so we prayed.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Muammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Hubban ibn al-Harith, who said:
m: I passed by Ali while he was in the house of Abu Musa and he was eating suhoor. When I arrived at the mosque, the prayer was called.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Safar, who said:
m: Ali ibn Abi Talib prayed the dawn prayer, then he said: This is when the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black thread. The reason for those who said this statement is that the time is the day and not the night. They said: The beginning of the day is the rising of the sun. And its last part is its setting. They said: If its beginning was the rising of dawn, then its last part would have to be the setting of twilight. They said: And in the consensus of the proof that the last part of the day is sunset, there is clear evidence that its beginning is its rising. They said: And in the hadith “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he ate suhoor after the rising of dawn,” there is the clearest evidence for the correctness of our statement. Mentioning the hadiths that were narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that:

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Abu Bakr narrated to us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said,
m: I said: Did you eat suhoor with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes. He said: If I wanted, I could say that it was the daytime, except that the sun had not risen.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Abu Bakr narrated to us, he said:
m: Asim did not lie about Zur, nor did Zur about Hudhayfah. He said: I said to him: O Abu Abdullah, did you eat suhoor with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes, it was the daytime, except that the sun had not risen. Ibn Bashar narrated, Mu'ammil narrated, Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to eat suhoor while I could see the arrows falling. I said: Is it still dawn? He said: It is dawn, except that the sun has not yet risen." Ibn Hamid narrated, Al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated, Amr ibn Qays and Khallad al-Saffar narrated, on the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish, who said: One day I woke up and went to the mosque, and I said: If only you would pass by Hudhayfah's door! So he opened it for me, and I entered, and he was heating food for him. He said: Sit down until you eat. He said: I want to fast. So he brought his food and ate, and I ate with him. Then he went to a she-camel in the house, and he milked it from one side, and I milked it from the other side, and he handed it to me, and I said: Don't you see the dawn? He said: Drink! So I drank, then I came to the door of the mosque and the prayer was called, so I said to him: Tell me about the last suhoor that you ate with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: It was the morning meal, except that the sun had not risen.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi told us, he said: Ruh ibn Ubadah told us, he said: Hammad told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If one of you hears the call to prayer and the vessel is in his hand, he should not put it down until he has finished his need from it.” Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated, saying: Ruh ibn Ubadah narrated, saying: Hammad narrated, on the authority of Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly, and he added to it: The muezzin would call to prayer when dawn broke. Ibn Humayd narrated, saying: Yahya ibn Wadhah narrated, saying: Al-Husayn narrated, and Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated, saying: I heard my father saying: Al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated, both of them said: Abu Ghalib narrated, on the authority of Abu Umamah, saying: The prayer was called and the vessel was in the hand of Umar. He said: Should I drink it, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes! So he drank it. Ibn Humayd narrated, saying: Yahya ibn Wadhah narrated, saying: Yunus narrated, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, saying: Bilal said: “I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call him to prayer while he wanted to fast. He called for a vessel and drank, then he handed it to me and I drank, then he went out to pray.”

c: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told me, he said, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muqal, on the authority of Bilal, he said:
m: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to call him to the dawn prayer, and he wanted to fast. So he called for a vessel and drank, then he handed it to me and I drank, then we went out to pray.

x: The most correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the interpretation that was narrated on the Surat al-Baqarah 2:187
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives

. They are your clothing and you are their clothing. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has decreed for you, and eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the nightfall.
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques

. These are the limits set by God, so do not approach them. Thus does God make clear His verses to the people that they may become righteous. authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The white thread is the whiteness of the day, and the black thread is the blackness of the night.

This is well-known in the speech of the Arabs. Abu Dhuʿad al-Ayyadi said: When a curtain lit up for us and a thread of light appeared from the morning As for the reports that were narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he drank or had suhoor and then went out to pray, this does not invalidate what we have said about that. Because it is not strange that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drank before dawn and then went out to pray, since the prayer - the dawn prayer - was during his time, and it was performed after dawn had appeared and its appearance was clear, and the call to prayer was made before its appearance. As for the report that was attributed to Hudhayfah: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to have suhoor and I could see the arrows falling,” it was verified and he was asked: Is it after dawn?

He did not answer that it was after dawn, but he said: It is dawn. This is from his statement that it is possible that its meaning is: It is dawn because of its proximity to it, even if it is not the same, as the Arabs say: This is so-and-so, she is likening him to someone other than the one she named, saying: He is he, likening him to him. Likewise, the statement of Hudhayfah: It is the morning, meaning: It is the morning, similar to it and close to it. Ibn Zayd said about the meaning of the white and black thread, what Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
h
Until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn

, he said: The white thread is what comes from under the night, reveals the night - and the black is what is above it. As for his statement: of dawn, then the Most High means: When the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread which is of dawn, and that is not all of dawn, but when that white thread becomes distinct to you, O believers, from dawn that which comes from under the night which is above it is the blackness of night, then from that time fast, then complete your fast from that until night.
And like what we said about that, Ibn Zayd used to say.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about his statement: of dawn, he said: That white thread is of dawn in relation to it, and not all of dawn. When this thread comes, which is its beginning, then the prayer is permissible and food and drink are forbidden to the fasting person.

x: In the words of God Almighty: “And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the night,” there is clear evidence of the error of the statement of the one who said: Eating and drinking are permissible for the one who wants to fast until sunrise. Because the white thread of dawn becomes distinct when the first light of dawn begins to rise. God, the Most High, has set a limit for those who are obligated to fast during the time that He has permitted eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse. So whoever claims that he may exceed that limit, it is said to him: What do you think if it is permissible for him to delay that until the morning or midday?
The one who says that is opposed to the Ummah.
And you are opposed to what the Book of God and the transmission of the Ummah have indicated, so what is the difference between you and him in terms of origin or analogy?
The difference between me and him is that God has ordered fasting during the day and not during the night, and the day is from sunrise.

That is what your opponents say, and the day, according to them, begins with the rising of the dawn, and that is the light of the sun and the beginning of its rising without its rising being complete, just as the end of the day is the beginning of its setting without its setting being complete. It is said to those who say that: If the day, according to you, is as you have described, it is the rising of the sun, the completion of its rising, and the disappearance of all the darkness of the night and the disappearance of its blackness - then likewise, according to you, the night is the completion of the setting of the sun, the disappearance of its light, and the completion of the blackness of the night. And its darkness?
That is so!
It is obligatory for fasting to be until the sunset and the disappearance of the light of the sun and its whiteness from the horizon of the sky!

That is so! They have made fasting obligatory until the sunset which is whiteness. And that is a statement that if they said it is refuted by the transmission of the argument, which is not permissible in what it has transmitted unanimously - error and forgetfulness, and that is sufficient as evidence of its error. And if they say: Rather, the beginning of the night is the beginning of its veil and its darkness, and the setting of the eye of the sun from us.

And likewise the beginning of the day: the rising of the first light of the sun, and the setting of the first veil of the night. Then the statement is reversed on him in that, and he asks the difference between that, so he will not say a statement about one of them except that he will make the same statement about the other. As for dawn, it is a source from the saying of the one who said: The water burst forth, burst forth at dawn, if it sprang forth and ran. And it was said to the one who rises from the signs of the sun’s light from the rising of the sun, dawn, because its light emanates upon them, and it pours upon them in their ways and their places, like the gushing water from its source. As for His statement: Then complete the fast until the night, then the Most High mentioned the fasting by saying that its last time is the approach of the night, just as He defined breaking the fast and the permissibility of eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse, and the beginning of the fast, by the coming of the first day and the first departure of the last night.

Thus He indicated that there is no fasting at night, just as there is no breaking the fast during the day on the days of fasting, and that the one who continues fasting starves himself in disobedience to his Lord, just as:

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said:
m: Abu Muawiyah, Wakiʿ and ʿAbdah narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham bin ʿUrwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of ʿAsim bin ʿUmar, on the authority of ʿUmar, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When the night comes and the day departs and the sun sets, then the fasting person has broken his fast.’”

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said: Abu Bakr bin ʿAyyash narrated to us, he said: Abu Ishaq al-Shaibani narrated to us
m: - and Hannad bin al-Sarri narrated to us, he said: Abu ʿUbaidah and Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-Shaibani - and Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated to us - and Abu al-Saʿib narrated to me, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of al-Shaibani - they all said in their hadith, on the authority of ʿAbdullah bin Abi Awfa, he said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey and he was fasting. When the sun set, he said to a man: Get off and slaughter a sheep for me. They said: If only you could spend the evening, O Messenger of God! He said: Get off and slaughter a sheep for me. The man said: O Messenger of God, if only you could spend the evening! He said: Get off and slaughter a sheep for me. He said: O Messenger of God, we have a day ahead of us! He said it to him a third time, so he got down and cut off his camel’s tail for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When night comes from here - and he pointed with his hand towards the east - then the fasting person has broken his fast.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Rafi’, who said:
m: God has made fasting obligatory until nightfall, so when nightfall comes, you are breaking your fast. If you wish, eat, and if you wish, do not eat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Abd al-A’la told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu al-A’aliyah,
m: that he was asked about continuous fasting, so he said: God has made fasting obligatory for this nation during the day, so when nightfall comes, if he wishes, he may eat, and if he wishes, he may not eat.

c: Ya’qub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told me, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, who said: Abu al-A’aliyah said
m: about continuous fasting: God said: Then complete the fast until the nightfall, so when nightfall comes, he is breaking his fast, so if he wishes, he may eat, and if he wishes, he may not eat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Ibn Dukayn told us, on the authority of Mis’ar, on the authority of Qatadah, who said: Aisha said:
m: Complete the fast until nightfall - meaning that she disliked continuous fasting.

x: If someone were to say: What is the reason for continuous fasting when one continues fasting? I have learned what: Abu Al-Sa'ib narrated to you, he said, Hafs narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, he said: Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr used to fast continuously for seven days, then when he grew old he made it five, then when he grew very old he made it three.

c: Abu Al-Sa'ib narrated to us, he said, Hafs narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, he said:
m: Ibn Abi Ya'mar used to break his fast once every month.

c: Ibn Abi Bakr Al-Muqaddami narrated to us, he said, Al-Farawi narrated to us, he said,
m: I heard Malik say: Amer bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubairi used to fast continuously on the sixteenth and seventeenth nights of Ramadan, not breaking his fast in between, so I met him and said to him: O Abu Al-Harith, what do you find that strengthens you in your continuous fasting? He said: Ghee, I drink it and find it moistens my veins, as for water, it comes out of my body. And what is similar to that, from those who did that, from those whose mention in the book would take too long? It was said: The reason for those who did that, God willing, was to seek purity for themselves and strength, not to seek righteousness for God through their actions. And they did that in the same way as Omar ibn al-Khattab used to command them to do, saying: Be rough and multiply, and mount the horses, and cut off the knees, and walk barefoot. He commanded them in that to be rough in their lives, so that they would not enjoy themselves and settle for a comfortable life, and incline towards ease and become cowardly and take refuge from their enemies. And many of the people of virtue have been reluctant - for those who continue - to continue.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq:
m: Ibn Abi Na’am used to fast continuously for days until he could not stand, so Amr ibn Maymun said: If the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had known this, they would have stoned him. Then in the successive reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prohibiting continuous fasting, which would take a long time to list in the book, we left out mentioning most of them, as mentioning some of them would suffice, since mentioning what we mentioned would suffice without citing evidence for the undesirability of continuous fasting with anything else.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Yahya ibn Sa’id told us, on the authority of Ubaydullah, he said, Nafi’ informed me, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade continuous fasting. They said: You fast continuously, O Messenger of God! He said: I am not like any of you, I eat and drink at night.” It has been narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that permission to fast continuously from dawn to dawn has been permitted.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam al-Masri Qaq narrated to us, Shu’ayb narrated to us, on the authority of al-Layth, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Haad, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Khabab, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri:
m: “He heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Do not fast continuously, so whoever among you wants to fast continuously, let him fast continuously until dawn. They said: O Messenger of God, you fast continuously! He said: I am not like you, I have food to feed me and a cupbearer to drink.”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abu Nu’aym narrated to us, he said: Abu Isra’il al-Absi narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Surat al-Baqarah 2:
m: h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives

. They are your clothing and you are their clothing. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has decreed for you, and eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the nightfall.
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques

. These are the limits set by God, so do not approach them. Thus does God make clear His verses to the people that they may become righteous. Hafs, on the authority of Umm Walad Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah: “She passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was eating suhoor, so he invited her to eat, and she said: I am fasting. He said: How do you fast? So she mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Where are you in terms of fasting continuously from the family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from dawn to dawn.” So the interpretation of the verse is: Then complete abstaining from what God has commanded you to abstain from, from the time the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread from the From dawn to night. Then it is permissible for you to do so after that until the same time, as Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement: Then complete the fast until the night, he said: From these four limits, so he recited:
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the intimacy with your wives
, so he recited until he reached: Then complete the fast until the night. My father and others from our sheikhs used to say this and recite it to us.

x: God Almighty means - by His statement:
h
And do not have sexual relations with them
, do not have sexual relations with your women. And by His statement:
h
And while you are in retreat in the mosques
, he says: In the state of your retreat in the mosques, and that is the state of their confining themselves to the worship of God in their mosques.

i: And the root of the word contact is standing, and confining the soul to something, as Al-Tarfah Ibn Hakim said:
x: The girls of the night spent the night around me, engrossed in the weeping, with one dead among them.
He means by his saying: dedicated, residing, as Al-Farazdaq said: You see around them the pious ones as if they were devoted to an idol in the pre-Islamic era.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the direct contact that God meant by His saying:
h
And do not have sexual relations with them
Some of them said: The meaning of that is sexual intercourse, not any other meanings of direct contact.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His saying:
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques - in Ramadan or other than Ramadan
, God forbade him from having sexual relations with women during the day and night until he completes his retreat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata’ told me:
m: h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques
, he said: sexual intercourse.

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said:
m: They used to have sexual relations while they were in retreat, until the verse was revealed:
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques
, he said: When a man was in retreat and left the mosque, he could have sexual intercourse if he wished, and God said:
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques
, meaning: Do not approach them as long as you are in retreat, in a mosque or elsewhere.
Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak narrated something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: There were people who used to have intercourse with their wives while they were in iʿtikaf there, but God forbade them from doing so.

c: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in iʿtikaf in the mosques

, he said: If a man left the mosque while he was in iʿtikaf and found his wife, he could have sexual relations with her if he wished, but God, the Almighty, forbade them from doing so, and informed them that this was not permissible until he completed his iʿtikaf.

c: Musa ibn Harun told us, he said, ʿAmr ibn Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of As-Suddi:
m: h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in iʿtikaf in the mosques
, he said: Whoever is in iʿtikaf is fasting, and women are not permissible for him as long as he is in iʿtikaf.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques
, he said: The neighbors. So when one of you goes out from his house to the House of God, he should not approach women.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas used to say: Whoever goes out from his house to the House of God, he should not approach women.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques
, he said: When the people were in retreat, a man would go out and have sexual relations with his wife, then return to the mosque, but God forbade them from doing that.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: When they were in retreat, a man would go out to relieve himself, have intercourse with his wife, then wash himself, then return to his retreat. So they were forbidden from doing that. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: They forbade intercourse with women in the mosques, where the Ansar used to have intercourse, so he said: Do not have intercourse with them while you are in i’tikaf, he said: In i’tikaf, meaning neighbors. Ibn Jurayj said: So I said to Ata’: Intercourse is direct contact? He said: Intercourse itself! So I said to him: What about kissing and touching in the mosque? He said: As for what is forbidden, it is intercourse, and I dislike all of that in the mosque.

c: I was told by Husayn ibn al-Faraj,
m: who said: Al-Fadl ibn Khalid told us, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And do not have intercourse with them, meaning intercourse.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is in all meanings of direct contact, from touching, kissing, and intercourse.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me,
m: who said: Ibn Wahb told us, who said: Malik ibn Anas said: The person in i’tikaf should not touch his wife, nor touch her, nor take pleasure in anything from her, a kiss or anything else.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques
, he said: Sexual relations, whether intercourse or not, are all forbidden to him. He said: Sexual relations without intercourse, skin to skin.

x: The reason for those who said this is that God, the Most High, mentioned Himself, was general in prohibiting sexual relations, and did not specify one thing over the other. This is based on what He made general, until an argument comes that must be accepted, that He meant by it direct relations without direct relations. The more correct of the two statements in my opinion is the statement of those who said: The meaning of this is sexual relations, or what occurred during sexual relations, which requires a ritual bath. This is because there is no statement about this except one of two statements: Either making the ruling of the verse general, or making its ruling specific to the meanings of direct relations. The reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have been unanimous: that his wives used to lick him while he was in retreat. So when this was authenticated from him, it was known that what He meant by it from the meanings of direct relations was some and not all.

c: Ali bin Shuaib told us, he said, Ma’n bin Isa al-Qazzaz told us, he said, Malik told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aishah,
m: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed i’tikaf, he would bring his head close to me and I would comb his hair.”

c: Yunus Qaq told me, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr and Umrah: That Aisha said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not enter the house except for a human need, and he would enter upon me while I was in the mosque with my head and my feet.”

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would bring his head close to me while he was in the mosque, and I would be in my room, and I would wash it and his feet.”

c: Sufyan told us, he said, Ibn Fadil and Ya’la ibn Ubayd told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Tamim ibn Salamah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah, she said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would go out to me from the mosque while he was in I’tikaf, and I would wash it while I was menstruating.”

c: Muhammad ibn Mu’ammar told me, he said, Hammad ibn Mas’adah told us, he said, Malik ibn Anas told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri and Hisham ibn Urwah,
m: both of them, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would go out to me with his head and his feet while he was in I’tikaf.” Since it is authentic from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what we mentioned about Aishah washing his head while he was in I’tikaf, it is known that what is meant by his saying,
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in I’tikaf in the mosques

, is not all that is required by the name of direct contact, and that it refers to some of the meanings of direct contact and not all of them. If this is the case, and it is agreed that sexual intercourse is among what is meant by it, it is obligatory to prohibit sexual intercourse for the person in seclusion and the like, and that is everything that takes the place of direct contact in terms of enjoyment.

x: By that, the Most High means: these things that I have explained: eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse during the month of Ramadan during the day without an excuse, and sexual intercourse with women during seclusion in the mosques. He says: I have specified these things for you, and I have commanded you to avoid them at the times that I have commanded you to avoid them, and I have forbidden them to you during them, so do not approach them, and keep away from doing them, for you will deserve the punishment that is deserved by the one who transgresses My limits, disobeys My command, and commits sins.

Some of the people of interpretation used to say: The limits of God: His conditions. This is a meaning close to the meaning that we have mentioned, except that what we have said about it is more similar to the interpretation of the word. That is because the limit of everything is what it has limited of meanings and distinguished between it and others. His saying: Those are the limits of God means the forbidden things that He distinguished from the absolutely permissible things, so He defined them with their attributes and descriptions, and made them known to His servants.
It was mentioned by those who said that this means conditions:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: As for the limits of God, they are His conditions. And some of them said: The limits of God, are His disobedience. It was mentioned by those who said that:

c: I was told by Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: he said, I heard Al-Fadl bin Khalid, he said, Surat al-Baqarah 2:187
h
Lawful to you on the night of the fast is the approach to your wives

. They are your clothing and you are their clothing. God knows that you were deceiving yourselves, so He has turned to you in forgiveness and pardoned you. So now have intercourse with them and seek what God has decreed for you, and eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the nightfall.
h
And do not have sexual relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques
. These are the limits set by God, so do not approach them. Thus does God make clear His verses to the people that they may become righteous.

c: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Those are the limits of God, he says: disobeying God - meaning directly in seclusion.

x: God Almighty means by that: Just as I have explained to you, O people, the obligation of My duties upon you regarding fasting, and I have made known to you its limits and times, and what is upon you from it when you are at home, and what is permissible for you in it while traveling and sick, and what is necessary for you to avoid while you are in seclusion in your mosques, so I have made all of that clear to you - so I will explain My rulings, My permissible and forbidden things, and My limits. My commands and prohibitions are in My Book and My revelation, and on the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the people. And what is meant by His saying: Perhaps they will fear God, is that I make that clear to them so that they may fear My prohibitions and sins, and avoid My wrath and anger, by refraining from doing what I have made clear to them in My verses that I have forbidden them, and I have commanded them to abandon and leave.

evidence.text: It has been narrated that in the reading of Abdullah: It is lawful for you on the night of fasting to have sexual intercourse with your wives.
Abu Hisham said: This is how Muadh read it.
And some of them read that: And follow what God has prescribed for you.

Who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abd al-Razzaq narrated, Ibn Uyaynah narrated, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: How do you read this verse: And seek or follow?
My father and others from our sheikhs used to say this and recite it to us.

x: God Almighty meant by that: And let not some of you consume the wealth of others unjustly. God Almighty made the one who consumes his brother's wealth unjustly like the one who consumes his own wealth unjustly. Similar to that is the saying of God Almighty: And do not insult one another (al-Hujurat 49:11), and His saying: And do not kill yourselves (al-Nisa 4:29) meaning: do not insult some of you to others, and do not kill some of you to others. Because God Almighty made the believers brothers, so the one who fights his brother is like the one who kills himself, and the one who insults him is like the one who insults himself. And the Arabs do the same, they refer to themselves with their sisters, and refer to their sisters with themselves, so they say: My brother and your brother, which of us is stronger. Meaning: I and you are fighting, so we see who is stronger - so the one who speaks about himself refers to himself with his brother, because a man's brother is like his own self to them.

i: And from that is the saying of the poet:
x: My brother and your brother are in the valley of the eagle, there is no Arab in it The interpretation of the words:
h
And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly
Eating it unjustly: eating it in a way other than that which God has permitted for its eaters. As for his statement:
h
And bring it before the judges
, it means: And dispute with it - meaning: with your money - before the judges in order to consume a portion - a group - of people’s money in sin and you know.

And what he means by his statement: in sin, is the forbidden thing that God has forbidden you, and you know, that is: And you intentionally eat that in sin, with the intention of what God has forbidden you from, and knowing that your action is against God and a sin, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Mu’awiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly
h
and bring it before the judges

, this is about a man who has money, and he has no evidence for it, so he denies the money, and disputes with them about it before the judges while he knows that the right is against him, and he knows that he is sinful: eating something forbidden.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid regarding the statement of God said:
m: h
And bring it before the judges
, he said: Do not dispute while you are unjust.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly

or send it before the judges, and it was said: Whoever walks with his opponent while he is unjust to him, is sinful until he returns to the truth. Know, O son of Adam, that the judge’s ruling does not make permissible for you what is unlawful or justify what is unjust to you. Rather, the judge rules according to what he sees and what the witnesses testify to, and the judge is a human being who makes mistakes and gets things right. Know that whoever has been judged in his favor unjustly, his dispute will not end until God brings them together on the Day of Resurrection, and He will judge against the one who is unjust in favor of the one who is right, with something better than what the one who is unjust judged against the one who is right in this world.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And bring it before the judges
, he said: Do not bring your brother’s money before the judge while you know that you are unjust, because his judgment does not make lawful for you something that was forbidden to you.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly

or send it in bribery to the rulers in order to consume a portion of the people’s wealth in sin while you know. As for falsehood, he says: A man among you wrongs his companion, then sues him to cut off his wealth while he knows that he is unjust, so that is what His statement means: and send it in bribery) to the rulers.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Khalid Al-Wasiti told me, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly
, he said: It is a man who buys a commodity and returns it and returns dirhams with it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly

or send it [in bribery] to the judges, he said: He would be more argumentative than him and more knowledgeable of argument, so he would argue with him about his wealth unjustly, so that he would eat his wealth unjustly. And he recited, O you who have believed, do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly except it be trade by mutual consent
r
(An-Nisa’: 29)

. He said: This is the gambling that the people of ignorance practiced. The origin of idlaa is a man sending a bucket in a well with a reason attached to it. So it was said to the one arguing for his claim: He provided such and such an argument, if his argument that he uses as evidence is a reason for him, and he is attached to it in his dispute, like the one who draws water from a well with a bucket that he has sent in it with the reason to which the bucket is attached. It is said in both of them - I mean from the argument and from sending the bucket into the well because: So-and-so presented his argument, so he is sending it down, and he lowered his bucket into the well, so he is sending it down. As for his saying: And send it down to the judges, there are two aspects of parsing in it: One of them: That his saying: And send it down is in the accusative case in apposition to his saying:
h
And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly

, meaning: And do not… And they brought it to the judges, and it was mentioned that this is the case in Abu’s reading with the repetition of the letter of prohibition: And do not bring it to the judges. And the other of them: the accusative on the letter, so its meaning then is: Do not eat your wealth among yourselves unjustly while you are bringing it to the judges, as the poet said: Do not forbid a behavior and then do the same. Shame on you if you do it. Meaning: Do not forbid a behavior while you are doing it yourself. It is better for it to be in the subjunctive mood - according to what was mentioned in Abu’s reading - than for it to be in the accusative case.

x: It was mentioned that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the waxing and waning of the crescent moons and the changing conditions of them, so God, the Most High, revealed this verse, in response to their question.
Mentioning the report about that:

c: Bishr bin Mu'adh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Sa'id told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: "
h
They ask you about the new moons

. Say, They are measurements of time for the people. Qatada said: They asked the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that: Why were these new moons created? So God revealed about them what you hear: They are measurements of time for the people. So He made them for the fasting of the Muslims and for their breaking of the fast, and for their rituals and their Hajj, and for the waiting period of their wives, and for the place of their religion, among other things. And God knows best what is good for His creation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi', he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that they said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why were the new moons created? Then God revealed: “
h
They ask you about the new moons
. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for mankind and for Hajj.’” God made them measurements of time for the Muslims’ fasting and breaking their fast, for their Hajj and their Surat Al-Baqarah 2:189
h
They ask you about the new moons
. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj. And
h
righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs

, but righteousness is of him who fears God. And enter houses from their doors and fear God that you may be successful. rituals, for the waiting period of their wives, and for the settlement of their debts.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Measures of time for mankind and Hajj
, he said: They are measurements of time for the people in their Hajj, fasting, breaking their fast, and their rituals.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: The people said, ‘Why were the new moons created?’ Then this verse was revealed: “
h
They ask you about the new moons

. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for mankind.’” for their fasting and breaking their fast, for their Hajj and their rituals. He said: Ibn Abbas said: And the time of their Hajj, the waiting period of their wives, and the settlement of their debts.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
They ask you about the new moons
. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for the people.’” They are the times of divorce, menstruation, and Hajj.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: Al-Fadl bin Khalid narrated to us, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us on the authority of Al-Dahhak: “
h
They ask you about the new moons
. Say: They are measurements of time for the people.” He meant: the resolution of their religion, the time of their Hajj, and the number of their wives.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the new moons, so this verse was revealed: “
h
They ask you about the new moons
. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for the people,’” by which they know the end of their religion, the number of their wives, and the time of their Hajj.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yahya, on the authority of Ali:
m: that he was asked about his statement: set times for the people, he said: They are the times of the month: like this and like this and like this - and he held up his thumb - so when you see it, then fast, and when you see it, then break your fast, and if it is hidden from you, then complete thirty.

x: So the interpretation of the verse - since the matter is as we mentioned from the one whose statement we mentioned in that - is: They ask you, O Muhammad, about the new moons, their new moons, their new moons, their new moons, their full ... So say, O Muhammad: Your Lord has made a difference between that, in order to make the new moons about which you asked, and the difference between them and others in what He has made a difference between them and Him, as times for you and others among the children of Adam in their livelihoods, you watch for their increase and decrease, their disappearance and their concealment and your seeing them, times for your debts, and the expiration of the term of employment of those whom you have hired, and the end of the waiting period of your women, and the time for your fasting and breaking your fast, so He has made them times for the people.
As for His saying, and the Hajj, he means: and for the Hajj. He says: He has also made them a time for your Hajj, by which you know the time of your rites and your Hajj.
It was said: This verse was revealed about a people who would not enter their homes from the door if they entered ihram.

Those who said that mentioned: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: I heard al-Baraa’ saying: When the Ansar performed Hajj and were hungry, they would not enter their houses except from the back. He said: Then a man from the Ansar came and entered from his door, and he was asked about that, so this verse was revealed: And
h
righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Baraa’, he said:
m: When they entered ihram in the pre-Islamic period, they would enter houses from their backs and not from their doors, so this verse was revealed: And
h
righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us,
m: I heard Dawud, on the authority of Qays ibn Habtar: “When some people entered ihram, they did not enter a garden from its door, nor a house from its door, nor a home from its door. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions entered a house, and there was a man from the Ansar called Rifa’ah ibn Tabut, so he came and climbed over the wall, then he entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he left the door of the house, or he said: from the door of the house, Rifa’ah left with him. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What made you do that? He said: O Messenger of God, I saw you exiting from it, so I exited from it! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am an Ahmas man! He said: If you are an Ahmas man, then our religion is one!” Then God, the Most High, revealed: “
h
Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs
, but righteousness is of him who fears God. And enter houses from their doors.”

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And righteousness is not that you enter houses from the backs, meaning: righteousness is not that you enter houses from the windows in the backs of houses, or the doors on their sides, which the people of ignorance used to do. So they were forbidden to enter from them, and were commanded to enter from their doors.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: There were some people from the people of Hijaz who, when they entered ihram, did not enter from the doors of their houses and entered from their backs, so this verse was revealed: But righteousness is he who fears God 1:13.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs

, but righteousness is of him who fears God. And enter houses from their doors,” he said: When a man of the polytheists entered ihram, he would dig a hole in the back of his house, make a ladder, and enter through it. He said: “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came one day with a man from the polytheists. He said: He came to the door to enter and entered through it. He said: The man went to enter through the hole. He recited: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is the matter with you? He said: I am a heathen! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And I am a heathen.”

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he said:
m: There were some Ansar who, when they entered ihram for Umrah, nothing would come between them and the sky. They were embarrassed by that. A man would go out slowly for Umrah, and a need would appear to him after he had left his house. He would return and not enter through the door of the room because the roof of the door would stand between him and the sky. He would open the wall behind him, then he would stand in his room and order what he needed to be done, and it would come out to him from his house. It was reported that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered ihram for Umrah at the time of Hudaybiyyah, and he entered a room. A man from the Ansar from Banu Salamah entered after him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: I am a zealot. Az-Zuhri said: The zealots did not care about that. The Ansari said: And I am a zealot! He said: I am following your religion. Then God, the Most High, revealed:
h
Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And righteousness is not that you enter houses the entire verse

. Qatada said: This tribe of the Ansar in the pre-Islamic period, if one of them entered the state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah, he would not enter a house through its door, unless he climbed over a wall, and they converted to Islam while they were like that, so God, the Most High, revealed about that what you hear, and forbade them from doing that, and informed them that it was not righteousness for them to do that, and He commanded them to enter houses through their doors.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And righteousness does not consist in entering houses from their backs

, for “some people from the Arabs, when they performed Hajj, would not enter their houses from their doors. They would dig through their backs. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the Farewell Hajj, he came walking with a man from those people who was a Muslim. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached the door of the house, the man hid behind him and refused to enter. He said: O Messenger of God, I am a mahram! - meaning: I am in a state of ihram - and those who do that are called the hams. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am also a mahram! So enter.” So the man entered, and God, the Most High, revealed: And enter houses from their doors.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs

, but righteousness is of one who fears God and enters houses from their doors, and “that men from the people of Medina, if one of them feared something from his enemy, would enter the state of ihram and be safe. When he entered the state of ihram, he would not enter through the door of his house, but would make a tunnel in the back of his house. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, there was a man in the state of ihram like that - and the people of Medina used to call the garden the haysh - and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered a garden, and entered it from its door, and that man in the state of ihram entered with him. A man called out to him from behind him: O so-and-so, you are in the state of ihram and you have entered! He said: I am Ahmas! He said: O Messenger of God, if I am in the state of ihram, then I am in the state of ihram, and if I am Ahmas, then I am Ahmas.” So God, the Most High, revealed:
h
Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs
, to the end of the verse, so God permitted the believers to enter through their doors.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, who said:
h
Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs

, but righteousness is of one who fears God and enters houses from their doors. He said: “When the people of Madinah and others were in ihram, they would not enter houses except from their backs, and that is by climbing over them. So when one of them entered the state of ihram, he would not enter the house except by climbing over it from its back. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered one day the house of some of the Ansar, and a man who had entered the state of ihram entered after him. They denounced him for that and said: This is an immoral man! So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Why did you enter from the door when you had entered the state of ihram? He said: I saw you, O Messenger of God, enter, and I entered after you! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am a fanatic! The Quraysh were called the fanatics at that time. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that, the Ansari said: My religion is your religion! So God, the Most High, revealed: “
h
Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs
” verse.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: I said to Ata’ about his statement:
h
And righteousness is not that you Surat Al-Baqarah 2
h
They ask you about the new moons
. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj. And
h
righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs

, but righteousness is of him who fears God. And enter houses from their doors and fear God that you may be successful. enter houses from their backs, He said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to enter houses from their backs and they considered it righteousness, so he said: Righteousness, then he described righteousness, and he ordered them to enter houses from their doors. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Kathir informed me: He heard Mujahid say: This verse was about the Ansar, they would enter houses from their backs, seeking righteousness thereby.

x: So the interpretation of the verse is: Righteousness, O people, is not that you enter houses from their backs during your state of ihram, but righteousness is in the one who fears God, so he fears Him, avoids His prohibitions, and obeys Him by performing the obligatory duties that He has commanded him to do. As for entering houses from their backs, there is no righteousness towards God in that, so enter them from wherever you wish, from their doors or other doors, unless you believe that entering them from their doors is forbidden under any circumstances, because that is not permissible for you to believe, because it is something that I have not forbidden to you.

God Almighty means by that: And fear God, O people, so beware of Him and fear Him, by obeying Him in what... He has commanded you to do what He has obligated you to do, and to avoid what He has forbidden you, so that you may succeed and be successful in your requests with Him, and attain eternal life in His gardens and eternity in His bliss. We have explained the meaning of success in what has come before, with what indicates it.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of this verse.

Some of them said: This verse is the first verse revealed in ordering the Muslims to fight the polytheists. They said: The Muslims were ordered in it to fight whoever of the polytheists fought them, and to refrain from fighting whoever refrained from fighting them, then it was abrogated by Bara'ah.

Those who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Sa'd and Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, on the authority of Abu Ja'far, on the authority of al-Rabi' regarding his statement: "
h
And fight in the way of God those who fight you but do not transgress

. Indeed. God does not like transgressors," he said: This is the first verse revealed in fighting in Medina. When it was revealed, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would fight whoever fought him, and refrain from whoever refrained from him, until Bara’ah was revealed. Abd al-Rahman did not mention Madinah.

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And fight in the way of God those who fight you to the end of the verse
: This has been abrogated! And he recited God’s statement,
h
And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together (al-Tawbah 9

:36), and this is the abrogator. And he recited, A declaration of freedom from God and His Messenger, until he reached, So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them to Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful (al-Tawbah 9:1-5).

x: Others said: Rather, this is a command from God, the Most High, to the Muslims to fight the infidels, and it has not been abrogated. Rather, the aggression that God forbade them from is His prohibition against killing women and children. They said: And the ruling on the prohibition against killing them is still in effect today. They said: So nothing has been abrogated from the ruling of this verse.

Who said that: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sadaqah Al-Dimashqi, on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya Al-Ghassani, he said: I wrote to Umar bin Al-Aziz asking him about his statement: “
h
And fight in the way of God those who fight you but do not transgress
. Indeed. God does not like transgressors.” He said: So he wrote to me: That is in regard to women and children and those of them who have not waged war against you.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High: And fight in the way of God those who fight you, regarding the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they were commanded to fight the infidels.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And fight in the way of God those who fight you but do not transgress

. Indeed. God does not like transgressors.” He said: Do not kill women, nor children, nor the elderly, nor those who throw down their weapons and withhold their hands. If you do this, then you have transgressed.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz, he said,
m: Umar bin Abdul Aziz wrote to Adi bin Artah: I found a verse in the Book of God: “
h
And fight in the way of God those who fight you but do not transgress
. Indeed, God does not like transgressors.” That is, do not fight those who do not fight you, meaning: women, children, and monks.

x: The more correct of these two statements is the statement made by Umar bin Abdul Aziz. Because the plaintiff’s claim that a verse was abrogated is likely not abrogated, without any evidence of the validity of his claim, is decisive. And no one is incapable of decisiveness. We have demonstrated the meaning of abrogation, and the meaning that precedes it, which proves the validity of abrogation, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. The interpretation of the verse - if the matter is as we have described - is: And fight, O believers, in the cause of God - and His cause is His path that He has made clear, and His religion that He has prescribed for His servants - the Most High says to them: Fight in My obedience and in accordance with what I have prescribed for you of My religion, and call to it whoever turns away from it and is arrogant with their hands and tongues, until they return to My obedience, or pay you the jizyah as a humiliation if they are People of the Book.

And the Most High commanded them to fight whoever of the disbelievers fought, not whoever of their women and children did not fight, for they are their property and assets, if the fighters among them are defeated and they are subdued. So that is the meaning of His statement:
h
Fight in the cause of God those who fight you

. Because He permitted restraint from those who restrained and did not fight from the polytheists of the idolaters, and those who refrained from fighting the Muslims from the infidels of the People of the Book on the basis of paying the jizyah as children. So the meaning of His saying: And do not transgress: Do not kill a child or a woman, nor those who pay you the jizyah from the People of the Book and the Magians, Indeed, God does not love the transgressors, those who exceed His limits, and consider permissible what God has forbidden them of killing those whom it is forbidden to kill from the women of the polytheists and their children.

God Almighty means by that: And kill, O believers, those polytheists who fight you wherever you find their locations and are able to kill them. This is the meaning of His statement: Wherever you encounter them. The meaning of being thaqafa in a matter is: being skilled in it and seeing it. It is said: he is thaqafa lahqaf, if he is well-advised in fighting and has insight into the places where he is killed. As for thaqfa, it has a different meaning, which is straightening out. So the meaning of: And kill them wherever you find them is kill them wherever you are able to kill them and see their locations. As for his statement: And expel them from where they expelled you, he means by that the emigrants who were expelled from their homes and dwellings to Mecca, so the Almighty said to them: Expel those who fight you - and they have expelled you from your homes - from their dwellings and homes as they expelled you from them.
The Almighty means by his statement:
h
And persecution is worse than killing

, and associating partners with God is worse than killing. I have previously explained that the origin of persecution is trial and examination. So the interpretation of the statement is: And the trial of the believer in his religion until he turns away from it and becomes an associator with God after his Islam is worse for him and more harmful than being killed while adhering to his religion, clinging to it, and being truthful in it, as Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, he said, ʿIsa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God:
h
And persecution is worse than killing
, he said: The believer’s turning away from idolatry is worse for him than killing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And persecution is worse than killing
, meaning: polytheism is worse than killing.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: I was told by Ammar bin al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada:
h
And persecution is worse than killing
, meaning: polytheism is worse than killing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And persecution is worse than killing
, he said: polytheism.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Abdullah bin Kathir told me, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And persecution is worse than killing
, he said: persecution is polytheism.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Al-Fadl ibn Khalid say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
h
And persecution is worse than killing
, he said: Polytheism is worse than killing.

c: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the words of God Almighty:
h
And persecution is worse than killing
, he said: The persecution of disbelief.

x: The readings differ in the reading of that. The majority of the readers of Medina and Mecca read it: “
h
And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there

. But if they fight you, then kill them.” Meaning: Do not initiate fighting with the polytheists at al-Masjid al-Haram until they initiate it with you. But if they initiate it with you there at al-Masjid al-Haram in the sanctuary, then kill them, for God has made the reward of the disbelievers for their disbelief and evil deeds, killing in this world and long-lasting disgrace in the Hereafter, as Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, Yazid told us, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there
