, they did not fight there until they initiated fighting, then it was abrogated after that and He said: And fight them until there is no more persecution - until there is no more polytheism - and religion is for God (al-Baqarah 2:193), that is, it is said: There is no god but God, for which the Prophet of God fought, and to which he called.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Al-Hajjaj ibn Al-Munhal said: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them.” So God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, not to fight them at the Sacred Mosque unless they initiate fighting there. Then God abrogated that by saying: So when the sacred months have passed,
h
then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9

:5). So God commanded His Prophet, when the term has expired, to fight them outside the sacred precincts and at the House, until they testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, that he said: And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you therein, so they did not fight them therein. Then He abrogated that later and said: Fight them until there is no more persecution (al-Baqarah 2:193).

x: Some of them said: This is a decisive verse that has not been abrogated.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told us,
m: who said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, who said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: But if they fight you, in the sacred precinct, then kill them. This is the punishment of the disbelievers. Do not fight anyone therein. Whoever attacks you and fights you, then fight him as he fights you. The most prominent reciters of Kufa read it as: “
h
And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there
. But if they fight you, then kill them.” Meaning: Do not initiate killing until they initiate it.

x: Those who said this: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, on the authority of Abi Hammad, on the authority of Hamza al-Zayyat, he said: I said to al-A’mash: What do you think of your reading: “
h
And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there

. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers. But if they cease, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” If they kill them, how do they kill them? He said: When one of the Arabs is killed, they say: We killed him, and when one of them is struck, they say: We struck him.
The most correct of these two readings is the reading of the one who read: “
h
And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there

. But if they fight you, then kill them.” Because God, the Most High, did not command His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions in a situation - if the polytheists fought them - to surrender to them until they killed one of them, after He had given him and them permission to fight them, so the reading of permission to kill them after they had killed one of them is more appropriate than the reading of what we have chosen. Since that is the case, it is known that God, the Most High, had given them permission to fight them, if the fighting began with the polytheists, before they killed one of them and after they killed one of them. God the Almighty abrogated this verse by saying: And fight them until there is no more persecution (al-Baqarah 2:193), and His saying:
h
Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9
:5) and similar verses in this regard.
We have already mentioned some of the statements of those who said that it was abrogated, and we will mention the statements of those whose mention we were present who were not mentioned.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And do not fight them at Al-Masjid Al-Haram until they fight you therein
, he said: It was abrogated by His saying:
h
Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His saying:
h
And do not fight them at Al-Masjid Al-Haram until they fight you therein
, he said: until they initiate it with you. This had been forbidden, but God permitted it for him, and it remained steadfast until God commanded him to fight them later.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The readings differ in the reading of that.
The majority of the readers of Medina and Mecca read it: “And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there.
The most prominent reciters of Kufa read it as: “And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these two readings is the reading of the one who read: “And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there.

Because God, the Most High, did not command His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions in a situation - if the polytheists fought them - to surrender to them until they killed one of them, after He had given him and them permission to fight them, so the reading of permission to kill them after they had killed one of them is more appropriate than the reading of what we have chosen.

x: By that, the Most High means: If the disbelievers who are fighting you cease fighting you and their disbelief in God, and abandon that and repent, then God is Forgiving of the sins of those among them who believed and repented from their polytheism, and turned to God from their past sins and their days that have passed, Merciful to them in their afterlife, through His grace to them, and His giving them what He gives the people of His obedience of reward, for their turning to His love from their disobedience, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then if they cease - if they repent - then God is Forgiving and Merciful.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And fight the polytheists who fight you until there is no more fitnah, meaning: until there is no more polytheism with God, and until no one is worshipped besides Him, and the worship of idols, gods and rivals disappears, and worship and obedience are for God alone, without any other idols or statues, as Qatada said in what he said:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And fight them until there is no more fitnah
, he said: until there is no more polytheism.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And fight them until there is no more fitnah
, he said: until there is no more polytheism.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, he said: polytheism, and religion is for God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, he said, Amr ibn Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, he said: As for persecution, it is polytheism.

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, he said: Fight until there is no more polytheism.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
h
And fight them until there is no more fitnah
, meaning polytheism.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
, he said: until there is no more disbelief, and he recited: You fight them or they submit (al-Fath 48:16).

c: Ali ibn Dawud told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And fight them until there is no more persecution

, he said: polytheism. As for the religion that God mentioned in this place, it is worship and obedience to God in His commands and prohibitions, and from that is the saying of al-A’sha: He is Dan Al-Rabab, when they hated religion, Draka in the Battle of Wasil He means by his saying: When they hated the religion, when they hated obedience and refused it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: And the religion will be for God, meaning: until none is worshipped except God, and that is There is no god but God, for which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought and to which he called, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been commanded to fight the people until they say “There is no god but God, establish prayer, and pay zakat. If they do that, then their blood and wealth are protected from me except for what is due, and their reckoning is with God.”

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the religion will be for God, that is, it will be said: There is no god but God. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “God has commanded me to fight the people until they say: There is no god but God,” then he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Ar-Rabi’.

x: What God, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
But if they desist

, is that if those who fight you from among the disbelievers desist from fighting you, and enter your religion, and acknowledge the obligations that God has imposed upon you, and abandon what they are doing of worshipping idols, then refrain from transgressing against them, fighting them, and jihad against them, because aggression should not be directed except against the wrongdoers - and they are the polytheists who have abandoned worshipping God and worshipping other than their Creator.
Is it permissible to transgress against the wrongdoer by saying: There is no aggression except against the wrongdoers?
The meaning of that is not the way you have gone. Rather, it is in the form of retribution, for the aggression that the polytheists have committed.

He says: Do to them as they did to you, just as it is said: If you treat me unjustly, I will treat you unjustly. The second is not unjust, just as Amr ibn Shas al-Asadi said: We have punished the aggressors of yesterday with retribution, whether they follow you step by step. Rather, this was similar to His statement: God mocks at them (al-Baqarah 2:15), and So they mock at them, God mocks at them (al-Tawbah 9:79). We have explained the reason for this and its counterparts previously. And what we have said about this Surat Al-Baqarah 2:193
h
And fight them until there is no more persecution
and religion is for God. But if they cease, then let there be no aggression except against the wrongdoers. interpretation was said by a group of the people of interpretation.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
There shall be no aggression except against the wrongdoers
, and the wrongdoer is the one who refuses to say: There is no god but God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
There shall be no aggression except against the wrongdoers
, he said: They are the polytheists.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Uthman ibn Ghiyath told us, he said,
m: I heard ʿIkrimah regarding this verse:
h
There shall be no aggression except against the wrongdoers
, he said: They are those who refuse to say: There is no god but God.

x: Others said the meaning of his statement:
h
There shall be no aggression except against the wrongdoers
, is: Do not fight except those who fight.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
But if they desist
, there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers, meaning: Do not fight anyone except those who fight you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: h
But if they desist

, there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers, for God does not like aggression against the wrongdoers or anyone else, but He says: Transgress against them in the same way that they transgressed against you.

x: Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say about His statement:
h
But if they desist
, there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers, it is not permissible to say
h
But if they desist

unless it is known that only some of them will desist, so it is as if He said: If some of them desist, there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers among them. So he implied, as he said: And whoever performs ‘Umrah during Hajj, let him offer whatever is easy of sacrifice (al-Baqarah 2:196), meaning: then he must offer whatever is easy of sacrifice, and as he says: To whomever you are going, I am going, meaning: to him. And some of them denied the implied meaning in that, and interpreted it as: if they desist, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful to whoever desists, and there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers who do not desist.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying,
h
The sacred month for the sacred month

, is Dhul-Qa'dah, which is the month in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the Umrah of Hudaybiyyah, but the polytheists of Mecca prevented him from entering the House and Mecca, in the sixth year of his migration. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with the polytheists in that year, on the condition that he would return the following year and enter Mecca and stay there for three days. When the following year came, which was the seventh year of his migration, he set out to perform Umrah with his companions in Dhul-Qa'dah - which is the month in which the polytheists prevented him from entering the House in the sixth year - and the people of Mecca left the city for him until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered it, and he fulfilled his needs there, and completed his Umrah, and stayed there for three days - then he left it and returned to Medina.

God, the Most High, said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the Muslims with him, The sacred month - meaning Dhul-Qi’dah, in which God brought you to His sanctuary and His House, despite the dislike of the polytheists of Quraysh, until you had had your fill of it - the sacred month, in which the polytheists of Quraysh prevented you the previous year before it until you turned away from the sanctuary against your will, so you did not enter it, and you did not reach the House of God. So God, O believers, distanced you from the polytheists by bringing you into the sanctuary in the sacred month against their dislike of that, because of what they did to you in the sacred month of preventing and preventing you from reaching the House, as Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay’ told me, he said, Yusuf told us - meaning: Ibn Khalid al-Samti - he said, Nafi’ ibn Malik told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement,
h
And the sacred things are retaliation

, he said: They are the polytheists, they detained Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - in Dhul-Qi’dah, so God returned him in Dhul-Qi’dah and brought him into the sacred House, so He took revenge for him.
Among them: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
The sacred month for the sacred month

, and for sacred things there is retaliation, he said: The Quraysh were proud of their turning back the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Hudaybiyyah while in the state of ihram in Dhul-Qa’dah from the sacred city, so God brought him into Mecca the following year in Dhul-Qa’dah, so he completed his Umrah, and he paid the retaliation for what had been prevented between him and it on the day of Hudaybiyyah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told me, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
A sacred month for a sacred month

, and sacred things are retaliation. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions came and performed Umrah in Dhul-Qi’dah, with the sacrificial animals. When they reached Hudaybiyyah, the polytheists turned them away. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with them on the condition that he would return that year and would remain in Makkah for three days and would not enter it except armed as a rider, and would leave, and would not leave with anyone from the people of Makkah. So they slaughtered the sacrificial animals in Hudaybiyyah, and shaved and shortened their hair. When it was the following year, the Prophet of God and his companions came and entered Makkah, and performed Umrah in Dhul-Qi’dah, and stayed there for three nights. The polytheists had boasted to him when they turned him back on the day of Hudaybiyyah, so God cut him off from them, and He let him enter Makkah in the same month in which they had turned him back in Dhul-Qi’dah. Then God said:
h
A sacred month for a sacred month
, and sacred things are retaliation.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada and on the authority of Uthman, on the authority of Muqsim,
m: regarding the statement:
h
The sacred month for the sacred month

, and for sacred things there is retaliation, they said: This was during the journey of Hudaybiyyah. The polytheists prevented the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from the House during the sacred month, so they made a judgment with the polytheists that day: You may perform Umrah the following year - during this month in which they prevented them. So God, the Most High, made for them a sacred month in which they would perform Umrah, in place of the month in which they prevented them, and for that reason He said: And for sacred things there is retaliation.

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to me, he said: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
The sacred month for the sacred month

, and for sacred things there is retaliation, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the Umrah of Hudaybiyyah in Dhul-Qa’dah in the sixth year of his migration, the polytheists prevented him and refused to let him go. Then they made peace with him in their peace treaty on the condition that they would leave Mecca for him for three days the following year, and they would leave him there. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them after the conquest of Khaybar in the seventh year, and they left Mecca for him for three days. During that Umrah, he married Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The sacred month for the sacred month
h
and the sacred things are retaliation

, they prevented the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Sacred House in Dhul-Qi’dah, so God admitted him to the Sacred House the following year, and took revenge for him from them, so He said:
h
The sacred month for the sacred month
h
and the sacred things are retaliation

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’, he said:
m: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions came and entered the state of ihram for Umrah in Dhul-Qi’dah, and they had the sacrificial animals with them, until when they were at Al-Hudaybiyyah, the polytheists stopped them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with them that he would return that year until he returned the following year, and he would stay in Makkah for three days and not take with him any of the people of Makkah. So they slaughtered the sacrificial animals at Al-Hudaybiyyah, and shaved their heads and cut their hair. Then when it was the following year, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions came and entered Makkah? So they performed Umrah in Dhul-Qi'dah and stayed there for three days. The polytheists had boasted about him when they turned him back on the day of Hudaybiyyah, so God took revenge on him from them and let him enter Mecca in the same month in which they had turned him back in Dhul-Qi'dah. God the Most High said:
h
The sacred month for the sacred month
, and for sacred things there is legal retribution.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father.
m: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying:
h
And the sacred things are retaliation

, they are the polytheists, they had detained Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the House in Dhul-Qi’dah, and they boasted about that, so God returned him in Dhul-Qi’dah, and God brought him into the Sacred House, and took revenge for him from them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about his saying:
h
The sacred month for the sacred month

, until he finished the verse, he said: All of this has been abrogated, he ordered him to fight the polytheists, and he recited: Fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together (al-Tawbah 9:36), and he recited: Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you (al-Tawbah 9:123), the Arabs. So when he finished with them, God Almighty said: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden until he reached His saying: and they are subdued (al-Tawbah 9:29), he said: They are the Romans. He said, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding this verse:
h
The sacred month for the sacred month
h
and the sacred things are retaliation
, he said: God has commanded you to retaliate and to take from you the transgressor.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I said to Ata’ and asked him about his statement:
h
The sacred month for the sacred month
h
and the sacred things are retaliation
, he said: It was revealed at Al-Hudaybiyyah. They were prevented in the sacred month, so it was revealed:
h
The sacred month for the sacred month
: an Umrah in a sacred month, for an Umrah in a sacred month.

x: God, the Most High, called Dhul-Qiʿdah the sacred month because the Arabs in the pre-Islamic era forbade fighting and killing in it, and laid down their weapons in it, and no one killed anyone in it, even if a man met the killer of his father or son. They called it Dhul-Qiʿdah because they refrained from raids and wars in it, so God called it by the name that the Arabs used to call it. As for the sacred things, they are the plural of sacredness, just as darkness is the plural of darkness and rooms are the plural of room. God Almighty said:
h
And the sacred things are retaliation

, so He made the plural because He meant: the sacred month, the sacred city, and the sacredness of ihram. So God Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad and the believers with him: Your entry into the sacred place, with your ihram, in this sacred month of yours, is retaliation for what you were prevented from the same last year.
And these are the sacred things that God made retaliation.
The people of interpretation differed regarding what was revealed in His statement:
h
But whoever transgresses against you
, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you.

Some of them said: According to what Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muʿawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement:
h
But whoever transgresses against you
, transgress Surat Al-Baqarah 2:194
h
The sacred month for the sacred month
, and for sacred things there is legal retribution.
h
So whoever transgresses against you

, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you. And fear God and know that God is with the righteous. against him in proportion to his transgression against you. This and similar verses were revealed in Mecca, and the Muslims at that time were few: and there was no general authority that could subdue the polytheists. The polytheists were treating them with insults and harm, so God commanded the Muslims, whoever among them is to be punished should be punished in proportion to what was done to him, or be patient, or forgive, for that is better.

When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) migrated to Medina, and God strengthened his authority, he ordered the Muslims to stop their grievances to their authority, and not to transgress against one another like the people of the Jahiliyyah.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: So whoever fights you, O believers, from the polytheists, then fight them as they fought you. They said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) in Medina, after the Umrah of the Qadima.
Those who said this are:

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said:
m: h
So whoever transgresses against you
, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you, so fight them in it as they fought you.

x: The most similar of the two interpretations is what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the verse, which was narrated from Mujahid. Because the verses before it are only a command from God to the believers to fight their enemy in a specific manner, and that is His saying:
h
And fight in the way of God those who fight you
and the verses after it. His statement:
h
So whoever transgresses against you

, transgress against him, is in the context of the verses that command fighting and jihad. God Almighty only imposed fighting on the believers after the migration. It is known from this that His statement:
h
So whoever transgresses against you

, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you, is Medinan, not Meccan, since the obligation to fight the polytheists was not obligatory for the believers in Mecca. His statement:
h
So whoever transgresses against you
, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you, is similar to His statement:
h
And fight in the way of God those who fight you
, and that its meaning is:
h
So whoever transgresses against you

in the Sacred Sanctuary and fights you, transgress against him in fighting, just as he transgressed against you by fighting you, because I have made the sacred things retaliation, so whoever among you, O believers, from the polytheists, violates a sacred thing in My Sacred Sanctuary, then violate it in the same way from him in it.

This verse was abrogated by God’s permission to His Prophet to fight the people of the sanctuary, starting in the sanctuary. His statement: And fight the polytheists all together (al-Tawbah 9:36) 1 is as we have mentioned, that it means: retribution, and following one word with another, even though their meanings differ, as He said:
And they plotted, and God plotted

and He said: So they mocked them, God mocked them (al-Tawbah 9:79), and what is similar to that in which one word was followed with another and the two meanings differed. The other: that it is in the sense of the enemy which is attack and leap. From the saying of the speaker: The lion attacked his prey. So the meaning of the statement is: So whoever attacks you - meaning whoever attacks you and leaps - unjustly, attack him - meaning attack him and leap towards him - in retaliation for what he did to you, not unjustly.
Then the letter ta’ is added to ‘ada, so it is said: ifta’ala instead of fa’ala, as it is said: iqtarabat hada al-amr meaning near, and ijtalabah also meaning brought and what is similar to that.

By that, God Almighty means: O believers, beware of transgressing His prohibitions and limits, lest you transgress them, and exceed what He alone has made clear to you. And know that God loves the pious, those who fear Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of this verse, and who meant by His saying:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
Some of them said: He meant by that: And spend in the way of God - and the way of God is His path which He commanded to take to His enemy from the polytheists to fight them and fight them,
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
- he said: And do not abandon spending in the way of God, for God will compensate you for it with a reward and provide for you soon.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abu al-Sa’ib Salim ibn Janadah and al-Hasan ibn Arfa told me, they said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hudhayfah:
m: h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: meaning in abandoning spending.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told me, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Shu’bah told us
m: - and Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Hudhayfah - and Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Abu Ja’far al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-A’mash - and Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim - all of them, on the authority of Shuqaiq, on the authority of Hudhayfah, he said: It is abandoning spending in the way of God.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: Spend in the cause of God, even if you have nothing but a share or an arrow. Shuʿbah is the one who doubts that.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: on whose authority al-Kalbi used to narrate, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If you have nothing but a share or an arrow, spend it.

c: Ibn Bashar told me, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: Concerning spending.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qays, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: Destruction is not that a man is killed in the cause of God, but rather refraining from spending in the cause of God.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Ismail ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: It was revealed about spending in the cause of God, meaning His statement:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi,
m: that he used to say about this verse:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

. He said: The people were in the cause of God, and a man would take provisions, and his provisions were better than the other. The poor man would spend from his provisions until nothing remained of his provisions, wanting to help his companion. So God revealed:
h
And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

c: Muhammad bin Khalaf al-Asqalani told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Mansur bin al-Mu'tamir, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: the freed slave of Umm Hani', on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God,
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: Let none of you say, I do not find anything. If he does not find anything but a pair of scythes, then let him equip it in the cause of God.

c: Ibn Abd al-A'la al-San'ani told us, he said, al-Mu'tamir told us, he said,
m: I heard Dawud - meaning Ibn Abi Hind - on the authority of Amir: That some of the provisions of the Ansar were withheld from them, and they had spent expenses. He said: So their opinion was bad, and they held back. He said: So God revealed,
h
And spend in the cause of God
h
and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: And the destruction was their bad opinion and their holding back.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us
m: - and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us - on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: Spending in the cause of God prevents you from fearing poverty.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

, he said: Qatada used to relate that Al-Hasan told him: that they used to travel and fight and not spend from their wealth - or he said: and they did not spend in that - so God commanded them to spend in their battles in the cause of God.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: Do not hold back from spending in the cause of God.

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And spend in the cause of God
- spend in the cause of God even if it is a rope -
h
and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
- you say: I do not have anything.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Ghassan told us, he said: Zuhair told us, he said: Khasif told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: When God commanded spending, they - or some of them - were saying: We will spend and our money will be gone and we will have nothing left! He said: So He said: Spend
h
and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
. He said: Spend and I will provide for you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr ibn Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: It was revealed about spending.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Hammam Al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: about destruction, he said: God commanded them to spend in the way of God, and He informed them that abandoning spending in the way of God leads to destruction.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I asked Ata’ about the statement of God, And spend in the way of God
h
and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: It means: Spend in the way of God, whether it is little or much. He said: Abdullah ibn Kathir said to me: It was revealed about spending in the way of God.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: A man should not say, I do not find anything! I am ruined! So let him prepare himself, even with a pair of scythes.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, meaning: Spend whether it is little or much, and do not surrender or spend anything and perish.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: Destruction: is that a man withholds himself and his wealth from spending in jihad in the cause of God. Bishr bin Muadh narrated that Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad narrated that Yunus narrated that Al-Hasan said about His statement,
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, so that you do not spend in the cause of God.

x: Others, who interpreted that, said that it refers to spending: meaning:
h
And spend in the cause of God
h
and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, so that you go out in the cause of God without spending or strength.
Mar mentioned that: Yunus narrated to me, he said:

c: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And spend in the cause of God
h
and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: If you do not have what to spend, then do not go out by yourself without spending or strength, so that you throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction.

x: Others said: Rather, it means: Spend in the cause of God, and do not throw yourselves with your own hands - in what you have committed of sins - into destruction, so that you despair of God’s mercy, but hope for His mercy
h
and do good
deeds.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharibi told me, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: It is the man who commits sins and throws himself into destruction, saying: There is no repentance for me.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, he said, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Bara’, he said:
m: A man asked him: Should I attack the polytheists alone and they kill me, would I have thrown myself into destruction? He said: No, destruction is in spending. God sent His Messenger and said: Then fight in the way of God; you are not charged with except yourself
r
(An-Nisa’: 84)
. Al-Hasan bin Arfa and Ibn Wakee’ narrated, they said: Wakee’ bin Al-Jarrah narrated, on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Surat Al-Baqarah 2:195
h
And spend in the cause of God
h
and do not throw [yourselves] with your [own] hands
into destruction [by refraining].
h
And do good
; indeed, God loves the doers of good. Al-Sabi’i, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, regarding the statement of God:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

, he said: It is a man who commits a sin and says: God will not forgive him. Ahmad bin Ishaq narrated, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated, he said: Israel narrated, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: I heard Al-Bara’, and a man asked him, saying: O Abu Ammarah, what do you think of the statement of God:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

, is it a man who advances and fights until he is killed? He said: No, but it is a man who commits sins, then throws himself into it and does not repent. Ibn Hamid narrated, he said: Yahya bin Wadheeh narrated, he said: Al-Hussein narrated, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: I heard Al-Bara’, and a man asked him, saying: A man who charges a battalion alone and fights, is he one of those who throw himself into destruction? He said: No, but destruction is when a person commits a sin and then throws his hand in it and says: My repentance is not accepted.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Hakam narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Jarrah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said:
m: I said to Al-Bara’ ibn Azib: O Abu ‘Amara, a man encounters a thousand of the enemy and attacks them, and he is alone, is he among those who said:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
? He said: No, let him fight until he is killed! God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “So fight in the way of God. You are not charged with except yourself”
r
(An-Nisa’: 84)

. Mujahid bin Musa narrated, Yazid narrated, Hisham narrated, and Yaqub narrated, Ibn Ulayyah narrated, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: I asked Ubaidah about the statement of God:
h
And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

(al-Baqarah 2:170). Ubaidah said: A man would commit a sin - I think he said: a great sin - and throw himself into it and be destroyed. Yaqub added in his hadith: So they were forbidden from that, and it was said: Spend in the cause of God
h
and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

. Yaqub bin Ibrahim narrated, Hisham narrated, Hisham narrated, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: I asked Ubaidah al-Salmani about that and he said: It is a man who commits a sin and surrenders, and throws himself into destruction, and says: There is no repentance for him! - meaning His statement:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ubaydah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: A man would commit a sin and throw himself into it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah:
m: h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: Despair.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr ibn Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus and Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah Al-Salmani, he said:
m: It is a man who commits a sin and surrenders, saying: I have no repentance! So he throws himself into it.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, he said, Ayoub told me, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah that he said:
m: It is about a man who commits a great sin and throws himself into it, and he sees that he has perished.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And spend in the way of God, and do not abandon jihad in His way.

Who said that: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Hayat told me, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Aslam Abi Imran, he said: We invaded Medina, meaning Constantinople, and the people of Egypt were led by Uqba bin Amir, and the group was led by Abd al-Rahman bin Khalid bin al-Walid. He said: So we formed two rows, I have never seen two rows wider or longer than them, and the Romans were sticking their backs to the city wall. He said: Then one of us charged at the enemy, and the people said: Stop! There is no god but God, he throws himself into destruction! Abu Ayyub al-Ansari said: You only interpret this verse in this way, that a man charges to fight seeking martyrdom, or to destroy himself! This verse was revealed about us, the Ansar! When God aided His Prophet and made Islam prevail, we, the Ansar, said among ourselves, secretly from the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace: We had left our families and our property to stay in it and fix it until God aided His Prophet.
Come, let us stay in our property and fix it! Then God sent down the report from the sky:
h
And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

(al-Baqarah 2:17). Throwing yourselves into destruction means that we should remain with our wealth and improve it, and abandon jihad. Abu Imran said: Abu Ayyub continued to strive in the cause of God until he was buried in Constantinople.

c: Muhammad ibn Ammarah al-Asadi and Abdullah ibn Abi Ziyad told me, they said: Abu Abd al-Rahman Abdullah ibn Yazid told us, he said: Haywah and Ibn Lahi’ah told me, they said: Yazid ibn Abi Habib told us, he said:
m: Aslam Abu Imran, the freed slave of Tajib told me, he said: We were in Constantinople, and the people of Egypt were led by Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of Syria were led by Fadala ibn Ubayd, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. A large column of Romans came out of the city. He said: So we lined up a large column of Muslims, and a man from the Muslims charged the Roman column until he entered them, then he came out to us facing him, so the people shouted and said: Glory be to God! He threw himself into destruction! Abu Ayoub Al-Ansari, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up. He said: O people, you interpret this verse in this way! This verse was revealed about us, the Ansar! When God made His religion victorious and its supporters increased, we said to each other secretly from the Messenger of God: Our wealth has been lost, so why don’t we take care of it and repair what was lost from it! Then God revealed in His Book, responding to what we intended to do, saying:
h
And spend in the cause of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, with the stay that we wanted to take care of the wealth and repair it, so He ordered us to fight. So Abu Ayyub continued to fight in the cause of God until God took him.

x: The correct thing to say about that in my opinion is that God, the Most High, ordered spending in His cause with His saying:
h
And spend in the cause of God - and His way is the path that He has prescribed for His servants and made clear to them

. Meaning: And spend in order to glorify My religion which I have prescribed for you, by fighting your enemy who wage war against you because of their disbelief in Me. And He forbade them from throwing themselves into destruction, saying:
h
And do not throw yourselves into destruction

. This is an example. The Arabs say to someone who submits to a command: So-and-so gave with his hands. And the same is said to someone who is able to do what is intended by him: He gave with his hands. So the meaning of His statement:
h
And do not throw yourselves into destruction
is: Do not surrender to destruction, giving it your burdens and thus perishing.

And the one who abandons spending in the way of God when it is obligatory upon him is surrendering to destruction by abandoning the fulfillment of God’s obligation upon him from his wealth. This is because God, the Most High, made one of the eight obligatory charity shares for His sake, saying: Zakat is only for the poor and the needy until His statement: and in the way of God and the wayfarer (al-Tawbah 9:60). Whoever neglects to spend what he is obligated to spend in the way of God on what he is obligated to, will be surrendering to destruction and throwing himself into destruction. Likewise, the one who despairs of God’s mercy due to a past sin of his is throwing himself into destruction, because God has forbidden that, saying:
“And do not despair of relief from God. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from God except the disbelieving people.”
Likewise, the one who abandons fighting and jihad against the polytheists, when it is obligatory upon him, when the Muslims need it, is neglecting an obligation and throwing himself into destruction.
Since all of these meanings are possible in His statement:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction

, and God, the Almighty, did not specify one of them over another, then the correct thing to say about that is to say: God has forbidden throwing ourselves into what will lead to our destruction, and surrendering to destruction - which is torment - by abandoning the obligations that are required of us. So it is not permissible for any of us to engage in something that God dislikes from us, which by engaging in it we deserve His torment. However, even if this is the case, the most likely interpretation of the verse is: And spend, O believers, in the way of God, and do not neglect spending in it, lest you perish by deserving - by neglecting it - My punishment, as Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction
, he said: Destruction is the punishment of God.
This is an announcement from him to them - after his ordering them to spend - of the punishment in the afterlife for those who neglect the obligatory spending in his path.
What is the reason for including the preposition ba in his statement:
h
And do not throw [yourselves] with your [own] hands
, when you know that what is known from the speech of the Arabs is: I threw to so-and-so a dirham rather than I threw to so-and-so a dirham?

It has been said that it was added similar to the speaker’s addition of the preposition ba in his statement: I pulled with the garment, “I pulled the garment,” I clung to it, and I clung to it, and It grows with oil (al-Mu’minun 23:20), but it is: It grows oil.
Others said: The letter Baa in His statement:
h
And do not throw [yourselves] with your own hands is the origin of the kunya

. Because every action that occurs is referred to as a kunya, it is compelled by it. Like when you say about a man you spoke to and you intended to refer to his action, so if you intended that you would say: I did it to him. They said: Since Baa is the origin, it is permissible to include Baa or exclude it in every action whose path is the path of its kunya. As for al-tahlaka, it is the taf'ala from al-hulaka.
What He, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
And do good

, is to do good, O believers, in performing what I have obligated you to do of My obligations, and avoiding what I have commanded you to avoid of sins, and in spending in My cause, and the strong among you visiting the weak who has a good relationship, for I love those who do good in that, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Zaid bin al-Habbab told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man from the Companions,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And do good
, for God loves those who do good he said: performing the obligations.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: Have good thoughts about God.
Those who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Hafs bin Omar told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah,
h
And do good
, for God loves the doers of good. He said: Have good thoughts about God, and He will bless you.
Others said: Do good by helping those in need.
Those who said that: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement:
h
And do good
, for God loves the doers of good, “Do good to those who do not have anything in their hands.”

The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that: Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Complete the Hajj with its rituals Surat Al-Baqarah 2:196 And complete the Hajj and Umrah for the sake of God.
h
But if you are prevented

, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animals reach their destination. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his scalp [must make up] a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. But when you are secure, then whoever enjoys [his ritual] From the Umrah to the Hajj, then whatever sacrifice can be obtained with ease. But whoever cannot find [one], then a fast of three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned. That is ten complete days. That is for him whose family are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear God and know that God is severe in penalty. and Sunnahs, and complete the Umrah with its limits and Sunnahs.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Ubaid bin Ismail Al-Hibari told me, he said: Abdullah bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah:
m: h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

, he said: It is in Abdullah's reading: And complete the Hajj and Umrah, he said: Do not go beyond the House with the Umrah, Ibrahim said: So I mentioned that to Saeed bin Jubair and he said: That is what Ibn Abbas said.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abdul Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Ibrahim
m: that he read: And complete the Hajj and Umrah.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abdul Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah
m: that he read: And complete the Hajj and Umrah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Salih told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

,” meaning: Whoever enters into the state of ihram for Hajj or Umrah, he is not to be released from his state of ihram until he completes it. The completion of Hajj is on the Day of Sacrifice, when he throws the pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqabah and visits the House, he has been released from his entire state of ihram. The completion of Umrah is when he circumambulates the House and performs Tawaf around Safa and Marwah, he has been released from his state of ihram.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us
m: - and Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us - all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God
, he said: What they were commanded in them.

c: I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding His statement:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

, he said: Ibrahim said, on the authority of Alqamah bin Qays, who said: Hajj is the rituals of Hajj, and Umrah does not go beyond the House. Ibn Humayd narrated, he said: Jarir narrated, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

, he said: He said: The rituals of Hajj are completed: Arafat, Muzdalifah and their places. And Umrah for the House, is to circumambulate the House and between Safa and Marwah, then to be released from ihram.

x: Others said: Its completion is to enter ihram for them separately from your family circle.

Those who said that: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, he said: Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn Salamah, on the authority of ʿAli that he said: A man came to ʿAli and said to him regarding this verse: And complete the Hajj and ʿUmrah for God, that you enter ihram from your family circle. Ibn Humayd narrated, he said: Harun ibn al-Mughira narrated, on the authority of ʿAnbasa, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn Salamah, he said: A man came to ʿAli may God be pleased with him and said: What do you think of the statement of God the Almighty: And complete the Hajj and ʿUmrah for God? He said: That you enter ihram from your family circle. Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Wakee’ narrated, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suqah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: The completion of Umrah is to enter ihram from the circle of your family.

Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Wakee’ narrated, on the authority of Thawr ibn Yazid, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of Tawus, who said: The completion of them is to perform them separately and return to your family. Al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of Tawus:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God
, he said: Perform them separately and temporarily from your family, and that is the completion of them.

Others said: The completion of Umrah is to perform them outside the months of Hajj, and the completion of Hajj is to perform all of its rituals, so that the one who performs it is not required to offer a blood sacrifice because of Qiran or Mut’ah.
Who said that: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

, he said: The completion of Umrah is that which is not in the months of Hajj. And whoever is in the months of Hajj and then stays until he performs Hajj, it is a Mut’ah, and he must offer a sacrificial animal during it if he can find one, otherwise he must fast three days during Hajj and seven when he returns.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God
, he said: Whatever is outside the months of Hajj is a complete Umrah, and whatever is in the months of Hajj is a Mut’ah, and he must offer a sacrificial animal.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said:
m: I heard Al-Qasim bin Muhammad say: Umrah during the months of Hajj is not complete. He said: So it was said to him: Umrah in Muharram? He said: They considered it complete.

x: Others said: Completing them means that you leave your family and do not want anyone else.

Those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, a man told me, on the authority of Sufyan, who said: It - meaning their completion - is that you leave your family, intending nothing but Hajj and Umrah, and you enter ihram from the miqat. It is not that you leave for trade or for any need, until when you are close to Mecca you say: If only I would perform Hajj or Umrah! That is sufficient, but the completion is that you leave for it, not for anything else.
Others said: Rather the meaning of that is: Complete Hajj and Umrah for God if you enter into them.

Those who said that: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: Umrah is not obligatory upon any of the people. He said: So I said to him: What about the statement of God the Most High:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

? He said: There is no one among creation who should, when he enters into a matter, except to complete it. So when he enters into it, he should not enter ihram for a day or two and then return, just as if he fasted one day, he should not break his fast in the middle of the day. Al-Sha'bi used to recite it with a raised voice.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Yahya bin Sa'id told us, on the authority of Shu'bah, he said, Sa'id bin Abi Burdah told me:
m: Al-Sha'bi and Abu Burdah were discussing Umrah. Al-Sha'bi said: It is voluntary,
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God
. Abu Burdah said: It is obligatory:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Al-Sha'bi
m: that he used to recite:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God
. It has been narrated from Al-Sha'bi that it was different from this statement, although the well-known statement from him is this, and that is what:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Minhal told us, he said, Abu Awanah told us, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha'bi, he said:
m: Umrah is obligatory. The reading of the one who said: Umrah is obligatory - is in the accusative case, meaning: Perform the obligation of Hajj and Umrah, as:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, he said:
m: I heard Abu Ishaq say: I heard Masruq say: You have been commanded in the Book of God with four things: to establish prayer, to pay zakat, Hajj, and Umrah. He said: Then he recited this verse: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God
r
(Al-ʿImran 3:97)
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

c: Abu al-Saʿib told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said:
m: I heard Layth narrating, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Masruq, he said: We have been commanded to perform four things: prayer, zakat, Umrah, and Hajj, so Umrah was placed in relation to Hajj as zakat was in relation to prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said,
m: Ali ibn Husayn and Saʿid ibn Jubayr said - and they were asked: Is Umrah obligatory for people? Both of them said: We do not know that it is obligatory, as God said:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

c: Suwar bin Abdullah narrated to us, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulaiman, who said:
m: A man asked Saeed bin Jubair about Umrah: Is it obligatory or voluntary? He said: Obligatory. He said: Al-Sha’bi says: It is voluntary! He said: Al-Sha’bi lied, and he recited:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul Razzaq informed us, he said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of someone
m: who heard Ata’ say regarding His statement:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God
, he said: They are two obligations, Hajj and Umrah.

x: The interpretation of these people regarding His statement, the Most High:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

, is that they are two obligatory obligations that God, the Most High, has commanded to be performed, just as He has commanded the establishment of prayer, and that they are two obligations, and He has made Umrah obligatory as Hajj is obligatory. They are a large number of the Companions, the Followers, and those who came after them from the successors. We did not like to make the book long by mentioning them and mentioning the narrations from them. They said: The meaning of his saying:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God
, is: perform the Hajj and Umrah.
Some of those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa bin Harun told us, he said: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God
, he said: perform the Hajj and Umrah.

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, Abu Naim narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, on the authority of Thawir, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali:
m: And perform Hajj and Umrah for the House, then it is obligatory like Hajj.

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to us, Abu Naim narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, Thawir narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: And complete Hajj and Umrah. Then Abdullah said: By God, were it not for the embarrassment and the fact that I did not hear anything from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, I would have said: Umrah is obligatory like Hajj.

x: It seems that they meant by their saying: Perform Hajj and Umrah: Perform them, with their limits and rulings, as was made obligatory upon you.

Others who read the reading of these people with the accusative of Umrah said: Umrah is voluntary, and they saw that there is no indication of its obligation in their placing Umrah in the accusative in the reading, since there are actions that a servant may be required to do and complete by entering into it, and the beginning of entering into it was not obligatory upon him. This is like the voluntary Hajj, there is no disagreement among all that if he enters into ihram for it, he must continue with it and complete it, and it was not obligatory for him to begin with. They said: Likewise, Umrah is not an obligation that must be entered into from the beginning, but the one who enters into it and makes it obligatory for himself to complete it after entering into it. They said: There is no evidence in God’s command to complete Hajj and Umrah that it is obligatory. They said: Rather, we made Hajj obligatory by His saying, the Almighty: And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses
r
(Al Imran 3:97)
Among those who said this are a group of the Companions, the Followers, and those who came after them from the Khalil.
Some of those who said this mentioned:

c: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us,
m: he heard Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, from Abu Ma’shar, from Ibrahim, he said: Abdullah said: Hajj is obligatory, and ‘Umrah is voluntary.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said:
m: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:196 And complete the Hajj and Umrah for the sake of God.
h
But if you are prevented

, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animals reach their destination. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his scalp [must make up] a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. But when you are secure, then whoever enjoys [his ritual] From the Umrah to the Hajj, then whatever sacrifice can be obtained with ease. But whoever cannot find [one], then a fast of three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned. That is ten complete days. That is for him whose family are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear God and know that God is severe in penalty.

c: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Abu Maʿshar, on the authority of An-Nakhaʿi, on the authority of Ibn Masʿud,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Uthma narrated to us, he said: Saʿid ibn Bashir narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: Umrah is not obligatory.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Samak, he said:
m: I asked Ibrahim about Umrah, and he said: It is a good Sunnah.

c: Yaqub narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, he said: Abu ʿAwanah narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: ʿAbdur-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, he said: Hammad narrated to us, he said:
m: Abdullah ibn Aoun, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, said: Umrah is voluntary.

x: As for those who read it with Umrah in the nominative case, they said: There is no reason for its accusative case. Umrah is only a visit to the House, and one does not deserve the name Mu’tamir unless he is a visitor to it. They said: And if he does not deserve the name Mu’tamir except by visiting it - which is when he reaches it and performs Tawaf around it and Safa and Marwa, then there is no action left after that that he is commanded to complete after that, just as the pilgrim is commanded to complete it after reaching it and Tawaf around it and Safa and Marwa, by coming to Arafat and Muzdalifah and standing at the places where he was commanded to stand, and doing all the other actions of Hajj that are part of its completion after coming to the House - then there is no reason for the one who says to the pilgrim: Complete your Umrah. If it does not have an understandable meaning, then the correct reading of Umrah is to raise it, as it is one of the righteous deeds for God, so it is raised by its predicate that comes after it, which is His saying: for God.

The most correct of the two readings in this regard, according to us, is the reading of the one who reads Umrah in the accusative case. On the connection of it to Hajj, meaning the command to complete them both. There is no meaning to the defect of those who defected in raising it by saying that Umrah is visiting the House. For when the person performing Umrah reaches it, there is no work left for him that he is commanded to complete. This is because when he reaches the House, his visit is over, and what remains for him is to complete the work that God commanded him to do in his Umrah and visit to the House, and that is circumambulating the House, and walking between Safa and Marwah, and avoiding what God commanded to avoid until he completes that. And that is work - even if it is something that he is obligated to do by making the visit obligatory upon himself - other than the visit.

This, with the consensus of the argument on reading Umrah in the accusative, and the contradiction of all the readings of the regions with the reading of those who read it in the nominative. In that, there is no need to cite evidence for the error of those who read it in the nominative. As for the first of the two opinions that we mentioned as correct in interpreting his statement: And Umrah is for God, according to the reading of those who read This is an installation, so the statement of Abdullah bin Masoud and those who said the same, that the meaning of this is:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

to the House, after He has made them obligatory for you, is not that this is a command from God the Almighty - to begin their work and enter into them, and perform their work in its entirety - with this verse. This is because the verse is open to the two meanings that we have described: that it is a command from God the Almighty to establish them initially and make them obligatory from Him upon the servants, and that it is a command from Him to complete them after entering into them, and after making their obligation obligatory upon Himself.

So since the verse is open to the two meanings that we have described, there is no argument in it for one of the two groups against the other, except that the other has the same against him in it. And since it is like this - and there is no report of the argument for the excuse in making the Umrah obligatory, decisive, and the nation is in dispute over its obligation - there is no meaning for the statement of one who says: It is an obligation, without proof indicating the correctness of his statement. Since the obligations are not obligatory upon the servants except by clear evidence of their obligation upon them.
If someone thought that it is obligatory like Hajj, and that the interpretation of those who interpreted His statement:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God
, meaning: establish their limits and obligations, is more appropriate than our interpretation, as Hatim bin Bakir al-Dhabi narrated to me, saying:

c: Ashhal bin Hatim al-Artba’i narrated to us, saying: Ibn Awn narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Juhadah, on the authority of a man, on the authority of his colleague, on the authority of his father - and his father was called Abu al-Muntafiq -
m: who said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Arafat, and I approached him until the necks of my mount and the necks of his mount intertwined, and I said: O Messenger of God, inform me of an act that will save me from the punishment of God and admit me into His Paradise. He said: Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, and establish the prescribed prayer, and pay the obligatory zakat, and perform Hajj and Umrah - Ashhal said: I think he said: and fast Ramadan - and see what you like people to do to you and do to them, and what you dislike people to do to you, leave them alone. And: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi and Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of al-Nuʿman bin Salim, on the authority of Amr bin Aws, on the authority of Abu Razin al-ʿUqayli, a man from Banu ʿAmir, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, my father is an old man who is unable to perform Hajj, ʿUmrah, or stabbing, and Islam has come to him, so should I perform Hajj on his behalf? He said: Perform Hajj and Umrah on behalf of your father. And what: Yaqub narrated to me, he said:

c: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah:
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon and said: Worship God and do not associate anything with Him, establish prayer, give zakat, perform Hajj and Umrah, and be upright and you will be upright. And similar reports, for these are reports that cannot be proven with the likes of them in the religion, even if their chains of transmission are weak, and that - despite their weak chains of transmission - they have in the reports variations that indicate that Umrah is voluntary and not an obligatory duty, which is what:

c: Muhammad ibn Humayd and Muhammad ibn Isa al-Damaghani narrated to us, they said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Arta’ah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace: that he was asked about Umrah: Is it obligatory? He said: No, and it is better for you to perform Umrah.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us
m: - and Yahya bin Talhah Al-Yarboui narrated to me, he said: Sharik narrated to us - on the authority of Muawiyah bin Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Salih Al-Hanafi, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hajj is jihad, and Umrah is voluntary.

x: Some of the foolish people claimed that it was confirmed to him that Umrah is obligatory, because he did not find a voluntary prayer without an imam from the obligatory prayers. So since it was confirmed that Umrah is voluntary, it must be obligatory for it, because the obligatory prayer is the imam of the voluntary prayer in all actions. So it is said to the one who says that: He has made Iʿtikaf voluntary, so what is the obligatory part of it that is the imam of his voluntary prayer? Then he is asked about Iʿtikaf: Is it obligatory or not? If he says: Obligatory, he has left the statement of the entire ummah. And if he says: Voluntary, it is said: What is it that made Iʿtikaf voluntary and Umrah obligatory, from the aspect that must be accepted? He will not say anything about one of them except that he will make the same thing obligatory about the other. And based on the evidence we have cited, the more correct of the two readings in Umrah is the reading of the one who reads it in the accusative case - and that the more correct of the two interpretations in His statement:
h
And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God

, is the interpretation of Ibn Abbas that we mentioned from him on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah from him: that he was commanded by God to complete their actions after entering them, and making them obligatory, according to what he commanded of their limits and Sunnahs - and that the more correct of the two sayings in Umrah is the saying of the one who said: It is voluntary, not obligatory - and that the meaning of the verse is: And complete, O believers, the Hajj and Umrah for God after you have entered them and made them obligatory for yourselves, according to what God has commanded you of their limits.

And God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed this verse to His Prophet, peace be upon him, in the Umrah of Hudaybiyyah in which he was prevented from the House, informing him and the believers in it of what is upon them in their ihram if they are left alone with the House, and explaining to them in it what is the way out for them from their ihram if they enter ihram and are prevented from the House. To mention the actions required of them in their Umrah that they performed in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and what is required of them after that in their Umrah and Hajj, he began by saying: “They ask you about the new moons. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj.’” (al-Baqarah 2:189). We have previously demonstrated the meaning of Hajj and Umrah with evidence, so we disliked lengthening the book by repeating it.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
But if you are prevented
, then whatever sacrifice can be obtained with ease.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the restriction that God imposed on those who were afflicted with it during their Hajj and Umrah, which is to offer whatever sacrifice is easy.
Some of them said: It is everything that prevents or detains the pilgrim and prevents him from doing the work that God has imposed on him during his ihram and his arrival at the Sacred House.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid
