m: that he used to say: Confinement is all confinement. He said: Any man who is obstructed during his pilgrimage Or his Umrah, then he sends his sacrificial animal from where he is prevented. He said: Mujahid said about his statement:
h
But if you are prevented
h
then if you are prevented

: a person becomes ill, or is broken, or is prevented by something that overpowers him, whatever it may be, then he should send whatever sacrificial animal he can easily, and he should not shave his head, nor should he be released, until the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Nu'aym told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata', he said:
m: Ihsar is anything that prevents.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Qatada, that he said
m: about the one Surat Al-Baqarah 2:196 And complete the Hajj and Umrah for the sake of God.
h
But if you are prevented

, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animals reach their destination. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his scalp [must make up] a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. But when you are secure, then whoever enjoys [his ritual] From the Umrah to the Hajj, then whatever sacrifice can be obtained with ease. But whoever cannot find [one], then a fast of three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned. That is ten complete days. That is for him whose family are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear God and know that God is severe in penalty. who is prevented: it is fear, sickness, and the one who prevents. If that befalls him, he sends his offering, and when the sacrificial animal reaches its destination, it becomes permissible.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if you are prevented

, then what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animal, he said: This is a man who is afflicted with fear, sickness, or something that prevents him from the House, he sends his offering, and when it reaches its destination, it becomes permissible.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: Everything that prevents the pilgrim from performing Hajj is a case of Ihsar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, Abu Jaʿfar said:
m: I think it was on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ibrahim bin al-Muhajir, on the authority of Ibrahim:
h
But if you are prevented
, he said: sickness, fracture, or fear.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muʿawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
But if you are prevented
h
then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal
, he said: Whoever enters ihram for Hajj or Umrah, then is prevented from performing Hajj or Umrah by an illness that exhausts him or an excuse that prevents him, then he must make it up.

x: The reason for those who say this statement is that Ihsar in the speech of the Arabs means: preventing an illness or the like, other than coercion and overpowering from a conqueror or a conqueror, except for the overpowering of an illness such as an illness or a bite or a wound or the loss of money or the breakage of a mount. As for preventing the enemy, and confining a detainer in a prison, and the dominance of a dominant force that prevents the pilgrim from reaching the House, whether by a sultan or a powerful person, the Arabs call this a confinement, not a blockade. They said: What indicates this is the statement of God, the Most High: And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers
r
(Al-Isra’: 8)

, meaning by it: a blocker, i.e. a detainer. They said: If the confinement of the dominant force for reasons other than those we have described was called a confinement, then it would be necessary to say: the enemy has been besieged.

They said: In the agreement of the languages of the Arabs on the enemy being besieged, and the enemy is besieged, not the enemy being besieged and they are besieged, and the man being besieged by a cause such as illness or fear - is the greatest evidence that God, the Most High, meant by His statement: If you are besieged, by an illness, fear, or a preventing cause. They said: We have made the enemy’s confinement and the pilgrim’s prevention from reaching the House to mean the confinement of illness, by analogy with what God, the Most High, has made for the sick person who is prevented from reaching the House by illness, not by the apparent meaning of His statement:
h
But if you are prevented
, then make an offering as easy as possible, since the confinement of the enemy, the ruler, and the oppressor is a preventive cause, similar to the preventive cause of illness and fracture.
Others said that the meaning of His statement:
h
But if you are prevented

, then make an offering as easy as possible, is if an enemy prevents you from reaching the House, or an oppressor from among the children of Adam prevents you. They said: As for the causes that occur in the body, such as illness, wounds, and the like, then that is not included in His statement:
h
But if you are prevented
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said:
m: The blockade is the blockade of the enemy, so the man sends his gift. If he is unable to reach the House due to the enemy, and if he finds someone to deliver it on his behalf to Mecca, then he sends it and enters ihram. Muhammad ibn Amr said: Abu Asim said: We do not know whether he said: He enters ihram, or: He exits ihram, from the day on which the owner of the gift is appointed if he buys it. Then if he is safe, then he must perform Hajj or Umrah. Then if he is afflicted with an illness that prevents him and he does not have a gift with him, then he exits ihram where he is prevented. If he has a gift with him, then he does not exit ihram until the gift reaches its destination. Then if he sends it, then he does not have to perform Hajj or Umrah the following year, unless he wishes.

c: I was told by Abu Ubaid al-Qasim ibn Salam,
m: who said: Yahya ibn Saeed told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There is no blockade except for one who is blocked by an enemy.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: like the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr on the authority of Abu Asim, except that he said: Then he sends it and becomes forbidden from the day on which he promised the owner of the gift if he bought it. Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith like the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr on the authority of Abu Asim. Malik ibn Anas said: “It has reached me that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions were released at Al-Hudaybiyyah, so they slaughtered the sacrificial animals and shaved their heads, and they were released from everything before they circumambulated the House, and before the sacrificial animals reached it. Then we did not know that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered any of his companions, or those who were with him, to make up for anything, or to return to anything.”

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us
m: on his authority, saying: Malik was asked about someone who was besieged by an enemy and prevented from reaching the House, so he said: He is released from everything, and he slaughters his sacrificial animals, and shaves his head where he is prevented, and he does not have to make up for it, unless he has never performed Hajj, in which case he must perform the Hajj of Islam. He said: The command with us regarding someone who is besieged by something other than an enemy, such as illness or the like, is to seek treatment as is necessary. And he ransoms himself, then makes it an Umrah, and performs Hajj the following year and offers a sacrificial animal.

x: The reason for those who said this statement - I mean those who said the statement of Malik - is that this verse was revealed about the polytheists besieging the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and his companions from the House, so God commanded His Prophet and those with him to slaughter their sacrificial animals and enter ihram. They said: God revealed this verse about the enemy besieging him, so it is not permissible to divert its ruling to a meaning other than that for which it was revealed. They said: As for the sick person, if he is unable to travel due to his illness until he misses Arafat, then he is a man who has missed Hajj, and he must exit his ihram with what exits someone who has missed Hajj - and he is not from the meaning of the one who is prevented for whom this verse was revealed.
The more correct of the two interpretations of the statement:
h
If you are prevented

, is the interpretation of those who interpret it as meaning: If the fear of an enemy, or illness, or a disease prevents you from reaching the House, i.e. your fear or illness makes you prevent yourselves and prevents them from performing what you have made obligatory upon yourselves of performing Hajj and ʿUmrah. That is why it is said: You are prevented, because the mention of fear and illness is omitted. It is said: My fear of so-and-so prevented me from meeting you, and my illness from so-and-so, meaning: it made me prevent myself from that. However, if the one preventing is a man or a human being, it is said: So-and-so prevented me from meeting you, meaning: he prevented me from it. If the meaning of the verse was what the interpreter thought from his statement:
h
If you are prevented
, that is, if an enemy prevents you from reaching Al-Bays, then it should be:
h
If you are prevented

What shows the correctness of what we have said, that the interpretation of the verse is intended to mean the confinement of someone other than the enemy, and that it only means fear of the enemy, is His statement:
h
Then when you are secure

, then whoever enjoys the ‘umrah until the Hajj. Security is achieved by the removal of fear. Since this is the case, it is known that the confinement that God meant in this verse is the fear that results in security. Since this is the case, the confinement of the one who is not imprisoned with fear for the life from his confinement is not included in the ruling of the verse according to its apparent meaning, even though his ruling may be included in our view by analogy. This is because the confinement of someone who is not fearful for the life from his confinement, such as the ruler whose punishment is not feared, the father, and the wife’s husband, if one of them or some of them is imprisoned and prevented from setting out to perform Hajj or reaching the House after requiring the forbidden person to enter ihram, is not included in the apparent meaning of His statement:
h
Then if you are prevented
, because we have described that its meaning is: If fear of an enemy prevents you - as indicated by His statement:
h
Then when you are secure
, then whoever enjoys the ‘umrah until the Hajj.

The report we mentioned earlier on the authority of Ibn Abbas explained that he said: The siege is the siege of the enemy. Since that is the more appropriate of the two interpretations of the verse for what we have described, and that was a prevention from reaching the House, then every obstacle that occurs to the pilgrim in ihram and prevents him from reaching the House, it has a similar ruling.
Then the people of knowledge differed in the interpretation of his statement:
h
Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal
Some of them said: It is a sheep.

Those who said that: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Qanad told us, he said, Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Abi Ishaq Al-Sabi’i, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
h
Whatever is easy of the sacrifice
, a sheep.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Rahman told us, and Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: h
Whatever is easy of the sacrifice
, a sheep.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdul Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Malik, he said:
m: I performed Tamattu’ and asked Ibn Abbas, he said:
h
Whatever is easy of the sacrifice
. I said, A sheep? He said, A sheep.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan narrated to us, he said, Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Malik, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, he said: From the eight pairs: camels, cows, goats, and sheep.

c: Abu Kurayb and Ya’qub bin Ibrahim narrated to us, they said, Hisham narrated to us, he said, Al-Zuhri informed us
m: - and he was asked about the statement of God, the Most High: whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say: From the sheep.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Yahya bin Wadheeh narrated to us, he said, Yunus bin Abi Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, from the eight pairs.

c: Ibn Abd Al-A’la narrated to us, he said, Khalid narrated to us, he said:
m: It was said to Al-Ash’ath: What did Al-Hasan say: whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal? He said: A sheep. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:196 And complete the Hajj and Umrah for the sake of God.
h
But if you are prevented

, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animals reach their destination. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his scalp [must make up] a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. But when you are secure, then whoever enjoys [his ritual] From the Umrah to the Hajj, then whatever sacrifice can be obtained with ease. But whoever cannot find [one], then a fast of three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned. That is ten complete days. That is for him whose family are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear God and know that God is severe in penalty.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal
, he said: The largest is a camel, the middle is a cow, and the smallest is a sheep.

c: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, he said: Yazid ibn Zuraʿ told us, he said: Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same, except that it was said: The largest is a camel, and he mentioned the rest of the hadith in the same way.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, he said: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Zurarah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: h
Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal
, a sheep.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Jamrah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly. Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’:
h
Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal

, a sheep. Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Ibn Yaman narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Nafi’ narrated, on the authority of Ata’, similarly. Musa ibn Harun narrated, he said: Amr ibn Hammad narrated, he said: Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: The one who is prevented from performing Hajj should send an offering, a sheep or more. Ubayd ibn Ismail Al-Habbari narrated, he said: Ibn Numayr narrated, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, he said: If a man enters ihram for Hajj and is prevented from performing Hajj, he should send whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, a sheep. He said: So I mentioned that to Saeed bin Jubair and he said: That is what Ibn Abbas said.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial offering is a sheep or more.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, and Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, he said, Abu Jamrah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial offering is a camel, a cow, a sheep, or a share in the blood money.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said,
m: I heard Yahya bin Saeed say: I heard Al-Qasim bin Muhammad say: Ibn Abbas used to think that the sheep is whatever is easy of the sacrificial offering.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial offering is a sheep.

c: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal is a sheep.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Sahl ibn Yusuf told us, he said: Hamid told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umair, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: The sacrificial animal is a sheep. It was said to him: Is it less than a cow? He said: Then I will recite to you from the Book of God what you will know that the sacrificial animal is a sheep. What about the gazelle? They said: A sheep. He said: A sacrifice that reaches the Kaaba (al-Ma’idah 5:90).

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Al-Hajjaj told us: Hammad told us, on the authority of Qais bin Sa’d, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: A sheep.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Dahlam bin Salih, who said:
m: I asked Abu Ja’far about his statement:
h
Whatever is easy of the sacrifice
, and he said: A sheep.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Malik bin Anas told him, on the authority of Ja’far bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father:
m: Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, used to say:
h
Whatever is easy of the sacrifice
. A sheep.

c: Al-Muthanna told us: Mutraf bin Abdullah told us: Malik told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, the same.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Malik told me:
m: It reached him that Abdullah ibn Abbas used to say: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal is a sheep.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, Malik said:
m: And that is dearer to me.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal is upon him - meaning the one who is prevented - a sacrificial animal. If he is able to afford it, then it is a camel, otherwise it is a cow, otherwise it is a sheep.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam al-Asqalani told us, he said, Ibn Abi Dhi’b told us, on the authority of Shu’bah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal is a sheep, and whatever is forbidden from the rites of God is better.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ashhab told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us: Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah told him:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal is a sheep.

x: Others said: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, of camels and cows, one year less than the other.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Mu’tamir told us, he said,
m: I heard Ubaydullah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, a cow less than a cow, and a camel less than a camel.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, he said:
m: A man asked Ibn Umar: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal? He said: Would you accept a sheep? As if he did not accept it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, a female camel or a cow. So he was asked: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal? He said: A female camel is less than a female camel, and a cow is less than a male cow.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, that he said:
m: h
Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal
, he said: A camel or a cow.

c: Abu Kurayb and Yaʿqub told us, they said, Hisham told us, he said, Al-Zuhri told us
m: - and he was asked about the statement of God:
h
Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal
, he said: Ibn ʿUmar said, of camels and cows.

c: Yaʿqub told me, he said, Ibn ʿUlayyah told us, he said, Ayyub told us, on the authority of Nafiʿ, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal
, he said: A female camel is less than a female camel, and a cow is less than a cow.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal
, he said: Camels and cows.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abdul Wahhab told us:
m: I heard Yahya bin Saeed say: I heard Al-Qasim bin Muhammad say: Abdullah bin Umar and Aisha used to say: What is easy of the sacrificial animal, of camels and cows.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Al-Walid bin Abi Hisham told us, on the authority of Ziyad bin Jubair, on the authority of his brother Abdullah or Ubaydullah bin Jubair, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Umar about the temporary marriage of sacrificial animal, and he said: A female camel. I said: What do you say about a sheep? He said: Is all of you a sheep? Is all of you a sheep?
b.via: his brother Abdullah or Ubaydullah bin Jubair

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid and Tawus, they said:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, a cow.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, he said: In the words of Ibn Umar: a cow or more.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Abu Ma’shar told me, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, he said: a camel or a cow, but as for a sheep, it is only a sacrifice.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: A camel is less than a camel, and a cow is less than a cow, and the sheep is a sacrifice. He said: A cow is worth forty or fifty.

c: Qatada told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Usamah told me, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: who used to say: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, is a cow.

c: Qatada told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Usamah bin Zaid told me: Saeed told him, he said:
m: I saw Ibn Umar and the people of Yemen coming to him and asking him about whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, and they would say: A sheep! A sheep! He would reply: A sheep! A sheep! He would urge them - except that a camel is less than a camel, and a cow is less than a cow, but whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, is a cow.

x: The more correct of the two opinions is the opinion of the one who said: Whatever is easy of the sacrificial offering is a sheep. Because God, the Most High, has only made obligatory whatever is easy of the sacrificial offering. This applies to everything that is easy for the Mahdi to offer, whatever that which he offers, unless God, the Most High, has specified something from that, in which case whatever is specified from that is excluded from the group that is permitted by the apparent meaning of the revelation, and all other things other than that are sufficient if the Mahdi offers it as a sacrificial offering, after it has earned the name of sacrificial offering.

Those who refused that a sheep be among the easiest sacrifices, because it does not deserve the name of a sacrifice, just as if he sacrificed a chicken or an egg, he would not have been a sufficient sacrifice.

If there were a difference in the Mahdi of the chicken and the egg, similar to that in the Mahdi of the sheep, then their path would be the same: in that each of them has fulfilled what is required of him according to the apparent revelation, since neither of the two offerings could be considered a fulfilment - by offering what he offered of that - of what God has obligated upon him in his confinement. However, when the Mahdi brought out what is less than a year old of sheep, and a two-year-old of goats, camels, and cows and above of teeth - from being a Mahdi of what God has obligated upon him in his confinement or his enjoyment - with the conclusive argument transmitted from our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an inheritance, that was excluded from being intended by his saying:
h
Then whatever is easy of the offering

, even though it was from what was easy for us of the offerings. Since there is a difference of opinion regarding the one-year-old sheep and the two-year-old goat, that is sufficient for his sacrifice, according to the apparent meaning of the revelation, because it is one of the easiest sacrifices.
What is the position of the word what in the words of God Almighty: Then what is easy of sacrifice?
raised.
With what?

It is abandoned. And that is upon him. Because the interpretation of the statement: And complete the Hajj and Umrah, O believers, for God. If something prevents you from completing that, such as sickness, or a broken bone, or fear of an enemy, then you must - for your release, if you want to release from your state of ihram - offer whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal. And we chose the nominative case in that, because most of the Qur’an came with its counterparts in the nominative case, such as His statement:
h
But whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head
, then a ransom of fasting Surat Al-Baqarah 2:196 And complete the Hajj and Umrah for the sake of God.
h
But if you are prevented

, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animals reach their destination. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his scalp [must make up] a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. But when you are secure, then whoever enjoys [his ritual] From the Umrah to the Hajj, then whatever sacrifice can be obtained with ease. But whoever cannot find [one], then a fast of three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned. That is ten complete days. That is for him whose family are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear God and know that God is severe in penalty. (al-Baqarah 2:184) and His statement:
h
But whoever cannot find [anything]
, then a fast of three days, and what is similar to that, which would take a long time to list in the book, we left mentioning it because what we mentioned sufficed with it.
And if it was said: The place of what is accusative, meaning:
h
If you are prevented

, then offer whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal, then the one who said it would not be mistaken. As for the sacrificial animal, it is a plural, its singular is a gift, based on the assumption of the seriousness of the saddle, and the plural is serious, lightened.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah Maʿmar ibn al-Muthanna, on the authority of Yunus, who said:
m: Abu Amr ibn al-ʿAla’ used to say: I do not know of any letter in speech that resembles it. And with the softening of the ya’ and the sukoon of the dal in al-Hadi, it was recited by the reciters in every country, except what was mentioned on the authority of al-Aʿraj, for Abu Hisham Al-Rifai told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Bashar, on the authority of Asad, on the authority of Al-Araj, that he read: A gift that reaches the Kaaba (al-Ma’idah 5:95) with a heavy kasra on the dal, and he read: Until the gift reaches its place, with a heavy kasra on the dal. And there is a difference of opinion regarding that from Asim, so my difference from him is in agreement with Al-Araj, and his disagreement with the reading of the rest of the readings. And the gift, in my opinion, is called a gift because it is a gift that the one who gives it to God, the Almighty and Majestic, draws near to Him, like a gift that a man gives to someone else, drawing near to Him. It is said from it: I gave the gift to the House of God, so I give it as a gift. Just as it is analogous to a gift that a man gives to someone else: I gave it to so-and-so as a gift, and I give it. And the sacrificial animal is called a gift, and from it is the saying of Zuhair bin Abi Salma, mentioning a man who was taken prisoner, likening him in his sanctity to the sacrificial animal that is given as a gift: I have never seen a group of people take a gift as a gift, nor have I ever seen a neighbor of a house being taken captive!

x: By this, God the Almighty means:
h
If you are prevented
and want to exit your state of ihram, then you must offer whatever is easy of sacrificial animals. And do not exit your state of ihram
h
if you are prevented

until the sacrificial animal - which I have made obligatory upon you to exit your state of ihram in which you were prevented, before its completion and the completion of its rituals and rites - reaches its destination. This is because shaving the head is an exit from the state of ihram that the pilgrim had made obligatory upon himself. So God forbade him from exiting his state of ihram by shaving it until the sacrificial animal - which God the Almighty has permitted him to exit by offering - reaches its destination. Then the scholars differed regarding the location of the sacrificial animal that God the Almighty meant, which when it reaches it, the person prevented from exiting the state of ihram in which he was prevented.

Some of them said: The place of the Hadi of the one who is prevented from slaughtering it is the place where he is released and it is permissible for him to shave his head when he reaches it, if he is prevented from slaughtering it, if it is something that can be slaughtered, or slaughtering it if it is something that can be slaughtered, whether in the open area, slaughtering or slaughtering, or in the Haram, where he is detained. And if it is not out of fear of an enemy, then he is not released until he circumambulates the House and runs between Safa and Marwah. This is the opinion of those who said: The Ihsar is the Ihsar of the enemy and nothing else.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Malik bin Anas told me:
m: It reached him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were released at Al-Hudaybiyyah, so they slaughtered the Hadi and shaved their heads and were released from everything before circumambulating the House, and before the Hadi reached him. Then we did not know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered any of his companions or those who were with him to complete anything or return to anything.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Malik told me, from Nafi’:
m: That Abdullah ibn Umar went out to Mecca to perform Umrah during the Fitnah and said:
h
If you are prevented

from the House, we will do as we did with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he entered ihram for Umrah because the Prophet had entered ihram for Umrah in the year of Hudaybiyyah. Then Abdullah ibn Umar looked into his matter and said: Their command is only one. He said: He turned to his companions and said: Their command is only one. I bear witness to you that I have made Hajj obligatory along with Umrah. He said: Then he performed one Tawaf and saw that this was sufficient for him and he offered a sacrifice. Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: This is the practice with us regarding one who is besieged by an enemy, just as the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were besieged. As for one who is besieged by someone other than an enemy, he is not permitted to go outside the House. He said: Malik was asked about one who is besieged by an enemy and prevented from going outside the House, so he said: He is permitted to do everything and slaughter a sacrifice. He should shave his head where he was confined, and he does not have to make up for it, unless he has never performed Hajj, in which case he should perform the Hajj of Islam.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Malik told us, he said, Yahya ibn Saeed told me, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar:
m: Abdullah ibn Umar, Marwan ibn al-Hakam, and Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr gave a fatwa to Ibn Hazaba al-Makhzumi, who was struck down during Hajj by some route: He should treat himself with what is necessary, and redeem himself, then make it an Umrah and perform Hajj the following year, and offer a sacrifice. Yunus said: Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: This is the matter with us for one who is confined without an enemy. He said: Malik said: And everyone who is prevented from Hajj after he has entered ihram, either by illness, or by a mistake in the number, or Ibn Bashar told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, I heard Yahya bin Saeed say, Ayoub bin Musa told me that Dawud bin Abi Asim told him that he performed Hajj once and fell ill, so he returned to At-Taif and did not perform Tawaf between Safa and Marwa. So he wrote to Ata bin Abi Rabah asking him about that, and Ata wrote to him: shed blood. The reason for those who said what Malik said: that the place of the sacrificial animal when besieged by the enemy is to slaughter it where its owner is detained, is what:

c: Abu Kurayb and Muhammad ibn ‘Amara al-Asadi told us, they said: Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, he said: Musa ibn ‘Ubaydah told us, he said:
m: Abu Marra, the freed slave of Umm Hani’ told me, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, he said: When the sacrificial animal was below the mountains that overlook Wadi al-Thaniyah, the polytheists approached it and turned it away. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered the sacrificial animal where they detained it - which was al-Hudaybiyah - and shaved his head.

x: Some people took his example and shaved their heads when they saw him shave, and others waited and said: Perhaps we can circumambulate the House! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on those who have their hair cut short! It was said: And those who have their hair cut short! He said: May God have mercy on those who shave their heads! It was said: And those who have their hair cut short! He said: And those who have their hair cut short!”

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Qattan told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of ʿUrwah, on the authority of al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, who said:
m: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote down the deal between him and the polytheists of Quraysh - and that was at al-Hudaybiyyah, in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah - he said to his companions: ‘Get up, slaughter your sacrifices, and shave your heads. ’ By God, not a single one of them got up until he had said that three times. When none of them got up, he got up and went to Umm Salamah and mentioned that to her. Umm Salamah said: ‘O Prophet of God, go out, and do not speak a word to any of them until you have slaughtered your sacrifices and called your barber so that you may shave your heads. ’ So he got up and went out, and he did not speak to any of them until he had done that. When they saw that, they got up and slaughtered their sacrifices, and some of them made They said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered his sacrificial animal when the polytheists prevented him from entering the House at Hudaybiyyah, and he and his companions left. They said: Hudaybiyyah is not part of the sanctuary. They said: In such a case there is clear evidence that the meaning of his saying: “until the sacrificial animal reaches its place,” is until it reaches the place of slaughtering or slaughtering and the place of eating and benefiting from it in the place of slaughtering and slaughtering. As was narrated from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar matter, when meat was brought to him - brought to him by Barrah - from charity that he had given to her, so he said: Bring it near, for it has reached its place. Meaning, it has reached its place of being good and lawful for him by being given as a gift to him, after it had been charity given to Barrah.
b.via: al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn al-Hakam

x: Some of them said: The place of the sacrificial animal of the one who is prevented is the sanctuary, and there is no other place for it.

Those who said that: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ammarah bin Umair, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid: That Amr bin Saeed Al-Nakha’i assumed ihram for Umrah, and when he reached Dhat Al-Shaqooq, he was bitten by it. So his companions went out to the road to look for people, and there they found Ibn Mas’ud, so they mentioned that to him, so he said: Let him send a sacrificial animal, and make a day of leadership between you, and when the sacrificial animal is slaughtered, then let him be released, and he must complete his Umrah.

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Sulayman bin Mihran, on the authority of Ammarah bin Umair and Ibrahim, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid that he said:
m: We went out in ihram for Umrah, and among us was Al-Aswad bin Yazid, until we stopped at Dhat Al-Shaqooq, and a companion of ours was bitten, and that was very hard on him, so we did not know what to do with him! So some of us went out to the road, and there we saw a group of people, Abdullah bin Mas’ud, so we said to him: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, one of our men was bitten, so what should we do with him? He said: He will send with you the price of the sacrificial animal, and you will set a day as a guide between you and him. When the sacrificial animal is slaughtered, he will be released and he must perform Umrah the following year.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Muammil narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara bin Umair, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid, he said:
m: While we were at Dhat Ash-Shuquq, a man from among us made the Talbiyah for Umrah, and he was bitten. Abdullah passed by us, so we asked him, and he said: Set a day as a guide between you and him, and he will send the price of the sacrificial animal, and when he is slaughtered, he will be released and he must perform Umrah.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Muhammad bin Ja’far narrated to us, he said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, he said:
m: I heard Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i narrating, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid, he said: A man from among us made the intention to perform Umrah, and he was bitten, and a group of people came out, among whom Surat Al-Baqarah 2:196 And complete the Hajj and Umrah for the sake of God.
h
But if you are prevented

, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animals reach their destination. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his scalp [must make up] a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. But when you are secure, then whoever enjoys [his ritual] From the Umrah to the Hajj, then whatever sacrifice can be obtained with ease. But whoever cannot find [one], then a fast of three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned. That is ten complete days. That is for him whose family are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear God and know that God is severe in penalty. was Abd God bin Mas’ud, so they asked him, and he said: He will send with the sacrificial animal, and set a day as a guide between you and him, and when that day comes, he will be released. And Amara bin Umair said: That was enough for you, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah - and he must perform Umrah next year.

c: Abu Al-Sa'ib told me, he said, Abu Mu'awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Amara, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid, he said:
m: We went out as a pilgrims, and when we were at Dhat Al-Shuquq, a friend of ours was bitten. We stopped on the road to ask what to do with him, and there was Abd God bin Mas'ud in a group, so we said to him: Has a friend of ours been bitten? He said: Make a day between you and your friend, and let him send with the sacrificial animal, and when he slaughters the sacrificial animal, let him become ihram, and then he must perform the minor pilgrimage.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Aswad told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Masoud:
m: That Amr bin Saeed Al-Nakha’i declared his intention to perform Umrah, and when he reached Dhat Ash-Shuqooq, he was bitten by it. So his companions went out to the road to look for people, and there they found Ibn Masoud, and they mentioned that to him. He said: Let him send a sacrificial animal, and set a day between you and him, and when he slaughters the sacrificial animal, let him be released from the state of ihram, and he must perform his Umrah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
But if you are prevented

, then whatever is easy of sacrificial animal, meaning: Whoever enters into ihram for Hajj or Umrah, then is prevented from entering the House due to an illness that exhausts him or an excuse that prevents him, then he must slaughter whatever is easy of sacrificial animal, a sheep or more to be slaughtered on his behalf. If it is the Hajj of Islam, then he must perform it, but if it is a Hajj after the obligatory Hajj or Umrah, then he does not have to perform it. Then he said: And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination. If he has entered ihram for Hajj, then its destination is the Day of Sacrifice. If he has entered ihram for Umrah, then the destination of his sacrificial animal is when he reaches the House.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if you are prevented

, then [offer] whatever sacrifice you can afford. This refers to a man from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was prevented from entering the House, so he would offer a sacrifice to the House and remain in his state of ihram until the sacrificial animal reached its destination. When the sacrificial animal reached its destination, he would shave his head, and God would complete his Hajj. Ihsar also means that he is prevented from Hajj, so he must offer a sacrifice: if he is able, of camels, otherwise of cattle, or of sheep. He should make his Hajj an Umrah and send his sacrifice to the House. When he slaughters the sacrificial animal, he is released from his state of ihram, and Hajj is required of him the following year.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Bishr bin Al-Sarri told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salamah, he said:
m: Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asked about the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
But if you are prevented
, then make an offering with ease, so if the pilgrim is prevented, he sends the offering, and when he slaughters it, he is released, and he is not released until he slaughters his offering.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said:
m: I heard Ata’ say: Whoever is prevented during his Umrah and sends an offering and intercepts it, he must give something in charity or fast. And whoever intercepts his offering while he is a pilgrim, the place for the offering and the state of ihram is the day of sacrifice, and there is nothing upon him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata,
m: similarly. The two hadiths of Musa, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, his statement:
h
But if you are prevented

, then [offer] an offering as is easy for you, and do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its destination, a man enters into ihram and then leaves and is prevented, either by being bitten or sick, so he is unable to travel, or his mount breaks, so he stays and sends an offering, a sheep or more. If he is healthy and travels and catches up, then he does not have to offer an offering. If he misses Hajj, then it becomes an ‘umrah, and he is required to perform Hajj the following year. If he returns, he remains in ihram until he slaughters on his behalf on the Day of Sacrifice. If he hears that his companion did not slaughter on his behalf, he returns to ihram and sends another offering, and meets his companion on the day of slaughtering on his behalf in Mecca, so they slaughter on his behalf in Mecca, and he is released from ihram, and he is required to perform Hajj and ‘umrah the following year.

x: Some people say: two ‘umrahs. If he entered ihram for Umrah, then returned and sent his sacrificial animal, then he must perform two Umrahs the following year.
Some people say: No, rather three Umrahs, and something similar to what they did during Hajj when they did it, he must perform Hajj and two Umrahs.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Qannad told us, he said: Ishaq Al-Azraq told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: If a man is prevented, he should send his sacrificial animal if he is unable to reach the House due to the enemy. If he finds someone to carry it on his behalf to Makkah, then he should send it in his place and meet with the owner of the sacrificial animal. When he is safe, then he must perform Hajj and Umrah. If he is afflicted with an illness that prevents him and he does not have a sacrificial animal with him, then he may exit the state of ihram wherever he is prevented. If he has a sacrificial animal with him, then he does not exit the state of ihram until the sacrificial animal reaches its place when he sent it, and he is not required to perform Hajj the following year, nor may he perform Umrah unless he wishes.

x: The reason for those who said this statement is that the place of gifts and sacrificial animals is the Sacred Sanctuary, because God Almighty mentioned the sacrificial animals and gifts and said: “And whoever honors the symbols of God - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts. Therein you have benefits for a specified term. Then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House” (al-Hajj 22:32-33). So He made their place the Sacred Sanctuary, and there is no place for the sacrificial animal below it. They said: As for what the arguments claim about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtering his gifts at Al-Hudaybiyyah when he was prevented from the House, it is not… This is according to the consensus statement. That is because: Al-Fadl bin Sahl told me, he said, Makhul bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Mujaz’ah bin Zahir Al-Aslami, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Najiyah bin Jundub Al-Aslami, he said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was prevented from offering the sacrificial animal, and I said: O Messenger of God, send with me the sacrificial animal so that we may slaughter it in the Sacred Sanctuary!

He said: How will you do with it? I said: I will take it to valleys so that they will not be able to reach it! So I set off with it until I slaughtered it in the Sacred Sanctuary. They said: This report has shown that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered his sacrificial animal in the Sacred Sanctuary, so there is no argument for someone who claims to slaughter it at Al-Hudaybiyyah outside the Sacred Sanctuary.

Others said: The meaning of this verse and its interpretation are not according to these two aspects that we have described, from the statement of the two groups that we have mentioned, their disagreement on what we have mentioned. They said: The meaning of this is: If you, O believers, are prevented from your Hajj - and you are prevented from continuing to perform the ihram due to an obstacle such as illness or fear of an enemy - and performing what is required of you and your Hajj, until you miss the standing. In Arafat, then you must make up for what you missed of your Hajj, along with making up for the Hajj that you missed. The people of this opinion said: The one who is prevented from Hajj - due to illness, ailments, etc. - is not released from his ihram except by circumambulating the House and walking between Safa and Marwa, if he misses Hajj. They said: As for if he is able to witness the scenes, then he is not prevented.

They said: As for Umrah, there is no confinement in it, because its time is always present. They said: The one performing Umrah is not released from his ihram except by doing another act that is required of him in his ihram. They said: The one performing Umrah is not included in this verse, but rather it refers to the pilgrim. Then the people of this opinion differed.

Some of them said: There is no confinement today by an enemy, just as there is no confinement due to illness. It is permissible for the one who missed it to release himself from his ihram before circumambulating the House and walking between Safa and Marwa.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Tawus, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: There is no confinement today.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said,
m: Abd Al-Wahhab said, I heard Yahya bin Saeed say: Abd al-Rahman bin al-Qasim told me: Aisha said: I do not know of a person in ihram who is permitted to do anything less than the House.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: There is no confinement except for one who is prevented by an enemy, so he is permitted to do Umrah, and he is not required to do Hajj or Umrah.

x: Others among them said: The siege of the enemy is established today and after today, in the manner we mentioned from their three statements that we narrated from them.
He mentioned those who said that, and said the meaning of the verse:
h
But if you are prevented
from Hajj until it passes you by, then you must make an offering as easy as possible for it has passed you by:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim, he said:
m: Abdullah bin Umar used to disapprove of the condition in Hajj, and he used to say: Is not the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sufficient for you? If one of you is prevented from Hajj, he should circumambulate the House and Safa and Marwah, then he is permitted to do everything until he performs Hajj the following year, and he offers an offering. Or fast, if he does not find a sacrificial animal.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abd al-Wahhab told us, he said, Ubaydullah ibn Umar told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: The one who is prevented from doing anything does not become free from it until he reaches the House, and he remains in his state of ihram as it is, unless he is injured or wounded, in which case he is treated with what will fix it and he is to pay the ransom. When he reaches the House, if it was an ‘umrah, he completes it, and if it was a Hajj, he cancels it with an ‘umrah, and he is required to perform Hajj the following year and offer a sacrificial animal. If he does not find any, then he is to fast for three days during Hajj and seven when he returns.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Yahya ibn Sa’id told us, on the authority of Ubaydullah, he said, Nafi’ told me:
m: Ibn Umar passed by Ibn Hazaba while he was in al-Saqiya, and he saw a fracture in him, so he asked him for a fatwa, and he ordered him to remain as he was, not to become free Surat Al-Baqarah 2:196 And complete the Hajj and Umrah for the sake of God.
h
But if you are prevented

, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animals reach their destination. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his scalp [must make up] a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. But when you are secure, then whoever enjoys [his ritual] From the Umrah to the Hajj, then whatever sacrifice can be obtained with ease. But whoever cannot find [one], then a fast of three days during the Hajj and seven when you have returned. That is ten complete days. That is for him whose family are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear God and know that God is severe in penalty. from anything until he reaches the House, unless he is injured, in which case he is treated, and he is required to offer whatever sacrificial animal he can. And he was in ihram for Hajj.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said,
m: Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, said: Salim bin Abdullah informed me: Abdullah bin Omar said: Whoever is prevented after he has entered into ihram for Hajj, and is prevented by fear or illness or is unable to carry a back 1 or something of all kinds, then he should treat his prevention with everything he needs, except that he is not permitted to have sexual intercourse or perfume, and he should redeem himself with the ransom that God has commanded: fasting or charity or sacrifice. If he misses Hajj while he is prevented from that, or he misses standing in the stations of Arafat before dawn on the night of Muzdalifah, then he has missed Hajj, and his Hajj becomes an Umrah: he should go to Mecca and perform Tawaf around the House and Safa and Marwa, and if he has an offering with him, he should slaughter it in Mecca near the Sacred Mosque, then shave his head or shorten it, then he should be free from women and perfume and other things, then he should perform Hajj the following year and offer whatever offering he can of the offering.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Malik bin Anas told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that he said:
m: The one who is prevented from performing Hajj is not released until he has circumambulated the House and between Safa and Marwa. If he is forced to wear clothes that he does not need, or to take medicine, he should do so and pay the ransom. This is what was narrated from Ibn Umar regarding being prevented by illness and the like. As for the one who is prevented by the enemy, he used to say something similar to what we mentioned before on the authority of Malik ibn Anas that he used to say.

c: Tamim ibn al-Muntasir told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, he said, Ubaydullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’:
m: Ibn Umar wanted to perform Hajj when al-Hajjaj stayed with Ibn al-Zubayr, so his two sons Salim and Ubaydullah spoke to him and said: It will not harm you if you do not perform Hajj this year, for we fear that there will be fighting between the people and you will be prevented from the House! He said: If I am prevented from the House, I will do as we did with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the infidels of Quraysh prevented him from the House, so he shaved his head and returned. As for what they mentioned regarding Umrah, their saying: There is no prevention or confinement in it, it is: - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told me, on the authority of Abu Bashar, on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah bin Al-Shakheer: That he entered into the state of Umrah but was prevented. He said: So he wrote to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Omar, and they wrote to him: Send the sacrificial animal, then stay until he is released from his Umrah. He said: So he stayed for six or seven months.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ala bin Al-Shakheer, he said:
m: I went out to perform Umrah, and I fell from my camel, and broke my leg, so we sent to Ibn Abbas and Ibn Omar to ask them, and they said: Umrah does not have a time like the time of Hajj, you are not released until you circumambulate the House. He said: So I stayed in Ad-Dathina or near it for seven or eight months.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Malik told me, on the authority of Ayoub bin Abi Tamima Al-Sakhtiyani, on the authority of a man from the people of Basra
m: who was old, that he said: I went out to Mecca, and when I was on some of the way, I broke my thigh, so I sent to Mecca to Abdullah bin Abbas, and Abdullah bin Abbas and Abdullah bin Omar and the people were there, and no one gave me permission to release myself. So I remained in that state for seven months, until I was released for Umrah.
b.via: a man from the people of Basra

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: Concerning a man who was injured while performing Umrah, he said: He should remain in his state of ihram until he comes to the House and performs Tawaf around it and between Safa and Marwah, and shaves or shortens his hair, and there is nothing upon him.

x: The most correct of these statements in interpreting this verse is the statement of the one who said: God, the Almighty, meant by His statement:
h
But if you are prevented

, then make such offering as is easy for you, and do not shave your heads until the offering reaches its destination, every person who is prevented in ihram, whether for Umrah or for Hajj. He made the place of his offering the place where he was prevented, and he made the release from his ihram for him by his offering reaching its place - and he interpreted the place of sacrifice or slaughtering, and that is when he is released from his slaughter or slaughtering, whether in the sanctuary or outside, and he is obligated to make up for what he was released from of his ihram before completing it if he finds a way to it. This is due to the frequency of the reports “from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was prevented from the House in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah while he and his companions were in a state of ihram for Umrah, so he and his companions slaughtered the sacrificial animals by his command, and they were released from their ihram before reaching the House, then they completed the ihram from which they were released in the following year.”

And none of the scholars of the biography or others claimed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or any of his companions remained in their ihram waiting to reach the House, and to be released by circumambulating it and running between Safa and Marwah, nor did they delay the arrival of his sacrificial animals to the Haram. So the most deserving of action to be followed is the action of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, since no report came prohibiting it, and no proof was established for its prevention. So since that was the case, and the scholars differed in what we chose from the statement in that, then whoever interpreted the meaning of the verse interpreted it as we did, and whoever contradicted that, then it was proven by what we said about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the transmission, the one that was transmitted from him was the most deserving of the interpretation of the verse, since the scholars did not dispute that this verse was on that day.
It was revealed, and regarding the ruling of the polytheists preventing him from entering the House, it was revealed.
A report similar to what we have said about that was narrated:

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Abi Uthman told me, he said, Yahya bin Abi Katheer told me:
m: Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas told him, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Amr Al-Ansari told me: He heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever breaks or limps has been released, and he has to perform another Hajj. He said: So I told Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurairah about that, and they said: He is truthful.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Marwan told us, he said, Hajjaj Al-Sawaaf told us
m: - and Hamid bin Mas’adah told us, he said, Sufyan bin Habib told us, on the authority of Hajjaj Al-Sawaaf - on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly, and on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurairah. The meaning of this report is the command to complete the Hajj from which one has been released, similar to the action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions in completing their Umrah from which they were released in the year Al-Hudaybiyyah the next year, in the year of the Umrah of the issue. It is said to the one who claims that the one who is besieged by an enemy, if he is released from his voluntary ihram, does not have to make up for it, and that the one who is besieged by an illness must make up for it: What is the reason that obligated one of them to make up for it, and dropped it from the other, and both of them have been released from the ihram that he was required to complete, were it not for the impeding illness?

x: Because the verse was only revealed regarding the one who was besieged by the enemy, it is not permissible for us to transfer its ruling to something other than what it was revealed regarding.

A group of scholars have defended you on that, but we accept what you said about it. Why is the ruling on prevention due to illness and besiegement not the ruling on prevention due to the enemy, since they agree in being prevented from reaching the House and completing the work of their ihram, even if the reasons for their prevention differ, so one of them is prevented due to an illness in his body, and the other is prevented by an obstacle? Then he is asked about the difference between that from a principle or analogy, so he will not say anything about one of them except that he obligates the same thing about the other.

As for those who said: There is no besiegement in the Umrah, it is said to them: You know that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only He was prevented from the House while he was in a state of ihram for Umrah, so he was released from his state of ihram. What is your proof that he was not prevented from performing it? Or have you seen that if someone said: There is no prevention in Hajj, but it is a loss, and the one who missed Hajj must perform it in his state of ihram until he circumambulates the House and walks between Safa and Marwah, because it was not authentically reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he established a Sunnah for prevention in Hajj?

A group of the imams of religion have said that. As for Umrah, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, established what he established in it, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed in its ruling what was between the release and the completion of what he did, may God bless him and grant him peace. In it there is prevention without Hajj. Is there a difference between it and it? Then he reverses the statement in that, so he will not say anything about one of them except that he obliges the same in the other.
By that, may God be glorified, He means:
h
If you are prevented

, then what is easy of the sacrificial animal, and do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its destination, unless one of you is forced to shave it, either due to illness, or because of harm to his head from vermin or something else, in which case he should shave there due to necessity. The one who has been afflicted with it, and if the sacrificial animal has not reached its destination, then he must shave his head and he must do so, and pay a ransom of fasting, charity, or ritual sacrifice. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said:
m: I said to Ata’: Is there harm on his head? He said: Lice and other things, headaches, and whatever is on his head.

x: Others said: He should not shave if he wants to redeem the Hajj by performing the ritual sacrifice or feeding the poor, except after expiation. And if he wants to redeem by fasting, he should shave and then fast.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ubaydullah bin Muadh told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: If the pilgrim has harm on his head, he should shave when he sends the sheep, or feeds the poor, and if he is fasting, he should shave and then fast after that.

x: Who said that?

evidence.text: Al-Sha'bi used to recite it with a raised voice.
The reading of the one who said: Umrah is obligatory - is in the accusative case, meaning: Perform the obligation of Hajj and Umrah, as:
He said: Then he recited this verse: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God (Al-ʿImran 3:97), And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God.

Others who read the reading of these people with the accusative of Umrah said: Umrah is voluntary, and they saw that there is no indication of its obligation in their placing Umrah in the accusative in the reading, since there are actions that a servant may be required to do and complete by entering into it, and the beginning of entering into it was not obligatory upon him.
Abu Ja’far said: As for those who read it with Umrah in the nominative case, they said: There is no reason for its accusative case.

If it does not have an understandable meaning, then the correct reading of Umrah is to raise it, as it is one of the righteous deeds for God, so it is raised by its predicate that comes after it, which is His saying: for God.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the two readings in this regard, according to us, is the reading of the one who reads Umrah in the accusative case.
This, with the consensus of the argument on reading Umrah in the accusative, and the contradiction of all the readings of the regions with the reading of those who read it in the nominative.
In that, there is no need to cite evidence for the error of those who read it in the nominative.

As for the first of the two opinions that we mentioned as correct in interpreting his statement: And Umrah is for God, according to the reading of those who read This is an installation, so the statement of Abdullah bin Masoud and those who said the same, that the meaning of this is: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God to the House, after He has made them obligatory for you, is not that this is a command from God the Almighty - to begin their work and enter into them, and perform their work in its entirety - with this verse.

And based on the evidence we have cited, the more correct of the two readings in Umrah is the reading of the one who reads it in the accusative case - and that the more correct of the two interpretations in His statement: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God, is the interpretation of Ibn Abbas that we mentioned from him on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah from him: that he was commanded by God to complete their actions after entering them, and making them obligatory, according to what he commanded of their limits and Sunnahs - and that the more correct of the two sayings in Umrah is the saying of the one who said: It is voluntary, not obligatory - and that the meaning of the verse is: And complete, O believers, the Hajj and Umrah for God after you have entered them and made them obligatory for yourselves, according to what God has commanded you of their limits.

And with the softening of the ya’ and the sukoon of the dal in al-Hadi, it was recited by the reciters in every country, except what was mentioned on the authority of al-Aʿraj, for Abu Hisham Al-Rifai told us, he said, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Bashar, on the authority of Asad, on the authority of Al-Araj, that he read: A gift that reaches the Kaaba (al-Ma’idah 5:95) with a heavy kasra on the dal, and he read: Until the gift reaches its place, with a heavy kasra on the dal.
And there is a difference of opinion regarding that from Asim, so my difference from him is in agreement with Al-Araj, and his disagreement with the reading of the rest of the readings.

x: God Almighty means by that: The time of Hajj is the well-known months. The months are raised by Hajj, even if it has a time, not a description or an attribute, since they were not limited by a definition, by adding to a definite or familiar thing, so the raising in them became like the raising in the saying of the Arabs in a similar place: The Muslims are on one side, and the infidels are on the other side, by raising the side that was not limited to a known limit. If it was said: The side of their land, or their country, then the accusative would be the statement. Then the people of interpretation differed in his saying: Hajj is well-known months.
Some of them said: He means the well-known months, Shawwal and Dhul-Qadah, and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: his saying: Hajj is well-known months, he said: Shawwal, Dhul-Qadah, and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan and Sharik told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Ibrahim bin Ismail bin Nasr Al-Salami narrated to us, he said, Ibrahim bin Ismail bin Abi Habeeba narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud bin Husayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said:
m: The months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Abu Salih narrated to us, he said, Mu'awiyah narrated to me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Hajj is in well-known months

, and they are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. God, the Exalted, made them for Hajj, and the rest of the months for Umrah. So it is not appropriate for anyone to enter ihram for Hajj except in the months of Hajj, and Umrah is entered into ihram in every month.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Al-Hammani narrated to us, he said, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Hajj is in well-known months
, he said: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman and Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us
m: - and al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us - saying: Ath-Thawri narrated to us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, similarly?
Ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu Uwana narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and al-Sha’bi similarly.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan and Isra’il narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isra’il narrated to us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amir,
m: similarly.

c: Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - and Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi - and Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan - and Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak - and Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’ and Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Al-Walid told us, he said: Hammad told us, on the authority of Ubaydullah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah and the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah in The Hajj are well-known months.

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim told me, he said: Abu Nu’aym told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: The Hajj is well-known months, he said: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah and the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim narrated to us, Abu Naim narrated to us, Hussain bin Aqil narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: Shawwal, Dhul-Qi'dah, and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Hussain bin Aqil Al-Khurasani narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim say: Then he mentioned something similar.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant Shawwal, Dhul-Qi'dah, and all of Dhul-Hijjah.
Mention of those who said that.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Yahya bin Saeed narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said:
m: I said to Nafi': Did Abdullah name the months of Hajj? He said: Yes, Shawwal, Dhul-Qi'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Bakr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said:
m: I said to Nafi': Did you hear Ibn Umar name the months of Hajj? He said: Yes, he used to name Shawwal, Dhul-Qi'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Ata' said:
m: h
The Hajj is in well-known months
, Ata' said: They are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah. I narrated to me from Ammar, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Hajj is in well-known months
, the months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah, and sometimes he said: and the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Hajj is in well-known months
, he said: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said:
m: The months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah, and Dhul-Hijjah.

x: If someone were to say to us: What is the reason for those who say this statement, and you know that the Hajj rituals are not performed after the days of Mina are over? It would be said: The meaning of that is not what you imagined, but rather what they meant by their statement: Hajj is three complete months, that they are the months of Hajj, not the months of Umrah, and that the months of Umrah are other months of the year.
