And what indicates that this is what they meant in their statement is what: - Ya'qub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi', he said, Ibn Umar said: That you separate the months of Hajj and Umrah, and perform Umrah in months other than the months of Hajj, completes the Hajj of one of you and completes his Umrah.

c: Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami told me, he said, my father told me, he said, Shu'bah told us, he said:
m: I did not meet Ayyub - or he said: I did not meet Ayyub - except that he asked me about the hadith of Qays bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, who said: I said to Abdullah: A woman among us has performed Hajj, or she wants to perform Hajj, should she perform Umrah with her Hajj? He said: I do not see these except during the months of Hajj. He said: Then Ayyub, and whoever has something like this hadith, says to me: Qays bin Muslim told you, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, that he asked Abdullah?!

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said:
m: I heard Al-Qasim bin Muhammad say: Umrah during the months of Hajj is not complete. He said: So it was said to him: Umrah in Muharram? He said: They used to consider it complete. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan narrated, he said: Ishaq bin Yusuf narrated, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said: I asked Al-Qasim bin Muhammad about Umrah during the months of Hajj. He said: They did not consider it complete. Ibn Bayan Al-Wasiti narrated, he said: Ishaq narrated, on the authority of Abdullah bin Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin: He used to prefer Umrah during the month of Muharram. He said: Should it be during the months of Hajj? He said: They did not consider it complete. Ibn Bayan narrated, he said: Ishaq narrated, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, he said: Ibn Umar said to Al-Hakam bin Al-Araj or someone else: If you obey me, I will wait until the people of Muharram come out to Dhat Irq and assume Ihram for Umrah from there. Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated, Wahb bin Jarir narrated, Shu'bah narrated, on the authority of Abu Ya'qub, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: For me to perform Umrah in the first ten days of Dhul-Hijjah is more beloved to me than to perform Umrah in the twentieth. Ibn Bashar narrated, Abdur-Rahman narrated, Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, who said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud about a woman among us who wanted to combine Umrah with her Hajj, so he said: Asham God says:
h
The Hajj is in well-known months

, I do not think they are anything other than the months of Hajj. Ahmad bin Al-Miqdam narrated, who said: Hizam Al-Qat'i narrated, who said: I heard Muhammad bin Sirin say: No one among the people of knowledge doubts that Umrah in months other than the months of Hajj is better than Umrah in the months of Hajj. And similar examples of this, which would take too long to mention in this book, indicate that the meaning of what was said by those who said: The time of Hajj is three complete months, is that they are not the months of Umrah, and that they are months for performing Hajj but not for performing Umrah, even though the ritual of Hajj is performed in some of them and not in all of them. As for those who said: The interpretation of that is: Shawwal, Dhul-Qa'dah and the Surat al-Baqarah 2:197 Hajj is [during] well-known months, so whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein - there is no sexual relations nor wickedness nor disputing during Hajj. And whatever you do of good - God knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. And fear Me, O you of understanding. ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, they said: God, the Most High, intended by His saying:
h
The Hajj is in well-known months to inform His creation of the time for their Hajj

, not to inform them about the time for Umrah. They said: As for Umrah, the whole year has a time for it, due to the convergence of reports "from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he performed Umrah in some of the months of Hajj, then there is no authentic report from him to the contrary." They said: Since that is the case, and the time for the Hajj rituals ends with the passing of the tenth of Dhul-Hijjah, it is known that the meaning of His saying:
h
The Hajj is in well-known months is the time for Hajj
, two months and some of the third.

x: The correct statement regarding that, according to us, is the statement of those who said: The meaning of that is: The Hajj is two months and ten days of the third. Because that from God is information about the time for Hajj, and no Hajj rituals are performed after the passing of the days of Mina. So it is known that He did not mean by that the entire third month. And if He did not mean by that all, then the statement of those who said: and the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah is correct.
How is it said:
h
The Hajj is in well-known months
, which are two months and some of a third?

The Arabs do not refrain from using such a thing, especially at times, so they say: Today he has two days since I have not seen him, but they mean by that: a day and some of another, and as God, the Most High, said: But whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him (al-Baqarah 2:203), but he hastens in a day and a half. And the doer among them may do the action in an hour, then he extends it year by year and month, so he says: I visited him this year, and I came to him today, and he does not mean by that that his action was taken from the beginning of the time he mentioned to the end, but he means that he did it then, and at that time. Likewise,
h
The Hajj is in well-known months

, and what is meant by it is: The Hajj is two months and some of another. So the meaning of the verse is: The time of your Hajj, O people, is two months and some of a third, which are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah, and the tenth of Dhul-Hijjah.
What God, the Most High, meant by His statement:
h
And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein

, is whoever makes Hajj obligatory upon himself and obliges himself to do it in them - meaning: in the well-known months that He mentioned. And his imposing it upon himself is the determination to do everything that God has made obligatory for the pilgrim to do, and to leave everything that God has commanded him to leave.
The people of interpretation have differed regarding the meaning by which a man is obligated to perform Hajj, after all of them agreed that the meaning of imposition is: obligation and compulsion.
Some of them said: The imposition of Hajj is the declaration of ihram.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah al-Madani ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: his saying:
h
And whoever has made Hajj obligatory therein
he said: whoever is in the state of ihram for Hajj.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, and Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: Talbiyah.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told us, he said, Zaid told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri: And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them, he said: The obligation is Ihram, and Ihram is Talbiyah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Ibrahim - meaning Ibn Muhajir - on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them, he said: The obligation is Talbiyah.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them, he said: Those who are in Ihram.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Na’im told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The obligation is Talbiyah, and he may return if he wishes as long as he has not entered Ihram.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So whoever has made Hajj obligatory therein, he said: The obligation is the declaration of ihram.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: So whoever has made Hajj obligatory therein, he said: The talbiyah.

c: Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Muslim narrated to us, he said: Abu Umar al-Dharir narrated to us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Jabr bin Habib, he said:
m: I asked al-Qasim bin Muhammad about: So whoever has made Hajj obligatory therein, he said: If you bathe, put on your garment, and declare the talbiyah, then you have made Hajj obligatory.

x: Others said: The obligation of Hajj is its ihram.
Those who said that: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said:

c: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Muawiyah narrated to me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Whoever performs Hajj therein, meaning: whoever enters into ihram for Hajj or Umrah.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, and Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, and al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Naim told us, they all said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
So whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them
, he said: So whoever enters into ihram - and the wording is from the hadith of Ibn Bashar.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sharik and al-Hasan ibn Salih told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: The obligation is ihram.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’ and some of our sheikhs, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement:
h
So whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them
, they said: The obligation of Hajj is ihram.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah:
m: h
So whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them
, this is when entering ihram.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Hussain bin Aqil told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The obligation is Ihram.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abdul-Razzaq told us, Hussain bin Aqil Al-Khurasani told us,
m: I heard Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abdul-Razzaq told us, Al-Thawri told us, Al-Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them, he said: Whoever enters Ihram.

x: This second statement may have the meaning of what we have said, that the one who said it, ihram, was the obligation by determination, and it may have been by determination and talbiyah, as those who said the first statement said. We only said that the obligation of Hajj is ihram, because of the consensus of all on that. And we said that ihram is the man’s obligation of what the muhrim must oblige himself to do, as we described earlier, because the statement on that is not without one of three matters: Either the man is not in ihram except by talbiyah, and doing everything that the one who obligates ihram must do himself, and if that is the case, then it is necessary that he is not in ihram except by stripping off for ihram, and that the one who does not strip off for it is not in ihram. And in the consensus of all that he may be in ihram because he is not stripped of his clothes, by his obligation of ihram, there is what indicates that he may be in ihram even if he does not talbiyah, since talbiyah is part of the rituals of ihram, just as stripping off for him is part of its rituals.

And in their consensus that he may be in a state of ihram by leaving some of the rituals of his Hajj, there is evidence that the ruling on other rituals of his Hajj is the same as his ruling. Or - if this statement is invalid - he may be in a state of ihram even if he does not put on the talbiyah, or strip off, or make the determination that we have described. And in the consensus of all that he is not in a state of ihram who does not make the determination to enter ihram and impose it upon himself, if he is one of those who are accountable, there is evidence of the invalidity of this statement. And since these two views are invalid, then the third view is clear: that a man may be in a state of ihram by making ihram obligatory by his determination, in the manner we have explained, even if he does not show that by stripping off, saying the talbiyah, or doing some of the rituals that he is required to do.
And if that is correct, then what we have said is correct, that the obligation of Hajj is what is linked to its obligation with determination, in the manner we have explained before.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of obscenity in this place.
Some of them said: It is obscene speech to a woman, such as saying: If we become permissible, I will do such and such to you, without using euphemisms for it, and the like.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ahmad ibn Hammad al-Dulabi and Yunus told us, they said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of His father
m: said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the word rafth in the statement of God: No obscenity nor wickedness. He said: It is the insinuation of sexual intercourse, which is the araba of the speech of the Arabs, and it is the lowest form of rafth.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ruh ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of Ibn Tawus,
m: regarding His statement: No obscenity, he said: Rafth is araba and insinuating sexual intercourse with women.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awn, he said: Ziyad ibn Husayn told us, he said: My father Husayn ibn Qays told me:
m: I went up with Ibn Abbas during the Hajj and I was his close friend. When it was after I had entered ihram, Ibn Abbas said: I took hold of the tail of his camel, and he began to twist it while he was chanting and saying: They walk with us whispering, if the bird is truthful, we will be with you, Lamisa. He said: I said: Do you engage in obscenity while you are in a state of ihram? He said: Obscenity is what is said in front of women.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu al-ʿAliyah al-Riyahi, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: That he used to exhort while he was in a state of ihram and say: They walk with us whispering, if the bird is truthful, we will be with you, Lamisa. He said: I said: Do you speak obscenely while you are in a state of ihram?! He said: Obscenely is what is said in front of women.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yunus told me: Nafi’ told him that
m: Abdullah ibn Umar used to say: Obscenely is coming to women, and speaking about that for men and women, if they mention it with their mouths.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said,
m: I said to Ata’: Is it permissible for a man in ihram to say to his wife: When I become unmarried, I will have intercourse with you? He said: No! That is obscenity. He said: Ata’ said: Obscenity is less than sexual intercourse.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr told me, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Ata’ said:
m: Obscenity is sexual intercourse and less than that of obscene speech.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I said to Ata’: A man saying to his wife: When I become unmarried, I will have intercourse with you, he said: That is obscenity!

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Husayn, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, he said:
m: I was walking with Ibn Abbas while he was in ihram, and he was reciting a rajaz and saying: They walk with us whispering, if the bird is truthful, we will be with you, Lamisa. He said: I said: Do you engage in obscenity, O Ibn Surat al-Baqarah 2:197 Hajj is [during] well-known months, so whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein - there is no sexual relations nor wickedness nor disputing during Hajj. And whatever you do of good - God knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. And fear Me, O you of understanding. Abbas, while you are in a state of ihram? He said: Obscenity is that in which you address women.

c: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, he said: Sufyan and Yahya ibn Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Az-Zubayr As-Saba’i and Ata’ narrated to us that
m: he heard Tawus say: I heard Ibn Az-Zubayr say: It is not permissible for a person in a state of ihram to engage in ihram. So I mentioned it to Ibn Abbas and he said: He is right! I said to Ibn Abbas: What is ihram? He said: Insinuation.

c: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, he said: Yahya narrated to us, he said: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said: Al-Hasan ibn Muslim narrated to me, on the authority of Tawus
m: that he used to say: It is not permissible for a person in a state of ihram to engage in ihram. Tawus said: Obscenity is saying while in a state of ihram: When you are released from ihram, I will have intercourse with you.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, he said: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Fitr narrated to us, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Husayn, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, he said:
m: There is no obscenity except that in which you address women.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abdurrahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Marthad, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: They disliked i’rabah - meaning: alluding to sexual intercourse - and it is forbidden.

c: Amr ibn Ali told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Tawus:
m: that he heard his father say: i’rabah is not permissible. I’rabah means alluding.

c: Amr ibn Ali told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God, the Most High: So no obscenity. He said: The obscenity mentioned here is not the obscenity mentioned in Lawful to you on the night of the fast is approaching your wives
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:187)
. And from obscenity is alluding to sexual intercourse, which is i’rabah in the speech of the Arabs.

c: Amr ibn Ali told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’:
m: that he disliked i’rabah for the one in ihram.

c: Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Tawus told me that
m: his father used to say: Rafath is the expression of what is hidden from women, and rafath is the clarification of sexual intercourse.

c: Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Al-Hasan bin Muslim told us that
m: he heard Tawus say: It is not permissible for a pilgrim to engage in sexual intercourse.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me,
m: who said, Abu Salih told us, who said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: No obscenity. He said: Obscenity is having intercourse with women, kissing, winking, and exposing her to obscene speech, and the like.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us,
m: who said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, who said, Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ibn Umar used to say to the guide: Do not expose yourself to mentioning women.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar and Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Rafath in fasting is sexual intercourse, and Rafath in Hajj is intercourse. He used to say: Entering and touching is sexual intercourse.

x: Others said: Rafath in this case is sexual intercourse itself.
Those who said that: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, he said: Rafath is sexual intercourse.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Abdul-Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Rafath is intercourse with women.

c: Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about obscenity, and he said: Intercourse.

c: Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Bakr bin Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: said: Al-Rafth is sexual intercourse, but God is generous and uses euphemisms for whatever He wills.

c: Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ziyad bin Husayn, on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, he said:

x: The correct statement in my opinion regarding that is that God, the Most High, forbade - whoever makes Hajj obligatory in The months of Hajj - about obscenity, so he said:
h
And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein

, there is no obscenity. Obscenity in the speech of the Arabs originally means: obscenity in speech, as we have explained previously, then it is used as a metaphor for sexual intercourse. So since that is the case, and the people of knowledge differed in its interpretation, and in this prohibition from God: about some of the meanings of obscenity or all of its meanings? - it must be on all of its meanings, since no report came, specifically obscenity, which is in speech among women, from the rest of the meanings of obscenity, and it must be accepted. Since it is not permissible to transfer the apparent ruling of a verse to an inner interpretation, except with a solid proof.

Its ruling, from the generality of its apparent meaning to its hidden interpretation, is transmitted by consensus. That is because there is no disagreement among all of them that obscenity in the presence of other than women is not prohibited for a person in ihram, so it was known from this that the verse refers to some obscenities and not others. Since that is the case, it is necessary that nothing from the meanings of obscenity be prohibited for a person in ihram, except what is unanimously agreed upon as prohibited for him, or an argument for its prohibition is established that must be accepted.

That which is specified in the verse and is permitted is Surat al-Baqarah 2:197 Hajj is [during] well-known months, so whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein - there is no sexual relations nor wickedness nor disputing during Hajj. And whatever you do of good - God knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. And fear Me, O you of understanding. excluded from the prohibition, and the prohibition is established for all that the argument did not specify from the meaning of obscenity in the verse, like what its ruling would have been if nothing was specified from it, because what was specified from that and excluded from its generality, we were only required to exclude its ruling from the prohibition by the command of the One whose command it is not permissible to contradict, so the ruling of what the meaning of the verse included - after what was specified from it - was the ruling that the servants were obliged to impose by it, if nothing was specified from it, because the reason for what was not specified from it after what was specified from it is similar to the reason for it before something was specified from it.

x: The most correct of the opinions that we have mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse in this regard is the opinion of those who said: The meaning of His statement, nor disobedience, is the prohibition of disobeying God by hunting game, and doing what God has prohibited the pilgrim from doing while in a state of ihram. This is because God, the Most High, said:
h
And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein

, there is no sexual relations nor disobedience, meaning by that: he should not engage in sexual relations nor commit disobedience, meaning he should not do what God has prohibited him from doing while in a state of ihram, and he should not disobey God while in a state of ihram. We have learned that God, the Most High, has prohibited His disobedience to everyone, whether he is in a state of ihram or not. He has also prohibited insulting one another by nicknames while in a state of ihram or otherwise, by His statement: And do not insult one another, nor call one another by nicknames (al-Hujurat 49:11).

It is prohibited for a Muslim to insult his brother in any state, whether Hajj is obligatory or not. If this is the case, then there is no doubt that what God has forbidden the servant from doing in terms of immorality while in a state of ihram and the obligation of Hajj, is what was not immorality while in a state of ihram and before his ihram for Hajj, just as the obscene talk that He has forbidden him from doing while in a state of ihram is what he had absolutely before his ihram. Because there is no meaning in saying about what God has forbidden to His creation in all states: None of you should do while in a state of ihram what is forbidden for him to do in all states. Because there is no basis for it being specific to the state of ihram, and it has been generalized to all states of ihram and ihram. If this is the case, then it is known that what the pilgrim is forbidden from of immorality, and it is specifically for him during his ihram, and it is said to him: If Hajj is made obligatory, do not do it, is what he had absolutely before the time of Hajj being made obligatory.

This is what we have described and mentioned, that God, the Most High, has specifically prohibited the pilgrim during his ihram from what He has prohibited him from: perfume, clothing, shaving, cutting nails, killing game, and everything else that God has specifically prohibited the pilgrim during his ihram. So the interpretation of the verse is: whoever has made Hajj obligatory during the months of Hajj and enters ihram during them, then he should not engage in sexual relations with women, nor should he have intercourse with them, nor should he commit immorality by doing what God has prohibited him from doing during his ihram for Hajj: killing game, cutting hair, cutting nails, and other things that God has prohibited him from doing while he is in ihram.
The people of interpretation differed regarding this.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is: The prohibition of the pilgrim arguing with anyone. Then the proponents of this statement differed.
Some of them said: It is forbidden to argue with one's companion until it angers him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Minhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, he said:
m: Argumentation is that some of them argue with each other until they become angry.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Bishr, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: And there is no argument, argumentation is anger, that you become angry with a Muslim, except that you rebuke a slave and admonish him without angering him, and there is no sin on you, God willing, in that.

c: Ibn Wakeeʿ told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Argumentation is that you argue with your companion until he angers you or you anger him.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri and Qatadah, they said:
m: Argumentation is clamor and contention while you are in a state of ihram.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Bakr told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, Ata’ said:
m: Argumentation is that which angers your companion, from argumentation.

c: Ali told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And there is no arguing during Hajj, he said: Argumentation is contention and contention until you anger your brother and companion, so God forbade that.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Argumentation is that you argue with your companion until you anger him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Argumentation is disputation.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri and Qatadah, they said:
m: It is noise and disputation while you are in a state of ihram.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And there is no disputation during Hajj, they disliked disputation.

x: Others among them said: Disputation in this case means: cursing.
Those who said that are mentioned:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me: Nafi’ told him that
m: Abdullah ibn Umar used to say: Argumentation during Hajj means cursing, disputing, and quarrels.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: Argumentation means cursing and disputing.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Argumentation means cursing.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us
m: - and Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us - all of them on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatadah, he said: Argumentation means cursing.

x: Others among them said: Rather, he meant by that specifically argumentation and disputation, and he only meant the difference of opinion about who has completed the Hajj more than the pilgrims.

Those who said that: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, he said: Disputation, when the Quraysh gathered in Mina, these would say: Our Hajj is more complete than your Hajj! And those would say: Our Hajj is more complete than your Hajj!
Others among them said: Rather, it was a difference that would occur between them on the day on which the Hajj was, so they were forbidden from that.

Those who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Jabr ibn Habib, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, that he said: Disputation in the Hajj is when some of them say: The Hajj is today! And some of them say: The Hajj is tomorrow!
Others said: Rather, their disagreement was about the Hajj stations, which of them was correct, the station of Abraham.
Those who said that: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement:
h
And there is no disputing during the Hajj

, he said: They used to stand at different stations disputing, each of them claiming that his station was the station of Abraham, but God cut him off when He informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of their rituals.
Others said: Rather, His statement, may He be glorified:
h
And there is no disputing during the Hajj
, is report from God Almighty about the correctness of the Hajj time at one Miqat, neither before nor after it, and about the length of the action of the Nasi’.
Those who said that: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement:
h
And there is no disputing during the Hajj
, he said: The Hajj has been corrected and there is no disputing in it.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.
m: h
And there is no disputing during the Hajj

, he said: No month can be postponed, and no doubt about the Hajj, it has been made clear. They would omit Muharram and then say: Safaran for Safar and the month of Rabi’ al-Awwal, then they would say: the two months of Rabi’ for the month of Rabi’ al-Akhir and Jumada al-Ula, then they would say: Jumadayan for Jumada al-Akhira and for Rajab, then they would say for Sha’ban: Rajab, then they would say for Ramadan: Sha’ban, then they would say for Shawwal: Ramadan, and they would say for Dhul-Qa’dah: Shawwal, then they would say for Dhul-Hijjah: Dhul-Qa’dah, then they would say for Muharram: Dhul-Hijjah, and they would perform Hajj in Muharram. Then they would start over and calculate the number of days to come as they started, and they would say: Muharram and Safar and the two months of Rabi’, so they would perform Hajj in Muharram so that they would perform Hajj twice every year, then they would omit another month and count according to the first number, and they would say: Safaran and the two months of Rabi’, similar to their number at the beginning of what they omitted.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.
m: Towards it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah Fal told us, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The companion of the postponement that was postponed for them was Abu Thamama, a man from Banu Kinanah.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr,
m: on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh? On the authority of Mujahid:
h
And there is no disputing during Hajj
, he said: There is no doubt about Hajj, God has made the matter of Hajj clear.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And there is no disputing during Hajj
, he said: The matter of Hajj has been set straight, so do not argue about it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And there is no disputing during Hajj
, he said: There is no month that is postponed, and there is no doubt about Hajj, it has been made clear.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Karim, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And there is no disputing during Hajj
, he said: The time of Hajj has been known, so there is no disputing or doubt about it.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz and Al Alaa, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: It is a known month in which there is no dispute.

c: Ahmad narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Israel narrated to us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And there is no disputing during Hajj
, he said: There is no doubt about Hajj.

c: Al Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al Hussain narrated to us, he said: Hisham narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj informed us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And there is no disputing during Hajj
, he said: Disputing about Hajj.

c: Al Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: On the authority of Mujahid,
h
And there is no disputing in Hajj

, Hajj has been made clear. He said: They used to perform Hajj in Dhul-Hijjah for two years, and in Muharram for two years, then they performed Hajj in Safar for two years. They used to perform Hajj every year in every month for two years, then the Hajj of Abu Bakr in the two years coincided with the Hajj of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by one year, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj the following year in Dhul-Hijjah, and that was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Time has come back to its original state as it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And there is no disputing in Hajj
, he said: God has made clear the matter of Hajj and its features, so there is no dispute about it.

x: The most correct of these statements regarding His statement,
h
And there is no disputing in Hajj

, is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of that is: Disputing about Hajj and its time has become obsolete, and its matter and time have become consistent with one time, with agreed-upon rituals that do not differ, and there is no dispute or quarrel about it. This is because God, the Most High, mentioned that the time of
h
Hajj is in well-known months

, then He denied the differences in its time, Surat al-Baqarah 2:197 Hajj is [during] well-known months, so whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein - there is no sexual relations nor wickedness nor disputing during Hajj. And whatever you do of good - God knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. And fear Me, O you of understanding. which the people of ignorance differed about in their polytheism.

We chose this interpretation in this regard, and we saw it as more correct than what contradicted it, because of what we have previously explained in the interpretation of His statement: nor disobedience, that it is not permissible for what was specifically prohibited in that situation to be [except for what is] absolutely permissible in the situation that contradicts it, which is the situation of ihram. This is because the ruling on what was specifically prohibited is the ruling on the situation of ihram, if it is the same in the situation of ihram and the situation of ihram, so there is no reason for it to be specific to one situation rather than another, and it has been applied to all situations. Since this is the case, and there is no meaning to the statement of the speaker in the interpretation of His statement:
h
And there is no disputing during Hajj

, that its interpretation is: Do not argue with your companion until you anger him, except for one of two meanings: Either he meant: Do not argue with him falsely until you anger him, and that is something that has no basis.

Because God the Almighty has forbidden arguing falsely in every situation, whether the one arguing is forbidden or not. So there is no reason for the forbidden thing to be specific to the state of ihram, because the states of ihram and ihram are equal in God’s prohibition of it. Or he may have meant: Do not argue with him about the truth, and that is also not justified. Because if the person in ihram sees a man intending to commit an immoral act, it is his duty to argue with him in order to prevent him from doing so, or if he sees him trying to oppress him and take from him a right that he has usurped from him, it is his duty to argue with him about it and debate with him until he is free of it. Arguing and debate do not occur between people except for one of two reasons: either because of injustice, or because of the truth. So if from one of its aspects it is not permissible to do it in any case, and from the other aspect it is not permissible to leave it in any case, then which of its aspects is specifically forbidden in the state of ihram?

Likewise, there is no basis for the statement of those who interpreted it to mean cursing, because God, the Most High, has forbidden believers from cursing each other, through the tongue of His Messenger, peace be upon him, in every situation, as he, peace be upon him, said: Cursing a Muslim is immorality, and fighting him is disbelief. So if a Muslim is forbidden from cursing a Muslim in every situation, whether it is forbidden or not, then there is no basis for saying: Do not curse him while in a state of ihram if you enter ihram.
And in what was narrated from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, of the hadith that:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, he said, Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: Whoever performs Hajj to this House and does not utter obscenities or commit immorality, will emerge as if he were the day his mother bore him.

c: Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, he said, Hajjaj narrated to us, he said, Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Abu Hazim,
m: On the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs Hajj to this House and does not utter obscenities or commit sin, will emerge from his sins as on the day his mother bore him.

c: Ahmad ibn al-Waleed narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja’far narrated to us, saying: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, like the hadith of Ibn al-Muthanna, on the authority of Wahb ibn Jarir.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja’far narrated to us, saying: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, also likewise.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Waleed narrated to us, saying: Shu’bah narrated to us, saying: Mansur informed me, saying:
m: I heard Abu Hazim narrating, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs Hajj to this House and does not utter obscenities or commit sins, will emerge from his sins as his mother bore him.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakee’ and Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Hazim - on the authority of Abu Hurayrah - saying:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar - except that he said: He returned as his mother bore him.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar - except that he said: He returned to his family as the day his mother bore him.

c: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaaf, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar - except that he said: He will return to his family as on the day his mother bore him.

c: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Yahya ibn Abi Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaf, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs Hajj to this House - meaning the Ka’bah - and does not utter obscenities or commit sins, will return as on the day his mother bore him.

c: Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabah told us, he said, Hisham ibn Bashir told us, on the authority of Sayyar, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Abu Hurairah
m: said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs Hajj for the sake of God and does not utter obscenities or commit sins, will return as he was on the day his mother bore him. This is a clear indication 1 that his statement,
h
There is no disputing during Hajj

, means denying that Hajj should involve disputing and arguing during its time, without prohibiting people from disputing among themselves about matters that concern them or do not concern them. This is because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us that whoever performs Hajj and does not utter obscenities or commit sins, will have earned from God the honor that He described as having earned through his Hajj, leaving the obscenities and sins that God has forbidden the pilgrim from during his Hajj, without adding disputing to them. If the argument that God mentioned in His statement: And
h
there is no disputing during Hajj

was something that God forbade in this verse - in the manner that was interpreted by those who interpreted it: that it is argumentation, disputes, insults, and the like - then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have singled out the pilgrim who is mentioned as deserving of the honor that he described as being due to him, whose matter is to avoid two of the things that God forbade him from doing in his Hajj, without the third that is coupled with them. But since the meaning of the third differs from the meaning of its two companions, in that it is report of the meaning that we described, and the other two are in the meaning of the prohibition that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed that the one who avoids them in his Hajj deserves what was described of God’s honoring him, which he informed that He will honor him with - since they were in the meaning of the prohibition - and the one who refrains from them is obedient to God by refraining from them, he left out mentioning the third, since it is not in their meaning, and opposing its path is their path. If that is the case, then what is more deserving of reading from the readings is the difference between the i'rab of jedal and the i'rab of rifth and fusuq, so that the listener of that - if he is one of the people of understanding languages - knows that what is the reason for the difference between their i'rabs is the difference in their meanings. And it is correct to read all of that with the agreement of its i'rab despite the difference in its meanings, since the Arabs used to follow some words with i'rabs, with the difference in meanings, especially in this type of speech. So the most pleasing reading to me in that - since the matter is as you have described - is the reading of the one who read: There is no filth, no fusuq, no jedal in Hajj, raising rifth and fusuq and giving them a tanween, and opening jedal without a tanween. And that is the reading of the group of the Basrans, and many of the people of Mecca, among them Abdullah bin Katheer and Abu Amr bin Al-Ala. As for the saying of the one who said: Its meaning is: the prohibition of the disagreement of those who disagree about who has completed Hajj, and those who say: Its meaning is the prohibition of someone saying: Tomorrow is the Hajj, contradicting the saying of another: Today is the Hajj. The statement in its narration is sufficient to prove its weakness and frailty. This is because it is a statement whose authenticity cannot be known except by a widespread report or a true report that necessitates knowledge that this was the case, so the verse was revealed prohibiting it, or that its meaning is in some meanings of the argument and not others, and there is no report of that in the manner that we have described. As for our evidence for the statement that we have said, that it is a denial from God, the Most High, regarding the months of Hajj, this is the difference that the Jahiliyyah used to differ among themselves before, as we have described. As for our evidence that the Jahiliyyah used to do this, the widespread report among the people of narrations is that the Jahiliyyah used to do this, along with the evidence of the statement of God, the Most High: “The postponement is only an increase in disbelief by which those who disbelieve go astray. They make it lawful one year and forbid it another year.” (al-Tawbah 9:37) Abu Jaʿfar said: By that, He, the Most High, means: Do, O believers, what I have commanded you to do in your Hajj, by completing your rituals in it, and performing your obligatory duty in your state of ihram, and avoiding what I have commanded you to avoid of obscenity and immorality in your Hajj, so that you may deserve a great reward. So whatever you do of that and other good and righteous deeds, seeking My pleasure and seeking My reward, for I am All-Knowing of it, and I will record all of it, so that I may give you its reward and recompense you for it, for nothing is hidden from Me, and nothing you intended by your deeds is concealed from Me, for I am aware of your secrets, and I am All-Knowing of the secrets of your souls.

x: It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about a people who performed Hajj without provisions, and some of them, when they entered ihram, He threw away the provisions he had with him and started with other provisions. So God, the Most High, commanded those of them who had not taken provisions for their journey, and those of them who had provisions to take care of their provisions and not throw them away.
Mention of the narrations that were narrated in that regard:

c: Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada’i told me, he said: Amr ibn Abd al-Ghaffar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Suqah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar Qad:
m: When they entered ihram and had provisions with them, they would throw them away and start with other provisions. So he got off? God said: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is piety. So they were forbidden from that, and were commanded to take provisions of cakes, flour, and gruel.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah Al-Mukhrami told us, she said, Shababah told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: They used to perform Hajj without taking provisions, so the following was revealed: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is piety. Amr Surat al-Baqarah 2:197 Hajj is [during] well-known months, so whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein - there is no sexual relations nor wickedness nor disputing during Hajj. And whatever you do of good - God knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. And fear Me, O you of understanding. ibn Ali told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Suqah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, regarding His statement: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is piety. He said: Cakes and oil.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Suqah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: It is cakes and gruel.

c: And Amr told us, he said, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: There were people who used to perform Hajj without taking provisions, so God revealed: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is piety.

c: Amr told us, he said, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, he said, Abdul Malik ibn Ata’ told us,
m: a Kufan from Kufa 1. I told Al-Hasan ibn Yahya, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement, And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is fear of God, he said: Dates and gruel.

c: Amr told us, Abu Asim told us, Hanzala told us,
m: Salim was asked about the provisions of the pilgrim, and he said: Bread, meat, and dates. Amr said: I heard Abu Asim once say:

c: Hanzala told us:
m: Salim was asked about the provisions of the pilgrim, and he said: Bread and dates.

c: Amr told us, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: Some of the Bedouins used to perform Hajj without provisions, and they would say: We put our trust in God! So God, the Most High, revealed: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is fear of God.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us, he said: Ishaq told us, on the authority of Omar bin Dhir, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The pilgrim among them did not take provisions, so God revealed: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is fear of God.

c: Amr Qaqaq narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, on the authority of Umar ibn Dharr - and Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Umar ibn Dharr narrated to us
m: - on the authority of Mujahid, he said: They used to travel without taking provisions, so this verse was revealed: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya said in his hadith: They used to perform Hajj without taking provisions.

c: Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, he said: Al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Umar ibn Dharr, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to us, he said: Umar ibn Dharr narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid narrating, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Abdul-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The people of the horizons used to go out for Hajj, seeking help from people without provisions, saying: We are relying on you. So God revealed: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty: And take provisions, he said: The people of the horizons would go out for Hajj, seeking to connect with people without provisions, so they were commanded to take provisions.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is piety, he said: The people of Yemen sought to connect with people, so they were commanded to take provisions and not to enjoy themselves. He said: And the best provision is piety.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is piety. He said: They did not take provisions, so they were commanded to take provisions, and the best provision is piety.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is piety. Al-Hasan used to say: Some people from Yemen used to perform Hajj and travel without taking provisions, so God commanded them to spend and take provisions in the way of God, then He informed them that the best provision is piety.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArubah,
m: regarding His statement: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is piety, he said: Qatada said: There were people from Yemen who would perform Hajj without taking provisions - then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Bishr, on the authority of Yazid.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, ʿAbd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muʿammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is piety, he said: There were people from Yemen who would go to Mecca without provisions, so God commanded them to take provisions, and He informed them that the best provision is piety.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God, he said: There were people who would leave their families and they did not have provisions with them, saying: We are going on pilgrimage to the House of God, but He does not feed us! So God said: And take provisions that will hold your faces back from the people. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is piety, so some people from Yemen used to perform Hajj without taking provisions, so God commanded them to take provisions, and He informed us that the best provision is piety.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Nuʿaym narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suqah, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr:
m: And take provisions, he said: gruel, flour, and cakes.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Wakeeʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suqah, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr:
m: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is piety, he said: khushkaanj and gruel.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Wakeeʿ narrated to us, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAtaʿ al-Bakkaʿi, he said:
m: I heard al-Shaʿbi say regarding His statement: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is piety, he said: It is food, and food at that time was scarce. I said: What is food? He said: Dates and gruel.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is piety, and the best provision of this world is benefit from clothing, food, and drink.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And take provisions, for indeed, the best provision is fear of God. He said: The people would take provisions to a pass, and when they reached that pass, they would rely on God and not take provisions.

c: Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi told me, he said, al-Maharibi told us, he said, Sufyan said
m: regarding His statement: And take provisions, he said: They were commanded to make barley flour and cake. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abdul-Razzaq narrated, my father narrated, he heard Ikrimah say about the verse: And take provisions, he said: It refers to gruel and flour. Yunus narrated, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated, he said: Ibn Zayd said about the verse: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God, he said: There were tribes of Arabs who forbade provisions when they went out for Hajj and Umrah, in order to be guests of people, so God Almighty said to them: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. Amr bin Abdul-Hamid Al-Ahli narrated, he said: Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: People used to come to Mecca without provisions, so God revealed: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God.

x: The interpretation of the verse then is: Whoever has made Hajj obligatory during the months of Hajj and enters ihram therein, then he should not engage in sexual relations or commit sin. The matter of Hajj has been made right for you, and your Lord has made known to you its time and limits. So fear God in what He has commanded you and forbidden you regarding your Hajj and your rituals. For whatever good you do that He has commanded you to do or urged you to do, He knows it. And provision yourself with what will suffice you to fulfill the obligation of your Lord upon you in your Hajj and your rituals. For there is no righteousness towards God, the Exalted, in your neglecting to provision yourselves and asking people, nor in wasting and spoiling your provisions. Rather, righteousness lies in fearing your Lord by avoiding what He has forbidden you to do in your journey for your Hajj, and doing what He has commanded you to do, for it is the best provision, so provision from it.
And similar to what we have said in this regard, a report was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement: The best provision is piety, he said: Piety is an action in obedience to God. We have already explained the meaning of piety in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

x: By that, He, the Most High, means: And fear Me, O people of intellects and understandings, by performing My obligations upon you that I have made obligatory upon you in your Hajj and your rituals, and other than that of My religion that I have prescribed for you, and fear My punishment by avoiding My prohibitions that I have forbidden you, so that you will be saved from what you fear of My wrath and punishment upon you, and you will attain what you seek of winning My Paradise. And He, the Most High, specifically addressed those with understanding, because they are the ones who distinguish between truth and falsehood, and the ones who have correct thought and knowledge of the realities of things that are perceived by intellects and understood by intellects. He did not give any share to anyone other than the ignorant in His address, since they were ghosts like cattle, and images like beasts, rather they are more astray from them.
Al-Albab is the plural of Lab, which means mind.

evidence.text: If that is the case, then what is more deserving of reading from the readings is the difference between the i'rab of jedal and the i'rab of rifth and fusuq, so that the listener of that - if he is one of the people of understanding languages - knows that what is the reason for the difference between their i'rabs is the difference in their meanings.

So the most pleasing reading to me in that - since the matter is as you have described - is the reading of the one who read: There is no filth, no fusuq, no jedal in Hajj, raising rifth and fusuq and giving them a tanween, and opening jedal without a tanween.
And that is the reading of the group of the Basrans, and many of the people of Mecca, among them Abdullah bin Katheer and Abu Amr bin Al-Ala.

x: By that, He, the Most High, means: There is no blame upon you, O believers. And the blame is hardship, as: - Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Mu'awiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

, and there is no blame upon you for buying and selling before and after Ihram. And His saying: that you seek bounty from your Lord, means: that you seek bounty from your Lord. It is said from it: I sought bounty from God - and from the bounty of God - I seek it seeking, if I asked for it and sought it, and I sought it I seek it seeking, Abd Bani Al-Hashas said: He wanted you, and you did not want him until you found him, as if you had made an appointment with him yesterday Meaning: Your request and adherence. It was said that the meaning of seeking bounty from God is seeking God’s provision through trade, and that this verse was revealed about a people who did not think that they should trade when they were in ihram, seeking righteousness through that.
So God, the Most High, informed them that there is no righteousness in that, and that they may seek His bounty through buying and selling.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Omar bin Dhar, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They used to perform Hajj but did not trade, so God revealed:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
, he said: During the season.

c: Yaqoub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Omar bin Dhar told us, he said,
m: I heard Mujahid narrating, he said: There were people who did not trade during the days of Hajj, so this verse was revealed about them:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

c: Muhammad ibn Amara al-Asadi told me, he said, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, he said, Abu Laila told us, on the authority of Buraydah,
m: regarding the words of God Almighty:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
, he said: When you are in a state of ihram, that you buy and sell.

c: Taliq ibn Muhammad al-Wasiti told us, he said, Asbat told us, he said, al-Hasan ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Taimi, he said,
m: I said to Ibn Umar: We are people who rent, so do we have a Hajj? He said: Do you not circumambulate the House, come to the place of pilgrimage, stone the Jamarat, and shave your heads? We said: Yes! He said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about what you asked me about, but he did not know what to say to him, until Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down to him with this verse:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
to the end of the verse, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are pilgrims.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: She used to recite this verse:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
during the seasons of Hajj.

c: Abdul Hamid told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Mansur bin Al-Mu’tamir,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

, he said: It is trade in buying, selling, and purchasing. There is nothing wrong with it. Narrated on the authority of Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i, who said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That he used to recite it:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
during the seasons of Hajj.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us,
m: who said: We were told by Uthman bin Saeed, on the authority of Ali bin Musahhir, on the authority of Ibn Surat Al-Baqarah 2:198
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

. So when you depart from Arafat, remember God at the sacred monument and remember Him as He has guided you, although before that you were among those astray. Jurayj, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The people’s trade in the pre-Islamic era was ‘Ukaz and Dhu al-Majaz, but when Islam came, it was as if they hated that, until God, the Most High, revealed:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

c: Al-Hasan bin ‘Arfa narrated to us,
m: who said: Shababah bin Suwar narrated to us, who said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Umaimah, who said: I heard Ibn ‘Umar - and he was asked about a man who was performing Hajj and had merchandise with him - so Ibn ‘Umar recited:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us
m: - and Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Hisham told us - he said, Yazid bin Abi Ziyad told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said, they did not trade during the days of Hajj, so this verse was revealed:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he recited:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
during the seasons of Hajj.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya ibn Wadh told us, Talhah ibn Amr al-Hadrami told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the Hajj seasons
, this is how Ibn Abbas read it.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Layth told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
, he said: Trade in this world, and the reward in the Hereafter.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
, he said: Trade was made permissible for them during the seasons. He said: So they did not buy or sell at Arafat during the pre-Islamic period.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

, this tribe of Arabs did not stop for a broken or lost thing on the night of departure, and they used to call it the night of the chest, and they did not seek trade or sale on it, so God Almighty permitted all of that to the believers, that they should stop for their needs, and seek from the bounty of their Lord.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abi Yazid, he said:
m: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr reciting:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
during the seasons of Hajj.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: Dhu al-Majaz and Ukaz were places of trade for the people in the pre-Islamic era, but when Islam came, they abandoned that, until the verse was revealed:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
during the seasons of Hajj.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim and al-Muthanna narrated to us, they said: Abu Naim narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Suqah, he said:
m: I heard Saeed bin Jubair say: Some of the pilgrims used to call al-Daj, so they would camp on the left side of Mina, and the pilgrims would camp at the mosque of Mina, so they would not trade, until the verse was revealed:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
, so they performed Hajj.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim narrated to me.
m: He said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Omar bin Dhir told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: There were people who performed Hajj but did not trade, until the verse was revealed:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
, and they were permitted to trade, ride, and take provisions. Musa bin Harun narrated, Amr bin Hammad narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

, referring to trade. He said: Trade during the seasons. Muhammad bin Saad narrated, my father narrated, my uncle narrated, my father narrated, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

, referring to trade. He said: When people entered ihram, they would not engage in any trade until they had completed their Hajj, so God made it permissible for them. Al-Muthanna narrated, Abu Nuʿaym narrated, Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They used to avoid buying and selling during the seasons, saying: Days of remembrance! So God revealed:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
for God, so they performed Hajj. Abu Kurayb narrated, Wakiʿ narrated, on the authority of Talhah bin Amr, on the authority of Ataʿ, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: He used to recite it:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
during the seasons of Hajj.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Al-Hammani narrated to us, he said, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: There is nothing wrong with trading during Hajj, then he recited:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
. I narrated to Ammar, he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, his saying:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

, he said: This tribe of Arabs did not stop for a broken person or for a lost thing, and they did not wait for a need, and they used to call it the Night of Sadr, and they did not seek trade during it. So God permitted all of that, that they would stop for their need, and seek bounty from their Lord.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Mandal narrated to us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Muhajir, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: the freed slave of Umar, he said: I said to Umar: O Commander of the Faithful, did you trade during Hajj? He said: And was their livelihood except in Hajj?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-Ala bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of a man from Banu Taym God, he said:
m: A man came to Abdullah bin Omar and said: O Abu Abdul Rahman, we are a people who rent, and they claim that we do not have Hajj! He said: Do you not enter ihram as they do, and do tawaf as they do, and throw stones as they do? He said: Yes! He said: Then you are a pilgrim! A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and asked him what you had asked about, so this verse was revealed:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
b.via: a man from Banu Taym God

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When they left Arafat, they did not engage in any trade, nor did they stop for a broken or lost animal, so God permitted that and said:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
to the end of the verse.

c: Saeed told me, on the authority of al-Rabi’ al-Razi, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Ukaz, Majanna, and Dhu al-Majaz were markets in the pre-Islamic era, and they used to trade in them. When Islam came, it was as if they had sinned by them, so they asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so God revealed:
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord
during the seasons of Hajj.

x: By His saying: Then when you have departed, He meant when you return from where you started. Therefore, the one who throws lots between the left and right is called Faydh, because he collects the lots and then throws them between the left and right. From this is the saying of Bishr bin Abi Khazim Al-Asadi: I said to her: Return his paradise to him! She returned it as a generous gift is returned. Then the Arab scholars differed about Arafat, the reason for which it was declined and it is a definite noun, and is it the name of a single place or a group of places?

Some of the Basran grammarians said: It is a name that belonged to a group such as Muslimat and Muminat, and a single area was named after it. It was declined as the single area was named after it, since it was declined before the area was named after it, leaving it as it was. Because the ta’ in it became like the ya’ and waw in Muslims and Muslims because it is masculine, and the tanween became like the nun, so when it was named after it, it was left as it is, just as Muslims is left as it is when it is named after it. He said: Some Arabs do not decline it when it is named after it, and they liken the ta’ to the feminine ha’, and that is ugly and weak.

i: They cited as evidence the saying of the poet:
x: Her skirt is from Adhraat, and her people are in Yathrib, the lowest part of her house is a high view Some of them do not add the nun to dhara'at, and so does 'Aanat, which is a place.

Some of the Kufians said: 'Arafat was declined because they are on a feminine plural with a ta'. He said: And similarly, whatever was from a feminine plural with a ta', then you named a man, a place, a land, or a woman with it, it was declined. He said: The Arabs hardly ever name something from a plural except as a plural, then make it one after that.

Others of them said: It is not a narrative remnant, nor is it a transferred name, but the place is named, it and its sides, with 'Arafat, then the spot was named with it. It is a name for the place, and its singular is not singular. He said: This is only permissible in places and locations, and it is not permissible in other things. He said: That is why the Arabs put the ta' in the accusative case in that, because it is a place. Even if it was narrated, it would not be permissible, because whoever named a man Muslimat or Muslims did not transfer it in grammar from what it was originally, so it contradicted: Aanat and Adhraat, which were named by the names narrated.
The scholars differed about the meaning for which Arafat was called Arafat.

Some of them said: It was called that because when Abraham, the friend of God, peace be upon him, saw it, he recognized it by the description that he had for it, so he said: I have recognized it!! So it was called Rafat by that.
