This statement by its speaker indicates that Arafat is the name of a place, and it was called that for itself and what is around it, just as it is said: a garment of morals, or a land of Sabasib, so it is collected by what is around it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When Ibrahim called the people to Hajj and they responded to him with the Talbiyah, and those who came to him came, God commanded him to go out to Arafat, so he went out, and when he reached the tree at Al-Aqaba, Satan met him to turn him back, so he threw seven pebbles at him, saying Allahu Akbar with each pebble, so he flew and landed on the second Jamrah, but it also stopped him, so he threw it and said Allahu Akbar, so it flew and landed on the third Jamrah, so he threw it and said Allahu Akbar. When he saw that he could not bear it, and Ibrahim did not know where to go, he set off until he came to Dhul-Majaz, and when he looked at it and did not recognize it, he passed, and for that reason it was called Dhul-Majaz. Then he set off until he came to Arafat, and when he looked at it, he recognized the description, and said: I have recognized! So it was called Arafat. Ibrahim stood at Arafat, and when evening came, he approached the gathering place, and it was called Muzdalifah. Then he stood.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Na’im ibn Abi Hind, he said:
m: When Gabriel stood with Ibrahim, peace be upon them both, at Arafat, he said: I recognize! So Arafat was called that.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said,
m: Ibn al-Musayyab said, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: God sent Gabriel to Ibrahim, so he performed Hajj with Surat Al-Baqarah 2:198
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

. So when you depart from Arafat, remember God at the sacred monument and remember Him as He has guided you, although before that you were among those astray. him, and when he came to Arafat, he said: I recognize! He had come to it once before that, and that is why it was called Arafat.

x: Others said: Rather, it was called that by itself and by other places besides it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Waki’ bin Muslim Al-Qurashi told us, on the authority of Abu Tahfah, on the authority of Abu Al-Tayfil, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It was called Arafat because Gabriel, peace be upon him, used to say to Abraham: This is such and such a place, this is such and such a place. He would say: You have known! That is why it was called Arafat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: It was called Arafat because Gabriel used to show Abraham, peace be upon them, the rituals, and he would say to him: I know, I know! So it was called Arafat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: The base of the mountain next to Urna and what is behind it is a place of standing, until you reach the mountain, Mount Arafat. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Arafat is the spring, the spring, and the spring, and that is the saying of God: Then when you have poured forth from Arafat, which is the middle ravine. Zakariya said: What flows from the mountain on which the imam stands to Arafat is from Arafat, and what is behind that mountain is not from Arafat. This statement indicates that it was called that, similar to what is called one by the name of a group of different people.

x: The most correct statement in this regard in my opinion is to say: It is the name of one person called by a group. If it is inflected, it is taken as the collective noun that originally had it. If it is not inflected, it is taken as the name of a single known spot, so it is not inflected as the names of cities and villages are not inflected.

By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: So when you have gone forth and returned from Arafat to where you began your journey from, then remember God, meaning by that: prayer and supplication at the sacred monument. We have previously explained that the monuments are the landmarks, from the saying of the speaker: I felt this matter, meaning I knew, so the monument is the landmark. It was called that because the prayer at it, the residence, the overnight stay, and the supplication are among the landmarks of the Hajj and its obligations that God has commanded His servants to do.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, who said:
m: It is recommended for the pilgrim to pray at his place of residence in Muzdalifah if he is able, because God said: So remember God at the sacred monument and remember Him as He has guided you. As for the sacred monument, it is the area between the two mountains of Muzdalifah from the passes of Arafat to Muhsir. The passes of Arafat are not part of the sacred monument. And the people of interpretation said what we said about that.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Hannad ibn al-Sarri told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ra’idah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Ibn Umar saw people crowding together at the mountain in a group, so he said: O people, the entire group is a sacred monument.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: that he was asked about his statement:
h
Then remember God at the sacred monument
, he said: It is the mountain and what is around it.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Hakim bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: What is between the two mountains that are in the vicinity of the sacred monument.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us
m: - and Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us - on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: I asked him about Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, and he said: It is between the two mountains of Muzdalifah.

c: Al-Hasan Qaq told us, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram is all of Muzdalifah. He said: Muammar: And Qatadah said the same.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: Then remember God at Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, he said: It is between the two mountains of Muzdalifah, it is Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah bin Umar about Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, and he said: If you go with me, I will inform you of it. He said: So I went with him and we stopped, and when the Imam had finished the ritual, he continued on and we continued on with him, until when the riders’ hands descended, and we were at the furthest point of the mountains towards Arafat, he said: Where is the one asking about Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram? I entered it! I said: What did I enter it? He said: All of them are rituals up to the furthest point of the sanctuary.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said: Israel told us, and Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun Al-Awdi, he said:
m: I asked Abdullah bin Omar about Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, he said: If you insist on me, I will leave it. He said: When the people had finished the ritual from Arafat and the riders’ hands descended at the lowest point of the mountains, he said: Where is the one asking about Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram? I said: Here I am! He said: I entered it! I said: What did I enter it? He said: When the riders’ hands descended at the lowest point of the mountains, it is a ritual towards Mecca. Hannad narrated, he said: Wakee' narrated, on the authority of Ammarah ibn Zadhan, on the authority of Makhul al-Azdi, he said: I asked Ibn Umar on the day of Arafah about al-Mash'ar al-Haram, and he said: Al-Zamani. When it was the next day and we came to Muzdalifah, he said: Where is the one who asked about al-Mash'ar al-Haram? This is al-Mash'ar al-Haram. Hannad narrated, he said: Ibn Abi Zaidah narrated, he said: Dawud narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said: al-Mash'ar al-Haram is all of Muzdalifah. Hannad narrated, he said: Ibn Abi Zaidah narrated, he said: Dawud narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: I said to Ata', Where is Muzdalifah? He said: When you pass through the two narrow passages of Arafah, then that is to Muhsar. He said: The two narrow passages are not the narrow passages of Arafah from Muzdalifah, but their passages. He said: Stand between them if you wish, but I prefer that you stand in front of the rainbow. Come to us for the sake of the people's path!

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Ibn Umar saw them crowding at Qahzah, so he said: Why are these crowding? Everything here is a sacred place!

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Al-Mashʿar Al-Haram is all of Muzdalifah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement: And when you depart from Arafat, remember God at Al-Mashʿar Al-Haram, that is on the night of Jumuʿah. Qatada said: Ibn Abbas used to say: What is between the two mountains is a sacred place.

c: Musa told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Al-Mashʿar Al-Haram is what is between the mountains of Muzdalifah, and it is said: It is Qarn Qahzah. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’, Then remember God at Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, which is Muzdalifah, and it is a plural. And he mentioned on the authority of Abdurrahman Ibn Al-Aswad what: - Hannad narrated to us, he said, Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abdurrahman Ibn Al-Aswad, he said: I did not find anyone to tell me about Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram.

c: Ahmad Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Sa’id Ibn Jubayr said:
m: Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram is what is between the two mountains of Muzdalifah.

c: Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Qais narrated to us, on the authority of Hakim Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Sa’id Ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Umar about Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram and he said: I do not know. And I asked Ibn Abbas and he said: What is between the two mountains.

c: Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Israel narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Al-Jubail and what is around it are sacred places.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Thawir, who said:
m: I stood with Mujahid at Jubail and he said: This is the sacred monument.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, Hassan bin Atiyah told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Jubail and what is around it are sacred monuments.

x: We made the beginning of the boundary of the sacred monument next to Mina, the end of Wadi Muhsar next to Muzdalifah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: All of Arafat is a place of standing except for Urnah, and all of Jam’a is a place of standing except for Muhsar.

c: Ya’qub told me, Hisham told me, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, who said:
m: All of Muzdalifah is a place of standing except for Wadi Muhsar.

c: Ya’qub told me, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, who said:
m: Someone who heard Urwah bin Az-Zubayr say something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, he said: Abdullah bin al-Zubayr said
m: in his sermon: Know that all of Arafat is a place of standing except for Batn Urnah. Know that all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing except for Batn Muhsir.

x: However, even if that is the case, I prefer for the pilgrim to make his standing for the remembrance of God from the sacred monument, at Quzah and what is around it, because:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Ismail ibn Mujammi, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith al-Makhzumi, on the authority of Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abi Rafi’, on the authority of Ali, who said:
m: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived at Muzdalifah in the morning, he went out and stood at Qazhah, and al-Fadl rode behind him, then he said: This is the place of standing, and all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing.” Abu Kuraib narrated, Yunus bin Bakir narrated, Ibrahim bin Ismail bin Mujammi' narrated, on the authority of Abdurrahman bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Zaid bin Ali bin Al-Hussein, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abi Rafi', on the authority of Abi Rafi', on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Hannad and Ahmad Al-Dulabi narrated, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Saeed bin Abdurrahman bin Yarbu', on the authority of Ibn Al-Huwayrith, who said: I saw Abu Bakr standing on Qazhah and saying: O people, wake up! O people, wake up! Then he pushed. Ibn Hamid narrated, Harun narrated, on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman, on the authority of Yusuf bin Mahak, who said: I performed Hajj with Ibn Umar, and when morning came at Jam'ah, he prayed the dawn prayer, then he went out and we went out with him until he stood with the Imam on Qazhah, then the Imam pushed, and he pushed with his push. As for the statement of Abdullah bin Omar when he arrived at Muzdalifah: All of this is a sign to Mecca, its meaning is: they are landmarks of the Hajj, and some of the Hajj rituals are performed in each spot of them, because all of that is the sacred Surat Al-Baqarah 2:198
h
There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord

. So when you depart from Arafat, remember God at the sacred monument and remember Him as He has guided you, although before that you were among those astray. monument where the one standing is from it to the valley of Mecca, fulfilling what he is required to do of standing at the sacred monument from the collection. As for the statement of Abdul Rahman bin Al-Aswad: I did not find anyone to tell me about the sacred monument, because it is possible that he meant. I did not find anyone to tell me about the limit of its beginning and the end of its end in its right and truth. Because the limits of that, despite their correctness, so that there is no increase or decrease in it, are only comprehended by a few of the people of knowledge about it. However, even if no one stood at the limit of its beginning and the end of its end in a standing in which there is no increase or decrease except for those I mentioned, the place of need for standing is not hidden from any of the residents of that area and many others. And the same is true for the rest of the sacred monuments of Hajj, and the places where God the Almighty has obligated His servants to perform the rituals such as Arafat, Mina and the Haram.

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And remember God, O believers, at the Sacred Monument, by praising Him and thanking Him for His favors toward you. And let your remembrance of Him be with submission to His command, obedience to Him, and thanks for what He has bestowed upon you of success, for He has guided you to it from the ways of His friend Abraham, after what you were in of polytheism, confusion, and blindness to the path of truth, and after misguidance, like His remembrance of you with guidance until He saved you from the Fire with it, after you were on the brink of a pit from it, and He saved you from it. And that is the meaning of His statement: as He has guided you. As for His statement: and if you were before that among those astray, some of the Arabs direct the interpretation of in to the interpretation of “ What, and the interpretation of the lam in li-min to la.

So the interpretation of the speech according to this meaning: And you were not, before God guided you to what He guided you to of the religion of His friend Abraham, which He chose for whomever He was pleased with from among His creation, except among those who went astray. And among them is he who directs the interpretation of in to qad. So its meaning, according to the saying of the speaker of this article: And remember God, O believers, as He reminded you of guidance and guided you to what He was pleased with from religions and sects, and you were before that among those who went astray.

evidence.text: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: She used to recite this verse: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj.

Narrated on the authority of Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i, who said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That he used to recite it: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj.

Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya ibn Wadh told us, Talhah ibn Amr al-Hadrami told us, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the Hajj seasons, this is how Ibn Abbas read it.

Abu Kurayb narrated, Wakiʿ narrated, on the authority of Talhah bin Amr, on the authority of Ataʿ, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: He used to recite it: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that, and from Who is meant by the command to proceed from where the people proceeded? And who are the people who were commanded to proceed from the place of their proceeding?

Some of them said: What is meant by his saying: Then proceed, is the Quraysh and those who were born from Quraysh, who were called in the pre-Islamic era the Hams. They were commanded in Islam to proceed from Arafat, which is the place from which all the people proceeded except the Hams. This is because the Quraysh and those who were born from Quraysh used to say: We will not leave the sanctuary, so they did not witness the people’s standing at Arafat with them, so God commanded them to stand with them.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Tafawi told us, he said:
m: Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Quraysh and those who followed their religion - and they were the Hams - would stand at Muzdalifah, saying: We are the people of God! And those other than them would stand at Arafat, so God revealed:
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

c: Abdul-Warith bin Abdul-Samad bin Abdul-Warith told us, he said, my father told me, he said, Aban told us, he said, Hisham bin Urwah told us, on the authority of Urwah:
m: He wrote to Abdul-Malik bin Marwan: You wrote to me regarding the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to a man from the Ansar: I am Hams, and I do not know whether the Prophet said it or not? However, I heard it being narrated from him. The Hams were the religion of the Quraysh - and they were polytheists - and those of the Quraysh who were born in Khuza'ah and Banu Kinanah, they would not leave from a room, rather they would leave from Muzdalifah, which is the sacred monument. Banu Amir were the Hamsa, because Quraysh gave birth to them. It was said about them:
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed
, and that all the Arabs proceeded from Arafat except the Hamsa. They would leave when they woke up from Muzdalifah.

c: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi told me, he said, Abu Tuba told us, he said, Abu Ishaq al-Fazari told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Husayn ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The Arabs would stand at Arafat, and the Quraysh would stand further away at Muzdalifah, so God revealed:
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed
, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised the standing to the standing of the Arabs at Arafat.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’:
m: h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

, from where the group of people proceed. Ibn Humayd narrated, Al-Hakam narrated, Amr ibn Qays narrated, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: When the Day of Arafah comes, God descends to the lowest heaven with the angels and says: Come to Me, My servants, believe in My promise and believe in My messengers! He says: What is their reward? It is said: That you forgive them. That is what He said: “
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

and ask forgiveness of God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Muhammad ibn Amr narrated, Abu Asim narrated, Isa narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh - and Al-Muthanna narrated, Abu Hudhayfah narrated, Shibl narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh - on the authority of Mujahid:
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

, he said: Arafah. He said: Quraysh used to say: We are the Hams, the people of the sanctuary, and we do not shorten the sanctuary, and we proceed from Muzdalifah, so they were commanded to reach Arafah.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then depart from where the people depart

, Qatada said: The Quraysh and all their allies and their nephews did not depart from Arafat, but rather departed from Al-Maghmas, and they said: We are only the people of God, so we will not leave His sanctuary. So God commanded them to depart from where the people departed from Arafat, and He informed them that the Sunnah of Abraham and Ishmael was thus: departing from Arafat.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

, he said: The Arabs used to stand at Arafat, and the Quraysh would consider it too much to stand with them, so the Quraysh would stand at Muzdalifah, so God commanded them to proceed with the people from Arafat.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed
, he said: The Quraysh and every nephew and Surat Al-Baqarah 2:199
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

and ask forgiveness of God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. ally of theirs would not proceed with the people from Arafat, they would stand in the Haram and not leave it, saying: We are the people of God’s Haram, so we should not leave its Haram? So God commanded them to proceed
h
from where the people proceed
, and it was the Sunnah of Abraham and Ishmael to proceed from Arafat.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Najih, he said:
m: The Quraysh - I do not know before the Elephant or after it - invented the matter of the Hums, an opinion they had among themselves. They said: We are the sons of Abraham, the people of the sanctity, the guardians of the House, the inhabitants of Mecca and its residents. No one among the Arabs has a right like ours or a place like ours, and the Arabs do not recognize him as they recognize us. So do not glorify anything in the open area as you glorify the sanctuary, for if you do that, the Arabs will belittle your sanctuary. And they said: We have glorified the open area as they have glorified the sanctuary. So they left standing at Arafat and leaving it, and they know and acknowledge that it is one of the sacred places and the pilgrimage and the religion of Abraham, and they see that all the people should stand at it and leave it, except that they said: We are the people of the sanctuary, so it is not appropriate for us to leave the sanctuary, nor should we glorify anything else as we glorify it, we the Hums - and the Hums are the people of the sanctuary. Then they made for those who were born from the Arabs who were residents of the sanctuary the same as they were born to them, so that what was permissible was permissible for them, and what was forbidden was forbidden for them. Kinanah and Khuza'ah had entered into that with them. Then they innovated in that matters that had not existed, until they said: The Hims should not eat curds or spit out butter while they are in the state of ihram, nor enter a house of hair, nor seek shade if they seek shade except in leather skins as long as they are in the state of ihram. Then they raised that, and said: The people of the sanctuary should not eat food that they brought with them from the sanctuary into the sanctuary, if they come as pilgrims or as a pilgrim, nor should they circumambulate the House when they arrive for the first circumambulation except in the clothes of the Hims, and if they do not find any of that, they should circumambulate the House naked. So the Arabs attacked him and submitted to him, and they took what was prescribed for them, and they remained like that until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God revealed - when He established his religion for him and prescribed his pilgrimage for him: “
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

and ask forgiveness of God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful” - meaning the Quraysh and the Arab people - so He raised them in the year of the pilgrimage to Arafat and to stand on it and proceed from it. So God removed the matter of the Hums - and what the Quraysh had innovated from it - from the people with Islam, when God sent His Messenger.

c: Bahr bin Nasr narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Al-Zinad informed me, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: The Quraysh used to stand at Qazah, and the people used to stand at Arafat. He said: Then God revealed:
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

x: Others said: Those addressed by His statement: Then proceed are all Muslims, and the meaning of His statement:
h
From where the people proceed
, from the plural of people, is Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him.
Mention of those who said that: Narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Salam, who said:

c: Harun bin Muawiyah Al-Fazari narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bistam, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said:
m: He is Ibrahim.

x: What we see as correct in the interpretation of this verse is that it refers to Quraysh and those who were enthusiastic with them from the rest of the Arabs, due to the consensus of the jurists among the people of interpretation that this is its interpretation. Since this is the case, the interpretation of the verse is: And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein, there is no sexual relations nor disobedience nor disputing during Hajj.
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

, and ask forgiveness of God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And whatever you do of good - God knows it. And since this is what we have described as its interpretation, it is from the advanced meaning of delay, and the delayed meaning of precedence, in a manner similar to what we have explained previously in a similar case. And were it not for the consensus of those whose consensus I have described that this is its interpretation, I would have said: The most correct of the two interpretations of the interpretation of the verse is what Ad-Dahhak said, that God meant by His saying:
h
from where the people proceed
, from where Ibrahim proceeded.

Because the departure from Arafat is undoubtedly before the departure from Jam’ah, and before the obligation of the remembrance at Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram. Since that is undoubtedly the case, and God the Almighty only commanded the departure from the place from which the people departed, after the remembrance of the departure from Arafat had ended, and after He commanded its remembrance at Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, then He said after that: Then depart from where the people departed, it was known from this that He did not command the departure except from the place from which they had not departed, not the place from which they had departed, and the time for the departure from the place from which they had departed had expired, there is no reason to say: He departed from it. Since there is no reason for that, and it is not permissible for God the Almighty to command something that has no meaning, it would be clear that what He said regarding the interpretation in that is correct, and that what contradicted it is corrupt, were it not for the consensus that we have described, and the reports that we have mentioned from those who interpret it, whose words we have narrated, are consistent with what we have mentioned.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How can this mean: And the people are a group, and Abraham, peace be upon him, is one, and God Almighty says: Then pour forth from where the people pour forth?

The Arabs do this a lot, and they indicate by mentioning the group to one person, and from that is the saying of God Almighty: Those to whom the people said, ‘Indeed, the people have gathered against you’
r
(Al Imran 3:173)
and the one who said that is one, and he is, according to what the narrations of the people of the biography have agreed upon, Nu’aym ibn Mas’ud al-Ashja’i.
And from that is the saying of God Almighty: O messengers, eat from the good foods and work righteousness
r
(Al Mu’minun: 51)
, it is said: By that he meant the Prophet, peace be upon him, and there are similar examples of that in the speech of the Arabs more than can be counted.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: So when you have departed from ʿArafat, returning to Mina, then remember God at the Sacred Monument, and call upon Him and worship Him there, just as He reminded you of His guidance and granted you success in what He approved for His friend Abraham, guiding him to it from the law of His religion, after you had been astray from it.
And in the word then in His statement:
h
Then depart from where the people depart

, there are two interpretations: One of them is what Ad-Dahhak said, that its meaning is: Then, flow and return to Mina from where Ibrahim, my friend, flowed from Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, and ask Me for forgiveness for your sins, for I am Forgiving and Merciful to you, as:

c: Ismail bin Saif Al-Ajli told me, he said, Abdul-Qahir bin Al-Sari Al-Salami told us, he said, Ibn Kinanah - whose nickname is Abu Kinanah - told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Abbas bin Mirdas Al-Salami, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I called upon God on the Day of Arafah to forgive my nation’s sins, and He answered me that I have forgiven, except for its sins between me and My creation. So I repeated the supplication that day, but I did not receive any answer, so when it was the morning of Muzdalifah, I said: O Lord, You are able to compensate this wronged person for his injustice, and forgive this wrongdoer! So He answered me that I have forgiven. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, laughed. He said: So we said: O Messenger of God, we saw you laughing on a day when you did not laugh! He said: I laughed at the enemy of God, Satan, when he heard what he heard, as he called for woe and destruction, and put dirt on his head.

c: Muslim bin Hatim Al-Ansari told me, he said, Bashar bin Bakir Al-Hanafi told us,
m: they both said, Abdul Aziz bin Abi Rawad told us, on the authority of Nafi’, “On the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delivered a sermon to us on the eve of Arafah and said: O people, God has prolonged your stay in this place of yours, so He has accepted from your good doer and given to your good doer what he asked for, and has given your bad doer to your good doer, except for the consequences between you. So flow in the name of God. So when it was the morning of the gathering, he said: O people, God has prolonged your stay in this place of yours, so He has accepted from your good doer and given to your good doer what he asked for, and has given your bad doer to your good doer, and has compensated for the consequences between you from Him, so flow in the name of God. So his companions said: O Messenger of God, yesterday you left us sad and grieving, and today you left us happy and joyful! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yesterday I asked my Lord for something and He did not find for me, I asked Him for the consequences but He refused me, so today Gabriel came to me and said: Indeed Your Lord sends you peace and says: “I have guaranteed compensation for the sins from Me.” These two reports have shown that God’s forgiveness of the sins that His creation has committed among themselves is only on the morning of Friday, and that is at the time when He, the Most High, said:
h
Then proceed from where the people proceed

and ask forgiveness of God, for your sins, for He is Forgiving of them at that time, as a favor from Him to you, Merciful to you. The other of them is: Then proceed from Arafat to the Sacred Monument, and when you proceed to it from there, remember God in His presence as He has guided you.

x: What he meant by the words of God Almighty:
h
So when you have completed your rites
, is that when you have finished your Hajj and slaughtered your women, then remember God. It is said: A man performed a ritual sacrifice, he ...

Some of them said: In their ignorance, after completing their Hajj and rituals, the people would gather and boast about the deeds of their fathers. So God commanded them in Islam to mention their Lord with praise, thanks and glorification, and to oblige themselves to mention Him frequently, just as they obliged themselves in their ignorance to mention their fathers.

Those who said that: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Ishaq bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Othman, on the authority of Anas, regarding this verse, he said: They would mention their fathers during Hajj, and some of them would say: My father used to feed the poor! And some of them would say: My father used to strike with the sword!
Some of them would say: My father used to cut the forelocks of the Banu So-and-so!

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told me, he said, Abdul Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They would say: Our fathers used to slaughter camels and do such-and-such! So this verse was revealed: Remember God
h
as you remember your fathers
or with a more intense remembrance.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il:
m: h
So remember God as you remember your fathers
, or with a stronger remembrance. He said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to remember the deeds of their fathers.

c: Abu Kurayb told us,
m: he heard Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash say: When the people of the Jahiliyyah finished the Hajj, they would stand at the House and remember their fathers and their days: My father used to feed the poor! My father used to do that! So that is what His statement:
h
So remember God as you remember your fathers
. Abu Kurayb said: I said to Yahya ibn Adam: From whom is that? He said: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And remember God as you remember your fathers

, he said: When they completed their rituals, they would stand at the Jamrah and remember their fathers, and remember their days in the pre-Islamic era and the deeds of their fathers, so this verse was revealed.

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Qays, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And remember God as you remember your fathers
, he said: When they completed their rituals, they would stand at the Jamrah and remember their days in the pre-Islamic era and the deeds of their fathers. He said: So this verse was revealed.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And when you have completed your rituals, remember God
h
as you remember your fathers
, he said: The Arabs boasted among themselves about the deeds of their fathers on the Day of Sacrifice when they finished, so they were commanded to remember God instead of that.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And when Surat Al-Baqarah 2:200
h
So when you have completed your rites
, remember God
h
as you remember your fathers
or with a more intense remembrance. But among the people is he who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have no share in the Hereafter. you have completed your rites, remember God
h
as you remember your fathers

. Qatada said: When the people of the Jahiliyyah completed their rites in Mina, they would sit in circles and remember the deeds and actions of their fathers in the Jahiliyyah, and their orators would preach and their narrators would narrate about it. So God, the Almighty, commanded the Muslims to remember God as the people of the Jahiliyyah remembered their fathers, or even more so.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So remember God as you remember your fathers

or with a greater remembrance, he said: When they completed their rituals, they would gather and boast, and remember their fathers and the days of that, so they were commanded to replace that with the remembrance of God, remembering Him as they remember their fathers or with a greater remembrance.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr and Ikrimah.
m: They said: They used to mention the deeds of their fathers in the pre-Islamic era when they stood at Arafat, so this verse was revealed.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Kathir informed me that
m: he heard Mujahid say: That is on the Day of Sacrifice, when they slaughter. He said: He said:
h
So remember God as you remember your fathers
. He said: The Arabs used to boast about the deeds of their fathers on the Day of Sacrifice when they finished, so they were commanded to remember God, the Almighty, instead of that.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: So remember God as sons and children remember their fathers.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Ja’far narrated to us, he said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Uthman bin Abi Rawad, on the authority of Ata’ that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
As you remember your fathers
. He said: It is the saying of the boy: O father!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
So remember God as you remember your fathers
, meaning by remembrance, the sons remember their fathers.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ told me:
m: h
As you remember your fathers
, his father! his mother!

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Salih bin Umar told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: Like the boy who is always glorifying his father and mother.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’, his statement:
h
So when you have completed your rites
, remember God
h
as you remember your fathers
or with a greater remembrance, he stands: like the sons remember their fathers or with a greater remembrance.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So when you have completed your rites
, remember God
h
as you remember your fathers
or with a more intense remembrance, meaning: as children remember their fathers.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd told us, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
As you remember your fathers
, meaning: the sons remember their fathers.

x: Others said: Rather, it was said to them: Remember God
h
as you remember your fathers

, because when they completed their rituals and called upon their Lord, they did not remember anyone other than their fathers, so they were commanded to remember God in a manner similar to the remembrance of their fathers.
The one who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
So when you have completed your rituals
, remember God
h
as you remember your fathers

or with a greater remembrance, he said: When the Arabs completed their rituals and stayed in Mina, a man would stand and ask God and say: O God, my father had a large bowl, a large dome, and much wealth, so give me the same as You gave my father!! He was not remembering God, but rather he was remembering his fathers, and asking to be given in this world.

x: The correct interpretation of this, in my opinion, is to say: God, may He be glorified, commanded His believing servants to remember Him by obeying Him, submitting to His command, and worshipping Him, after completing their rituals. And that remembrance may be the takbir that God Almighty commanded in His saying: And remember God during the appointed days (al-Baqarah 2:203), which He made obligatory upon whoever has completed his rituals after completing his rituals, so He then made it obligatory for him to remember Him in a way that was not obligatory for him before that, and He urged to maintain it as children maintain the remembrance of their fathers in increasing it, by submitting to Him, and supplicating to Him, by desiring Him for their needs, like the supplication of a son to his father, and a child to his mother and father, or even more than that, since whatever blessing they and their fathers had was from Him, and He is its Guardian.
And we said: The remembrance that God Almighty commanded the pilgrim to do after completing his rituals in His saying:
h
So when you have completed your rituals
, remember God
h
as you remember your fathers

or with a greater remembrance: it is possible that it is the takbir that we described, because there is no remembrance of God that He commanded the servants to do after completing their rituals that was not obligatory upon them before. Their completion of their rituals, except for the glorification that God has made specific to the days of Mina. Since that is the case, and it is known that He, the Most High, has made it obligatory upon His creation after they have completed their rituals to remember Him in a way that was not obligatory upon them before that, and there is nothing of His remembrance that was specific to that time except the glorification that we have mentioned, then it is clear that what we have said about interpreting that as we have described is correct.
By that, He, the Most High, means:
h
So when you have completed your rites
, O believers, then remember God
h
as you remember your fathers

or even more, and desire from Him what He has of good in this world and the Hereafter with supplication and humility, and make your deeds purely for His sake and to seek His pleasure, and say: Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. And do not be like those who bought the life of this world for the Hereafter, so their deeds were for the world and its adornments, so they ask their Lord for nothing but its enjoyment, and they have no share in the reward of God, nor any portion in His Paradise and the Generous things He has prepared for His friends, as the people of interpretation said about that.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of ʿAsim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il:
m: “And among the people is he who says: Our Lord, give us in this world,” Give us sheep! Give us camels! “And he will have no share in the Hereafter.”

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said:
m: In the pre-Islamic era, they used to say: Give us camels, then he mentioned something similar. Abu Kurayb narrated that he heard Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash regarding the statement of God, the Almighty, And among the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter, saying: They, meaning the people of ignorance, would stand - meaning after completing their rituals - and say, O God, provide us with camels! O God, provide us with sheep! Then God revealed this verse: And among the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter. Abu Kurayb said: I said to Yahya ibn Adam: From whom is he? He said: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il.

c: Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Uthman, on the authority of Anas:
m: And among the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter, he said: They would circumambulate the House naked and supplicate, saying, O God, send us rain, and grant us victory over our enemy, and return us righteous to righteous people!

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
And among the people is he who says, Our Lord, give us in this world,
victory and provision, and they do not ask for anything for their Hereafter.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
And among the people is he who says, Our Lord, give us in this world, and he will have no share in the Hereafter.
This is a slave who intended the world, for it is work and hardship.

c: Musa told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding the statement:
h
And among the people is he who says, Our Lord, give us in this world, and he will have no share in the Hereafter.
He said: When the Arabs completed their rituals and stayed in Mina, a man among them would not remember God, but rather he would remember his father? And he was left with no share in this world.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And when you have completed your rites
, remember God
h
as you remember your fathers

or with a greater remembrance, he said: They were three types in those places on that day: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the disbelievers, and the hypocrites. Among the people are those who say, Our Lord, give us in this world, and they have no share in the Hereafter. They only performed Hajj for the sake of this world and to ask for it, they do not want the Hereafter, nor do they believe in it. Among them are those who say, Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good, the verse. He said: The third type is: And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in the life of this world, the verse. As for the meaning of the Creator, we have explained it in other places, and we have mentioned the differences of those who differed in its interpretation, and what is correct with us regarding its meaning with the evidence from the proofs, is that it is the share, which is sufficient for us to repeat it in this place.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the good that God mentioned in this place.
Some of them said: He means by that: And among the people is he who says, Our Lord, give us well-being in this world and well-being in the Hereafter.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding His statement, Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, he said: In this world, well-being, and in the Hereafter, well-being. Qatada said: "And a man said: O God, whatever You were going to punish me with in the Hereafter, hasten it for me in this world, so he became ill with an illness that exhausted him in his bed, so his situation was mentioned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him, and it was said to him: He supplicated for such and such, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one has the strength to bear the punishment of God, but say: "Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." So he said it, and it was only a few days - or a short time - until he recovered.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Saeed bin Al-Hakam told us, he said, Yahya bin Ayoub told us, he said,
m: Humayd said, I heard Anas bin Malik say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited a man who had become like a plucked chick. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Were you supplicating to God for something?’ - or: ‘Ask God for something?’ He said, ‘I said: ‘O God, whatever You are going to punish me with in the Hereafter, punish me with it in this world.’ He said: ‘Glory be to God! Is anyone capable of that or able to bear it? Why didn’t you say: ‘O God, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and save us from the torment of the Fire?’”

x: Others said: Rather, God, the Almighty, meant: good in this context - in this world, knowledge and worship, and in the Hereafter, Paradise.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Ibad told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: “And among them are those who say: ‘Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter.’” He said: Good in this world is knowledge and worship, and in the Hereafter, Paradise.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding the statement: Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire, he said: Worship is in this world, and Paradise is in the Hereafter.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Waqid Al-Attar told us, he said, Ibad bin Al-Awwam told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding the statement: Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good, he said: The good in this world is understanding the Book of God and knowledge.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I heard Sufyan Ath-Thawri say [regarding] this verse: Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, he said: The good in this world is knowledge and good provision, and the good in the Hereafter is Paradise.

x: Others said: The good in this world is wealth, and in the Hereafter is Paradise.

Who said that: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said: And among them is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire,’ he said: These are the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and the believers.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And among them is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good,’ these are the believers. As for the good of this world, it is wealth, and as for the good of the Hereafter, it is Paradise.

x: The correct statement in that, in my opinion, is to say: God, the Most High, informed us about a group of people of faith in Him and His Messenger who performed Hajj to His House, asking their Lord for good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and to protect them from the punishment of the Fire. And good from God, the Most High, may include well-being in the body, livelihood, provision, and other things, as well as knowledge and worship. As for the Hereafter, there is no doubt that it is Paradise, because whoever does not attain it on that day has been deprived of all good deeds and has departed from all meanings of well-being. We only said that this is the most appropriate interpretation of the verse, because God, the Almighty, did not specify in His statement - informing about the one who said that - any of the meanings of goodness, nor did He establish a specific meaning indicating that what is meant by that is some and not others.

What is required from saying about it is what we said: that it is not permissible to specify any of the meanings of that, and to rule for it by its generality over what God has generalized. As for His statement: And save us from the punishment of the Fire, he means by that: avert from us the punishment of the Fire. It is said from it: I Surat Al-Baqarah 2:201 And among them are those who say, "Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." saved him so-and-so, I save him, protection, protection, and protection, extended, and perhaps they said: May God protect you, protection, if you averted harm or misfortune from him.

What He, the Most High, means by His saying: Those is those who say after completing their rituals: Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire, out of their desire for what is with God, the Most High, and their knowledge that all good is from Him, and that grace is in His hand and He gives it to whomever He wills. So He, the Most High, knows that they will have a share and portion of their Hajj and rituals, and a great reward for the work they have earned and endured with their wealth and their lives, and He has given them that without the other group, who suffered what they suffered from the fatigue and toil of their work?
They undertook what they undertook of their travels, without any desire for the reward and recompense with their Lord, but out of a base hope for the worldly gain and seeking its immediate ruins, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And among the people is he who says

, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter, he said: This is a slave who intended this world, for it is work and hardship, “And among them is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’ Those will have a share of what they have earned,” meaning: a portion of their deeds.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding:
h
And among the people is he who says

, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter, they only performed Hajj for the sake of this world and asking, they do not want the Hereafter and do not believe in it. And among them is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire,’ he said, “These are the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers. “Those will have a share of what they have earned,
h
and God is swift in account
.” These people will be rewarded for what they did in this world. As for His statement,
h
And God is swift in account

, He, the Most High, means that He encompasses the deeds of both groups, one of whom asked, Our Lord, give us in this world, and the other asked, Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. So He measured for them the swiftest of accounts, then He will reward each group for their deeds. The Most High described Himself as swift in account, because He, the Most High, counts whatever He counts of the deeds of His servants without crossing one’s fingers, or thinking, or thinking, as the weak and helpless among creation do. However, nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom in either of them escapes Him, then He will reward His servants for all of that. Therefore, He, the Most High, praised Himself for the speed of reckoning, and informed His creation that there is no equal to them, so His reckoning requires a contraction of the hand or a fullness of the chest.

x: He, may He be glorified, means: Remember God with monotheism and glorification on specific days, which are the days of stoning the Jamarat. On that day, He commanded His servants to say Allahu Akbar after the prayers and during the stoning, with each pebble of the Jamarat that is thrown? A Jamarat from the Jamarat. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And remember God during the appointed days
, he said: the days of Tashreeq.

c: Muhammad bin Nafi’ al-Basri told me, he said, Ghundar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And remember God during the appointed days
, he means by the appointed days, the days of Tashreeq, and three days after the sacrifice.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Mu’awiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And remember God during the appointed days
, meaning the days of Tashreeq.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja’far narrated to us, saying: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mukhallad narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He heard him on the day of the departure saying, after he had departed, glorifying God in the mosque, and interpreting:
h
And remember God during the appointed days

c: Ali ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu’awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And remember God during the appointed days
, meaning the days of Tashreeq.

c: Abdul Hamid ibn Bayan al-Sakari narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
And remember God during the appointed days

, he said: They are the days of Tashreeq. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: My father narrated, on the authority of Talha ibn Amr, on the authority of Ata’, similarly. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated, he said: Abu Asim narrated, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, the Almighty:

x: “If someone were to say: ‘When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the days of Mina that they are days of eating, drinking and remembering God, he did not inform his nation that they are the numbered days that God mentioned in His Book. So what is the objection that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meant by his saying: ‘and remembering God’ the known days?” It was said: It is not permissible that he meant that. Because God did not require His remembrance on the known days as He required on the numbered days. Rather, He described the known days, may He be glorified, as days on which the name of God is mentioned over the livestock, so He said: That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of God on known days over what He has provided for them of grazing livestock (al-Hajj 22:27). So He did not require His remembrance on the known days as He required His remembrance on the numbered days, rather He informed that they are the days of His remembrance over the livestock.

It was known, when he said - may God bless him and grant him peace - about the days of Tashreeq: They are days of eating, drinking and remembering God, so he excluded his statement: And remembering God absolutely without condition, nor in addition to the fact that it is a remembrance on the livestock, that he meant by that the remembrance that God mentioned in His Book, so He made it obligatory on His servants absolutely without condition, nor in addition to the meaning of the numbered days, and that if he had intended by that, it would have been sufficient to describe the known days with it, so he would have connected his statement: And remembering to the fact that he remembered God on the livestock that He provided for them, like the way God described that, but he called it by the name of remembrance without connecting it to anything, like the way God Almighty called it by the name of remembrance when He said: And remember God on the numbered days.
This was one of the clearest proofs that he meant by that what God mentioned in His Book, and made obligatory in the appointed days.

Because the blame is only lifted from the worker in what he was required to leave, so he is permitted to do his work by lifting the blame upon him in his work? Or in what he was required to do, so he is permitted to leave it by lifting the blame upon him in leaving it. As for what the worker is required to do, there is no reason to lift the blame upon him in it if it is his work, and his duty is his work. Because it is impossible for the one who is performing an obligation to be in difficulty in performing it, it is permissible to say: We have removed the difficulty for you in it. h
there is no sin upon him

, or: there is no blame upon him, from his obligation of leaving on the second day of the days of Tashreeq, so the difficulty is removed from him in the place, or his obligation of staying until the third day, so the difficulty is removed from him in leaving on the second day. If his obligation was on the second day of the days of Tashreeq, staying until the third day of them, so the difficulty is removed from him in leaving on the second day of them - and that is the haste for which it was said: But whoever hastens within two days,
h
there is no sin upon him
- then there is no meaning in his attributing it to the interpretation of the one who interpreted that
h
There is no sin upon him
, so there is no blame upon him,
h
and whoever delays
h
there is no sin upon him

. Because the one who delays until the third day is only delaying from performing an obligation upon him, abandoning the acceptance of the concession of leaving. There is no reason to say: There is no blame upon you for your standing in performing the duty upon you, for what we described before - or his obligation on the second day is the departure, so he is permitted to stand in the standing until the third day, so there is no meaning to say: There is no blame upon you for hastening the departure which is your obligation and you must do it, for what we mentioned of the reason. Likewise, there is no meaning in the statement of those who said: Its meaning is: So whoever hastens within two days,
h
there is no sin upon him
and there is no blame upon him for his departure, if he avoids killing the game until the end of the third day. Because if that was an acceptable interpretation of its speaker, then his statement:
h
And whoever delays
h
there is no sin upon him

would invalidate his claim. Because there is no disagreement among the Ummah that hunting for the pilgrim after his departure from Mina on the third day is permissible, so what is the reason for removing the blame from him in his statement:
h
And whoever delays
h
there is no sin upon him

, if he delays until the third day and then departs? This is in addition to the consensus of the proof that if the pilgrim throws stones, slaughters, shaves and circumambulates the House, then everything is permissible for him, and the explicit statement of the inherited narration from the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - something similar to that, which: - Hannad bin Al-Sari Al-Hanthali narrated to us, he said:

c: Abdul-Raheem bin Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm, on the authority of Umrah, she said:
m: I asked Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her: When does the pilgrim become permissible? She said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When you have stoned, slaughtered, and shaved your head, everything is lawful for you except women. He said: Al-Zuhri mentioned, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), something similar. As for the one who interpreted that to mean:
h
There is no sin upon him

until the next year, there is no reason to specify a time for that, because it removes the sin from the pilgrim in the coming year without his past sins. Because God, the Most High, did not limit that to negating the sin of a future time by the apparent revelation, nor by the tongue of the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him), rather the apparent meaning of the revelation shows that the one who hastens in the two days and the one who delays, there is no sin upon either of them in the state he is in, and not in any other state. The report from the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) clearly states that when his Hajj ends as he was commanded, he is free from his sins as on the day his mother bore him. In that, from the apparent meaning of the revelation, and the explicit statement of the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him), there is clear evidence of the corruption of the statement of the one who said: The meaning of his statement:
h
There is no sin upon him
is that
h
there is no sin upon him
from the time his Hajj ends until the next year.

x: If someone were to say to us: What is the reason for the lam in His statement:
h
for whoever fears God
? And what is its meaning? It was said: The meaning of the one who brought it is the meaning of his saying:
h
There is no sin upon him
. Because in his saying:
h
There is no sin upon him

there is a meaning: We have reduced his sins and expiated his transgressions, so there was a meaning in that: We made the expiation of sins for whoever feared God in his pilgrimage. So he left out mentioning that we made the expiation of sins, being satisfied with the meaning of his saying:
h
There is no sin upon him
Some of the grammarians of Basra claimed that it is as if when he mentioned this concession, he informed about a matter, so he said:
h
For whoever fears God
, meaning: This is
h
for whoever fears God

Some of them denied that from his saying, and claimed that the attribute must have something to which it is related, because it does not exist by itself, but in what he claimed from the connection of an abandoned statement. So the meaning of the speech according to him was: We said:
h
And whoever delays
h
there is no sin upon him
h
for whoever fears God
, and his saying:
h
And whoever delays
h
there is no sin upon him
took the place of the statement.

Some of the Arabists claimed that the place of dropping the sin is in the one who hastened, so it was made in the one who delayed, which is the one who performed And he did not fall short, like what is made upon the one who falls short, as is said in speech: If you give charity secretly, it is good, and if you reveal it, it is good, and they are different. Because if the one who gives charity publicly does not intend to show off, it is good, even if keeping it secret is better. And in describing the two states of the two who give charity as good, there is no description of one of them as sinful. And God Almighty informed about the two who left by denying the sin from them, and it is impossible for Him to deny from them anything except what was in their leaving it sinful, according to what the speakers of this statement interpreted. And in the consensus of all that if they both left the departure and stayed in Mina, they would not be sinful, what indicates the corruption of the interpretation interpreted by the one from whom we have narrated this statement.
He also said: There is another aspect to it: which is the meaning of the prohibition of the two groups from one group accusing the other of sin, as if he meant by his saying:
h
There is no sin upon him

, that the one who is hasty should not say to the one who is late: You are sinful, nor the one who is late to the one who is hasty: You are sinful, meaning: neither of them accuses the other of sin. This is also an interpretation of the saying of all the people of interpretation that contradicts it, and that is sufficient as evidence of his error.

By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And fear God, O believers, in what He has imposed upon you of His obligations, so fear Him in neglecting them and being negligent in them, and in what He has forbidden you to do in your Hajj and your rituals or to perform them, and in what He has charged you in your ihram for your Hajj to be short in performing it and performing it, and know that you will be gathered to Him, so He will reward you for your deeds - the good among you for his good, and the evildoer for his evil - and He will repay every soul among you for what it has done, and you will not be wronged.

This is a description from God, the Blessed and Exalted, of the hypocrites. God, the Most High, says: And among the people is he whose outward speech and openness please you, O Muhammad, and he calls God as a witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the most quarrelsome of opponents, arguing with falsehood. Then the people of interpretation differed about who this verse was revealed about.

Some of them said: It was revealed about Al-Akhns bin Shuraik, who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and claimed that he wanted to convert to Islam, and he swore that he had come only for that purpose, then he went out and corrupted some of the Muslims' money.
He mentioned who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life
h
and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart

, yet he is the most hostile of opponents. He said: It was revealed about Al-Akhns bin Shuraiq Al-Thaqafi - who was an ally of Banu Zuhra - and he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina and showed him Islam, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was amazed by that from him, and he said: I only came seeking Islam, and God knows that I am truthful, and that is His saying:
h
And he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart

. Then he went out from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and passed by a crop belonging to some Muslims and donkeys, so he burned the crops and hamstrung the donkeys, so God Almighty revealed: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and livestock. As for the most stubborn of quarrels, it is the most crooked of quarrels, and regarding him was revealed: Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (Al-Humazah: 1), and regarding him was revealed: And do not obey every worthless swearer until He became an arrogant and dissolute person (al-Qalam 68:13-15).

x: Others said: Rather, this was revealed regarding a group of hypocrites who spoke about the raid that befell the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Raji'.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said,
m: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, the client of Zaid bin Thabit, he said, Saeed bin Jubair or Ikrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When this raid befell the companions of Khubayb at Raji' between Mecca and Medina, some hypocrites said: Woe to these slanderers who perished like this! They neither stayed in their homes, nor did they deliver the message of their master! Then God the Almighty revealed regarding that of the hypocrites’ speech, and what those people attained of testimony and goodness from God: And of mankind is he whose speech in worldly life pleases you, meaning: what he shows with his tongue of Islam,
h
and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart

, meaning: of hypocrisy, but he is the most hostile of opponents, meaning: he is argumentative when he speaks to you and returns to you, and when he turns away, meaning: he leaves you, “he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and livestock. And God does not love corruption,” meaning: he does not love his work and is not pleased with it, “and when it is said to him, ‘Fear God,’ pride in sin seizes him. Sufficient for him is Hell, and an evil resting place indeed. And of mankind is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God,” those who sold themselves to God by striving in the way of God and fulfilling His right, until they perished in that—meaning this secret.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad,
m: the freed slave of Zaid ibn Thabit, on the authority of Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas—or: on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, said: When the expedition in which Asim and Murthad were present was defeated at Raji’, some men from the hypocrites said: Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant all hypocrites, and what he meant by his saying:
h
And among the people is he whose speech in worldly life pleases you
h
and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart
, is the difference between his secret and his open actions.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Abi Ma’shar told me, he said, my father Abu Ma’shar Najih told me, he said,
m: I heard Saeed Al-Maqburi discussing with Muhammad bin Ka’b, and Saeed said: Indeed, in some books, it is stated that God has servants whose tongues are sweeter than honey, and whose hearts are more bitter than aloes, and they wear for people the cloak of sheep from softness, and they chew the worldly life with religion, and God the Most High said: Do they dare to do so, and are deceived by Me? By My glory, I will send upon them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered. Muhammad bin Ka’b said: This is in the Book of God, may He be glorified. Saeed said: Where is it in the Book of God? He said: The saying of God the Most High: “And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life,
h
and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart

, yet he is the most hostile of opponents. And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and livestock, and God does not like corruption.” Saeed said: Do you know about whom this verse was revealed? Muhammad bin Kaab said: The verse is revealed about a man, then it becomes general.
