c: Yunus bin Abdul A'la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Al-Layth bin Sa'd told me, on the authority of Khalid bin Yazid, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Al-Qurazi, on the authority of Nawf - and he used to read books - he
m: said: I find a description of some people from this nation in the revealed Book of God: A people who fight for the world with religion, their tongues are sweeter than honey, and their hearts are more bitter than aloes, they dress for people like sheep's thorns, but their hearts are the hearts of wolves. So they dare against me! And they are deceived by me! I swear by myself that I will send upon them a trial that will leave the wise among them perplexed. Al-Qurazi said: I pondered it in the Qur’an, and if they were the hypocrites, I found it:
h
And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life
h
and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart
, yet he is the most hostile of opponents, “And of the people is he who worships God on the edge; if good befalls him, he is content therewith.” (al-Hajj 22:11).
b.via: Nawf - and he used to read books - he

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life
h
and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart
, he said: He is the hypocrite.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And of the people is he whose speech pleases you, he said: His outward appearance in this world, and he calls God to witness in the dispute, he only wants the truth.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’, regarding his statement:
h
And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life
h
and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart

, yet he is the most hostile of opponents, he said: This is a servant who had good speech but bad deeds, and he comes to the Messenger of God God’s Messenger (may God’s prayers and peace be upon him) said, And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said,
m: “I said to Ata’: ‘And among the people is he whose speech about worldly life pleases you,
h
and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart
.’” He said, He says something in his heart that is different, and God knows that. And in His saying:
h
And God bears witness to what is in his heart
, there are two ways of reading it: The general reading is:
h
And God bears witness to what is in his heart

, meaning that the hypocrite whose words please the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calls God to witness to what is in his heart that his words are in accordance with his belief, and that he is a believer in God and His Messenger, while he is a liar, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And among the people is he whose words please you in worldly life to And God does not love corruption, “A man used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: O Messenger of God! I bear witness that you have come with the truth and honesty from God! He said: Until the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is pleased with his words, then he says: By God, O Messenger of God, God knows what is in my heart just as my tongue has uttered!” This is what he said:
h
And God bears witness to what is in his heart

, he said: These are the hypocrites, and he recited the words of God, the Most High: When the hypocrites come to you, they say, ‘We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God,’ until he reached Indeed, the hypocrites are liars (al-Munafiqun 63:1), because they bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. Al-Suddi said:
h
And God bears witness to what is in his heart
, he says: God knows that I am truthful and that I want Islam.

c: Musa bin Harun told me that, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, on the authority of Asbat.
m: Mujahid said: And God bears witness in the dispute that he only wants the truth.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me that, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: on his authority.

x: Others read it:
h
And God bears witness to what is in his heart
, meaning:
h
And God bears witness to what is in his heart

of hypocrisy, and that he conceals in his heart something other than what he shows with his tongue, and to his lie in his heart. This is the reading of Ibn Muhaisin. Ibn Abbas interpreted it in that sense, and we mentioned the narration from him in that previously in the hadith of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Yunus ibn Bakir, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, which we mentioned earlier. What we choose in that from the saying of the reciters is the reading of those who read:
h
And God bears witness to what is in his heart
, meaning: He calls God to witness to what is in his heart, due to the consensus of the evidence from the recitation on it.
The most stubborn of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:204 And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life,
h
and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart

, yet he is the most quarrelsome of opponents. men is the one who is fiercely quarrelsome. It is said in the case of a verb from him: You have been stubborn, O this one, and you were not the most pleasant, so you give birth to stubbornness and stubbornness. If he defeats the one who is arguing with him, then it is said about him: You have defeated so-and-so, so you have defeated him.

i: From this comes the saying of the poet:
x: Then I will destroy them with the destruction that will befall the peers of the opponents.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: Its interpretation is: He is a debater.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad told me, he said: Saʿid bin Jubayr or ʿIkrimah told me, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
And He is the most fierce of opponents
, meaning: He is a debater, if he speaks to you and argues with you.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He is the most fierce of opponents
, he means: He is very harsh in disobeying God, he debates with falsehood, and if you wish you will see him knowledgeable in tongue but ignorant of action, he speaks with wisdom but acts with sin.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muʿammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And He is the most fierce of opponents
, he said: He debates with falsehood.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: He is not straight in his argument, but crooked.

Who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And he is the most stubborn of opponents, he said: An oppressor who does not stand upright.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abdullah bin Katheer told me, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The most stubborn of opponents is the one who does not stand upright in his dispute.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: The most stubborn of opponents, the most crooked of opponents.

x: Both of these sayings are close in meaning, because crookedness in the dispute comes from argument and stubbornness.
Others said: The meaning of this is: He is lying in what he said.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Al-Hasan.
m: He said: The one who is stubborn in his quarrel and speaks falsely. This statement may have the same meaning as the first two statements, if the speaker meant that he argues with falsehood and lies, arguing and deviating from the truth. As for al-Khasam, it is a source from the saying of the speaker: I argued with so-and-so with an argument and a dispute. This is report from God Almighty about the hypocrite who informed his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he is pleased when he speaks with his speech and logic, and God testifies that he is right in what he says, due to the intensity of his argument and dispute with falsehood and lies.

evidence.text: And in His saying: And God bears witness to what is in his heart, there are two ways of reading it: The general reading is: And God bears witness to what is in his heart, meaning that the hypocrite whose words please the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calls God to witness to what is in his heart that his words are in accordance with his belief, and that he is a believer in God and His Messenger, while he is a liar, as:

Others read it: And God bears witness to what is in his heart, meaning: And God bears witness to what is in his heart of hypocrisy, and that he conceals in his heart something other than what he shows with his tongue, and to his lie in his heart.
This is the reading of Ibn Muhaisin.

What we choose in that from the saying of the reciters is the reading of those who read: And God bears witness to what is in his heart, meaning: He calls God to witness to what is in his heart, due to the consensus of the evidence from the recitation on it.

x: What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
And when he turns away
, is when this hypocrite turns away from you, O Muhammad, turning away from you, as:

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, he said, Saʿid ibn Jubayr or ʿIkrimah narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
And when he turns away
, he said: meaning: and when he leaves you, he strives. And some of them said: and when he becomes angry.

x: Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said
m: about His statement:
h
And when he turns away

, he said: When he becomes angry. So the meaning of the verse is: And when this hypocrite leaves you, O Muhammad, angry, he will do on earth what God has forbidden him, and he will try to disobey God, cut off the road, and corrupt the path for God’s servants, as we mentioned earlier about the actions of Al-Akhns bin Shuraik Al-Thaqafi, about whom Al-Suddi mentioned that this verse was revealed, of burning the crops of the Muslims and killing them. And the word sai in Arabic means work, and it is said from it: So-and-so is striving for his family, meaning: he works, so with what… It benefits them, and from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: He sought Kindah in a way that was not consistent with Qais, so he harmed its enemy and built for it Meaning by that: He did good deeds for them. And as we said about that, Mujahid used to say.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And when he turns away
, he strives, he said: He worked. And the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the corruption that God, the Almighty, attributed to this hypocrite.

x: Some of them said: Its interpretation is what we said about it: From his cutting off the road and frightening the wayfarer, as we mentioned before about the action of Al-Akhns bin Shuraik. And some of them said: Rather, the meaning of that is: He severed the ties of kinship and shed the blood of Muslims.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He strived throughout the land to cause corruption therein
, he severed the ties of kinship and shed the blood of Muslims.

x: So if it is said: Why did you not do such and such! Next: I draw closer to God the Almighty through him.

The correct thing to say about that is that God the Blessed and Exalted described this hypocrite as if he turned away from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and he would commit corruption on God’s earth. Corruption may include all sins. This is because committing sins is corruption on earth, so God did not specify his description with some meanings of corruption over others. It is possible that this corruption on his part was in the sense of highway robbery, and it is possible that it was otherwise. Whichever of these was on his part, it was corruption on earth, because that on his part is a sin against God the Almighty. However, what is more similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation is that he was highway robbery and frightening people. This is because God the Almighty described him in the context of the verse as striving throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and offspring, and that is by an act that frightens people, more similar to the act of severing family ties.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the reason for the destruction of this hypocrite whom God described with the description of destroying crops and offspring.
Some of them said: That was from him burning the crops of a group of Muslims and hamstringing their donkeys.

m: Musa bin Harun told me that, ʿAmr bin Hammad told me that, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi.

x: Others said: What Abu Kurayb told us that, ʿUthman told us that, Al-Nadr bin Arabi told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And when he turns away

, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and offspring (30:41). He said: When he turns away, he strives throughout the land with aggression and injustice, so God withholds the rain thereby, destroying crops and offspring. God does not love corruption. He said: Then Mujahid recited: Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned so that He may let them taste some of what they have done that they may return (30:41). He said: Then he said: By God, it is not your sea, but every village on running water is a sea. What Mujahid said, even if it was a doctrine of interpretation that the verse could bear, then what is more similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation than the interpretation is what we mentioned from al-Suddi, so that is why we chose it.

As for the tillage, it is the crop, and the offspring is the offspring and children. And his destruction of the crop is his burning it. It may be possible that it was as Mujahid said, by the withholding of rain because of his disobedience to his Lord and his efforts to spread corruption in the land. It may be possible that it was by his killing those who were in charge of it and those who were in charge of it until it was corrupted and destroyed. Likewise, it is possible in the meaning of his destruction of the offspring: that it was by his killing his mothers or fathers from whom the offspring comes, so by his Surat Al-Baqarah 2:205
h
And when he turns away

, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And God does not like corruption. killing the fathers and mothers their offspring would be cut off. It may be possible that it is as Mujahid said, but even if the verse could bear it, what is more appropriate to its apparent meaning is what al-Suddi said.

However, al-Suddi mentioned that the one about whom this verse was revealed was his killing of the donkeys of the people from among the Muslims and his burning of their crops. And even if it is permissible for it to be so, it is not invalid that the verse was revealed about him, and what is meant by it is everyone who follows his path in killing every animal that he killed that is not permissible to kill under any circumstances, and that is permissible to kill in some cases - if he killed it unjustly. Rather, it is so in my opinion, because God, the Blessed and Exalted, did not specify one thing over another, but rather He spared it. And what we said about the generality of that was said by a group of the people of interpretation.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya and Abd al-Rahman told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Tamimi:
m: that he asked Ibn Abbas:
h
And destroys the crops and the offspring
He said: The offspring of every animal.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Atiyyah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Tamimi
m: that he asked Ibn Abbas, he said: I said: What do you think of His statement: the crops and the offspring? He said: The tillage is your tillage, and the offspring is the offspring of every animal.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas about the tillage and the offspring, and he said: The tillage is what you till, and the offspring is the offspring of every animal.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man from Tamim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And destroy the tillage and the offspring, the offspring of every animal and people as well.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And destroy the tillage, he said: the plants of the earth, and the offspring of every animal that walks, of people and animals.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And destroys the crops
, he said: the plants of the earth, and the offspring, the offspring of everything.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir,
m: On the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said: The crops are the plants, and the offspring are the offspring of every animal.

c: I was told on the authority of Ammar ibn Al-Hasan,
m: he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ: And the crops will perish, he said: The crops that people till are the plants of the earth, and the offspring are the offspring of every animal.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I said to ʿAta’:
h
And destroys the crops and the offspring

. He said: The crops are the plants, and the offspring of people and livestock. He said: O He kills the offspring of people and livestock. He said: And Mujahid said: He seeks in the land the destruction of the crops - the plants of the earth - and the offspring of everything from Animal.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak
m: regarding his statement:
h
And destroys the crops and the offspring
, he said: The crops are the origin, and the offspring are every animal and people are among them.

c: Ibn Abd Al-Raheem Al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, he said,
m: Saeed bin Abd Al-Aziz was asked about the corruption of the crops and the offspring and what are they: which crops, and which offspring? Saeed said: Makhul said: The crops are what you cultivate, and as for the offspring, the offspring of everything.

x: Some of the reciters have read:
h
And destroys the crops and the offspring
, raising he destroys, meaning: And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life, and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the most hostile of opponents,
h
and destroys the crops and the offspring
h
and when he turns away

, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein, and God does not like corruption, so he responds to he destroys and He calls God to witness as a kindness to him. This is an invalid reading in my opinion, even though it has a way out in Arabic, because it contradicts what is agreed upon by the evidence from the reading in this regard, the reading and destroy the crops and the offspring and that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b and his copy of the Qur’an - as he mentioned to us - it is to corrupt it and destroy the crops and the offspring.
This is one of the clearest proofs for the correctness of the reading of those who read it: and destroy in the accusative case, in apposition to to corrupt it.

By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: God does not love sins, blocking the way, and frightening the road. Corruption is a verbal noun from the saying: blocking something corrupts, similar to their saying: he went, he went, he went. Some Arabs make the verbal noun of corrupt corrupt, and the verbal noun of dhahab, he went, he went.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: Some of the reciters have read: And destroys the crops and the offspring, raising he destroys, meaning: And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life, and he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the most hostile of opponents, and destroys the crops and the offspring, and when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein, and God does not like corruption, so he responds to he destroys and He calls God to witness as a kindness to him.

This is an invalid reading in my opinion, even though it has a way out in Arabic, because it contradicts what is agreed upon by the evidence from the reading in this regard, the reading and destroy the crops and the offspring and that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b and his copy of the Qur’an - as he mentioned to us - it is to corrupt it and destroy the crops and the offspring.
This is one of the clearest proofs for the correctness of the reading of those who read it: and destroy in the accusative case, in apposition to to corrupt it.

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And if it is said to this hypocrite whom He described as He described His Prophet, peace be upon him, and informed him that he likes what He said in this worldly life: Fear God and fear Him in your corruption in God's land, and your striving in it with what God has forbidden you of His disobedience, and your destruction of the crops of the Muslims and their offspring - he will be arrogant and will be overcome with pride and zeal for what God has forbidden him, and he will persist in his error and misguidance. God, may His praise be exalted, said: So He has spared him the punishment of his error and misguidance. He will burn in the fire of Hell,
h
and what an evil resting place
it is for those who burn in it.
The people of interpretation differed as to who is meant by this verse.
Some of them said: It means every immoral person and hypocrite.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzayʿ told me, he said, Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman told us, he said, Bastam ibn Muslim told us, he said, Abu Rajaʿ al-ʿAttardi told us, he said:
m: I heard Ali regarding this verse: And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life to
h
And God is Kind to His servants
, Ali said: They fought, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when it is said to him
, ‘Fear God,’ pride in sin seizes him to His statement:
h
And God is Kind to His servants

, he said: When ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him finished reciting the rosary, he would enter his resting place and send for some young men who had read the Qur’an, among them Ibn Abbas and the nephew of ʿUyaynah. They would come and read the Qur’an and study it, and when it was time for the siesta, he would leave. He said: So they passed by this verse:
h
And when it is said to him
, ‘Fear God,’ pride in sin takes hold of him, “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God.
h
And God is Kind to His servants

,” Ibn Zayd said: And these are the mujahidin in the way of God. Ibn Abbas said to some of those who were beside him: The two men fought! Umar did not say anything, so he said: What did you say? He said: Nothing, O Commander of the Faithful! He said: What did you say? The two men fought? He said: When Ibn Abbas saw that, he said: I see here someone who, when commanded to fear God, is seized by pride in sin. And I see someone who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. This one stands and commands this one to fear God, but if he does not accept and pride in sin takes hold of him, this one says: And I will sell myself! So fight him, and the two men fought! Umar said: Your land belongs to God 1 O Ibn Abbas.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant Al-Akhns bin Shuraik. We have already mentioned those who said that before. As for his saying:
h
And what an evil resting place

, he means: And what an evil bed and cradle is Hell, which God Almighty has threatened this hypocrite with, and which he has prepared for himself through his hypocrisy, immorality, and rebellion against his Lord.

He, may His praise be exalted, means: And among the people is he who sells himself for what God has promised to those who strive in His cause and buys for it their souls by His saying: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise (al-Tawbah 9:111). We have already demonstrated that the meaning of bought is sold, in other than this place, for something that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. As for His saying:
h
Seeking the pleasure of God

, it means that this buyer buys, if he buys, he seeks the pleasure of God, and He puts seeking in the accusative case by His saying: buys. So it is as if He said: And among the people is he who sells himself, for the sake of
h
seeking the pleasure of God
, then He left for the sake of and made the verb work on it.
Some of the Arabists claimed that He put that in the accusative case on the verb, on buys, as if He said: For the sake of
h
seeking the pleasure of God

, so when He removed the lam, it made the verb work, and He said: And similar to it is: He feared death (al-Baqarah 2:19), and the poet, who is Hatim, said: Forgive the faults of the generous person for his hoarding, and turn away from the words of the mean person out of generosity. He said: When the lam is removed, the verb is applied to it.

Some of them said: Any verbal noun that is placed in the place of the condition, and in the place of an, then the ba and the lam are appropriate in it, like you say: I came to you from fear of evil - and for fear of evil - and because I feared evil, so the description is not known, so it is deleted and the verbal noun is used in its place. He said: If the description was a single letter, it would not be permissible to delete it, just as it is not permissible for someone who said: I did this for you and for so-and-so to drop the lam. Then the people of interpretation differed about who this verse was revealed about, and who it meant.
Some of them said: It was revealed about the Muhajireen and the Ansar, and it meant the mujahideen in the way of God.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Husayn bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God
, he said: The Muhajireen and the Ansar.

x: Some of them said: It was revealed about specific men from the Muhajireen.

Who said that: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Hussein narrated to us, Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah: And of the people is he who sells himself,
h
seeking the pleasure of God

, he said: It was revealed about Suhaib bin Sinan, Abu Dharr Al-Ghifari Jundub bin Al-Sakn. The people of Abu Dharr captured Abu Dharr, so he escaped from them and went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he returned as a migrant, they confronted him, and they were at Marr Al-Dhahran, so he also escaped until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for Suhaib, his people took him, so he ransomed himself from them with his money. Then he went out as a migrant, and Qunfudh bin Umair bin Jud’an caught up with him, so he gave him what remained of his money and set him free.
Narrated on the authority of Ammar, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among mankind is he who sells himself
h
seeking the pleasure of God

(al-Baqarah 2:14), he said: There was a man from the people of Mecca who had converted to Islam and wanted to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and migrate to Medina, but they prevented him and detained him. He said to them: I will give you my house and my wealth and whatever I had! Surat Al-Baqarah 2:207 And among the people is he who sells himself,
h
seeking the pleasure of God

. And God is kind to His servants. So leave me alone, so join this man! But they refused. Then some of them said to them: Take from him whatever he had and leave him alone! So they did, so he gave them his house and his wealth, then he left. Then God, the Almighty, revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina:
h
And among mankind is he who sells himself
h
seeking the pleasure of God

(al-Baqarah 2:14). When he approached Medina, ʿUmar met him with some men, and ʿUmar said to him: The sale is profitable! He said: And your sale, so do not lose! He said: What is that? He said: Such and such was revealed concerning you.

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is everyone who sells himself in obedience to God and jihad in His cause, or enjoining what is right.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Husayn bin al-Hasan Abu Abdullah told us, he said, Abu Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad
m: said: Hisham bin Amir charged the ranks until he tore them, so they said: He threw himself into destruction!! Abu Hurairah said: And among the people is he who sells himself,
h
seeking the pleasure of God

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Mus’ab bin Al-Miqdam narrated to us, he said: Israel narrated to us, on the authority of Tariq bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, on the authority of Al-Mughirah, he said:
m: Umar sent an army and they besieged the people of Hisn, and a man from Bajila came forward and fought and was killed, so most of the people said about him: He threw himself into destruction! He said: When that reached Umar, Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him, he said: They lied! Doesn’t God the Almighty say: “And among the people is he who sells himself,
h
seeking the pleasure of God
. And God is Kind to His servants”?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Dawud told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Hisham bin Amir charged the row until he split it, and Abu Hurairah said: And among the people is he who sells himself,
h
seeking the pleasure of God

c: Suwar bin Abdullah Al-Anbari told us, Abdurrahman bin Mahdi told us, Hazm bin Abi Hazm told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan recite: “And among the people is he who sells himself,
h
seeking the pleasure of God

. And God is Kind to His servants.” Do you know why it was revealed? It was revealed about a Muslim meeting an unbeliever and he said to him: Say: There is no god but God, and if you say it, your blood and wealth will be protected except for a right due to them! But he refused to say it, so the Muslim said: By God, I will sell myself for God! So he went forward and fought! Until he was killed.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Ziyad bin Abi Muslim told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Khalil, he said:
m: Umar heard a man recite this verse: And among the people is he who sells himself,
h
seeking the pleasure of God
. Umar said: To God we belong and to Him we shall return! A man enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong, and he was killed.

x: What is more appropriate to the apparent meaning of this verse than the interpretation is what was narrated from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, and Ibn ʿAbbas may God be pleased with them, that it refers to enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. This is because God, the Most High, described two groups: One of them is a hypocrite who says with his tongue the opposite of what is in his heart, and if he is able to disobey God, he does it, and if he is not able to, he seeks it, and if he is forbidden, pride in sinning takes hold of him. The other of them is a seller of his soul, seeking God’s pleasure. So the apparent interpretation is that the group described as having sold their souls to God and sought His pleasure, only bought themselves to attack the wicked group seeking God’s pleasure. So this is the most likely and most apparent interpretation of the verse?

As for what was narrated about the revelation of the verse concerning Suhaib, this is not objectionable, since it was not denied that a verse could be revealed from God to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, for any reason, and what is meant by it is everyone who is included in its apparent meaning. The correct thing to say about this is that God, the Exalted, described someone who sells himself seeking His pleasure, so everyone who sells himself in His obedience until he is killed in it, or is killed even if he is not killed, what is meant by his owner is: And among the people is he who sells himself,
h
seeking the pleasure of God

- whether that was in jihad against the enemy of the Muslims, or in enjoining what is right or forbidding what is wrong. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of compassion, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here, and that it is the tenderness of mercy.

This means: God has vast mercy for His servant who sells himself to Him in the struggle against those who oppose Him in His command from among the people of polytheism and immorality, and for His other believing servants in their immediate and later life. He will fulfill for them the reward for what they did in obeying Him in this world, and He will make them dwell in His gardens for what they did therein to please Him.

evidence.text: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Ziyad bin Abi Muslim told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Khalil, he said: Umar heard a man recite this verse: And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God.

x: The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of "peace" in this place.
Some of them said: It means Islam.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin ʿAmr told me, he said: Abu ʿAsim told us, on the authority of ʿIsa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God the Almighty: "
h
Enter into peace
," he said: Enter into Islam.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muʿmar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Enter into peace
,” he said: Enter into Islam.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Enter into peace completely
,” he said: Peace is Islam.

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: h
Enter into peace
,” he said: Into Islam.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of al-Nadr ibn Arabi, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Enter into Islam.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “
h
Enter into peace
,” He said: Peace is Islam.

c: I was told by Al-Husayn bin Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid who said, Ubayd bin Sulayman told us who said, I heard Adh-Dahhak say, “
h
Enter into peace
,” into Islam.

x: Others said, “Rather, it means: Enter into obedience.”
Mention of those who said that:

c: I was told by Ammar
m: who said, Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, from his father, from Ar-Rabi’: “
h
Enter into peace
,” meaning: Enter into obedience. The reciters differed in the recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of the people of Hijaz read it as “
h
Enter into peace
” with a fatha on the seen, and the majority of the reciters of the Kufians read it with a kasra on the seen. As for those who opened the seen in as-Salam, they interpreted it as Musalama, meaning:
h
Enter into peace
and reconciliation and abandon war and paying the jizyah. As for those who read it with a kasra on the seen, they differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them interpreted it as Islam, meaning:
h
Enter into Islam completely

Some of them direct it to reconciliation, meaning: enter into reconciliation. And he cites as evidence that the letter seen is broken and it means reconciliation, the words of Zuhair ibn Abi Salma: You both said that if we achieve peace with money and a known matter, we will surrender. The first interpretation of his saying: “
h
Enter into peace
” is the saying of those who said: It means:
h
Enter into Islam completely

. As for the one who reads it with a kasra on the seen, which is more correct than the two readings, because if it is read in this way - even though it may have the meaning of peace - then the meaning of Islam and the continuation of a good matter among the Arabs is more prevalent than peace and reconciliation.

i: And the verse of my brother Kinda is recited:
x: I called my tribe to peace when I saw them turn their backs By breaking the seen, meaning: calling them to Islam when they apostatized, and that was when Kinda apostatized with Al-Ash'ath, after the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Abu Amr bin Al-Ala used to read all the mentions of "peace" in the Qur'an with the fatha, except for this one in Surat Al-Baqarah, as he used to specify it with the kasra on its seen, directing its meaning to Islam and not to anything else. We chose what we chose from the interpretation of his statement: "
h
Enter into peace

", and we diverted its meaning to Islam, because the verse is addressed to the believers, so the address, since it was addressed to the believers, would not go beyond one of two things: Either it is addressed to the believers in Muhammad who believed in him and what he brought. If that is the case, then there is no meaning in saying to them, who are the people of faith: Enter into the peace of the believers and make peace with them, because peace and reconciliation are only commanded to those who are at war by abandoning war, but as for the clients, it is not permissible to say to them: Make peace with so-and-so, and there is no war or enmity between them.

Or is it addressed to the people of faith in the prophets who came before Muhammad, peace be upon him, who believed in them and what they brought from God, but denied Muhammad and his prophethood, and it was said to them: “
h
Enter into peace

,” meaning Islam? Not peace. Because God, the Almighty, only commanded His servants to believe in Him and in His Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, and what he brought, and to that He called them, without peace and reconciliation. Rather, He forbade His Prophet, peace be upon him, in some cases from Surat Al-Baqarah 2:208 O you who have believed,
h
enter into Islam completely
and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. calling the people of disbelief to peace, saying:
“So do not weaken and call for peace while you are the upper hand and God is with you”

Rather, He permitted him, peace be upon him, in some cases, if they called him to peace, to initiate the reconciliation, so He, the Most High, said to him: “But if they incline to peace, then incline to it” (al-Anfal 8:61).
As for their call to peace initially, it is not found in the Qur’an, so it is permissible to direct his statement: “
h
Enter into peace
” to that.
If someone were to say to us: Which of these two groups was called to Islam entirely? It would be said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: The believers in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought were called to it.
Others said: It would be said: The believers in the prophets before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who denied Muhammad were called to it.
What is the reason for the believer’s call to Islam through Muhammad and what he brought?

The reason for his call to that is the command to him to act according to all of its laws, and to establish all of its rulings and limits, without neglecting some of it and acting according to some of it. If that is its meaning, then his statement: entirely is an attribute of “peace,” and its interpretation would be: Enter into acting according to all of the meanings of peace, and do not neglect any of it, O people of faith in Muhammad and what he brought. And similar to this meaning was what Ikrimah used to say in interpreting that.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
Enter into peace completely

,” he said: It was revealed about Tha’laba, Abdullah bin Salam, Ibn Yamin, Asad and Asid, the sons of Ka’b, Sa’iyyah bin Amr, and Qays bin Zayd - all of them Jews - they said: O Messenger of God, Saturday is a day that we used to venerate, so leave us and let us celebrate it! And the Torah is the Book of God, so leave us and let us stand in prayer for it at night! So it was revealed: “O you who have believed,
h
enter into peace completely

and do not follow the footsteps of Satan.” Ikrimah has clearly stated the meaning of what we have said about that, that the interpretation of that is a call to the believers to reject all meanings that are not part of the rulings of Islam, and to act according to all the laws of Islam, and to forbid neglecting any of its limits.

x: Others said: Rather, the group that was called to peace and was told: Enter into it, by this verse, are the People of the Book, and they were commanded to enter Islam.
Those who said that are mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Abi Jurayj narrated to me, he said, Ibn Abbas said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Enter into Islam completely
, meaning the People of the Book.

c: I was told by Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: he said, I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl ibn Khalid say, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding the statement of God the Almighty:
h
Enter into Islam completely
, he said: meaning the People of the Book.

x: The correct statement regarding that, in my opinion, is that God the Almighty commanded those who believed to enter into the implementation of all the laws of Islam. And those who believed may be included in those who believed those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what he brought, and those who believed in the prophets and messengers before him and in what they brought. God the Almighty called both groups to implement the laws of Islam and its limits, and to preserve the obligations that He imposed, and He forbade them from neglecting any of that. So the verse is general for everyone included in the name of faith, so there is no reason for some to be specific to it and not others.
And similar to the interpretation that we mentioned about that, Mujahid used to say:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty: “
h
Enter into peace completely
,” he said: Enter Islam completely, enter into all the deeds.

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His statement: completely, is general, all together, as: - Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, ʿAbd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muʿammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His statement: “in peace completely,” he said: all together.

c: Musa told us, he said, ʿAmr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: “in peace completely,” He said: All together.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ: In Islam, all together. He said: All together. And on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, the same.

c: Abu Kurayb told us,
m: who said: Wakiʿ ibn Al-Jarrah told us, on the authority of An-Nadr, on the authority of Mujahid: Enter Islam all together.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated to me, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, Ibn Abbas narrated to us:
m: All of them, all together.

c: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ibn Zayd narrated to us:
m: All of them, all together, and he recited: And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together (al-Tawbah 9:36), all together. I narrated from Al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid, he said:

c: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement: Enter into Islam all together, he said: All together.

x: By that, the Most High means: O believers, act according to all the laws of Islam, and enter into belief in it in word and deed, and leave the ways and traces of Satan from following them, for he is a clear enemy to you in his enmity. And the way of Satan that He forbade them from following is that which contradicts the rulings of Islam and its laws, including the celebration of the Sabbath, and all the traditions of the people of religions that contradict the religion of Islam. I have explained the meaning of the steps with evidence that testifies to its correctness in the past, so I hated to repeat it in this place.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the recitation of that.
The majority of the reciters of the people of Hijaz read it as “Enter into peace” with a fatha on the seen, and the majority of the reciters of the Kufians read it with a kasra on the seen.
As for those who read it with a kasra on the seen, they differed in its interpretation.

As for the one who reads it with a kasra on the seen, which is more correct than the two readings, because if it is read in this way - even though it may have the meaning of peace - then the meaning of Islam and the continuation of a good matter among the Arabs is more prevalent than peace and reconciliation.

And the verse of my brother Kinda is recited: I called my tribe to peace when I saw them turn their backs By breaking the seen, meaning: calling them to Islam when they apostatized, and that was when Kinda apostatized with Al-Ash'ath, after the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: If you err on the truth, and go astray from it, and oppose Islam and its laws, after My proofs and clear evidence of guidance have come to you, and the correctness of the matter of Islam has become clear to you with the evidence that has cut off your excuse, O believers, then know that God is Almighty, and nothing can prevent Him from taking revenge on you, and nothing can prevent Him from punishing you for your opposition to His command and disobedience to Him. He is wise in what He does to you of His punishment for your disobedience to Him, after He has established the proof against you, and in other matters of His. A number of the people of interpretation have said that the clear proofs are Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an. This is close to what we have said in the interpretation of that. Because Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an are among the proofs of God against those who were addressed by these two verses.

However, what we have said in the interpretation of that is more correct, because God, may He be glorified, has provided evidence against those rabbis of the People of the Book who opposed Islam, with what He entrusted to them in the Torah and the Gospel, and what came before them on the tongues of their prophets with the commandment of it. So that and other proofs of God, may He be glorified and exalted, against them, along with what is required of them from the proofs of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur’an. Therefore, we have chosen what we have chosen from the interpretation of that. And the people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said in that.
Mention of the statements of those who have said in the interpretation of His statement:
h
If you slip

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: regarding His statement:
h
If you slip
, he says: If you go astray.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father,
m: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
If you slip
, he said: Slipping is polytheism. He mentioned the statements of those who interpreted his statement:
h
After the clear proofs have come to you

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
After the clear proofs have come to you
, he said: After Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to you.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
If you slip
h
after the clear proofs have come to you
, he said: Islam and the Qur’an.

c: I was told on the authority of Ammar,
m: he said: Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’: So know that God is Exalted in Might and Wise, he said: Exalted in His vengeance, Wise in His command.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Do those who disbelieve in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought wait for anything but that God should come to them in the canopies of clouds and the angels? Then the readings differed in the reading of His statement: and the angels.

Some of them read: Do they wait for anything but that God should come to them in the canopies of clouds and the angels, in the nominative case, in apposition with the angels to the name of God, the Blessed and Most High, meaning: Do they wait for anything but that God should come to them? And the angels are in canopies of clouds.
Who said that: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, on the authority of Abu Ubaid al-Qasim bin Salam, who said:

c: Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar al-Razi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah, who said
m: - in the reading of Abi bin Ka’b:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them

with the angels in canopies of clouds? - He said: The angels come in canopies of clouds, and God Almighty comes as He wills. I narrated this hadith on the authority of Ammar bin al-Hasan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’, regarding his statement:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds and the angels
? and the verse. Abu Jaafar al-Razi said: In some readings it is:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them
with the angels in canopies of clouds, like His statement:
h
And the Day the heaven will split open with clouds and the angels will be sent down gradually
? (al-Furqan 25:25).

x: Others read it as:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds and the angels

? In the accusative case, as an apposition. By angels, on shadows, meaning: Do they wait for anything but that God should come to them in the shadows of clouds and in the angels? Likewise, the reading of shadows differed: Some of them read it: in shadows, and some of them: in shadows. Whoever read it in shadows, then he directed it to the fact that it is the plural of shadow, and shadow, the plural of shadows and shadows, just as lightness is pluralized as khalal and khalal, and jalal is pluralized as jalal and jalal. As for the one who read it in shadows, then he made it the plural of shadow, as we mentioned from their plural of khalal as khalal. It may be possible that his reader was like that, he directed it to the fact that it is the plural of shadow, because shadow and shadow can both be plurals of shadows.

The correct reading in that, in my opinion, is: Do they wait for anything but that God should come to them in the shadows of clouds, according to the hadith "It was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There are windows in the clouds in which God comes surrounded". He indicated by his saying: Taqāt that they are shades, not shadows, because the singular of thull is Azlāt, which is taq, and following the script of the Mushaf. Likewise, what is obligatory in everything whose meanings agree but whose reading differs is the recitation, and there is no indication for one of the two readings that separates it from the other other than the difference in the script of the Mushaf, then what should be preferred is the recitation of it that agrees with the script of the Mushaf. As for what is the first of the two readings in or the angels, the correct one is to raise it, in apposition to the name of God, the Blessed and Most High, meaning:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them

in the shades of clouds, or anything but that the angels should come to them, according to what was narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka’b. Because God, the Most High, has informed in more than one place in His Book that the angels will come to them.
He, the Most High, said:
h
And your Lord will come with angels

, rank upon rank (al-Fajr 89:22), and He said: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them or your Lord should come or some of the signs of your Lord should come? (al-An’am 6:158). If someone is confused about God’s statement, the Most High: And the angels, rank upon rank, and thinks that its meaning is different from the meaning of His statement,
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds and the angels

? since His statement, and the angels in this verse is in the form of a collective noun, and in the other it is in the form of a singular noun, then that is a mistake in thinking. This is because the angel in His statement,
h
And your Lord will come with angels

, means all and the meaning of the angels. The Arabs mention the singular in the sense of all, so they say: So-and-so has many dirhams and dinars, meaning: dirhams and dinars, and the camel and the sheep perished, meaning a group of camels and sheep.
Likewise, his statement:
h
And the angels means the angels
Then the people of interpretation differed regarding his statement:
h
The clouds have fallen
, and whether it is related to the action of God, the Most High, or to the action of the angels. And who comes in it?

Some of them said: It is related to the action of God, and its meaning is: Do they wait for anything but that God should come to them in the shade of the clouds, and that the angels should come to them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin ʿAmr told me, he said: Abu ʿAsim told us, on the authority of ʿIsa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High: Do they wait for anything but that God should come to them in the shade of the clouds? He said: It is other than the clouds, it was only for the Children of Israel in their wandering when they went astray, and it is the one in which God will come on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muʿmar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Do they wait for anything but that God should come to them in the shade of the clouds? He said: God will come to them and the angels will come to them at death.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ikrimah said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds

? He said: Glasses of clouds, and the angels are around Him. Ibn Jurayj said: And others said: And the angels are with death. And this statement of Ikrimah, even if it is in agreement with the statement of those who said that His statement:
h
In canopies of clouds is related to the action of the Lord

, the Blessed and Exalted, which we mentioned earlier, it is different from it in the description of the angels. That is because the required reading, according to the interpretation of this statement of Ikrimah regarding the angels, is the lowering, because he interpreted the verse:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds
and with the angels. Because he claimed that God, the Most High, comes in canopies of clouds and the angels are around Him. This is if the meaning of his statement:
h
And the angels around Him is that they are around the clouds
, and the ha’ in around Him is from the mention of the clouds. And if the meaning of his statement:
h
And the angels around him is that they are around the Lord

, Blessed and Exalted be He, and he made the ha in around him from the mention of the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, then his statement is similar to the statement of others whose statement we have mentioned, without disagreeing with them in that. And others said: Rather, his statement: in the shades of clouds is from the connection of the action of the angels, and the angels only come in it. As for the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, He comes as He wills.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on Al-Rabi’ regarding his statement:
h
Do they await except that God should come to them in the shades of clouds and the angels the verse

, he said: That is on the Day of Resurrection, the angels will come to them in the shades of clouds. He said: The angels come in the shades of clouds, and the Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, comes as He wills.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of his statement: in the shades of clouds that it is related to the action of the Lord Almighty, and that its meaning is:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them
in the shades of clouds and the angels should come to them, because:

c: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Zamaʿah ibn Salih, on the authority of Salamah ibn Wahram, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, among the clouds are windows in which God comes surrounded, and that is his statement:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them in the shades of clouds and the angels and the matter has been decided
? As for the meaning of his statement:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them in the shades of clouds and the angels and the matter has been decided

? It is: they do not await. We have explained that with its reasons in what has preceded in this book of ours before. Then there was a difference of opinion regarding the description of the coming of the Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, which He mentioned in His statement:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them

x: Some of them said: There is no description for that other than that with which He described Himself, the Almighty and Majestic, of coming, arrival, and descent. And it is not permissible to force anyone to speak about that except with information from God, the Almighty and Majestic, or from a sent Messenger. As for speaking about the attributes and names of God, it is not permissible for anyone in terms of extraction except with what we have mentioned.

i: Others said:
x: His coming, the Almighty and Majestic, is similar to what is experienced from the coming of the one who comes from one place to another, and his moving from one place to another. Others said: The meaning of His statement:
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them
He means by it: Do they await anything but that God’s command should come to them, as it is said: We feared that the Banu Umayyah would come to us, meaning: their judgment.
Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Do they await anything but that His reward, reckoning, and punishment should come to them, as God, the Almighty and Majestic, said:
Rather, it is the plotting of night and day

and as it is said: The governor cut off the thief or struck him, but his helpers cut him off. We have already explained the meaning of the clouds in the past of this book of ours, so there is no need to repeat it. Because its meaning here is the same as its meaning there.

The meaning of the statement then is: Do those who abandon entering into peace completely, and follow the footsteps of Satan, wait for God to come to them in the shadows of the clouds, and decide in their matter what He will decide?

c: Abu Kuraib narrated that Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘You will stand in one place on the Day of Resurrection for a period of seventy years. No one will look at you and no judgment will be passed between you. You will be stopped, and you will weep until your tears stop, then Surat Al-Baqarah 2:210
h
Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds and the angels

, and the matter should be decided? And to God are all matters returned. you will shed blood, and you will weep until it reaches your chins, or you will be restrained and you will cry out and say: Who will intercede for us with our Lord so that He may judge between us?’ They will say: Who is more deserving of that than your father Adam? God formed his soil and created it with His hand, and breathed into him from His spirit, and sealed his mouth. Then Adam will be brought and asked to do that, but he will refuse. Then they will examine the prophets, one by one, and every time they come to a prophet, he will refuse.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Until they come to me. When they come to me, I will go out until I come to the examination.’” Abu Hurairah said: O Messenger of God, what is the examination? He said: In front of the Throne, so I prostrated, and I did not stop prostrating until God sent an angel to me who took hold of my arm and lifted me up. Then God said to me: O Muhammad! I said: Yes! And He knows best. He said: What is the matter with you? I said: O Lord, You promised me intercession, so intercede for me among Your creation and judge between them. He said: I have accepted your intercession, I will come to you and judge between you. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: So I turned back until I stood with the people, and while we were standing we heard a loud noise from the sky, so we were terrified, and the people of the lowest heaven descended with the same number of jinn and humans as those on earth, until when they came close to the earth, the earth shone with their light and they took their places, so We said to them: Is our Lord among you? They said: No, even if they were not there. Then the people of the second heaven descended with twice as many angels as had descended, and twice as many jinn and humans as were in it, until when they came near the earth, the earth shone with their light, and they took their ranks. We said to them: Is our Lord among you? They said: No! He is coming. Then the people of the third heaven descended with twice as many angels as had descended, and twice as many jinn and humans as were in the earth, until when they came near the earth, the earth shone with their light, and they took their ranks. We said to them: Is our Lord among you? They said: No! He is coming. Then the people of the heavens descended in multiplication, until the Almighty descended in the shadows of the clouds and the angels, and they had a chant of their glorification, saying: Glory be to the Possessor of the Kingdom and Sovereignty! Glory be to the Lord of the Throne, the Possessor of Might! Glory be to the Living Who does not die! Glory be to the One Who causes the creation to die and does not die! Glory be to the Holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit! Holy, Holy! Glory be to our Most High Lord! Glory be to the One with the Authority and Majesty! Glory be to Him forever, forever! Then the Blessed and Exalted will descend, carrying His Throne on that day eight, and today they are four! Their feet are on the borders of the lowest earth, the heavens are within their grasp, and the Throne is on their shoulders. So God Almighty placed His Throne wherever He willed on the earth, then a caller will call out a call that all creatures will hear, saying: O company of jinn and mankind, I have been listening since the day I created you until this day of yours, I hear your speech, and I see your deeds, so listen to me, for these are your records and your deeds that we read to you, so whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself!

x: This report indicates the error of Qatadah’s interpretation of his statement: and the angels that he meant the angels who come to them at death, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned that they come to them after the Hour comes in the place of reckoning, when the sky is split open. The report was narrated in a similar manner from a group of the Companions and Followers. We disliked lengthening the book by mentioning them and what they said about that. It also clarifies the correctness of what we chose in reading his statement: and the angels in the nominative case, meaning: and the angels come to them. It shows the error of the reading of the one who reads it in the accusative case, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informed us that the angels come to the people of the Resurrection in their place when the sky is split open, before their Lord comes to them, in the shades of clouds.

Unless the reader of that went to the view that the Almighty meant by his statement: unless God comes to them in the shades of clouds, and in the angels who come to the people of the place of standing when God comes to them in the shades of clouds. The clouds, so that would be a facet of interpretation, even if it is far from the saying of the people of knowledge, and the evidence of the Book and the proven narrations of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

By that, God, may His praise be glorified, means: And the separation of judgment with justice among creation, as we mentioned before on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: From taking the right of every oppressed person from every oppressor, even the retaliation for the horned one from the horned one among the animals. As for His statement: And to God will return all matters, it means: And to God will return the judgment among His creation on the Day of Resurrection, and the judgment between them in their affairs that occurred in this world, from the oppression of some of them by others, and the transgression of the transgressors among them of the limits of God and disobedience to His command, and the goodness of the good among them and his obedience to Him in what He commanded him to do - so He will separate between the oppressors, and will reward the people of goodness with goodness, and the people of evil with what He sees, and He will be generous to those among them who were not disbelievers and forgive.

Therefore, the Most High said: And to God all matters return, even though all matters of this world and the Hereafter originate from Him and are destined for Him. This is because His creation in this world wronged one another, and sometimes some of His creation would judge between them in this world, and some of His servants would judge between them, and some would be unjust and some would be just, and one would be right and one would be wrong. He would be able to execute the judgment on some, but it would be impossible for some, due to his strength and power. So He informed His servants, may He be exalted, that all of that will be referred to Him on the Day of Resurrection. He will do justice to each person and will repay each person with the right recompense where there is no injustice and no one is immune from the implementation of His judgment upon him, where the weak and the strong, the poor and the rich are equal, injustice will vanish and the authority of justice will descend.

The Almighty and Majestic included the definite article in matters because He, may His praise be exalted, meant by it all matters, and did not mean by it some without others. So that was in the sense of the saying of the speaker: I like honey - and the mule is stronger than the donkey. The definite article is included in it because He did not mean by it some without others, but rather it meant generality and collection.

evidence.text: Then the readings differed in the reading of His statement: and the angels.

Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar al-Razi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah, who said - in the reading of Abi bin Ka’b: Do they await anything but that God should come to them with the angels in canopies of clouds? - He said: The angels come in canopies of clouds, and God Almighty comes as He wills.
Others read it as: Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds and the angels?
Likewise, the reading of shadows differed: Some of them read it: in shadows, and some of them: in shadows.

Whoever read it in shadows, then he directed it to the fact that it is the plural of shadow, and shadow, the plural of shadows and shadows, just as lightness is pluralized as khalal and khalal, and jalal is pluralized as jalal and jalal.
As for the one who read it in shadows, then he made it the plural of shadow, as we mentioned from their plural of khalal as khalal.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in that, in my opinion, is: Do they wait for anything but that God should come to them in the shadows of clouds, according to the hadith "It was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There are windows in the clouds in which God comes surrounded".

Likewise, what is obligatory in everything whose meanings agree but whose reading differs is the recitation, and there is no indication for one of the two readings that separates it from the other other than the difference in the script of the Mushaf, then what should be preferred is the recitation of it that agrees with the script of the Mushaf.

As for what is the first of the two readings in or the angels, the correct one is to raise it, in apposition to the name of God, the Blessed and Most High, meaning: Do they await anything but that God should come to them in the shades of clouds, or anything but that the angels should come to them, according to what was narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka’b. Because God, the Most High, has informed in more than one place in His Book that the angels will come to them.

That is because the required reading, according to the interpretation of this statement of Ikrimah regarding the angels, is the lowering, because he interpreted the verse: Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds and with the angels.

It shows the error of the reading of the one who reads it in the accusative case, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informed us that the angels come to the people of the Resurrection in their place when the sky is split open, before their Lord comes to them, in the shades of clouds.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Ask, O Muhammad, the Children of Israel, who do not expect - by turning to My obedience, and repenting to Me by acknowledging your prophethood and believing in you, in what I have brought them from Me - except that I come to them in the shade of clouds with My angels, and I will decide the judgment between you and those who believed in you and believed in you through what I have sent down to you of My books, and imposed upon you and upon them of the laws of My religion, and between them, how many signs and indications I brought to them before you of what I imposed upon them of My obligations, so I commanded them with it of My obedience, and I followed up on them with My proofs at the hands of My prophets and messengers before you, supporting them in their truthfulness, making clear that they are from Me, and clearly that they are from My evidence of the truthfulness of My vow and My messengers in what I have imposed upon them of believing them and believing you, but they disbelieved in My proofs, and denied My messengers, and changed My favors before them, and altered My covenant and testament to them.
As for the verse, I have explained its interpretation in what has preceded in our book sufficiently, and it is here as follows:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them
, what God mentioned in the Qur’an and what He did not mention, and they are the Jews.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’, regarding his statement:
h
Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them

, meaning: God gave them clear signs, the staff of Moses, and his hand, and He cut off the sea for them, and He drowned their enemy while they were looking on, and He shaded them with clouds, and He sent down upon them manna and quails, and that is from the signs of God that He gave the Children of Israel in many other signs, with which they disobeyed God’s command, so they killed God’s prophets and messengers, and changed His covenant and testament to them, God said:
h
And whoever changes the favor of God
after it has come to him - then indeed, God is severe in penalty.

x: God informed His Prophet of these verses, and commanded him to be patient with those who denied him and were arrogant towards his Lord, and informed him that that was what those who came before him from the ancestors of the nations before them did with their prophets, despite his supporting them with arguments, and that those among them from the Jews are only remnants of those whose customs were [in that way], from those whose stories were told to him from the Children of Israel.
By blessings, may His praise be glorified, He means Islam and what He imposed of the laws of His religion. And what he means by his saying:
h
And whoever changes the favor of God

, is whoever changes what he has pledged to God in His favor, which is Islam, of work and entering into it and disbelieves in it, then he will be punished with the punishment He promised for disbelief in it, and God is severe in punishment and painful in torment. So the interpretation of the verse is: O you who have believed in the Torah and believed in it, enter into Islam all together, and abandon disbelief and what Satan has called you to of his misguidance, and clear proofs have come to you from Me through Muhammad and what I have shown you through his hands of arguments and lessons, so do not change My covenant with you in him and in what he has brought to you from Me in your Book that he is My Prophet and Messenger, for whoever among you changes that and alters it, then I will punish him with a painful punishment.
And similar to what we said about His statement:
h
And whoever exchanges the favor of God after it has come to him
, a group of the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And whoever exchanges the favor of God after it has come to him
, he said: He disbelieves in it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And whoever exchanges the favor of God, he said, he says: He who exchanges it with disbelief.

c: I was told by Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father,
m: on Al-Rabiʿ:
h
And whoever exchanges the favor of God after it has come to him
, he says: And whoever disbelieves in His favor after it has come to him.

x: By that, God, the Most High, means: The love of the immediate pleasures of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve. They seek therein to multiply and boast, and seek leadership and boasting, and they are too arrogant to follow you, O Muhammad, and to acknowledge what you have brought from Me, out of their arrogance towards those who believed in you and followed you, and they mock those who followed you from the people of faith and belief in you, in their abandonment of multiplying and boasting about the world and its adornments of luxury and money by seeking leadership, and their turning to seeking what is with Me by rejecting the world and abandoning its adornments. And those who worked for Me, and turned to obeying Me, and rejected the pleasures and desires of this world, following you, seeking what is with Me, and protecting themselves from them by performing My obligations and avoiding my sins, will be above those who disbelieved on the Day of Resurrection, by admitting the righteous into Paradise, and admitting the disbelievers into the Fire.
