And a group of them said something similar to what we said about that interpretation.
Who said that: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement:
h
The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve

, he said: The disbelievers seek and demand the world, and they ridicule those who believe, in their pursuit of the Hereafter. Ibn Jurayj said: I do not think it was except from Ikrimah, he said: They said: If Muhammad were a prophet as he says, our nobles and leaders would have followed him! By God, only those in need, like Ibn Masoud, followed him!

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those who fear God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection
, he said: Above them, in Paradise.

x: What he means by that is: And God will give those who fear God on the Day of Resurrection from His blessings and bounties and abundant gifts, without Him holding them accountable for the bounties He has bestowed upon them.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: What is there in His statement:
h
He provides for whom He wills without account of praise

The meaning of the praise in it is the report that He is not afraid of running out of His treasures, so He needs to account for what comes out of them, since the accounting of the giver is only to know the amount of the gift that comes out of His kingdom to someone else, so that He does not exceed in His gifts to what would be unfair to Him. So our Lord, blessed and exalted be He, is not afraid of running out of His treasures, nor of anything being diminished from His kingdom, by giving what He gives to His servants, so He needs to account for what He gives and count what remains. This is the meaning in His statement:
h
And God provides for whom He wills without account
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of: the nation: in this place, and about the people whom God described as: they were one nation.
Some of them said: they are those who were between Adam and Noah, and they were ten generations, all of them were on a law of truth, then they differed after that.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Hammam bin Munabbih told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: There were ten generations between Noah and Adam, all of them on a law of truth. Then they differed, so God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners. He said: And it is likewise in the reading of Abdullah: the people were one nation, then they differed.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding His statement: the people were one nation, he said: they were all on guidance, then they differed, so God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, so the first prophet He sent was Noah.

x: The interpretation of the nation, according to this statement that we mentioned from Ibn Abbas, is religion, as Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani said: I swore, and I left no doubt for you. Can a slave be held accountable if he is obedient? Meaning: of religion. So the interpretation of the verse was based on the meaning of what these people said: People were a community united on one religion and one faith, then they differed, so God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners. The origin of the nation is the group that gathers on one religion, then the report about the nation is sufficient from the report about the religion, because it indicates it, as God the Most High said: And if God had willed, He would have made you one community (al-Ma’idah 5:48) - (al-Nahl 16:93), meaning: people of one religion and one faith. So Ibn Abbas interpreted his statement:
h
People were one community to mean that people were people of one religion until they differed

Others said: Rather, the interpretation of that is: Adam was on the truth, an imam for his descendants, so God sent the prophets among his descendants. They directed the meaning of the nation to obedience to God, and the call to His Oneness and following His command, from the saying of God the Almighty: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth (al-Nahl 16:120), meaning by his saying: a nation, an imam in goodness to be emulated and followed.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
Mankind was one nation
, he said: Adam.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his saying:
h
Mankind was one nation

, he said: Adam. He said: There were ten prophets between Adam and Noah, so God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners. Mujahid said: Adam was a nation on its own. It is as if the one who said this statement, permitted calling one by the name of the group, for the gathering of the good morals that are in the scattered group in the one he called the nation, as it is said that so-and-so is a nation alone, he takes the place of the nation. It may be permissible that he called him thus, because he is a cause for the gathering of the scattered people on what he called them to of good morals. So when Adam, peace be upon him, was a cause for the gathering of those who gathered on his religion from his descendants until their disagreement, he called him thus a nation.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: People were one nation on one religion, so he extracted Adam’s offspring from his loins and presented them to Adam.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: I was told by Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ja’far, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’,
m: his saying:
h
People were one nation - and on the authority of his father

, on the authority of al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu al-A’aliyah, on the authority of Abu bin Ka’b, who said: They were one nation when they were presented to Adam, so he created them on that day upon Islam, and they acknowledged his servitude, and they were one nation, all Muslims, then they differed. After Adam, my father used to recite: “
h
Mankind was one nation

, then they differed, so God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners concerning that over which they differed. And God only sent the messengers and revealed the books when there was a difference.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Mankind was one nation

, he said: When He brought them forth from the loins of Adam, they were never one nation except on that day, then God sent the prophets. He said: This is when the nations were divided. The interpretation of the verse according to this statement is similar to the interpretation of the statement of those who said the statement of Ibn Abbas: that people were of one religion between Adam and Noah - and we explained its meaning there - except that the time when people were one nation is different from the time that Ibn Abbas specified.

x: Others said the opposite of all of that in that, and they said: The meaning of His statement:
h
Mankind was one nation
is of one religion, then God sent the prophets.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Mankind was one nation
, meaning: It was one religion, so God sent prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners.

x: The most correct interpretation of this verse is to say: God Almighty informed His servants that
h
mankind was one nation
, following one religion and one creed, as: Musa bin Harun said, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
Mankind was one nation
, meaning: one religion based on the religion of Adam, then they differed, so God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners.
The religion they were on was the religion of truth, as Abi bin Kaab said, and as:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: It is in the reading of Ibn Masoud: they differed from him, about Islam. So they differed in their religion, so when they differed in their religion, God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners, And He sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people concerning that in which they differed, out of His mercy to His creation, and as an apology to them. It is possible that the time in which they were one nation was from the time of Adam to the time of Noah, peace be upon them, as Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas, and as Qatadah said. And it is possible that it was when He presented his creation to Adam. It is possible that it was at a different time - and there is no evidence from the Book of God or a report that proves the argument for which of these times it was. So it is not permissible to say about it except what God the Almighty said: that mankind were one nation, then God sent among them, when they differed, the prophets and messengers. Ignorance of the time of that does not harm us, just as knowledge of it does not benefit us, if knowledge of it is not obedience to God. However, whatever it was, the evidence of the Qur’an is clear that those whom God told us about being one nation were only one nation in faith and the religion of truth, without disbelief in God or associating partners with Him. That is because God the Almighty said in the Surah in which Yunus is mentioned: “And mankind were not but one nation, then they differed. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them concerning that over which they differ”
r
(Yunus 10:19)

. So God the Almighty threatened for the difference, not for the unity, nor for their being one nation. If their unity before the difference had been on disbelief, then the difference had occurred after that, it would only have been by some of them converting to faith. If that were the case, then the promise would have been more appropriate for His wisdom, may He be glorified, in that situation than the threat, because it is a situation in which some of them turn to His obedience. It is impossible for Him to threaten in a situation of repentance and return, and leave that in a situation in which everyone agrees on disbelief and polytheism.

x: As for His statement,
h
So God sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners

, it means that He sent messengers to give good tidings to those who obey God of a great reward and a noble destination. And by His statement, and as warners, He means to warn those who disobey God and disbelieve in Him of severe punishment, bad reckoning, and eternal life in the Fire. And He sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed, meaning by that: so that the Book—which is the Torah—would judge between the people concerning that over which those who differed differed. So God, may He be glorified, added the judgment to the Book, and that He is the One Who judges between the people, not the prophets and messengers, since whoever among the prophets and messengers judges with a judgment, judges only by what the Book that God, may He be glorified, has shown them.

So the Book, by indicating what its description indicates of its correctness of the ruling, was the judge between the people, even if the one who decides the judgment between them is someone other than Him.

God Almighty means by His saying: And there is no difference in it, and there is no difference in the Book that He revealed, which is the Torah, except those who were given it, meaning by that the Jews from the Children of Israel, who were given the Torah and knowledge of it, and the ha in His saying: were given it refers to the Book that God revealed, after the clear proofs had come to them, meaning by that: after the arguments and evidence of God had come to them that the Book about which they differed and in its rulings was from God, and that it is the truth about which they cannot differ or act contrary to what is in it. So God Almighty informed about the Surat al-Baqarah 2:213 Mankind was one community, then God sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners, and He sent down with them the Book with the truth to judge between the people concerning that wherein they differed.
h
And none differed therein except those who were given it
after clear proofs had come to them, out of jealous animosity between themselves.
h
So God guided
those who believed to the truth concerning that wherein they differed,
h
by His permission
h
And God guides whom He wills to a straight path

. Jews from the Children of Israel that they contradicted the Book, the Torah, and they differed in it, knowing what they were doing, deliberately contradicting God in what they contradicted Him in regarding His command and the ruling of His Book. Then He, the Most High, informed us that their deliberate sin that they committed, and their committing the disobedience that they committed, from their opposition to His command, was only out of envy among themselves. And envy is a source from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so envied so-and-so, if he transgressed and assaulted him and exceeded his limits. And from that, it is said of a wound if it is prolonged, and of a sea if its water increases and overflows, and of a cloud if it falls on a land and it becomes fertile, Bagha, all of that has one meaning, which is its increase and exceeding its limit.
So the meaning of His statement, the Most High,
h
And none differed therein except those who were given it

after the clear proofs had come to them, out of envy among themselves, is from that. He says: The disagreement of these different Jews from the Children of Israel, in My Book that I revealed with My Prophet, was not due to their ignorance of it, but rather their disagreement about it and their opposition to its ruling, after its proof had been established for them, was out of envy among them, seeking leadership from some of them over others, and humiliation from some of them to others, as: - I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan, he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, he said: Then He returned to the Children of Israel in His statement:
h
And none differed therein except those who were given it

, meaning: except those who were given the Book and knowledge, after the clear proofs had come to them, out of envy among themselves, meaning: envy for the world, and seeking its kingdom, its adornment and its decoration, which of them would have the kingdom and awe among the people, so some of them were envious of others, and some of them struck the necks of others.
Then the people of Arabic differed about min in His statement: after the clear proofs had come to them, what is its ruling and meaning? What is the consistent meaning of his statement:
h
And none differed therein except those who were given it
, after clear proofs had come to them, out of envy among themselves.
Some of them said: From, that refers to those who were given the Scripture, and what comes after it is a connection to it. However, he claimed that the meaning of the statement is:
h
And none differed therein except those who were given it
, out of envy among themselves, after clear proofs had come to them.

Some of them denied this and said: There is no meaning to what this speaker said, nor to presenting envy before from, because if from is the one that brings it, then it is a mistake to precede it, because envy is a verbal noun, and the connection to the verbal noun does not precede it. The denier claimed that who is an exception, and that after clear proofs had come to them is an exception with another exception, and that the interpretation of the statement is:
h
And none differed therein except those who were given it
, they did not differ therein except out of envy, they did not differ except after clear proofs had come to them, so it is as if he repeated the statement for emphasis.

This second statement is more similar to the interpretation of the verse. Because the people did not differ except after the proof was established against them and the clear proofs came from God, and likewise they did not differ except out of enmity. So that is more similar to the interpretation of the verse.
What God Almighty means by His saying:
h
So God guided

, is that He guided those who believed, and they are the people of faith. By God and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, those who believe in him and in what he brought, that it is from God, when those who were given the Scripture differed concerning it. And their disagreement in which God let them down, and guided those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to it, because of his correctness: Friday, they went astray from it, and it was imposed on them as it was imposed on us, so they made it the Sabbath. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “We are the last to come, but we will be the first, except that they were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them. And this is the day about which they differed,
h
so God guided
us to it. So the Jews will have tomorrow and the Christians will have the day after tomorrow.”

c: Muhammad bin Hamid narrated to us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ayyad bin Dinar al-Laythi, he said:
m: I heard Abu Hurairah say: Abu al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned the hadith.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said, Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah:
m: h
So God guided
those who believed to the truth about which they differed,
h
by His permission

. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are the last to come, but we will be the first people to enter Paradise, except that they were given the Book before us, and we were given it after them. After them, God guided us to the truth regarding what they differed about,
h
by His permission

. This is the day to which God has guided us, and the people will follow us on it. Tomorrow will be for the Jews, and the day after tomorrow will be for the Christians. Another thing they differed about was what Ibn Zayd said, which is:

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
So God guided

those who believed to Islam, and they differed about prayer, some of them prayed towards the east, and some of them prayed towards Jerusalem, so He guided us to the qiblah. They differed about fasting, some of them fasted part of a day, and some of them fasted part of a night,
h
so God guided
us to it. They differed about Friday, so the Jews took the Sabbath, and the Christians took Sunday,
h
so God guided

us to it. They differed about Abraham, so the Jews said: He was a Jew! And the Christians said: He was a Christian! So God cleared him of that, and made him a monotheist, a Muslim, and he was not one of the polytheists for those who call upon him from the people of polytheism. They differed about Jesus, so the Jews made him a slander, and the Christians made him a god,
h
so God guided
us to the truth about him. This is what God Almighty said:
h
So God guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed
h
by His permission

x: So the guidance of God, the Most High, was for those who believed in Muhammad and what he brought, when these parties of the Children of Israel who were given the Book differed about the truth,
h
by His permission

, that He guided them to the truth that was upon those who were before the differing ones, whom God described in this verse, since they were one nation, and that is the religion of Abraham, the upright Muslim, the friend of the Most Merciful, so they became a middle nation, as their Lord described them, so that they would be witnesses over the people, as:

c: I was told by ʿAmmar ibn al-Hasan,
m: he said, ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
h
So God guided those who believed to that over which they differed
h
so God guided

them when they differed, that they remained upon what the messengers had brought before the difference: they remained upon sincerity to God alone, and worshipping Him without partner, and establishing prayer, and paying zakat, so they remained upon the first matter that was before the difference, and they avoided the difference, so they were witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection, they were witnesses over the people of Noah, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, and the people of Shuʿayb. And the people of Pharaoh: that their messengers had delivered to them, and that they denied their messengers. And in the reading of Abi bin Kaab it is: (So that they may be witnesses over mankind on the Day of Resurrection.
h
And God guides whom He wills to a straight path
), so Abu Al-Aaliyah used to say: In this verse is the way out from doubts, misguidance and tribulations.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
So God guided those who believed to that over which they differed
, he said: The disbelievers differed over it,
h
so God guided
those who believed to the truth from that. And in the reading of Ibn Masoud it is:
h
So God guided those who believed to that over which they differed
, on the authority of Islam.

x: As for his statement:
h
By His permission

, He, the Most High, means: By His knowledge, of what He has guided them to. We have already explained the meaning of permission, since it means knowledge in other places, so there is no need to repeat it here. As for his statement:
h
And God guides whom He wills to a straight path

, he means by it: And God guides whom He wills of His creation and directs him to the straight path of truth in which there is no crookedness, just as He guided those who believed in Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, when those who were given the Scripture differed concerning it out of envy among themselves, so He guided them to the truth and the right path in it.

In this verse is a clear statement of the correctness of what the people of truth have said: That every blessing upon the servants in their religion or their worldly life is from God, the Most High, the Most Great.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: What is the meaning of His statement:
h
So God guided those who believed to that over which they differed
? Did He guide them to the truth, or did He guide them to the difference? If He guided them to differences, then He only led them astray! And if He guided them to the truth, then how was it said,
h
So God guided those who believed to that over which they differed
That is not in the way you have gone to. Rather, the meaning of that is:
h
So God guided
those who believed to the truth in that over which they differed in the Book of God, which they were given.
Some of them disbelieved in changing it, and some of them remained steadfast in the truth and correctness in it - and they are the people of the Torah who changed it -
h
so God guided
to the truth from that over which they changed and distorted, those who believed from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

If what we said is unclear to someone who is unaware, then he said: How can it be as you said, and min is in the Book of God in the truth, and the lam in His statement: for that over which they differed, and you change the lam in the truth, and the min in the difference, in the interpretation that you interpret and make it inverted? It was said: That is present and widespread in the speech of the Arabs, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, only addressed them with their logic, and from that is the saying of the poet: It was a duty to say what you say, just as adultery was a duty to be stoned. Stoning is the obligation for adultery, as the other said: A lamp is a source of pride for the generous, and the eye is adorned with it when it is exposed. Rather, the lamp is that which is adorned with the eye, not the eye with a lamp.
Some of them said: The meaning of His statement,
h
So God guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they differed
, is that the people of the first books differed, so some of them disbelieved in the book of others, and they were all from God,
h
so God guided
the people of faith in Muhammad to believe in all of them. That is one statement, but the first is the more correct of the two statements, because God only informed of their differences in one book.

evidence.text: He said: And it is likewise in the reading of Abdullah: the people were one nation, then they differed.
Musa bin Harun told me, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: It is in the reading of Ibn Masoud: they differed from him, about Islam.
And in the reading of Abi bin Kaab it is: (So that they may be witnesses over mankind on the Day of Resurrection.
And in the reading of Ibn Masoud it is: So God guided those who believed to that over which they differed, on the authority of Islam.

x: As for his saying: Or did you think, it is as if he asked with or at the beginning, not preceded by a question letter, because of a previous statement that is connected to it. And if there was no statement before it that would be connected to it, and it was a beginning, it would only be with a question letter. Because if a speaker had said, initiating a statement to another: Or do you have your brother? He would have said something that has no meaning. But if he had said: Are you a man who is arrogant with your strength, or do you have your brother to support you? He would have been correct. We have explained some of this meaning in the past in this book of ours, enough so that there is no need to repeat it. The meaning of the statement is: Or do you think that you, O believers in God and His Messengers, will enter Paradise, and that you have not been afflicted with the hardships, trials and tests that afflicted those who came before you from the followers of the Prophets and Messengers, so that you were afflicted with what they were afflicted with and tested with from hardship - which is severe need and poverty, adversity - which are illnesses and afflictions - and you were not shaken as they were - meaning: and they were not afflicted with fear and terror from their enemies, severe and exhausted, such that the people were impatient for God’s victory over them and said: When will God be our supporter?

c: Then God informed them that
m: His victory from them was near, and that He would make them superior to their enemy, and would make them victorious over him, so He fulfilled for them what He promised them, and made their word supreme, and extinguished the fire of the war of those who disbelieved. This verse - according to what the people of interpretation claim - was revealed on the Day of the Trench when the believers faced what they faced of severe hardship from the fear of the confederates, and the severe harm of the cold and the hardship of the life in which they were on that day. God Almighty says to the believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when there came to you armies and We sent upon them a wind and armies you did not see until His saying: “And when the eyes turned away and the hearts reached to the throats and you assumed about God [various] assumptions. There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking” (al-Ahzab 33:9-11).

x: Those who said that this verse was revealed on the Day of the Confederates:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? They were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken, he said: This was revealed on the Day of the Confederates when their leader said: God and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion (al-Ahzab 33:12).

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you

? They were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken, he said: It was revealed on the Day of the Confederates, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were afflicted with affliction and siege, and they were as God, the Almighty, said: And hearts reached to the throats. As for His statement:
h
And such [trial] has not yet come to you

, most Arab scholars interpret it to mean: and has not yet come to you, and they claim that what is a conjunction and a filler. I have explained the statement about what the Arabs call a connection, what is its ruling, in other places so that there is no need to repeat it. As for the meaning of his statement:
h
The likeness of those who passed away before you

, it means: the likeness of those who passed away and went before you. I have indicated in other places that the likeness is the resemblance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, his statement:
h
Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed away before you

? They were afflicted with poverty and hardship and were shaken. 1 Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Jurayj, he said: His statement:
h
Until the Messenger and those who believe say
, he said: He is the best of them and the most knowledgeable of them about God. And in his statement:
h
Until the Messenger says

, there are two ways of reading: nominative and accusative. And whoever raises it says: Since it was appropriate in its place for what he did, he invalidated the action until it is in it. Because even does not work on a verb, but rather it works on yaf’al, and if it is preceded by a verb, and what comes after it is a verb that has already been done and finished, and what came before it of the verb was not long, then the eloquent speech of the Arabs in this case is to raise yaf’al, and to invalidate the work of even from it. This is like the saying of the speaker: I stood up to so-and-so until I hit him, and the raising is the correct speech in I hit him, if he means: I stood up to him until I hit him, if the hitting had already happened and he had finished it, and the standing was not long in duration. But if what comes before even of the verb is in the form of a long-term verb, and what comes after it of the verb is in the form of an unbroken verb, then the correct speech is to put yaf’al in the accusative case, and to put even into the accusative case, and this is like the saying of the speaker: So-and-so kept asking you until he spoke to you, and he kept looking at you until he made you stand, so the correct speech - which is not correct other than it - is to put yaf’al in the accusative case with even, as the poet said: They are trampled upon until their mounts are exhausted and even the horses are not led by reins. So he put takal in the accusative case, and the verb that comes after hatta is past tense, because the verb that came before it is long and long. The correct reading, if that is the case, is: And they were shaken
h
until the Messenger says

, putting yaqool in the accusative case, because the shaking is a long verb like the shaking of camels. And the earthquake in this case is fear of the enemy, not the earthquake of the earth, and that is why it was long. And the accusative case in yaqool, even though it has the meaning of a verb, is more eloquent and correct than the nominative case in it.

evidence.text: The correct reading, if that is the case, is: And they were shaken until the Messenger says, putting yaqool in the accusative case, because the shaking is a long verb like the shaking of camels.

x: By that, God the Almighty means: Your companions ask you, O Muhammad: What do they spend from their wealth, so that they give it in charity? And on whom do they spend it? So say to them: Whatever you spend from your wealth and give in charity, then spend it and give it in charity and make it for your fathers and mothers and your relatives, and for the orphans among you, and the needy, and the wayfarer, for whatever good you do for them, God knows it, and He will count it for you until He pays you your wages for it on the Day of Resurrection, and He will reward you for what you obeyed Him with your goodness. And the good that God the Almighty said in His statement: “Say: Whatever good you spend,” is the money that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked his companions to spend from, so God answered them about it as He answered them in this verse.

In his saying: What, there are two ways of parsing. One of them is that what means: what thing? So it is in the accusative case by his saying: they spend. The meaning of the statement then is: They ask you, in what do they spend? And it is not in the accusative case by they ask you. The other of them is: the nominative case. There are two ways of parsing in this: One of them: That dha which is with ma has the meaning of alladhi, so ma is raised with dha and dha to ma, and yanfaqu is connected to dha.

i: For the Arabs may connect dha and hadha, as the poet said:
x: Lentils!

What is the matter with the servants over you? I am safe, and you are carrying this free man! So you carry from the connection of this. Then the interpretation of the speech then is: They ask you what they spend? And the other of the two aspects of raising: That what is in the meaning of: what thing, so what is raised, even if his saying: they spend is applied to it, since it was the agent in it, and it is they spend, it is not appropriate to present it before it.

i: That is because the interrogation does not allow the verb to be presented before the interrogative letter, as the poet said:
x: Don't you ask a person what he is trying to do, love and death, or misguidance and falsehood?

As the other said: They said: You know the houses from Mina, but I do not know everyone who visits Mina. So he raised all and did not make it an object of knowing, since the meaning of his saying: And not everyone who visits me, I know, was denying knowledge of the one who visits me, so it became in the meaning of: No one.
This verse [was revealed] - according to what was mentioned - before God imposed the zakat on wealth.
He mentioned those who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives,’” he said: When this verse was revealed, it was not zakat, but rather it was the spending that a man spends on his family, and charity is what he gives in charity, so zakat abrogated it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: The believers asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, where they should put their money? Then this verse was revealed: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer,’” so that is voluntary spending, and zakat is other than that. He said: Mujahid said: They asked and he gave them a fatwa on that: Whatever you spend of good is for parents and near relatives and what was mentioned with them.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told me, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abi Nujayh regarding the statement of God: They ask you, what they should spend, he said: They asked him and he gave them a fatwa on that: For parents and near relatives and what was mentioned with them.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about his statement: “Say: Whatever you spend of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:215 They ask you, [O Muhammad], what they should spend. Say, "Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer. And whatever good you do - indeed, God is Knowing of it." good is for parents and near relatives,” he said: This is from the voluntary acts. He said: He says: They are more deserving of your favor than others.

x: What al-Suddi said: That there was no zakat on the day this verse was revealed, but rather it was a provision that a man spends on his family, and charity that he gives in charity, then zakat abrogated it, a statement that could be as he said, and it could be otherwise, and there is no evidence in the verse for the correctness of what he said. Because it is possible that his saying: “Say: Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives” 2:177 is an urging from God, the Most High, to spend on those whose spending is not obligatory, such as fathers, mothers, relatives, and those mentioned with them in this verse, and a definition from God to His servants of the places of virtue in which spending is spent, as He said in the other verse: “And he gives wealth, in spite of love for Him, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and to free slaves. And he establishes prayer and gives zakah” 2:177.

This is the statement that we have made in the statement of Ibn Jurayj that we have mentioned. We have explained the meaning of poverty and the meaning of the traveler previously, so there is no need to repeat it.
By that, God the Most High meant by His statement:
h
Fighting has been prescribed for you
, that fighting has been made obligatory for you, meaning: fighting the polytheists,
h
and it is hateful to you
The scholars differed as to who was meant by the obligation of fighting.
Some of them said: It meant the Companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in particular, and not others.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I asked Ata', I said to him:
h
Fighting has been prescribed for you
h
and it is hateful to you
, is warfare obligatory for people because of it? He said: No! It was prescribed for those people at that time.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman bin Sa'id told us, he said, Khalid told us, on the authority of Husayn bin Qays, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Fighting has been prescribed for you
h
and it is hateful to you
, he said: It was abrogated by: They said, 'We hear and we obey' (al-Baqarah 2:285).

x: This is a statement that has no meaning, because the abrogation of rulings is from God the Most High, not from the servants. And His statement: They said, ‘We hear and obey’ (al-Baqarah 2:285- An-Nisa’: 46), is a report from God about His believing servants, and that they said it, and there is no abrogation from it.

c: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, he said, Mu’awiyah ibn Amr told us, he said, Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari told us, he said:
m: I asked Al-Awza’i about the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
Fighting has been prescribed for you

, although it is hateful to you, is fighting obligatory for all people? He said: I do not know, but the imams and the general public should not abandon it, but as for a man in particular, no. Others said: It is upon everyone until someone who is sufficient to do so performs it, and then the obligation of that is dropped from the rest of the Muslims, like praying over the dead, washing the dead, and burying them. And the majority of Muslim scholars agree with this.

x: This is what is correct according to us, because of the consensus of the evidence on that, and because of the statement of God the Almighty:
“God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home, by a degree. But to all God has promised good”

c: So God the Almighty informed us that
m: the preference is for those who strive with their wealth and their lives, and that for them and for those who sit at home is the best. If those who sit at home were neglecting an obligation, then they would have been given the worst, not the best.

x: Others said: It is an obligation incumbent upon the Muslims until the Day of Judgment. He mentioned who said that.

c: Hubaish bin Mubashir told us, he said, Ruh bin ʿUbadah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi ʿAsim, he said:
m: I said to Saʿid bin Al-Musayyab: I know that fighting is obligatory upon the people! So he remained silent, and I know that if he denied what I said, he would explain it to me. We have already explained the meaning of His statement: He wrote what is sufficient.

x: By that, He, the Most High, means:
h
And it is hateful to you
. So He left out mentioning It is sufficient because His statement: It is hateful to you indicates it, just as He said:
And ask the town
And similar to what we have said about that, it was narrated from ʿAta’ in its interpretation.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of ʿAta’,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And it is hateful to you

, he said: It is hateful to you at that time. Hatred with the dammah: is what a man forces himself to do without anyone forcing him to do it. Hatred with the fathah of the kaf, is what someone else forces him to do and he brings it upon himself unwillingly. Among those who narrated this statement from him is Muʿadh ibn Muslim.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Ishaq narrated to us, he said, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, on the authority of Muʿadh ibn Muslim
m: said: Dislike is hardship, and dislike is compulsion. Some Arab scholars used to say: Dislike and dislike are two words with one meaning, such as: washing and washing, weakness and weakness, and fear and fear.

x: Some of them said: Dislike with a damma on the kaf is a noun, and dislike with a fatha on it. Source.
By that, the Most High means: Do not hate fighting, for perhaps you hate it and it is good for you, and do not love abandoning jihad, for perhaps you love it and it is bad for you, as:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, ʿAmr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Fighting has been prescribed for you

, although you dislike it. But perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you. And perhaps you like a thing and it is bad for you.” That is because the Muslims hated fighting, so He said: Perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you. He said: In fighting you have spoils, victory, and martyrdom, and in sitting you do not gain victory over the polytheists, nor do you become martyrs, nor do you inflict anything.

c: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Salami told me, Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Mujahid told me, Ubaydullah ibn Abi Hashim al-Ju’fi told me, Amir ibn Wathilah told me,
m: “Ibn Abbas said: I was riding behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O Ibn Abbas, be content with what God has decreed, even if it is against your desires, for it is established in the Book of God. I said: O Messenger of God, where? I have read the Qur’an. He said: In His saying: “
h
And perhaps you dislike a thing which is good for you
; and perhaps you like a thing which is bad for you. And God knows, while you do not know.”

x: By that, God Almighty means: God knows what is good for you and what is bad for you. So do not dislike what I have prescribed for you of jihad against your enemy and fighting those whom I have commanded you to fight, for I know that your fighting them is good for you in this life and in the hereafter, and your abandoning their fighting is bad for you, and you do not know what I know about that. God Almighty urges them with that to jihad against His enemies, and encourages them to fight those who disbelieve in Him.

By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: O Muhammad, your companions ask you about the sacred month, which is Rajab, about fighting in it. And the lowering of fighting means repeating about it. And this is how Abdullah bin Mas'ud read it, as he mentioned to us, and: - I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan, he said, Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi', his saying: "
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting in it
," he said: He says: They ask you about fighting in it. He said: And this is how he used to read it: about fighting in it.

Say, O Muhammad: Fighting in it - meaning in the sacred month - is great, meaning it is great before God to make it permissible and shed blood in it. And the meaning of His saying: "Fighting in it" is say: Fighting in it is great. And he only said: "Say: Fighting in it is great," because the Arabs did not clash their spears in it, so a man would meet the killer of his father or brother in it and not provoke him out of respect for him. And it is called Mudar Al-Asamm, because the sounds of weapons and their clashing stilled in it. And: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam Al-Masry told me, he said, Shuaib bin Al-Layth told us, he said, Al-Layth told us, he said, Al-Zubayr told us, “On the authority of Jabir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not fight in the sacred month unless he was attacked, or he fought until that time came, he stayed until it passed.”

And the saying of God, may He be glorified: And he was averted from the path of God. The meaning of averting from something is preventing it and repelling it. From this it was said: So-and-so turned his face away from so-and-so, if he turned away from him and prevented him from looking at him. And His saying: And he disbelieved in him, means: and he disbelieved in God, and the ba’ in it refers to the name of God which is in the path of God. The interpretation of the statement: And he was averted from the path of God and disbelieved in Him, and from the Sacred Mosque, and expelling the people of the Sacred Mosque - and they are its people and its guardians - is greater in the sight of God than fighting in the sacred month. So, turning people away from the path of God is elevated by His statement: It is greater in the sight of God. And His statement:
h
And expelling his family from it is in apposition to turning people away

Then He began the story of the trial and said: And trial is greater than killing, meaning polytheism is greater and more serious than killing, meaning: whoever killed Ibn al-Hadrami, whose killing you condemned in the sacred month.

Some of the Arab scholars claimed that his statement, and the Sacred Mosque, is connected to fighting, and that its meaning is: They ask you about the sacred month, about fighting in it, and about the Sacred Mosque. So God Almighty said: And the expulsion of its people from it is greater in the sight of God than fighting in the sacred month. This statement, despite its being outside the statements of the scholars, is a statement without basis. Because the people were not in doubt about the enormity of what the polytheists had done to the Muslims in expelling them from their homes in Mecca, so they needed to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the polytheists’ expulsion of them from their homes, and whether that was their right? Rather, none of the Muslims claimed that against them, nor did they ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that.

Since that was the case, the people only asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about what they doubted about his ruling, such as their doubt about the matter of killing Ibn al-Hadrami, when they claimed that his killer was one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he killed him in the sacred month. So they asked about his matter because of their doubt in His ruling. As for the polytheists expelling the people of Islam from the Sacred Mosque, there was not one of them who doubted that it was an injustice on their part to them, so they were asked about it. There is no disagreement among all the people of interpretation that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the reason for killing Ibn al-Hadrami and his killer.
Mentioning the narration from those who said that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, al-Zuhri and Yazid ibn Ruman told me,
m: “on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abdullah ibn Jahsh in Rajab on his return from the first Badr, and he sent with him eight men from the Muhajireen, none of whom were from the Ansar. He wrote him a letter, and ordered him not to look at it until he had traveled for two days, then he would look at it and carry out what he was ordered to do, and not to force any of his companions.” The companions of Abdullah ibn Jahsh were from the Muhajireen. From Banu Abd Shams: Abu Hudhayfah [bin Utbah] bin Rabi’ah - and from Banu Umayyah, - bin Abd Shams, then from their allies: Abdullah ibn Jahsh bin When Abdullah bin Jahsh had traveled for two days, he opened the letter and looked at it, and it said: When you look at this letter of mine, travel until you reach Nakhlah between Mecca and Taif, and watch the Quraysh there and learn for us some report about them. When Abdullah bin Jahsh looked at the letter, he said: We hear and obey. Then he said to his companions: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has ordered me to go to Nakhlah and watch the Quraysh there until I bring him report from them, and he has forbidden me to do so. He went on and his companions went with him, and no one remained behind him, safe from them. He proceeded through the Hijaz until he reached a mine above the branch called Bahran. Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and ʿUtbah ibn Ghazwan lost a camel of theirs which they were riding, so they stayed behind in pursuit of it. ʿAbdullah ibn Jahsh and the rest of his companions continued until they stopped at Nakhalah. A caravan of Quraysh passed by him carrying raisins, fat and merchandise from the Quraysh. Among them were ʿAmr ibn al-Hadrami, ʿUthman ibn ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mughira, his brother Nawfal ibn ʿAbdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, and al-Hakam ibn Kaysan, a client of Hisham ibn al-Mughira. When the people saw them, they feared them, and they had stopped close to them. ʿUkasha ibn Muhsin appeared to them, and he had shaved his head. When they saw him, they felt safe and said: Ammar! We have no problem with them. The people consulted about them, and that was on the last day of Jumada, and the people said: By God, if you leave the people tonight, they will enter the sanctuary and protect themselves from you, and if you kill them, you will kill them in the sacred month! The people hesitated and were afraid to advance on them, then they encouraged them, and they agreed to kill whoever they could of them and take what they had with them. So Waqid bin Abdullah al-Tamimi shot Amr bin al-Hadrami with an arrow and killed him, and Uthman bin Abdullah and al-Hakam bin Kaysan were taken prisoner, and Nawfal bin Abdullah escaped and outmaneuvered them. Abdullah bin Jahsh and his companions advanced with the caravan and the two prisoners until they arrived to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina.

x: Some of the family of Abdullah bin Jahsh mentioned that Abdullah bin Jahsh said to his companions: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has a fifth of what you have taken as spoils. That was before the fifth of the spoils was imposed, so he set aside a fifth of the caravan for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and divided the rest among his companions. When they arrived The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I did not command you to fight in the sacred month! So he stopped the caravan and the two prisoners, and refused to take anything from that. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that, the people were disappointed, and they thought that they were doomed. The Muslims rebuked them for what they did and said to them: You did what you were not commanded to do, and you fought in the sacred month when you were not commanded to fight!

The Quraysh said: Muhammad and his companions have made the sacred month permissible, and they shed blood in it, and took money in it, and took [men] captive! So whoever among the Muslims who were in Mecca Surat Al-Baqarah 2:217 They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say, "Fighting in it is great sin, but averting people from the way of God and disbelief in Him and al-Masjid al-Haram and the expulsion of its people from it are greater in the sight of God.
h
And persecution is greater than killing

. And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever Whoever among you turns back from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter,
h
and those are the companions of the Fire
; they will abide therein eternally. responded to them said: They only did what they did in Jumada!

And the Jews said - taking this as a good omen for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace -: Amr ibn al-Hadrami was killed by Waqid ibn Abdullah! Amr, the war has been prolonged, and al-Hadrami, the war has been present! And Waqid ibn Abdullah, the war has been initiated! So God made that happen for them and for them. When the people increased in that, God, the Almighty, revealed to His Messenger: They ask you about “The sacred month is fighting in it, that is, about fighting in it. Say, ‘Fighting in it is a great sin,’ until His saying:
h
And persecution is greater than killing

, that is, if you were killed in the sacred month, then they have prevented you from the path of God while disbelieving in Him, and from the Sacred Mosque, and your expulsion from it since you are its people and its guardians, is greater in the sight of God than killing those you killed from among them.
h
And persecution is greater than killing

, that is, they were tempting the Muslim from his religion until they returned him to disbelief after his belief, and that is greater in the sight of God than killing, and they will not cease fighting you until they return you from your religion if they are able, that is, they are persisting in the worst and greatest of that, without repenting or desisting. So when the Qur’an was revealed with this matter, and God relieved the Muslims of the fear they were in, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the caravan and the two prisoners.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us from al-Suddi:
m: “They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say, ‘Fighting in it is a great sin,’” that is, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a detachment- They were seven men - and Abdullah bin Jahsh Al-Asadi was appointed over them, and among them were Ammar bin Yasir, Abu Hudhayfah bin Utbah bin Rabi’ah, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Utbah bin Ghazwan Al-Salami, an ally of Banu Nawfal, Suhayl bin Bayda, Aamer bin Fuhayrah, and Waqid bin Abdullah Al-Yarbu’i, an ally of Umar bin Al-Khattab. He wrote a letter with Ibn Jahsh and ordered him not to read it until he reached Batn Malal. When he reached Batn Malal, he opened the letter, and it said: “Go until you reach Batn Nakhl.” He said to his companions: “Whoever wants to die, let him go and make a will, for I am making a will and will proceed according to the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” So he set out, and Saad bin Abi Waqqas and Utbah bin Ghazwan lagged behind him, and they lost their mounts, and they came to Harran looking for it, and Ibn Jahsh set out to Batn Nakhl, and there they found Al-Hakam bin Kaysan, Abdullah bin Al-Mughira, Al-Mughira bin Uthman, and Amr bin Al-Hadrami. They fought, and captured Al-Hakam bin Kaysan and Abdullah bin Al-Mughira, and Al-Mughira escaped, and killed Amr bin Al-Hadrami, who was killed by Waqid bin Abdullah. This was the first booty that the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, captured. When they returned to Medina with the two prisoners and the money they had captured, the people of Mecca wanted to ransom the two prisoners, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let us see what our two companions have done. When Saad and his companion returned, he ransomed the two prisoners. The polytheists attacked him and said: Muhammad claims that he follows the obedience of God, and he was the first to make the sacred month permissible, and he killed our companion in Rajab! The Muslims said: We killed him in Jumada! - and it was said: on the first night of Rajab, and the last night of Jumada - and the Muslims sheathed their swords when Rajab began. Then God Almighty revealed, reproaching the people of Mecca: “They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say: Fighting in it is great.” “It is not permissible. What you have done, O group of polytheists, is greater than killing in the sacred month, when you disbelieved in God.” And you turned away Muhammad and his companions from him, and the expulsion of the people of the Sacred Mosque from it, when they expelled Muhammad, is greater than killing in the sacred month, and the fitnah - which is polytheism - is greater in the sight of God than killing in the sacred month, so that is His saying:
h
And averting from the way of God and disbelief in Him and the Sacred Mosque and the expulsion of its people from it are greater in the sight
of God, and fitnah is greater than killing.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la al-San’ani told us, he said, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman al-Taymi told us, on the authority of his father: that a man told him, on the authority of Abu al-Suwar,
m: telling him on the authority of Jundub ibn Abdullah, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: that he sent a group, and he sent Abu Ubaydah over them. When he was about to set out, he cried out of longing to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he sent a man in his place called Abdullah ibn Jahsh, and wrote him a letter, and ordered him not to read the letter until he reached such and such: And do not compel any of your companions to travel with you. So when he read the letter, he said, ‘I hear and obey the command of God and His Messenger!’

c: So he told them
m: the report and read the letter to them, and two men returned.” The rest of them went on. They found Ibn al-Hadrami and killed him, and they did not know whether it was Rajab or Jumada. The polytheists said to the Muslims: You did such and such in the sacred month! They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him the story. Then God Almighty revealed: “
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein

. Say: Fighting therein is a great sin. But averting people from the way of God and disbelief in Him and al-Masjid al-Haram and the expulsion of its people therefrom are greater in the sight of God. And persecution is polytheism.” Some of those who - I think he said - were in the expedition said: By God, only one killed him! So he said: If it was good, then you have been appointed! And if it was a sin, then you have committed it!

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding God’s statement:
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein

, he said: A man from Banu Tamim was sent by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in an expedition, and he passed by Ibn al-Hadrami carrying wine from Taif to Mecca, so he shot him with an arrow. So he killed him. There was a covenant between Quraysh and Muhammad, so he killed him on the last day of Jumada al-Akhira and the first day of Rajab. Quraysh said: In the sacred month! We have a covenant! So God, the Almighty, the Majestic, revealed: Fighting therein is a great sin, and averting people from the way of God and disbelief in Him and averting people from the Sacred Mosque and expelling his people from it are greater in the sight of God than killing Ibn al-Hadrami, and sedition is disbelief in God, and worshipping idols is greater than all of this.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri and Uthman al-Jazari, and on the authority of Muqsim,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, he said: Waqid bin Abdullah met Amr bin al-Hadrami on the first night of Rajab, and he thought it was Jumada, so he killed him, and he was the first of the polytheists to be killed. The polytheists taunted the Muslims and said: Do you kill in the sacred month? Then God revealed: “
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein

. Say, ‘Fighting therein is a great sin.’ And averting people from the way of God and disbelief in Him and al-Masjid al-Haram,” meaning: averting people from the way of God and disbelief in God, and al-Masjid al-Haram, meaning: averting people from the way of God and disbelief in God, and the expulsion of his people therefrom is greater in the sight of God, than the killing of Amr ibn al-Hadrami, and persecution, meaning: the polytheism in which you are, is also greater than that. Al-Zuhri said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to forbid fighting in the sacred month, then he permitted it later.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: “
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein

. Say, ‘Fighting therein is a great sin.’” That is because the polytheists turned away the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and turned him back from al-Masjid al-Haram in a sacred month, so God granted victory to His Prophet in a sacred month of the following year. The polytheists criticized the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for fighting in a sacred month, so God, the Almighty, said: and averting people from the way of God and disbelieving in God. And that Muhammad sent a detachment, and they met Amr ibn al-Hadrami as he was coming from Taif on the last night of Jumada and the first night of Rajab, and that the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, thought that that night was from Jumada, and it was the first of Rajab, and they did not realize it, so one man from them killed him, and that the polytheists sent to taunt him about that, so God Almighty said: “
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein

. Say: Fighting therein is great.” And other things are greater than that, Hindering people from the way of God and disbelieving in Him and al-Masjid al-Haram and expelling its people therefrom. Expelling the people of al-Masjid al-Haram is greater than what happened to Muhammad, and associating partners with God is worse.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Abu Malik:
m: He said, when the verse was revealed: “
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein
. Say: Fighting therein is great.” to His saying:
h
And persecution is greater than killing
, they were arrogant about it. So he said: And persecution, the polytheism in which you are residing, is greater than what you were arrogant about.

c: I was told on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan
m: said, Abdullah ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Husayn, “On the authority of Abu Malik al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abdullah ibn Jahsh with an army, and he encountered some polytheists in Batn Nakhl, and the Muslims thought that it was the last day of Jumada, and it was the first day of Rajab, so the Muslims killed Ibn al-Hadrami, and the polytheists said: Do you not claim that you are making the sacred month and the sacred land sacred, and you have killed in the sacred month? So God revealed: “They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say: Fighting in it is greater in the sight of God.” From what you were arrogant about killing Ibn al-Hadrami, and the ‘fitnah’ - in which you are residing, meaning polytheism - is greater than killing.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: who said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, who said: And he used to name them - he said: Waqid ibn Abdullah al-Tamimi met Amr ibn al-Hadrami in Batn Nakhl and killed him.

c: Al-Qasim told us,
m: who said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, I said to Ata’, regarding his statement:
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein

, about whom was it revealed? He said: I do not know. Ibn Jurayj said: And Ikrimah and Mujahid said: About Amr ibn al-Hadrami. Ibn Jurayj said, and Ibn Abi Husayn informed us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, that too.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said:
m: Say, ‘Fighting therein is a great sin, and averting people from the way of God and disbelief in Him and al-Masjid al-Haram,’ - he said: He means averting people from al-Masjid al-Haram and expelling its people from it - all of this is greater than the killing of Ibn al-Hadrami -
h
and persecution is greater than killing

- disbelief in God and worshipping idols, is greater than all of this. I narrated to Al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said, I heard Abu Mu’adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid, he said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman al-Bahili informed us, he said, I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say about his statement: “
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein

. Say, ‘Fighting therein is a great sin,’” the companions of Muhammad, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:217 They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say, "Fighting in it is great sin, but averting people from the way of God and disbelief in Him and al-Masjid al-Haram and the expulsion of its people from it are greater in the sight of God.
h
And persecution is greater than killing

. And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever Whoever among you turns back from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter,
h
and those are the companions of the Fire

; they will abide therein eternally. may God bless him and grant him peace, They killed Ibn al-Hadrami in the sacred month, so the polytheists reproached the Muslims for that, so God said: Fighting in the sacred month is a great sin, and greater than that is preventing people from the path of God and disbelieving in it, and expelling the people of the Sacred Mosque from the Sacred Mosque.

x: These two reports that we mentioned from Mujahid and al-Dahhak, inform us of the correctness of what we said about removing the prevention and disbelief in it, and that its remover is greater in the sight of God. They confirm the correctness of what we narrated in that from Ibn ʿAbbas, and indicate the error of those who claimed that it was raised in conjunction with the great sin, and the statement of those who claimed that its meaning is: And greater is preventing people from the path of God, and he claimed that His statement:
h
And expelling his people from it is greater in the sight of God
, is a separate report from what preceded it, a subject.

c: Yaʿqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Ismail bin Salim told us, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And persecution is greater than killing
, he said: He meant disbelief.

c: Bishr bin Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And expelling His family is greater than him in the sight of God. Then he reproached the polytheists for their evil deeds, saying: And trial is greater than killing, meaning: polytheism with God is greater than killing. And similar to what we said about the interpretation of that, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed Amr bin Al-Hadrami on the last night of Jumada and the first night of Rajab, the polytheists sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reproaching him for that, so he said: “They ask you about the sacred month. Fighting in it. Say, fighting in it is a great sin.” And other things are greater than that: Hindering people from the path of God and disbelieving in Him and the Sacred Mosque and expelling its people from it is greater than what happened to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: As for the people of Arabic, they differed about what raised his statement:
h
And hindered people from the path of God

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: There are two views regarding raising it: One of them is that the hindering is returned to the greater, meaning: Say, fighting in it is a great sin and hindering people from the path of God is greater. God and disbelief in Him. And if you wish, you can make the turning away a great thing, meaning: Say, fighting in it is a great thing, and turning away from the path of God and disbelief in Him is a great thing.

He said, so Al-Farra’ made a mistake in both of his interpretations. That is because if he raises the turning away in conjunction with it is a great thing, the interpretation of the statement becomes: Say, fighting in the sacred month is a great thing and turning away from the path of God and disbelief in it. And that is an interpretation contrary to what all the people of Islam are upon. Because no one claimed that God, the Blessed and Exalted, made fighting in the sacred months disbelief in God, rather it is not permissible for a rational person who understands what he says to imagine saying it. And how is it permissible for someone with a sound nature to say it, when God, the Most High, says in the aftermath of that:
h
And expelling his people from it is greater in the sight of God

?! If the statement was as he saw it permissible in this interpretation, then it would be necessary that expelling the people of the Sacred Mosque from the Sacred Mosque was greater in the sight of God than disbelief in it, because he says in the aftermath of it:
h
And expelling his people from it is greater in the sight of God

And in establishing the proof that there is nothing Greater in the sight of God than disbelief in Him, which shows the error of this statement. However, if the aversion is raised, in the sense of what he claimed to be the other face - and that raising it means: and a great aversion from the path of God, then it is said: "And the expulsion of his people from it is greater in the sight of God" - the meaning becomes that the expulsion of the people of the Sacred Mosque from the Sacred Mosque is greater in the sight of God than disbelief in God and aversion from His path, and from the Sacred Mosque. And the one who interprets that in the same way, enters into the error like that which the speaker of the first statement entered into: of making some of the characteristics of disbelief greater in the sight of God than disbelief itself. And that is something that no one can imagine to be wrong and corrupt.

And some of the Arabists from Basra used to say the first statement in raising the aversion, and they claim that it is connected to the great, and they make his statement: "And the expulsion of his people" raised as a subject. And we have shown the corruption of that and the error of its interpretation.
Then the people of interpretation differed regarding his statement: "
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein
. Say: Fighting therein is great," is it abrogated or the ruling is established?

Some of them said: It is Abrogated by the words of God the Almighty: And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together (al-Tawbah 9:36), and by His words: Kill the polytheists (al-Tawbah 9:5).
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ ibn Maysarah said:
m: Fighting was permitted in the sacred month in Surat Bara’ah, his words: So wrong not yourselves therein, and fight the polytheists all together (al-Tawbah 9:36): He says: In them and other than them.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said, Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to forbid fighting in the sacred month, then he permitted it later.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a fixed ruling, fighting is not permitted for anyone in the sacred months by this verse, because God made fighting in them a major sin.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I said: Ata’ said: “
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein

. Say: Fighting therein is great.” I said: What is wrong with them! And then it is not permissible for them to raid the people of polytheism in the sacred month, then raid them after that? So Ata’ swore to me by God: It is not permissible for people to raid in the sacred month, nor to fight in it, nor is it recommended. He said: And they are not called to Islam before they fight, nor to the jizyah, so they left that.

x: The correct statement in that is what Ata’ bin Maysarah said: That the prohibition of fighting the polytheists in the sacred months was abrogated by the statement of God, the Most High: “Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve [lunar] months in the Book of God on the Day He created the heavens and the earth. Of these, four are sacred. That is the right religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight the polytheists collectively as they fight you collectively.” (al-Tawbah 9:36). We only said that it abrogates His statement: “
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein

. Say: Fighting therein is great,” because of the evidence of the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He invaded Hawazin in Hunayn and Thaqif in Taif, and sent Abu Amir to Awtas to fight the polytheists there, during some of the sacred months, which were in Shawwal and some of Dhu al-Qa’dah, which are among the sacred months.

It was known from this that if fighting during these months was forbidden and a sin, he would have been the furthest from doing it, may God bless him and grant him peace. Another thing is that all the people of knowledge of the biography of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do not dispute that the Pledge of Ridwan to fight the Quraysh was in Dhu al-Qa’dah, and that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, only called his companions to it on that day because he had heard that the polytheists had killed Uthman ibn Affan when he sent him to them with the message he had sent him with. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged to fight the people and fight them, until Uthman returned with the message. A peace treaty took place between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Quraysh, so he stopped fighting them at that time and fighting them.
That was in Dhu al-Qa’dah, which is among the sacred months. So if that was the case, then it is clear that what we said in his statement:
h
They ask you about the month If someone thinks that the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months was after the Prophet
, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made them lawful for what we have described of his wars, then he has thought out of ignorance. This is because this verse - I mean His statement:
h
They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein - is about the matter of Abdullah bin Jahsh and his companions

, and what happened to them and the matter of the man they killed. So God revealed this verse about him at the end of Jumada al-Akhira in the second year after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Medina and migrated to it. The battles of Hunayn and Ta’if were in Shawwal in the eighth year after his arrival in Medina and migrated to it, and there was a period of time between them that is not hidden from anyone.
God Almighty means: And the polytheists of Quraysh will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able to do so, as:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me, Al-Zuhri and Yazid ibn Ruman told me, on the authority of ʿUrwah ibn Al-Zubayr:
m: And they will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able, meaning: They will persist in the worst and greatest of that, without repenting or desisting, meaning: To tempt the Muslims from their religion until they turn them back to disbelief, as they used to do with those of them whom they were able to do before the migration.

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, Abu ʿAsim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: And they will continue to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able, he said: The polytheists of Quraysh.
