x: What He, the Most High, means by His statement:
h
And whoever among you turns back from his religion

, is whoever among you turns back from His religion, as He, the Most High, said: So they turned back, following their footsteps (al-Kahf 18:64), meaning by His saying: So they turned back, they returned.

i: And from that it was said:
x: So-and-so took back his right from so-and-so, if he took it back from him. And the doubling was shown in His saying: returns because the lam of the verb is still in the jussive mood, and if it is still then the analogy is to leave the doubling, and it may be doubled and assimilated while still, based on the dual and plural. And His saying: So he died while he was a disbeliever, He says: Whoever turns back from his religion, the religion of Islam, So he died while he was a disbeliever, he dies before he repents from his disbelief, so they are the ones whose deeds have been in vain.

He means by His saying: Their deeds have been in vain, they have become null and gone. And by its length: the loss of its reward, and by the length of the reward for it and the recompense in the abode of this world and the hereafter. And His saying:
h
And those are the companions of the Fire

, they will abide therein eternally, meaning: those who turned back from their religion and died in their disbelief, they are the people of the Fire, eternally therein. And He made them its people Because they do not leave it, they are its residents who reside in it, just as it is said: These are the people of such-and-such a neighborhood, meaning: its residents who reside in it. And what he means by his saying:
h
They will abide therein forever is that they will remain there for a long time

, without any time or end. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:217 They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say, "Fighting in it is great sin, but averting people from the way of God and disbelief in Him and al-Masjid al-Haram and the expulsion of its people from it are greater in the sight of God.
h
And persecution is greater than killing

. And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever Whoever among you turns back from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter,
h
and those are the companions of the Fire
; they will abide therein eternally.

evidence.text: And this is how Abdullah bin Mas'ud read it, as he mentioned to us, and: - I was told by Ammar bin Al-Hasan, he said, Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi', his saying: "They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting in it," he said: He says: They ask you about fighting in it.
He said: And this is how he used to read it: about fighting in it.
He wrote a letter with Ibn Jahsh and ordered him not to read it until he reached Batn Malal.

So he sent a man in his place called Abdullah ibn Jahsh, and wrote him a letter, and ordered him not to read the letter until he reached such and such: And do not compel any of your companions to travel with you.
So when he read the letter, he said, ‘I hear and obey the command of God and His Messenger!’
So he told them the report and read the letter to them, and two men returned.”

x: By that, the Most High means: Those who believed in God and His Messenger and what he brought, and by His saying:
h
And those who emigrated

, those who abandoned living with the polytheists in their cities and being their neighbors in their homes, so they moved away from them and their neighborhood and their country, to another place by emigration 1... ... 2 because they moved away from it to what they moved to. The origin of emigration is the reciprocal from the emigration of a man to a man due to enmity that occurs between them, then it is used for everyone who emigrated from something because of something he disliked from it. The emigrants from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were called emigrants because of what we described of their emigration from their homes and dwellings out of their dislike of settling among the polytheists and under their authority, such that they were not safe from their temptation for themselves in their homes - to the place where they were safe from that.

As for His saying: And they struggled, it means: and they fought and waged war. The root of the word mujahidah is mufa’ala, from the saying of a man: so-and-so exerted so-and-so on such-and-such - if he made him suffer and struggled - he exerted him with effort. If the action is done by two people, each of whom suffers from the other with hardship and difficulty, it is said: so-and-so is striving with so-and-so - meaning: each of them does to the other what exhausts and makes him suffer - so he is striving with him with striving and struggle. As for the path of God, it is His way and His religion. So the meaning of His statement if:
h
And those who emigrated

and struggled in the cause of God and those who migrated from the authority of the polytheists by emigrating for them, fearing their temptation for their religions, and fought them for the sake of God’s religion in order to bring them into it and in that which pleases God, those are the ones who hope for the mercy of God, meaning: they hope that God will have mercy on them and admit them into His Paradise by virtue of His mercy towards them.

And God is Forgiving, meaning He covers the sins of His servants by pardoning them, and bestows mercy upon them. This verse was also mentioned to have been revealed about Abdullah bin Jahsh and his companions.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, that a man told him, on the authority of Abu Al-Suwar,
m: telling him on the authority of Jundub bin Abdullah, he said: When what happened with Abdullah bin Jahsh and his companions and the matter of Ibn Al-Hadrami happened, some of the Muslims said: If they did not gain any sin in their journey - I think he said: - then they will have no reward for it. So God revealed: “Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the cause of God - those are the ones who hope for the mercy of God. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: Az-Zuhri and Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, on the authority of Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, who said:
m: God, the Almighty, revealed the Qur’an with what He revealed of the matter, and God relieved the Muslims in the matter of Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his companions - meaning: in their killing of Ibn Al-Hadrami - and when the state they were in when the Qur’an was revealed was cleared to Abdullah ibn Jahsh and his companions, they hoped for the reward, and they said: O Messenger of God, do we hope to have a battle in which we will be given the reward of the mujahideen? So God, the Almighty, revealed about them: Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the cause of God - those are the ones hoping for the mercy of God, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. So God placed them in the greatest hope because of that.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh narrated to us,
m: who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, who said: God praised the companions of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the best praise, and said: Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and striven in the cause of God - those are the ones hoping for the mercy of God, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. These are the best of this nation. Then God made them people of hope as you hear, and that whoever hopes seeks, and whoever fears flees.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly.

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: Your companions ask you, O Muhammad, about wine and drinking it. And wine is every drink that has intoxicated the mind, concealing it and covering it. It is from the saying of the one who said: I covered the vessel, or the man was intoxicated, if he entered into the wine. It is said: He is in the people's cloak and their cloak, meaning he entered into people's honor. And the hyena is called: Khamri Umm Aamer, meaning he concealed himself. And whatever disease and drunkenness intoxicates the mind, mixes with it and covers it, is wine. And from that also is the woman's veil, because she covers her head with it, so she covers it. And from that it is said: He walks for you with wine, meaning hidden, as Al-Ajjaj said: In the shining of eagles, wine does not come, directing the earth and driving the trees What he means by his saying: The wine does not come, does not come hidden or stealthily, but openly with banners and armies.

And the eagles are the plural of eagle, which are banners. As for gambling, it is the passive participle of the speaker’s saying: He made this matter easy for me, if it is obligatory for me, so he makes it easy for me with ease and ease, and the gambler is the obligatory, with lots it is obligatory, or an opener or something else.

i: Then it was said to the gambler, Yasir and Yasir, as the poet said:
x: I became like a fool who turns the dice after he has been taken away.

As Al-Nabigha said: Or Yasser, the arrows went abundantly, sorry, the friend ate them, he was dislocated By al-Yāsir he means: the gambler. Gambling is also called maysār. Mujahid used to say something similar to what we have said about that.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
, he said: Gambling. It was called maysār because they say: Make money and make money, like saying: Put down such and such.

c: Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: All gambling is from maysār, even children playing with nuts. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated, he said: Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, he said: Abdullah said: Beware of these branded young girls that you drive away, for they are from gambling. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, he said: Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umair, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, the same. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Nafiʿ narrated, he said: Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said: Beware of these young girls that you drive away, for they are from gambling. Ali ibn Saʿid al-Kindi narrated, he said: Ali ibn Musahhir narrated, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said: Gambling is gambling. Ibn Bashar narrated, he said: Abu ʿAmir narrated, he said: Sufyan narrated, on the authority of ʿAsim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said: Everything that has a risk - or: is in danger, Abu ʿAmir was not sure - is from gambling. Al-Walid bin Shuja Abu Hammam narrated that Ali bin Masaher narrated that Asim narrated that Muhammad bin Sirin said: All gambling is maysir, even playing with dice while standing and shouting and with a feather placed on a man’s head. Ibn Hamid narrated that Jarir narrated that Asim narrated that Ibn Sirin said: Every Surat Al-Baqarah 2:219
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say, "
h
In them is great sin

and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit." And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, "The excess." Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may give thought. game in which there is gambling, such as drinking, shouting or standing, is maysir. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la narrated that Khalid bin Al-Harith narrated that Al-Ash’ath narrated that Al-Hasan said: Maysir is gambling. Ya’qub bin Ibrahim narrated that Al-Mu’tamir narrated that Laith narrated that Tawus and Ata’ said: All gambling is maysir, even the children’s playing with sticks and nuts. Ibn Hamid narrated that Hakam narrated that Amr narrated that Ata’ narrated that Sa’id said: Maysir is gambling.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik bin Umair told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Ubaid God, he said:
m: Beware of these two Kaaba, which are used to warn people, for they are part of gambling.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Urubah, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: As for his statement: and gambling, it refers to all forms of gambling.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Salim told me, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Umar,
m: that he heard Umar ibn Ubaydullah say to al-Qasim ibn Muhammad: Backgammon is gambling. What do you think of chess? Is it gambling? Al-Qasim said: Everything that distracts from the remembrance of God and from prayer is gambling.

c: Ali ibn Dawud told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Gambling is gambling. In the pre-Islamic era, a man would bet on his family and his wealth, and whichever of them gambled with his companion would take his family and wealth.

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, he said, Amr ibn Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: Gambling is gambling.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Gambling is gambling.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair, they said:
m: Maysir is all gambling, even the nuts that children play with.

c: I was told by Al-Hussein,
m: he said, I heard Abu Muadh Al-Fadl bin Khalid, he said, I heard Ubaidullah bin Sulaiman narrating, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, his statement: And Maysir, he said: Gambling.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, he said:
m: Maysir is gambling.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Badr Shuja’ bin Al-Walid told us, he said, Musa bin Uqbah told us, on the authority of Nafi’
m: that Ibn Umar used to say: Gambling is from Maysir.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Maysir is the arrows of the Arabs and the dice of the Persians. He said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ata bin Maysarah claimed that Maysir is all gambling.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abd al-Aziz, he said, Makhul said:
m: Gambling is gambling.

c: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dhara’ told us, he said, al-Fadl ibn Sulayman and Shuja’ ibn al-Walid told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: Gambling is gambling. As for His statement: “Say:
h
In them is great sin

and [yet, some] benefit for people,” He, the Most High, means by that: Say, O Muhammad, to them: In them, meaning in wine and gambling, is great sin. So the great sin in them is what was mentioned by al-Suddi in what was mentioned by Musa ibn Harun, he said, Amr ibn Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: As for his saying:
h
There is a great sin in them
, the sin of alcohol is that a man drinks and becomes drunk and harms people. The sin of gambling is that a man gambles and thus prevents the truth and is unjust.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Say, ‘
h
There is a great sin in them
,’ he said: This is the first reason for which wine was criticised.

c: Ali ibn Dawud told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: Say, ‘
h
There is a great sin in them
,’ means what is diminished from the faith of the one who drinks it.

x: What is more deserving of the interpretation of the great sin that God, the Most High, mentioned is that it is in gambling in wine: in wine what al-Suddi said: The loss of the mind of the wine drinker when he becomes intoxicated from drinking it until he loses knowledge of his Lord, and that is the greatest of sins. And that is the meaning of what Ibn Abbas said, God willing. As for gambling, it distracts from the remembrance of God and from prayer, and causes enmity and hatred between those who are gambling because of it, as our Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, described it in His saying:
h
Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God

and from prayer (al-Ma’idah 5:91). As for His saying: and benefits for people, the benefits of alcohol were its prices before it was prohibited, and the pleasure they attained by drinking it, as Al-A’sha said in describing it: We have from its morning a malicious soul, depression, and the memory of worries whose harm never goes away.

At dinner, she is in good spirits, has a lot of pleasure and money, and is proud of her ecstasies. As Hassan said: We drink it and it leaves us kings and lions, and the encounter does not end us. As for the benefits of gambling, they are the shares of the camels they get. This is because they used to gamble on the camels, and if one of them escaped, his companion would slaughter him, then they would divide up tenths according to the number of arrows. In this regard, A’sha of Banu Tha’labah said: And the roots of the left I called to the dew and the deserted lands I fear their loss And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The benefits here are what they get from the camels.

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, he said: Amr ibn Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for their benefits, the benefit of wine is in its pleasure and price, and the benefit of gambling is in what is gained from the gambling.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafai told us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: “Say:
h
In them is great sin
and [yet, some] benefit for people,” he said: Their benefits were before they were forbidden.

c: Ali ibn Dawud told us, he said: Abu Salih told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And benefits for people, he said: He says in what they get from its pleasure and joy when they drink it. The reading of this differed: Most of the people of Medina and some of the Kufians and Basrans read it: “Say: in them is a great sin” with the letter ba, meaning say: in. Drinking this and gambling this are great sins.

x: Others from the two cities of Basra and Kufa read it: Say in them is a great sin, meaning many sins. It seems that they saw that sin means sins even though it is the same in wording, so they described it with its meaning of many.
The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who read it with the letter ba’: Say in them is a great sin, because they all agreed on his saying:
h
And their sin is greater than their benefit

, and his reading with the letter ba’. In this is clear evidence that what was described as the first sin of that is greatness and largeness, not greatness in number. If what was described as that was greatness, it would have been said:
h
And their sin is greater than their benefit

By that, He, the Mighty and Sublime, meant: And the sin of drinking this [wine] and gambling this is greater and more harmful to them than the benefit they attain through them. This was the case because when they were drunk, some of them would attack each other and fight each other, and if they were secretive, evil would occur between them because of it, which would lead them to what they would sin for. This verse was revealed about alcohol before it was explicitly forbidden, so God, the Most High, attributed the sin to them, and the sin is due to their causes, since it was caused by their cause. A number of the people of interpretation have said: The meaning of this is: Their sin after they were forbidden is greater than their benefit before they were forbidden.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
And their sin is greater than their benefit
, he said: Their benefits were before the prohibition, and their sin was after they were forbidden.

c: I was told by ʿAmmar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: And benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit, the benefits were revealed before the prohibition, and the sin was revealed after it was forbidden. Al-Husayn narrated, he said: I heard Abu Muadh, he said:

c: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed me, he said:
m: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
And their sin is greater than their benefit
, he said: Their sin after the prohibition is greater than their benefit before the prohibition.

c: Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Muawiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And their sin is greater than their benefit
, he said: What is lost of the religion and the sin in it is greater than what they gain in its joy when they drink it.

x: We chose what we said about that interpretation because of the frequency of the reports and their agreement that this was revealed before the prohibition of alcohol and gambling, so it was known from that that the sin that God mentioned in this verse and attributed to them, he meant the sin that occurs as a result of their causes - as we have described - not the sin after the prohibition.
Narrations indicating what we said, that this verse was revealed before the prohibition of alcohol:

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: When the verse was revealed: “
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say, ‘
h
In them is great sin
and [yet, some] benefit for people,’” some people disliked it because of His statement:
h
In them is great sin
, and some people drank it because of His statement:
h
And benefit for people
, until the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying
r
(An-Nisa’: 43)

. He said: So they would leave it out during prayer and drink it at times other than the time of prayer, until the verse was revealed: Intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it (al-Ma’idah 5:90). So Umar said: What a waste for you! Today it has been linked to gambling!

c: Muhammad ibn Muammar told me, he said, Abu Aamer told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Hamid told us, on the authority of Abu Tawbah al-Misri, he said,
m: “I heard Abdullah ibn Umar say: God, the Almighty, revealed three verses about wine. The first of which was revealed was: ‘
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say, “
h
In them is great sin

.”’ The verse. They said: O Messenger of God, we benefit from it and drink it as God, the Almighty, said in His Book! Then this verse was revealed: ‘O you who believe! Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated.’ The verse. They said: O Messenger of God, we do not drink it when the prayer is near. He said: Then this verse was revealed: ‘Intoxicants, gambling, idolatry, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid them.’ The verse. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Wine has been forbidden.” Ibn Hamid narrated, Yahya bin Wadh narrated, Al-Hussein narrated, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan, who said: God said: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are Surat Al-Baqarah 2:219
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say, "
h
In them is great sin

and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit." And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, "The excess." Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may give thought. intoxicated until you know what you are saying, and “
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say, “
h
In them is great sin

and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit,” so the verse in Al-Ma’idah abrogated it, and He said: O you who have believed, indeed, wine and gambling are but… Al-Ma’idah 5:1-2. Ibn Bashar narrated, on the authority of Abdul Wahhab, who said, Aouf narrated, on the authority of Abu Al-Qamous Zaid bin Ali, who said: God, the Almighty, revealed three times about wine. The first thing that was revealed was God’s statement: “
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say, ‘
h
In them is great sin

and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit.’” He said: “So whoever God willed among the Muslims drank it, until two men drank it and entered into prayer and began to utter words that Awf did not know what they were saying. So God, the Almighty, revealed about them: “O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying.” So whoever drank it among them drank it, and they began to avoid it when praying, until - according to what Abu al-Qamus claimed - a man drank it and began to wail over those killed at Badr: Greetings, Umm Amr. And do you have any greetings for your family? Let me wake up early, for I saw death digging for Hisham. Banu Mughirah would have sacrificed a thousand men or camels for him. Like a full moon, crowned with a hump Like a full moon, full of noble men and women He said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of that, he came in a panic, dragging his cloak in fear, until he reached him. When the man saw him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised something that was in his hand to hit him. He said: I seek refuge in God from the wrath of God and His Messenger! By God, I will never eat it again! Then God revealed its prohibition: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement until His saying: Will you then desist? (al-Ma’idah 5:90). Then Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: We have desisted, we have desisted!! Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated: Ishaq al-Azraq narrated on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: Four verses were revealed concerning wine: “
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say, ‘
h
In them is great sin

and [yet, some] benefit for people.’” So they abandoned it. Then the following verse was revealed: You take from it an intoxicant and good provision. (al-Nahl: 67) So they drank it. Then the two verses were revealed in al-Ma’idah 5:Indeed, wine and gambling and idols and divining arrows until His saying: So will you not desist?

c: Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, he said: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: He said: This verse was revealed:
h
They ask you about wine and gambling

, and they continued drinking it until Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf made food and invited some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them Ali ibn Abi Talib, and he recited: Say, ‘O you disbelievers,’ but he did not understand them. Then God the Almighty revealed a verse that is strict about alcohol: O you who believe! Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying. So it was permissible for them to drink from the dawn prayer until the sun rose or reached midday, then they would get up for the noon prayer while they were sane, then they would not drink it until they prayed the ‘Isha’ prayer, then they would drink it until midday and sleep, then they would get up for the dawn prayer while they were sane. They continued drinking it until Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas made a meal, and he invited some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them a man from the Ansar, so he roasted a camel’s head for them and then invited them to it. When they ate and drank from the alcohol, they became drunk and began to talk. Sa’d said something, and the Ansari became angry, so he lifted the camel’s jawbone and broke Sa’d’s nose. Then God revealed the abrogation and prohibition of alcohol, and said: Indeed, alcohol, gambling, idolatry, and divining arrows until His saying: Will you then desist?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada - and on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid -
m: regarding His statement:
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
, he said: When this verse was revealed, some people drank it and some left it, until its prohibition was revealed in Surat Al-Ma’idah.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Say, ‘There is great sin in them,’ he said: This is the first reason for which wine was criticized.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement: “
h
They ask you about wine and gambling

. Say, ‘There is great sin in them and [yet, some] benefit for people,” so God condemned them and did not prohibit them, because He wanted to extend the period and the appointed time for them. Then God revealed in Surat An-Nisa’ something more severe than it: Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, so they would drink it, and when the time for prayer came, they would stop, so drunkenness was forbidden to them. Then God Almighty revealed in Surat Al-Ma'idah after the Battle of the Confederates: O you who have believed, indeed, wine and gambling are but to: that you may be successful. So its prohibition came in this verse, a little of it and a lot of it, what intoxicates and what does not. And the Arabs at that time had no life more pleasing to them than it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement: “
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say:
h
In them is great sin

and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit.” He said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your Lord has preceded in prohibiting wine. He said: Then it was revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, wine, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars [to other than God], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it. (al-Maʿidah: 90), and wine was prohibited at that time.

c: Yunus narrated to me,
m: who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement:
h
They ask you about wine and gambling

, the entire verse, he said: Three verses were abrogated, in Surat al-Maʿidah, and by the punishment that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prescribed, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to strike them with a prescribed punishment for that, but he used to act according to his own opinion, and it was not a specified punishment, but it was a prescribed punishment. And he recited: Intoxicants and gambling are only forbidden verse.

x: By that, He, the Most High, means: And your companions ask you, O Muhammad: What do they spend of their wealth to give in charity? So say to them, O Muhammad: Spend from it what is beyond their means.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of extra in this context.
Some of them said: It means surplus.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Amr ibn Ali al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Wakee’ narrated to us
m: - H, and Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us - on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, saying: Pardon is that which is left over from your family.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “Say: Pardon,” meaning the excess.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: saying: It is the excess.

c: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Malik narrated to us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding His statement: pardon, he said: the excess.

c: Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: saying: pardon, meaning the excess.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘The excess,’” he said: The people used to work every day according to what it had, and if there was any surplus that day from their children, they would put it forward, and they would not leave their children hungry, and they would give it in charity to the people.

c: Amr ibn Ali told us, he said, Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, he said, Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Hasan
m: regarding His statement, “And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘The excess,’” he said: It is the surplus, the surplus of money.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: What was not clear to the one who spent it or gave it in charity.
Those who said this were:

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they ask you what they should spend
. Say: The excess,” meaning: What is not clear in your wealth.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Tawus,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty and Majestic: “
h
And they ask you what they should spend
. Say: The excess,” he said: The little of everything.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: The average in spending, as long as it is neither extravagance nor stinginess.
Those who said this were:

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told us, he said: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of al-Hasan In His statement:
m: h
And they ask you what they should spend
. Say, ‘The excess,’” He says: Do not exhaust your wealth until it runs out for the people.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: I asked Ata’ about His statement: “
h
They ask you what they should spend
. Say, ‘The excess,’” He said: Excess in spending means that you do not exhaust your wealth until it runs out and you ask the people.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: I asked Ata’ about His statement: “
h
They ask you what they should spend
. Say, ‘The excess,’” He said: Excess is as long as they are neither extravagant nor stingy in what is right. He said: Mujahid said: Excess is charity from surplus wealth.

c: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us,
m: who said: Yahya ibn Sa’id narrated to us, who said: Aouf narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement: “
h
They ask you what they should spend
. Say, ‘The excess,’” He said: It means that you do not exhaust your wealth.

x: Others said that the meaning of this is: Say ‘the excess’, take from them whatever they give you, little or much.
Those who said this were:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And they ask you what they should spend
. Say ‘the excess’,” meaning: Whatever they give you, little or much, accept it from them.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Whatever is good of your wealth.
Those who said this were:

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’, regarding his statement: “
h
They ask you what they should spend
. Say ‘the excess’,” he said: He says: The good of it, meaning: The best and purest of your wealth.

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatadah, he said: He used to say: The excess is the surplus, meaning: The best of your wealth.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is the obligatory charity.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qays bin Saad - or Isa, on the authority of Qays, on the authority of Mujahid - Abu Asim was not sure - the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:
m: h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say, "
h
In them is great sin

and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit." And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, "The excess." Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may give thought. statement of God Almighty: “Say: ‘Pardon’,” he said: the obligatory charity.

x: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: the meaning of pardon is: the surplus of a man’s money. On his own behalf and his family’s behalf in their essential needs. This is the virtue that the narrations of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) have demonstrated in permitting charity, and his charity in the ways of righteousness.
Mentioning some of the narrations that were narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding this:

c: Ali bin Muslim narrated to us, he said, Abu Asim and Ibn Ajlan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: A man said:
m: O Messenger of God, I have a dinar! He said: Spend it on yourself. He said: I have another! He said: Spend it on your family. He said: I have another! He said: Spend it on your children! He said: I have another! He said: Then you are more discerning!

c: Muhammad bin Muammar Al-Bahrani narrated to me, he said, Ruh bin Ubadah narrated to us, he said, Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, he said, Abu Al-Zubayr informed me that
m: he heard Jabir bin Abdullah say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “If one of you is poor, let him start with himself. If he has extra, let him start with himself and those he supports, then if he finds extra after that, let him give charity to others.”

c: Amr bin Ali narrated to us, Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Asim bin Umar bin Qatada, on the authority of Mahmud bin Labid,
m: “On the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a golden egg that he had found in some mine, and he said: O Messenger of God, take this from me as charity, for by God I do not own anything else this morning! So he turned away from him. Then he came to him from his right corner and said to him the same thing, so he turned away from him. Then he said to him the same thing, so he turned away from him. Then he said to him the same thing, so he said angrily: Give it to him! So he took it and threw it at him as if he had been wounded or hamstrung, then he said: One of you brings all his wealth and gives it in charity, and sits begging from people, for charity is only from surplus wealth.”

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Mukharami, who said:
m: I heard Abu al-Ahwas narrating, on the authority of ʿAbdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Give charity from the surplus, and start with those you are responsible for, and do not blame yourself for not having enough. And similar reports that would take too long to mention in detail in the book. So if what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted his nation to give in charity from their wealth, from what is surplus to the need of the one giving the charity, then the surplus from that is the pardon from the man’s wealth, since pardon in the speech of the Arabs, in wealth and in everything, means increase and abundance. And from that is His statement, may His praise be exalted: until they have pardoned meaning: they have increased in number and multiplied, and from that is the statement of the poet: But we bite the sword from it with the markets of the fat pile It means: those with a lot of fat. And from that it was said to a man: Take what he pardoned you from so-and-so, meaning what is left over and he cleared for you from his effort with what he did not exert himself, it was clear 1 that what God permitted in His saying: Say pardon to His servants from spending, so He permitted them to spend it if they wanted to spend it, is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained to his nation with his saying:
h
The best charity is that which you spend out of need
, and he permitted them with it.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: Why do you deny that pardon is the obligatory charity?

We deny that because the proof has been established that whoever has lost his money due from the obligatory zakat and all of his money is lost except for the amount that is obligatory for the people of the two shares of charity, he must hand it over to them, if the loss of his money was after his negligence in fulfilling the obligation, then they have his money, to them. And that is without a doubt his effort - if he hands it over to them - not his pardon. In naming God, the Most High, what He taught His servants to spend from their money as forgiveness, what nullifies that it is deserving of the name effort in a given situation. If that is the case, then it is clear that the statement of those who claim that the meaning of forgiveness is what the owner of the money gives to his leader and he gives it to him, regardless of how little or much his money is, and the statement of those who claim that it is the obligatory charity, is invalid. Likewise, there is no basis for the statement of those who say that its meaning is: what is not clear in your money, “because when Abu Lubab said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Part of my repentance is that I turn to God and His Messenger to give charity from my money, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A third of that is sufficient for you,” and likewise it was narrated from Ka’b ibn Malik that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said something similar to that.

There is no doubt that the third is from the wealth of the wealthy person, but for me it is as God the Most High said: And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly, but are between those extremes (al-Furqan 25:67), and as God the Most High said to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And do not make your hand as if it were chained to your neck nor stretch it forth to its utmost extent and you would sit down blamed and destitute
r
(Al-Isra’: 29)

, and that is what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, limited in what is less than that according to the amount of money and its capacity. Then the scholars differed regarding this verse: Is it abrogated or is the ruling on the servants still valid?
Some of them said: It is abrogated, abrogated by the obligatory zakat.

Those who said that: Ali bin Dawud told me, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘The excess.’” He said: This was before zakat was made obligatory.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘The excess.’” He said: No known obligation was made obligatory for it. Then he said: Adopt what is easy, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant (al-A’raf 7:199). Then the obligations were revealed after that by name.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘The excess.’” This was abrogated by zakat.

x: Others said: Rather, the ruling is confirmed and not abrogated.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qays bin Saad,
m: or Isa, on the authority of Qays, on the authority of Mujahid - Abu Asim was uncertain - he said: Pardon is the obligatory charity.

x: The correct statement in this regard is what Ibn ʿAbbas said, as narrated by ʿAtiyyah, that his saying, Say ‘Pardon’ is not an obligation imposed by God as a right in his wealth, but rather it is an announcement from Him of what pleases Him in terms of spending from what displeases Him, in response to someone who asked His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, about what pleases Him. It is an instruction from God to all of His creation based on what He taught them regarding non-obligatory charity, the ruling of which is fixed and does not abrogate a ruling that was before it that was different, nor is it abrogated by a ruling that occurred after it. So it is not appropriate for a pious and religious person to exceed in his voluntary charity, gifts, supererogatory gifts, and charity what His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught them in his saying, If any one of you has extra money, let him start with himself, then with his family, then with his children, then he should follow the path of extra money that pleases God and that He loves.

This is the balance between extravagance and miserliness, which God, the Almighty, mentioned in His Book, God willing. It is said to the one who claims that this has been abrogated: What is the evidence for its abrogation, and everyone has agreed, without disagreement, that a man may spend from his money in charity, a gift, or a will, a third? So what is the evidence that this has been abrogated?

q.l: If he claims that he means by his statement:
x: it has been abrogated, that giving the amnesty from the money is not obligatory, and that the obligation of that is dropped because of the existence of zakat on the money?

What is the evidence that giving the amnesty was an obligation, but the obligation of zakat dropped it, and there is no evidence in the verse that this was an obligation, since it was not a command from God, the Exalted, but rather it indicates that it is an answer to what the people asked about in order to recognize what pleases God in charity? And the one who claims this has no way to provide evidence that necessitates the validity of his claim.

As for the readings, they differed in the reading of al-ʿafu. The majority of the readers of Hijaz, the readers of the Haramayn, and most of the readers of Kufa read it: Qul al-ʿafu in the accusative case.

Some of the readers of Yasri read it: Qul al-ʿafu in the nominative case. Whoever reads it in the accusative case makes what one letter, and makes it accusative by saying: they spend, as I explained before - then he makes the pardon accusative based on that. So the meaning of the statement then is:
h
And they ask you what they should spend

? And whoever reads it in the nominative case makes ma a connection to dha, and they raised al-‘afu. So the meaning of the statement then is: What are they spending? Say: Al-thalith yanfiqunu, al-‘afu. And if he put al-‘afu in the accusative case, then made ma two letters, meaning: They ask you what are they spending? Say: They spend al-‘afu, and raised those who made ma one letter, meaning: What are they spending? Say: Al-thalith yanfiqunu, as a predicate, it would be correct and sound in Arabic. And with whichever of the two readings it was read, it is correct in my opinion, because their meanings are similar, with the prevalence of reading with each one of them.

However, the reading that I like the most, even if that is the case, is the reading of whoever reads it in the accusative case, because those who read it with it are more, and it is more well-known and famous.
What He, the Mighty and Sublime, means by His saying:
h
Thus does God make clear to you His signs

, is this: He makes clear, that is, just as I made clear to you My signs and proofs - which are His signs - in this Surah, and made you aware therein of what will save you from My punishment, and made clear to you My limits and My obligations, and alerted you therein to the evidence of My Oneness, then to the proofs of My Messenger to you, and guided you to the manifestation of guidance, so I make clear to you in the rest of My Book that I revealed to My Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, My signs and proofs and make them clear to you, so that you may reflect on My promise and My threat, My reward and My punishment, and choose My obedience, by which you will attain My reward in the Hereafter, and attain eternal bliss, over a few pleasures and a few desires, by engaging in My disobedience in this transient world, which whoever engages in will be returned to Me, and will end up in what he cannot bear of My punishment and torment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that: Ali bin Dawud told us, Abu Salih told us, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
Thus does God make clear to you the signs that you may give thought * In this world and the Hereafter
, he said: He means in the passing of this world and its passing away, and the coming of the Hereafter and its permanence.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
That you may give thought * In this world and the Hereafter
, he said: He says: Perhaps you may give thought to this Surat Al-Baqarah 2:219
h
They ask you about wine and gambling
. Say, "
h
In them is great sin

and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit." And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, "The excess." Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may give thought. world and the Hereafter, and recognize the superiority of the Hereafter over this world.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: His statement:
h
Thus does God make clear to you the signs that you may give thought * In this world and the Hereafter

, he said: As for this world, you know that it is a house of affliction then passing away, and the Hereafter is a house of reward then permanence, so you give thought and work for what remains of them. He said: And I heard Abu Asim mention something similar to this as well.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Thus does God make clear to you the signs that you may give thought * In this world and the Hereafter

, and that whoever ponders over them will know the superiority of one over the other, and will know that this world is a house of trial and then a house of destruction, and that the Hereafter is a house of reward and then a house of permanence, so be among those who make up for the need of this world for the need of the Hereafter.

evidence.text: The reading of this differed: Most of the people of Medina and some of the Kufians and Basrans read it: “Say: in them is a great sin” with the letter ba, meaning say: in.
Others from the two cities of Basra and Kufa read it: Say in them is a great sin, meaning many sins.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who read it with the letter ba’: Say in them is a great sin, because they all agreed on his saying: And their sin is greater than their benefit, and his reading with the letter ba’.
Abu Jaʿfar said: As for the readings, they differed in the reading of al-ʿafu.
The majority of the readers of Hijaz, the readers of the Haramayn, and most of the readers of Kufa read it: Qul al-ʿafu in the accusative case.
Some of the readers of Yasri read it: Qul al-ʿafu in the nominative case.
Whoever reads it in the accusative case makes what one letter, and makes it accusative by saying: they spend, as I explained before - then he makes the pardon accusative based on that.
And whoever reads it in the nominative case makes ma a connection to dha, and they raised al-‘afu.
And with whichever of the two readings it was read, it is correct in my opinion, because their meanings are similar, with the prevalence of reading with each one of them.

However, the reading that I like the most, even if that is the case, is the reading of whoever reads it in the accusative case, because those who read it with it are more, and it is more well-known and famous.

x: The people of interpretation differed as to when this verse was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed [regarding those who set aside the property of orphans who were with them, and were reluctant to mix with them in food or otherwise, and that was when the following verse was revealed: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best [al-An’am 6:152], and His statement: Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly
r
(An-Nisa’: 10)
It was mentioned that he said that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When the verse was revealed: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best (al-An’am 6:152- Al-Isra’: 34), they set aside the money of the orphans, so they mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse was revealed: “And if you mix with them, they are your brothers. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer.
h
And if God had willed

, He could have made you weak,” so they mixed with them. Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated, Jarir narrated, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse, And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, was revealed, Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire, and they will burn in a Blaze
r
(An-Nisa’: 10)

, whoever had an orphan with him set out and separated his food from his food, and his drink from his drink, and he would keep some of his food left over for him until he ate it or spoiled it. This was very difficult for them, so they mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God, the Almighty, revealed, “
h
And they ask you about orphans

. Say, ‘Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers.’” So they mixed their food with their food and their drink with their drink. Ibn Hamid narrated, Hakam narrated, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id, who said: When the verse: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best was revealed, he said: We used to prepare food for the orphan and some of it would be left over, so they would leave it until it spoiled. Then God revealed: But if you mix with them, they are your brothers. Yahya ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated, on the authority of Abu Usamah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Hakam, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila was asked about the wealth of an orphan, so he said: When the verse: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best was revealed, avoid mixing with them and avoid everything, even avoiding water. Then when the verse: And if you mix with them, they are your brothers was revealed, he said: So mix with them. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And they ask you about orphans

, the entire verse. He said: God had revealed before that in Surat Bani Israel: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, and it was too much for them, so they would not mix with them in food or anything else. This was difficult for them, so God revealed the dispensation and said: And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Muammar informed us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: When the verse: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best was revealed, the people kept away from the orphans and did not mix with them in food, drink, or money. He said: This was difficult for the people, so they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed: “
h
And they ask you about orphans
. Say, ‘Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, then they are your brothers.’”

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding His statement: “
h
And they ask you about orphans

. Say: ‘Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them’” 10:13, he said: So he mentioned to us, and God knows best, that it was revealed about the Children of Israel: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, until he reaches maturity. This was too much for them, so they would not mix with them in food, drink, or anything else. This was difficult for them, so God revealed the concession and said: “
h
And they ask you about orphans

. Say: ‘Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers.” He said: Mixing with them in riding an animal, drinking milk, and serving a servant. He said: The guardian who is in charge of their affairs, so there is no problem with him riding an animal, drinking milk, or being served by a servant.

x: Others said about this:

c: Amr bin Ali told me, Imran bin Uyaynah told us, Ata bin As-Sa'ib told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement: Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies
r
(An-Nisa’: 10)

, the verse, he said: There would be an orphan in a man’s care, and he would separate his food, drink, and utensils, and that was difficult for the Muslims, so God revealed: “But if you mix with them, then they are your brothers. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer,” and He permitted their mixing.

c: Abu As-Sa'ib told me, he said, Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, he said, Ash'ath told us, on the authority of Ash-Sha'bi, he said:
m: When this verse was revealed: “Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire. And they will burn in a Blaze”
r
(An-Nisa’: 10)

, he said: So the people avoided the orphans, and a man would separate his food from his food, his money from his money, and his drink from his drink. He said: This was difficult for the people, so the verse was revealed: “And if you mix with them, they are your brothers. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer.” Al-Sha’bi said: So whoever mixes with an orphan should be generous with him, and whoever mixes with him in order to eat from his wealth should not do so.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Mu’awiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: His statement: “
h
And they ask you about orphans

. Say, ‘Improvement for them is best.’” That is because when God revealed: Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies, and they will burn in a Blaze.
r
(An-Nisa’: 10)

, the Muslims were reluctant to include the orphans, and they were embarrassed to mix with them in anything, so they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: “Say, ‘Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers.’”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: I asked Ata’ bin Abi Rabah about the statement: “
h
And they ask you about orphans

. Say: ‘Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers.’” He said: When Surat An-Nisa’ was revealed, the people set aside their food and did not mix with them. He said: Then they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: How hard it is for us to set aside the food of orphans while they eat with us! So this was revealed: But if you mix with them, they are your brothers. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: They separated their food from their food, their milk from their milk, and their meat from their meat. That was hard for them, so this was revealed: But if you mix with them, they are your brothers. He said: Mixing with the orphan in the pastures and meat. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: The milk and his servants are the servant and riding the animal. Ibn Jurayj said: And in the dwellings. He said: And the dwellings on that day will be rare. Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated, Al-Husayn ibn Al-Hasan Al-Ashqar narrated, Abu Kudayna narrated, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verses were revealed: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best and Indeed, those who devour the property of orphans unjustly, the people avoided the wealth and food of the orphan until it was spoiled, whether it was meat or something else. This was difficult for the people, so they complained about it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: “
h
And they ask you about orphans

. Say, ‘Improvement for them is best.’” Muhammad ibn Amr narrated, Abu Asim narrated, Isa narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qays ibn Sa’d - or Isa, on the authority of Qays ibn Sa’d, Abu Asim was not sure - on the authority of Mujahid: And if you mix with them, they are your brothers, he said: mixing with the orphan in grazing and feeding.

x: Others said: Rather, avoiding and avoiding the orphan’s money was part of the Arabs’ morals, so they were asked about it because of its difficulty for them, and they gave a fatwa that was explained by God in His Book.
Those who said that: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: “
h
And they ask you about orphans

. Say, ‘Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer.’” He said: The Arabs were strict with the orphan to the point that they would not eat with him from the same plate, nor ride his camel, nor employ a servant for him. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about it, so he said: Say, ‘Improvement for them is best.’ Reforming his money and affairs is better for him, and if he mixes with him, eats with him, feeds him, rides his mount, carries him, employs his servant, and serves him, then that is better. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And they ask you about orphans

. Say, ‘Improvement for them is best’” to Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise. And that when people had an orphan in their care, they would put his food on one side and his milk on the other, for fear of sin, and that the believers were afflicted with Surat Al-Baqarah 2:220 In this world and the Hereafter.
h
And they ask you about orphans
. Say, "Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer.
h
And if God had willed

, He could have made you suffer. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise. hardship, so they did not have what they could make servants for orphans, so God said: Say, ‘Improvement for them is best, even if you mix with them’ to the end of the verse.

c: I was told on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj Tal,
m: I heard Abu Muadh say, Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
And they ask you about orphans

, they used to greatly honor the status of orphans in the pre-Islamic era, so they would not touch anything from their wealth, nor ride an animal for them, nor feed them food. They were afflicted with great hardship in Islam, until they needed the money of orphans. They asked the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the situation of orphans and about mixing with them. God revealed: And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers, meaning by mixing: riding an animal, serving a servant, and drinking milk.

x: The interpretation of the verse is: And your companions ask you, O Muhammad, about the wealth of orphans, and their mixing of their wealth with it in spending, food, drink, living together and service. So say to them: Your favor upon them by your reforming their wealth - without depriving them of any of their wealth, and without taking compensation from their wealth for your reforming that for them - is better for you with God and a greater reward for you, because of the reward and recompense for you in that, and it is better for them in their wealth in their immediate worldly life, because of the availability of their wealth for them. And if you mix with them and share with them your wealth with their wealth in your spending, food, drink and living together, and you take from their wealth a compensation for your taking care of their affairs and causes and reforming their wealth, for they are your brothers, and brothers help each other and protect each other, so the one with wealth helps the one in need, and the one with strength in body helps the one with weakness.

God Almighty says: So you, O believers, and your orphans, are likewise, if you mix with them with your money, mixing your food with their food, your drink with their drink, and the rest of your money with their money, and you gain from their money an excess that is attached to what you did of taking care of their money and their loyalty, and suffering their causes, on your view of them as a compassionate brother looks at his brother, acting between him and him according to what God has obligated and imposed upon him, then that is permissible for you, because you are brothers to one another, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers, he said: A man may mix with his brother.

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Maskeen, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: I hate for the orphan’s wealth to be like a turban.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakiʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham Al-Dastawai, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: I hate for the orphan’s money to be a source of shame to me, so that I mix his food with my food and his drink with my drink.

x: If someone were to say to us: How did He say:
h
Then your brothers
, and raise the brothers? And He said in another place: But if you fear, then
h
on foot or riding

(al-Baqarah 2:239). It was said: Because of the separation of their meanings. That is because the orphans of the believers are brothers of the believers, whether the believers mix with them with their money or do not mix with them. So the meaning of the statement is: And if you mix with them, they are your brothers. And the brothers are raised with the meaning that was not mentioned, which is them, because the statement indicates it, and because the report about them being brothers was not mentioned because of mixing with their rulers. If that was what was intended, the reading would have been in the accusative case, and its meaning would then be: And if you mix with them, then mix with your brothers. However, it was read in the nominative case because of what was described: that they are brothers to the believers who are next to them, whether they mix with them or not.
As for his saying:
h
On foot or riding

, it is in the accusative case because they are two states of the verb, not permanent, and he is not suitable with them. That is because if you had made he appear with them, the speech would be impossible. Do you not see that if someone were to say: If you fear your enemy that you pray standing, then he is
h
on foot or riding
, the intended meaning of the speech would be invalidated? That is because the interpretation of the speech is: If you fear that your enemy will make you pray standing, then pray
h
on foot or riding

. That is why it is in the accusative case in accordance with what precedes it from the speech, as you say in a similar speech: If you wear clothes, then white. You put it in the accusative case because you mean: If you wear clothes, then wear white - and you do not mean to report that all clothes that are worn are white. If you wanted to report on that, you would have said: If you wear clothes, then whiteness is in the nominative case, if the way the speech is presented is in the form of reporting from you about the wearer, that everything that is worn from clothes is white.
Because you mean then: If you wear clothes, then they are white.
Is it permissible to put the accusative in his saying:
h
Then your brothers

It is permissible in Arabic. As for the recitation, we have prevented it because of the consensus of the recitations on putting it in the nominative case. As for Arabic, we have permitted it because it is good to repeat with it what is carried in the verb that precedes it in both of them: And if you mix with them,
h
then your brothers
you mix with - so that would be permissible in the speech of the Arabs.

God Almighty means by that: Your Lord has permitted you to mix with orphans as He has permitted. You have it, so fear God in yourselves lest you mix with them while you want to consume their wealth unjustly, and make your mixing with them a pretext for you to corrupt their wealth and consume it unjustly, so that you deserve from Him a punishment that you cannot bear, for He knows whoever among you mixes with his orphan - and shares with him in his food, drink, residence, servants and caretakers while mixing with him - what he intends by mixing with him: to corrupt his wealth and consume it unjustly, or to reform it and make it fruitful? Because nothing is hidden from Him about it, and He knows which of you wants to reform his wealth and which one wants to corrupt it, as Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about the statement of God, the Most High: And God knows the corrupter from the reformer, he said: God knows when you mix your wealth with His: do you want to reform his wealth, or corrupt it and consume it unjustly?

c: Abu Al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Hafs bin Ghayath narrated to us, saying: Ash'ath narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Sha'bi:
m: "And God knows the corrupter from the reformer." Al-Sha'bi said: So whoever mixes with an orphan should be generous with him, and whoever mixes with him in order to consume his money should not do so.

x: God Almighty means by that:
h
And if God had willed

, He would have forbidden what He has made lawful for you of mixing with your orphans with your money, their money, so that would have been difficult for you and hard for you, and you would not have been able to fulfill what is required of you from the right of God Almighty and what is required of you from His obligation, but He has permitted it for you and made it easy for you, out of mercy and compassion for you.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement: "I would have made you miserable."
Some of them said what:

c: Muhammad bin Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Qays bin Sa'd - or Isa, on the authority of Qays bin Sa'd - on the authority of Mujahid - Abu Asim was not sure -
m: regarding God Almighty's statement: "
h
And if God had willed
, He would have made you miserable," He would have forbidden you pasture and animal feed.

x: Mujahid meant by that: the guardian of the orphan’s livestock tending with the orphan’s livestock, and eating from his food. Because he interpreted the statement: And if you mix with them, they are your brothers, as meaning the guardian mixing with the orphan’s livestock and food.

c: Ali ibn Dawud told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muʿawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
And if God had willed

, He could have made things difficult for you, meaning: If God had willed, He could have made things difficult for you, but He made things easy and facilitated, saying: “And whoever is rich, let him abstain. And whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable.”
r
(An-Nisa’: 6)

c: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if God had willed

, He could have made things difficult for you, meaning: He would have made things difficult for you, so you would not have fulfilled a right or performed an obligation. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly, except that he said: You did not act in accordance with what is right. Narrated to me by Musa, he said:

c: Amr narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of As-Suddi:
m: h
And if God had willed
, He could have made you suffer, meaning He would have made things difficult for you. Narrated to me by Yunus, he said:

c: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And if God had willed
, He could have made you suffer, he said: It would have been difficult for you in the matter. That is suffering. Narrated to us by Ibn Hamid, he said:

c: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if God had willed
, He could have made you suffer, he said:
h
And if God had willed

, He would have made what you took from the wealth of orphans a cause of destruction. And these statements that we have mentioned from those we have mentioned, even though the wording of those who said them differed, they are close in meaning. Because whoever is forbidden something has been made difficult for him in that thing, and whoever is made difficult for him in something has been made difficult in it, and whoever is made difficult in something or made difficult for him in it has made an effort. And all of that goes back to the meaning that I have described, which is that its meaning is: difficulty and hardship. Therefore, it is said: So-and-so was burdened if the matter was difficult for him and made him suffer, so he is burdened with burden, as God Almighty said: Hard for Him is what you are burdened with (al-Tawbah 9:128), meaning what is difficult for you and hurts you and burdens you, and from this is His Almighty’s saying: That is for he among you who fears hardship
r
(An-Nisa’: 25)

. This is if so-and-so is burdened. If someone else makes him do that, it is said: So-and-so burdened him with such-and-such, since he burdened him and forced him to do something that he was struggling to do, he burdened him with burden. Likewise, His saying: I would have burdened you means: I would have made hardship obligatory for you by forbidding you that which burdens you and makes you difficult, which you are not able to avoid and perform what is required of you for Him.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: I would have ruined you and destroyed you.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Talq bin Ghannam narrated to us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: He recited to us:
h
And if God had willed
, He could have made you miserable. Ibn Abbas said:
h
And if God had willed
, He could have made what you took from the property of orphans a cause of destruction.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Yahya bin Adam narrated to us, on the authority of Fadil - and Jarir, on the authority of Mansur - and Ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur - on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And if God had willed
, He could have made you miserable. He said: He could have made what you took a cause of destruction.

x: By that, the Most High means: God is mighty in His authority, and nothing can prevent Him from the punishment He has brought upon you if you were to help you with what you struggle to perform of His obligations and you were to Surat Al-Baqarah 2:220 In this world and the Hereafter.
h
And they ask you about orphans
