. Say, "Improvement for them is best. But if you mix with them, they are your brothers. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer.
h
And if God had willed

, He could have made you suffer. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise. fall short in doing it, and no one can prevent Him from doing that or anything else that He does to you or to others of that if He did it. But by the grace of His mercy, He has been gracious to you by not imposing that on you, and He is wise in that if He did it to you and in other than that of His rulings and management. There is no defect or deficiency or weakness or flaw in His actions, because it is the action of the One with wisdom who is not ignorant of the consequences of things, so His management is blameworthy in consequence, just as the actions of creation are blameworthy due to their ignorance of the consequences of things, due to their bad choices in them to begin with.

evidence.text: If that was what was intended, the reading would have been in the accusative case, and its meaning would then be: And if you mix with them, then mix with your brothers.
However, it was read in the nominative case because of what was described: that they are brothers to the believers who are next to them, whether they mix with them or not.
As for the recitation, we have prevented it because of the consensus of the recitations on putting it in the nominative case.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding this verse: Was it revealed to mean every polytheist woman, or was its ruling meant for some polytheists and not others? Was something abrogated from it after the ruling became obligatory or not?

Some of them said: It was revealed to mean the prohibition of marrying every polytheist woman to every Muslim, regardless of the types of polytheism she was, whether she was an idol worshipper, or a Jew, Christian, Zoroastrian, or from any other type of polytheism, then the prohibition of marrying the People of the Book was abrogated by His saying: “They ask you, [O Muhammad], what is lawful for them. Say: Lawful for you are all good things” to “And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you and your food is lawful for them. And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you” (Al-Ma'idah: 4, 5).
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told me, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe

, then he made an exception for the women of the People of the Book and said: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture, it is permissible for you when you have given them their due compensation (al-Ma’idah 5:5).

c: Muhammad bin Hamid told us, he said, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, they said,
m: h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe
, so the women of the People of the Book were abrogated from that, and they were made permissible for the Muslims.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe
, he said: The women of Mecca and other polytheists, then He made lawful from them the women of the People of the Book.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on Al-Rabiʿ, regarding His statement:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women to His statement

: that they may be reminded, he said: God forbade polytheistic women in this verse, then He revealed in Surat Al-Ma’idah, and made an exception for the women of the People of the Book, saying: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, if you have given them their due compensation (al-Ma’idah 5:5).

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed with the intention of its ruling being the polytheistic women of the Arabs, nothing was abrogated from it and no exception was made, rather it is a verse whose apparent meaning is general but whose interpretation is specific.
Who said that: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe
, meaning: the polytheistic Arab women among whom there is no book that they can read.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe
, he said: the polytheistic women are those who are not from the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:221
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe

. And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist woman, even though she might please you. And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe. And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he might please you. Those invite to the Fire, while God invites to Paradise and forgiveness. By His permission, He makes clear His verses to the people that they may be reminded. People of the Book, and Hudhayfah married a Jewish or Christian woman.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said: Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe
, meaning the polytheistic Arab women among whom there is no book that they can read.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe
, he said: the polytheistic women among the people of idols.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed to mean every polytheist, regardless of the type of polytheism she was, without specifying one polytheist over another, whether pagan, Zoroastrian, or People of the Book, and nothing of it was abrogated.

Those who said that: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-Asqalani told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Abdul Hamid ibn Bahram al-Fazari told us, he said, Shahr ibn Hawshab told us, he said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abbas say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade all types of women, except for the believing emigrant women, and he forbade every woman of a religion other than Islam.” And God, the Most High, said: And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his work has become worthless (al-Ma’idah 5:5). Talhah ibn Ubaydullah married a Jewish woman, and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman married a Christian woman, and Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, became extremely angry, to the point that he wanted to attack them. They said: We will continue, O Commander of the Faithful, and do not get angry! He said: If their divorce is permissible, then their marriage is permissible, but they were taken from you by a small and shameful act.
The most correct of these sayings in the interpretation of the verse is what Qatada said: That God the Most High meant by His saying:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe those polytheistic women who were not from the People of the Book

, and that the verse is general in its outward appearance but specific in its inward meaning, nothing was abrogated from it, and that the women of the People of the Book are not included in it. This is because God the Most High made it permissible by His saying:
h
And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you - for the believers to marry their chaste women

, just as He permitted them from the women of the believers. We have explained in other places in this book of ours, and in our book Kitab al-Latif min al-Bayan: that every two verses or two reports, one of which negates the ruling of the other in the innate nature of the mind, then it is not permissible to rule that one of them abrogates the ruling of the other, except with an argument from a report that conclusively proves the excuse of its coming.
This does not exist, because His statement: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture (al-Ma’idah 5:5) abrogates what had been made forbidden of women by His statement:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe

. Since this does not exist, then the statement of the one who says: This abrogates that, is a claim for which he has no proof, and the one who makes a claim for which there is no proof is arbitrary, and arbitrary is something that no one is incapable of. As for the statement that was narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar, may God be pleased with him: regarding his differentiation between Talhah and Hudhayfah and their two wives who were women of the Book, this statement has no meaning - because it contradicts what the nation has agreed upon to permit in the Book of God Almighty and the report of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: It was narrated from Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him
m: that he said something different, with a chain of transmission that is more authentic than it, which is: - It was narrated to me by Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi, who said: Muhammad bin Bishr narrated to us, who said: Sufyan bin Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, who said: Omar said: A Muslim man marries a Christian woman, but a Christian man does not marry a Muslim woman. Omar disliked Talhah and Hudhayfah may God have mercy on them marrying a Jewish or Christian woman, lest people follow their example in that and lose interest in Muslim women, or for other reasons, so he ordered them to release them, as Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said:
b.via: Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him

c: Ibn Idris narrated to us,
m: who said: Al-Salt bin Bahram narrated to us, on the authority of Shuqaiq, who said: Hudhayfah married a Jewish woman, so Omar wrote to him: Release her, so he wrote to him: Do you claim that it is forbidden, so I release her? He said: I do not claim that it is forbidden, but I fear that they will engage in prostitution among them. And: - Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated that Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ash'ath ibn Suwar, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'We marry the women of the People of the Book, but they do not marry our women.'" This report, even though there is something in its chain of transmission, is more correct to say, because everyone agrees on its correctness, than the report of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab. So the meaning of the statement is: And do not marry, O believers, polytheist women, other than the People of the Book, until they believe and believe in God and His Messenger and what was revealed to him.

x: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
And a believing slave woman in God and His Messenger and what he brought from God

, is better in the sight of God and more excellent than a free polytheist disbelieving woman, even if her lineage is noble and her origin is honorable. He says: And do not seek marriage with honorable polytheist women, for Muslim slave women are better to marry than them in the sight of God. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about a man who married a slave girl, and he was reprimanded for that, and a free polytheist woman was offered to him.
He mentioned who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe

. And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even though she might please you.” He said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Rawahah, and he had a black slave woman, and he became angry with her and slapped her. Then he became frightened and came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him about her story, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What is she, O Abdullah? He said: O Messenger of God, she fasts and prays and performs ablution well and bears witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God. He said: This is a believer. Abdullah said: By the One Who sent you with the truth, I will free her and marry her, so he did, and some of the Muslims criticized him and said: You marry a slave woman, and they wanted to marry to polytheists and marry them out of desire for their lineage, so God revealed about them: And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist and A believing slave is better than a polytheist.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Al-Hajjaj narrated to me, Ibn Jurayj said
m: about His statement:
h
And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe
, he said: Polytheistic women - because of their honor - until they believe.

x: God Almighty means by that: And if a polytheistic woman from among the People of the Book pleases you in beauty, lineage, and wealth, then do not marry her, for a believing slave woman is better in the sight of God than her. And it was put in the place of if because of the similarity of their points of articulation and their meanings, and for this reason each one of them is answered. In response to her companion, as we have explained previously.

By that, God the Almighty means that God has forbidden believing women to marry a polytheist, whoever the polytheist may be, and whatever type of polytheism he may be, so do not marry them, O believing men among them, for that is forbidden to you. And marrying them to a believing slave who believes in God and His Messenger and what he brought from God is better for you than marrying them to a free polytheist, even if his lineage is noble and his origin is honorable, and even if his lineage and ancestry please you. Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli used to say: This statement from God the Almighty is an indication that the guardians of a woman have more right to marry her than the woman.

c: Muhammad ibn Yazid Abu Hisham al-Rifaʿi told us, he said, Hafs ibn Ghiyath told us, on the authority of a sheikh whom he did not name, Abu Jaʿfar said:
m: Marriage with a guardian is in the Book of God, then he recited: And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe with the ta’ raised.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and al-Zuhri,
m: regarding the statement of God, And do not marry polytheistic men, he said: It is not lawful for you to marry a Jew or a Christian or a polytheist from outside your religion.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: And do not marry polytheistic men - because of their honor - until they believe.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of al-Husayn bin Waqid, on the authority of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri:
m: And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe, he said: Muslim women are forbidden to their men - meaning the men of polytheists.

x: God Almighty means by His statement, those, those whom you, O believers, have been forbidden to marry from among the men and women of the polytheists, who call you to the Fire, meaning: they call you to do what will lead you to the Fire, and that is the action that they are doing of disbelief in God and His Messenger. He says: And do not accept what they say, and do not seek their advice, and do not marry them or give them in marriage, for they will spare no effort in ruining you, but accept from God what He has commanded you to do and do it, and refrain from what He has forbidden you, for He is calling you to Paradise, meaning by that He is calling you to do what will lead you to Paradise, and will guarantee your salvation from the Fire if you do it, and to what will erase your sins or transgressions, so He will pardon them and conceal them for you. As for His statement, by His permission, it means: He is calling you to that by informing you of His path and way by which you can reach Paradise and be forgiven.

Then the Most High said: And He makes clear His signs to the people that they may be reminded. He says: And He clarifies His arguments and proofs in His Book which He revealed through the tongue of His Messenger to His servants, so that they may remember and take heed, and distinguish between the two matters, one of which is a call to the Fire and eternal residence in it, and the other is a call to Paradise and forgiveness of sins, so that they may choose the better of the two for themselves. And no one is ignorant of the distinction between these two except someone who is stupid and whose mind is flawed.
God Almighty means by His saying: "
h
And they ask you about menstruation

" and your companions ask you, O Muhammad, about menstruation. It was said: menstruation, because whatever is from the verb is past with the opening of the 'ayn of the verb and its breaking in the future, like the saying of the speaker: daraba yadrubu, habasa yahabus, and nazala yanzul, then the Arabs build its source on the maf'al and the noun on the maf'al, like al-mudarab, and al-mudarab from darabat, and nazala manzil and manzil. And it is heard in words with ya', alif and ya': al-ma'ish and al-ma'ash and al-mu'ayb and al-mu'ayb, as Ru'bah said about al-ma'ish: To you I complain of the hardship of life and the years that have passed while I pluck my feathers The people asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) - as we have been told - about menstruation, because before God made clear to them what they understood from His command, they would not live with a menstruating woman in a house, nor eat with them from the same vessel, nor drink from them.

c: So God informed them
m: with this verse that what is required of them during their women’s menstruation days is to avoid having intercourse with them only, without anything else such as sleeping with them, eating with them, or drinking with them, as: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement:
h
And they ask you about menstruation until he reached until they are pure

. So the people of ignorance would not have a menstruating woman live with them in a house, nor would she eat with them from the same vessel, so God revealed His remembrance regarding that, and He forbade her vagina as long as she was menstruating, and He permitted everything else: that she dye your hair, eat with you from your food, and sleep with you in your bed, if she was wearing a lower garment covering her from you.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly. It has been said that they asked about that because during their menstrual periods they would avoid coming to them where the blood exits, and they would come to them in their anuses. So God forbade them from approaching them during their menstrual periods until they were pure. Then He permitted them - if they were pure from their menstruation - to come to them from where He commanded them to stay away from them, and He forbade coming to them in their anuses in all cases.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, Khasif narrated to us, Mujahid narrated to me, saying:
m: They used to avoid women during menstruation and would approach them from behind. They asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, so God revealed:
h
And they ask you about menstruation
to
h

, then come to them from where God has ordained for you - in the vagina, do not go beyond it. It was said that the questioner who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that was Thabit ibn al-Dahdah al-Ansari.
Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi.

x: God Almighty means by that: Say to those of your companions who ask you about menstruation, O Muhammad: It is harmful. And harmful is that which causes harm from something disliked in it. In this context, it is called harmful because of its foul odor, filth, and impurity, and it includes various meanings of harmfulness, other than one.
The people of interpretation differed in explaining the interpretation of that, despite the similarity of the meanings of some of what they said about it.
Some of them said: His statement, Say it is harmful, say it is filth.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, ʿAmr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement, Say it is harmful, he said: As for harm, it is filth.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, ʿAbd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muʿmar told us, on the authority of Qatadah,
m: regarding his statement, Say it is harmful, he said: Say it is harmful, he said: filth.

x: Others said: Say it is blood.
Those who said that: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Muammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: “
h
And they ask you about menstruation
. Say: It is a harmful thing,” he said: The harmful thing is blood.
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
So keep away from women during menstruation

, so keep away from intercourse with women and sexual intercourse with them during their menstruation, as Ali ibn Dawud told me, Abu Salih told us, Muʿawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement:
h
So keep away from women during menstruation
, meaning keep away from sexual intercourse with their vaginas.
The scholars differed regarding what a man must keep away from a menstruating woman.
Some of them said: What is obligatory for a man is to keep away from her entire body, that is, to have intercourse with her with part of his body.

Those who said that: Ibn Bashar told us, Hammad ibn Masʿadah told us, Awf told us, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: I said to Ubaydah: What is permissible for me with my wife when she is menstruating? He said: The bed is one, and the blanket is different.

c: Tamim ibn al-Muntasir told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Muhammad told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah,
m: “On the authority of Nudbah, the freed slave of the family of Abbas, she said: Maymunah bint al-Harith - or Hafsah bint Umar - sent me to the wife of Abdullah ibn Abbas, and there was a kinship between them through women, and I found her bed separate from his bed, so I thought that was due to estrangement, so I asked her about his bed separate from her bed, and she said: I am menstruating, and when I menstruate, he separates from my bed. So I went back and told Maymunah - or Hafsah - about that, and she sent me back to Ibn Abbas, your mother says to you: You have abandoned the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for by God, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to sleep with one of his wives, even though she was menstruating, and there was nothing between him and her except a garment that did not go beyond the knees.”

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayyub ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, he said:
m: I said to Ubaydah: What is a man’s right with his wife if she is menstruating? He said: The bed is one and the blanket is different. If he finds nothing but to return to her from his garment, he should return it to her.

x: Those who said this statement based their argument on the fact that God the Almighty commanded us to avoid women during their menstruation, and He did not specify one thing over the other. This is general for all of their bodies, and it is obligatory to avoid everything from their bodies during their menstruation.
Others said: Rather, what God the Almighty commanded us to avoid from them is the place of harm, and that is the place from which blood comes out.
Those who said this mentioned:

c: Hamid bin Masʿadah told us, Yazid bin Zariʿ told us, ʿUyaynah bin ʿAbd al-Rahman bin Jawshan told us, Marwan al-Asfar told us, on the authority of Masruq bin al-Ajdaʿ
m: who said: I said to ʿAisha: What is permissible for a man to do with his wife when she is menstruating? She said: Everything except intercourse. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, Saeed narrated - and Ibn Bashar narrated, Abdul A’la narrated, Saeed narrated - from Qatada, who said: It was mentioned to us from Aisha that she said: Where were the one with the two beds and the one with the two blankets?! Ibn Bashar narrated, Abdul A’la narrated, Saeed narrated, from Qatada, from Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d, from Masruq, who said: I said to Aisha: What is forbidden to a man from his wife when she is menstruating? She said: Her vagina. Ibn Bashar narrated, Abdul Wahhab narrated, Ayoub narrated, from the book of Abu Qilabah: That Masruq rode to Aisha and said: Peace be upon the Prophet and his family. Aisha said: Abu Aisha! Welcome! So they gave him permission and he entered. He said: I want to ask you about something and I am shy! She said: I am only your mother, and you are my son! He said: What is a man’s right with his wife when she is menstruating? She said to him: Everything except her vagina.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Maymun ibn Mihran, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: He has what is above the izar.

c: Yaqub narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, he said: Ayyub narrated to us, on the authority of Nafi’: That Aisha said
m: about sleeping with a menstruating woman: There is nothing wrong with that if she is wearing an izar.

c: Yaqub narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, he said:
m: I asked Aisha: What is a man entitled to from his wife if she is menstruating? She said: Everything except the vagina.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: If a menstruating woman covers her vagina with a garment or something that covers the dirt, then there is nothing wrong with her husband touching her skin. Abu Kuraib narrated, he said: Ibn Idris narrated, he said: Yazid narrated, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he was asked: What is a man entitled to from his wife if she is menstruating? He said: What is above the izar. Yaqub bin Ibrahim narrated, he said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim narrated, he said: Al-Hakam bin Fadil narrated, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Beware of blood like Surat Al-Baqarah 2:222
h
And they ask you about menstruation
. Say, "It is a harmful thing,
h
so keep away from women during menstruation
h
and do not approach them until they are pure
h

, then come to them from where God has ordained for you. Indeed, God loves those who are constantly repentant
h
and loves those who purify themselves
. the spot on a sandal. Yaqub narrated, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated, he said:

c: Ayoub informed us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Umm Salamah, she said
m: about having intercourse with a menstruating woman: There is nothing wrong with that if there is a rag on her private parts.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: A man has everything from his wife except the vagina - meaning when she is menstruating.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: They sleep together in one blanket - meaning the menstruating woman - if there is a garment over the vagina.

c: Tamim told us, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Laith, he said:
m: We discussed in the presence of Mujahid a man who plays with his wife when she is menstruating. He said: Stab your penis wherever you want between the thighs, the buttocks, and the navel, as long as it is not in the anus or during menstruation.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Amir, he said:
m: Is it permissible for a man to have intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating? He said: If she stops causing harm.

c: Hamid ibn Masʿadah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zariʿ narrated to us, Imran ibn Hudayr narrated to me,
m: I heard ʿIkrimah say: Everything that a menstruating woman does is permissible for you except the flow of blood.

x: The reason for the one who said this statement is the evidence established by the mutawatir reports “from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to have intercourse with his wives while they were menstruating.” If it were obligatory to avoid all of them, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have done that. Since this was authentically reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is known that what God, the Most High, meant by His statement,
h
So keep away from women during menstruation

, is to avoid some of her body and not others. Since that is the case, it must be that this is the intercourse that is unanimously agreed upon as being forbidden for the husband in her vagina, not what there is disagreement about, such as intercourse with her in the rest of her body.
Others said: Rather, what God, the Most High, has commanded him to keep away from them during their menstruation is what is between the navel and the knee, and he has what is above and below that.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Shuraih, he said:
m: He has what is above the navel - and he mentioned the menstruating woman.

c: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Yazid told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas was asked about the menstruating woman: What does her husband have of her? He said: What is above the izar.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub and Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: Shuraih said:
m: He has what is above her navel.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday narrated to us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Waqid bin Muhammad bin Zaid bin Abdullah bin Omar, he said:
m: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab was asked: What is a man entitled to from a menstruating woman? He said: What is above the lower garment. The reason for those who said this is the soundness of the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is: - Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib narrated to me, he said:
b.via: Waqid bin Muhammad bin Zaid bin Abdullah bin Omar

c: Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad narrated to us, he said: Sulayman Al-Shaibani narrated to us
m: - and Abu Al-Sa’ib narrated to me, he said: Hafs narrated to us, he said: Al-Shaibani narrated to us - he said: Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Haad narrated to us, he said: I heard Maymunah say: “Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to have intercourse with one of his wives while she was menstruating, he would order her to put on a lower garment.”

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abdul Rahman bin Mahdi narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad,
m: “On the authority of Maymunah: That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to have intercourse with her while she was menstruating, above the lower garment.”

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to me, he said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: Whenever one of us was menstruating, he would order her to put on a waist wrapper, then he would have intercourse with her.

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: Al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Aswad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: Whenever one of us was menstruating, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would order her to put on a waist wrapper, then he would have intercourse with her. And there are similar reports that would take too long to mention all of them in this book. They said: What did the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, do that is permissible, which is his touching the menstruating woman’s part below and above the waist wrapper, that is below the knee and above the navel? And what is beyond that of the menstruating woman’s body, it is obligatory to avoid it, due to the general meaning of the verse.

x: The most correct of the opinions on this matter is the opinion of those who said: A man has the right to do with his menstruating wife what is above and below the waist wrapper, for the reason we mentioned for them.
The reciters differed in the recitation of this.
Some of them recited it: until they are pure with a damma on the ha’ and a light sukoon on it.

Others recited it with a shaddah on the ha’ and a fatha on it. As for those who recited it with a light sukoon on the ha’, they directed its meaning to: And do not approach women during their menstruation until the menstrual blood stops and they become pure.
A group of the people of interpretation said this interpretation.
Those who said this mentioned:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi and Mu’ammil told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not approach them until they are pure
, he said: the cessation of the blood.

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, on the authority of Sufyan - or ʿUthman ibn al-Aswad:
m: h
And do not approach them until they are pure
, until their bleeding stops.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadheeh narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah al-Atki narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not approach them until they are pure

, he said: until the bleeding stops. As for those who read it with a shaddah on the ha’ and a fathah, they meant: until they wash themselves with water. They stressed the ta’ because they said: the meaning of the word is: until they are pure, the ta’ was assimilated into the ta’ because their points of articulation are close together.

x: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of those who read: until they are pure, with a shaddah on the ha’ and a fathah, meaning: until they wash themselves, because everyone agrees that it is forbidden for a man to approach his wife after her menstrual bleeding has stopped until she is pure. The difference of opinion is only about the purification that God, the Most High, meant, so He permitted him to have intercourse with her.
Some of them said: It is washing with water, it is not permissible for her husband to approach her until she washes her entire body.
Some of them said: It is ablution for prayer.

Others said: Rather, it is washing the vulva, so if she washes her vulva, that is her purification by which it is permissible for her husband to have intercourse with her. If there is consensus from all that she is not permissible for her husband when the blood stops until she is purified, it is clear to us that the more correct of the two readings is the one that is rejected due to confusion in the understanding of its listener. And that is what we chose, since in the reading of its reader with the ha’ being pronounced with a light and damma, there is what prevents confusion for its listener due to a mistake in its interpretation, so he sees that the husband of the menstruating woman has intercourse with her after her menstrual blood stops and before she washes and purifies herself. So the interpretation of the verse is: They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harmful thing, so keep away from intercourse with your wives during the time of their menses, and do not approach them until they wash and purify themselves from their menses after it stops.
He said: Abu Jaʿfar: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
Then when they have purified themselves
, then have intercourse with them, that is, when they have bathed and purified themselves with water, then have intercourse with them.
Is intercourse with them obligatory at that time?
No. If someone says: What is the meaning of His statement: Then have intercourse with them?

It is said: That is the permissibility of what was forbidden before that of intercourse with them, and the release of what was forbidden during menstruation. This is like His saying: And when you are in ihram, then hunt (al-Ma’idah 5:2). And his saying: So when the prayer is finished, disperse throughout the land (al-Jumu’ah: 10), and what is similar to that.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: So when they purify themselves.
Some of them said: The meaning of that is, then when they bathe.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Mu’awiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So when they purify themselves means: So when you purify yourself from blood and purify yourself with water.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi and Mu’ammil told us, they said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So when they purify themselves means: So when they bathe.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yahya bin Wadheeh told us, he said, Ubaydullah Al-Atki told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his saying: So when they purify themselves, he means: They bathe.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Sufyan - or Uthman bin Al-Aswad:
m: “So when They purify themselves, if they bathe.

c: Imran bin Musa narrated to us, Abdul Warith narrated to us, Amer narrated to us, from Al-Hasan:
m: Regarding the menstruating woman who sees purity, he said: Her husband should not have intercourse with her until she bathes and prayer becomes permissible for her.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim:
m: That he disliked for him to have intercourse with her until she bathes - meaning the woman when she is pure.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: Then when they purify themselves for prayer.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to us, he said: Laith informed us, from Tawus and Mujahid that they said:
m: If a woman purifies herself from blood and her husband wants to order her to perform ablution before she bathes - if he is overcome by lust, then let him have intercourse.

x: The most appropriate of the two interpretations of the verse is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of His statement: “Then when they purify themselves” is when they bathe, because everyone agrees that she does not become pure by ablution with water in the purity that makes prayer permissible for her. The statement is not without one of two things: Either its meaning is: When they purify themselves from impurity, then come to them. If that is its meaning, then it should be that when the bleeding stops, then it is permissible for her husband to have intercourse with her, if there is no apparent impurity. This is if his saying: When they purify themselves is permissible to use in purification from impurity, and I do not know of it being permissible except on the basis of dislike of speech. Or its meaning is: When they purify themselves for prayer. And in the consensus of all of the evidence that it is not permissible for her husband to have intercourse with her when her menstrual bleeding stops, if there is no impurity, other than purification with water if she has it, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:222

Say, "It is a harmful thing,
h

h

, then come to them from where God has ordained for you. Indeed, God loves those who are constantly repentant

The consensus of all of the Ummah that prayer is not permissible for her except after bathing is the clearest evidence for the correctness of what we have said: that having intercourse with her is forbidden except after bathing, and that the meaning of His statement:
h
Then when they have purified themselves
is that when they bathe, they have become pure in a way that suffices for them for prayer.

h
Then have intercourse with them from where God has commanded you

Then come to them from where God has commanded you

Then come to them from where God has commanded you

m: regarding His statement:

Then come to them from where God has commanded you
, he said: From where He has commanded you to keep away from them.

c: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said:

then come to them from where God has commanded you
. He says: Pure, not menstruating women.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then come to them from where God has commanded you
, he said: He says: Pure, not menstruating women.

c: Musa bin Harun narrated to me, he said: Amr bin Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: from where God has commanded you, from purity.

c: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Salamah bin Nabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Go to them, in a state of purity other than menstruation. I narrated to me from Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Muadh, he said:

c: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Go to them from where God has commanded you
, he said: Go to them when they are pure, not menstruating.

c: Amr bin Ali narrated to us, he said: Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: Salamah bin Nabit narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
Go to them from where God has commanded you
, he said: Purity other than menstruation in the vagina.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: So go to women before marriage, not before fornication.
Those who said that: Amr ibn Ali told us, Waki’ told us, Ismail al-Azraq told us, on the authority of Abu Umar al-Asadi, on the authority of Ibn al-Hanafiyyah:
h
Go to them from where God has commanded you
, he said: from the lawful side, from the side of marriage.

The most correct of the sayings in the interpretation of that, in my opinion, is the saying of those who said: Its meaning is: Go to them from the place of their purification. That is because every command has a meaning, so there is a prohibition against its opposite and its opposite. Likewise, the prohibition of something is a command against its opposite. So if the meaning of his saying:
h
Go to them from where God has commanded you
, was to go to them from the place of the blood outlet which I forbade you from going to them from during their menstruation, then his saying:
h
And do not approach them until they are pure

, would have to be interpreted as: Do not approach them from the place of the blood outlet, not from any other part of her body, so it would be absolute during her menstruation to go to them from their anus. And in the consensus of all: that God Almighty did not make permissible in the case of menstruation from coming to them from their backsides anything that He forbade in the case of purity, nor did He forbid from that in the case of purity anything that He permitted in the case of menstruation, which shows the corruption of this statement.

And then, if the meaning of that was as the speakers of this statement interpreted it, then the statement would have to be: So when they purify themselves, then come to them where God has commanded you, so that the meaning of the statement would then be according to the interpretation that they interpreted it, and that would be an order to come to them in their vaginas. Because the well-known statement, when that is intended, is to say: So-and-so came to his wife from the front of her vagina - and it is not said: He came to her from her vagina - unless he came to her from the front of her vagina in a place other than the vagina.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: Even if that is the case, the meaning of the statement is not: Then approach them in their vaginas - but rather it means: Then approach them from their front in their vaginas - as one says: I approached this matter from its source.
If that is the case, then there is no doubt that the source and direction of the matter is other than it, and that this is what it seeks. If that is as you claim, then the meaning of his statement:
h
Then approach them from where God has commanded you must be other than what you claim it means when you say

: Approach them from the direction from which the blood comes out and from where you were commanded to keep away from them - but it is necessary that its interpretation be as follows: Then approach them from their faces in their faces, just as the statement of the speaker: Approach the matter from its source means: Seek it from its source, and the source of the matter is not the sought-after matter. So likewise the source of the vagina - which God commanded us to approach in their statement - must be other than the vagina. If this is the case, and the meaning of the statement according to them is: Then approach them from their faces in their vaginas, then it must be, according to their statement, forbidden to approach them in their vaginas from their backsides.

If they said this, then whoever said it is outside the saying of the people of Islam, and contradicts the text of the Book of God, the Most High, and the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is because God says: Your women are a place of cultivation for you, so approach your place of cultivation however you wish, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted approaching them in their vaginas from their backsides. It has become clear, then, since the matter is as we have described, that the interpretation of whoever said this is incorrect: Then approach them in their vaginas where I have forbidden you from approaching them during their menstrual period, and the correct statement that we have said is that its meaning is: Then approach them in their vaginas from the face that God has permitted you to approach them, and that is during their purity and cleanliness, not during their menstruation.

What the Almighty means by His statement, Indeed, God loves those who repent, is those who turn from turning away from God and from His obedience to Him and to His obedience. We have already explained the meaning of repentance. There is disagreement about the meaning of His statement,
h
And loves those who purify themselves
Some of them said: They are those who purify themselves with water.
Those who said that are:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadheeh told us, Talhah told us, on the authority of ʿAta’,
m: regarding His statement, Indeed, God loves those who repent, he Surat Al-Baqarah 2:222
h
And they ask you about menstruation
. Say, "It is a harmful thing,
h
so keep away from women during menstruation
h
and do not approach them until they are pure
h
Then when they have purified themselves
, then come to them from where God has ordained for you. Indeed, God loves those who are constantly repentant
h
and loves those who purify themselves
. said: Those who repent from sins,
h
And loves those who purify themselves
, he said: Those who purify themselves with water for prayer.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said: Abu Nuʿaym told us, he said: Talhah told us, on the authority of ʿAta’,
m: something similar.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Wakiʿ told us, on the authority of Talhah bin ʿAmr, on the authority of ʿAta’:
m: Indeed, God loves those who repent, from sins they did not commit,
h
And loves those who purify themselves
, with water for prayer.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: God loves those who repent, from sins,
h
and loves those who purify themselves
, from the backsides of women, that they come to them.
Those who said this are:

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Abu Nuʿaym told us, Ibrahim ibn Nafiʿ told us,
m: I heard Sulayman, the freed slave of Umm Ali, saying, I heard Mujahid say: Whoever has intercourse with his wife in her backside is not one of those who purify themselves.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is:
h
and loves those who purify themselves
, from sins, that they return to them after repenting from them.
Those who said this are:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He loves those who repent, from sins, who have not committed them,
h
and loves those who purify themselves
, from sins, who do not return to them.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard is the saying of those who said: God loves those who repent from sins,
h
and loves those who purify themselves

with water for prayer. Because that is the most likely of its apparent meanings. God, the Most High, mentioned the matter of menstruation, and forbade them from things they used to do in their ignorance: such as not living with menstruating women, eating with them, drinking with them, and other things that God, the Most High, disliked from His servants. When the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, God, the Most High, revealed to him about that, and explained to them what He disliked from what He was pleased with and loved, and informed them that He loves those of His creation who repent to His pleasure and love, repenting from what He dislikes.
Among what He explained to them of that was that He forbade them from approaching their women, even if they were pure from their menstruation, until they bathe. Then He said:
h
And do not approach them until they are pure

. When they are pure, then come to them, for God loves those who purify themselves, meaning: those who purify themselves from major ritual impurity and minor ritual impurity for prayer, and women who purify themselves with water - from menstruation, postpartum bleeding, major ritual impurity, and minor ritual impurity - from menstruation, postpartum bleeding, major ritual impurity, and minor ritual impurity. Rather, He said: And He loves those who purify themselves - and did not say those who purify themselves - and before that, the mention of purification for women occurred, because mentioning those who purify themselves does not include men and women. If He had mentioned that by mentioning those who purify themselves, men would not have had a share in that, and it would have been specifically for women.

So God Almighty mentioned His mention with the general mention of all His accountable servants, since He had all worshipped by purifying themselves with water, even though the reasons that necessitate purification with water differed in some meanings and agreed in others.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The reciters differed in the recitation of this.
Some of them recited it: until they are pure with a damma on the ha’ and a light sukoon on it.
Others recited it with a shaddah on the ha’ and a fatha on it.
As for those who recited it with a light sukoon on the ha’, they directed its meaning to: And do not approach women during their menstruation until the menstrual blood stops and they become pure.
As for those who read it with a shaddah on the ha’ and a fathah, they meant: until they wash themselves with water.

Abu Ja’far said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of those who read: until they are pure, with a shaddah on the ha’ and a fathah, meaning: until they wash themselves, because everyone agrees that it is forbidden for a man to approach his wife after her menstrual bleeding has stopped until she is pure.

If there is consensus from all that she is not permissible for her husband when the blood stops until she is purified, it is clear to us that the more correct of the two readings is the one that is rejected due to confusion in the understanding of its listener.

And that is what we chose, since in the reading of its reader with the ha’ being pronounced with a light and damma, there is what prevents confusion for its listener due to a mistake in its interpretation, so he sees that the husband of the menstruating woman has intercourse with her after her menstrual blood stops and before she washes and purifies herself.

x: God Almighty means by that: Your women are the place of cultivation for your children, so come to your place of cultivation
h
however you wish

and wherever you wish. What He meant by the cultivated land is the cultivation, the cultivation is the planting, but since they are among the causes of cultivation, they were made a place of cultivation since the meaning of the statement was understood. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Maharibi told us, he said:

c: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: Come to your tilth, he said: The place where the child is raised.

c: Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: Your women are your tilth, as for the tilth, it is a farm in which one plows.

x: God Almighty means by that: So marry the one who has been raised for your children from wherever you wish of the ways of coming. And coming in this place is a metaphor for the name of sexual intercourse.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His statement,
h
However you wish
, some of them said: The meaning of His statement, How, is how.
Those who said that: Abu Kurayb told us, he said:

c: Ibn ʿAtiyyah told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of ʿAta’, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: Come to your tilth,
h
however you wish

, he said: He may come to her however he wishes, as long as he does not come to her from her anus or during menstruation. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated, Abu Ahmad narrated, Sharik narrated, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you

, so approach your tilth however you will, meaning: Go to her however you will, facing or from behind, as long as you do not come to her in the anus or during menstruation. Ali ibn Dawud narrated, Abu Saleh narrated, Mu’awiyah narrated, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
Go to your tilth however you will
, meaning by tilth the vagina. He said: Come to it however you will, facing or from behind, and
h
however you wish

, as long as you do not go beyond the vagina to anything else, which is His statement: Go to them from where God has ordained for you. Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated, Abu Ahmad narrated, Sharik narrated, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Ikrimah,
h
Go to your tilth however you will

, meaning: Come to her however you will, as long as he does not do the work of the people of Lot. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated, Abu Ahmad narrated, Al-Hasan ibn Salih narrated, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
Then go to your tilth however you wish
, he said: Come to her
h
however you wish
, and avoid the anus and menstruation. Ubaydullah ibn Saad narrated, he said: My uncle narrated, he said: My father narrated, he said: Yazid narrated, that Ibn Ka’b used to say: His statement:
h
Then go to your tilth however you wish
, means: Come to her lying down, standing, turning away, facing or from your back
h
however you wish
, if he is in her vagina. Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim narrated, he said: Hisham narrated, he said:

c: Hisin informed us, on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamadani, he said:
m: I heard him narrating that a Jewish man met a Muslim man and said to him: Does one of you come to his wife while lying down? He said: Yes. He said: So he mentioned that to the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him). He said: So this verse was revealed:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
, so approach your tilth when or how ye will. He said: However you will, after he has intercourse in the vagina.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you

, so approach your tilth when or how ye will, whether you wish standing, sitting, or on your side, if he comes to her from the side from which menstruation comes, and it does not extend to anything else.

c: Musa ibn Harun told us, he said: Amr ibn Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: And approach your tilth when or how ye will means approach your tilth when or how ye will, from the front, and do not approach her from behind. However ye will, he said: However ye will.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr ibn al-Harith told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal: that Abdullah ibn Ali told him:
m: that he had heard that some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were sitting one day and a Jewish man was near them. One of them said: I come to my wife while she is lying down.

x: Another said: I come to her while she is standing.

Another said: I come to her on her side and kneeling. The Jew said: You are nothing but like animals! But we come to her in one way! Then God, the Most High, revealed: Your wives are a place of cultivation for you, meaning intercourse.
Others said: The meaning of
h
however you wish
is from wherever you wish, and in whatever direction you like.

Those who said that: Sahl bin Musa al-Razi told us, he said, Ibn Abi Fadik told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Ismail bin Abi Habeeba al-Ashhal, on the authority of Dawud bin al-Hussain, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: that he disliked that a woman be approached in her anus, and he said: The cultivation is from the front from which offspring and menstruation come, and he forbade approaching a woman in her anus and he said: This verse was revealed: Your women are a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth however you will, meaning: from any direction you will.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn Wadheeh told us, he said, al-Ataki told us, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: So approach your tilth however you will, he said: her back to her stomach, not in a squint - meaning the anus.

c: Ubaydullah bin Saad told us, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Yazid,
m: [on the authority of al-Harith bin Ka’b], on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say: Water your plants from where they grow. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then go to your tilth however you wish

, meaning: from wherever you wish. It was mentioned to us - and God knows best - that the Jews said: The Arabs approach women from their backsides, and if they do that, the child is born cross-eyed. So God proved their story false and said: Your women are your tilth, so go to your tilth
h
however you wish

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: He says: Go to women from [other than] their backsides in every way. Ibn Jurayj said: I heard Ata’ bin Abi Rabah say: We discussed this in the presence of Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abbas said: Go to them from wherever you wish, from the front and from the back. A man said: As if this is permissible! Ata’ denied that this should be like this, and he denied it, as if he only meant the vagina, from the front and from the back in the vagina.

x: Others said that the meaning of his statement:
h
However you wish is whenever you wish
Mention of the one who said that:

c: I was told by Husayn ibn al-Faraj
m: who said, I heard Abu Mu’adh al-Fadl ibn Khalid who said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us who said, I heard al-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
Then go to your tilth when or how you will
, meaning: whenever you will.

c: Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me
m: who said, Ibn Wahb told us who said, Abu Sakhr told us, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah al-Bajali - who is Ammar al-Dahni - on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr who said: While Mujahid and I were sitting with Ibn Abbas, a man came to him and stood over his head and said: O Abu al-Abbas - or: O Abu al-Fadl - will you not explain to Surat Al-Baqarah 2:223 Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth
h
however you wish

and put forth [something] for yourselves. And fear God and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers. me the verse about menstruation? He said: Yes! So he recited: And they ask you about menstruation until he reached the end of the verse, and Ibn Abbas said: From where the blood came, that is why you were commanded to come. So the man said to him: O Abu al-Fadl, what about the verse that follows it: Your women are a tilth unto you, so go to your tilth when or how you will? He said: Yes! Woe to you! And in the anus there is tilth!! If what you say is true, then menstruation would have been abrogated! If it is done from here, I will come from here! But: Wherever you are, night and day.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Wherever you want, and wherever you want.
Those who said this mentioned:

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Nafi’, who said:
m: When the Qur’an was recited to Ibn Umar, he would not speak. He said: One day I recited this verse:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
; so approach your tilth
h
however you wish
. He said: Do you know about whom this verse was revealed? I said: No! He said: It was revealed about approaching women from behind.

c: Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Nafi’, who said:
m: One day I recited:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
; so approach your tilth
h
however you wish
. Ibn Umar said: Do you know about whom it was revealed? I said: No! He said: It was revealed about approaching women from behind.

c: Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Muslim Abu Muslim told me, he said, Abu Omar Al-Dareer told us, he said,
m: Ismail bin Ibrahim, the owner of Al-Karabis told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Nafi’, he said: I was holding the Mushaf for Ibn Omar, when he recited this verse: Your women are a place of sowing for you, so go to your place of sowing
h
however you wish
. He said: That he should have intercourse with her from behind.

c: Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said, Abdul Malik bin Muslima told us, he said, Al-Darawardi told us, he said,
m: It was said to Zaid bin Aslam: Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir forbids having intercourse with women from behind. Zaid said: I bear witness that Muhammad told me that he does it.

c: Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said, Abu Zaid Abdul Rahman bin Ahmad bin Abi Al-Ghamr told us, he said, Abdul Rahman bin Al-Qasim told me, on the authority of Malik bin Anas
m: that it was said to him: O Abu Abdullah, people narrate from Salim: The slave, or: the foreigner, lied about my father!! Malik said: I bear witness that Yazid ibn Ruman told me, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, the same as Nafi’ said. It was said to him: Al-Harith ibn Ya’qub narrates on the authority of Abu al-Habbab Sa’id ibn Yasar that he asked Ibn Umar, saying: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, we buy female slaves and we protect them for them? He said: What is al-Tahmidh? He said: The anus. Ibn Umar said: Ugh! Ugh! A believer would do that! - or he said: A Muslim! - Malik said:

c: I bear witness on the authority of Rabi’ah that he told me on the authority of Abu al-Habbab, on the authority of Ibn Umar, the same as Nafi’ said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, he said: Amr ibn Tariq told us, he said: Yahya ibn Ayyub told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi, he said:
m: I said to Abu Majid al-Ziyadi: Nafi’ narrates on the authority of Ibn Umar about a woman’s anus. He said: Nafi’ lied! I was in the company of Ibn Umar and Nafi’ Mamluk, and I heard him say: I have not looked at my wife’s vagina for such and such a time.

c: Abu Qilabah narrated to me, he said: Abdus Samad narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: Go to your tillage
h
however you wish
, he said: In the anus.

c: Abu Muslim narrated to me, he said: Abu Umar Ad-Dareer narrated to us, he said: Yazid ibn Zari’ narrated to us, he said: Ruh ibn Al-Qasim narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Abu Ad-Darda’ was asked about having intercourse with women in their anus, and he said: Does anyone do that except a disbeliever? Ruh said: I witnessed Ibn Abi Mulaykah being asked about that, and he said: I wanted to do it with a slave girl of mine last night, but it was difficult for me, so I used oil or lard. I said to him: Glory be to God!!

c: Qatada told us that Abu Ad-Darda’ said:
m: Does anyone do that except a disbeliever? He said: May God curse you and curse Qatada! I said: I will never narrate anything from you! Then I regretted it after that.

x: The proponents of this statement based their argument on what they said:

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam told me, he said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways al-Aʿsha told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Bilal, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar:
m: That a man came to his wife from behind and felt bad about that, so God revealed: Your wives are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth
h
however you wish

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Nafiʿ told me, on the authority of Hisham ibn Saʿd, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ ibn Yasar:
m: That a man had intercourse with his wife from behind during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people disapproved of that and said: Has he made her miserable? So God, the Exalted, revealed: Your wives are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth
h
however you wish

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Go to your tilth
h
however you wish
- if you wish, then practice coitus interruptus, and if you wish, do not practice coitus interruptus.

Those who said that: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Al-Hasan bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Isa bin Sinan, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: Then go to your tillage
h
however you wish
If you wish, then practice isolation, and if you wish, then do not.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Zaidah bin Umair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: If you wish, then practice isolation, and if you wish, then do not.

x: As for those who said: The meaning of His statement:
h
However you wish is however you wish

, front or back, in the vagina and front, they said: The verse was revealed in response to the objection of a group of Jews who objected to approaching women from their front instead of their backsides. They said: And in that is evidence of the correctness of what we said, that its meaning is as we said.
And they supported their statement with what they said with:

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to me, he said, Al-Maharibi narrated to us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Abaan ibn Salih, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: I presented the Qur’an to Ibn Abbas three times, from the beginning to the end, stopping at each verse and asking him about it, until he reached this verse:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you

, so approach your tilth when or how ye will. Ibn Abbas said: This tribe of Quraysh used to treat women well in Mecca and enjoy themselves with them, whether they were from the front or the back. When they came to Medina, they married among the Ansar, and went to do with them as they used to do with women in Mecca. They disapproved of that and said: This is something that we have never done before! The hadith spread until it reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God, the Most High, revealed concerning that:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you

, so approach your tilth when or how ye will. If you wish, then from the front, and if you wish, then from the back, and if you wish, then from the back. What is meant by that is the place of the child for the tilth. He says: Go to the field from wherever you want.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq,
m: with his chain of transmission, something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, he said:
m: I heard Jabir say: The Jews used to say: If a man has intercourse with his wife in her vagina from behind, his child will be cross-eyed. Then God, the Most High, revealed: Your wives are as a tilth unto you, so approach your tilth when or how ye will.

c: Mujahid ibn Musa told us, he said, Yazid ibn Harun told us, he said, Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: The Jews said:
m: If a man has intercourse with his wife in her vagina from behind, and they have a child, he will be cross-eyed. Then God, the Most High, revealed:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
, so approach your tilth when or how ye will.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Khathim, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, on the authority of Hafsa bint Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr,
m: “on the authority of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man married a woman and wanted to marry her, but she refused him and said: Until I ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Umm Salamah said: So she mentioned that to me, and Umm Salamah mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Send for her. So when she came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to her:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
, so approach your tilth when or how ye will, one valve, one valve.
b.via: Hafsa bint Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu’awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman, on the authority of Ibn Sabit, on the authority of Hafsa bint Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said:
m: The Muhajirun came and married among the Ansar, and they were…” They would come, and the Ansar would not do that, so a woman said to her husband: Until I go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him about that! So she went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was too shy to ask him, so I asked, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called her and recited to her:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
, so go to your tilth when or how ye will, one valve, one valve.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told me, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, on the authority of Hafsah bint Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Umm Salamah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Sabit, on the authority of Hafsa bint Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Umm Salamah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
, so approach your tilth
h
however you wish
, he said: One valve, one valve.

c: Muhammad bin Muammar Al-Bahrani told me, he said, Yaqub bin Ishaq Al-Hadrami told us, he said, Wahib told me, he said, Abdullah bin Othman told me, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Sabit, he said:
m: I said to Hafsa, I want to ask you about something, but I am too shy to ask you. She said: Ask, my son, whatever you wish! He said: I said: I am asking you about intercourse with women in their backsides? She said: Umm Salamah told me: The Ansar did not collect taxes, and the Muhajireen used to hide them. Then a man from the Muhajireen married a woman from the Ansar. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Hisham.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us: Wahb ibn Jarir told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadir:
m: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: The Jews used to say: If a man comes to his wife while she is lying down, the child will be born cross-eyed. Then the verse was revealed:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
, so come to your tilth when or how ye will.

c: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Tusi told me, al-Hasan ibn Musa told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, who said:
m: “ʿUmar came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I am ruined!! He said: What ruined you? He said: I moved my saddle tonight! He said: So he did not answer him at all. Then God revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, this verse: ‘
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
, so come to your tilth when or how ye will.’ Come forward and go back, and avoid the anus and menstruation.”

c: Zakariya bin Yahya Al-Masri narrated to us, Abu Saleh Al-Harrani narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, that Amir bin Yahya informed him, on the authority of Hanash Al-San'ani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that some Surat Al-Baqarah 2:223 Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth
h
however you wish

and put forth [something] for yourselves. And fear God and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers. people from Himyar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him about some things. A man among them said: O Messenger of God, I am a man who loves women, so what do you think of that? So God, the Most High, revealed in Surat Al-Baqarah what they asked about, and revealed among what the man asked about:
h
Your women are as a tilth unto you
, so approach your tilth
h
however you wish
. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Go to her, facing or from behind, if that is in the vagina.

x: The correct statement regarding that, in our view, is the statement of those who said: The meaning of his statement:
h
However you wish is from any aspect you wish

. That is because how in the speech of the Arabs is a word that, when it begins a speech, indicates a question about aspects and methods. So it is as if the speaker says to a man: How did you get this money? He means: From which aspects will you get it? Therefore, the respondent answers by saying: [from such and such], as the Almighty said, informing about Zachariah in his question to Maryam 19:How did you get this? She said, ‘It is from God’
r
(Al Imran 3:37)

. It is similar to where and how in meaning, and therefore their meanings overlap, so where became confusing to its listeners and interpreters, until some of them interpreted it to mean where, some to mean how, and others to mean when - and it is different from all of that in its meaning, and they have differences.

That is because where is an interrogative letter about places and locations - and the difference in the meanings of these letters is only proven by the difference in the answers to them. Do you not see that if a questioner asked another and said: Where is your money? He would say: In such and such a place, and if he said to him: Where is your brother? The answer would be to say: In such and such a town or in such and such a place, so he answers him with the report about the place he asked him about. So it is known that where is a question about the place. And if someone said to another: How are you? He would have said: Good, or well, or in good health, and he would have told him about his current condition. Then he would know that the question is about the condition of the person being asked about his condition. If he had said to him: How does God revive this dead person?, the answer would have been to say: From such and such a perspective, so he would have described a statement similar to what God described to the one who said: How does God revive this person after his death? (al-Baqarah 2:259) in action, when He resurrected him after his death.

The poets have distinguished between that in their poems. Al-Kumait bin Zaid said: Remember who I am and where I drank it, he orders himself like this, the camel attack He also said: Where and how can I get this joy? From where there is no passion or doubt. The question is about the face, and the question is about the place, as if he said: From which face, and from which place did the joy return to you? What indicates the corruption of the statement of those who interpreted the statement of God the Most High:
h
Then go to your tilth when or how you will
