, as how you will - or interpreted it to mean: wherever you will, or whenever you will, or where you will - is that if a speaker were to say to another: How can we come to your family?, the answer would be to say: From the front, or from the back, as God the Most High informed us about Mary, when she was asked: How did you get this? She said: It is from God.
Since that is the answer, it is known that the meaning of the statement of God the Most High:
h
Then go to your tilth when or how you will

is: So go to your tilth from wherever you will, from all the directions of coming - and that other interpretations of the verse have no interpretation. Since this is correct, then it is clear that the statement of the one who claims that His statement,
h
Then go to your tilth however you wish is evidence of the permissibility of approaching women from behind is permissible

. Because there is no place to cultivate it in the anus, but God the Almighty said, A place to cultivate for you, so go to the tilth from whichever direction you wish. And which place to cultivate in the anus is it said: Go to it from its direction? And what we have explained shows the correctness of the meaning of what was narrated from Jabir and Ibn Abbas: that this verse was revealed regarding what the Jews used to say to the Muslims: If a man approaches a woman from behind in her vagina, the child will be born cross-eyed.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: Put good things forward for yourselves.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa told me, he said, ʿAmr told us, he said, Asbat told us, from Al-Suddi:
m: As for His statement, And put things forward for yourselves, it means good things.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Put the remembrance of God forward for yourselves when having intercourse and coming to the tilth before coming to it.

Those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Muhammad bin Katheer told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Waqid, on the authority of Ata’ - he said: I think it was on the authority of Ibn Abbas -
h
And send forth for yourselves
, he said: He says: In the name of God, the name of God, before intercourse.
What is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse is what we narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi, which is that His statement,
h
And send forth for yourselves

, is a command from God, the Most High, to His servants to send forth good and righteous deeds for the Day of their return to their Lord, as a number of them for themselves when they meet Him in the place of reckoning, for God, the Most High, said: And whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with God [Al-Baqarah 2:111- Al-Muzzammil 73:20]. We said that this is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, because God, the Most High, mentioned after His statement,
h
And send forth for yourselves

, the command to avoid Him in committing His sins. So what is more appropriate to be before the threat of disobedience - since the threat of disobedience is general - is the command to obey in general.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: What is the point of the command to obey in His statement: And put forward for yourselves from His statement: Your women are a tilth unto you, so come to your tilth however you will?

That is not what you imagined, but rather what he meant by it is: And put forward for yourselves from the good things that We have urged you to do by saying: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘Whatever you spend of good is for parents and near relatives,’” and what follows from the rest of what they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were answered about, from what God, the Most High, mentioned in these verses.

Then the Most High said: We have made clear to you what is right for you and what guides you to what pleases your Lord. So offer for yourselves the good that He has commanded you to do, and take a covenant with Him regarding it, so that you will find it with Him when you meet Him in your afterlife. And fear Him in His disobedience, lest you approach it, and in His limits, lest you neglect them. And know that you will inevitably meet Him in your afterlife. So the one who is estranged from the good is reminded of his goodness, and the one who does evil is reminded of his evil.

This is a warning from God Almighty to His servants, lest they commit any of the sins He has forbidden them to do, and a warning to them of His punishment when they meet Him, as we have explained before. He ordered His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to give good tidings to His servants of success on the Day of Resurrection, of the honor of the Hereafter, and of eternal life in Paradise, to whoever among them is a doer of good, a believer in His Books and His Messengers, and in meeting Him, who confirms his faith in word, by doing what his Lord has commanded him to do, and has imposed upon him of His obligations in what He has obligated him of His rights, and by avoiding what He has commanded him to avoid of His sins.

evidence.text: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Nafi’, who said: When the Qur’an was recited to Ibn Umar, he would not speak.
He said: One day I recited this verse: Your women are as a tilth unto you; so approach your tilth however you wish.

Ibrahim bin Abdullah bin Muslim Abu Muslim told me, he said, Abu Omar Al-Dareer told us, he said, Ismail bin Ibrahim, the owner of Al-Karabis told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Nafi’, he said: I was holding the Mushaf for Ibn Omar, when he recited this verse: Your women are a place of sowing for you, so go to your place of sowing however you wish.

x: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of His statement:
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths

Some of them said that it means: And do not make Him a reason for your oaths, and that is when one of you is asked for something good and to reconcile people, he says: I swear by God that I will not do that - or I have sworn by God that I will not do it, so he excuses himself in not doing good and reconciling people by swearing by God.
Who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths
. He said: It is the man who swears an oath about something that is not right, then he uses his oath as an excuse. God says:
h
That you are righteous and fear God
is better for him than continuing with what is not right. And if you swear, then atone for your oath and do what is best for you.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father,
m: similarly, except that he said: And if you swear, then atone for your oath and do what is best.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Ubaydullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths lest you be righteous and fear God and make peace between people

,” he said, “It is when a man swears not to speak to his relatives or give charity, or when there is a dispute between him and a person, so he swears not to make peace between them and says, ‘I have sworn.’ He said, ‘He breaks his oath.
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said, Yazid ibn Zari’ told us, he said, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths lest you be righteous and fear God

, he said: Do not use God as an excuse, that one of you swears not to maintain family ties, not to strive for righteousness, and not to give charity from his wealth. Hold on, hold on, may God bless you, for this Qur’an came to abandon the command of Satan, so do not obey him, and do not carry out his command in any of your vows or oaths.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: h
And do not make God an object of your oaths
, he said: It is a man who swears that he will not reconcile between people and will not fulfill his oaths, so when it is said to him, he says: I have sworn.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I asked Ata’ about His statement: “
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths lest you be righteous and fear God and make peace between people
,” he said: A man swears that he will not do good, a good thing, he says: I have sworn! God said: Do what is best and atone for your oath,
h
and do not make God an object of your oaths

c: I was told by Al-Husayn
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths

the verse: It is a man who forbids what God has made lawful for himself, so he says: I have sworn! It is not permissible unless I fulfill my oath. So God commanded them to atone for their oaths and do what is lawful.

c: Musa told us
m: who said: Amr told us who said: Asbat told us from As-Suddi who said: “
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths lest you be righteous and fear God and make peace between people

.” As for atonement, it is an object of your oaths, so you swear by God not to speak to him or connect with him. As for tabru, it is a man who swears not to be righteous with a relative and he says: I have sworn! So God commanded that he should not make his oath an object of his oath between himself and his relative, and that he should be righteous with him, and not care about his oath. As for tasalhuwa, a man tries to reconcile two people but they disobey him, so he swears that he will not reconcile them, so he should reconcile them and not care about his oath. This was before the expiations were revealed.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths
, he said: He swears that he will not fear God, nor maintain kinship ties, nor reconcile two people, so his oath should not prevent him.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Do not object by swearing by God in your speech among yourselves, so that you make that an excuse for yourselves to refrain from doing good.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: And do not make God an Surat Al-Baqarah 2:224 And do not make God an excuse for your oaths to prevent you from being righteous and fearing God and making peace between people. And God is Hearing and Knowing. object of your oaths, meaning: Do not make me an object of your oath not to do good, but atone for your oath and do good.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths lest you be righteous and fear God and make peace between people
,” a man would swear an oath to do something of righteousness and piety that he would not do, so God, the Almighty, forbade that and said:
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths
lest you be righteous.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths

, he said: It is a man who swears that he will not be righteous to his relatives, will not maintain kinship ties, and will not make peace between two people. He said: Let him do so, and expiate for his oath.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i,
m: regarding His statement: “
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths to prevent you from being righteous and fearing God and making peace between people

,” he said: Do not swear that you will not fear God, and do not swear that you will not be righteous and do good, and do not swear that you will not pray, and do not swear that you will not make peace between people, and do not swear that you will kill and cut off.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr ibn Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: and Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His statement:
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths
, the verse, they said: He is the man who swears that he will not be righteous, fear God,
h
and make peace between people
. And he was commanded to fear God, to make peace between people, and to atone for his oath.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa - and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us
m: - on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement:
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths
, so they were commanded to maintain ties of kinship, do good,
h
and make peace between people
. If he swears an oath that he will not do that, then let him do it, and let him abandon his oath.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father,
m: on Al-Rabiʿ, regarding His statement:
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths

, the verse, he said: That is about a man who swears that he will not be righteous, will not maintain ties of kinship, and will not make peace between people. So God commanded him to abandon his oath, maintain ties of kinship, enjoin what is good,
h
and make peace between people

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Harb told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Aswad, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha,
m: regarding His statement: “
h
And make not God an object of your oaths lest you be righteous and fear God and make peace between people
,” she said: Do not swear by God even if you are righteous.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I was told that His statement:
h
And make not God an object of your oaths
, the verse, was revealed about Abu Bakr, concerning Mastih.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And make not God an object of your oaths
, the verse, he said: A man swears that he will not enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, or maintain ties of kinship.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And make not God an object of your oaths
, he said: He swears that he will not fear God, nor maintain ties of kinship, nor make peace between two people. So his oath does not prevent him.

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Makhul that he said
m: about the statement of God the Most High: And do not make God an excuse for your oaths, he said: It is when a man swears that he will not do good, nor maintain kinship ties, nor reconcile between people. God forbade them from that.

x: The most correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the interpretation of the one who said: Its meaning is: Do not make an oath by God an excuse for you to refrain from doing good between you and God and between people. This is because the word arada in the speech of the Arabs means strength and severity. It is said from it: This matter is an excuse for you, meaning by that: strength for your reasons. And it is said: So-and-so is an excuse for marriage? meaning strength 1, and from it is the statement of Kaʿb ibn Zuhair in describing she-camels: From every freshness of the penis, if it sweats, it is presented by the obscured and unknown flags Meaning by its strength: its power and intensity. So the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And do not make God a source of strength for your oaths is: Do not make God a source of strength for your oaths in that you do not do righteousness, nor fear God, nor make peace between people.

But if one of you swears an oath and sees that which is better than what he swore to do, such as neglecting righteousness and making peace between people, then let him break his oath, and be righteous,
h
and fear God
h
and make peace between people
, and expiate for his oath.

i: He left out mentioning la from the speech, because the speech indicates it, and what was mentioned is sufficient for what he left out, as Imru’ al-Qais said:
x: I said: I swear to God I will stay seated even if they cut off my head and my limbs in front of you.
Meaning: So I said: By God's oath I will not leave, so He omitted la, as the statement was sufficient to indicate it. As for his saying:
h
That you be righteous
!, there is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of righteousness that God the Most High meant.
Some of them said: It is doing all good.

Others said: It is being righteous to one's relatives, and I have mentioned those who said that previously. The most correct of that is the saying of those who said: It means doing all good, because all good deeds are from righteousness, and God did not specify in His saying:
h
That you be righteous a meaning over a meaning of righteousness
, so it is general. Being righteous to relatives is one of the meanings of righteousness. As for His saying:
h
And fear God

, its meaning is: That you fear your Lord, so you fear Him and fear His punishment in His obligations and limits, lest you neglect them or transgress them. We have already mentioned the interpretation of those who interpreted that it means piety before.
Others said in its interpretation:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told us, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
That you are righteous and fear God
, he said: A man would swear an oath to do something of righteousness
h
and fear God
but he would not do it, so God the Almighty forbade that and said: “
h
And do not make God an object of your oaths
, lest you be righteous
h
and fear God
h
and make peace between people

” (al-Anbiya’ 2:10). He said: And it is said: Do not fear each other by Me, you swear by Me while you are lying, so that people will believe you and you will make peace between them, so that is His statement:
h
That you are righteous and fear God (al-Anbiya’ 2
:10). As for His statement: “
h
And make peace between people

,” it is making peace between them in a good manner in which there is no sin, and in what God loves and not in what He hates. As for what we mentioned from al-Suddi: that this verse was revealed before the expiations for oaths were revealed, then this is a statement for which there is no evidence in the Book or the Sunnah. And the report of what was, its authenticity cannot be known except by a true report, otherwise it would be a claim that is not difficult for anyone to prove or contradict. It is not impossible that this verse was revealed after explaining the expiations for oaths in Surat Al-Ma’idah, and it was sufficient to mention it there instead of repeating it here, since those addressed by this verse knew the expiations required for oaths that the one who swears breaks.

x: God Almighty meant by that: And God is All-Hearing of what the one who swears by God among you says when he swears. He said: By God, I will not be righteous, nor will I be pious, nor will I reconcile between people, nor will I be able to do anything other than what you say and swear. He is All-Knowing of what you intend and seek with your oath. Do you want good or something else? Because I am the Knower of the unseen and what the hearts conceal. Nothing is hidden from Me, and nothing is concealed from Me, whether it is declared or concealed. This is a threat and warning from God Almighty. He Almighty says: And fear, O people, lest you show with your tongues what I have forbidden you from saying, or with your bodies what I have forbidden you from doing, or conceal in your souls and resolve in your hearts of wills and intentions to do what I have warned you against, lest you thereby deserve from Me the punishment that I have made known to you.
For I am aware of everything that you declare or conceal.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths
, and in the meaning of unintentional oaths.

Some of them said in its meaning: God will not hold you accountable for the oaths that your tongues have uttered in haste and haste, and He requires you to make expiation for them if you did not intend to swear or take an oath. This is like the saying of someone: I did this, by God, or: I will do it, by God, or: I will not do it, by God, based on the speaker's tongue being pre-emptive in what he said of the oath.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told us, he said, Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: It is: Yes, by God and no, by God.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, she said: No, by God and yes, by God.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Aisha,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: I asked Aisha about the vain oath, she said: It is: No, by God and yes, by God, what people take back.

c: Hannad told us, he said,
m: Waki’, Abdah, and Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha regarding the statement of God:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, she said: No, by God, and yes, by God. Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, she said: No, by God, and yes, by God. He connected his words with it. Ibn Humayd narrated that Hakam ibn Salim narrated on the authority of Abdul Malik on the authority of Ata’ who said: I entered with Ubayd ibn Umair upon Aisha and he said to her: O Mother of the Believers, what about His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
? She said: No, by God, and yes, by God. It is not among the oaths you have made.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, Hisham told us, Ibn Abi Laila told us, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: I came to Aisha with Ubayd ibn Umair, and Ubayd asked her about his statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
. Aisha said: It is a man saying: No, by God, and Yes, by God, as long as he has not made up his mind to do so.

c: Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, who said:
m: I set out with Ubayd ibn Umair to Aisha while she was a neighbor in Thabir. Ubayd asked her about idle oaths, and she said: No, by God, and yes, by God.

c: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Harashi told us, Hassan ibn Ibrahim al-Karmani told us, Ibrahim al-Sayegh told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: Aisha said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is a man saying in his house: No, by God, and yes, by God.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aisha,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, she said: They are people who argue about a matter, and one of them says: No, by God, and Yes, by God, and No, by God, they argue about a matter, their hearts are not set on it.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: A man’s saying: No, by God, and Yes, by God, connects his speech with it, there is no expiation for it.

c: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to us, he said: Mughirah narrated to us, from al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: It is a man who says: No, by God, and Yes, by God, connecting his speech.

c: Humayd bin Mas’adah narrated to us, he said: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Ibn Awn narrated to us, he said:
m: I asked Aamer about His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: It is: No, by God, and Yes, by God.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: My father told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, similarly.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Wakee’ told me, they said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayyub told us, he said, Abu Qilabah said
m: about: No, by God, and yes, by God, I hope it is a language - and Yaqub said in his hadith: I hope it is a language - and Ibn Wakee’ said in his hadith: I hope it is a language, and he had no doubt. Abu Kurayb, Ibn Wakee’ and Hannad told us, they said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, he said: No, by God, and yes, by God.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: I heard Aisha say about His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, she said: No, by God, and yes, by God.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Mughul, on the authority of Ata’,
m: similarly.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: It is the saying of al-Nas 114:No, by God, and yes, by God.

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi and Ikrimah, they said:
m: No, by God, and yes, by God.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: I entered with Ubayd ibn Umair upon Aisha and asked her, and she said: No, by God, and yes, by God. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, Hafs narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila and Ash’ath, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Aisha,
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

. She said: No, by God, and yes, by God. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, my father and Jarir narrated, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: No, by God, and yes, by God. Ibn Wakee’ and Hannad narrated, Ya’la narrated, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, who said: Aisha said regarding the statement of God,
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, she said: It is your saying, No, by God, and Yes, by God. It does not constitute a binding oath. Hannad narrated, Abu Al-Ahwas narrated, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Idle talk is when a man says, No, by God, and Yes, by God, connecting his words with it, as long as it is not something that his heart is committed to.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Amr told me, that Saeed bin Abi Hilal told him:
m: that he heard Ata bin Abi Rabah say: I heard Aisha say: The futility of an oath is a man saying: No, by God, and yes, by God, regarding what his heart has not decided upon.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Amr said, and Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Hussain Al-Nawfali told me, on the authority of Ata, on the authority of Aisha, that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, he said: Two men engage in a transaction, and one of them says: By God, I will not sell it to you for such and such, and the other says: By God, I will not buy it for such and such, so this is futility and he will not be held accountable for it.

x: Others said: Rather, futility in an oath is the oath that the swearer swears while he believes that it is as he swore, then it becomes clear that it is not so, and that it is different from what he swore.

Who said that: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he used to say: Idle oaths are when a person swears something thinking it is what he swore, but it is not.

c: Muhammad bin Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
. Idle oaths are when a man swears something he sees as true, but it is not true.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Mu’awiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

. This is about a man who swears to do something harmful but does not do it, and he sees something better than it, so God commands him to atone for his oath and do what is better. Idle oaths are also when a man swears something in which he does not spare any effort to be truthful, but he errs in his oath. This is the one who must make expiation and there is no sin on him.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar,
m: regarding His statement,
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: An unintentional mistake.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding this verse,
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, he said: It is when you swear an oath, and you think it is as you swore, but it is not. So God will not hold him accountable and there is no expiation, but the accountability and expiation are for what he swore to with knowledge.

c: Hannad and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said, Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Al-Fadl ibn Dahlam, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: It is a man who swears an oath, but he does not think it is anything other than what he swore.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: It is a man who swears an oath, thinking it is as it is, but it is not.

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said, Abdah narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, he said: It is a man who swears to something, and he believes that it is so, but it is not as he said, so there is no expiation for him. Hannad, Abu Kurayb, and Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, they said, Wakee’ narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan - and Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said, Al-Thawri narrated to us - on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: It is a man who swears an oath, and he does not believe that it is as he swore, but it is not.

c: Muhammad bin Amr narrated to me, he said, Abu Asim narrated to us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: regarding the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:225 God will not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for what your hearts have earned. And God is Forgiving and Forbearing. statement of God,
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: Whoever swears by God and does not know except that he is truthful in what he swore.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths

, a man swears an oath about something, knowing nothing but that it is as he swore, so it is not as he swore, like saying: This is a house for so-and-so, but it is not his, and this is a garment for so-and-so, but it is not his.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding His statement,
h
God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths
, he said: It is a man who swears an oath about something, thinking that it is as he swore, but it is not. He said: So He will not hold you accountable for that. He said: And he loved to disbelieve.

c: Musa bin Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi told us, he said, al-Jaʿfi told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Mansur, he said: Ibrahim said:
m: God will not hold you accountable for what is futile in your oaths. He said: That he swears to something while he believes that it is true and it is a lie, then that is futile, and he will not be held accountable for it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: something similar, except that He said: If you swear to something, and you think you are telling the truth, but you are not.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Hisin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, that he said:
m: Idle talk is a man who swears oaths, and he thinks that it is as he swore.

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told us, he said, Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ziyad, he said:
m: It is the one who swears an oath, believing that he is truthful in it.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Yaqub bin Ishaq Al-Hadrami told us, he said, Bakir bin Abi Al-Sumait told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: It is an unintentional mistake. A man swears about something, believing that it is so, but it is not so.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur and Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Idle talk, a man swears about something, believing that it is so, so there is no expiation for it.

c: Hannad and Ibn Wakee’ told us
m: - Hannad said: Wakee’ told us, and Ibn Wakee’ said: My father told me - on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, he said: I heard Zararah bin Awfa say: It is the man who swears an oath, believing that it is as he swore. Ahmad bin Hazim narrated, Abu Naim narrated, Umar bin Bashir narrated: Aamer was asked about this verse:
h
God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths

, he said: Unintentional oaths are when a man swears an oath without sparing himself from the truth, but it is otherwise. This is the unintentional oath for which he will not be held accountable. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths

, an unintentional oath is an unintentional mistake, that is, you swear about something and you think it is as you swore, but it is not. So there is no expiation for it and no sin in it. Musa narrated, Amr narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
h
God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths
, as for unintentional oaths: a man swears an oath and he thinks it is as you swore, but it is not. He does not have to make expiation for it.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths
, he said: An unintentional oath is an unintentional mistake: that he swears about something while he believes that it is as he swore. This is something for which he does not have to make expiation.

c: Hannad told us,
m: who said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said: As for the oath for which its owner is not held accountable, a man swears an oath while he believes that he is telling the truth, and that is an unintentional oath.

c: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me,
m: who said: Hisham told us, who said: Hisayn told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, something similar, except that he said: A man swears about something while he believes that it is as he swore, but it is not. There is no expiation for it, and it is idle oaths.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, and on the authority of Ibn Abi Talhah - this is what Ibn Abi Jaafar said - they said:
m: Whoever says: By God, I did such and such, thinking that he did it, then it becomes clear to him that he did not do it, then this is a idle oath, and there is no expiation for it.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: It is an unintentional mistake, like a man saying: By God, this is such and such, and he thinks that he is telling the truth, but it is not. Muammar said: Qatada also said the same.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr told us, he said:
m: Saeed was asked about idle oaths. Saeed said, and Makhul said: The mistake is not intentional, but the expiation is for what your hearts have decided.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abdul Aziz, on the authority of Makhul that he said:
m: The idle oath for which God will not hold you accountable is when a man swears an oath about something he thinks he is telling the truth, but it turns out that it is not, so there is no expiation for it, and God has forgiven him.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, he said: If he swears an oath and he believes that he is telling the truth, but he is lying, then he will not be held accountable for it. But if he swears an oath and he knows that he is lying, then that is what he will be held accountable for.

x: Others said: Rather, idle oaths are among the oaths that its owner swears in a state of anger, without a decision in his heart or resolve, but rather as a connection to the speech.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Malik bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Waseem, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: A futile oath is to swear while you are angry.

c: Ibn Hameed told us, he said, Yahya bin Wazeh told us, he said, Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Tawus, he said:
m: Every oath that a man swears while he is angry, there is no expiation for it, as God says:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
. The reason for saying this statement is:

c: Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Marwazi told me, he said: Omar bin Yunus Al-Yamami told us, he said: Sulayman bin Abi Sulayman Al-Zahri told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no oath in anger.

x: Others said: Rather, the idle oath is: swearing to do what God has forbidden and to leave what God has commanded to do.
He mentioned who said that:

c: Hannad told us, he said, Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: He is the one who swears to commit a sin, but does not fulfill it and expiates his oath, his saying:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

c: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: The vain oath: is that a man swears to commit a sin to God, and God will not hold him accountable for nullifying it.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: similarly, and he added to it, he said: And he must expiate it.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul Ala and Yazid bin Harun told me, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Saeed,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: It is the man who swears to commit a sin, and God will not hold him accountable. To atone for his oath and do what is better.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us
m: - and Ibn Wakeeʿ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Shuʿbah - on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse: God will not punish you for what is unintentional in your oaths, he said: A man swears to commit a sin, but God will not punish him for not doing it.

c: Al-Hasan ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar narrated to us, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of ʿIsa ibn bint Dawud ibn Abi Hind, he said: Khalid ibn Ilyas narrated to us, on the authority of Umm Abihi:
m: That she swore that she would not speak to her granddaughter - the daughter of Abu al-Jahm - so she went to Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, Abu Bakr, and ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: There is no oath for a sin, and there is no atonement upon her.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, he said: It is a man who swears an oath to commit a sin, but God will not hold him accountable for abandoning it if he abandons it. I said: What should he do? He said: He should atone for his oath and abandon the sin.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: It is a man who swears to do something forbidden, so God will not hold him accountable for not doing it.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said
m: regarding the unintentional oath, he said: It is the oath in disobedience. He said: Do you not read and understand? God said:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, but He will hold you accountable for your deliberate oaths (al-Ma’idah 5:89), he said: He will not hold him accountable for omitting it, but He will hold him accountable for completing it. He said: He said: Do not make God the target of your oaths until His saying: For God is Forgiving and Merciful.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: A man swears an oath to commit a sin, but God will not hold him accountable for leaving it, and he disbelieves.

c: Muhammad bin al-Muthanna told us, he said: Wahb bin Jarir told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq,
m: regarding a man who swears an oath to commit a sin, and he said: Does he disbelieve in the steps of Satan? He does not have to make expiation.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding a man who swears an oath to commit a sin, he said: Its expiation is that he repents from it.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi
m: that he used to say: He should abandon the sin and not expiate, and if I had ordered him to make the expiation, I would have ordered him to complete it according to what he said.

c: Yahya bin Dawud Al-Wasiti told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: Every oath that it is not permissible for you to fulfill, there is no expiation for it. The reason for those who said this statement from the hadith is that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Katheer, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:225 God will not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for what your hearts have earned. And God is Forgiving and Forbearing. “Whoever vows something that he does not own, then his vow is not valid, and whoever swears to disobey God, then his oath is not valid, and whoever swears to sever family ties, then his oath is not valid.”

c: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me, he said, Ali bin Masaher told us, on the authority of Haritha bin Muhammad, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath to sever family ties or to disobey God, then his righteousness is that he breaks it and takes back his oath.

x: Others said: The idle oath is every oath that a man connects to his words, without intending to impose it on himself.

Those who said that: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: The idle oath is that a man connects his words to an oath: By God, they will eat, by God, they will drink, and the like, without intending to swear by it, nor intending to swear by it. There is no expiation for him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Hisham Al-Dastawai, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: Idle oaths, what he says: By God, you will eat, by God, you will drink.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: God will not hold you accountable for your idle oaths, he said: They are two men bargaining over something, and one of them says: By God, I will not buy it from you for such and such, and the other says: By God, I will not sell it to you for such and such.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab: that Urwah told him:
m: that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Idle oaths are what is done in jest, argument, and dispute, and talk that the heart does not rely on. The chastity of the one who said this statement from the hadith, what: - Muhammad bin Musa al-Harashi narrated to us, he said, Ubayd God bin Maymun al-Muradi narrated to us, he said, Aouf al-A’rabi narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hasan bin Abi al-Hasan, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by some people who were shooting - meaning: they were shooting - and with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a man from his companions, so a man from the people shot and said: By God, you hit, and I missed! So the one who was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The man broke his oath, O Messenger of God! He said: No, the oaths of the archers are futile and there is no expiation or punishment for them.”

x: Others said: Futile oaths are what was from an oath in the sense of a supplication from the one who swears upon himself: If he does not do such and such, or in the sense of polytheism and disbelief.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Hakam Al-Masri told us, he said, Ismail ibn Marzouq told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, he said: It is like a man saying: God has blinded my sight if I do not do such and such - God will take me out of my wealth if I do not come to you tomorrow, so this is it, and God will not leave him wealth or children. He says: If God were to hold you accountable for this, He would not leave you anything.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Hakam told us, he said, Ismail told us, he said, Yahya ibn Ayoub told me, on the authority of Amr ibn Al-Harith, on the authority of Zaid ibn Aslam,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Hakam told us, he said, Ismail ibn Marzouq told us, he said, Yahya ibn Ayoub told me that
m: Zaid ibn Aslam used to say regarding the statement,
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, it is like a man saying: He is a disbeliever and he is a polytheist. He said: He will not hold him accountable until that is from his heart.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, he said: The unintentional oath in this is: swearing by God that is on the tongues, so He made it unintentional, which is that he says: He is a disbeliever in God while he is associating partners with God, and he is calling upon another god along with God, so this is the unintentional oath that God mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah.

x: Others said: The unintentional oaths are those for which there is expiation.

Who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, this is about a man who swears to do something harmful but does not do it, then he sees something better than it, so God commanded him to expiate his oath and do what is better.

c: Yahya bin Ja’far told me, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
, he said: The expiatory oath.

x: Others said: The unintentional oath is what the swearer breaks out of forgetfulness.

Who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Hisham briefed us, he said, Mughira told me, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: It is a man who swears an oath and then forgets it, meaning in His statement:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

In the speech of the Arabs, lagha is any speech that is blameworthy and meaningless and abandoned. It is said: someone lagha in his speech, yalghwa lagha if he says something ugly. From this is the statement of God, the Most High: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it (al-Qasas 28:55), and His statement: And when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity (al-Furqan 25:72). It is heard from the Arabs: laghayat in the name of someone, meaning I was fond of mentioning him in an ugly way. So whoever says laghayat, says: lagha lagha, which is the language of some Arabs, and from this is the statement of the rajaz poet: And the pilgrims' flocks are restrained from idle talk and obscene speech. If the vain talk is as described, and the one swearing by God: I did not do such and such, and he did, and I did such and such, and he did - and he continued his speech with that, by way of a slip of the tongue, without intentionally committing a sin in his oath, but due to a habit that has become established for him.

In haste to speak, and the one who says: By God, this belongs to so-and-so, and he sees it as he said, or: By God, this is not so-and-so! and he sees it as he is not him, and the one who says: They will do such-and-such, by God - or: He will not do such-and-such, by God, in the manner we described of haste to speak and the tongue being quick to follow custom, without intending to swear falsely, and the one who says: He is a polytheist, or he is a Jew or a Christian, if he does not do such-and-such - or if he does such-and-such without intending to be a disbeliever or a Jewish or Christian, all of them are saying something that is vulgar and reprehensible in speech, and they swear oaths with their tongues as long as their hearts do not intend sin in them, it is known that they are idle in their oaths, and they are not required to pay expiation in the immediate life, nor to be punished in the hereafter, because God, the Most High, has informed us that He will not hold His servants accountable for their idle oaths, and that what He will hold them accountable for is what their hearts intend sin in.

And since that is the case, and it is authentic from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees that something else is better than it, let him do what is better, and expiate for his oath, so he made expiation obligatory by the one who swore not to do what he swore not to do, along with the obligation to do what is better than what he swore not to do, and the fine in money - or the obligation of the rewarder to replace the rewarders - is undoubtedly a punishment like some of the punishments that God, the Most High, mentioned, made as a deterrent to His creation for what they transgressed from His limits, even though they all agree that they are a test and expiation for those who were punished with them for what they were punished for, it was clear that whoever was obligated to expiate in his immediate worldly life for what he swore of oaths and then broke it, even if it was an expiation for his sin, God took him to task with it by obligating him to expiate with it, even if what He hastened of His punishment for that, dropped his punishment in his afterlife.

And since God, the Most High, mentioned, took him to task with it, it is not permissible for someone who said: To say, and he has taken him to task for it: It is from the idle talk for which the one who says it will not be held accountable. Since that is not permissible, then it is clear that the statement narrated from Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Idle talk is an oath to commit a sin, because if that were the case, then the one who swears to commit a sin will not have to make expiation for breaking his oath. And in Saeed’s requiring expiation for him, there is clear evidence that its owner will be held accountable for it, because of what we have described, that the one who is required to make expiation for his oath is not one who will not be held accountable for it. Since idle talk is what we have described, from what God the Most High has informed us that He will not hold us accountable for - and every oath for which its owner is required to make expiation in the immediate case, or God the Most High has threatened its owner with punishment for it in the hereafter, even if He has waived its expiation in the immediate case - is something that the hearts of the swearers have earned, and the souls of the swearers have deliberately committed sin in it.

Anything other than that is idle talk, and we have explained its aspects. The interpretation of the statement then is: Do not make God, O believers, a force for your oaths, and an argument for yourselves in your oaths, that you will not be righteous, nor fear God, nor make peace between people. Indeed, God will not hold you accountable for what your tongues have uttered of your oaths, which are ugly and reprehensible oaths, without you intending to sin, nor intending in your hearts to impose the oaths that you have sworn. Rather, He will only hold you accountable for what you intentionally made in making the oath and imposing it upon yourselves, and you resolved to swear on what you swore with intent and will. In that case, you will be required to either pay expiation in the immediate future, or to be punished in the hereafter.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning that God, the Most High, threatened His servants with His saying:
h
But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned
, that He will hold them accountable for it, after all of them agreed that the meaning of His saying: for what your hearts have earned is what you have intentionally done.
Some of them said: The meaning that God has threatened to hold His servants accountable for is the oath of one of them that is false and wrong.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: If a man swears an oath and he believes that he is telling the truth but he is lying, he will not be held accountable for it. But if he swears and he knows that he is lying, then that is what he will be held accountable for.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, he said, Hussain Al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Mansur, he said: Ibrahim said:
m: h
But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned
, he said: That he swears on something and he knows that it is false, then that is what he will be held accountable for.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned
, that is, you swear and you are lying.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn (al-Ma’idah 5:89), and that is the false oath, which a man swears to commit injustice or to sever ties, and there is no expiation for that unless he abandons that injustice, or returns that money to its people, and that is the saying of the Most High: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price until His saying: And for them is a painful punishment
r
(Al-Imran: 77)

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us,
m: on the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:225 God will not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will impose blame upon you for what your hearts have earned. And God is Forgiving and Forbearing. authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned
, what you have sworn.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: You will not be held accountable until you ascend to the matter. Then you swear by God, there is no god but Him, and you make a covenant with Him.

x: According to this interpretation, what is required is that the words of God, the Most High, But He will punish you for what your hearts have earned, should be in the Hereafter with whatever punishments He wills - and that expiation is only required of the one who swears in oaths that are futile. Likewise, it was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: that he did not see expiation except in oaths that are futile. As for what the hearts have earned and made a covenant in sin, he did not require expiation for it. We have already mentioned the narration from them regarding that previously. Since this is their interpretation of the verse, then according to their doctrine, the meaning of the verse in Surat Al-Ma'idah is:
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths
. Its expiation is feeding ten poor people from the average of that with which you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave.

But whoever cannot find [anything] - then a fast of three days. That is the expiation for your oaths when you swear. But He will hold you accountable for what you have made deliberate, so guard your oaths. And similar to what we mentioned from Ibn Abbas regarding this, Saeed bin Jubair, Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, and a group other than them said, and we mentioned the narration from them earlier.

Others said: The meaning that God threatened His servants with in this verse is the oath of the one who swears falsely, knowing it to be false. In this, God made expiation obligatory, according to them, but not the unintentional oath that the one who swears swears while he is mistaken in his oath, thinking that what he swore is as he swore, but that is not the case.
Who said that: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said:

c: Yazid bin Zari’ narrated to us, he said: Sa’id narrated to us, from Qatada:
m: h
But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned
meaning: for what your hearts have deliberately conceived, and what you have deliberately committed as sin, then you must make expiation for this. I narrated to Ammar, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Ja’far narrated to us, from his father, from Al-Rabi’,
m: similarly. It seems that the speakers of this statement directed the interpretation of God holding His servant accountable for what his heart has earned of false oaths, to it being His holding him accountable for it by obligating him to make expiation for it.

x: Another group said something similar to the statement of Qatada, regarding the obligation of expiation for the one who swears a false oath, including ‘Ata’ and Al-Hakam.

c: Abu Kurayb and Ya’qub narrated to us, they said: Hisham narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj informed us, from ‘Ata’ and Al-Hakam,
m: that they used to say about the one who deliberately swore falsely: he must make expiation.

x: Others said: Rather, that has two meanings: One of them is that the servant is held accountable for it in this world by God obligating him to make expiation for it, and the other… He will be held accountable for it in the Hereafter unless he pardons.
Those who said this: Musa bin Harun told me, he said:

c: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned

. As for what your hearts have earned, it means what your hearts have decided upon. A man swears an oath that he knows is false, intending to get his matter done. There are three types of oaths: idle, deliberate, and false. A man swears an oath intending to do something, then he sees something better than that. This is the oath that God the Most High said: But He will hold you accountable for what you have deliberated upon. This has an expiation. It is as if the author of this article directed the interpretation of his statement: But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned to something other than what he directed the interpretation of his statement: But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn, and made his statement:
h
For what your hearts have earned the oaths that the swearer swears with the knowledge that his oath is invalid - and his statement
: For what you have sworn, the oath in which he renews the perjury or the fulfillment, and while he is swearing by it, he is determined to fulfill it.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the belief in polytheism and disbelief.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam told me, he said, Ismail bin Marzuq told us, he said, Yahya bin Ayoub told me, on the authority of Muhammad - meaning Ibn Ajlan -
m: that Zaid bin Aslam used to say about the statement of God, the Most High:
h
But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned
, like a man saying: He is a disbeliever, he is a polytheist. He said: God will not hold him accountable until that is from his heart.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths

, he said: The unintentional oath in this is the oath by God that is on the tongues, so He made it unintentional, and it is to say: He is a disbeliever in God, and then he associates partners with God, and he calls upon another god along with God. This is the unintentional oath that God the Most High said in Surat Al-Baqarah,
h
But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned
, he said: for what was in your hearts in truth, and He will hold you accountable for it. If there was no truth in your heart, He will not hold you accountable for it, even if you sinned.

x: The correct statement in this regard is that God, the Most High, has threatened His servants that He will hold them accountable for the oaths their hearts have earned. What their hearts earn of oaths is what they intended and resolved to do with knowledge and awareness of what they intended and wanted. This can be in two ways: One of them is the resolve to do something by which the one who resolves it is sinful and deserving of being held accountable by God for it. This is like swearing that he did not do something that he did not do, and that he did do something that he did do, intending, it is said, to lie, and remembering that he did do what he swore he did not do, or that he did not do what he swore he did do. So the one who swears by this - if he is one of the people of faith in God and His Messenger - will be in the will of God on the Day of Resurrection. If He wills, He will hold him accountable for it in the Hereafter, and if He wills, He will pardon him by His grace, and there is no expiation for it in the immediate future, because it is not one of the oaths that one breaks.

The expiation is only required for oaths that are broken. The one who swears falsely in his oath, his oath is not one in which breaking the oath begins, so expiation is required for it. The other aspect of them: is in the form of the intention to impose the oath contract while he is determined to do so. This is something for which its owner will not be held accountable until he breaks it after his oath. So if he breaks it after his oath, he will be held accountable for what his heart had acquired - of swearing by God for sin and lying - in the immediate future with the expiation that God made as expiation for his sin.

God Almighty means by that: And God is Forgiving to His servants regarding their vain oaths, which God Almighty has informed us about. He mentioned that He will not hold them accountable for it, even if He had willed and taken them to task for it, and had He taken them to task for it, they would have disbelieved in it in this world by disbelief in it, and if He had willed and taken them to task in the Hereafter by punishing it, He would have covered them up in it, and pardoned them by pardoning them for the punishment in it, and other than that of their sins, Forbearing in not hastening the punishment of those who disobey Him for their sins.
God Almighty means by His saying: For those who swear for those who swear by a tool, and the tool The oath, as:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Muslima bin Alqamah told us, Dawud bin Abi Hind told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab,
m: regarding his statement: For those who swear they swear. It is said: So-and-so swore, he swears, he swears, as the poet said: We are enough for those who are lost in the dust, and we have broken our oaths It is said: Alwa and Alwa, as the rajaz poet said: Oh, how I love you, how I love you It was also narrated that they say: Ilwa with a broken alif. Tarabus means looking and waiting. The meaning of the statement: For those who swear to abstain from their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. So he left out mentioning that they should abstain, being satisfied with the indication of what appeared from the statement.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the oath by which a man is considered an oath from his wife.

Some of them said: The oath by which a man is considered an oath from his wife is that he swears to her - in a state of anger in order to harm - that he will not have intercourse with her in her vagina. However, if he swears not in order to harm her, and not in anger, then he is not an oath from her.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Hannad bin Al-Sarri told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Harith bin Umaira, on the authority of Umm Atiyah, she said, Jubayr said:
m: Breastfeed my nephew along with your son! She said: I cannot breastfeed two! So he swore that he would not come near her until she weans him. When she weaned him, he passed by the gathering, and the people said to him: What you have fed him is good! Jubayr said: I swore that I would not come near her until she weans him! The people said to him: This is an oath!!

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, Shuʿbah narrated to us, on the authority of Samak,
m: that he heard ʿAtiyyah ibn Jubayr say: Umm Sibah, a relative of mine, died, and my father’s wife used to breastfeed him. So he swore that he would not go near her until she weaned him. When four months had passed, it was said to him: She has separated from you! - and I think Abu Jaʿfar was not sure. - He said: So he came to ʿAli to seek his legal opinion, and he said: If you said that in anger, then you have no wife, and otherwise she is your wife. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, Abu Dawud narrated, Shu'bah narrated, Samak informed me, I heard 'Atiyyah ibn Jubayr - they mention it from 'Ali. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Abd al-Majid narrated, Dawood narrated, from Samak, from a man from Banu 'Ajil, from Abu 'Atiyyah: His brother died and left behind a young son. Abu 'Atiyyah said to his wife: Suck him! She said: I fear that you will make them miserable. So he swore that he would not come near her until she weaned them. So he did until she weaned them. Then Abu 'Atiyyah's nephew went out to the gathering, and they said: How well Abu 'Atiyyah has fed his nephew! He said: No! Umm 'Atiyyah claimed that I was making them miserable, so she swore that she would not come near her until she weaned them. So they said to him: Your wife is forbidden to you! So I mentioned that to Ali may God be pleased with him, and Ali said: I only wanted good, and the oath is only used in anger.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Dawud narrated to us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Abu Atiyah:
m: that his brother died - and he mentioned something similar.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb:
m: that a man's brother died, so he said to his wife: Suckle my nephew. She said: I am afraid that you will fall on me! So he swore that he would not touch her until she is weaned. So he refrained from her, and when she weaned him, he took the boy out to his people, and they said: You have fed him well! So he mentioned his situation to them, and they mentioned his wife. He said: So he went to Ali - and made him swear by God: What did you mean by that? - meaning the oath. He said: So he returned her to him. - Ali bin Abdul A'la told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ash'ath bin Suwar, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Atiyah bin Abi Atiyah, he said: My brother died and left behind an orphan who was a breastfed child, and I was a poor man, and I did not have what I could to breastfeed him. He said: My wife, who had a son from her whom she breastfed, said to me: If you take care of yourself for me, I will take care of them for you! I said: How can I take care of myself for you? She said: Do not come near me. I said: By God, I will not come near you until you wean them. He said: So I weaned them and they went out to the people, and they said: We see that you have taken good care of them! He said: So I told them the story, and they said: We see that you have sworn an oath against her and she has separated from you! He said: So I came to Ali and told him the story, and he said: The only thing that is meant by ila’ is ila’.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr al-Barsani told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Jabir ibn Surat Al-Baqarah 2:
m: 226 For those who swear off their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. But if they return, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Zayd, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: There is no ila’ except in anger.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: There is no ila’ except in anger.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Rahman told us, he said, Abu Wakee’ told us, on the authority of Abu Fazarah, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Asamm, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: There is no ila’ except in anger.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Abu Atiyyah, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: There is no ila’ except in anger.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul A'la told us, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Qatada, that Ali said:
m: If a man says to his wife while she is breastfeeding: By God, I will not come near you until you wean my child, meaning by that the good of his child, he said: There is no ila' on him.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ishaq bin Mansur Al-Saluli told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Muslim Al-Ta'ifi, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Sa'id bin Jubayr, he said:
m: A man came to Ali and said: I said to my wife that I would not come near her for two years. He said: I have sworn an oath against her. He said: I only said it because she is breastfeeding! He said: Then no. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Ja'far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Abi Atiyah, on the authority of Ali that he used to say: The ila' is what is done in anger, in which a man says: By God, I will not come near you, by God, I will not hold you! But what is done to improve matters of breastfeeding or otherwise, then it is not ila' and there is no separation from it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us
m: - meaning Ibn Mahdi - he said, Hammad ibn Zaid told us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of al-Hasan: that he was asked about it and he said: No, by God, it is not ila’.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Bishr ibn Mansur told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’
m: who said: If he swears for the sake of breastfeeding, then it is not ila’.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Shihab about a man who says: By God, I will not approach my wife until my child is weaned! He said: I do not know of ila’ except by swearing by God, in what a man wants to harm his wife by avoiding her, and we do not know of the obligation of ila’ except for those, so we do not think that this one who swore to avoid his wife until his child is weaned swore except for a matter in which he seeks good, so we do not see that what is obligatory for this is what is obligatory for the one who turns away in anger.

x: Others said: It is the same if a man swears to his wife that he will not have intercourse with her in her vagina, whether he swears in anger or not, all of that is an oath.

Those who said that: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim - about a man who said to his wife: If I have intercourse with you until you wean your child, then you are divorced, so he left her for four months. He said: It is ila'.

c: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abdul A'la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Abu Ma'shar, on the authority of Al-Nakha'i, he said:
