m: Everything that prevents him from having intercourse with her, and he leaves her until four months have passed, then it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban ibn Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Abu 'Awana told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Al-Qa'qa'
m: who said: I asked Al-Hasan about a man whose wife was breastfeeding a boy, so he swore that he would not have intercourse with her until she weaned her child, so he said: I do not see this as anger, but rather ila' is in anger. He said: Ibn Sirin said: I do not know what this is that they are talking about?! God said: For those who swear not to have sexual intercourse to God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing when four months have passed, then let him propose to her if he desires her.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim -
m: regarding a man who swore not to speak to his wife - he said: They used to consider ila’ to mean sexual intercourse.

c: Abu al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Every oath that prevents sexual intercourse until four months have passed is ila’.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Ismail and Ash’ath, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: Every oath It prevents sexual intercourse, so it is an oath.

x: Others said: Every oath that a man swears to harm his wife is an oath from him to her, whether he swears to have sexual intercourse or otherwise, whether he swears with pleasure or displeasure.

Those who said that mentioned: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abd al-Razzaq narrated, Muammar narrated, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: Every oath that comes between a man and his wife is an ila’, if he says: By God, I will make you angry, by God, I will make you miserable, by God, I will beat you, and things like this. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin al-Hakam narrated, he said: My father and Shu’ayb narrated, on the authority of al-Layth, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b al-Amiri: That a man from his family said to his wife: If I speak to you for a year, then I am divorced. He consulted al-Qasim and Salim, and they said: If I speak to her before a year, then I am divorced, and if I do not speak to her, then I am divorced if four months have passed. Muhammad bin Bashar narrated, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated, he said: Sufyan narrated, he said: I heard Hammad say: I said to Ibrahim: Is an oath to swear that he will not have intercourse with her, or speak to her, or touch her head, or to make her angry, or to forbid her, or not to make her miserable?
He said: Yes.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us
m: He said, Shu'bah told us: I asked Al-Hakam about a man who said to his wife: By God, I will annoy you! So he left her for four months. He said: It is ila'.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told us,
m: he heard Shu'bah say: I asked Al-Hakam, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told us, he said,
m: Ibn Shihab said, Sa'id bin Al-Musayyab told me: If a man swears that he will not speak to his wife for a day or a month, he said: Then we think that is ila'. He said: Unless he swore that he would not speak to her, but he then touched her, we do not think that is ila'. Al-Fi' is when he returns to his wife and speaks to her or touches her. Whoever does that before the four months have passed, has fulfilled his vow. Whoever returns after four months while she is in her waiting period, has fulfilled his vow and owns his wife, but she has been divorced once.

x: The reason for those who say that ilaʿ is only in case of anger or harm is that God, the Most High, made the period set for ilaʿ as a way out for the woman from the man’s oppression and harm towards her, in what she has of good companionship and good treatment. If the man is not oppressing her or harming her by his oath and vow to refrain from intercourse with her, but rather he is seeking her satisfaction and fulfilling her need thereby, then he is not turning away by his oath. Because there is no meaning to the woman’s right to him from her husband’s mistreatment and bad treatment, so the period that was set for the ilaʿ is a way out for her from it. As for the reason for those who say that ilaʿ in case of anger or satisfaction is the same, it is the generality of the verse, and that God, the Most High, did not specify in His statement,
h
For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives
, a waiting period of four months, some without others, but rather He made it general for every imaan and one who swears.

So every one who swears to his wife not to have sexual relations with her for a period that is longer than the period that God has set for him to wait, then he turns away from his wife according to some of them. And according to some of them: He is a guardian, even if the duration of his oath is the period that he was given to wait for. As for the reason of those who said what Al-Sha’bi, Al-Qasim and Salim said: That God, the Most High, mentioned that the period that He set for the guardian is a way out for the woman from her husband’s bad treatment of her and his harm to her. And the oath against her that he will not have intercourse with her or approach her is not more likely to be from the meanings of bad treatment and harm than the oath against her that he will not speak to her or harm her or anger her. Because all of that is harm to her and bad treatment of her.

The most correct of the interpretations that we mentioned in that is the saying of those who said: Every oath that prevents the swearer from intercourse for more than the period that God has given the guardian to wait for, saying whether that was in anger or pleasure. And that is for the reason that we mentioned before for those who say that. We have already discussed the corruption of the statement of those who disagreed with that in our book: Kitab al-Latif, which is sufficient, so we disliked repeating it in this place.

God Almighty means by that: If they return to abandoning what they swore to do with them, such as abandoning intercourse with them, and they have intercourse with them and break their oaths, then God is Forgiving for what they lied about in their oaths not to have intercourse with them, then they have had intercourse with them, and for what they have done to them in advance, of swearing to what they should not have sworn to, so they swore to it, Merciful to them and to other believing servants of God. The root of faʿ is to return from one state to another, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them” until His saying: until it returns to the command of God (al-Hujurat 49:9), meaning: until it returns to the command of God.

i: From this is the saying of the poet:
x: It came and did not fulfill what it came for, and there are human needs that cannot be fulfilled.

It is said: Fa'a so-and-so yaf'i'ah - like jah and fa'a. And fa'a al-mara. As for in the shade, it is said: Fa'a al-zul yaf'i'u fay'an wafyan. It may also be said: fay'an in the first meaning, because fa' in all things means returning. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that, except that they differed about what makes the one who turns back fa'i'.
Some of them said: It does not become fa'i' except through intercourse.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told us, he said, Mu'ammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Fa'i' is intercourse.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Na'im told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ziyad bin Abi al-Ja'd, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Fa'i' is intercourse.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja'far told us, he said, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of a companion of his, on the authority of al-Hakam bin Utaybah, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, he said:
m: The spoils of war are sexual intercourse.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq,
m: similarly.

c: Abdul Hamid bin Bayan narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Yazid narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail, he said:
m: Aamer did not consider al-Fay’ to be anything other than sexual intercourse.

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated to us, he said: Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, he said: Ismail narrated to us, on the authority of Aah,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar narrated to us, he said: Abdul Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: Al-Fay’ is sexual intercourse.

c: Abu Abdullah Al-Nasha’i narrated to us, he said: Ishaq Al-Azraq narrated to us, on the authority of Samyan, on the authority of Ali bin Badhima, on the authority of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:
m: 226 For those who swear off their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. But if they return, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Saeed bin Jubair, similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: Al-Fay’ is sexual intercourse, he has no excuse except to have sexual intercourse, even if he is in prison or traveling - Saeed Al-Qa’il.

c: Muhammad bin Yahya narrated to me, he said: Abdul A’la narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, that he said:
m: He has no excuse until he has intercourse.

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Hammad and Iyas, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi - one of them
m: said: on the authority of Masruq - he said: Al-Fay’ is sexual intercourse - and the other said on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: Al-Fay’ is sexual intercourse.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul A'la told us, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab -
m: regarding a man who swore an oath to divorce his wife, then became preoccupied with illness - he said: He has no excuse until he has intercourse.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Mu'adh ibn Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr -
m: regarding a man who swore an oath to divorce his wife before or after consummating the marriage, and something happens to him that prevents him, or he does not find anything to do: that if four months have passed, she has more right to herself.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam and al-Sha'bi, they said:
m: If a man divorces his wife, then he wants to return to her, there is no return except intercourse.

x: Others said: Return is the return by the tongue or the heart in a case of an excuse, and in a case other than an excuse, intercourse.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan and Ikrimah, that they said:
m: If he has an excuse, then he has a witness, then that is for him, meaning in the case of a man who swore an oath from his wife and was distracted by illness or a road, he has a witness to return to his wife. Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated, ‘Abd al-A’la narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of a companion of his, on the authority of al-Hakam, who said: “An-Nakha’i and I discussed that matter, and An-Nakha’i said: ‘If he has an excuse, then call him to witness, for he has fulfilled his obligation.’ I said: ‘He has no excuse until he has intercourse.’ So we went to Abu Wa’il, who said: ‘I hope that if he has an excuse, then call him to witness, it is permissible.’ Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated, ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated, Mu’ammar narrated, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: ‘If he swears an oath, then becomes ill or imprisoned or travels and returns to her, then he has an excuse not to have intercourse.’ I heard al-Zuhri say something similar.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim -
m: regarding the woman who has given birth and her husband taking her back - he said: This is in Muharrib, the companions of Abdullah were asked about it and they said: If he is unable to do so, he should atone for his oath and have witnesses to the spoils of war.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiya told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Al-Sha’tha’
m: who said: A guest came to him and he swore an oath to have intercourse with his wife and she gave birth, so he wanted to take intercourse but he was unable to approach her because of her childbirth, so he came to Alqamah and mentioned that to him, so he said: Have you not returned in your heart and are you satisfied? He said: Yes! He said: Then you have returned! She is your wife! Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abdul-Razzaq narrated, Muammar narrated, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim: A man swore an oath not to have intercourse with his wife and she gave birth before four months had passed. He wanted to have intercourse with her but could not because of the blood until four months had passed. So he asked Alqamah bin Qais about her and said: Did you not take her back in your heart? He said: Yes! He said: She is your wife. Imran bin Musa narrated, Abdul-Warith narrated, Aamer narrated, on the authority of Al-Hasan: If a man has intercourse with his wife and is not able to have intercourse with her due to an excuse, he said: He bears witness that he has taken intercourse with her and she is his wife. Imran narrated, Abdul-Warith narrated, Aamer narrated, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muadh ibn Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: And Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: If a man swears an oath to be divorced from his wife and then tries hard to have intercourse with her but is unable to, then he may have witnesses to take her back.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of al-Hasan and Ikrimah:
m: That they were asked about a man who had an oath to be divorced from his wife, and something distracted him, so he had witnesses to take his wife back. They said: If he has an excuse, then that is his right. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, Ghundar narrated, Shu'bah narrated, on the authority of al-Hakam, who said: Ibraaheem and I went to Abu al-Sha'tha', and it was narrated that a man from Banu Sa'd ibn Hammam had sworn an oath to have intercourse with his wife, and she gave birth, but he was unable to approach her. So he asked al-Aswad - or one of the companions of 'Abdullah - and he said: If he has a witness, then she is his wife. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated, Ghundar narrated, Shu'bah narrated, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said: If he has an excuse, then he has a witness, and that is his - meaning the one who has an oath from his wife. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated, Shu'bah narrated, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he used to narrate on the authority of Abu al-Sha'tha', on the authority of Alqamah and the companions of 'Abdullah, that they said - regarding a man who swore an oath to have intercourse with his wife, and she gave birth - they said: If he has a witness, then she is his wife. Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated from Mughirah from Hammad, who said: If a man swears to have intercourse with his wife and then returns, let him bear witness to his spoils. If a man swears to have intercourse with his wife while he is in a land other than the land in which his wife is, let him bear witness to his spoils. If he bears witness and does not know that this does not count as his intercourse with her, and four months pass before he has intercourse with her, then she is his wife. If he knows that there is no spoils except in intercourse in this case, then he returns and let him bear witness to his spoils and he does not have intercourse with her until four months have passed, then she is separated from him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, he said,
m: Ibn Shihab said, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me: If a man swears an oath not to have intercourse with his wife, he said: If he is sick and is unable to touch her, or he is traveling and is detained, he said: If he returns and expiates his oath, then he has witnesses to his return before four months have passed, then we do not see it except that it is permissible for him to keep his wife, and nothing of her divorce has been lost. He said, and Ibn Shihab said - about a man who swears an oath not to have intercourse with his wife, and he has nothing left for her except one divorce, and he wants to return at the end of that while he is sick or traveling, or she is sick or menstruating or absent and he is unable to reach her, until four months have passed - is there a dispensation for him in any of that, to expiate his oath while he is unable to have intercourse with his wife? He said: We see, and God knows best, that if he returns before the four months, then she is his wife, after he bears witness to that and expiates for his oath. If that does not reach her from his return, then he has returned before it is a divorce. I narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, who said:
m: The return is intercourse. If he is not able to have intercourse and he is sick or absent or is in a state of ihram or something for which he has an excuse, then he returns with his tongue and bears witness to his consent, then that is a return for him, God willing.

x: Others said: The return is the return with the tongue in all cases.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ad-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur and Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The spoils of war are to be given with one’s tongue.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ziyad al-A’lam, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: The spoils of war are to bear witness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told me, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ziyad al-A’lam, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah
m: said: If he has fulfilled his vow, it is sufficient for him. He says: He has fulfilled his vow.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Ismaʿil ibn Rajaʿ
m: who said: They mentioned the oath of ilaʿ in the presence of Ibrahim, so he said: What if his penis does not ejaculate? If he testifies, then she is his wife.

x: The different scholars differed in the interpretation of the oath of ilaʿ in proportion to their difference in the meaning of the oath that constitutes ilaʿ. So whoever said: A man cannot be imaʿ from his wife, the oath that God mentioned in His Book, except by swearing to her that he will not have intercourse with her, made the ilaʿ to return to doing what he swore not to do of intercourse with her, and that is intercourse in the vagina if he is able to do that and is able to do so. And if he is not able to do that and is not able to do so, then he creates the intention to do it if he is able to do it and is able to do so, and expresses what he intended of that with his tongue so that the Muslims know, according to the opinion of whoever said that. As for the statement of the one who saw that the spoils are sexual intercourse and nothing else, he did not make the obstacle an excuse for him, nor did he give him a way out of his oath other than returning to what he swore to leave, which is sexual intercourse.

As for the one who said that he may have turned away from her by swearing to stop talking to her, or to upset her or anger her or something similar from the oaths, then the spoils according to him are returning to leaving what he swore to do - which would upset her - by intending to go back on it, and expressing that with his tongue, in every situation in which he intended to spoils.

The most correct statement in that according to us is the statement of the one who said: The spoils are sexual intercourse, because a man does not turn away from his wife according to us except by swearing to stop having sexual intercourse with her for the period we mentioned, for the reasons we described before. So if that is the oath, then the spoils that nullifies the ruling of the oath from him, there is no doubt that it is not permissible for it to be anything other than what the one who swore to do contrary to it. Because when he made his ruling, if he did not return to what he had vowed to leave, the ruling that God explained to them in His Book, then the return was to that, and it is known that he did what he had vowed to leave if he was able to do it, and that is intercourse. However, if he was prevented from returning - which is intercourse - by an excuse, then it is not permissible for him to be abandoning intercourse with her in reality.

Because a person only abandons what he has a way to do and leave. As for the one who has no way to do something, then he is not going to be abandoning it. Since that is the case, then making the determination in himself to have intercourse with her is sufficient for him in the case of an excuse, until he finds the way to have intercourse with her. And if he expressed that with his tongue and testified against himself in that case to return and return, that would be more pleasing to me.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: The meaning of this is: Then God Surat Al-Baqarah 2:226 For those who swear off their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. But if they return, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. is Forgiving to you regarding what you have committed by returning to them, of breaking the oath that you swore to them by God not to deceive them, Merciful to you in lightening for you the expiation for the oaths that you swore to them, then you broke it.

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul A’la told us, he said, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, Then if they return, then God is Forgiving and Merciful he said: There is no expiation upon him.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: If he returns, then there is no expiation upon him.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Habban ibn Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: They used to see in the statement of God: Then if they return, then God is Forgiving and Merciful that his expiation was his returning.

x: This interpretation that we mentioned is the interpretation that is required according to the opinion of those who claim that every person who breaks an oath is in trouble in the situation, so there is no expiation for his breaking it, and that its expiation is breaking it. As for the opinion of those who obligated the perjurer in every oath he swore [to atone], whether the oath was broken or not, then its interpretation is: Then God is Forgiving for those who swear to have intercourse with their wives in what they broke in their oaths, by returning and atonement for their oaths, with what God obligated those who break their oaths in terms of atonement, Merciful to them, by dropping the punishment for that in the immediate and the future, by atonement for it with what He imposed on them of punishment and atonement, and with what He made for them of the four months of grace, so He did not make for the woman from whom her husband swore what He made for her after the four months, as: - Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Yahya bin Bishr told us, that he heard Ikrimah say: “For those who swear to have intercourse with their wives, a waiting period of four months.

But if they return, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And if they decide on divorce” - he said: And that is the mercy of God! He gave him control over her for the four months except for one who has an excuse. Because God said:
And those on whose part you fear desertion, admonish them and forsake them in bed
Some of those who said: If the master returns, he must make expiation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives

, a waiting period of four months means a man swears to his wife by God that he will not marry her, so he waits four months, and if he marries her, he expiates his oath by feeding ten poor people or clothing them or freeing a slave. Whoever cannot find that, then he must fast for three days.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Shihab told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, saying, Habban bin Musa told us, saying, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, saying, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: saying: If he swears an oath and has intercourse with her before the four months have passed, he must atone for his oath.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, saying, Habban told us, saying, Ibn Abi Al-Mubarak told us, saying, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim -
m: regarding the woman in childbirth whose husband takes her back - he said: This is in Muharrib, the companions of Abdullah were asked about it, and they said: If he is unable to do so, he must atone for his oath and have witnesses to the spoils.

c: Bishr told us, saying, Yazid told us, saying, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: saying: If he takes her back, he must atone for his oath, and she is his wife. I narrated from Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, similarly.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, saying, Uthman told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding the oath, he said: He must stop before the four months have passed, and if he takes her back, she is his wife, and he must swear an oath: he must atone for it if he breaks his oath.

x: This second interpretation is the correct one in our view, because we have explained the reasons in our book. The Book of Oaths, that breaking an oath requires expiation in every oath in which breaking an oath begins after swearing, whether it is an oath of disobedience or an oath of obedience.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the statement of God the Most High:
h
And if they decide on divorce
Some of them said: The meaning of that is: For those who swear to keep away from their wives, there is
h
a waiting period of four months

. If they return and return to what God has made obligatory for them of treating them kindly during the four months that God has made obligatory for them to wait from them and to intercourse with them, and to treat them in that as is obligatory, then God is Forgiving and Merciful to them. And if they abandon the return to them during the four months that God has made obligatory for them to wait until they complete, then their wives from whom they swore are divorced by their continuing. And their continuing, according to those who say that, is evidence of the master's intention to divorce his wife from whom he swore. Then the interpreters of this interpretation differed among themselves about the divorce that applies to her after the lapse of the four months.
Some of them said: It is an irrevocable divorce.

Those who said that: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Muhammad bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Khalas or Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ali, he said: If four months have passed, then it is an irrevocable divorce.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Ali and Ibn Masoud used to consider it as a divorce, if four months have passed then she has more right to herself. Qatada said: The statement of Ali and Abdullah about the oath of abstention is more pleasing to me.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul A’la told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Ali said
m: about the oath of abstention: If four months have passed then she is irrevocably divorced by one divorce.

c: Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Abu Salamah:
m: Uthman bin Affan and Zaid bin Thabit used to say: If four months have passed, then it is an irrevocable divorce.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, he said: Ata Al-Khurasani narrated to us, he said:
m: Abu Salamah bin Abdul-Rahman heard me asking Ibn Al-Musayyab about Al-Ila’, so I passed by him and he said: What did Ibn Al-Musayyab say to you?

c: So I narrated to him
m: what he said, and he said: Shall I not tell you what Uthman bin Affan and Zaid bin Thabit used to say? I said: Yes! He said: They used to say: If four months have passed, then it is one, and she has more right to herself.

c: Ali bin Sahl narrated to us, he said: Al-Walid narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani, he said: Abu Salamah bin Abdul-Rahman narrated to us: Uthman bin Affan said:
m: If four months have passed from the day he swore an oath, then it is an irrevocable divorce.

c: Ya’qub narrated to me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, or I narrated to him, on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani,
m: On the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Uthman and Zaid: They used to say: If four months have passed, then it is a final divorce.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, he said:
m: Abdullah bin Unays swore an oath to divorce his wife, and she remained for six months. Then Ibn Masoud came to him and asked him, and he said: Inform her that she has taken control of her affairs. So he went to her and informed her, and gave her a dowry of a pound of silver.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: that he used to say about the oath: If four months have passed, then it is an irrevocable divorce.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Abu al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Abdullah bin Unays swore an oath to divorce his wife. He went out and was absent from her for six months, then he came and entered upon her, and it was said: She has been divorced from you! So he went to Abdullah and mentioned that to him, and Abdullah said to him: She has been divorced from you, so go to her and inform her and propose to her.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, on the authority of Ata’, who said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamir, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud
m: that he said, regarding ila’: If four months have passed, then it is one irrevocable divorce.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-A’la told me,
m: who said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamir: A man from Banu Hilal, whose name was so-and-so ibn Unays, or Abdullah ibn Unays, wanted from his wife what a man wants from his wife, but she refused, so he swore that he would not go near her. Then he sent a messenger to the people the next day, so he went out and was absent for six months, then he came back and did what he thought was wrong with his wife!

c: So he went out to the people and told them
m: about his displeasure with his wife when he went out, and his satisfaction with them when he came back. The people said: She has become forbidden to you! So he went to Ibn Mas’ud and asked him about that, and Ibn Mas’ud said: Didn’t you know that she has become forbidden to you? He said: No! He said: Go and ask permission to see her, for she will deny it. Then tell her that the oath you swore has become a divorce, and tell her that it is only one, and that she is the one who has control over herself. If she wishes, you may propose to her, and she will be with you for two days, otherwise she is the one who has control over herself.
b.via: So he went out to the people and

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: Regarding ila’, if four months have passed, it is an irrevocable divorce, and she must observe the waiting period of three menstrual periods.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur,
m: Al-A’mash, and Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim: That Abdullah ibn Unais swore an oath against his wife, and four months passed, then he had intercourse with her while he was forgetful. He came to Alqamah, and he went with him to Abdullah, and Abdullah said: She is divorced from you, so propose to her for herself. He gave her a dowry of a pound of silver.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah:
m: that Nu’man ibn Bashir swore an oath to divorce his wife, so Ibn Mas’ud struck his thigh and said: When four months have passed, then acknowledge the divorce.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, al-Mu’tamir told us, he said,
m: I heard Dawud, on the authority of Aamir: that Ibn Mas’ud said about the freed slave: If four months have passed and he has not returned, then his wife has been separated from him by one divorce, and he is a suitor.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The intention to divorce is the expiration of the four months.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abu Najih, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: said about ila’: If four months have passed, then it is one irrevocable divorce.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Khalid bin Mukhallad told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Burqan, on the authority of Abdul A’la bin Maimun bin Mihran, on the authority of Ikrimah, that he said:
m: If four months have passed, then it is one irrevocable divorce. He mentioned that on the authority of Ibn Abbas.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Nu’aym told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ziyad bin Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The determination of divorce is the expiration of the four.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, he said, al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr:
m: The Emir of Mecca asked him about the mawla, so he said: Ibn Umar used to say: If four months have passed, then she has control over her affairs, and Ibn Abbas used to say the same.

c: Abu Hisham told us: Hafs told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: If four months have passed, then it is an irrevocable divorce.

c: Abu Hisham told us: Hafs told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Salim Al-Makki, on the authority of Ibn Al-Hanafiyyah,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: My father and Shuaib told us, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Abaan bin Salih, on the authority of Ibn Shihab: Qubaysah bin Dhu’aib said
m: about the oath: It is an irrevocable divorce, and she should complete her waiting period, and she has more control over her own affairs.

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Shuraih:
m: A man came to him and said: I swore an oath from my wife, and four months have passed before I could return to her husband? Shuraih said: But if they decide on divorce - then indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. He did not say more than that. So he came to Masruq and mentioned that to him, and he said: May God have mercy on Abu Umayyah, if we had said what he said, no one would have released him! He only came to him to release him! Then he said: It is an irrevocable divorce, and you are one of the suitors.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah:
m: that he heard Al-Shaʿbi narrating: that he witnessed Shuraih - and a man asked him about Ila’ - and he said:
h
For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives
h
a waiting period of four months

(al-Anʿam 2:14). He said: So I got up from him and went to Masruq and said: O Abu ʿAishah, and I told him what Shuraih had said, and he said: May God have mercy on Abu Umayyah, if all the people said the same, who would release someone like this! Then he said: If four months pass, then it is one irrevocable divorce.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, he said:
m: I read in the book of Abu Qilabah with Ayoub: I asked Salim bin Abdullah and Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, and they said: If four months pass, then it is one irrevocable divorce.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: If four months pass, then it is one irrevocable divorce, and he may propose to her during the waiting period.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father -
m: regarding a man who says to his wife: By God, nothing will ever come between my head and yours! And he swears that he will never come near her, and if four months pass and he does not return, then it is one irrevocable divorce, and he is a suitor - the statement of Ali, Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, Abd al-A'la narrated, Sa'id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan: He was asked about a man who said to his wife: If I come near you, then you are divorced three times. He said: Then if four months pass, then it is an irrevocable divorce, and that is dropped. Suwar narrated, he said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, and Abu Hisham Surat Al-Baqarah 2:227
h
And if they decide on divorce

, then indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. narrated, he said: Waki' narrated, both of them, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim, he said: I heard al-Hasan and Muhammad say regarding ila': If four months pass, then she is separated from him with an irrevocable divorce, and he is a suitor among the suitors. Ya'qub narrated, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: We used to talk about ila' that if four months pass, then it is an irrevocable divorce. Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Uthman narrated, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim regarding ila': He said: If four months pass, then she is separated from him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Dawud told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Nakha’i, who said:
m: If he approaches her before the four months, she is separated from him by three things. If he leaves her until the four months have passed, she is separated from him by ila’, in the case of a man who said to his wife: You are divorced three times if I approach you for a year.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Muadh ibn Hisham told us, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad stayed at Hind’s house one night with Umm Uthman, the daughter of Umar ibn Ubaydullah. When he came to her, she ordered her maids to close the doors on him, so he swore that he would not come to her until she came to him. So it was said to him: If four months pass, she is gone from you.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Aouf told us, he said:
m: It has reached me that if a man swears to divorce his wife and four months have passed, then it is a final divorce, and he may propose to her if he wishes.

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
For those who swear to divorce their wives
, there is
h
a waiting period of four months

- in what he swears, and if the four months have passed, then she is forbidden to him, so she observes the waiting period of the divorced woman, and he is one of the suitors. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abd al-Razzaq narrated, Muammar narrated, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb, who said: If four months have passed, then it is an irrevocable divorce. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: “
h
For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives
h
a waiting period of four months
is required.
h
But if they return

, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” This is about a man who swears not to have sexual relations with his wife and says: By God, my head and your head will never meet, and I will never come near you or have intercourse with you! The people of the Jahiliyyah used to consider it a divorce, so God set a limit for them of four months. If he returns, then it is as if he has sworn to her, and she is his wife. If four months have passed and he has not returned, then it is an irrevocable divorce, and she has more right to herself, and this is one of the speeches.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly.

c: Musa narrated to me,
m: who said: Amr narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
h
For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives
h
a waiting period of four months
. He said: Ibn Masʿud and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab used to say: If four months have passed, she is considered to be irrevocably divorced, and she has more right to herself.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Wahb told us, on the authority of Jubayr, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: For those who swear the verse, he is the one who swears not to approach his wife, and if four months pass and he does not return and does not divorce her, she is separated from him by the oath. If she returns to him, then a new dowry, and a marriage with proof, and the consent of the guardian.

x: Others said: Rather, what is due to her after the passage of four months is a divorce, in which the husband has the right to take her back.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Malik told us, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Abu Bakr bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham, they said:
m: If a man swears to be away from his wife and four months pass, then one, and he has the right to take her back.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab He
m: said: If four months have passed, it is a divorce, and he has the right to take her back.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Umayya, on the authority of Makhul, he said:
m: If four months have passed, it is a divorce, and he has the right to take her back.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman, he said:
m: It is one, and he has more right to her, meaning: If the four months have passed, and Al-Zuhri used to issue fatwas based on what Abu Bakr said.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told us, he said, Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Shihab told me, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me that he said:
m: If a man swears to divorce his wife and the four months have passed before he returns, it is a divorce, and he has more right to her as long as she is in her waiting period.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, he said, Abu Yunus Al-Qawi told us, he said:
m: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said to me: Who are you? I said: From the people of Iraq! He said: Perhaps you are one of those who say: If four months have passed, then she is divorced! No! Even if four years have passed.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told us, Hajjaj ibn Rushdin told us, Abdul-Jabbar ibn Umar told us, on the authority of Rabia that he said
m: about ila’: If four months have passed, then it is a divorce, and she begins her waiting period, and her husband has more right to take her back.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Idris told us,
m: Ibn Shabramah used to say: If four months have passed, then he has the right to take her back, and he argued based on the Qur’an, and interpreted this verse: And their husbands have more right to take them back in that period
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:228)
, then he took it out: “For those who swear off their wives is
h
a waiting period of four months
h
But if they return
, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
h
And if they decide on divorce
, then indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.”

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Abu Omar said:
m: And we are in that, meaning in the oath, according to the saying of our companions Al-Zuhri and Makhul: that it is a divorce - meaning: the passage of the four months - and he has more control over her during her waiting period.

x: Others said: The meaning of his statement: For those who swear off their wives to his statement: For God is Hearing and Knowing is For those who swear off to abstain from their wives, she waits four months according to his command and her command, And if they return after the four months have passed to them, and return to their companionship with them in kindness, and stop deserting them, and come to have sexual intercourse with them, “then God is Forgiving and Merciful. *
h
And if they decide on divorce

” and initiate divorce for them after the four months, then God is Hearing of their divorcing them, Knowing of what they did to them of good and evil. Those who interpreted this interpretation said: The passing of the four months obliges the woman to demand from her husband who has abstained from her, whether to return or to divorce him. And the ruler must inform the husband of that, and if he returns or divorces, otherwise the ruler divorces him.

Who said that: Ali bin Sahl told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Al-Muthanna bin Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: that Umar said about the oath: There is nothing on him until he stops, divorces or keeps.

c: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Shabawayh told me, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Yahya bin Ayoub told us, on the authority of Al-Muthanna, on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Ghundar told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak, who said:
m: I heard Saeed bin Jubair narrating, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab: that he said about the oath: If four months have passed, he does not give him anything.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Amr bin Salamah, on the authority of Ali:
m: that he used to stop the mawla after four months until he returned or divorced.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Amr ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ali, he said,
m: regarding Al-Ila’: He is to be stopped.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Bakir ibn Al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Ali:
m: He used to stop him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Bakir ibn Al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Ami:
m: He used to stop him.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Marwan ibn Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: The mawla is to be stopped after the expiry of the four months until he returns or is divorced. Abu Kurayb said, Ibn Idris said: This is the opinion of the people of Madinah.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Marwan, on the authority of Ali,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Asim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Marwan bin Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ali, who said:
m: The one who has a free will either return to his wife or divorce her.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Mis’ar, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Tawus:
m: Uthman used to stop the one who has a free will, according to the opinion of the people of Madinah.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, he said: Abu Nu’aym told us, he said: Mis’ar told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, he said:
m: I met Tawus and asked him, and he said: Uthman used to follow the opinion of the people of Madinah.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-Samad told us, he said: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, who said:
m: There is no time limit for him, and it is a sin. He is stopped in the oath, so he either keeps her or divorces her.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: that Abu Al-Darda said
m: about Al-Ila: If four months have passed, then he is to be stopped: either he returns or he divorces her.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab:
m: that Abu Al-Darda used to say: It is a sin, and his wife is not forbidden to him after four months, and he should make her waiting period after four months.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul A’la told us, he said
Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: that Abu Al-Darda and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: He is to be stopped when the four months have passed, and either he returns or he divorces her. And he continues to persist in disobedience until he returns or is divorced. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Qatada: Abu al-Darda and Aisha said: The client is stopped after the four months have passed, so he either returns or is divorced. Ibn Bashar narrated, he said: Abd al-A’la narrated, he said: Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu al-Darda and Saeed bin al-Musayyab, similarly. Abu Kurayb narrated, he said: Ibn Idris narrated, he said: Al-Hasan narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, he said: Aisha said: He is stopped after the four months have passed, so he either returns or is divorced. He said: I said: Did you hear it? He said: Do not rebuke me. Abu Muslim Ibrahim bin Abdullah narrated, he said: Imran bin Maysarah narrated, he said: Ibn Idris narrated, he said: Hasan bin al-Furat narrated, on the authority of Aisha, similarly.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Jabbar bin Al-Ward narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha,
m: similarly.

c: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said:
m: Ubaidullah bin Umar Surat Al-Baqarah 2:227
h
And if they decide on divorce

, then indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. narrated to me, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that she said: If a man swears not to touch his wife, and four months pass, then he can either keep her as God has commanded him, or divorce her, and what he has done does not require a divorce or anything else.

c: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, he said:
m: Yunus bin Yazid, Najiyah bin Bakr, and Ibn Abi Al-Zinad informed me, on the authority of Abi Al-Zinad, he said: Al-Qasim bin Muhammad informed me: Khalid bin Al-Aas Al-Makhzumi had the daughter of Abu Saeed bin Hisham, and he used to swear about her many times that he would not come near her for a long time. He said: I heard Aisha say to him: Do you not fear God, O Ibn Al-Aas, regarding the daughter of Abu Saeed? Do you not feel embarrassed? Do you not recite this verse in Surat Al-Baqarah? He said: It is as if she considers him sinful, and does not see that he has left his family.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Yahya ibn Saʿid told us, on the authority of ʿUbayd God, on the authority of Nafiʿ, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, that he said
m: about the freed slave: Nothing is permissible for him except what God has made permissible: Either he returns, or he divorces. Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated, Abdullah bin Numayr narrated, Ubaydullah narrated, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, something similar. Abu Kurayb narrated, Ibn Idris narrated, Ubaydullah narrated, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: It is not permissible for the guardian not to do what God has commanded him, i.e., to make clear that she should be returned to him, or to divorce him after the expiry of the four months - to make clear that she should be returned to him or to divorce him. Abu Kurayb said: Ibn Idris said, and he added: And I took her back to him, so he said, a statement meaning: He has the right to take her back. Abu Kurayb narrated, Ibn Idris narrated, Shu’bah narrated, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr: Umar said something similar to what Ibn Umar said. Mujahid bin Musa narrated, Yazid bin Harun narrated, Jarir bin Hazim narrated, Nafi’ narrated, Ibn Umar said regarding ila’: It should be stopped at four months.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ubaydullah ibn Umar told me, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said:
m: If a man swears not to touch his wife, and four months pass, then he can either keep her as God has commanded him, or divorce her, and what he has done does not require a divorce or anything else from him.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Umar about ila’ and he said: The rulers rule accordingly.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: The master is to be stopped after the four months have passed, and he can either divorce her or return to her. Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Shabawayh narrated: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated: Yahya bin Ayoub narrated: Ubaidullah bin Umar narrated: Suhayl bin Abi Saleh narrated: his father said: I asked twelve men from the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife. All of them said: There is nothing wrong with him until four months have passed, then he should stop. If he returns, then fine. Otherwise, he should divorce. Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated: Abdul-Wahhab narrated: Dawud narrated: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab - regarding a man who divorces his wife - said: He did not think that separation should enter upon him until he divorced her. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna narrated: Ibn Abi Uday narrated: Dawud narrated: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab regarding the oath of divorce if four months have passed: God has only made it a time that it is not permissible for him to exceed until he returns or divorces her. If he exceeds that, then he has disobeyed God, and his wife is not forbidden to him.

c: Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, he said:
m: If four months have passed, then he must either return to her or divorce her.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashar narrated to us, they said: Abd al-A’la narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab,
m: regarding ila’: He is to be stopped at the end of the four months, then he must either return to her or divorce her.

c: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Umar, or I narrated to him from him, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, he said:
m: I asked Ibn al-Musayyab about ila’ and he said: He is to be stopped. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Ata al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, and on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, they said: The mawla is to be stopped after the expiry of the four days, and he either returns or divorces. Ali bin Sahl narrated, he said: Al-Walid bin Muslim narrated, he said: Malik bin Anas narrated, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab and Abu Bakr bin Abd al-Rahman bin al-Harith bin Hisham, something similar to that, meaning something similar to what Umar bin al-Khattab said about the oath of abstention: There is nothing upon him until he is stopped, and he divorces or keeps her. Muhammad bin al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Muhammad bin Jaʿfar narrated, he said: Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid: He said about the oath of abstention: He is to be stopped.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives
h
a waiting period of four months
, he said: If four months have passed, it is taken and he is held back until he takes his wife back or divorces her.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar:
m: that Marwan held him back after six months.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Abdul-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Umar bin Abdul-Aziz,
m: regarding the oath of abstention: It is stopped at four months, until he returns or divorces her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Abu Salih told us, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives
h
a waiting period of four months

refers to a man who swears to his wife by God that he will not marry her, so he waits four months, and if he marries her, he expiates for his oath. If four months pass before he marries her, the ruler forces him: either he returns and takes her back, or he resolves to divorce her, as God Almighty said. Musa bin Harun narrated, Amr bin Hammad narrated, Asbat narrated, on the authority of Al-Suddi: “
h
For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives
h
a waiting period of four months

. If they return [to their wives],” the verse. He said: Ali and Ibn Abbas used to say: If a man swears not to have sexual relations with his wife and the four months pass, he is stopped and asked: Have you kept her or divorced her? If he keeps her, she is his wife, and if he divorces her, she is divorced.

c: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
For those who swear not to have sexual relations with their wives
, he said: It is the man who swears that he will not have intercourse with his wife so-and-so, so God has set four months for him to wait. He said: God’s statement:
h
A waiting period of four months
, he waits, “
h
But if they return
[to their wives], then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
h
And if they decide on divorce

, then indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.” So if you bring it to the Imam, he sets a period of four months for him. If he returns [to his wife], otherwise he is divorced. If you do not bring it to the Imam, then it is her right and she leaves it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Malik, he said:
m: Divorce does not take place for the one who has been given a wali until he is stopped, and he is not considered a wali until he swears for more than four months. So if he swears for four months, then there is no ila’ on him, because he is stopped at the four months, and the oath is no longer required of him, so the ila’ is gone.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Ibn Zayd, he said, Ibn Umar said:
m: Until it is brought to the ruler, and my father used to say that, and he would say: No, by God, even if four years have passed, until he is given a wali.

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, he said, Abu Nu’aym told us, he said, Fitr told us, he said,
m: Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said, and I was with him: If a man swears an oath to divorce his wife for four years, we will not divorce her until we are together, so if he returns, he returns, and if he intends to divorce, he intends to.

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, he said, Abu Nu’aym told us, he said, Abdul Aziz al-Majshun told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn, he said,
m: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: He is given a wali after the four months have passed.

x: Others said: The ila’ is nothing.
Who said that: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, who said: I asked Ibn Al-Musayyab about Ila’ and he said: It is nothing.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Ja’far bin Burqan told me, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Umar about a man who swore an oath against his wife, and four months passed without him returning to her, so he recited this verse: For those who swear an oath against their wives,
h
a waiting period of four months
(al-Mawrid 2:10).

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Mis’ar told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, who said:
m: I sent to Ata’ to ask him about Ila’, and he said: I have no knowledge of it.

x: Others of this opinion said: Rather, the meaning of his statement:
h
And if they decide on divorce
is: And if they refuse to return, after the imam has stopped them regarding Ila’ or divorce.
Who said that: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, who said:

c: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: I stop Ila’ When the four days have passed, if he returns, he makes her his wife, and if he does not return, he makes it an irrevocable divorce.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The master is stopped when the four days have passed, and if he does not return, it is an irrevocable divorce.

x: The most similar of these statements to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the Book of God Almighty is the statement of Umar ibn Al-Khattab And Uthman and Ali, may God be pleased with them, and those who said what they said about divorce, that his statement: “
h
But if they return
, then indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful.
h
And if they decide on divorce

, then indeed God is Hearing and Knowing,” only means that if they return after the imam has stopped them after the expiration of the four months, and they return to fulfilling God’s right over them for their wives whom they had sworn off, then indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful to them.
h
And if they decide on divorce

, and they divorce them, then indeed God is Hearing, of their divorce if they divorce, Knowing of what they did to them. And we said that this is more similar to the interpretation of the verse, because God, the Most High, mentioned when He said:
h
And if they decide on divorce
, “then indeed God is Hearing and Knowing,” and it is known that the expiration of the four months is not heard, but rather it is known.

If the intention to divorce had been after the expiration of the four months, the verse would not have concluded with God mentioning the report that God Almighty is Hearing, Knowing. Just as He did not conclude the verse in which the return to His obedience was mentioned, in the guardian returning to his wife whom he had sworn to, and fulfilling her right to her, with mentioning the report that He is severe in punishment, since it was not a place of threat for disobedience. Rather, He concluded that with mentioning the report of His description of Himself Almighty as Forgiving, Most Merciful, since it was a place of promising the one who turns back to His obedience. Likewise, He concluded the verse in which the statement and the speech were mentioned, with His description of Himself, that He is Hearing of the speech and the action Knowing, so He Almighty said: And if those who swear to divorce their wives decide to divorce those of their wives from whom they have sworn, then indeed, God is Hearing of their divorcing them if they divorce them, Knowing of what they have done to them, of what is permissible for them and what is forbidden for them.
We have thoroughly explained the evidence for the validity of this statement in our book: The Book of Al-Latif Min Surat Al-Baqarah 2:227
h
And if they decide on divorce
, then indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. Al-Bayan An Ahkam Shara’i’ Al-Din, so we disliked repeating it in this place.

evidence.text: Do you not recite this verse in Surat Al-Baqarah?

Ahmad bin Hazim told us, Abu Naim told us, Ja’far bin Burqan told me, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran, who said: I asked Ibn Umar about a man who swore an oath against his wife, and four months passed without him returning to her, so he recited this verse: For those who swear an oath against their wives, a waiting period of four months (al-Mawrid 2:10).

x: God Almighty means: And the divorced women who were divorced after their husbands had consummated the marriage with them and had intercourse with them, if they are menstruating and pure - they shall wait concerning themselves, from marrying their husbands, three menstrual periods.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of the menstrual period that God meant by His saying: they shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods.
Some of them said: It is menstruation.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding God's saying:
h
And the divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods
, he said: Menstruation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi':
m: three menstrual periods, meaning three menstrual periods. He says: She waits for three menstrual periods.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj told us, Hammam bin Yahya told us,
m: I heard Qatada regarding the statement of God,
h
And divorced women shall wait

, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods, he said: He made the waiting period of divorced women three menstrual periods, then He abrogated from it the divorced woman who was divorced before her husband had consummated the marriage with her, and those who have despaired of menstruation, and those who have not menstruated, and the pregnant woman.

c: Ali bin Abdul A’la told us, he said: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: The menstrual periods are menstruation.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And divorced women shall wait
, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods, he said: Three menstrual periods.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Amr bin Dinar said:
m: The menstrual periods are menstruation, on the authority of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of a man
m: who heard Ikrimah say: The menstrual periods are menstruation, not purity. God the Almighty said: Then divorce them at their prescribed period (al-Talaq 65:1), and He did not say: for their menstrual periods.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And divorced women shall wait
, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods, he said: Three menstrual periods.

c: Musa told us, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of As-Suddi:
m: h
And divorced women shall wait
, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods. As for three menstrual periods, it means three menstrual periods.

c: Humayd bin Mas’adah told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Ibrahim An-Nakha’i:
m: That it was reported to ‘Umar, who said to ‘Abdullah bin Mas’ud: You must speak about it. He said: You are more entitled to speak! He said: You must speak. He said: I say: Her husband has more right to her as long as she has not performed ghusl after the third menstrual period. He said: That is my opinion, and it agrees with what I had in mind! So Umar ruled accordingly.

c: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul A’la narrated to us, he said: Sa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Al-Nakha’i, on the authority of Qatadah:
m: Umar ibn Al-Khattab said to Ibn Mas’ud, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul A’la narrated to us, he said: Sa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Al-Nakha’i:
m: Umar ibn Al-Khattab and Ibn Mas’ud said: Her husband has more right to her as long as she has not performed ghusl, or they said: It is permissible for her to pray.

c: Humayd ibn Mas’adah narrated to us, he said: Yazid ibn Zari’ narrated to us, he said: Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Arubah narrated to us, he said: Matar narrated to us, that Al-Hasan told them:
m: A man divorced his wife and delegated that to a man from his family, or: a person from his family, but the one who delegated that to him was negligent until his wife entered her third menstrual period and brought her water close to perform ghusl. The one who was assigned to do that went to the husband, and the husband came and she wanted to wash herself. He said: O so-and-so! She said: What do you want? He said: I have taken you back! She said: By God, you cannot do that! He said: Yes, by God! He said: They went up to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, and he took her oath by God, there is no god but Him: If you had washed yourself when he called you, she would have washed herself. She said: No, by God, I had not done so, and I had brought my water near so that I could wash myself. He returned her to her husband and said: You have more right to her as long as she has not washed herself after the third menstrual period.

c: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari,
m: in a similar manner.

c: Imran ibn Musa told us, he said: Abd al-Warith told us, he said: Yunus told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said: Umar said:
m: He has more right to her as long as she has not washed herself after the third menstrual period.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu al-Walid told us, he said: Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Jubayr:
m: That Umar ibn al-Khattab divorced his wife, and she wanted to wash herself after the third menstrual period, so Umar ibn al-Khattab said: My wife, by the Lord of the Kaaba! So he reviewed it. Ibn Bashar said: I mentioned this hadith to Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi and he said: I heard this hadith from Abu Hilal, on the authority of Qatadah, and Abu Hilal does not accept this.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, he said:
m: We were with Umar ibn al-Khattab when a woman came and said: My husband divorced me once or twice! He came and I had given birth, closed my door, and taken off my clothes! Umar said to Abdullah: What do you think? He said: I think she is his wife, and it is not permissible for her to pray. Umar said: And I see that.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja’far told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad:
m: that he said - about a man who divorced his wife and then left her until she entered her third menstrual period, and she wanted to wash herself, and she put down her water to wash herself, so he took her back -: Umar and Abdullah Ibn Mas’ud approved of it.

c: Muhammad Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad,
m: similarly, except that he said: And she put down the water to wash herself, so he took her back, so he asked Abdullah and Umar and they said: He has more right to her as long as she has not washed herself.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Umar and Abdullah used to say: If a man divorces his wife with a divorce in which he has the right to take her back, he has more right to her as long as she has not washed herself from her third menstrual period.

c: Ya’qub Ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: that Umar Ibn Al-Khattab was He said: If a man divorces his wife once or twice, he has more right to take her back, and there is inheritance between them, as long as she has not performed ghusl after the third menstrual period.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: That a man divorced his wife once or twice, then he delegated her to one of his family members, and the man was negligent until she entered her bathing place and was about to perform her ritual ablution, then his chamberlain came to him and said: Have I taken you back? She said: No, by God! He said: Yes, by God! She said: No, by God! He said: Yes, by God! He said: So they disagreed, and they went to Al-Ash'ari, and he made her swear by God: Have you performed ghusl and is it permissible for you to pray? She refused to swear, so he returned her to him. Mujahid bin Musa narrated, Yazid bin Harun narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Al-Nakha’i: ‘Umar consulted Ibn Mas’ud about a man who divorced his wife once or twice, and she menstruated for the third time. Ibn Mas’ud said: I think he has more right to her as long as she has not performed ghusl. ‘Umar said: I Surat Al-Baqarah 2:228
h
