And divorced women shall wait
, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods.
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

, if they believe in God and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back in that period, if they desire reconciliation. And women shall have rights similar to those against them, according to what is equitable. And men shall have rights over them. A degree, and God is Almighty, Wise. agree with what I had in mind! So he returned her to her husband. Humayd bin Mas’adah Qay narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, An-Nu’man bin Rashid narrated, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: ‘Ali used to say: He has more right to her as long as she has not performed ghusl for the third time. Muhammad bin Bashar narrated, on the authority of Abu Ahmad, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of ‘Amr bin Dinar, who said: I heard Saeed bin Jubair say: If the bleeding stops, there is no going back. Abu Al-Sa'ib narrated, Abu Mu'awiyah narrated, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: If a man divorces his wife while she is pure, she observes a waiting period of three menstrual cycles, in addition to the menstrual cycle from which she became pure. Muhammad bin Yahya narrated, on the authority of Abdul A'la, who narrated, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Matar, on the authority of Amr bin Shu'aib, that Umar asked Abu Musa about it - and he had heard of his ruling on it - and Abu Musa said: I ruled that her husband has more right to her as long as she has not performed ghusl. Umar said: If I had ruled otherwise, I would have given you a headache. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, on the authority of Abdul Razzaq, who narrated, on the authority of Mu'ammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa'id bin Al-Musayyab, who said: Ali bin Abi Talib said - regarding a man who marries a woman and then divorces her once or twice - he said: Her husband has the right to take her back until she performs ghusl from the third menstrual cycle and it becomes permissible for her to pray. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Zaid bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah, he said: Uthman sent to my father asking him about her, and my father said: How can a hypocrite issue a fatwa?! Uthman said: I seek refuge in God from you being a hypocrite, and we seek refuge in God from calling you a hypocrite, and we seek refuge in God from the evil of such a thing being in Islam, and then you die without making it clear! He said: Then I think that he has more right to her until she performs ghusl after the third menstrual period, and prayer becomes permissible for her. He said: I do not know of Uthman who did not follow that. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, he said: And Muammar narrated, on the authority of Qatadah, they said: A man took his wife back when she put on her clothes and wanted to perform ghusl, so he said: I have taken you back. She said: No! So she performed ghusl. Then he took her to Al-Ash’ari, and he returned her to him. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Zaid bin Rafi’, on the authority of Ma’bad al-Juhani, he said: If a divorced woman washes her vagina after the third menstrual period, she is separated from him and becomes permissible for other husbands. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, that Umar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: It is permissible for her husband to take her back until she washes herself after the third menstrual period and fasting is permissible for her. Muhammad bin Bashar and Muhammad bin al-Muthanna narrated, they said: Ibn Abi Uday narrated, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, he said: Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: He has more right to her as long as she has not washed herself after the third menstrual period. Muhammad bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-A’la narrated, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Durast, on the authority of al-Zuhri, On the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ali, similarly.

x: Others said: Rather, the menstrual period that God, the Most High, has commanded the divorced women to observe is purity.

Those who said that: Abdul Hameed bin Bayan told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, she said: The menstrual periods are the pure periods.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abdullah bin Umar told me, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Al-Qasim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha,
m: the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she used to say: The menstrual periods are the pure periods.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Umrah and Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: If the divorced woman enters her third menstrual period, she is separated from her husband and is permissible for other husbands. Al-Zuhri said: Umrah said: Aisha used to say: The menstrual period is purity, and it is not the menstruation. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abd al-Rahman bin al-Harith bin Hisham, like the statement of Zaid and Aisha. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, like the statement of Zaid. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated, he said: Muammar narrated, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab and Sulayman bin Yasar: that Zaid bin Thabit said: If a divorced woman enters her third menstrual period, she is separated from her husband and is protected from other husbands. Muammar said: Al-Zuhri used to issue fatwas based on the statement of Zaid. Muhammad bin Bashar narrated, he said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated, he said: I heard Yahya bin Saeed say: It has reached me that Aisha said: The menstrual periods are only the pure periods. Humayd ibn Masʿadah narrated, Yazid ibn Zuraiʿ narrated, Saʿid narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: If she enters her third menstrual period, he has no right to take her back. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abi ʿUdayy and ʿAbd al-ʿAʿla narrated, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, regarding a man who divorced his wife once or twice. Zayd ibn Thabit said: If she enters her third menstrual period, he has no right to take her back. Ibn Abi ʿUdayy added, saying: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: He has more right to her as long as she has not performed ghusl. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Ibn Abi Uday narrated, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Zaid and Ali, similarly. Ibn Bashar narrated, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated, he said: Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Abu al-Zinad, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit, he said: If she enters her third menstrual period, she has no inheritance. Yaqub narrated, he said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated, and Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, he said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated, they both said: Ayoub narrated, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar: That al-Ahwas - a man from the nobles of the people of Ash-Sham - divorced his wife once or twice, and she died while she was in her third menstrual period. It was brought to Mu’awiyah, but he did not find any knowledge of it. So he asked Fadalah ibn Ubayd and the companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) who were there, but they did not find any knowledge of it. So Mu’awiyah sent a rider to Zaid ibn Thabit, and he said: She does not inherit from him, and if she dies, he does not inherit from her. Ibn ‘Umar held that view. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abdul-Razzaq narrated, Muammar narrated, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Sulayman bin Yasar: That a man called Al-Ahwas from the people of Ash-Sham divorced his wife once. Then he died, and she had entered her third menstrual period. The matter was brought to Muawiyah, but he did not know what to say, so he wrote about it to Zayd bin Thabit. Zayd wrote to him: If the divorced woman enters her third menstrual period, there is no inheritance between them. Muhammad bin Yahya narrated, Abdul-A’la narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Sulayman bin Yasar: That a man called Al-Ahwas, and he mentioned something similar on the authority of Muawiyah and Zayd. Muhammad bin Yahya narrated, Abdul-A’la narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, who said: Ibn Umar said: If she enters her third menstrual period, there is no return for him to her. Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated, Abdul-Wahhab narrated, Ubaydullah narrated, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said about the divorced woman: If she enters her third menstrual period, she is divorced.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Umar ibn Muhammad told me, Nafi’ told him, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar and Zaid ibn Thabit,
m: that they used to say: If a woman’s bleeding begins from the third menstrual period, she does not inherit from him and he does not inherit from her, and she is free from him and he is free from her.
b.via: Abdullah ibn Umar and Zaid ibn Thabit

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Yahya ibn Sa’id told us, he said,
m: it reached me on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit who said: If a woman is divorced and she enters the third menstrual period, there is no inheritance between them and no return.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told me, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said,
m: I heard Yahya ibn Sa’id say: I heard Salim ibn Abdullah say the same as Zaid ibn Thabit.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said,
m: I heard Yahya say: I was told on the authority of Abaan ibn Uthman that he used to say the same.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ubaydullah told us, on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit,
m: something similar. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated, Shu'bah narrated, on the authority of Abd Rabbih ibn Sa'id, on the authority of Nafi': Mu'awiyah sent for Zaid ibn Thabit, and Zaid wrote to him: If she enters her third menstrual period, she is divorced. Ibn 'Umar used to say this. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated, Hisham narrated, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated, on the authority of Sulayman and Zaid ibn Thabit, that they said: If she menstruates for the third time, there is no taking her back and no inheritance. Mujahid ibn Musa narrated, Yazid narrated, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated, on the authority of Qays ibn Sa'd, on the authority of Bakir ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Ashja', on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit, who said: If a man divorces his wife and she sees blood in her third menstrual period, her waiting period has ended. Ibn Hamid narrated, Jarir narrated, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Musa ibn Shaddad, on the authority of 'Umar ibn Thabit al-Ansari, who said: Zaid ibn Thabit used to say: If a divorced woman menstruates for the third time before her husband takes her back, he does not have the right to take her back.

c: Muhammad bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul A'la told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Durast, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab:
m: That Aisha and Zaid bin Thabit said: If she enters her third menstruation, he has no right to return to her.

x: In Arabic, menstruation is the plural of qur', and the Arabs may make it plural aqra'. It is said in a verb from it: a woman has menstruated - if she has become menstruating and pure - so she recites iqra'. The origin of qur' in Arabic is: the time for the arrival of something that is usually at a known time, and for the departure of something that is usually at a known time. Therefore, the Arabs say: I have read someone's need with me, meaning: its fulfillment is near and the time for its fulfillment has come. And I read the star if the time of its setting has come, and I read if the time of its rising has come.

i: As the poet said:
x: If the dust has settled and I have read, I feel the sky is fading away from it It was said: The wind blew at the right time, as Al-Hudhali said: The barrenness of the Banu Shaleel is hated when the wind blows for its reader.

Meaning: it blew on time and when it blows. That is why some Arabs called the time of menstruation qur’, since it is blood that usually appears from a woman’s vagina at one time and remains hidden at another, so they called the time of its coming qur’, just as those Surat Al-Baqarah 2:228
h
And divorced women shall wait
, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods.
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

, if they believe in God and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back in that period, if they desire reconciliation. And women shall have rights similar to those against them, according to what is equitable. And men shall have rights over them. A degree, and God is Almighty, Wise. who called the time of the wind’s onset qur’. That is why “the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Fatimah bint Abi Hubaish: Leave off praying during your menstrual periods.”

That is to say: Leave off praying during the days of your menstrual period. Other Arabs called the time of the onset of purity Qur’an, since the time of its onset was the time of the menstrual blood’s disappearance, and the onset of purity was the usual time for it to come. Al-A’sha Maymun ibn Qays said about that: Every year you are a brave warrior, your determination to conquer is tightened to its furthest point. She inherits wealth, and there is elevation in remembrance, because of the menstrual periods of your women that are lost in it. So He made the menstrual period the time of purity.

Because we have described the meaning of the menstrual period, the interpretation of the statement of God, Divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods, was difficult for the people of interpretation.

Some of them saw that what the divorced woman who has menstrual periods was commanded to do was the menstrual periods, and that is the time of its coming due to its usual period in which it comes - so He made it obligatory for her to wait three menstrual periods by herself from proposing to husbands.

Others saw that what she was commanded to do was the menstrual periods of purity - and that is the time of its coming due to its usual period in which it comes - so He made it obligatory for her to wait three menstrual periods in order to not propose to husbands. If the meaning of the menstrual cycle is as we have described, and God Almighty has commanded the one who wants to divorce his wife not to divorce her except when she is pure and has not had intercourse, and He has forbidden him to divorce her while she is menstruating, then the divorced woman who has had menstrual cycles and has had intercourse with her must wait a limited number of times by herself after her husband divorces her, and she must wait for three menstrual cycles between the two periods of purity, each of which is a menstrual cycle, which is different from what she considered for herself to be menstrual cycles that she must wait.

When they have ended, she is permissible for husbands and her waiting period has ended. This is because if she does that, she has entered the number of divorced women who wait for three menstrual cycles by herself between the two periods of purity, each of which has a different menstrual cycle. If she does that, she has fulfilled what her Lord Almighty has obligated her to do according to the apparent meaning of His revelation. It has become clear, if the matter is as we have described, that the third menstrual cycle of her menstrual cycles, as we have explained, is the third purity, and that with its end and the coming of the menstrual cycle that follows it, her waiting period has ended. If a foolish person thinks that since we call the time of the onset of purity a menstrual period, and the time of the onset of menstruation a menstrual period, then we must make the woman’s waiting period end with the end of the second period of purity, since the period of purity in which he divorced her, the menstruation that follows it, and the period of purity that follows it are all menstrual periods, then he has thought out of ignorance.

The ruling, according to us, in everything that God has revealed in His Book is based on what the apparent meaning of the revelation implies, unless God, the Most High, makes clear to His servants that He intended it specifically, either by revelation in His Book or by the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. If He makes some of it specific, then what was specific is not included in the generality of the ruling, and the rest is general, as we have explained in our book, The Book of Latif al-Qawl min al-Bayan ‘an Usul al-Ahkam, and other books of ours. So the menstrual periods, which are the periods of menstruation between two periods of purity, are not counted among the periods of the woman who is waiting for herself after divorce, due to the consensus of all the people of Islam: that the periods for which God has made it obligatory for her to wait are three menstrual periods, between each of which there are times that differ in meaning from the menstrual periods for which she is waiting.
And since they are entitled to the name of menstrual periods, according to us, then it is from the consensus of all that she is not permitted to wait except for what we have described before.

This verse is clear evidence of the error of the one who said: The wife of the master who has sworn to divorce her is permissible for husbands after the expiration of four months, if she has menstruated three times in the four months. Because God, the Most High, only made the waiting period obligatory for her after the master has decided to divorce her and to pronounce the divorce upon her, by saying: “But if they decide on divorce, then indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.
h
And divorced women shall wait

concerning themselves three menstrual periods.” So God, the Most High, made it obligatory for the woman, if she becomes divorced, to wait three menstrual periods. It is known that she was not divorced on the day her husband divorced her, because everyone agrees that the sworn oath is not a divorce that requires the waiting period for the master. Since that is the case, the waiting period is only obligatory for her after the divorce, and the divorce only applies to her as we have explained before.

As for the meaning of His statement: and the divorced women, it is: and those who are free to go, not forbidden by husbands nor engaged. And the statement of the one who says: So-and-so is divorced is only the result of the statement of the one who says: The man divorced his wife, so she is divorced. As for their saying: She is divorced, it is from their saying: Her husband divorced her, so she was divorced, and she is divorced with a divorce, and she is divorced. It has been narrated that some of the Arab tribes used to say: The woman is divorced. This is only said to her if her husband leaves her alone, as it is said to a neglected ewe without a shepherd or a guardian, if she goes out alone from her family to graze, released: She is divorced. So the woman released is likened to her, and she was called by the same name as the ewe whose case we described. As for their saying: The woman is divorced, it has a different meaning.

It is only said of this when she gives birth. This is from the divorce, and the first is from the divorce. We have explained that waiting is to stop marriage and to restrain oneself from it, in other than this place.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: And it is not lawful for them meaning the divorced women, to conceal what God has created in their wombs of menstruation if they are divorced. It is forbidden for them to conceal from their husbands who have divorced them the divorce in which they have the right to take it back, seeking thereby to nullify their rights to take it back from them.
He mentioned who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: God Almighty said:
m: h
And divorced women shall wait

concerning themselves three menstrual periods until His saying: And men have a degree over them, and God is Exalted in Might and Wise. He said: It has reached us that what was created in their wombs is pregnancy, and it has reached us that it is menstruation, so it is not permissible for them to conceal that, so that the waiting period ends and he does not have the right to return if it is his.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And
h
it is not permissible for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
he said: Menstruation.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And
h
it is not permissible for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
he said: The greatest of that is menstruation.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, he said,
m: I heard Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Hakam, he said, Ibrahim said in He said:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
. He said: Menstruation.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Khalid al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
. He said: Menstruation. Then Khalid said: Blood.

x: Others said: It is menstruation, but what God, the Most High, has forbidden her to conceal from what He has created in her womb of that, is that she says to her divorced husband, when he wanted to take her back before the third menstruation: I have had my third menstruation, lying in order to nullify his right with her false statement in that.
Those who said that: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ubaidah ibn Mu'tab, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His statement:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
, he said: menstruation. A woman observes the waiting period of two menstrual periods, then her husband wants to take her back, so she says: I have menstruated for the third time.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
, he said, most of what he meant was menstruation.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning that she was forbidden to conceal from her divorced husband is pregnancy and menstruation together.
Those who said that: Hamid ibn Mas'adah told us, he said, Yazid ibn Zurai' told us, he said, Al-Ash'ath told us, on the authority of Nafi', on the authority of Ibn Umar:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
, of menstruation and pregnancy. It is not permissible for her to conceal her menstruation if she is menstruating, and it is not permissible for her to conceal her pregnancy if she is pregnant.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying:
m: I heard Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And
h
it is not permissible for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
, he said: Pregnancy and menstruation. Abu Kurayb said: Ibn Idris said: This is the first hadith I heard from Mutraf.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: pregnancy.

c: Ismail bin Musa Al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari narrated to us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, And
h
it is not permissible for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
, he said: menstruation and childbirth.

c: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Muslim bin Khalid Al-Zanji narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And
h
it is not permissible for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
, he said: menstruation and childbirth.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

, he said: It is not permissible for a divorced woman to say: I am menstruating, when she is not menstruating, nor to say: I am pregnant, when she is not pregnant, nor to say: I am not pregnant, when she is pregnant.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid ibn Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Menstruation and pregnancy, he said: Its interpretation is that she should not say: I am menstruating, when she is not menstruating, nor I am not menstruating, when she is menstruating, nor: I am pregnant, when she is not pregnant, nor: I am not pregnant, when she is pregnant.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Hajjaj, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Nafi’, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar to this interpretation of this verse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, and he added to it, he said: And all of that is due to the woman’s hatred for her husband Surat Al-Baqarah 2:228
h
And divorced women shall wait
, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods.
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

, if they believe in God and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back in that period, if they desire reconciliation. And women shall have rights similar to those against them, according to what is equitable. And men shall have rights over them. A degree, and God is Almighty, Wise. and her love for him.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

, he said: It is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs of menstruation and pregnancy. It is not lawful for her to say: I have menstruated, when she has not, and it is not lawful for her to say: I have not menstruated, when she has menstruated. It is not lawful for her to say: I am pregnant, when she is not, or to say: I am not pregnant, when she is pregnant.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

, the verse, he said: They should not conceal menstruation or childbirth. It is not permissible for her to conceal it while he does not know when it will be permissible, lest he take her back - harming him.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It is not permissible for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
, meaning the child. He said: Menstruation and the child are what women are entrusted with.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant pregnancy. Then those who said that differed regarding the reason why the man was forbidden to conceal that.
Some of them said: She was forbidden to do that so that the husband’s right to take her back would not be nullified, if he wanted to take her back before she gave birth to her pregnancy.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Qubath bin Razin, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah that he told him:
m: That Umar bin Al-Khattab said to a man: Recite this verse. So he recited, and he said: So-and-so is among those who conceal what God has created in their wombs, and she was divorced while she was pregnant, so she concealed it until she gave birth.
b.via: on the authority of Ali bin Rabah that he

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If a man divorces his wife once or twice while she is pregnant, he has more right to take her back as long as she has not given birth, and this is what He said:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
if they believe in God and the Last Day.

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Qubath bin Razin, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah that he told him: That Umar bin Al-Khattab said to a man: Recite this verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Bishr,
m: that he heard Ikrimah say: Divorce is two times with a return between them. If he decides to divorce her after these two, then it is a third time. If he divorces her three times, then she is forbidden to him until she marries another husband. Rather, those mentioned in the Qur’an: “
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

if they believe in God and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back” are the ones who were divorced once or twice, then concealed their pregnancy in order to escape from their husband. But if the three divorces were completed, then he has no right to take her back until she marries another husband.

x: Others said: The reason why they were forbidden from concealing that is that in the pre-Islamic era, they used to conceal it from their husbands, fearing that they would return to them, until they married someone else, so the lineage of the pregnancy - which is from the divorced husband - would be attributed to the one she married. God forbade them from doing that.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Bishr ibn Muadh told us, Suwaid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
, he said: When a woman was divorced, she concealed what was in her womb and her pregnancy in order to take the child to someone other than its father, so God disliked that for them.

c: Muhammad ibn Yahya told me, he said: Abdul A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

, he said: God knew that among them were those who concealed the child. And in the days of ignorance, a man would divorce his wife while she was pregnant, and she would conceal the child and take it to someone else, and conceal it for fear of taking him back. So God forbade that and presented it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, from Qatada:
m: h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
. He said: A woman would conceal her pregnancy until she gave it to another man.

x: Others said: Rather, the reason why they were forbidden to conceal that is that when a man wanted to divorce his wife, he would ask her: Is she pregnant? So that he would not divorce her while she was pregnant by him, because of the harm that would befall him and his child if he separated from her. So they were commanded to be truthful in that, and they were forbidden to lie.
Those who said that were Surat Al-Baqarah 2:229 Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God
, then there is no blame upon them for what she has given herself in ransom. These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them.
And whoever transgresses The limits of God, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. mentioned:

c: Musa narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi:
m: h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs

. So a man wants to divorce his wife, so he asks her: Are you pregnant? So she conceals it, wanting to leave him, so he divorces her while she has concealed it until she gives birth. And if he finds out about that, she is returned to him, as a punishment for what she concealed, and her husband has more right to take her back, humiliated.

x: The most correct of these opinions in interpreting the verse is the opinion of those who said: What the divorced woman was forbidden to conceal from her husband who divorced her once or twice is what God created in her womb - menstruation and pregnancy. Because there is no disagreement among all that the waiting period ends with the birth of the child whom God created in her womb, just as it ends with blood if she sees it after the third period of purity, according to the opinion of those who said: the menstrual period is purity, and according to the opinion of those who said: it is menstruation, if it stops from the third period, then she purifies herself by bathing. If this is the case, and God Almighty only forbade them from concealing the divorced husband whose matter we have described, what would be their concealment of it for the duration of his right that God gave him after divorcing them until their number expired, and that right was nullified by their giving birth to what was in their wombs if they were pregnant, and by the expiration of the three menstrual periods if they were not pregnant, it is known that they are forbidden from concealing from their divorced husbands from each of them - I mean menstruation and pregnancy - just as they are forbidden from the other, and that there is no meaning to the specificity of the one who was conceived that what is meant by the verse is one of them without the other, since they were both among what God created in their wombs, and that in each of them there is a meaning of the duration of the husband’s right to end at a limit, like what is in the other.

And the one who has made that specific - and attributed it to one of the two meanings without the other - is asked about the proof of the validity of his claim from an origin or argument that must be accepted. Then the statement is reversed on him in that, so he will not say a statement about one of them except that it is obligatory for the other like it. As for what Al-Suddi said: that it means that it is forbidden for women to conceal their husbands’ pregnancy when they want to divorce them, then this statement contradicts what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation. That is because God the Most High said: “Divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods.
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
” meaning:
h
And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs
of the three menstrual periods, if they believe in God and the Last Day.

That is because God the Most High mentioned the prohibition of that upon them, after describing them with what He described them with, of separating from their husbands by divorce, and informing them of what is required of them in terms of waiting, informing them thereby of what is forbidden to them and what is permissible, and what is required of them in terms of waiting and what is obligatory upon them in it.

c: So what he informed them
m: of was that it is obligatory upon them not to conceal their husbands’ menstruation and pregnancy, which is that by establishing this and ending this to a limited end, the rights of their husbands are cut off, to their detriment. So his prohibition of what he prohibited them from doing, that it be of the description of what came before it and followed it after it, is more appropriate than it being of the description of what was not mentioned before it.

x: If someone were to say: What is the meaning of his saying: If they believe in God and the Last Day? Is it permissible for them to conceal that from their husbands if they do not believe in God or the Last Day, so that the prohibition of that was specific to those who believe in God and the Last Day? It was said: The meaning of that is not what you have gone to. Rather, its meaning is: A divorced woman concealing from her divorced husband what God created in her womb of menstruation and childbirth during the days of her waiting period after his divorce, to harm him, is not the action of one who believes in God and the Last Day, nor is it his morals. Rather, it is the action of one who does not believe in God and the Last Day, and their morals are from the disbelieving women. So, O believing women, do not adopt their morals, for that is not permissible for you if you believe in God and the Last Day, and you are from the Muslims.

It is not that the believing women are the ones specifically prohibited from that, not the disbelieving women. Rather, it is obligatory upon every woman who is bound by God’s obligations and has menstrual periods - if she is divorced after consummating the marriage with her during her waiting period - not to conceal from her husband what God created in her womb of menstruation and pregnancy.

Baʿulah is the plural of Baʿl, which is the husband of a woman. From this is the saying of Jarir: Prepare your clothes and jewelry, for Jarir is your husband and you are his wives. The husband may be pluralized as ba'ulah and ba'ul, just as fahal is pluralized as fahuul and fahuulah, the male as well as the males and masculinity. Likewise, what is on the pattern fa'ul from the plural, the Arabs often add the ha' to it, but as for what is on the pattern fa'al, the ha' is rarely added to it in their speech: and it has been reported from them. Al-'Azm and al-'Azma, and from it the saying of the rajaz poet: Then I buried the dung and bones. It has been said: Stones and stones, skill and skill, male and female, for males. As for the interpretation of the words, it is: And the husbands of divorced women, upon whom We have imposed that they wait by themselves for three menstrual periods and We have forbidden them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, are more entitled and more deserving of returning them to themselves during their waiting for the three menstrual periods and the days of pregnancy, and their return to their pregnancy, than they are to prevent them from themselves, as: - Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: And their husbands have more right to return them in that case if they want reconciliation means: If a man divorces his wife once or twice while she is pregnant, he is more entitled to return her as long as she has not given birth.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And their husbands have more right to take them back. He said: During the waiting period.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, Yahya bin Wadheeh narrated to us, Al-Husayn bin Waqid narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said: God the Almighty said:
m: “Divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods. It is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, if they believe in God and the Last Day.
h
And their husbands have more right to take them back in that period

if they desire reconciliation.” This is because if a man divorced his wife, he had more right to take her back, even if he divorced her three times. This was abrogated, and He said: Divorce is twice. (al-Baqarah 2:229) Muhammad bin Amr narrated to us, Abu Asim narrated to us, Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement:
h
And their husbands have more right to take them back in that period
, in their waiting period.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, Shibl narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan,
m: On the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: During the waiting period.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their husbands have more right to take them back during that period

, meaning: during the menstrual cycles, during the three menstrual periods, or three months, or if she was pregnant, then if her husband divorced her once or twice, he may take her back if he wishes, as long as she was in her waiting period.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their husbands have more right to take them back during that period
, he said: A woman used to conceal her pregnancy until she gave it to another man, so God forbade them from that and said:
h
And their husbands have more right to take them back during that period
, Qatada said: They have more right to take them back during the waiting period.

c: I was told on the authority of Ammar,
m: he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
And their husbands have more right to take them back during that period
, he said: During the waiting period, as long as he did not divorce her three times.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told me, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And their husbands have more right to take them back in that case
, meaning: they have more right to take her back in a state of humiliation, as punishment for concealing her pregnancy from her husband.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: And their husbands have more right to take them back, they have more right to take them back, as long as the waiting period has not expired.

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of al-Dahhak:
m: h
And their husbands have more right to take them back in that case
, he said: as long as she is in the waiting period, if he wants to take her back.

x: If someone were to say to us: So the husband - who divorced her once or twice after consummating the marriage with her - has no right to take her back In her three menstrual periods, unless he intended to reform her and his situation by returning? It was said: As for what is between him and God, the Most High, it is not permissible, if he intended to harm her by returning, not to reform her and his situation, to return to her. As for the ruling, it is ruled that he returns to her, similar to what we ruled on him regarding the length of his return to her if she concealed from him her pregnancy that God created in her womb or her menstruation until her waiting period ended, to harm him, and God has forbidden concealing that. So it was the same in the ruling, regarding the length of her husband’s return to her, and she sinned in concealing from him what she concealed from that until her waiting period ended, she and the one who obeyed God by not concealing that from him, even if they differed in obeying God in that and disobeying Him.

Likewise, the one who returns to his wife who was divorced once or twice after consummating the marriage with her and they are both free, and if he intended to harm the return by returning, then he is ruled to return, even if he was sinful in his innocence in his action, and he preferred what God did not permit him, and God is the guardian of his punishment for what he did of that. As for the servants, it is not permissible for them to stand between him and his wife whom he has taken back by the ruling of God Almighty that she is then his wife. If he tries to harm her after taking her back without the right that God has given him, he shall take for them the rights that God Almighty has obligated husbands to wives, so that the harm he intended from that will return to him and not to her.
In His statement:
h
And their husbands have more right to take them back in that case

, there is clear evidence for the correctness of the statement of those who said: If the master decides to divorce and divorces his wife from whom he swore an oath, then he has the right to take her back in that divorce, and for the corruption of the statement of those who said: If the passage of four months, then he decided to divorce, and that it is an irrevocable divorce, because God Almighty only informed His servants of what is required of them if they swore an oath from their wives, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:229 Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God
, then there is no blame upon them for what she has given herself in ransom.

These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses The limits of God, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. and what is required of women from the rulings in this verse regarding the men’s oath and their divorce, if they decided to do that and left the spoils of war.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: And they have from good companionship and good treatment from their husbands, like what is required of them from obedience in what God Almighty has made obligatory for him from her.

Who said that: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding His statement: And women have rights similar to those against them, according to what is equitable, he said: If they obey God and obey their husbands, then he must treat them well, refrain from harming them, and spend on them from his wealth.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: And women have rights similar to those against them, according to what is equitable, he said: They should fear God in them, just as they should fear God in them.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: And they have rights over their husbands in terms of pretense and kindness, just as they have rights over them in that.

Who said that: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Bashir ibn Salman, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I like to adorn myself for my wife as I like her to adorn herself for me, because God the Most High says: And they have rights similar to those against them, according to what is equitable.

What I think is more appropriate in interpreting the verse is: And for women who have been divorced once or twice - after consummation - upon their husbands that they should not take them back during their three menstrual periods, if they wish to take them back during them, unless they wish to set things right for them and their situation, and that they should not take them back to cause them harm, just as they are obligated upon them, if they wish to take them back during them, that they should not conceal what God has created in their wombs of children and menstrual blood, to cause them harm in order to tempt them with themselves. That is because God, the Most High, mentioned that He forbade divorced women from concealing from their husbands during their menstrual periods what God has created in their wombs, if they believe in God and the Last Day, and He made their husbands more entitled to take them back during that period if they wish to set things right, so God forbade each one of them from harming the other, and He made known to each one of them what is due and what is due from that, then He followed that with His saying: And they have rights similar to those against them according to what is equitable.

So he explained that what each of them owes to his companion in terms of not harming him is like what he owes to his companion in terms of that. This interpretation is more similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation than any other. It may be possible that everything that each of them owes to his companion is included in that, even though the verse was revealed in what we have described. Because God, the Most High, has made a right for each of them over the other, so each of them has a right over the other in terms of fulfilling his right to him, like what he owes to him. Then what was said by Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Abbas, and others is included in the verse.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said: The meaning of the degree that God has given men over women is the superiority that God has given them over them in inheritance, jihad, and the like.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said: Abu ʿAsim told us, on the authority of ʿIsa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement: And men have a degree over them, he said: The superiority that God has given him over her in terms of jihad, and the superiority of his inheritance over her inheritance, and everything that He has given her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And men have a degree over them, he said: Men have a degree in superiority over women.

x: Others said: Rather, that degree is leadership and obedience.

Those who said that: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His statement: And men have a degree over them, he said: Leadership.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: And men have a degree over them, he said: Obedience. He said: The wives obey the men, but the men do not obey them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Azhar told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad,
m: regarding His statement: And men have a degree over them, he said: I do not know except that they have the same as those over them, if they recognize that degree.

x: Others said: That degree he has over her, because of what he gave her of the dowry, and that if she accuses him, she is punished, and if he accuses her, she is cursed.

Those who said that: Muhammad bin Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ubaidah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement: And men have a degree over them, he said: Because of what he gave her of her dowry, and that if he accuses her, he curses her, and if she accuses him, she is flogged and remains with him.
Others said: That degree he has over her, is his favor to her, and fulfilling her right to her, and his pardoning what is due to him from her or some of it.

Those who said that: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Bashir bin Salman, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I do not like to purify all of my rights over her, because God the Most High says: And men have a degree over them.
Others said: Rather, that degree he has over her, is that he gave her a beard and forbade her from that.
Those who said that: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me, he said, Ubaid bin Al-Sabah told us, he said, Hamid told us, he said: And men have a degree over them, he said: a beard.

The most appropriate of these sayings in the interpretation of the verse is what Ibn Abbas said, which is that the degree that God the Most High mentioned in this place is the man’s forgiveness of his wife for some of what is due from her, and his overlooking it for her, and fulfilling all of what is due from him to her. That is because God the Most High said: And men have a degree over them, following His statement: And women have rights similar to those against them according to what is equitable, so God the Most High informed that the man has the right to refrain from harming her by returning to her during her three menstrual periods and in other matters and rights of hers, just as he has the right over her to refrain from harming him by concealing from him what God created in their wombs and other rights of his. Then he urged men to take advantage of their women if they neglected to perform some of what God had obligated them to do.

God the Almighty said: Men have a degree over them by being generous to them and forgiving them of some of what they have to do. This is the meaning intended by Ibn Abbas when he said: I do not like to claim all of my rights over her, because God the Almighty says: Men have a degree over them. The meaning of degree is rank and status. This statement of God, the Most High, although it appears to be the apparent meaning of a report, its meaning is the meaning of urging men to take advantage of women, so that they will have an advantage over them in degree.

By that, God, the Most High, means: And God is Exalted in Might in His vengeance on whoever disobeys His command and transgresses His limits, so he comes to women during menstruation, and God makes it a condition for his oaths to be righteous and pious and to reconcile between people, and prevents his wife by swearing, and harms her by returning to him after his divorce, and for those women who conceal what God has created in their wombs for their husbands, and they marry within their number and leave waiting for themselves until the time that God has set for them, and they commit other sins against Him, Wise in what He has planned in His creation, and in what He has ruled and decreed between them of His rulings, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding His statement: And God is Exalted in Might, Wise he says: Exalted in His vengeance, Wise in His command. God Almighty threatened His servants with this statement because He had previously stated what He had forbidden them or prohibited them from, from the beginning of His statement: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe to His statement: And men have a degree over them, then He followed that with the threat, so that those of understanding would be deterred, and so that those of wisdom would remember and fear His punishment and beware of His torment.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that: Some of them said: It is an indication of the number of divorces in which a man has the right to take his wife back, and the number by which his wife is separated from him. He mentioned those who said that this verse was revealed because the people of ignorance and the people of Islam before its revelation did not have an end to their divorces that would separate his wife from him if he took her back during her waiting period from him, so God the Most High made a limit for that, and by the divorce reaching it he forbade the man from his divorced wife, except after a husband, and made her then more in control of herself than him.
He mentioned the reports that came with what we said in that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: A man would divorce as he wished, then if he took his wife back before her waiting period ended, she would be his wife. A man from the Ansar became angry with his wife and said to her: I will not come near you and you are not permissible for me. She said to him: How? He said: I will divorce you, and when your time is near I will take you back, or I will divorce you, and when your time is near I will take you back. He said: So she complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God Almighty revealed: “Divorce is twice. Then, keep [her] in an acceptable manner” (2:170).

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father,
m: a man said to his wife during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will not shelter you nor let you become permissible. So she said to him: What should you do? He said: I will divorce you, and when your waiting period is about to end, I will take you back. So when will you become permissible? So she came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed: “Divorce is twice. Then, keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment” 2:170. So the people welcomed him anew, some of whom had divorced and some of whom had not.

c: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: In the days of ignorance, a man would divorce his wife three times, ten times, or more than that, then take her back during the waiting period. So God made the punishment for divorce three divorces.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: In the days of ignorance, a man would divorce his wife then take her back, there was no punishment for that, she was his wife and he did not take her back during her waiting period. So God made the punishment for that three menstrual periods, and He made the punishment for divorce three divorces.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, Divorce is twice, he said: Divorce - before God made divorce three times - had no time limit. A man could divorce his wife a hundred times, then if he wanted to take her back before she was permissible, he could do so. A man divorced his wife, and when she was about to be permissible, he Surat Al-Baqarah 2:229 Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God

, then there is no blame upon them for what she has given herself in ransom. These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses The limits of God, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. took her back. Then he divorced her again after that to harm her by leaving her, until before her waiting period had ended, he took her back. He did that repeatedly, and when God knew that from him, He made divorce three: twice, then after the two times, either keeping her on good terms or releasing her with kindness.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: Divorce is twice, then keeping her on good terms or releasing her with kindness. As for his saying, Divorce is twice, it is the time limit at which she must take her back.

c: Hannad narrated to us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas narrated to us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment, he said: If a man wants to divorce his wife, he divorces her twice. If he wants to take her back, then he has the right to take her back. If he wishes, he may divorce her again, and she is not lawful for him until she marries another husband.

x: The interpretation of the verse according to this report that we mentioned is: The number of divorces that you, O people, have upon your wives, if they have been consummated with them, is two divorces. Then what is obligatory upon whoever among you takes her back after the two divorces is to keep her in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment, because he has no right to take her back after the two divorces, if he releases her and then divorces her a third time.

Others said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a definition from God Almighty, who mentioned to His servants the Sunnah of divorcing their wives if they wanted to divorce them - not an indication of the number by which a woman is separated from her husband.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement: Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment, he said: He divorces her after she has purified herself from intercourse, then he leaves her until she is purified again, then he divorces her if he wishes, then if he wants to take her back, he takes her back, then if he wishes he divorces her, otherwise he leaves her until she completes three menstrual cycles and is separated from him by it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment, he said: If a man divorces his wife twice, then let him fear God in the third divorce. Either he keeps her in kindness and treats her well, or he releases her with kindness and does not deprive her of any of her rights.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: Divorce is twice, then either keeping her in kindness or releasing her with kindness, he said: A man divorces his wife when she is pure and has not had intercourse. If she menstruates and then becomes pure, then the menstrual cycle is complete. Then he divorces her a second time as he divorced the first, if he likes to do so. If he divorces her a second time and she menstruates a second time, then they are two divorces and two menstrual cycles. Then God the Most High said in the third: Either keep her in an acceptable manner or release her with kindness, so he divorces her during that entire menstrual cycle if he wishes, when she gathers her clothes around her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly - except that he said:
m: So she menstruated the second time as he divorced the first, so these are two divorces and two menstrual cycles. Then he said: The third - and the rest of the hadith is like the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Asim.

x: The interpretation of the verse according to what these people say: The law of divorce that We have established and permitted for you if you want to divorce your wives: is that you divorce them twice in every period of purity, once. Then what is obligatory upon you after that is either to keep them in an acceptable manner or release them with kindness.

What is more appropriate to the apparent meaning of the revelation is what was said by ʿUrwah and Qatadah, and those who said something similar to their statement: that the verse is only evidence of the number of divorces that constitute prohibition, the length of time it takes to take her back, and the time in which she can be taken back. This is because God, the Most High, said in the verse that follows it: But if he has divorced her, she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband, so He made known to His servants the amount by which a woman is forbidden to her husband except after another husband. He did not specify the time in which divorce is permissible and the time in which it is not permissible. Thus, the interpretation of the verse is directed to what was narrated from Ibn Masʿud and Mujahid, and those who said something similar to their statement.

As for His statement: Either keep her in an acceptable manner or release her with good treatment, there is a difference of opinion among the interpreters of the verse regarding its interpretation and what it means.

Some of them said: God, the Most High, meant by that the evidence of what is required of husbands for women who have been divorced twice - after they have taken her back from the second divorce - of treating them kindly, or separating from them with a divorce.

Who said that: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata’: Divorce is twice. He said: He says: Upon the third divorce, either he keeps her in an acceptable manner, or he releases her with kindness. And others said the same. He said: Mujahid said: A man has more control over his wife in two divorces from someone else, so if he speaks the third time, she has no right to him, and she waits for someone else.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said:
m: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of his statement: ‘Divorce is twice, either keeping her in an acceptable manner or releasing her with kindness.’ So where is the third? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Keeping her in an acceptable manner or releasing her with kindness.’ It is the third.” Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, Yahya ibn Saeed and Abdurrahman ibn Mahdi narrated, Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Ismail ibn Samee’, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, Divorce is twice. So where is the third? He said: Either keeping [her] in an acceptable manner or releasing [her] with kindness. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated, Abdurrazaq narrated, on the authority of Ath-Thawri, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: A man said: O Messenger of God, God says: Divorce is twice, then keeping [her] in an acceptable manner. So where is the third? He said: Release [her] with kindness. Ibn Bashar narrated, on the authority of Abu Ahmad, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Or releasing [her] with kindness. He said: In the third. Al-Muthanna narrated, on the authority of Ishaq, on the authority of Abdurrazaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah, who said: There was no time for divorce until God revealed: Divorce is twice. He said: The third: Keep her in kindness or release her with good treatment.

x: Others among them said: Rather, God meant by that the indication that they are obligated to them after the second divorce, whether to return her in kindness or release her with good treatment, by not taking her back until their waiting period is over, so they become more in control of themselves. And they denied the statement of the first ones who said: It is evidence of the third divorce.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: Either keep her in kindness or release her with good treatment, if he divorces her once or twice, he either keeps her - and keeps: takes her back - in kindness, or he keeps quiet about her until her waiting period is over, so she is more entitled to herself.

c: Ali bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Or release her with good treatment. And releasing her means leaving her until her waiting period is over.

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Juwaybir narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment, he said: He means two divorces between which there is a reconsideration, so he was commanded to keep her or release her with good treatment. He said: If he divorces her a third time, she is not lawful for him until she marries another husband.

x: It seems that those who said this statement that we mentioned on the authority of As-Suddi and Ad-Dahhak went to the meaning of the statement: Divorce is twice, then in each of them keeping [her] with good treatment or releasing [her] with good treatment. This is a doctrine that the apparent meaning of the revelation allows, were it not for the report that I mentioned on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which was narrated by Ismail ibn Samiʿ on the authority of Abu Razin, for following the report on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more appropriate for us than anything else. So since that is what is required, then it is clear that the interpretation of the verse is: The divorce that the husbands of women have over their wives in which there is a return, twice. Then the matter after that if they return to them the second time, is either to keep them in an acceptable manner, or to release them from them with kindness by the third divorce, until they become separated from them, so that what they had against them of taking her back is nullified, and they become more in control of themselves than they are.
If someone says: What is that keeping that is acceptable?
It is said: They are: Ali bin ʿAbd al-ʿAʿla al-Maharbi narrated to us, he said:

c: ʿAbd al-Rahman bin Muhammad al-Maharbi narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: Then keep them in an acceptable manner, he said: The acceptable means treating her well.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: ʿAbdullah bin Salih narrated to us, he said: Muʿawiyah bin Salih narrated to me, on the authority of ʿAli bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: Then keep them in an acceptable manner, he said: Let him fear God in the third divorce, so either he keeps her in an acceptable manner and treats her well.

x: What is releasing her with kindness?

They are: - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Abu Saleh narrated to us, he said, Muawiyah narrated to me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or release with kindness, he said: He releases her and does not deprive her of any of her rights.

c: Muhammad bin Saad narrated to me, he said, my father narrated to me, he said, my uncle narrated to me, he said, my father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Either keep her in an acceptable manner or release her with kindness, he said: It is the solemn covenant.

c: Musa narrated to me, he said, Amr narrated to us, he said, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Or release her with kindness, he said: Kindness means that he gives her her rights, so he does not harm her or insult her.

c: Ali bin Abdul A’la narrated to us, he said, Abdul Rahman bin Muhammad Al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: Or release her with kindness, he said: Release with kindness means that he leaves her until her waiting period is over, and he gives her a dowry if he owes her if he divorces her. This is the release with kindness, and the enjoyment is according to the means.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding Surat Al-Baqarah 2:229 Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God

, then there is no blame upon them for what she has given herself in ransom. These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses The limits of God, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. his statement: And they took from you a solemn covenant
r
(An-Nisa’: 21)
, he said: His statement: Either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with kindness.

x: What is the reason for the removal of the retention and the release?

It is omitted, and it is sufficient to indicate what appeared in the speech from its mention, and its meaning is: Divorce twice, so the obligatory matter in that case is to keep her in kindness or release her with kindness. We have explained that in His statement:
h
Then follow up with kindness and pay her back with kindness (al-Baqarah 2
:178), so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them

, and it is not lawful for you, O men, to take from your women, if you want to divorce them - because of your divorce and separation from them - anything of what you gave them of the dowry and gave them, rather what is obligatory upon you is to release them with kindness, and that is to give them their rights of the dowry and the enjoyment and other things that are obligatory upon them from you, unless they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
The reciters differed in the recitation of that.

Some of them read it as: Except if they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God. This is the reading of most of the people of Hijaz and Basra, meaning: Except if the man and woman fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God. It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b: Except if they think that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said: Thawr told me, on the authority of Maymun ibn Mihran, he said:
m: In the letter of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, the ransom is one divorce. He said: So I mentioned that to Ayoub, so we went to a man who had an old copy of the Qur’an of Ubayy that was from a trustworthy person, so we read it and it said: Except if they think that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.

x: But if they think that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, then there is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with. She is not lawful for him afterward until she marries another husband.

i: The Arabs may put suspicion in the place of fear, and fear in the place of suspicion in their speech, because their meanings are similar, as the poet said:
x: I heard a word about fate saying, and I was not afraid, Salam, that you would find fault with me.
Meaning: I did not think.

Others from the people of Medina and Kufa read it: Except that they fear that they will not be able to establish the limits of God. As for the one who reads it like that from the people of Kufa, it is mentioned from him that he read it like that, based on the reading of Ibn Masoud, and it is mentioned that in the reading of Ibn Masoud it is: Except that you fear that they will not be able to establish the limits of God. Reading it like that, based on the reading of Ibn Masoud that was mentioned from him, is wrong.

i: That is because if Ibn Masoud read it as it was mentioned from him, then he only applied fear to an alone, and that is not proven to be correct, as the poet said:
x: If I die, bury me next to a vine, so that its roots will water my bones after my death.

Do not bury me in the desert, for I fear that if I die, I will not taste it. As for his reader: Except that they fear with that meaning, he has applied it to the one whose name is not mentioned, and to that - so he applied it to three things: the one who is not mentioned, which is the name of what its agent is not mentioned, and to that which represents two things, and the Arabs do not say in their speech: thinking that they will stand up. But the reading of that in this way is correct, unlike the way in which the one we mentioned read it in this way, based on the reading of Abdullah whom we described, but on the condition that what is meant by it when it is read in this way is: Except that they fear that they will not establish the limits of God - or: that they will not establish the limits of God, so the factor in that is other than fear, and fear is a factor in what its agent is not mentioned.

And that is the correct reading according to us, because what follows indicates its correctness, which is His statement: And if you fear that they will not establish the limits of God, so it was clear that the first means: Except that you fear that they will not establish the limits of God.
What is the case in which there is fear that they will not uphold the limits of God, so that it is permissible for the man to take from her what he gave her?
