The case of her rebellion and her showing him his hatred for him, so that there is fear that she will abandon obedience to God in what is obligatory for her husband, and there is fear that her husband - due to her failure to fulfill the rights that God has obligated for him - will abandon fulfilling his duty towards her. That is when there is fear that they will not uphold the limits of God and obey Him in what each of them has obligated for the other, and the case in which the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) permitted Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas to take what he had given his wife when she rebelled against him, out of hatred for him, as:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I read to Fadil, on the authority of Abu Hurayz, that he asked Ikrimah: Did khul’ have a basis? He said: Ibn Abbas used to say: “The first divorce in Islam was the sister of Abdullah bin Ubayy: She came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, nothing will ever bring my head and his head together! I lifted the side of the tent, and I saw him coming with a group, and he was the blackest of them, the shortest of them in stature, and the ugliest of them in face! Her husband said: O Messenger of God, I gave her the best of my wealth! A garden, so if she returns my garden to me! What do you say? She said: Yes, and if she wishes, she may return it! He said: Then separate them.”

c: Muhammad bin Muammar told me, he said, Abu Amir told us, he said, Abu Amr al-Sadusi told us, on the authority of Abdullah - meaning Ibn Abi Bakr - on the authority of Umrah,
m: “on the authority of Aisha, that Habeeba bint Sahl was married to Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas, and he beat her and broke her breast, so she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the morning prayer and complained about him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Thabit and said: Take some of her wealth and separate from her. He said: Is that right, O Messenger of God?” He said: Yes. He said: I gave her two gardens as a dowry, and they are in her possession. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take them and leave her. So he did.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Ruh narrated to us, he said: Malik narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Umrah, that she told him, on the authority of Habibah bint Sahl al-Ansariyyah:
m: That she was married to Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas, and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw her at his door at dawn, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Who is this? She said: I am Habibah bint Sahl, neither I nor Thabit bin Qays!! - her husband - so when Thabit came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: This is Habibah bint Sahl, mentioning what God willed that she mention! Habibah said: O Messenger of God, I have everything that he gave me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take from her.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadh narrated to us, Al-Hasan ibn Waqid narrated to us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rabah, on the authority of Jamila bint Abi ibn Salul:
m: that she was with Thabit ibn Qays and rebelled against him, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to her and said: O Jamila, what do you dislike about Thabit? She said: By God, I do not dislike his religion or his character, except that I dislike his ugliness! So he said to her: Will you return the garden? She said: Yes. So she returned the garden and they were separated.

x: It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning them - I mean concerning Thabit ibn Qays and his wife.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: This was revealed The verse is about Thabit bin Qais and Habeeba, he said: She complained about him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you return his garden to him? She said: Yes. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and mentioned that to him, and he said: Would that please me? He said: Yes. Thabit said: I have done it. Then the verse was revealed: “And it is not lawful for you to take back anything you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God

, then there is no blame upon them for what she gives in ransom. These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them.” As for the people of interpretation, they differed about the meaning of fearing that they will not keep within the limits of God.

x: Some of them said: That is when the woman shows bad character and treatment of her husband, so if that is apparent from her to him, it is permissible for him to take what she gave as ransom for separating from her.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
, unless the rebellion and bad character are on her part, so she calls you to ransom herself from you. Then there is no blame upon you for what she ransomes herself with.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Hisham bin Urwah told me: Urwah used to say: Ransom is not lawful unless the corruption is on her part. And he did not say: It is not permissible for him, until you say: I will not fulfill my oath to you, nor will I wash for you from sexual impurity.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Amr ibn Dinar told me, he said: Jabir ibn Zayd said:
m: If the evil is from her, then the ransom is permissible.

c: Al-Rabi’ ibn Sulayman told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Abi Al-Zinad told me, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah:
m: That his father used to say: If the bad character and bad treatment is from the woman, then her divorce is permissible.

c: Ali ibn Sahl told me, he said: Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father that he said:
m: Divorce is not valid until the corruption is from the woman.

c: Abdul Hamid ibn Bayan Al-Qannad told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Aamer:
m: Concerning a woman who said to her husband: I will not fulfill my oath to you, nor will I obey any command from you, nor will I wash for you from sexual impurity! He said: What is this - and he moved his hand - I will not fulfill my oath to you, nor will I obey any command from you!! If a woman hates her husband, let him take her and leave her.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair
m: that he said, regarding a woman who has been granted khul‘: He should advise her, and if she desists, otherwise he should abandon her. If she desists, otherwise he should beat her. If she desists, otherwise he should refer her case to the ruler, who will send an arbitrator from his people and an arbitrator from her people. The arbitrator from her people will say: Do such and such to her and do such and such to her! And the arbitrator from his people will say: Do such and such to him and do such and such to him. Whichever of them is more unjust, the ruler will return him and take him by the hand. If she is disobedient, he will order her to divorce him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Ja‘far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi‘,
m: regarding His statement: Divorce is twice, then keep [her] in an acceptable Surat Al-Baqarah 2:229 Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God

, then there is no blame upon them for what she has given herself in ransom. These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses The limits of God, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. manner to His statement:
h
There is no blame upon them for that by which she ransoms herself

, he said: If the woman is content, happy and obedient, it is not permissible for him to hit her until she ransoms herself from him. If he takes something from her for that, then whatever he takes from her is forbidden. If the rebellion, hatred and injustice are on her part, then it is permissible for him to take from her what she ransomed herself with.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God

, he said: It is not permissible for a man to divorce his wife unless she gives that to him. As for him harming her until she divorces him, then that is not right. If she is rebellious and shows him hatred and treats him badly, then it is permissible for him to divorce her.

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
, he said: The dowry,
h
Unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God

- and the limits of God are that the woman is rebellious, for God has commanded the husband to admonish her with the Book of God, and if she accepts, then fine, otherwise he should abandon her. Desertion means that he does not have intercourse with her or lie with her in the same bed, and turns his back to her and does not speak to her. If she refuses, he should speak harshly to her and curse her so that she will return to his obedience. If she refuses, he should beat her, but not severely. If she refuses except with impurity, then he is permitted to pay her a ransom.

x: Others said: Rather, the fear of that is that she will not fulfill her oath to him, nor obey his command, and say: I will not bathe for you after sexual impurity, nor obey any command of yours! Then, according to them, it is permissible for him to take what he gave her in exchange for his separation from her.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, he said, al-Hasan said:
m: If she says: I will not bathe for you after sexual impurity, nor fulfill any oath of yours, nor obey any command of yours, then at that time, khul’ is permissible. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, Abd al-A’la narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: If a woman says to her husband: I will not fulfil my oath with you, nor will I obey any command of yours, nor will I perform ritual ablution for you, nor will I carry out any of the limits of God, then her money is permissible for him. Ibn Humayd narrated, Harun ibn al-Mughira narrated, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salim, who said: I asked al-Sha’bi, saying: When is it permissible for a man to take from his wife’s money? He said: If she shows her hatred and says: I will not fulfil my oath with you, nor will I obey any command of yours. Ibn Humayd narrated, who said: Jarir narrated, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: He was amazed by the statement of someone who said: The ransom is not permissible until you say: I will not perform ritual ablution for you, and he said: The adulterer commits adultery and then performs ritual ablution!

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding the rebellious wife, he said: A woman may disobey her husband and then obey him, but if she disobeys him and does not fulfill his oath, then in that case the ransom is permissible.

c: Musa narrated to me, he said, Amr narrated to us, he said, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them

, it is not permissible for him to take anything from her dowry, unless they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, so if they do not keep within the limits of God, then the ransom is permissible for him, and that is for her to say: By God, I will not keep within my oath to you, nor will I obey anything from you. And I will not honor you, nor will I wash you from sexual impurity, for these are the limits of God. So if the woman says that, then the ransom is permissible for the husband to take and divorce her.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, he said, Anbasa told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Muqsim,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And do not prevent them from marrying you in order to take away part of what you have given them
, unless they commit an immorality
r
(An-Nisa’: 19)
, in the reading of Ibn Mas’ud, he said: If she disobeys you and harms you, then what you took from her is permissible for you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them

, he said: Khul’. He said: And it is not permissible for him unless the woman says: I will not fulfill his oath, nor will I obey his command, so he accepts it for fear that he will mistreat her if he keeps her, and transgress the right. And others said: Rather, the fear of that is that she will initiate a statement to him with her tongue: that she is his. Hating.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam Al-Masry told us, he said, my father and Shuaib bin Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Ayoub bin Musa, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, he said:
m: Khul’ is permissible for a woman to say to her husband: I hate you, and I do not love you, and I fear that I will sleep next to you, and I will not fulfill your right - and she will be content with the Khul’.

x: Others said: Rather, what permits him to take the ransom is the fear that they will not abide by the limits of God from both of them, due to each one of them hating the company of the other.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Hamid bin Mas’adah told us, he said, Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, he said, Aamer said:
m: Her money is permissible for him due to his disobedience and her disobedience.

c: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Tawus said: The ransom is permissible for him as God the Most High said, and he did not say the words of the foolish: I will not fulfill my oath to you, but it is permissible for him The ransom is what God Almighty said, Except if they both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, in what He has imposed on each of them from the other in companionship and friendship.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said:
m: I heard Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say, Except if they both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, he said: In what God has imposed on them in companionship and friendship.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Ibn Shihab told me, he said, Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab told me, he said:
m: Khul’ is not permissible until they both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God in the companionship that is between them.

x: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who recited: It is not permissible for a man to take ransom from his wife for separating from her, until the fear of disobeying God from each of them upon himself - in his negligence in what is required of him from his companion - from both of them, according to what we mentioned from Tawus and Al-Hasan, and those who said their sayings about that. Because God Almighty only permitted the husband to take ransom from His wife, when the Muslims fear that they will not uphold the limits of God.

If the matter is as you have described, then it is obligatory that it be forbidden for the man to accept the ransom from her, if the rebellion is from her less than him, so that he will have the same hatred for her as she does?

The matter in that is contrary to what you thought. That is because her rebellion against him is an invitation for him to fall short in her duty, and to punish her for her bad action towards him, and that is the meaning that requires the Muslims to fear that they will not uphold the limits of God. But if the negligence of each one of them in the duty of the right of his companion has been found, and the bad companionship and relationship has become apparent to the Muslims, then there is no place for fear, since the feared thing has already been found. And the occurrence of something is feared before it happens, but after it happens there is no reason to fear it or to increase its hatred.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement:
h
But if you fear that they will not keep the limits of God - that
is, if it is feared that the husband and the wife will not keep them, then it is forbidden. He has the ransom for fear of them both being wasted.
Some of them said: It is the woman’s belittling of her husband’s rights, her bad obedience to him, and her verbal abuse of him.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God
, then
h
there is no blame upon them for that by which she ransoms herself

. He said: It is her failure to keep within the limits of God, her belittling of her husband’s rights, and her bad character, so she says to him: By God, I will not fulfill my oath to you, nor will I lie down with you, nor will I obey any command of yours. If she does that, then the ransom is permissible for him from her.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yahya bin Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding His statement:
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God
, then
h
there is no blame upon them for that by which she ransoms herself
. He said: If she says: I will not bathe for you from major ritual impurity, then it is permissible for him to take from her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said,
m: Yunus, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, said: Khul’ is permissible when they fear that they will not uphold the limits of God and perform the limits of God in the relationship between them.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: If you fear that they will not obey God.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Sufyan bin Waki’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Aamer:
m: If you fear that they will not uphold the limits of God, he said: That they will not obey God.

c: Muhammad bin Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The limits are obedience.

x: The correct statement in that is: If you fear that they will not uphold what God has made obligatory upon them of the obligations, in what each one of them has made obligatory upon the other of the rights of the other, of the relationship with kindness and good companionship, then there is no blame upon them for what she ransomed herself with. What we narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Al-Sha’bi, and what we narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan and Al-Zuhri may be included in that: Because what is obligatory upon the husband over the wife is obedience to him in what God has made obedience to him obligatory in it, And do not harm him with words, nor refuse him if he calls her for his need, for if she disobeys what God has commanded her to do in this, then she has neglected the limits of God that He has commanded her to establish. As for the meaning of: establishing the limits of God, it is working with them, disobeying them and not neglecting them - and we have explained that before in this book of ours with what indicates its correctness.

What God Almighty means by that is: If you fear, O believers, that the spouses will not fulfill what God has set for each of them over the other of rights and what He has made obligatory for him of duty, and you fear that they will neglect God’s duty and transgress His limits in that, then there is no blame on them in that case for what the woman ransomes herself with from her husband, and there is no blame on them for what this woman gives in exchange for her husband’s separation from her, nor on this for what he takes from her of compensation and compensation for him.

Would the woman be at fault if the harm was from the man in that which she ransomed herself with, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:229 Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God

, then there is no blame upon them for what she has given herself in ransom. These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses The limits of God, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. so there would be no blame on them for what she gave in exchange for her separation, if the rebellion was from her?

If she knew in If she harms him in order to take from her what he gave her, then his harm is only in order to take from her what God has forbidden him to take in the manner in which God has forbidden him to take from her, then she is able to refrain from giving him that in a manner that does not harm her in person or religion or in the loss of a right of hers - because it is not permissible for her to give it to him except in a manner that is willingly given to him by giving it to him in a manner that is permissible for him to take from her. Because when she gives him that which is not permissible for him to take from her, and she is able to prevent him from that in a manner that does not harm her in person or religion or in a right of hers that she fears losing, then she has shared in the sin by giving him that which is not permissible for him to take from her in the manner in which she gave it to him. Therefore, the blame was removed from her if the rebellion was before her, and she gave him what she gave of ransom willingly, seeking thereby her safety and the safety of her companion from burden and sin. And if she gives it to him in this manner, by deserving reward and recompense from God the Most High, she is more deserving, God willing, of blame and hardship.

Therefore, God the Most High said: There is no blame upon them so the hardship was removed from her in what she gave in this manner. The face of the ransom for his separation from her, and from him in what he took from her, since she was giving in the meaning that we described, and he was taking from her what she gave without harm, but rather seeking safety for himself and for her in their religions and avoiding burdens and sin. And his saying: There is no blame upon them may be directed to another face of interpretation: which is that if she had given what she gave of the ransom in a way other than the way that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted for the wife of Thabit bin Qays bin Shammas, and that was because she disliked the morals of her husband, or the ugliness of his character, and the like of that of the matters that people dislike from one another - but on turning from it with her face to another other than him in a way of corruption and what is not permissible for her - it was forbidden for her to give anything in return for her asking him for her separation in that way, because her asking him for separation in that way is a sin on her part.
And that is the woman who has been divorced by khul’ - if she was divorced in that way - whom it was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he called a hypocrite, as:

c: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me, he said,
m: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without a valid reason, God will forbid her the scent of Paradise. And he said: Those who seek divorce by khul’ are hypocrites.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Muzahim bin Dawud bin ‘Ulayyah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Layth bin Abi Sulaym, on the authority of Abu al-Khattab, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah, on the authority of Abu Idris, on the authority of Thawban,
m: the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Those who seek divorce by khul’ are hypocrites.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Hafs bin Bishr told us, he said: Qays bin al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Ash’ab bin Suwar, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Thabit bin Yazid, on the authority of ‘Uqbah bin ‘Amir al-Juhani, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those who seek divorce by khul’ are hypocrites.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab told us, and Ya’qub told me, he said: Ibn ‘Ulayyah told us, they both said:
m: Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Thawban: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Any woman who asks her husband for a divorce without a valid reason, the fragrance of Paradise will be forbidden to her.’”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, ‘Arim told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Asma’ al-Rahbi, on the authority of Thawban, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. So if there are ways in which a woman can redeem herself from her husband that would cause her hardship, and she is subject to that hardship and sin in redeeming herself, and there are ways in which the hardship and sin are on the man but not the woman - and there are ways in which they are subject to both of them - and there are ways in which they are not subject to hardship or sin, it was said regarding the way in which there is no hardship or sin on them, since it was in what they tried and intended from their separation with the reward that the woman gave to her husband: There is no sin on them in what she redeems herself with, from the way that was permitted to them, and that is that they fear that they will not uphold the limits of God, with each one of them standing with the other. Abu Ja'far: Some Arabists have claimed that there are two aspects to this: One of them: That what is meant by it is: There is no blame on the man for what the woman redeems herself with, but not the woman, even though they are both mentioned, as He said in Surat al-Rahman 55:From them come forth pearls and coral (al-Rahman 55:22) and they are from salt, not fresh water. He said: And similar to it is: And when they reached the place where they met, they forgot their fish (al-Kahf 18:61), and the one who forgot was the companion of Moses alone. He said: And similar to it in speech is that you say: I have two beasts that I ride and draw water from, and you ride one of them and draw water from the other, and this is from the breadth of Arabic that is used as evidence for its breadth in speech. They said: And the other aspect: That they both share in that there is no blame on them, since she gives what the husband has been denied in sin. She shares in it, because if she gives what sin is thrown away, she needs something like that.

x: So he did not hit the mark in either of the two aspects, nor in his argument in what he used as evidence from His saying: From them come forth pearls and coral (al-Rahman 55:22). As for his saying: There is no blame upon them, we have explained the correctness of it, and we will explain the correctness of his saying: There come out of them pearls and coral (al-Rahman 55:22) in its place when we come to it, God willing. We only made a mistake in saying that, because God Almighty has informed us about His placing of hardship on the spouses if the woman ransomes herself from her husband according to what He permitted, and He informed us about the two seas that pearls and coral come out of them, so He added to two. So if it is permissible for someone to say: What is meant by it is only the report about one of them, in what is not impossible for it to be about them, then it is permissible in every report that is about two people - and it is not impossible for it to be correct for it to be about them - to say: It is only the report about one of them.

And that is reversing the concept from the speech of the people and what is known from their usage in their conversations. And it is not permissible to interpret the Book of God Almighty and His revelation, may He be glorified, on the oddities of speech, and it has a correct and existing aspect in the concept that is current among the people.

Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: There is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with, meaning that they are removed from them. Is the wing in everything that the woman redeemed herself with, or in some of it?

Some of them said: What is meant by that is: There is no blame upon them for what she redeems herself with from her dowry that her husband from whom she is seeking divorce had given her. They argued for their statement that the end of the verse is a reference to the beginning, and that the meaning of the statement is: It is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them unless they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God

, then there is no blame upon them for what she redeems herself with from what you have given them. They said: What God has made lawful for them from that - when they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God - is what was forbidden to them before the fear of that for them. They argued for that with the story of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, “and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only ordered his wife, when she rebelled against him, to return what Thabit had given her as dowry, and that she offered more but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not accept it.”
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: that he was He said: It is not permissible for him to take from her more than what he gave her. And he said: God says: There is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with, meaning: of the dowry - and this is how he used to recite it: for what she ransomed herself with from him.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Hakam told us, he said, Bishr ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, he said:
m: I heard Amr ibn Shu’ayb, Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, and Al-Zuhri say about the rebellious woman: He should not take from her except what he gave her.

c: Ali ibn Sahl told us, he said, Al-Walid told us, Abu Amr told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: The rebellious woman, he should not take from her except what he gave her.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Mu’ammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’:
m: that he disliked taking more in the divorce than he gave her.

c: Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za’idah told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: He disliked for a man to take from the divorced woman more than what he gave her. And he thought that he should take less than that.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman told us
m: He said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: He should not take from her more than what he gave her.

c: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me,
m: who said: Hisham told us, who said: Ismail bin Salim told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: He disliked taking from her more than what he gave her - meaning the woman who had been divorced by Khula’.

c: Abu Kurayb and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us,
m: who said: Ibn Idris told us, who said: I heard Layth, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to say: He should not take from the woman who had been divorced by Khula’ more than what he gave her.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us,
m: who said: Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, who said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, that he said about the woman who had been divorced by Khula’: I prefer that he not take more.

c: Al-Muthanna told me,
m: who said: Hajjaj told us, who said: Hammad told us, on the authority of Hamid: Al-Hasan disliked taking from her more than what he gave her.

c: Muhammad bin Yahya told us,
m: who said: Abdul A’la told us, who said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Matar: He asked Al-Hasan - or: Al-Hasan was asked - about a man who married a woman for two hundred dirhams, and he wanted to divorce her. Is it permissible for him to take four hundred? He said: No, by God, that is to take from her more than what he gave her!

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, he said:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: He should not take from her more than what he gave her. Muammar said: It was reported to me from Ali that he used to think that he should not take from her more than what he gave her.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, from Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Ibn al-Musayyab, he said:
m: I do not like to take from her everything that he gave her, until he leaves her from it what will sustain her.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said:
m: Abd Surat Al-Baqarah 2:229 Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God

, then there is no blame upon them for what she has given herself in ransom. These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses The limits of God, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said:

c: Muammar narrated to us, from Ibn Tawus:
m: that his father used to say about the woman who ransomed herself: It is not permissible for him to take from her more than what he gave her.

c: Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, he said:
m: It is not permissible for a man to take from his wife more than what he gave her.

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by that is: There is no blame upon them for what she ransomed herself with from Little of what you own and much of it. They argued for their statement by the generality of the verse, and that it is not permissible to refer a general appearance to a specific interior meaning except with an argument that must be accepted. They said: There is no argument that must be accepted that the verse is intended to refer to some of the ransom and not some, from a principle or analogy, so it is according to its apparent meaning and generality.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Katheer,
m: the freed slave of Samura: that a rebellious woman was brought to Umar, so he ordered her to be taken to the house of Katheer al-Zabl for three days, then he called for her and said: How did you find her? She said: I have not found comfort since I was with him except these nights that kept me locked up! So he said to her husband: Take it off even if it is just her earring.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Katheer,
m: the freed slave of Samura, he said: Umar bin al-Khattab took a rebellious woman and admonished her, but she did not accept good, so he locked her up in the house of Katheer al-Zabl for three days, and he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Ibn Ulayyah. Ibn Bashar and Muhammad bin Yahya said, Abd al-A’la told us, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman: That a woman came to Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and complained about her husband, so he said: She is disobedient. So he made her stay in the dunghill, and when morning came he said to her: How did you find your place? She said: I have never been with him on a night that was more pleasing to my eyes than this night! So he said: Take even her turban.

c: Nasr ibn Ali told us, Abd al-A’la told us, Ubaydullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’:
m: That a female slave of Safiyyah sought divorce from her husband with everything she owned except her clothes, and Ibn Umar did not find fault with that.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, they said, Mu’tamir told us,
m: he heard Ubaydullah narrating, on the authority of Nafi’: It was mentioned to Ibn Umar that a female slave of his sought divorce from her husband with all her wealth, so he did not find fault with her or disapprove of that.

c: Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu’i told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Raja’ ibn Haywah, on the authority of Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb:
m: He did not see any harm in taking from her more than he had given her, then he recited this verse:
h
There is no blame upon them for that by which she ransoms herself

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said
m: regarding khul’: Take what is less than the knot of her hair, even if the woman ransoms herself with some of her money.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: Khul’ is less than the knot of her head.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja’far narrated to us, saying: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he said
m: regarding the woman who has been divorced by khul’: Take from her even if it is her knot.

c: Ya’qub narrated to me, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Mughira narrated to us, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: Khul’ is less than the knot of her head, and the woman may ransom herself with some of her money.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil: that al-Rabi’ bint Mu’adh ibn ‘Afra’ She told him:
m: I had a husband who would belittle me when he was present, and deprive me when he was away. She said: One day I made a mistake, so I said: I will divorce you for everything I own! He said: Yes! She said: So I did. She said: My uncle Muadh ibn Afra’ took the dispute to Uthman ibn Affan, and he approved the divorce, and ordered him to take the knot of my head or something less than it - or she said: something less than the knot of my head.
b.via: that al-Rabi’ bint Mu’adh ibn ‘Afra’ She

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told me: Habban ibn Musa told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us: al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: There is no problem with what he divorced her for, whether little or much, even if he tied it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Habban ibn Musa told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: If he wishes, he may take from her more than what he gave her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Jurayj told us: Amr ibn Dinar told me that he heard Ikrimah said:
m: Ibn Abbas said: He should take from her even her earring - meaning in the case of khul’.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Mutraf bin Abdullah told us, he said, Malik bin Anas told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of a female slave of Safiyyah bint Abi Ubaid:
m: That she sought khul’ from her husband with everything she had, and Abdullah bin Umar did not deny that.
b.via: a female slave of Safiyyah bint Abi Ubaid

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, he said, Hamid told us, on the authority of Raja bin Haywah, on the authority of Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb:
m: that he recited this verse: There is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with He said: He takes more than what he gave her.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Yazid and Sahl bin Yusuf and Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Humayd, he said:
m: I said to Raja bin Haywah: Al-Hasan says about the woman who sought khul’: He should not take more than what he gave her, and he interpreted,
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
. Raja said: Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb permitted taking more than what he gave her, and he interpreted, There is no blame upon them. In what she ransomed herself with.”

x: Others said: This verse was abrogated by His saying:
h
And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount
, do not take from it anything
r
(An-Nisa’: 20)
Mention of those who said that:

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Abd al-Samad bin Abd al-Warith told us, he said: Uqbah bin Abi al-Sahba’ told us, he said:
m: I asked Bakr about a woman who has been divorced by khul’, can he take anything from her? He said: No! And he recited: And they have taken from you a solemn covenant
r
(An-Nisa’: 21)

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hajjaj told us, he said: Uqbah bin Abi al-Sahba’ told us, he said:
m: I asked Bakr bin Abdullah, about a man whose wife wants him to divorce her, he said: It is not permissible for him to take anything from her. I said: God Almighty says! Mentioned in His Book: There is no blame upon them concerning that by which she ransomed herself? He said: This was abrogated. I said: How did you memorize it? He said: I memorized in Surat An-Nisa’ the saying of God Almighty:
h
And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount
, do not take from it anything
r
(An-Nisa’: 20)

x: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: If it is feared that the man and the woman will not uphold the limits of God - in the manner we have explained - then there is no blame upon them for what the woman redeems herself with from her husband, from what little or much she owns, from what is permissible for Muslims to own, even if that comes to all of her property. Because God, the Most High, mentioned, did not specify what He permitted them of that to a limit that cannot be exceeded, rather He made that general in everything that she redeems herself with. However, I choose for the man, as a recommended and not an imperative, if it becomes clear from his wife that her redemption from him is not for disobedience to God, but rather out of fear for her religion, that he separates from her without ransom or compensation. If his soul is stingy with that, then he does not reach the point of taking from her all that he gave her.
As for what Bakr ibn ʿAbdullah said, that this ruling in the entire verse is abrogated by His saying:
h
And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given her a ransom
, then you have given her a ransom.
“If one of them gives a great amount of money to you, do not take anything from it.”

This is a meaningless statement, and it is a distraction to clarify his mistake, for two reasons: First: The consensus of all the Companions, Followers, and those who came after them from the Muslims on his mistake, and the permissibility of taking the ransom from the woman who redeems herself for her husband, and in that is sufficient evidence for his mistake from others. Second: The verse in Surat An-Nisa’, God only forbade the husband of the woman from taking from her anything of what he gave her, if the man wanted to replace one wife with another without there being any fear from the Muslims for them, one of them taking the place of the other, that they would not uphold the limits of God, and there is no rebellion from the woman towards the man.

If the matter is thus, then it has been proven that the husband taking money from his wife in a way that compels her and harms her until she gives him something from her money in order to separate from her is forbidden, even if that is a grain of silver or more. As for the verse in Surat Al-Baqarah, it only indicates that God Almighty permitted him to take the ransom from her in a case of fear for them that they would not They establish the limits of God, with the woman’s disobedience and her request to separate from the man, and his desire for her. So the matter that permitted the husband to take ransom from the woman in Surat Al-Baqarah is the opposite of the matter for which he was forbidden to take ransom in Surat An-Nisa, just as the prohibition in Surat An-Nisa is different from the generality and permissibility in Surat Al-Baqarah. Rather, it is permissible in the two rulings to say: one of them is abrogating, if the meanings of the ruling are the same, then the rulings in it are different due to the difference in times and periods.

As for the difference in rulings due to the difference in the meanings of the ruling in one case and one time, this is the ultimate wisdom, and is understood by reason and instinct, and it is from the abrogating and the abrogated in isolation. As for what Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said, that the meaning of the verse is: There is no blame upon them for what she ransoms herself with from him - meaning by that: from what you have given them - it is similar to the statement of Bakr in his claim that his statement: There is no blame upon them for what she ransoms herself with was abrogated by his statement: And if you have given one of them a great amount, do not take from it anything, because he claimed in the Book of God what is not found in the copies of the Muslims’ Mushafs. It is said to the one who said what he said: The imams of religion whom you know have said that the meaning of that is: There is no blame upon them for what she ransoms herself with from her property, so is there any proof that can be made clear from them other than the claim?

They argued with the apparent meaning of the revelation, and I claimed in it in particular! Then the statement is reversed on him in that, so he will not say a statement in any of that, except that he will impose the same in the other. We have explained the evidence with witnesses to the correctness of the statement of the one who said: The husband may take from her all What the ransomed woman gave, whom God permitted to ransom - in our book, the Book of Al-Latif, so we disliked repeating it in this place.

The Most High meant by that: Those are the landmarks of His chapters between what He has made lawful for you and what He has forbidden for you, O people, so do not transgress what He has made lawful for you from the matters that He has made clear and preferred for you from the lawful, to what He has forbidden for you, so exceed His obedience to disobey Him. And what the Most High meant by His saying: Those are the limits of God, so do not transgress them, are these things that were explained to you in these verses that have passed: from marrying idolatrous Surat Al-Baqarah 2:229 Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.
h
And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them
unless both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
h
But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God
, then there is no blame upon them for what she has given herself in ransom.

These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses The limits of God, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. polytheists, and polytheists marrying Muslim women, to having intercourse with women during menstruation, and what was explained in the verses that passed before His saying: Those are the limits of God, of what He has made lawful for His servants and forbidden for them, and what He has commanded and forbidden. Then the Most High said to them: These things - whose lawful and unlawful I have made clear to you - are My limits, meaning by that: the landmarks of the chapters between My obedience and My disobedience, so do not transgress them, meaning: do not transgress what I have made lawful for you what I have forbidden you, and what I have commanded you to do to what I have forbidden you from, and my obedience to me to disobey me, for whoever transgresses that, meaning whoever goes beyond it and exceeds it, to what I have forbidden or forbidden him, then he is the oppressor - and he is the one who did what he should not do, and put the thing in the wrong place.

We have previously demonstrated the meaning of oppression and its origin with its evidence indicating its meaning, so we disliked repeating it in this place. And similar to what we said in that, the people of interpretation said, even if the words of their interpretation differ from the words of our interpretation, except that the meaning of what they said in that [leads] to the meaning of what we said in it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them means by the limits, obedience.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak
m: regarding his saying: These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them “The limits of God, so do not transgress them.” He says: Whoever divorces for a period other than the waiting period has transgressed and wronged himself, And whoever transgresses the limits of God - it is those who are the wrongdoers.

x: What was mentioned by Ad-Dahhak has no meaning in this context, because no mention was made of divorce during the waiting period, so it is said: Those are the limits of God. Rather, the number of times during which the divorcer has the right to take her back and the number during which he does not have the right to take her back was mentioned, without mentioning the divorce during the waiting period.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The reciters differed in the recitation of that.
Some of them read it as: Except if they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
This is the reading of most of the people of Hijaz and Basra, meaning: Except if the man and woman fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
It has been mentioned that this is in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b: Except if they think that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.

He said: So I mentioned that to Ayoub, so we went to a man who had an old copy of the Qur’an of Ubayy that was from a trustworthy person, so we read it and it said: Except if they think that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God.
Others from the people of Medina and Kufa read it: Except that they fear that they will not be able to establish the limits of God.

As for the one who reads it like that from the people of Kufa, it is mentioned from him that he read it like that, based on the reading of Ibn Masoud, and it is mentioned that in the reading of Ibn Masoud it is: Except that you fear that they will not be able to establish the limits of God.
Reading it like that, based on the reading of Ibn Masoud that was mentioned from him, is wrong.

That is because if Ibn Masoud read it as it was mentioned from him, then he only applied fear to an alone, and that is not proven to be correct, as the poet said: If I die, bury me next to a vine, so that its roots will water my bones after my death.

But the reading of that in this way is correct, unlike the way in which the one we mentioned read it in this way, based on the reading of Abdullah whom we described, but on the condition that what is meant by it when it is read in this way is: Except that they fear that they will not establish the limits of God - or: that they will not establish the limits of God, so the factor in that is other than fear, and fear is a factor in what its agent is not mentioned.

And that is the correct reading according to us, because what follows indicates its correctness, which is His statement: And if you fear that they will not establish the limits of God, so it was clear that the first means: Except that you fear that they will not establish the limits of God.

Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, he said, Anbasa told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Badhima, on the authority of Muqsim, regarding His statement: And do not prevent them from marrying you in order to take away part of what you have given them, unless they commit an immorality (An-Nisa’: 19), in the reading of Ibn Mas’ud, he said: If she disobeys you and harms you, then what you took from her is permissible for you.
And he said: God says: There is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with, meaning: of the dowry - and this is how he used to recite it: for what she ransomed herself with from him.

Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu’i told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Raja’ ibn Haywah, on the authority of Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb: He did not see any harm in taking from her more than he had given her, then he recited this verse: There is no blame upon them for that by which she ransoms herself.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, he said, Hamid told us, on the authority of Raja bin Haywah, on the authority of Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb: that he recited this verse: There is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with He said: He takes more than what he gave her.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding what this statement of God the Most High indicated.

Some of them said: It indicates that if a man divorces his wife with a third divorce, after the two divorces about which God the Most High said: Divorce is twice, then that wife of his is not permissible for him after the third divorce, until she marries another husband - meaning: other than the one who divorced him.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr bin Mu'adh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari' told us, he said, Sa'id told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: God made divorce three, so if he divorces her once, he has more right to her as long as the waiting period has not ended, and her waiting period is three menstrual periods. If the waiting period ends before he takes her back, then she is separated from him by one divorce, and she has more right to herself, and he becomes a suitor among the suitors. So when a man wanted to divorce his wife, he would look at her menstrual period, until she became pure, then he would divorce her with one divorce before her waiting period in the presence of two just witnesses. If he decides to take her back, he may take her back as long as she is in her waiting period. If he leaves her until her waiting period is over, she is separated from him once. If he decides to divorce her after the first divorce while she is in her waiting period, he should wait for her menses, and when she becomes pure, he should divorce her again before her waiting period. If he decides to take her back, he should take her back, and she remains with him on one condition. If he decides to divorce her, he should divorce her a third time when she becomes pure. This is the third about which God, the Most High, said: She is not lawful to him until she marries a husband.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abu Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if he divorces her
, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband, meaning: If he divorces her three times, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: If he divorces her once or twice, then he has the right to take her back as long as the waiting period has not expired. He said: The third is his statement:
h
And if he divorces her - meaning the third time - then he has no right to take her back until she marries another husband

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: something similar.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of As-Suddi:
m: h
And if he divorces her
- after the two divorces - then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband, and this is the third.

x: Others said: Rather, this statement indicates what is required of a man who releases his wife with kindness after the two divorces, about which God the Most High said: Divorce is twice. They said: Rather, God the Most High explained with this statement the ruling of His statement:
h
Or release her with kindness
. Know that if a man releases his wife after the two divorces, then release is not permissible for him in the same way except after another husband.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: But if he divorces her, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband. He said: He returned to His statement:
h
Then keep her in an acceptable manner or release her with kindness

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: What Mujahid said about this is more correct in our view, because of what we mentioned from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the report that we narrated from him that he said - or he was asked and it was said: This is the saying of God the Most High: Divorce is twice. So where is the third? He said: Then keep [her] in an acceptable manner
h
or release [her] with good treatment

. So the Messenger of God (peace and Surat al-Baqarah 2:230 But if he divorces her, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him. But if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them if they return to each other
h
if they think that they can keep within the limits of God
. And these are the limits of God which He makes clear to a people who know. blessings of God be upon him) informed that the third is his saying:
h
Or release [her] with good treatment

So since release with good treatment is the third, then it is known that his saying: But if he divorces her, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband, is an indication of the third divorce in isolation, and that it is only a statement of what is permissible for the one who releases her with good treatment if he releases his wife after the two divorces, and what is forbidden to him from her, and the state in which he is permitted to marry her, and the signs of His servants that after release as described, a man has no right to return to his wife.
If someone were to say: Which of the two marriages did God mean by His statement:
h
Then she shall not be lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him

, the marriage that involves sexual intercourse, or the marriage that is a marriage contract? It was said: Both. That is because if a woman marries a man in a marriage contract, and he does not have intercourse with her in that marriage until he divorces her, she is not lawful to the first. Likewise, if he has intercourse with her without marriage, she is not lawful to the first by the consensus of the entire ummah. Since that is the case, it is known that the interpretation of His statement:
h
Then she shall not be lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him is a valid marriage
, then he has intercourse with her in that marriage, then he divorces her.
If the mention of sexual intercourse is not found in the Book of God, the Most High, then what is the evidence that its meaning is what you said?
The evidence for that is the consensus of the entire ummah that that is its meaning.
And then, God the Most High said:
h
And if he divorces her

, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him. So if she marries a husband other than him after the divorce before the end of her waiting period, then there is no doubt that she is married in a marriage other than the meaning in which God the Most High permitted her to do so, even if the mention of the waiting period was not accompanied by His saying:
h
And she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him
, because He indicated that this is the case by His saying: And divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods. And likewise His saying:
h
And if he divorces her

, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him, even if the mention of intercourse, touching, and penetration was not accompanied by it, it indicated that this is the case, by His revelation to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and His clarification of this on His tongue to His servants.
He mentioned the reports narrated about this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Ubayd God ibn Ismail al-Habbari, Sufyan ibn Wakee’, and Abu Hisham al-Rafa’i told me:

c: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of al-Aswad, on the authority of Aisha, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who divorced his wife and she married another man, and he consummated the marriage with her and then divorced her before having intercourse with her. Is she permissible for her first husband? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: She is not permissible for her first husband until the other husband tastes her honey and she tastes his honey.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, he said:
m: I heard her say: “The wife of Rifa’ah Al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I was with Rifa’ah and he divorced me, so my divorce was final, and I married Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Zubayr, and he has nothing but the hem of a garment! So he said to her: Do you want to go back to Rifa’ah? No, not until you taste his honey and he tastes your honey.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me:
m: That Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told him: That the wife of Rifa’ah Al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha:
m: “Rifa’ah al-Qurazi divorced his wife and her divorce was final, then he married her after Abd al-Rahman bin al-Zubayr. She came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, she was with Rifa’ah, and he divorced her the last of the three divorces. Then she married Abd al-Rahman bin al-Zubayr after him, and by God, he has nothing with him, O Messenger of God, except something like a tuft of hair. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled and said to her: Perhaps you want to go back to Rifa’ah! No, not until you taste his honey and I taste your honey. She said: Abu Bakr was sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Khalid bin Sa’id bin al-’As was at the gate of al-Harjah, and he had not been given permission. Khalid began to call out to Abu Bakr, saying: O Abu Bakr, will you not stop this woman from what she is saying openly in the presence of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?”

c: Muhammad bin Zaid Al-Adami told us, Yahya bin Salim told us, on the authority of Ubaid God, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha,
m: “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, until he tastes of her honey what he tasted the first time.”

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I heard Ubayd God say, I heard Al-Qasim narrating on the authority of Aisha, he said, she said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, until he tastes from her honey what his companion tasted.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Ubayd God, he said, Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Aisha:
m: “A man divorced his wife three times, so she married a husband who divorced her before he touched her. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Is she permissible for the first wife? He said: No, until he tastes her honey as the first wife tasted.”

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, Musa bin Isa Al-Laithi told us, on the authority of Zaida, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid,
m: On the authority of Umm Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a man divorces his wife three times, she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband, and each of them tastes the honey of the other.

c: Al-Abbas ibn Abi Talib told me, he said, Saad ibn Hafs al-Talhi told us, he said, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Abu al-Harith al-Ghifari, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Until he tastes her honey.

c: Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-Asqalani told me, he said, my father told me, he said, Shaiban told us, he said, Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us, on the authority of Abu al-Harith al-Ghifari, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about a woman whose husband divorces her three times, then she marries another husband, and he divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, and the first husband wants to take her back, he said: No, until he tastes her honey.”

c: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Anmati told me, he said, Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Dinar told us, he said, Yahya ibn Yazid al-Hana’i told us, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik,
m: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a man who divorced his wife three times, and another man married her and divorced her before consummating the marriage: Can she return to her first husband? He said: No, until he tastes her honey and she tastes his honey.”

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim and Yaqub ibn Mahan told me, they said: Hisham told us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Yasar, on the authority of Ubayd God, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: That Al-Ghamisa’ - or Al-Rumaisa’ - came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, complaining about her husband, and claiming that he did not have intercourse with her. He said: It was not long before her husband came and claimed that she was lying, but that she wanted to return to her first husband. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are not allowed to do so until another man tastes your honey.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad, on the authority of Salim ibn Razin al-Ahmari, on the authority of Salim ibn ʿAbdullah, on the authority of Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar,
m: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a man who marries a woman and then divorces her before consummating the marriage, and she marries another husband who divorces her before consummating the marriage: Can she return to the first one? He said: No, until she tastes his honey and he tastes her honey.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad, on the authority of Razin al-Ahmari, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was asked about a man who divorces his wife three times, and a man marries her, and he closes the door and divorces her before consummating the marriage with her: Can she return to her other husband? He said: No, until he tastes her honey.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Murthad, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Razin, on the authority of Ibn Umar:
m: He asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was giving a sermon, about a man who divorced his wife and she married after him, then he divorced her or died: Can the first one marry her? He said: No, until she tastes his honey.

x: God Almighty means by His statement: If he divorces her, that if the woman who was separated from her husband by the last of the three divorces, after her second divorcer married her, divorced her husband who married her after her separation from the first, there is no blame upon them, God Almighty says: There is no blame upon the woman who was divorced by this second: after her separation from the first, and after his marriage to her - and upon the first husband to whom she was forbidden by her separation from him by the last of the divorces, to return to each other with a new marriage, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muʿawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: If he divorces her, there is no blame upon them if they return to each other
h
if they think that they can keep within the limits of God

, he says: If she marries after the first and the other consummates the marriage with her, there is no blame upon the first to marry her if the other divorces her or dies, for she is permissible for him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Juwaybir told us,
m: on the Surat al-Baqarah 2:230 But if he divorces her, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him. But if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them if they return to each other
h
if they think that they can keep within the limits of God

. And these are the limits of God which He makes clear to a people who know. authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: If he divorces one or two times, he has the right to take her back, as long as the waiting period has not expired. He said: The third is his statement:
h
If he divorces her meaning the third time

, so he has no right to take her back until she marries another husband and he has consummated the marriage with her. If he divorces her this last one is after he has consummated the marriage with her, there is no blame upon them if they return to each other meaning the first one,
h
if they think they can keep within the limits of God

x: As for his statement:
h
If they think they can keep within the limits of God

, its meaning is if they hope to keep within the limits of God. Keeping within the limits of God means acting upon them. The limits of God are what He has commanded them to do and made obligatory for each one of them upon the other, and He has made obligatory for each one of them because of the marriage that is between them. We have explained the meaning of the limits and the meaning of keeping them, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
Mujahid used to say in his interpretation of His statement:
h
If they think that they can keep within the limits of God
, what:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
If they think that they can keep within the limits of God
, if they think that their marriage is not based on deception.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: Some of the people of interpretation have interpreted His statement: If they think to mean: if we are certain. And that is baseless, because no one knows what will happen except God, the Most High. So if that is the case, then what is the meaning by which a man and a woman are certain that if they reconcile, they will keep within the limits of God? But the meaning of that, as God, the Most High, said: If they think, is: hoping for that and hoping for it. And that which is in His statement: that they can keep within, is in the accusative case with thinking. And the an in an yatarajaa, some of the Arabists put it in the accusative case due to the absence of the preposition, because the meaning of the statement is: There is no blame upon them if they retreat - so when it was deleted in what was making it a genitive, it was made a genitive, as if he said: There is no blame upon them if they retreat.
And some of them said: Its position is a genitive, even if it does not have a preposition with it, and if it is deleted, its position is known.
What the Almighty means by His statement,
h
And these are the limits set by God

, are these matters that He has made clear to His servants regarding divorce, taking back a wife, ransom, waiting period, ila’, and other matters that He makes clear to them in these verses. The limits set by God – the features of the chapters of what is lawful and unlawful, obedience to Him and disobedience to Him. He makes them clear, He distinguishes between them, and He makes their rulings known to them, for a people who know them when God makes them clear to them, and they know that they are from God, so they believe in them and act according to what God has deposited in them of His knowledge, unlike those whose hearts God has sealed and decreed that they do not believe in them and do not believe that they are from God, for they are ignorant that they are from God and that they are a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy.

For this reason, He singled out the people who know with the clarification, not those who are ignorant, since those who are ignorant that they are from Him, His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had despaired of many of them believing in them, even though he had made them clear to them as a proof against them and obligated them to act according to it. Rather, he excluded it from being a statement to them, due to their failure to acknowledge and believe in it.

God Almighty means by that: And when you divorce, O men, your women, and they have fulfilled their term, meaning: their appointed time for them, from the expiration of the three menstrual periods, if she is one of the menstruating women, and the expiration of the months, if she is one of the months, then keep them, meaning: then take them back if you want to take them back in the divorce in which there is a return: and that is either in one divorce or two divorces, as God Almighty said: Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] according to acceptable terms or release [her] with good treatment. As for His saying: according to acceptable terms, he meant: with what He permitted of taking her back, from having witnesses to taking her back before the expiration of the waiting period, without taking her back by intercourse and sexual intercourse.
