Because that is only permissible for the man after the return, and in good health with that and the treatment as God has commanded and made clear to you, O people, or release them on good terms, meaning: or let them complete their waiting period and the rest of their term that you have set for them ends according to their number, on good terms.
He says: by fulfilling their full rights over you, in accordance with what you have obligated you to do for them of dowry, compensation, maintenance, and other rights that they have had before you,
h
and do not keep them

, to harm them, in order to transgress, meaning: and do not take them back, if you take them back in their waiting period, to harm them, in order to prolong the period of their waiting period, or to take from them some of what you gave them by their requesting a khul’ from you, in order to harm them by keeping them and taking them back, to harm them and transgress. And his saying: So that you may transgress, he says: So that you may wrong them by exceeding in your affair the limits which I have made clear to you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dahha, on the authority of Masruq:
m: h
And do not keep them

, to cause them harm, he said: He divorces her, until when her waiting period is about to end, he takes her back, then he divorces her, and leaves her until when her waiting period is about to end, he takes her back, and he does not want to keep her: that is the one who causes harm and takes the signs of God in jest.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said:
m: Al-Hasan was asked about the saying of God the Most High: “
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, either keep them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms.
h
And do not keep them
, to cause them harm, to transgress,” he said: A man would divorce a woman then take her back, then divorce her then take her back, harming her, so God forbade them from that.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, either keep them according to acceptable terms or release Surat Al-Baqarah 2:231
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, either keep them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms.
h
And do not keep them
to harm them in order to transgress. And whoever does that has certainly wronged himself.
h
And do not take the verses of God in jest
, and remember the favor of God upon you and what He has sent down to you of the Book and wisdom.
h
He admonishes you with it
. Fear God
h
and know that God is Knowing of all things

. them according to acceptable terms, he said: God forbade harm, harm, that a man divorces his wife and then takes her back on the last day remaining of the term, until he has fulfilled nine months for her, in order to harm her thereby.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: He forbade harm, and harm in divorce is that a man divorces his wife and then takes her back. The rest of the hadith is like the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr.

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me, he said, my father told us, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, either keep them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms. But do not keep them for harm in order to aggravate [your waiting period],” a man would divorce his wife and then take her back before the end of her waiting period, then divorce her. He did that to harm her and make things difficult for her, so God revealed this verse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding His statement: “
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, either keep them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms.
h
And do not keep them

for harm in order to aggravate [your waiting period],” he said: A man would divorce his wife once, then leave her, until her waiting period was almost over, then he would take her back, then he would divorce her, until her waiting period was almost over, then he would take her back. He had no need for her, he only wanted to harm her by doing that. God forbade that and advanced in it, and said: And whoever does that has wronged himself.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: God the Most High said:
m: h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, either keep them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms.
h
And do not keep them

to cause harm in order to transgress.” So if a man divorces a woman and she has fulfilled her term, then he should take her back according to acceptable terms or release her with kindness, and it is not permissible for him to take her back to cause harm, and he has no desire for her, unless he harms her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And do not keep them

, to injure them, in order to aggravate their condition, he said: It is about a man who swears to divorce his wife, and when any part of her waiting period remains, he takes her back, harming her by doing so and prolonging it for her, so God forbade them from doing that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail ibn Abi Uways told us, on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, on the authority of Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dailami:
m: That a man would divorce his wife and then take her back, and he had no need for her and did not want to keep her, in order to prolong her waiting period in order to harm her, so God, the Most High, revealed: “
h
And do not keep them
, to injure them, in order to aggravate their condition. And whoever does that has wronged himself,” extolling that.

c: I was told by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj,
m: he said, I heard Abu Muadh al-Fadl ibn Khalid, he said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman al-Bahili told us, he said, I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And do not keep them

, to injure them, it is a man who divorces his wife once, then… He returns to her, then divorces her, then returns to her, then divorces her, to harm her thereby, so that she may seek a divorce from him.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, either keep them according to acceptable terms or release them according to acceptable terms.
h
And do not keep them
, [even] for harm, in order to aggravate [their] waiting period. And whoever does that has wronged himself.
h
And do not take the verses of God in jest

.” He said: It was revealed about a man from the Ansar called Thabit ibn Yasar, who divorced his wife, and when her waiting period had expired except for two or three days, he took her back, then divorced her, and did that to her until nine months had passed, harming her, so God, the Most High, revealed:
h
And do not keep them
, [even] for harm, in order to aggravate [their] waiting period.

c: Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid told me, he said, my father told me,
m: he heard Abdul Aziz being asked about the divorce of harm, so he said: He divorces then takes her back, then divorces then takes her back. This is the harm that God said:
h
And do not keep them
, [even] for harm, in order to aggravate [their] waiting period.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Abu Jaʿfar said:
m: The origin of tasreeh is from saraḥal-qawm, which is what was released from their livestock for grazing. It is said about the livestock sent out for grazing: this is saraḥ al-qawm, meaning their livestock sent out for grazing. And from this is the saying of God the Most High: “And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat. And for you is adornment in them when you drive them back home and when you drive them out to pasture.” (al-Nahl 16:5-6), meaning by His saying: when you drive them out to pasture, when you send them out to graze. It was said to a woman, if her husband leaves her alone and separates her from him: let her go, as an example of letting go of one’s livestock to graze, and as a comparison to it.

x: God Almighty meant by that: And whoever takes his wife back, after divorcing her in the divorce in which he has the right to take her back, to harm her, in order to transgress the limits of God in her matter, has wronged himself, meaning: he has thereby earned her a sin, and has thereby made her incur a punishment from God. We have previously explained the meaning of injustice, and that it is putting something in the wrong place, and doing what the doer is not supposed to do.

He, the Most High, means: And do not take the signs of God and His sections between what is lawful and unlawful, and His commands and prohibitions, in His revelation and sending down, as a mockery and a game, for He has made clear to you in His sending down and the verses of His Book, what you have of returning to your women, in the divorce in which He has made it permissible for you to return to them, and what you do not have of them, and what is the permissible aspect for you from them, and what is not permissible, and what is the divorce in which you have to return to them, and what you do not have of them, and how the aspects of that are, as a mercy from Him to you and a blessing from Him to you, so that He may make for some of you, from what is disliked, if there is something in it from its owner that harms him, the way out and salvation through divorce and separation, and He made what He has made for you from returning to them a way for you to reach what he has disputed with him and what his desires have called him to, after his separation from them from them, so that you may thereby attain the satisfaction of your desires from them, as a blessing from Him to you. Do not take what I have made clear to you of that in the verses of My Book and My revelation - as a favor from Me in explaining it to you, and as a favor and mercy from Me to you - as a game and a mockery.
And in the meaning: What we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Shabawayh told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Ayoub bin Sulayman told us, he said, Abu Bakr bin Abi Awshi told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Bilal, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Atiq and Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sulayman bin Arqam: that Al-Hasan told them:
m: That the people were during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a man would be divorced or freed, and it would be said: What did you do? He would say: I was only joking! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever divorces or frees a woman in jest, it is permissible for him to do so. Al-Hasan said: And it was in this regard that the verse, ‘
h
And do not take the verses of God in jest
,’ was revealed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And do not take the verses of God in jest

, he said: A man would divorce his wife and say, ‘I only divorced her in jest!’ Then he would marry, free her, or give charity, and he would say, ‘I only did it in jest!’” They were forbidden from doing that, and God Almighty said:
h
And do not take the verses of God in jest

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ishaq bin Mansur told us, on the authority of Abd al-Salam bin Harb, on the authority of Yazid bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu al-Ala’, on the authority of Hamid bin Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Musa:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry with the Ash’aris. Abu Musa came to him and said: O Messenger of God, you became angry with the Ash’aris! He said: One of you says: I have divorced, I have taken her back. This is not the divorce of Muslims. Divorce a woman before her waiting period.”

c: Abu Zaid told us, on the authority of Ibn Shabah, who said: Abu Ghassan al-Nahdi told us,
m: who said: Abd al-Salam ibn Harb told us, on the authority of Yazid Abu Khalid - meaning al-Dalani - on the authority of Abu al-Ala al-Awdi, on the authority of Hamid ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Why does one of you say to his wife: I have divorced you, I have taken you back? This is not the divorce of Muslims. Divorce the woman before her period of purity.”

x: By that, the Most High means: And remember the blessing of God upon you through Islam, which He bestowed upon you and guided you to it, and all of His blessings that He has given you over all of His creation, so thank Him for that by obeying Him in what He has commanded you and forbidden you from, and also remember with that what He has sent down to you from His Book, which is: the Qur’an that He sent down to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and remember that and act upon it and observe His limits in it, and wisdom means: and what He has sent down to you of wisdom, which are the Sunnahs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught you and prescribed for you. I have mentioned the difference of opinion among those who differed regarding the meaning of wisdom previously in His statement:
h
And He teaches them the Book and wisdom (al-Baqarah 2
:129), so there is no need to repeat it in this place.
By His statement:
h
He admonishes you with it

, the Most High means He admonishes you with the Book that He has sent down to you, and the ha in His statement: with it refers back to the Book. And fear God, meaning: And fear God, in what He has commanded you to do and in what He has forbidden you to do in His Book which He has revealed to you, and in what He has revealed and explained to you through the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, lest you neglect it and transgress its limits, and thus deserve what you cannot bear of His painful punishment and humiliating torment. And His statement:
h
And know that God is Knowing of all things

, meaning: And know, O people, that your Lord, who has set these limits for you, and prescribed these laws for you, and imposed these duties upon you, in His Book and in His revelation to His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of everything you do - good or evil, good or bad, obedience or disobedience - is All-Knowing, and nothing of that is hidden from Him, whether it is apparent or hidden, whether it is secret or public, and He will reward you for good with good and for evil with evil, unless He pardons and forgives, so do not expose yourselves to His punishment and wrong yourselves.

It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about a man who had a sister who was married to her cousin, but he divorced her and left her without taking her back until her waiting period was over. Then he proposed to her from him, but he refused to marry her to him and prevented her from him, and she was willing to marry him. Then the people of interpretation differed about the man who did that, so this verse was revealed about him.
Some of them said that the man was: Mu'qil bin Yasar Al-Muzani.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told me, he said, Abdul Ala told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Mu'qil bin Yasar, who said:
m: His sister was married to a man, so he divorced her, then he left her, and when her waiting period was over, he proposed to her. Mu'qil became angry about that, and said: He left her while he was able to have her!! So he stood between him and her, so God the Most High revealed:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Dahlam, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Muqal bin Yasar:
m: That his sister was divorced by her husband, and he wanted to take her back, but Muqal prevented her, so God the Most High revealed:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands, to the end of the verse.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Mukhrami narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Ibad bin Rashid narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Muqal bin Yasar narrated to me, saying:
m: I had a sister who was being proposed to, but people prevented her, until my cousin proposed to me, so I married her, and they stayed together for as long as God willed, then he divorced her with a revocable divorce, then he left her until her waiting period ended, then she proposed to me, so he came to propose to her with the suitors, so I said to him: She proposed to me but people refused her, so I preferred her to you, then I divorced her with a revocable divorce. When she proposed to me, you came to me to propose to her with the suitors! By God, I will never marry her! He said: So this verse was revealed:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis. He said: So I atoned for my oath and married her to him.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, from Qatada:
m: h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis. He mentioned to us that a man divorced his wife with one divorce, then he was separated from her until her waiting period was over, then he came close after that to propose to her, and the woman was the sister of Muqal bin Yasar, so Muqal bin Yasar was disgusted by that and said: He was separated from her while she was in her waiting period, and if he wanted to, he could take her back, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:232
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis. This is instructed to whoever among you believes in God and the Last Day. That is
h
purer for you

and better. And God knows, while you do not know. then he wants to take her back now that she has separated from him! So he refused to marry her to him. He told us that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet of God called him and recited it to him, so he abandoned his zeal and submitted to God’s command.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the words of God the Almighty:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands, to the end of the verse. He said: This verse was revealed about Ma’qil ibn Yasar. Al-Hasan said: Ma’qil ibn Yasar told me that it was revealed about him. He said: I married my sister to a man and he divorced her. When her waiting period was over, he came to propose to her. I said to him: I married you to my sister and provided for you and honored you, then I divorced her, then you came to propose to her! She will never come back to you! He said: He was a truthful man, there was nothing wrong with him, and the woman loved to come back to him. God the Almighty said:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an acceptable basis. He said: I said: Now I will do it, O Messenger of God!

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, Yahya ibn Wadheeh narrated to us, Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us, on the authority of Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani, who said:
m: The sister of Muqal ibn Yasar was married to a man and he divorced her. He proposed to him but her brother refused her, so this verse was revealed:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
to the end of the verse.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands the verse, he said: It was revealed about a woman from Muzaynah whose husband divorced her and she turned away from him, so another man married her, so her brother Muqal ibn Yasar prevented her, harming her for fear that she would return to her first husband. Ibn Jurayj said: And Ikrimah said: It was revealed about Muqal ibn Yasar. Ibn Jurayj said: His sister Jamal bint Yasar was married to Abu al-Badah. He divorced her, and her waiting period ended, so he proposed to her, but Muqal bin Yasar prevented her.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis, it was revealed about a woman from Muzaynah whose husband divorced her, and her brother prevented her from returning to her first husband, who was Muqal bin Yasar, her brother.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he did not say in it: and he is Muqal bin Yasar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani:
m: That Fatima bint Yasar was divorced by her husband, then he changed his mind and proposed to her, but she refused. Ma'qil said: We married you to her and you divorced her and she did so! Then God revealed:
h
So do not prevent them
from marrying their husbands.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatadah,
m: regarding His statement:
h
So do not prevent them

, he said: It was revealed about Ma'qil bin Yasar. His sister was married to a man and he divorced her. When her waiting period was over, he came and proposed to her, but Ma'qil prevented her and refused to marry her to him. So this verse was revealed about her. He meant the guardians, he said:
h
So do not prevent them
from marrying their husbands.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Muqal ibn Yasar, he said:
m: My sister was with a man and he divorced her with a final divorce, so he proposed to her, but I refused to marry her to him, so God revealed:
h
So do not prevent them
from marrying their husbands, the verse.

x: Others said that man was Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, he said, Amr ibn Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, do not prevent them from marrying their husbands if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis, he said: It was revealed about Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, and he had a cousin and her husband divorced her with a final divorce, so her waiting period ended, then he went back wanting to take her back. As for Jabir, he said: You divorced our cousin, then you want to marry her a second time! The woman wanted her husband and had satisfied him. So this verse was revealed.

x: Others said: This verse was revealed to indicate that a man should not harm his female guardian and prevent her from marrying him.
He mentioned who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
So do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands

, this is about a man who divorces his wife once or twice, and her waiting period expires, then he decides to marry her and take her back, and the woman wants to, but her guardians prevent her from that, so God, the Most High, forbade them from preventing her.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis, a man would divorce his wife, then she would become separated from him and her waiting period would end, and he wanted to take her back and she would agree to that, but her family would refuse, God, the Most High, said:
h
So do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands
if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said,
m: Habban bin Musa said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dahha, on the authority of Masruq, regarding His statement:
h
So do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands
, he said: A man would divorce his wife and then decide to marry her again, but the woman’s guardians would refuse to marry her, so God, the Most High, said:
h
So do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands
if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of his companions, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands, he said: A woman is with a man and he divorces her, then he wants to return to her, so her guardian should not prevent her from marrying him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, al-Layth told me, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: God, the Most High, said:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands, the verse, so if a man divorces a woman And he is her guardian, and her waiting period has ended, so he has no right to prevent her from inheriting from her, and prevent her from seeking a chaste husband.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term

, do not prevent them, that is, a man divorces his wife once, then remains silent about it, so he is a suitor among those who propose. So God said to the guardians of the woman: Do not prevent them, meaning: do not prevent them from returning to their husbands in a new marriage, if they agree among themselves on what is acceptable, if the woman is satisfied and wants to return to her husband in a new marriage.

x: The correct statement regarding this verse is that God, the Most High, revealed it as evidence of His prohibition on the guardians of women from harming those who were guardians of women, by preventing them from those whom they wanted to marry from the husbands they had, so they separated from them by what separates the woman from her husband by divorce or annulment of the marriage. It may have been revealed in the case of Maqal ibn Yasar and his sister, or in the case of Jabir ibn Abdullah and his cousin. Whichever of the two, the verse indicates what I have mentioned. What is meant by the Almighty’s saying:
h
So do not prevent them

is: do not make things difficult for them by preventing them, O guardians, from returning to their husbands in a new marriage, seeking thereby to harm them. It is said: So-and-so prevented so-and-so from marrying, he prevents her, and it was mentioned to us that one of the tribes of the Arabs says: Adhal ya’dhal in their language.

So whoever says Adhal in his language, if he turns to yaf’al, he says: Ya’dhal with the fatha on the dhad. The reading is with the damma on the dhad without the kasra, and the damma is from the language of those who say Adhal. The root of Adhal is narrow, and from this is the saying of Omar, may God have mercy on him: The people of Iraq have made things difficult for me, they are not pleased with my guardian and my guardian is not pleased with them, meaning: they forced me to do something very difficult that I cannot bear to do. It also includes the incurable disease, which is the disease that cannot be treated, because it is difficult to treat and exceeds the limits of medicine. Which has a cure, including the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: I did not throw a horse to a believer, God willing, that is a positive and incurable one. And from this it was said: The space became narrow due to the army’s large number, if it became too narrow for them because of their large number.

And it was said: The woman became narrow, if the child was implanted in her womb and it was too narrow for him to come out of her. And from this is the saying of Aws bin Hajar: Your brother who is always loyal is not the one who criticizes you when he leaves and pleases you when he comes. But it is the distant one if you are safe and your companion is the closest if the matter is difficult And that which is in His statement: that they marry, is in the accusative case with His statement: prevent them from getting married.

The meaning of His statement: if they agree among themselves on what is good, is if the husbands and women agree on what is permissible and may be in exchange for their goods from dowries, and a new, renewed marriage, as:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Umair ibn Abd God, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Marry the widows. A man said: O Messenger of God, what are the relationships between them? He said: What their families agree upon.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn al-Harith told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

x: In this verse is clear evidence of the correctness of the statement of those who say: There is no marriage except with a guardian from the agnates. That is because God Almighty forbade the guardian from preventing the woman if she wanted to marry and forbade him from doing so. So if the woman had the right to marry herself without her guardian’s permission to marry her, or she had the right to appoint someone she wanted to appoint to marry her, then her guardian’s prohibition against preventing her would not have any clear meaning, since he would have no way to prevent her. That is because if whenever she wanted to marry, it Surat Al-Baqarah 2:232
h
And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term
, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands if they agree among themselves on an equitable basis. This is instructed to whoever among you believes in God and the Last Day.
That is
h
purer for you

and better. And God knows, while you do not know. would be permissible for her to marry herself, or to marry someone she had appointed to marry her, then there is no impediment for her from anyone, so her impediment is forbidden from preventing her. In the corruption of the statement that there is no meaning to God’s prohibition of what He prohibited, there is the correctness of the statement that the woman’s guardian has a right to her marriage, and the contract is not valid without him. This is the meaning that God has commanded the guardian to do: to marry her if a suitor proposes to her and she accepts him, and he is satisfied with her guardians, and it is permissible in the ruling of Muslims for her to marry someone like him, and He has forbidden him from doing otherwise: to prevent her, and to prevent her from what she wants from that, and she and the suitor are satisfied with it.

God Almighty means by His saying that, what is mentioned in this verse about the prohibition of the woman’s guardians from preventing her from marriage, He says: This that I have forbidden you from doing of preventing them from marriage, is a lesson from me for whoever among you, O people, believes in God and the Last Day - meaning he believes in God, so he makes Him One and acknowledges His Lordship, and the Last Day He says: And whoever believes in the Last Day, so he believes in the resurrection for recompense, reward and punishment, so that he may fear God in himself, so that he does not wrong her by harming his guardian and preventing her from marrying someone she is satisfied with for herself, from those whom she has given permission to marry.
If someone were to say to us: How is it said: That is an admonition, while it is addressed to all, and He said before:
h
So do not prevent them

? And if it is permissible to say that when addressing all, is it permissible to say to a group of people while you are addressing them: O people, this is your slave, and this is your servant, while you mean: This is your servant, and this is your slave? It is said: No, that is not permissible with the established names, because what the names are added to is something else, so it is not understood. A listener hears someone saying to a group: O people, this is your slave, meaning that he meant this is your slave, unless the speaker makes a mistake in his speech. If he seeks a way to correct his speech, he will divert his speech to the fact that he has turned away from addressing the people with what he intended to address them, to addressing one man from them or from others, and he has left conversing with the people with what he intended to converse with them in speech.

This is not the case in this regard, because this has been so common on the tongues of the Arabs in their speech and language, until the kaf—which is a metaphor for the name of the one being addressed in it—has become like the form of a letter from the letters of the word that is connected. And the word becomes like the saying of the speaker: this, as if there is no name of the one being addressed with it. So whoever says: That is admonished for whoever among you believes in God and the Last Day, he confirms the kaf in that as unified and open when addressing one woman, one man, dual, and plural. And whoever says: That is what is admonished for, he breaks the kaf when addressing one woman, and opens it when addressing one man, and says when addressing two of them: That is what they both say, and when addressing the plural: That is what they say. It has been said that his statement:
h
This is an admonition to whoever among you believes in God

, is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for this reason he made it singular, then he returned to addressing the believers by saying: Whoever among you believes in God.
If the interpretation is directed in this way, there is no difficulty in it.
God Almighty means by His statement: This, - their marriage to their husbands and their husbands returning to them, with what He has permitted them of a new marriage and dowry, is
h
purer for you
, O guardians, husbands and wives. And by His statement:
h
Purer for you

, He means better and more beneficial to God than their husbands separating them. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of zakat, so there is no need to repeat it. As for his saying: and purer, he means by that: purer for your hearts and their hearts and the hearts of your husbands from suspicion. That is because if there is a love relationship in the soul of each of them - I mean the husband and the woman - it is not certain that they will go beyond that to something other than what God has permitted for them, and it is not certain that their guardians will not precede their hearts from them with something that would make them chaste and that they will be innocent of it.

So God, the Most High, commanded the guardians - if the spouses want to return after the separation, with a new marriage, in the case in which they were permitted to return, not to prevent his guardian from what she wanted from that, and to marry her. Because that is better for all of them, and purer for their hearts from what is feared to precede them with hateful meanings. Then the Almighty informed His servants that He knows of their secrets and hidden matters what some of them do not know of others, and He guided them by His words to them in this place, that He only commanded the guardians of women to marry off those whom they were guardians of from women if the woman and the husband who is proposing to marry agree among themselves in a good manner, and He forbade them from preventing them from doing so, because He knew what is in the heart of the suitor and the fiancée of the predominance of desire and the inclination of each one of them towards the other with affection and love, so the Almighty said to them: Do what I have commanded you to do, if you believe in Me, and in My reward and My punishment in your place in the Hereafter, for I know in the heart of the suitor and the fiancée what you do not know of desire and love.
And your doing that is better for you with God and for them, and purer and cleaner for your hearts and their hearts in this life.

evidence.text: He told us that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet of God called him and recited it to him, so he abandoned his zeal and submitted to God’s command.
The reading is with the damma on the dhad without the kasra, and the damma is from the language of those who say Adhal.

x: God Almighty means by that: And the women who have children born to them from their husbands before their separation from them by divorce, or who have children born to them after their separation from them, from intercourse that they had with them before the separation, suckle their children, meaning by that: They are more entitled to suckle them than others. And that is not an obligation from God Almighty upon them to suckle them, if the child is born to him, a living, wealthy child. Because God Almighty said in Surat An-Nisa' Al-Qusra: And if you disagree, then another woman shall suckle for him (al-Talaq 65:6) So God Almighty informed: That if the mother and the child disagree about the wage for which the woman suckles her child, then another woman other than her shall suckle him, so He did not make it obligatory upon her to suckle her child. It was thus known that his statement: Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two years, is an indication of the maximum period of breastfeeding, which, if the parents disagreed about breastfeeding the child after them, is set as a limit to be reached between them, not an indication that it is obligatory for mothers to breastfeed their children.
As for his statement: two years, he means two years, as Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, he said, ʿIsa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nabjh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
, two years.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. The origin of the word hawl comes from the saying of the speaker: the state of this thing, if it moved. And from this it was said: so-and-so moved from such-and-such a place, if he moved from it.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: What is the meaning of mentioning complete in His statement:
h
And mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years

, after His statement: They shall breastfeed for two years, and in mentioning the two years there is no need to mention the complete ones, since it would not be difficult for a listener who heard His statement: And mothers shall breastfeed their children for two years, what is meant by it? What is the reason for which Zaid mentioned complete?

The Arabs may say: So-and-so stayed in such-and-such a place for two years, or two days, or two months, but he actually stayed there for a day and some of another, or a month and some of another, or a year and some of another, so it was said: Two complete years so that the listeners would know that what was meant by it was two complete years, not a year and some of another.

And this is as God the Most High said: “And remember God during the appointed days. So whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him. And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him.” (al-Baqarah 2:203) It is known that the one who hastens only hastens in a day and a half, and likewise on the third day of the days of Tashreeq, and that none of it is complete, but the Arabs do that at specific times, so they say: Today is two days since I have not seen him, but they mean by that a day and some of another. And the action that you do at the hour or moment may be attributed to the year, time, and day, so you say: I visited him in such-and-such year - and so-and-so killed so-and-so at the time of Siffin, and they do that because they do not mean by that to report the number of days and years, but rather they mean by that to report the time in which the one being reported was, so it is permissible to say the two years, and the two days, as I described before.
Because the meaning of the speech in that is: I did it then, and at that time. Likewise, his statement:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
, since breastfeeding is permissible for two years, but not for two years, and Surat al-Baqarah 2:233
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing

. And upon the father of the child is their food and clothing on equitable terms. No soul shall be charged except [with that within] its capacity. Neither shall a mother be made to suffer harm on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child. And upon the heir is a similar [duty].
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation

, there is no blame upon them. But if they both desire weaning, there is no blame upon them. If you wish to have your children nursed, there is no blame upon you as long as you give what you have given in an acceptable manner.

And fear God and know that God is Seeing of what you do. the speech would have been general in that, without clarifying the two years as complete, and it was said: Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two years, possibly meaning one year and some other, he removed the confusion from his listeners by saying: complete, that it may mean one year and some other, and he made clear by saying: complete, about the time of completion of the period of breastfeeding, and that it is the completion of the two years with their expiration, without the expiration of one of them and some of the other.

Then the people of interpretation differed about what this verse indicated, regarding the limit of breastfeeding of newborns: Is it a limit for every newborn, or is it a limit for some and not others?

Some of them said: It is a limit for some and not others. He who said that: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd al-Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the one who gives birth after six months: She breastfeeds for two full years, and if she gives birth after seven months, she breastfeeds for twenty-three months to complete thirty months, and if she gives birth after nine months, she breastfeeds for twenty-one months.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: similarly, and he did not trace it back to Ibn Abbas.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Ubayd, he said:
m: A woman who gave birth after six months was brought to Uthman, so he said: A woman was brought to me, and I do not think she has given birth to anything but good report - or something like that - she gave birth after six months! Ibn Abbas said: If she completes the breastfeeding, then the pregnancy is six months. He said: Ibn Abbas recited:
h
And his gestation and weaning is thirty months (al-Ahqaf 46
:15), so if she completes the breastfeeding, then the pregnancy is six months. So Uthman released her.

x: Others said: Rather, this is the limit for breastfeeding every child whose parents disagreed about breastfeeding him, and one of them wanted to reach maturity with him. The other is to fall short of it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
, so God Almighty made breastfeeding two complete years for whoever wanted to complete breastfeeding, then He said:
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation
, there is no blame upon them, if they wanted to wean him before the two years or after them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: I said to Ata’:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
. He said: If his mother wants to stop shortening it to two years, she must make it up to him - not to increase it unless he wishes.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Mihran told us, and Ali Ibn Sahl told me, Zaid Ibn Abi Al-Zarqa’ told us,
m: all of them on the authority of Al-Thawri regarding his statement:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing

, and completion is two years. He said: If the father wants to wean him before the two years and the woman does not agree, then he is not allowed to do that. And if the woman says: I will wean him before the two years, and the father says: No, then she is not allowed to wean him until the father agrees, until they meet. If they meet before the two years, then they should wean him, and if they disagree, then they should not wean him before the two years. This is due to His statement:
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation

x: Others said: Rather, God the Most High indicated by His saying:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
, that there is no breastfeeding after the two years, because breastfeeding is only what is in the two years.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, he said, Al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar that they said:
m: God the Most High says:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
, and we do not see breastfeeding after the two years as prohibiting anything.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yunus Ibn Yazid, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said:
m: Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas used to say: There is no breastfeeding after the two years.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Abu Al-Duha, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: said: Whatever is from breastfeeding after two years, or within two years after weaning, then there is no breastfeeding.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya bin Saeed and Abd al-Rahman told us, they said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah,
m: that he saw a woman breastfeeding after two years, so he said: Do not breastfeed him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Shaibani, he said:
m: I heard al-Sha’bi say: Whatever is from a wound or a snuff or a sip within two years, then it is forbidden, and whatever is after two years does not prohibit anything.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: that he used to narrate on the authority of ʿAbdullah, that he said: There is no breastfeeding after weaning, or after two years.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Hasan Ibn ʿAtiyya told us, he said, Israʿil told us, on the authority of ʿAbd Al-Aʿla, on the authority of Saʿid Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: Breastfeeding does not prohibit after completion, rather what prohibits is that which produces flesh and creates bone.

c: Al-Hasan Ibn Yahya told us, he said, ʿAbd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muʿammar told us, on the authority of ʿAmr Ibn Dinar: that Ibn ʿAbbas said:
m: There is no breastfeeding after weaning for two years.

c: Hilal bin Al-Ala Al-Raqi narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to us, he said, Ubaidullah narrated to us, on the authority of Zaid, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
, he said: There is no breastfeeding except in these two years.

x: Others said: Rather, His statement:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years

, was an indication from God, the Most High, to His servants that it is obligatory for the mothers of newborns to breastfeed them for two complete years. Then God, the Most High, made that easier by saying: For whoever desires to complete the nursing, so He gave the choice in that to the fathers and mothers. If they want to complete it, they complete two years, and if they want to wean the newborn before that, that is up to them, as long as they consider the newborn.
Who said that: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
And mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years

, then God revealed the ease and alleviation after that, so He, the Most High, said: For whoever desires to complete the nursing. I narrated on the authority of Ammar, he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding his statement:
h
And mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years

, meaning the divorced women, they shall breastfeed their children for two complete years. Then He revealed the dispensation and alleviation after that, so He said: For whoever desires to complete the nursing. Who said: The mothers whom God mentioned in this place: are those who have been divorced from their husbands, as we described before.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
to If you have given what you have given in kindness. As for
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
, the man divorces his wife and has a child from her, and she breastfeeds his child for him as another woman breastfeeds him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
, he said: If a man divorces his wife while she is breastfeeding his child.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: similarly.

x: The most correct of the statements regarding his statement:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the breastfeeding

, is the statement that Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, and ʿAta’ and Ath-Thawri agreed with him on this statement, and the statement that was narrated on the authority of ʿAbdullah bin Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn ʿUmar: which is that it is an indication of the end to which the breastfeeding of a newborn ends if his parents disagree about his breastfeeding, and that there is no breastfeeding after two years that prohibits anything, and that it refers to every newborn, whether he was born at six months or seven or nine. As for our saying: It is an indication of the end to which breastfeeding ends when the parents disagree about it, because when God the Most High mentioned a limit for that, it was not permissible for what is beyond His limit to be in agreement in ruling with what is below it.

Because if that were the case, the limit would have no rational meaning. Since that is the case, there is no doubt that what is less than two years of the term, since it is a time for breastfeeding, what is beyond it is not a time for it, and that it is a time to stop breastfeeding, and that the completion of the completion of breastfeeding, since it is the completion of two years, and the complete of things has no meaning to increase it, there is no meaning to increase in breastfeeding over two years, and that what is less than two years of breastfeeding is forbidden, what is beyond it is not forbidden. Rather, we said: It is an indication that it is intended for every newborn, regardless of the time of his birth, six months or seven or nine, because God the Most High mentioned it in general with His saying:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years
, and He did not specify some newborns without others.

We have demonstrated the corruption of the statement of particularity without the clarification of God the Most High in His Book, or on the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in our book, The Book of Explanation of the Principles of Rulings, in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: God the Most High has clarified that by His saying:
h
And his gestation and weaning is thirty months (al-Ahqaf 46

:15), and He made that a limit for both meanings, then it is not permissible for the gestation and breastfeeding to be more than the limit that God the Most High has set. Whatever is less than nine months of the pregnancy period is an addition to the breastfeeding period, and whatever is more than the pregnancy period is a reduction from the breastfeeding period. It is not permissible for both of them to exceed thirty months, as God the Most High has set.

The duration of pregnancy - according to this statement - if it reaches two complete years, the newborn should not be breastfed for more than six months, and if it reaches four years, the breastfeeding should be nullified and he should not be breastfed, because the pregnancy has taken thirty months and has exceeded its limit, or the one who says this statement claims that the duration of pregnancy will not exceed nine months, so he is out of the argument of all the proof, and is stubborn about what exists and is seen, and they are sufficient as proof of the error of his claim if he claims that. So Surat al-Baqarah 2:233
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing

. And upon the father of the child is their food and clothing on equitable terms. No soul shall be charged except [with that within] its capacity. Neither shall a mother be made to suffer harm on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child.
And upon the heir is a similar [duty].
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation

, there is no blame upon them. But if they both desire weaning, there is no blame upon them. If you wish to have your children nursed, there is no blame upon you as long as you give what you have given in an acceptable manner. And fear God and know that God is Seeing of what you do. which of the two matters did the one who says this statement resort to, and the corruption of his statement becomes clear to those with understanding.
What is the meaning of his statement - if the matter is as you described -
h
And his gestation and weaning is thirty months (al-Ahqaf 46

:15), and you mentioned earlier that it is not permissible for what exceeds the limit of God, the Most High, to be similar to what is less than His limit in ruling? And you said: Pregnancy and weaning may exceed thirty months?
God, the Most High, did not make His statement:
h
And his gestation and weaning is thirty months (al-Ahqaf 46
:15), a limit for His servants to worship not to exceed, just as He made His statement:
h
And mothers shall breastfeed their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing

, a limit for breastfeeding a newborn whose breastfeeding is established, and the servants’ worship of carrying his parents when they disagree about it, and one of them wants to harm him. This is because the command from God, the Most High, is only in that which the servants have the path to obeying Him by doing it and disobeying Him by leaving it. As for that which they have no path to doing or leaving it, then that is something that it is not permissible to command, forbid, or worship Him with. If this is the case, and pregnancy is something that women cannot shorten or lengthen, so they give birth whenever they want and leave birth whenever they want, then it is known that His statement,
h
And his gestation and weaning is thirty months (al-Ahqaf 46

:15), is only a statement from God Almighty that the one who created him is the one whose mother carried him, gave birth to him, and weaned him in thirty months, not a command that the period of his gestation and weaning should not exceed thirty months, for what we have described. Likewise our Lord Almighty said in His Book, “And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment.

His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his gestation and weaning is thirty months” (al-Ahqaf 46:15). If a foolish person thinks that when God, the Most High, mentioned that those who created Him were carried by their mothers, gave birth to them, and weaned them in thirty months, then it is necessary that all of His creation be like that, and that this is evidence that the pregnancy and weaning of all His servants is thirty months, then it is necessary that the description of all of His servants be that they say when they reach maturity and reach forty years of age: My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve (al-Ahqaf 46:15), as God was described by the one described in this verse. And among us are those whose disbelief in God is so strong, and their ingratitude for the favors of their Lord upon them, and their boldness towards their parents with killing, cursing, and various kinds of hardships, when they complete forty years of age and reach maturity, what is known is that God did not mean by this verse a description of all of His servants, but rather it is known that He only described some of them and not others, and that is something that no one denies or rejects.

Because the number of people born after seven months is more than the number of those born after four or two years, just as the number of those born after nine months is more than the number of those born after six or seven months.

The readings differed in reading this, so the majority of the people of Medina, Iraq and Syria read it: Whoever wants to complete the breastfeeding with the ya’ in yatum and the nasb of breastfeeding - meaning: whoever among the fathers and mothers wants to complete the breastfeeding of his child.
Some of the people of Hijaz read it: Whoever wants to complete the breastfeeding with the ta’ in yatum and the nasb of breastfeeding as a description.

The correct reading in this according to us is the reading of those who read with the ya’ in yatum and the nasb of breastfeeding. Because God the Most High said: And mothers shall suckle their children, so they complete it if they and the child want to suckle their mother, and this is the reading that came with the widespread transmission that established the evidence, not the other reading. It has been narrated in breastfeeding by hearing from the Arabs that the ra’ in it is broken. If it is correct, then it is similar to agency and agency and indication and indication, and the dowry of something is skill and skill - then suckling and suckling are permissible, as it was said: harvest and harvest. As for the reading, it is with the fat-ha and nothing else.

God Almighty means by His saying: And upon the father of the child, and upon the fathers of the children for the wet nurses, their provision, meaning: the provision of their mother. And by provision He means: what sustains them from food, and what they need from nourishment and food. And their clothing, and by clothing He means: clothing. And by His saying: in a reasonable manner, He means what is due for someone like her from someone like him, since God Almighty knows the differences in the conditions of His creation in wealth and poverty, and that among them are those who are wealthy and those who are poor, and in between. So he ordered each one to spend on those he is obliged to support, from his wife and child, according to his means, as God Almighty said: “Let one with an abundance spend from his abundance, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what God has given him.
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity.”
(al-Talaq 65:7), and as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement: “
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing

. And the father shall bear the cost of their food and clothing on equitable terms,” he said: If a man divorces his wife while she is nursing his child, and they agree that she should breastfeed for two complete years, then the father shall bear the cost of the wet nurse and clothing her on equitable terms according to his means. We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity.

c: Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told me, he said: Zaid told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan,
m: his saying:
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the breastfeeding
, and completion is the two years, and upon the child’s father, upon the father is her food and clothing according to what is reasonable.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
And the father shall bear the cost of their food and clothing according to what is acceptable
. He said: It is upon the father.

x: God Almighty means by that: No soul shall bear any responsibility except that which is not difficult for it, nor is it difficult for it to obtain if it wishes. Rather, God the Most High meant by that: God does not obligate men to provide for those who breastfeed their children from their divorced wives, except what they are able to do and find a way to do, as God the Most High said: Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what God has given him (al-Talaq 65:7), as Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told me, he said, Zayd told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan: No soul is charged except with that within its capacity, except what it is able to do. And the word was is the verb from the speaker’s saying: This matter was within my capacity, so it is within my capacity. And it is said: This that I gave you is my capacity, meaning: what I am able to give you, so it is not difficult for me to give it, and I gave you from my effort, if you give him what you are able to give, so it is difficult for you to give it.

The meaning of His statement: No soul shall be charged except with that within its capacity, is what was described: that it shall not be charged except with what it can do by giving what it was charged with giving, so that it is not made difficult or exhausted, not what the ignorant people of destiny thought, that its meaning is: no soul shall be charged except with what it has been given the ability to do of acts of obedience. Because if that were as you claimed, then His statement, the Most High: See how they set forth for you examples, then they have gone astray and are not able to find a way (Al-Isra’: 48-al-Furqan 25:9), since it indicates that they are not able to find a way to what they were charged with, it would be necessary for the people to be in one state, having been given the ability to do what they were prevented from doing. And that from its speaker, if he said it, is an impossibility in his speech, and a false claim that is not imagined to be long.

And since the corruption of this statement is clear, it is known that what the Most High informed us that He charged souls from their capacity is not what He informed us that He charged them with what they are not able to find a way to.

The readings differed in the reading of that. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Kufa and Ash-Sham read it as: La tudharar waladaha bi-waladha with a fatha on the ra’, with the interpretation: la tudharar, as a prohibition. Its position when read in this way is in the jussive mood, except that it is moved, since the doubling was left with the lightest of the movements, which is the fatha. If it was moved to the kasra, it would be permissible, following the movement of the lam of the verb, the movement of its ‘ayn. If you wish, then it is because when the jussive is moved, it is moved to the kasra.

Some of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read it as: No mother should be harmed by her child, in the nominative case. Whoever reads it in this way, his reading does not carry the meaning of prohibition, but rather it is [in the sense of] report, in apposition with his saying: No soul is charged except [with that within] its capacity.

Some of the grammarians of Basra have claimed that the meaning of whoever raised: No mother should be harmed by her child, is thus in the ruling: - that no mother should be harmed by her child - i.e.: it is not appropriate for her to be harmed.

i: So when it is appropriate was deleted, and it is not appropriate for her to be harmed was in its place, it remained in its wording, and he cited as evidence for that the saying of the poet:
x: The judge who will come one day, if he decides his case, must not be unjust and intentional.

He claimed that it was raised with the intention of meaning it should be. What is narrated from the Arabs by hearing is not what he said. That is because it was narrated from them by hearing: Fa-ta-san’i-ma-da, if they wanted to say: Fa-ta-ree-tan-ta-san’i-ma-da, they would put it in the accusative case with the intention of an. And if they did not intend an and did not mean it, they would say: Fa-ta-ree-ma-da, and they would put Ta-ree-ma-da, because there is no an before it, just as there was a an before tasna’u. So if the meaning of his saying: La-ta-daar, if it was read in the nominative case, was: It should be that you should not be harmed, or It should not be that you should be harmed, then Ya-ta-daar and An were deleted and Ta-daar was used in place of Ya-ta-daar, then it would have been obligatory to read it—if it was read with that meaning—in the accusative case, not in the nominative case, so that the intended meaning would be known by the accusative that was left before it, as was done with his saying: Fa-ta-seena-ma-da.

But the meaning of that is what we said when it is raised in conjunction with ta-kafala: No soul is burdened beyond its capacity, and No mother is harmed by her child. He meant by that: that there is nothing in that in the religion of God, His rule, and the morals of the Muslims.

The more correct of the two readings in that is the reading of the one who reads in the accusative, because it is a prohibition from God, the Most High, to each of the parents of the child from harming his companion to him, and it is forbidden for them to do so by the consensus of the Muslims. If that were report, then it would be forbidden for them to harm him in the same way. And with what we said about that - that it means a prohibition - the people of interpretation interpreted it.
Those who said that mentioned: Surat al-Baqarah 2:233
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing

. And upon the father of the child is their food and clothing on equitable terms. No soul shall be charged except [with that within] its capacity. Neither shall a mother be made to suffer harm on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child. And upon the heir is a similar [duty].
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation

, there is no blame upon them. But if they both desire weaning, there is no blame upon them. If you wish to have your children nursed, there is no blame upon you as long as you give what you have given in an acceptable manner. And fear God and know that God is Seeing of what you do.

c: Muhammad bin ʿAmr told us, he said, Abu ʿAsim told us, on the authority of ʿIsa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, she does not refuse to breastfeed him because that would be difficult for his father, and the father shall not be harmed by his child, so he prevents his mother from breastfeeding him because that would make her sad.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najeh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated, Sa’id narrated, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, nor shall a father by his child, he said: God the Most High forbade harming and presented it, so God forbade harming the father by taking the child from his mother, if she was satisfied with what he was breastfed with other than her, and the mother was forbidden from throwing the child to his father to cause harm. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, he said:

c: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Muammar informed us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, throwing him to his father to cause harm, nor a father by his child, he said: nor the father, so he takes him from her to cause harm, if she is satisfied with the reward of breastfeeding as other than her is satisfied, then she is more entitled to it if she is satisfied with that. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, he said: That is if he divorces her, so he has no right to harm her by taking the child away from her, if she is satisfied with him as others are satisfied with, and she has no right to harm him by burdening him with what he cannot bear, if he is a poor person, so she throws his child to him.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abu Zuhair narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, a mother shall not be harmed by her child, nor a father by his child. He said: A mother shall not be harmed by her child by throwing him to him if the father is alive, or to his agnates if the father is dead. And the father shall not be harmed by the woman if she wants to breastfeed her child, nor shall he take him away.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, meaning: A man shall not take his child from his wife and give it to someone else for the same reward that she would accept, and a mother shall not be harmed by her child, so that the mother throws her child to him, saying: I will not have him for a while, wasting him, but she has the right to breastfeed him until he seeks a wet nurse.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab - and he was asked
m: about the statement of God, the Most High:
h
And mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years

to A mother shall not be harmed by her child, nor shall a father by his child, Ibn Shihab said: Mothers have more right to breastfeed their children as long as they accept breastfeeding them for the same reward that others are given, and a mother does not have the right to be harmed by her child and refuse to breastfeed him, harming him while she is given the same reward that others are given. The child is not to be taken from his mother to harm her, and she accepts from the reward what is given to someone else.
b.via: Ibn Shihab - and he was asked

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told me, he said, Zaid told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, she shall not throw her child to the father if he separates from her, harming him thereby, nor a father by his child, and the father shall not take her child from her to harm her thereby.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zaid said
m: regarding his statement: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, nor a father by his child, he said: He shall not take him from her while she loves to breastfeed him, harming her, nor shall she throw him upon him while he cannot find anyone to breastfeed him, nor can he find anyone to breastfeed him with.

c: Amr bin Ali Al-Bahili told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told me, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, he said: Do not abandon him and his breastfeeding, out of hatred for her, which is harmful to his father, and do not prevent him from what is with him, which is harmful to her.

x: Some of them said: The mother whom a man is forbidden from harming is the boy’s wet nurse.

Who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Harun Al-Nahwi told us, he said, Al-Zubayr bin Al-Kharbat told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, he said: She is the wet nurse. So the meaning of the statement is: A father of a child shall not be harmed by his mother by his child from her, nor a mother of a child of his father by her child from him. Then he left out mentioning the agent in is harmed, so it was said: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, nor a child of his by his child, just as it is said when one is forbidden from honoring a man at that time in a matter whose agent is not named, and the prohibition of honoring him is not intended to target a specific person: Amr shall not be honored, nor shall he sit with his brother. Then he left out the doubling, so it was said: Do not be harmed, so the second ra’, which was in the jussive mood if the doubling had been shown, was moved by the movement of the first ra’.

Some of the Arabists have claimed that it was moved to the fatha in this position because it is the last of the movements. What he said has no meaning. Because it would have been permissible for it to be so if the meaning of the statement was: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, and the one forbidden from harming was the mother. However, if the meaning of the statement were so, then the kasra in tadhar would have been more eloquent than the fatha, and reading it with it would have been more correct than reading it with the fatha, just as: stretching the garment is more eloquent than stretching it. And in the consensus of the reciters on reading: La tadhar with the fatha without the kasra, there is clear evidence of the neglect of the statement of the people of Arabic that I have quoted in this regard. If the one who said this said it out of his assumption that the meaning of it is: A mother shall not be harmed, and that the mother is raised by her action, and that the first ra' is the kasra, then he has neglected the interpretation of the statement, and has contradicted the statement of all the people of interpretation that we have quoted.

That is because God, the Most High, preceded each of the parents of the newborn with the prohibition of harming the other with their newborn, not that He prohibited each of them from harming the newborn. How can he forbid him from harming a boy, when a boy is still an infant - it is not permissible for him to harm anyone? If that was its meaning, the revelation would have been: A mother shall not harm her son.
Others among the Arab scholars have claimed that the kasra in tadhar is permissible.

Since God Almighty has forbidden each of the parents of a child from harming his companion because of their child, it is the right of the Imam of the Muslims, if a man wants to take his child from his mother after she has separated from him, and she is nursing him, taking care of him, and breastfeeding him, with what someone else would nurse him with, take care of him with, and breastfeed him with as wages, that the father should take her child, as long as the boy is in need of her for that, for the wages that someone else would give her.
