And it is his right, if the boy does not accept the breast of anyone other than his mother, or the one born to him does not find anyone to nurse his child even if he accepts the breast of anyone other than his mother, or he is poor and does not find what he can hire a wet nurse with, and does not find anyone to volunteer to nurse his child, that he should take his mother who has separated from his father.

By breastfeeding and fostering him. Because if God Almighty forbade each of his parents from harming his companion because of him, then harming him is more likely to be forbidden, with what harming him entails of harming his companion.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the inheritor that God Almighty meant by His saying: And upon the heir is the same, and which inheritor is he? And whose inheritor is he?

Some of them said: He is the inheritor of the boy. They said the meaning of the verse is: And upon the inheritor of the boy if [his father] is dead, is the same as what was upon his father during his life.
Who said that: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And upon the heir is the same, on the heir of the child.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And upon the heir is the same, on the heir of the child.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And upon the heir is the same, he said: And upon the heir of the child is the same as upon his father. Then the proponents of this statement differed regarding the heir of the newborn, whom God Almighty has obligated to do the same as described.

x: Some of them said: He is the heir of the child from his father’s side from his agnates, whoever he may be, a brother, or an uncle, or a cousin, or a nephew.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Jurayj told us: Amr bin Shuaib told him: Saeed bin al-Musayyab told him:
m: Umar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: Regarding his statement: And upon the heirs is the same, he said 1 - he made a waqf for the paternal uncles of a deceased person as a result of his support, like the agnates.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: And upon the heirs is the same, on the agnates.

c: Amr bin Ali told us: Abdullah bin Idris and Abu Asim told us: Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, who said:
m: Umar made a waqf for the paternal uncles of a deceased person as a result of his breastfeeding.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus 10:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: If a man dies and his wife is pregnant, then her expenses are from her share, and the expenses of her child are from his share of his money if he has any. If he does not have money, then his expenses are on his agnates. He said: He used to interpret his statement: And the same is upon the heirs as referring to men.

c: Amr ibn Ali told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: The agnates are the men, not the women.

c: Abu Kurayb and Amr ibn Ali told us, they said, Ibn Idris told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin:
m: Abdullah ibn Utbah came with the orphan’s guardian, and there was someone with the orphan who was talking about his expenses, so he said to the guardian of the orphan: If he did not have money, I would have ordered you to pay his expenses, because God the Most High says: And the same is upon the heir.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said:
m: Abdullah ibn Utbah came to me regarding the breastfeeding of a boy, so he made his breastfeeding part of his wealth, and he said to his guardian: If he had no wealth, we would have made his breastfeeding part of your wealth. Don’t you see him saying: And the same is upon the heir?

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement: And the same is upon the heir, he said: The heir is responsible for what the father is responsible for, if the boy has no wealth. And if he has a cousin or a male relative who inherits from him, then he is responsible for the expenses.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Surat al-Baqarah 2:
m: h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing

. And upon the father of the child is their food and clothing on equitable terms. No soul shall be charged except [with that within] its capacity. Neither shall a mother be made to suffer harm on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child. And upon the heir is a similar [duty].
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation

, there is no blame upon them. But if they both desire weaning, there is no blame upon them. If you wish to have your children nursed, there is no blame upon you as long as you give what you have given in an acceptable manner. And fear God and know that God is Seeing of what you do. Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the same is upon the heir, he said: The guardian, whoever he may be.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Abdullah ibn Muhammad Al-Hanafi told us, he said, Abdullah ibn Uthman told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Ya’qub told us
m: - meaning Ibn Al-Qasim - on the authority of Ata’ and Qatadah - regarding an orphan who has nothing, are his guardians forced to spend on him? They said: Yes, he should spend on him until he reaches adulthood.

c: I was told by Ya’la ibn Ubaid, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: If the father of a child dies and the child has money, his breastfeeding is taken from the money. And if he has no money, it is taken from the agnates. And if the agnates have no money, his mother is forced to spend on him.

x: Others among them said: Rather, it is upon the heir of the newborn, whoever they may be, of men and women.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada
m: that he used to say: And upon the heir is the same, upon the heir of the newborn is what was upon the father of the wage of breastfeeding, if the child has no money, upon the men and women according to what they inherit.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of al-Zuhri:
m: That Umar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, fined three people, all of whom inherit the child, the wages of breastfeeding him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin:
m: That Abdullah bin Utbah made the expenses of a child from his money, and he said to his heir: If he had no money, we would have taken you for his expenses. Do you not see that he says: And upon the heir is the like thereof.

x: Others among them said: He is from his heirs, whoever among them is a mahram to the newborn. As for whoever is a mahram to him but is not a mahram, such as a cousin, a freed slave, and the like, then he is not among those whom God meant by His saying: And upon the heir is the like thereof.
Those who said this statement are: Abu Hudhayfah, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad.
Another group said: Rather, what God the Most High meant by His saying: And upon the heir is the same, is the child himself.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam al-Masri told us, he said, Abu Zur’ah Wahb God ibn Rashid told us, he said, Haywah ibn Shuraih told us, he said, Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah told us, that
m: Bashir ibn al-Nadr al-Muzani - who was a judge before Ibn Hujairah in the time of Abdul-Aziz - used to say: And upon the heir is the same, he said: The heir is the child.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri told us, he said, Haywah told us, he said, Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb:
m: And upon the heir is the same, he said: It is the child.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Haywah ibn Shuraih, he said, Ja’far ibn Rabi’ah told me:
m: Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb used to say: The heir is the child, meaning His saying: And upon the heir is the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak:
m: And the same is upon the heir, he said: He means by the one who is breastfed, the child who is breastfed.

x: The interpretation of that is as they have interpreted it: And upon the heir of the child, is the same as what was upon the child for him.
Others said: Rather, it is what remains from the parents of the child, after the death of the other one of them.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hanafi told me, he said, Abdullah bin Uthman told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, he said,
m: I heard Sufyan say about a boy who has an uncle and a mother who is breastfeeding him, he said: His breastfeeding is between them, and he is lifted from the uncle according to the amount that the mother inherits, because the mother is forced to spend on her child.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his statement: like that.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: And upon the heir of the boy after the death of his parents, is the same as what was upon his father of the wages for breastfeeding and spending on him, if the child does not have any money.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said, Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement: And upon the heir is the like thereof, he said: Upon the heir is the breastfeeding of the child.

c: Amr ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, they said, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Abu Awana narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And upon the heir is the like thereof, he said: The reward for breastfeeding.

c: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And upon the heir is the like thereof, he said: Breastfeeding.

c: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Abu Awana narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement: And upon the heir is the like thereof, he said: The reward for breastfeeding.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Utbah:
m: And upon the heir is the like thereof, he said: Breastfeeding.

c: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said,
m: Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Utbah, regarding his statement: And the heir is responsible for the same, he said: Spending according to what is reasonable.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: And upon the heir is the same, he said: Upon the heir is what the father is obligated to do with breastfeeding, if the boy does not have money.

c: Sufyan narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Breastfeeding.

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, he said, Abu Nu’aym narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: And upon the heir is the same, he said: Breastfeeding.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Abu Uwana narrated to us, on the authority of Ata ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: Breastfeeding.

c: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, he said, Abu Uwana narrated to us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of al-Sha’bi,
m: And upon the heir is the same, he said: The reward for breastfeeding.
Amr narrated to us, he said, Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Abu Uwana narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and al-Sha’bi likewise.

c: Abu Kurayb and Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, they said, Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, he said,
m: I heard Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And upon the heir is the like thereof, he said: Breastfeeding.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisham and Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: similarly.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said: Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And upon the heir is the like thereof, he said: in the maintenance of the heir, if he has no money.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Qais bin Sa’d, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said: Abd Al-Rahman told us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Qais bin Sa’d, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And upon the heir is the like thereof, he said: Maintenance according to what is reasonable.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And upon the heir is the like thereof, on the guardian to sponsor him and breastfeed him, if the newborn has no money.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: And upon the heir is the like of that, he said: And upon the heir is whoever he is, like what was described of breastfeeding. Ibn Jurayj said: And Abdullah bin Kathir informed me, on the authority of Mujahid: The same in breastfeeding, he said: And upon the heir is the like of that, he said: And upon the heir is also his guardianship and breastfeeding, if he has no money, and that he does not harm his mother.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And upon the heir is the like of that, he said: His expenses until he is weaned, if his father did not leave him any money.

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Sa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah:
m: And upon the heir is the like of that, he said: And upon the heir of the child is what was upon the father of the wage of breastfeeding, if the child has no money.

c: Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hanafi told me, he said, Abdullah bin Uthman told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the heir is responsible for the same, he said: The heir of a child is responsible for the same as his father, if his father has died and he has no wealth, then the heir is responsible for the reward of breastfeeding.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And the heir is responsible for the same, he said: If he dies and has no wealth, then the heir is responsible for breastfeeding the child.

x: Others said: Rather, the interpretation of that: And upon the heir is the same: that he should not be harmed.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Amr bin Ali and Muhammad bin Bashar told us, they said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ali bin al-Hakam, on the authority of al-Dahhak bin Muzahim:
m: And upon the heir is the same, he said: that he should not be harmed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement: And upon the heir is the same, he said: that he should not be harmed, nor should he pay a penalty.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: And upon the heir is the same, that he should not be harmed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, al-Layth told us, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: And mothers shall breastfeed their children for two years, he said: Mothers are more entitled to breastfeed their children as long as they accept their breastfeeding for what others are given of reward. A mother is not to be harmed by her child, so she refuses to breastfeed him to harm him, and she is given what others are given for him. And the child’s father is not to take his child away from his mother to harm her, and she accepts from the reward what others are given, and upon the heir is the same, like what is upon the father in that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told us, he said, Zaid told us, on the authority of Sufyan:
m: and upon the heir is the same, he said: that he should not be harmed, and he is responsible for the same as the father in terms of spending and clothing.

x: Others said: Rather, the interpretation of that is: And upon the heir of the child is the same as what was upon the child’s father, Surat al-Baqarah 2:233
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing

. And upon the father of the child is their food and clothing on equitable terms. No soul shall be charged except [with that within] its capacity. Neither shall a mother be made to suffer harm on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child. And upon the heir is a similar [duty].
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation

, there is no blame upon them. But if they both desire weaning, there is no blame upon them. If you wish to have your children nursed, there is no blame upon you as long as you give what you have given in an acceptable manner. And fear God and know that God is Seeing of what you do. in terms of providing for his mother and clothing her in a reasonable manner.

Who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak: And upon the heir is the like of that. He said: Upon the heir at death is the same as what the father owes to the wet nurse in terms of expenses and clothing. He said: And by the heir he means: the child who is being breastfed: that the wage for what his mother breastfed him be taken from his money - if he has any money. If the child has no money and his agnates do not have any money, then his mother is not entitled to any wage, and she is forced to breastfeed her child without pay.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of As-Suddi:
m: And upon the heir is the like of that. He said: Upon the heir of the child is the same as what the child owes in terms of expenses and clothing.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: And upon the heir is the same as what God, the Most High, mentioned.

Who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata’: What does God, the Most High, say: And upon the heir is the like of that? He said: Like what God the Most High mentioned.

The most correct of the sayings in the interpretation of His statement: And upon the heir is the like of that: is that what is meant by the heir is what Qubaysah ibn Dhuʿayb and Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said, and what we mentioned earlier: that what is meant by the heir is the newborn. And in His statement: The like of that: that what is meant by it is: like what was upon his father of his mother’s sustenance and clothing in a reasonable manner, if she is among the needy, and if she is afflicted with a disease and a disability, and if she has no profession, and does not have a husband who makes her independent, and if she is among the wealthy and healthy, then like what was upon his father for her of the wages of breastfeeding him. And we said: This interpretation is more correct than the rest of the interpretations that we mentioned, because it is not permissible to say anything in the interpretation of the Book of God the Most High except with a clear proof, as we explained at the beginning of this book.

And since that was the case, and his statement: And upon the heir is the same, its apparent meaning is possible: And upon the heir of the newborn boy is the same as what was upon the child for him, and possible: And upon the heir of the child is the same as what was upon him during his life of leaving harm to the mother and from the expenses of the child, and other interpretations, in the manner that we have mentioned previously, and all of the proofs have agreed that among the heirs of the newborn is one who is not obligated to pay anything for his expenses and the wages of breastfeeding, it is thus correct to indicate that the rest of his heirs, other than his fathers and mothers and grandfathers and grandmothers from his father’s or mother’s side, are in his ruling, in that they are not obligated to pay him expenses or wages for breastfeeding, since the master of the blessing is among his heirs, and he is one of those who is not obligated to pay him expenses or wages for breastfeeding.

It is necessary by their consensus on that the ruling for all his heirs, except for those who were excluded, is his ruling. And if it is invalid that the meaning of that is what we have described - that it is intended for the heirs of the newborn - then the length of the other statement, which is that it is intended for the heirs of the newborn other than the newborn, is more appropriate. Because the one who is closer in kinship to the newborn than the one who is more distant from him - if it is not valid for him to be obligated to provide for his expenses and the wages for breastfeeding him - then the one who is more distant from him in kinship is more likely not to be obligated to do that. As for what we said about the obligation of the mother’s provision and clothing in a reasonable manner for her child - if the mother has the characteristics we have described - in the same way that she was obligated to provide for the newborn, then there is no disagreement among all the people of knowledge about it.
So what we said about the interpretation of the verse is correct by the widespread transmission of inheritance from someone whose contradiction is not permissible.

God Almighty means by His statement: If they both desire, if He means the father and mother of the newborn, to wean, meaning: to wean their child from the milk. And by weaning He means weaning, and it is a source from the saying of the speaker: I separated so-and-so, I separate him from him, if he separated from him from the mixture that was between them. So the weaning of the weaned child is the same, it is his withholding of milk, cutting it off and drinking it, and his separation from his mother’s breast to nourish himself with the foods that an adult man nourishes himself with. And what we said about that is what the people of interpretation said.

Who said that: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, his saying: If they both desire weaning, he said: If they desire to wean him before the two years.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: If they both desire weaning, he said: If they desire to wean him before the two years or after.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: If they both desire weaning by mutual consent, he said: Weaning. As for his saying: By mutual consent and consultation, he means by that: By mutual consent of the parents of the child and consultation between them. Then the people of interpretation differed about the time when God dropped the blame from them, if they weaned him with their mutual consent and consultation, and what times did God, the Most High, mean by His saying:
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation

x: Some of them said: He meant by that, if they desire weaning within the two years by mutual consent and consultation, then there is no blame upon them.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation
, he said: If they desire to wean him before the two years and they both desire that, then let them wean him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: If the mother desires to wean her child before the two years, and that is by mutual consent and consultation, then there is no problem with it.

c: Sufyan told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: If they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation, he said: Consultation is for less than two years. She does not have the right to wean him unless he is satisfied, and he does not have the right to wean him unless she is satisfied.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Consultation is less than two years,
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation
less than two years, there is no blame upon them, if they do not agree, then she has no right to wean him before two years.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Nu’aym told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Consultation is less than two years, she has no right to wean him until they agree.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Al-Laith told me, he said, Aqil told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: But if they both desire weaning, they wean their child, by mutual consent and consultation less than two complete years, there is no blame upon them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told me, he said, Zaid told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, he said: Consultation is less than two years, if they agree before that, and that is His saying: But if they both desire “A weaning by mutual consent and after consultation. So if the woman says: I will wean him before two years, and the father says: No, then she is not allowed to wean him before two years. And if the mother does not agree, then he is not allowed to do that until they meet. If they meet before two years, then they should wean him. If they disagree, then they should not wean him before two years. This is His statement:
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and after consultation
, there is no blame upon them.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and after consultation
, he said: before two years, there is no blame upon them.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and after consulting each other, there is no blame upon them, at any time they desire that, before the two years or after that.
Those who said this were mentioned:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and after consulting each other, there is no blame upon them, that they wean him before the two years or after that. As for his saying: by mutual consent and after consulting, it means: by mutual consent and after consulting regarding what is in the best interest of the child to wean him, as Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and after consulting, he said: not wronging themselves or their child, there is no blame upon them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who said: If they both intended weaning within two years with their mutual consent and consultation, because the completion of two years is the end of the breastfeeding and its completion, and there is no consultation after its completion, but rather consultation and consent before its end. If a careless person thinks that consultation after the completion of two years has a correct meaning, since there are some boys who have an illness that requires them to be left and to be nourished by their mother’s milk, then if that is the case, then it is a treatment, like the treatment of drinking some medicines, not breastfeeding. As for breastfeeding that occurs during weaning before the end of its duration, with the consent and consultation of the parents of the child whom God Almighty has dropped the sin from them for weaning him before the end of his duration, its limit is the limit that God Almighty has defined in His saying:
h
Mothers may breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing
, as we have explained previously.

As for sin, it is hardship, as Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: There is no blame upon them, so there is no blame upon them.

God Almighty means by that: And if you want to have wet nurses other than their mothers breastfeed them with the same reward that others breastfeed them with, or out of fear of your children being neglected by their mothers’ milk stopping, or other reasons, then there is no blame upon you in having them breastfeed, if you accept what you have given in a good manner. And similar to what we have said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And if you wish to have your children nursed by female foster mothers, fearing that the boy would be lost, there is no blame upon you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi told us, he said, Abdullah ibn Uthman told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, he said, Abu Bishr Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us,
m: Surat al-Baqarah 2:233
h
Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing

. And upon the father of the child is their food and clothing on equitable terms. No soul shall be charged except [with that within] its capacity. Neither shall a mother be made to suffer harm on account of her child, nor a father on account of his child. And upon the heir is a similar [duty].
h
But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation

, there is no blame upon them. But if they both desire weaning, there is no blame upon them. If you wish to have your children nursed, there is no blame upon you as long as you give what you have given in an acceptable manner. And fear God and know that God is Seeing of what you do. he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And if you wish to have your children nursed by female foster mothers, if the woman says: I am not able to do it, then my children are gone! Then another woman should be brought to breastfeed him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, who said:
m: A woman should not abandon her child after they have agreed that she should breastfeed, and they have become Muslim, and they are forced to do so. He said: If they are unable to breastfeed due to divorce or death, then the boy should be offered wet nurses. If he accepts a wet nurse, that is permissible and she should breastfeed him. If he does not accept a wet nurse, then his mother must breastfeed him for a fee if he has money or for his agnates. If he has no money nor does his agnates, she is forced to breastfeed him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told me, he said, Zaid told us,
m: all on the authority of Sufyan: And if you wish to have your children breastfed, there is no blame upon you, if the mother refuses to breastfeed him, then there is no blame upon the father to have someone else breastfeed him for him.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zaid said
m: regarding his statement: And if you wish to have your children breastfed, there is no blame upon you if you pay what you have given in an equitable manner, he said: If the mother agrees to have her child breastfed, and the father agrees to have his child breastfed, then there is no blame upon them. They differed regarding his statement: If you pay what you have given in an equitable manner.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: If you pay their mothers what you left them for in terms of wages for breastfeeding them, according to what she is entitled to until her milk stops, or the situation in which the father of the child is excused for seeking a wet nurse for his child other than his mother, and having her breastfeed him.

Mention of those who said that: He told me Muhammad ibn Amr said, Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: If you give what you have given in a fair manner, he said: the calculation of what the child was breastfed with.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: If you give what you have given in a fair manner, the calculation of what the child was breastfed with.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: If you give what you have given in a fair manner, if she says - meaning the mother -: I am not able to bear it, it has gone to my children, then she should have another woman breastfeed him for him, and her reward should be given to her in proportion to what she breastfed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I said - meaning to Ata’ -: And if you want to have your children breastfed? He said: His mother and others, There is no blame upon you if you surrender, he said: If you surrender her reward, what you have given, he said: What you have given.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: If you surrender for breastfeeding, with the consultation of you and the mothers of your children whom we have breastfed, and with the consent of you and them to breastfeed them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: There is no blame upon you if you surrender what you have given in an acceptable manner, he said: If that was with their consultation and consent.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqeel told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: There is no blame on them if they breastfeed their children - meaning the parents of the child - if they are safe and do not cause harm.

c: I was told by Ammar
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
h
If you hand over what you have given in a reasonable manner
, meaning: if that was with their consultation and consent.

i: Others said:
x: Rather the meaning of that is:
h
if you hand over what you have given in a reasonable manner

to the one you breastfed after the mother of the wet nurse refused, from the wages, in a reasonable manner. He who said that: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told me, he said, Zaid told us, all of them, on the authority of Sufyan regarding his statement:
h
If you hand over what you have given in a reasonable manner

, he said: If you hand over to this one whom you hire her wages in a reasonable manner - meaning: to the one who breastfed the newborn, if the mother refuses to breastfeed him. Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the sayings in interpreting that is the saying of the one who said: Its interpretation is: And if you want to breastfeed your children until they are fully breastfed, and you and their mothers do not agree on weaning them, and you do not see that as being in their best interest, then there is no blame upon you if you have a wet nurse breastfeed them, if their mothers refuse to breastfeed them due to a disease in them or for no reason, if you hand over to their mothers and to the other wet nurse their rights that you gave them in a reasonable manner.

By this meaning, he means: what God has made obligatory for them upon you, which is that you should pay them their wages for what he left them for, in the case of breastfeeding and at the time of the contract of employment. This is the meaning that Ibn Jurayj said, and Mujahid, As-Suddi and those who said what they said agreed with him in part. We have decided for this interpretation that it is more deserving of the interpretation of the instrument than any other, because God Almighty mentioned before His statement: And if you wish to have your children breastfed, the command to wean them, and He explained the ruling on weaning them before the completion of two complete years, saying: But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent in the two complete years, there is no blame upon them. So what is more deserving of the ruling of the verse - since it has explained the reason for weaning before two years - is that what follows that is the ruling on abandoning weaning and completing breastfeeding until its end, and that - since it has explained the ruling of the mother if she chooses to breastfeed with what someone else breastfeeds with in payment - that what follows that of the ruling is the clarification of her ruling and the ruling of the child if she refuses to breastfeed him, as it was like this in other places in the Book of God Almighty, and that is in His statement: “But if they breastfeed for you, then give them their payment and consult among yourselves in kindness.

But if you disagree, then another woman shall breastfeed for him” (al-Talaq 65:7). So He followed the mention of the mothers’ consent to breastfeed their children with the mention of their refusal to breastfeed them. So it is the same in His statement: And if you wish to have your children breastfed. Rather, we chose - in His statement:
h
If you hand over what you have given in a reasonable manner

- what we chose from the interpretation, because God Almighty has made it obligatory for the father of the child to hand over to her the right of his mother from what he gave her as wages for breastfeeding him after she was separated from him, just as He has made that obligatory for him for whoever he hired for that who is not related to his birth, and He has ordered him to give each one of them her right in a reasonable manner for breastfeeding his child. So His statement: If you hand over is not meant to mean: If you hand over to the mothers of your children who breastfeed their rights, more so than it is meant to mean: If you hand that over to wet nurses other than them, nor are the strangers of the child, more so that they are meant by that from the mothers, since God Almighty has made it obligatory for the father of the child for whoever he hired to breastfeed his child, to hand over her wages to her like what He made obligatory for the other.
As for the meaning of His statement: in a just manner, its meaning is: in general and kindness, and avoiding shortcomings and injustice in what is required of wet nurses.

God Almighty means by His statement: And fear God, and fear God in what He has imposed on some of you from others of rights, and in what He has obligated your women for your men and your men for your women, and in what He has obligated upon you for your children. So beware of disobeying Him and transgressing in that - and in other than His obligations and rights - His limits, and thereby deserving His punishment. And know that God, of what you do, of deeds, O people, their secret and their public, their hidden and their apparent, their good and their evil, [is] All-Seeing. He sees and knows it, so nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing of it is hidden from Him. He counts all of that for you, until He rewards you with the best of it. And his evil. The meaning of Baseer is one with sight, and it has the same meaning as seeing.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The readings differed in reading this, so the majority of the people of Medina, Iraq and Syria read it: Whoever wants to complete the breastfeeding with the ya’ in yatum and the nasb of breastfeeding - meaning: whoever among the fathers and mothers wants to complete the breastfeeding of his child.
Some of the people of Hijaz read it: Whoever wants to complete the breastfeeding with the ta’ in yatum and the nasb of breastfeeding as a description.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in this according to us is the reading of those who read with the ya’ in yatum and the nasb of breastfeeding.

Because God the Most High said: And mothers shall suckle their children, so they complete it if they and the child want to suckle their mother, and this is the reading that came with the widespread transmission that established the evidence, not the other reading.
As for the reading, it is with the fat-ha and nothing else.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.
The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Kufa and Ash-Sham read it as: La tudharar waladaha bi-waladha with a fatha on the ra’, with the interpretation: la tudharar, as a prohibition.
Some of the people of Hijaz and some of the people of Basra read it as: No mother should be harmed by her child, in the nominative case.

Whoever reads it in this way, his reading does not carry the meaning of prohibition, but rather it is [in the sense of] report, in apposition with his saying: No soul is charged except [with that within] its capacity.

So if the meaning of his saying: La-ta-daar, if it was read in the nominative case, was: It should be that you should not be harmed, or It should not be that you should be harmed, then Ya-ta-daar and An were deleted and Ta-daar was used in place of Ya-ta-daar, then it would have been obligatory to read it—if it was read with that meaning—in the accusative case, not in the nominative case, so that the intended meaning would be known by the accusative that was left before it, as was done with his saying: Fa-ta-seena-ma-da.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in that is the reading of the one who reads in the accusative, because it is a prohibition from God, the Most High, to each of the parents of the child from harming his companion to him, and it is forbidden for them to do so by the consensus of the Muslims.

And in the consensus of the reciters on reading: La tadhar with the fatha without the kasra, there is clear evidence of the neglect of the statement of the people of Arabic that I have quoted in this regard.

x: God Almighty means by that: And those of you who die, of the men, O people, and die, and leave wives, their husbands wait for themselves.
So where is the report about those who die?

It is abandoned, because he did not intend to intend to inform about them, but rather he intended to intend to inform about the duty of the women in waiting for the waiting period upon the death of their husbands, so he diverted the report from those who he began mentioning from the dead, to inform about their husbands and the duty of the waiting period upon them, since the meaning of what was intended by the speech was known and understood. It is similar to the saying of the speaker in speech: Some of your garment is torn, in omitting the report of what the speech began with, to inform about some of its causes.

i: And likewise the wives who are required to wait, since he only obligated them to wait for the causes of their husbands, he diverted the speech from informing about the one he began mentioning, to informing about the one he intended to inform about, as the poet said:
x: Perhaps if the wind blew me away, Ibn Abi Dhiban would regret it.

He said: Perhaps, then he said: That they may regret it, because the meaning of the words is: Perhaps Ibn Abi Dhiban will regret it, if the wind sways me against him, so he returned the report to what he intended, even though he had begun by mentioning something else.

i: And from this is the saying of the poet:
x: Didn't you know that Ibn Qais was killed without blood, and the house of humiliation has arrived?

Ibn Qais cancelled it, and he began by mentioning him, and he told about his killing, that it was humiliation. Some Arabists have claimed that the predicate of those who die is omitted, and that the meaning of the statement is: And those of you who die and leave wives behind, it is proper for them to wait after their death. He claimed that their death was not mentioned, as some words are omitted - and that they wait is in the nominative case, since it occurred in the place of should, and should is in the nominative case. We have shown the corruption of the statement of those who said that they wait is in the nominative case, since it occurred in the place of should in the past, so there is no need to repeat it. Another of them said: those who was not mentioned at all, because those in their predicate became like the interpretation of the recompense: Whoever meets you from us, you will attain good, whoever meets you from us, you will attain good.
He said: This is not permissible except in the sense of recompense.
In the two couplets that we have mentioned there is clear evidence that the statement on this matter is contrary to what they said.
As for his statement:
h
They shall wait concerning themselves

, he means by it: They shall keep themselves - refraining from husbands, perfume, adornment, and moving from the dwelling in which they lived during the lifetime of their husbands - for four months and ten days, unless they are pregnant, in which case they shall have to wait like this until they give birth. Then when they give birth, their waiting period ends at that time.
The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that: Some of them said the same as we said in it:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
h
they shall wait concerning themselves
four months and ten days, so this is the waiting period of the woman whose husband has died, unless she is pregnant, in which case her waiting period is until she gives birth to what is in her womb.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
h
they shall wait concerning themselves

four months and ten days, Ibn Shihab said: God made this waiting period for the woman whose husband has died, so if she is pregnant, then her waiting period is until she gives birth to her pregnancy, and if he delays beyond four months and ten, then whatever he delays, he does not permit her until she gives birth to her pregnancy.

x: We only said that what we described was meant by waiting, because the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are consistent.
And Sallam said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said:

c: Wakee’ and Abu Usamah narrated to us, on the authority of Shu’bah, and Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Ja’far narrated to us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Hamid bin Nafi’, he said:
m: I heard Zainab, the daughter of Umm Salamah, narrating, Abu Kurayb said: Amhu Usamah said: “On the authority of Umm Salamah, that a woman’s husband died and her eyes were complaining, so she came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask him about kohl, so he said: One of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:234
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
h
they shall wait concerning themselves

four months and ten days. Then when they have fulfilled their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner. And God is Acquainted with what you do. you would be in the worst of conditions during the pre-Islamic era, and she would stay in her house for a year if her husband died, and a dog would pass by her and she would throw dung at it! Why not four months and ten days?”

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us,
m: I heard Yahya ibn Saeed say, I heard Nafi’, on the authority of Safiyya bint Abi Ubayd, that she heard Hafsa bint Umar, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrate, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: It is not permissible for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn for more than three days, except for a husband, for whom she should mourn for four months and ten days. Yahya said: Mourning, according to us, means not wearing perfume, not wearing clothes dyed with saffron or turquoise, not applying kohl, and not adorning oneself.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Safiyya bint Abi Ubaid, on the authority of Hafsa bint Umar:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not permissible for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days, except for a husband.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said,
m: I heard Yahya bin Saeed say, Humayd bin Nafi’ told me: Zainab, the daughter of Umm Salamah, told him, on the authority of Umm Salamah - or Umm Habibah - the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that her daughter’s husband had died, and that she feared for her eye. Humayd claimed on the authority of Zainab: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: One of you used to throw dung at the end of a year, but it is only four months and ten days.” Ibn Bashar narrated, Yazid ibn Harun narrated, Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated, on the authority of Humayd ibn Nafiʿ, that he heard Zaynab bint Umm Salamah narrating on the authority of Umm Habibah or Umm Salamah that she said: “A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after her husband had died, and she had been complaining about her eye, and she wanted to apply kohl to her eye. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘One of you used to throw dung after a year, but it is only four months and ten days.’” Ibn Bashar said, Yazid said, Yahya said: So I asked Humayd about throwing dung. He said: When a woman in the pre-Islamic era had her husband die, she would go to the worst of her house and stay in it for a year, and when a year had passed, she would throw dung behind her. Ibn Bashar narrated, Yazid narrated, Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Humayd ibn Nafiʿ, with this chain of transmission similar to it. Abu Kurayb narrated, Ibn Idris narrated, Ibn Uyaynah narrated, on the authority of Ayyub ibn Musa and Yahya ibn Saʿid, on the authority of Humayd. Ibn Nafiʿ, on the authority of Zainab bint Umm Salamah, on the authority of Umm Salamah: “A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My daughter’s husband died and her eye is complaining. Should she apply kohl? He said: One of you used to throw dung at the end of a year, but now it has been four months and ten! I said: Why do you throw dung at the end of a year? He said: When the husband of one of the women of the Age of Ignorance died, she would put on her most modest clothes and sit in the worst of her houses. When a year had passed, she would take a piece of dung and roll it on the back of a donkey and say: I have become free from kohl.”

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Ahmad bin Yunus narrated to us, he said: Zuhair bin Muawiyah narrated to us, he said: Yahya bin Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Hamid bin Nafi’, on the authority of Zainab bint Abi Salamah, on the authority of her mother Umm Salamah and Umm Habibah,
m: the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “A woman from Quraysh came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My daughter’s husband died, and I fear for her eyes, and she wants kohl? He said: One of you used to throw dung at the end of a year! But it is only four months and ten!” Hamid said: So I said to Zainab: What is the end of a year? Zainab said: When a woman’s husband died in the pre-Islamic era, she would go to her worst house and sit there until a year had passed, then she would go out and throw a dung beetle behind her.
b.via: her mother Umm Salamah and Umm Habibah

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha:
m: She used to give a fatwa to a woman whose husband had died, that she should mourn for her husband until her waiting period was over, and not wear dyed or saffron-colored clothing, and not apply kohl to her eyes, or any kohl that had perfume in it, even if her eyes were sore, but she should apply aloes and any kohl that did not contain perfume, except kohl, and not wear jewelry, and wear white and not wear black.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: regarding a woman whose husband had died: She should not apply kohl, nor perfume, nor spend the night away from her house, nor wear dyed clothing. Except for a cloak that she wraps around herself. Hamid bin Mas'adah narrated, Sufyan narrated, Ibn Jurayj narrated, on the authority of Ata' who said: It reached me on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: A woman whose husband has died is forbidden from adorning herself and using perfume. Nasr bin Ali narrated, Abd al-A'la narrated, Ubaydullah narrated, on the authority of Nafi', on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: A woman whose husband has died is not to wear dyed clothes, nor touch perfume, nor apply kohl, nor comb her hair. And he did not see any harm in her wearing a cloak.

x: Others said: A woman whose husband has died is only commanded to wait for herself from her husbands in particular. As for perfume, adornment, and spending the night away from home, she was not forbidden from that, nor was she commanded to wait for herself from it. He who said that: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan: that he permitted adornment and pretense, and he did not see mourning as anything.

c: Hamid bin Masʿadah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ataʿ, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
h
they shall wait concerning themselves

four months and ten, he did not say, she shall wait concerning herself four months and ten,” she ... The proponents of this statement argued that God Almighty only ordered the deceased to wait before marrying, and they made the ruling of the verse specific, and what:

c: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Salami told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, and Muhammad ibn Muammar al-Bahrani told us, he said, Abu Amir told us,
m: they both said, Muhammad ibn Talhah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Haad, on the authority of Asma bint Umays, she said: When Jafar was killed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Take three days off, then do whatever you want.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Naim and Ibn al-Salt told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Talhah, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, on the authority of Asma, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. They said: This hadith from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has made clear: There is no mourning for a woman whose husband has died, and that the interpretation of his statement:
h
They shall wait
, concerning themselves, four months and ten days, is:
h
They shall wait
, concerning themselves, from husbands and nothing else.

x: As for those who have made mourning obligatory for a woman whose husband has died, and refraining from moving from the home in which she was living on the day her husband died, they have relied on the apparent meaning of the revelation, and they said: God has commanded the woman whose husband has died to wait, concerning herself, for four months and ten days. He has not commanded her to wait for something specifically mentioned in the revelation, but rather He has made the meanings of waiting general. They said: It is obligatory for her to wait, concerning herself, from everything, except for what an argument has given her that must be accepted. They said: Waiting, concerning herself, from perfume, adornment, and moving, is included in the generality of the verse, just as waiting, concerning herself, from husbands is included in it. They said: The report that we mentioned about adornment and perfume has been authenticated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

As for the transfer, Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Yunus bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Falih bin Sulayman, on the authority of Saʿd bin Ishaq bin Kaʿb bin ʿUjrah, on the authority of his aunt, on the authority of Al-Fariʿah bint Malik, the sister of Abu Saʿid Al-Khudri, she said: My husband was killed while I was in a house, so I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for permission to transfer, and he gave me permission. Then he called me after I had turned away, so I returned to him, and he said: O Fariʿah, until the book reaches its term. They said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, clarified the authenticity of what we said about the meaning of waiting for a woman whose husband has died, and he invalidated what contradicted it. They said: As for what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, it has no meaning, as it goes beyond the apparent meaning of the revelation and the established report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

They said: As for the report that was narrated on the authority of Asma bint Umays, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he ordered her to wear three days of mourning, then to do whatever she wanted - it does not indicate that there is no mourning for the woman, rather it only indicates the Prophet's, may God bless him and grant him peace, order for her to wear three days of mourning, then to do whatever she wanted of wearing whatever clothes she wanted of what is permissible for a woman in her waiting period to wear, which were not adornments or perfumed, because there may be clothes that are not adornments or clothes that are to be worn. This is like what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted the woman whose husband died to wear of the clothes of the clan and the Yemeni cloaks, because that is not adornment or clothes to be worn.
Likewise, every garment that has not been dyed after it was woven, which people dye to beautify it, she may wear it, because she wears it without adorning herself with the adornment that people know.
If someone were to say to us: How is it said:
h
They shall wait concerning themselves

four months and ten, and not say: and ten? Since the revelation is thus: Is the deceased’s waiting period ten days, or days? It is said: Rather, she waits by the days and nights. If he says: Since that is the case, how is it said: and ten? And it is not said: and ten? And ten without the ha is from the number of nights, not days? If that meaning is permissible in it, what you said, would you permit: I have ten, and you mean ten men and women? I say: That is permissible in the number of nights and days, but it is not permissible like that in the number of the sons of Adam, men and women. That is because the Arabs, in the days and nights in particular, if the number is vague, the nights are predominant, so that according to what has been narrated to us from them, they say: We fasted ten days of the month of Ramadan, because they give precedence to the nights over the days.

That is because the number in their view has been based on the nights, not the days. If they show the explanation of the number, they drop the ha’ from the feminine number and keep it in the masculine number, as God Almighty said: He subjected them to seven nights and eight days in succession (al-Haqqah 69:7). He dropped the ha’ from seven and kept it in eight. As for the sons of Adam, it is the custom of the Arabs, when men and women gather together, and then their number is unclear, to make it out to be the number of males without the females. This is because the males of the sons of Adam are marked, singular and plural, with a mark other than that of their females, and this is Surat Al-Baqarah 2:234
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
h
they shall wait concerning themselves
four months and ten days. Then when they have fulfilled their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner.

And God is Acquainted with what you do. not the case with all other things besides them. This is because the males of others may be marked with the mark of the female, as the male and female are called sheep, and the males and females of cows are called cows, but this is not the case with the sons of Adam.
What is the meaning of adding these ten days to the months?

It has been said about that, as: - Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to us, he said, Abu Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, regarding his statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
h
they shall wait concerning themselves
four months and ten, he said: I said: Why were these ten included with the four months?
He said: Because the soul is breathed into it in the ten.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said, Abu Asim narrated to me, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatadah, he said:
m: I asked Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: What is the matter with the ten? He said: In it the soul is breathed.

x: God Almighty means by that: When they reach the term in which it is permissible for them to do what was forbidden to them in their waiting period due to the death of their husbands - that is after their waiting period has ended, and the four months and ten days have passed, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner.

i: He says:
x: There is no blame upon you, O guardians - the guardians of the woman - for what the deceased does with themselves at that time, such as perfuming themselves and beautifying themselves and moving from the dwelling in which they were observing their waiting period, and marrying someone they are permitted to marry, in an acceptable manner.

He means by that: in what God has permitted and made permissible for them. It has been said: He meant marriage in particular. It has been said: The meaning of His statement: in an acceptable manner is only lawful marriage.

Who said that: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: There is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner, he said: the lawful and good.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: There is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner, he said: the lawful and good marriage.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: His statement:
h
In what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner
, he said: it is the lawful and good marriage.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: it is marriage.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: h
In what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner
, he said: in marriage from His identity, if he is known.

x: God Almighty means by that: And God is All-Aware of what you do, O guardians, in the matter of the women you are guardians of, of preventing them from marrying whomever they want to marry in a good manner, and other matters of yours and theirs, He is All-Aware, meaning He has experience and knowledge, nothing of it is hidden from Him.

God Almighty means by that: There is no blame upon you, O men, for what you suggest of proposing marriage to women, for women who are observing the waiting period after the death of their husbands, and you have not explicitly made a marriage contract.
The insinuation that is permitted in that is what:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And there is no blame upon you for what you suggest of proposing marriage to women
, he said: The insinuation is to say: I want to get married, and I love a woman for her matter and her matter, he suggests to her by speaking to her in a good manner.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: There is no blame upon you for what you offer of proposing to women. He said: I want to get married.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Proposing is what is not set up for proposing. Mujahid said: A man said to a woman at her husband’s funeral: Do not get ahead of me with yourself! She said: I have already preceded you!

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said, Shuʿbah narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
And there is no blame upon you for that which you make indirect proposal to women
, he said: Insinuation, as long as it is not set up for the proposal.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Hakam narrated to us, on the authority of ʿAmr, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: Insinuation, as long as you make indirect proposal to women, he said: Insinuation is to say to a woman during her waiting period: I do not want to marry anyone other than you, God willing, and I wish that I had found a righteous woman, and he does not set up a proposal for her as long as she is in her waiting period.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, ʿAbdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said, Muʿawiyah narrated to me, on the authority of ʿAli, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And there is no blame upon you for that which you make indirect proposal to women

, he said: He makes indirect proposals to her during her waiting period, he says to her: If you see that you should not precede me with yourself, and I wish that God had prepared a way between me and you, and similar words, so there is no blame. He narrated to me Al-Muthanna said, Adam Al-Asqalani told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
And there is no blame upon you for that which you express of proposal of marriage to women
, he said: It is for him to say to her during her waiting period: I want to get married, and I wish that God had provided me with a wife, and something like this, and he does not set out to propose.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Ubaydah,
m: regarding this verse, he said: He mentions her to her guardian, he says: Do not precede me with her.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And there is no blame upon you for what you express of marriage proposal to women
, he said, he says: You are indeed beautiful, and indeed you are a good wife, and indeed you are on the path to good.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: that he disliked to say: Do not get ahead of me with yourself.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
And there is no blame upon you for that which you express of marriage to women
, he said: It is the man saying to the woman: You are indeed beautiful, and indeed you are a good woman, and indeed you are toward good.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid
m: regarding His statement:
h
And there is no blame upon you for that which you express of marriage to women
, he said: He approaches the woman during her waiting period and says: By God, you are indeed beautiful, and indeed women are among my needs, and indeed you are toward good, God willing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail, on the authority of Muslim al-Bateen, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: It is a man saying: I want to get married, and if I get married, I will treat my wife well - this is an insinuation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail, on the authority of Muslim al-Bateen, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And there is no blame upon you for that which you express of a proposal of marriage to women
, he said: He says: I will give you, I will treat you well, I will do to you such and such.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, ʿAbd al-Wahhab told us, he said,
m: I heard Yahya ibn Saʿid, he said, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim told me regarding His statement:
h
In that which you express of a proposal of marriage to women
, he said: A man saying to a woman during her waiting period, insinuating a proposal of marriage: By God, I am interested in you, and I am anxious about you, and something like this.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi told us, he said, I heard Yahya ibn Saʿid He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim told me:
m: He heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: In what you have suggested in the engagement of women, it is the man saying to the woman: You are beautiful, you are successful, and you are on the path to goodness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I said to Ata’: What does the suitor say? He said: He suggests indirectly, and does not reveal anything. He says: I have a need, and be happy, you are successful, praise be to God, and he does not reveal anything. Ata’ said: And she says: I hear what you are saying, and does not promise anything, and does not say: Perhaps that is it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid ibn Nasr told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim told me:
m: He heard al-Qasim say about a woman whose husband dies, and the man wants to propose to her and wants to speak to her, what is the most beautiful thing to say? He said: He says: I am interested in you, I am keen on you, I am amazed by you, and similar statements.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And there is no blame upon you for what you express in marriage proposal to women
, he said: There is no problem with a gift in exposing marriage.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hisham narrated to us, he said: Mughira informed us, he said:
m: Ibrahim did not see any problem in giving her a gift during her waiting period, if it was his business.

c: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Aamer,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And there is no blame upon you for what you express in marriage proposal to women
, he said: He says: You are a benefactor, you are an admirer, you are beautiful, and if God has decreed something, it will be.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, regarding his saying:
h
And there is no blame upon you for what you propose to women
. He said: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi used to say: You are indeed amazed, and I am indeed desirous of you.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us, and he told me
m: - meaning Shabib - on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi that he said regarding this verse: And there is no blame upon you for that which you express of proposal to women, he said: Do not take her covenant that she will not marry anyone other than you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And there is no blame upon you for that which you express of a proposal of marriage to women
, he said: My father used to say: Everything that was, without deciding on the marriage contract, is what God Almighty said:
h
And there is no blame upon you for that which you express of a proposal of marriage to women

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told me, he said, Zayd told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Sufyan. He said:
h
And there is no blame upon you for what you suggest of proposing marriage to women
. The insinuation, as we have heard, is that a man says while she is in her waiting period: You are beautiful, you are good, you are a good person, I admire you, and so on. This is the insinuation.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman, on the authority of his aunt Sakina bint Hanzala ibn Abdullah ibn Hanzala, who said:
m: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn ʿAli came to me while I was in my waiting period and said: O daughter of Hanzala, I am one of those who know my kinship to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the right of my grandfather over me, and my precedence in Islam. I said: May God forgive you, O Abu Jaʿfar! You propose marriage to me during my waiting period, and you are being questioned about! He said: Have you already done so? I only told you about my kinship to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and my position! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon Umm Salamah, who was with her cousin Abu Salamah, and he died, and the Messenger of God, Surat al-Baqarah 2:235 There is no blame upon you for what you hint at of betrothal to women or what you conceal within yourselves. God knows that you will mention them, but do not make a secret promise to them except by saying an appropriate word. And do not determine to tie the marriage knot until the term has reached its term. And know that God knows what is within your souls, so beware of Him and know that God is Forgiving and Forbearing. may God bless him and grant him peace, kept mentioning to her his status with God while he was straining his hand, until the mark of the mat was on his hand from the intensity of his straining his hand, and that was not a sermon.
b.via: his aunt Sakina bint Hanzala ibn Abdullah ibn Hanzala

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Aqil told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: And there is no blame upon you for what you make indirect proposal to women, he said: There is no blame upon the one who proposes to them before they are released, if they are in their souls about that.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Malik told me, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin al-Qasim, on the authority of his father
m: that he used to say about the statement of God, the Most High: And there is no blame upon you for what you make indirect proposal to women: that a man says to a woman while she is in the waiting period after the death of her husband: You are dear to me, and I am eager for you, and God is driving good and provision to you, and similar words.

x: The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of The sermon.
