Some of them said: The sermon is the mention, and the sermon is the testimony. It is as if the one who said this statement interpreted the statement: There is no blame upon you for what you offer of mentioning women in their presence. The one who said this statement claimed that he said: Do not make secret appointments with them, because when he said: There is no blame upon you, it is as if he said: Mention them, but do not make secret appointments with them.
Others of them said: He proposed, he proposed and he proposed. He said: And the statement of God the Most High:
“He said: So what is your business, O Samaritan?”
it is said that it is from this.

i: He said:
x: As for the sermon, it is the one who is being addressed [by it], from their saying: He preached on the pulpit and he preached. Abu Jaʿfar said: And the sermon, in my opinion, is the action of the speaker’s saying: I proposed to so-and-so, like the sitting, from his saying: He sat, or the sitting, from his saying: He sat. And the meaning of their saying: So-and-so proposed to so-and-so, is that he asked her to propose to him in her person, and that is his need, from their saying: What is your business?
Meaning: What is your need, and what is your matter? As for the insinuation, it is what was from the tune of speech by which the listener understands what is understood explicitly.

God Almighty means by His saying: or you concealed it within yourselves, or you concealed it within yourselves and kept it secret, from proposing to them, and intending to marry them while they are of their number, then there is no blame upon you in that also, if you did not intend to tie the marriage knot until the book reaches its term.

i: It is said from it: So-and-so concealed this matter in his soul, so he concealed it, and concealed it, if he hid it, he concealed it and we concealed it, and he sat in the shelter and did not hear his concealment in my soul, but it is said: I concealed it in the house or on the ground, if I hid it in it, and from it is His saying, God Almighty: As if they were hidden eggs (al-Saffat 37:49) meaning hidden, and from it is the saying of the poet:
x: Three of the three old ones who were from the frost And it is with a taa’, which is better, and yakun.
It is said: his clothes protected him from the cold and he protected the house from the wind. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Or you concealed it within yourselves, he said: Concealment is mentioning her proposal to himself, without revealing it to her. All of this is a known solution.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: Or you concealed it within yourselves, he said: That he enters and converts to Islam and is guided if he wishes, and does not say anything.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdul-Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, he said,
m: I heard Yahya bin Saeed say: Abdul-Rahman bin Al-Qasim told me: that he heard Al-Qasim bin Muhammad say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: Or you concealed it within yourselves, he said: You made it in your soul to marry her and concealed it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told me, he said, Zayd told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Sufyan: Or you concealed it within yourselves, he said: That he was pleased in his soul to marry her.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: Or did you conceal it within yourselves, he said: Did you keep it secret?

x: In God’s permission of what He permitted of insinuating marriage to a woman in her waiting period during her waiting period and His prohibition of explicitness, what made clear the difference between the ruling on insinuating in all meanings of speech and the ruling on explicitness, from it. If that is the case, it becomes clear that insinuating slander is not explicitly stating it, and that the punishment for insinuating slander, if it were obligatory as it is obligatory by stating it, then it would be obligatory from the sin of insinuating a proposal during the waiting period, similar to what is obligatory by deciding to contract marriage during it. And in the distinction of God the Most High between their two rulings in that, there is clear evidence of the difference in the rulings of that in slander.
By that, the Most High means: God knows that you will mention the women in their waiting period in the engagement in yourselves and with your tongues, as:

c: Ibn Wakeeʿ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: God knows that you will mention them, he said: the engagement.

c: Abu Al-Saʿib Salim ibn Junadah told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
There is no blame upon you for what you express of engagement to women
, he said: your mentioning them in your soul. He said: So it is the statement of God: God knows that you will mention them.

c: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaidah narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement: God knows that you will mention them, he said: It is the sermon.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the secret that God the Most High forbade His servants from making promises to those who are waiting for him.
Some of them said: It is adultery.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Hammam narrated to us, on the authority of Salih al-Dahhan, on the authority of Jabir ibn Zayd:
m: But do not make a secret promise to them, he said: adultery.

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAʿla narrated to us, he said, al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: regarding His statement: But do not make a secret promise to them, he said: adultery.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Yahya narrated to us, he said, Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Abu Naʿim narrated to us, he said,
m: Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Majlaz: But do not make secret promises to them. He said: Adultery. It was said to Sufyan al-Taymi: Did he mention it? He said: Yes.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of a man, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding making promises, like the statement of Abu Majlaz.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Yazid ibn Ibrahim told us, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: Adultery.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya told us, he said, Ash’ath and Imran told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman and Yahya told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: I heard Ibrahim say: Do not make secret promises to them, he said: Adultery.

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim told me, he said, Abu Nuʿaym told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Aʿla told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement: Do not make secret promises to them, he said: Adultery.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: But do not make secret promises to them, he said: adultery.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Suwaid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement: But do not make a secret promise to them, he said: Fornication.
Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak.

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me: Yazid ibn Harun told us: Juwaybir told us, on the authority of al-Dahhak:
m: Do not make a secret promise to them, he said: The secret is adultery.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: said: Do not make secret promises to them. He said: That secret is suspicion. A man would enter because of suspicion and he would propose marriage, so God forbade that except for one who said something good.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Mansour told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: and Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak and Sulayman At-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Majlaz: that they said: Adultery.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on Ar-Rabiʿ, his statement: But do not make secret promises to them, refers to obscenity and submissive speech.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: ʿAbd Al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muʿmar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: But do not make secret promises to them, he said: It is obscenity.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Do not take their covenant and their pledges regarding their number that they will not marry anyone other than you.

Who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Do not make secret promises to them, meaning: Do not say to her: I am in love, and promise me that you will not marry anyone other than me, and so on.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement: Do not make secret promises to them, he said: He does not make her promise to do so-and-so that she will not marry anyone other than him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Aamer,
m: Mujahid, and Ikrimah, they said: He does not take her covenant during her waiting period that she will not marry anyone other than him.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, he said:
m: It was mentioned to me on the authority of Al-Sha’bi that he said regarding this verse: Do not make secret promises to them, he said: Do not take her covenant that she will not marry anyone other than you.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Hakam narrated to us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: But do not make a secret promise to them, he said: He does not take her oath that she will not marry anyone other than him.

c: Ya’qub narrated to me, he said, Hisham narrated to us, he said, Ismail bin Salim narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: I heard him say regarding His statement, And do not make a secret promise to them, he said: He does not take her oath that she will not marry anyone other than you, and do not require the marriage contract until the waiting period expires.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us,
m: Surat al-Baqarah 2:235 There is no blame upon you for what you hint at of betrothal to women or what you conceal within yourselves. God knows that you will mention them, but do not make a secret promise to them except by saying an appropriate word. And do not determine to tie the marriage knot until the term has reached its term. And know that God knows what is within your souls, so beware of Him and know that God is Forgiving and Forbearing. on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: And do not make a secret promise to them, he said: He does not take a covenant from her that she will not marry anyone other than him.

c: Musa narrated to me, he said, Amr narrated to us, he said, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: But do not make a secret promise to them, he said: Keep to yourself, for I will marry, and he takes a covenant from her: Do not marry anyone other than me.

c: Bishr bin Mu’adh narrated to us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ narrated to us, he said, Sa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: But do not make a secret promise to them, He said: This is about a man who takes a woman’s oath while she is in her waiting period that she will not marry anyone else. So God forbade that and advanced it, and permitted engagement and speaking in a good manner, and forbade indecency and submissive speech.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us, and Ali told me, he said, Zaid told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Sufyan: But do not make a secret promise to them, he said: That you make a secret promise to her on such and such, on the condition that you will not marry anyone else.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement: Do not make a secret promise to them, he said: A secret promise is that he takes from her a pledge and a covenant that she will confine herself to him and not marry anyone else.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. And others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: That a man says to her: Do not get ahead of me with yourself.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, and he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid in God says:
m: But do not make secret promises to them. He said: A man saying to a woman: Do not let yourself be taken away from me, for I will marry you, this is not permissible.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: It is a man saying to a woman: Do not let yourself be taken away.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: But do not make secret promises to them. He said: A promise is to say: Do not let yourself be taken away from me.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: But do not make secret promises to them, that is to say: Do not let yourself be taken away from me.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And do not marry them during their waiting period secretly.

Who said that: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: But do not make a secret appointment with them, he said: Do not marry them secretly, then he keeps her, until when she is ready, he reveals that and consummates the marriage.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: But do not make a secret appointment with them, he said: My father used to say: Do not make a secret appointment with them, then he keeps her and she has acquired the marriage contract, then when she is ready, he reveals that and consummates the marriage.

x: The most correct of the statements in interpreting that is the interpretation of the one who said: The secret, in this place, is adultery. That is because the Arabs call sexual intercourse and a man’s penetration of a woman a secret, because that is something that happens between men and women in secret and not apparent and not seen, so it is called a secret because of its concealment. From that is the statement of Ruʿbah ibn al-ʿAjaj: He kept her secrets after the honeymoon and did not put her between friction and love He meant by that: He refrained from having intercourse with her after a long period of doing so. From this is the saying of Al-Hutay’ah: Their neighbor's secret is forbidden to them, and their neighbor eats the tip of the bowl. Likewise, everything that a person hides in himself is called a secret. It is also said: He is in the secret of his people, meaning: in their best and most honorable.

Since the secret in her speech is only directed to one of these three aspects, and it was known that one of them was not meant by his saying: But do not make a secret promise to them, which is the secret that is the meaning of choice and honor, then there remained only the other two aspects, which is the secret that means what the self of the promiser concealed from the two who promised, and the secret that means covering and sexual intercourse. Since there remained nothing else, and the indication was clear that one of them was not meant by it, it is correct that the other is meant by it.

What is the indication that making a secret promise is not meant by it, according to what was said by the one who said that its meaning is: the man took a covenant from the woman that she would not marry anyone other than him, or according to what was said by the one who said: the man’s saying to her: Do not get ahead of me with yourself?

Because if the secret is in the meaning that those who said that interpreted it, then that secret will not be devoid of being the man’s promise to the woman and his asking her not to marry anyone other than him, or it is the marriage that he asked her to accept after the expiration of her waiting period and after he concluded the marriage contract for her, without anyone other than him. If the secret that God forbade the man from making promises to women in waiting is taking a pledge from them not to marry anyone other than him, then it is invalid that the secret means: what is hidden from matters in the souls, or is spoken about and not known, and the publicity of the matter becomes a secret. This is contrary to what is reasonable in the language of the one in whose tongue the Qur’an was revealed.

Unless the speaker of this statement says: God only forbade men from making promises to them in secret between them and them, not that the speech itself - even if it was announced - is a secret. It is said to him: If he says that, then the permissibility of their promise of marriage and engagement must be explicit and public, since what is forbidden in terms of promises is what is secret. If he says that is so, then he has departed from the opinion of the entire nation. However, this is not from the opinion of anyone who interpreted the verse that the secret here means a covenant not to marry anyone other than a covenanted one. If he says that is not permissible, then it is said to him: It is invalid that the meaning of that is: the man’s secret promise to the woman. Because the meaning of that, if that were so, would not be forbidden for him to promise her openly and publicly. And in that being forbidden to him secretly and publicly, it does not make clear that the meaning of the secret in this place is not the meaning of the man’s secret promise to the woman that she will not marry anyone other than him if her waiting period expires, or if this interpretation is invalid, the meaning of that is: the engagement and marriage that the woman promised the man that she will not go back to anyone other than him.

If that is the case, then it can only be with a guardian and witnesses, openly and not secretly. How can it be called a secret, when it is public and cannot be kept secret? And in the length of these aspects, it is an interpretation of his saying: But do not make secret appointments with them, with what we have shown from the evidence, and the clarity of the correctness of the interpretation of that is that it means intercourse and sexual intercourse. And since that is correct, then the interpretation of the verse: And there is no blame upon you, O people, in what you have presented to the women in waiting period after the death of their husbands, of proposing to women, and that is your need for them, so you did not explicitly state to them the marriage and the need for them, since you concealed it in yourselves, so you concealed your need for them and your proposing to them in yourselves, as long as they are in their number?

God knows that you will mention their engagement while they are in their waiting period, so He permitted you to hint at that to them, and He removed the hardship from what your souls concealed - a ruling from Him - but He forbade you from making an appointment with them to have intercourse during their waiting period, by one of you saying to one of them during her waiting period: I have married you in my soul, and I am only waiting for the end of your waiting period, and by that saying he asks her for the possibility of intercourse and sexual intercourse with her, so God, the Most High, forbade that.

Then God, the Most High, said: Except that you speak a respectable word, so He excepted the respectable word from what He forbade of a man making a secret appointment with a woman, and it is not of the same kind, but it is from the exception that I mentioned before: it comes with a meaning different from the one before it in the context specifically, and except in it has the meaning of but, so His saying: Except that you speak a respectable word is from it - and its meaning is: but say a respectable word.

God, the Most High, permitted him to say to her what is appropriate during her waiting period, and that is what He permitted him to say: And there is no blame upon you for that which you expressly propose to women, as:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: Except that you say a proper word, he said: He says: I am interested in you, and I hope that we will meet.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Except that you say a proper word, he said: It is His saying: If you see that you should not get ahead of me with yourself.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Except that you say a proper word, he said: He means insinuation.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Except that you say a decent word, he said: meaning insinuation.

c: Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And there is no blame upon you for that which you insinuate of marriage proposal to women to until the prescribed period has come to an end, he said: It is a man who enters upon a woman while she is in her waiting period and says: By God, you are truly worthy and noble, and you are truly desirable, and you delight me, and if something is destined to happen, it will be. This is the decent word.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said: Mihran told us
m: - and Ali told me, he said: Zayd told us - they both said: Sufyan said: Except that you say a decent word, he said: He says: I am desirous of you, and I hope, God willing, that we will meet.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: Except that you say a decent word, he said: He says: You have such and such with me, and you have such and such with me, and I will give you such and such. He said: All of this and what was before the marriage contract was concluded, all of this was abrogated by His statement:
h
And do not resolve on the marriage contract until the prescribed term has been fulfilled

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Unless you say a proper word, he said: A woman is divorced or her husband dies, so a man comes to her and says: Keep yourself to yourself, for I have a desire for you, so she says: And I am the same, so his soul longs for her. This is the well-known statement.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement: And do not resolve to tie the marriage knot, and do not validate the marriage knot during the waiting period of a woman in her waiting period, so that you make it obligatory between you and them and conclude it before the end of the waiting period, until the prescribed period has reached its term, meaning: they reach the term of the book that God Almighty explained in His statement: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten, so He made reaching the term of the book, and the meaning for those who are married, is that the man does not Surat al-Baqarah 2:235 There is no blame upon you for what you hint at of betrothal to women or what you conceal within yourselves. God knows that you will mention them, but do not make a secret promise to them except by saying an appropriate word.
And do not determine to tie the marriage knot until the term has reached its term.

And know that God knows what is within your souls, so beware of Him and know that God is Forgiving and Forbearing. marry the woman in her waiting period, so he resolves to tie the marriage knot with her until her waiting period has ended, so he reaches the term that God has set in His book for its expiration, as:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar and Amr bin Ali told us, they said, ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, and al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, ʿAbd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: until the prescribed period has reached its term, he said: until the waiting period has ended.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: until the prescribed period reaches its term, he said: until four months and ten days have passed.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: until the prescribed period reaches its term, he said: until the waiting period expires.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Sa’d told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: until the prescribed period reaches its term, he said: until the waiting period expires.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not determine to tie the marriage knot until the prescribed period reaches its term
, he said: until the waiting period expires.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: until the prescribed period reaches its term, he said: no. He marries her until her term is over.

c: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, he said, Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, he said, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not determine to tie the marriage contract until the prescribed period has reached its term
, he said: For fear that the woman will marry before the expiration of the waiting period.

c: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, he said, Abdul A’la narrated to us, he said, Sa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And do not determine to tie the marriage contract until the prescribed period has reached its term
, until the waiting period has ended.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Mihran narrated to us, and Ali narrated to me, he said, Zaid narrated to us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement: Until the prescribed period has reached its term, he said: Until the waiting period has ended.

x: By that, the Most High meant, and know, O people, that God knows what is in your souls of their desires and marriage to them and other matters of yours, so beware of Him. He says, so beware of God and fear Him in your souls, lest you do anything that He has forbidden you from, such as determining to tie the marriage contract with them, or making a secret appointment with them in Their number, and other things that He has forbidden you to do regarding them when they are in a state of waiting, and other than that, And know that God is Forgiving. Meaning: He is the One who conceals the sins of His servants and covers them, in what men conceal in their souls of proposing to women in a state of waiting, and mentioning them when they are in a state of waiting, and other than that of their sins. And His saying: Forbearing, meaning: He is the One who is patient and does not hasten to punish His servants for their sins.
God Almighty means by His saying:
h
There is no blame upon you
h
there is no blame upon you
if you divorce women. He says:
h
There is no blame upon you

in divorcing your wives and your husbands, as long as you have not touched them, meaning: as long as you have not had intercourse with them. And touching, in this instance, is a euphemism for the name of intercourse, as: - Hamid bin Mas'adah told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari' told us, and Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja'far told us, they both said, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa'id bin Jubayr, he said, Ibn Abbas said: Touching is intercourse, but God euphemizes what He wills with what He wills.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Touching is sexual intercourse.

x: There are different readings of this. The majority of the people of Hijaz and Basra read it as: Ma lam tamasuhunna with the opening of the ta’ of tamsuhunna, without an alif, from your saying: masastahu amsa masan and masisaan and masisa is shortened and doubled and not in the flow. It is as if they chose this reading, in order to link it to the reading agreed upon in His statement: And no man has touched me (Al Imran 3:47/Maryam 19:20).
Others read it as: Ma lam tamasuhuna, with a damma on the ta’ and the alif after the mim, as they linked it to the agreed-upon reading in His statement:
h
Then the freeing of a slave before they touch each other (al-Mujadilah
: 3). They made it mean the action of each of the man and woman towards the other, from your saying: I touched the thing, I touched it, I touched it.

What we see in that is that they are two readings with correct meanings, and they agree in interpretation, even if there is an additional meaning in one of them, which does not require a difference in the ruling and concept. For it is not unknown to a person of understanding, if it is said to him: You touched my wife, that the touched one has encountered from her body the same thing that his like has encountered from the body of the touched one. So each of them, even if the report is isolated about him that he is the one who touched his companion, it is understood by that same report that his touched companion has touched him. So there is no reason to rule for one of the two readings, with the agreement of their meanings, and the frequency of readings with each of them, that it is more correct than the other. Rather, the reader must be correct in his reading, whichever of them he reads.
Rather, what God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them

, is the divorced women before consummation of the marriage in which a dowry has been specified for them. And we only said that this is so, because every married woman is one of two things: either a dowry has been specified for her, or one that has not been specified for her. We know from what follows from the words of God the Almighty that what is meant by His words:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them

, is the one named. Because if the one meant by that was not the one for whom the dowry was imposed, then His words: or you impose upon them an obligation, would not have had a reasonable meaning. Since there is no meaning to the statement of someone:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them
, or before you have imposed an obligation.
Since there is no meaning to that, it is known that the correct interpretation of that is:
h
There is no blame upon you
if you divorce those of your women for whom the dowry was imposed before you have touched them, and those who were not imposed before the imposition.
God the Almighty meant by His words: or you impose upon them, or make it obligatory for them.
And by his saying: an obligation, an obligatory dowry, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Or you impose for them an obligation, he said: The obligation is the dowry. And the origin of the obligation is the obligatory, as the poet said: It was an obligation for what I did, just as stoning was an obligation for adultery. Meaning: Just as stoning was obligatory as a punishment for adultery. Therefore it was said: The Sultan imposed it on so-and-so for two thousand, meaning by that: He made it obligatory for him, and provided for him from the Diwan.

x: God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And provide for them
, and give them what they can enjoy from your money, according to your status and levels of wealth and poverty. Then the people of interpretation differed Surat Al-Baqarah 2:236
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them
or specified for them an obligation.
h
And provide for them

, the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability - a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the doers of good. regarding the amount that God commanded men to do from that.
Some of them said: The highest of it is the servant, and less than that is money, and less than that is clothing.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muʿammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, he said:
m: The highest of the enjoyment of divorce is the servant, and less than that is money, and less than that is clothing. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated, Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Ismail ibn Umayyah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Ahmad narrated, Abu Ahmad narrated, Sufyan narrated, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement:
h
And give them a provision according to their

means, according to the wealthier according to his ability and according to the poor according to his ability, I said to him: What is the average provision for a divorced woman? He said: Her veil, her shirt, her jilbab, and her cloak. Al-Muthanna narrated, Abu Saleh narrated, Mu’awiyah narrated, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “
h
And give them a provision according to their

means, according to the wealthier according to his ability and according to the poor according to his ability, a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the doers of good,” so this man marries a woman and does not specify a dowry for her, then he divorces her before marrying her, so God, the Most High, commanded him to give her a provision according to his hardship and evil. If he was well-off, he would provide her with a servant or something similar. If he was poor, he would provide her with three garments or something like that.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
And provide for them

, the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability, he said: I said to Ash-Sha’bi: What is the middle ground? He said: Her clothing in her house, her armor, her veil, her cloak, and her jilbab. Ash-Sha’bi said: Shuraih would provide for her with five hundred.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of ‘Amir:
m: Shuraih would provide for her with five hundred. I said to ‘Amir: What is the middle ground? He said: Her clothes in her house: a shield, a veil, a sheet, and a cloak.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Aamer Al-Shaabi that he said:
m: The average of the mut'ah is the woman's clothes in her house: a shield, a veil, a sheet, and a cloak.

c: Imran bin Musa told us, he said: Abdul-Warith told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Al-Shaabi:
m: Shuraih enjoyed five hundred. Al-Shaabi said: The average of the mut'ah: a shield, a veil, a sheet, and a cloak.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi' bin Anas
m: regarding his statement: "
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or appointed for them a dowry

. But give them a provision, the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability - a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the doers of good." He said: It is a man who marries a woman and does not give her a poor dowry, then he divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, so she is entitled to a provision according to what is acceptable but not a dowry. He said: The minimum of that is three garments, a shirt, a veil, a jilbab, and a lower garment.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them

until he reached a duty upon the doers of good. This is about a man who marries a woman and does not name a dowry for her, then he divorces her before consummating the marriage with her, so she is entitled to a reasonable dowry, but she is not entitled to a fixed portion. It was said: If he has enough, then a lower garment, a shirt, and a veil are essential.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah narrated to us, on the authority of Salih bin Salih, he said:
m: Aamer was asked: How much does a man give his wife in a dowry? He said: According to his wealth.

c: Ali bin Sahl narrated to me, he said: Muammil narrated to us, he said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Sa’d bin Ibrahim, he said:
m: I heard Humayd bin Abdur-Rahman bin Awf narrating on the authority of his mother, she said: It is as if I am looking at a black slave girl, Abdur-Rahman, the Imam of Abu Salamah, bathed her when he divorced her. Shu’bah was asked: What did he bathe her for? He said: He gave her a temporary marriage.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, on the authority of Sa'd Ibn Ibrahim, on the authority of Humayd Ibn Abdur-Rahman Ibn Awf, on the authority of his mother,
m: similarly, on the authority of Abdur-Rahman Ibn Awf.

c: Al-Hasan Ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdur-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Mu'ammar narrated to us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said:
m: He used to give her a temporary marriage with a servant, or with maintenance or clothing. He said: And Al-Hasan Ibn Ali gave her a temporary marriage - I think he said: with ten thousand.

c: Al-Hasan Ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdur-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Mu'ammar narrated to us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Sa'd Ibn Ibrahim:
m: That Abdur-Rahman Ibn Awf divorced his wife and gave her a temporary marriage with a servant.

c: I was told by Abdullah Ibn Yazid Al-Muqri, on the authority of Sa'id Ibn Abi Ayoub, he said: Aqeel narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: That he used to say about the temporary marriage of a divorced woman: The highest is the servant, and the lowest is clothing and maintenance. And he saw that it was as God the Most High said: Upon the wealthy is his due, and on the poor is his due.

x: Others said: The amount of that - if the husband and the wife disagree about it - is half the dowry of a woman like that who was married without a dowry specified in the contract. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and his companions.

The correct opinion on that is what Ibn ʿAbbas and those who said the same thing said: that what is due from that for the divorced woman on the man is according to the extent of his hardship and evil, as God the Most High said:
h
Upon the wealthy is his ability and on the poor is his ability
, not according to the extent of the woman. If that was due on the woman according to the dowry of her peers up to half of it, then God the Most High’s saying:
h
Upon the wealthy is his ability and on the poor is his ability
, would not have had an understood meaning, and the statement would have been:
h
And provide for them

according to their ability and half the dowry of their peers. And in God the Most High informing His servants that that is according to the extent of the man’s hardship and evil, not according to her ability and half the dowry of her peers, what shows the correctness of what we said and the invalidity of what contradicts it.

This is because a woman's dowry may be a large sum of money, and the man, when he divorces her, is poor and does not own anything. If he is ordered to pay half of her dowry, he is obligated to pay what some who have been well-off are unable to pay, so how about the one who is able to? If he does that to him, the judge has applied the ruling of the statement of God the Most High: Upon the wealthy is his means, and on the poor is his means - but that is according to the man's hardship and evil, and does not exceed a servant or her value, if the husband is well-off. If he is poor, and he can afford the minimum amount of clothing for her, which is three garments or something like that, then that is ordered against him. If he is unable to do that, then it is according to his ability. That is according to the effort of the just imam when the dispute is brought before him about it.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his statement:
h
And provide for them
, is it obligatory or recommended?

Some of them said: It is obligatory, and the provision is ordered from the wealth of the divorced man, just as he is ordered to pay for all the debts owed to him by others. They said: This is obligatory for every divorced woman, whoever she is from his wives.

Those who said this: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah used to say: Every divorced woman has a right to enjoyment, whether he has consummated the marriage with her or not, even if he has given her a share.

c: Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus 10:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: Every divorced woman has a right to enjoyment, and for the one whom he divorced before consummating the marriage and did not give her a share.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding this verse: And divorced women shall have a right to enjoyment according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:241)
, he said: Every divorced woman has a right to enjoyment according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, he said:
m: I heard Saeed bin Jubair say: Every divorced woman has a provision.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, he said:
m: Abu Al-Aaliyah used to say: Every divorced woman has a provision. Al-Hasan used to say: Every divorced woman has a provision.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Amir told us, he said, Qurrah told us, he said,
m: Al-Hasan was asked about a man who divorced his wife before consummating the marriage with her, does she have a provision? Al-Hasan said: Yes, by God! It was said to the questioner, who was Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, do you not read this verse: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and have already specified for them a provision, then half of what you specified? He said: Yes, by God!

x: Others said: The provision for a divorced woman from her divorced husband is obligatory, but it is obligatory for every divorced woman except for the divorced woman for whom a dower was specified. As for the divorced woman for whom a dower was specified, if she is divorced before consummating the marriage with her, then she is not entitled to a provision, but she is entitled to half of the specified dower.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Ubaydullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’:
m: Ibn Umar used to say: Every divorced woman has a pleasure, except the one who was divorced but did not consummate the marriage with her, and he had specified for her, then she is entitled to half the dowry, and there is no pleasure for her.

c: Tamim bin Al-Muntasir told us, he said, Abdullah bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Ubaydullah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday and Abdul-A’la told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab -
m: regarding the one who divorces his wife and has specified for her - that he said regarding pleasure: She had the pleasure in the verse in Al-Ahzab, but when the verse in Al-Baqarah was revealed, she was given half of her dowry if he had specified it, and there is no pleasure for her, and if he had not specified it, then she is entitled to the pleasure.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday and Abdul-A’la told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Sa’id,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr bin Mu’adh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada
m: said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab used to say: If he did not consummate the marriage with her, then he gave her a dowry in Surat Al-Ahzab, then the verse in Surat Al-Baqarah was revealed:
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry

, then give half of what you specified, so this verse abrogated what came before it, if he did not consummate the marriage with her, and he had specified a dowry for her, then he gave her half and no dowry.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashar told us, they said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saʿid Ibn Al-Musayyab, he said:
m: This verse was abrogated: O you who believe! When you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period to count for them, so provide for them (al-Ahzab 33:49), the verse in Al-Baqarah.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said, ʿAbd Al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Every divorced woman has a provision, except the one whom he Surat Al-Baqarah 2:236
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them
or specified for them an obligation.
h
And provide for them

, the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability - a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the doers of good. separated from and he had stipulated for her before he had consummated the marriage with her.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid -
m: regarding the woman whose husband divorces her before consummating the marriage, and he has set a dowry for her - he said: She is not entitled to a dowry.

c: Ya'qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayyub told us, on the authority of Nafi'
m: who said: If a man marries a woman and he has set a dowry for her, then he divorces her before consummating the marriage, she is entitled to half of the dowry, and she is not entitled to a dowry. But if he has not set a dowry for her, she is only entitled to a dowry.

c: Ya'qub told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said,
m: Ibn Abi Nujayh was asked, and I was listening: About a man who marries and then divorces her before consummating the marriage, and he has set a dowry for her, is she entitled to a dowry? He said: Ata' used to say: She is not entitled to a dowry.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar -
m: regarding the one for whom a dowry was imposed but he did not consummate the marriage - he said: If she is divorced, she is entitled to half the dowry and there is no enjoyment for her.

c: Muhammad bin al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Ja’far narrated to us, he said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: Shuraih used to say - regarding the man who divorces his wife before consummating the marriage with her, and he has specified a dowry for her - he said: She is entitled to half the dowry.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Shuraih, he said:
m: She is entitled to half the dowry.

x: Others said: Enjoyment is a right for every divorced woman, except that some of it is decided upon the divorcer, and some of it is not decided upon him, and he is obligated to give it between himself and God.

Who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said: There are two types of pleasures, one of which is decided by the ruler, and the other is a right upon the righteous: Whoever divorces before the marriage is prescribed and consummated, then he is to be taken for the pleasure, so there is no dowry due upon him. And whoever divorces after the marriage is consummated or prescribed, then the pleasure is a right.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab,
m: God said: “
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them
or specified for them a dowry.
h
And give them a provision

, the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability - a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the doers of good.” So if a man marries a woman and does not specify a dowry for her, then he divorces her before he touches her and before specifying a dowry for her, then he is only required to give a provision according to what is acceptable, which the ruler specifies for her according to what is acceptable, and she does not have to wait. God the Almighty said:
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry

, then give half of what you specified. So if a man divorces a woman and has specified a dowry for her but has not touched her, then she is entitled to half of her dowry, and she does not have to count it.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, he said, Zuhair told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, that he said:
m: There are two types of enjoyment, one of which the ruler decides, but the other is not decided: The enjoyment that the ruler decides is a right upon the doers of good, and the enjoyment that the ruler does not decide is a right upon the righteous.

x: Others said: The ruler and the ruler do not decide anything of that upon the divorcer, but rather that is from God the Almighty as an exhortation and guidance to enjoy the divorced woman.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam:
m: That a man divorced his wife, so she took his case to Shuraih, and he recited this verse: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous (al-Baqarah 2:241). He said: If you are among the righteous, then you are obligated to provide for her. And he did not rule in her favor. Shu’bah said: I found it written with me on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad, he said:
m: Shuraih used to say about the enjoyment of the divorced woman: Do not refuse to be among the doers of good, do not refuse to be among the righteous.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq,
m: that Shuraih said to the one who had consummated the marriage with her: If you are among the righteous, then enjoy it.

x: It seems that those who said this statement went in their abandonment of the obligation of enjoyment as an obligation for divorced women, to the saying of God Almighty: A right upon the doers of good, and His saying:
h
A right upon the righteous (al-Baqarah 2

:241), indicating that if it were obligatory with the obligation of the rights of money in every case, the righteous and the doers of good would not have been specified as a right upon them and not others, rather it would have been general for everyone among the people. As for those who obligated it upon everyone except the divorced woman for whom the dowry was imposed, they argued that when God Almighty said: And for divorced women is a right to enjoyment according to what is acceptable, an obligation upon them. “The righteous” (al-Baqarah 2:241), this was evidence that every divorced woman has a provision except for those whom God Almighty mentioned in His Book or on the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
So when He said:
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry

, then half of what you specified, this was evidence for them that her right is half of what was specified for her, because God made the provision in the verse before it, according to them, for someone other than what was specified for her. So it was known to them that God had specifically specified the provision for someone other than what was specified for her, that her ruling is different from the ruling for someone who was not specified for her if he divorced her before touching her, in what she has rights over the husband.

What is more correct than the statement in this regard in my opinion is the statement of those who said: Every divorced woman has a provision. Because God Almighty said: And for divorced women there is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous (al-Baqarah 2:241), so God Almighty made that for every divorced woman, and He did not specify some of them over others. No one can refer the apparent meaning of a general revelation to a specific hidden meaning, except with an argument that must be accepted.
God Almighty has singled out the woman who has been divorced before touching them, if it was prescribed for her, by His saying:
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry
, then half of what you specified, since He did not give her more than half of the dowry?

If God Almighty indicates the obligation of something in some of His revelations, then His indication of its obligation in the place where He indicated it is sufficient to repeat it, until it indicates the length of its obligation. And He indicated by His saying:
h
And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable (al-Baqarah 2

:241), the obligation of enjoyment for every divorced woman, so there is no need for the servants to repeat that in every verse and surah. And His indication that the woman who has been divorced before touching for whom the dowry was prescribed is entitled to half of what was prescribed for her does not indicate the length of the enjoyment for her. Because it is not impossible in speech if it was said:
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry

, then half of what you specified and the enjoyment. Since that was not impossible in speech, it was known that if half of the dowry was due to her, then its being required of her would not negate her right to enjoyment, and since their combination for the divorced woman was not impossible, and God, the Most High, mentioned, had indicated that it was obligatory for her, even if the indication of the obligation of one of them was in a verse other than the verse in which there was the indication of the obligation of the other, then their obligation to her was established and correct.
This, if there was no indication that the divorced woman for whom the dowry was specified if she was divorced before touching them, other than the statement of God, the Most High, mentioned:
h
And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable (al-Baqarah 2
:241), then how is it that in the statement of God, the Most High, mentioned: “
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them

or specified for them a dowry. But give them a provision,” the clear indication that if the one for whom the dowry was specified is divorced before touching, she is entitled to enjoyment like that for the one for whom the dowry was not specified? This is because when God the Most High said:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them

or appointed for them an obligation, it was known that He indicated by this the ruling on divorcing two types of women: one for whom an obligation was imposed, and the other for whom no obligation was imposed.

This is because when He said: or appoint for them an obligation, it was known that the other type was the one for whom an obligation was imposed, and that it was the divorced woman for whom an obligation was imposed before touching. Because He said:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them

, then God the Most High said: and give them a gift, so He made the gift obligatory for both types of them, the one for whom an obligation was imposed and the one for whom no obligation was imposed. So whoever claims that this is for one of the two types, he is asked for proof for his claim from the origin or similar, then the statement in that regard is reversed. He will not say anything about any of it except that he will be obligated to do the same in the other.

I see that the enjoyment of the woman is a right that is obligatory, if she is divorced, on her husband who divorced her, as we explained earlier - the husband is taken from it as he is taken from her dowry, and he is not released from it except by paying it to her or to someone who takes her place in collecting it from her, or by a release that is from her to him. I see that her way is the way of her dowry and all her debts before him, he is detained by it if he divorces her during it, if he does not have anything apparent that can be sold to him, if he refuses to give it to her then it is yours. We only said that because God Almighty said: And give them a benefit, so He commanded men to give them a benefit, and His command is obligatory, unless God Almighty clarifies that He meant by it encouragement and guidance, as we have explained in our book called Latif al-Bayan ‘an Usul al-Ahkam, for my saying:
h
And for divorced women there is a provision according to what is acceptable (al-Baqarah 2

There is no disagreement among all the interpreters that the meaning of this is: Divorced women have a right to their husbands in a reasonable manner. If that is the case, then the husband will not be released from what he owes her except by what we described before, of payment or release as we have explained. If a foolish person thinks that when God Almighty said: A right upon the doers of good and
h
A right upon the righteous (al-Baqarah 2

:241), that it is not obligatory, because if it were obligatory, it would be upon the doer of good and the unbelievers, the pious and the unpious, then God Almighty has commanded all of His creation to be among the doers of good and the righteous, and whatever is obligatory as a right upon the people of goodness and piety, it is more obligatory upon others and more binding upon them. And further, in the consensus of the argument that the enjoyment for the divorced woman who was not obligated before intercourse is obligatory by His saying:
h
And give them a provision

, the obligation of half of the dowry for the divorced woman who was obligated before intercourse by His saying: Then half of what you imposed, in what He obligated for them of that, the clear evidence that Surat Al-Baqarah 2:236
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them
or specified for them an obligation.
h
And provide for them

, the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability - a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the doers of good. this is a right obligatory upon every divorced woman by His saying:
h
And for divorced women there is a provision according to what is acceptable (al-Baqarah 2
:241). 241] And if he said: It is
h
a right upon the righteous (al-Baqarah 2

:241). And whoever denies what we said about that, is asked about the enjoyment for the divorced woman who was not obligated before touching. If he denies the obligation of that, he is out of the statement of the entire argument, and we will consider our debate with the deniers about twenty dinars as zakat, and those who pay zakat on goods if they are for trade, and the like. If he obligates that for her, he is asked the difference between the obligation of that for her, and the obligation for every divorced woman, and he stipulated in what he made for her of that that it is a right upon the righteous, just as he stipulated in what he made for the other that it is a right upon the righteous.
So he will not say a statement about one of them except that he will make the same statement about the other.
And everyone agreed that the divorced woman who was not obligated before touching has nothing from her divorced husband except the enjoyment.
Some of those who said that from the Companions and Followers, may God be pleased with them, mentioned:

c: Abu Kuraib and Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, they said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: If a man divorces his wife before he has set a dowry for her and before he has consummated the marriage with her, then she is only entitled to the dowry.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, he said, Al-Hasan said:
m: If a man divorces his wife without consummating the marriage with her or specifying a dowry for her, then she is entitled to nothing but the dowry.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, he said:
m: If a man marries a woman and then divorces her without specifying a dowry for her, then she is entitled to nothing but the dowry according to what is reasonable.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said:
m: If a man marries a woman and does not specify a dowry for her, then divorces her before he has touched her and before specifying a dowry for her, then she is entitled to nothing but the dowry according to what is reasonable.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them
or specified for them a dowry, he said: She is entitled to nothing but the dowry according to what is reasonable.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid narrated something similar - except that he said:
m: And there is no provision except in a reasonable manner.

c: Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them
to
h
and provide for them
, he said: This man was given a gift and he divorces her before he consummates the marriage with her, so he is only liable for the provision.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said
m: regarding this verse: It is the man who marries a woman and does not specify a dowry for her, then he divorces her before he consummates the marriage with her, so she is entitled to provision in a reasonable manner, but she is not entitled to a dowry.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: I was told on the authority of Al-Husayn Ibn Al-Faraj,
m: he said, I heard Abu Muʿadh say, Ubayd Ibn Sulayman told us, he heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, Unless you have touched them or appointed for them an obligation, this is a man who was given his wife as a gift, then he divorced her before he touched her, so she is entitled to a pleasure marriage but she has no obligation, and she does not have to wait.

x: As for the one who is well-off, he is the one whose livelihood has become spacious and rich, it is said from him: So-and-so has been well-off, so he is well-off and he is well-off. As for the one who is poor, he is the one who has little money, it is said: he has become stingy, so he is stingy, stingy, and he is poor. The readings differed in the reading of Al-Qadr.

Some of them read it: Upon the well-off is his amount and upon the poor is his amount. By moving the dal to the fatha from Al-Qadr, directing that to the noun from Al-Taqdir, which is from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so has estimated this matter.

i: Others read it with a sukoon on the dal, referring it to the source of that, as the poet said:
x: My feet are not cast in iron, clashing with fate, except for a need I want In my opinion, they are both readings that the Ummah has brought, and reading one of them does not change the meaning of the other, rather they are in agreement in meaning.

So whichever of the two readings the reader reads, he is correct. It is only permissible to choose some readings over others because of the separation of the chosen one over the other by adding a meaning that makes it valid and not the other. But if the meanings are in agreement in all of them, then there is no reason to rule that some of them are more deserving of being recited than others.
The interpretation of the verse then is:
h
There is no blame upon you
, O people, if you divorce women and have specified for them what you have not touched, because you divorced them before you had touched them before specifying for them,
h
and provide for them
all, for the wealthy and rich among you from their provision at that time according to his wealth and provision, and for the poor and needy among you from it according to his poverty and need.
God Almighty means by that:
h
and provide for them

a provision. It may be permissible for provisions to be in the accusative case, as a direct object of qadar, because provision is indefinite and qadar is definite. What he means by his saying, in a reasonable manner, is what God has commanded you to give them, without injustice or pushing them away from it. What he means by his saying, in a right upon the doers of good, is provision in a reasonable manner, a right upon the doers of good. So when the introduction of the definite article indicates the right, which is an attribute of the right, and the right is definite and the right is indefinite, it is in the accusative case as a direct object of it, as one says: the man came to me riding. It is possible that it is in the accusative case as a source of the sentence that precedes it, like the saying of the speaker: Abdullah is truly knowledgeable, so the truth is in the accusative case from the intention of the speech of the informant, as if he said I have informed you of that truly.

The first interpretation is the face of the speech, because the meaning of the speech is: So provide for them with a provision in a good manner, which is due from everyone among you who is a doer of good.

Some of them have claimed that it is in the accusative case meaning: I am truly deserving of that. What he said about that is contrary to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the recitation. Because God Almighty made the provision for the divorced women a right for them from their husbands, so the speaker of this statement claimed that the meaning of that is that God Almighty informed about Himself that it is due from the doers of good. The interpretation of the statement, if this is the case, is:
h
And provide for them

according to the ability of the wealthy and according to the ability of the poor, a provision according to what is acceptable and obligatory for the doers of good. By his saying: the doers of good, he means those who do good to themselves by hastening to obey God in what He has obligated them to do, and by performing what He has charged them with of His obligations.
If someone were to say: You have mentioned that sin is hardship, and God Almighty has said:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them

, is there any blame upon us if we divorce them after touching them, so that it is removed from us by our divorcing them before touching them? It was said: It has been narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: God does not love those who indulge in taste or those who indulge in taste.
Ibn Bashar narrated this to us, saying:

c: Ibn Abi ʿAdi and ʿAbd al-ʿAla narrated to us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “What is the matter with people who play with the limits set by God, saying: I have divorced you, I have taken you back, I have divorced you?”

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Mu’ammil narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace. So it is possible that the blame that was removed from people for divorcing their wives before touching them is that which was imposed on them after they had tasted them, as was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Some of them used to say: The meaning of his statement in this place: There is no blame is that there is no way for women - if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you have not specified for them a dowry - to follow you with a dowry or maintenance. This is a school of thought, were it not for what I have described, that what is meant by divorce before touching in this verse is two types of women: one for whom the dowry is due, and the other for whom the dowry is not due. If this is the case, then there is no reason to say: They have no right over you in terms of dowry, if the matter is as we have described. This may also have another meaning: that it means:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them
, at any time you wish to divorce them. Because there is no Sunnah in divorcing them, so a man may divorce them if he has not touched them while they are menstruating and pure at any time he likes.

This is not the case with a woman who has been consummated with and has been touched, because her husband has no right to divorce her if she is among the menstruating women - except for the waiting period when she is pure in a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse. So the blame that is dropped from the divorced woman who has not been touched during her menses is the blame that was taken by the divorced man after consummating the marriage with her during her menses, or during a period of purity in which he has had intercourse with her.

evidence.text: The majority of the people of Hijaz and Basra read it as: Ma lam tamasuhunna with the opening of the ta’ of tamsuhunna, without an alif, from your saying: masastahu amsa masan and masisaan and masisa is shortened and doubled and not in the flow.
It is as if they chose this reading, in order to link it to the reading agreed upon in His statement: And no man has touched me (Al Imran 3:47/Maryam 19:20).

Others read it as: Ma lam tamasuhuna, with a damma on the ta’ and the alif after the mim, as they linked it to the agreed-upon reading in His statement: Then the freeing of a slave before they touch each other (al-Mujadilah: 3).

Abu Jaʿfar said: What we see in that is that they are two readings with correct meanings, and they agree in interpretation, even if there is an additional meaning in one of them, which does not require a difference in the ruling and concept.
So there is no reason to rule for one of the two readings, with the agreement of their meanings, and the frequency of readings with each of them, that it is more correct than the other.
Rather, the reader must be correct in his reading, whichever of them he reads.

It was said to the questioner, who was Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, do you not read this verse: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and have already specified for them a provision, then half of what you specified?

Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam: That a man divorced his wife, so she took his case to Shuraih, and he recited this verse: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous (al-Baqarah 2:241).
The readings differed in the reading of Al-Qadr.
Some of them read it: Upon the well-off is his amount and upon the poor is his amount.

Others read it with a sukoon on the dal, referring it to the source of that, as the poet said: My feet are not cast in iron, clashing with fate, except for a need I want In my opinion, they are both readings that the Ummah has brought, and reading one of them does not change the meaning of the other, rather they are in agreement in meaning.
So whichever of the two readings the reader reads, he is correct.
What he said about that is contrary to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the recitation.

x: This ruling is from God, the Most High, as an explanation of His statement:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or specified for them an obligation

. The interpretation of that is: There is no blame upon you, O people, if you divorce women before you have touched them and have specified for them an obligation, then for them is half of what you specified for them before divorcing them, meaning: For them is half of what you gave them as a dowry. We only said that the interpretation of that is thus, because we have already explained it, that His statement: or specified for them an obligation, is an explanation from God, the Most High, to His servants of a ruling other than that which was specified for them if he divorced them before touching them. So it was known from that that the ruling for those to whom the word or was conjoined is not the ruling for those to whom it was conjoined.
The Almighty repeated His statement:
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them an obligation
, and mentioned them first in His statement:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them

, in order to remove doubt and confusion from His listeners, lest they think that the one whose ruling is the ruling that He described in this verse is not the one He began by mentioning and mentioning her ruling in the verse before it. As for his statement:
h
unless they forgive

, he means: unless those for whom half of that obligation is due from you forgive it, so they leave it to you and pardon you for it as a favor from them to you, if they are among those whose judgment is permissible in his wealth and they are adults of sound mind. Then their forgiveness is permissible in that case as they forgive you of that, so what they forgive you of it is dropped from you.

And that is the half that was due to them from the obligation after the divorce and before the forgiveness if she forgives it - or what she forgives. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry

, then give half of what you specified. So this man marries a woman and has specified a dowry for her, then he divorces her before he has touched her, so she is entitled to half of her dowry, she is not entitled to more than that.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
