And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry
, then give half of what you specified. He said: If a man divorces his wife and has specified for her a dowry, then give half of what he specified,
h
unless they forgive
it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry

, then give them half of what you specified. So this verse abrogated what came before it. If a delegation had not consummated the marriage with her, he had named a dowry for her, and given her half, and she had no provision.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry

, then give them half of what you specified. He said: It is the man who marries a woman and has specified a dowry for her, then divorces her before consummating the marriage, so she is entitled to half of what he specified for her, and she is entitled to the provision, and she has no waiting period.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Abdullah bin Salih told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry

, then give them half of what you specified. He said: If a man divorces a woman and has specified for her and she has not He touches her, so she is entitled to half of her dowry and there is no waiting period for her. It was mentioned that those who said about his statement:
h
unless they forgive
said the statement we mentioned of the interpretation.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Yahya bin Bishr told us:
m: He heard Ikrimah say: If he divorces her before he touches her and he has stipulated for her, then half of the stipulated dowry is hers on him, unless... and from him she leaves him. I narrated from Al-Husayn, he said, I heard Abu Muadh, he said, Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
unless they forgive
, he said: The woman leaves what is due to her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
unless they forgive

refers to the woman who has been married or is a virgin, and someone other than her father marries her. So God made forgiveness up to them: if they wish, they forgive, so they leave her, and if they wish, they take half of the dowry.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
unless they forgive
the woman leaves half of her dowry, which is all of what is due to her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me
m: He said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
unless they forgive
he said: The woman leaves half for her husband.

c: Hamid bin Mas'adah narrated to us, he said, Yazid bin Zari' narrated to us, he said, Abdullah bin Awn narrated to me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Shuraih:
m: h
Unless they forgive
, he said: If the woman wishes, she may forgive and leave the dowry.

c: Hamid bin Mas'adah narrated to us, he said, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said, Abdullah bin Awn narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Shuraih,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab narrated to us, he said, Ubaydullah narrated to us, on the authority of Nafi',
m: his saying:
h
Unless they forgive refers to the woman whose husband divorces her before consummating the marriage
, so she forgives half of it to her husband.

c: Musa narrated to me, he said, Amr narrated to us, he said, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
Unless they forgive
, either they forgive, so the previously married woman may give up part of her dowry, or she may give up all of it.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Abdullah bin Salih narrated to us, he said, al-Layth narrated to me, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab:
m: h
Unless they forgive

, he said: Forgiveness is up to them, if the woman is previously married, then she is more deserving. Thus, her guardian has no power over her, because she has taken control of her affairs. If she wants to forgive him, then she should give him half of what he has a right to, that is permissible. If she wants to take it, then she has more power over that.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Muammar told us, he said, Ibn Shihab told me:
m: h
Unless they forgive
, he said: women.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: h
Unless they forgive
, he said: the previously married woman gives up her dowry.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Abu Usamah Hammad bin Zaid bin Usamah told us, he said, Ismail told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Shuraih:
m: h
Unless they forgive
, he said: the woman forgives all of what is due to her.

x: I did not hear anyone say: Hammad bin Zaid bin Usama, except Abu Hisham.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said: Abda told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saʿid bin Al-Musayyab, he said:
m: If she wishes, she may abstain from her dowry, meaning in his statement: unless they abstain.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said: Ubayd God told us, on the authority of Israʿil, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Shuraih, he said:
m: The woman forgives and gives up half of the dowry.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Al-Zuhri said:
m: h
Unless they forgive
, the previously married women.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said:
m: h
Unless they forgive
, he said: The woman leaves half of herself.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
Unless they forgive
, he means women.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
Unless they forgive
, if she was a married woman, she would forgive.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: his saying:
h
Unless they forgive
, meaning the woman.

c: Ali bin Sahl told me, he said, Zaid told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Mihran told us,
m: all on the authority of Sufyan:
h
Unless they forgive
, he said: The woman if he has not consummated the marriage: that she leaves him the dowry, and does not take anything from him.

x: The people of interpretation differed about who God, the Most High, meant by His statement: in whose hand is the marriage tie.

Some of them said: It is the guardian of the virgin. They said: The meaning of the verse is: Or he leaves, the one who is responsible for the woman’s marriage contract from her guardians, for the husband the half that is due to the divorced woman before he touches her, so he forgives him for it, if the slave girl is one who is not allowed to have any control over her money.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: God permitted forgiveness and commanded it, so if she forgives, then as she forgives, and if she is stingy and her guardian forgives, it is permissible even if she refuses.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abu Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Or he in whose hand is the marriage knot forgives and he is the father of the virgin slave girl, God Almighty made Surat Al-Baqarah 2:237
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry
, then half of what you specified, unless they both forgive
h
or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives
. And to forgive is closer to righteousness.
h
And do not forget graciousness between you
. Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do. forgiveness up to him, she has no control over him if she is divorced, as long as she is in his custody.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah:
m: He in whose hand is the marriage knot is the guardian.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said, Alqamah said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah that he said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Mu’ammar told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Nakha’i, on the authority of Alqamah, he said:
m: He is The guardian.

c: Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said, Ubaydullah narrated to us, on the authority of Bayan al-Nahwi, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah and the companions of Abdullah
m: said: He is the guardian.
b.via: Alqamah and the companions of Abdullah

c: Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said, Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah that he said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Muammar narrated to us, on the authority of Hajjaj: Al-Aswad bin Zaid said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said, Abu Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, he said,
m: Tawus and Mujahid said: He is the guardian, then they went back and said: He is the husband.

c: Ya’qub narrated to me, he said, Hisham narrated to us, he said, Abu Bishr informed us, he said,
m: Mujahid and Tawus said: He is the guardian, then they went back and said: He is the husband.

c: Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said, Ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, he said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: A man married his sister, Her husband divorced her before consummating the marriage, so her brother forgave the dowry. Shuraih approved it and then said: I forgive the women of Banu Murrah. Amir said: No, by God, no more foolish judgment has ever been made than this: to allow the forgiveness of a brother in His statement:
h
Unless they both forgive it or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives it

. Shuraih then said about it: It is the husband. If he forgives the entire dowry, then he gives it all to her, or she forgives the half that was specified for her. If they both quarrel, then she is to take half of her dowry. He said: And forgiving is closer to piety.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Jarir ibn Hazim told us, on the authority of Isa ibn Asim al-Asadi:
m: Ali asked Shuraih about the one in whose hand is the marriage contract, and he said: It is the guardian.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Hisham told us, Mughirah told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Shuraih
m: that he used to say: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the guardian - then he stopped that and said: It is the husband.

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Sayyar told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: That a man married a woman and found her ugly, so he divorced her before consummating the marriage. Her guardian forgave her half of the dowry. He said: So she took his case to Shuraih, and Shuraih said to her: Your guardian has forgiven her. He said: Then he went back after that and made the one in whose hand was the marriage contract the husband.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan -
m: regarding the one in whose hand was the marriage contract - he said: The guardian.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur or someone else, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said:
m: Al-Hasan was asked about the one who holds the marriage contract, he said: He is the guardian.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: He is the one who married her.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The one who holds the marriage contract, he is the guardian.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Wakee’ and Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Abu Awana, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi, they said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayya told us, he said, Ibn Juwayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ubaydullah told us, on the authority of Isra’ik, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: Or he in whose hand is the marriage knot forgives he said: The guardian of the virgin.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Al-Zuhri told me:
m: h
Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives
, the guardian of the virgin.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives
, he is the guardian.

c: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, he said, Ibn Tawus told us, on the authority of his father - and on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ikrimah - Muammar
m: said: Al-Hasan also said it - they said: He in whose hand is the marriage contract is the guardian.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, he said:
m: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the father.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, he said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: He is the guardian.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the guardian of the virgin.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said - regarding the one in whose hand is the marriage contract -: the father. Ibn Zayd mentioned it on the authority of his father.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Zayd and Rabi’ah:
m: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the father with regard to his virgin daughter, and the master with regard to his female slave.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Malik said:
m: And that is if she divorces before consummating the marriage with her, then he has the right to… 1 Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the virgin whose guardian forgives him, so that is permissible, and her forgiveness is not permissible.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Yahya bin Bishr told us,
m: he heard Ikrimah say:
h
Unless they forgive

, that the woman forgives half of the dowry due to him and leaves him. If she is stingy unless she takes it, then she and her guardian who married her to the man, whether an uncle, a brother, or a father, may forgive half, for if he wishes he may do so, even if the woman does not like it.

c: Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Razi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: God permitted forgiveness and commanded it, so if a woman is chaste, her forgiveness is permissible, and if she is stingy and miserly, her guardian forgives and it is permissible. Pardon him.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract, is the guardian.

x: Others said: Rather, the one in whose hand is the marriage contract, is the husband. They said: The meaning of that is: Or the one in whose hand is the woman’s marriage contract pardons her and gives her the full dowry.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Abu Uthma narrated to us, he said, Habib narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Khalas ibn Amr, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: The one in whose hand is the marriage contract, is the husband.

c: Yaqub narrated to me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, he said, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, on the authority of Isa ibn Asim Al-Asadi:
m: Ali asked Shuraih about the one in whose hand is the marriage contract, he said: He is the guardian. Ali said: No, but he is the husband.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Ibrahim narrated to us, he said, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, on the authority of Isa ibn Asim, he said:
m: I heard Shuraih say: He said: Ali said to me: Who is the one in whose hand is the marriage contract? I said: My guardian. The woman. He said: No, it is the husband.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rifai narrated to us, he said: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ammar bin Abi Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He is the husband.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim narrated to me, he said: Abu Naim narrated to us, he said:
m: I said to Hammad bin Salamah: Who has the marriage contract in his hand? He mentioned on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Ammar bin Abi Ammar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The husband.

c: Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said: Ubaidullah narrated to us, he said: Israel informed us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He is the husband.

c: Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Shuraih, they said:
m: He is the husband.

c: Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ja’far, on the authority of Wasil bin Abi Sa’id, on the authority of Muhammad bin Jubayr bin Mut’im:
m: That his father married a woman and then divorced her before consummating the marriage with her, so he sent the dowry and said: I am more deserving of forgiveness.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Salih bin Kaysan:
m: that Jubayr bin Mut’im married a woman and divorced her before consummating the marriage with her, and he completed her dowry, and he interpreted:
h
Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives

c: Abu Hisham told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Jubayr:
m: that he divorced his wife before consummating the marriage with her, and he completed her dowry and said: I am more deserving of forgiveness.

c: Humayd bin Mas’adah told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, he said, Abdullah bin Awn told me, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Shuraih:
m: h
Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives
, he said: If the husband wishes, he may give her the full dowry.

c: Humayd told us, he said, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Abdullah bin Awn told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Shuraih, he said:
m: The one

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this is the opinion of the one who said: The meaning of his statement:
h
In whose hand is the marriage contract is the husband

. This is because everyone agrees that the guardian of a virgin or previously married female slave, whether a young girl or an adult, if he releases her husband from her dowry before divorcing her, or gives it to him as a gift or pardons him for it - that his release and pardon of it is invalid, and that her dowry is established before he releases him from it. So the way he releases him from it after divorcing her is the way he releases him from it before divorcing her. And another: that everyone agrees that the guardian of a woman who is under guardianship or not under guardianship, if he gives her divorced husband after her separation from him a dirham from her money, other than as a pardon from him for what was due to her from her dowry before that, then his gift of that is returned and invalid.

They are also unanimously agreed that her dowry is money from her money, so its ruling is the ruling of all her money. Another: Everyone is unanimously agreed that the paternal uncles of a virgin woman and the sons of her brothers from her father and mother are among her guardians, and that if some of them pardoned her money to her husband, before he had intercourse with her, or after he had intercourse with her - his pardon of what he pardoned him from it is invalid, and the woman’s right is established upon him in his condition. Likewise, the way of pardoning every guardian of hers, whoever he may be among the guardians, whether he is a father, grandfather, or maternal uncle. Because God Almighty did not specify some of those in whose hands the marriage contract is over others in the permissibility of his pardon, if they are among those whose judgment is permissible in his person and his money.

And it is said to whoever rejects what we have said, from those who claim that the one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the woman’s guardian: Is the statement in that devoid of one of two matters, since the one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the guardian according to you: Either that is every guardian who is permitted to marry his female ward, or that is some of them and not some? So he will not find a way to exit from one of these two categories.
That is so, he is asked: Which of these did he mean? If He said: Every guardian is permitted to marry his female ward.
Is it permissible for the emancipator of a female slave to marry his female slave with her permission after emancipating them?
Yes!
Is it permissible for him to pardon her if he pardons her dowry to her husband after divorcing her before consummation?
Yes! It is excluded from the statement of all. If he says: No!

Why? And what is it that prohibited him from doing that while he is her guardian who holds the contract of marriage? Then the statement is reversed on him in that, and the difference between it and the pardon of all other guardians is left.
For some and not for others. The proof is asked for that particularity, and God Almighty mentioned it in general and did not specify some and not for others.

Who is meant by it, if what is meant by that is some guardians and not for others? If he alludes to some of them, the proof is asked for that, and the statement is reversed in that, and his statement is opposed to that with the opposite of his claim. Then he will not say a statement in that except that he is obligated in the other like it.

If someone thinks that the woman If her husband leaves her, then he is no longer in possession of her marriage contract, and God Almighty mentioned that he only permitted the forgiveness of the one who has the marriage contract of the divorced woman in his possession, so it was known from that that the husband is not concerned with it, and that the one concerned with it is the one who has the marriage contract of the divorced woman in his possession after her separation from her husband. And in the length of that, that it is then in the husband’s possession, the correctness of the statement that it is in the possession of the guardian to whom the marriage contract is made to her. And if that is the case, then it is correct to say that the one who has the marriage contract in his possession is the guardian, for he neglected 1 and thought wrongly. That is because the meaning of that is: or the one who has the marriage contract in his possession forgives, and the definite article was only introduced in marriage.

Instead of adding to the letter ha’ to which marriage - if they were not in it - would have been added, as God Almighty said: For Paradise is the abode (al-Nazi’at 79:41), meaning: for Paradise is his abode, and as Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan said: They have a trait that God has not given to any other people, for dreams are not celibate. Meaning: Their dreams are not celibate. And the evidence for that is more than can be counted. So the interpretation of the statement is:
h
unless they forgive

or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives, and he is the husband who has the marriage contract of himself in his hand in every case before and after the divorce, not that it means: or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives, so the interpretation of the statement is what those who said it thought was the guardian and the woman’s guardian. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:237
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry
, then half of what you specified, unless they both forgive
h
or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives
And to forgive is closer to righteousness.
h
And do not forget graciousness between you

. Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do. Because the woman’s guardian does not have the right to the marriage contract of the woman without her permission, except in the case of her childhood, and that is a case in which no one has the right to the contract except some of her guardians, according to the opinion of most who saw that the one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the guardian. And God Almighty did not specify some of them in His saying:
h
Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives

some of them, so it is permissible to direct the interpretation to what they interpreted, if there was a reason for what they said about that. And after that, God Almighty mentioned it only alluded to in His saying:
h
And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry
, then half of what you specified unless they pardon, about mentioning the women who were mentioned in the verse before it, and that is His saying:
h
There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them

, and young girls are not called women, but rather they are called young girls or slave girls, and women in the speech of the Arabs as a whole is the name of the woman, and the Arabs do not say a girl, a girl, or a young girl woman, just as they do not say a young boy man.
And since that is the case, and His saying:
h
Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives
, according to those who claim that he is the guardian, is only:
h
Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives

what is required of his guardian who deserves that he be in charge of her money, either Either youth or foolishness. God Almighty mentioned in the two verses the stories of divorced women for the generality of the mention and not for its specificity, and He made forgiveness for them by saying:
h
unless they forgive
, it was known by His saying:
h
unless they forgive

, that the ones meant by the two verses in which He mentioned them are all of them and not some, since it was known that the forgiveness of one whose money is in charge of them is invalid. Since that is the case, it was made clear that the interpretation of His saying:
h
or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives

, requires that the guardians be the mature, adult women, who forgive what is due to them from the dowry by divorce before touching, like the guardians of young children who are in charge of their money due to foolishness.

And in the denial of those who say: the one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the guardian, the forgiveness of the guardians of the mature, adult women as we have described, and their differentiation between their rulings and the rulings of the guardians of others - what revealed the corruption of their interpretation that they interpreted in that. Those who say what they say about this will ask about the difference between that in origin or similar, so they will not say anything about any of this except that they will be obligated to say something different about it.
The people of interpretation differed about who was addressed by the statement: And that you pardon is closer to righteousness.
Some of them said: This was addressed to men and women.
Those who said this mentioned:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Jurayj narrating, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas: And that you pardon is closer to righteousness. He said: The one closest to righteousness is the one who pardons.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saʿid ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, he said:
m: I heard the interpretation of this verse: And that you pardon is closer to righteousness. He said: They both pardon. So the interpretation of the verse according to this statement is: And that, O people, some of you pardon what is due to him from his partner from the dowry before separation in the event of divorce, is closer to him to fearing God.

x: Others said: Rather, those who were addressed with this were the husbands of divorced women.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: And that you pardon is closer to righteousness, and that pardon is closer to righteousness. So the interpretation of this according to this statement is: And that you pardon, O you who are separating from your wives, and leave for them what is due to you to return to them from the dowry that you gave to them, or complete for them - by giving them the dowry that you had specified for them in the marriage contract if you had not given it to them - is closer to the fear of God.

x: And what I think is more correct of the two opinions regarding the interpretation of the verse is what Ibn Abbas said, which is that the meaning of this is: And that some of you pardon others, O husbands and wives, after separating from one another, what was due to one of you before the other, and leave it to him if he had any left before him. If he has nothing left, then he should pay it in full, which is closer to the fear of God.

What is there in forgiving that of drawing closer to the fear of God? It would be said to the forgiver and pardoner of what is due to him from his companion: What you did is closer to the fear of God?

a.l: It would be said to him:
x: What is in that of his drawing closer to the fear of God is his hastening in his forgiveness of that which God has called him to, and called him to and urged him to do. So his doing that - if he did it seeking the pleasure of God and preferring what He has called him to over his own desires - is known by that, since he preferred doing what He has called him to do, which He has not imposed on him, over his own desires: that when He imposed it on him and made it obligatory, he preferred it more, and when He forbade him, he avoided it more. This is his closeness to piety.

God Almighty says: And do not neglect, O people, to take advantage of one another, so that you abandon it. But let the divorced man be generous to his wife before having intercourse with her, so that he may complete her dower if he did not give her all of it. And if he has given her all that was imposed on her, then let him be generous to her by forgiving what is due to him, and he is permitted to take it back to her, which is half of it. If the man is stingy with that and refuses to take back half of it from her, then let the divorced woman be generous to him by returning all of it to him, if she had taken it from him. And if she had not taken it, then let her forgive all of it. If they did not do that and were stingy and abandoned what God had commanded them to do - that one of them takes from the other what is extra - then she gets half of what was stipulated for her in the marriage contract and he gets half of it.
And the people of interpretation said what we said about that.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told us, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr bin Mut’im, on the authority of his father Jubayr:
m: That he entered upon Sa’d bin Abi Qas and offered him his daughter, so he married her. When he left, he divorced her and sent her the dowry. He said: It was said to him: Why did you marry her? He said: He offered her to me, but I was reluctant to reject her! It was said: Why did you send the dowry? He said: Then where is the extra?

, he said: A woman is divorced by her husband who has stipulated a dowry for her but has not consummated the marriage with her, so she is entitled to half of the dowry. m: about His statement:

x: By that, the Most High means: Indeed, God, of what you do, O people, of what He has urged you to do and urged you to do, of forgiving one another for what was due to him before him as a right due to the marriage that was between you and your wives, and some of you being better than others in that, and in other matters that you do and leave behind in your affairs in yourselves and others, of what God has urged you to do and commanded you to do or forbidden you from, is Seeing, meaning by that: He has insight, nothing of that is hidden from Him, rather He counts it for you and preserves it, until He rewards the one among you who has done good for his good, and the one among you who has done evil for his evil.

God Almighty means by that: Be consistent in performing the prescribed prayers at their appointed times, and be committed to them and adhere to them, and to the middle prayer among them. And what we have said about that is what the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq bin Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, regarding His statement:
h
Guard the prayers
, he said: Guarding them means maintaining their time and not being forgetful about them.

c: Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Mas’udi told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq,
m: regarding this verse:
h
Guard the prayers
, so guarding them means praying at their time, and being forgetful about them means leaving their time. Then they differed regarding the middle prayer.

x: Some of them said: It is the Asr prayer.
Those who said that mentioned:

and the middle prayer

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Musʿab ibn Salam told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: The middle prayer is the Asr prayer.

c: Yaʿqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Hayyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali,
m: similarly.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Musʿab told us, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, he said:
m: I heard Ali say: The middle prayer is the Asr prayer.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, he said:
m: I asked Ali about the middle prayer, and he said: The afternoon prayer.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam Al-Masry told me, he said,
m: Abu Zur’ah Wahb God bin Rashid said, Haywah bin Shuraih told us, Abu Sakhr told us: He heard Abu Muawiyah al-Bajali from the people of Kufa say: I heard Abu al-Sahbaa al-Bakri say: I asked Ali bin Abi Talib about the middle prayer, and he said: It is the afternoon prayer, and it is the one with which Solomon bin David, peace be upon him, was tempted.
b.via: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam Al-Masry

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Sulayman al-Taymi told us, and Hamid bin Masʿadah told us, he said, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, he said, al-Taymi told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said:
m: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim, on the authority of Ibn Labiba, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah:
m: h
Guard the prayers
h
and the middle prayer
, which is the afternoon prayer, which is the afternoon prayer.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul Hakam told me, he said, my father and Shuaib ibn Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Yazid ibn Al-Haad, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever misses the ‘Asr prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth. Ibn ‘Umar saw the virtue of the ‘Asr prayer because of what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about it: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:238 Maintain the prayers, especially the middle prayer,
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient. It is the middle prayer.

c: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Al-A’la told me, he said, Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, he said,
m: Abu Salih claimed, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that he said: It is the ‘Asr prayer.

c: Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Al-Rahman ibn Wahb told me, he said, my uncle ‘Abdullah ibn Wahb told me, he said, ‘Amr ibn Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Shihab said: Ibn ‘Umar saw it as the middle prayer.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, ‘Affan ibn Muslim told us, he said, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, he said:
m: The middle prayer is the ‘Asr prayer.

c: Muhammad ibn Muammar told me, he said, Ibn Amir told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Abi Hamid told us, on the authority of Hamida,
m: the daughter of Abi Yunus, the freed slave of Aisha, she said: Aisha left us her belongings, and I found in Aisha’s copy of the Qur’an:
h
Guard the prayers
h
and the middle prayer
, which is the afternoon prayer,
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient.

c: Saeed ibn Yahya al-Umawi told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said,
m: he told us. Abdul Malik bin Abdul Rahman: His mother Umm Hamid bint Abdul Rahman asked Aisha about the middle prayer. She said: We used to recite it in the first letter during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
- Abu Jaʿfar said: He said: - The afternoon prayer
h
and stand before God
in obedience.”

c: Abbas bin Muhammad told me, Hajjaj told us,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Abdul Malik bin Abdul Rahman told me, on the authority of his mother Umm Hamid bint Abdul Rahman: that she asked Aisha, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
and the afternoon prayer.

c: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr,
m: Abu Sahl Al-Ansari, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha regarding his statement:
h
The middle prayer - she said
: The afternoon prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, he said:
m: It was in Aisha’s copy of the Qur’an:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, which is the afternoon prayer.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakiʿ narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Qays,
m: saying: Abdullah ibn Rafiʿ, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, narrated to me: Umm Salamah ordered me to write a copy of the Qur’an for her and said: When you reach the verse about prayer, inform me. So I informed her, and she dictated to me:
h
Guard the prayers
h
and the middle prayer
is the afternoon prayer.

c: ʿAmmar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father,
m: saying: Al-Hasan used to say: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAʿla narrated to us, saying: Al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, on the authority of his father,
m: saying: Qatadah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ayyub, on the authority of ʿAishah, that she said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Ayyub, on the authority of ʿAishah,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Hakam narrated to us, saying: Anbasah narrated to us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: saying: It was said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, who said: It was mentioned to us on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib that he said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: The middle prayer is the Asr prayer.

c: Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Hafsah:
m: that she ordered a man to write a copy of the Qur’an for her, and she said: When you reach this place, inform me. When he reached:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, she said: Write the Asr prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hajjaj ibn Al-Munhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah ibn Umar narrated to us, on the authority of Nafiʿ, on the authority of Hafsah,
m: the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she said to the scribe of her Qur’an: When you reach the times of the prayers, inform me so that I may tell you what she heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he told her, she said: Write, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Maintain the prayers
h
and the middle prayer
, which is the afternoon prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, on the authority of Zurbin Habish, he said:
m: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, we used to say that it was the afternoon prayer, before which there are two prayers during the day, and after which there are two prayers during the night.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, Hisham told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, he said: They were commanded to
h
guard the prayers
. He said: He specified the afternoon prayer,
h
and the middle prayer
, meaning the afternoon prayer.

c: I was told by Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding his statement:
h
and the middle prayer
, it is the afternoon prayer.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’, who said: It was mentioned to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Guard strictly the prayers
- meaning the obligatory prayers -
h
and the middle prayer
, meaning the afternoon prayer.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi told me, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Razin ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: I heard him say:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, he said: the afternoon prayer.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told me, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Isra'il told us, on the authority of Thawir, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: the middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of al-Dahhak, he said:
m: the middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, he said, Abu Nu'aym told us, he said, Isra'il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Razin ibn Ubayd, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say: it is the afternoon prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, he said, Ismail bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Wahb bin Jarir told us, he said, my father told us, he said,
m: I heard Yahya bin Ayoub narrating, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Murrah bin Mukhmar, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Hakam, he said: I heard Abu Ayoub say: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Ibn Sufyan told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer. The reason for those who said this is what:

c: Muhammad bin Muammar told me, he said, Abu Amir told us, he said, Muhammad - meaning Ibn Talhah - told us, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: The polytheists distracted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the afternoon prayer until it turned yellow - or red - so he said: They distracted us from the middle prayer! May God fill their bellies and graves with fire!

c: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Talhah narrated to us, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner - except that he said: May God fill their homes and graves with fire, just as they distracted us from the middle prayer.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, saying:
m: I heard Qatadah narrating, on the authority of Abu Hassan, on the authority of Ubaydah al-Salmani, on the authority of Ali, saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: al-Ahzab 33:“They distracted us from the middle prayer until the sun set. May God fill their graves and their homes with fire - or their bellies with fire. Shuʿbah was uncertain about the bellies and the homes.”

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur,
m: saying: I said to Ubaydah al-Salmani: Ask Ali ibn Abi Talib about the middle prayer. So he asked him, and he said: We used to think it was the morning, or the dawn, until I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the day of the Confederates: They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer! May God fill their graves and their homes with fire!

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Stirbin Shakal, on the authority of Ali, he said:
m: They distracted us on the day of the Confederates from the afternoon prayer, until I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer! May God fill their graves and their homes with fire or: their homes with fire.” Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, he said: Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, on the Day of the Confederates, on one of the plains of the Trench, and he said: They kept us from the middle prayer until the sun set! May God fill their graves and their homes with fire. Or their bellies and their homes with fire. Abu al-Saʿib and Saʿid ibn Numayr narrated, they said: Abu Muʿawiyah narrated, on the authority of al-Aʿmash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Shteer ibn Shakl, on the authority of Ali, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They kept us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer! May God fill their graves and their homes with fire! Then he prayed it between the two evening prayers, between sunset and night prayers. Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada’i narrated that Ali ibn Asim narrated that Khalid narrated that Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated that Ubaydah al-Salmani narrated that Ali said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pray the ‘Asr prayer on the day of the Trench until after the sun had set. He said: ‘What is wrong with them? May God fill their hearts and homes with fire! They prevented us from the middle prayer until the sun had set!’” Zakariya ibn Yahya al-Darir narrated that Ubaydullah narrated that Isra’il narrated that Asim narrated that Zur said: Ubaydah al-Salmani and I went to Ali and ordered Ubaydah to ask him about the middle prayer. He said: ‘O Commander of the Faithful, what is the middle prayer?’ He said: ‘We used to think it was the dawn prayer. While we were fighting the people of Khaybar, they fought until they exhausted us from praying. It was just before sunset. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O God, fill the hearts and bellies of these people who have distracted us from the middle prayer with fire - or fill their hearts with fire.’ He said: ‘So we knew that day that it was the middle prayer.’

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Hassan al-A’raj, on the authority of Ubaidah al-Salmani, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib:
m: “The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the Confederates: O God, fill their hearts and their homes with fire as they kept us busy, or: as they prevented us, from the middle prayer until the sun set!”

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, Thabit ibn Muhammad narrated to us,
m: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:238 Maintain the prayers, especially the middle prayer,
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient.

c: Muhammad ibn Talhah narrated to us, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Murrah, on the authority of Ibn Masʿud, who said:
m: “The polytheists prevented the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from the afternoon prayer until the sun turned yellow, or red, so the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘They distracted us from the middle prayer! May God fill their homes and hearts with fire – or: May God fill their hearts and homes with fire!’”

c: Muhammad ibn ʿAmara al-Asadi narrated to me, Sahl ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, Malik ibn Mughul narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard Talhah say: I prayed with Murrah in his house and he forgot, or he said: he forgot, so he stood up and told us, and I liked to hear it from a trustworthy person. He said: When the Day of the Trench came – meaning the Day of the Confederates – the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘What is wrong with them? They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer! May God fill their bellies and graves with fire!’”

c: Ahmad ibn Mani’ narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’ narrated to us, on the authority of al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

c: Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi narrated to me, he said: Ibad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, on the authority of Hilal ibn Khabab, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out on a military expedition, and the polytheists prevented him from praying the afternoon prayer until evening came, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, fill their homes and their bellies with fire as they prevented us from praying the middle prayer!”

c: Musa bin Sahl al-Ramli narrated to us, he said, Ishaq bin Abdul Wahid al-Mawsili narrated to us, he said, Khalid bin Abdullah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the Confederates: They distracted us from the middle prayer until the sun set! May God fill their graves and their homes with fire!”

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Amr bin Awn narrated to us, he said, Khalid informed us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: “The Confederates distracted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the afternoon prayer on the day of the Trench until the sun set, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They distracted us from the middle prayer! May God fill their graves and their homes with fire - or: their bellies with fire!”

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Sulayman bin Ahmad al-Harashi al-Wasiti narrated to us, he said, al-Walid bin Muslim narrated to us, he said, Sadaqah bin Khalid informed me, he said, Khalid bin Dahqan narrated to me, on the authority of Khalid bin Sablan, on the authority of Kuhayl bin Harmalah, he said:
m: Abu Hurayrah was asked about the middle prayer, so he said: We differed about it.” As you differed about it while we were in the courtyard of the house of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among us was the righteous man Abu Hashim bin Utbah bin Rabi’ah bin Abd Shams, so he said: I know that for you. So he stood up and asked permission to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and entered upon him, then he came out to us and said: Tell us that it is the afternoon prayer.

c: Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, he said: My father told us, and Ibn Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, they both said: Fadil bin Marzuq told us, on the authority of Shaqiq bin Uqbah Al-Abdi, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, he said:
m: This verse was revealed:
h
Guard strictly the prayers

and the afternoon prayer, he said: We recited it during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as much as God willed that we should recite it. Then God abrogated it and revealed:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: A man who was with Shaqiq said: So it is the afternoon prayer! He said: I have told you how it was revealed, and how God abrogated it, and God knows best.

c: Hamid bin Mas’adah told us, he said: Yazid bin Zari’ told us, and Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad bin Bakr and Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Ansari told us, they both said: Sa’id bin Abi Arubah told us, and Abu Kurayb told us, he said:
m: Abdah bin Sulayman, Muhammad bin Bishr and Abdullah bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The middle prayer is the ‘Asr prayer.

c: Issam bin Rawad bin Al-Jarrah told me, he said: My father told us, he said: Sa’id bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us that the middle prayer is the ‘Asr prayer.”

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abi ‘Adi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Al-Duha, on the authority of Shteer bin Shakl, on the authority of Umm Habibah,
m: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said on the day of Al-Khandaq: They kept us from the middle prayer, the ‘Asr prayer, until the sun set.” Abu Musa said: This is what Ibn Abi Uday said.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:
h
Guard the prayers
h
and the middle prayer
, which is the afternoon prayer.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Abd al-Salam told us, on the authority of Salim,
m: the freed slave of Abu Nusayr, who said, Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi told me, I was sitting with Abd al-Aziz ibn Marwan, and he said: O so-and-so, go to so-and-so and say to him: What did you hear from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the middle prayer? A man sitting there said: Abu Bakr and Umar sent me when I was a young boy to ask him about the middle prayer, so he took my little finger and said: This is the dawn prayer - and he held the one next to it. And he said: This is the noon prayer - then he held the thumb and said: This is the sunset prayer - then he held the one next to it and said: This is the night prayer - then he said: Which of your fingers are left? I said: The middle prayer. He said: Which prayer is left? I said: The afternoon prayer. He said: It is the afternoon prayer.

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, who said: It was mentioned to us that the polytheists kept them busy on the Day of the Confederates from the afternoon prayer until the sun set, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They kept us busy from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer, until the sun set! May God fill their homes and graves with fire!

c: Ibn al-Barqi told us,
m: who said: Umar and Ibn Abi Salamah told us, who said: Sadaqah told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Hassan, on the authority of Ubaydah al-Salmani, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said on the Day of the Confederates: O God, fill their homes and graves with fire, just as they kept us busy from the middle prayer until the sun set.”

c: Muhammad ibn Auf al-Taʿi told me,
m: who said: Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil ibn ʿAyyash told me, who said: My father told us, who said: Damdam ibn Zurʿah told me, on the authority of Shuraih ibn ʿUbayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ashʿari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.

x: Others said: Rather, the middle prayer is the noon prayer.

Those who said that: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Hammam told us, he said, Qatada told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit, he said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer.

m: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Makhrami told us, he said, Abu Amir told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of Zaid - meaning Ibn Thabit - similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Ibrahim, he said,
m: I heard Hafs ibn Asim narrating, on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit, he said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer.

c: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Sulayman ibn Dawud told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, and Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, he said, Umar ibn Sulayman told me
m: - from the descendants of Umar ibn al-Khattab - he said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abaan ibn Uthman narrating on the authority of his father, on the authority of Zaid ibn Thabit, he said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida narrated to us, he said: Abdul Samad narrated to us, he said: Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Umar bin Sulayman,
m: this is what Abu Zaida said, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abaan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit in his hadith, he said: The middle prayer is the noon prayer.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said: Abdullah bin Yazid narrated to us, he said: Haywah bin Shuraih and Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, they said: Abu Uqayl Zuhrah bin Ma’bad narrated to us: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab narrated to him that
m: he was sitting with Urwah bin Az-Zubayr and Ibrahim bin Talhah, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: I heard Abu Saeed Al-Khudri say: The middle prayer is the noon prayer. Then Abdullah bin Umar passed by us, and Urwah said: Send to Ibn Umar and ask him. So they sent a young man to him and he asked him, then the messenger came to us and said: He says: It is the noon prayer. We were not sure about what the young man said, so we all got up and went to Ibn Umar and asked him, and he said: It is the noon prayer.

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, a man from the Ansar told me, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit,
m: that he used to say: It is the noon prayer.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told me, Abu Ahmad told us, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, Adam told us, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Umar, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, who said:
m: The middle prayer is the noon prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, that he said:
m: The middle prayer is the noon prayer.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told us, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, Nafi’ bin Yazid told us, Al-Walid bin Abi Al-Walid Abu Uthman told me, Abdullah bin Dinar told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar,
m: that he was asked about the middle prayer, he said: It is the one that follows the forenoon prayer.

c: Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, he said: Nafi’ ibn Yazid narrated to us, he said: al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid narrated to me, that Muslim ibn Abi Maryam narrated to him, that
m: a group of Quraish sent to Abdullah ibn Umar asking him about the middle prayer, so he said to him: It is the one that follows the Duha prayer. They said to him: Go back and ask him, for it only made us more tired with it!! Then Abd al-Rahman ibn Aflah, the freed slave of Abdullah ibn Umar, passed by them, so they sent him to him as well, and he said: It is the one in which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) faced the Qiblah.

c: Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, he said: Nafi’ informed us, he said: Zuhra ibn Ma’bad narrated to me, he said: Saeed ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me:
m: He was sitting with Urwah and Ibrahim ibn Talhah, and Saeed said to him: I heard Abu Saeed say: The Dhuhr prayer is the middle prayer. Then Ibn Umar passed by us, and Urwah said: Send him and ask him. The boy asked him, and he said: It is the Dhuhr prayer. We were not sure about what the boy said, so we all stood up and asked him, and he said: It is the Dhuhr prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Uthman bin Umar told us, he said, Abu Amir told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Qais, on the authority of Ibn Abi Rafi’, on the authority of his father -
m: who was a freed slave of Hafsa - he said: Hafsa asked me to write down a copy of the Qur’an and she said to me: When you come to this verse, inform me so that I may dictate it to you as you have recited it to me. So when I came to this verse:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, I went to her and she said: Write:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
h
and stand before God

, devoutly obedient. So I met Ubayy bin Ka’b, or Zayd bin Thabit, and I said: O Abu al-Mundhir, Hafsa said such and such!! He said: It is as she said. Isn’t it more Surat Al-Baqarah 2:238 Maintain the prayers, especially the middle prayer,
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient. busy when we are with our sheep and camels at the time of the noon prayer?! The reason for saying that is:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, he said: Shuʿbah narrated to us, he said: ʿAmr ibn Abi Hakim informed me, he said:
m: I heard al-Zubayr narrating, on the authority of ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer at noon, and he did not pray a prayer that was more difficult for the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, than it. He said: So this verse was revealed: ‘
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
.’ And he said: ‘There are two prayers before it and two prayers after it.’”

c: Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi Thaʿb informed us, on the authority of al-Zubayr, he said:
m: A group of people from Quraysh passed by Zayd ibn Thabit, so they sent two men to him asking him about the middle prayer. Zayd said: It is the noon prayer. Two men from them went to Usamah ibn Zayd and asked him about the middle prayer. He said: It is the noon prayer. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer in the heat of the day, and there would be nothing behind him except one or two rows. The people would be at their siesta and doing business. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was about to burn people who do not attend the prayer in their homes! He said: Then this verse was revealed:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer

x: Others used to recite it:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
h
and stand before God

, devoutly obedient. It was mentioned that he used to say this in the same way: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated, Shuʿbah narrated, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn Yazid al-Azdi, on the authority of Salim ibn ʿAbdullah: Hafsah ordered a man to write a copy of the Qur’an and said: When you reach this verse:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, then notify me. When he reached her, he notified her and she said: Write:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
h
and stand before God

, devoutly obedient. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated, ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated, ʿUbaydullah narrated, on the authority of Nafiʿ: Hafsah ordered a slave of hers to write a copy of the Qur’an for her and said: When you reach this verse:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, then do not write it until I dictate it to you as I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recite it.
When he reached it, she ordered him to write:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient. Nafiʿ said: So I read that copy of the Qur’an and found the letter waw in it.

c: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman narrated to us, he said: Asad bin Musa narrated to us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Umar, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Hafsah,
m: the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “She said to the scribe of her Mushaf: When you reach the times of prayer, inform me so that I may command you what you heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say. So when he told her, she said: Write, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say:
h
Guard the prayers
, the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer.”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abdah bin Sulayman narrated to us, he said: Muhammad bin Amr narrated to us, he said: Abu Salamah narrated to me, on the authority of Amr bin Rafi’,
m: the freed slave of Umar, he said: It was written in Hafsah’s Mushaf:
h
Guard the prayers
, the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer,
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam al-Masri narrated to us, saying: My father and Shuaib narrated to us, on the authority of al-Layth,
m: saying: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zayd, on the authority of Amr ibn Rafi’, saying: Hafsah called me and I wrote a copy of the Qur’an for her and said: When you reach the verse of prayer, then inform me. So when I wrote:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, she said: And the afternoon prayer, I testify that I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father and Shuaib ibn al-Layth narrated to me, on the authority of al-Layth,
m: saying: Khalid ibn Yazid informed me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zayd: that he had heard from Abu Yunus, the freed slave of Aisha, something similar to that.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Al-Layth narrated to me, saying: Khalid narrated to me, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam:
m: that he had heard from Abu Yunus, the freed slave of Aisha, something similar to that.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Shu’bah informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Habirah ibn Yareem, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Guard strictly the prayers

, especially the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer. Mujahid ibn Musa narrated, on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Abdul Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’, who said: Ubayd ibn Umayr used to recite:
h
Guard strictly the prayers
, especially the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer,
h
and stand before God

, devoutly obedient. Ibn Bashar narrated, on the authority of Uthman ibn Umar, on the authority of Abu Amir, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Qays, on the authority of Ibn Abi Rafi’, on the authority of his father - who was the freed slave of Hafsa - who said: “Hafsa asked me to write down a copy of the Qur’an and said: When you come to this verse, inform me so that I may dictate it to you as you have recited it.” When I came to this verse:
h
Guard strictly the prayers
, especially the middle prayer, I went to her and she said: “Write: ‘
h
Guard strictly the prayers

, especially the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer.’ So I met Ubayy ibn Ka’b or Zayd ibn Thabit and said: O Abu al-Mundhir, Hafsa said such and such.” He said: It is as she said. Or is it not that we are most busy at noon prayer with our camels and sheep!

x: Others said: Rather, the middle prayer is the Maghrib prayer.

Those who said that: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Abd al-Salam told us, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abi Farwah, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb, he said: The middle prayer is the Maghrib prayer. Do you not see that it is neither the least of it nor the most of it, and it is not shortened while traveling, and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not delay it from its time nor did he hasten it?

Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb interpreted his saying: the middle to mean: the middle that is a characteristic of something, it is justice between the two matters, like a man of moderate stature, who is neither excessively tall nor short of stature, and for that reason he said: Do you not see that it is neither the least of it nor the most of it?
Others said: Rather, the middle prayer that God meant by His saying:
h
Guard strictly the prayers
h
and the middle prayer
, is the Fajr prayer.

Those who said that: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Affan told us, he said, Hammam told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Salih Abu Al-Khalil, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The middle prayer is the Fajr prayer.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said:
m: Ibn Abi Uday, Abdul Wahhab and Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: I prayed with Ibn Abbas in the morning prayer in the mosque of Basra, and he made the Qunut with us before bowing and said: This is the middle prayer about which God said:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi, who said:
m: I prayed behind Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibad bin Ya’qub Al-Asadi told me, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Awf Al-A’rabi, on the authority of Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi, who said:
m: I prayed behind Ibn Abbas at Fajr, and he made the Qunut in it and raised his hands and then said: This is the middle prayer about which God has commanded us to stand devoutly.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, Hisham told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said:
m: Ibn Abbas led us in the dawn prayer, and when he finished he said: God said in His Book:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer

, so this is the middle prayer. Abu Kuraib narrated, he said: Marwan narrated - meaning: Ibn Muawiyah - from Awf, from Abu Raja Al-Attardi, from Ibn Abbas, something similar. Ibn Bashar narrated, he said: Abdul Wahhab narrated, he said: Awf narrated, from Abu Al-Munhal, from Abu Al-Aaliyah, from Ibn Abbas: That he prayed the Fajr prayer in the mosque of Basra, and he prayed Qunut before bowing and said: This is the middle prayer that God mentioned:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
h
and stand before God

, devoutly obedient. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna narrated, he said: Abdul Wahhab narrated, he said: Al-Muhajir narrated, from Abu Al-Aaliyah, he said: I asked Ibn Abbas here in Basra, and his thigh was on my thigh, so I said: O Abu So-and-so, have you seen the middle prayer that God mentioned in the Qur’an? Will you not tell me which prayer it is? He said - and that was when they had finished the Fajr prayer - he said: Did you not pray the Maghrib and the last Isha’ prayer? I said: Yes! He said: Then did you pray this? He said: Then did you pray the first and the Asr? I said: Yes! He said: It is this.

c: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Damaghani told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, he said, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas told us, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah, he said:
m: I prayed behind Abdullah ibn Qays in Basra during the time of Umar, he said: I said to a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was next to me: What is the middle prayer? He said: This prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad told us, he said, Awf told us, on the authority of Khalas ibn Amr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: That he prayed the dawn prayer and made supplication before bowing, and raised his fingers and said: This is the middle prayer.

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu al-Aaliyah: That he prayed the dawn prayer with the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and when they finished, he said, I said to them: Which of them is the middle prayer? They said: The one you prayed before.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Uthma told us, he said, Saeed bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said:
m: The middle prayer is the dawn prayer.

c: Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, he said, Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulaiman told us, he said:
m: Ata’ used to think that the middle prayer is the dawn prayer.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yahya bin Wadheeh told us, he said, Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And the middle prayer
