, he said: The dawn prayer.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High:
h
Guard strictly the prayers
h
and the middle prayer
, he said: The dawn prayer.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Husayn, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Haad, he said: The middle prayer is the dawn prayer.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
, he said: The middle prayer is the dawn prayer. The reason for those who said this statement is that God, the Most High, said:
h
Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient, meaning:
h
And stand before God
in it, devoutly obedient. He said: There is no prescribed prayer among the five prayers in which there is Qunut except the Fajr prayer, so it is known from this that it is it and not the others.

x: Others said: It is one of the five prayers, but we do not know it specifically.
Those who said that: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said:

c: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Hisham bin Sa’d told me, he said:
m: We were with Nafi’, and with us was Raja’ bin Haywah, so Raja’ said to us: Ask Nafi’ about the middle prayer. So we asked him, and he said: A man asked Abdullah bin Umar about it and he said: It is among them, so observe them all.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, on the authority of Qais bin Ar-Rabi’, on the authority of Naseer bin Tha’luq Abu Ta’mah, he said:
m: I asked Ar-Rabi’ bin Khathim about the middle prayer, he said: Do you think that if I know it, will I observe it and Surat Al-Baqarah 2:238 Maintain the prayers, especially the middle prayer,
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient. neglect the rest of them? I said: No! He said: If you maintain them, you have maintained it.

c: Ibn Bashar and Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, they said: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said: Shuʿbah told us, he said:
m: I heard Qatadah narrating, on the authority of Saʿid Ibn Al-Musayyab, he said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were like this - meaning they differed in the middle prayer - and he interlaced his fingers.

x: The correct statement in that is what the narrations from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which we mentioned before in its interpretation, agreed upon: that it is the afternoon prayer.
And what God, the Most High, mentioned, urged us to do in that regard is similar to what was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in urging it, as:

c: Ahmad Ibn Muhammad Ibn Habib Al-Tusi told me, he said: Yaʿqub Ibn Ibrahim told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Ishaq, he said: Yazid Ibn Abi Habib told me, on the authority of Khair Ibn Naʿim Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Hubayrah Al-Sabaʿi - he
m: said: and he was trustworthy - on the authority of Abu Tamim Al-Jaishani, on the authority of Abu Basrah Al-Ghifari, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the afternoon prayer with us, and when He turned away and said: This prayer was made obligatory for those who came before you, but they were slow in it and abandoned it. So whoever among you prays it, his reward will be doubled, and there is no prayer after it until he sees the witness - and the witness is the star.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Al-Layth told me, he said, Khair bin Naim told me, on the authority of Ibn Hubayrah, on the authority of Abu Tamim Al-Jaishani: Abu Basrah Al-Ghifari said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the Asr prayer at Al-Mukhmas and said: This prayer was made obligatory upon those who came before you, but they neglected it and abandoned it. Whoever among you maintains it will be given its reward twice.” And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Pray early on a cloudy day, for whoever misses the Asr prayer, his deeds will be in vain.

c: Abu Kurayb told us that, he said, Waki’ told us, and Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said, Ayoub bin Suwaid told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abu Al-Muhajir, on the authority of Buraydah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever misses the Asr prayer, it is as if he has lost his family and his wealth. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever prays before sunrise and before sunset will not enter Hellfire. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) urged us to maintain it in a way that no other prayer was observed, even though maintaining all of them is obligatory. Thus, it is clear that the one that God specifically urged us to maintain, after He had made it general for all the obligatory prayers, is the one that His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) followed. He specifically urged it in a way that He did not specifically encourage any other prayer, and he warned his nation against neglecting it, as happened to the nations before them whose situation he described. He promised them double the reward for maintaining it as He promised for any other prayer. I think that this was the case because God, the Most High, made the night a time of rest, and people, with their preoccupation with seeking a livelihood and managing their means of earning, are calm, except for a few of them, and they are free to maintain God’s obligations and perform the obligatory prayers. The same applies to the dawn prayer, because that is a time when few people are able to earn and fulfill their needs, and there is no burden on them in maintaining it. As for the Dhuhr prayer, its time is the time when people say goodbye and rest from their demands, during times of intense heat and long hours of daylight, and the time to bid farewell to the souls and devote themselves to resting the bodies during the cold and winter days. The known times for people to do their demands and earning, and to be busy with their efforts to do what they need to do to obtain their sustenance are two times of the day. One of them is the beginning of the day after sunrise until the time of midday. God Almighty has lightened the burden of their duties at that time for His servants, and the weight of what distracts them from their efforts in their demands and earnings, even though He has urged them in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger at that time to pray, and promised them a great reward for it, without imposing it on them, and it is the Duha prayer. The other of them is the end of the day, and that is after people have cooled down and are able to do their work and seek a livelihood in summer and winter, until sunset. And He imposed upon them the Asr prayer, then He urged them to maintain it so that they would not waste it, because He knew of the preference of worshipping the immediate causes of their worldly life and seeking their livelihood in it, over the causes of their deferred afterlife, as He urged them to do in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He promised them a great reward for maintaining it, some of which I have mentioned in this book of ours, and we will mention the rest of it in our greatest book, God willing, from the Book of the Rulings of the Laws.

x: It was called the middle because it is in the middle of the five obligatory prayers, because before it are two prayers, and after it are two prayers, and it is in between them and in the middle of them. The middle prayer is the verb from the saying of the speaker: I entered the middle of the people, I entered their middle, a whip and a whip, if I entered their middle. It is said of the male: He is our middle one and of the female: She is our middle one.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his statement: devoutly obedient.
Some of them said: The meaning of devoutly obedient is obedience. And the meaning of that is:
h
And stand before God
in your prayer, obedient to Him in what He has commanded you to do in it and what He has forbidden you from doing.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ali bin Saʿid al-Kindi told me, he said: Abdullah bin al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn ʿAwn, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Obedient.

c: Abu al-Saʿib Salim bin Junadah told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ibn ʿAwn, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Abu Al-Muneeb told us, on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid:
m: h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, meaning: obedient.

c: Abu Al-Sa'ib narrated to me, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of Ata':
m: h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Obedient.

c: Ahmad bin Abdah Al-Himsi narrated to us, he said: Abu Awana narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Obedient.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar narrated to us, he said: Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Rabi' bin Abi Rashid, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: that he was asked about Qunut, and he said: Qunut is obedience.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said: Yahya bin Wadheeh narrated to us, he said: Ubaid bin Sulaiman narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: Qunut, which God mentioned in the Qur'an, means obedience.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib narrated to me, he said: Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, he said: Juwaybir narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: The people of every religion stand before God disobediently, so stand before God obediently.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Stand before God, obedient in everything, and obey Him in your prayers.

c: I was told by Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: he said, I heard Abu Muadh, he said, Ubayd told us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, devoutness means obedience. He said: Every religious person has a prayer, they stand in their prayers for God, disobediently, so stand before God, obedient.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Obedient.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa’d told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Obedient.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told me, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Obedient.

c: Imran bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me, he said, Khattab bin Othman told us, he said, Abu Ruh Abdul-Rahman bin Sinan Al-Sakuni told us,
m: a man from Hims whom I met in Armenia, he said, I heard Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan say about God’s statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Obedient.
b.via: Abu Ruh Abdul-Rahman bin Sinan Al-Sakuni

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding God’s statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Obedient.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding God’s statement:
h
And stand before God

, devoutly obedient, he said: Obedient. Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated, Fadil ibn Marzuq narrated, on the authority of Atiyyah, who said: They used to command their needs during prayer until the verse:
h
And stand before God

, devoutly obedient was revealed, so they stopped talking. He said: Devotedly obedient. Muhammad ibn ‘Amara al-Asadi narrated, Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated, Fadil informed us, on the authority of Atiyyah, regarding His statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient: They used to talk during prayer about their needs until the verse:
h
And stand before God

, devoutly obedient was revealed, so they stopped talking during prayer. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding the statement of God,
h
And stand before God

, devoutly obedient, that every religious person stands in disobedience, so stand before God, obedient. Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman narrated, on the authority of Asad bin Musa, who said: Ibn Lahi’ah narrated, on the authority of Diraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Every letter in the Quran that contains qunut, then it is only obedience.” Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid narrated, who said:

c: My father told me,
m: who said: Sa’id bin Abdul Aziz narrated, who said: Qunut is obedience to God. God the Most High says,
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, obedient. Sa’id bin Al-Rabi’ narrated, who said: Sufyan narrated, who said: Ibn Tawus said: My father used to say: Qunut is obedience to God.

x: Others said: Qunut in this verse means silence. They said: The interpretation of the verse is:
h
And stand before God
, silent about what God has forbidden you to say in your prayer.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient. In this verse, devoutness means silence.

c: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi in a report he mentioned, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said:
m: We used to stand in prayer and talk, and a man would ask his companion about his need, and he would tell him, and they would respond to him when he greeted, until I came and greeted him, but they did not respond to my greeting, so that was difficult for me, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished his prayer, he said: Nothing prevented me from returning your greeting except that we were commanded to stand in obedience and not speak in prayer - and qunut means silence.

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharibi told me, Al-Hakam bin Zuhair told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: We used to talk in prayer, and I greeted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he did not respond to me, so when he finished, he said: “God has decreed that you should not speak in prayer, and this verse was revealed: ‘
h
And stand before God
, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:238 Maintain the prayers, especially the middle prayer,
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient. obedient.’” Abdul Hamid bin Bayan Al-Sakari narrated, he said:

c: Muhammad bin Yazid told us,
m: and Abu Kuraib narrated, Q.L., Ibn Abi Zaidah, Ibn Numayr, Waki’, and Ya’la bin Ubaid, all of them, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Shabil, on the authority of Abu Amr Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, he said: We used to talk during prayer during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one of us would talk to his companion about a need, until this verse was revealed:
h
Guard strictly the prayers
, especially the middle prayer,
h
and stand before God
, devoutly obedient, so he ordered us to be silent. Hannad bin Al-Sarri narrated, he said:

c: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding the words:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: They used to talk during prayer, a man’s servant would come to him while he was praying and talk to him about his need, so they were forbidden to talk.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying, Harun ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn Adi, on the authority of Kalthoum ibn al-Mustaliq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masʿud, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to return my greetings during prayer. One day I came to him and greeted him, but he did not return my greetings. He said, ‘God will bring about whatever He wills in a matter!’ Because He has introduced for you in prayer that no one should speak except in remembrance of God, and in the proper manner of glorifying and praising Him: ‘
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient.’”

c: Yunus narrated to me, saying, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, ‘
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient,’ he said: When you stand in prayer, be silent, do not speak to anyone until you have finished it. He said, ‘And the obedient is the one who prays and does not speak.’

x: Others said that the qunut in this verse means stillness in prayer and humility in it. They said in interpretation of the verse: ‘
h
And stand before God
in your prayer, humbly submissive, with lowered wings, not frivolously or playfully.’”
Mention of who said that:

c: Salim bin Junada told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And stand before God

, devoutly obedient. He said: “Qunut includes prolonging the bowing, lowering the gaze, lowering the wing, and humility out of fear of God. Whenever one of the scholars stood up to pray, he would fear the Most Merciful and not turn around, or flip the pebbles, or play with anything, and he would think of something from the worldly affairs unless he forgot.”

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar, except that he said: Qunut includes stillness and humility.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And stand before God

, devoutly obedient. He said: Qunut includes humility, and lowering the wing out of fear of God. Whenever one of the jurists from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to pray, he would not turn around, or flip the pebbles, or think of something from the worldly affairs unless he forgot, until he finished. Narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Qunut means stagnation, then he mentioned something similar. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father,
m: on al-Rabiʿ, regarding His statement:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient, he said: Qunut means stagnation - meaning standing in prayer and standing up for Him.

x: Others said: Rather, qunut in this instance means supplication. They said: The interpretation of the verse is:
h
And stand before God
, desirous of your prayer.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, and Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said:
m: Ibn Abi ʿUdayy, ʿAbd al-Wahhab, and Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, all of them, on the authority of ʿAwf, on the authority of Abu Rajaʿ, he said: I prayed with Ibn ʿAbbas in the morning in the mosque of Basra, and he led us in qunut before bowing, and he said: This is the middle prayer about which God said:
h
And stand before God
, devoutly obedient.

x: The most correct of these sayings in interpreting His statement:
h
And stand before God

, devoutly obedient, is the saying of those who say: Its interpretation is: Obedient. That is because the root of qunut is obedience, and obedience to God in prayer may be by remaining silent about what God has forbidden, such as speaking in it. Therefore, some interpreted qunut in this place as silence in prayer - one of the meanings that God has imposed on His servants in it - except for reciting the Qur’an or mentioning it in a manner that is appropriate for it.
What indicates that they said that as we have described is the saying of al-Nakhaʿi and Mujahid, who:

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, he said: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim and Mujahid, they said:
m: They were talking in prayer, one of them ordering his brother to do something, so the verse:
h
And stand before God

, devoutly obedient was revealed. He said: So they stopped talking. Qunut is silence, and qunut is obedience. So Ibrahim and Mujahid made qunut silence in obedience to God, according to what we have said about that interpretation. And obedience to God in it may be through humility, lowering the wing, prolonging the standing, and supplication, because all of that is not outside of one of two meanings: that it is from what the worshipper is commanded to do, or from what he is encouraged to do, and the servant is obedient to God with all of that, and he is obedient to his Lord in it. And qunut originally means obedience to God, then it is used for everything with which the servant obeys God. The interpretation of the verse is: Preserve the prayers
h
and the middle prayer
h
and stand before God

in them obediently, by leaving some of you talking to others and other meanings of speech, other than reading the Qur’an in them, or remembering God in a manner befitting Him, or supplicating to Him in them, not disobeying God in them by neglecting their limits, and being negligent in what is due to God upon you in them and in other duties of God.

evidence.text: She said: We used to recite it in the first letter during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer - Abu Jaʿfar said: He said: - The afternoon prayer and stand before God in obedience.”

Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, he said: My father told us, and Ibn Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, they both said: Fadil bin Marzuq told us, on the authority of Shaqiq bin Uqbah Al-Abdi, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, he said: This verse was revealed: Guard strictly the prayers and the afternoon prayer, he said: We recited it during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as much as God willed that we should recite it.

Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Uthman bin Umar told us, he said, Abu Amir told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Qais, on the authority of Ibn Abi Rafi’, on the authority of his father - who was a freed slave of Hafsa - he said: Hafsa asked me to write down a copy of the Qur’an and she said to me: When you come to this verse, inform me so that I may dictate it to you as you have recited it to me.
Others used to recite it: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer and stand before God, devoutly obedient.

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated, ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated, ʿUbaydullah narrated, on the authority of Nafiʿ: Hafsah ordered a slave of hers to write a copy of the Qur’an for her and said: When you reach this verse: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, then do not write it until I dictate it to you as I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recite it.
Nafiʿ said: So I read that copy of the Qur’an and found the letter waw in it.

Ibn Bashar narrated, on the authority of Uthman ibn Umar, on the authority of Abu Amir, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Qays, on the authority of Ibn Abi Rafi’, on the authority of his father - who was the freed slave of Hafsa - who said: “Hafsa asked me to write down a copy of the Qur’an and said: When you come to this verse, inform me so that I may dictate it to you as you have recited it.”

The interpretation of the verse is: Preserve the prayers and the middle prayer, and stand before God in them obediently, by leaving some of you talking to others and other meanings of speech, other than reading the Qur’an in them, or remembering God in a manner befitting Him, or supplicating to Him in them, not disobeying God in them by neglecting their limits, and being negligent in what is due to God upon you in them and in other duties of God.

x: God Almighty means by that: And stand before God in your prayer, obedient to Him, because we have explained its meaning. If you fear an enemy, O people, you fear them for yourselves when you meet them, that you pray standing on your feet on the ground, obedient to God, then pray as men, walking on your feet, while you are in your war and fighting and striving against your enemy, or riding, on the backs of your beasts, because that will suffice you then from standing from you, obedient. And because we said that the meaning of that is thus, it is permissible to put men in the accusative with the omitted meaning. This is because the Arabs do that in the recompense specifically, because the second part is similar to the one conjoined to the first part. This is explained by their saying: If good, then good, and if evil, then evil, meaning: If you do good, you will receive good, and if you do evil, you will receive evil, so they conjoin the answer to the first because the second is completed by the first.
Likewise, his statement:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding

, meaning: If you fear that you will pray standing on the ground, then pray on foot. Rijal is the plural of rajul and rajul. As for the people of Hijaz, they say to one man rajul, and it is heard from them: So-and-so walked to the House of God barefoot as a man. It has been heard from some Arab tribes that one of them should say rajul two men, as some of Banu Uqayl said: Ali, if Laila saw in seclusion that two barefoot men would disdain the House of God So whoever says two men for the male, he says two men for the female. It is permissible in the plural of the masculine and feminine in it to say: The people came to me, my men and my men like kasali and kasali. It has been narrated from some of them that he used to read it: If you fear, then men with a shaddah. And from some of them that he used to read: men. Both readings are not permissible to read with according to us, because they are contrary to the inherited reading that is widespread in the lands of the Muslims.

As for the riders, it is the plural of rider, it is said: he is a rider, and they are riders, and ... it is said: A rider from the people came to us, and riders. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughira told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: I asked him about his statement:
h
On foot or riding
, he said: When chasing, he prays wherever his face is, riding or walking, and he makes the prostration lower than the bowing, and he prays two rak’ahs, gesturing.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On foot or riding
, he said: The prayer of the striker is two rak’ahs, gesturing.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On foot or riding
, he said: He prays two rak’ahs wherever his face is, nodding.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: h
On foot or riding
, he said: If you chase horses, nod.

c: Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, from Malik, from Saeed, he said:
m: He nods with a gesture.

c: Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Hisham narrated to us, from Yunus, from Al-Hasan:
m: While
h
on foot or riding
, he said: When fighting, he prays while riding or walking, wherever his face is, nodding with a gesture.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said, Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Nujayh, from Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding

, the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in fighting on horseback, so if fear occurs, then let a man pray in every direction, standing or riding, or as much as he is able to nod with his head or speak with his tongue.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said, Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Nujayh, from Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: Or riding for the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He also said: Or riding, or as much as he is able to nod with his head. The rest of the hadith is similar.

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, Juwaybir narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding
, he said: If they meet in battle and they pursue or are pursued or pursued by seven, then their prayer is two Takbirs, gesturing, no matter which direction they are in.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, he said: Hisham narrated to us, he said: Juwaybir narrated to us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
On foot or riding

, he said: That is when fighting, he prays wherever he is facing, riding or on foot, if he is pursued or pursued by seven, then let him pray one Rak’ah, gesturing, nodding, and if he is unable to do so then let him say two Takbirs.

c: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Fadl ibn Dahlam, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding
, he said: One Rak’ah while you are Surat Al-Baqarah 2:239
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding

. But when you are secure, then remember God as He has taught you that which you did not know. walking, and your camel is placed with you and your horse is galloping with you, no matter which direction it is in.

c: Musa narrated to me, he said: Amr narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of As-Suddi:
m: h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding
. As for on foot, it means on your feet, if you fight. A man prays nodding his head wherever he is facing, and a rider on his mount nods his head wherever he is facing.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding

. The verse. God has made it permissible for you, if you are afraid during fighting, to pray while riding, and while running, nodding your head from wherever your face is, if you are able to pray two rak’ahs, otherwise one.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding
. He said: That is when fighting.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: regarding the statement:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding
, he said: If the enemy pursues, it is permissible for them to pray in front of whatever direction they are,
h
on foot or riding
, nodding with a gesture of two rak’ahs. Qatada said: One rak’ah is sufficient.

c: I was told by Ammar,
m: he said: Ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on al-Rabi’, regarding the statement:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding
, he said: If they feared the enemy, they prayed two rak’ahs, whether riding or walking.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding the statement:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding

, he said: A man prays in the prescribed battle on his mount and on his mount wherever his face is, nodding with a gesture of water at every bowing and prostration, but prostration is lower than bowing. This is when swords clash with each other, this is in pursuit.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, he said:
m: Qatada used to say: If he is able, then two rak’ahs, otherwise one, gesturing, if he wishes, riding or walking. God Almighty said:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said,
m: regarding the one who is afraid and is being pursued by the enemy, he said: If he is able to pray two rak’ahs, otherwise he prays one rak’ah.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: One rak’ah.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Shu’bah narrated to us, he said:
m: I asked Al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatadah about the prayer of combat, and they said: One rak’ah.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, he said, Shu’bah narrated to us, he said:
m: I asked Al-Hakam, Hammad and Qatadah about the prayer of combat, and they said: He nods wherever his face is.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Muhammad bin Ja’far narrated to us, on the authority of Hammad,
m: Al-Hakam and Qatadah: That they were asked about the prayer during combat, and they said: One rak’ah wherever your face is.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib narrated to me, he said, Ibn Fadil narrated to us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Suwar, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Sirin about the prayer of combat. The defeated one said: How could he?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Yazid, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Jabir bin Ghurab
m: said: We were fighting the people and Harim bin Hayyan was our leader. Then the time for prayer came and they said: Prayer, prayer! Harim said: A man prostrates wherever his face is prostrating. He said: And we are facing the east.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, he said:
m: Harim bin Hayyan was in charge of an army, and the enemy was approaching, so he said: Every man among you should prostrate under his garden wherever his face is prostrating, or whatever is easy for him, so I said to Abu Nadrah: What is easy for him? He said: He gestures.

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, he said, Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Abu Muslimah told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, he said: Jabir bin Ghurab told me, he said:
m: We were with Harim bin Hayyan fighting the enemy facing the east, and the time for prayer came, so they said: Prayer! He said: A man prostrates under his garden in prostration.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding His statement:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding
, he said: You pray wherever you are, riding or walking, and wherever your mount takes you, nodding for the obligatory prayer.

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said: Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, he said: Al-Mas’udi told us, he said: Yazid Al-Faqir told me, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, he said:
m: The prayer of fear is one rak’ah.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Musa bin Muhammad Al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding this verse, he said: If he is afraid, he prays in whatever state he is in.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Malik said - and I asked him about the statement of God:
h
on foot or riding

- he said: On foot or walking. If it only meant people, it would not have come except on foot and the verse would have been cut off. They are men: pedestrians. He read: They come to you on foot and on every lean camel (al-Hajj 22:87). He said: They come on foot and riding.

x: The fear for which the worshipper must pray the obligatory prayer on foot, on foot, or while riding, is the fear for his life when fighting a battlefield or fencing in a battle ordered to be fought, from an enemy of the Muslims, or a warrior, or a wild beast, or a charging camel, or a flowing flood, and he fears drowning in it. And everything that is most likely to lead to a person’s death if he prays the prayer of security, then if that is the case, then he may pray the prayer of intense fear wherever his face is, indicating the generality of the Book of God:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding
, and he did not specify the fear for that to any type, after the fear is, its description is as I mentioned.

Rather, we said that the fear that allows the one praying to pray in this way is the one that most likely leads to death by performing the prayer within its limits, and that is in the case of intense fear, because:

c: Muhammad bin Hamid and Sufyan bin Wakee’ told me that Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Nafi’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the prayer of fear: The emir and a group of people with him stand and prostrate once, then a group of them stand between them and the enemy. Then those who prostrated leave with their emir, then they are in the place of those who did not pray, and those who did not pray stand forward and pray with their emir one prostration. Then their emir leaves having completed his prayer, and after his prayer each of the two groups prays a prostration for himself, even if the fear is more intense than that” on foot or on horseback.

c: Saeed bin Yahya al-Umawi told me that my father told me that Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said:
m: If they mix - meaning in combat - then it is only remembrance. And a sign with the head. Ibn Umar said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And if they are more than that, then they pray standing or riding. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, distinguished between the ruling on the prayer of fear in cases other than combat and pursuit, and the ruling on the prayer of fear in cases of intense fear and combat, according to what we narrated from Ibn Umar. So it was known from this that the words of God Almighty:
h
But if you fear
, then
h
on foot or riding

, only meant the fear whose description we have described. And similar to what Ibn Umar narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it was narrated from Ibn Umar that he used to say:

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Ayoub, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar that he said
m: regarding the prayer of fear: He prays with a group of people one rak’ah, and a group stands guard. Then those who he prayed with go until they stand in place of their companions. Then those come and he prays with them one rak’ah, then he says the salutation, and each group stands and prays one rak’ah. He said: If the fear is more intense than that,
h
on foot or riding

. As for the number of rak’ahs in that state of prayer, I like that he does not shorten its number in a state of security. If he shortens it and prays one rak’ah, I see that it is sufficient, because: - Bishr bin Mu’adh told me, he said, Abu ‘Awanah told us, on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, he said: “God imposed prayer on the tongue of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the city four, and in travel two rak’ahs, and in fear one rak’ah.” - Abu Ja’far said: The interpretation of that is:
h
So when you are secure

, O believers, from your enemy being able to kill you while you are busy with your prayer that He imposed upon you - and from others whom you feared for yourselves while you were praying - and you are reassured, then remember God in your prayer and other than it by thanking Him, praising Him, and thanking Him for what He has bestowed upon you of success in attaining the truth from which your enemies from among the disbelievers in God have strayed, just as He reminded you by teaching you of His rulings, His lawful and unlawful things. And report of the nations that came before you, and the report that will happen after you - in the immediate world and the hereafter, which others were ignorant of and which harmed you, from that and other things, as a blessing from Him to you with that, so He taught you from it what you did not know before He taught you. And Mujahid used to say about His statement:
h
So when you are secure
, what: - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said, Waki’ narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
So when you are secure

, he said: you left the place of travel for the place of residence. And similar to what we have said about that, Ibn Zayd said - Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said about His statement:
h
And when you are secure
, remember God, he said:
h
So when you are secure

, then perform the prayer as God has enjoined upon you - if fear comes, they have a dispensation. And His statement here: Remember God, he said: The prayer, as He has taught you that which you did not know.

x: This statement that we mentioned from Mujahid, the statement of others is more correct than it, because of the consensus of all that when the fear is removed, it is obligatory upon the one praying the obligatory prayer - even if he is traveling - to perform it with its bowing and prostration and its limits, standing on the ground, not walking or riding, as is obligatory upon him if he is residing in his city and country, except for what is permitted to him of shortening it during his travel. And there is no mention of travel in this verse, so His statement:
h
So remember God as He has taught you that which you did not know is directed towards it
. Prayer was mentioned in times of security and times of intense fear, so God Almighty informed His servants of the nature of what is obligatory upon them in prayer in both cases. Then He said:
h
And when you are secure
and the fear is removed, then establish your prayer and remember Me in it and in other times, like what I made obligatory upon you before the occurrence of the state of fear.

And after that, if it was mentioned for travel, then God Almighty wanted to inform His creation of the nature of what is obligatory upon them in Prayer after their standing, for he said: So when you stand, remember God as He taught you what you did not know, and he did not say: Then when you are safe. And in the words of God Almighty: Then when you are safe, there is clear evidence of the correctness of the statement of the one who interpreted that to what we said about it, and contrary to the statement of Mujahid.

evidence.text: It has been narrated from some of them that he used to read it: If you fear, then men with a shaddah.
Both readings are not permissible to read with according to us, because they are contrary to the inherited reading that is widespread in the lands of the Muslims.

x: God Almighty meant by that: And those of you who die, O men, and leave wives behind, meaning wives who were his wives during his life, through marriage, not through right hand possession. Then He diverted the report from mentioning the one with whom the report began, similar to what preceded in His statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten (al-Baqarah 2:234), to the report about mentioning their husbands. We have mentioned the reason for that, and we have demonstrated the correctness of the statement about it in its counterpart that came before it, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Then the Almighty said:
h
A will for their wives
. The reciters differed in the recitation of that: Some of them read:
h
A will for their wives
, with the accusative of the will, meaning: let them make
h
a will for their wives
, or: they must make a will,
h
a will for their wives
Others read:
h
A will for their wives
with the nominative of the will. Then the Arab scholars differed in the reason for raising the will.

Some of them said: It was raised in the sense: the will was written upon them. And the reason for that was that it is like that in the recitation of Abdullah. So the interpretation of the speech is according to what this speaker said: And those of you who die and leave wives, a will is written upon them for their wives - then he left out mentioning it was written and the will was raised with that meaning, even though it was left out.

Others among them said: Rather, the will is raised by his saying: for their wives, so he interpreted it as: for their wives a will. The first statement is more correct in that, which is that if the will is raised, it is raised in the meaning: a will was written upon you for your wives. Because the Arabs conceal their indefinite nouns before them if they conceal them, and if they reveal them they begin with them before them, so you say: A man came to me today, and if they say: A man came to me today, they hardly say it except that the man is present, referring to him with this, or absent and the one being reported has known his report, or by deleting this and concealing it even if they delete it, to know the listener in the sense of the speaker, as God Almighty said: A surah we have sent down (al-Nur 24:1) and Disavowal from God and His Messenger (al-Tawbah 9:1). So it is the same in His statement:
h
A will for their wives

The most correct of the two readings in this, according to us, is the reading of the one who reads it in the nominative case, because the apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates that the residence of the woman whose husband died in the house of her deceased husband for a full year was her right before the revelation of His statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days (al-Baqarah 2:234), and before the revelation of the verse of inheritance, and because the report about The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner that is indicated by the apparent meaning, was that their husbands recommended that to them before their death, or they did not recommend that to them.
What is the evidence for that?
When God, the Most High, said:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, a bequest is made for their wives, and the testator undoubtedly only recommends during his lifetime what he orders to be implemented after his death, and it was impossible for him to make a bequest after his death, and God, the Most High, only made the wife of the deceased reside for a year after his death, we know that it is a right for her that is due from his wealth without a bequest from him to her, since it was impossible for the deceased to make a bequest after his death.

If the meaning of the speech was as interpreted by the one who said: Let him make a bequest, then the revelation would have been: And those whom death approaches and leave wives behind, a bequest is made for their wives, as He said: It is prescribed for you, when death approaches any of you, if he leaves wealth, that he make a bequest (al-Baqarah 2:18). Surat Al-Baqarah 2:240 And those among you who die and leave wives behind them - they shall bequeath to their wives a provision for a year without turning them out. But if they go out, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves of appropriate kindness.
h
And God is Exalted in Might and Wise

. And then, if that was obligatory for them by a will from their deceased husbands: that would not be a protection for them if their husbands did not bequeath it to them before their death, and their heirs would have been embarrassed before the year, and God the Most High said: other than expelling.

But the matter in that is contrary to what its reader thought in its interpretation: a bequest for their husbands, meaning: that God the Most High had ordered their husbands to bequeath to them. Rather, the interpretation of that is:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind
, God has prescribed for their wives a commandment from Him to them, O believers - that you not expel them from their husbands’ homes for a year, as God the Most High said in Surat An-Nisa’:
without causing harm, a commandment from God
then He left out mentioning: God has prescribed, being satisfied with the indication of the speech on it, and the commandment was removed in the meaning that we mentioned before.
Is it permissible to put the will in the accusative case, meaning: we are bequeathing, they have a will?

No, because that would only have been permissible if the will had preceded the speech in which it is appropriate for the will to be excluded from it, but if it had not preceded what would have been appropriate for it to be in the accusative case by its exclusion from it, then it is not permissible to put it in the accusative case in that sense.

Some of those who said: The residence for a full year was a right for the husbands of the deceased after their death, according to what we said, whether their husbands bequeathed it to them or did not bequeath it to them, and that this was abrogated by what we mentioned about the four months and ten and the inheritance.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Munhal told us, he said, Hammam bin Yahya told us, he said,
m: I asked Qatada about his statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall bequeath to their wives a provision for a year without expulsion, so he said: If a woman’s husband died, she was entitled to residence and maintenance for a year from her husband’s wealth, as long as she did not expel it. Then He abrogated that later in Surat An-Nisa, and made for her a known portion: an eighth if he had a son, and a quarter if he did not have a son, and her waiting period is four months and ten days, so the Most High said:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days (al-Baqarah 2:234). So this verse abrogated what came before it about the matter of the year.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding His statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall bequeath to their wives a provision for a year without expulsion (al-Baqarah 2:234). He said: This was before the verse of inheritance was revealed, so if a woman’s husband died, she had the right to housing and maintenance for a year if she wished, so He abrogated that in Surat An-Nisa, and made for her a known portion: He made for her an eighth if he had a son, and if he did not have a son, then she has a quarter, and He made her waiting period four months and ten days, so He said: “
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
, they shall wait, if they did not have a son, if they did not have a son, then they shall wait ... “
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days. So if a man died and left his wife, she would observe a waiting period of one year in his house, and he would spend on her from his money. Then God, the Most High, revealed after that:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days. This is the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died, unless she is pregnant, in which case her waiting period is until she gives birth. And He said about her inheritance: And for them is a fourth of what you leave if you have no child; but if you have a child, then for them is an eighth.
r
(An-Nisa’: 12)
, so God explained the inheritance of a woman, leaving a will and spending.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh who said: I heard Ubaydullah ibn Sulayman who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
And a bequest for their wives

, a provision for a year without expulsion, that if a man died, he would spend on his wife during his year until a year, and he would not remarry until the year was complete. This was abrogated: The provision for her was abrogated by a quarter and an eighth of the inheritance, and the year was abrogated by four months and ten.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak
m: regarding His statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind

, a bequest for their wives, a provision for a year without expulsion, he said: If a man dies, he should spend on his wife until a year, and he would not remarry until the year had passed, so God the Most High revealed:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind
, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten, so the period of one year was abrogated, and the provision for her was abrogated by the inheritance: a quarter and an eighth.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: I asked Ata’ about his statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall bequeath to their wives a provision for a year without turning them out, he said: The woman’s inheritance from her husband was from a quarter of his 1: that she may live if she wishes from the day her husband dies until a year, he says: But if they go out, there is no blame upon you, the verse, then what God imposed of inheritance abrogated it, he said, and Mujahid said: A provision for their wives means living for a year, then this verse abrogated the inheritance.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: When the will was made, the wives of the dead had a year’s maintenance. God abrogated that which was written for the wife from the yearly maintenance by inheritance, and He made for her a quarter or an eighth. And in His statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten, he said: This is the abrogator.

x: Mention of those who said: That was for them by a will from their husbands to them:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, from Qatadah,
m: his statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind

, the verse, he said: This was from before the obligatory shares, so the man would make a will to his wife and to whomever he wished. Then that was abrogated later, and God the Most High added their inheritance to those who were entitled to inherit, and He made for the woman if he had a child an eighth, and if he had no child then she has a quarter. And he used to spend on the woman for a year from her husband’s money, then he moved from his house. So the waiting period of four months and ten abrogated it, and the quarter or an eighth abrogated the will for them, so the will became for the relatives who do not inherit.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, a bequest for their wives to as regards what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner, on the day this verse was revealed, when a man died, he would bequeath to his wife her maintenance and housing for a year, and her waiting period was four months and a month. If she went out when the four months and ten days had passed, her maintenance would cease, so that is what He said: And if they go out, and this was before the verse of inheritance was revealed, so the quarter and the eighth abrogated it, so she took her share, and she was not entitled to housing or maintenance.

c: Ahmad bin Al-Muqaddam told me, he said, Al-Mu’tamir told us,
m: he heard my father say, Qatada claims that a woman was bequeathed her maintenance until the end of the year. It was mentioned that he said: This abrogated what they had of the provision for a year, without clarifying how it was for them:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall bequeath to their wives a provision for a year, he said: It is abrogated. - Al-Hasan bin al-Zubayr told us, he said, Usamah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, he said: I heard Ibrahim say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, they said:
m: h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall bequeath to their wives a provision for a year without expulsion, this was abrogated by the verse of inheritance and what was imposed on them in it of a quarter and an eighth, and the term of the year was abrogated by making its term four months and ten.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He stood up to address the people here, and he recited to them Surat Al-Baqarah, and explained to them from it, and he came to this verse: If he leaves wealth, a bequest to parents and relatives (al-Baqarah 2:180). He said: So this was abrogated. Then he read until he came to this verse:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them
to His saying: without turning them out, then he said: And this. And others said: This verse is a fixed ruling, nothing of it was abrogated.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days (al-Baqarah 2:234), he said: This was for the woman in waiting, she would wait with her husband’s family, and that was obligatory upon her, then God revealed:
h
And those of you who die and leave wives behind them

, they shall bequeath to their wives a maintenance for a year without turning them out to His saying: from what is acceptable. He said: God made for them the completion of the year, seven months and twenty nights, and a will: if she wishes, she may live in her will, and if she wishes, she may go out, and this is the saying of God the Most High: but if they go out, there is no blame upon you, He said: And the waiting period is as it is obligatory.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa - and Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us
m: - on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said. This verse abrogated her waiting period with his family, she may observe the waiting period wherever she wishes, and this is the saying of God the Most High: but if they go out, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves, Ata’ said: Inheritance came to abrogate the residence, she may observe the waiting period wherever she wishes, and she has no residence.

x: The most correct of these statements in my opinion is that it is said that God Almighty had made for the wives of men who died after their death, a residence for a year in his house, and their expenses from the money of their dead husband until the end of the year, and it was obligatory upon the heirs of the deceased not to evict them before the completion of the year from the residence in which he lived, and if they abandoned their right to that and left, the heirs of the deceased would not be in trouble for their leaving. Then God Almighty abrogated the maintenance with the verse of inheritance, and nullified what He had made for them of a residence for a year of seven months and twenty nights, and returned them to four months and ten days, on the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me, Hajjaj told us, Haywah ibn Shuraih told us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Saʿd ibn Ishaq ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah,
m: who told him on the authority of his aunt Zaynab bint Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah, on the authority of Fariʿah, the sister of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: Her husband went out in search of a Surat Al-Baqarah 2:240 And those among you who die and leave wives behind them - they shall bequeath to their wives a provision for a year without turning them out. But if they go out, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves of appropriate kindness.
h
And God is Exalted in Might and Wise

. slave of his, and caught up with him in a nearby place and fought him, and some of his slaves helped him against him, so they killed him. So she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My husband went out in search of a slave of his, and he was met by foreigners who killed him, and I am in a place where there is no one else but me, and I have decided to move to my family! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Rather, stay where you are until the written term is fulfilled. As for his saying: provision, its meaning is: He made that provision for them, meaning the will that God wrote for them. And provision is in the accusative case because in his saying:
h
A will for their wives

, there is a meaning: God provided them with provision, so it was said: provision is a source of meaning, not of wording. His saying: other than expulsion, its meaning is that God, the Most High, made what He made for them of the will a provision from Him for them until a year, not expulsion from her husband’s dwelling, meaning: there is no expulsion from it until the year ends. So the accusative of other is used as an attribute of provision, like the saying of the one who says: This is standing, not sitting, meaning: This is standing, not sitting with it, or: there is no sitting in it.
b.via: Saʿd ibn Ishaq ibn Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah

x: Some of them have claimed that it is accusative in the meaning: Do not expel them, and that is a mistake in the statement. Because if it is accusative according to this interpretation, it is accusative from another statement other than the first, but it is accusative because of what accusative of the provision is for it.

God Almighty means by that: that the provision that God made for them until a year in the wealth of their husbands after their death and in their homes, and He forbade their heirs from expelling them, is only for them as long as they stay in their husbands’ homes, and that their rights from that are nullified by their exit if they leave their husbands’ homes before a year on their own, without expulsion from the heirs of the deceased. Then God Almighty informed: that there is no blame on the guardians of the deceased for their exit and their abandonment of mourning for their husbands. Because staying a year in their husbands’ homes and mourning for him is the completion of a full year, it was not obligatory upon them, but rather it was a permission from God Almighty for them if they stayed the entire year mourning. But if they go out, there is no blame on the guardians of the deceased or on them for what they did with themselves of good, and that is abandoning mourning.

He says: There is no blame upon you for adorning yourself, wearing perfume, and getting married, because that is for them. We only said: There is no blame upon them for going out, even though God Almighty said: There is no blame upon you. Because if there was a sin on them in that, then there would be a sin on the man’s guardians in that by leaving them and going out, even though they were able to prevent them from doing so. But since there was no sin on them in going out and not mourning, the blame was removed from the guardians of the woman and others for what they did of good, and that was in themselves. The narration from the people of interpretation has already passed with what we said about that before. As for His saying:
h
And God is Exalted in Might and Wise

, He, the Most High, means: And God is Exalted in Might, in His vengeance upon those who disobeyed His command and prohibition and transgressed His limits, from men and women, so He prevented those men from their wives and husbands from what He had imposed upon them in the verses that came before: of pleasure, dowry, and bequest, and expelling them before the end of the year, and abandoning the observance of the prayers and their times, and He prevented those women from what God had obligated them to do of waiting after the death of their husbands, and He disobeyed His command in observing the times of the prayers, Wise, in what He decreed between His servants of His judgments that had come before His saying:
h
And God is Exalted in Might and Wise
, and in other than that of His judgments and decrees.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the recitation of that: Some of them read: A will for their wives, with the accusative of the will, meaning: let them make a will for their wives, or: they must make a will, a will for their wives.
And the reason for that was that it is like that in the recitation of Abdullah.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the two readings in this, according to us, is the reading of the one who reads it in the nominative case, because the apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates that the residence of the woman whose husband died in the house of her deceased husband for a full year was her right before the revelation of His statement: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days (al-Baqarah 2:234), and before the revelation of the verse of inheritance, and because the report about The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a manner that is indicated by the apparent meaning, was that their husbands recommended that to them before their death, or they did not recommend that to them.

x: God Almighty means by that: And for the woman who divorces her husband, there is provision. He means by that: what she enjoys of clothes, clothing, expenses, servants, and other things that she enjoys. We have previously explained the meaning of that, and the differences of scholars about it, and the correct statement about that according to us, is sufficient from The scholars differed about the meaning of this verse regarding divorced women.

Some of them said: It refers to married women who have had sexual intercourse. They said: We only said that because the rights of divorced women who have not been consummated with in the temporary marriage have been explained by God the Almighty in the verses before it, so we know from that that this verse explains the matter of those who have been consummated with in that.

Those who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa ibn Maymun told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, regarding His statement: And divorced women shall have a right to provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous, he said: The married woman is given a right to provision if he has sexual intercourse with her according to what is acceptable.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, and he added to it: Shibl mentioned it, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse indicates that every divorced woman has a temporary marriage, and God, the Most High, revealed it to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because it contains an additional meaning to what is in it from the other verses of temporary marriage, since what is in it from the verses of temporary marriage is only to explain the ruling on the untouched if she is divorced, and in this verse is to explain the ruling on all divorced women in temporary marriage.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding this verse: And divorced women have a right to provision according to what is acceptable, an obligation upon the righteous, he said: Every divorced woman has a right to provision according to what is acceptable, an obligation upon the righteous.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri -
m: regarding the slave woman whose husband divorces her while she is pregnant - he said: She waits in her house. He said: I have not heard anything about the temporary marriage of a slave woman that I can remember, and God, the Most High, said: A right to provision according to what is acceptable, an obligation upon the doers of good, and she has the temporary marriage until she gives birth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Habban bin Musa told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: I said to him: Is there a temporary marriage for a slave woman with a free man? He said: No. I said: What about a free woman with a slave? He said: No. Amr bin Dinar said: Yes, Divorced women shall have a right to provision according to what is acceptable - an obligation upon the righteous.

x: Others said: This verse was revealed because when God, the Most High, revealed His words:
h
And give them provision according to what is acceptable
, the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability - a provision according to what is acceptable - an obligation upon the doers of good”

a Muslim man said: Then we will not do that if we do not intend to do good. Then God revealed: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous, so that was obligatory upon them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “
h
And give them provision according to what is acceptable

- the wealthy according to his ability and the poor according to his ability - a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the doers of good” (al-Baqarah 2:236), a man said: If I did well, I would do it, but if I did not want to do it, I would not do it! Then God revealed: And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous.

x: The correct statement regarding that is what Sa’id bin Jubayr said, that God, the Most High, revealed it as evidence for His servants that every divorced woman has a provision according to what is acceptable. Because God, the Most High, mentioned in all the verses of the Qur’an that mention the enjoyment of women, especially women, so He explained in the verse in which He said: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them or appointed for them an obligation (al-Baqarah 2:236), and in His saying: O you who believe, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you Surat Al-Baqarah 2:241 And divorced women have a right to provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous. have touched them (al-Ahzab 33:49), what they are entitled to from enjoyment if they are divorced before touching them, and in His saying: O Prophet, tell your wives, if you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you (al-Ahzab 33:28), the ruling on those who have been consummated with, and the ruling on young girls remains if they are divorced after they have been married, and the ruling on unbelievers and slave girls.

So God, the Most High, mentioned it comprehensively in His saying: And for divorced women there is a provision according to what is acceptable, He mentioned all of them, and informed that they are entitled to provision, just as He specified the divorced women described by their characteristics in all the verses of the Qur’an, and for this reason He repeated mentioning all of them in this verse. As for his statement:
h
It is truly upon the righteous
, we have already explained the meaning of his statement:
h
It is truly upon the righteous (al-Baqarah 2

:236). There is no need to repeat it here. As for the righteous: they are those who feared God in His commands, prohibitions, and limits, so they carried out what He charged them to carry out out of fear of Him and dread of His punishment.
The explanation of the interpretation of that has already been presented explicitly in the narration.

God Almighty says: Just as I have explained to you what is required of you for your wives and what is required of your wives for you, O believers, and I have made known to you My rulings and the right that is due to some of you over others in these verses, so I explain to you the rest of the rulings in My verses that I revealed to My Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this book, so that you may understand - O believers in Me and My Messenger - My limits, and understand what is required of you from My obligations, and know thereby what is good for your religion and your worldly life, your immediate and your future life, so that you may act upon it to reconcile your differences, and attain thereby My abundant reward in your afterlife.

God Almighty means: Have you not seen?, Have you not known, O Muhammad? This is from the vision of the heart, not the vision of the eye, because our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not realize those about whom God informed us of this report, and the vision of the heart is what he saw, his knowledge of it. So the meaning of that is: Have you not known, O Muhammad, those who left their homes and they were thousands? Then the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His statement: and they were thousands.

Some of them said: In the number, meaning the sum of a thousand. Whoever said that: Ibn Wakee' told us, he said, my father told us, and Amr ibn Ali told us, he said, Wakee' told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Maysarah al-Nahdi, on the authority of al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement:
h
Have you not seen those who left their homes and they were thousands

, fearing death? He said: They were four thousand, they left fleeing from the plague, they said: We are going to a land where there is no death! Until when they were in such and such a place, God said to them: Die. Then a prophet from among the prophets passed by them and called upon his Lord to revive them, so He revived them, and he recited this verse: Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, but most of mankind are not grateful.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Maysarah al-Nahdi, on the authority of al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes

, by the thousands, for fear of death? He said: They were four thousand who went forth fleeing from the plague, so God caused them to die. Then a prophet from among the prophets passed by them and called upon his Lord to revive them so that they might worship Him, so He revived them.

c: Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar narrated to us, he said, Ismail ibn Abd al-Karim informed us, he said, Abd al-Samad narrated to me:
m: that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: Some people from the Children of Israel were afflicted with a calamity and hardship during the time, so they complained about what had befallen them and said: If only we had died so that we could find relief from what we are in! Then God revealed to Ezekiel: Your people cried out in distress, and claimed that they wished to die and find rest. But what rest would they have in death? Do they think that I am not able to resurrect them after death? So go to such and such a cemetery, for in it are four thousand - Wahb said: They are the ones about whom God said: Have you not seen those who left their homes by the thousands, for fear of death? - so stand among them and call them, and their bones had been scattered, separated by birds and beasts. Ezekiel called out to them and said: O bones, God commands you to come together! So the bones of every person came together together. Then Ezekiel called out a second time and said: O bones, God commands you to be covered with flesh. So they were covered with flesh, and after the flesh, skin, and they became bodies. Then Ezekiel called out a third time and said: O souls, God commands you to return to your bodies!

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
