Have you not considered those who went forth from their homes

, and they were thousands? He said: A large number, they went forth fleeing from jihad in the cause of God, so God caused them to die, then He brought them back to life and commanded them to fight their enemy, so that is what He said: And fight in the cause of God, and know that God is Hearing and Knowing. (al-Baqarah 2:244) Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of ʿAnbasa, on the authority of Ashʿath ibn Aslam Al-Basri, he said: While ʿUmar was praying and there were two Jews behind him, and whenever ʿUmar wanted to bow, he would faint 1, then one of them said to his companion, Is he him? So when ʿUmar turned away, he said: “What do you think of what one of you said to his companion, ‘Is he him?’ They said: We find it in our book: ‘A horn of iron, given what is given to Ezekiel, who protected the dead by God’s permission.’” Omar said: We do not find in the Book of God Ezekiel nor anyone who revives the dead by God’s permission, except Jesus. They said: Do you not find in the Book of God and messengers We have not related to you
r
(An-Nisa’: 164)

? Omar said: Yes! They said: As for the resurrection of the dead, we will tell you: The Children of Israel were struck by a plague, and some of them left until they were a mile away, and God killed them. They built a wall around them, and when their bones had decayed, God sent Ezekiel, who stood over them and said, Whatever God wills. So God sent them to him, and God revealed concerning that:
h
Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes
, and they were thousands? The verse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Arta’ah, he said:
m: They were four thousand.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes
, and they were thousands? until His saying:
h
Then He revived them

. He said: There was a village called Dawardan before Wasit, and the plague struck it, so most of its people fled and settled in a part of it, and those who remained in the village perished, and the others were saved, and not a single one of them died. When the plague was over, they returned safely. Those who remained said: “Our companions were wiser than us. If we had done as they did, we would have survived!” If the plague strikes again, we will go out with them. So it struck the next year, and they fled, and they were thirty-some thousand, until they came to that place, which was a sparse valley. Then an angel called to them from the bottom of the valley and another from the top: Die! So they died, and when they were destroyed and their bodies had decayed, a prophet called Ezekiel passed by them. When he saw them, he stopped over them and began to contemplate them, twisting his jaw and fingers. Then God revealed to him: O Ezekiel, do you want me to show you how I bring them back to life? He said: His contemplation was only due to his amazement at God’s power over them. He said: Yes! So it was said to him: Call! So he called: O bones, God commands you to gather together! Then the bones began to fly towards each other, until they became bodies of bones. Then God revealed to him to call out: O bones, God commands you to be clothed with flesh. So they were clothed with flesh and blood, and the clothes in which they died were on them. Then it was said to him: Call out! So he called out: O bodies, God commands you to rise, so they rose.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, he said:
m: Mansur bin Al-Mu'tamir claimed, on the authority of Mujahid: That they said when they were revived: Glory be to You, our Lord, and praise be to You, there is no god but You. So they returned to their people alive, knowing that they had been dead, with the mark of death on their faces, and they did not wear a garment except that it became greasy like a shroud, until they died at the appointed times that were written for them.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awsaja narrated to us, on the authority of Ata al-Khurasani:
m: h
Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes
, and they were thousands? He said: They were three thousand or more.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Abbas said:
m: They were forty thousand and eight thousand, and they were enclosed in pens, and their bodies were exhausted and they stank. Today that stench can be found in that tribe of the Jews, and they were thousands fleeing from jihad in the way of God, so God killed them and then brought them back to life, and He commanded them to jihad, and that is what He said: And fight in the way of God (al-Baqarah 2:110 and 244), the verse.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih,
m: that when Caleb ibn Yufna was taken by God after Joshua, He left among them - meaning among the Children of Israel - Ezekiel ibn Buzay, who was the son of the old woman. He was called the son of the old woman because she asked God for a child when she had grown old and barren, so God gave him to her, and for that reason he was called the son of the old woman. He is the one who prayed for the people whom God mentioned in the Book for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as we have been told: “
h
Have you not considered those who went forth from their homes
, and they were thousands, for fear of death? And God said to them, ‘Die,’ then He brought them back to life. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, but most of the people do not give thanks.”

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, he said:
m: It reached me that it was from their story that they went forth fleeing from some epidemic, from the plague, or from a disease that was afflicting the people, for fear of death, and they were thousands, until when they settled in a high place in the country, God said to them, ‘Die,’ and they all died, so the people of that country went to They forbade them a pen away from the wild beasts, then left them in it, because they were too many to be absent. Time and ages passed by them, until they became rotten bones. Ezekiel bin Buzay passed by them, stopped over them, and was amazed at their situation, and mercy entered him for them. Then it was said to him: Do you want God to revive them? He said: Yes! Then it was said to him: Call them and say: O rotten bones that have decayed and decayed, let each bone return to its companion. So he called them with that, and he looked at the bones jumping up and taking one another. Then it was said to him: Say: O flesh, nerves and skin, cover the bones by the permission of your Lord. He said: So he looked at them and the nerves took the bones, then the flesh, skin and hair, until they were all created together, with no souls in them. Then he prayed for life for them, and something from the sky covered him, so distressed him that he fainted from it. Then he came to and the people were sitting saying: Glory be to God, glory be to God, God has revived them.

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying:
h
And they are thousands
, and they are united.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
Have you not considered those who went forth from their homes
by the thousands for fear of death? And God said to them, “Die.
h
Then He revived them

, “He said: A village was afflicted with the plague, so a group of them went forth and a group remained, so the plague struck the group that remained, and the group that went forth did not suffer anything. Then it was lifted, then it descended the following year, so a group went forth more than the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:243 Have you not considered those who left their homes, thousands in number, for fear of death? But God said to them, "Die."
h
Then He revived them

. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, but most of mankind are not grateful. first group, so the plague raged upon the group that remained. Then when it was the third year, it descended and they all went forth and left their homes, so God, the Most High, said: “
h
Have you not considered those who went forth from their homes

by the thousands?” It was not division that drove them forth, as one goes forth for war and fighting, their hearts were united, rather they went forth fleeing. So when they were where they went seeking life, God said to them, Die, in the place to which they went seeking life. They died, then God revived them. God is indeed full of bounty to mankind, but most people are not grateful. He said: A man passed by it and it was bones looming, so he stopped to look and said: How can God revive these after their death? (al-Baqarah 2:259), so God caused him to die for a hundred years. He mentioned the reports of those who said: The departure of these people from their homes was to flee from the plague.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Al-Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes

, thousands in number, for fear of death? He said: They went forth fleeing from the plague, so He caused them to die before their appointed times, then He brought them back to life until their appointed times.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes
, thousands in number, for fear of death? He said: They fled from the plague, so God said to them: Die, then He brought them back to life to complete the rest of their appointed times.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar,
m: regarding God’s statement: God the Almighty said:
h
Have you not considered those who went forth from their homes

, by the thousands, for fear of death? He said: The plague broke out in their village, so some people went out and others remained, so those who remained in the village perished and the others remained. Then the plague broke out in their second village, so some people went out and others remained, and those who went out were more than those who remained. So God saved those who went out, and those who remained perished. Then the third time, they all went out except a few, so God killed them and their animals,
h
then He revived them
and they returned to their country, having rejected their village and those they had left behind. And they multiplied in it, saying to one another: Who are you?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said:
m: I heard Amr ibn Dinar say: The plague broke out in their village. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Asim. Bishr bin Muadh narrated, Suwaid narrated, Saeed narrated, on the authority of Qatada:
h
Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes

, and they were thousands? God detested them for fleeing death, so He caused them to die as a punishment, then He sent them back to the rest of their appointed times to complete them. Had the appointed times of the people come, they would not have been sent back after their death. I narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hasan, who narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, regarding the words of God the Almighty: Have you not seen those who went forth? He said: These were a people from the Children of Israel. When the plague struck them, their rich and nobles would go forth, and their poor and lowly ones would stay. He said: Death raged upon those who remained, and those who left were saved. Those who went forth said: If we had stayed as these stayed, we would have perished as they perished! And those who remained said: If we had set out as these set out, we would have been saved as they were saved! They all left in one year, their rich and nobles, their poor and their lowly ones. Then He sent death upon them and they became shining bones. He said: The people of the villages came to them and gathered them in one place. Then a prophet passed by them and said: O Lord, if You wished, You could revive these people so that they could inhabit Your land and worship You! He said: Would you like me to do that? He said: Yes! He said: Then say: Such and such! So He spoke it, and he looked at the bones, and the bone would come out from the bone that it was not from to the bone that it was from. Then He spoke as He was commanded, and behold, the bones were covered with flesh. Then He commanded another command and spoke it, and behold, they were sitting, glorifying and magnifying God. Then it was said to them: Fight in the cause of God and know that God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Saeed bin Abi Ayoub told me, on the authority of Hammad bin Othman, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: He said about those whom God caused to die and then brought back to life: They are people who fled from the plague, so God caused them to die as a punishment and hatred, then brought them back to life for their appointed times.

x: The more correct of the two opinions in interpreting His statement:
h
and they are thousands

is the opinion of the one who said: He meant by thousands a large number, without the opinion of the one who said: He meant by it the unity, meaning the unity of their hearts, and that they left their homes without any separation or hatred between them, but fleeing: either from jihad or from the plague, because of the consensus of the proof that this is the interpretation of the verse, and the strange opinion does not contradict what was widely said by the Companions and the Followers. The first of the sayings - regarding the number of people whom God described as leaving their homes - is the correct one, the saying of those who limited their number to more than ten thousand, less than those who limited it to four thousand, three thousand, and eight thousand. This is because God Almighty mentioned that they were thousands, and those less than ten thousand are not called thousands.

Rather, it is said that they are thousands, if they are three thousand or more up to ten thousand. It is not permissible to say that they are five thousand, or ten thousand. Rather, the plural of its little is af’al, and it is not pluralized as af’al, like all the other little plurals that are second. Its singular is silent because of the alif at the beginning. The Arabs choose to pluralize its few letters as afā’al in every letter that begins with a ya’, waw, or alif, just as they pluralized al-waqt awqātān and al-yawm ayyāmān and al-yusr aysārā because of the waw and ya’ at the beginning of that.

i: Sometimes they may pluralize that as af’al, but the most eloquent of their speech is what we have mentioned, such as the saying of the poet:
x: They were three thousand and a battalion of two thousand non-Arabs from Banu al-Fidam.

As for his saying: fearing death, it means that they went out from fear of death, fleeing from it, as Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: fearing death, fleeing from their enemy, until they tasted the death from which they fled. So he commanded them to return, and he commanded them to fight in the way of God, and they are the ones who said to their prophet: Send us a king so that we may fight in the way of God (al-Baqarah 2:246).

God, the Most High, urged His servants with this verse to persevere in jihad in His way, and to be patient in fighting the enemies of His religion. And he encouraged them by informing them and reminding them that death and life are in His hands and to Him, not His creation, and that fleeing from fighting and escaping from jihad and meeting enemies, to fortify themselves in fortresses, and hiding in homes and houses, does not save anyone from His judgment if it befalls them, nor does it ward off the causes of His death if it befalls them, just as it did not benefit those fleeing from the plague, whose description was described by God Almighty in His saying:
h
Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes

, thousands in number, for fear of death? Their flight from their homelands, and their moving from their homes to the place to which they hoped to reach safety, and a refuge to escape death, until God’s command came to them and left them all lying dormant and dead, and on the earth perished, and those who were directly affected by the affliction of the epidemic and mixed with themselves the great affliction were saved from what befell them.

By this, the Most High means: God is full of grace and favor upon His creation, by showing them the path of guidance, warning them against the path of ruin, and other blessings that He bestows upon them in their worldly life and their religion, their souls and their wealth - just as He revived those who left their homes, and they were thousands, for fear of death after He had caused them to die, and He made them an example and a lesson for His creation, by which they may be admonished, and a lesson from which they may learn, and so that they may know that all matters are in His hand, so that they may submit to His judgment, and direct all desire and fear to Him.

c: Then the Most High informed us that
m: the effect of those of His servants upon whom He bestows His great blessings and bestows His immense favors is that they become ungrateful for Him and direct their desire and fear to someone other than Him, and take a god besides Him, out of ingratitude for His blessings, the smallest of which requires from him a gratitude that would be overwhelming and a praise that would burden him. So the Most High said: But most people are not grateful. He said: They are not grateful for My blessings that I bestowed upon them and My favor that I bestowed upon them, by their worshipping someone other than Me and directing their desire and fear to someone other than Me who has no power to harm or benefit them, and does not possess death or life or resurrection.

evidence.text: Then a prophet from among the prophets passed by them and called upon his Lord to revive them, so He revived them, and he recited this verse: Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, but most of mankind are not grateful.

x: God Almighty means by that: And fight, O believers, in the way of God, meaning: in His religion to which He has guided you, not in obedience to Satan, the enemies of your religion, who turn you away from the path of your Lord. And do not hide from fighting them when you meet them, and do not be cowardly in fighting them, for in My hand is your life and your death. And let none of you be prevented from meeting them and fighting them by fear of death and the fear of his own demise by fighting them, so that this prompts him to turn away from them 1 and flee from them, so that you are humiliated, and the death that you feared will come to you in your place of safety to which you have fled, just as it came to those who left their homes fleeing from death, whose story I have told you, but their flight from it did not save them from its descent upon them when My command came to them and My judgment befell them?

And there is no harm to those who are lightly guarded behind them, for their fates have defended them and diverted them from their sins. So fight in the way of God whomever I have commanded you to fight from among My enemies and the enemies of My religion. For whoever among you is saved, I will save him, and whoever among you is killed, his killing is by My decree. Then the Most High said to them: And know, O believers, that your Lord is Hearing of the words of those among your hypocrites who say to those among you who are killed in My way: If they had obeyed us and stayed in their homes, they would not have been killed. Knowing of what their hearts conceal of hypocrisy, disbelief, and lack of gratitude for My blessings upon them, and My favors with them in themselves and their families, and other matters of their affairs and the affairs of My servants. The Most High says to His believing servants: So thank Me, you, by obeying Me in what I have commanded you of fighting your enemy in My way, and other matters of My commands and prohibitions, for these have disbelieved in My blessings.

And know that God hears their words, and knows them and others, and what they are doing of faith and disbelief, obedience and disobedience, encompassing all of that, until He rewards each one according to his deeds, whether good or evil.
There is no basis for the statement of those who claim that His statement,
h
And fight in the cause of God
, is a command from God to those who left their homes in their thousands to fight, after He had revived them. Because His statement,
h
And fight in the cause of God

, if the matter is as they have interpreted it, is not without one of three matters: Either it is an apposition to His statement, Then God said to them, ‘Die,’ and that is impossible for Him to cause them to die and command them to fight in His cause while they are dead. Or it is an apposition to His statement,
h
Then He revived them
, and that is also meaningless. Because His statement,
h
And fight in the cause of God
, ... an order from God to fight, and His saying:
h
Then He revived them
, is report of a past action. It is not eloquent to link a future report to a past report, if they were both report, because their meanings would be different.
So how can the order be linked to a past report? Or its meaning could be:
h
Then He revived them

and said to them, Fight in the way of God, then He dropped the statement, as God Almighty said: And if you could but see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, [saying], ‘Our Lord, we have seen and heard.’ (al-Sajdah 32:12), meaning they say: Our Lord, we have seen and heard. This is also permissible in a place where the apparent meaning of the speech indicates a need for it, and the listener understands that it is intended for the speech even if it is not mentioned. As for places where there is no indication of a need for the speech, there is no basis for a claimant to claim that it is intended there.

God Almighty means by that: Who is this who spends in the way of God, helping the weak, or strengthening the needy who wants to fight in the way of God, and gives from them a poor person? That is the good loan that the servant lends to his Lord. God Almighty called it a loan because the meaning of a loan is that a man gives someone else his money as his property, so that he may repay it in kind if he requires it. So since the one who gives to the needy and poor in the way of God, he only gives them what he gives them from that seeking what God has promised him of a great reward with Him on the Day of Resurrection, He called it a loan, since the meaning of a loan in the language of the Arabs is what we have described. God Almighty made it a good because the giver gives that out of God's encouragement and urging him to do it, seeking reward from Him. So it is obedience to God, and disobedience to Satan.

i: This is not because God needs any of His creation, but rather it is like the Arabs saying: I have a loan of truth for you, and a loan of evil, for the matter in which you come to a man’s delight or his displeasure, as the poet said:
x: Every person will be repaid for his loan, good or bad, and he will be indebted to him who lent him.

A person’s loan: what he has done in advance of his good or bad deeds. This verse is similar to the verse in which God the Almighty said: “The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain [of corn] which grows seven ears, in each ear is a hundred grains. And God multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And God is All-Encompassing and Knowing.”
(al-Baqarah 2:261) In a similar vein to what we have said in this regard, Ibn Zayd said:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan
? He said: This is in the way of God, So He will multiply it for him many times over, he said: Seven hundred times for one.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, he said:
m: When the verse:
h
Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan

so He will multiply it for him many times over was revealed, Ibn al-Dahdah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, do I not see that our Lord is asking us for a loan? He only gave it to us for ourselves! I have two lands: one in the upper part and the other in the lower part, and I have given the better of them as charity! He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: How many bunches of dates are there for Ibn al-Dahdah in Paradise. Bishr ibn Mu’adh narrated that Yazid narrated that Sa’id narrated that Qatada said: When a man heard this verse during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said: I will lend to God. So he went to his best garden and gave it in charity. Qatada said: Your Lord asks you for a loan, as you hear, and He is the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy, and He asks His servants for loans. Muhammad ibn Mu’awiyah al-Anmati al-Naysaburi narrated that Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated that Hamid al-A’raj narrated that Abdullah ibn al-Harith narrated that Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: When the verse:
h
Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan

was revealed, Abu al-Dahdah said: O Messenger of God, does God want a loan from us? He said: Yes, O Abu al-Dahdah! He said: Your hand! He said: So he gave him his hand and said: I have loaned my Lord my garden, a garden with six hundred palm trees. Then he came walking until he came to the garden and Umm Ad-Dahdah was in it with her children, so he called her: O Umm Ad-Dahdah! She said: At your service! He said: Come out! I have loaned my Lord a garden with six hundred palm trees. As for his statement: Then He will multiply it for him many times over, then it is a promise from God, the Most High, to the lender and the spender of his money in the way of God, of multiplying the reward for his loan and his spending, without limit or end, as Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of As-Suddi: Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? He said: No one knows what this multiplication is.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of a friend of his
m: who mentioned on the authority of some scholars who said: God gave you the world as a loan, and you asked it as a loan. If you give it willingly, He will multiply it for you from one good deed to ten to seven hundred, or more than that. But if He takes it away from you unwillingly, and you are patient and do good, then prayer and mercy will be for you, and guidance will be obligatory for you.

x: The readings differed in the reading of His statement: He will multiply it with the alif and raising it, meaning: who lends God a goodly loan, so He multiplies it for him. He connected He will multiply it to His statement: he lends.
Others read it with that meaning: He will multiply it, except that they read it with a shaddah on the ʿayn and omitted the alif.

Others read it:فيزيدهه لهby proving the alif inيزيدand making it accusative, meaning a question. It is as if they interpreted the statement: Who is the lender to God a good loan so He may multiply it for him? So they made his statement:فيزيدههthe answer to the question, and they made: Who is it that will lend God a good loan a noun. Becauseالذis its conjunction, like Amr and Zaid. It is as if they directed the interpretation of the statement to the saying of the speaker: Who is your brother so you may honor him? Because the most eloquent in answering the question with the fa, if there is nothing before it to connect it with from a future verb, is to make it accusative.
The most correct of these readings in our view is the reading of the one who read:فيزيدهه لهby proving the alif. And he raisedيزيد. Because in his statement:
h
Who is it that will lend God a good loan there is a meaning of recompense

. And if the fa enters into its answer, its answer with the fa can only be nominative. Therefore, the nominative case in yudhifa’uhu is more correct in our view than the accusative case. We chose the alif in yadhifadh rather than deleting it and emphasizing the ‘ayn, because that is the more eloquent of the two languages and the most common on the tongues of Arabs.

By that, the Most High means that He is the One in whose hand is the sustenance of the servants and their expansion, and not others whom the polytheists claimed to be gods, and took as lords besides Him whom they worship.
This is similar to the report narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, they said: Hajjaj narrated to us, and ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muhammad al-Raqashi narrated to me, he said: Hajjaj and Abu Rabia narrated to us, they said: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Thabit,
m: Hamid and Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, he said: “Prices rose during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: O Messenger of God, prices have risen, so set prices for us! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is the Expander, the Constrictor, the Provider, and I hope that I will meet God with no one seeking injustice against me in my life or wealth.”

x: By that, may God bless him and grant him peace, he meant that high prices, cheap prices, abundance and scarcity are in the hand of God, and no one else. Likewise, the Almighty’s statement: And God withholds and expands, meaning by His statement: withholds, He is referring to His withholding of sustenance from whomever He wills of His creation, and by His statement: and expands, He means by His expansion of sustenance to whomever He wills of them. Rather, by saying that, the Most High intended to urge His believing servants - upon whom He has bestowed His bounty and made His provision abundant - to strengthen those among them who are poor with His money, and to assist them by spending on them and helping them to rise up to fight His enemy among the polytheists in His cause. So the Most High said: Who will provide for himself a reserve with Me by giving to the weak believers and those in need among them what will help them to fight in My cause, so that I may multiply for him from My reward many times what I have given him and strengthened him with?

Indeed, I, O Generous One, am the One who withheld provision from the one I summoned you to help and give, to test him with patience in what I have afflicted him with, and I have expanded upon you to test you with your work in what I have expanded upon you, so I will see how you obey Me in it, so I will reward each one of you according to the extent of your obedience in what I have afflicted you with and tested you with, of wealth and poverty, spaciousness and narrowness, when you return to Me in your afterlife, and your destination to Me in your return. And similar to what we have said in that, those who have reached us from the people of interpretation said.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: in His statement:
h
Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan

? the verse, he said: He knew that among those who fight in His cause there are those who do not find strength, and among those who do not fight in His cause there are those who find wealth, so He summoned these people and said:
h
Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan

so He may multiply it for him many times over? And God withholds and expands. He said: He made it easy for you while you were too heavy to go out and did not want to, and he withheld this while he was happy to go out and it was reserved for him, so strengthen him with what is in your hand, and you will have a share in that.

x: By that, the Most High means: And to God is your return, O people. So fear God in yourselves, lest you neglect His obligations and transgress His limits, and lest those among you who have been given abundant provision work in a way other than what their Lord has permitted them to work in, and lest the poor among you - when their provision is withheld from them - bear their poverty in disobeying Him and doing what He has forbidden, and thus deserve, upon their return to their Creator, a painful punishment that they cannot bear. Qatada interpreted his statement:
h
And to Him you will be returned
, as meaning that you will be returned to the dust.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And to Him you will be returned
, from the dust He created them, and to the dust they will return.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: The readings differed in the reading of His statement: He will multiply it with the alif and raising it, meaning: who lends God a goodly loan, so He multiplies it for him.
Others read it with that meaning: He will multiply it, except that they read it with a shaddah on the ʿayn and omitted the alif.
Others read it:فيزيدهه لهby proving the alif inيزيدand making it accusative, meaning a question.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of these readings in our view is the reading of the one who read:فيزيدهه لهby proving the alif.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
Have you not seen
, O Muhammad,
h
have you not seen

in your heart, so that you know by My report to you, O Muhammad, to the assembly, meaning: to the leaders of the Children of Israel, their nobles and their chiefs, after Moses, meaning: after Moses had been taken and died,
h
when they said to a prophet of theirs

, ‘Send us a king, and we will fight in the way of God,’ so it was mentioned to me that the prophet who said that to them was Samuel, son of Bali, son of Alqamah, son of Jerham, son of Elihu, son of Tehuban Zuph, son of Alqamah, son of Mahath, son of Amosah, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah, son of Alqamah, son of Abi Yasif, son of Korah, son of Izhar, son of Qahath, son of Levi, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham. Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated that Ibn Ishaq narrated that Wahb ibn Munabbih narrated that Al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim narrated that Ishaq narrated that Ismail ibn Abd Al-Karim narrated that Abd Al-Samad ibn Muqal narrated that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: He is Shmuel, he is Shmuel - and he did not give his lineage as Ibn Ishaq did.

Al-Suddi said: Rather his name is Shimon. He said: He was named Shimon because his mother prayed to God to grant her a boy, and God answered her prayer and granted her a boy, and she gave birth to a boy and named him Shimon, saying: God heard my prayer. Musa narrated that Amr narrated that Asbat narrated that Al-Suddi said: So Shimon is a verb in the view of Al-Suddi, from her saying: God heard her prayer.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his saying:
h
Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after Moses
h
when they said to a prophet of theirs
? He said: Samuel.

x: Others said: Rather, the one whom his people from the Children of Israel asked to send them a king to fight in the way of God was Joshua bin Nun bin Ephraim bin Joseph bin Jacob bin Isaac bin Abraham.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me that, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their prophet said to them
, he said: Their prophet after Moses was Joshua bin Nun. He said: He is one of the two men upon whom God bestowed His blessings. As for his statement:
h
Send us a king so that we may fight in the way of God
, the people of interpretation differed regarding the reason for which the leaders of the Children of Israel asked their prophet for that.

x: Some of them said: The reason for their asking him was what:

c: Muhammad bin Hamid told us, he said: Salamah bin al-Fadl told us, he said: Muhammad bin Ishaq told me, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, he said:
m: After Moses, Joshua bin Nun was left among the Children of Israel, to establish the Torah and the command of God among them until God took him. Then he left Caleb son of Youfna among them to establish the Torah and the command of God until God took him. Then he left Ezekiel son of Buzi, the son of the old woman, among them. Then God took Ezekiel, and the events among the Children of Israel became great, and they forgot what God had promised them, until they set up idols and worshipped them instead of God. Then God sent to them Elijah son of Nassi son of Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron son of Imran as a prophet. And the prophets from the Children of Israel after Moses were sent to them to renew what they had forgotten of the Torah. Elijah was with one of the kings of the Children of Israel called Ahab, and he listened to him and believed him. So Elijah used to establish his command for him. The rest of the Children of Israel had taken an idol to worship instead of God, so Elijah began to call them to God, but they did not listen to anything from him except what was from that king. And the kings were scattered in the Levant, each king having a part of it that he consumed. Then that king - who was with Elijah, who was in charge of his affairs and saw him on the right path among his companions - said one day: O Elijah, by God, I do not see what you are calling people to except falsehood! By God, I do not see so-and-so and so-and-so - and he listed the kings of the Children of Israel - worshipping idols instead of God, except as we are, eating, drinking and enjoying ourselves as kings, and their affair that you claim is false does not diminish their worldly life, and we do not see us as having any advantage over them. They claim - and God knows best - that Elijah regained Surat al-Baqarah 2:246 Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses,
h
when they said to a prophet of theirs
, “Send us a king, and we will fight in the cause of God.” He said, “Would you perhaps, if fighting is decreed upon you, not fight?” They said, “
h
And why should we not fight in the cause of God

while we have been expelled from our homes and our children?” But when fighting was decreed upon them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And God is Knowing and Wise. Knowing of the wrongdoers. his senses and made his hair and skin stand up, then he rejected it and left it. So the king did that as his companions did, he worshipped idols and did what they did. Then after him, Elisha was succeeded among them, and he was among them as God willed him to be, then God took him to Himself. And successors were left among them, and sins became great among them, and with them was the Ark, which they inherited from their ancestors, in which was the Shekinah and the remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind. And no enemy would meet them, and they would bring the Ark forward and march with them, except that God would defeat that enemy. Then He left among them a king called Ila', and God had blessed them in their mountain of Elijah, so that no enemy would enter upon them, and they would not need anyone else with him. And one of them - as they say - would gather dirt on a rock, then he would throw grain into it, and God would bring forth for him what he and his family would eat for a year. And one of them would have an olive tree, and he would squeeze from it what he and his family would eat for a year. When their events became great, and they abandoned God's covenant with them, an enemy came down upon them, so they went out to him, and brought out the Ark with them as they used to bring it out, then they marched with it, and they fought until it was taken from their hands. Then their king Ila' came and was informed that the Ark had been taken and stolen, so his neck bent, and he died of grief over it. So their situation was disturbed for them, and their enemy trampled them, until some of their children and women were killed. And among them was a prophet whom God had sent to them, but they would not accept anything from him. He was called Samuel, and he is the one whom God mentioned to His Prophet Muhammad:
h
Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after Moses
h
when they said to a prophet of theirs
, ‘Send us a king, and we will fight in the way of God,’ to His saying,
h
And we have been expelled from our homes and our children
, God says:
h
But when fighting was prescribed for them

, they turned back, except for a few of them, to His saying, Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers. Ibn Ishaq said: Among their stories, as some of the people of knowledge told me, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, was that when calamity befell them and their land was trampled upon, they spoke to their prophet Samuel ibn Bali and said, Send us a king, and we will fight in the way of God. The basis of the Children of Israel was to unite under kings, and the kings obeyed their prophets. The king would lead the crowds, and the prophet would take care of his affairs and bring him report from his Lord. If they did that, their situation would be good, but if their kings became arrogant and abandoned the matter of their prophets, their situation would be corrupted. So the kings suffered when the group followed them in misguidance and abandoned the matter of the messengers.

x: A group would lie and not accept anything from them, and a group would kill. This affliction continued with them until they said to him:
h
Send us a king so that we may fight in the way of God

. He said to them: There is no loyalty, no truthfulness, and no desire for jihad among you. They said: We only feared Jihad and were reluctant to do so because we were forbidden in our lands, and no one could tread upon them, and no enemy could prevail over us. But when that comes to pass, then Jihad is inevitable, so we obey our Lord in fighting our enemy, and we protect our sons, women, and children.

c: I was told by Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding His statement:
h
Have you not seen the assembly of the Children of Israel

? to And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers, al-Rabiʿ said: It was mentioned to us - and God knows best - that when death approached Moses, he appointed his young man Joshua ibn Nut as his successor over the Children of Israel, and that Joshua ibn Nun led them according to the Book of God, the Torah, and the Sunnah of His Prophet Moses. Then Joshua ibn Nun died, and another appointed him as his successor, who led them according to the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then another appointed him as his successor, who led them according to the conduct of his two companions. Then another appointed him as his successor, and they recognized him and disapproved. Then another appointed him as his successor, and they disapproved of most of his command. Then another was appointed as his successor, but they denied his entire command. Then the Children of Israel came to one of their prophets when they were harmed in their lives and their wealth, and they said to him: Ask your Lord to decree fighting for us! And that prophet said to them: Would you perhaps, if fighting were prescribed for you, not fight? until His saying: And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after Moses
h
when they said to a prophet of theirs

, ‘Send us a king,’ he said, Ibn Abbas said: This was when the Torah was lifted and the people of faith were extracted, and the tyrants had expelled them from their homes and their children. I narrated to them on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, he said, I heard Abu Muadh, he said, Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
When they said to a prophet of theirs
, ‘Send us a king,’ he said: This was when the Torah was lifted and the people of faith were extracted.

x: Others said: The reason for their asking their prophet was what: - Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, he said, Amr narrated to us, he said, Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: “
h
Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after Moses
h
when they said to a prophet of theirs

, ‘Send us a king, so that we may fight in the cause of God? God said: The Children of Israel were fighting the Amalekites, and the king of the Amalekites was Goliath, and they prevailed over the Children of Israel, imposed a tribute on them and took their Torah. The Children of Israel were asking God to send them a prophet with whom they could fight. The tribe of prophethood had perished, and none remained of them except a pregnant woman. They took her and locked her in a house, fearing that she would give birth to a slave girl and replace her with a boy, because of what she saw of the desire of the Children of Israel for her child.

So the woman began to pray to God to grant her a boy, and she gave birth to a boy whom she named Simeon. The boy grew up, so she sent him to learn the Torah in Jerusalem, and an elder among their scholars took care of him and adopted him. When the boy reached the age of God sending him as a prophet, Gabriel came to him while the boy was sleeping next to the elder, and he did not wish anyone 1 for him except him, so he called him in the old man’s tone: O Shmaul! So the boy got up in a panic to the old man, and said: O my father, did you call me? The old man thought about saying: No, lest the boy be frightened, so he said: My son, go back and sleep! So he went back and slept. Then he called him a second time, and the boy came to him again and said: Did you call me? He said: Go back and sleep, if I call you a third time, do not answer me! When it was the third time, Gabriel appeared to him and said: Go to your people and convey to them the message of your Lord, for God has sent you among them as a prophet.
When he came to them, they denied him and said: You hastened the prophethood and it did not come to you! They said: If you are truthful, then
h
send us a king so that we may fight in the way of God
, a sign of your prophethood! So Shimon said to them: Perhaps if fighting is decreed upon you, you will not fight.

It is not permissible in the statement of God, the Most High: “We fight in the way of God” if it is read with the letter nun other than in the subjunctive mood, in the sense of recompense and condition of the command. If someone thinks that the nominative case is permissible and it was read with the letter nun meaning: that with which we fight in the way of God, then that is not permissible. Because the Arabs do not conceal two letters. But if it had been read with the letter ya, it would have been permissible to raise it, because if it had been read like that, it would be a connection to the king, so the interpretation of the statement then would be: Send us someone who will fight in the way of God, as God the Almighty said: And send among them a Messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses, (al-Baqarah 2:129), because His saying: recites is a connection to the Messenger.

God the Almighty meant by that: The Prophet whom they asked to send them a king to fight in the way of God said: Would you consider that if it is written, meaning if fighting is imposed upon you, that you will not fight, meaning that you will not fulfill what you promise God from yourselves, of jihad in His way, for you are people of breaking and treachery and lack of loyalty to what you promise? They said, ‘
h
Why should we not fight

in the cause of God?’ That is, the leaders of the Children of Israel said to their prophet: And what prevents us from fighting in the cause of God, our enemy and the enemy of God, ‘while we have been driven out from our homes and our children,’ by force and oppression?
What is the reason for the inclusion of an in His statement:
h
And why should we not fight in the cause of God
? and its deletion from His statement: And why do you not believe in God while the Messenger invites you? (al-Hadid 57:8)?

They are two eloquent dialects of the Arabs: An is deleted once with the word Malik, so you say: Malik la do’l khadh, meaning: Malik is not doing it, as the poet said: You are the one who wants to go and you are the one who doesn't want to go after him This is the speech for which the speaker does not need to provide evidence for its correctness, since it is widespread on the tongues of the Arabs. It is proven that there is another in it, directing her saying: Malik to its meaning, since its meaning was: What prevented you?

As God Almighty said: What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you? (al-A’raf 7:12), then He said in another surah in its counterpart: What is the matter with you that you are not with those who prostrate?

i: (al-Hijr 15:32), so He placed ma prevented you in place of malik and malik in place of ma prevented you, because their meanings are the same, even if their words differ, as the Arabs do in their counterparts, whose meanings agree but whose words differ, as the poet said:
x: He says, if you tell her and she recites: Is there not a brother who is always delicious?

So he entered in the permanent Baa with Hal, which is an interrogative. And it is only entered in the report of Ma which has the meaning of negation, because the meaning of interrogation and negation are close. And some of the Arabists used to say: I entered An, in that you do not fight, because it means the speaker saying: What is wrong with you not fighting? If that were permissible, it would have been permissible to say: What is wrong with you! Tell us that you stood up, and what is wrong with you that you are standing, and that is not permissible. Because prevention only applies to the future of actions, as it is said: I prevented you from standing up, and it is not said: I prevented you that you stood up. Therefore, it was said in Malik: What is wrong with you that you do not stand up, and it was not said: What is wrong with you that you stood up. And others of them said: An here is redundant after Ma la, as it is added to Lama and Law, and it is added in this meaning a lot.

i: He said:
x: And its meaning is: And what is wrong with us that we do not fight in the way of God? So he made An work, and it is redundant. And Al-Farazdaq said:
h
If Ghatafan had no sins
, then their nobles would have been killed for a long time.
Meaning:
h
If Ghatafan had no sins
or excess, then I would have done it.

Others denied what this speaker said, which we have narrated from him. They said: It is not permissible to make an redundant in speech, while it is correct in Surat al-Baqarah 2:246 Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses,
h
when they said to a prophet of theirs
, “Send us a king, and we will fight in the cause of God.” He said, “Would you perhaps, if fighting is decreed upon you, not fight?” They said, “
h
And why should we not fight in the cause of God

while we have been expelled from our homes and our children?” But when fighting was decreed upon them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And God is Knowing and Wise. Knowing of the wrongdoers. meaning and the speech needs it. They said: The meaning is: What prevents us from fighting? So there is no basis for the claim of the one who claims that an is redundant, the meaning is understood correctly. They said: As for his saying:
h
If Ghatafan had no sins
The word la is not redundant in this case, because it is a denial, and when denial is denied, it becomes an affirmation.
They said: So his saying,
h
If Ghatafan had no sins
, is an affirmation of their sins, just as one says, Your brother does not stand, meaning, He stands.
Others said: The meaning of his saying,
h
Why should we not fight
? is:
h
Why should we not fight

? Then the waw was deleted and left, just as one says in speech, Why do you want to go to so-and-so? So the waw was dropped from it, because an is a non-established letter in nouns. They said: We allow it to be said, Why do you want to stand? but we do not allow, Why do you want to stand? because standing is a sound noun and Why do you want to stand? They said: The Arabs may say: Beware of speaking, meaning: Beware of speaking.

Others denied this from their saying and said: If it were permissible to say that according to the interpretation interpreted by the speaker whose statement we have mentioned, then it would have to be permissible to say: I hit you with the slave girl and you are responsible, meaning: And you are responsible for the slave girl, and to say: I saw you, I mean, meaning: I saw you and I mean. Because the Arabs say: Beware of speaking falsely. They said: If the waw was implied in an, then all of what we mentioned would have been permissible, but that is not permissible, because what comes after the waw of the verbs is not permissible for it to fall on what comes before it.

i: They cited as evidence for the corruption of the statement of the one who claimed that the waw is implied with an the saying of the poet:
x: So reveal your secrets to those who deserve them, and beware of revealing them to anyone else.
And that if it had an implied waw, it would not be permissible to place fi ghayrhum before it. As for the interpretation of his statement:
h
And we were expelled from our homes and our children

, it means: And those of our men and women who were defeated were expelled from their homes and their children, and from captivity. This statement appears to be general but its inner meaning is specific, because those who said to their prophet:
h
Send us a king so that we may fight in the way of God
, were in their homes and countries, and he was only expelled from his home and his children from those who were taken captive and subjugated. As for his statement:
h
But when fighting was prescribed for them

, they turned away, except for a few of them, he says: So when fighting their enemy and jihad in His cause was imposed upon them, they turned away, except for a few of them, he says: They turned away, turning away from fighting, and they neglected what they asked their prophet of the obligation of jihad.

And the few whom God exempted from them are those who crossed the river with Talut. We will mention the reason for the turning away of those who turned away. Among them, and the crossing of those who crossed the river after God willing, when we come to it. God Almighty says: And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers, meaning: God is All-Knowing of those among them who wronged themselves, so God broke His promise to them, and disobeyed the command of his Lord in what he initially asked Him to impose upon him. This is from God Almighty as a rebuke to the Jews who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their denial of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their disobedience of the command of their Lord. God Almighty says to them: You, O group of Jews, disobeyed God and disobeyed His command in what you asked Him to impose upon you initially, without your Lord initiating the imposition of what you disobeyed Him in, so you are more deserving of His disobedience - in what He initiated for you of imposing His obligation.
And in this speech there is something omitted, and mentioning what was mentioned suffices from what was omitted from it. The meaning of the statement is: They said:
h
Why should we not fight

in the cause of God when we have been expelled from our homes and our children? So their prophet asked their Lord to send them a king to fight with him in the cause of God, so He sent them a king, and he prescribed fighting for them, “
h
But when fighting was prescribed for them
, they turned away, except for a few of them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers.”

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: It is not permissible in the statement of God, the Most High: “We fight in the way of God” if it is read with the letter nun other than in the subjunctive mood, in the sense of recompense and condition of the command.
If someone thinks that the nominative case is permissible and it was read with the letter nun meaning: that with which we fight in the way of God, then that is not permissible.

But if it had been read with the letter ya, it would have been permissible to raise it, because if it had been read like that, it would be a connection to the king, so the interpretation of the statement then would be: Send us someone who will fight in the way of God, as God the Almighty said: And send among them a Messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses, (al-Baqarah 2:129), because His saying: recites is a connection to the Messenger.

x: God Almighty meant by that: And their prophet Samuel said to the leaders of the Children of Israel: God has given you what you asked for, and has sent you Saul as a king. When their prophet Samuel said that to them, they said: How can Saul have kingship over us, when he is from the tribe of Benjamin, son of Jacob? And the tribe of Benjamin is a tribe in which there is no kingship or prophethood, and we are more deserving of kingship than he, because we are from the tribe of Judah, son of Jacob. And he was not given ample wealth means: Saul was not given a lot of wealth, because he was a water-carrier. It was said: He was a tanner. And the reason for God giving Saul kingship over the Children of Israel, and their saying what they said to their prophet Samuel, was:
h
How can he have kingship over us
, when we are more deserving of kingship than he, and he was not given ample wealth?

What: - Ibn Hamid narrated to us, he said, Salamah bin Al-Fadl narrated to us, he said, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated to me, he said, some of the people of knowledge narrated to me, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, he said: When the leaders of the Children of Israel said to Samuel bin Bali what they said to him, God asked their prophet Samuel to send them a king, so God said to him: Look at the horn in which there is oil in your house, and if a man enters upon you and the oil in the horn is dripping, he is the king of the Children of Israel, so anoint his head with it and make him king over them, and tell him what had come to him - so he waited for that man to enter upon him. And Talut was a tanner who made leather, and he was from the tribe of Benjamin, son of Jacob. And the tribe of Benjamin was a tribe among which there was no prophethood or kingship. So Talut went out in search of his mount that had lost him, and with him was his slave.

They passed by the house of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and Talut’s slave said to Talut: Why don’t you take us to this prophet and ask him about the matter of our mount, so he can guide us and pray for our well-being! Talut said: There is no harm in what you said! So they entered upon him, and while they were with him, mentioning to him the matter of their beast and asking him to pray for them regarding it, the oil in the horn seeped out. The Prophet, peace be upon him, went to him and took it, then said to Talut: Bring your head near! So he brought it near, and anointed it with it, then said: You are the king of the Children of Israel whom God has commanded me to make you king over them! - and Talut's name in Syriac was: Saul bin Qais bin Abial bin Dhirar bin Yaharb bin Afih bin Ais bin Benjamin bin Jacob bin Isaac bin Abraham - so he sat with him, and the people said: Talut is king!!

So the leaders of Israel came to their prophet and said to him: What is the matter with Talut ruling over us, while there is no kingdom in the house of prophethood? You know that prophethood and kingship are in the house of Levi and the house of Judah! He said to them: God chose him over you and increased him abundantly in knowledge and body.

c: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said, Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Samad bin Maqal, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, he said:
m: The Children of Israel said to Samuel:
h
Send us a king

so that we may fight in the way of God! He said: God has spared you from fighting! They said: We fear those around us, so we will have a king to whom we may turn! So God revealed to Samuel: Send them Talut as a king, and anoint him with holy oil. Talut's father had some extra donkeys, so he sent him and a servant of his to seek them. They came to Samuel to ask him about them, and he said: God has sent you as a king over the Children of Israel. He said: Me? He said: Yes. He said: Didn't you know that my tribe is the lowest of the tribes of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes. He said: Didn't you know that my tribe is the lowest of the tribes of my tribe? He said: Yes. He said: Didn't you know that my house is the lowest of the houses of my tribe? He said: Yes! He said: What is the sign? He said: What is the sign that you will return and your father has found a donkey, and when you are in such and such a place, the revelation will come down to you! So he anointed him with holy oil. Then he said to the Children of Israel: God has sent to you Saul as a king. They said:
h
How can he have kingship over us
when we are more deserving of kingship than he, and he has not been given an abundance of wealth? He said: God has chosen him over you and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, Amr bin Hammad told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: When the Children of Israel denied Simeon, they said to him: If you are truthful, then
h
send us a king

so that we may fight in the way of God as a sign of your prophethood. Simeon said to them: Perhaps if fighting is prescribed for you, will you not fight? They said: And why should we not fight in the way of God? The verse. He called upon Surat Al-Baqarah 2:247
h
And their prophet said to them

, "Indeed, God has sent to you Saul as a king." They said, "How can he have the kingdom over us while we are more deserving of the kingdom than he is, and he has not been given ample wealth?" He said, "Indeed, God has chosen him over you and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature. And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills,
h
and God is all-Encompassing

." All-Knowing God, and a stick was brought to him that was the size of the man who would be sent among them as a king. He said: Your companion will be as tall as this stick. So they measured themselves against it, but they were not like it. Talut was a water carrier who used to water his donkey. His donkey had fallen short, so he set off looking for it on the road. When they saw him, they called him and compared him to it, and he was the same. Then their prophet said to them: God has sent you Talut as a king. The people said: I have never been more of a liar than you are now! We are from the tribe of the kingdom, but he is not from the tribe of the kingdom, and he was not given ample wealth for us to follow him for that reason! The prophet said: God has chosen him over you and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: Talut was a water carrier who sold water.

c: Bishr ibn Muadh narrated to us,
m: who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: God sent Talut as a king, and he was from the tribe of Benjamin, a tribe that had neither a kingdom nor a prophethood. There were two tribes among the Children of Israel: a tribe of prophethood and a tribe of kingdom. The tribe of prophecy was the tribe of Levi, to whom Moses belonged, and the tribe of the kingdom was Judah, to whom David and Solomon belonged. When he was sent from a tribe other than the tribe of prophecy and kingdom, they denied it and were amazed at it and said: How can he have the kingdom over us when we are more deserving of the kingdom than he? They said: How can he have the kingdom over us when he is not from the tribe of prophecy or the tribe of kingdom? Then God the Most High said: God has chosen him over you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Send us a king
, their prophet said to them:
h
God has sent you Saul as a king

. They said: How can he have the kingdom over us? He said: He was from a tribe that had neither kingship nor prophecy, so he said: God has chosen him over you and increased him abundantly in knowledge and body.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And their prophet said to them
, ‘Indeed,
h
God has sent you Saul as a king
,’ and there were two tribes among the Children of Israel: a tribe of prophethood and a tribe of caliphate. Therefore, they said,
h
How can he have kingship over us
? They said, And
h
how can he have kingship over us
, when he is not from the tribe of prophethood or the tribe of caliphate? He said, God chose him over you
h
and increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature

c: I was told on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: he said, I heard Abu Mu’adh, he said, Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim say regarding His statement,
h
How can he have kingship over us
? and he mentioned something similar. Narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hasan, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, he said:
m: When the Children of Israel said to their prophet: Ask your Lord to prescribe fighting for us! That prophet said to them: Would you perhaps if fighting were prescribed for you? The verse, he said: So God sent Talut as a king. He said: There were two tribes among the Children of Israel: the tribe of prophethood and the tribe of kingdom, and Talut was neither from the tribe of prophethood nor from the tribe of kingdom. So when He sent them a king, they denied that and were amazed and said:
h
How can he have kingship over us
when we are more deserving of kingship than him and he has not been given an abundance of wealth? They said:
h
How can he have kingship over us
when he is not from the tribe of prophethood nor from the tribe of kingdom? He said: God has chosen him over you. The tool.

c: Muhammad bin Saad narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Didn’t they mention Talut when they said:
h
How can he have kingship over us

when we are more deserving of kingship than him and he has not been given an abundance of wealth? They did not say that except that there were two tribes among the Children of Israel: in one of them was the prophethood, and in the other was the kingship, so no one would be sent except one who was from the tribe of prophethood, and no one would rule on the earth except one who was from the tribe of kingship. And that He sent Saul when He sent him, and he was not from one of the two tribes, and He chose him over them, and He increased his knowledge and body. And for that reason they said:
h
How can he have kingship over us
when we are more deserving of kingship than him, and he was not from one of the two tribes? He said: So God chose him over you to: And God is Hearing and Knowing.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: Ibn Abbas said, His statement: Have you not seen the assembly of the Children of Israel after Moses the verse, this was when the Torah was lifted and the people of faith were extracted, and the tyrants had expelled them from their homes and their children, and when fighting was prescribed for them, and that was when the Ark came to them. He said: There were two tribes among the Children of Israel: a tribe of prophethood and a tribe of caliphate. The caliphate could not be except in the tribe of caliphate, and prophethood could not be except in the tribe of prophethood. So their prophet said to them:
h
God has sent you Saul as a king
. They said:
h
How can he have kingship over us

when we are more deserving of kingship than he? And he was not from either of the two tribes: neither the tribe of prophethood nor the tribe of caliphate? “He said: God has chosen him over you,” the verse. It has been said: The meaning of kingship in this place is: the command over the army.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Mujahid said
m: regarding his statement:
h
God has sent you Saul as a king
, he said: He was the commander of the army.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: He was a commander over the army.

x: We have already explained the meaning of how and the meaning of kingship previously, so there is no need to repeat it here.

God Almighty means by His statement: Indeed, God has chosen him over you, their prophet Samuel said to them: Indeed, God has chosen him over you, meaning: He chose him over you, as Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas: Indeed, God has chosen him over you, he said: He chose him over you.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Indeed, God has chosen him over you, he said: He chose him over you.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: God chose him over you, he chose him. As for his saying:
h
And increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature

, he means by that that God expanded his knowledge and stature for him, and gave him knowledge in excess of what He gave to others who were addressed with this speech. And that is because he mentioned that a revelation came to him from God, and as for the body, he was given an increase in his height over them that no one else was given, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Muqal told me, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, he said:
m: When the Children of Israel said: How can he have the kingdom over us when we are more deserving of the kingdom than him and he has not been given an abundance of wealth? He said: God has chosen him over you and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and body. He said: The Children of Israel gathered and Talut was above them from his shoulders and upwards. Al-Suddi said: “A stick was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that would be the same height as the man who would be sent among them as a king, and he said: Your companion’s height will be the same as this stick. So they measured themselves with it, but they were not like it. So they measured Talut with it and he was like it.”
Musa told me that, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi.

i: Others said:
x: Rather, the meaning of that is: God chose him over you and increased him along with choosing him with abundance in knowledge and body.
He means by that: He expanded for him along with that in knowledge and body.
He who said that mentioned:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: God chose him over you and increased him abundantly in knowledge and body, after this.

x: God Almighty meant by that: The kingdom belongs to God and is in His hand, without anyone else. He gives it, he says: He gives it to whomever He wills, so He places it with him and makes it special for him, and withholds it from whomever He loves from among His creation. He says: Do not be surprised, O assembly of the leaders of the Children of Israel, that God would send Saul as a king over you, even if he was not from the people of the royal house, for the kingdom is not an inheritance from fathers and ancestors, but it is in the hand of God, and He gives it to whomever He wills from among His creation, so do not choose from God. And a group of the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me, he said, some of the people of knowledge told me, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih:
m: And God gives His kingdom to whomever He wills, the kingdom is in the hand of God, He places it where He wills, you do not have the right to choose in it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: His kingdom is his authority.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills, His authority. As for His statement,
h
And God is all-Encompassing
, All-Knowing, he means by that:
h
And God is all-Encompassing

in His grace, so He bestows it upon whomever He loves, and He increases it for whomever He wills, All-Knowing of who is worthy of the kingdom that He gives him, and the grace that He bestows, so He gives it to him because of His knowledge of him, and because what He gives him is worthy: either for the sake of reform through it, or so that he himself may benefit from it.

x: This report from God Almighty about His Prophet who informed about it, is evidence that the leaders of the Children of Israel who were told this statement, did not acknowledge God's sending of Talut as a king over them when their Prophet informed them of that and made them aware of his virtue with which God favored him, but they asked him for evidence of the truth of what he told them about that and informed them of it. So the interpretation of the statement, since the matter was as we described: And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing, so they said to him: What is the sign of that if you are of the truthful? "Their Prophet said to them:
h
The sign of his kingship

is that the Ark will come to you." This story, even though it was report from God Almighty about the leaders of the Children of Israel and their Prophet, and what they had begun with their Prophet asking him to ask God to send them a king to fight with them in His cause, and report of what they had done in denying their Prophet after knowing his prophethood, then breaking the promise they had made to God and His Messenger, of jihad in the cause of God, by easing it when they were called upon to fight those they had called upon to fight, and God granted victory to a few of the group, while many of them were discouraged from their kingship and sitting back from jihad with him, then it is a lesson for those who were among the immigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from their descendants and sons, the Jews of Qurayza and Nadir, and that they would not go beyond their denial of him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he had commanded them and forbidden them, despite their knowledge of his truthfulness and their knowledge of the reality of his prophethood, after they had been seeking God’s help through him against their enemies before his message, and before God sent him to them and to others.

That they would be like their ancestors and their forefathers who denied their prophet Samuel bin Bali, despite their knowledge of his truthfulness, and their awareness of the truth of his prophethood, and their refusal to fight with Talut when God sent him as a king over them, after they asked their prophet to send a king with whom they could fight their enemy and fight with him in the way of their Lord, starting with their prophet, and after their prophet Samuel consulted them about that, and urged the people of faith in God and His Messenger from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight in His way, and warned them from staying behind their prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he met the enemy, and opposing the people of disbelief in God and in Him, like what the leaders of the Children of Israel were like in staying behind their king Talut when he marched to fight the enemy of God, Goliath, and their preference for ease and humility over directly engaging in the heat of jihad and fighting in the way of God, and he urged them to advance to confront the people of disbelief in Him in war, and to abandon the fear of fighting them when their number was small and the number of their enemies was large and intense.

Their strength is in His saying: Those who think that they will meet God say, ‘How often has a small company overcome a large one by God’s permission? And God is with the patient.’ (al-Baqarah 2:249), and His, the Most High, informing His believing servants that in His hand is victory and triumph, good and evil. As for the interpretation of His saying:
h
Their prophet said to them
, it means: to the leaders of the Children of Israel who said to their prophet: Send us a king so that we may fight in the way of God. And His saying:
h
The sign of his kingship

, the sign of the kingship of Talut - which you asked me about - is evidence of my truthfulness in Say: God sent him over you as a king, even though he was not from the tribe of the kingdom - that the Ark might come to you, in which there is tranquility from your Lord.
