This is the Ark that the Children of Israel, when they encountered an enemy, would bring before them and march with, so that no enemy would stand up to them, and no one who opposed them would prevail over them, until they neglected God’s command and their disagreement with their prophets increased, so God took it from them time after time, returning it to them in each case, until He took it from them the last time and did not return it to them, and He will not return it to them for the rest of eternity.
Then the people of interpretation differed about the reason for the coming of the Ark, which God made its coming to the Children of Israel a sign of the truth of their prophet Samuel in his saying:
h
God has sent you Saul as a king
. And had the Children of Israel robbed it Surat Al-Baqarah 2:248 And
h
their prophet said to them
, "Indeed,
h
the sign of his kingship
is that there will come to you the Ark, in which is tranquility from your Lord
h
and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind

, carried by the angels. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers." before that, so God returned it to them when He made its coming a sign of Saul’s kingship, or had they not robbed it before that, but God initiated it with them in the beginning?

Some of them said: Rather, it was with them from the time of Moses and Aaron, inheriting it, until kings from The people who disbelieved in him, then God returned him to them as a sign for the kingdom of Talut. And he said about the reason for his return to them what I will mention, which is: - Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: Eli, who raised Samuel, had two young sons who introduced something into the offering that was not in it. The whip of the offering that they used to whip it with was two hooks, so what they took out was for the priest who whipped it, so his sons made it into hooks. And when the women came to pray in the sanctuary, they would cling to them. While Samuel was sleeping in front of the house in which Eli was sleeping, he heard a voice saying: Samuel!!

So he jumped up to Eli and said: At your service! What is the matter with you! You called me? He said: No! Go back and sleep! So he went back and slept, then he heard another voice saying: Samuel!! So he jumped up to Eli also and said: At your service! What is the matter with you! You called me? He said: I did not do it. Go back and sleep. If you hear anything, say: Here I am, command me to do it! So he went back and slept, and he heard a voice again saying: Samuel!! So he said: Here I am! It is I! Command me to do it! He said: Go to Eli and tell him: The love of his son prevented him from admonishing his two sons to speak ill of my sanctuary and my offering, and to disobey me. So I will take away from him the priesthood and his son, and I will destroy him and them! When morning came, Eli asked him and he told him. He was very frightened. Then an enemy from around them went to them, so he ordered his two sons to go out with the people and fight that enemy.

So they went out and brought with them the ark in which were the two tablets and the staff of Moses, so that they might be victorious by it. When they and their enemy prepared to fight, Eli began to expect report: What did they do? Then a man came to him while he was sitting on his chair and told him: Your two sons have been killed, and the people have been defeated! He said: What happened to the ark? He said: The enemy took it! He said: He gasped and fell on his back from his seat and died. Those who had taken the Ark captive went and placed it in the house of their gods. They had an idol that they worshipped, so they placed it under the idol and the idol was above it. The next day the idol was under it and it was above the idol. Then they took it and placed it above it and nailed its feet to the Ark. The next day the idol’s hands and feet had been cut off and it was lying under the Ark.

Some of them said to each other: You know that the God of the Children of Israel cannot stand up to anything, so take it out of the house of your gods! So they took the Ark out and placed it in a corner of their village. The people of that corner where they had placed the Ark felt pain in their necks, and they said: What is this?! A slave girl who was with them from the captives of the Children of Israel said to them: You will not cease to see what you hate as long as this Ark was among you! So take it out of your village! They said: You have lied! She said: The sign of that is that you bring two cows that have calves that have never been yoke upon them, then put the calf behind them, then put the ark on the calf and send them on and hold back their children, for they will go with it in submission, until when they have gone out of your land and come to the land of the children of Israel, they will break their yoke and come to their children.

So they did that, and when they had gone out of their land and come to the nearest land of the children of Israel, they broke their yoke and came to their children and put it in a wasteland where there was harvest from the children of Israel. The children of Israel were terrified and came to it, and no one would come near it except that he died. Then their prophet Samuel said to them: Intercept, and whoever feels strength in himself, let him come near it. So they presented the people to him, but no one was able to come near it except two men of the children of Israel, who were given permission to carry it to the house of their mother, who was a widow. He stayed in their mother's house until Talut became king, and the situation of the Children of Israel was settled with Samuel.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, some of the people of knowledge told me, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, he said:
m: Samuel said to the Children of Israel when they said to him: How can he have kingship over us when we are more deserving of kingship than him and he has not been given ample wealth? He said: God chose him over you and increased him abundantly in knowledge and body, and
h
the sign of his kingship
, and his kingship is from God, is that the Ark will come to you, and return to you what is in it of tranquility
h
and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind

, and it is what you used to defeat the enemy who met you and triumph over them with it. They said: If the Ark comes to us, then we are satisfied and at peace! The enemy who captured the Ark was at the bottom of Mount Elijah between them and Egypt, and they were idolaters, and among them was Goliath. Goliath was a man who had been given abundant body, strength in striking, and the intensity of war, and he was mentioned among the people for that. When the Ark was taken, it was placed in a village in Palestine called Azdud. They had placed the Ark in a church where their idols were. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) promised the Children of Israel that the Ark would come to them, their idols would wake up in the church with their heads upside down. God sent a mouse to the people of that village. The mouse would attack a man and he would wake up dead, having eaten what was in his stomach from his anus. They said: By God, you know that a calamity has befallen you that has never befallen any nation before. We do not know that it has befallen us except since this Ark was among us!! Although you have seen your idols wake up with their heads upside down every morning, something that had never been done to them until this Ark was with them! So they took it out from among you. They called for a cart and loaded the Ark on it, then hung it on two bulls, then beat their sides, and the angels came out with the bulls driving them, and the Ark did not pass by a place on earth except that it was holy. They were not alarmed by anything except the Ark on a cart pulled by oxen, until it stopped before the Children of Israel. They glorified and praised God, and they were serious in their war, and they gathered strength against Talut.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: When
h
their prophet said to them
: God has chosen Talut over you and has increased him in knowledge and stature - they refused to surrender the leadership to him, until he said to them:
h
The sign of his kingship
is that the Ark will come to you, in which is tranquility from your Lord. So he said to them: Have you seen that The Ark has come to you, containing tranquility from your Lord
h
and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind

, carried by the angels!! When Moses threw down the tablets, they were crushed and lifted up. He came down and gathered what remained and put it in that Ark. Ibn Jurayj said, Yaʿla ibn Muslim informed me, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Only one sixth of the tablets remained. He said: The Amalekites had taken that Ark captive - and the Amalekites were a group of ʿAd who were in Jericho - so the angels came with the Ark, carrying it between heaven and earth while they were looking at the Ark, until they placed it with Talut. When they saw that, they said: Yes! So they surrendered to him and made him king. He said: Whenever the prophets attended a battle, they would bring the Ark before them. They would say: Adam came down with that Ark and the corner. I have been informed that the Ark and the staff of Moses are in the Sea of Galilee, and that they will emerge before the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Abd al-Samad bin Maqal told us:
m: He heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: When Jeremiah destroyed the Holy House and burned the books, he stood on the side of the mountain and said: How can God revive these after their death? So God caused him to die for a hundred years, then He resurrected him. (al-Baqarah 2:259). Then God returned those of the Children of Israel whom He had returned after seventy years from the time he caused him to die, and they lived for thirty years, completing the hundred. When the hundred years had passed, God returned his soul to him, and it had lived, and it was in its original state. 00 1 ... 2 So when He wanted to return the Ark to them, God revealed to one of their prophets, either Daniel or someone else: If you want the disease to be lifted from you, then take this Ark away from you! They said: With a sign of what? He said: By the sign that you bring two hard cows that have never done any work, and when they see it, they put their necks under the yoke until it is fastened on them, then the Ark is fastened on a wheel, then it is hung on the two cows, then they are set free and they go where God wants them to go. So they did that, and God assigned four angels to lead them, and the two cows went quickly, until when they reached the edge of the sanctuary, they broke their yoke, cut their ropes, and went. Then David and those with him came down to them, and when David saw the Ark, he leapt toward it with joy. We said to Wahab, Why leapt toward it? He said, It is like dancing. His wife said to him, You have made it so light that the people almost hate you for what you have done! He said, Are you delaying me in obeying my Lord? You will not be my wife after this.

x: Others said: Rather, the Ark, which God made a sign for the kingdom of Talut, was in the wilderness, and Moses, peace be upon him, was behind it with his servant Joshua, so the angels carried it until they placed it in the house of Talut.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement: Indeed,
h
the sign of his kingship

is that the Ark will come to you, wherein is tranquility from your Lord, the verse: Moses had left it with his servant Joshua bin Nun while he was in the wilderness, and the angels came carrying it until they placed it in the house of Talut, so he became in his house.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father,
m: on Al-Rabiʿ, regarding His statement: Indeed,
h
the sign of his kingship

is that the Ark will come to you, the verse: Moses - according to what was mentioned to us - had left the Ark with his servant Joshua bin Nun while he was in the wilderness. He told us that the angels carried him from the wilderness until they placed him in the house of Talut, so the Ark was in his house.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on that is what Ibn Abbas and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: that the Ark It was with an enemy of the Children of Israel who had taken it from them. That is because God Almighty said, informing about His Prophet at that time, his saying to his people, the Children of Israel:
h
The sign of his kingship

is that the Ark will come to you. The definite article does not enter into such names except in what is known to those who are addressing them. The informant and the informed knew it. It was known from this that the meaning of the statement is:
h
The sign of his kingship
is that the Ark will come to you which you have known, which you used to seek victory from,
h
in it is tranquility from your Lord
. If that was a Ark from the Arks, and their value and the extent of its benefit were not known to them before that, it would have been said:
h
The sign of his kingship
is that the Ark will come to you in which is tranquility from your Lord.
If a heedless person thinks that they had known that Ark and the extent of its benefit and what was in it, and it was with Moses and Joshua, then This is something whose error is not hidden.

c: It has not been reported to us that
m: Moses ever encountered an enemy with the Ark, nor his servant Joshua. Rather, what is known about the matter of Moses and the matter of Pharaoh is what God has related of their affair, as well as his affair and the affair of the tyrants. As for his servant Joshua, those who said this claim claimed that Joshua succeeded him in the wilderness until he returned to them when Talut became king. If the matter is as they described, then what is the condition of the Ark in which they knew it? So it is permissible to say:
h
The sign of his kingship
is that the Ark will come to you, which you have known and Surat Al-Baqarah 2:248 And
h
their prophet said to them
, "Indeed,
h
the sign of his kingship
is that there will come to you the Ark, in which is tranquility from your Lord
h
and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind

, carried by the angels. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers." known its matter? And in the corruption of this statement with what we have mentioned, I clarify the evidence for the correctness of the other statement, since there is no statement in that for the people of interpretation other than them. And the description of the Ark, as we have been informed, was as follows:

c: Muhammad bin Askar and Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, they said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Bakkar bin Abdullah told us, he said:
m: We asked Wahb bin Munabbih about the Ark of Moses: What was it? He said: It was about three cubits by two cubits.

x: God Almighty means by His saying: in it, in the Ark, tranquility from your Lord.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of Ṣakīna.
Some of them said: It is a gentle wind with a face like a human face.
Those who said that are:

c: Imran bin Musa told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Warith bin Saʿid told us, he said: Muhammad bin Juhada told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu Waʿil, on the authority of ʿAli bin Abi Talib, he said:
m: Ṣakīna is a gentle wind with a face like a human face.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said: Sufyan told us
m: - and al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Sufyan told us - on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of ʿAli, he said: Ṣakīna has a face like a human face, then it is a gentle wind.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Therein is tranquility from your Lord
, he said: A gentle wind with a form. Yaqub said in his hadith: It has a face. Ibn Al-Muthanna said: Like the face of a human being.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said, Ali said:
m: Tranquility has a face like the face of a human being, and it is a gentle wind.

c: Hannad ibn Al-Sarri told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Khalid ibn Arara, he said, Ali said:
m: Tranquility is a strong wind, and it has two heads.

c: Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak, he said:
m: I heard Khalid ibn Arara narrating something similar from Ali.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, he said,
m: Shu’bah, Hammad bin Salamah, and Abu Al-Ahwas told us, all of them, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, on the authority of Ali, similarly. And others said: It has a head like the head of a cat and two wings.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God the Most High:
h
Therein is tranquility from your Lord
, he said: The tranquility and the shrike came, and Gabriel came with Abraham from Ash-Sham. Ibn Abi Nujayh said, I heard Mujahid say: The tranquility has a head like the head of a cat and two wings.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The Sakinah has two wings and a tail.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: It has two wings and a tail like the tail of a cat.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the head of a dead cat.

Those who said that: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, on the authority of some of the scholars of the Children of Israel, he said: The Sakina is the head of a dead cat, if it screamed in the chest with the scream of a cat, they were certain of victory and conquest came to them.
Others said: It is a golden basin from Paradise, in which the hearts of the prophets were washed.

Those who said that: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Uthman ibn Saeed told us, he said, Al-Hakam ibn Dhahir told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
h
In it is tranquility from your Lord
, he said: A golden basin from Paradise, in which the hearts of the prophets were washed.

c: Musa ibn Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
In it is tranquility from your Lord

, the Sakina is a golden basin in which the hearts of the prophets were washed, God gave it to Moses, and in it He placed the tablets. The tablets, as far as we know, were made of pearls, rubies, and emeralds.

x: Others said: The serenity is a spirit from God speaking.
Those who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said:

c: Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said:
m: We asked Wahb bin Munabbih, so we said to him: Tranquility? He said: A spirit from God that speaks. If they differ about something, it speaks and informs them of what they want.

c: Muhammad bin Askar told us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said: Bakr bin Abdullah told us:
m: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih, and he mentioned something similar.

x: Others said: Tranquility is what you know of the verses and you find peace in them.
Those who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said:

c: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I asked Ata bin Abi Rabah about His statement:
h
In it is tranquility from your Lord
, the verse, he said: As for tranquility, it is what they know of the verses, they find peace in them.

x: Others said: Tranquility, mercy.
Mention of those who said that: I was told, on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hasan, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father,
m: on Al-Rabi’:
h
In it is tranquility from your Lord
, meaning mercy from your Lord.

x: Others said: Tranquility is dignity.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us,
m: who said: Abdul-Razzaq told us, who said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
In it is tranquility from your Lord
, meaning dignity.

x: The most correct of these statements regarding the meaning of tranquility is what Ata bin Abi Rabah said: From the thing that souls find tranquility in from the verses that they know. That is because tranquility in the speech of the Arabs is the active participle, from the saying of the speaker: So-and-so has settled into such-and-such, if he is reassured by it and his soul is calmed by it, so he is calm and tranquil, like your saying: So-and-so has resolved to do this matter with resolve and determination.

i: And the judge ruled between the people with a judgment and a decision, and from it is the saying of the poet:
x: God has a grave, what does it gain?

It has brought peace and dignity. If the meaning of tranquility is what I have described, then it is permissible for it to be what Ali said about Abu Talib, according to what we have narrated from him, and it is permissible for it to be what Mujahid said, according to what we have narrated from him, and it is permissible for it to be what Wahb ibn Munabbih said and what al-Suddi said, because all of that is sufficient verses that calm the souls and bring joy to the hearts. If the meaning of tranquility is what we have described, then it has become clear that the verse that was in the Ark, which the souls were reassured by because of their knowledge of the correctness of its matter, is actually named after a verb and is not the same, because the speech indicates it.
God Almighty means by His saying:
h
And a remnant
, the remaining thing, from the saying of the speaker: There remains a remnant of this matter, and it is a verbal noun from it, similar to tranquility from the word sakina. And His saying:
h
Of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, means by it: of the inheritance of the family of Moses and the family of Aaron.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the remnant that remained of their inheritance.
Some of them said: That remnant was the staff of Moses, son of Aaron, and the fragments of the tablets.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Hamid bin Masʿadah told us, he said, Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of ʿIkrimah, he said:
m: I think it was on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas that he said regarding this verse:
h
And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: the fragments of the tablets.

c: Muhammad bin ʿAbdullah bin Buzaʿiʿ told us, he said, Bishr told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, Dawud said:
m: And I think it was on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abu Al-Walid told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding this verse:
h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: The staff of Moses and the fragments of the tablets.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: So in the Ark there was the staff of Moses and the fragments of the tablets, according to what was mentioned to us.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: The remainder is the staff of Moses and the fragments of the tablets.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, as for the remainder, it is the staff of Moses and the fragments of the tablets.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
m: h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: The remainder is the staff of Moses and the fragments of the tablets. Aaron, the staff of Moses and Athor from the Torah.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab Al-Thaqafi told us, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding this verse,
h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: The Torah, the fragments of the tablets, and the staff. Ishaq said, Waki’ said: And its fragments are its broken pieces.

c: Ya’qub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: The fragments of the tablets.

x: Others said: Rather, that remainder is the staff of Moses and the staff of Aaron, and something from the tablets.
Those who said that: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said:

c: Jabir bin Nuh narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: That the Ark will come to you,
h
in it is tranquility from your Lord
h
and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: It was in it the staff of Moses, the staff of Aaron, two tablets of the Torah, and manna.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said:
m: I heard my father, on the authority of Atiyah bin Saad, regarding his statement:
h
And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: The staff of Moses, the staff of Aaron, the clothes of Moses, the clothes of Aaron, and the fragments of the tablets.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the staff and the sandals.
Those who said that: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said:

c: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said:
m: I asked al-Thawri about his statement:
h
And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
. He said: Some of them say: The rest is a handful of manna and the fragments of the boards - and some of them say: The staff and the sandals.

x: Others said: Rather, it was the staff alone.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Bakkar bin Abdullah told us, he said:
m: We said to Wahb bin Munabbih: What was in it? - meaning in the chest - he said: It was in it the staff of Moses and the knife.

x: Others said: Rather, it was the fragments of the tablets and what was broken from them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, he said,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said regarding His statement:
h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he said: When Moses threw down the tablets, they were broken and he lifted them up, so he put the remainder in that chest.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I asked Ata’ bin Abi Rabah about His statement:
h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:248 And
h
their prophet said to them
, "Indeed,
h
the sign of his kingship
is that there will come to you the Ark, in which is tranquility from your Lord
h
and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, carried by the angels. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers." he said: Knowledge and the Torah.

x: Others said: Rather, it was jihad in the way of God.
Mention of those who said that:

c: I was told by Al-Hussein bin Al-Faraj,
m: he said, I heard Abu Muadh, he said, Ubaidullah bin Sulayman told us, he said, I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And a remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, he meant by the remainder, fighting in the way of God, and with that they fought with Talut, and with that they were commanded.

x: The most correct of the statements regarding that is to say: God The Almighty mentioned that the Ark which He made a sign of the truth of the words of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said to his nation:
h
God has sent you Saul as a king
. In it is tranquility from Him
h
and a remnant

of the inheritance of the family of Moses and the family of Aaron. It is possible that that remnant is: the staff, the broken tablets, the Torah, or some of it, the sandals, the clothes, and jihad in the way of God, and it is possible that it is some of that. This is a matter whose knowledge cannot be attained by way of extraction or language, and knowledge of that cannot be attained except by report that requires knowledge. And the people of Islam do not have any report about that due to the aspect that we have described. And since this is the case, it is not permissible to approve one statement and weaken another, since what we have said is permissible.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the description of the angels carrying that Ark.
Some of them said: The meaning of that is: They carry it between the heaven and the earth, until they place it among them.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: The angels came with the Ark, carrying it between the heaven and the earth, and they were looking at it, until they placed it with Talut.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: When he said to them, meaning the Prophet, to the Children of Israel: And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills, they said: Who can tell us that it is God who gave him this? It is only because of your desire in it! He said: If you have lied to me and accused me, then the sign of his kingdom is: That there will come to you the Ark, in which is tranquility from your Lord, the verse. He said: So the angels came down with the Ark during the day, looking at it with their own eyes, until they placed it among them. They acknowledged it, but they were not pleased, and they left, angry. He recited until he reached: And God is with the patient.

c: Moses told me, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: When
h
their prophet said to them
what he said to them: that God chose him over you and increased him abundantly in knowledge and body, they said: If you are truthful, then bring us a sign that this is a king! He said:
h
The sign of his kingship
is that the Ark will come to you, in which is tranquility from your Lord
h
and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind
, carried by the angels. The Ark and what was in it were in the house of Talut, so they believed in the prophethood of Simeon and submitted to the kingdom of Talut.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The angels will carry it
, he said: They will carry it until they place it in the house of Talut.

x: Others said: The meaning of that is: The angels will drive the beasts that will carry it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of some of his sheikhs, he said:
m: h
The angels will carry it
on a wheel on a cow.

c: Al-Hasan told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Abd al-Samad ibn Maqal told us that
m: he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: Four angels were entrusted with the two cows that walked with the Ark, driving them. The two cows walked with them quickly, until they reached the edge of Jerusalem and left.

x: The more correct of the two statements is the statement of the one who said: The angels carried the Ark until they placed it for them in the house of Talut, standing among the Children of Israel. This is because God, the Most High, said: The angels carry it, and He did not say: The angels bring it. And what the cows dragged in haste, even though the angels were their drivers, is not its carrier. Because the known carrying is the direct carrying of what the carrier himself carries. As for what he carried on, even though it is permissible in the language to say he carried it in the sense of the carrier’s assistance, and that his carrying was for its cause, its path is not the path of what he directly carried himself, in the way people know it among themselves. Directing the interpretation of the Qur’an to the most common languages is more appropriate than directing it to the most unfamiliar, if there is a way to do so.
God Almighty meant by that: that His prophet Samuel said to the Children of Israel: Indeed, in your coming the Ark, in which there is a Shekinah from your Lord
h
and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind

, the angels carrying it, is a sign for you, meaning: a sign and indication for you, O people, of my truthfulness in what I told you: that God sent you Talut as a king, if you had lied to me in what I told you about God giving him kingship over you, and you accused me in my telling you about that, if you are believers, meaning by that: if you were to believe me when the sign came that you asked me about my truthfulness in what I told you about the matter of Talut and his kingship. We only said that meaning because the people had disbelieved in God in their denial of their prophet and their response to his saying: Indeed, God has sent you Talut as a king, by saying: How can he have kingship over us when we are more deserving of kingship than he?

And in their questioning of him was the sign of his truthfulness. Since that was disbelief on their part, it is not permissible to say to them while they are disbelievers: There is a sign for you in the coming of the Ark if you are among the people of faith in God and His Messenger. And they are not among the people of faith in God or His Messenger. But the matter in that is as we have described its meaning, because they asked for a sign of the truth of his report to them so that they would acknowledge his truthfulness, so he said to them: In the coming of the Ark - as he described to them - there is a sign for you if you are at its coming as well, believing in what I said to you and informed you of.

In this report from God, the Most High, there is something omitted that is sufficient to mention due to the indication of what was mentioned. The meaning of the statement is: Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers. So the Ark came to them, containing tranquility from their Lord and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron had left behind, carried by the angels. At that time, they believed their prophet and acknowledged that God had sent Saul as a king over them, and they submitted to him. This is indicated by his statement:
h
So when Saul set out with the soldiers

. And he would not have separated them except after their approval of him and their surrender of the kingdom to him, because he was not one of those who could force them to do so, so it is thought that he forced them to do so unwillingly. As for his saying: He preferred, he means by it: he went out with the army and departed with it.

The root of separation is cutting. It is said, from it: the man separated from such and such a place - meaning he cut it off and passed it, heading to another place. He separates the bone and the saying from another place, so he separates it if he cuts it and separates it. And he separated the child if he cuts him from the milk. A decisive saying separates and distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and it is not rejected. And it was said: Talut separated with the soldiers on that day from Jerusalem, and they were eighty thousand fighters. None of the Children of Israel stayed behind from the separation with him except one who was sick due to his sickness, or an old man due to his old age, or an excused one who did not have the strength to rise with him.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, some of the people of knowledge told me, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, he said:
m: Talut went out with them when they were at ease. For him, and none stayed behind except an old man with an illness, or a blind man with an excuse, or a man in a village who had no choice but to stay behind.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: When the Ark came to them, they believed in the prophethood of Simeon, and they submitted to the kingdom of Talut, so they went out with him and they were eighty thousand.

x: When Talut separated them as we have described, he said:
h
God will test you with a river
, meaning:
h
God will test you with a river

, to know how you obey Him. We have already demonstrated that the meaning of testing is examination, in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it. And what we have said about that, Qatada used to say.

c: Bishr bin Muʿadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God the Most High:
h
God will test you with a river
, he said: God tests His creation with whatever He wills, to know who obeys Him and who disobeys Him. And it was said that Talut said:
h
God will test you with a river

, because they complained to Talut about the scarcity of water between them and their enemy, and they asked him to pray to God for them to make a river flow between them and their enemy, so Talut then said to them what he was told that he said of His statement:
h
God will test you with a river

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said, Some scholars told me, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said:
m: When Talut set out with his soldiers, they said: The waters will not carry us, so pray to God for us to make a river flow for us. Talut said to them:
h
God will test you with a river
(al-Quran 2:17).

c: The river that Talut told them that
m: God will test them with, it was said: It is a river between Jordan and Palestine.

x: Those who said that: Al-Muthanna told me, he said:

c: Ishaq told us, he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: h
God will test you with a river
. Al-Rabiʿ said: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that it is a river between Jordan and Palestine.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
God will test you with a river

. He said: It was Surat Al-Baqarah 2:249 So when Talut set out with the soldiers, he said, "Indeed, Allah will test you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it, then indeed he is of me,
h
except for he who scoops up a handful with his hand

." So they drank from it, except for a few of them. But when he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said, "We have no strength today against Goliath." And his soldiers. Those who believe that they will meet God say, “How often has a small company overcome a large one by God’s permission?”
h
And God is with the patient
. mentioned to us that it is a river between Jordan and Palestine.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God will test you with a river
, he said: It is a river between Jordan and Palestine.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: When Talut set out with the soldiers to fight Goliath, Talut said to the Children of Israel:
h
God will test you with a river
, he said: A river between Palestine and Jordan, a river with sweet, good water.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the River of Palestine.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: h
God will test you with a river
, so the river with which the Children of Israel were tested is the River of Palestine.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
God will test you with a river
, it is the River of Palestine. As for his statement: “
h
So whoever drinks from it is not of me

, and whoever does not taste it is of me, except for he who takes a handful with his hand. So they drank from it, except for a few of them.” This is a report from God, the Most High, about what Talut said to his soldiers when they complained to him about their thirst, so he informed them that God would test them with a river.

c: Then he informed them that the test that he informed them
m: about from God from that river is that whoever drinks from its water is not of him, meaning by that: that he is not of the people of his guardianship and obedience, nor of the believers in God and in meeting Him. And what indicates that this is the case is the statement of God, the Most High, the Most High: So when he had crossed it, he and those who believed with him, so He brought out those who had not crossed the river from among those who believed, then He concluded the mention of the believers in God and in meeting Him when they approached Goliath and his soldiers with His statement:
h
Those who thought that they would meet God said
h
How often has a small company overcome a large company by God’s permission

c: And He informed them that
m: whoever did not taste it—meaning: whoever did not taste the water from that river. The letter ha’ in his statement: and whoever drinks from it, and in his statement: and whoever does not taste it, refers to the river, and the meaning is its water. The reason for leaving out the mention of the water is that the listener understands by mentioning the river that what is meant by it is the water in it. The meaning of his statement: and did not taste it, is: and whoever does not taste the water of that river is from me, meaning: He is from the people of my authority and obedience, and the believers in God and in meeting Him. Then he made an exception from whoever in his statement: and whoever does not taste it, those who scoop up a handful with their hands, so he said: And whoever does not taste the water of that river, except a handful that he scoops up with his hand, then he is from me. Then the reading differed in the reading of his saying:
h
Except for he who scoops up a handful with his hand

. The majority of the people of Medina and Basra read it as: ghurfa, with the accusative of the ghain from ghurfa, meaning one room, from your saying, scooped a room, and the room is the verb itself from scooping.

x: Others read it with the damma, meaning the water that goes into the hand of the scooper. So ghurfa is the noun, and ghurfa is the verbal noun. And the most pleasing of the two readings in that to me is the damma of the ghain in ghurfa, meaning: except for the one who scoops a handful of water, because of the difference between ghurfa if its ghain is open, and it is not a verbal noun for it. That is because the verbal noun of scooping is scooping, and ghurfa is the verbal noun: ghurfa. So since ghurfa is different from the verbal noun of scooping, the room that has the meaning of the noun, as we have described, is more similar to ghurfa that has the meaning of the verb.
It was mentioned to us that most of them drank from that water, so whoever drank from it became thirsty, and whoever scooped a handful was quenched.
Who said that: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “
h
So whoever drinks from it is not of me

, and whoever does not taste it, then he is of me, except for he who takes a handful with his hand. So they drank from it, except for a few of them.” So the people drank according to their certainty. As for the disbelievers, they would drink but not be satisfied. As for the believers, a man would take a handful with his hand and it would suffice and satisfy him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So whoever drinks from it is not of me

, and whoever does not taste it, then he is of me, except for he who takes a handful with his hand. He said: The disbelievers used to drink but they would not be satisfied, and the Muslims used to take a handful and that would suffice them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father,
m: on al-Rabiʿ: “
h
So whoever drinks from it is not of me

, and whoever does not taste it, then he is of me, except for he who takes a handful with his hand. So they drank from it, except for a few of them.” He meant the believers among them. The people were many, so they drank from it except for a few of them, meaning the believers among them. One of them would take a handful and that would suffice him and satisfy his thirst.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He said, when the Ark and what was in it were in the house of Talut in the morning, they believed in the prophethood of Simeon and submitted to the kingdom of Talut, so they went out with him and they were eighty thousand. Goliath was one of the greatest and most powerful of people, so he went out walking in front of the army, and his companions did not gather to him until he defeated whoever he met. So when they went out, Talut said to them:
h
God will test you with a river
h
so whoever drinks from it is not of me

, and whoever does not taste it is of me. So they drank from it in awe of Goliath, so four thousand of them crossed, and seventy-six thousand returned, so whoever drank from it became thirsty, and whoever did not drink from it except a handful was quenched.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: God cast it on the tongue of Talut when He separated with the soldiers and said: No one should accompany me except someone who has the intention of jihad. No believer stayed behind, and no hypocrite followed him. They returned as disbelievers, because of their lie in what they said when they said: They said: We will not touch this water, not a sip or anything else 1. That is because he said to them:
h
God will test you with a river

, the verse. They said: We will not touch this, not a sip or anything else. He said: And the rest took the sip and drank from it until it was enough for them, and some of them were left over. He said: And those who did not take the sip were stronger than those who took it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said
m: regarding His statement:
h
So whoever drinks from it is not of me

, and whoever does not taste it, then he is of me, except for he who takes a sip with his hand, so each person drank according to the amount in his heart. So whoever took a sip and obeyed him, he was satisfied for his obedience. And whoever drank a lot, he disobeyed and was not satisfied for his disobedience.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq in a hadith,
m: which he mentioned on the authority of some of the people of knowledge, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, regarding His statement:
h
So whoever drinks from it is not of me

, and whoever does not taste it is of me, except for one who takes a handful with his hand, God Almighty says: So they drank from it, except for a few of them, and it was - as they claim - that those of them who continued to drink from what was forbidden did not see him, and whoever did not taste it except as he was commanded: a handful with his hand, it was sufficient for him and was enough for him.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement: So when he exceeded it, so when Talut exceeded the prohibition. The letter ha’ in jawazah refers to the river, and it is a metaphor for the name of Talut. His statement, and those who believed with him, means: and those who believed crossed the river with him, they said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers. Then there was a difference of opinion regarding the number of those who crossed the river with him that day, and those of them who said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers.
Some of them said: Their number was the number of the people of Badr: three hundred and a few men.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Harun bin Ishaq al-Hamadani told us, he said, Mus’ab bin al-Muqaddam told us
m: - and Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us - they both said, Isra’il told us, he said, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-Bara’ bin Azib, he said: We used to say that the number of the companions of Badr was the same as the number of the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except a believer: three hundred and a few men.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Abu Bakr told us, he said, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-Bara’ He
m: said: We used to say that the number of the companions of Badr on the day of Badr was the same as the number of the companions of Talut, three hundred and thirteen men, who crossed the river.

c: Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Abu Amir narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said:
m: We used to say that the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were on the day of Badr three hundred and some men, the same number as the companions of Talut, whoever crossed with him, and none crossed with him except a believer.

c: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, he said, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said, Mu’ammil narrated to us, he said, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said:
m: We used to say that the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were on the day of Badr the same number as the companions of Talut, the day they crossed the river, and none crossed with him except a Muslim.

c: Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, he said, Abu Ahmad narrated to us, he said, Mis’ar narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Sa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: “It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions on the day of Badr: You are the same number as the companions of Talut on the day they crossed the river, and none crossed with him except a Muslim.” He met. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr were three hundred and some men.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, he said:
m: God counted those who believed at the river, and they were three hundred, and more than ten and less than twenty, then David, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and completed the number with him.

x: Others said: Rather, four thousand crossed the river with him, and the people of faith were saved from the people of disbelief and hypocrisy when they met Goliath. He who said that: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: Four thousand of the Children of Israel crossed the river with Talut, and when he and those who believed with him crossed it and looked at Goliath, they also turned back and said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers. So three thousand, six hundred and eighty-something turned back from him, and he was saved with three hundred and some-something, the number of the people of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:249 So when Talut set out with the soldiers, he said, "Indeed, Allah will test you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it, then indeed he is of me,
h
except for he who scoops up a handful with his hand

So they drank from it, except for a few of them. But when he and those who believed with him had crossed it, they said, "We have no strength today against Goliath." And his soldiers. Those who believe that they will meet God say, “How often has a small company overcome a large one by God’s permission?”
h
And God is with the patient
. Badr.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, al-Husayn told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: When he and those who believed with him crossed it, those who drank said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers.

x: The more correct of the two sayings in that regard is what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and said by al-Suddi: That he crossed the river with Talut, the believer who did not drink from the river except a handful, and the disbeliever who drank from it a lot. Then the distinction between them occurred after that by seeing Goliath and meeting him, and the people of polytheism and hypocrisy withdrew from him, and they are the ones who said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers, and the people of insight followed the command of God according to their insight, and they are the people of steadfastness in faith, and they said:
h
How often has a small company overcome a large company by God’s permission
h
And God is with the patient

. If someone who is heedless thinks that it is not permissible for anyone to have crossed the river with Talut except the people of faith who remained steadfast with him in their faith, and those who did not drink from the river except a mouthful, because God, the Most High, said: So when he had crossed it, he and those who believed with him, then it was known that only the people of faith crossed with him, according to what was narrated in the report from Al-Bara’ bin Azib, and because if the people of disbelief had crossed the river as the people of faith crossed it, God would not have specifically mentioned the people of faith in that, because the matter in that is contrary to what he thought.

That is because it is not strange that the two groups - I mean the group of faith and the group of disbelief - crossed the river. God informed His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, about the believers crossing, because they were among those who crossed it with their king, and He left out mentioning the people of disbelief, even though they crossed the river with the believers. What indicates the correctness of what we said about that is the statement of God, the Most High: “So when he and those who believed with him crossed it, they said, ‘We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers.’
h
Those who thought that they would meet God said
h
How often has a small company overcome a large company by God’s permission
?’” So God, the Most High, made it obligatory that those who thought that they would meet God are those who said when crossing the river:
h
How often has a small company overcome a large company by God’s permission
, not others who do not think that they will meet God - and that those who do not think that they will meet God are those who said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers.
It is not permissible to attribute faith to someone who denies that he will meet God, or has doubts about it.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the matter of these two groups, I mean those who said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers, and those who said: How often has a small group overcome a large group by God’s permission, who they are.

Some of them said: The group who said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers, are people of disbelief in God and hypocrisy, and they are not among those who witnessed the battle of Goliath and his soldiers, because they turned away from Talut and those who remained with him to fight the enemy of God, Goliath and those with him, and they are the ones who disobeyed God’s command by drinking from the river.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi,
m: on that. And it is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas, and we have mentioned the narration on that authority from him earlier.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: Those who think that they will meet God, are those who scooped up and obeyed, those who went with Talut were the believers, and those who doubted sat back.

x: Others said: Both groups were people of faith, and none of them drank from the water except a handful, rather they were all people of obedience, but some of them had more certainty than others. They are the ones about whom God said:
h
How often has a small company overcome a large company by God’s permission
. The others were weaker in certainty, and they were the ones who said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: “So when he and those who believed with him had passed it, they said: “We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers.”
h
Those who thought that they would meet God said
h
How often has a small company overcome a large company by God’s permission
h
And God is with the patient
. And by God, some of the believers are better in strength and determination than others, they are all believers.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
How often has a small company overcome a large company by God’s permission

, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his companions on the day of Badr: “You are equal in number to the companions of Saul: three hundred.” Qatada said: And with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr were three hundred and a few.

c: Yunus told me.
m: He said, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said: Those who did not take the room were stronger than those who took it, and they are the ones who said: How often has a small company overcome a large one by God’s permission?
h
And God is with the patient

. And it is necessary according to the statement narrated from Al-Bara’ bin Azib: that no one crossed the river with Talut except a number of the companions of Badr - that both groups that God described with what He described them with, their matter is on the throat of what Qatada and Ibn Zayd said about them.

x: The first of the two statements in the interpretation of the verse is what Ibn ʿAbbas, Al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj said, and we have mentioned the evidence for that previously. As for the interpretation of His statement:
h
Those who think that they will meet God said
, it means: Those who know and are certain that they will meet God said.

c: Musa told me, he said, ʿAmr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Those who think that they will meet God said

, those who are certain. The interpretation of the statement: Those who are certain of the Resurrection and believe in the return to God said to those who said: We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers: How many a small company means by how many many, a small company has been defeated, a large company by God’s permission means by God’s decree and destiny,
h
and God is with the patient

means: with those who confine themselves to His pleasure and obedience. We have already explained the aspects of conjecture, and that one of its meanings is: certain knowledge, which indicates the correctness of that in the past, so we disliked repeating it. As for the group, they are a group of people, it does not have a singular form from its word, and it is like the group and the individuals. It is plural for categories, and categories in the nominative, and categories in the accusative and genitive, with the opening of its nun in all cases. And categories in the nominative by declension of its nun in the nominative and leaving the ya in it, and in the accusative, category, and category in the genitive, so the declension in its nun in the genitive and accusative is in it. And in all of that, the ya is maintained in it as it is. If it is added, it is said: these are your categories, by confirming the nun and deleting the tanween, as those whose language is: these are years said, in the whole year: these are your years, by confirming the nun and declension and deleting the tanween from it for the addition. And the same applies to every defective word such as hundred and leap, few and glory. As for what was defective from the beginning, its plural is with the taa, such as number and numbers, and connection and connections. As for his saying:
h
And God is with the patient

, it means: God is the helper of the patient in striving in His cause and other than that of His obedience, and their victory and their victory over His enemies who turn people away from His path, and those who oppose the path of His religion. Likewise, it is said to every person who helps a man against another: he is with him, meaning he is with him in helping him and supporting him.

evidence.text: Then the reading differed in the reading of his saying: Except for he who scoops up a handful with his hand.

The majority of the people of Medina and Basra read it as: ghurfa, with the accusative of the ghain from ghurfa, meaning one room, from your saying, scooped a room, and the room is the verb itself from scooping.
Others read it with the damma, meaning the water that goes into the hand of the scooper.

And the most pleasing of the two readings in that to me is the damma of the ghain in ghurfa, meaning: except for the one who scoops a handful of water, because of the difference between ghurfa if its ghain is open, and it is not a verbal noun for it.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
And when they came forth to face Goliath and his soldiers

, and when Talut and his soldiers came forth to face Goliath and his soldiers. The meaning of His statement: came forth is that they went to the open space of the earth, which is what is exposed and level. That is why it is said of a man who relieves himself that he relieves himself, because people in ancient times in the pre-Islamic era used to relieve themselves in the open space of the earth, so it was said: So-and-so has come forth to the open space of the earth. And that is as it was said: He defecated, because they used to relieve themselves in the excrement of the earth, which is the calm part of it, so it was said to the man: He defecated, meaning he went to the excrement of the earth. As for his saying: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience, it means that Talut and his companions said: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience, meaning: send down patience upon us. And his saying: And make firm our feet, meaning: strengthen our hearts to fight them, so that our feet are firm and do not flee from them, and give us victory over the disbelieving people, who disbelieved in you and denied you as a god and worshipped other than you, and took idols as lords.
God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And they defeated them

, that Talut and his soldiers defeated Goliath’s companions, and David killed Goliath. This statement is inherited, but he left it out because it was sufficient to indicate what appeared of it. That is because the meaning of the statement is: And when they came forward to face Goliath and his soldiers, they said, ‘Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.’ So their Lord responded to them, poured out His patience upon them, made their feet firm, and gave them victory over the disbelieving people.
h
So they defeated them by God’s permission
. But he left it out because it was sufficient to indicate in his statement:
h
So they defeated them by God’s permission
, that God had answered their supplication to Him, and the meaning of his statement:
h
So they defeated them by God’s permission is that they were defeated by God’s decree and predestination
It is said: The people defeated the army with a complete defeat and my defeat. And David killed Goliath.
This David is David bin Ishi, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the reason for his killing him was as follows:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abdul-Razzaq told us, Bakr bin Abdullah told us,
m: I heard Wahb bin Munabbih narrating, he said: When Talus went out - or he said: when he appeared - to Goliath, Goliath said: Bring me someone who will fight me, if he kills me, then my kingdom is yours, and if I kill him, then your kingdom is mine! So David was brought to Talus, and he ruled that if he killed him, he would marry his daughter to him, and that he would rule over his wealth. So Talus dressed him in weapons, but David was reluctant to fight him with weapons, and he said: God did not grant me victory over him, weapons are of no use! So he went out to him with a slingshot and a bag full of stones, then he went out to him. Goliath said to him: Are you fighting me? David said: Yes! He said: Woe to you! You only went out as you go out to a dog with a slingshot and stones! I will surely squander your flesh and feed it today to birds and wild beasts! David said to him: You are an enemy of God, worse than a dog! David took a stone and slinged it, and it hit between his eyes until it penetrated his brain, and he killed Goliath and those with him fled, and David's head was shaken. When they returned to Saul, the people claimed to have killed Goliath.

x: Some of them brought swords, something from his weapon or his body, and David hid his head. Saul said: Whoever brings his head is the one who killed him! So David brought it, then he said to Saul: Give me what you promised me! Saul regretted what he had stipulated and said: The daughters of kings must have a dowry, and you are a bold and brave man, so he accepted her dowry of three hundred foreskins from our enemies. He hoped to kill David by doing so. So David raided and captured three hundred of them, cut off their foreskins, and brought her. Saul had no choice but to marry her to him. Then he felt remorse, so he wanted to kill David until he fled from him to the mountain, so Talut rose up to him and besieged him. One night, sleep overcame Talut and his guards, so David went down to them and took Talut's pitcher from which he used to drink and perform ablution, and cut off hairs from his beard and some of the edges of his clothes.

Then David returned to his place and called out to him: You have slept and your guard slept, for if I wanted to kill you last night I would have done so, for this is your pitcher, and some of the hair from your beard and the edges of your clothes! And he sent it to him, so Talut knew that if he wanted to he would kill him, so that made him feel sympathetic towards him and he reassured him, and he made a covenant with him by God that he would not see any harm in him. Then he left. Then at the end of Talut's affair, he was plotting to kill him. Talut would not fight an enemy except that he was defeated, until he died. Bakkar said: Wahb was asked while I was listening: Was Talut a prophet to whom revelation was sent? He said: No revelation came to him, but there was with him a prophet called Samuel who was receiving revelation, and he was the one who made Talut king.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: There was the prophet David and four brothers, and their father was with them, an old man. Their father stayed behind, and David stayed behind with him from among his brothers to tend his father’s sheep for him, and he was one of the youngest of them. His four brothers went out with Talut, and his father called him and the people had drawn close together and were getting close to each other. Ibn Ishaq said: David, according to what some of the people of knowledge told me on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, was a short, blue-eyed man. He had little hair on his head, and his heart was pure and clean. His father said to him: O my son, we have prepared for your brothers provisions that will strengthen them against their enemy, so go out with it to them, and when I give it to them, come to me quickly. He said: I will do so. So he went out and took with him what he had carried for his brothers, and with him his saddlebags in which he carried stones, and his sling with which he used to shoot his sheep. When he was separated from his father, he passed by a stone and said: O David, take me and put me in your saddlebags to kill Goliath with me, for I am the stone of Jacob! So he took it and put it in his saddlebags, and walked. While he was walking, he passed by another stone and said: O David, take me and put me in your saddlebags to kill Goliath with me, for I am the stone of Isaac! So he took it and put it in his saddlebags, and then he went. While he was walking, he passed by a stone and said: O David, take me and put me in your saddlebags to kill Goliath with me, for I am the stone of Abraham! So he took it and put it in his saddlebags, and then he went. He went to the people and gave his brothers what he had sent to them with him. He heard in the army the people talking about Goliath and his great status among them, and the people’s awe of him, and what they magnify of his status, so he said to them: By God, you are magnifying something about this enemy that I do not know what it is!! By God, if I saw him, I would kill him! So bring me to the king. So he was brought to King Talut, and he said: O king, I see you magnifying the status of this enemy! By God, if I saw him, I would kill him! He said: O my son, do you not have the strength to do that? And have you not tried it yourself? He said: A lion was attacking a sheep from my flock and caught up with it, so I took hold of its head, and loosened its jaws from it, and took it from its mouth, so call for me a shield so that I may throw it at me. So a shield was brought and he threw it around his neck, and it represented a scene that filled Talut’s eyes and himself and those of the Children of Israel who were present with him, so Talut said: By God, perhaps God will destroy him with it! So when morning came, they returned to Goliath, When the people met, David said: Show me Goliath! So they showed him to him on a horse for his nation. When he saw him, the three stones began to leap from his saddlebags, and this one said: Take me! and this one said: Take me! and this one said: Take me! So he took one of them and put it in his sling, then he twisted it with it, then he sent it, and he struck it between the eyes of Goliath and crushed him, and he turned from his mount, and killed him. Then his army fled, and the people said: David killed Goliath! And Talut was deposed and the people turned to David in his place, until no mention of Talut was heard, except that the People of the Book claim that when he saw the Children of Israel turning away from him to David, he intended to assassinate David and wanted to kill him, but God turned that away from him and from David, and he recognized his sin, and sought repentance from it to God. It has been narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih regarding the matter of Talut and David, a statement contrary to the two narrations that we mentioned before, which is what: - Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim said, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me: He heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: When the Children of Israel surrendered the kingdom to Saul, God revealed to the prophet of the Children of Israel: Tell Saul to attack the people of Midian, and leave no one alive in it without killing him, for I will make him victorious over them. So he went out with the people until he reached Midian, and killed everyone in it except their king, whom he captured and drove away their livestock. Then God revealed to Samuel: Do you not marvel at Saul, when I commanded him with my command and he disobeyed it, and brought their king as a captive, and drove away their livestock! So tell him: I will remove the kingdom from his house, and he will not return to it until the Day of Resurrection, for I only honor those who obey me, and I humiliate those who disdain my command! So he met him and said to him: What did you do!! Why did you bring their king as a captive, and why did you drive away their livestock? He said: I only drove away the livestock to bring them near. Samuel said to him: God has removed the kingdom from your house, and he will not return to it until the Day of Resurrection. The Resurrection! So God inspired Samuel: Go to Ishi, so that he may direct his sons to you, and anoint the one who commanded you with the holy oil, so that he may be king over the children of Israel. So he went until he came to Ishi and said: Show me your sons. So Ishi called his eldest son, and a large, handsome man came. When Samuel looked at him, he was pleased and said: Praise be to God, God is All-Seeing of His servants! So God inspired him: Your eyes see what is apparent, and I know what is in the hearts, not like this! So he said: Not like this, show me another. So he showed him six, each of which said: Not like this. So he said: Do you have any other children? He said: Yes! I have a ruddy boy, and he is a shepherd among the sheep. So he said: Send for him. So when David came, a ruddy boy came, so he anointed him with the holy oil and said to his father: Keep this secret, for if Talut finds out about it, he will kill him. So Goliath went with his people to the children of Israel, and they camped, and Talut went with the children of Israel And he camped, and prepared for battle. So Goliath sent you to Talut: Why did he kill my people and your people? Come forward to me, or bring forward to me whomever you wish, for if I kill you, the kingdom will be mine, and if you kill me, the kingdom will be yours. So Talut sent a shouter in his camp: Who will come forward to fight Goliath? If he kills him, the king will marry him to his daughter, and share in his kingdom. So Ishi sent David to his brothers - Al-Tabari said: He is Ishi, but the narrator said: Ishi - and they were in the camp, and he said: Go and provide your brothers with provisions, and tell me report of the people, what they have done! So he came to his brothers and heard a voice: The king says: Who will come forward to fight Goliath? If he kills him, the king will marry him to his daughter. So David said to his brothers: Is there a man among you who will come forward to fight Goliath, kill him, and marry the king’s daughter? They said: You are a foolish boy! And who can stand Goliath, and he is one of the remaining tyrants!! When he did not see them Surat Al-Baqarah 2:251 So they defeated them by permission of Allah, and David killed Goliath. Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom and taught him whatever He willed. And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted. But Allah is full of bounty to the worlds. wanting to do that, he said: I will go and kill him! So they rebuked him. They became angry with him, and when they forgot about him, he went until the caller came and said: I will go forth to fight Goliath! So he took him to the king, and said to him: No one answered me except a young man from the children of Israel, this is he! He said: O my son, are you going forth to fight Goliath? He said: Yes. He said: Have you noticed anything in yourself? He said: Yes, I was a shepherd among the sheep and a lion attacked me, so I took hold of his jaws and ripped them apart. So he called for a bow and a complete tool, so he put them on and mounted the horse, then he walked close to them, then he turned his horse away, and returned to the king, and the king and those around him said: The young man is a coward! So he came and stood before the king, and he said: What is the matter with you? David said: If God does not kill him for me, this horse and this weapon will not kill him! So let me fight as I wish. He said: Yes, my son. So David took his saddlebags and girded them, and threw stones into them, and took his sling with which he used to herd, then he went towards Goliath. When he approached his army, he said: Where is Goliath going forth? To me? So he came out to him on a horse, fully armed. When Goliath saw him, he said: Come to me?! He said: Yes. So he brought me a sling and a stone as a dog is brought! He said: That is it. He said: I will surely divide your flesh between the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth! David said: Or will God divide your flesh! So David put a stone in his sling and turned it and sent it towards Goliath, and it hit the nose of the egg that was on Goliath until it mixed with his brain, so he fell from his horse. So David went to him and cut off his head with his sword, and he brought it in his saddlebags, and cut off his turban until he threw it in front of Talut, so they rejoiced greatly. And Talut left, and when he was inside the city he heard the people mentioning David, so he felt bad. So David came to him and said: Give me my wife! He said: Do you want the king’s daughter without a dowry? David said: You did not stipulate a dowry from me, and I have nothing!! He said: I will not charge you more than you can bear, you are a bold man, and in our mountains there are thugs who fight people, and they are uncircumcised, so if you kill one of them Two hundred men, so bring me their foreskins.
