So whenever he killed a man, he would string his foreskins on a thread, until he had stringed two hundred foreskins. Then he brought them to Talut and threw them to him, and said: Give me my wife, I have done what you stipulated. So he married him to his daughter, and most of the people mentioned David, and this increased his amazement among the people. Talut said to his son: You will kill David! He said: Glory be to God, you do not deserve that! He said: You are a foolish boy! I do not think that he will expel you and your family from the kingdom! When he heard that from his father, he went to his sister and said to her: I fear that your father will kill your husband David, so tell him to be careful and hide from him. His wife said that to him, so he disappeared. When morning came, Talut sent someone to call David for him, and his wife had made himself asleep on his bed and covered him. When Talut’s messenger came, he said: Where is David? Let him answer the king! She said to him: He spent the night complaining and is now asleep, you see him on The bed.

c: So they returned to Talut and told him that.
m: He stayed for an hour, then sent for him. She said: He is asleep and has not woken up yet. So they returned to the king, and he said: Bring him to me, even if he is asleep. So they went to the bed and did not find anyone on it.
b.via: So they returned to Talut and

c: So they went to the king and told him.
m: So he sent for his daughter and said: What made you lie? She said: He ordered me to do that, and I feared that if I did not do it, he would kill me! And David was fleeing in the mountain until Talut was killed and David became king after him.
b.via: So they went to the king and

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Talut was the commander of the army, so Abu Dawud sent with David something to his brothers, and David said to Talut: What is it for me to kill Goliath? He said: You have a third of my kingdom, and I will marry you to my daughter. So he took his saddlebags and put three marwa in them, then he named those stones of his: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, then he put his hand in and said: In the name of my God and the God of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob! So he went out. On Abraham, he put it in his spear, and it pierced thirty-three eggs from his head, and killed thirty thousand behind him.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: On that day, Talut Abu Dawud crossed the river with those who crossed, with thirteen of his sons, and Dawud was the youngest of his sons. So he came to him one day and said: O my father, I do not throw anything with my spear except that I kill it! So he said: Be happy, my son! For God has placed your provision in your spear. Then he came to him another time and said: O my father, I entered among the mountains and found a lion lying down, so I mounted it and took hold of its ears, but it did not frighten me! He said: Be happy, my son! For this is good that God will give you. Then he came to him another day and said: O my father, I walk among the mountains and glorify God, and there is not a mountain that does not glorify God with me! So he said: Be happy, my son! For this is good that God has given you. And Dawud was a shepherd, and his father’s shepherd came behind him to him and to His brothers brought food. So the Prophet, peace be upon him, brought a horn with oil in it, and an iron cat 1, and he sent it to Talut and said: Your companion who kills Goliath will have this horn placed on his head and it will boil until it is oiled with it, and it will not run down his face. It will be on his head like a crown, and he will enter this cat and fill it. So Talut called the Children of Israel and tested it with them, but none of them agreed with him. When they finished, Talut said to Abu Dawud: Do you have any children left who did not witness us? He said: Yes! My son Dawud remains, and he brings us food. When Dawud came to him, he passed by three stones on the road, so they spoke to him and said to him: Take us, O Dawud, and you will kill Goliath with us! He said: So he took them and put them in his bag. Talut had said: Whoever kills Goliath, I will marry him to my daughter, and I will make his ring part of my kingdom. So when Dawud came, they placed the horn on his head and it boiled until it was oiled with it, and he put the cat on it and filled it. He was a sick, yellow man, and no one else had worn it. But when David put it on, the garment tightened on him until it fell apart. Then he walked to Goliath, and Goliath was one of the strongest and most powerful people, and when he looked at David, he cast fear of him into his heart, so he said to him: O young man! Go back, for I will have mercy on you by killing you! David said: No, I will kill you! So he took out the stones and put them in the slingshot, and every time he lifted one he named it, and said: This is in the name of my father Abraham, and the second: in the name of my father Isaac, and the third: in the name of my father Israel. Then he turned the slingshot and the stones returned to one stone, then he sent it and struck it between Goliath’s eyes, and it pierced his head and killed him, and it continued to kill every person it hit, penetrating him until no one was able to live. So they defeated them, and David killed Goliath, and Talut returned, and David married his daughter to him, and he put his ring in his kingdom. The people turned to David and loved him. When Talut saw that, he felt angry and envied him, so he wanted to kill him. David knew that he wanted to kill him. Then he laid out a wineskin for him in his bed. Then Talut entered David’s sleep while David had fled, so he struck the wineskin and tore it, and the wine flowed out of it, and a drop of wine fell into his mouth. He said: May God have mercy on David! How much wine he drank!! Then David came to him from the midwife in his house while he was sleeping, and he placed two arrows at his head, and at his feet, and two arrows on his right and two arrows on his left, then he came down. When Talut woke up, he was struck by arrows and recognized them, so he said: May God have mercy on David! He is better than me. I defeated him and killed him, and he defeated me and stopped me! Then one day he rode and found him walking in the wilderness and Talut was on a horse, so Talut said: Today I will kill David! - and David was not overtaken when he was frightened - so Talut ran after him, so David was frightened and became intense and entered a cave, and God inspired the spider to build a house around him. When Talut reached the cave, he looked at the spider’s construction and said: If he had entered here, he would have torn through the spider’s house! So he imagined it, so he left it. I narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that when David came to them, he had placed with him a bag containing three stones, and that Goliath came out to them and called: Is there no man for a man? So Talut said: Who will come out to him? Otherwise, I will come out to him. So David stood up and said: I will! So Talut stood up to him. So he tightened his armor on him, and he began to see him staring at it and rising, and Talut was amazed by that, so he tightened all his tools on him. And that David threw one of those stones at them, and hit the people, then he threw a second stone, and hit them, then he threw a third and killed Goliath. So God gave him the kingdom and wisdom and taught him whatever He wanted, and he became the leader over them, and they gave him obedience.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd told me
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: Have you not seen the assembly of the Children of Israel? So he read until he reached his money, “But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers,” he said: God revealed to their prophet: Among the sons of so-and-so is a man through whom God will kill Goliath, and among his signs is this horn that you will place on his head and water will gush forth. So he came to him and said: God revealed to me that among your sons is a man through whom God will kill Goliath! He said: Yes, O Prophet of God! He said: So he brought out for him twelve men like the pillars, And among them was a man who was skilled in them, so he began to show them to the horn, but he did not see anything, so the big one would say: Go back! So he would return it to him. So God revealed to him: We do not take men for their appearance, but we take them for the righteousness of their hearts. He said: O Lord, he claimed that he had no other son! He said: He lied! So he said: My Lord has lied to you and said: You have a son other than them! He said: He has told the truth, O Prophet of God, I have a short son and I was ashamed for people to see him, so I put him among the sheep! He said: Where is he? He said: In such and such a valley, on such and such a mountain. So he went out to him, and found the valley flowing between him and the spot where he used to rest. He said: And he found him carrying two sheep, two sheep, crossing the torrent with them and not wading through the torrent with them. When he saw him, he said: This is him, no doubt! This one is merciful to animals, so he is more merciful to people! He said: So he placed the horn on his head and it flowed. So he said to him: My nephew, have you seen anything here that pleases you? He said: Yes. If I swim, the mountains swim with me, and if a tiger, wolf or beast comes and takes a sheep, I go to it and open its jaws to release it, but it does not provoke me! He said: And I found his row with him 1. He said: So he passed by three stones, one of which was climbing on top of the other, each one of them saying: I am the one who takes! And this one said: No! Rather, he takes me! And the other said the same. He said: So he took them all and threw them in his row. So when he came with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they went out, their prophet said to them: Indeed, God has sent you Talut as a king. So there was from the story of their prophet and their story what God mentioned in His book, and he recited until he reached: And God is with the patient. He said: Their matter came together and they were all together, and he recited: And give us victory over the disbelieving people. And Goliath came out on his piebald mule, with a bow in his hand, and he said: Who will come out? Show me your heads! He said: So Talut was terrified by him, he said: So he turned to his companions and said: Who is a man who will suffice me today? Goliath? David said: As for him. He said: Come! He said: So he took off his armor and put it on him. He said: And God breathed into him from His spirit until it filled him. He said: So he threw an arrow and put it in the armor. He said: So David broke it and it did not harm him at all, three times, then he said to him: Take it now! David said: O God, make it one Surat Al-Baqarah 2:251 So they defeated them by permission of Allah, and David killed Goliath. Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom and taught him whatever He willed. And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted. But Allah is full of bounty to the worlds. stone. He said: And he named one Abraham, another Isaac, and another Jacob. He said: So he gathered them all together and they were - one stone. He said: So he took them and took a sling, and turned it to shoot with it and said: Shoot me as a lion and a wolf shoot, shoot me with a bow! He said: I will not shoot you today except with it! He said to him the same thing also, and he said: Yes! And you are more insignificant to me than a wolf! So he turned it and in it was the command of God and the authority of God. He said: So its path was hidden as it was ordered. He said: Then a canopy came and struck him between the eyes until it came out from the back of his neck, then it killed so-and-so of his companions behind him. And God defeated them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: When they crossed - meaning the river about which God said, informing about what Talut said to his soldiers: God will test you with a river - and Goliath came, and fighting him was difficult for Talut, so Talut said to the al-Nas 114:If Goliath is killed, I will give the one who kills him half of my kingdom, and I will share everything I own with him! So God sent David, and David was on that day in the mountain as a shepherd, and nine of David’s brothers had fought with Talut, and they were more loyal to him, richer than him, more known among the people than him, and more respected by Talut than him, so they fought and left him with their sheep, so David said when God cast into his soul what he cast and honored him: I will entrust my sheep to my Lord today, and I will go to the people, and I will see what I have heard of the king’s saying to the one who killed Goliath! So David went to his brothers, and they blamed him when he came to them, and they said: Why did you come? He said: To kill Goliath, for God “I am able to kill him. So they mocked him.” Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: Abu Dawud had sent something with Dawud to his brothers, so he took a bag and put three stones in it, then he named them Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Ibn Jurayj said, they said: He was weak and in poor condition, so he passed by three stones and they said to him: Take us, O David, and fight Goliath with us! So David took them and threw them in his bag. When he threw them, he heard one of them say to its companion: I am the stone of Aaron, with whom he killed such-and-such a king. The second said: I am the stone of Moses, with whom he killed such-and-such a king. The third said: I am the stone of David, who will kill Goliath! The two stones said: O stone of Dawud, we are your helpers! So they became one stone. The stone said: O Dawud, throw me, for I will seek help from the wind—and the sniffer of his egg, according to what they say, and God knows best, in it are six hundred pounds—and I will strike Goliath’s head and kill him! Ibn Jurayj said, and Mujahid said: He named one of them Abraham, the other Isaac, and the other Jacob. And he said: In the name of my God and the God of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob! And he put them in his turban. Ibn Jurayj said: So he set out until he reached Talut and said: You have given to whoever killed Goliath half of your kingdom and half of everything you own! Will that be enough for me if I kill him? He said: Yes! And the people were mocking David, and David’s brothers were even more severe than him. And Talut would not send anyone who claimed to kill Goliath to him except that he would dress him in a coat of mail that he had, and if it was not worthy of him, he would take it off him. And it was a complete coat of mail from Talut’s coat of mail, so David dressed him in it, and when he saw its worth to him, he ordered him to advance. So David advanced and stood in a place where no one else could stand, and he was wearing the coat of mail. So Goliath said to him: Woe to you! Who are you? I have mercy on you! Let someone other than you from these kings advance to me! You are a weak, poor man, so go back! David said: I am the one who will kill you by God’s permission, and I will not go back until I kill you! So when David refused to do anything but fight him, Goliath advanced to him to take him by the hand. He had power over him, so he took the stone out of the bag, called upon his Lord and threw the stone at him, and the wind blew his egg off his head, and the stone hit Goliath’s head until it entered his stomach and killed him. Ibn Jurayj said, and Mujahid said: When he threw the stone at Goliath, it blew thirty-three eggs off his head, and thirty thousand people were killed behind him. God the Almighty said: And David killed Goliath. So David said to Saul: Give me what you have given me. But Saul refused to give him that. So David went and lived in one of the cities of the Children of Israel until Saul died. When he died, the Children of Israel went to David and brought him and made him king, and gave him the treasures of Saul, and said: Goliath was not killed except by a prophet! God the Almighty said: And David killed Goliath,
h
and God gave him the kingdom and wisdom
and taught him what He willed.

x: By that, God the Almighty meant: And God gave David the kingdom and wisdom and taught him what He willed. The ha’ in His statement:
h
And God gave him refers to David
. And the kingdom means authority, and wisdom means prophecy. And His statement:
h
And taught him of what He willed

means: He taught him the making of armor and the estimation of the chain, as God Almighty said: And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you to protect you from your violence (al-Anbiya 21:80). It has been said that the meaning of His statement:
h
And God gave him the kingdom and wisdom is that God gave David the kingdom of Saul and the prophethood of Samuel
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Moses told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: David became king after he killed Saul, and God made him a prophet, and that is His statement:
h
And God gave him the kingdom and wisdom
, he said: Wisdom is the prophecy, He gave him the prophecy of Simeon and the kingdom of Saul.

x: By this, the Most High means: And if it were not that God repels some people, who are the people of obedience to Him and faith in Him, from others, who are the people of disobedience to God and polytheism with Him - just as He repelled those who stayed behind from Talut on the day of Goliath from the people of disbelief in God and disobedience to Him, and He gave them what they asked of their Lord in the beginning: of sending a king over them to fight with him in His cause, with those who fought with him from the people of faith in God, certainty and patience, Goliath and his soldiers - the earth would have been corrupted, meaning: its people would have perished by God’s punishment of them, so the earth was corrupted by that. But God is gracious to His creation and is merciful to them, by repelling the righteous among His creation from the wicked, the obedient from the disobedient among them, and the believer from the disbeliever.

This verse is an announcement from God, the Most High, about the hypocrites who were at the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who stayed behind from his battles and fighting with him because of the doubt in their souls and the sickness of their hearts, and the polytheists and disbelievers among them, and that He only repels from them the punishment for their disbelief by hastening them. And their hypocrisy is in the belief of the believers in Him and His Messenger, who are the people of insight and seriousness in the matter of God, and those who have certainty in the fulfillment of God’s promise to them for fighting His enemies and the enemies of His Messenger, of victory in this life and winning His Paradise in the hereafter. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And were it not that God repels some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted, he says: And were it not that God repels the wicked by righteousness, and repels him by the rest of the people’s descendants from one another, the earth would have been corrupted, with the destruction of its people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And were it not that God repels some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted, he says: And were it not that God defends the wicked by righteousness, and by the rest of the people’s descendants from one another, its people would have been destroyed.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Hanzala, on the authority of Abu Muslim, he said:
m: I heard Ali say: If there were no remnants of Muslims among you, you would have perished.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if God had not repelled some people by means of others
, the earth would have been corrupted, he said: All those on earth would have been destroyed.

c: Abu Hamid Al-Himsi Ahmad Ibn Al-Mughira told us, he said, Yahya Ibn Saʿid told us, he said, Hafs Ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Suqah, on the authority of Wabra Ibn ʿAbd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, God repels calamity from a hundred households of his neighbors through the righteous believer. Then Ibn ʿUmar recited:
h
And if God had not repelled some people by means of others
, the earth would have been corrupted.

c: Ahmad Abu Hamid Al-Himsi told me, he said, Yahya Ibn Saʿid told us, he said, Uthman Ibn ʿAbd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir Ibn ʿAbdullah, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, God reforms, through the righteousness of the Muslim man, his children and his children’s children, the people of his household and the households around him, and they will remain in God’s protection as long as he is among them.”

x: And We have demonstrated his saying: the worlds, and we have mentioned the narration about it. As for the readings, they differed in the reading of his saying:
h
And had God not repelled some people by means of others

A group of the readings read it: And had God not repelled as a source, from the saying of the one who says: God repelled His creation, so He repels a repelling. They based their choice of that on the fact that God, the Most High, is the only One who repels His creation, and no one defends Him and overcomes Him.

Another group of the readings read it: And had God not defended the people as a source, from the saying of the one who says: God defended His creation, so He defends a repelling and a defense. They based their choice of that on the fact that many of His creation are hostile to the people of God’s religion and His guardianship and the believers in Him, so they are, by their war against them and their hostility towards them, defending God with their suspicions, and overcoming them with their ignorance, and God is their defender from His friends and the people of His obedience and belief in Him.

The statement in that, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that the readings have read, and the group of the nation has come with them, and there is no change in the meaning of the other in the reading with one of the two letters. This is because whoever defends another from something, then he defends him from it with something that he defends. And whenever the one who is defended refrains from defending himself, then he defends the one who defends him. There is no doubt that Goliath and his soldiers were, by fighting Talut and his soldiers, trying to overcome the party of God and his soldiers, and in their attempt to do so, they were trying to overcome God and defend what He had guaranteed them of victory. This is the meaning of God defending those whom He defended with those who fought Goliath and his soldiers from among His friends. So it is clear that the reading of those who read:
h
And had God not repelled some people by means of others
, and the reading of those who read: And had God not defended some people by means of others, are the same in interpretation and meaning.

evidence.text: As for the readings, they differed in the reading of his saying: And had God not repelled some people by means of others.
A group of the readings read it: And had God not repelled as a source, from the saying of the one who says: God repelled His creation, so He repels a repelling.
Another group of the readings read it: And had God not defended the people as a source, from the saying of the one who says: God defended His creation, so He defends a repelling and a defense.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The statement in that, in my opinion, is that they are two readings that the readings have read, and the group of the nation has come with them, and there is no change in the meaning of the other in the reading with one of the two letters.

So it is clear that the reading of those who read: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, and the reading of those who read: And had God not defended some people by means of others, are the same in interpretation and meaning.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
These are the signs of God

, these are the signs in which God recounts the matter of those who left their homes by the thousands for fear of death, and the matter of the leaders of the Children of Israel after Moses who asked their prophet to send them Talut as a king, and the signs that follow until His saying: But God is full of bounty to the worlds. By his saying:
h
The signs of God

, he means His arguments, signs, and proofs. God the Most High says: These are the arguments that I have informed you of, O Muhammad, and made known to you - of My ability to kill in one hour those who fled from death, and they are thousands, and My bringing them back to life after that, and My giving Talut the rule of the Children of Israel after he had been a water-carrier or a tanner from outside the household of the kingdom, and My taking that away from him because of his disobedience to My command, and My transferring his kingdom to David because of his obedience to Me, and My giving victory to the companions of Talut despite their small number and weak power over Goliath and his soldiers despite their large number and severe violence - My arguments against those who denied My blessings, disobeyed My command, and disbelieved in My Messenger from the People of the Two Books, the Torah and the Gospel, who know what I have related to you of the hidden report that they know is from Me.

You, O Muhammad, did not make it up or fabricate it, because you are illiterate and not one of those who have read the books, so that they would be confused about your matter, and they would claim that you read that and learned it from some of their books. But these are My arguments against them, which I recite to you, O Muhammad, with the certain truth as it was, without any addition, distortion, or change in any of it from what it was. And indeed, you, O Muhammad, are among the messengers. He says: Indeed, you are a messenger who is followed in My obedience and in preferring My pleasure over your own desires. So follow in this matter of yours the path of My messengers who came before you, who adhered to My command and preferred My pleasure over their own desires, and were not changed by desires and worldly ambitions, just as Talut changed his desire and preferred his kingdom over what I have for the people of My authority.

But you prefer My command as the messengers who came before you preferred it. The second part is complete, and it will be followed, God willing, by the third part of the third volume, and it begins with: The statement on the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “These are the messengers. We have preferred some of them over others.”

evidence.text: You, O Muhammad, did not make it up or fabricate it, because you are illiterate and not one of those who have read the books, so that they would be confused about your matter, and they would claim that you read that and learned it from some of their books.

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: “These are the messengers.
We preferred some of them over others. Among them were those to whom God spoke, and He raised some of them in degrees.”

By His saying, Those, the Almighty means the messengers whose stories God narrated in this Surah, such as Moses, son of Imran, Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel, David, and all those whose stories He mentioned in this Surah.

The Almighty says: These are My messengers, some of whom I have favored over others, so I spoke to some of them, and the one I spoke to among them was Moses, peace be upon him, and I raised some of them in degrees over others, with honor and high status, as:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: “These are the messengers. We have favored some of them over others,” he said: He says: Among them are those to whom God spoke, and He raised some of them in degrees above others. He says: God spoke to Moses, and sent Muhammad to all people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. What indicates the correctness of what we said in this regard is: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given five things that were not given to anyone before me: I have been sent to the red and the black, I have been aided by terror, for the enemy is terrified by me from a distance of a month’s journey, the earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me, spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and they were not made lawful for anyone before me, and it was said to me: Ask and you will be given, so I saved it as intercession for my nation, and it will be granted to you, God willing, by those who do not associate anything with God.”

x: The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And We gave Jesus
, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit.
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
And We gave Jesus
, son of Mary, clear proofs,
h
and We gave Jesus

, son of Mary, the arguments and evidence of his prophethood: healing the blind and the leper and raising the dead and the like, along with the Gospel that I revealed to him, in which I explained what was imposed upon him. And the Most High means by His saying:
h
And We supported him

, and strengthened him and aided him, with the Holy Spirit, meaning with the Spirit of God, who is Gabriel. We have already mentioned the difference of opinion among the scholars regarding the meaning of with the Holy Spirit, which is more correct than what was said about it in what came before, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying:
h
And if God had willed
, those who came after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them.

God Almighty means by that: If God had willed, those who came after them would not have fought, meaning: after the messengers whom He described as having preferred some of them over others and raised some of them in degrees, and after Jesus, son of Mary, who came to them with signs that contained a deterrent for whomever God guided and granted success. What he means by his saying:
h
After the clear proofs came to them

, is: after the signs of God came to them that made the truth clear to them and made the path clear to them. It has been said that the ha and the mim in his saying: after them are from the mention of Moses and Jesus.
Who said that? Surat Al-Baqarah 2:253 These are the messengers, some of whom We have favored over others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and He raised some of them in degrees.
h
And We gave Jesus
, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. And if Allah had willed, those after them would not have fought after the clear proofs had come to them, but they differed.
Some of them believed, and some of them disbelieved. He disbelieved. If God had willed, they would not have fought. But God does what He wills.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if God had willed
, those who came after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them, meaning: after Moses and Jesus.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
And if God had willed
, those who came after them would not have fought one another after the clear proofs had come to them. He said: after Moses and Jesus.

x: By that, the Most High meant: But those who came after the messengers differed, because God, the Most High, did not will that they not fight, so they fought
h
after the clear proofs came to them

from their Lord prohibiting fighting and disagreement, and after the proof was established against them regarding the Oneness of God, the message of His messengers, and the revelation of His Book. So some of them disbelieved in God and His verses, and some of them believed in that.

c: So the Most High informed us that
m: they did what they did of disbelief and sins, after they knew that the proof had been established against them that they were in error, deliberately disbelieving in God and His verses. Then the Most High said to His servants:
h
And if God had willed

, they would not have fought, meaning: If God had wanted to prevent them - by His protection and guidance for them - from disobeying Him so that they would not fight, they would not have fought or differed, but God does what He wills, by granting this one success in obeying Him and believing in Him, so he believes in Him and obeys Him, and letting this one down, so he disbelieves in Him and disobeys Him.

x: God Almighty means by that: O you who believe, spend in the way of God from what We have provided you of your wealth, and give in charity from it, and give from it the rights that We have imposed upon you.
And Ibn Jurayj used to say the same, according to what we have heard from him:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, spend from what We have provided for you, he said: from zakat and voluntary acts. Before a Day comes when there is no trading, no friendship, and no intercession, meaning: Save for yourselves with God in this world from your wealth, by spending from it in the way of God, and giving charity to the poor and needy, and giving what God has made obligatory upon you in it, and buy with it what He has prepared for His friends of honor, by presenting that for yourselves as long as you have the path to buying it through what I have called you to and commanded you to do of spending from your wealth, before a Day comes when there is no trading, meaning: before a Day comes when there is no trading, meaning: you will not be able to buy what you used to buy - by spending from your wealth that I have provided for you - by what I have commanded you to do or called you to do in this world, being able, because it is a day of recompense, reward, and punishment, not a day of work, earning, and obedience over disobedience, so you will have a path to the ranks of the people of honor by spending at that time - or by working in obedience to God.

c: Then the Most High informed them that
m: on that day, with the increase in the work by which one attains the pleasure of God or attains His honor by spending money, since there was no money there with which that could be attained, there will be no beneficial friendship as there was in this world, for a man’s friend in this world would benefit him therein by supporting him against whoever tried to harm him and wanted to harm him, and by supporting him in that. So He, the Most High, also made them despair of that, because no one on the Day of Resurrection will help anyone against God. Rather, Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous (al-Zukhruf 43:67), as God, the Most High, said.

c: He also informed them that
m: on that Day, with their loss of the way to buy what they had the way to buy in this world by spending from their money and working with their bodies, and their lack of helpers from friends and supporters from brothers, they will have no intercessor to intercede with God, as they had in this world.

x: Some of them used to intercede for others in this world by kinship, neighborhood, friendship, and other reasons, but all of that will be invalidated on that Day, as God, the Most High, informed us about what His enemies from the people of Hell will say in the Hereafter when they are in it: So we will have no intercessors * Nor a close friend (Ash-Shu’ara’: 100, 101). This verse is general in its interpretation of intercession, but its intended meaning is specific. Rather, its meaning is: Before a Day comes in which there will be no trading, no friendship, and no intercession, for the people who disbelieve in God. Because the people of God’s guardianship and belief in Him intercede for one another. We have explained the validity of that in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here.
Qatada used to say about this:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, spend from what We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there will be no exchange, no friendship, and no intercession. God knows that people love one another in this world and intercede for one another. But as for the Day of Resurrection, there will be no friendship except the friendship of the righteous. As for his statement:
h
And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers

, then God Almighty means by that: And those who deny God and reject Him and His messengers, are the wrongdoers, meaning: They are those who put their denial in the wrong place, and do things other than what they are supposed to do, and say things that they are not supposed to say. We have already demonstrated the meaning of injustice with evidence in the past, so there is no need to repeat it.

x: In the words of God Almighty in this place:
h
And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers

, there is clear evidence of the correctness of what we have said, and that His words: nor friendship nor intercession, are only intended for the people of disbelief, and therefore He followed that with His words:
h
And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers

. Thus He indicated that the meaning of that is: We deprived the disbelievers of support from friends, and intercession from friends and relatives, and We were not wrongdoers towards them in doing that to them, since that was a punishment from Us for what they had done previously of disbelief in God in this world. Rather, the disbelievers are the wrongdoers themselves because of the actions they committed for which they deserved punishment from their Lord.
How was the threat directed to the infidels, when the verse begins with mentioning the people of faith?

The verse preceded it by mentioning two types of al-Nas 114:one of them is the people of disbelief, and the other is the people of faith, and that is His saying: But they differed, and among them were those who believed and those who disbelieved (al-Baqarah 2:253).

Then God the Most High followed up His mention of the two groups with what He mentioned to them, by urging the people of faith in Him to do what brings them closer to Him by spending in His obedience, and in fighting His enemies from among the people of disbelief in Him, before the coming of the day whose description He described, and in which He informed about the state of His enemies from among the people of disbelief in Him, since fighting the people of disbelief in Him was in disobeying Him, and their spending was in blocking people from His path, so He the Most High said:
h
O you who have believed

, spend from what We have provided you in My obedience, since the people of disbelief in Me used to spend in disobeying Me, before a day comes in which there is no trading, and the people of disbelief will be overtaken by buying what they neglected to buy in their worldly life, and they will have no friend on that day to help them against Me, and no intercessor for them who will intercede with Me so that his intercession for them will save them from My punishment.

And this is on that day, My punishment upon them is for their disbelief, and they are the wrongdoers themselves rather than Me, because I am not unjust to My servants. And: Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim told me, he said, Amr bin Abi Salamah told me, he said, I heard Omar bin Sulayman narrating, on the authority of Ata bin Dinar, that he said: Praise be to God who said,
h
And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers
, and did not say: The wrongdoers are the disbelievers.

We have previously demonstrated the interpretation of his saying: God. As for the interpretation of His statement: There is no god but He, its meaning is: the prohibition of worshipping anything other than God, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, whose description is what He described Himself with, may He be exalted, in this verse.

i: He says:
x: God to whom the worship of creation belongs, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, there is no god but Him, there is no deity but Him.

Meaning: And do not worship anything other than the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, Whom neither drowsiness overtakes nor sleep, and whose description is what He described in this verse. This verse is a clarification from God Almighty to those who believe in Him and His Messenger regarding what the different clear proofs brought after the messengers, whom God Almighty informed us that He preferred some of them over others, and they differed about it and fought over it, some out of disbelief in it and some out of belief in it. Praise be to God who has guided us to believe in Him and enabled us to acknowledge Him. As for His statement, the Living, it means the One who has eternal life and permanence that has no beginning with a limit and no end with a term, since everything other than Him, if it were living, then its life would have a limited beginning and an extended end that ends when its term ends and ends when its end comes to an end.
And what we said about that was said by a group of people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar bin Al-Hassan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, regarding his saying: The Living, the Living who does not die.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

x: The scholars differed in their interpretation of this.

Some of them said: God called Himself Alive because He directs matters according to their proper course and determines things according to their proper measures. He is Alive by management, not by life.
Others said: Rather, he is alive with a life that is an attribute of his.

Others said: Rather, it is one of the names by which he was called, so we said in submission to his command. As for his saying: Al-Qayyum, it is the fa’ul from the word qiyam and its root is al-qayyum. The ‘ayn of the verb, which is a waw, was preceded by a silent ya’, and they merged and became a doubled ya’. The Arabs do the same with every waw that is the ‘ayn of the verb and is preceded by a silent ya’. The meaning of his saying: Al-Qayyum is the one who provides for what He created and preserves, as Umayyah said: The sky, the stars, the sun, and the moon were not created to float with it. His power is the Dominant, the Self-Sustaining, the Bridge, Heaven and Hell Except for a matter of great importance And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: The Self-Sustaining, he said: The One who is in charge of everything.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Jaʿfar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Al-Qayyum is the guardian of everything, He protects it, provides for it, and preserves it.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Al-Qayyum, meaning the One who is upright.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: The Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, he said: The Ever-Sustaining, the Eternal.

x: God Almighty means by His statement,
h
He is not overcome by drowsiness
, that
h
he is not overcome by drowsiness
so that he dozes off, nor by sleep so that he finds sleep heavy.

i: And drowsiness is the soundness of sleep, and from it is the saying of Adi bin Al-Ruqa’: And Sinan, I mean sleepiness, I saw a squint in his eye, but he is not asleep And the evidence for what we said:
x: that it is the coagulation of sleep in the human eye, is the saying of Al-A’sha Maymun bin Qais: Sleeping with the bed partner if you come after drowsiness and before sleep Another said: The strangers came early in the year of sleep, and it ran through the thorns of the stream.

Meaning: When she wakes up from sleep, and the drowsiness of sleep is in her eyes. It is said: So-and-so is asleep, so he is asleep, sleep, and sleepiness, and he is sleepy, if he is like that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the Almighty’s statement:
h
He is not overtaken by drowsiness
, he said: drowsiness is drowsiness, and sleep is sleep.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He is not overcome by drowsiness
, drowsiness is drowsiness.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada and al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He is not overtaken by drowsiness
, they said: drowsiness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him
, he said: Drowsiness is drowsiness, and it is less than sleep, and sleep is heaviness.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
He is not overcome by drowsiness
or sleep. Drowsiness is drowsiness, and sleep is heaviness.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me: Yazid told us: Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: the same.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
He is not overcome by drowsiness
or sleep. As for sleepy, it is the smell of sleep that takes hold of the face and makes a person drowsy.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
h
He is not overcome by drowsiness
or sleep. He said: Drowsiness, drowsiness: between sleeping and being awake.

c: Abbas bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Munjab bin Al-Harith told us, he said, Ali bin Masaher told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Yahya bin Rafi’:
m: h
He is not overtaken by drowsiness
, he said: drowsiness.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
He is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep
, he said: the drowsy one, who gets up from sleep without reason, to the point that he might take up the sword against his family.

x: What God Almighty meant by His statement,
h
Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him

, is that He is not afflicted by plagues nor affected by disabilities. This is because drowsiness and sleep are two meanings that overwhelm the understanding of the one with understanding, and remove the one who is afflicted by them from the state he was in before they afflicted him. The interpretation of the statement, since the matter is as we have described: God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living who does not die, the Self-Sustainer over all that is below Him in provision, provision, management, and disposition from one state to another,
h
He is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep

, what changes others does not change Him, nor does He remove Him from what He has always been in, the changing of states and the disposition of nights and days, rather He is the Everlasting in one state, and the Self-Sustainer over all of creation.

If He slept, He would be overcome and subdued, because sleep Surat Al-Baqarah 2:255 Allah - there is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Drowsiness does not overtake Him nor sleep.
h
To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth
. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?
h
He knows what is before them

and what is behind them, but they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills. His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth. And He is not tired of preserving them, and He is the Most High, the Most Great. overcomes and subdues the sleeper. If He were to sleep, the heavens and the earth and everything in them would be leveled, because the existence of all that is by His management and power.
Sleep distracts the manager from management, and drowsiness prevents the one who is destined from being destined by His sleep, as:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, he said: Al-Hakam bin Abaan narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God: Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep, that Moses asked the angels: Does God sleep? So God inspired the angels and commanded them to keep him awake for three days, and not to let him sleep. So they did, then they gave him two bottles and held him back, then they left him and warned him not to break them. He said: So he began to doze off while they were in his hands, one in each hand. He said: So he began to doze off and wake up, and doze off and wake up, until he dozed off a moment and struck one of them with the other and broke them. Muammar said: It is only a parable that God made, meaning: So are the heavens and the earth in His hands.

c: Ishaq bin Abi Israel narrated to us, he said, Hisham bin Yusuf narrated to us, on the authority of Umayyah bin Shibl, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating from Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the pulpit. He said: It occurred to Moses’ mind: Does God, the Most High, sleep? So God sent an angel to him who kept him awake for three days, then gave him two bottles, one in each hand, and ordered him to keep them. He said: So he began to sleep and his hands almost met, then he would wake up and hold one of them away from the other. Then he slept and his hands were aligned and the two bottles broke. He said: God gave him an example that if God were to sleep, the heavens and the earth would not be able to hold together.”

x: What the Most High means by His statement,
h
To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth

, is that He is the Owner of all of that without partner or equal, and the Creator of all of it without any gods or objects of worship. What He means by that is that nothing should be worshipped other than Him, because the slave is at the disposal of his Master, and he has no service to anyone other than Him except by His command.

i: He says:
x: So everything in the heavens and the earth is My property and My creation, so no one of My creation should be worshipped other than Me, and I am its Owner, because the slave should not worship anyone other than his Master, and he should not obey anyone other than his Master. As for his saying:
h
Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission

He means by that: Who is he that can intercede for His slaves if He wants to punish them, unless He leaves him alone and permits him to intercede for them? And the Almighty said that because the polytheists said: We only worship these idols of ours so that they may bring us closer to God! So God the Almighty said to them: What is in the heavens and what is on the earth is Mine, along with the heavens and the earth, so worship should not belong to anyone other than Me. So do not worship the idols that you claim bring you closer to Me, for they do not benefit you with Me nor do they avail you at all. And no one can intercede with Me for anyone except by leaving him alone, and intercession is for whoever intercedes for him, from among My messengers, My saints, and those who obey Me.

God Almighty means by that: He encompasses everything that was and everything that will be, with knowledge that nothing of it is hidden from Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Hakam:
m: h
He knows what is before them
, the world, and what is behind them, the Hereafter.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
He knows what is before them
, what has passed of this world, and what is behind them, of the Hereafter.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: His statement,
h
He knows what is before them
, is what has passed before them of this world, and what is behind them, is what will come after them of this world and the Hereafter.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
He knows what is before them
, he said: [As for] what is before them, it is the world, [as for], and what is behind them, it is the Hereafter. As for His statement:
h
And they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills

, He, the Most High, means that He is the All-Knowing from whom nothing is hidden, encompassing all of that, and He knows it without anyone else besides Him, and that no one knows anything besides Him except what He wills to know, so He willed it and knew it. What He means by that is that worship is not established for one who is ignorant of things, so how can one who does not understand anything at all worship an idol or a statue?! He says: So devote worship to the One who encompasses all things, knows them, and nothing, small or great, is hidden from Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge, he says: they do not know anything of His knowledge, except what He wills, that is, that He teaches them.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the Throne, which God Almighty mentioned in this verse that it encompasses the heavens and the earth.
Some of them said: It is the knowledge of God Almighty.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib and Salim bin Janadah told us, they said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Jaʿfar bin Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: His Throne encompasses His knowledge. He said: His Throne encompasses His knowledge.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us: Mutraf told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar bin Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly, and he added to it: Do you not see his saying:
h
And their preservation does not burden Him

x: Others said: The chair is the place for the feet.
Who said that?

c: Ali bin Muslim al-Tusi told me, he said, Abd al-Samad bin Abd al-Warith told us, he said, my father told me, he said, Muhammad bin Juhada told me, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, on the authority of Ammarah bin Umair, on the authority of Abu Musa, he said:
m: The chair is the place for the feet, and it makes a creaking sound like the creaking of a saddle.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth
, for the heavens and the earth are in the interior of the Throne, and the Throne is between the hands of the Throne, and it is the place of His feet.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
His throne encompasses the heavens and the earth
, he said: His throne is the one that is placed under the throne, on which the kings place their feet.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ammar Al-Dahni, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin, who said:
m: The chair is the place of the feet.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ:
h
His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth
. He said: When the verse
h
His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth

was revealed, the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Messenger of God, this Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth, so how about the Throne? So God Almighty revealed: And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal until His saying: Glory be to Him and He is exalted above what they associate with Him. (al-Zumar 39:67) Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement,
h
His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth
, Ibn Zayd said:

c: My father told me, he said,
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The seven heavens in comparison to the Throne are like seven dirhams thrown into a shield.’” He said, “And Abu Dharr said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘The Throne in comparison to the Throne is like an iron ring thrown into a desert on the earth.’”

x: Others said: The chair is the throne itself.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: The Kursi is the Throne.

x: Each of these sayings has a face and a school of thought, but what is more deserving of the interpretation of the verse is what came in the hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is what:

c: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad Al-Qatwani told me, he said, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Khalifa, he said:
m: “A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘Pray to God to admit me into Paradise!’ So the Lord, may He be glorified, glorified Him, then said: ‘
h
His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth

, and He sits on it and nothing of it is left the size of four fingers - then he said with his fingers and gathered them together - and it makes a creaking sound like the creaking of a new saddle when it is ridden, because of its weight.”

c: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told me, he said, Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Khalifa, on the authority of Umar, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Khalifa, who said:
m: A woman came, and he mentioned something similar. As for what indicates its authenticity from the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, it is the statement of Ibn Abbas, which was narrated by Ja’far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on his authority that he Surat Al-Baqarah 2:255 Allah - there is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Drowsiness does not overtake Him nor sleep.
h
To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth
. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?
h
He knows what is before them

and what is behind them, but they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills. His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth. And He is not tired of preserving them, and He is the Most High, the Most Great. said: It is His knowledge. This is because the statement of the Most High: And He is not burdened by their preservation indicates that this is the case. So He informed that He is not burdened by the preservation of what He knows and encompasses of what is in the heavens and the earth. Just as He informed about His angels that they said in their supplication: Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge
r
(Ghafir 40:7)
, so the Most High informed that His knowledge is with everything, so is His statement:
h
His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth

x: The origin of the word kursi is knowledge. From this, the word book is used for a document containing written knowledge.

i: From this, the rajaz poet said in describing a hunter: Even if he acquired it, it would be consecrated It means knowledge, and from this scholars are called chairs, because they are the ones who are relied upon, just as it is said: the pegs of the earth, meaning by this that they are the scholars through whom the earth is made good, and from this the poet said:
x: They are surrounded by white faces and a group of chairs when events come He means by this: knowledgeable about the incidents and calamities of things.

The Arabs call the origin of everything, the throne, and it is said from it: So-and-so is generous of the throne, meaning generous of origin. Al-Ajjaj said: The Holy One, the Master of Jerusalem, knows that Abu al-Abbas is more deserving of the soul. With the metal of the generous king He means by that: the noble in origin, and it is narrated: In the noble and honorable mine The statement in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And He is not burdened by their preservation, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.

And he does not find it difficult or burdensome to memorize them, nor does it burden him. It is said: This matter has brought me closer, so it is bringing me closer and closer. It is also said: What has brought you closer is bringing me closer, meaning: What has burdened you is burdensome to me. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And their preservation does not burden Him
, meaning: it does not burden Him.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And their preservation does not burden Him
, he said: Their preservation does not burden Him.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their preservation does not burden Him
, their preservation does not burden Him, their preservation does not exhaust Him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatadah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their preservation does not burden Him
, he said: Nothing is burdensome to Him.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me, he said, Yusuf bin Khalid Al-Samti told us, he said, Nafi’ bin Malik told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their preservation does not burden Him
, he said: Their preservation does not burden Him.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, and Yahya bin Abi Talib told us, he said, Yazid told us,
m: they both said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
h
And their preservation does not burden Him
, he said: It does not burden Him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Ubaid, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: similarly.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I heard him - meaning Khallad - say: I heard Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Madini say about this verse: And their preservation does not tire Him, they said: It does not burden Him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa bin Maimun, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And their preservation does not tire Him, he said: He does not tire Him.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And their preservation does not burden Him
, he said: It does not burden Him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
And their preservation does not burden Him
, meaning: their preservation does not burden Him.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their preservation does not burden Him
, he said: Their preservation does not become difficult for Him.

x: The ha, mim and alif in His statement, He preserved them, are from the mention of the heavens and the earth. So the interpretation of the statement is:
h
His throne encompasses the heavens and the earth

, and preserving the heavens and the earth is not burdensome to Him. As for the interpretation of his saying: And He is the Most High, it means: And God is the Most High. The active participle of the word al-‘Ali is derived from the phrase ala which means to rise up. So, he is alif and ali. The alif is the one who is elevated and raised above his creation by his power.
And also his saying: The Great, the One with greatness to whom everything is inferior, so nothing is greater than Him, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: The Great is the one who has been perfected in his greatness.

x: The scholars differed regarding the meaning of his saying: And He is the Most High.

Some of them said: By that he means: He is the Most High above all other similarities and likenesses. They denied that the meaning of that is: He is the Most High in place. They said: It is not permissible for a place to be devoid of Him, and there is no meaning to describing Him as being high in place, because that is describing Him as being in a place rather than a place.

Others said: The meaning of this is: He is the Most High over His creation, by the elevation of His place above the places of His creation. Because He, the Most High, is mentioned above all of His creation, and His creation is below Him, just as He described Himself as being on the Throne, so He is thus high above them. They also differed on the meaning of his saying: the Great.
Some of them said: The meaning of the great in this place is: the most important.

i: The verb maf’al was changed to fa’il, just as it was said of aged wine, aged wine, as the poet said:
x: As if the old wine from the Isfanat was mixed with pure water Rather, it is freed.

They said: His saying, The Great, means: The One Who is glorified, Whom His creation glorifies, fears, and is devout toward. They said: The statement of the speaker, He is great, can only have two meanings: One is what we have described, that He is glorified, and the other is that He is great in area and weight. They said: And in the length of the statement that the meaning of that is that He is great in area and weight, the statement of what we have said is correct.
Others said: Rather, the interpretation of His saying:
h
The Great is that He has a greatness that is an attribute of His

. They said: We do not describe His greatness with a manner, but we attribute that to Him from the aspect of affirmation, and we deny that it is in the sense of resembling the greatness known to the servants. Because that is likening Him to His creation, and it is not like that. These people denied what the people of the article that we mentioned earlier said, and they said: If the meaning of that was that He is great, then it would be necessary that He was not great before He created creation, and that the meaning of that would be nullified when creation perishes, because He has no greatness in these circumstances.

Others said: Rather, His saying that He is the Great is a description of Himself as great. They said: Everything that is less than Him of His creation has the meaning of smallness, because they are small compared to His greatness.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that.

Some of them said: This verse was revealed about a group of the Ansar - or about a man from them - who had children whom they had converted to Judaism or Christianity. When God brought Islam, they wanted to force them to convert to Islam, but God forbade them from doing so until they themselves chose to enter Islam.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: A woman would be a miser, and she would promise herself that if she had a child alive, she would convert him to Judaism. When Banu Nadir were expelled, there were some of the sons of the Ansar among them, so they said: We will not abandon our sons! Then God Almighty revealed: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion
. The right course has become distinct from error.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: A woman would be maimed and her children would not survive - Shuʿbah said: Rather, they were maimed - so she would make a covenant with him if she had a surviving child to convert him to Judaism. He said: When Banu Nadir were expelled, some of them were among them, so the Ansar said: What should we do with our children? Then this verse was revealed: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion

. Verily, the right course has become distinct from error.” He said: Whoever wishes to stay may stay, and whoever wishes to go may go. Humayd ibn Masʿadah narrated, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated, Dawud narrated, and Yaʿqub narrated, Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of ʿAmir, who said: There was a woman from the Ansar who was poor and did not have a living child. She would vow that if her child lived, she would leave him with the People of the Book according to their religion. Then Islam came and groups of the sons of the Ansar were following their religion. They said: We only made them follow their religion while we thought that their religion was better than ours! But when God brought Islam, we will force them! Then this verse was revealed:
h
There is no compulsion in religion
. So there was a distinction between those who chose Judaism and Islam. Those who joined them chose Judaism, and those who stayed chose Islam. The wording of the hadith is that of Humayd.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I heard Dawud, on the authority of Amer, with a similar meaning, except that he said: The separation between them was the expulsion of the Banu Nadir by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so those of them who were Jews but did not convert to Islam joined them, and those who converted to Islam remained.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer,
m: something similar, except that he said: The expulsion of Al-Nadir to Khaybar, so whoever chose Islam stayed, and whoever disliked it went to Khaybar.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad al-Harashi,
m: the client of Zayd ibn Thabit, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion

. Verily, the right way has become distinct from error.” He said: It was revealed about a man from the Ansar from Banu Salim ibn Awf, called al-Husayn, who had two Christian sons, and he was a Muslim man. So he said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Should I not compel them, for they have refused to accept anything but Christianity? So God revealed that about him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, who said:
m: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about the statement: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion

. Verily, the right course has become distinct from error.” He said: This was revealed about the Ansar. I said: Especially? He said: Especially! He said: A woman in the pre-Islamic period would vow that if she gave birth to a child, she would place him among the Jews, seeking thereby to prolong his life. He said: Then Islam came and they were among them. When the Nadir were expelled, they said: O Messenger of God, are our children and brothers among them? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent about them, then God revealed: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion

. Verily, the right course has become distinct from error.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your companions have been given a choice. If they choose you, then they are of you, and if they choose them, then they are of them.” He said: Then expel them with them.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion

. Verily, the right course has become distinct from error” to There is no separation in it, he said: “It was revealed about a man from the Ansar called Abu Al-Hussain, who had two sons. Some merchants from Ash-Sham came to Madinah carrying oil. When they sold and wanted to return, the sons of Abu Al-Hussain came to them and invited them to Christianity. They became Christians and returned to Ash-Sham with them. Then their father came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My sons have become Christians and have left. Should I seek them out? He said: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion

,” and he was not commanded that day to fight the People of the Book. He said: May God distance them! They are the first to disbelieve! Abu Al-Hussain felt sorry for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he did not send for them, so the verse was revealed: “But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission”
r
(An-Nisa’: 65)
. Then it was abrogated:
h
There is no compulsion in religion
, so he ordered fighting the People of the Book in Surat Bara’ah.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
There is no compulsion in religion

, he said: The Jews, the Jews of Banu Nadir, were breast-feeding men from the Aws, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered their expulsion, their sons from the Aws said: We will go with them, and we will follow their religion! But their families prevented them and forced them to convert to Islam, and this verse was revealed about them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, and Ahmad ibn Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
There is no compulsion in religion
. He said: There were some people from the Ansar who were being breastfed by Banu Qurayzah, and they wanted to force them to convert to Islam, so this verse was revealed: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion
. The right course has become distinct from error.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said:
m: The Nadir were Jews and they were breastfed, then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Asim, Ibn Jurayj said, and Abd al-Karim informed me, on the authority of Mujahid: that the sons of the Aws had followed their religion, they followed the religion of the Nadir.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Shaʿbi:
m: That a woman from the Ansar used to vow that if her son lived, she would make him one of the People of the Book. Then when Islam came, the Ansar said: O Messenger of God, should we not force our children who are Jews to convert to Islam? We only made them into it because we see that Judaism is the best religion. But since God brought Islam, should we not force them to convert to Islam? Then God, the Most High, revealed: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion
. Verily, the right way has become distinct from error.”

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi, similarly, and he added: The distinction between those who chose the Jews among them and those who chose Islam was the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir. So whoever went out with Banu al-Nadir was one of them, and whoever left them chose Islam.
