c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no compulsion in religion to his statement
: the firmest handhold, he said: This is abrogated.

c: Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Razi told me, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid and Wa’il, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Some people from the Ansar were being breastfed by Banu Al-Nadir, and when they were exiled, their families wanted to bring them back to their religion, so the verse was revealed:
h
There is no compulsion in religion

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: The People of the Book are not forced to change their religion if they pay the jizya, but they are allowed to remain in their religion. They said: The verse is specifically for the infidels, and nothing was abrogated from it.
Who said that? Surat Al-Baqarah 2:256
h
There is no compulsion in religion
. The right way has become distinct from the wrong.
h
So whoever disbelieves in Taghut
and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

c: Bishr bin Muadh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
There is no compulsion in religion

. Verily, the right way has become distinct from the wrong.” He said: This tribe of Arabs was forced into it because they were an illiterate nation and had no book that they knew of, so nothing was accepted from them except Islam. And the People of the Book are not forced into it if they acknowledge the jizya or the kharaj and are not tempted away from their religion, so they are released.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Sulayman told us, Abu Hilal told us, Qatada told us
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no compulsion in religion

, he said: It is this tribe of Arabs, they were forced into religion, nothing was accepted from them except killing or Islam, and the People of the Book had the jizya accepted from them, and they were not killed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us, Amr bin Qais told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no compulsion in religion

, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to fight the idolaters of the Arabian Peninsula, and he did not accept from them anything but: There is no god but God, or the sword. Then he commanded that the jizya be accepted from those other than them, and he said: “
h
There is no compulsion in religion
. The right path has become distinct from the wrong path.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no compulsion in religion
, he said: The Arabs had no religion, so they were forced into religion by the sword. He said: And the Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians are not to be compelled, if they pay the jizyah.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say to his Christian slave: O Jarir, convert to Islam. Then he said: This is what they used to say to him.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
There is no compulsion in religion
. Verily, the right course has become distinct from error.” He said: That was when the people entered Islam and the People of the Book paid the jizya.

x: Others said: This verse is abrogated, and was revealed before fighting was made obligatory.
Who said that?

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ya’qub bin Abdul Rahman Al-Zuhri told me, he said:
m: I asked Zaid bin Aslam about the statement of God Almighty:
h
There is no compulsion in religion

. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca for ten years and did not compel anyone in religion, but the polytheists refused except to fight them, so he asked God’s permission to fight them and He gave him permission.

x: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: This verse was revealed concerning a specific group of people. He said: What he meant by the words of God Almighty:
h
There is no compulsion in religion

are the People of the Book, the Magians, and everyone who came to affirm his religion that was contrary to the religion of truth and took the jizya from him, and they denied that any of it was abrogated. We said: This statement is the most correct of the statements on this matter, because we have demonstrated in our book Kitab al-Latif min al-Bayan ‘an Usul al-Ahkam: that the abrogating verse is not the abrogator except for that which negates the ruling of the abrogated, so it is not permissible for them to come together. As for that which appears to be general in terms of commands and prohibitions, but its inner meaning is specific, then it is separate from the abrogating and abrogated.
And since that was the case, and it was not impossible to say:
h
There is no compulsion in religion

for anyone from whom the jizyah was taken, and there was no evidence in the verse that its interpretation was otherwise, and all the Muslims had transmitted from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he forced a people to Islam and they refused to accept anything from them except Islam, and he ruled that they should be killed if they refused it, such as the idolaters among the polytheists of the Arabs, and the one who apostatized from his religion, the religion of truth, to disbelief and those like them, and that he left the compulsion of others to Islam by accepting the jizyah from him and confirming his false religion, such as the People of the Book and those like them, it was clear from that that the meaning of his saying:
h
There is no compulsion in religion is that there is no compulsion in religion for anyone from whom it was permissible to accept the jizyah by
paying the jizyah and accepting the rule of Islam.
There is no meaning to the claim of those who claim that the verse abrogated the ruling, by permitting war.

What do you say about what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and those who narrated on his authority: that it was revealed about a group of Ansar who wanted to force their children to convert to Islam?

This is not proven to be true, but the verse may have been revealed for a specific matter, and then its ruling is general for everything that is similar in meaning to the one it was revealed for. Those about whom this verse was revealed - according to what Ibn Abbas and others mentioned - were people who followed the religion of the people of the Torah before the contract of Islam was established for them, so God Almighty forbade forcing them to convert to Islam, and He revealed a verse forbidding that, the ruling of which applies to everyone who is in the same category as them, who follows a religion from which it is permissible to take the jizyah and to confirm it with them, in the manner we have mentioned about that.
The meaning of his saying:
h
There is no compulsion in religion is that no one is forced to follow the religion of Islam
. The definite article was inserted into religion to define the religion that God meant by His saying:
h
There is no compulsion in it

, and that it is Islam. It may be possible that they were inserted after the letter ha’ that was mentioned in the religion, and the meaning of the statement then would be: He is the Most High, the Most Great, there is no compulsion in His religion, right guidance has become distinct from error. And this statement seems to me to be more similar to the interpretation of the verse.
As for his saying:
h
The right path has become clear

, it is a source of the saying of the speaker: I have been guided, so I am guided, guidance, guidance, and guidance, and that is if he hits the truth and the right. As for al-ghay, it is a source of the saying of the speaker: So-and-so has gone astray, so he goes astray, ghayyan and ghayat. Some Arabs say: So-and-so went astray, and the correct reading is: Your companion has not gone astray, nor has he gone astray (al-Najm 53:2) with the fat-ha, and it is the more eloquent of the two languages, and that is if he transgressed the truth and exceeded it, he went astray. The interpretation of the statement then is: The truth has become clear from falsehood, and the direction of his quest has become clear to the seeker of truth and guidance, so he has been distinguished from misguidance and error. So do not force anyone from the People of the Book, and from whom you have permitted the taking of the jizya, to follow your religion, the religion of truth.
For whoever deviates from guidance after it has become clear to him, then his affair is with his Lord, and He is the Guardian of his punishment in his afterlife.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of Taghut.
Some of them said: It is the devil.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hassan bin Faid al-Absi, he said, Umar bin al-Khattab said:
m: The tyrant is the devil.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told me, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hassan bin Fa’id, on the authority of Umar,
m: similarly.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The tyrant is the devil.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Zakariya told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: The tyrant is the devil.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So whoever disbelieves in Taghut
, he said: Satan.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The tyrant is Satan.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
So whoever disbelieves in Taghut
, in Satan.

x: Others said: The tyrant is the magician.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-A’la told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Al-A’la, that he said:
m: The tyrant is the magician. Abdul-Ala was contradicted in this narration, and I will mention the disagreement later.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Hammad bin Masada told us, Aouf told us, on the authority of Muhammad, who said:
m: The tyrant is the magician.

x: Others said: Rather, the tyrant is the priest.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, he said:
m: The tyrant is the soothsayer.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Rafi’, he said:
m: The tyrant is the soothsayer.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
So whoever disbelieves in Taghut
, he said: Soothsayers upon whom devils descend, casting judgments on their tongues and hearts.

c: Abu Al-Zubayr told me, on the authority of Jabir Ibn Abdullah,
m: that he heard him say: -and he was asked about the tyrants to whom they used to turn for judgment, so he said-: There was one in Juhayna, and one in Aslam, in every tribe there was one, and they were soothsayers upon whom devils descended.

x: The correct statement regarding the tyrant, in my opinion, is that he is anyone who is tyrannical towards God and is worshipped instead of Him, either by force on the one who worships him, or by obedience on the part of the one who worships him, whether that worshipped person is a human being, a devil, an idol, a statue, or whatever it may be. I think that the root of taghut is taghut, from the saying of the speaker: someone transgressed, if he exceeded his limits, so he went beyond his bounds, like tyranny from arrogance, and khalboot from khalb, and similar names that come in the estimation of faʿaloot with the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:256
h
There is no compulsion in religion
. The right way has become distinct from the wrong.
h
So whoever disbelieves in Taghut
and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing. addition of waw and ta.

Then its lam - I mean the lam of taghut - was moved and given an ‘ayn, and its ‘ayn was changed and made in place of its lam, as was said: jadhab and jabadh, jadhhab and jabadh, saʿiqa and saʿiqa, and similar names that are in this example.

So the interpretation of the statement is: whoever denies the Lordship of every deity other than God, disbelieves in Him, and believes in God, meaning: and believes in God that He is his God, Lord, and object of worship, has grasped the firmest handhold, meaning: he has grasped the firmest thing to which one can grasp in seeking salvation for himself from God’s torment and punishment, as:

c: Ahmad bin Saeed bin Yaqoub Al-Kindi told me, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, Ibn Abi Maryam told us, on the authority of Hamid bin Uqbah, on the authority of Abu Dardaa:
m: That he visited a sick person from his neighbors and found him in the market, gurgling, and they did not understand what he wanted. So he asked them: Does he want to speak? They said: Yes, he wants to say: I believe in God and disbelieve in Taghut. Abu Dardaa said: How do you know that? They said: He kept repeating it until his tongue broke, so we know that he only wanted to utter it. Abu Dardaa said: Your companion has succeeded! God says: “
h
So whoever disbelieves in Taghut
and believes in God has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And God is Hearing and Knowing.”

x: The handle, in this place, is an example of the faith that the believer holds fast to, so he likened him in his attachment to it and his adherence to it to the one who holds fast to the handle of something that has a handle to which he holds fast, since everything that has a handle only holds fast to the handle of the one who wants it. God Almighty made the faith that the disbeliever in the tyrant who believes in God adheres to, one of the strongest bonds of all things, by saying: the most trustworthy. And al-Wathqa means the most trustworthy. It is said of a male: He is the most trustworthy, and of a female: She is the most trustworthy, just as it is said: So-and-so is the best, and So-and-so is the best. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: with the firmest handhold, he said: faith.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The firmest handhold is Islam.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Sawda’, on the authority of Ja’far - meaning Ibn Abi al-Mughira - on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He has grasped the firmest handhold
, he said: There is no god but God.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Sawda al-Nahdi, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
He has grasped the firmest handhold
, similarly.

x: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
It has no break

, it has no brokenness. The ha and the alif in His statement: it has refer back to the handle. The meaning of the words: Whoever disbelieves in the tyrant and believes in God, has held fast to the obedience of God in a way that he does not fear, while holding fast to it, that he will be let down by Him, and his submission when he needs Him in the terrors of the Hereafter, like one who holds fast to the firm bonds of things whose bonds he does not fear will break. The root of the word fasm is kasr, and from this comes the saying of A’sha of Banu Tha’labah: Her smile is different from the scattered plants, neither broken nor separated. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Its condition will never end
, he said: God does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
It has no break
, he said: It has no interruption.

x: God Almighty means, And God is All-Hearing, the belief of the believer in God alone and the disbeliever in the tyrant, when he acknowledges the oneness of God and disavows the rivals and idols that are worshipped besides God, All-Knowing of what he has resolved to do of the oneness of God and the sincerity of His Lordship in his heart, and what his conscience has concealed of disavowal of the gods, idols, and tyrants, and other than that which the soul of every one of His creation has concealed. No secret is hidden from Him, and no matter is hidden from Him, until He rewards each on the Day of Resurrection for what his tongue has uttered and his soul has concealed, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.

evidence.text: Some Arabs say: So-and-so went astray, and the correct reading is: Your companion has not gone astray, nor has he gone astray (al-Najm 53:2) with the fat-ha, and it is the more eloquent of the two languages, and that is if he transgressed the truth and exceeded it, he went astray.

x: God Almighty means by His statement:
h
God is the ally of those who believe

, He is their supporter and helper, and He takes care of them with His help and guidance. He brings them out from darknesses. He means by that: He brings them out from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith. Rather, what is meant by darkness in this place is disbelief. And He made darkness for disbelief an example because darkness obscures the sight from perceiving things in order to prove them, and likewise disbelief obscures the sight of the hearts from perceiving the truths of faith and knowledge of its soundness and the soundness of its causes. So the Most High informed His servants that He is the Guardian of the believers, and the One who makes them see the truth of faith, its paths, its laws, and its proofs, and He is their Guide and the One who guides them to His proofs that remove doubts from them, by revealing from them the motives for disbelief, and the darkness of its veils [from] the sight of the hearts.

c: Then the Most High informed us
m: about the people who disbelieved in Him, saying: And those who disbelieve, meaning those who deny His Oneness, their allies, meaning their supporters and helpers who support them, the Taghut, meaning the rivals and idols whom they worship instead of God, will lead them out of the light into darkness, meaning by light faith, as we have explained, into darkness, meaning by darkness the darkness of disbelief and its doubts that prevent the eyes of the hearts from seeing the light of faith, and the truths of its proofs and paths. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: “
h
God is the ally of those who believe

. He brings them out from darknesses into the light,” meaning: from misguidance to guidance. And those who disbelieve, their allies are the false gods, the devil. He brings them out from the light into darknesses, meaning: from guidance to misguidance.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: “God is the protector of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light.” The darkness is disbelief, and the light is faith. “And those who disbelieve, their protectors are false deities. They bring them out from the light into darknesses.” They bring them out from faith into disbelief.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding the words of God Almighty: “God is the protector of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light,” meaning: from disbelief to faith. “And those who disbelieve, their protectors are false deities. They bring them out from the light into darknesses,” meaning: from faith to disbelief.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abdah bin Abi Lubabah, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: or Muqsim, regarding the statement of God: “
h
God is the ally of those who believe

. He brings them out from darknesses into the light. As for those who disbelieve, their allies are false gods. They bring them out from the light into darkness.” He said: There were people who believed in Jesus, and people who disbelieved in him. Then when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, those who disbelieved in Jesus believed in him, and those who believed in Jesus disbelieved in him. That is, He brings those who disbelieved in Jesus to faith in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for those who disbelieve, their allies are false gods, they believed in Jesus and disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: They bring them out from the light into darkness.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I heard Mansur, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abdah bin Abi Lubabah, he said, regarding this verse: “God is the protector of those who believe. Surat al-Baqarah 2:257
h
God is the ally of those who believe

. He brings them out from darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve - their ally is Taghut. He brings them out from light into darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. He brings them out from darknesses into the light,” to Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally, he said: They are those who believed in Jesus, son of Mary, but when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them, they disbelieved in him, and this verse was revealed about them.

x: This statement that we mentioned on the authority of Mujahid and ʿAbdah ibn Abi Lubabah indicates that the meaning of the verse is specific, and that - since the matter was as we described - it was revealed regarding those Christians who disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and regarding those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the idol worshippers who did not acknowledge the prophethood of Jesus, and all other religions whose people denied Jesus.
Were the Christians right before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, and then they denied him?

Whoever among them followed the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, was on the right path, and God Almighty meant them when He said: O you who have believed, believe in God and His Messenger
r
(An-Nisa’: 136)
Is it possible that his statement,
h
And those who disbelieve - their allies are false gods who lead them out of the light into darkness
, means someone other than those whom Mujahid and Abdah mentioned that they meant by it, from among the believers in Jesus, or other than the people of apostasy in Islam?

Yes, it is possible that the meaning of that is that those who disbelieve, their allies are the tyrants, who stand between them and faith, and lead them astray until they disbelieve, so their leading them astray until they disbelieve is their expulsion of them from faith, meaning their turning them away from it, and depriving them of its goodness, even if they were not in it before, like the saying of a man: My father expelled me from his inheritance, if someone else owned it during his lifetime, so he deprived him of his share of it, and that speaker never owned this inheritance so he would be expelled from it, but when he deprived him and was prevented from what he would have had if he had not deprived him, it was said: He expelled him from it. And like the saying of a person: So-and-so expelled me from his battalion, meaning: He did not make me one of its people, and he was never in it before that. So his saying:
h
They take them out from the light into the darkness
, it is possible that their expulsion of them from faith to disbelief is according to this meaning, even though what Mujahid and Abdah said is more similar to the interpretation of the verse.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How did He say: And those who disbelieve - their allies are Taghut, they drive them out of the light, so that the predicate of Taghut was gathered by His saying: they drive them out, and Taghut is one?
Taghut is a name for a group and a single word, and it may be pluralized as Taghut.

If its singular and plural are made into one word, it would be similar to their saying: a just man, and just people, and a man of innate nature, and people of innate nature, and what is similar to that from the names that come unified in wording, their singular and plural, and as Al-Abbas bin Mirdas said: We said: Submit, we are your brothers! Your hearts are free from hatred.

God Almighty means by that: These are the ones who disbelieved, the companions of the Fire, the people of the Fire who will abide therein eternally - meaning in the fire of Hell - without others of the people of faith, without limit or end ever.
God Almighty means by His statement:
h
Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord

? O Muhammad, have you not seen in your heart the one who argued with Abraham, meaning: the one who disputed with Abraham, meaning: Abraham, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his Lord because God had given him the kingdom, meaning by that: he argued with him and disputed with him about his Lord, because God had given him the kingdom. This is an expression of astonishment from God Almighty, mentioned by His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord. That is why to was included in His statement:
h
Have you not seen the one who argued
? This is what the Arabs do when they want to express astonishment at a man for some of his actions that they disapprove of. They say: What do you see of this one?!

The meaning is: Have you seen the likes of this one, or like this one?! It was said: He who argued with Abraham about his Lord was a tyrant in Babylon called Nimrod bin Canaan bin Cush bin Sam bin Noah. It was also said that he was Nimrod bin Falakh bin Eber bin Shalih bin Arphaxad bin Sam bin Noah.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: Have you not considered him who argued with Abraham about his Lord because God had given him the kingdom? He said: He is Nimrod bin Canaan.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr Ibn Arabi, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord
? He said: We were told that he was a king called Nimrod, and he was the first tyrannical king on earth, and he was the owner of the palace in Babylon.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: His name is Nimrod, and he was the first to be arrogant on earth. He argued with Abraham about his Lord.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord because God had given him the kingdom

? He said: It was mentioned to us that the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord was a king called Nimrod, and he was the first tyrant to act tyrannically on earth, and he was the owner of the palace in Babylon.

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: He is Nimrod bin Canaan.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: He is Nimrod.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said: Zaid bin Aslam told me
m: something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us: Al-Hussein told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah Ibn Kathir told me that
m: he heard Mujahid say: He is Nimrod. Ibn Jurayj said: He is Nimrod, and it is said that he was the first king on earth.

x: By that, God the Almighty means: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord
h
when Abraham said

to him: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death, meaning: My Lord is the One in whose hand is life and death, He gives life to whomever He wills and causes death to whomever He wills after giving life. He said: I do that, I give life and cause death, I spare whomever I want to kill but I do not kill him, so that is from me bringing him back to life, and that is called Surat Al-Baqarah 2:258 Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham concerning his Lord because God had given him the kingdom?
h
When Abraham said

, "My Lord is He who gives life and causes death." He said, "I give life and cause death." Abraham said, "Then God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." So the disbeliever was confounded, and God does not guide.

The unjust people revival among the Arabs, as God the Almighty said: And whoever saves one, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely (al-Ma’idah 5:32), and I kill another, so that is from me killing him. Abraham, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: God, who is my Lord, brings the sun from its east, so bring it - if you are truthful that you are a god - from its west! God the Almighty said: Then the disbeliever was dumbfounded, meaning: he was cut off and his argument was invalidated. It is said: He slandered, slandered, slandered. It has been narrated that some Arabs say in this sense: He slandered. It is also said: He slandered a man, if you fabricated a lie against him, slander, slander, and slander.

c: It was narrated from some of the reciters
m: that he recited: So the one who disbelieved was dumbfounded, meaning: So Abraham who disbelieved was dumbfounded. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
When Abraham said

, ‘My Lord is He who gives life and causes death.’ He said, ‘I give life and cause death.’ And he mentioned to us that he called for two men and killed one of them and spared the other, so he said: I give life to this one! I spare whomever I wish, and I kill whomever I wish! Then Abraham said: Then God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west. “So he who disbelieved was confounded,
h
and God does not guide the wrongdoing people

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: I give life and cause death, I kill whomever I wish and spare whomever I wish, I leave him alive and do not kill him. And he said: The rulers of the earth, its east and its west, were four men: two believers and two disbelievers. The two believers were: Solomon, son of David, and Dhul-Qarnayn, and the disbelievers were: Bukhtanassar and Nimrod, son of Canaan. No one else ruled it. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated, Abd al-Razzaq narrated, Muammar narrated, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam: The first tyrant on earth was Nimrod. People would go out to buy food from him. Ibrahim would go out to buy food with whoever he wanted. When people passed by him, he would say: Who is your Lord? They would say: You! Until Ibrahim passed by. He said: Who is your Lord? He said: He who gives life and causes death? He said: I give life and cause death! Ibrahim said: God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west! The disbeliever was dumbfounded. He said: So he sent him back without food. Ibrahim returned to his family and passed by a dusty dune. He said: Shall I not take some of this and bring it to my family so that they may be pleased when I enter upon them? So he took some and went to his family. He put down his belongings and went to sleep. His wife went to his belongings and opened them. There was the best food anyone had ever seen. She made him some and brought it to him. His family had not had any food before. He said: Where did this come from? She said: From the food you brought! So he knew that God had provided for him, so he praised God. Then God sent an angel to the tyrant: Believe in me and I will leave you to your kingdom! He said: Is there a Lord other than me?! So he came to him a second time and said that to him, but he refused. Then he came to him a third time and he refused. So the angel said to him: Gather your forces for three days! So the tyrant gathered his forces, and God commanded the angel to open a gate of mosquitoes for him. The sun rose and they did not see it because of its large number, so God sent mosquitoes upon them and they ate their flesh and drank their blood, so nothing remained but the bones, and the king was as he was, nothing of that had happened to him. Then God sent a mosquito upon him and it entered his nostril, so he remained for four hundred years hitting his head with hammers, and the most merciful of people to him was the one who gathered his hands and hit his head with them. He was a tyrant for four hundred years, so God tortured him for four hundred years as his kingdom was, and God caused him to die. He is the one who built a tower reaching to the sky, and God destroyed his building from the foundations. He is the one about whom God said: Then God destroyed their building from the foundations (al-Nahl 16:26).

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told me
m: about the statement of God: Have you not considered him who argued with Abraham concerning his Lord? He said: He was Nimrod. He was in Mosul and people would come to him, and when they entered upon him he would say: Who is your Lord? They would say: You! He would say: Their leader. So when Abraham entered with a camel, he went out to argue with it for his son. He said: He examined them all and said: Who is your Lord? They would say: You! He would say: Their leader! Until Abraham examined them twice and said: Who is your Lord? He said: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death! He said: I give life and cause death. If I wish, I will kill you and cause you to die, and if I wish, I will keep you alive. Abraham said: God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west!! So the one who disbelieved was confounded,
h
and God does not guide the wrongdoing people

. He said: Get this man away from me and do not show him anything! Then all the people came out, and Abraham's sacks were clattering, until when he looked at the blackness of the mountains of his people, he said: My children, Ishmael and Isaac, would grieve me! If I could fill these two sacks from this valley and go with them, my children's eyes would be refreshed, until night falls and I pour it out! He said: So he filled them, then sewed them up, then came with them. The children threw themselves at them with joy, and he put his head in Sarah's lap for a while, then she said: What makes me sit still! Abraham has come tired and exhausted, if only I could get up and make him food until he gets up! He said: So she took a pillow and put it in its place, and slipped away little by little so as not to wake him. He said: So she went to one of the two baskets and opened it, and there were pure dates the likes of which had never been seen with anyone before, so she took some of it, kneaded it, and baked it. When she came to wake Abraham, she went to him and placed it in front of him, and he said: What is this, Sarah? She said: From your sacks! You have come and we have neither little nor much! He said: So he went to look at the other bag and it was the same, so he knew where it was from.
b.via: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: who said:
h
When Abraham said

to him: My Lord is He Who gives life and causes death! He - meaning Nimrod - said: So I give life and cause death! So he called for two men and spared one of them and killed the other. He said: I give life and cause death! He said: That is, I spare whomever I wish. Abraham said: God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west! “So he who disbelieved was confounded.
h
And God does not guide the wrongdoing people

c: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: When Abraham came out of the fire, they brought him to the king, although he had never entered before. So he spoke to him and said to him: Who is your Lord? He said: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death! Nimrod said: I give life and cause death! I will bring four men into a house and they will neither be fed nor given water, until they perish from hunger. I will feed two and give them water and they will live, and I will leave two behind and they will die. Abraham realized that he had the power, through his authority and kingdom, to do that. Abraham said to him: My Lord is He who brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west! The disbeliever was astonished and said: This man is mad! So they brought him out. Do you not see that because of his madness he dared to attack your gods and break them, and that the fire did not consume him! He feared that he would be disgraced among his people, I mean Nimrod, and this is what God Almighty said: And that was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people (al-An’am 6:83). So he claimed that he was a god, and he ordered Abraham to be taken out.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me that
m: he heard Mujahid say: I give life and cause death. I give life, but I do not kill, and I cause death to whomever I kill. Ibn Jurayj said: Two men were brought to him, and he killed one of them and left the other, so he said: I give life and cause death. He said: I kill, and I cause death to whomever I kill, and I give life. He said: I keep alive, but I do not kill.

c: Ibn Humayd told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us:
m: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that Nimrod said to Abraham, among other things: What is this god that you worship and call to worship, and mention of whose power you glorify Him over others? Abraham said to him: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. Nimrod said: So I give life and cause death! Abraham said to him: How do you give life and cause death? He said: I will take two men who deserved to be killed in my judgment, and I will kill one of them and thus cause him to die, and I will pardon the other and leave him alone and thus cause him to live! Abraham then said to him: God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west. I know that it is as you say! At that, Nimrod was dumbfounded and did not respond to him, and he knew that he could not bear that. God Almighty says: Then the one who disbelieved was dumbfounded, meaning the argument fell upon him, meaning Nimrod.

x: His statement,
h
And God does not guide the wrongdoing people

, means: And God does not guide the people of disbelief to an argument with which they can refute the argument of the people of truth when arguing and disputing, because the arguments of the people of falsehood are refuted. We have explained that the meaning of injustice is to put something in the wrong place, and the unbeliever puts his denial of what he denied in the wrong place, so by doing so he is unjust to himself. Ibn Ishaq said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me:
m: h
And God does not guide the wrongdoing people
, meaning: He does not guide them in the argument in the dispute, because of their misguidance.

evidence.text: It was narrated from some of the reciters that he recited: So the one who disbelieved was dumbfounded, meaning: So Abraham who disbelieved was dumbfounded.

x: God Almighty meant by His statement:
h
Or like the one who passed by a town
, similar to what He meant by His statement:
h
Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord
, of Muhammad’s amazement at him, may God bless him and grant him peace. His statement,
h
Or like the one who passed by a town
, is a continuation of his statement,
h
Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord

? His statement, Or like the one is a continuation of his statement, To the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, even though their wording differs, because their meanings are similar. Because his statement,
h
Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord
, means: Have you seen, O Muhammad, the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord? Then he continuated it by saying,
h
Or like the one who passed by a town
, because it is the custom of the Arabs to continuate speech with a similar meaning that precedes it, even if its wording differs from its wording.

Some Basra grammarians claimed that the kaf in his saying: or like the one who passed by a village, is redundant, and that the meaning is: Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham, or the one who passed by a village? We have previously explained that it is not permissible for there to be something in the Book of God that has no meaning, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
The people of interpretation differed about the one who passed by a village and it was desolate.
Some of them said: He is Ezra.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Najiyah bin Ka’b:
m: h
Or like the one who passed by a town
and it was desolate on its roofs, he said: Ezra.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Abu Khuzaymah told us,
m: I heard Sulayman bin Buraidah regarding his statement:
h
Or like the one who passed by a town
, he said: He is Ezra.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Or like the one who passed by a town
and it was desolate on its roofs, he said: It was mentioned to us that it was Ezra.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada [similarly].
m: Narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Or like the one who passed by a town
, he said: Al-Rabiʿ said: It was mentioned to us, and God knows best, that the one who passed by the town was Ezra.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
Or like the one who passed by a town
and it was desolate upon its roofs, he said: Ezra.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Or like the one who passed by a village, he said: Ezra.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Or like one who passed by a town and it was desolate upon its roofs
, that he is Ezra. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:259
h
Or like the one who passed by a town

and it was desolate on its roofs. He said, "How will Allah revive this after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then He resurrected him. He said, "How long did you remain?" He said, "I remained a day or part of a day." He said, "Rather, you remained a hundred years. So look at your food and your drink. And look at your donkey, and We will make you a sign to the people. And look at the bones - how We raise them up and then clothe them with flesh. But when it became clear to him, he said, “I know that God has power over all things.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Salim al-Khawass told us:
m: Ibn Abbas used to say: He is Ezra.

x: Others said: He is Urmia bin Hilkiah, and Muhammad bin Ishaq claimed that Urmia is Al-Khidr.

c: Ibn Hamid told us that, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us that:
m: Al-Khidr’s name - according to what Wahb ibn Munabbih claimed about the Children of Israel - was Urmia ibn Hilkiah, and he was from the tribe of Aaron ibn Imran.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Abd al-Samad bin Muqal told us:
m: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say regarding His statement:
h
How can God revive this after its death
? that when Urmia destroyed the Holy House and burned the books, he stood on the side of the mountain and said:
h
How can God revive this after its death

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Salamah told us, he said, Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, he said: He is Urmia.

c: Muhammad bin Askar told me, he said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said,
m: I heard Abdul Samad bin Muqal, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, the same.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa bin Maimun, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair,
m: regarding the statement of God: Or like one who passed by a town and it was desolate on its roofs, he said: He was a prophet, and his name was Urmia.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Qais bin Saad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubayd,
m: similarly.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Bakr ibn [Mudar] told me, he said:
m: They say, and God knows best, that he is Urmia.

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is that it is said that God Almighty amazed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at someone who said - when he saw a village lying desolate on its roofs -
h
How can God revive this after its death

? while knowing that He had begun its creation from nothing. His knowledge of His ability to begin it did not convince him, so he said: How can God revive it after its death! We do not have any clarification from the aspect from which it is correct to state the name of the one who said that. It is possible that this was Ezra and it is possible that it was Urmia, and we do not need to know his name, since the purpose of the verse was not to define the name of the one who said that, but rather it was intended to define for those who denied the ability of God to revive His creation after their death, and to return them after their annihilation, and that He is the One in Whose Hand is life and death from among the Quraysh and those who denied that from the rest of the Arabs, and to establish the argument with that against those who were among the Jews of the Children of Israel who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by informing his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what would remove their doubts about his prophethood, and cut off their excuse for his message, since this report that he revealed to his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his book, was from the report that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his people did not know, and knowledge of that was only with the People of the Book, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his people were not among them, rather he was illiterate and his people were illiterate.

So it was known by that to the People of the Book from the Jews who were among his emigrants, that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not know that except by revelation from God to him. If the intention was to report the name of the one who said that, then the indication would have been directed at him in a way that would eliminate the excuse and remove doubt. However, the intention was to criticize what he said, so God Almighty made that clear to His creation.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the village that the speaker passed by:
h
How can God revive this after its death
Some of them said: It is Jerusalem.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Sahl bin Askar and Muhammad bin Abdul Malik told me, they said, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me:
m: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: When Urmia saw the destruction of the Holy House like a great mountain, he said:
h
How can God revive this after its death

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Abd al-Samad bin Muqal told us:
m: that he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: It is the Holy House.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say that.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that it was the Holy House, which Ezra came to after it had been destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Or like one who passed by a town and it was desolate upon its roofs
, that he passed by the Holy Land.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: Or like one who passed by a town, he said: The town is Jerusalem, which Uzair passed by after Nebuchadnezzar had destroyed it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: Or like the one who passed by a village. He said: The village is Jerusalem, which Uzair passed by and Nebuchadnezzar had destroyed.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the village in which God destroyed those who left their homes, thousands in number, for fear of death, so God said to them: Die.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding the statement of God, the Most High: Have you not considered those who went forth from their homes, and they were thousands? He said: A village where the plague had descended. Then he related their story, which we mentioned in its place, from him, until he reached, Then God said to them, ‘Die,’ in the place where they had gone seeking life, so they died and then God revived them, Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, but most of the people do not give thanks. (al-Baqarah 2:243) He said: A man passed by it and it was bones flaring up, so he stopped to look and said:
h
How can God revive these after their death
? So God caused him to die for a hundred years and then resurrected him, until His statement: He did not revive him.

x: The correct statement about this is like the statement about the name of the speaker:
h
How can God revive this after its death
? They are the same and do not differ.

God Almighty means by His saying: And it is empty, that it is devoid of its people and inhabitants. It is said of this: The house became empty, empty, empty and Khawwayan. The village may also be called Khawit, and the first is more expressive and articulate. As for a woman in childbirth, it is said: Khawit takhwa khawaan incomplete, and it may be said of her: Khawwat takhwa, as is said of the house. Likewise: Khawwa al-Jawf yakhwa khawwaan severe. If what was said of the house was said of the cavity, and of the house what was said of the cavity, it would be correct, but what I mentioned is more eloquent. As for thrones, they are buildings and houses, the singular of which is throne, and the plural of its little is a’rish. Every building is a throne. It is said: So-and-so’s throne is a house, he erects a throne, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: And they did not erect a throne (al-A’raf 7:137), meaning they did not build, and from this it is said: the throne of Mecca, meaning its tents and buildings.
And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: Empty, ruins. Ibn Jurayj said: It reached us that Ezra went out and stood by the Holy House which had been destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar, so he stood and said: What was farther from you than Jerusalem, fighting, and wealth was what it was!! So he was sad.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And it is desolate on its thrones, he said: It is in ruins.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, who said: Uzair passed by it and Bukht Nasr had destroyed it.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And it is empty on its thrones, he said: fallen on its roof.

x: The meaning of that, as mentioned to us, is that when the one who said it passed by the Holy House, or the place that God mentioned that he passed by, it was in ruins after he had known it to be inhabited, he said: How can God revive this after its ruins?

Some of them said: He said what he said out of doubt in God’s ability to revive it, so God showed him His ability to do so by giving him an example in himself, then He showed him the place that he had denied His ability to build and revive. He revived what he had seen before its destruction, and He populated what had been there before its destruction. That is because the one who said that was - as he mentioned to us - in his time, it was inhabited by its people and inhabitants, then he saw it empty on its thrones, its people perishing, and they were scattered by killing and captivity, so that not one of them remained in that place, and their homes and dwellings were destroyed, so that nothing remained but a trace. So when he saw it like that after the state in which he had known it, he said: How will God revive this after its destruction and populate it, in astonishment - according to what some of the people of interpretation said - so he showed him how he revived it by what he had struck for him in himself, and in what was in his water skin and in his food, then he made him know his ability to do that and other things, by showing him in reviving it what was amazing to him in God’s ability to revive it, he saw it with his own eyes until he saw it with his own sight.
So when he saw that, he said: I know that God is over all things competent. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:259
h
Or like the one who passed by a town

and it was desolate on its roofs. He said, "How will Allah revive this after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then He resurrected him. He said, "How long did you remain?" He said, "I remained a day or part of a day." He said, "Rather, you remained a hundred years. So look at your food and your drink. And look at your donkey, and We will make you a sign to the people. And look at the bones - how We raise them up and then clothe them with flesh. But when it became clear to him, he said, “I know that God has power over all things.” The reason for saying that was as follows: Ibn Humayd narrated that Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, that he used to say: God said to Jeremiah when He sent him as a prophet to the Children of Israel: O Jeremiah, before I created you I chose you, before I formed you in your mother’s womb I sanctified you, before I brought you out of her belly I purified you, before you reached maturity I made you a prophet, before you reached maturity I chose you, and for a great matter I selected you.

So God, the Most High, sent Jeremiah to the king of the Children of Israel to guide him and direct him and bring him the report from God between him and him. He said: Then the events became great among the Children of Israel, and they committed sins and made permissible the forbidden things, and they forgot what God had done to them and how He had saved them from their enemy Sennacherib. Then God revealed to Urmia: Go to your people from the children of Israel, and tell them what I command you, and remind them of My blessings upon them, and tell them their events, then he mentioned what God sent Jeremiah with to his people from the children of Israel. He said: Then God revealed to Jeremiah: I will destroy the children of Israel with Japheth - and Japheth is the people of Babylon, and they are from the descendants of Japheth, son of Noah - and when Jeremiah heard the revelation of his Lord, he cried out and wept and tore his clothes and threw ashes on his head, and said: Cursed is the day in which I was born, and the day in which I met the Torah, and the worst of my days is the day in which I was born, for I did not leave the last of the prophets except for what is evil for me!

If He had intended good for me, He would not have made me the last of the prophets from the children of Israel! For my sake they will be afflicted with misery and destruction! When God heard the supplication of Al-Khudz and his weeping and how he said, He called to him: Urmia! Is what I have revealed to you hard for you? He said. Yes, O Lord, destroy me before I see in the Children of Israel what I do not like. God said: By My mighty glory, I will not destroy the Holy House and the Children of Israel until the command is from You in this! Then Jeremiah rejoiced at what his Lord had said to him, and his soul was content, and he said: No, by Him who sent Moses and His prophets with the truth, I will never command my Lord to destroy the Children of Israel!

c: Then he came to the king of the Children of Israel and told him
m: what God had revealed to him, and he was happy and cheerful and said: If our Lord punishes us, it is for many sins that we have committed against ourselves, and if He pardons us, it is by His power. Then they remained after this revelation for three years, and they only increased in disobedience and persisted in evil, and that was when their destruction approached, so the revelation decreased when they did not remember the Hereafter, and it was withheld from them when the world and its affairs distracted them. So their king said: O Children of Israel, desist from what you are doing before a punishment from God touches you, and before He sends upon you kings who have no mercy on you, for your Lord is close to repentance, His hands are extended with goodness, and He is merciful to those who repent to Him! But they refused to give Him up any of what they were doing. And God put in the heart of Bukht Nasr bin Nebuchadran bin Sennacherib bin Darias bin Marwad bin Faligh bin Eber, and Nimrod, the companion of Abraham, peace be upon him, who argued with him about his Lord, to march to Jerusalem, then do there what his grandfather Sennacherib had wanted to do. So he went out with six hundred thousand banners, seeking the people of Jerusalem. When he had departed, the report reached the king of the children of Israel: Nebuchadnezzar has come with his soldiers seeking you. So the king sent for Jeremiah, and he came to him and said: O Jeremiah, where is your claim to us that our Lord revealed to you that the people of Jerusalem should not be destroyed until you give the order to do so? Jeremiah said to the king: My Lord does not break His promise, and I trust in Him. When the time drew near and their kingdom was about to end, and God was determined to destroy them, God sent an angel from Him and said to him: Go to Jeremiah and ask him, and command him to do what he asked him to do. The angel came to Jeremiah in the form of a man from the Children of Israel. Jeremiah said to him: Who are you? He said: I am a man from the Children of Israel asking you for a question about some of my affairs! So he gave him permission, and the angel said: O Prophet of God, I have come to you to ask you about my relatives, and I have maintained ties of kinship with them as God has commanded me to do. I have treated them only well, and I have not spared them any honor, so my honoring them will only increase their anger towards me. So advise me about them, O Prophet of God! So he said to him: Treat what is between you and God well, and maintain ties of kinship as God has commanded you to maintain ties of kinship, and be glad with good report. So the angel turned away from him, and remained for a few days, then came to him in the form of the man who had come to him, and sat before him. Jeremiah said to him: Who are you? He said: I am the man who came to you about my family! The Prophet of God said to him: Haven't their morals been purified for you yet, and haven't you seen from them what you love? He said: O Prophet of God, by Him who sent you with the truth, I do not know of any honor that anyone can bestow upon his relatives except that I have bestowed upon them, and better than that! The Prophet said: Go back to your family and be good to them. I ask God, who reforms His righteous servants, to reform your relationship, and to gather you together for His pleasure, and to spare you His wrath! The king got up from his presence and stayed for days, and Nebuchadnezzar and his soldiers descended around the Holy House more than the locusts, and the Children of Israel were terrified by them, and that was difficult for the king of the Children of Israel, so he called Jeremiah and said: O Prophet of God, where is what God promised you? He said: I trust in my Lord. Then the king came to Jeremiah while he was sitting on the wall of the Holy House, laughing and rejoicing in the victory that his Lord had promised him. He sat before him and Jeremiah said to him: Who are you? He said: I am the one who asked you twice about my family. The Prophet said to him: Has it not been time for them to recover from what they are in? The king said: O Prophet of God, everything that happened to me from them before today, I used to endure with patience, and I knew that what they have in it is My anger. But when I came to them today, I saw them doing something that does not please God and that God does not love. The Prophet said: What action did you see them doing? He said: O Prophet of God, I saw them doing a great action that angers God. If they had been as they were before today, my anger would not have been so intense, and I would have been patient with them and hoped for them. But today I became angry for God and for you, so I came to you to tell you about their situation. I ask you by God - who sent you with the truth - not to call upon your Lord to destroy them. Then Jeremiah said: O King of the heavens and the earth, if they are right and correct, then spare them, but if they are angry with you and doing something that you are not pleased with, then destroy them! When the word left Jeremiah’s mouth, God sent a thunderbolt from the sky into the Holy House, and the place of sacrifice caught fire and seven of its gates were swallowed up. When Jeremiah saw that, he cried out, tore his clothes, and threw ashes on his head, saying: O King of the heavens and Most Merciful of the merciful, where is the appointment that you promised me? Then it was called: Jeremiah, what happened to them did not happen except because of your fatwa that you issued to our Messenger! The Prophet was certain that it was his fatwa that he issued three times, and that he was the Messenger of his Lord. Then Jeremiah flew until he mingled with the wild beasts. Nebuchadnezzar and his soldiers entered Jerusalem, stomped on the Levant, killed the Israelites until they were annihilated, and destroyed Jerusalem. Then he ordered his soldiers to fill each man's shield with dirt and throw it into Jerusalem. They threw dirt into it until they filled it. Then he turned back to the land of Babylon, taking with him the captives of the Israelites. He ordered them to gather everyone who was in Jerusalem. All the young and old of the Israelites gathered around him, and he chose seventy thousand boys from among them. When the spoils of his soldiers came out and he wanted to divide them among them, the kings who were with him said to him: O king, all our spoils are yours, but divide among us these boys whom you have chosen from the Israelites! So he did, and each one of them got four boys. Among those boys were: Daniel, Azariah, Mishael, and Hananiah. Nebuchadnezzar divided them into three groups, one third settled in the Levant, one third took captive, and one third killed. He took the vessels of the Holy House and brought them to Babylon, and the seventy thousand boys and brought them to Babylon. This was the first incident in which God Almighty mentioned the Children of Israel, their innovations and their injustice. When Nebuchadnezzar turned away from him, returning to Babylon with the captives of the Children of Israel, Jeremiah came on his donkey, with grape juice in a jug and a basket of figs, until he reached Elijah. When he stood there and saw the devastation there, he doubted and said:
h
How can God revive this after its death

? So God caused him to die for a hundred years, and his donkey, his juice, and his basket of figs were with him where God caused him to die, and he caused his donkey to die with him. God blinded the eyes of him so that no one saw him. Then God resurrected him and said to him: How long have you remained? He said: A day or part of a day. He said: “Rather, you have remained a hundred years. So look at your food and your drink; it has not stale.” He said: It has not changed. “And look at your donkey, and We will make you a sign to mankind. And look at the bones - how We raise them up and then cover them with flesh.” So he looked at his donkey, some of it connected to others - and it had died with him - by veins and nerves, then He covered it with flesh until it was whole, then the spirit ran through it and it stood up braying. And he looked at its juice and its figs, and behold, they were as they were when he laid them down; they had not changed. And when he saw of God’s power what he saw, he said, I know that God has power over all things. Then God gave Jeremiah life after that, and he is the one who sees the wildernesses of the earth and the countries.

c: Muhammad bin Askar and Ibn Zanjawayh told me, they said: Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, he said: Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me:
m: He heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: God revealed to Jeremiah while he was in the land of Egypt: Go to the land of Elijah, for this is not a place for you to stay. So he rode his donkey, until he was on a part of the road, and with him was a basket of grapes and figs, and he had with him a new water skin, so he filled it with water. When he saw the sight of Jerusalem and the surrounding villages and mosques, he looked at indescribable ruins. When he saw the destruction of Jerusalem like a great mountain, he said:
h
How can God revive this after its death

?! So he walked until he found a home there, so he tied his donkey with a new rope, and hung up his water skin, and God cast sleep upon it. When he slept, God took his soul for a hundred years. When seventy years had passed, God sent an angel to a great Persian king called Yousk, saying: God commands you to go forth with your people and destroy Jerusalem, Ilya, and its land until it returns to its former state. The king said: Give me three days to prepare for this work and to prepare the tools for it. So he gave him three days, and he appointed three hundred chieftains, and gave each chieftain a thousand workers and the tools he needed to prepare them. So his chieftains went to it with three hundred thousand workers. When they set out to work, God restored the spirit of life to Jeremiah's eye, while the rest of his body was dead. So he looked at Ilya and Surat Al-Baqarah 2:259
h
Or like the one who passed by a town

and it was desolate on its roofs. He said, "How will Allah revive this after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then He resurrected him. He said, "How long did you remain?" He said, "I remained a day or part of a day." He said, "Rather, you remained a hundred years. So look at your food and your drink. And look at your donkey, and We will make you a sign to the people. And look at the bones - how We raise them up and then clothe them with flesh. But when it became clear to him, he said, “I know that God has power over all things.” the surrounding villages, mosques, and rivers, and the fields working, threshing, and renewing themselves, until they became as they were. After thirty years, exactly one hundred, the spirit was restored to him. He looked at his food and drink, they had not stale, and he looked at his donkey standing as it was on the day he tied it, it had not eaten or drunk, and he looked at the ashes on the donkey’s neck, they had not changed to new, and a hundred years of wind, a hundred years of cold, and a hundred years of heat had passed over it, and they had not changed or deteriorated at all. Jeremiah’s body had shriveled from decay, so God made new flesh grow for him and raised his bones while he was watching. God said to him: Look at your food and your drink, they have not stale, and look at your donkey, and We will make you a sign to the people, and look at the bones, how We raise them up and then cover them with flesh. So when it was clear to him, he said, I know that God has power over all things.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Abd al-Samad bin Muqal told us:
m: He heard Wahb bin Munabbih say about His statement:
h
How can God revive these after their death
?: When Jeremiah destroyed the Temple in Jerusalem and burned the books, he stood on the side of the mountain and said:
h
How can God revive these after their death

? So God caused him to die for a hundred years. Then God returned those of the Children of Israel who were returned after seventy years from the time he caused him to die, and they lived for thirty years, completing the hundred. When the hundred years had passed, God restored his soul, and it had returned to its original state. He began to look at the bones, how they were joined together, then he looked at the bones, how they were covered with nerves and flesh. When that became clear to him, he said: I know that God has power over all things. God, the Most High, said: Look at your food and your drink; they have not spoiled. He said: So his food was figs in a basket and a jug of water.

c: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Or like the one who passed by a town

and it was desolate on its roofs, that Ezra passed by kneeling from Ash-Sham on his donkey with juice, grapes, and figs. When he passed by the town and saw it, he stopped over it and folded his hands and said:
h
How can God revive this after its death

? - not as a lie or doubt - so God caused him and his donkey to die and they perished, and a hundred years passed over them. Then God revived Ezra and said to him: How long did you stay? He said: I stayed a day or part of a day! It was said to him: Rather, you stayed a hundred years! So look at your food of figs and grapes, and your drink of juice, it has not become stale, the verse.

x: God Almighty means by His saying: Then He raised him up, then He raised him up alive after his death. We have already demonstrated the meaning of resurrection. As for the meaning of his saying: How long did you stay?, How long is an interrogative in the speech of the Arabs about the amount of the number, and in this place it is in the accusative case with labhat, and its interpretation is: God said to him: How much time did you stay dead before I raised you from your death to life? The one sent said after his death: I stayed dead until you raised me to life for one day or part of a day. He mentioned that the messenger was Jeremiah, or Ezra, or whoever God told this report about. He said: I stayed a day or part of a day, because God Almighty had taken his soul at the beginning of the day, then returned his soul to him at the end of the day after a hundred years. He was asked: How long did you stay?

He said: I stayed a day, while he saw that the sun had set. So that was a day for him, because he mentioned that he took his soul at the beginning of the day, and he was asked about the amount of time he had stayed dead at the end of the day, while he saw that the sun had set, so he said: I stayed a day, then he saw the rest of the sun that had not set, so he said: Or part of a day, meaning: rather part of a day, as God Almighty said: And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more (37:147), meaning: rather more. So his saying: or part of a day, was a return from his saying: I stayed a day.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: “Then He sent him. He said, ‘How long did you stay?’ He said, ‘I stayed a day or part of a day.’” He said: It was mentioned to us that he died in the morning, then He sent him before sunset, and he said, I stayed a day. Then he turned and saw the remainder of the sun, so he said, Or part of a day. He said, Rather, you stayed a hundred years.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
How can God revive this after its death
? He said: He passed by a village and was amazed and said:
h
How can God revive this after its death

? So God caused him to die at the beginning of the day, and he remained for a hundred years, then He resurrected him at the end of the day, and He said: How long did you remain? He said: I remained for a day or part of a day. He said: Rather, I remained for a hundred years.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn al-Hasan,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, who said: Al-Rabiʿ said: God caused him to die for a hundred years, then He resurrected him. He said: How long did you stay? He said: I stayed a day or part of a day. He said: Rather, I stayed a hundred years.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: When he stood at the Holy House which had been destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar, he said:
h
How can God revive this after its death

? How can He restore it as it was? So God caused him to die. He said: And it was mentioned to us that he died at noon, and was resurrected before sunset after a hundred years, so he said: How long did you stay? He said: A day. When he saw the sun, he said: Or part of a day.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
Then look at your food and your drink
; it has not become stale, that the years that have passed have not changed it. His food - according to some of them - was a basket of figs and grapes, and his drink was a small bowl of water.
Some of them said: Rather, his food was a basket of grapes and a basket of figs, and his drink was a skin of juice.

Others said: Rather, his food was a basket of figs, and his drink was a wine jug - or: a wine bottle. We have previously mentioned what some of them said about this, and we will mention what is in it in the future, God willing. As for his saying: It was not made lawful for him, there are two ways of reading it: One of them: It was not possible to delete the ha’ in the connection and to keep it in the pause. And whoever reads it like that, then he makes the ha’ in yatasanna an extra conjunction, like his saying: So follow their guidance (al-An’am 6:90), and he made tafa’alat from it: tasnayt tasnayyan, and he reasoned in that by saying that sunnah is the plural of sanawat, so tafa’alat is correct. And whoever says in the year sanayna, then it is permissible, even if it is rare, that tasnayt tafa’alat, the nun was replaced with a ya’ because the nuns are many, just as they said tazanayt, and its original form is zan.

And some people said: it is taken from His statement: from black mud that has been altered (al-Hijr 15:26, 28, 33), which is the variable. And that also, if it is like that, then it is also from what its nun was replaced with a ya’. It is a general reading of the Kufa reading. The other of them: proving the ha’ in connection and pause. Whoever reads it in this way, then he makes the ha’ in yatasanna the lam of the verb, and makes it jussive with lam, and makes fa’ala from it: tasannahat and yaf’ulu atsanah tasannahan, and he said in the diminutive of sunnah sanayha and suniyah, asnayt ‘ad’l-qawm and asnahat ‘ad’l-hum, if you stayed for a year. This is a general reading of the people of Medina and Hijaz.

The correct reading in my opinion is to prove the ha’ in both connected and paused pronunciations, because it is proven in the Muslims’ Mushaf, and there is a correct explanation for proving it in both cases.

i: The meaning of his saying:
h
