m: Take four birds and divide them towards you, then place them on seven mountains, and place a part of them on each mountain, then call them and they will come to you running. So Abraham took four birds and cut them into pieces, he did not put a part of a bird with its companion. Then he put the head of one with the leg of another, and the chest of one with the wing of another, and divided them among seven mountains, then he called them and each part flew to its companion, then they all came to him.

x: Others said: Rather, God commanded him to do that on every mountain.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then place a portion of them on every mountain, he said: Then scatter them on every mountain, they will come to you running, and thus God brings the dead to life.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then divide them into parts on every mountain, then call them, they will come to you running. Thus does God bring the dead to life. It is a parable that God gave to Abraham.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told us,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: Then place a portion of them on every mountain, then scatter them in portions on every mountain, then call them, Come, by God’s permission. Thus God brings the dead to life. An example that God gave to Abraham, peace be upon him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told me, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: He ordered him to make their legs, heads, and wings different, then he would place a part of them on each mountain.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
Then place on every mountain a portion of them
, so Ibrahim made a distinction between their legs and their wings.

x: The most appropriate interpretation of the verse is what Mujahid said, which is that God Almighty commanded Abraham to distribute the parts of the four birds, after cutting them up, on all the mountains that Abraham used to reach at the time God commanded him to distribute that and scatter them on them in parts. Because God Almighty said to him: Then place on every mountain a part of them, and all is a letter that indicates the encompassment of what it is added to, its wording is one but its meaning is collective. If that is the case, then it is not permissible for the mountains on which God commanded Abraham to distribute the parts of the four birds to be outside of one of two meanings: either some of them, or all of them. If it was some, then it is not permissible for that some to be anything other than what Abraham had the means to distribute the members of the four birds upon him.
Or it could be all of them, and it could also be like that.

c: God Almighty has informed us that
m: He ordered him to do this on every mountain, and that was either every mountain that Abraham knew specifically, or the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:260
h
And when Abraham said

, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." He said, "Do you not believe?" He said, "Yes, but [it is] to reassure my heart." He said, "Then take four birds and bring them close to you, then place a portion of them on every mountain, then call them, they will come to you running. And know that God is Exalted in Might and Wise." mountains on the earth. As for the statement of those who said: That there are four mountains, and the statement of those who said: They are seven, we do not have any evidence for the correctness of any of that, so we permit saying it. Rather, God commanded Abraham, peace be upon him, to make the four birds into separate parts on each mountain, so that Abraham would see His ability to gather their parts while they were scattered and dispersed in various different places, so that He would bring some of them together with others, and they would return, as they were before they were cut up and torn apart, and before their parts were scattered on the mountains, as living birds that fly, so that Abraham’s heart would be reassured, and he would know that this is how God gathered the limbs of the dead for the resurrection, and He gathered their parts after decay, and returned each of their limbs to its place as it was before the destruction.

x: The part of everything is some of it, whether it is all divided into it correctly, or not divided. So, in this sense, it is different from the meaning of the arrow. Because the arrow of something is the part that is all divided into it correctly. That is why the word Nasir is often used in their speech when mentioning their shares of inheritance: the arrows, not the parts. As for his saying: Then call them, its meaning is what I mentioned earlier on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: It is that he was commanded to say to the parts of the birds after distributing them on every mountain: Come with God’s permission.

Was Abraham commanded to call them while they were torn into pieces on the tops of the mountains, dead or after they had been brought back to life? If he was commanded to call them while they were torn apart and had no soul in them, then what is the point of commanding those who have no life in them to come? Because he was commanded to call them after they had been brought back to life, then what need was there for Abraham to call them when he saw them spread out on the tops of the mountains?

The command of God Almighty mentioned by Abraham, peace be upon him, to call upon them while they were separate parts, is only a command of creation, like God’s saying to those whom He transformed into apes after they had been humans: Be apes, despised (al-Baqarah 2:65), not a command of worship, so it would be impossible except after the existence of the one commanded to worship.

By that, the Most High means: And know, O Abraham, that the One Who revived these birds after you tore them apart and scattered their parts over the mountains, then gathered them together and restored their souls until He restored them to their original state before you scattered them, is Mighty, in His might when He strikes those He strikes from among the tyrants and arrogant ones who disobeyed His command, disobeyed His messengers, and worshipped other than Him, and in His vengeance until He takes vengeance on them, Wise in His command.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq told us:
m: And know that God is Mighty and Wise. He said: Mighty in His power, Wise in His command.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: And know that God is Exalted in Might in His punishment, Wise in His command.

Since this is the case, whether the reader reads it with a damma on the sad: fasirhunna ilayk, or with a kasra on it fasirhunna, since they are two well-known languages with the same meaning.

However, even if this is the case, what I prefer is to read it with it: fasirhunna ilayk, with a damma on the sad, because it is the higher and more famous of the two languages, and the most common among Arab tribes.

x: This verse refers to His saying: Who is it that will loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And God withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned. (al-Baqarah 2:245) The verses that follow it until His saying:
h
The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God

, from the stories of the Children of Israel and their story with Talut and Goliath, and what follows from the report of the one who argued with Abraham, and the matter of the one who passed by the city that was desolate on its roofs, and the story of Abraham and his asking his Lord what he asked, from what we have mentioned before, is an objection from God, the Most High, with what He objected with from their stories between that, as an argument from Him in part against the polytheists who were denying the resurrection and the establishment of the Hour, and an exhortation from Him in part to the believers to strive in His way which He commanded them in His saying: And fight in the way of God and know that God is Hearing and Knowing (al-Baqarah 2:244), in which He informs them that He is their supporter even if their number is small and the number of their enemy is great, and He promises them victory over them, and He teaches them His way with regard to those who follow their path of seeking the pleasure of God that He is their supporter, and with regard to those who follow the path of their enemies from the disbelievers that He is their deserter and divides their gathering and weakens their plot, and as a severing from Him in part.

The excuse of the Jews who were among the emigrants of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what he informed his Prophet of their hidden affairs and the concealed secrets of their ancestors and forefathers that no one else knew, so that they would know that what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought them was from God, and that it was not a guess or fabrication, and an excuse from him to the hypocrites among them, so that they would beware of their doubts about the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, lest his wrath and power befall them like what he befell their ancestors who were in the village that he destroyed and left desolate. Then the Almighty returned to the report about the one who lends God a good loan, and what reward He has for him for his loan, so He said: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of God, meaning by that: the example of those who spend their wealth on themselves in jihad against the enemies of God with their lives and their wealth, is like a grain of wheat or barley or other plants of the earth whose yield is spiked by a sower, so it sprouts, meaning: it produces, seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains, meaning: so likewise the one who spends his wealth on himself in the way of God, his reward is seven hundred times for each of his expenditures, as:

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Like a seed that grows seven ears, and in each ear is a hundred grains. So this is for whoever spends in the way of God, he will have a reward of seven hundred.

c: Yunus told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “
h
The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain [of corn] which grows seven spikes
; in each spike is a hundred grains. And God multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills,” he said: This is the one who spends on himself in the way of God and goes out.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his saying: “
h
The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain of corn

: it grows seven spikes, and in each spike is a hundred grains.” The verse. So whoever pledged allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to emigrate and stayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, and did not meet anyone except with his permission, his good deed would be seven hundred times greater. And whoever pledged allegiance to Islam, his good deed would be ten times greater.

x: If someone says: Have you ever seen an ear of wheat containing a hundred grains, or has it reached you, and used it as an example of someone who spends his money in the way of God? It was said: If that exists, then that is it. Otherwise, it is possible that its meaning is: Like an ear of grain that produces seven ears, in each ear a hundred grains, if God put that in it. It is possible that its meaning is: In each ear a hundred grains, meaning that if it is sown, it produces a hundred grains, so what happened from the seed that was from it from the hundred grains is added to it, because it was from it.
Some of the people of interpretation interpreted that in this way.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: his saying:
h
The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain of corn which grows seven spikes
, in each spike is a hundred grains. He said: Each spike grows a hundred grains, so this is for the one who spends in the way of God:
h
And God multiplies for whom He wills
, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.

x: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of His saying:
h
And God multiplies for whom He wills

Some of them said: God multiplies the reward of good deeds for whomever He wills of His servants. He promises the one who gives but does not spend in His cause less than what He promised the one who spends in His cause of multiplying one by seven hundred. As for the one who spends in His cause, He does not decrease what He promised him of multiplying the seven hundred by one.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: This is multiplied for whoever spends in the way of God - meaning the seven hundred -
h
And God multiplies for whom He wills
, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing, meaning for someone other than the one who spends in His way.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: God multiplies for whomever He wills of those who spend in His cause from seven hundred to two thousand thousand times. This is a statement mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas from a source whose chain of transmission I did not find, so I left mentioning it.
What is more deserving of the interpretation of His statement,
h
And God multiplies for whom He wills

, is that God multiplies from the seven hundred to whatever multiplication He wills, for whomever He wills of those who spend in His cause. Because the reward and multiplication were not mentioned for anyone other than the one who spends in the cause of God, so it is permissible for us to direct what God Almighty promised in this verse of multiplication to it being a promise from Him for working in other than His cause, or for other than spending in the cause of God.

God Almighty means by that: And God is Vast, that He increases whomever He wills of His creation who spend in His cause, more than the seven hundred times that He promised them He would increase, Knowing of who among them deserves the increase, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
And God multiplies for whom He wills
, and God is all-Encompassing and Knowing, he said: All-Encompassing means to increase from His abundance, Knowing means to know who He increases.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: And God is Vast, for those multiples, Knowing of what those who spend their money in obedience to God spend.

By this, God the Almighty means: The one who gives his money to the mujahideen in the way of God to help them in fighting the enemies of God. God the Almighty says: The one who helps the mujahideen in the way of God by spending on them and their loads and other provisions, then does not follow up his spending on them with a favor from us by spending that on them, nor does he harm them. So his favor to them is by showing them that he has done them - through his actions and gifts that he gave them to strengthen them in fighting their enemy - a favor, and he shows that either by word or action. As for the harm, it is his complaining to them because of what he gave them and strengthened them from spending in the way of God, that they did not fulfill their duty in jihad, and similar words with which he harms the one on whom he spent. Rather, this is a condition for the one who spends in the way of God, and the reward is obligatory for the one who is not a thief or a harmer of the one on whom he spends in the way of God, because the spending that is in the way of God is that by which the face of God is sought and what is with Him is sought.

So if the meaning of spending in the way of God is what we have described, then there is no reason for the one who spends on the one on whom he spends, because he has no hand in it nor any favor for which he deserves from him - if he does not reward him for it - a thief or harm, since his spending is what he spent on him with the intention of seeking God’s reward and seeking His pleasure, and his reward is upon God, not upon the one on whom he spent it.
A group of interpreters said something similar to the meaning we mentioned.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Those who spend their wealth in the way of God and do not follow up what they have spent with insult or injury - their reward is with their Lord, God knew that some people boast about their gifts, so He disliked that and spoke about it, saying: “A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And God is Free of need and Forbearing.”

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: He said to the others, meaning: God said to the others, and they are those who do not go out to fight their enemy: Those who spend their wealth in the way of God and do not follow up what they have spent with [the curse of God] or injury, he said: So he set conditions for them. He said: And the one who goes out, he did not set a condition for him, little or much - meaning the one who goes out, the one who goes out in jihad whom God mentioned in His statement:
h
The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a seed 1

:10. Ibn Zayd said: My father used to say: If someone who gives something from this or strengthens himself in the way of God harms you, and you think that your greeting will be burdensome to him, then stop greeting him. Ibn Zayd said: So he was forbidden from the best of Islam. He said: A woman said to my father: O Abu Usamah, guide me to a man who truly goes out in the way of God, for they do not go out except to eat fruits!! I have a quiver and arrows in it. So he said to her: May God not bless your quiver or your arrows, for you have harmed them before you gave them! He said: A man was saying to them: Go out and eat the fruits!

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They do not follow up what they have spent with reproach or injury
, he said: It is better for a man not to spend his money than to spend it and then follow it up with reproach or injury. As for his saying:
h
For them is their reward with their Lord
, it means: for those who spend their money in the way of God, according to what is mentioned. The ha and the mim in for them refer back to those. The meaning of his saying:
h
They will have their reward with their Lord is that they will have their reward and recompense for the expenditures they spent in the way of
God, and then did not follow it up with favors or harm. And His statement:
h
And there is no fear for them
, nor shall they grieve, means: And they, with what they have of reward and recompense for their expenditure that they spent according to what we stipulated,
h
and there is no fear for them

when they come before God and leave this world, nor in the terrors of the Resurrection, and that its hardships will befall them or that God’s punishment will befall them in it, nor will they grieve for what they left behind them in this world.

x: What God Almighty meant by His saying: kind speech, is beautiful speech, and a man’s supplication for his Muslim brother, and forgiveness, meaning: and covering up for him when he knows of his faults and bad condition, is better in the sight of God, than charity that he gives to him, followed by harm, meaning: complaining about it to him, and harming him because of it, as:- Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak: A good word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by harm. He said: It is better for him to keep his money than to spend his money and then follow it with favors and harm. As for his saying:
h
Rich and Forbearing
, he means: And God is Rich from what they give in charity, Forbearing, when He does not hasten to punish those among you who show off with their charity and harm those to whom they give it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: regarding this, what: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The rich, the one who is perfect in his wealth, and the forbearing, the one who is perfect in his forbearance.

x: By that, the Most High means:
h
O you who have believed

, who believed in God and His Messenger, do not invalidate your charities, meaning: do not invalidate the rewards of your charities by reminding others of them and causing harm, just as the disbelief of the one who spends his money to show off to people is invalidated, which is his showing off to them with his work, and that is that he spends his money in what people see on the surface as wanting God, the Most High, so they praise him for it, while he does not want God by it nor does he seek reward from Him, but rather he spends it thus outwardly so that people praise him for it and say: He is generous and noble, and he is a righteous man, so they praise him well for it, and they do not know what is hidden in his intention in spending what he spent, so they do not know what he is doing in terms of denying God, the Most High, and the Last Day. As for his statement:
h
And does not believe in God and the Last Day

, its meaning is: He does not believe in the Oneness of God and His Lordship, nor that he will be resurrected after his death, so he will be rewarded for his deeds, so he does his deeds for the sake of God and seeks His reward and what is with Him in his afterlife.

This is the characteristic of the hypocrite. We only said that he is a hypocrite because the one who shows his disbelief and declares his polytheism is known to not be a hypocrite in any of his deeds. Because the hypocrite is the one who shows off to people by doing deeds that are apparently for God, but inwardly the secret of his doer is suspicious, intending by it to be praised by people. The disbeliever does not imagine to anyone that all his deeds are for the devil - if he declares his disbelief - not for God. And whoever is like that, then he is not a hypocrite in his deeds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Abu Hani’ al-Khawlani said, on the authority of Amr ibn Harith, he said: A man goes out to fight, he does not steal, nor fornicate, nor embezzle, and he does not return with enough! So it was said to him: Why is that? He said: A man goes out, and when a calamity from God that He has decreed upon him befalls him, he curses and reviles his leader and curses the moment he went out to fight, and says: I will never return to fight with him again! So this is against him, and not for him, like spending in the way of God followed by reviling and harm. God has given an example of it in the Qur’an:
h
O you who have believed
, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, until the end of the verse.

x: God Almighty means by that: The likeness of this one who spends his wealth to be seen by people
h
and does not believe in God and the Last Day

. The ha’ in His statement: Then his likeness refers back to the one, like the likeness of a fine sand, and a fine sand is one and all. So whoever makes it all, then the singular is a fine sand, like a date and dates and a palm tree and palm trees.

i: And whoever makes it singular, then the plural is fine sand, and fine sand, and fine sand, as the poet said:
x: Bird sites on the row Safwan is the smooth stone.

His saying: There is dust on it, means: there is dust on the rock. Then a downpour struck it, means: a heavy, intense rain struck the rock, as Imru’ al-Qais said: An hour passed, and then a downpour descended upon her, falling down on her sides and pouring down. It is said: And the sky was wet, so it is wet with rain. And: And the earth was wet, so it is wet. And his saying:
h
So he left it bare

, means: So the downpour left the clear rock bare. The solid stone is the solid one on which there is nothing of plants or anything else. It is one of the lands in which nothing grows, and likewise one of the heads, as Ru’bah said: When she saw me, she created the camouflaged, shining, noble forehead Hence, a thick, slow-boiling pot is called a solid pot. It has become solid, and hence the saying of Ta’abbata Sharran: I am not a thunderstorm nor a solid line that is defenseless against goodness. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:264
h
O you who have believed
, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, like one who spends his wealth [only] to be seen by the people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day.

So his example is like that of a smooth rock upon which is dust, then a downpour strikes it and leaves it bare. They are not able to do anything of what they have earned. And Allah does not guide the people. The unbelievers Then the Almighty mentioned the hypocrites whose deeds were given as an example, saying: “So their deeds are
h
like a smooth rock

that had dirt on it, then a downpour of rain fell on it and took away the dirt on it, leaving it pure with no dirt on it or anything. The Muslims see them outwardly as having deeds - just as dirt is seen on this smooth rock - because they show off to them. But when the Day of Resurrection comes and they turn to God, all of that will vanish, because it did not belong to God, just as a downpour of rain took away the dirt that was on the smooth rock, leaving it smooth with nothing on it.” So His statement,
h
They will not be able
, means: those who spend their wealth to be seen by people, and do not believe in God or the Last Day.
He says:
h
They will not be able

on the Day of Resurrection to receive the reward for anything they earned in this world, because they did not work for their afterlife, nor to seek what is with God in the Hereafter, but rather they did it to be seen by people and to seek their praise. And their share from their deeds is what they wanted and sought with them.

c: Then the Most High informed us that
m: He does not guide the disbelieving people, meaning: He does not guide them to the truth in their spending and other things, and He does not grant them success in it, while they prefer falsehood over it, but He leaves them in their misguidance, wandering blindly. So the Almighty said to the believers: Do not be like the hypocrites, whose actions are described by this example, so that you nullify the rewards of your charity by showing favors to those to whom you gave it and by harming them, just as the reward of the hypocrite who spent his money to show off to people, and he does not believe in God and the Last Day, is nullified in the sight of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, and he recited until he reached for anything they have earned. This is a parable that God gave for the deeds of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. He says:
h
They will not be able
to do anything of what they have earned on that Day, just as this rain left the clear rocks with nothing on them, the purest they had ever been.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: Do not invalidate your charities by showing off until His saying:
h
And God does not guide the disbelieving people
. This is a parable that God gave for the deeds of the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. He says:
h
They will not be able
to do anything about what they have earned on that day, just as this rain left the pure rocks clean with nothing on them.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury until His saying: for anything they have earned. As for the rock on which there is dust, the rain fell and its dust was removed and left it solid. Likewise, this one who spends his money to show off to people, the showing off goes with his spending, just as this rain has taken the dust of this rock and left it pure. Likewise, the showing off has left him unable to do anything with what he has sent forward. So He said to the believers: Do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, so they are invalidated just as the charity of showing off is invalidated.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: It is better for a man not to spend his wealth than to spend it and then follow it up with favors and injury. So God gave an example of him like the example of a disbeliever who spends his wealth and does not believe in God or the Last Day. So God gave an example of both of them:
h
Like a smooth rock
upon which is dust, and a downpour strikes it and leaves it bare. So too is the one who spends his wealth and then follows it up with favors and injury.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury to
h
like a smooth rock
upon which is dust, then a downpour strikes it and leaves it bare, with nothing on it. And so is the hypocrite on the Day of Resurrection; he will not be able to do anything with what he earned.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, Ibn Jurayj said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Do not nullify your charities by reminders or injury
, he said: He reminds others of his charity and causes them harm in it until he nullifies it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, Then they do not follow up what they have spent with reminders or injury, so he recited,
h
O you who have believed
, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, until he reached,
h
They will not be able

to do anything with what they have earned, then he said, Do you see the downpour leaving any dust on the rock? Likewise, from you and your injury, it does not leave anything of what you have spent. And he recited His statement,
h
O you who have believed
, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, and he recited, and whatever you spend, so he recited until he reached, and you will not be wronged
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:270-272)
. We have explained the meaning of Safwan sufficiently, but we wanted to mention those who said the same thing about it from the people of interpretation.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
Like a smooth rock
, like a rock.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
Like a smooth rock
, and a smooth rock is a rock.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for Safwan, it is the stone called Al-Safa.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: Safwan, meaning the stone. The explanation of it has already been mentioned. This is a mention of what we said about it:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for wabil, it means heavy rain.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: Then a downpour struck him, and a downpour is a heavy rain.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, similarly.

x: Mention of those who said something similar to what we said about that:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He left it pure, he said: clean.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He left it pure, he said: He left it pure, with nothing on it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said, his statement:
h
He left it intact
, he said: There is nothing on it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: Solid,
h
so he left it bare

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
He left it intact
, there is nothing wrong with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He left it intact
, with nothing on it.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And the example of those who spend their wealth by giving it in charity, and using it for the sake of God, and by it strengthening the needy among the warriors and mujahideen in the way of God, and in other acts of obedience to God, seeking His pleasure.
h
And to strengthen themselves

means by that: and to strengthen them in spending that in obedience to God and to achieve it, from the saying of the speaker: Make so-and-so steadfast in this matter - if you correct his resolve, and make it true, and strengthen his opinion in it - make him steadfast, as Ibn Rawahah said: So God confirmed what He gave you, as He confirmed Moses, and gave him victory like the one they had given him. God the Almighty meant by this: that their souls were certain and believed in God’s promise to them regarding what they spent in His obedience without favor or harm, so He made them steadfast in spending their money seeking God’s pleasure, and corrected their resolve and opinions, out of certainty in that, and belief in God’s promise to them.

That is why some of the people of interpretation said about His statement: and confirmation, and confirmation, and some of them said: and certainty, because the confirmation of the souls of those who spent their money seeking God’s pleasure was only out of certainty and belief in God’s promise.
Mention of those who said that from the people of interpretation:

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: h
And as confirmation from themselves
, he said: Confirmation and certainty.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq Al-Ahwazi told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: And confirmation from themselves, he said: And confirmation from themselves, steadfastness and support.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And as a confirmation from themselves
, he said: Certainty from themselves. He said: Confirmation is certainty.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ali bin Ma’bad told us, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And as confirmation from themselves
, he said: Certainty from themselves.

x: Others said: The meaning of his saying:
h
And to make sure of themselves
is that they were making sure of the place where they put their alms.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And to make sure of themselves
, he said: They make sure where they put their money.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Uthman bin al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
And to make sure of themselves
. So I said to him: What is that making sure? He said: They make sure where they put their money.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And to make sure of themselves
, he said: They were making sure where to put it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ali bin Ali bin Rafa’ah, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And to make sure of themselves
, he said: They used to make sure where they put their money - meaning their zakat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Ali, he said:
m: I heard al-Hasan recite: Seeking the pleasure of God
h
and to strengthen themselves
. He said: If a man intended to give a charity that would be confirmed, if it was for God, he would go ahead, but if doubt arose in him, he would hold back.

x: This interpretation that we have mentioned from Mujahid and Al-Hasan is an interpretation that is far-fetched in meaning from what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the recitation. That is because they interpreted the statement, and to reassure themselves, to mean: and to verify. They claimed that it was said thus because the people were verifying where they put their money. If the interpretation was thus, it would have been: and to reassure themselves. Because the source of speech was on the form tafaʿalat at-tafaʿal, so it is said: takramat takramaan, and takalamat takalamaan, and as God, the Most High, said: Or He takes them in fear (al-Nahl 16:47), from the speaker saying: So-and-so feared this matter out of fear. Likewise, His statement, and to reassure themselves, if it was from the people’s verification of putting their charity in its proper places, the statement would have been: and to verify themselves, not to verify.
But the meaning of that is what we said, that it is: and to reassure themselves from the people themselves, with the soundness of the resolve and the oath by the promise of God, the Most High.
Why do you deny that this is similar to the statement of God Almighty: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion (al-Muzzammil 73:8), and He did not say: with complete devotion?

This is contrary to that. That is because it is only permissible to say in it: Tabatilan because it is apparent and Tabatilu ilayhi, so its appearance indicates something that was left out of the speech from which it was said: Tabatilan. That is because what was left out is: Tabatilu, so God tests you with Tabatilu ilayhi.

And the Arabs sometimes do the same: they bring out the sources in words other than the words of the verbs that preceded them, if the previous verbs indicate what they were brought out from, as God the Almighty said:
And God caused you to grow from the earth a plant
and He said:
And He caused it to grow a good plant

And the plant is the source of nabat. That is only permissible because anbata came before it, so it indicates what was left out from which it was said nabatan. The meaning is: God caused you to grow, so you grew from the earth a plant. There is no statement in his saying:
h
And to strengthen themselves

, which could be thought to be a deviation from its structure. The meaning of the statement is: And they are certain in placing the alms in their proper places, so it is directed to the meanings to which his saying: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion was directed, and what is similar to that from the sources that are modified from the verbs that are apparent before them.
Others said: The meaning of his saying:
h
And as confirmation from themselves
, is and as a reward from themselves.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And as a confirmation from themselves
, he said: as a reward from themselves.

x: This statement is also far from the meaning of steadfastness, because steadfastness is not known in any speech to mean reward, unless the interpreter meant that: that the souls of the spenders were rewarded in their steadfastness of their owners. If that was the meaning of the speech, then reward is not in the meaning of steadfastness, so it is translated as it.

By that, He, the Almighty and Majestic, means: “The parable of those who spend their wealth, giving it in charity and spending it in the obedience of God, without any favour upon those to whom they give it, nor any harm from them thereby, seeking the pleasure of God and believing in His promise, is like a garden.” And Paradise is the garden. We have previously demonstrated that Paradise is the garden, by sufficient evidence of its repetition.
h
On a hill

, a hill is a protruding part of the land that rises above the torrent. And He, the Most High, described it thus because that which rises above the torrents and valleys is rougher, and the gardens of the rough land are, I think, better in fruit, planting and cultivation than that which is softer. And for this reason, A'sha of Banu Tha'labah said in describing a garden: What a garden of the gardens of sadness, green and lush, upon which pouring rain has fallen He described it as one of the gardens of sadness, because the plants and vegetation of sadness are better and stronger than the plants and crops of valleys and hills.

There are three languages for Al-Rabwah, and a group of readers have read each of them. It is Rabwah with a damma on the ra’, and this is how most of the readers of Medina, Hijaz, and Iraq read it. Rabwah with a fatha on the ra’, and this is how some of the people of Ash-Sham and some of the people of Kufa read it. It is said that it is a language of Tamim. Rabwah with a kasra on the ra’, and this is how Ibn Abbas read it, as mentioned.

I do not accept that it should be read except in one of the two languages: either with the ra’ open or with the damma. Because people in their cities read it with one of them. I prefer reading it with the damma more than with the fatha, because it is the more common of the two languages among the Arabs. As for the kasra, then in refusing to read it with it, there is a clear indication that reading it with it is not permissible. It was called a hill because it grew, became thick and high, from the saying: This thing grew, if it swelled and became large. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his Surat Al-Baqarah 2:265 And the parable of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of Allah and strengthening of their souls is like that of a garden on a height which is struck by heavy rain, so it produces its fruit double; but if heavy rain does not strike it, then dew. And Allah is Seeing of what you do. statement: Like a garden
h
on a hill
, he said: The hill is the apparent, level place.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abdul Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, he said, Mujahid said:
m: It is the flat, elevated land.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Like a garden
h
on a hill
, he said: rising from the earth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: Like a garden
h
on a hill
, and a hill is a high place where rivers do not flow, and in which there are gardens.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
On a hill
h
on a hill
of land.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: Like a garden
h
on a hill
, and a hill is a raised part of the earth.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: Like a garden
h
on a hill
, he said: a high place where rivers do not flow.

x: Others said: It is level.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan
m: regarding his statement:
h
Like a garden on a height
, he said: It is the flat land that rises above the waters.

x: As for his saying: A downpour struck it, He, may His praise be glorified, means: A downpour of rain struck the garden on the hill, which is the land of the garden, and it is a heavy, abundant rain. His saying:
h
It yielded its fruit twice as much

, means Paradise: it yielded twice as much fruit when it was struck by a downpour of rain. Eating is the thing eaten, and it is like terror and mockery, and similar nouns that come with the form fa’l.

i: As for eating, with the alif open and the kaf silent, it is the act of eating, and it is said from it: I ate eating, and I ate one meal, as the poet said:
x: There is no food if you get it through spoils, nor hunger if you starve it through love.

So he opened the alif because it means action. And what indicates that this is the case is his saying: nor hunger. And if he closed the alif of the word eat, its meaning would be: the food that I ate, so the meaning of that would then be: what food I ate was booty.
As for his saying:
h
If it does not receive heavy rain
, then dew, dew is the dew and softness of rain, as in:

c: Abbas bin Muhammad told us, Hajjaj told us, Ibn Jurayj said:
m: Fatal means dew - on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for dew, it is the dew.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: If no downpour falls on it, then a drizzle, meaning a shower.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: Fatal, he said: Dew is the drizzle of rain, meaning the softness of it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: Fatal means to be overwhelmed.

x: What the Almighty means by this parable is: Just as the fruit of this paradise whose description has been described has become weak when the downpour is abundant, if this downpour misses, so does the dew. God weakens the charity of the one who gives charity and spends his money seeking His pleasure and to strengthen himself, without any favor or harm, whether his spending is little or much. His spending will not be disappointed or failed, just as the paradise whose description has been described by the Almighty becomes weak, whether the rain falls on it little or much. He does not fail in its goodness under any circumstances. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, a group of people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying: So it yields its fruit doubled, but if no downpour falls on it, then a drizzle, he said: Just as the fruit of that garden was doubled, so too the fruit of this spender was doubled.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then it yields its fruit double, but if no downpour falls on it, then dew. This is an example that God gave for the deeds of the believer, saying: His goodness has no successor, just as the goodness of this Paradise has no successor in any case, either downpour or dew.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: This is an example of someone who spends his money seeking the pleasure of God.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
Those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of God verse
, he said: This is an example that God has given for the actions of the believer.

x: How was it said: If no downpour falls on it, then a drizzle, when this is report about something that has already happened?

It means was. The meaning of the statement is: So it produced its fruit double, and if the downpour did not hit it, dew hit it. This is in the statement like the saying of the speaker: I kept two horses, and if I did not keep two, then one at its value, meaning: unless I was - it is necessary to imply was, because it is a predicate.

i: And from it is the saying of the poet:
x: If we were related, you would not have given birth to me as a mean person, and you would not have found it useful to acknowledge her.

By that, may His praise be exalted, He means, And God, of what you do, O people, in your expenditures that you spend, is All-Seeing. Nothing of it or of your actions in it or otherwise is hidden from Him. He knows who among you spends with favor and harm, and who spends seeking the pleasure of God and to strengthen himself, so He counts you until He rewards all of you according to your work, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. Rather, what He, the Most High, means by this statement is a warning against His punishment for the expenses that His servants spend and other actions: that one of His creation should do something that He has previously forbidden, or be excessive in what He has commanded, because that is in the sight and hearing of God, He knows it and counts it against them, and He is watching His creation.

evidence.text: Abu Jaʿfar said: This interpretation that we have mentioned from Mujahid and Al-Hasan is an interpretation that is far-fetched in meaning from what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the recitation.
There are three languages for Al-Rabwah, and a group of readers have read each of them.
It is Rabwah with a damma on the ra’, and this is how most of the readers of Medina, Hijaz, and Iraq read it.
Rabwah with a fatha on the ra’, and this is how some of the people of Ash-Sham and some of the people of Kufa read it.
Rabwah with a kasra on the ra’, and this is how Ibn Abbas read it, as mentioned.
Abu Jaʿfar said: I do not accept that it should be read except in one of the two languages: either with the ra’ open or with the damma.
Because people in their cities read it with one of them.
As for the kasra, then in refusing to read it with it, there is a clear indication that reading it with it is not permissible.

x: The meaning of this is: “O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, like one who spends his wealth [only] to be seen by people and does not believe in God and the Last Day. His example is like that of a smooth rock upon which is dust, then a downpour strikes it and leaves it bare. They are unable to do anything with what they have earned.”
h
Would any of you like to
have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, beneath which rivers flow, for him therein of all kinds of fruits, and he was overcome with old age? The verse. The meaning of his saying:
h
Would any of you like
h
would any of you like

, to have a garden, meaning: an orchard, of palm trees and grapevines with rivers flowing beneath it, meaning: from beneath the garden, for him in it of all kinds of fruits, and the ha in his saying: for him refers to one, and the ha and the alif in in it refer to the garden, and he was afflicted, meaning: and one of you was afflicted, of old age and he had weak offspring.
And He, the Most High, made the garden of palm trees and grapes, which He, the Most High, said to His believing servants:
h
Would any of you like to

have, as an example of the spending of the hypocrite who spends to show off to people, not seeking the pleasure of God? So people - because of what appears to them of his charity for giving what he gives and his apparent work - praise him and thank him for that work during his life, in its beauty like the beauty of the garden, and it is the paradise that God, the Most High, made an example of his work, of palm trees and grapes in which he has all kinds of fruits, because his work that he does outwardly in this world has all kinds of good in this world, by which he defends himself, his blood, his wealth and his offspring, and by which he gains praise and good commendation from people, and by which he takes his share of the spoils, along with many things that are too numerous to count, so he has in that from all kinds of good in this world, just as He, the Most High, described the paradise that He described as an example of his work, that it has all kinds of fruits.

Then He, the Most High, said: And old age overtook him, and he had weak offspring, meaning that the owner of the garden was overtaken by old age, and he had weak offspring, young children, and there struck it, meaning: the garden was struck by a whirlwind in which was fire, and it was burned,” meaning that his garden was burned by the wind in which was fire, while he was in need of it and in need of its fruits due to his old age and his weakness in cultivating it, and while his children were young and unable to revive it and take care of it. So he was left with nothing, and he was in greater need of his garden and its fruits than ever before, due to the affliction that struck it from the whirlwind in which was fire. He says: Likewise, the one who spends his money to be seen by people, God extinguishes his light, takes away the splendor of his work, and nullifies his reward, until he meets Him and returns to Him when he is most in need of his work, when there is no one to pardon him, no forgiveness for his sins, and no repentance, and his work is wasted, just as Paradise, whose description is described by God Almighty, is burned when its owner grows old and his offspring are young, when they are most in need of it, so its benefits are nullified for him.
This example that God gave for those who spend their money to be seen by people in this verse is similar to the other example that He gave for them in His saying: “
h
Then their example is like that of a smooth rock upon which is dust
, and a downpour strikes it and leaves it bare. They are not able to do anything with what they have earned.”

The people of interpretation have disputed over the interpretation of this verse, but the meanings of their statements about it, even though their expressions differed, return to the meaning that we have stated about it. The best of them in explaining its meaning, and the closest to the truth in his statement about it, is al-Suddi.

c: Musa told me, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines with rivers flowing beneath it

, and in it he has all kinds of fruits, and he is afflicted with old age and has weak children, and then a whirlwind containing fire strikes it and burns it up?” This is another example of spending for show. He spends his money to show off to people, and his money is gone while he is showing off, so God will not reward him for it. So when the Day of Resurrection comes and he needs his spending, he will find that it has been burned by showing off and is gone, just as this man spent on his garden, until it grew and his children increased and he needed his garden, and a poisonous wind came and burned his garden, and he did not find anything of it. So is the one who spends for show.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
Would any of you like to
have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, as an example of someone who is excessive in obeying God until he dies. He said, He says:
h
Would any of you like to

have a world in which he does not work in obedience to God, like someone who has gardens beneath which rivers flow, for him therein are all kinds of fruits, and old age afflicts him and he has weak offspring, and
h
a whirlwind in which there is fire

strikes it and it is burned up, so his example after his death is like the example of someone whose garden was burned up while he was old and could not benefit from it at all, and his children were young and could not benefit from it at all. And likewise the excessive after death, everything is a regret for him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated on the authority of Abd al-Malik on the authority of Ata’ who said: Umar asked the people about this verse, but he did not find anyone who could satisfy him, until Ibn Abbas, who was behind him, said: O Commander of the Faithful, I feel something about it in myself. He said: I turned to him and he said: Move here, why do you belittle yourself? He said: This is a parable that God, the Almighty, has given, saying: One of you would like to spend his life doing the deeds of the good and the happy, until when he is most in need of ending it with good, when his life is over and his end is near, he ends it with one of the deeds of the miserable, which spoils it all, and burns him when he is most in need of it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah:
m: That Umar recited this verse:
h
Would any of you like to
have a garden of date palms and grapevines? He said: This is a parable for a person: He does a good deed, until when he is at the end of his life and most in need of it, he does a bad deed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said,
m: I heard Abu Bakr ibn Abi Malikah, narrating on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair that he heard him say: Umar asked the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Why was this verse revealed:
h
Would any of you like to

have a garden of date palms and grapevines? They said: God knows best. Umar became angry and said: “Say: We know or we do not know.” Ibn Abbas said: I have something in mind about it, O Commander of the Faithful. Umar said: Say it, O son of my brother, and do not belittle yourself! Ibn Abbas said: You have given an example of a deed. Umar said: What deed? He said: Deed. Umar said: A rich man used to do good deeds, then God sent Satan to him, so he committed sins until he drowned out all his deeds. He said: I heard Abdullah bin Abi Malekah narrating something similar to this, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who heard it from him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: I heard Abu Bakr Ibn Abi Malekah narrating that he heard Ubayd Ibn Umair, Ibn Jurayj said: And I heard Ubayd God Ibn Abi Malekah saying: I heard Ibn Abbas, they both said: That Umar Ibn Al-Khattab asked the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar, except that Umar said: For a man who does good deeds, then Satan is sent to him and he does sins.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: I asked Ata’ about it. Then Ibn Jurayj said: And Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me, on the authority of Mujahid, they said: It is a parable for deeds. Ibn Jurayj said: And Ibn Abbas said: It is a parable for deeds. He begins by doing a righteous deed, and it is a parable for Paradise, which is made of palm trees and grapes, beneath which rivers flow, and in which he has all kinds of fruits. Then he commits an evil at the end of his life, and he persists in his evil until he dies in that state, and the hurricane in which there is fire that burned Paradise is a parable for his evil in which he died. Ibn Abbas said: Paradise was his livelihood and the livelihood of his children, and it was burned, and he was not able to defend his Paradise because of his old age. His offspring were unable to defend their paradise because of their youth, until it was burned. He says: This is his example, he meets me while he is the poorest of all, he does not find anything with me, and he is unable to defend himself from the punishment of God, and he is unable because of his old age and the young age of his children to work for paradise. Likewise, there is no repentance if the work is cut off when he dies. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Mujahid, I heard Ibn Abbas say: He is like the one who neglects to obey God until he dies. Ibn Jurayj said, and Mujahid said:
h
Would any of you like to

have a world in which he does not work in obedience to God, like this one who has a paradise? So his example after his death is like the example of this one when his paradise was burned while he was old and could not benefit from it at all, and his children were young and could not benefit him at all. Likewise, the one who neglects after death, everything is a regret for him. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:266
h
Would any of you like to

have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, beneath which rivers flow, for him therein of all kinds of fruits, and he was afflicted with old age while he had weak offspring, and then a whirlwind in which was fire struck it and it was burned? Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses that you may give thought.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Would any of you like to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines with rivers flowing beneath it

? The verse means: A strong poisonous wind struck it. Thus does God make clear to you the signs that you may give thought. This is an example, so understand the examples of God, the Almighty and Majestic, for He said: And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge. (al-Ankabut 29:43) This is a man who has grown old, his bones have weakened, and his dependents have increased, then his garden was burned down, leaving the rest of it behind, when he was in dire need of it. He says:
h
Would any of you like
his deeds to be lost on the Day of Resurrection when he was in dire need of it?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Would any of you like to have a garden to his statement

: and it was burned up, he said: his garden was gone when he was in greatest need of it when he was old and unable to earn a living, and he has weak offspring, who could not benefit him. He said: Al-Hasan used to say: and it was burned up, so it was gone when he was in greatest need of it, so that is his statement:
h
Would any of you like
his deeds to be lost when he was in greatest need of them?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: God has set forth a beautiful example, and all His examples are beautiful, blessed and exalted be He. He said, He said:
h
Would any of you like to

have a garden of palm trees until His saying: in which are all kinds of fruits. He said: He made it in his youth, then old age overtook him and he had weak offspring at the end of his life, then a hurricane with fire came and burned his garden, so he did not have the strength to plant something like it, and his offspring had no good to return to him. And likewise the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection, when he is returned to God, the Most High, he has no good to seek repentance for, just as this man does not have the strength to plant something like his garden, and he does not find any good that he has prepared for himself that will return to him, just as his offspring did not avail him of this, and he was deprived of his reward when he was the poorest to it, just as this man was deprived of his garden when he was the poorest to it when he was old and his offspring were weak. This is a parable that God Almighty gave for the believer and the disbeliever in what they were given in this world: How the believer is saved in the Hereafter, and honor and bliss are stored up for him, and wealth is stored up for him in this world, and wealth is spread out for the disbeliever in this world that is cut off, and evil is stored up for him that he will never leave, and he will remain in it humiliated forever, because he [bragged to his companion] and trusted in what he had, and was not certain that he would meet his Lord. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ:
m: h
Would any of you like to
have a garden, the verse. He said: [This is a parable that God has set forth]:
h
Would any of you like to

have a garden of palm trees and grapes [in which he has all kinds of fruits], and the man [has grown old and weak], and he has young children [and God has tested them] in their garden, so God sent upon it a hurricane with fire in it, and it was burned, and the man was unable to defend his garden due to old age, nor his children due to their young age, so his garden was lost when he was in greatest need of it. He says:
h
Would any of you like to

live in misguidance and sin until death comes to him, and he comes on the Day of Resurrection with his deeds lost to him when he was in greatest need of them? He will say: Son of Adam, you came to Me when you were in greatest need of good, so where is what you have put forth for yourself?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said, and he recited the words of God, the Almighty: O you who believe, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, then he gave an example of that and said:
h
Would any of you like to

have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, until he reached and a whirlwind containing fire struck it and it was burned up? He said: Its rivers flowed and its fruits were flowing, and he had weak offspring, and a whirlwind containing fire struck it and it was burned up.
h
Would any of you like

this? Just as one of you beautifies himself when he gives from his charity and spending, until he has a garden with me and its rivers flow and its fruits are flowing and it is for his children and his children’s children, and a whirlwind strikes it and burns it up.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding His statement:
h
Would any of you like to have a garden of date palms and grapes with rivers flowing beneath it

? A man planted an orchard in which there were all kinds of fruits, but he became old and had weak offspring, and a hurricane with fire struck it and it was burned, so he was unable to protect his orchard from his old age, and his offspring were unable to protect his orchard, so his livelihood and the livelihood of his offspring were lost. This is a parable that God has given for the disbeliever, saying: He will meet Me on the Day of Resurrection while he is in greatest need of any good that may come to him, but he will not find any good for himself with Me, and he will not be able to protect himself from any of God’s punishment.

x: We have shown that what is more deserving of the interpretation of this is what we have mentioned, because God, the Most High, preceded His believing servants with the prohibition of showing off and causing harm in their charity. Then He gave an example of the one who shows off and causes harm to the one who gives charity to him, and He likened him to the hypocrite who spends his wealth to show off to people. The story of this verse and the example before it was similar to the example given to them before it, so it was more appropriate to connect it to its counterpart than to interpret it as being similar to what was not mentioned before it or with it.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How was it said: And old age afflicted him, when it is a past tense verb, and was it linked to his saying:
h
Would any of you like to

This is so, because his saying: Ayud can be put in it if instead of an, so when it is suitable with if and if, and their meaning is both the future, the Arabs allowed themselves to return the verb with the interpretation of if, to yaf’al with an, so that is why he said: fa’asabaha, and in his school of thought it is like if, since it resembles an in the meaning of recompense, so it was put in its places, and an was answered with the answer of if and if with the answer of an, so it is as if it was said:
h
Would any of you like
if he had a garden of palm trees and grapes with rivers flowing beneath it and he had all kinds of fruits in it and he was afflicted with old age?
How is it said here: And he has weak offspring, and He said in
r
(An-Nisa’: 9)
, And let those fear who, if they left behind them, would be weak offspring?

Because fa’il is pluralized as fa’la’ and fa’al, so it is said: a charming man, from a charming and charming people. As for the hurricane, it is a violent wind that blows from the earth to the sky, like a column, gathering hurricanes.
From this is the saying of Yazid bin Mufrij Al-Himyari: People who sheltered us, but their shelter was a storm of the corruption of wasteful Iraq.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of his saying: A hurricane in which there was fire, and it was burned.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is: a wind that contains strong poisons.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me, he said, Yusuf bin Khalid Al-Samti told us, he said, Nafi’ bin Malik told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A whirlwind in which is fire
, a wind in which is a strong poisonous wind.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Atiyah told us, he said, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding:
h
A whirlwind in which is fire
, he said: The hot poisons from which the jinn were created, which burn.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Then a whirlwind of fire struck it and it was burned. He said: It is the hot poisonous winds that leave no one behind.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Hammani told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Tamimi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: A tornado in which there is fire, so it burns, which kills.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The poisons from which the jinn were created are one part of seventy parts of fire.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: A hurricane in which there is fire, so it burns, it is a wind in which there is a strong poisonous wind.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: A hurricane in which there is fire, he said: A severe poisonous wind.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A hurricane in which there is fire, meaning: A strong poisonous wind struck it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: A hurricane in which there is fire, so I was burned. As for the hurricane, it is the wind, and as for the fire, it is the poisonous winds.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: A hurricane in which there is fire, meaning: a strong, poisonous wind.

x: Others said: It is a wind with severe cold.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said:
m: Al-Hasan used to say regarding his statement:
h
A whirlwind in which there is fire
, and it was burned, in it is freezing cold.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: A hurricane in which there is fire, so it burned, meaning by the hurricane, a wind in which there is hail.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Just as your Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, has explained to you the matter of spending in His cause, and how He directed it, and what you have and what you do not have to do with it, likewise He explains to you the verses other than that, so He informs you of its rulings, its lawful and unlawful aspects, and He clarifies its proofs for you, as a favor from Him to you, so that you may reflect, meaning: so that you may reflect with your minds, so that you may ponder and consider God’s proofs in it and learn what is in it of its rulings, so that you may obey God with it. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:266
h
Would any of you like to

have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, beneath which rivers flow, for him therein of all kinds of fruits, and he was afflicted with old age while he had weak offspring, and then a whirlwind in which was fire struck it and it was burned?
Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses that you may give thought. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, he said: Mujahid said:
m: Perhaps you will reflect, he said: You will obey.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Thus does God make clear to you the signs that you may give thought, meaning: about the passing of this world and its annihilation, and the coming of the Hereafter and its permanence.

evidence.text: Ibn Wakee’ told us, my father told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah: That Umar recited this verse: Would any of you like to have a garden of date palms and grapevines?

x: What He, the Most High, meant by His saying: O you who believe, is to believe in God, His Messenger, and the verses of His Book. And what He meant by His saying: Spend, is to give zakat and charity, as:- Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement:
h
Spend from the good things you have earned

, meaning: give in charity. By this, He, the Most High, means: Pay zakat from the good things you have earned through your own actions, either through trade or industry, from gold and silver. And by the good things, He means the good things.
He says: Pay zakat on your money that you have earned lawfully and give in your zakat gold and silver, the good ones and not the bad ones, as:

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Shuʿbah, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding this verse:
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned
, he said: from trade.

c: Musa bin Abd al-Rahman told me, he said, Zaid bin al-Habbab told us, he said, and Shu’bah told me, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Hatim bin Bakr Al-Dhabi told me, he said, Wahb told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Adam told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Spend from the good things which you have earned
, he said: lawful trade.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata bin al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muqal:
m: h
Spend from the good things you have earned
, he said: There is no bad in the wealth of the believer, but do not aim at the bad part of it when you spend.

c: Issam bin Rawad bin Al Jarrah told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Abu Bakr Al Hudhali told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, he said:
m: I asked Ali bin Abi Talib, may God’s prayers be upon him, about his saying:
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned
, he said: From gold and silver.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Of the good things which you have earned
, he said: Trade.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Spend from the good things you have earned
, meaning: from the best of your wealth and your souls.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned
, he said: from this gold and silver.
