x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And also spend from what We have produced for you from the earth, so give in charity and give zakat from the palm trees, grapevines, wheat, barley, and whatever zakat is required from the plants of the earth, such as:

c: Issam bin Rawad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hudhali told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, he said:
m: I asked Ali, may God’s prayers be upon him, about the words of God Almighty: And of what We have produced for you from the earth, he said: He means from the grain and the fruit, and everything has a zakat.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And from what We have produced for you from the earth
, he said, the palm trees.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And from what We have produced for you from the earth
, he said: from the fruit of the palm tree.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned
, he said: from trade, and from that which We have produced for you from the earth, from fruits.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And of what We have produced for you from the earth, he said: This is about fruit and grain.

x: What he meant by his saying, may His praise be exalted: And do not intend to do that which is unclean, is not intentional, and not on purpose. It was mentioned that this is in Abdullah’s reading: And do not lead from ‘ummat, and this is from ‘yammamma, and the meaning is the same even if the words differ. It is said: I intended for someone, I went to him, I went to him, meaning: I intended for him and I went to him deliberately, as Maymun bin Qais Al-A’sha said: I went to Qais, and how many lands are there between them, and how many are the most important and difficult ones? And as:- Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And do not intend to do so with unclean water, and do not do so deliberately.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And do not perform tayammum, do not do it deliberately.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, similarly.

x: By the bad, He, may His praise be glorified, means the bad, the not good. He says: Do not intentionally give the bad part of your money in your charity, but give charity from the good and pure. This verse was revealed about a man from the Ansar who hung a straw basket - in the place where the Muslims hung their dates as charity - as charity from his dates.
Who said that?

c: Al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Adi ibn Thabit, on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn Azib,
m: regarding the statement of God, the Almighty:
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned

and from that which We have produced for you from the earth until His statement: And God is Free of need, Praiseworthy, he said: It was revealed about the Ansar. When the days of the palm harvest came, the Ansar would bring out the stalks of unripe dates from their walls and hang them on a rope between the two pillars in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that the poor emigrants would eat from them. A man among them would take the husks and put them in with the stalks of unripe dates, thinking that this was permissible. So God, the Almighty, revealed about those who did that: And do not aim at the bad thereof, spending [in charity], he said: Do not aim at the husks thereof, spending [in charity].

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us,
m: Al-Suddi claimed, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, something similar, except that he said: Some of them would deliberately put the straw in the bucket, thinking that it was permissible for him, due to the large number of straws that were placed, so the following was revealed about those who did that: And do not aim at the bad thereof, spending [yourselves], the straw that had been washed, and if it were given to you, you would not accept it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, he said:
m: They used to bring in charity the worst of their dates and the worst of their food, so the verse was revealed:
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned
Al-Bara’ bin Azib. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:267
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned

and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward the bad thereof, spending while you would not take it except by closing your eyes to it. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.

c: Issam bin Rawad told me, he said, my father told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hudhali told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah al-Salmani, he said:
m: I asked Ali about the saying of God: “
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned
and from that which We have produced for you from the earth.
h
And do not aim towards the bad thereof

, spending [something].” He said: Ali said: This verse was revealed regarding the obligatory zakat. A man would go to the dates and harvest them, setting aside the good ones. Then when the one giving charity came, he would give him some of the bad ones. So God the Almighty said:
h
And do not aim towards the bad thereof
, spending [something].

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abdul Jalil bin Hamid Al-Yahsabi told me: Ibn Shihab told him, he said, Abu Umamah bin Sahl bin Hanif told me
m: regarding the verse in which God Almighty said, And do not give away the bad thereof, spending it, he said: It is the ja’rur and the color of Habiq, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade it from being taken in charity.
b.via: Abu Umamah bin Sahl bin Hanif

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And do not give away the bad part of it, spending. He said: They used to give in charity - meaning from the palm trees - its stalks and its husks, but they were forbidden from that, and they were commanded to give in charity the good part.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned
until His saying:
h
And know that God is Free of need and Praiseworthy

. It was mentioned to us that a man would have two gardens during the time of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would take the worst of them in terms of dates and give them in charity, and mix some chaff with it. So God criticized them for that and forbade them from it.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not aim towards the bad thereof
, spending it, he said: You intend to take the worst of your wealth and give it in charity, and you will not take it unless you close your eyes to it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: A man used to give away the worst of his money in charity, so this verse was revealed: And do not give away the bad therefrom, spending [yourselves].

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Abdullah bin Kathir told us:
m: He heard Mujahid say: And do not aim at that which is bad, spending it. He said: In the baskets that are kept free. He saw some husks among them, so he said: What is this? Ibn Jurayj said: I heard Ata’ say: A man hung some husks among the baskets that are hung in Madinah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is this? What a bad thing to hang this!! Then the verse was revealed: And do not aim at that which is bad, spending it.

x: Others said that the meaning of this is: Do not spend on the bad and forbidden things, and fail to spend on the good and lawful things.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said - and I asked him about the words of God Almighty:
h
And do not give away that which is bad
, spending from it, - he said: The bad and unlawful, do not give away that which is unlawful, spending from it, for God Almighty does not accept it.

x: The interpretation of the verse is the interpretation that we narrated from the one we narrated from among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, [because of the authenticity of its chain of transmission], and the agreement of the people of interpretation on that, without what Ibn Zayd said.

By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And you will not take the wicked from your rights, and the ha in His statement: by taking it is from the mention of the wicked, unless you turn a blind eye to it, meaning: unless you turn away in taking it from some of what is due to you from your right, so you make it permissible for yourselves. It is said: So-and-so overlooked some of So-and-so’s rights, so he overlooks them. And from that is the saying of Al-Tirmaah bin Hakim: No people have tempted us with the odd number, and there are men who are content to turn a blind eye to injustice.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is that you will not take the bad from your creditors in the case of your rights owed to them, except because you have overlooked what is owed to you by them.
Who said that?

c: Issam bin Rawad told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Abu Bakr al-Hudhali told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Ubaidah, he said:
m: I asked Ali about it and he said: And you will not take it unless you close your eyes to it, meaning: And none of you should take this bad thing until it is digested for him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muammil told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib:
m: h
And you would not take it unless you close your eyes to it
, meaning: If a man had something on a man, and he gave it to him, he would not take it, unless he saw that he had diminished his right.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not aim towards the bad thereof

, spending [in charity] while you would not take it [in charity] unless you close your eyes to it, meaning: If you had a right over someone, and he came to you with a right less than your right, you would not take into account the good until you reduced it. That is what His statement means: unless you close your eyes to it. So how can you accept for Me what you would not accept for yourselves, when My right over you is from the best of your wealth and your souls? This is His statement: By no means will you attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love
r
(Al Imran 3:92)

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And you will not take it except that you close your eyes to it, he said: Do not take it from your creditors or in your sales except with an increase over the good in the measure.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned

and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward the bad thereof, spending [in charity] while you would not take it [from God] unless you closed your eyes to it.” That is because some men were giving the zakat of their wealth in the form of dates, and they were giving the chaff as zakat. He said: If some of them were to ask for some and then pay it, they would not take it unless they saw that his right had been closed to him.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
And you would not take it unless you closed your eyes to it
, meaning: If a man owed you a debt and he paid you something worse than what you owed him, would you take it from him unless you were reluctant to do so?

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, Yazid told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned
until His statement: unless you close your eyes to it, he said: When God commanded them to pay zakat, a hypocrite would come with cold food of dates or other things, and God disliked that and said:
h
Spend from the good things which you have earned

and from that which We have produced for you from the earth, meaning: You would not take it except that you close your eyes to it, meaning: There was no man among you who had a right over another man and gave him less than his right and took it, except that he knew that he had diminished it, so do not accept for me what you would not accept for yourselves, so he took something, while closing his eyes to it, diminishing his right.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: You will not take this bad, filthy thing - if you buy it from its people - at the price of the good thing, unless they turn a blind eye to its price.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And you would not take it unless you closed your eyes to it
, he said: If you found it being sold in the market, you would not take it until you had taken some of its price.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And you would not take it unless you close your eyes to it
, meaning: You would not take this bad thing at the price of this good thing unless you close your eyes to it.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: You would not take this bad, filthy thing if it were given to you, unless you turn a blind eye to it and take it while you are reluctant to do so, out of shame before the one who gave it to you.
Who said that?

c: Al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Adi ibn Thabit, on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn Azib:
m: And you would not take it except that you close your eyes to it, he said: If you were given something, you would not accept it except out of shyness before its owner, that he sent you something that he had no need for.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, he said,
m: Al-Suddi claimed, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Al-Baraa, something similar, except that he said: Except out of shyness before his companion, and anger that he sent you something that he had no need for.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: You will not take this bad part of your right, unless you close your eyes to your right.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Maqal:
m: And you will not take it, he says: And you will not take it from what is rightfully yours, unless you close your eyes to it, he says: I close my eyes to you from my right.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: You will not take what is forbidden unless you turn a blind eye to the sin that is upon you in taking it.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said - and I asked him about his statement:
h
And you would not take it unless you close your eyes to it -
he said, he says: I would not take that forbidden thing unless you close your eyes to what is in it of sin. He said: And in the speech of the Arabs: By God, he took Surat Al-Baqarah 2:267
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned

and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward the bad thereof, spending while you would not take it except by closing your eyes to it. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy. it, and he closed his eyes to what is in it, and he knew that it was forbidden and false.

x: What is more appropriate to interpret this in our view is to say: God, the Almighty, urged His servants to give charity and zakat from their wealth, and imposed it upon them, so that what was imposed from their wealth became a right for the people of the two shares of charity. Then God, the Exalted, commanded them to take out from the good - which is the good of their wealth - the good. This is because the people of the two shares are partners with the owners of the wealth in their wealth, in what is due to them from charity after it is due. There is no doubt that every two partners in wealth, each one of them has according to his ownership, and neither of them has the right to prevent his partner from his right from the property in which he is a partner, by giving him - according to his right from it - from something else that is worse and inferior. Likewise, the one who pays zakat on his wealth, God has forbidden him to give the people of the two shares, from what is due to them from his wealth of the good and good right, so that they became partners in it, from the bad and bad other than it, and he prevents them from what is their right in the good from his good wealth.

As if the owner of the money was all bad and not good, then zakat is obligatory on it and the people who have two shares of charity in it become partners in what God has obligated them to do with it. He is not required to give them the good and pure money from other than his money from which they have a right. Then God the Blessed and Most High said to the owners of wealth: “Purify from the best of your wealth, and do not give the bad and poor to those who have a share of charity, and withhold from them what is due to them from the good and pure wealth. You will not take the bad for yourselves in place of the good that is due to you from those who are obligated to do so from among your partners, creditors, and others, except out of disregard on your part, and because you are reluctant to take it.” He says: And do not do to those who are obligated to do so from your wealth, what you would not be pleased for others to do to you in your rights that are due to you from their wealth.

If a man volunteers to give charity that is not obligatory, then although I dislike for him to give in it anything but the best and purest of his wealth, because God Almighty is more deserving of being brought near to Him with the most honorable and purest of wealth, and charity is the offering of the believer, so I do not forbid him to give in it anything other than the best, because what is less than the best may be more beneficial due to its abundance or the greatness of its danger, and it is better placed for the poor, and for those who are given it as a means of drawing near to God Almighty, than the good, due to its smallness or the smallness of its danger and the small benefit of its benefit to the one who gives it. And the group of scholars said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zari’ narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Alqamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin,
m: saying: I asked Ubaydah about this verse: “
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned

and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward the defective therefrom, spending [in charity] while you would not take it [from God] unless you close your eyes to it.” He said: That is about zakat. A counterfeit dirham is more beloved to me than a date.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Salamah ibn Alqamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, he said:
m: I asked Ubaydah about that, and he said: That is only in zakat, and a counterfeit dirham is more beloved to me than a date.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said:
m: I asked Ubaidah about this verse: “
h
O you who have believed
h
spend from the good things which you have earned

and from that which We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim toward the bad therefrom, spending [in charity] while [yourselves] would not take it.” Ubaidah said: This is only about what is obligatory, and there is nothing wrong with a man volunteering a date, and a counterfeit dirham is better than a date.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Sirin,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not give away that which is bad

, spending it, he said: This is only in the obligatory zakat, but as for voluntary charity, there is nothing wrong with a man giving a counterfeit dirham in charity, and a counterfeit dirham is better than a date.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Know, O people, that God Almighty is independent of your charity and anything else. Rather, He has commanded you to do it and imposed it on your wealth, out of mercy from Him to you, so that He may enrich your dependents, strengthen your weak ones, and reward you abundantly for it in the Hereafter, not because He is in need of you in it.
By his saying: Hamid, he means that He is praised by His creation for the blessings He bestowed upon them and the grace He extended to them, such as:

c: Al-Husayn bin Amr bin Muhammad Al-Anqazi told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And God is Rich and Praiseworthy
, regarding your charity.

x: By this, the Almighty means: Satan promises you, O people, by giving charity and paying the obligatory zakat on your wealth, that you will become poor, and orders you to immorality, meaning: and orders you to disobey God Almighty and abandon His obedience, and God promises you forgiveness from Him, meaning: God Almighty promises you, O believers, that He will cover your immorality, by pardoning you for your punishment for it, and He will forgive you your sins for the charity that you give, and bounty, meaning: and He promises you that He will replace your charity, and He will bestow upon you from His gifts, and He will bestow upon you abundantly in your provisions, as:- Muhammad bin Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Al-Husayn bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Two are from God, and two are from Satan: Satan threatens you with poverty, he says: Do not spend your wealth and keep it for yourself, for you will need it, and orders you to immorality, “and God promises you forgiveness from Him,” for these sins, and bounty in provision.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying:
h
Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality
, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. He said: forgiveness for your immorality, and bounty for your poverty.

c: Hannad told us, he said, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The devil has a bond with the son of Adam, and the angel has a bond. As for the bond of the devil, it is a threat of evil and a denial of the truth. As for the bond of the angel, it is a threat of good and a belief in the truth. So whoever finds that, let him know that it is from God and let him praise God. And whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge in God from the devil. Then he recited: “The devil threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality.” Ibn Humayd narrated, Al-Hakam bin Bashir bin Salman narrated, Amr narrated, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: A person has a touch from the king and a touch from the devil. The touch from the king is a promise of good and belief in the truth, and the touch from the devil is a promise of evil and denial of the truth. Abdullah recited:
h
Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality

, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. Amr said: “We heard in this hadith that it was said: If one of you feels something from the touch of the king, let him praise God and ask Him for His bounty, and if he feels something from the touch of the devil, let him seek forgiveness from God and seek refuge from the devil.”

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib told us, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas - or: on the authority of Marra - he
m: said: Abdullah said: Behold, the king has a gathering and the devil has a gathering. The king’s gathering is a promise of good and a belief in the truth, and the devil’s gathering is a promise of evil and a denial of the truth. That is because God says: “
h
Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality

, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.” So if you find something of this, then praise God for it, and if you find something of this, then seek refuge in God from the devil.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God bin Abdullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality

, he said: The angel has a touch, and the devil has a touch. The touch of the angel is a promise of good and a belief in the truth, so whoever finds it, let him praise God. The touch of the devil is a promise of evil and a denial of the truth, so whoever finds it, let him seek refuge in God.

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ata bin Al-Saib told us, on the authority of Murrah Al-Hamdani, that Ibn Masoud said:
m: The king has a touch and the devil has a touch. The touch of the king is to promise him good and to believe in the truth, and the touch of the devil is to promise him evil and to deny the truth. So whoever feels something from the touch of the king, let him praise God for it, and whoever feels something from the touch of the devil, let him seek refuge in God from him. Then he recited this verse: “
h
Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality
, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Fitr, on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’, on the authority of Amer bin Abdah, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: something similar. Ibn Humayd narrated that Jarir narrated on the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:268
h
Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality

, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing. authority of Ata’ on the authority of Murrah ibn Sharahil on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud who said: “Satan has a gathering and the angel has a gathering. As for the gathering of Satan, it is a denial of the truth and a threat of evil. As for the gathering of the angel, it is a threat of good and a belief in the truth. So whoever finds that, let him know that it is from God and let him praise God for it. And whoever finds the other, let him seek refuge from Satan.” Then he recited:
h
Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality
, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty.

x: God Almighty means: And God is Vast in the bounty that He promises to give you from His bounty and the vastness of His treasuries, Knowing of your expenditures and the charity that you spend and give in charity, He counts them for you until He rewards you for them when you come to Him in your afterlife.

evidence.text: Then he recited this verse: “Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality, while God promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means that God grants accuracy in word and deed to whomever He wills of His servants, and whoever among them is granted accuracy in that has been granted much good.
The interpreters differed on this.
Some of them said, the wisdom that God mentioned in this place is: the Qur’an and understanding it.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good
, meaning: knowledge of the Qur’an, its abrogating and abrogated verses, its clear and ambiguous verses, its beginning and end, its lawful and unlawful verses, and its likes.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He gives wisdom to whom He wills
, he said: Wisdom is the Qur’an, and understanding is in the Qur’an.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He gives wisdom to whom He wills
, and whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good. Wisdom is understanding in the Qur’an.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hilali told us, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Mahdi bin Maimun told us, he said, Shuaib bin Al-Habhab told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah:
m: h
And whoever is given wisdom has certainly been given much good
, he said: The Book and understanding it.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He gives wisdom to whom He wills the verse
, he said: It is not prophethood, but rather it is the Qur’an, knowledge, and jurisprudence.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: Jurisprudence is in the Qur’an.

x: Others said: The meaning of wisdom is accuracy in speech and action.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said:
m: I heard Mujahid say: And whoever is given wisdom, he said: accuracy.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
He gives wisdom to whom He wills
, he said: He gives correctness to whom He wills.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
He gives wisdom to whom He wills
. He said: The Book. He gives its accuracy to whom He wills.

x: Others said: It is knowledge of religion.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us that Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
He gives wisdom to whom He wills
, meaning reason in religion. And he recited: And whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: Wisdom is the mind.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I said to Malik: What is wisdom? He said: Knowledge of the religion, understanding it, and following it.

x: Others said: Wisdom is understanding.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Wisdom is understanding.

x: Others said: It is fear.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement:
h
He gives wisdom to whom He wills

, and whoever has been given wisdom, the verse, he said: Wisdom is fear, because the beginning of everything is fear of God. And he recited: Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge
r
(Fatir 35:28)

x: Others said: It is prophecy.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He gives wisdom to whom He wills

, and whoever has been given wisdom, the verse, he said: Wisdom is prophecy. We have previously explained the meaning of wisdom - that it is taken from judgment and the separation of judgment, and that it is the right thing to do - with what indicates its correctness, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. If that is the meaning, then all the statements made by those who said that we mentioned are included in what we said about that. Because being right in matters is only through understanding them, knowledge, and awareness. If that is the case, then the one who is right through his understanding of the places of correctness in his matters is an understanding person who fears God, is a knowledgeable jurist, and prophethood is one of its categories. Because the prophets are guided, they are understanding, and they are granted success in being right in matters, and prophethood is some of the meanings of wisdom. The interpretation of the statement: God grants the right thing to say and do to whomever He wills, and whoever God grants that to has certainly been granted much good.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And none will take heed of what his Lord has admonished him with in these verses, in which He admonished those who spend their wealth with what He admonished them with and others, in them and in other verses of His Book, and remember His promise and His threat therein, and refrain from what his Lord has admonished him from, and obey Him in what He has commanded him to do, except those of understanding, meaning: except those of intellects, who have understood the commands and prohibitions of God Almighty. So He, the Most High, said that sermons are of no benefit except to those who are wise and patient, and that reminders are not prohibitive except to those who are wise and intelligent.

By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And whatever expenditure you spend - meaning: whatever charity you give - or whatever vow you make, meaning by vow, what a person obligates himself to do as a justification in obeying God, and drawing closer to Him: from charity or good deeds, God knows it, meaning that God knows all of that, nothing of it escapes Him, and nothing of it is hidden from Him, little or much, but He counts it, O people, for you until He rewards you all for all of that. So whoever among you spends, gives charity, and vows seeking the pleasure of God and strengthening himself, He will reward him with what He promised him of multiplication, and whoever spends and gives charity to show off to people and vows to Satan, He will reward him with what He promised him of punishment and painful torment, like that which:- Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty: And whatever you spend or vow, God knows it, and He counts it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Then, the Most High threatened those whose spending was for show and whose vows were in obedience to Satan, saying: And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers. That is, for those who spent their money to show off to people and in disobeying God, and whose vows were for Satan and in obedience to him, there are no helpers. They are the plural of helper, just as the word ashraf is the plural of sharif. What He means by His statement: there are no helpers is those who will support them from God on the Day of Resurrection, and will repel His punishment from them on that Day with strength and severe force, and not with ransom. We have shown that the oppressor is the one who puts something in the wrong place. God called the one who spends to show off to people and the one who makes vows to do something other than obey Him an oppressor, because he spends his money in the wrong place and makes vows to do something other than what he should have put it in, and that is his oppression.

x: If someone were to say to us: How did he say: For God knows it, and not say: He knows them both, and he mentioned the vow and the expenditure? It was said: He said: For God knows it, because he meant that God knows what you spent or vowed, and that is why he used the metaphor.
What He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures

, if you announce your charitable expenditures and give them to those to whom you have given them, they are good, meaning: then they are good things. But if you conceal them, meaning: if you cover them up and do not announce them, and give them to the poor, meaning: and give them to the poor in secret, it is better for you, meaning: then concealing them is better for you than announcing them. This is in voluntary charity, as:- Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement:
h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures

, they are good, but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you. Everything is acceptable if the intention is sincere, and secret charity is better. He mentioned to us that charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement:
h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures

, they are good, but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, he said: Everything is acceptable if the intention is sincere, and charity given in secret is better. And he used to say: Charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures

, they are good, but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, so God made secret voluntary charity better than its public one by seventy times. And He made the obligatory charity: its public one is better than its secret one, it is said: twenty-five times. And so are all the obligatory and voluntary acts and all things.

c: Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Hanafi told me, he said, Abdullah bin Othman told us, he said, Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, he said,
m: I heard Sufyan say about His statement:
h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures
, they are good, but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, he said: It is other than zakat.

x: Others said: What God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures
, they are good, is that
h
if you disclose your charitable expenditures

to the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, they are good, but if you conceal them and give them to their poor, it is better for you. They said: As for what is given to the poor Muslims of zakat and voluntary charity, concealing it is better than doing it publicly.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman ibn Shuraih told me, that
m: he heard Yazid ibn Abi Habib say: This verse was revealed:
h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures
, they are good, regarding charity given to the Jews and Christians.

c: Abdullah bin Muhammad al-Hanafi told me, he said, Abdullah bin Othman told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, he said, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, he said:
m: Yazid bin Abi Habib used to order the distribution of zakat in secret. Abdullah said: I like it to be given in public, meaning zakat.

x: God did not specify in His statement:
h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures

, they are good [one thing over another], so that is general except for what is obligatory zakat, for the obligatory duties have been agreed upon by all that the virtue lies in announcing and displaying them, except for zakat, about which we mentioned the difference of opinion among those who differed, with all of them agreeing that it is obligatory, so its ruling that the virtue lies in paying it publicly is the ruling of all other duties besides it.
The reading of this differed.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to read it: And it will expiate for you with a taa. And whoever reads it like this means: And charity will expiate for you some of your misdeeds.

x: Others read: And He will expiate for you with the letter ya, meaning: And God will expiate for you through your charity, as mentioned in the verse, your bad deeds. And he read that after the majority of the people of Medina, Kufa and Basra read: And We will expiate from you with the letter nun and the letter is jazm, meaning: And if you conceal it and give it to the poor, We will expiate from you some of your misdeeds, meaning that God Almighty will reward the one who conceals the charity by expiating some of his misdeeds with the charity that he concealed.

The most correct reading in this regard in our view is the reading of those who read: And We will atone for you with a noon and the letter is in the jussive mood, meaning that God is informing about Himself that He will reward the one who conceals his voluntary charity seeking His face with his charity, by atonement for his sins. If it is read in this way, then it is in the jussive mood in the place of the fa’ in His statement:
h
So it is better for you
. Because the fa’ there takes the place of the answer to the reward.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How did you choose the Jazm based on the sequence in the position of the Fa, and leave the choice of its sequence based on what comes after the Fa, and you know that the most eloquent of speech in the sequence in response to the penalty is the nominative, and the Jazm is only permissible?

We chose that, to indicate with its certainty that expiation - I mean God's expiation of the sins of the one who believes, is inevitably included in what God promised the one who believes that He will reward him for his charity. Because if that is in the certainty, it indicates what we said inevitably. And if it were raised, it would be possible that it is included in what God promised that He will reward him with, and that it is a new report that He expiates the sins of His believing servants, other than rewarding them with that for their charity. Because what comes after the fa in the response to the reward is a new report, so what is conjoined to the new report is in the same ruling as what is conjoined to it, in that it is not included in the reward. And for that reason, we chose the certainty of nakfir in conjunction with it to the position of the fa in His statement:
h
so it is better for you
, and to read it with the letter nun.
What is the reason for including min in His statement: And We will remove from you some of your misdeeds?

The reason for its inclusion in that is in the meaning: And We will expiate for you from your misdeeds what We will to expiate from them, not all of them, so that the servants may be in awe of God, and not rely on His promise as He promised on the charities that the charity giver conceals, so that they dare to transgress His limits and disobey Him.

i: Some Basra grammarians said:
x: The meaning of min is to drop it from this place, and the meaning of that is interpreted as: And We will expiate your sins from you. Abu Jaʿfar said: By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And God is All-Aware of what you do in your charity, whether it is concealed, or announced, or secretly or openly, and in other than that of your deeds, He is All-Knowing.

By that, He means: He has experience and knowledge, nothing of that is hidden from Him, for He encompasses all of it, and He has recorded all of it for its people, until He gives them the reward for all of it, and the recompense for its little and its much.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed.
It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read it: And it will expiate for you with a taa.
And whoever reads it like this means: And charity will expiate for you some of your misdeeds.

And he read that after the majority of the people of Medina, Kufa and Basra read: And We will expiate from you with the letter nun and the letter is jazm, meaning: And if you conceal it and give it to the poor, We will expiate from you some of your misdeeds, meaning that God Almighty will reward the one who conceals the charity by expiating some of his misdeeds with the charity that he concealed.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct reading in this regard in our view is the reading of those who read: And We will atone for you with a noon and the letter is in the jussive mood, meaning that God is informing about Himself that He will reward the one who conceals his voluntary charity seeking His face with his charity, by atonement for his sins.
If it is read in this way, then it is in the jussive mood in the place of the fa’ in His statement: So it is better for you.
And for that reason, we chose the certainty of nakfir in conjunction with it to the position of the fa in His statement: so it is better for you, and to read it with the letter nun.

x: By that, the Most High means: It is not your duty, O Muhammad, to guide the polytheists to Islam, so that you prevent them from voluntary charity and do not give them from it, so that they may enter Islam out of their need for it, but God guides whomever He wills of His creation to Islam and grants them success in it, so charity does not prevent them, as:- Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Shu’bah, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not give charity to the polytheists, so the verse was revealed: ‘And you do not spend except seeking the countenance of God,’ so he gave charity to them.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Abu Dawud told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Iyas, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: They did not submit to their polytheist relatives, so this verse was revealed:
h
You are not responsible for their guidance
, but God guides whom He wills.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: They were afraid to submit to their polytheist relatives, until this verse was revealed:
h
You are not responsible for their guidance
, but God guides whom He wills.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar and Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ja’far bin Iyas, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: They did not submit to their polytheist relatives, so the verse was revealed:
h
You are not responsible for their guidance
, but God guides whom He wills, and He gave them permission.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Iyas, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: There were some people from the Ansar who had relatives and kinship from Qurayza and al-Nadir, and they were afraid to give them charity, and they wanted them to convert to Islam, so the verse was revealed:
h
You are not responsible for their guidance
al-Baqarah 2:17.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It was mentioned to us that some men from among the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you give charity to those who are not of our religion?! So God revealed in that regard the Qur’an:
h
You are not responsible for their guidance

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement:
h
You are not responsible for their guidance

, but God guides whom He wills, he said: If a Muslim man had a kinship with a polytheist and he was in need, he would not give him charity, saying: He is not of my religion!! So God, the Almighty, revealed:
h
You are not responsible for their guidance
, the verse.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying: “
h
You are not responsible for their guidance
, but God guides whom He wills. And whatever you spend of good is for yourselves.” As for:
h
You are not responsible for their guidance
, it means the polytheists. As for the spending, it is among its people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Yaqub Al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr, he said:
m: “They used to give charity [to the poor of the People of the Covenant, but when the number of poor Muslims increased, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not give charity except to the people of your religion. So this verse was revealed,” permitting charity to those who are not of the religion of Islam...]. as:- Surat Al-Baqarah 2:272
h
You are not responsible for their guidance

, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever you spend of good is for yourselves. And you do not spend except seeking the countenance of Allah. And whatever you spend of good will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: He will repay you, and you will not be wronged, he said: It is returned to you, so what is your wealth and why do you harm Him and show off to Him? Your spending is only for yourself and seeking the countenance of God, and God will reward you.

x: As for his statement:
h
For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God
, it is a statement from God the Almighty about the way and purpose of spending. The meaning of the statement is: Whatever good you spend, it is for yourselves. You spend
h
for the poor who are restricted in the cause of God

. The lam in al-fuqara is returned to the place of the lam in fa-lan-fakura as if he said: And whatever you spend of good - meaning: whatever you give in charity of money is for the poor who are restricted in the way of God.

So when he interrupted the speech with his saying: fa-lan-fakura and inserted the fa’ which is the answer to the condition in it, he left repeating it in his saying: fa-l-fuqara since the meaning of the speech was understood, as:

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
You are not responsible for their guidance
, but God guides whom He wills. And whatever you spend of good is for yourselves.” As for
h
You are not responsible for their guidance
, it means the polytheists. As for the expenditure, he explained its people and said:
h
For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God
. It was said: These poor people whom God mentioned in this verse are the poor immigrants in general, not other poor people.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God
, the emigrants of Quraysh in Medina with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he ordered charity to be given to them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement:
h
For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God the verse
, he said: They are the poor immigrants in Medina.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God
, he said: The poor immigrants.

x: God Almighty means by that: Those whose jihad against their enemy has made them confine themselves and prevent them from acting, so they are unable to act. We have previously demonstrated that the meaning of confinement is that a man confined by his illness, poverty, or his struggle against his enemy, or other ailments, is brought to a state in which he prevents himself from acting on his causes, as was sufficient in what has been previously stated.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Those who are confined in the way of God, he said: They confined themselves in the way of God for the sake of conquest.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God

, he said: The entire land was unbelief, no one could go out seeking from the bounty of God, if he went out he would go out in unbelief, and it was said: The entire land was at war with the people of this country, and they did not go in any direction except that they had an enemy in it, so God the Almighty said:
h
For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God
, the verse, they were here in the cause of God.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: those whom the polytheists besieged and prevented them from moving.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: For the poor who were confined in the way of God, the polytheists confined them in Medina.

x: If the interpretation of the verse was as al-Suddi interpreted it, the speech would have been: for the poor who were confined in the way of God, but it is confined, so that indicates that it was their fear of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:273 For the poor who are restricted in the cause of Allah, unable to move about in the land. The ignorant thinks them to be rich because of their abstinence.
h
You will recognize them by their mark
h
They do not ask people insistently

. And whatever you spend of good - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it. the enemy that caused these poor people to be in the state in which they confined themselves - while they were in the way of God - not that the enemy was the one who confined them. It is said of someone who is imprisoned by the enemy: the enemy has besieged him. If the man is imprisoned out of fear of the enemy, it is said: the fear of the enemy has besieged him.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: They are unable to move about in the land or travel in the countries, seeking a livelihood and seeking earnings, so they do not need charity, for fear of the enemy and fear for themselves from them, as:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They are unable to travel on earth, they confined themselves in the path of God to the enemy, so they are unable to trade.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: They are not able to travel throughout the land, meaning trade.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said, his statement, They are unable to travel throughout the land, was that one of them was unable to go out seeking God’s bounty.

x: What he means by that is: The ignorant person of their situation and condition thinks they are rich because of their abstinence from asking, and their refraining from exposing themselves to what is in people’s hands, out of their patience in the face of hardship and distress, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The ignorant think they are rich

, meaning: The ignorant thinks they are rich because of their self-restraint. What he means by his saying: from chastity is that he refrains from asking people for money. It is the action of abstinence from something, and abstinence from something means leaving it, as Ru’bah said: So he forgave her secrets after the honey Meaning: innocent and avoided.

x: By that, the Most High means: You will know them, O Muhammad, by their mark, meaning by their signs and traces, from the words of God Almighty: Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration (al-Fath 48:29). This is the language of the Quraysh. Some Arabs say: By their mark, extending it.

i: As for Thaqeef and some of Asad, they say: By their mark, and from that is the saying of the poet:
x: A young man whom God has blessed with beauty, with a features that are not difficult for the eye to see.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the mark that God Almighty said was for these poor people whose characteristics He described, and that they are known by it.
Some of them said: It is humility and modesty.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You will recognize them by their mark
, he said: humility.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Layth, he said:
m: Mujahid used to say: It is humility.

x: Others said: He meant by that: You can recognize them by the signs of poverty and the need on their faces.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
You will recognize them by their mark
, by the mark of poverty upon them.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
You will recognize them by their mark
, he said: You will recognize in their faces the effort and need.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: You can recognize them by the shabbiness of their clothes. They said: Hunger is hidden.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: You will recognize them by their appearance, he said: The appearance is the shabbiness of their clothes. And hunger was hidden from the people, and the clothes they went out in could not be hidden from the people.

x: The most correct of the statements in this regard is to say: God the Almighty informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He knows them by their signs and the traces of need in them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would recognize those signs and traces from them when he saw them with his own eyes, so he would recognize them and his companions by them, just as one recognizes a sick person and knows that he is sick by seeing them. It is possible that those marks were due to humility on their part, or that they were the signs of need and distress, or that they were the shabbiness of their clothes, or that they were all of these. The signs of need and the traces of distress in a person are recognized and known to be from need and distress by seeing them, not by description. This is because a sick person may become sick in some of his illnesses, similar to the effects of effort from poverty and need.

A rich person with a lot of money may wear shabby clothes, so he dresses like the needy, so there is no indication in any of that by description that the one described is sick and needy. Rather, this is known by seeing them by their marks as God described, similar to what is known that he is sick by seeing them, without describing him by his description.
It is said: The questioner was persistent in his question, if he was insistent, so he is persistent in it.
Did these people ask people without insistence?

It is not permissible that they were asking people for something in the form of charity, whether insistently or not. This is because God the Almighty described them as people of chastity, and that they were only known by their appearance. So if asking was their custom, then their characteristic would not have been chastity, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have needed to know that they knew by evidence and signs, and the apparent question would have indicated their condition and their situation. In the report that:- Bishr narrated to us, he said, Yazid narrated to us, he said, Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Hilal bin Hisn, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, he said, “Once we were in need, so it was said to me: Why don’t you go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and ask him! So I went to him, my neck bowed, and the first thing he told me was: Whoever seeks chastity, God will grant him chastity, and whoever seeks independence, God will grant him independence, and whoever asks us, we will not withhold anything from him and we will find it.”

He said: “Then I came back to myself and said: Should I not seek chastity so that God may grant me chastity? So I came back, and I did not ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for anything after that, until the world turned against us and drowned us, except for those whom God protected.” Clear evidence that chastity is a meaning that negates the meaning of the question from one person, and that whoever is described as chaste is not described as a question, whether insistently or not.
If the matter is as you described, then what is the point of his saying:
h
They do not ask people insistently
, when
h
they do not ask people insistently
or otherwise.
The reason for that is that when God Almighty mentioned them as being chaste, and made known to His servants that they are not people of begging in any way by His saying:
h
The ignorant think them rich because of their self-restraint

, and that they are only known by their appearance, He increased His servants’ clarification of their matter and good praise of them, by denying the greed and humility that is found in those who are persistent in begging, from them. Some of those who said this would say: This is similar to the saying: I have rarely seen anyone like so-and-so! Perhaps he has never seen anyone like him or anyone comparable to him. And similar to what we said about the meaning of insistence, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
They do not ask people insistently
, he said: They do not insist in asking.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
They do not ask people insistently
, he said: He is the one who is insistent in asking.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They do not ask people insistently

, he mentioned to us “that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: God loves the forbearing, rich, self-restrained person, and hates the rich, obscene, vulgar, importunate beggar,” he said: And he mentioned to us “that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: God, the Almighty, hates three things for you: idle talk, wasting wealth, and asking too much.” So if you wish, you will see him gossiping all day and at the beginning of his night, until he is found as a corpse on his bed, God will not give him a share of his day or night. And if you wish, you will see him with wealth [spending it] on his desires, pleasures, and amusements, and diverting it from the right of God, and that is wasting wealth. And if you wish, you will see him spreading his arms, asking people in his hands, and if he is given, he is excessive in praising them, and if he is prevented, he is excessive in criticizing them...

x: Abu Jaafar said...

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim narrated to us, he said: Mu'tamir narrated to us, on the authority of Ayman bin Nabil, he said: An old man from Ghafiq narrated to me:
m: Abu Darda used to look at the horses tied up among the mules and camels. He would say: The people of these - meaning the horses - are among those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly. They will have their reward with their Lord, and they will have no fear, nor will they grieve.

x: Others said: He meant by that people who spent in the way of God, neither extravagance nor stinginess.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Those who spend their wealth until his statement: nor will they grieve, these are the people of Paradise. He mentioned to us that “the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: The many are the lowest. They said: O Prophet of God, except for whom? He said: The many are the lowest. They said: O Prophet of God, except for whom? He said: The many are the lowest. They said: O Prophet of God, except for whom? Until they feared that it had passed and would not be returned, until he said: Except for the one who speaks with the wealth like this and like this, to his right and to his left, and like this in front of him and like this behind him, and they are few. He said: These are people who spent in the way of God, which He has made obligatory and is pleased with, without extravagance, poverty, waste, or corruption.” It has been said that these verses, from His saying:
h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures
, they are good to His saying:
h
And there will be no fear concerning them

, nor will they grieve, were among the things that were practiced before the revelation of what is in Surat Bara’ah regarding the details of zakat, but when Bara’ah was revealed, they limited it to that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
If you disclose your charitable expenditures
, they are good until His saying:
h
And there will be no fear concerning them
, nor will they grieve. This was done before Bara’ah was revealed, but when Bara’ah was revealed with the obligatory charity expenditures and their details, the charity expenditures ended with it.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: those who raise. Usury is the increase in something. It is said: So-and-so increased over so-and-so, if he increased over him, he increases irbaa. The increase is usury, and the usury of something is if it increases over what it was and becomes large, so it grows usury. The hill is called [rabiyyah] because of its increase in size and its overlooking the flat ground around it, from their saying: raba yarbu. And from that it is said: So-and-so is in the hill of his people, meaning that he is in highness and honor among them. The origin of usury is elevation and increase, then it is said: so-and-so increased, meaning he made [his money, when] he increased it. The usurer is called murab because he doubles the money that he had from his creditor immediately, or because he increases it because of the term that he postpones it to him, so he increases it to the term that he had before his debt became due.
Therefore, God, the Most High, said:
O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied.
And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said,
m: regarding the usury that God forbade: In the days of ignorance, a man would have a debt owed to another man, and he would say: You have such and such, and you will defer it from me! So he would defer it from him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The usury of the people of ignorance was: a man sells a commodity for a specified period, and when the period comes and the other party does not have enough money to pay it, he increases it and delays it.

x: Then He, the Most High, said: Those who practice usury, the description of which we have described in this world, will not rise in the Hereafter from their graves, except as one rises whom Satan has beaten into insanity, meaning by that: Satan drives him crazy in this world, and he is the one who strangles him and makes him fall down, from insanity, meaning: from madness. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty:
h
Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity
, on the Day of Resurrection, regarding consuming interest in this world.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Rabia bin Kulthum told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Those who consume interest will not stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity
, he said: That is when he is raised from his grave.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Rabia bin Kulthum told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: On the Day of Resurrection it will be said to the usurer: Take your weapon for war, and he recited: They will not rise except as one rises who is being beaten by Satan into insanity, he said: That is when he is raised from his grave.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr:
m: h
Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity
. The verse, he said: The one who consumes interest will be raised on the Day of Resurrection insane, choking.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who consume interest will not stand
, the verse, and that is the sign of the people of interest on the Day of Resurrection, they will be sent mad by Satan.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: They do not stand except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity, he said: It is the madness that Satan drives mad. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity
, he said: They will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with madness from Satan in them. And in some readings it is: They will not stand on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity
, he said: Whoever dies while consuming interest will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection in a state of confusion, like one who is being beaten by Satan into insanity.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity
, meaning: into madness.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
Those who consume interest will not stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity

, he said: This is their example on the Day of Resurrection. They will not stand with the people on the Day of Resurrection except as one who is being strangled among the people stands, as if he were strangled, as if he were insane.

x: The meaning of his saying: The devil drives him crazy with his touch, is that he drives him crazy with his touch. It is said: The man was touched and possessed, so he is possessed and possessed, all of that when a touch befalls him and he goes crazy. And from it is the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, those who fear God - when an impulse touches them from Satan, they remember (al-A’raf 7:201), and from it is the saying of Al-A’sha: And she becomes, after a long night, as if she has been visited by a group of jinn.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: What do you think of someone who does what God has forbidden of usury in his trade and does not eat it? Does he deserve this threat from God?

Yes, and what is meant by usury in this verse is not eating, except that those about whom these verses were revealed on the day they were revealed, their food and their diet were from usury, so He mentioned them in their description, thereby making usury great for them, and making their situation in their food ugly.

And in the words of God, the Most High: “O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of usury if you should be believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger” (al-Baqarah 2:278-279) the verse, what indicates the correctness of what we said in that, and that the prohibition from God in that was for all meanings of usury, and that working with it and eating it and taking it and giving it are the same, like what the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have shown in his saying:
h
May God curse the one who consumes usury and the one who pays it
, the one who writes it down and its two witnesses, if they know about it.

By that God the Most High means: that with which He described them, that they will rise from their graves on the Day of Resurrection, like the rising of one who is possessed by Satan from madness. So God the Most High said: This which we mentioned will befall them on the Day of Resurrection, from the ugliness of their condition, and the horror of their rising from their graves, and the evil that has befallen them, is because they used to lie and slander in this world and say: Trade which God has permitted for His servants is like usury. That is because those who consumed usury from the people of ignorance, when the money of one of them became due to his creditor, the creditor would say to the creditor of the right: Give me more time and I will give you more of your money. So it would be said to them if they did that: This is usury that is not permissible. So if it was said to them that, they would say: It is the same to us whether we increase it at the beginning of the sale or when the money is due!
So God belied them in their statement and said: And God has permitted trade.

He, may His praise be exalted, means: And God has permitted profits in trade, buying and selling, and has forbidden usury, meaning the increase that the owner of the money increases because of his Surat Al-Baqarah 2:275
h
Those who consume interest cannot stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity

. That is because they say, "Trade is just like interest." But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden interest. So whoever receives an admonition from his Lord and desists may have what is past, and his affair is with Allah. But whoever returns [to evil] - those are [those] who will be punished. The companions of the Fire will abide therein eternally. creditor’s increase in the term, and his delaying his debt to him. God, the Almighty, says: So the two increases, one of which is from the direction of selling, and the other from the direction of delaying the money and the increase in the term, are not the same.

That is because I have forbidden one of the two increases - which is the direction of delaying the money and the increase in the term - and permitted the other of them, which is the direction of the increase in the capital with which the seller buys his goods that he sells, so he keeps its excess. So God, the Almighty, said: The increase from the direction of selling is not like the increase from the direction of usury, because I have permitted selling and forbidden usury, and the matter is My matter and the creation is My creation, I decree regarding them as I will, and I enslave them as I want, none of them has the right to object to My judgment, nor to disobey My command, but they are obliged to obey Me and submit to My judgment.
