Then He, the Most High, said: But whoever receives an admonition from his Lord and desists, meaning by admonition: the reminder and the intimidation that He reminded them of and frightened them with in the verses of the Qur’an, and He threatened them with punishment for consuming usury.

God, the Most High, says: But whoever comes to him, “and desists from eating usury and is deterred from doing it and refrains from it - he shall have what is past, meaning: what he ate and took and passed, before the admonition and prohibition from his Lord came in that regard - and his affair is up to God, meaning: and the affair of the one who eats it after the admonition from his Lord and the prohibition comes, and after the one who eats it has stopped eating it, is up to God in His protection and guidance. If He wills, He will protect him from eating it and make him steadfast in stopping it, and if He wills, He will let him down from that - and whoever returns, meaning: and whoever returns to eating usury after it was prohibited, and says what he used to say before the admonition from God came in prohibiting it, from His saying:
h
Trade is but like usury

, “they are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally,” meaning: so those who do that and say it are the people of the Fire, meaning the Fire of Hell, they will abide therein eternally.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: So whoever receives an admonition from his Lord and desists, then he shall have what is past, and his affair is with God. As for the admonition, it is the Qur’an, and as for what is past, then he shall have what he consumed of usury.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
God destroys interest
, that God reduces interest and eliminates it, as:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: God destroys usury, he said: It decreases. This is similar to the hadith narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Usury, even if it is a lot, will decrease. As for His saying: “And He increases the charitable deeds,” He, may His praise be glorified, means that He multiplies their reward, increases them and makes them grow for Him. We have explained the meaning of usury before, and usury, and its origin, sufficiently enough to repeat it.

x: How does God increase charity?

It multiplies the reward for its Lord, as God Almighty said: The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain of corn which grows seven spikes, and in each spike is a hundred grains.
(al-Baqarah 2:261), and as He said: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over?
(al-Baqarah 2:245), and as:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibad bin Mansur told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim:
m: that he heard Abu Hurairah say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty accepts charity and takes it with His right hand and nurtures it for one of you as one of you nurtures his foal, until a morsel of food becomes like Mount Uhud. Confirmation of that is in the Book of God Almighty: ‘Do they not know that it is God who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities?’ (al-Tawbah 9:104), and ‘
h
God destroys interest
and gives increase for charities.’”

c: Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Aqta’ told me, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibad ibn Mansur, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah - and I do not think
m: that he has attributed it to the Prophet - he said: God Almighty accepts charity, but He does not accept anything but what is good.
b.via: Abu Hurayrah - and I do not think

c: Muhammad bin Omar bin Ali Al-Muqaddami told me, he said, Rayhan bin Saeed told us, he said, Ibad told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Aisha, she said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, accepts charity, and He does not accept from it except what is good, and He nurtures it for its owner as one of you nurtures his foal or his young camel, until a morsel of food becomes like Mount Uhud, and the confirmation of that is in the Book of God, the Mighty and Sublime: ‘
h
God destroys interest
and gives increase for charities.’”

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If a servant gives charity from good things, God accepts it from him, takes it in His right hand, and raises it as one of you raises his foal or his young camel. And a man gives a morsel of food in charity, and it grows in the hand of God - or he said: in the palm of God Almighty - until it becomes like Mount Uhud, so give charity.’”

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, he said,
m: I heard Yunus, on the authority of a companion of his, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, he said, Abu Hurayrah said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty accepts charity with His right hand, and He does not accept from it except what is good, and God raises for one of you his morsel of food as one of you raises his foal or young camel, until he meets it on the Day of Resurrection and it is greater than Mount Uhud.”

x: As for his statement:
h
And God does not love every disbelieving sinner

, what he means by that is: And God does not love every person who persists in disbelief in his Lord, who considers it permissible to eat and feed usury - sinful, persisting in sin, in what He has forbidden him from eating usury and what is forbidden and other sins, who does not refrain from that nor desist from it, nor learn from the admonition of his Lord with which He admonished him in His revelation and the verses of His Book.

This is report from God Almighty that those who believed, meaning those who believed in God and His Messenger, and in what he brought from their Lord, of the prohibition of usury and consuming it, and other than that from the rest of the laws of his religion. And did righteous deeds which God Almighty commanded them to do, and which He urged them to do. And established prayer the obligatory prayer within its limits, and performed it according to its Sunnahs. And give the zakat which is imposed on them from their wealth, after what they had previously done of consuming usury before the admonition came from their Lord, they will have their reward meaning the reward for that from their deeds, faith and charity, with their Lord on the day when they will need Him in their afterlife, and there will be no fear concerning them on that day from His punishment for what they had done in their ignorance, and their disbelief before the admonition of their Lord came to them, from consuming what they had eaten of usury, because of what they had repented and turned to God Almighty from that when the admonition came to them from their Lord, and their belief in the promise and threat of God, nor will they grieve over their abandonment of what they had abandoned in this world of consuming usury and acting upon it, when they witness the abundant reward of God Almighty, and they are for abandoning what they abandoned of that in this world seeking His pleasure in the Hereafter, so they attain what they were promised for abandoning.
By that, the Most High means:
h
O you who have believed

, believe in God and His Messenger, fear God, meaning: fear God for yourselves, so fear Him by obeying Him in what He has commanded you to do, and refraining from what He has forbidden you to do, and leave, meaning: abandon, what remains of interest, meaning: leave seeking what remains for you of excess on your capital that you had before it became usurious—if you are believers, meaning: if you are confirming your faith in word and your belief with your tongues, with your actions.

It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about a people who converted to Islam and they had money owed to them by other people as interest, so they had collected some of it from them and some remained, so God, may He be glorified and praised, forgave them for what they had collected before this verse was revealed, and forbade them from collecting what remained of it.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
O you who have believed
h
fear God and give up what remains of interest

to and do not wrong. He said: This verse was revealed about Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib and a man from Banu Al-Mughira, who were partners in the pre-Islamic era, lending interest to people from Thaqeef, from Banu Amr, and they are Banu Amr bin Umair. Then Islam came and they had great wealth in interest, so God revealed: And give up what remains of the surplus that was in the pre-Islamic era, of interest.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, Al-Husayn narrated to us, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
O you who have believed

, fear God and give up what remains of your interest if you are believers, he said: Thaqeef had made peace with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the condition that whatever interest they owed to people and whatever interest people owed to them would be abolished. When the conquest took place, Atab ibn Asid was appointed as governor of Mecca, and Banu Amr ibn Umair ibn Awf used to take interest from Banu Al-Mugheerah, and Banu Al-Mugheerah used to charge them interest during the pre-Islamic period. Islam came and they had a lot of money on them. Banu Amr came to them asking for their interest, but Banu Al-Mugheerah refused to give them any in Islam, and they referred that to Atab ibn Asid. Atab wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed: “
h
O you who have believed

, fear God and give up what remains of your interest if you are believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger,” until and you will not be wronged. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to Atab and said: If they are satisfied, then fine them, otherwise I will declare war on them. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement:
h
Fear God and give up what remains of interest

, he said: They used to take interest from Banu al-Mughira, claiming that they were Masoud, Abd al-Yalil, Habib and Rabi’ah, the sons of Amr ibn Umair, so they were the ones who had interest from Banu al-Mughira, then Abd al-Yalil, Habib, Rabi’ah, Hilal and Masoud converted to Islam.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Fear God and give up what remains of interest if you are believers
, he said: It was interest that they used to trade with in the pre-Islamic era, but when they converted to Islam they were ordered to take their principal.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
If you do not do so
, if you do not abandon what remains of the usury. There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement:
h
So be warned of war from God and His Messenger
. The general reading of the people of Medina is: Fa-adhanu with the short alif of fa-adhanu and the opening of its dhal, meaning: be with knowledge and permission.

Others read it, and it is a general reading of the Kufians: Fa’adhanu with an extension of the alif in his saying: Fa’adhanu and a kasra on its dhal, meaning: Fa’adhanu ghairkum: inform them and tell them that you are at war with them.

The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: Fa-adhanu with a short alif and a fatha on the dhal, meaning: know that and be certain of it, and be with permission from God Almighty for you to do that. We chose this because God the Almighty ordered His Prophet (peace be upon him) to denounce whoever persists in his polytheism which is not permissible to remain in, and to kill whoever apostatizes from Islam among them in every case unless he returns to Islam, whether the polytheists inform him that they are at war with him or not. So if the one who was ordered to do this is one of two things: Either he was a polytheist who persisted in his polytheism which is not permissible to remain in, or he was a Muslim who apostatized and war was declared. In either case, he was only denounced to war, not ordered to declare it if he decided to do so.

Because if the matter was up to him, and he persisted in eating usury and considered it permissible for him and the Muslims were not informed of war, then war is not obligatory upon them. And that is not his ruling in either of the two cases. It is known that he is the one who is authorized to wage war, not the one who authorized it. And this is the interpretation that the people of interpretation interpreted it.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: O you who have believed, fear God
h
and give up what remains of interest
, to his statement:
h
Then be warned of war from God and His Messenger
: whoever persists in usury and does not desist from it, then it is the duty of the leader of the Muslims to ask him to repent, and if he desists, well and good, otherwise his neck should be struck.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, he said, Rabia bin Kulthum told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: On the Day of Resurrection, it will be said to the usurer: Take your weapon for war.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Rabia bin Kulthum told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And give up what remains of interest

, if you are believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger,” God threatened them with killing as you hear, so He made them a source of embarrassment wherever they were found.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
If you do not do so
h
then be warned of war from God and His Messenger
, he threatened the one who consumes usury with death.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said, Ibn Abbas said:
m: His statement:
h
So be informed of a war from God and His Messenger
, so be certain of a war from God and His Messenger.

x: All of these reports indicate that his saying:
h
So be warned of war from God
, is a warning from God Almighty to them of war and killing, not an order for them to be warned of others.
By that, God Almighty means: And if you repent, and you stop eating usury and return to God Almighty.
You shall have your principal, from the debts that you owe people, without the increase that you have created on top of that as usury from you, as:

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
But if you repent
h
you shall have your capital

, and the money that they have on the backs of men, their capital was made their capital when this verse was revealed. As for the profit and the surplus, it is not theirs, and they should not take anything from it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: God abolished usury and made their capital their capital.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Abi ʿAruba, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if you repent
, you may have your principal, he said: What they had of debt, so he made it possible for them to take their principal and not add anything to it.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And if you repent, then you shall have your principal which you advanced, and the interest is dropped.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It was mentioned to us that “the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon on the day of the conquest: Beware, all the usury of the Age of Ignorance is abolished, and the first usury to be introduced was the usury of Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib.”

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon: All usury is abolished, and the first usury to be abolished is the usury of Al-ʿAbbas.”

x: What he means by his saying, Do not wrong is by taking your capital that was yours before the usury from your creditors, without the profits that you increased from the one from whom you took that from your creditors, so that you take from them what you are not entitled to take, or that was not yours before, Do not wrong, meaning: nor does the creditor who gives you that without the usury that you had imposed on him because of the increase in the term, reduce from you a right that you have over him and prevent it from you, because what was in excess of your capital was not a right that you had over him, so by preventing it from you he is being unjust to you. Ibn Abbas and other interpreters used to say something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: “And if you repent,
h
you shall have your capital
sums. You shall not be wronged,” so they increase, nor shall you be wronged, so they decrease.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: “
h
You shall have your capital
. Do not wrong, nor shall you be wronged,” he said: Do not reduce your capital, and do not take what is not permissible for you.

evidence.text: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of His statement: So be warned of war from God and His Messenger.
The general reading of the people of Medina is: Fa-adhanu with the short alif of fa-adhanu and the opening of its dhal, meaning: be with knowledge and permission.

Others read it, and it is a general reading of the Kufians: Fa’adhanu with an extension of the alif in his saying: Fa’adhanu and a kasra on its dhal, meaning: Fa’adhanu ghairkum: inform them and tell them that you are at war with them.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard is the reading of the one who reads: Fa-adhanu with a short alif and a fatha on the dhal, meaning: know that and be certain of it, and be with permission from God Almighty for you to do that.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And if one of your creditors from whom you collect your principal, is in hardship meaning: insolvent with regard to your principal that they owed you before the usury: then give them respite until they are able to pay it. His saying: one in hardship is raised by was, so the predicate is left out, which is what we mentioned. It is only appropriate to leave out its predicate because the Arabs imply that its predicates are used for indefinite nouns. If was in this position had been directed to mean a verb that is self-sufficient and complete, it would have been a correct interpretation, and there would have been no need for a predicate in that case. So the interpretation of the statement in that case would be: And if there is one in hardship among your creditors with your principal, then let there be a postponement until it is easy to pay.

It has been mentioned that this is in Abu Ka’b’s reading: And if the debtor is in hardship, meaning: And if the debtor is in hardship, then grant him respite until he is able to pay. Although this is permissible in Arabic, it is not permissible to read it according to us, because it is different from the script of the Muslims’ Qur’ans. As for his saying: Then let him be given a reprieve until it is easy, he means: You should give him a reprieve until it is easy, just as he said: But whoever among you is ill or has an ailment in his head, then a ransom of fasting (al-Baqarah 2:196). We have already mentioned the reason for raising what was similar to it in the past before, so there is no need to repeat it. Al-Maysara, derived from Al-Yusr, like Al-Rahmah and Al-Mashamah. The meaning of the words: If one of your creditors is in hardship, then you must give him time until he is able to pay the debt that you owe him, so that he becomes one of those who are able to pay it.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Wasil bin Abdul A’la told me, he said, Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if he is in hardship
, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay, he said: It was revealed regarding usury.

c: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin:
m: A man brought a case before Shuraih, and he ruled against him and ordered that he be imprisoned. A man said to Shuraih: He is insolvent, and God says in His Book:
h
But if he is in hardship

, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to pay! Shuraih said: That is only in the case of usury! God says in His Book: Indeed, God commands you to render trusts to whom they are due, and when you judge between people to judge with justice
r
(An-Nisa’: 58)
. God does not command us to do something and then punish us for it.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if he is in hardship
, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay, he said: That is regarding usury.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughirah told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: that Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim had a debt owed to him, so he would come to him and stand at his door and say: O so-and-so, if you are well-off, then pay it, and if you are poor, then go to a place of ease.

c: Yaqub told us, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Muhammad, he said:
m: A man came to Shuraih and spoke to him, and he kept saying: He is in financial difficulty, he is in financial difficulty!! I thought that he was speaking to him about a prisoner, so Shuraih said: Usury was in this neighborhood of the Ansar, so God the Almighty revealed:
h
But if he is in hardship
, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay, and God the Almighty said: Indeed, God commands you to render trusts to whom they are due
r
(An-Nisa’: 58)
. So God the Almighty would not command us to do something and then punish us for it! Deliver trusts to their owners.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if he is in hardship
, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay, he said: Then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay his capital.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
But if he is in hardship

, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay. The command in usury is that the one in hardship should be given a reprieve, and the reprieve is not in the case of a trust, but rather the trust should be returned to its people.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr bin Hammad told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And if he is in hardship, then let there be postponement with the capital, until he is easy, he says: until he is rich.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
But if he is in hardship
, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay. This is regarding usury.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak regarding his statement:
h
But if he is in hardship

, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay. This is regarding usury, and the people of the Age of Ignorance used to trade with it. Then when those of them who converted to Islam converted to Islam, they were ordered to take their principal.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
But if he is in hardship
, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him, meaning what is required.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja’far,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if he is in hardship
, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay, he said: death.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And if he is in hardship, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay. He said: This is regarding usury.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding a man who marries until he is well off, he said: until death, or until separation.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: Then a respite until it is easy, he said: That is in usury.

c: Ahmad told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Mandil told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Then give him a reprieve until he is able to pay it. He said: He would delay it and not add anything to it. And if someone’s debt became due and he did not find anything to give him, he would add to it and delay it.

c: Ahmad bin Hazim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Mandil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And if he is in hardship, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay. He said: He should delay it and not add anything to it.

x: Others said: This verse is general for everyone who has a right over an insolvent man, regardless of the source of that right, whether it is a lawful debt or usury.
Who said that?

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: Whoever is in hardship, let there be postponement until it is easy for him, and for you to give in charity is better for you. He said: And so is every debt owed by a Muslim. It is not permissible for a Muslim who has a debt owed by his brother and knows that he is in hardship to imprison him, nor to pursue him until God makes it easy for him. Rather, postponement was made in what is permissible, and for that reason debts are based on that.

c: Ali bin Harb told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
But if he is in hardship
, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to repay. He said: It was revealed regarding debt.

x: The correct statement regarding his statement:
h
But if he is in hardship

, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him to pay, is that it refers to the creditors who had converted to Islam during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had debts on which they had accrued interest in the pre-Islamic era. Islam overtook them before they could collect them from them, so God commanded that what remained of the interest be removed after they converted to Islam, and that their principal be collected from those of their creditors who were solvent, or that those of them who were insolvent be given postponement of their principal until it is easy for them to pay. This is the ruling for anyone who converts to Islam and has usury that he has imposed on a creditor. Islam nullifies what he owed his creditor before the usury, and he is obligated to pay his capital - which was taken from him or was imposed on him before the usury - to him, if he is solvent.

If he is insolvent, he is given a reprieve from his owner’s capital until he is solvent, and the surplus on the capital is nullified for him. However, even though the verse was revealed about those we mentioned, and it was meant by them, the ruling that God ruled: granting the insolvent a respite from the usurer’s capital after the usury has been prolonged, is a ruling that is obligatory for everyone who owes a debt to a man that has become due to him, and he is insolvent in paying it: that he is granted a respite until he is able to pay it. Because the debt of every creditor is in the money of his creditor, and his creditor must pay it from it - not on his neck. So if his money is lost, he has no way to get it back by confiscating it or selling it. This is because the money of the creditor will not be without one of three aspects: either it is on the neck of his creditor, or it is on his conscience that he pays it from his money, or it is in his own money specifically.
If it is in his specific money, then when that money Surat Al-Baqarah 2:280
h
But if he is in hardship

, then let there be postponement until [a time of] ease. But if you remit [your wealth] by charity, that is better for you, if you only knew. becomes void and nonexistent, the debt of the owner of the money becomes void. And that is something that no one says. Or it may be around his neck. If that is the case, then when his soul is lost, the debt of the creditor is void, even if the creditor fails to fulfill his right and multiples of that. No one says that either. It has become clear, then, that since this is the case, the debt of the owner of the money is in the possession of his creditor, and he must pay it from his money. If his money is gone, he has no way to pay it, because he has no way to pay the right of his owner from it if it had been present. And if there is no way to pay it, he has no way to imprison him while he is lacking in his right.
Because he is not preventing him from having a right, he has a way to pay it, so he is punished for delaying it by imprisonment.

By that, God Almighty means: And that you give charity from your principal to this insolvent person, “is better for you, O people, than that you give him time to recover his principal, so that you may collect your principal from him when he recovers, if you only knew, the place of virtue in charity, and what reward God has made obligatory for the one who forgives the debt of his insolvent creditor.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: The meaning of this is: And that you give charity with your capital to the rich and poor among them, is better for you.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: But if you repent, you may have your capital, meaning the money that is on the backs of men. Their capital was given to them when this verse was revealed. As for the profit and the surplus, they are not theirs, and they should not take anything from it. But if you give in charity, it is better for you, meaning that giving in charity the original money is better for you.

c: Yaqub told me that Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And that you give in charity, meaning the capital, for it is better for you.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And that you give in charity is better for you
, he said: from your capital.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Qubaysah bin Uqbah told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And that you give in charity is better for you
, he said: That you give in charity with your principal.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: And if you give it in charity to the needy, it is better for you - similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And that you give in charity is better for you
, he said: And that you give in charity from your principal to the poor, it is better for you. So Al-Abbas gave it in charity.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: h
But if he is in hardship
, then grant him postponement until it is easy for him. But if you give him charity, it is better for you.” He said: And if you give him charity from your capital, it is better for you.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
And that you give in charity is better for you

, meaning: on the one who is insolvent. As for the one who is wealthy, then no, but the capital should be taken from him. As for the one who is insolvent, taking from him is permissible, but giving charity on his behalf is better.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: And to give in charity from your principal is better for you than to postpone your payment until it is easy. So God Almighty chose charity over postponement.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: “
h
But if he is in hardship
, then grant him postponement until it is easy for him. But if you remit it by charity, it is better for you,” he said: From granting him postponement, if you only knew.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Then granting a respite until it is easy for you, and that you give charity is better for you, and granting a respite is obligatory. And God Almighty has given charity better than granting a respite, and charity is for every person in need, but not for the person who is well off.

x: The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who said: Its meaning is: And that you give charity to the insolvent from your principal is better for you. Because he follows the mention of its ruling in the two meanings. And attaching it to what follows it is more beloved to me than attaching it to what comes after it.
It has been said that these verses on the rulings on usury are the last verses revealed in the Qur’an.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, and Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: that Umar bin Al-Khattab said:
m: The last thing to be revealed in the Qur’an was the verse on usury, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away before he could explain it, so abandon usury and suspicion.

c: Humayd ibn Masʿadah narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, on the authority of ʿAmir:
m: ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, stood up and praised God and extolled Him, then he said: As for what follows, by God, I do not know whether we are ordering you to do something that is not good for you, and I do not know whether we are forbidding you from something that is good for you. And among the last verses of the Qur’an to be revealed were the verses on usury, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died before he could explain them to us, so leave that which makes you doubt for that which does not make you doubt.

c: Abu Zaid Umar ibn Shabah told me, he said, Qubaysah told us, he said, Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Asim al-Ahwal, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The last thing that was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the verse on usury. We command something without knowing whether there is anything wrong with it, and we forbid something, perhaps there is nothing wrong with it.

evidence.text: Although this is permissible in Arabic, it is not permissible to read it according to us, because it is different from the script of the Muslims’ Qur’ans.

x: It was also said: This verse is also the last verse revealed from the Qur’an.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, Abu Tamila told us, Al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid Al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The last verse revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God, the verse, so it is the last verse of the Book to be revealed.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said, Sahl bin Amer told us, he said, Malik bin Mughol told us, on the authority of Atiyah, he said:
m: The last verse to be revealed was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The last verse to be revealed was: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: Ibn Abbas said, the last verse revealed in the Qur’an was: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.” Ibn Jurayj said: They say that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived nine nights after that, and it began on Saturday, and he died on Monday.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me:
m: It reached him that the most recent verse in the Qur’an about the Throne is the verse of debt.

x: By that, He, the Most High, means: Beware, O people, of a day when you will be returned to God, and you will meet Him on that day, lest you respond to Him with evil deeds that will destroy you, or with shameful deeds that will disgrace you, or with scandals that will disgrace you and tear down your veils, or with grave sins that will ruin you and will incur for you from God a punishment that you cannot bear. Indeed, it is a day of recompense for deeds, not a day of seeking forgiveness, or a day of resignation, repentance, and turning back. Rather, it is a day of recompense, reward, and accountability. On that day, every soul will be given its reward for what it has done and acquired of evil and good. There will be no small or great deed left out, of good and evil, except that it will be brought, and its reward will be given in full with justice from its Lord, and they will not be wronged.

How can he be wronged who was rewarded for an evil deed with the like of it, and for a good deed with ten times the like?! No, rather, He has been just to you, O wrongdoer, and has been generous to you, so He has bestowed upon you the best and most abundantly, O doer of good. So, a man feared his Lord, took precautions against Him, and watched Him lest his day should come upon him while his back was heavy with burdens and light with good deeds, for He, the Almighty, warned and excused, and preached and delivered the message.

By that, the Most High means: O you who believe in God and His Messenger: When you contract a debt, meaning: when you trade on credit, or buy with it, or deal with it, or take it, for a specified term, meaning: for a known time and agree upon it among yourselves. This may include a loan and a salam, and everything in which a salam is permissible with a specified term for its sale becomes a debt on the seller of what was handed over to him. It is possible to sell a present property that can be sold for deferred prices. All of this is from the deferred debts for a specified term, if their terms are known with a set limit. Ibn Abbas used to say that this verse was revealed specifically about peace.
He mentioned the narration about it:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Yahya bin Isa al-Ramli told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, he said, Ibn Abbas said
m: regarding: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, he said: Salam in wheat, in a known measure for a known term.

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Mukhrami told me, he said, Yahya bin Al-Samit told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Hayyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt, he said: It was revealed regarding the Salam, in a known measure for a known term.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Zaid bin Abi Al-Zarqa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abi Hayyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: This verse was revealed: When you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down, in the case of a loan, in wheat, in a known measure for a known term.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muhibb told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hayyan al-Taymi, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: This verse was revealed: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, regarding an advance payment for wheat, for a specified measure for a specified term.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Hassan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: I bear witness that the guaranteed advance, for a specified term, is that God Almighty has permitted it and authorized it. And he recited this verse: When you contract a debt for a specified term.

x: If someone were to say: What is the point of his saying: with a debt, when he indicated this with his saying: If you contract a debt, and could there be a debt without a debt, such that it was necessary to say: with a debt? It was said: Since the Arabs had a saying: Tada’ana meaning: We reciprocated, and meaning: We took and gave in return for a debt, God made clear with His saying: in return for a debt, the meaning that He intended to inform whoever heard His saying: You reciprocated, of its ruling, and He informed them that it is the ruling of a debt and not the ruling of reciprocity.
Some of them claimed that this is an emphasis like his saying: Then the angels prostrated, all of them together (al-Hijr 15:30-73), and what he said about that in this place is meaningless.

What He, may His praise be exalted, meant by His saying: Then write it down, is to write down the debt that you have taken on for a specified period, whether it is a sale or a loan. Scholars differed about whether it is obligatory or recommended to write the book.
Some of them said: It is an obligatory right and a necessary duty.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down, he said: Whoever sells for a specified term, he is commanded to write it down, whether it is small or large, for a specified term.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. He said: So whoever contracts a debt should write it down, and whoever sells should have it witnessed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ
m: regarding his statement: If you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down, so this was obligatory. And he narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: similarly, and he added to it, he said: Then the permission and the flexibility arose, he said: If some of you trust others, then let the one who is trusted discharge his trust and let him fear God, his Lord.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It was mentioned to us that Abu Sulayman al-Mar’ashi was a man who accompanied Ka’b. One day he said to his companions: Do you know of a wronged person who called upon his Lord but was not answered? They said: How could that be? He said: A man sold something and did not write it down or bear witness. When his money was due, its owner denied it, so he called upon his Lord but was not answered, because he had disobeyed his Lord. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:282 O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write it down between you in justice. And let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write, and let the one upon whom the debt is dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not withhold from it anything. But if the one upon whom the debt is is If the one who is in the wrong is a fool or weak or cannot dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice.
h
And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men

. But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of them errs, then one of them can remind the other. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon, and do not be weary of writing it down, whether it is young or old. That is more just in the sight of Allah and more suitable for testimony and more suitable so that you do not have doubts. Unless it is a present trade which you conduct among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it down. And bring witnesses when you make a transaction, and let neither scribe nor witness be harmed. But if you do, it is indeed a transgression on your part. And fear Allah, and Allah teaches you. And Allah is Knowing of all things.

x: Others said: The subscription of the book with the debt was obligatory, but it was abrogated by His saying: If some of you trust others, then let the one who is trusted discharge his trust.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Shabrama, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: There is nothing wrong if you trust him not to write or bear witness, because of his saying: If some of you trust others, Ibn Uyaynah said, Ibn Shabrama said, on the authority of al-Sha’bi: This is what it ends with.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Abdul-Wahhab told us, he said, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer,
m: regarding this verse: O you who believe! When you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down, until he reached this place: But if one of you trusts another, let the one who is trusted discharge his trust, he said: He permitted that, so whoever wants to trust his companion, let him trust him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Harun told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: If he trusts him, he should not testify against him and he should not write it down.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Al-Shaʿbi, who said: They used to think that this verse, If some of you trust others, abrogated what came before it regarding writing and witnesses, as a concession and mercy from God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Other than Ata’ said:
m: The Book and the testimony were abrogated: If some of you trust others.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: This was abrogated by His statement: If some of you trust others, then let the one who is trusted discharge his trust. He said: Were it not for this verse, it would not have been permissible for anyone to be given a loan except with a written document and witnesses or proof. So when this came, it abrogated all of this, and it turned to trust.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Hajjaj told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, he said:
m: I asked al-Hasan, I said: Everyone who sells a sale should have witnesses? He said: Did you not see that God the Almighty says: Let him who is trusted discharge his trust?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer,
m: regarding this verse: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down, until he reached this place: But if one of you trusts another, let the one who is trusted discharge his trust, he said: He permitted that, so whoever wants to trust his companion, let him trust him.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement: If some of you trust others, he said: If you have witnesses, then be firm, and if you do not have witnesses, then be free and at ease.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, he said:
m: I said to Al-Sha’bi: What do you think of a man who borrows something from another man, and is he required to bear witness? He said: So he read until His statement: If some of you trust others, abrogated what came before it.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Muhammad bin Marwan Al-Uqaili told us, he said, Abdul Malik bin Abi Nadrah told us,
m: [on the authority of his father], on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that he read: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term to: If some of you trust others, he said: This abrogated what came before it.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And let the debt book be written for a specified period between the creditor and the debtor, a writer with justice, meaning: with truth and fairness in the book that he writes between them, in a way that does not deprive the one with the right of his right or diminish it, nor does it oblige him to have an argument against the one who owes him a debt in it falsely, nor does it oblige him to do what is not upon him, like:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let a scribe write between you in justice
, he said: The scribe should fear God in his book, so he should not leave out any truth from it, nor add any falsehood to it. As for his saying:
h
And no scribe shall refuse to write as God has taught him

, he means: And no scribe who has been asked to write this shall refuse to write among them the book of religion as God has taught him to write, so He has made him special with the knowledge of this and has deprived many of His creation of it. Scholars have differed on the obligation of the writer to write if he is asked to write, similar to their disagreement on the obligation of the writer to write on the one who has the right.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: And let no scribe refuse, he said: It is obligatory for the scribe to write.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: I said to Ata’: His statement: And no scribe shall refuse to write, is it obligatory that he not refuse to write? He said: Yes. Ibn Jurayj said: And Mujahid said: It is obligatory for the scribe to write.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And no scribe should refuse to write as God has taught him, similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer and Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let no scribe refuse to write as God has taught him
, they said: If they do not find a scribe and you are called, do not refuse to write for them.

x: Mention of those who said: It is abrogated. We have mentioned a group of those who said: Everything in this verse about the command to write, witness, and pledge is abrogated by the verse at the end of it. I will mention the statement of those we left out there with some meanings.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: And let not the scribe refuse, he said: It was a firm statement, then it was abrogated by: And let not the scribe nor the witness be harmed (al-Baqarah 2:282).

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: And let a scribe write between you with justice,
h
and let no scribe refuse to write as God has taught him
. So this was obligatory upon the scribes.

x: Others said: It is obligatory, but it is obligatory for the writer when he is finished.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
And let a scribe write between you in justice
h
and let no scribe refuse to write as God has taught him
, he says: A scribe should not refuse to write if he is free.

x: The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is that God, the Almighty, commanded those who are in debt for a specified period to write down the books of debt among themselves, and commanded the scribe to write that down among themselves with justice. God’s command is a binding obligation, unless there is evidence that it is guidance and encouragement. There is no evidence that His command, the Almighty, to write down the books in this regard, and to present it to the scribe so that he does not refuse to write that down, is a recommendation and guidance. So that is an obligation upon them that they cannot neglect, and whoever neglects it will be at fault for neglecting it. There is no basis for the argument of those who claim that the command to do so was abrogated by His statement: But if one of you trusts another, let him who is trusted discharge his trust. Because God Almighty only permitted this when there is no way to a book or a writer.
However, when the book and the writer are present, then the obligation - if the debt is for a specified term - is what God Almighty commanded in His statement: “Then write it down,
h
and let a scribe write between you in justice
h
And let no scribe refuse to write as God has taught him

.” The abrogating verse is only that which does not allow the combination of its ruling and the ruling of the abrogated verse in one case, in the manner that we have explained. As for that in which one of them does not negate the ruling of the other, then it is not abrogating or abrogated at all. If it were necessary that his statement, “
h
And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe

, then a pledge taken in possession. But if one of you trusts another, let the one who is trusted discharge his trust,” abrogate his statement, “If you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down.
h
And let a scribe write between you in justice
h
And let no scribe refuse to write as God has taught him
,” then it would be necessary that his statement,
h
And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the relieving himself or you have touched women and you find no water

, then seek clean earth (al-Ma’idah 5:6) abrogate ablution with water—in the city when there is water there and when traveling—which God the Almighty has made obligatory in His statement, O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows (al-Ma’idah 5:6), and that his statement regarding expiation for zihar, But whoever cannot find [a scribe], then a fast of two consecutive months (al-Mujadilah 58:4) abrogate his statement,
h
Then the freeing of a slave before they touch (al-Mujadilah 58

:3). The one who says that the saying of God Almighty: If some of you trust others, let him who is trusted discharge his trust abrogates His saying: If you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down: What is the difference between him and the one who says about tayammum and what we mentioned, who Surat Al-Baqarah 2:282 O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down.

And let a scribe write it down between you in justice. And let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write, and let the one upon whom the debt is dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not withhold from it anything. But if the one upon whom the debt is is If the one who is in the wrong is a fool or weak or cannot dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice.
h
And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men

. But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of them errs, then one of them can remind the other. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon, and do not be weary of writing it down, whether it is young or old. That is more just in the sight of Allah and more suitable for testimony and more suitable so that you do not have doubts. Unless it is a present trade which you conduct among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it down.

And bring witnesses when you make a transaction, and let neither scribe nor witness be harmed. But if you do, it is indeed a transgression on your part. And fear Allah, and Allah teaches you. And Allah is Knowing of all things. claims that everything that is permitted in a state of necessity due to the reason of necessity, its ruling in a state of necessity abrogates its ruling in all its states: similar to his saying that the command to write down books of debts and rights is abrogated by His saying: “
h
And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe
, then a security deposit in possession. But if some of you trust others, let him who is trusted discharge his trust”?

The difference between me and him is that his statement: If some of you trust others is separate from his statement: If you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit, and the ruling on travel if there is no scribe has ended with his statement: The security deposit. What he meant by his statement: If some of you trust others is: If you contract a debt for a specified term, and some of you trust others, then let the one who has been entrusted fulfill his trust.

What is the proof of that from the origin or analogy, and the ruling has been passed in the religion in which the writer and the writer have a way with His saying: And God teaches you, and God is Knowing of all things? As for those who claim that His statement, Then write it down, and His statement, And let no scribe refuse, are in the form of exhortation and guidance, they ask for proof for their claim in that, then they oppose it with the rest of the commands of God Almighty that He commanded in His Book, and they ask for the difference between what they claimed in that and what they denied in other things. So they will not say anything about that except that they will impose the same in the other.
Mention of those who said: Justice in His saying:
h
And let a scribe write between you in justice is the truth

What he means by that is: Let the writer write, and let the one who owes the debt dictate, who is the creditor who is indebted. He says: Let the debtor take charge of dictating the book of what he owes of the owner of the money to the writer, and let him fear God, his Lord, the one who dictates to the one who owes the debt, so let him beware of His punishment for depriving the one who owes the debt of anything, lest He unjustly reduce it from him or take it from him transgressively, so that he is taken to a place where he is not able to pay it off except from his good deeds, or to bear from his bad deeds, as:

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: So let him write and let the one who has the right dictate. So this was obligatory. And let him fear God, his Lord, and not withhold anything from it. He said: Let him not wrong anything from it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement: And he does not withhold anything from it, he said: He does not diminish anything from this man’s right if he dictates.

x: What he meant by his statement, may His praise be exalted: If the one who owes the debt is foolish or weak, is that if the debtor who owes the money is foolish, meaning: ignorant of the correctness of what he owes, he should dictate it to the scribe, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: If the one who has the right is a fool, as for the fool, he is the one who is ignorant of dictation and matters.

x: Others said: Rather, the fool in this place, whom God meant, is the young child.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: If the one who has the right is a fool, as for the fool, he is the young one.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: But if the one who has the right is a fool or weak, he said: He is the young boy, so let his guardian dictate with justice.

x: The most appropriate of the two interpretations of the verse is the interpretation of the one who said: The fool in this place is the one who is ignorant of dictation, and the correct place for that is his mistake, because we have previously explained that the meaning of foolishness in the speech of the Arabs is ignorance. His statement, If the one who owes the debt is a fool, may include anyone who is ignorant of the correctness of what he dictates from his mistake, young or old, male or female. However, what is more appropriate, according to the apparent meaning of the verse, is that it refers to anyone who is ignorant of the place of error and its correctness: from the adult men who are not given authority over them, and women. Because He, the Most High, began the verse with His statement, O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, and the child and the one who is given authority over them, it is not permissible to lend them a debt, and that God, the Most High, has excluded from those whom He has commanded to dictate the book of debt with the foolish, the weak and the one who is unable to dictate it.

So in His, the Most High, separation of the weak from the foolish and the one who is unable to dictate the book in the description with which He described each one of them, what informed that each one of the three categories whose descriptions He distinguished between them is not the other two categories. If this is the case, it is known that the one described as foolish among them, not weak, is the one who has the ability to dictate, except that the obligation of dictation has been removed from him due to his ignorance of the place of correctness of that from his error, and that the one described as weak among them is the one who is unable to dictate, even if he is strong and wise, either because of a defect in his tongue or he is mute, and that the one described as being unable to dictate is the one who is prevented from dictating, either because of the imprisonment in which he is unable to have the scribe who writes the letter present so that he can dictate to him, or because of his absence from the place of dictation, so he is unable because of his absence to dictate the book.

So God, the Almighty, the Exalted, removed the obligation of dictating that from them, for the reasons we described - if they had them - and excused them for not dictating because of them, and He commanded, when the obligation of that fell upon them, the guardian of the right to dictate to him, saying: But if the one upon whom the right is owed is foolish or weak or is unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate with justice, meaning: the guardian of the right. There is no basis for the statement of those who claim that the fool in this case is the young one, and that the weak one is the old fool. Because if that is as he said, then his statement, Or he is unable to dictate himself, would mean the incapable of rational men who are permitted to dictate in their wealth and lives, either because of a defect in his tongue such as muteness or some other defect, or because he is absent from the place of writing.

And if that is the meaning of it, then the meaning of his statement, So let his guardian dictate with justice, would be invalidated, because a rational, sane person is not given authority over his wealth even if he is mute or absent, and no one may rule over his wealth except by his order. And in the correctness of the meaning of that, there is what invalidates the statement of those who claim that the fool in this case is the young child, or the old fool.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: If the one who has the right is foolish or weak or is unable to dictate, then let his guardian dictate with justice, he says: the guardian of the right.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
But if the one upon whom the right is owed is a fool or weak or is unable to dictate himself

, then let his guardian dictate with justice, he said, he says: If he is unable to do that, then let the one who owes the right dictate with justice. Mentioning the narration of the one who said: What is meant by the weak in this place is the fool, and by his saying: So let his guardian dictate with justice, is the guardian of the foolish and the weak.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: If the one who has the right is a fool or weak or is unable to dictate, he said: The guardian of the fool or weak is ordered to dictate justly.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for the weak, he is the fool.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: As for the weak, he is the fool.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: If the one who has the right is a fool or weak, he does not know, so he establishes this person’s right and is ignorant of that, so he appoints him in his position until he establishes this person’s right. We have shown that the first of the two interpretations is correct in this regard. As for his saying: Let his guardian dictate with justice, he means: with truth.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And bring two witnesses to bear witness to your rights. It is said: So-and-so is my witness to this money, and my witness to it.
As for his saying: From your men, he means from your free Muslims, not your slaves, and not your free infidels, as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men
, he said: the free men.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ali bin Saad told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:282 O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write it down between you in justice. And let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write, and let the one upon whom the debt is dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not withhold from it anything. But if the one upon whom the debt is is If the one who is in the wrong is a fool or weak or cannot dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice.
h
And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men

. But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of them errs, then one of them can remind the other. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon, and do not be weary of writing it down, whether it is young or old. That is more just in the sight of Allah and more suitable for testimony and more suitable so that you do not have doubts. Unless it is a present trade which you conduct among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it down. And bring witnesses when you make a transaction, and let neither scribe nor witness be harmed. But if you do, it is indeed a transgression on your part. And fear Allah, and Allah teaches you. And Allah is Knowing of all things.

x: By that, the Most High means: If there are not two men, then let there be a man and two women as witnesses. And the man and two women were raised, in response to the universe. And if you wish, you can say: If there are not two men, then let a man and two women testify to that. And if you wish, then if there are not two men, then a man and two women testify against him. And if you say: If there are not two men, then a man and two women, that would be correct. All of that is permissible. If it were a man and two women in the accusative case, it would be permissible, based on the interpretation: If they are not two men, then bring as witnesses a man and two women.
His saying: From among the martyrs whom you accept, means: from among the just ones whose religion and righteousness are accepted, such as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men
, he said: in religion, But if there are not two men, then a man and two women, and that is in religion, from among those whom you accept as witnesses, he said: just.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: h
And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men
, God Almighty commanded that two just men from among their men should bear witness, But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses.

x: The reading of this differed. The majority of the people of Hijaz and Madinah and some of the people of Iraq read: That one of them should go astray, then one of them should remind the other with the opening of the alif of an and the accusative of tadhal and tadhkar, meaning: if they are not two men, then a man and two women, so that one of them can remind the other if she goes astray. According to them, it is from the advanced meaning of the delayed. Because according to them, the masculine is what should be in place of tadhal. Because the meaning is what we described in their statement. They said: We only put tadhkar in the accusative because the recompense for what came before it is connected to what came before it, so its answer is returned to it, as you say in speech: It is pleasing to me that the questioner asks and is given, meaning: It is pleasing to me that the questioner is given if he asks - or: if he asks.

What pleases you is the giving and not the asking. But his saying: that he asks for what came before, is connected to what came before it, which is his saying: so that I may like it, so he opened an and put it in the accusative, then he followed that with his saying: he is given, so he put it in the accusative with the accusative of his saying: so that I may like it that he asks in sequence with it, even though it is in the meaning of the recompense.

Others read it in the same way, but they read it with a sukoon on the dhal of thikr and a light kaf. The readers of this also differ among themselves in the interpretation of their reading of it in this way.

Some of them interpreted it to mean: So one of them becomes the other male by their coming together, meaning: that if her testimony and the testimony of her companion come together, it is valid just as the testimony of one male is valid in a debt, because the testimony of each one of them alone is not valid in what is valid in debts except by the coming together of two women on the testimony of one, so their testimony then becomes like the testimony of one male, so it is as if each one of them - according to the interpretation of that in this sense - made her companion with her male. And he went to the saying of the Arabs: So-and-so’s mother reminded him, meaning she gave birth to him as a male, so she reminds him of him, and she is a woman who is masculine, if she gives birth to male children. And this is a saying that is narrated from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah that he used to say.
I was told about this on the authority of Abu Ubaid al-Qasim ibn Salam, who said:

c: I was told on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah,
m: who said: The interpretation of his statement:
h
Then one of them reminds the other is not from the remembrance after forgetting
, but rather it is from the remembrance, meaning: that if she testifies with the other, their testimony becomes like the testimony of the male.

x: Others of them directed it to mean remembrance after forgetting.

Others read it as: If one of them should go astray, then one of them should remind the other, with a kasra on in in his statement: If she goes astray, and raising she should remind and emphasizing it, as if it means starting the report about what the two women will do if one of them forgets her testimony, the other reminds her, from the confirmation of the forgetful memory and reminding her of that, and the cessation of that from what came before it. The meaning of the speech according to the reader of that is the same:
h
And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men

, and if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses, for if one of them goes astray, the other will remind her, on the resumption of the report about her action if one of them forgets her testimony, from the other reminding her forgetful companion. This is the reading that Al-A'mash and those who took it from him used to read.

Al-A'mash put the word tadalal in the accusative case because it is in the place of the jussive with the letter of recompense, which is in. The interpretation of the statement according to his reading is: in tadalal, so when one of the two lams merged into the other, he moved it to the lightest of the movements, and raised tadhkira with the fa because it is the answer to the recompense.

The correct reading in our view is the reading of those who read it with the fat-ha on an from his statement: that one of them should go astray, and with the shaddah on the kaf from his statement: then one of them should remind the other. And with the accusative of the ra’ from it, meaning: if there are not two men, then let a man and two women bear witness, so that if one of them goes astray the other can remind her. As for the accusative of fatathakkar, it is by conjunction with tadalal, and an is opened by taking the place of kay and it is in the position of a reward, and the answer comes after it, as it is sufficient to open it - I mean by opening an - from kay, and the second is coordinated - I mean: fatathakkar - with tadalal, so that it is known that what took the place of what he was working on, and it is apparent, has indicated it and conveyed its meaning and its work - that is, from kay.

We chose this in the recitation, because of the consensus of the authority of the ancient and modern reciters on this, and the uniqueness of Al-A’mash and those who recited his recitation in this, which is unique from them. It is not permissible to abandon a recitation that the Muslims brought, widely spread among them, for another. As for our choice of fa-ta-thakkar with emphasis on the kaf, it means: repeating the remembrance from one of them to the other, and defining her as [forgetting] that, in order to remember. So emphasising it is better than lightening it. As for what was narrated from Ibn Uyaynah regarding the interpretation that we mentioned, it is a wrong interpretation that has no meaning, for various reasons: One of them: It is contrary to what all the interpreters say.
