The second: It is known that the error of one of the two women in the testimony that she testified against is her going away from it and forgetting it, like the error of a man in his religion: if he is confused about it and deviates from the truth.

And if one of them becomes like this, how is it permissible for the other to become a male with her, with her forgetting her testimony and her error in it? And for the one who is lost in her testimony at that time, there is no doubt that she is more in need of reminder than of remembrance, unless he meant that if the memory weakens its companion from remembering her testimony, it sharpens her in remembering what she was weak in remembering and forgot, so it strengthens her with remembrance until it makes her like a man in her strength in remembering what she was weak in remembering of that, just as something strong in its work is called male, and just as a sword that is sharp in its strike is called a sword of remembrance, and a man of remembrance means: persistent in his work, strong in striking, sound in resolve. If this is what Ibn Uyaynah meant, then it is one of the schools of thought for interpreting that, except that if it is interpreted in this way, then his interpretation of it becomes similar to our interpretation that we interpreted it in, even if the reading with that meaning differs from the reading that we have chosen.

And the meaning of the reading in that case is correct according to the reading he chose from lightening the kaf in his saying: So remember. And we do not know of anyone who interpreted that in this way, and it is recommended to read it in this way with that meaning. So the correct reading of it - since the matter is general as we have described - is what we have chosen. It was mentioned that he interpreted his statement:
h
That one of them should go astray and then one of them should remind the other in a similar way to the interpretation that we mentioned in it

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men

. But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses - so that if one of them errs, the other can remind her.” God knew that there would be rights, so He took for some of them trust from others, so take with God’s trust, for he is more obedient to your Lord and more capable of handling your wealth. By my life, if he is righteous, the Book will only increase him in good, and if he is wicked, then it is more appropriate that he pays it if he knows that there are witnesses against him.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: That one of them forgets and the other reminds her, meaning: that one of them forgets and the other reminds her.

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: That one of Surat Al-Baqarah 2:282 O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write it down between you in justice. And let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write, and let the one upon whom the debt is dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not withhold from it anything. But if the one upon whom the debt is is If the one who is in the wrong is a fool or weak or cannot dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice.
h
And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men

. But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of them errs, then one of them can remind the other. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon, and do not be weary of writing it down, whether it is young or old. That is more just in the sight of Allah and more suitable for testimony and more suitable so that you do not have doubts. Unless it is a present trade which you conduct among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it down. And bring witnesses when you make a transaction, and let neither scribe nor witness be harmed. But if you do, it is indeed a transgression on your part. And fear Allah, and Allah teaches you. And Allah is Knowing of all things. them should forget, he said: One of them should forget the testimony, and the other should remind her.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: That one of them should go astray, he said: If one of them forgets, the other will remind her.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
That one of them should go astray and then one of them should remind the other
, he said: Both of them are linguistic, and they are the same, and we read, then she should remember.

evidence.text: And he recited this verse: When you contract a debt for a specified term.
Abu Jaafar said: The reading of this differed.
Others read it in the same way, but they read it with a sukoon on the dhal of thikr and a light kaf.
The readers of this also differ among themselves in the interpretation of their reading of it in this way.

Others read it as: If one of them should go astray, then one of them should remind the other, with a kasra on in in his statement: If she goes astray, and raising she should remind and emphasizing it, as if it means starting the report about what the two women will do if one of them forgets her testimony, the other reminds her, from the confirmation of the forgetful memory and reminding her of that, and the cessation of that from what came before it.
This is the reading that Al-A'mash and those who took it from him used to read.

The interpretation of the statement according to his reading is: in tadalal, so when one of the two lams merged into the other, he moved it to the lightest of the movements, and raised tadhkira with the fa because it is the answer to the recompense.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading in our view is the reading of those who read it with the fat-ha on an from his statement: that one of them should go astray, and with the shaddah on the kaf from his statement: then one of them should remind the other.

We chose this in the recitation, because of the consensus of the authority of the ancient and modern reciters on this, and the uniqueness of Al-A’mash and those who recited his recitation in this, which is unique from them.
It is not permissible to abandon a recitation that the Muslims brought, widely spread among them, for another.

If this is what Ibn Uyaynah meant, then it is one of the schools of thought for interpreting that, except that if it is interpreted in this way, then his interpretation of it becomes similar to our interpretation that we interpreted it in, even if the reading with that meaning differs from the reading that we have chosen.
And the meaning of the reading in that case is correct according to the reading he chose from lightening the kaf in his saying: So remember.
And we do not know of anyone who interpreted that in this way, and it is recommended to read it in this way with that meaning.
So the correct reading of it - since the matter is general as we have described - is what we have chosen.

x: The people of interpretation differed regarding the situation in which God forbade the martyrs from refusing to answer if they were called upon with this verse.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: The witnesses do not refuse to answer, if they are called to bear witness to the Book and the rights.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the words of God Almighty:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, a man would go around the great ocean in which there were people, calling them to bear witness, but none of them would follow him. He said: Qatada interpreted this verse:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, to bear witness for a man against a man.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar that he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, he said: A man would go around among a large group of people calling them to bear witness, but none of them would follow him, so God Almighty revealed:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, he said: Do not refuse to testify when you are called upon to testify.

x: Others said something similar to these, except that they said: This must be imposed on the one who is called to bear witness to rights if there is no one else. But if there is someone else, then he has a choice in responding to that. If he wants to, he can respond, and if he wants, he can not respond.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abu Asim told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: And the witnesses shall not refuse if they are called upon. He said: If he wishes, he may testify, and if he wishes, he may not testify, and if no one else is found, he may testify.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: And the witnesses should not refuse when they are called - to testify against whomever the caller wants to call upon, and to carry out what he has of testimony - from answering.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Abu Amer told us, on the authority of al-Hasan:
m: h
And the witnesses shall not refuse when they are called upon
, he said: al-Hasan said: residence and testimony.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, he said: Al-Hasan used to say: It combines two matters: Do not refuse to testify if you have a testimony, and do not refuse if you are called upon to testify.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, meaning: whoever is needed from the Muslims should testify to a testimony if he has it, and it is not permissible for him to refuse when he is called upon.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And the witnesses shall not refuse when they are called upon
, he said: to establish it, and he shall not begin with it, if he is called upon to establish it.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And the witnesses shall not refuse, when they are called - to provide the testimony they have for the caller - from answering him and providing it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:283 And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit. But if one of you trusts another, then let him who is trusted discharge his trust and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony. And whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart is sinful. And Allah is Knowing of what you do. on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And the witnesses shall not refuse when they are called upon
, he said: if they testify.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And the witnesses shall not refuse if they are called upon, he said: If they had testified before that.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And the witnesses shall not refuse if they are called upon, meaning: if they have been called upon to bear witness.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, he said: If you have a testimony and are called upon.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Layth told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, he said: If it is a testimony, then perform it. So if you are called to bear witness, then if you wish, then go, and if you wish, then do not go.

c: Suwar bin Abdullah told us, he said, Abdul Malik bin Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, he said:
m: I said to Abu Majlaz: People invite me to bear witness between them, and I hate to bear witness between them? He said: Leave what you hate, and if you bear witness, then respond when invited.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Amer, he said:
m: The witness has the option as long as he does not testify.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
. He said: To establish the testimony.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Amir, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: In establishing the testimony.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Amir Al-Muzni told us, he said,
m: I heard Ata’ say: That is in establishing the testimony, meaning his statement:
h
And the witnesses shall not refuse when they are called upon

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Abu Hura told us,
m: he told us on the authority of Al-Hasan that a questioner asked him, he said: I am called to testify, but I hate to testify to it. He said: Then do not answer if you wish.

c: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, who said:
m: I asked Ibrahim, saying: I am called to testify and I fear that I will forget? He said: Then do not testify if you wish.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Abu Amir told us, on the authority of Ata’, he said:
m: For the residence.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: And the witnesses shall not refuse if they are called upon, he said: If they have already testified.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid bin Nasr told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
And the witnesses shall not refuse when they are called upon
, he said: He is the one who has the testimony.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying:
h
And the witnesses shall not refuse when they are called upon

, he said: The witness shall not refuse to come forward and testify, if he is free. Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I said to Ata’: And the witnesses should not refuse if they are called upon. He said: They are those who have already testified. He said: It does not harm a person if he refuses to testify if he wishes. I said to Ata’: What is the matter with him? If he is called to write, he must not refuse, and if he is called to testify, he is not obligated to testify if he wishes! He said: Likewise, the writer must write, and the witness is not obligated to testify if he wishes. There are many witnesses.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, he said: If he testifies, then let him not refuse when he is called upon to come and give testimony and establish it.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And let not the witnesses refuse, he said: Al-Hasan interpreted it as: if he had a testimony and was called upon to present it.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon

, he said: If a man writes his testimony, or testifies for a man and he testifies, and the writer who writes the document - they are called to the conclusion of the truth, then it is upon them to respond and testify to what they testified to.

x: Others said: It is an order from God Almighty for the man and woman to respond if they are called to testify to rights that they have not testified to, initially, not to establish the testimony, but it is a recommended order, not an obligation.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Aaliyah Al-Abdi Ismail bin Al-Haitham told me, he said, Abu Qutaybah told us, on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq, on the authority of Atiyah Al-Awfi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon
, he said: You were commanded to bear witness, so if you wish, bear witness, and if you wish, do not bear witness.

c: Abu Al-Ali told me, he said, Abu Qutaybah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Thabit Al-Asri, on the authority of Ata’,
m: similarly.

x: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: [The meaning] of that is: The witnesses should not refuse to answer, if they are called to establish and give testimony before someone with authority or a ruler who takes from the one who is owed what is owed to him, for what is his. We said that this statement is more correct than all other statements, because God Almighty said:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon

, and He ordered them to respond to the call for testimony and He made the name martyrs obligatory for them. It is not permissible for the name martyrs to be obligatory for them unless they were martyred before that and testified to what their testimony made the name martyrs obligatory for them. As for before they testify to something, it is not permissible for them to be called martyrs. Because if that name were obligatory for them and they had not testified to something that would warrant this name by their testimony, there would not have been anyone on earth with a sound mind who did not deserve to be called a witness, meaning that he would testify, or that he is fit to testify.

Since it would be wrong to call by that name anyone except one who has testimony for another, or one who has established his testimony and therefore this name is required of him, it is known that the meaning of his saying:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon

, is the one whose description we have described as someone who has been called upon to give testimony, or has testified, and has been called upon to do so. Because the one who has not testified and has not been called upon to give testimony before giving testimony is not worthy of the name of martyr or witness, for what we have described before. Although the inclusion of the definite article in martyrs clearly indicates that the people mentioned in the prohibition against not responding to the testimony are known people who are known for their testimony, and that they are the ones whom God Almighty commanded the people of rights to call to witness by saying: “And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men.

But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses.” Since that is the case, it is known that they were only commanded to respond to their caller in order to establish their testimony after they were martyred and testified. If that were a command for those who refused from among the people and were called to testify, it would have been said: And no witness shall refuse when called. However, even if this is the case, what we say about the one who is called to testify to bear witness to it, if he is in a place where there is no one else who is fit to bear witness, then the obligation upon him is to respond to the caller to it, just as it is obligatory upon the writer if he is called to write in a place where there is no one else who writes, then it is obligatory upon him to write, just as it is obligatory upon the one who is in a place where there is no one else who knows the faith and the laws of Islam, and an ignorant person of the faith and the obligations of God comes to him, and he asks him to teach him and explain that to him, that he should teach him and explain it to him.

We did not make what we made obligatory upon the man to respond to the testimony if he is called initially to bear witness to what he testified to based on this verse, but rather on other evidence, which is what we mentioned. And it is obligatory upon the man to revive what he is able to revive of the right of his Muslim brother. Martyrs is the plural of martyr.

By that, may His praise be exalted, He means: And do not be weary, O you who borrow from people for a term, of writing down the small amount of the debt, meaning: its little, or its large amount - meaning: or its large amount - for its term, for the term of the right, for the writing is more accurate for the term and the money.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And do not be weary of writing it down, whether small or large, until its term, he said: It is the debt. The meaning of his saying: And do not get bored is: do not get tired. It is said: I got bored, so I get bored, boredom, and from this comes the saying of Labid: I am tired of life and its length and people asking me: How is Labid? And from it Zuhair said: I'm tired of the costs of life, and whoever lives to be eighty years old, I don't care, gets tired It means: I am bored. Some Basran grammarians said: The interpretation of his saying: until his term is until the term of the witness. Its meaning is until the term in which his testimony is permissible. We have explained what is said about this.

x: God Almighty means by His saying: That, the subscription of the book of religion until its term. What he means by his saying: more just, is more equitable with God. It is said: The ruler was just, so he is just, and he is just, if he was fair in his ruling and achieved the truth in it. So if he was unjust, it is said: he was just, so he is just, and he is just. And from this is the saying of God Almighty: But as for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell (al-Jinn 72:15), meaning: the unjust. And the group of interpreters said the same as we said about that. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:283 And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit. But if one of you trusts another, then let him who is trusted discharge his trust and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony. And whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart is sinful. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: his saying: That is more just with God, he said: more just with God.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And more correct for testimony. Its origin is from the saying: I straightened it from its crookedness, meaning I made it straight and level. The Book is more just in the sight of God, and more correct for the testimony of witnesses on what is in it, because it contains the words that the seller, the buyer, the creditor, and the borrower have acknowledged on his behalf. Thus, there is no difference between the witnesses in their words in their testimony, because their testimony is united on what the Book contains. And if their testimony is united on that, the judgment between them is clearer for the judges who resort to it, in addition to other reasons. And it is more just in the sight of God, because He has commanded it. And following the command of God is undoubtedly more just and equitable in the sight of God than abandoning it and deviating from it.
What He, may His praise be glorified, meant by His saying: and nearer, is closer, from closeness, which means nearness.
What he means by his saying: Do not doubt, is that you do not doubt the testimony, as:

c: Musa told us, Amr told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: That is more likely to prevent you from having doubts, meaning: that you do not doubt the testimony. It is a fabrication of suspicion. The meaning of the words: And do not be tired, O people, of writing down the right that you have before those you have lent to from the people for a term, whether that right is small or large, for your writing that is more just with God, and more correct for the testimony of your witnesses to it, and closer to you so that you do not doubt what your witnesses testify to against you of the right and the term if it is written.

x: Then He, the Most High, made an exception from what He forbade them from doing, that they should be bored with writing down the books of their rights over their creditors, with the rights they have over them, what is due to them from them from a right from a sale for present cash hand to hand, so He permitted them to leave writing down the books with that. Because each one of them, I mean the sellers and buyers, receives, if what is due between them in what they sell in cash, what is due from the two parties before the separation, so they have no need in that for one of the two parties to write down from the other party a book of what is due to them from them, and they have received what is due to them from them. Therefore, the Most High said: Except it be a present trade which you circulate among yourselves, with no term, delay, or forbearance,
h
There is no blame upon you if you do not write it down
, meaning present trade.
A group of interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: Except that it is a present trade that you carry out among yourselves, meaning: with you in the country, you see it, so you take and give, then there is no blame on these people if they do not write it down.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: And do not be weary of writing it down, whether it is small or large, until its term, until His saying:
h
There is no blame upon you if you do not write it down

, he said: God commanded that you not be weary of writing it down, whether it is small or large, until its term, and He commanded that what was hand to hand be witnessed, whether it was small or large, and He permitted them not to write it down. There are different readings of this. So I read it in general, as is the reading of the Hijaz and Iraq, and in general, except that it is a present trade, with the nominative case.

x: Some of the Kufian reciters were unique in reciting it in the accusative case. This is even though it is permissible in Arabic, since the Arabs used to put indefinite and qualified nouns in the accusative case with kāna, and to imply an unknown noun with kāna, so you would say: If it was a good food, bring it to us, and to raise it, so you would say: If it was a good food, bring it to us, and then follow the indefinite noun with its predicate in the same way as its inflection. What I have chosen from the recitation, and I do not permit reading in any other way, is the nominative case in present trade, due to the consensus of the reciters on that, and the anomaly of those who read it in the accusative case from them. The anomaly does not object to the argument.

i: Among what came in the accusative case is the saying of the poet:
x: My eyes, why don't you cry for forgiveness if there is a stabbing or an embrace between them?

And the other said: By God, my al-Nas 114:what a people of Harrah if there were ever more hideous stars!! The Arabs do this with indefinite nouns, because we have described that the predicates of indefinite nouns follow their names. One of its rules is that there is a nominative and an accusative with it. If they raise both of them, they remember that the indefinite noun follows its predicate. If they place both of them in the accusative case, they remember that kāna is accompanied by an accusative and a nominative. They find that the indefinite noun is followed by its predicate, and they omit the unknown in kāna, because it can be a pronoun.

Some people thought that whoever read it: except that it is a present trade, read it with the meaning: except that it is a present trade, so he claimed that the reader of that should have read it with a ya’, and he ignored the correct place to read it in terms of grammar, and he was obligated to do something other than what he was obligated to do. That is because when the Arabs make an indefinite noun with kāna feminine with its description or predicate, they feminize kāna once and masculine another time, so they said: If it is a young girl, then buy it - and if it is a young girl, then buy it. Kāna is sometimes masculine - even if the indefinite noun with the description is in the accusative or nominative - and sometimes it is feminine. Some Basra grammarians have claimed that his statement: Except that it is a present trade is in the nominative case, in which the present trade is in the nominative case, because it is complete, and there is no need for a predicate, meaning: except that it exists or occurs or takes place.

So he obligated himself to do what was not necessary for it, because he only obligated himself to do that, since he did not find was in the accusative case, and he found the present trade in the nominative case, and he ignored the permissibility of his statement: You circulate it among you being the predicate of was, so that he does not need to obligate himself to what he obligated. And what was said by those we have mentioned from the Basrans is not wrong in Arabic, except that what we have said is more similar to the speech of the Arabs, and more correct in meaning: which is that there are two aspects to his saying: You circulate it among yourselves: One of them is that it is in the accusative case, as it has taken the place of the predicate of was, and the present trade is its subject. And the other: that it is in the nominative case as following the present trade, because the predicate of the indefinite follows it.
So its interpretation is: except that it is a present trade circulating among you.

By that, He, the Most High, means: And have witnesses to the small and large rights that you have traded, whether immediate or deferred, cash or women. For my allowing you to refrain from subscribing to books among yourselves regarding rights that are valid between you, from one another, for a present trade that is ongoing between you, hand to hand and in cash, is not like my allowing you to refrain from having witnesses to the one to whom you sold or from whom you bought something. Because in your refraining from having witnesses to that, there is fear of harm to both parties: As for the buyer, if the seller denies the sale, and he has evidence of his ownership of what he sold, and the buyer does not have evidence of his purchase from him, then the seller’s word with his oath is accepted and it is ruled in his favor, so the buyer’s money is void. As for the seller, if the buyer denies the purchase and the seller’s ownership of what he sold has ceased, and the price of what he sold is due to him from the buyer, then he swears to that, so the seller’s right to the price of what he sold is void.
So God Almighty commanded both parties to have witnesses, so that the right of one party would not be lost before the other party. Then they differed about the meaning of his saying:
h
And have witnesses when you make a sale
. Is it an order from God that it is obligatory to have witnesses when making a sale, or is it recommended?
Some of them said: It is recommended. If he wants, he can bear witness, and if he wants, he cannot bear witness.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Shaqiq, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And bring witnesses when you make a transaction

, he said: If he wishes, he will bear witness, and if he wishes, he will not bear witness. Have you not heard his statement: But if one of you trusts another, then let the one who is trusted discharge his trust?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Al-Rabi bin Subaih told us, he said:
m: I said to Al-Hasan: What do you think of the statement of God Almighty:
h
And bring witnesses when you make a transaction
? He said: If you bring witnesses to it, then it is trustworthy for what you have, but if you do not bring witnesses to it, then there is no problem.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, Suwaid told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Subaih, who said:
m: I said to al-Hasan: O Abu Saeed, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And bring to witness when you make a transaction, I sell to a man and I know that he will not pay me back for two or three months. Do you see any harm in not bringing to witness against him? He said: If you bring to witness, then he is trustworthy for what you have, but if you do not bring to witness, then there is no harm.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
m: h
And have witnesses when you make a sale
, he said: If they wish, they may have witnesses, and if they wish, they may not have witnesses.

x: Others said: Witnessing this is obligatory.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: Unless it is a present trade which you carry out among yourselves, then
h
there is no blame upon you if you do not write it down
, but have witnesses to it when you make a transaction. God has commanded that what is hand to hand be witnessed to, whether it is small or large.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: Whatever was a sale on the spot, if he wanted, he could have witnesses, and if he wanted, he could not have witnesses. And whatever was a sale on credit, God commanded that it be written down and that Surat Al-Baqarah 2:283 And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit. But if one of you trusts another, then let him who is trusted discharge his trust and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony. And whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart is sinful. And Allah is Knowing of what you do. witnesses be brought to it. And that is in this case.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is that witnessing every sale and purchase is a necessary right and an obligatory duty, because we have explained that every command of God is an obligation, except for what His proof has been established from the aspect that must be accepted as being a recommendation and guidance. We have demonstrated that it is the statement of those who said: It was abrogated by His statement: So let the one who is entrusted fulfill his trust, in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of that.

Some of them said: This is a prohibition from God, the writer of the book between the people of rights and the witness, that he should not harm his people, so this one writes what the dictator did not dictate, and this one testifies to what the witness did not testify to.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told me, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed
h
And neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed
” by writing what was not dictated to him, nor the witness by testifying to what was not testified to.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, he said:
m: Al-Hasan used to say: And no scribe shall be harmed, so that he does not add or distort anything, nor a witness, he said: He does not conceal testimony, and he does not testify except to the truth.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: A witness should fear God in his testimony, neither subtracting from it any truth nor adding any falsehood to it. A writer should fear God in his book, neither leaving out any truth nor adding any falsehood to it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed
, he said:
h
And neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed
, so he writes what he does not dictate, nor the witness, so he testifies to what he did not testify to.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, And let no scribe or witness be harmed, he said: And let no scribe be harmed by writing other than what was dictated to him. He said: And the scribes at that time will be few, and they will not know what to write, so he will be harmed by writing other than what was dictated to him, and their right will be nullified. He said: And the witness will be harmed by changing his testimony, and their right will be nullified.

x: The root of the word, according to the interpretation of those we mentioned, is: Neither a writer nor a witness shall be harmed. Then the ra’ was assimilated into the ra’, because they are of the same type, and it was moved to the fatha, and its place is the jazm, because the fatha is the lightest of the movements.

Others who interpreted this word in this way said: The meaning of this is: Neither a scribe nor a witness shall be harmed by refraining from someone who calls them to perform what they have of knowledge or testimony.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed
, he said: That they should perform what came before them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: I said to Ata’: Neither a scribe nor a witness shall be harmed. He said: They shall not be harmed, if they convey what they have of knowledge.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: h
And neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed
, he said: That he calls them and they say: We have a need.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ and Mujahid:
m: h
And neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed
, they said: It is obligatory for the scribe to write, nor the witness, they said: If he has testified, accept it.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: The one who writes and the one who witnesses shall not be harmed, the writer and the witness. The interpretation of the word according to their doctrine is: and he shall not be harmed, in the sense that the doer of the act is not named.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: Umar used to recite: Neither a scribe nor a witness shall be harmed.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak, who said: Ibn Masʿud used to recite: And do not cause harm.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah bin Kathir told me, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: that he used to recite: Neither scribe nor witness shall be harmed, and that he used to say in its interpretation: The one who has the right goes out and calls his scribe and his witness to testify, and perhaps he is busy or in need, so that he may sin if he leaves that at that time because of his busyness and need. Mujahid said: He does not get up from his busyness and need, so that he finds himself in trouble or is embarrassed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: h
And neither a scribe nor a witness shall be harmed

. Harm is when a man says to another man, although he has no need of him, God has commanded you not to refuse when you are called! and he harms him by doing so, while he is satisfied with something else. So God, the Almighty, forbade him from doing that and said: But if you do, then it is a transgression on your part.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: h
And neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed
, meaning: The scribe or the witness will have a need that he cannot avoid, so he will say: Let him go.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: And let no scribe or witness be harmed, he said: He may be ill or busy, he says: So he will not be harmed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid
m: that he used to say: Neither a writer nor a witness should be harmed. He said: A man should not come and say: Go write for me and bear witness for me! He says: I have a need, so find someone else! He says: Fear God, for you have been commanded to write for me! This is harm, and he says: Leave him and find someone else. The witness is in that position.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And let neither scribe nor witness be harmed

, he said: A man calls the scribe or the witness, and the scribe or the witness says: We have a need! So the one who calls them says: God, the Almighty, has commanded you to respond in writing and testimony! God, the Almighty, says: Let them not be harmed.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid bin Sulaiman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak, regarding His statement:
h
And let not the scribe or the witness be harmed

, it is a man who calls the scribe or the witness while they are in need of something important, and they say: We have something important, so look for someone else! He says: By God, He has commanded you to respond! So He commanded him to look for someone else and not to harm them, meaning: He should not distract them from their important need while he finds someone else.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And neither a scribe nor a witness shall be harmed

, meaning: It is not appropriate for you to intercept a man who has a need and harm him by saying to him: Write for me! So you do not leave him until he writes for you and miss his need, nor to one of your witnesses while he is busy and you say: Go and bear witness for me! Preventing him from his need while you find someone else. Narrated on the authority of Ammar, he said:

c: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his saying:
h
And let not a scribe or a witness be harmed

, he said: When this verse was revealed: And let not a scribe refuse to write as God has taught him, one of them would come to the scribe and say: Write for me! He would say: I am busy, or: I have a need, so go to someone else! He would cling to him and say: You were commanded to write for me! But he would not leave him and would harm him with that while he could find someone else. And a man would come and say: Go with me and bear witness for me! He would say: Go to someone else, for I am busy, or: I have a need! He would cling to him and say: You were commanded to follow me! But he would harm him with that while he could find someone else. So God, the Almighty, revealed:
h
And let not a scribe or a witness be harmed

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: h
And neither a scribe nor a witness shall be harmed
. He says: I have a need, so leave me alone! He says: Write for me. And neither a witness, likewise.

x: The most correct of the statements on this matter is the statement of the one who said: The meaning of this is:
h
Neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed

, meaning: Nor shall the one who asks this one to write or the one who asks this one to testify harm them, by refusing to let this one write for him unless he is busy with his own affairs, and refusing to let this one do anything but answer him to testify while he is not free, according to what the proponents of that statement said from the statement we mentioned before. We said that this statement is more correct than any other, because the address from God the Almighty in this verse from its beginning to its end is in the form of: do, or do not do, it is only addressed to those who have rights and those who have a written contract between them, and those who are testified for or against for what they have incurred among themselves of debts.

As for what was of command or prohibition in it for others, it is only in the form of a command and prohibition for the absent one who is not addressed, like His saying: And let a scribe write between you, and His saying:
h
And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called

, and the like. So the face - since those commanded in it are addressed by His saying: But if Surat Al-Baqarah 2:283 And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe, then a security deposit. But if one of you trusts another, then let him who is trusted discharge his trust and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony. And whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart is sinful. And Allah is Knowing of what you do. you do it, it is a transgression on your part - is that the command is returned to the one who is being written and the one who is being testified to, which is more likely to be returned to the writer and the witness.

However, if the writer and the witness were the ones who were forbidden from causing harm, it would have been said: And if they do it, it is a transgression on their part. Because they are two, and they are not addressed by His saying: nor shall he be harmed, rather the prohibition by His saying: nor shall he be harmed, is a prohibition for the absent one who is not addressed. So directing the speech to what is similar to what is in the context of the verse is more appropriate than directing it to what is different from it.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And if you harm the scribe or the witness, and what you are forbidden from doing, then it is a transgression on your part, meaning: a sin and disobedience on your part.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak:
m: And if you do, then it is a sin on your part, meaning: If you do other than what I command you to do, then it is a sin on your part.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And if you do, then it is a transgression on your part, and transgression is disobedience.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ: And if you do so, then it is a transgression on your part. Transgression is disobedience.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: If a writer is harmed and writes something other than what the one who dictated it dictated, and a witness is harmed and changes his testimony, then that is a transgression on your part, meaning: then it is a lie.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: And if you do, then it is a transgression on your part, transgression is lying. He said: This is a transgression, because the writer lied and changed his book and lied, and the witness lied and changed his testimony.

c: So God informed them that
m: he lied.

x: We have previously demonstrated that what is meant by his saying:
h
Neither the scribe nor the witness shall be harmed

, is that the one who writes and the one who witnesses shall not be harmed, to the extent that is sufficient. His saying: And if you do so, is only to inform those who harm them of His ruling on them, and that whoever harms them has disobeyed his Lord and sinned against Him, and committed what is not permissible for him, and has gone beyond the obedience of his Lord in that.

What He, the Most High, means by His saying, And fear God, is fear God, O you who are in debt in the Book and witnesses, lest you harm them, and in other than that of God’s limits lest you neglect them. What He means by His saying, And God teaches you, is He explains to you what is obligatory for you and upon you, so act upon it. And God is Knowing of all things, meaning: of all things] of your deeds and other things, He counts them against you, to reward you for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement: And God teaches you, he said: This is a teaching that He taught you, so take it.

evidence.text: So I read it in general, as is the reading of the Hijaz and Iraq, and in general, except that it is a present trade, with the nominative case.
Some of the Kufian reciters were unique in reciting it in the accusative case.

What I have chosen from the recitation, and I do not permit reading in any other way, is the nominative case in present trade, due to the consensus of the reciters on that, and the anomaly of those who read it in the accusative case from them.

Some people thought that whoever read it: except that it is a present trade, read it with the meaning: except that it is a present trade, so he claimed that the reader of that should have read it with a ya’, and he ignored the correct place to read it in terms of grammar, and he was obligated to do something other than what he was obligated to do.

x: The readings differed in the reading of that. The readers in all the countries read it as a writer, meaning: And you did not find anyone to write for you the book of the debt that you borrowed for a specified period, a pledge in possession.

A group of the ancients read: And you did not find a book, meaning: And you did not have a way to write down the book of religion, either because the inkwell and the paper were not available, or because the writer was not available even if you found the inkwell and the paper. The reading that is not permissible other than it according to us is the reading of the regions, And you did not find a writer, meaning: someone who writes. Because that is how it is in the Muslims’ copies of the Qur’an. [Abu Jaʿfar said: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means:] And if you, O debtors, are on a journey where you cannot find a writer to write for you, and you have no way to write down the book of the debt that you have borrowed for a specified term between you, which I have ordered you to write down and have witnesses to, then take as a pledge the debts that you have borrowed for the specified term, pledges that you collect from whomever you are borrowing from in this way, so that it will be a trust for you with your money.
Mention of those who said what we said about that:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Zuhair told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe

, then a pledge taken in possession. So whoever is on a journey and makes a sale on credit and does not find a scribe, then he is permitted to take a pledge taken in possession, but if he finds a scribe, he does not have the right to take a pledge.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement:
h
And if you are on a journey and cannot find a scribe
, meaning: a scribe to write for you, then a pledge is taken.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: Whatever was a sale on credit, God Almighty commanded that it be written down and witnessed, and that is in the present situation. If people were on a journey and they made a sale on credit and did not find [a writer], then it is a pledge that is taken possession of.

x: Mention of those who interpreted this based on the reading we mentioned:

c: Abu Kuraib told us, Hisham told us, Yazid bin Abi Ziyad told us, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: If you do not find a book, he means by the book the writer, the paper, the inkwell, and the pen.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Jurayj told us, he said, my father told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he read: If you do not find a writer, he said: Perhaps a man finds a page but does not find a writer.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He used to recite it: If you do not find a book, and he would say: Perhaps the writer is found but the page or ink is not found, and something similar to this statement.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And if you are on a journey and you cannot find a book, he says: ink - he reads it like this - he says: If you cannot find ink, then at that time the pledges are taken, then a pledge taken, he said: The pledge is only taken while travelling.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Shu’ayb bin Al-Habhab, he said:
m: Abu Al-Aaliyah used to recite it: If you do not find a book, Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The inkwell is found but the paper is not found.

x: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of his statement: A pledge taken. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as: Farhan Maqbudha, meaning the collection of a pledge, just as rams are the collection of a ram, mules are the collection of a mule, and sandals are the collection of sandals.
Another group read it as: farahn maqbudah meaning the plural of rahan, and rahan is the plural of rahan.
Some of them interpreted it as the plural of rahan, like saqf and saqf.

Others read it as farhan with a lightened ha meaning plural of rahn, just as saqf is pluralized as saqf. They said: We do not know of a noun with the pattern fa’l that is pluralized as fa’l and fa’l except al-rahn and al-rahn, and al-saqf and al-saqf.

What is more correct in this regard is the reading of the one who read it: Farhan Maqbudah. Because this is the well-known plural of a noun on the pattern of faʿl, as is said: habl and habal and kaʿab and kaʿab, and similar to these names. As for the plural of faʿl on the pattern of faʿl or faʿl, it is rare and rare, and only occurs in a few letters. It was said: saqf and saqf and saqf and qalb and qalb and qalb from: qalb an-nakhl. And jad and jad, for jad which means luck. As for what came from the plural of faʿl on the pattern of faʿl, it is tht and tht, and ward and ward and khud and khud. The one who read it as: a pledge in possession was prompted to read it as such, I think, despite its anomaly in the plural of faʿl, because he found the wager used in the case of a horse bet, so he wanted to divert that from the ambiguous wording of a wager of horses, which is not in the meaning of a wager, which is the plural of rahn, and he found the wager used in the plural of rahn, as Qanab said: Suad has left, and Aden has become distant from her, and the pledge in your heart has been closed to her.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: If the debtor is trustworthy with the owner of the money and the debt, and does not take a pledge from him during his travel as a pledge for his debt, due to his trustworthiness with him regarding his money and his confidence, and let the debtor fear God, his Lord, meaning: let him fear God, his Lord, in what he owes of his creditor’s debt, lest he deny it, or be lenient with him, or try to take it away, and expose himself to God’s punishment for something he cannot bear, and let him pay his debt that he entrusted to him, to him. We have mentioned the statement of those who said: This ruling is from God Almighty, abrogating the rulings in the verse before it: from God Almighty’s command to have witnesses and to write. We have demonstrated the most correct of what is said about it, so there is no need to repeat it in this place.

And: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement: If some of you trust others, then let the one who is trusted discharge his trust, he only meant by that: while traveling, but not while at home, and he has a scribe, so he does not have the right to take a pledge or trust others.

What Al-Dahhak said, that the creditor does not have the right to trust the debtor while he has access to the scribe, the book, and witnesses, even if he is traveling, is as he said, because we have proven its validity in what has passed before. As for what he said, that the matter in the mortgage is also like the trust: in that the owner of the right does not have the right to mortgage his money if he finds a way to the writer and the witness, whether at home or traveling, then it is a statement that has no meaning, due to the authenticity of the report “on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: He bought food for women and mortgaged his armor with it. It is permissible for a man to pledge what he owes and pledge what he has a right to, whether traveling or at home, due to the authenticity of the report we have mentioned from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and it is known that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not - when he pledged what we have mentioned - not have a scribe or a witness, because it was not difficult for him in his city at any time to have a scribe and a witness.

However, if they make a sale and present a pledge, then it is obligatory upon them - if they find a way to a scribe and a witness, or the sale or the two are for a specified period - to write that down and bear witness to the money and the pledge. It is only permissible to leave the writing and the witness in that case, when they do not have a way to do that.

This is a speech from God Almighty to the witnesses whom the debtor and the owner of the money ordered to bear witness, so He said to them: “And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called” - and do not conceal, O witnesses, after you have testified your testimony before the judges, just as you testified to what you testified to, but respond to the one for whom you testified if he calls you to establish your testimony against his opponent regarding his right before the judge who will take his right for him.

i: Then the witness, may His praise be glorified, informed us of what he must do in concealing his testimony, and his refusal to give it and perform it when the person testifying needs him to do it before a ruler or someone in authority, so He said:
x: And whoever conceals it.
Meaning: And whoever conceals his testimony, then his heart is sinful.
He says: His heart is wicked, and by concealing it he has acquired disobedience to God, as:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement: “And do not conceal testimony. And whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful.” It is not permissible for anyone to conceal testimony that he has, even if it is against himself and his parents. And whoever conceals it has committed a great sin.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement: And whoever conceals it, then his heart is sinful, meaning: his heart is wicked.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Salih told us,
m: he Surat Al-Baqarah 2:284
h
To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills. And God is over all things competent. said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The greatest of the major sins is associating partners with God, because God says: Indeed, whoever associates partners with God - God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire (al-Ma’idah 5:72), and bearing false witness, and concealing testimony, because God Almighty says: And whoever conceals it - then indeed his heart is sinful.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to say: The witness must testify wherever he is called to testify and inform about it wherever he is asked to inform about it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, he said, Amr ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: If you have a testimony and he asks you about it, then tell him about it, and do not say: Tell it to the emir, tell him about it, perhaps he will reconsider or be cautious. As for His statement: And God is Knowing of what you do, he means: of what you do in your testimony, whether it is giving and carrying it out, or concealing it when someone needs it from you, and other than that of your secret and public actions, He is Knowing, He counts it against you, so that He may reward you for all of that with your reward, either good or evil according to the extent of your deservingness.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying:
h
To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth

, is that God owns everything in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, small and large, and to Him belongs the management of all of it, and in His hand is its disposition and its turning, and nothing of it is hidden from Him, because He is its disposer, owner and manager. Rather, what He, the Most High, meant by this is the concealment of the testimony of witnesses. He says: Do not conceal the testimony, O witnesses. Whoever conceals it, his heart will explode, and his concealment of it will not be hidden from Me, because I am All-Knowing, and in My hand is the control of everything in the heavens and the earth and its dominion. I know the hidden and the obvious of that, so fear My punishment for your concealment of the testimony, and a threat from God for that to whoever conceals it, and a warning from Him for him with it.

c: Then He informed them
m: of what He would do to them in the Hereafter and to those of their peers who concealed a sin and then hid it, or showed a sin and then showed it from themselves - from the accountability for it, so He said:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it

, meaning: And whether you disclose what you have of testimony on the right of the owner of wealth, denial and rejection, or conceal it and conceal it in your souls, and other than that of your evil deeds,
h
God will bring you to account for it

, meaning by that: He will hold you accountable for it from your deeds, so He will punish whomever He wills among you of the wrongdoers for his evil deeds, and forgive whomever He wills among you of the wrongdoers. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding what was meant by his saying:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

x: Some of them said what we said: that he meant by it the witnesses who concealed their testimony, and that he included with them everyone who was like them and who concealed or showed disobedience.
Who said that?

c: Abu Zaydah Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaydah told me, he said, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, he said: He means in testimony.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
, he said: In testimony.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, Abd Al-A’la told us:
m: Dawud was asked about his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, so he told us on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: It is testimony if you conceal it.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Amr and Abu Saʿid:
m: that he heard ʿIkrimah say about this verse:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
, he said: about testimony.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
, he said: Regarding testimony.

c: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Yazid bin Abi Ziyad told us, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said
m: about this verse,
h
And if you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, he said: It was revealed regarding concealing testimony and establishing it.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, meaning: concealing testimony in order to establish it properly.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed as an announcement from God Almighty to His servants that He will hold them accountable for what their hands have earned and what their souls have told them, which they did not do. Then the interpreters of that differed as well.
Some of them said: Then God abrogated that by saying: “
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has committed” (al-Baqarah 2:286).

Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated that Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated on the authority of Musʿab ibn Thabit on the authority of Al-ʿAlaʿ ibn ʿAbdur-Rahman on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: When the verse was revealed: “
h
To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth
. And if you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it,
h
God will bring you to account for it
,” the people were distressed by that and said: O Messenger of God, will we be held accountable for what we tell ourselves? We are doomed! Then God, the Almighty, revealed:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity

2:286 until His saying: Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake 2:286. My father said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God said: Yes. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us 2:286 until the end of the verse.
My father said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the Almighty, said: Yes.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Wakee’ told us, and Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Adam ibn Sulayman,
m: the client of Khalid ibn Khalid, he said, I heard Saeed ibn Jubayr narrating, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When this verse was revealed: “
h
And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills,” something of it entered their hearts that had never entered them before, “so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We hear, we obey, and we submit.” He said: So God, the Almighty, cast faith into their hearts. He said: So God, the Almighty, revealed: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord (al-Baqarah 2:285). Abu Kurayb said: So he recited: Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake (al-Baqarah 2:286). He said: So he said: I have done it. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us (al-Baqarah 2:286). He said: I have done it. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear (al-Baqarah 2:286). He said: I have done it. “And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people” (al-Baqarah 2:286). He said: I have done it.

c: Abu al-Raddad al-Masri Abdullah bin Abdul Salam told me, he said, Abu Zur’ah Wahb God bin Rashid told us, on the authority of Haywah bin Shuraih, he said,
m: I heard Yazid bin Abi Habib say: Ibn Shihab said, Saeed bin Marjana told me, he said: I came to Abdullah bin Omar and he recited this verse: “
h
And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills.” Then Ibn Omar said: If we take this verse to task, we will be destroyed! Then Ibn Omar cried until his tears flowed. He said: Then I came to Abdullah bin Abbas and said: O Abu Abbas, I came to Ibn Omar and he recited this verse:
h
And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it

, the verse, then he said: If we take this verse to task, we will be destroyed! Then he cried until his tears flowed! Ibn Abbas said: May God forgive Abdullah bin Omar! The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless you and grant you peace, distinguished between them, as Ibn Omar distinguished between them. Then God revealed, “
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity

. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned.” (al-Baqarah 2:286), so God abrogated the whispering and established the saying and the action.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Yunus bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Saeed bin Marjana narrating:
m: While he was sitting, he heard Abdullah bin Omar reciting this verse, “
h
To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth

. Whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it,” the verse, and he said: By God, if God were to punish us for this, we would surely perish! Then Ibn Omar cried until he heard his sobs, and Ibn Marjana said: So I got up and went to Ibn Abbas and mentioned to him what Ibn Omar had recited, and what he did when he recited it, and Abdullah bin Abbas said: May God forgive Abu Abd al-Rahman! By my life, the Muslims felt from it what Abdullah bin Omar felt when it was revealed, and after it God revealed,
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity (al-Baqarah 2

:286) to the end of the surah. Ibn Abbas said: So this whispering was something that the Muslims could not bear, and the matter came to the point that God, the Almighty, decreed that the soul shall have what it has earned and shall bear what it has earned in word and deed.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us,
m: I heard al-Zuhri say about the verse: Whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, he said: Ibn Umar read it and wept and said: We will be held accountable for what we tell ourselves! So he wept until his sobs were heard, and a man got up from him and went to Ibn Abbas and mentioned that to him, and he said: May God have mercy on Ibn Umar, the Muslims found something similar to what he found, until the verse was revealed: “
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has committed” (al-Baqarah 2:286).

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdul-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Hamid al-Aʿraj,
m: on the Surat Al-Baqarah 2:284
h
To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills. And God is over all things competent. authority of Mujahid, he said: I was with Ibn ʿUmar, and he said: Whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, the verse, and he wept. So I went to Ibn ʿAbbas and mentioned that to him, and Ibn ʿAbbas laughed and said: May God have mercy on Ibn ʿUmar! Does he not know why it was revealed? When this verse was revealed, it greatly distressed the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: O Messenger of God, we are lost! “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Say: We hear and obey,” so it was abrogated by: “The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers,” to His saying: And upon it is whatever it has earned (al-Baqarah 2:285), so they were excused from the talk of the soul, and they were held accountable for their deeds.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim:
m: that his father recited:
h
And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

, and his eyes filled with tears. report of his action reached Ibn Abbas, who said: May God have mercy on Abu Abd al-Rahman! He did as the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did when it was revealed, and the verse that came after it abrogated it:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity (al-Baqarah 2

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: This verse was abrogated:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity (al-Baqarah 2

c: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu Ahmad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Adam bin Sulayman, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: When this verse was revealed: Whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, they said: Will we be held accountable for what our souls tell us but our limbs do not act upon it? He said: Then this verse was revealed: “
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred”
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:286)
. He said: And he says: I have done so. He said: So this nation was given the final verses of Surat Al-Baqarah, which the nations before it were not given.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said, Ismail told us, on the authority of Amer:
m: h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills.” He said: Then the verse after it abrogated it, His statement: “
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity

. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned.” (al-Baqarah 2:286) Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi:
h
And if you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, he said: The verse that came after it abrogated it:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity (al-Baqarah 2
:286). And His statement: And if you disclose, he said: He will be held to account for what he disclosed of a secret or concealed of a secret, so the verse that came after it abrogated it.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Sayyar told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: When this verse was revealed: “
h
And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills,” he said: There was severity in it, until this verse was revealed that follows it:
h
For her is what she has earned
