, and against her is what she has earned (al-Baqarah 2:286). He said: So it abrogated what came before it.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, he said:
m: They mentioned to Al-Sha’bi:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
, until he reached
h
For her is what she has earned
, and against her is what she has earned (al-Baqarah 2:286). He said: Al-Sha’bi said: This is what it came to, I went back to the end of the verse.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said,
m: I told Yazid, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
, he said, Ibn Masoud said: The accounting was before the revelation of:
h
For her is what she has earned
, and against her is what she has earned (al-Baqarah 2:286), so when it was revealed, the verse that came before it was abrogated.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak mention, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, something similar.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said:
m: h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
was abrogated by She shall have what she has earned, and she shall bear what she has earned (al-Baqarah 2:286).

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b,
m: and Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid, and on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, they said: This verse was abrogated:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity (al-Baqarah 2
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
, the verse.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah and Amer,
m: similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, Al-Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it to the end of the verse
, he said: He erased it: “
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. It will have [the consequence of] whatever it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] whatever it has earned” (al-Baqarah 2:286).

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He said: This verse - meaning His statement:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity (al-Baqarah 2
:286) - abrogated the verse that came before it:
h
And if you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, he said: It was abrogated by his statement:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity (al-Baqarah 2

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd told me, he said:
m: When this verse was revealed:
h
And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

to the end of the verse, it was very difficult for the Muslims and they said: O Messenger of God, if something occurred to us, we would not act upon it and God would hold us accountable for it? He said: Perhaps you will say as the Children of Israel said: We hear and disobey! They said: Rather, we hear and obey, O Messenger of God! He said: Then the Qur’an was revealed to relieve them: “The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers”
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:285)
to His saying: “
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has earned”
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:286)
. He said: So He directed it to deeds, and left what occurred in the hearts.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Sayyar Abu Al-Hakam, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah bin Mas’ud,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, he said: This verse abrogated the one after it:
h
For her is what she has earned
, and against her is what she has earned (al-Baqarah 2:286).
b.via: Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah bin Mas’ud

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

, he said: On the day this verse was revealed, they were held accountable for what their souls whispered to them and what they did, so they complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: If one of us does something and does not act, will we be held accountable for it? By God, we do not control whisperings!! So God abrogated it with this verse that follows with His statement:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:286)
, so the talk of the soul was something that you could not bear.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada: That Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her, said: It was abrogated by His statement:
h
For her is what she has earned
, and against her is what she has earned (al-Baqarah 2:286).

x: Others said - among those who said that the meaning of this is: God Almighty informs His servants that He will hold them accountable for what their hands have earned and what their limbs have done, and for what their souls have told them of things they did not do -: This verse is decisive and has not been abrogated, and God Almighty will hold His creation accountable for what they have done and for what they did not do of things they insisted on doing in their souls and intended and wanted, so He will forgive the believers for it and hold the people of disbelief and hypocrisy accountable for it.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

, it was not abrogated, but when God, the Almighty, gathers all creation on the Day of Resurrection, God, the Almighty, will say: I will inform you of what you concealed in yourselves of which My angels have not seen. As for the believers, He will inform them and forgive them for what they told themselves, which is His statement:
h
God will bring you to account for it

, meaning: He will inform you. As for the people of doubt and suspicion, He will inform them of what they concealed of denial, which is His statement: But He will take you to task for what your hearts have earned (al-Baqarah 2:225), of doubt and hypocrisy.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

. That is the secret of your deeds and their public aspects, by God’s account of you. There is no believing servant who conceals good in himself in order to make it pervasive to you, but if he does it, ten good deeds will be recorded for him because of it. But if he is not destined to do it, one good deed will be recorded for him because of it, because he is a believer, and God is pleased with the secrets of the believers and their public aspects. And if it is evil that he thinks of himself, God will see it and inform him of it on the Day when secrets are exposed. But if he does Surat Al-Baqarah 2:284
h
To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills. And God is over all things competent. not do it, God will not hold him accountable for it until he does it. But if he does it, God will overlook it, as He said: Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds. (al-Ahqaf 46:16) Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

, the verse, he said: Ibn Abbas said: God will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:My scribes have not written down of your deeds except what is apparent of them. As for what you concealed within your souls, I will bring you to account for it today, so forgive whomever You will and punish whomever You will.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Ali bin Asim told us, he said, Bayan told us, on the authority of Bishr, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, he said:
m: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God Almighty will say, while the creatures hear: My writing was only for them to write down about you what was apparent from you. As for what you concealed, they did not write it down nor did they do it. I, God, know all of that better than you, so forgive whomever You will, and punish whomever You will.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

. Ibn Abbas used to say: When people are called to account, God will inform them of what they used to conceal in their souls that they did not do, and He will say: Nothing was hidden from Me, and I will inform you of what you used to conceal of evil, and your guardians were not aware of it. So this is the accounting.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Ubaid bin Sulayman, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, he said: It is decisive, nothing has abrogated it. He says:
h
God will bring you to account for it
, meaning: God will know it on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:You concealed such and such in your heart! He will not hold you accountable for it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Amr ibn ʿUbayd, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: It is decisive and has not been abrogated.

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And if you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, he said: of doubt and certainty.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the words of God Almighty:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
, he said: in doubt and certainty.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly.

x: The interpretation of this verse according to the statement of Ibn ʿAbbas, which was narrated by ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah: “And if you disclose what is in your souls of any deeds and show it with your bodies and limbs, or conceal it and keep it secret within your souls and none of My creation knows about it, I will call you to account for it, and I will forgive all of that for the people of faith, and I will punish the people of polytheism and hypocrisy in My religion.” As for the narration narrated from him by Ad-Dahhak on the authority of ʿUbaid ibn Sulayman from him, and according to what Ar-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said, its interpretation is: If you disclose what is in your souls and do it of sins, or conceal its will within your souls and hide it, God will know it of you on the Day of Resurrection, and He will forgive whomever He wills and punish whomever He wills. As for the statement of Mujahid, its meaning is similar to the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas, which was narrated by Ali bin Abi Talha.

Others said - among those who said: This verse is decisive and has not been abrogated, and they agreed with those who said: The meaning of that is: God, the Almighty, knows best what He will do to His servants regarding their actions that they have revealed and concealed - its meaning is: God will hold all of His creation to account for all of their evil actions that they have revealed and all of what they have concealed, and He will punish them for it. However, His punishment of them for what they have concealed of what they did not do is whatever calamities and matters that befall them in this world that cause them grief and pain.
Who said that?

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

, the verse, he said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, used to say: Whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, God sends upon him anxiety and grief equal to the one he intended to do of the bad deed but did not do it, and that is his expiation.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
. He said: Aisha used to say: Every servant who intends to commit a sin or thinks about it, God will bring him to account for it in this world. He will fear, grieve, and worry.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Abu Tamila told me, on the authority of Ubaid, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: Aisha said
m: about that: Every servant who has an evil thought and a sin and thinks about it, God will hold him accountable in this world. He will fear and grieve and his worry will be intense, but nothing of that will reach him, just as he has an evil thought and did not do anything of it.

c: Al-Rabi’ narrated to us, saying: Asad bin Musa narrated to us, saying: Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Umayyah,
m: that she asked Aisha about this verse:
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it
and Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it
r
(An-Nisa’: 23)

. She said: No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless you and grant you peace, and he said: O Aisha, this is God’s pursuit of the servant with what befalls him of fever, calamity, and thorn, even the merchandise that he puts in his sleeve and loses it, and is alarmed by it and finds it in his thorn, until the believer emerges from his sins as red gold emerges from the bellows.

x: The first of the opinions we have mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse is the opinion of those who said: It is decisive and not abrogated. This is because abrogation does not occur in a ruling except by negating it with another, which negates it in all its aspects. And in His statement, the Most High, the Majestic: “
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity

. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has committed” (al-Baqarah 2:286), there is no negation of the ruling that He informed His servants with His statement: Or you conceal it,
h
God will bring you to account for it

. Because accountability does not entail punishment or retribution for the sins for which the servant is held accountable. God, the Most High, has informed us about the criminals that when their books of deeds are presented to them on the Day of Resurrection, they will say: Woe to us!

What is this book that leaves out nothing small or great but that it has enumerated it? (al-Kahf 18:94). So He informed that their books record their minor and major deeds. So the books, even though they record minor and major sins, were not, by virtue of their recording of the people of faith in God and His Messenger, and the people of obedience to Him, that they would be punished for everything the books record of sins. Because God, the Almighty, promised them forgiveness for minor sins, by their avoiding major sins. He said in His revelation:
If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your lesser sins and admit you to a noble entrance.

So that is God’s reckoning of His believing servants with what He will reckon them with of the matters that their souls concealed, without requiring them to be punished from Him, but rather His reckoning of them - God willing - for them, so that He may make them know His favor upon them by His pardoning them for them, as we have been informed from the Messenger of God, may God bless you and grant you peace, in the report that:

c: Ahmad ibn al-Muqaddam narrated to me, saying, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying,
m: I heard my father, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Safwan ibn Mahraz, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God will bring His believing servant close on the Day of Resurrection until He covers him with His cloak, and He will make him acknowledge his sins and say: Do you know? He will say: Yes! He will say: I concealed them in this world and forgive them today! Then He will show him his good deeds and say: ‘Here, read your record’ (al-Haqqah 69:19) or something like that. As for the disbeliever, he will be called out before all witnesses.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed and Hisham, and Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Hisham told us, they both said
m: in their hadith on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Safwan bin Mahraz, he said: While we were circumambulating the House with Abdullah bin Umar and he was circumambulating, a man came to him and said: O Ibn Umar, did you not hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon you) say about the secret conversation? He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon you) say: The believer draws near to his Lord until He places His protection over him, and He confesses his sins to him and says: Do you recognize such and such? He says: O Lord, forgive - twice - until he has reached what God willed for him to reach, He says: I concealed them from you in the world, and I forgive them for you today. He said: Then he will be given his record of good deeds - or: his book - in his right hand. As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, it will be called out to them before all witnesses: “These are the ones who lied about their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.”
r

That God does with His believing servant: by making him aware of his bad deeds, until He makes him aware of His favor upon him by forgiving him for them. Likewise, the Most High does in holding him accountable for what he has revealed of himself and what he has concealed of that, then He forgives him all of that after making him aware of His favor and generosity upon him, and He conceals it from him. And that is the forgiveness that God has promised His believing servants, as He said:
h
Then He forgives whom He wills

x: If someone were to say: His statement,
h
For her is what she has earned

, and against her is what she has committed (al-Baqarah 2:286), indicates that all of creation will not be held accountable except for the sin they have committed, and will not be rewarded except for the good they have earned? It was said: That is so, and the servant will not be held accountable for anything of that except for doing what he was forbidden to do, or leaving what he was ordered to do.
If that is the case, then what is the meaning of God Almighty’s threat to us for what our souls conceal in His saying:
h
And He punishes whom He wills
, Surat Al-Baqarah 2:284
h
To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth
h
And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it
h
God will bring you to account for it

. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills. And God is over all things competent. if it is for her what she earned and against her what she acquired, and what our hearts conceal and our souls conceal - of the intention to sin, or the desire to disobey - our limbs did not acquire?

God, the Most High, has promised the believers that He will pardon them for what is greater than what one of them intends to commit of sins but did not do so, and this is what we mentioned of His promise to pardon them for their minor sins if they avoid their major ones. Rather, the threat from God, the Most High, in His saying:
h
And He punishes whom He wills

, is based on what the souls of those who concealed doubt in God, and doubt in His Oneness, or in the prophethood of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought from God, or in the afterlife and resurrection - from among the hypocrites - concealed, in the manner that Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and those who said something similar to them said, that the interpretation of His saying: Or you conceal it, God will call you to account for it, is based on doubt and certainty. However, we say that the one who is threatened with His saying:
h
And He punishes whom He wills
, is the one who conceals from himself what he conceals through doubt and uncertainty in God, and in what doubt in God is disbelief, and the one who is promised forgiveness with His saying:
h
Then He forgives whom He wills

, is the one who conceals what he conceals, the intention to advance on some of what God has forbidden from things that were permissible at the beginning of its permissibility, so He forbade it to His creation, may He be glorified, or to abandon what God has commanded to be done, from what was permissible at the beginning of its permissibility, so He made it obligatory for His creation to do it. For the one who intends to do that from the believers - if he does not correct his intention with what he intends to do, and realize what his soul has concealed from that by advancing on it - will not be held accountable for it, as was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, it will be recorded as a good deed for him, and whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, it will not be recorded as a bad deed for him. This is what we have described, and that is what God will hold His believing servants accountable for, and then He will not punish them for it.

As for the one whose soul conceals doubt in God and suspicion in the prophethood of His prophets, he is the one who will perish forever in the Fire, and whom God, the Most High, has threatened with painful torment, saying:
h
And He punishes whom He wills
The interpretation of the verse is: And if you disclose what is in your souls, O people, so you show it, or conceal it, so your souls conceal it,
h
God will bring you to account for it

, so your believer will know His favor in pardoning and forgiving him, so He will forgive him, and He will punish your hypocrite for the doubt that his soul conceals in the oneness of his Creator and the prophethood of His prophets.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God Almighty is able to pardon what this believer’s soul has hidden of the desire to sin, and to punish the unbeliever for what his soul has hidden of doubt in the oneness of God Almighty and the prophethood of His prophets, and to punish each one of them for what he has done, and other matters.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: The readings differed in the reading of that.
The readers in all the countries read it as a writer, meaning: And you did not find anyone to write for you the book of the debt that you borrowed for a specified period, a pledge in possession.
The reading that is not permissible other than it according to us is the reading of the regions, And you did not find a writer, meaning: someone who writes.
Mention of those who interpreted this based on the reading we mentioned:

Yaqub told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said, Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid: He used to recite it: If you do not find a book, and he would say: Perhaps the writer is found but the page or ink is not found, and something similar to this statement.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And if you are on a journey and you cannot find a book, he says: ink - he reads it like this - he says: If you cannot find ink, then at that time the pledges are taken, then a pledge taken, he said: The pledge is only taken while travelling.

Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj told us, he said, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Shu’ayb bin Al-Habhab, he said: Abu Al-Aaliyah used to recite it: If you do not find a book, Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The inkwell is found but the paper is not found.
Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of his statement: A pledge taken.

The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as: Farhan Maqbudha, meaning the collection of a pledge, just as rams are the collection of a ram, mules are the collection of a mule, and sandals are the collection of sandals.
Another group read it as: farahn maqbudah meaning the plural of rahan, and rahan is the plural of rahan.
Others read it as farhan with a lightened ha meaning plural of rahn, just as saqf is pluralized as saqf.
Abu Jaʿfar said: What is more correct in this regard is the reading of the one who read it: Farhan Maqbudah.

The one who read it as: a pledge in possession was prompted to read it as such, I think, despite its anomaly in the plural of faʿl, because he found the wager used in the case of a horse bet, so he wanted to divert that from the ambiguous wording of a wager of horses, which is not in the meaning of a wager, which is the plural of rahn, and he found the wager used in the plural of rahn, as Qanab said: Suad has left, and Aden has become distant from her, and the pledge in your heart has been closed to her.

Abu al-Raddad al-Masri Abdullah bin Abdul Salam told me, he said, Abu Zur’ah Wahb God bin Rashid told us, on the authority of Haywah bin Shuraih, he said, I heard Yazid bin Abi Habib say: Ibn Shihab said, Saeed bin Marjana told me, he said: I came to Abdullah bin Omar and he recited this verse: “And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it.

He said: Then I came to Abdullah bin Abbas and said: O Abu Abbas, I came to Ibn Omar and he recited this verse: And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, the verse, then he said: If we take this verse to task, we will be destroyed!

Then Ibn Omar cried until he heard his sobs, and Ibn Marjana said: So I got up and went to Ibn Abbas and mentioned to him what Ibn Omar had recited, and what he did when he recited it, and Abdullah bin Abbas said: May God forgive Abu Abd al-Rahman!

Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, I heard al-Zuhri say about the verse: Whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, he said: Ibn Umar read it and wept and said: We will be held accountable for what we tell ourselves!

x: By that, may His praise be exalted, He meant that the Messenger - meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - believed, so he acknowledged - what was revealed to him, meaning: what was revealed to him from his Lord of the Book, and what is in it of what is permissible and what is forbidden, and promise and threat, and command and prohibition, and other than that from the rest of the meanings that it contains. And he mentioned that when this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: It is right for him.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord

. He mentioned to us that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he has the right to believe. It has been said that it was revealed after His statement: “And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills. And God is over all things competent.” Because the believers in the Messenger of God from among his companions were distressed by what God threatened them with of holding them accountable for what they concealed in their souls, so they complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Perhaps you will say: We hear and disobey, as the Children of Israel said! They said: Rather, we will say: We hear and obey! So God revealed for that reason from the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the statement of his companions: “
h
The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord

, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers.” He says: And the believers also believed with their Prophet in God and His angels and His books and His messengers, the two verses. We have mentioned those who said that before.

x: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of his statement: And He wrote it. The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the readers of Iraq read it as and His books in the plural form of the book, meaning: and the believers, all of them believe in God and His angels and all of His books that He sent down to His prophets and messengers.

A group of the people of Kufa read it: And His Book, meaning: And the believers, all of them believe in God and His angels and in the Qur’an that He revealed to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: It was narrated from Ibn Abbas
m: that he used to read it: And His Book, and he said: The Book is more than the books. It is as if Ibn Abbas was directing the interpretation of that to something like His saying: “By the declining day. Indeed, mankind is in loss.”
r

, meaning the type of people and the type of the Book, as one says: How many are the dirhams and dinars of so-and-so, meaning the type of dirhams and dinars. And although this is a well-known doctrine, what is more pleasing to me than reading it in the plural form is to read it in the plural form. Because what precedes it is a plural, and what follows it is likewise - I mean by that: And His angels, His books, and His messengers - so adding the books in the plural form to it is more pleasing to me than making it Surat Al-Baqarah 2:285
h
The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord
, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers.
h
We make no distinction between any of His messengers

, and they say, "We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination." unified and excluding it in the pronunciation in the singular form, so that it would be later in the pronunciation in meaning with the pronunciation of what precedes it and what follows it, and with its meaning.

x: As for His saying:
h
We make no distinction between any of His messengers
, then He, the Most High, informed of that about the believers that they would say that. In the discussion of the reading of those who read
h
We make no distinction between any of His messengers

with the letter nun, there is something left out, and the indication of what was mentioned is sufficient. That which was left out is: they say. The interpretation of the statement is: And the believers, all of them believe in God and His angels and His books and His messengers, they say:
h
We make no distinction between any of His messengers
. And the mention of they say was left out because the statement indicates it, just as it was left out in His statement: “
h
And the angels will enter upon them from every gate
. Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured.” (13:23-24), meaning: they say: Peace.

A group of the early scholars read: He does not differentiate between any of His messengers with the letter ya, meaning: “And the believers all believe in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. None of them differentiates between any of His messengers, believing in some and disbelieving in others. Rather, they believe in all of them, and they acknowledge that what they brought was from God, and that they called to God and to His obedience.

They differ in their actions from the Jews who acknowledged Moses and denied Jesus, and the Christians who acknowledged Moses and Jesus and denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and rejected his prophethood, and from the nations like them who denied some of God’s messengers and acknowledged others, such as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: “We do not differentiate between any of His messengers,” as the people did - meaning the Children of Israel - they said: So-and-so is a prophet, and so-and-so is not a prophet, and so-and-so we believe in, and so-and-so we do not believe in.

x: The reading that we do not accept other than that in our view with the letter nun is: We do not differentiate between any of His messengers, because it is the reading whose proof is established by widespread transmission, which prevents sympathy, collusion, forgetfulness, and error, in the sense of what we described of: They say we do not differentiate between any of His messengers, and no objection is made to an anomalous reading, on what the proof has brought by transmission and inheritance.

By that, He, the Most High, means: And all of the believers said, We heard, the saying of our Lord and His command to us with what He commanded us to do, and His prohibition of what He prohibited us from doing, and we obeyed, meaning: We obeyed our Lord in what He imposed upon us of His obligations and enslaved us with His obedience, and we submitted to Him. And His statement, Your forgiveness, our Lord, means: And they said, Your forgiveness, our Lord, meaning: Forgive us, our Lord, with Your forgiveness, just as one says, Glory be to You, meaning: We glorify You, glory be to You. We have previously explained that forgiveness and pardon are the concealment by God of the sins of the one whom He has forgiven, and His pardon of him for violating His cover with it in this world and the hereafter, and His pardon of the punishment - upon him. As for His saying: And to You is the return, He, may His praise be glorified, means that they said: To You, our Lord, is our return and our place of return, so forgive us our sins.

If someone were to say to us: What is the subject of his statement: Your forgiveness? It was said to him: Its occurrence is the source of the location of the command. And the Arabs do the same with the sources and nouns if they replace the command, and convey the meaning of the command, they make it the accusative, so they say: Thank God, so-and-so, and praise be to Him, meaning: thank God and praise Him. And prayer, prayer, meaning: pray.

i: And they say in the nouns: God, God, O people, and if it is raised with the meaning: He is God, and: This is God - and directed to the report and in it is the interpretation of the command, it is permissible, as the poet said:
x: Some of them are Umair and Ashba 5 Umair and among them is Al-Saffah Worthy of loyalty if the brother of help says: Weapon, weapon If his saying, Your forgiveness, our Lord, had come in the nominative case in the reading, it would not have been a mistake, but rather it would have been correct, as we have described.

It was mentioned that when this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as praise from God to him and his nation, Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: God Almighty has praised you and your nation well, so ask your Lord.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Bayan, on the authority of Hakim bin Jabir, he said:
m: When the verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “
h
The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord
, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers.
h
We make no distinction between any of His messengers

. And they say, “We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination,” Gabriel said: God Almighty has praised you and your nation well, so ask - out of respect - and he asked: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity to the end of the surah.

evidence.text: Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the reading of his statement: And He wrote it.

The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the readers of Iraq read it as and His books in the plural form of the book, meaning: and the believers, all of them believe in God and His angels and all of His books that He sent down to His prophets and messengers.

A group of the people of Kufa read it: And His Book, meaning: And the believers, all of them believe in God and His angels and in the Qur’an that He revealed to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he used to read it: And His Book, and he said: The Book is more than the books.
And although this is a well-known doctrine, what is more pleasing to me than reading it in the plural form is to read it in the plural form.

In the discussion of the reading of those who read We make no distinction between any of His messengers with the letter nun, there is something left out, and the indication of what was mentioned is sufficient.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The reading that we do not accept other than that in our view with the letter nun is: We do not differentiate between any of His messengers, because it is the reading whose proof is established by widespread transmission, which prevents sympathy, collusion, forgetfulness, and error, in the sense of what we described of: They say we do not differentiate between any of His messengers, and no objection is made to an anomalous reading, on what the proof has brought by transmission and inheritance.

And they say in the nouns: God, God, O people, and if it is raised with the meaning: He is God, and: This is God - and directed to the report and in it is the interpretation of the command, it is permissible, as the poet said: Some of them are Umair and Ashba 5 Umair and among them is Al-Saffah Worthy of loyalty if the brother of help says: Weapon, weapon If his saying, Your forgiveness, our Lord, had come in the nominative case in the reading, it would not have been a mistake, but rather it would have been correct, as we have described.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: God does not burden a soul with worship except to the extent that it can bear, so He does not make it difficult or exhaust it.

We have previously explained that wasaa is a noun derived from the saying of the speaker: This matter was sufficiency for me, like jahd and wajd from: This matter exerted itself upon me and I found it sufficiency, as in:

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity

, he said: They are the believers, and God heard their religious matter, so God, the Most High, said: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty (al-Hajj 22:78), and He said: God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship (al-Baqarah 2:85), and He said: So fear God as much as you are able (al-Taghabun 64:116). Al-Qasim narrated, Al-Husayn narrated, Hajjaj narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said: When this was revealed, the believers were in great distress because of it and said: O Messenger of God, we repent from the deeds of the hand, foot and tongue! How do we repent from the whisperings? How do we refrain from them? Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came with this verse:
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. You cannot refrain from the whisperings.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. Its capacity, its ability. And the talk of the soul was something they could not bear.

x: What He, may He be glorified, means by His saying: for it is for the soul which He informed that He does not charge it except within its capacity.
He says: for every soul what it has committed and done of good, and upon it, meaning: and upon every soul, what it has earned, what it has done of evil, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying: “
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
. It will have whatever it has earned,” meaning: of good, and it will bear whatever it has earned, meaning: of evil - or he said: of bad.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: For her is what she has earned, he says: what good she has done, and against her is what she has acquired, he says: and against her is what evil she has done.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Qatada, similarly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Abbas:
m: She shall have what she has earned, and she shall bear what she has earned, the work of the hand, foot, and tongue.

x: The interpretation of the verse is: God does not charge a soul except according to its capacity. He does not overburden it or make things difficult for it in the matter of its religion, nor does He hold it accountable for its desire if it desires, nor for a whisper if it occurs to it, nor for a thought if it crosses its heart.
This is a teaching from God Almighty to His believing servants, how they should supplicate Him, and what they should say in their supplication to Him.

Its meaning is: Say: Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget something that You have imposed upon us to do and we do not do it, or make a mistake in doing something that You have forbidden us to do and we do it, without intending to disobey You, but out of ignorance and error, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake
, if we forget something that You have made obligatory upon us, or make a mistake, [and] do something that You have forbidden us.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake
, he said: It has reached me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty has forgiven this nation for its forgetfulness and what their souls have thought about.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, he said,
m: Al-Suddi claimed that when this verse was revealed: Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make a mistake, he said, Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to him: So say that, O Muhammad.

x: If someone were to say to us: Is it permissible for God Almighty to hold His servants accountable for what they forgot or made a mistake, and they ask Him not to hold them accountable for that? It was said: Forgetfulness has two aspects: one is due to the servant’s negligence and carelessness, and the other is due to the forgetful person’s inability to memorize what he was entrusted with and his mind’s weakness in bearing it. As for that which is done by the servant in a manner of neglect and negligence, it is his abandonment of what he was commanded to do. That is what the servant desires from God the Almighty in abandoning it and holding him accountable for it, which is forgetfulness. God the Almighty punished Adam (peace be upon him) with it and expelled him from Paradise, and He said about that:
And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot, and We found on his part no firm will

It is the forgetfulness about which God the Almighty said: So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs (al-A’raf 7:51). So the servant’s desire to God the Almighty in his saying: Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake

, in what he forgot about what he was commanded to do in this manner that we have described, as long as his abandonment of what he abandoned was not negligence on his part, or neglect, or disbelief in God the Almighty. If that is disbelief in God, then asking God to leave him and hold him accountable is not permissible, because God the Almighty has informed His servants that He will not forgive them for associating partners with Him.

c: So asking him to do what He has informed them that
m: he will not do is wrong. Rather, asking for forgiveness would be in cases such as forgetting the Qur’an after memorizing it due to being distracted from it and from reading it, or forgetting a prayer or fasting due to being distracted from them by something else until he neglected them. As for that for which the servant is not held accountable, due to the inability of his constitution to memorize it, and the inability of his mind to bear what he was entrusted to observe, then that from the servant is not a sin, and he is not a sinner by it. So there is no reason for the servant to ask his Lord to forgive him, because it is a question from Him to forgive him for what he has not committed a sin. This is like the matter that overcomes him while he is keen to remember and memorize it, like a man who is keen to memorize the Qur’an with diligence from him, so he recites it, then he forgets it without being distracted by anything else, but due to the inability of his constitution to memorize it, and the inability of his mind to bear remembering what he has deposited in his heart of it, and similar forgetfulness, then that is something for which it is not permissible to ask the Lord to forgive, because the servant has no sin in it, so He forgives him for it based on his own earning. And also the error has two faces: One of them: From the aspect of what the servant was forbidden from, so he does it with intent and will, and that is a mistake on his part, and he is taken by it. It is said from it: So-and-so made a mistake and erred in what he did of the action, and he sinned, if he did what he sinned in and did it, and from it is the saying of the poet: People blame the prince if they make a mistake, but the guide is not to be blamed. That is, they made a mistake, and this is the way in which the servant asks his Lord to forgive him for any sin he committed, except for what was disbelief. The other of them: what he did out of ignorance of it, and thinking that he had done it, like someone who eats at night in the month of Ramadan thinking that dawn has not yet come, or delays a prayer on a cloudy day while waiting for its time to come in by delaying it, then its time comes out while he thinks that its time has not come. This is from the error placed on the servant, for which God the Almighty has placed the sin on His servants, so there is no reason for the servant to ask his Lord not to hold him accountable for it.
b.via: So asking him to do what He has

x: Some people have claimed that the servant’s asking his Lord not to hold him accountable for what he forgot or made a mistake is only an action on his part that his Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, has commanded him to do, or that which He has urged him to do in terms of humility and submission to Him in asking. As for the way he asks for forgiveness, this has no basis in their view. Surat Al-Baqarah 2:286 Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have whatever it has gained, and it will bear whatever it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear.
h
And pardon us
h
and forgive us
; and have mercy upon us.
h
You are our Master
, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.
To explain these people, we will provide a book in which, God willing, we will provide sufficient information for those who are able to understand it.
By that, the Most High means: Say: Our Lord,
h
and do not place upon us a burden
, meaning by burden the covenant, as the Most High said:
He said, ‘Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourselves My burden?’
What He meant by His statement,
h
And do not place upon us a burden

, is do not place upon us a covenant that we are unable to carry out and are not able to do, as You placed upon those before us, meaning: upon the Jews and Christians who were charged with tasks, and whose covenants and pledges were taken from them to carry them out, but they did not carry them out, so they were hastened to receive punishment. So God, the Most High, concealed the desire of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by asking Him not to place upon them from His covenants and pledges actions - if they neglected them, or made mistakes in them, or forgot them - like what He placed upon those before them, so that He would befall them, due to their mistakes in it and their neglect of it, like what He befell those before them.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: Do not impose upon us a burden, he said: Do not impose upon us a covenant or a pact, as You imposed upon those before us, he said: as You imposed upon those before us.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Musa bin Qais Al-Hadrami, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not place a burden upon us
, he said: a covenant.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: a covenant, he said: a covenant.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah told us, he said, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: a covenant, he said: a covenant.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Our Lord,
h
and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us
. And the burden is the covenant that was upon the Jews before us.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not place upon us a burden
, he said: A covenant that we cannot bear or fulfill, as You placed upon those before us, the Jews and Christians, but they did not fulfill it, so You destroyed them.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Isra, he said: covenants.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
m: The covenant is the pledge. And you took upon you My covenant
r
(Al Imran 3:81)
, he said: My covenant.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And you took upon you My covenant
r
(Al Imran 3:81)
, he said: My covenant.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Do not burden us with sins and guilt, as You burdened the nations before us, and turn us into apes and pigs as You turned them.
Who said that?

c: Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, he said, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Ali bin Harun, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us
, he said: Do not transform us into apes and pigs.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: Our Lord,
h
and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us
, do not place upon us a sin for which there is no repentance or expiation.

x: Others said: The meaning of Isr with a kasra on the alif is: heaviness.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ammar,
m: who said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabiʿ, regarding his statement: Our Lord,
h
and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us
, meaning: the severity that You placed upon those of the People of the Book whom we mentioned.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: I asked him - meaning Malik - about his saying:
h
And do not place a burden upon us
, he said: The burden is the severe matter.

x: As for the word asr, with the alif open, it is what a man has in common with another due to kinship or blood relation. A kinship between me and so-and-so has made me sympathetic to him, meaning: it made me sympathetic to him. And what makes me sympathetic to him, meaning: what makes me sympathetic to him. And between me and him is a kinship bond that makes me sympathetic to him, meaning: a kinship bond that makes me sympathetic to him.

By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: And also say: Our Lord, do not burden us with work that we cannot bear to do, because its burden is too heavy for us. And this is how the group of people of interpretation interpreted it.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear, is an emphasis that is emphasized, just as it was emphasized for those who came before you.

c: Yahya bin Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear
, he said: Do not burden us with deeds that we cannot bear.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear, do not impose upon us of religion that which we have no ability to bear, so that we are unable to do it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
And do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear
, the transformation of monkeys and pigs.

c: Salam bin Salem Al-Khuza’i told me, he said, Abu Hafs Omar bin Saeed Al-Tanukhi told us, he said, Muhammad bin Shuaib bin Shabur told us, on the authority of Salem bin Shabur,
m: regarding his statement: Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear, he said: The young men.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear, from the severity and shackles that were upon them from the prohibition.

x: We said that the interpretation of that is: And do not charge us with deeds that we cannot bear to do, in the manner that we said about that, because it follows the believers’ question to their Lord that He not punish them if they forget or make a mistake, and that He not place a burden on them as He placed on those before them. So attaching that to the meaning of what preceded it of their question of making the religion easy was more appropriate than what contradicted that meaning.
In this also, from the words of God Almighty, reporting on the believers from their asking Him for that, is the clear indication that they asked Him for His obligations upon them by saying:
h
And do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear
, because they followed that with their saying:
h
And pardon us

, asking their Lord to pardon them for any shortcomings if they were on their part in some of what He commanded them to do of His obligations, so He would pardon them for it and not punish them for it, if what He charged them with of His obligations was light on their bodies.
Some of the interpreters said something similar to what we said about this.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And pardon us
, he said: Pardon us if we fall short of something of what you have commanded us to do. Likewise, his saying:
h
And forgive us
, meaning: And cover up for us a mistake if we commit it between us and you, so do not reveal it or disgrace us by revealing it. We have already explained the meaning of forgiveness.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And forgive us
if we violate something that you have forbidden us from.

x: By that, may His praise be glorified, He means: Envelop us with Your mercy by which You will save us from Your punishment, for no one will be saved from Your punishment except through Your mercy to him, not through his deeds.
And our deeds will not save us if You do not have mercy on us, so guide us to that which pleases You from us, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said,
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,
h
And have mercy on us
, he said, he means: We cannot do what you have commanded us to do, nor leave what you have forbidden us from, except through your mercy. He said: And no one is saved except through your mercy.

x: What He, may His praise be exalted, means by His saying,
h
You are our Master
, is that
h
You are our Master

through Your support, not those who oppose You and disbelieve in You, because we believe in You and obey You in what You have commanded us and forbidden us. You are the Master of those who obey You and the enemy of those who disbelieve in You and disobey You. So support us, because we are Your party, against the disbelieving people, who denied Your Oneness and worshipped gods and rivals instead of You, and obeyed Satan in their disobedience to You. In this position, the word mawla is a passive participle, from: Wali so-and-so is the guardian of so-and-so’s affair, so he is his guardian, and he is his guardian and master. The ya of wali became an alif because of the open lam before it, which is the root of the noun. They mentioned that when God Almighty revealed this verse to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, God responded to him in all of that.
Mention the report that came with that:

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim and Muhammad bin Khalaf told me, they said, Adam told us, he said, Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: he Surat Al-Baqarah 2:286 Allah does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have whatever it has gained, and it will bear whatever it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear.
h
And pardon us
h
and forgive us
; and have mercy upon us.
h
You are our Master

, so give us victory over the disbelieving people. said: When this verse was revealed: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, and when he reached the words: Your forgiveness, our Lord, God Almighty said: I have forgiven you. When he recited: Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake
, God Almighty said: I will not burden you. When he recited:
h
And forgive us

, God Almighty said: I have forgiven you. When he recited: And have mercy upon us, God Almighty said: I have had mercy upon you. When he recited: And give us victory over the disbelieving people, God Almighty said: I have given you victory over them.

c: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, he said:
m: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, say: Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake

. So he said it, and Gabriel said: He has done it. Gabriel said to him: Say: Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. So he said it, and Gabriel said: He has done it. He said: Say: Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. So he said it, and Gabriel said: He has done it. He said: Say: “
h
And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us
. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.” So he said it, and Gabriel said: He has done it.

c: Musa told me, he said, Amr told us, he said, Asbat told us, he said:
m: Al-Suddi claimed that this verse was revealed: Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake
, so Gabriel said to him: He did that, O Muhammad, “Our Lord,
h
and do not place upon us a burden like that which You placed upon those before us
. Our Lord,
h
and do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear
h
And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us
. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people,” so Gabriel said to him in all of that: He did that, O Muhammad.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Wakiʿ narrated to us, and Sufyan narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Adam bin Sulayman,
m: the freed slave of Khalid, he said: I heard Saʿid bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God Almighty revealed: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord until His saying: Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake
. So he recited: Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake

. He said: I have done so. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. He said: I have done so. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. He said: I have done so. “
h
And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us
. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.” He said: I have done so.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said, Ishaq bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Musʿab bin Thabit, on the authority of Al-ʿAlaʿ bin ʿAbd Al-Rahman bin Yaʿqub, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: God Almighty revealed: Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake
. My father said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty said: Yes.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abu Ahmad told us, on the authority of Adam bin Sulayman, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity

. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has committed. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred.” He said, and he said, I have done so. “Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us.” He said, and he said, I have done so. So this nation was given the final verses of Surat al-Baqarah, and the nations before it were not given them.

c: Ali bin Harb Al-Mawsili narrated to us, he said, Ibn Fadil narrated to us, he said, Ata bin Al-Sa’ib narrated to us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord to His statement: Your forgiveness, our Lord, he said: I have forgiven you,
h
God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity
, to His statement:
h
Do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake
, he said: I will not impose blame upon you, Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us, he said: I will not impose a burden upon you, to His statement:
h
And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us
, You are our Protector, to the end of the surah, he said: I have pardoned you and forgiven you, and have mercy upon you, and given you victory over the disbelieving people.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim
m: that God’s response to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was specific.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement: Our Lord,
h
do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake

. Gabriel, peace be upon him, used to say to him: Ask it! So the Prophet of God, may His praise be exalted, asked it of his Lord, and He gave it to him, and it was specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Al-Muthanna bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Abu Naim told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq:
m: That when Muadh finished this surah: And give us victory over the disbelieving people, he would say: Amen.

They mentioned that when God Almighty revealed this verse to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, God responded to him in all of that.

You are our Master, so give us victory over the disbelieving people. said: When this verse was revealed: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it, and when he reached the words: Your forgiveness, our Lord, God Almighty said: I have forgiven you.
